synopsis: Luscombe 8A pilot reported the aircraft got away from him during a hand prop exercise with an instructor, striking a truck and another aircraft.
summary: A student pilot hand-propping an aircraft forgot to retard the fully advanced throttle while distracted by a vehicle, causing the unoccupied plane to move forward. The aircraft struck a parked truck and the vertical stabilizer of a nearby plane, resulting in damage to all three.

synopsis: A C182RG nose landing gear collapsed during landing with all indications normal up to the point of the collapse.
summary: During a Cessna 182RG training flight, a student pilot and instructor executed a short-field landing where the nose gear collapsed upon touchdown, causing the propeller to strike the runway. The reporter noted the approach was stabilized and proper, but the cause of the collapse remains unknown.

synopsis: A PC-12 nose landing gear failed to extend, so after all troubleshooting options were exhausted, an emergency nose gear up landing was completed with the propeller feather which resulted in very little damage.
summary: The pilot executed a gear-up landing after the nose gear failed to extend and lock, resulting in two propeller blades contacting the runway. While the blades were damaged, the aircraft structure remained intact, and the cause of the gear failure remains undetermined.

synopsis: A C150 pilot declared an emergency and diverted after his engine lost power at cruise but power recovered during descent. A Mechanic believed water in the fuel was the problem.
summary: The pilot experienced engine power fluctuations at 4,500 feet while on Approach radar services, forcing a descent and consideration of a lake landing. Power recovered at 2,000 feet allowing a safe landing, and a mechanic later attributed the issue to suspected water in the fuel system.

synopsis: A Ballon's Rotator Vent Control Lines became entangle resulting the loss of aircraft control and a rapid descent to ground contract. The Pilot recovered and continued the flight.
summary: The pilot reported that control lines to the balloon rotator vents became entangled at 1,000 feet AGL, causing a rapid descent and surface strike. The balloon recovered with no damage to persons or property and landed 30 minutes later.

synopsis: SAV Controller voiced concern regarding RADAR/ARTS Mode S problems, describing a recent event and suggesting the replacement of some of the subject equipment. Reporter suggests improved trouble shooting and technical support.
summary: An air traffic controller reported unsafe Mode S data block coasting and stitching in the SAV ARTS system, which the monitor falsely indicated as functional. Switching to Channel B restored tracking, confirming the monitor failed to display the true Mode S status and creating an unsafe separation environment.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described an IFR vs. VFR vs. VFR-ON-TOP flight plan confusion event, noting more training is necessary for some controllers regarding this issue.
summary: An air traffic controller noticed a flight plan error where "VFR IN TOP" was entered for an IFR aircraft at 9,500 feet. The controller corrected the field to OTP/95 and re-issued a VFR on top clearance after confirming the pilot's IFR status.

synopsis: Air Carrier inbound to RFD described a less than cooperative ATC Controller during vectors for the airport, the Controller seemed reluctant to approve deviations while displaying a general unprofessional attitude.
summary: During an arrival into RFD in IMC, the pilot requested a weather deviation, leading to a hostile exchange with the RFD Approach Controller who eventually told the crew to find their own way and ceased communication. The crew broadcast intentions in the blind and contacted Chicago Center for vectors before RFD re-established contact five minutes later.

synopsis: While on a high, fast approach the Captain extended the speed brakes, landing gear and set flaps 20 in order to regain the profile then received a Stall Warning when airspeed decayed rapidly because of the extended speed brakes.
summary: The pilot flying experienced a stick shaker at 3,800 feet during approach after leaving speed brakes extended while configuring flaps. The crew recovered by stowing the brakes and advancing thrust, then discontinued the approach for a successful second attempt.

synopsis: A Q400's Master Caution alerted #1 DC GEN so the takeoff was rejected and after maintenance action to MEL the generator the #1 ENG failed to start so additional maintenance was required.
summary: The flight crew aborted a takeoff roll on Runway 15 due to a #1 DC GEN caution following maintenance, then aborted an Engine #1 start at 16% NH due to rising ITT and white smoke. The aircraft was towed back to the gate with no fire indication, classified as a hung start.

synopsis: EMB145 First Officer describes a blown tire event at rotation and the subsequent return to their departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a massive vibration and suspected blown tires immediately after rotation. They returned for a safe landing with gear down after confirming right main gear damage, resulting in one minor passenger ankle injury during evacuation.

synopsis: CRJ700 Captain experiences a red DUCT FAIL warning on the left side passing FL240 during climb. Cabin begins to depressurize as the bleed valves are automatically closed and the flight diverts to a suitable airport. The aircraft had a history of duct fail warnings that could not be duplicated by maintenance.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a left DUCT FAIL warning during climb, causing automatic bleed shutoff and rapid cabin altitude rise. They descended to 6,000 feet and landed safely, noting that the checklist's immediate emergency depressurization step could be dangerous at high altitudes and that the systems manual incorrectly describes ram air valve function.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain aborted takeoff when IAS flag appeared twice on his tape, the previous leg was flown in icing conditions.
summary: The pilot rejected takeoff at 90–95 KTS on Runway 28 after the IAS flag appeared on both PFDs. The decision was made due to suspected airspeed system issues linked to previous icing conditions and the forecast of further weather.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Captain noted that the commercial airport chart for MCC does not indicate that the airport uses a right traffic pattern and so they elected to continue a left traffic pattern opposite other traffic.
summary: The flight crew descended to an uncontrolled airport and briefed a left traffic pattern based on a commercial chart that omitted the required right pattern for Runway 16. After landing, they discovered the Airport Facility Directory listed a right pattern, prompting a recommendation to report the chart error and reference the AFD for future uncontrolled airport operations.

synopsis: Multiple miscommunications and an unexpected delay in parking at a remote ramp exposed the flight crew of a B747 to a conflict with traffic landing on Runway 26R at MIA.
summary: The flight crew crossed Runway 26L to the Northeast Ramp at Miami but stopped due to missing ground personnel, placing the aircraft on Runway 26R's extended centerline. A landing aircraft passed 100–150 feet overhead, an incident attributed to miscommunication between operations and ground crew regarding the parking location.

synopsis: MD-82 flight crew reported they shut down right engine when excessive vibration was detected in descent. Single engine landing at destination followed.
summary: The MD80 crew experienced heavy vibration at 10,000 feet caused by a failed right engine turbine bearing. The pilot identified the source, declared an emergency, and shut down the engine, resulting in a safe single-engine landing and taxi to the gate.

synopsis: A C150 pilot, trying to optimize his ground speed by flying low, struck an electrical wire but surprisingly did no damage.
summary: A Cessna 150 pilot flying low in a rural area to increase ground speed struck a wire at 30 feet while distracted by the GPS. The pilot believes the wire bounced off the beacon without causing damage, but the incident highlighted the dangers of low-level flight and cockpit distraction.

synopsis: An SR22 pilot failed to note the autopilot had disconnected upon intercepting the ILS to CRQ. ATC received an altitude alert and provided vectors back for a successful hand flown ILS.
summary: The pilot flying an ILS approach to CRQ in IMC experienced an unannounced autopilot disengagement, causing the aircraft to go off course. ATC issued an altitude alert and vectored the pilot to 4,000 feet for a hand-flown approach, which was completed without further incident.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a directed go around event where he/she failed to realized an arrival aircraft was changed to a parallel runway with traffic cleared for takeoff.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared a B737 for takeoff on Runway XXL while an A319 was on final, causing a runway incursion and ASDE-X alert. The controller realized the error, ordered the A319 to go around, and attributed the incident to fatigue from working late.

synopsis: ZDV Controller described a failed hand off event claiming the ERAM equipment has entirely too many anomalies to be in use with live traffic.
summary: A Salt Lake controller handed off a Citation V to Sector 32 Radar, but the receiving controller could not see the data block due to an ERAM anomaly. This caused a delay in radar acceptance while the aircraft climbed through another's altitude, which the reporter attributes to system errors and inadequate training.

synopsis: Tower Controller voiced concern regarding some foreign student pilots that do not understand certain control instructions such as 'expedite', the reporter noting this lack of language understanding creates a safety hazard.
summary: Air traffic control instructed a PA28 pilot to expedite crossing Runway 11R due to traffic, but the pilot did not understand the term. The controller attributed this communication failure to the student pilot's lack of English proficiency, citing it as a safety hazard.

synopsis: ZSE Controller described an unsafe condition when preparations for handling multiple foreign military aircraft were not properly briefed or planned.
summary: An air traffic controller managed multiple military fighter aircraft returning from military airspace without adequate staffing or prior briefing on foreign pilots with poor English. The controller attributed the unsafe situation to administrative failures in briefing and coordination, noting that late assistance and non-standard communication practices complicated traffic separation.

synopsis: The flight crew of a B737 received a GPWS Terrain warning for no apparent reason on short final to Runway 18 at BHM. They appropriately executed a go around.
summary: The crew received a GPWS 'Too Low Terrain' alert on short final to Runway 18 while on glide slope and airspeed, prompting a go-around. The reporter suggests this may be a GPWS anomaly, noting a NOTAM regarding terrain warnings for the Runway 36 RNAV approach.

synopsis: A B737-700 flight crew reported LE Flap Transit light after takeoff that went out, only to reappear on arrival. They diverted to a nearby airport that had longer runways and landed without incident.
summary: The flight crew experienced a Leading Edge Flaps Transit light and erroneous 'Airspeed Low' warnings during approach due to faulty slat #5 signals. After two go-arounds and declaring an emergency, they landed safely at a nearby airport with adequate stopping margins.

synopsis: A B737-700 Captain reported a near-stall incident in climb when the aircraft dropped out of VNAV into Vertical Speed mode. Reporter stated this is not an uncommon occurrence.
summary: The pilot flying experienced a low airspeed warning during climb after VNAV disengaged and Vertical Speed mode engaged unnoticed. The pilot manually lowered the nose and advanced power, recovering airspeed quickly without stalling or deviating from ATC clearances.

synopsis: B737-300 reserve flight crew reports operating a delayed flight with the Captain arriving first and doing the cockpit set up and the First Officer arriving with the passengers already boarded and the flight ready to depart. Passing FL310 the cabin altitude warning horn sounds and an emergency descent is initiated. It is discovered that the landing elevation is incorrectly set to 11,000 FT instead of 1,000 FT.
summary: The Captain incorrectly set the landing altitude to 11,000 feet instead of 1,000 feet on an analog panel during preflight due to poor visibility and schedule pressure. This caused a cabin altitude warning at FL310, prompting an emergency descent to 10,000 feet before the error was corrected and the flight continued.

synopsis: The clumsy attempt to get an on time departure while awaiting a maintenance release resulted in an extensive ground delay and a takeoff accomplished without the appropriate weight and balance data for an A319 flight crew.
summary: The flight crew departed without re-issued Final Weights after a ground delay for a Forward Lavatory Flush Motor MEL, believing initial weights were valid. An ACARS message 39 minutes post-takeoff flagged invalid weights due to the return-to-gate prompt, which the crew noted should have been sent immediately.

synopsis: The Captain of a yet to depart Eastbound Transpacific flight during extreme weather conditions voiced concern over conflicts between himself and a harried Dispatcher who was too overwhelmed with higher priority situations to discuss new routes and alternates for the flight.
summary: Pilots reported that Dispatch refused to revise the flight plan or alternates despite severe weather, turbulence, and wind shear, stating they had no time. Consequently, the crew was forced to independently plan a new route and alternates for an international flight after Dispatch dismissed their safety concerns.

synopsis: An international Captain reported extreme fatigue experienced by him and his First Officer on a non-augmented Far East leg following a Pacific crossing.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced severe microsleeps and physical impairment during a six-hour leg due to cumulative sleep debt and circadian disruption following a 24-hour duty period. The crew reported violating CRM/TEM concepts and described the flight assignment as unsafe, recommending augmentation or schedule changes to prevent future risks.

synopsis: A B747-400 Relief Pilot reported experiencing high vibration and loud noise from #1 engine after takeoff. They returned to departure airport where they were advised they had struck a bird.
summary: The flight crew experienced a growling noise, N2 vibration, and smoke from engine one shortly after takeoff, leading to a fuel dump and return to the departure airport. Post-landing investigation identified a bird strike as the cause of the engine damage.

synopsis: A320 Captain reports an ACARS failure en route at FL360. At about the same time the aircraft flies out of the current ZFW sector without a frequency change. Over twenty minutes pass before the crew detects the lost comm situation and contacts Center.
summary: The flight crew experienced ACARS failure and flew NORDO for 28 minutes during cruise due to an ATC handoff error and missed sector frequency changes. They reestablished contact via another aircraft and reported the inoperative ACARS to maintenance after landing.

synopsis: A B737-400 N2 gauge failed during start which caused a starter disconnect, so the crew did not motor to clear fuel. After the MEL was completed, on start a tailpipe fire ignited which the ground crew reported as an engine fire so emergency equipment was dispatched.
summary: During engine start, a faulty N2 gauge and MEL procedures led to a false fire report from Operations, likely caused by tailpipe torching. The crew verified no actual fire, completed the engine fire checklist without discharging bottles, and returned to the gate.

synopsis: Immediately after takeoff an A320 ECAM alerted ENG 1 BLEED AIR FAULT, then YELLOW SYS RSV OVERHEAT so an emergency was declared and the aircraft returned to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced an ENG 1 BLEED AIR FAULT and HYD YELLOW SYS RSV OVERHEAT shortly after takeoff, resulting in inoperative spoilers, yaw damper, and nose wheel steering. They declared an emergency, returned, and performed an overweight ILS landing in gusty winds without incident.

synopsis: An ERJ-170 flight crew descending on the LINNG STAR to 24R at CYYZ failed to comply with the required crossing altitude restriction between 13,000 and 11,000 at YOUTH when cleared to descend to 8,000 MSL. Only after descending below 11,000 did they read the chart note explaining the difference between US and Canadian descent clearances on STARs.
summary: Pilots on the LINNG 3 Arrival to Runway 24R descended to 8,000 feet per ATC clearance, inadvertently crossing fix YOUTH below the mandatory 11,000-foot restriction. The deviation occurred because the crew missed a chart note requiring adherence to STAR profile restrictions even when a lower altitude is assigned.

synopsis: A319 Captain reports a cracked windshield on the First Officer's side at FL370. Descent is initiated to FL230 per QRH but the crack continues to grow and the Captain elects to divert to a suitable airport.
summary: During cruise at FL370, the Captain observed a crack with arcing heating elements in the First Officer's windshield. The crew descended to 11,000 feet to halt the spread, diverted, and landed uneventfully without declaring an emergency.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier crew descending into CYYZ was confused, as are many US based crews, about the descent STAR procedure after the clearance statement 'DESCEND to XX;000 FT' and the aircraft is on the arrival routing.
summary: Two pilots flying a Toronto arrival were confused by conflicting company and official memos regarding STAR altitude restrictions. They descended to ATC-assigned altitudes rather than complying with all published STAR restrictions, resulting in uncertainty about proper procedure despite no ATC intervention.

synopsis: During cruise flight an EMB-145 main landing gear tire exploded which resulted in material loudly banging the fuselage, so without knowing the sound's source, an emergency was declared and flight diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: The flight crew declared an emergency at FL270 after hearing loud banging from the nose area during a turn, suspecting a structural issue. Post-landing inspection revealed a blown left inboard main tire, though the aircraft landed safely and was deplaned at the gate.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Fractional on the TEB JAIKE 3 STAR was told by ATC that the aircraft was off track 0.4 NM and the crew reported that same Honeywell FMS System with software V5.1 had the same issue previously and it should be updated to V6.0.
summary: Pilots descending on the JAIKE 3 STAR into TEB experienced persistent 0.4 NM left FMS deviations between 15,000 and 9,000 feet despite ATC heading corrections. The crew attributes the navigational error to outdated 5.1 software and recommends an upgrade to version 6.0 to prevent future incidents.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A revised PDC was given which indicated TYI J79 SBY THEN AS FILED after the filed routing TYI JFK DPK MAD... so the crew omitted the VILLS and JOANI because they thought they were cleared SBY then JFK.
summary: The flight crew misinterpreted a PDC clearance stating "TYI J79 SBY THEN AS FILED" as a direct routing from SBY to JFK, omitting intermediate waypoints. ATC later identified the deviation and issued a heading change to rejoin the route, with no violation cited.

synopsis: An Air Carrier crew was unable to contact ATC during the climb and because of level 5 convective activity they declared an emergency in the blind, changed course to avoid the severe weather and ATC said nothing at the frequency change.
summary: During initial climb to 16,000 feet, the crew could not contact JAX Center due to frequency congestion and turned heading 180 to avoid level 5 convective activity. They attempted to declare an emergency with uncertain reception before the handoff was completed and the flight resumed uneventfully.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 3 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An First Officer flying the PSP SBONO 1 Arrival misunderstood the Controller's 11,000 FT CLOWD crossing clearance and momentarily descended below 11,000, then returned. The Commercial Chart MAA altitude formatting at CROWD was confusing.
summary: The First Officer descended below the cleared 11,000 FT while approaching CLOWD Intersection on the SBONO approach due to mishearing the clearance and confusing it with the chart's 10,000 FT MAA. The Captain clarified the altitude within 30 seconds, resulting in no traffic conflict.

synopsis: A B727's Number 3 Generator failed mechanically resulting in all three bus tie breakers opening and numerous other breakers popping. An emergency was declared while the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced multiple generator failures and circuit breaker trips shortly after takeoff due to a mechanical failure in Generator 3 causing a kilowatt spike. They declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport, and landed safely after reengaging the Number 1 bus tie breaker on final approach.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports that no published serviceability limits exists for V-chips or crack damages in their Engineering Document 56-11-00, for cockpit acrylic windows on B767 aircraft. Only glass window pane damage limits are published, raising question of when do cracks become un-serviceable in acrylic windows.
summary: A B767-300 crew reported small cracks in the L3 cockpit acrylic window, noting a lack of specific serviceability limits for acrylic in Engineering Document 56-11-00. The reporter requested that Engineering define acrylic window limits or remove material-specific references to clarify when cracks render the window unserviceable.

synopsis: A SR22 pilot landed hard on his first touch and go but continued landing practice. After the fourth touch and go, he landed at which time prop damage was discovered so he flew the aircraft 30 miles for maintenance because it had operated normally up to that point.
summary: The pilot performed touch-and-goes, experienced a hard landing with a bounce, and later discovered curled propeller tips. Despite no in-flight engine failure or damage evidence, the pilot elected to ferry the aircraft 30 NM for inspection and repair.

synopsis: Lakes amphibian student pilot reports an emergency landing on a highway.
summary: The pilot made an emergency landing on a highway. The narrative does not specify the aircraft, phase of flight, cause, or outcome.

synopsis: Although cleared for visual approach by New Orleans TRACON, a congested Tower frequency at HUM prevented the flight crew of a BE20 from making timely contact. A traffic conflict with one of several helicopters operating at the airport resulted, followed by a TCAS RA and a go around by the reporter's aircraft.
summary: A fixed-wing crew executing a visual approach to Runway 36 at HUM could not contact the Tower due to constant helicopter clearances. The Captain initiated a missed approach to avoid a runway incursion and an airborne helicopter, attributing the hazards to a single controller being overwhelmed.

synopsis: A TEB FBO marshaling crew guided a G-V into a tight ramp area and directed a 180 degree turn between aircraft which may have allowed their jet blast to damage nearby aircraft.
summary: While taxiing a Gulfstream V at Teterboro, the crew followed marshalers' instructions to perform a tight 180-degree turn near parked aircraft. The resulting engine exhaust disengaged a gust lock on a nearby jet, which the reporter attributed to the close proximity of the maneuver and gusty winds.

synopsis: C177RG pilot reports a power loss while cruising at 12,000 FT in IMC and elects to continue to destination. Post flight reveals the engine air filter to be completely iced over.
summary: The pilot of a Cardinal RG experienced power loss and altitude deviations at 12,000 feet IMC due to induction icing, despite no airframe icing. By adjusting the mixture, the pilot maintained flight and landed safely, later discovering a frozen air filter and cowling ice.

synopsis: ARTCC Controller reported an air carrier missed a crossing restriction, then discussed who was responsible.
summary: A B737 pilot failed to comply with a crossing restriction at ZZZ at FL190, crossing instead at FL230 and missing the point by several miles. The air traffic controller reported that the flight crew ignored the restriction to perform a flight idle descent, arguing that compliance is the sole responsibility of the pilot.

synopsis: ARTCC Controller has a plan to separate aircraft, becomes distracted thinking about a personal situation, and loses separation between two aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller managing a PC12 and LJ60 near a refueling track lost situational awareness due to a personal distraction, causing a potential conflict. The controller recovered by directing the LJ60 to climb to FL190 after the pilot reported visual contact with the PC12.

synopsis: Three pilots and three controllers reported an incident where, due to Controller coordination issue, one air carrier started takeoff roll when another was crossing the runway downfield, resulting in an aborted takeoff.
summary: Local Control issued a departure clearance to a CRJ2 on Runway XXL while a CRJ7 was crossing, causing the CRJ2 to abort takeoff. The error resulted from flipping the wrong flight strip during high coordination workload, compounded by the controller answering a phone call.

synopsis: B737 Captain experiences an equipment door warning light climbing out of 13,000 FT and elects to return to the departure airport due to an apparently high cabin altitude.
summary: During climb to 14,000 feet, the crew received 'EQUIP' and 'DOORS' light annunciations and returned to base. Maintenance rectified a faulty E & E compartment door handle and deferred the door light under the MEL, resolving the issue.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reports being cleared to cross Runway 24L at LAX after an A380 departure, to discover that the red stop bar lights are on. The aircraft stops beyond the hold bars and the Tower is queried. The crew is informed that they are cleared to cross but are required to stop for the red hold bar lights by FAR. A vehicle was clearing the runway after the A380 departure.
summary: The flight crew landed at LAX and was cleared to cross Runway 24L shortly after an A380 departure. They inadvertently crossed the hold short line before stopping for illuminated red stop bars caused by a runway inspection vehicle, requiring a delay until the lights were extinguished.

synopsis: A CRJ-90 flight crew aborted their takeoff when the First Officer accidentally moved the flap lever from 20 to 8 while checking thrust setting on the roll.
summary: During takeoff, the First Officer inadvertently bumped the flap lever from 20 to 8 degrees while confirming thrust, triggering a configuration warning. The crew discontinued the takeoff, reset the flaps, and successfully departed on a second attempt.

synopsis: An Air Carrier First Officer described his ready reserve duty period followed by a rest period and then a duty assignment flight schedule which did not allow adequate rest and resulted in calling in fatigued.
summary: A pilot on late-night ready reserve was released after 10 hours of rest and assigned an afternoon flight the next day, resulting in insufficient sleep due to conflicting circadian rhythms. The pilot attributes this fatigue risk to Crew Scheduling's failure to designate specific reserve types, forcing pilots to prepare for contradictory duty scenarios simultaneously.

synopsis: Following an apparent engine malfunction on final, an EMB145 filled with smoke so thick the flight crew could not see the instruments. Even with ice encrusted windscreens, they were able to land then successfully evacuate the aircraft.
summary: The Pilot Not Flying reported that during a final approach in icing and low visibility, Engine 2 vibration and smoke filled the cockpit, likely caused by an oil leak. The crew landed immediately, evacuated the aircraft, and found no injuries despite thick smoke obscuring instruments and the view.

synopsis: ATC cleared a B737-800 for takeoff, but that flight crew thought an aircraft on approach was lined up on their runway. As they delayed ATC commanded the other aircraft to go around as that aircraft's crew questioned their landing clearance.
summary: The crew stopped their aircraft on Runway Bravo after the First Officer identified a conflicting landing aircraft, prompting a Tower go-around. The reporter attributed the incident to an ATC error that cleared the crew for takeoff while another aircraft was landing on the same runway.

synopsis: A B737-800 Captain selected MCP SPD during climb in moderate turbulence and later a FMC 'BUFFETT ALERT' was noticed, followed by airspeed in the yellow arc. The autopilot was disconnect and a stall recovery completed with a 200-300 FT altitude loss.
summary: During a climb to FL360 in turbulence, the Captain used Airspeed Intervention of 270, causing a buffet alert and momentary stick shaker. The crew recovered by disconnecting the autopilot and advancing throttles, losing 200-300 feet, and attributed the event to improper speed selection instead of using VNAV.

synopsis: A Captain report's he performed a preflight type walk-around for a hail damage inspection of their CRJ-700 aircraft after Maintenance Control informed him the procedure would be adequate for dispatch. The First Officer suggested calling Chief Pilot who agreed. Mechanic at next station showed Captain the hail dents on flaps and spoilers that were missed.
summary: A CRJ-700 captain performed a walk-around inspection after hail exposure while parked at the gate, finding no damage under wet, overcast conditions. A mechanic later discovered dents on the flaps and spoilers, revealing that pilot inspections missed damage visible only on dry surfaces with proper lighting.

synopsis: An MD82 climbing to FL340 with anti-ice began an uncommanded descent at FL327 because of poor aircraft performance and so requested a descent to FL320.
summary: The flight crew descended from FL327 to FL325 due to icing and performance issues while climbing to FL340, despite performance charts indicating the climb was feasible with anti-ice on. ATC noted the descent occurred before clearance was issued, though light rime ice and turbulence were observed.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier crew over mountainous terrain understood they were cleared to 10,000 FT, but while descending through 13,000 FT, ATC commanded a LOW ALTITUDE ALERT with an immediate climb to 14,500 FT. No EGPWS warning alerted.
summary: The flight crew descended to 10,000 feet after verifying the altitude selector, but ATC issued a low altitude alert and instructed an immediate climb to 14,500 feet due to a clearance discrepancy. The First Officer manually climbed to 14,500 feet, and the crew continued the approach without incident or GPWS warnings.

synopsis: Bell 412, recently out of maintenance, started counterclockwise spin on startup as soon as pilot rolled RPM up toward 100%. Full right pedal, full down collective, and RPM roll back stopped spin at 270 degrees. Minor injury to ground assistant and minor damage to aircraft.
summary: During engine start, a helicopter spun 270 degrees counter-clockwise after the pilot advanced throttles, striking a plastic pillar and injuring a medical staff member. The crew attributed the incident to uncommanded left pedal input despite prestart checks, resulting in minimal damage and a tow to maintenance.

synopsis: A B767 First Officer on the Oceanic LAX SADDE Arrival was issued a constraint 60 west of VTU at FL190, but a previous FMC programming error correction deleted the restriction which caused them cross the restriction high.
summary: The flight crew entered an incorrect speed/altitude restriction in the FMC while transitioning from oceanic to LAX airspace, inadvertently deleting a prior ATC crossing clearance. This error caused the aircraft to miss the required descent point, necessitating a revised clearance for a best rate of descent to FL190.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: An ERCO 415-D propeller struck a bird in flight, causing severe engine vibration as about 5-6 inches of the propeller came off. The pilot shut the engine down and landed safely at a nearby airport.
summary: A pilot and passenger experienced a bird strike at 3,500 feet, causing propeller damage and vibration during cruise. The pilot secured the engine and executed an emergency landing on Runway XX without radio contact, relying on visual clearance and see-and-avoid procedures.

synopsis: Tower Controller described an alleged wake turbulence event when turning a light aircraft through the path of a previous departing air carrier. The light aircraft claimed ATC took him through the wake.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared a BE36 and an MD88 for departure, directing the BE36 behind the MD88 while both were climbing near 3,000 feet. The BE36 pilot later claimed the controller routed the aircraft directly through the MD88's wake turbulence, though the controller believed traffic advisories were unnecessary.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described an airspace violation and unsafe condition, claiming the Controller responsible has been identified to Management but no action has been taken.
summary: Controller Mr. Y approved a C750 with bad routing, creating a descent conflict and violating the reporter's airspace by handing off the aircraft to the wrong sector. This negligence forced adjacent sectors to intervene to resolve the conflict and comply with crossing restrictions.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a probable loss of separation event during a military re-fueling exercise when maneuvering intentions by the tanker were not clarified.
summary: An air traffic controller managing two sectors allowed refueling Aircraft Y to maneuver right due to sun angle, causing a conflict with Aircraft X on a left vector. The controller's subsequent instructions failed to maintain separation, and the controller noted they should have defined the tanker's maneuver more precisely.

synopsis: ZBW Controller described a confused routing event initiated by N90 noting the procedure in question should be formalized and contained in an LOA.
summary: ZBW Sector 32 controllers reported that two aircraft departing KHPN were handed off from N90 on a DIRECT HTO route instead of the expected DIRECT BEADS. This routing discrepancy caused the climbing departures to conflict head-on with descending JFK arrivals due to a 40-degree track difference.

synopsis: A B757-200 LE SLAT DISAGREE EICAS alerted during landing preparations so an emergency was declared. During a vector delay the LE Slat Disagree Checklist was completed, followed by a normal landing.
summary: During a visual approach, the flight crew received a LE SLAT DISAGREE EICAS message after selecting flaps 1. They declared an emergency, diverted to the longest runway, and landed safely after completing non-normal checklists.

synopsis: A B747-400 developed a 5.0 engine vibration after takeoff, and after the thrust was reduced then advanced compressor stalls resulted so as a precaution the flight returned to the departure airport. Apparently a bird was ingested during takeoff.
summary: The pilot reported a loud rumbling noise and Engine 1 vibration during gear retraction, followed by three compressor stalls when advancing thrust. The aircraft returned to the departure airport after fuel dumping, where maintenance found compressor blade damage and a blood trail in the aft engine area.

synopsis: An air carrier Captain flying a PHX arrival into the sun followed a TCAS RA climb, but because of his white shirt's glare in the PFD, was unable to see the Vertical Speed TCAS advisory and so executed an escape maneuver to assure separation.
summary: The pilot and First Officer encountered a TCAS RA while approaching a small GA aircraft. Sun glare on the PFD obscured the advisory, causing the pilot to manually climb and subsequently dip 400 feet below the ESDEE crossing altitude during recovery.

synopsis: A reserve First Officer reported that after landing at either 0500 or 0700, reserve pilots are expected to be phone ready for next day assignments during that day, which does not allow for adequate rest. The reporter called in fatigued for an trip and was docked pay.
summary: Pilots reported fatigue after flying all-nighters and receiving early morning reserve calls while required to remain phone-available during crew rest. One pilot missed a 0300 call due to sleep deprivation, resulting in pay docking and a missed flight despite the unsafe scheduling practices.

synopsis: A pilot reports hearing a 'thump' during departure rotation of their B747-400 aircraft. Passenger later notified Flight Attendant about seeing rubber flying past their window. All cockpit indications were normal. After arrival, Mechanic finds the right main wing landing gear, main tire tread cap was missing, inboard flap had large gash, with rubber marks and punctures in the lower wing.
summary: During departure, the crew heard a thump and later learned a tire blew, causing rubber to strike the wing and flap. Post-flight inspection confirmed the tire tread was missing and the aircraft underside sustained punctures, though the flight and landing remained normal with no system leaks.

synopsis: During approach, an A320 ECAM alerted FLAPS LOCKED - DUE TO ALIGNMENT, so an emergency was declared, the QRH procedure completed, and a normal landing ensused.
summary: The flight crew encountered a "FLAPS LOCKED - DUE TO ALIGNMENT" ECAM message on approach, causing flaps to remain near position 2. They declared an emergency, followed QRH procedures, and executed an uneventful landing with the flaps locked in the failed position.

synopsis: During climb, an A319 ECAM alerted HYD Y RSVR LO LVL, so an emergency was declared. After a normal landing, the emergency was terminated.
summary: The crew experienced a Hydraulic Y failure and stood by with equipment for potential further issues. They executed a normal landing, terminated the emergency with Tower, and proceeded to the gate.

synopsis: An A319 Captain addressed his confusion with terminology used by LAS Departure with regard to complying with altitude restrictions on the RNAV SID's when flights first check in after takeoff and established on their climb to FL190 per their PDC assigned SID.
summary: Pilots reported confusion during LAS departures regarding RNAV SID altitude restrictions when Departure Control issued "Climb to 190" clearances. Inconsistent clarifications between "comply with restrictions" and "unrestricted climb" caused differing interpretations among crew members due to similar phraseology.

synopsis: B767-200 flight crew reports burning significantly more fuel than planned during arrival to SFO due to weather.
summary: A Boeing 767-200 crew encountered turbulence, icing, and extensive vectoring below 15,000 feet at 180 knots, burning 4,000 pounds more fuel than planned. The aircraft landed with only 7,000 pounds, which the crew deemed an unacceptable safety margin due to unforecasted weather and traffic conditions.

synopsis: Both members of the flight crew of a CRJ-700 failed to note the 'revised' routing on their PDC delivered ATC clearance which included a different SID from the filed route. Quick recognition of the problem and its resolution when handed off to Departure Control prevented any meaningful track deviation.
summary: The crew programmed the LAXX6 transition for an LAX departure but received a revised clearance from SoCal Departure to go direct to PEVEE on the HOLTZ9 SID. The pilot attributed the initial FMS error to confusion between the route and revised clearance sections on the PDC, though no deviation occurred.

synopsis: A Base Inspector reports a Technician noticed an oxygen hose for a new crew O2 mask for the Captain's position on a Dassault Falcon 2000 aircraft, was not the same type of hose and did not have the in-line flow indicator as the previous unit had, even though the Part Numbers (P/N) were the same. Concerns raised again about the Manufacturer's Quality Assurance breakdowns involving oxygen related equipment.
summary: The pilot discovered an oxygen mask leak at FL430, prompting a replacement order from Dassault Falcon. The manufacturer subsequently admitted the new unit had the wrong supply hose installed without a flow indicator, requiring its return.

synopsis: C210 pilot reports inadvertently orbiting in and out of Class B airspace on a law enforcement mission. An iPad was being used for navigation and a magenta course line from the departure airport to the scene coincided with and obscured a line denoting a Class B floor change from 5,000 FT to 4,000 FT.
summary: Law enforcement pilots in a state aircraft inadvertently entered Class B airspace while orbiting at 4,500 feet near a towered airport. The incursion occurred because iPad navigation software obscured the airspace boundary, and the crew accepted a squawk 1200 clearance instead of requesting continued flight following.

synopsis: When they were given vectors for the ILS Runway 6 at TEB the flight crew of a Hawker Horizon selected the 'Activate Vectors' mode of the Honeywell FMS, which removed the fix prior to the FAF, DANDY--which has a mandatory crossing at 1,500 MSL--from the display. They continued at their previously assigned 2,000 MSL, unaware of the need to cross the fix at the required altitude. ATC caught the impending error and advised the crew of the need to descend.
summary: The flight crew intercepted the ILS 6 at TEB while maintaining 2,000 feet but received a late instruction to be over DANDY at 1,500 feet. Because the Honeywell FMS did not display the DANDY fix, the crew relied on raw data to descend and complete the approach uneventfully.

synopsis: LJ55 crew experience severe turbulence at FL390, first loosing 1,000 FT then going 1,500 FT above assigned altitude in ZFW Airspace. The crew was deviating around thunderstorms in IMC at the time, although none were reported or detected within 40 NM of the aircraft during the incident.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence while level at FL390, causing an uncommanded descent to FL380 and climb to FL405 within 25 seconds. Although radar showed no storms ahead, the crew prioritized aircraft integrity over maintaining altitude and later requested FL410 once clear.

synopsis: A SA226 pilot operating under Class B Airspace reported that the Rockwell Collins autopilot disengaged without issuing a warning which almost allowed the aircraft to climb into the Class B as he checked ATIS altimeter.
summary: A pilot climbing out of ZZZ enroute to ZZZ1 in a Rockwell Collins APS 80-equipped aircraft stopped at 3,500 feet to maintain separation from traffic. The autopilot disengaged without an aural warning, causing an unintended climb to 4,020 feet indicated before the pilot manually corrected the altitude.

synopsis: While acting as a safety pilot reporter discovers that his flying partner has descended early to the next step down altitude on a VOR approach.
summary: Two high-time retired pilots conducting practice instrument approaches descended 900 feet below the required 2,400 feet due to misreading the approach chart. The safety pilot identified the error late, but the aircraft cleared obstacles by 600 feet with no reported harm or ATC intervention.

synopsis: CE560 Captain departing SFO Runway 28R reports turning left to 200 degrees at 2,500 FT on the Offshore 5 departure instead of the 6 DME point as depicted. ATC points out the error.
summary: The Captain and First Officer departed SFO on the Offshore Five SID but turned to heading 200 at 2,500 feet instead of waiting until 6 DME from the VOR. This error occurred because the crew relied on the narrative text and overlooked the graphical depiction of the turn point, prompting a controller correction.

synopsis: DA2000 Captain is informed by ATC that he has drifted outside the designated airspace while doing maneuvers for a checkride. The on board display, which had been programed by the crew to remain withing the designated area, indicated that they had not drifted out.
summary: Pilots conducting an FAA Type Rating Test northwest of TXK VOR were accused by ATC of drifting 31 miles from the VOR, exceeding the 25-mile limit. The crew maintained their onboard EFIS display showed they remained within the assigned area and completed the training without further incident.

synopsis: ZDV Controller described a loss of separation event, when during step down altitude assignments to EGE, one aircraft encountered turbulence and initiated an unexpected climb toward another aircraft.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managed a TBM8 and G-4 landing at EGE, instructing both to expect approaches from VOAXA. Severe turbulence caused the TBM8 to climb unexpectedly, resulting in lost separation before the controller restored spacing and filed PIREPs.

synopsis: ZOB Controller reported being surprised when a clearance 'direct Harrisburg' resulted in the aircraft proceeding to the airport instead of the VOR.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a "direct Harrisburg" clearance intending the VOR, but the pilot interpreted it as the airport and flew direct to MDT. The controller noted no separation loss occurred but highlighted that identical names for airports and VORs cause confusion, recommending explicit "airport" phrasing for clarity.

synopsis: A80 Controller described a unsafe condition with regard to the testing of a new RNAV STAR, noting the MIT requirements with ZTL must be enforced, anomaly reporting procedures improved and automation enhanced to provide additional information to controllers.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that ZTL/DALAS failed to maintain required 7-10 MIT spacing for a B757, B767, and MD88 using the test-phase RPTOR STAR, forcing late vectors and speed restrictions. The controller attributed the issue to inadequate upstream separation, poor automation data blocks, and a lack of supervisor logging for these anomalies.

synopsis: ZTL Controller described a TCAS RA event between an ATL Air Carrier arrival and a parachute jump aircraft operating near the arrival route, the reporter suggesting the jump aircraft be assigned a different frequency and provided with more awareness training.
summary: A VFR jump plane descended unexpectedly from 15,500 feet toward an inbound B737 at 13,000 feet, triggering a Resolution Advisory. The B737 descended to 12,500 feet without incident, while the controller attributed the conflict to the jump plane's proximity to the arrival stream and lack of communication.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ARTCC controller reported working very light traffic on two displays during midshift. An aircraft was forgotten and violated adjacent airspace.
summary: An air traffic controller working low-altitude sectors lost track of Aircraft X after changing its frequency three times and failing to coordinate a handoff due to a 'carrot' indicating no auto-hand. The controller deviated the aircraft into an adjacent ARTCC without coordination, recommending combined scope displays to prevent such oversights.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a Low Altitude Alert when clearing an aircraft for an approach outside his airspace, the reporter not issuing a climb because the aircraft in question had already pasted to obstructing antenna.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared a C172 for a GPS approach at 030 but received a Low Altitude warning while the aircraft was 10 miles outside the boundary. The controller reviewed the Minimum Vectoring Altitude map, found the MVA was 037, and took no action because the aircraft was past the antenna.

synopsis: Ground Controller described a go around event when the Local Controller failed to note the requested intersection departure on the strip, assumed traffic was at the end of the runway and cleared the aircraft for takeoff.
summary: Local Control cleared a C182 for takeoff from Intersection C, mistakenly believing it was at the runway end while a PA28 was in the pattern. Ground Control corrected the error, preventing a collision as the C182 stopped after passing the hold short line, though both aircraft were delayed.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: Approach Controller reported a readback hearback issue which resulted in controlled flight towards terrain.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a descent clearance to aircraft Y, but a fragmented speech pattern caused the pilot to read back and descend to 2000 feet instead of the assigned 2600 feet. This communication error resulted in aircraft Y passing below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude near an obstruction before the controller corrected the situation.

synopsis: NCT Controller voiced concern regarding an IFR aircraft that was routed through a known unmanned rocket activity special airspace area, adding additional concern regarding Controller/Supervisor attitude regarding this procedure.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported that a Sunol Sector Instructor and Supervisor allowed Aircraft X to descend into active rocket airspace up to 15,300 FT, claiming pilots must avoid non-TFR special use areas. The reporting Controller vectored the aircraft west to avoid the zone after the Sunol team ignored instructions and failed to advise the pilot of the hazard.

synopsis: M03 Controller described a developing conflict invoving IFR departures assigned RNAV SIDS. The reporters indicated that both similar sounding fix names CRSON and CASLN as well as Controller awareness issues were causal factors.
summary: An ATC controller observed a CRJ2 departing Runway 36C turn northwest instead of northeast because the pilot lacked the filed CRSON fix in their database. The controller issued vectors to the Memphis VOR to resolve the deviation, noting that similar departure names caused the confusion.

synopsis: An air carrier flight crew reported another aircraft pushed back from an adjacent gate after they were already pushed back, with their brakes set and were starting engines. The other aircraft's right wing passed well under their left wing while doing so.
summary: The pilot reported that while starting engines after pushback, another aircraft's right wing passed four to five feet under their left wing. The pilot attributed the incident to a tight ramp area and questioned Ground Control's clearance for the simultaneous push.

synopsis: An A320 series ECAM alerted 'ENG 2 COMPRESSOR VANE' below 80 KTS on takeoff, then after the reject the ECAM alerted ECAM 'ENG 2 FAIL' and also 'EGT HIGH'. The aircraft was returned to the gate.
summary: The crew aborted takeoff below 80 KTS after an ECAM 'ENG 2 COMPRESSOR VANE' warning and audible compressor stall. Following an 'ENG 2 FAIL' indication with red EGT, they completed ECAM procedures, taxied to the gate, and released brakes to cool the aircraft.

synopsis: B737 Captain experiences a NMAC with a GA aircraft at 1,300 FT while turning a visual final to Runway 28R at PBI. Evasive action is initiated at the same time a TCAS RA is annunciated.
summary: The flight crew of a FAR 121 aircraft on a visual approach to Runway 28R at PBI encountered a C-172 converging below them near the shoreline. The pilot executed a TCAS climb to avoid a near miss, attributing the conflict to the controller's failure to provide traffic information about the unmonitored sightseeing aircraft.

synopsis: A B757 approaching TNCA in holding had an airborne conflict with another aircraft after a single Controller, working all ATC positions, was overloaded and not communicating adequately in the non radar environment.
summary: A pilot reported a TCAS RA conflict with an Aero Commander while approaching TNCA Runway 11 in a non-radar environment. The crew attributed the incident to an overloaded controller managing multiple duties on a single frequency with significant language barriers, resulting in missed transmissions and unsafe separation.

synopsis: CRJ200 flight crew reports being cleared to line up and wait for traffic landing on an intersecting runway. The First Officer reads back the clearance then reads the takeoff checklist at the Captain's request and the Captain begins the takeoff roll. The Tower notes the takeoff commencing and calls for the reject as the landing traffic rolls through the intersection.
summary: The flight crew misinterpreted a "line up and wait" clearance as a takeoff authorization and began rolling on Runway 5 while landing traffic was present. They aborted the takeoff after ATC canceled the clearance, attributing the error to complacency, fatigue, and hearing what they expected rather than what was spoken.

synopsis: The flight crew of a B767-200 suffered the loss of multiple PFD and NAV Display presentations while in a holding pattern at their destination. They were able to continue to a safe landing in VMC conditions utilizing the standby airspeed indicator and the functional parts of the Captain's display.
summary: The crew experienced multiple flight display failures, including the Captain's airspeed indicator and the First Officer's PFD and ND, while holding at MQU. Despite unsuccessful recovery attempts, they completed the ILS approach to SKBO using standby instruments and the Captain's remaining displays under VFR conditions.

synopsis: A321 Captain experiences autopilot disconnect followed by ECAM messages for ELAC 1 and 2 Pitch Faults. While preforming ECAM actions another ECAM message appears for FCTL Stabilizer Jam appeared. An emergency is declared and flight continues to a flaps 3 landing on the longer runway.
summary: The crew experienced autopilot disconnection and multiple flight control faults, including ELAC pitch failures and a stabilizer jam, during an RNAV arrival descent. They declared an emergency, reverted to Direct Law, and landed uneventfully on the longer runway before taxiing to the gate.

synopsis: An A321 flight crew were confronted with low yellow and green hyrdualic system quantities enroute following maintenance action at their departure airport. After draining excess fluid from the systems, Maintenance personnel had failed to insure that there was no leakage from the reservoirs.
summary: Contract Maintenance failed to detect a Green hydraulic leak after servicing, causing low pressure and quantity alerts two hours into the flight. The crew diverted, manually extended the landing gear, and landed safely, with the cause attributed to the maintenance oversight.

synopsis: A B717 Aft Cargo Door was partially closed ajar so that the Door Warning System indicated proper closure but after takeoff the aircraft would not pressurized. The crew returned to the departure airport where door was discovered.
summary: The flight crew experienced uncontrolled cabin pressurization shortly after takeoff due to a misaligned aft cargo door, forcing an immediate return to the departure airport. A ground crew member later reseated the door, resolving the issue and confirming the door gap caused the pressurization failure.

synopsis: After being lit up by a green laser and reporting it to ATC the flight crew of a Q-400 was unable to lower the nose gear. They performed a go around, extended the nose gear using the alternate gear extension procedure and landed without incident.
summary: During the visual approach, the crew was illuminated by a green laser and subsequently experienced a nose gear extension failure. After a go-around and successful alternate gear extension, the aircraft landed normally on Runway 32, requiring maintenance for the gear issue.

synopsis: SF340 Captain discovers the altitude preselect (APA) is inoperative during approach and contacts Maintenance Control after landing. The Captain is instructed to write up and MEL the autopilot because Contract Maintenance is not available to properly sign off the APA and allow the aircraft to return to base.
summary: During descent, the pilot found the Altitude Pre-selector (APA) inoperative and landed safely. Maintenance Control pressured the pilot to defer the entire Autopilot System instead of the APA to keep the aircraft in service due to bankruptcy constraints, despite this conflicting with MEL procedures.

synopsis: A BAE-125 flight crew rejected their takeoff and cancelled their flight due to excessive surging of the right engine during power up for takeoff.
summary: The First Officer reported that during takeoff, the left rudder pedal moved fully forward and right engine indications fluctuated, prompting the Captain to abort. The aircraft cleared the runway, and maintenance was contacted to inspect the aircraft before further operations.

synopsis: EMB-145EP First Officer reported on climb he received a call from Flight Attendant who reported fuel venting from the left wing, which was confirmed by the quantity indicators. They declared an emergency and diverted to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: During climb-out on a ferry flight, the flight attendant observed fuel venting from the left wing with quantities dropping. The crew executed the fuel leak QRH, declared an emergency, and diverted to the nearest suitable airport.

synopsis: B757-200 flight crew reported right engine flamed out on descent. Crew declared an emergency, ran the procedure, and successfully restarted the engine.
summary: The Pilot Not Flying reported a right engine failure at 18,000 feet during descent, likely caused by a low-pressure pump issue. The crew secured and successfully restarted the engine at 10,000 feet, landed safely, and ARFF inspection found no visible damage.

synopsis: A Maintenance Base Mechanic reports their General Maintenance Manual (GMM) policies and procedures were ignored when a new Left-Hand (L/H) Outboard (O/B) Flap and Flaperon did not go through their Flight Control Shop prior to being installed on a company B777-200 aircraft. No Inspections were accomplished, no company tracking or Parts Tags, nor FAA-8130 Serviceability Tags were issued.
summary: A B777-200 at the ZZZ Maintenance Base received replacement left outboard flap and flaperon units following an engine fire. The reporter states these parts are not serviceable because required home shop inspections, company tracking tags, and FAA-8130 documentation were never completed per General Maintenance Manual and FAR Part 145.

synopsis: A Fuel Tank Technician reports about finding their left and right fuel tank, wing venting air blowers had been unplugged from an A320 aircraft in their company Hangar, creating an unsafe work environment.
summary: A fuel crew member reported that on an A320 in the hangar, fuel tank venting blowers were repeatedly unplugged or operating poorly by unknown mechanics. This unsafe practice prevented proper tank purging for entry, prompting the crew to request a briefing for the maintenance team.

synopsis: HU-269-C Instructor pilot reported experiencing a rough running engine, so a precautionary landing in a parking lot was performed.
summary: The pilot reported a rough-running engine during flight and executed a precautionary landing in a parking lot. After inspection, the company owner flew the helicopter to the home base.

synopsis: SR22 Instructor reports inadvertently entering a TFR beneath ORD Class B during a VFR flight to PWK. No TFR information appeared on the Garmin Perspective System until after several reboots, after the fact.
summary: An instructor and student in an SR22 penetrated an active Chicago shoreline TFR during VFR training after missing the FDC NOTAM and experiencing a Garmin Perspective display failure. ATC provided no warnings, and the crew only learned of the violation post-landing when Approach contacted them.

synopsis: A C172 pilot reported losing contact with the Tower, either because of radio or electrical system malfunctions. He squawked 7600 and landed.
summary: The pilot returned to the home airport after an alternator cleaning resolved an electrical issue, but the generator failed again en route, causing total radio failure. Unable to communicate, the pilot squawked 7600 and executed a visual left downwind landing.

synopsis: A UAV pilot overloaded with checklist and descent procedures failed to cancel his IFR clearance with ATC.
summary: A pilot conducting a UAV chase descent from 18,000 to 15,000 feet inadvertently descended below the assigned altitude while rushing through checklists. The error was corrected when the non-flying pilot alerted the pilot flying to an ATC call, resulting in a successful IFR cancellation and no further incident.

synopsis: A BE36 pilot was unable to remain on the hard surface when he attempted to exit the runway to the left after suffering a left brake failure on the landing roll. He struck a taxi light after departing the taxiway at the end of the runway.
summary: The pilot reported a left brake failure immediately after landing, causing the aircraft to yaw right and preventing a timely runway exit. While attempting to turn onto the last taxiway, the aircraft rolled off onto grass and struck a taxi light with the left main landing gear before the engine was shut down.

synopsis: IFR corporate aircraft inbound to HSA voiced concern regarding ATC's handling with regard to timely descent opportunities because of apparent airspace constrictions. The reporter noted that, allegedly, air carriers are having the same issues.
summary: The flight crew encountered a steep, unstabilized descent into HSA due to Houston Center refusing a requested handoff to New Orleans Approach, forcing a direct transfer to Gulfport. This resulted in an uncomfortable profile requiring speed brakes, which the crew attributed to inter-facility workload issues and denied alternate routing requests.

synopsis: An air carrier dispatcher related his concerns about what he believes to be an example of willing efforts on the part of Maintenance Controllers to coerce flight crews and Dispatchers to agree to fly unairworthy aircraft to locations where necessary maintenance can be performed at lower cost to the company.
summary: A dispatcher and Captain rejected a Maintenance Controller's suggestion to fly an aircraft with a bound horizontal stabilizer trim and grinding noise to a maintenance base. The flight was delayed 3 hours due to aircraft swaps, and the issue was later traced to failed bearings in the trim wheels.

synopsis: C182 pilot reports inadvertently entering ORD Class B airspace after carefully preflighting using a web site to determine that his proposed flight track would not enter Class B airspace. DPA was used for planning but the flight actually departed DPA and entry into Class B on the south bound flight.
summary: The pilot inadvertently entered a nearby VOR instead of the departure airport into an online flight planner, causing a G1000-equipped aircraft to penetrate the 3,600-foot floor of ORD Class B airspace during a ferry flight. The pilot descended below the shelf after realizing the error, attributing the incident to failing to verify the flight planning tool's data against paper charts.

synopsis: ZTL Controller described a below MVA event involving an IFR NORDO aircraft.
summary: The Aerostar pilot lost two-way communication with Charleston Approach at 6,000 FT MSL while flying through terrain requiring higher altitudes. The pilot attributed the issue to a communication failure, eventually contacting Atlanta Center and completing the flight without incident or altitude advisories from controllers.

synopsis: LAX Controller described a potential conflict when a departure from Runway 25R on the HOLTZ9 SID initiated a wrong turn, the pilot reporter noting an incorrect aircraft FMS departure runway entry may have caused the event.
summary: An ATC controller and Falcon 2000 crew were involved during departure from LAX Runway 25R on the HOLTZ9 SID. The aircraft drifted north due to an FMS auto-sequence inhibition after a runway change from 25L to 25R, requiring an immediate ATC traffic alert and vector to correct the flight path.

synopsis: B737 flight crew received clearance to taxi to a certain gate, but had another gate in mind and proceeded to taxi to the wrong gate. The error was realized before a serious traffic conflict materialized. Reporting First Officer attributes part of the problem to lack of good CRM on the Captain's part.
summary: The flight crew of an arriving aircraft mistakenly taxied onto the uncontrolled ramp at Gate 2 instead of the assigned Gate 1 due to confusion and the Captain's refusal to stop for clarification. The error was corrected after a 180-degree turn, avoiding a collision with another aircraft on the ramp.

synopsis: For reasons not provided by the reporter the flight crew of a B737-300 was unable to prevent the aircraft from briefly exiting the runway on the landing roll before regaining control and returning to the hard surface. When an inspection by airport personnel identified no obvious problems the crew elected to taxi the aircraft to the gate.
summary: After landing, the Captain struggled to keep the aircraft on the runway as it pulled hard left and departed the left side. Although airport Operations inspected the aircraft and found no visible damage, the Captain attributed the swerve to an unknown aircraft issue.

synopsis: An A320 flight crew initiated a low speed rejected takeoff upon receipt of a Reverser Unlocked ECAM at about 70 KIAS.
summary: The flight crew aborted takeoff on an Airbus after a Reverser Unlocked ECAM warning appeared at 70 KIAS. The aircraft was safely stopped, exited the runway, and taxied back to the gate with no injuries or further issues.

synopsis: An A319 developed a pungent chemical smell in the cabin at the top of descent, so the crew donned oxygen masks to escape the fumes and sought medical attention after landing.
summary: During descent, a flight attendant reported a worsening chemical smell and burning eyes in the forward galley and lavatory, which later spread to the cabin. The crew expedited landing, coordinated maintenance, and sought medical evaluation while the airline investigates the fume source for a permanent fix.

synopsis: An A321 Captain reported that during descent after the engines were throttled up at 7,000 FT a dirty socks smell was detected for up to two minutes, then it subsided.
summary: A flight attendant reported a heavy "dirty sock" fume smell after throttle up at 7,000 feet, which subsided by the gate. The flight attendant subsequently underwent a medical evaluation.

aircraft: Challenger Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Dispatched with a deferred Spoileron Fault Message and faced with a Yaw Damper Inop CAS status message -- which cleared during taxi as required -- the flight crew of a CL-600 encountered repeated abrupt roll inputs during acceleration above 10,000 FT that forced a return to their departure airport. They declared an emergency, added additional airspeed for the approach and landed safely despite aircraft oscillations described by their Flight Attendant, '...as though the aircraft was being flown by a two year old!'
summary: The flight crew experienced severe yaw and roll oscillations above 10,000 feet after deferring a left spoileron fault and resetting a Yaw Damper One Inoperative message. They declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport, and landed with extra speed due to sluggish controls, suspecting the deferred MEL item caused the issue.

synopsis: A CRJ-145 crew reported an odor and haze which developed into heavy smoke after takeoff so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport. An engine oil seal leak was suspected.
summary: The flight crew encountered increasing smoke and haze in the cockpit shortly after takeoff, prompting an emergency return. Turning off the recirculation fan cleared the smoke, and the Captain executed an overweight landing in high crosswinds with no fire evidence found on the ground.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 3 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier Captain approaching the concourse had to stop his aircraft twice to avoid fueling trucks which did not remain within ground traffic safety lines or give way to taxiing aircraft.
summary: While taxiing to a gate at ORD, the flight crew stopped twice because fuel trucks ignored safety lines, with one driving under the left wing. The pilot reported that Ramp Tower confirmed this is a recurring issue caused by drivers knowingly disregarding airport rules, creating a collision risk.

synopsis: Corporate IFR departure from GEU entered PHX Class B while awaiting the issuance of an IFR clearance from Luke ATC, the reporter questioning the fact that GEU controllers are unable to issue certain IFR clearances prior to take off.
summary: The pilot and a student departed Glendale (GEU) Runway 19 under a left downwind instruction but inadvertently entered Phoenix Class B airspace before receiving an IFR clearance. The violation resulted from cockpit distractions, delayed contact with Luke AFB Approach, and the airport's unique limitation where the tower cannot issue IFR clearances for Runway 19 departures.

synopsis: A C172 pilot reported dialing up the wrong CTAF frequency at FDK airport and experienced a conflict on takeoff roll.
summary: The pilot tuned to the incorrect CTAF frequency (122.7 instead of 122.725) at Frederick Airport and failed to hear traffic during takeoff. A Piper Arrow executed a go-around at 200 feet directly in front of the departing aircraft, creating a conflict caused by the frequency error and lack of visual contact.

synopsis: A C150 pilot reported losing control on takeoff roll, ground looping and leaving the runway which resulted in damage to left gear.
summary: The pilot reported that a C150 pulled right during takeoff from a grass strip despite corrective rudder and brake inputs. The aircraft turned 180 degrees and stopped in brush with the left gear detached and the rudder cable broken.

synopsis: IFR MU2 with failed transponder was refused ATC service by ZNY at FL220, the pilot questioning ATC services.
summary: The pilot reported a transponder failure after entering IFR, forcing a descent to 8,000 feet for a Tower-to-Tower clearance instead of maintaining FL220. The pilot cancelled IFR to proceed VFR with an intermittent transponder on code 1200, citing safety concerns regarding low-altitude turbine operations.

aircraft: Piper Single Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: PA-12-150 pilot reported a rough running engine early in the climb and returned to land at the departure airport.
summary: The pilot reported a rough-running engine at 100 feet AGL after takeoff and was cleared to land on runway XXR. The aircraft landed and taxied under power without further incident, and Tower classified the event as non-reportable.

synopsis: Tower Controller providing OJT described a AMASS alert requiring the issuance of a go-around. The reporter acknowledged that instructor intervention was late.
summary: During training, the reporter allowed the CPC-IT to manage a situation where a second aircraft on short final was too close behind a landing aircraft. AMASS alerted the team to send the second aircraft around, prompting a recommendation for the CPC-IT to make decisions more aggressively.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a potential conflict event when, during the relief briefing, the Controller being relieved failed to maintain awareness of current traffic.
summary: During a relief briefing, Departure Control requested Tower to stop a departing CRJ9 at 2,000 FT due to a climbing helicopter, but the briefing controller likely missed the call. The incoming controller relayed the instruction to the pilot, preventing separation loss, though coordination between Local and Departure was lacking.

synopsis: ZAB Controller described a very busy and complex control period involving multiple military aircraft all apparently scheduled in the same airspace at the same time without prior coordination.
summary: An air traffic controller managing high workload in Sector 90/47 encountered multiple military aircraft (F16s, A10s, C130) requesting TOMBSTONE MOA without proper MARSA coordination. The controller identified a single F16 entering Class A airspace without clearance due to poor military scheduling and lack of sector splitting, prompting traffic advisories to prevent conflict with A10s.

aircraft: Cessna Single Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Tower Controller described an unauthorized runway crossing event that resulted in a go around, the reports indicating similar call signs, missed read backs and minimal experience levels as contributing factors.
summary: A new private pilot flying a Cessna (XXX) mistakenly entered Runway XXR due to confusion with a similar call sign (XXY), forcing a B737 on short final to go around. The pilot attributed the error to simultaneous transmissions blocking the correct readback and poor visibility, though no collision occurred.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reported loss of all fuel quantity indicators. They elected to divert to a nearby airport even as Dispatch recommended continuing to destination.
summary: During cruise at FL350, the crew lost fuel quantity indications and received an AUTO XFLOW INHIBIT message. Despite Dispatch advising to continue, the crew declared an emergency and diverted to a nearby airport due to unknown fuel quantity and potential imbalance risks, landing safely before continuing to the original destination after maintenance.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reports an amber 'speed brake do not arm' warning light at 55 KTS and rejects the takeoff. Maintenance MEL's the 'auto speed brake' and 'speed brake load alleviation' systems and the flight departs.
summary: The pilot and First Officer observed an amber 'speed brake do not arm' light during takeoff at 55 KTS, prompting a rejected takeoff at 60 KTS. After completing checklists and assigning MELs to the auto speed brake and load alleviation systems, the flight continued.

synopsis: A B737-700 crew reported that the ground crew disconnected the tow bar after pushback without any communications, which caused the aircraft to roll backward because the brakes were not set.
summary: During pushback, the Ground Controller disconnected the tug and headset before receiving clearance from the Captain, causing the aircraft to roll forward with brakes unset. The incident resulted from the ground crew disconnecting without verbal clearance, compounded by poor radio communications and static noise.

synopsis: A B767-300 Captain reported a 'Rudder Ratio' EICAS message prompted a diversion to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The crew experienced a Rudder Ratio annunciator light and EICAS message during cruise. They advised Dispatch and ATC of the malfunction and landed at the nearest suitable airport.

synopsis: A300 flight crew reports being dispatched with the right inner fuel gauge inoperative with the fueler verifying that 12.8 thousand pounds of fuel were loaded in the RI tank for a total fuel load of 42.3. Prior to top of descent, it is noticed the right inner fuel valve has closed indicating the RI was out of fuel.
summary: The crew departed an A-300 with an inoperative right inner fuel gauge, relying on logbook entries that incorrectly stated 12.8 units of fuel. En route, the tank emptied prematurely due to suspected fuel transfer after fueling, forcing the crew to manage imbalance and land with less fuel than planned.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports he mistakenly deactivated #2 engine anti-ice valve according to MEL 30-27-01A, instead of MEL 30-27-01A. Flight crew returned the A320 aircraft to gate after noticing improper anti-ice valve indication during engine start.
summary: A mechanic troubleshooting a sticking #2 engine anti-ice valve on an A320 mistakenly deferred the discrepancy using MEL 30-27-01A instead of 01D, likely due to poor cockpit lighting. The error caused improper valve indications at engine start, requiring a gate turnback to apply the correct MEL.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a loss of separation event when coordination with a Tower regarding missed approach instructions were less than clear, the reporter indicating changes in the Tower/TRACON LOA would improve coordination and operations.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller released a Piper PA-28 for takeoff referencing an SR20 on ILS 36 final, assuming the Tower would provide visual separation. The Tower cleared the Piper without maintaining separation, causing a loss of separation that required the controller to issue traffic alerts and vector the Piper behind the SR20.

synopsis: Tower Supervisor described an unauthorized runway crossing that resulted in a go around event, noting similar call signs were involved.
summary: An air carrier flight on final for Runway 4R was instructed to go around after a C172 entered the runway due to a readback error caused by similar call signs. The controller failed to verify the takeoff clearance after hearing a squelch, leading to the runway incursion.

synopsis: Tower Supervisor witnessed an ASDE-X alarm when traffic was cleared to land on an occupied runway forcing a landing runway change, the reporter indicated the Local Controller should have scanned the runway before issuing a clearance.
summary: A C208 received a landing clearance for Runway 4L while a C172 was holding in position, triggering an ASDE-X alarm. The controller likely failed to record the incoming aircraft or maintain an adequate scan, resulting in a runway change to 4R.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described an extremely busy and complex traffic period that resulted in an airspace infraction and loss of separation event, the reporter acknowledging he should have insisted on splitting the combined position during the relief briefing.
summary: An air traffic controller reported becoming overwhelmed after taking over a combined position with excessive traffic, multiple airports, and blocked communications. The controller attributed the unsafe situation to delayed sector splitting, staffing shortages, and a culture of complacency regarding separation standards.

synopsis: Tower Controller clears aircraft for takeoff thinking the aircraft was at Runway 9R when it was at Runway 9L. When the aircraft started to depart, a landing aircraft went around.
summary: Local North controller and Aircraft X were involved when Aircraft X went around due to Aircraft Y, who mistakenly held short of Runway 9L instead of 9R, entering the active runway. Aircraft Y was cleared to continue takeoff and depart, while Aircraft X rejoined the pattern and landed safely.

synopsis: ARTCC Controller reported numerous issues with UAV aircraft mission control and coordination.
