summary: Air traffic controllers reported erratic UAV missions in Class D airspace with inaccurate flight plans and missing lost link procedures. These issues, including significant TAS errors and poor coordination, hindered IFR traffic management and relied on unreliable commercial phone lines for communication.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported losing Number 2 Engine on takeoff roll. Takeoff was rejected and the flight returned to the gate, where a Mechanic reported turbine failure.
summary: During takeoff below 80 KTS with flex thrust set, Engine 2 failed, prompting a rejected takeoff and return to the gate. The attending mechanic attributed the failure to a turbine malfunction.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A CRJ-50 First Officer reported noticing after departure the yaw damper had failed resulting in abnormal rudder movement. They declared an emergency and returned to departure airport.
summary: The crew departed after a spoileron delay, but above 10,000 feet, a yaw damper failure caused rudder oscillation. They maintained control, slowed to 250 knots, declared an emergency, and returned to the departure airport for a safe landing with no injuries.

synopsis: An MD-83 flight crew reported losing their fuel quantity indicating system in flight. They declared an emergency and returned to departure airport.
summary: During climb, the crew experienced total fuel quantity display failure and incorrect right fuel flow, prompting an emergency return to the departure airport. The First Officer executed an overweight ILS landing in low visibility, after which fuel indications returned to normal.

synopsis: Three Mechanics, unfamiliar with the V2500 engine on A320 aircraft, report about their involvement with installing improper Thrust Reverser lockout pins in the Hydraulic Control Units (HCU). Reversers did not deploy on landing after aircraft was released from Heavy Maintenance Visit (HMV).
summary: Mechanics on an A320 in Hangar ZZZ inadvertently left Thrust Reverser lockout pins installed due to missing streamers and skipped operational checks. Consequently, the Thrust Reversers failed to deploy upon landing at the next destination.

synopsis: A student pilot became NORDO in an airport traffic pattern and apparently could not see the Tower's light signal so after five missed approaches, one including an MD80 near miss, he finally landed.
summary: A student pilot lost radio contact during solo touch-and-go operations on Runway 17L and switched to Runway 17R, cutting off an MD-80 on final. The MD-80 executed a go-around while the student landed safely, citing bright sun glare obscuring tower lights and an inoperative radio as causes.

synopsis: A PA-34 pilot and flight instructor reported finding the main wheel brakes were not working during landing roll. The Instructor pilot used the parking brake to bring the aircraft to a stop, during which both main gear tires were blown.
summary: During landing, the pilot reported total brake failure despite pre-departure tests, requiring the second pilot to use the parking brake to stop the aircraft. This resulted in blown main tires, with the cause attributed to an unknown brake system failure or potential maintenance issues.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: The pilot of light single reported an NMAC with a helicopter who allegedly was not following procedures at SEZ.
summary: A pilot on final approach to Sedona (SEZ) encountered a commercial sightseeing helicopter paralleling their flight path at 100–150 feet lateral separation and the same altitude. The reporter attributed the incident to the helicopter's failure to monitor CTAF, make position calls, or comply with right-of-way rules, noting the aircraft was not detected by the pilot's traffic advisory system.

synopsis: A C172 pilot reported running out of fuel and landing safely in a field.
summary: During cruise at 4,500 feet, the pilot experienced an engine sputter and suspected fuel exhaustion, leading to a forced landing in a field after rejecting a distant airport and roads with power lines. The pilot executed a soft field landing, radioed that they were safe, and abandoned the aircraft.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: The pilot of a high performance single engine aircraft reported a NMAC with an experimental on approach to OJC. ATC reported they were not in contact with any other aircraft in the area.
summary: A pilot flying a private aircraft on VFR descent into OJC at 4,000 feet executed an aggressive maneuver to avoid a yellow aircraft passing within 300 feet. The pilot attributed the near-miss to poor visual lookout and suspected the other aircraft was not squawking Mode C or was outside radar coverage.

aircraft: Embraer Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A Line Mechanic working Embraer aircraft reports about an unprofessional maintenance work environment at his Air Carrier that he feels is symptomatic of a malaise that stems from a clear disregard and contempt of the signature sign-off process, involving a climate of complacency and mis-management over the years.
summary: A mechanic reported that a night Lead Mechanic signed an Airworthiness Release for a tire worn beyond limits after dismissing the mechanic's objection and yelling at him. The mechanic subsequently received difficult assignments, while management allegedly ignored these improper entries and a culture of non-compliance persists.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a conflict event when incorrect descent instructions were issued to aircraft on top of another, the controller believe instructions were being issued to the lower aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller at Airport North lost separation between a C56X and a P180 while managing heavy traffic and multiple conflicts. The controller attributes the incident to mistakenly issuing a descent clearance to the higher aircraft due to workload and mixed-up data tags.

synopsis: ZLA Controller described a TCAS RA event apparently triggered by a glider operating close to an Air Carrier descending into ONT, the reporter suggesting that gliders communicate with ATC and be restricted to areas clear of Air Carrier operations.
summary: An air traffic controller managing an A319 arrival mistakenly identified a glider squawking 1202 as eastbound, causing the pilot to execute a climb in response to a resolution advisory. The controller subsequently lost radar contact with the glider and issued a pilot's discretion clearance to 15,000 feet.

synopsis: ATL Controller described the failure of the ASDE-X to display a vehicle tag on Runway 9, noting several similar events over the past week.
summary: A Ground Center controller observed a vehicle stopped on Runway 9R with no corresponding tag on the ASDE-X. The reporter noted this recurring issue over the past week and requested a fix for the ASDE-X system.

synopsis: D10 Controller described a 'stuck mike' event during triple simultaneous ILS approach procedures into DFW. The controller voiced concern regarding the lack of Guard Frequency availability and other outdated facility communications gear.
summary: An air traffic controller managing triple simultaneous ILS approaches to DFW could not communicate with an aircraft due to a stuck microphone. The controller diverted traffic because the facility lacked accessible emergency frequencies and modern interfaces at their position, causing significant disruption.

synopsis: An A321 ECAM alerted L/G LGCIU 1 FAULT after takeoff so the ECAM procedures were followed and when the landing gear were lowered at the destination, three green down and three red up lights illuminated. After a go around to complete the procedures a normal landing followed and maintenance found a disconnected linkage at the gate.
summary: The flight crew experienced landing gear system faults and conflicting indications during approach, prompting a go-around. After consulting a second captain and confirming the gear was down and locked, they landed normally; maintenance later found disconnected linkage.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier First Officer reported taking evasive action to a TERRAIN, PULL UP warning during a night descent into DRO after they started the approach descent too early with an 11,000 FT MVA within ten miles of the airport.
summary: A Part 121 crew descending visually to Runway 21 at Durango at night received a GPWS "terrain, terrain, pull-up" warning after initiating descent too early in mountainous terrain. The Captain immediately climbed with full power, avoiding ground contact, and attributed the event to premature descent planning.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier First Officer reported a near miss with what appeared to be a weather balloon at 11,000 FT between BRAND and KORRY Intersections on the LGA KORRY 3 Arrival.
summary: Pilots on a KORRY 3 arrival into LGA encountered a weather balloon near BRAND at 11,000 feet, causing distraction that resulted in missing the 10,000-foot restriction at KORRY. The crew notified ATC, descended to 10,000 feet, and completed an uneventful landing.

synopsis: An Air Carrier Inspector, reports finding a left-hand Main Landing Gear (MLG) Anti-Skid System electrical wiring harness to the Wheel Spin Transducers cross-wired in the axles. Outboard (O/B) harness routed to Inboard (I/B) and I/B to O/B. He was performing a Receiving Inspection of the A320 MLG from a Contract Repair Station Overhaul Vendor.
summary: A contract repair station vendor overhauled landing gear assemblies for an air carrier and found the left main landing gear anti-skid transducer wiring harnesses incorrectly routed during receiving inspection. The vendor repaired the part after discovering the outboard and inboard harnesses were swapped.

synopsis: A P180's Cabin Pressure Light alerted climbing through FL230 so an emergency was declared and during descent the Manual Mode selection restored normal pressurization. The emergency was canceled and the flight continued at 10,000 FT.
summary: The flight crew declared an emergency during climb from 23,000 feet due to an Auto Pressurization Mode failure. After descending to 10,000 feet and switching to Manual Mode, the cabin stabilized, allowing the crew to cancel the emergency and continue to their destination.

synopsis: Pilot operating from LHW expressed frustration regarding FSS inability to provide current information on Restricted Areas.
summary: A pilot reported receiving conflicting Restricted Area R3005A-E status information from Flight Service Station (FSS) and Wright Field advisory during pattern flight. While FSS repeatedly provided incorrect "hot" status, the advisory confirmed the areas were "cold," causing the pilot to fear potential entry into hazardous airspace due to misinformation.

synopsis: An instructor pilot reported that his student pilot on a solo cross country had a C172 fuel system malfunction which caused him to land successfully in a field.
summary: A student pilot executing a solo VFR cross-country flight experienced an engine failure after the fuel annunciator lit and power enrichment failed. The student contacted Military GCA, executed the emergency checklist, and landed safely in a wheat field with no injuries or aircraft damage.

synopsis: C550B Captain reported right main landing green light failed to illuminate on approach. Flight crew diverted to alternate where a visual check confirmed gear was down.
summary: The crew experienced a right main landing gear light failure during approach. They diverted to an alternate airport, confirmed gear extension with the tower, and landed safely.

synopsis: An Amphibious aircraft pilot made a gear up landing during his Biannual Flight Review because both he and the examiner had been practicing water landings and additionally were distracted about post flight activities.
summary: A pilot and instructor landed an amphibious aircraft gear-up during a flight review after returning from water operations. Distractions regarding logbook signing and navigation discussions caused both crew members to skip the gear checklist, resulting in minimal damage to the keel and sponson rub strips.

synopsis: PAO Controller described a NMAC when traffic on a right base to NUQ Runway 14 reported a conflict with traffic in the pattern at PAO for Runway 13, the reporter noting unfamiliar pilots landing NUQ in this configuration should be advised of VFR traffic at PAO.
summary: A C130 pilot reported a near mid-air collision with a PAO pattern aircraft while turning base near NUQ, despite the controller observing no conflict. The reporter attributes the incident to the C130 pilot's lack of awareness regarding the adjacent busy VFR tower and suggests PAO requires more airspace.

synopsis: Tower Controller described an ASDE-X Alarm event activated even though the conflicting aircraft was obviously clear of the landing runway.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managed an intersecting runway operation between a B737 on final and a CL60 exiting Runway YY onto Runway XXL. An ASDE-X go-around alert triggered, but the controller withheld instructions because the CL60 had already cleared the runway, ensuring separation without an overflight.

synopsis: TRACON Controller providing OJT described a TCAS RA event between an Air Carrier departure and a Photo Mission C172, the reporter listing developmental fatigue, traffic complexity and facility practices as contributing to the conflict.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller conducting OJT with a fatigued trainee lost separation between a C172 photo flight and a B757 departure due to the C172 ignoring a heading restriction. The conflict was resolved when the B757 pilot responded to a Resolution Advisory, prompting the controller to discontinue training and separate the aircraft.

aircraft: Enstrom Helicopter Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Tower Controller providing OJT described a NMAC between two inbound aircraft, a C172 and a helicopter, both VFR, the reporter listing a number of facility training policies that contributed to this event.
summary: An ATC trainee on Local Control failed to properly separate a C172 and a helicopter in Class Delta airspace, resulting in a near mid-air collision within 100 feet. The reporter attributes the incident to the trainee's inadequate skills, incorrect traffic alerts, and management's failure to address the trainee's lack of progress.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a TCAS RA event involving two Air Carrier departures, the first declaring an emergency and requesting an immediate return to the departure airport, separation was not insured with the following aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller managing an MD83 emergency and a trailing B737 issued conflicting clearances that caused both aircraft to react to TCAS alerts. The controller admitted the loss of positive separation resulted from a hasty reaction to the emergency without a complete traffic scan, though both aircraft landed safely.

synopsis: A B737-800's right engine ingested a bird on takeoff which caused substantial fan blade and cowling floor damage so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the airport. Recent farming activity near the airport attracted birds.
summary: During takeoff roll at 145 KIAS, the crew struck a large bird, causing substantial fan blade and cowling damage to engine #2. After declaring an emergency and holding for checklists, the First Officer flew a visual approach to an uneventful landing with fire crews standing by.

synopsis: A B757's Center Hydraulic Quantity gauge dropped to .23 so the QRH was completed, an emergency declared and the flight diverted. A faulty Quantity Gauge was found.
summary: The crew experienced a Center Hydraulic Low Quantity indication and R-Yaw Damper light, prompting QRH actions and an emergency declaration. Post-landing inspection revealed no leak, suggesting a potential transmitter or indication problem.

synopsis: An Air Carrier Crew reported a near miss at about 2,000 FT with a single engine aircraft after takeoff from IAH.
summary: A departing crew from IAH 15R received a TCAS RA at 1,500–2,500 feet AGL due to unseen single-engine traffic, resulting in a near midair collision within 300 feet. The crew attributed the avoidance solely to the TCAS, noting the Tower provided no advisories and appeared indifferent to the incident.

synopsis: A B737-800 encountered severe turbulence at FL380 where, in a downdraft, it descended to FL310 after which an emergency was declared and upon arrival at the destination paramedics met the aircraft to attend the injured.
summary: Pilots flying at FL380 encountered severe downdrafts and turbulence after ATC routed them closer to weather, causing an uncommanded descent to FL310 and triggering stick shaker and overspeed warnings. The crew declared an emergency, recovered control, and landed safely with paramedics meeting the aircraft to check for injuries.

synopsis: A B757 First Officer called in fatigued following a three day European trip, then a three day West Coast trip and a scheduled night departure to the UK after getting home on the red eye from the West Coast trip.
summary: A pilot reported fatigue after six consecutive days of international flying, including a red-eye and 18 time zones, followed by a scheduled double-pump pairing to the UK. The pilot requested that their sick bank not be depleted for this fatigue call, noting the pairing would be illegal under new rest rules.

synopsis: An ERJ145 Captain performed a slow speed reject because the EICAS alerted BLD VLV 1 FAIL and at the gate the cracked high stage bleed valve was replaced.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff below 80 knots after receiving a BLD VLV 1 FAIL EICAS message caused by a cracked high stage valve. Maintenance replaced the valve, and the aircraft departed uneventfully with no fault attributed to the crew.

synopsis: An EMB145 Captain dropped a beverage can onto the flight station floor at cruise altitude which ruptured the container spraying liquid throughout the cockpit. Ultimately, liquid dripped onto the Center Console and caused the Pressure Controller to fail, subsequently depressurizing the aircraft. An emergency was declare and the flight diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: A beverage can rupture in the cockpit caused a Pressurization Controller failure and rapid cabin decompression. The crew completed memory items and QRH procedures, coordinating with ATC and maintenance to execute a normal approach and landing without incident.

synopsis: A300 flight crew experiences stuck flaps during approach at less than 15 degrees with system 1 and 2 flap fault lights illuminated. An emergency is declared, QRH procedures complied with, and an uneventful landing ensues.
summary: During approach, flaps systems 1 and 2 faulted, leaving flaps stuck below 15 degrees despite handle cycling. The crew declared an emergency, completed the QRH procedure, and executed an uneventful landing after leveling at 3,000 MSL.

synopsis: A321 flight crew describes an autopilot disengagement and an ECAM messages for ELAC 1 and 2 faults and a stabilizer jam at FL340. Moderate vibration is felt through the airframe lasting 10 to 15 seconds just prior to the messages. An emergency is declared and flight diverts to the nearest suitable airport, landing in Direct Law after gear extension.
summary: During cruise at FL340, the crew experienced uncommanded autopilot disengagement, airframe vibrations, and multiple ELAC and stabilizer failures causing a reversion to Alternate Law. The pilots declared an emergency, diverted to the nearest airport, and landed uneventfully in Direct Law due to these redundant flight control system failures.

synopsis: CE680 Captain experiences a MAU 1 failure at FL340 resulting in the loss of Autopilot, Yaw damper, ADC, attitude and heading indicator. After the failure the aircraft is no longer RVSM capable and the crew diverts to a suitable airport.
summary: The Pilot Non-Flying reported a Modular Avionics Unit failure at FL430 causing loss of autopilot, air data, and pressurization, forcing a manual descent to FL280. The crew diverted after struggling with high workload and an impatient controller while managing passenger concerns and company coordination.

synopsis: MD83 Captain experiences a tail compartment temperature high light during climb out. QRH procedures are complied with and flight returns to departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced a Tail Comp Hot warning during climb out, identified a real duct leak, and declared an emergency. They landed with the left engine retarded and shut it down on taxi, noting all supporting elements performed well.

synopsis: A B727-200's 'A' Hydraulic System developed a leak so the Captain diverted to a nearby airport with multiple runways and more suitable weather than the destination airport.
summary: The crew diverted to a closer airport due to a leak in Hydraulic System A, following QRH limitations and avoiding potential runway closures at the destination. They executed an uneventful landing, though the cause of the malfunction remains unknown.

synopsis: A319 First Officer describes a night visual approach to Runway 26 at ABQ that results in an ATC low altitude alert followed quickly by an EGPWS terrain warning. The escape maneuver is initiated until clear then the visual approach is continued to landing. Reporter recommends against night visual approaches to Runway 26.
summary: The flight crew descended below the 9,200 FT minimum vectoring altitude during a visual approach to Runway 26 at ABQ, triggering an EGPWS warning. The Captain executed an escape maneuver, climbed to 1,500 FT, and subsequently completed a stabilized visual approach.

synopsis: An MD80 flight crew, during an approach following a go around for an antiskid failure caution, armed the ILS for approach before receiving clearance. An altitude excursion was the result.
summary: During a go-around for an anti-skid failure, the crew selected ILS mode before approach clearance while monitoring traffic, causing the autopilot to capture the glideslope and descend 400 feet below the cleared 4,000-foot altitude. The deviation occurred because both pilots were distracted by ATC traffic calls and missed the mode change until alerted.

synopsis: An A310 ECAM alerted EXCESSIVE CABIN VERTICAL SPEED and EXCESSIVE CABIN ALTITUDE as the aicraft climbed through 11,000 FT.The QRH was complied with and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: During climbout at 11,000 FT, the crew received excessive cabin altitude warnings and leveled at 13,000 FT while donning oxygen masks. The pilot returned to the departure airport after failing to control pressure with manual controls, suspecting a stuck full-open outflow valve.

synopsis: Galley carts are coming out of the storage compartment during takeoffs and landings due to insufficient length of the locking mechanism.
summary: Cabin crew reported that galley carts dislodged from storage during takeoff and landing because the installed locking mechanisms were too short to secure them properly. The insufficient lock length caused the carts to move despite being stowed.

synopsis: A cargo loading tail jack was found released (separated) from a fuselage jack pad mount ball in high wind conditions. Fuselage skin crack damage was found on the B747-400 tailcone.
summary: During a pre-departure walk-around in high winds, a faulty tail jack released from the fuselage jack ball and damaged the tailcone skin. The jack contacted the fuselage 12 inches from the mount, resulting in a crack in the skin.

synopsis: A Mechanic signed-off a Lubrication (grease) Work Card for the Left-hand (L/H) and Right-Hand (R/H) Main Landing Gears (MLG) and Truck Bogie Pivot Pins on a B767-300 aircraft, after returning from a break for heat and fatigue, without completing the job.
summary: A mechanic performing maintenance on the right-hand main landing gear pivot pins signed the work card before completing the task due to heat, fatigue, and distraction. The incident was caused by a memory lapse, resulting in incomplete maintenance being documented as finished.

synopsis: A Tug Driver and a Brake Rider in the flight deck of a B767-300 lost communications with each other after the tug and tow bar became disconnected.
summary: A Brake Rider towing a B767-300 experienced a towbar break-away on Taxiway Yankee, shearing the intercom cord. The rider subsequently applied brakes to stop the uncontrolled aircraft after noticing it drifting left of the centerline and hearing rumbling sounds.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot landed on RNT Runway 34 and expected to hear a clearance on Taxiway A to his parking, His expectation overrode the actual clearance which was to 'Exit on Taxiway A and hold.' He did not hold and a near collision with another aircraft occurred.
summary: The pilot landed at RNT and misinterpreted a taxi clearance due to expectation bias, failing to look both ways before entering Taxiway A. This caused a near-collision with another aircraft, which stopped after the controller issued an immediate hold position instruction.

synopsis: A pilot reported his M20E landing gear collapsed after what appeared to be a normal approach and landing with the gear extended.
summary: The pilot landed a single-engine aircraft after practicing maneuvers, but the landing gear collapsed upon touchdown, causing the props to strike the runway and the aircraft to belly-skid. The pilot suspects dim gear-down indicator lights in bright sunlight led to a false confirmation that the gear was locked, though the exact mechanical cause remains unknown.

synopsis: A PA22 throttle linkage became disconnected inflight causing the engine to run at full RPM, so the pilot shut the engine down on short final for a dead stick landing. The linkage was repaired.
summary: The pilot experienced a throttle linkage disengagement causing full engine RPM, necessitating a dead stick landing that resulted in rolling off the runway. A mechanic subsequently repaired the linkage.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described an apparent rapid descent by an aircraft flying through weather and noted that improved ATC weather RADAR could assist in these types of situations.
summary: An air traffic controller observed a PC12 in rapid descent from 21,000 to 11,500 feet while avoiding precipitation. The controller re-established contact, directed the pilot to maneuver between weather cells, and cleared a climb back to 21,000 feet, noting a potential need for better weather radar.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a probable loss of separation event during a ERAM testing period, the Controller listed the lack of Preferential Settings ('pref-set') availability as one causal factor.
summary: An air traffic controller managing a 48-hour ERAM test used incorrect preferential settings while handling Air Carrier X and Y during a double arrival stream. The controller cleared both aircraft to descend with a minimum separation of 5 NM, noting that using another controller's settings was a distraction and recommending better altitude margin management.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier crew approached ABQ for a night visual to Runway 26 and momentarily leveled after an GPWS warning, but continued the approach and after landing decided a Runway 26 night approach was ill advised.
summary: The flight crew received a single Terrain warning and Pull Up light at 8,500 feet MSL while approaching ABQ at night. The captain initiated a brief go-around instead of a full terrain avoidance maneuver, later admitting this was an error requiring an ASAP report.

synopsis: A flight crew reported while taxiing on Taxiway S and after crossing Runway 30 they failed to turn right on Taxiway Q to Runway 27 because the Taxiway Q signage on Taxiway S after crossing Runway 30 was confusing.
summary: The flight crew missed Taxiway Quebec while taxiing to Runway 27 after receiving clearance to cross Taxiway 30, turning onto Taxiway Papa instead. The pilot attributed the error to confusing signage and noted that the hotspot depiction omitted the intersection of Taxiways T, P, and Q.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A pilot taxied from an FBO at LZU with clearance to Runway 25 via Taxiway D, but was not able to identify the very faded Runway 7/25 hold short line on D. A runway incursion occurred, although he stopped a great distance from the actual runway.
summary: The pilot violated the hold-short line for Runway 25 while taxiing on Taxiway D due to extremely obscure ground markings that were difficult to see even in bright daylight. Although the pilot held short of the runway boundary initially, they inadvertently entered the safety area before being instructed to return to the FBO ramp.

synopsis: A C152 Instructor reported engine failure due to fuel exhaustion. A safe forced landing was executed in a nearby park.
summary: During a cross-country VFR training flight, the pilot experienced an engine quit due to apparent fuel exhaustion and performed an emergency landing in a park. The pilot noted that 2.0 gallons of fuel were removed, despite POH data indicating sufficient endurance for the flight duration.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Corporate Jet flight crew entered 30.38 in the altimeters on visual approach to GRB, but received an ATC low altitude alert because the actual altimeter was 29.38.
summary: The crew incorrectly entered an altimeter setting of 30.38 instead of 29.38 from the Approach Controller's ATIS. After ATC issued a low altitude alert, the crew corrected the setting and continued a visual approach to Runway 24 at GRB in VFR conditions.

synopsis: A C206 pilot made a rudder input counter to a slight yaw during the landing flare and inappropriately also made an aileron input which caused the aircraft to skid off the runway striking a wingtip and the propeller.
summary: The pilot reported a runway excursion during landing at 70 KTS with full flaps, caused by an unconscious right control input while correcting a left yaw. The aircraft skidded off the runway, resulting in damage to the right wing and propeller, though no injuries occurred.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a 'Low Altitude' alert event when traffic on the ILS descended below the published mandatory altitudes, the reporter listing possible confusion regarding flight plan status and weather conditions as contributing factors.
summary: A Local Controller issued a Low Altitude Alert to a PA31 descending below 7,000 feet while not established on the ILS 29R approach. The pilot climbed to 7,000 feet, reported the airport in sight, and was cleared to land safely after the controller suspected the pilot was attempting a VFR operation despite IFR status.

synopsis: Tower Controller described an airspace incursion event, the reporter listed the STAR RADAR weather display colors as less than desired for control purposes.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a left turn to heading 350 for an IFR departure at 5,000 feet, but the pilot deviated to heading 075 due to weather misidentified as light precipitation on the STARS radar. The controller attributed the deviation to the radar displaying extreme weather as green instead of brown, requesting a system correction.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described an unsafe situation in the facility with regard to ERAM equipment and ICAO Flight Plan modifications, the reporter suggested additional instruction on the subject process in lieu of briefings.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a CEDAR memo regarding ICAO flight plan templates was insufficient because most controllers lack training on the system. The controller noted that previous data entry errors caused deviations in other facilities and recommended hands-on instruction instead of briefings.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a possible loss of separation event between an IFR departure and an IFR inbound aircraft cleared for a Visual Approach, the event occurring during approach services to a VFR Towered airport.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller cleared a Baron for a visual approach at 5,000 feet while a Caravan departed, assuming the Baron would turn right and the Caravan would turn left. The Caravan deviated south and the Baron did not turn, but the controller determined the aircraft diverged safely with at least three miles separation.

synopsis: A B737-300 pressurization system failed at FL350 so an emergency was declared, a descent begun and the QRH completed as they diverted to a nearby airport. The cabin and aircraft altitudes met at 15,000 FT.
summary: Pilots managed a gradual cabin depressurization at FL350 by executing an emergency descent through thunderstorms to 10,000 feet. They landed with a 16-knot tailwind to prioritize passenger safety, resulting in three medical examinations with no transports required.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot reports ATC altitude assignments on MOTIF 4 Arrival into MDW are consistantly at odds with the published restrictrictions.
summary: Pilots reported that during the MOTIF 4 arrival into MDW, ATC frequently issued altitude clearances conflicting with the published STAR, such as at MINOK. This mismatch forces pilots to constantly reprogram the FMC, increasing cockpit complexity and task loading in a high-workload environment.

synopsis: A B757 Reserve First Officer called in fatigued after being assigned another short call trip because she was only able to get six hours of sleep in the previous 38 hours.
summary: A fatigued pilot reported being assigned a short-call duty after only six hours of sleep in 38 hours, following a long trip with insufficient rest. The pilot refused the assignment due to being unfit, citing unsafe scheduling practices and crew shortages as the cause.

synopsis: A B767-300 Captain rejected the takeoff at about 80 KTS after he detected an EGT fluctuate and roll back. Neither reverse nor heavy braking was used on the 10,000 FT runway.
summary: The Captain aborted a takeoff at 80 KTS due to left engine EGT fluctuation and rollback, noting that autobrakes failed to engage. Although the aircraft stopped safely, the Captain admitted to deviating from procedure by not using reverse thrust, acknowledging that doing so would have improved deceleration.

synopsis: An EMB-135-BJ encountered significant wake turbulence behind a B747 on arrival into LAX that resulted in a 90 degree roll and 30 degree nose down pitch. Flight Attendant reported slight injuries.
summary: During descent to LAX at 13,000 feet, the flight crew encountered severe wake turbulence from a preceding B747, causing a 90-degree roll. The incident injured a flight attendant and dislodged galley contents, though prior securing by the crew prevented more serious damage.

synopsis: A BE36 main gear tire failed on landing so the pilot, unable to taxi off the runway, had Maintenance replace the tire on the runway with Airport Rescue and Fire Fighters standing by.
summary: The pilot reported a left main tire flat upon landing, preventing taxi off the active runway. After maintenance replaced the tire and tube, the pilot taxied to the FBO and requested an inspection of the wheel and gear assembly.

aircraft: Cessna Twin Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: When the left engine started to run rough, the pilot of a Cessna twin declared an emergency and returned to his departure airport.
summary: The pilot reported a rough-running left engine shortly after departure with no instrument indications. An emergency was declared, and the aircraft was vectored back to the departure airport for a safe landing without incident.

synopsis: A BE36 exited the runway when the left main tire failed during the takeoff roll.
summary: The pilot reported a left main tire failure during takeoff roll, causing the aircraft to partially leave the runway without structural damage. The pilot attributed the event to insufficient preflight inspection and ignoring a bumpy taxi sensation, noting the aircraft was repaired and returned to service.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described an airspace violation when the aircraft involved apparently confused FL330 with FL230, the reporter listed a phraseology modification that might prevent future altitude assignment confusion.
summary: A Sector X controller cleared a B737 at FL340 to descend to FL330, but the pilot read back FL230 and descended into Sector Y. The pilot was subsequently assigned FL300, and the controller attributed the error to ambiguous flight level phrasing, resolving to use explicit digit separation in future clearances.

synopsis: Tower Supervisor described a 'corrected' conflict event unknowingly set up by the Local Controller, but caught by the reporter. The reporter indicated that the minimally experienced Controller was focused on another operation and failed to note the error.
summary: The Flight Line Manager observed a Local Controller instructing a B737 to line up on Runway 21 while a Mooney was approaching, caused by the controller's distraction with a pipeline aircraft. Two other controllers intervened immediately to prevent a collision, resulting in no loss of separation.

synopsis: ARTCC Controller reported a violation of negative RVSM aircraft coordination requirements, recommending refresher training should be conducted.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a Negative RVSM military aircraft flew at FL320 in RVSM airspace without prior sector coordination or notification. The controller attributed this to a failure to follow 7110.65 requirements and recommended mandatory briefing clarification.

synopsis: A80 Controller described a less than required arrival spacing event but elected not to issue a go around.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller at a Parallel Monitor Position allowed a trailing B767 to continue an approach despite spacing dropping to 2.36 miles behind a lead B737. The controller deemed the spacing sufficient for Tower and safe, noting that a 3-mile Transfer Control Point would have made the operation legal.

synopsis: A B757-200 flight crew declared an emergency and diverted to an airport with a longer runway after the left hydraulic system failed when the landing gear was extended.
summary: The crew experienced low left hydraulic quantity and pressure on final approach, prompting a go-around and emergency diversion. After a normal landing, the aircraft was pinned and towed due to a nose wheel fluid leak.

synopsis: Following a spike in oil temperature on the right engine a Q-400 flight crew shut it down, declared an emergency and returned to their departure airport. The reporter believes inflight shutdowns at his airline are becoming commonplace and suggested review of maintenance procedures as an ameliorative measure.
summary: The flight crew secured the right engine during climb after oil temperature spiked despite reducing power, forcing a return to the departure airport. The aircraft landed safely, but the reporter criticized the airline for assigning the flight attendants to duty shortly after the incident and called for a maintenance policy review.

synopsis: EMB170 Captain describes the conditions leading up to a fatigue call.
summary: A reserve pilot with 23 years of experience called in fatigued during the sixth day of a reserve sequence due to inconsistent scheduling, excessive duty hours, and inadequate rest. The pilot attributed the call to a lack of humane consideration for reserve pilots, warning that such conditions lead to increased fatigue and sick calls.

synopsis: An EMB-145 descending via the PHLBO STAR suffered an NMAC with opposite direction VFR traffic.
summary: During descent on the PHLBO STAR into EWR, the crew received a TCAS RA and visual contact with a head-on Cessna at approximately 8,000 feet. The pilot increased descent rate to achieve 200–300 feet of separation, attributing the near-miss to the VFR aircraft's improper altitude and lack of timely ATC traffic advisories.

synopsis: EMB170 Captain describes difficulties opening and arming the main cabin door as reported and demonstrated to him by the A Flight Attendant. Maintenance cannot improve the intermittent operation of the door and the aircraft is refused by the crew.
summary: The flight crew and maintenance personnel encountered an intermittent L1 door arming failure after landing, where the handles would not move to the armed position consistently. Due to suspected rigging issues and the inability to guarantee safe emergency egress, the crew refused to sign off the aircraft for revenue service.

synopsis: PA-28 instructor pilot reported that student pilot caught a foot between brake pedal and crossbar, which resulted in a runway excursion on landing. Instructor was unable to overcome stuck brake.
summary: During a practice power-off 180 approach with a student pilot, the student's left foot became stuck between the toe brake pedal and crossbar, locking the left brake on final. The aircraft skidded off the runway into the grass with only a flat spot on the left main tire as damage.

synopsis: CE650 Reports being cleared for takeoff from Runway 26L at ATL and at the same time instructed to turn right to 310 at the middle marker. At the marker, which is very shortly after takeoff, the crew is unsure of the turn and delays slightly eliciting a query from the Controller and a further turn to 340.
summary: A crew departing ATL Runway 26L experienced a 20-second delay initiating a turn at the middle marker due to confusion over a local ATC procedure not found in published charts. The pilot reported that requiring an immediate turn during critical climb duties is unsafe and recommended removing this procedure.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A CL65 flight crew was unable to extend flaps for their approach. ATC declared an emergency for them and they landed without incident on the longest runway at their planned destination airport.
summary: The flight crew received a flap fail caution at zero degrees 30 minutes into flight and executed a zero-flap landing without incident. Although the crew did not declare an emergency, the Tower did so, and post-flight inspection revealed no damage.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described an emergency event when an inbound helicopter encountered weather and fuel issues but failed to provide ATC with critical information regarding same.
summary: An ATC controller vectored a B206 helicopter inbound to an airport with marginal VFR conditions (OVC010). The pilot failed to report fuel criticality until declaring an emergency after being unable to descend through clouds, resulting in a crash response while the controller attempted to find a cloud break.

synopsis: ZOB Controller described a TCAS RA event during holding operations at POLAR Intersection, apparently activated by an unknown VFR aircraft maneuvering in and/or near the holding pattern airspace.
summary: An air traffic controller managing a DC-9 holding at POLAR near DTW issued a TCAS Resolution Advisory after a VFR aircraft with erratic transponder codes climbed into the DC-9's altitude. The DC-9 pilot followed the RA to avoid a potential collision, while the unknown aircraft continued displaying inconsistent codes before exiting the airspace.

synopsis: TRACON Controller chronicled an emergency event when a C182 was encountering weather, experiencing fuel issues, having navigational difficulties and was having problems communicating with ATC.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller assisted a C182 pilot who became ill and lost fuel indications while attempting an ILS approach in mountainous terrain with poor radar coverage. Despite confusion over frequencies and a missed approach, the controller vectored the aircraft to a safe landing after the pilot recovered instrument readings.

synopsis: A B737-700 flight crew failed to comply with a STAR crossing restriction following a comm radio static problem which required they utilize the #2 Comm for ATC communications. During the switchover the Captain had failed to turn up the #2 volume and missed the clearance.
summary: The crew experienced VHF #1 static while on the RAVEN arrival to BWI, causing the Pilot to miss a descent clearance from Approach. Consequently, they missed the NICCO crossing restriction by 600–800 feet due to delayed radio switching and slow automation response, though the aircraft was recovered and the faulty transmitter was replaced.

synopsis: High and fast on the descent while attempting to get back on schedule, the flight crew of a B737-300 extended the landing gear at an airspeed in excess of the limit to do so. A delayed descent clearance from ATC may have contributed to the conundrum.
summary: The Captain and First Officer extended landing gear at 290 KIAS during descent due to a high energy state and ATC distraction, exceeding the 270 KIAS limit. They slowed immediately, landed safely, and reported no damage after a post-flight inspection.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain laments the large amount of FOD found under an near his aircraft during preflight.
summary: The flight crew discovered over 50 pieces of FOD in the gate Safety Zone while preparing for departure, noting that Ground Operations had failed to conduct a required walkdown. The reporter attributed this to inconsistent cleaning habits and requested leadership intervention to prevent potential engine ingestion.

synopsis: A B737 Captain reported the chronic failure on the part of ground crews at BWI to inspect for and remove FOD in the safety zones of gates used by their jets.
summary: The pilot reported significant Foreign Object Debris (FOD) in the Safety Zone at BWI during taxi-in, noting that Ramp Agents had not performed an effective pre-arrival walkdown. The pilot collected 50 items, including metal parts and trash, and attributed the hazard to a lack of proactive FOD prevention and leadership engagement at the station.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain laments the large amount of FOD found under and around his aircraft during preflight.
summary: A pilot observed Ramp Agents at LAS failing to conduct FOD walkdowns during an aircraft swap, leaving debris in the Safety Zone. The pilot manually collected various items while agents remained inactive, prompting a call for the Station Manager to enforce the FOD program to prevent engine ingestion.

synopsis: A B757 Captain requested revised flight plan information after ATC revised the transcontinental routing, but Dispatch failed to responded because they did not have time for such requests.
summary: The pilot reported that during a transcontinental night flight with a significant reroute, Dispatch failed to provide requested updated flight and fuel plans or operational information. The pilot attributed this lack of support to potential staffing or training issues and questioned the utility of the Dispatch service.

synopsis: A319 Captain describes receiving a terrain warning during a night visual approach to Runway 26 at ABQ and executing a go around. The second approach is successful.
summary: The pilot and First Officer initiated a go-around during a night visual approach to Runway 26 at ABQ after receiving terrain warnings caused by being vectored high and far from the airport by Approach. The reporter attributed the incident to late descent clearances and an unknown RNAV approach that would have provided safer guidance.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reports possible P56 incursion when lost communication with PCT occurs after being cleared from BAL direct to DCA and expect vectors. The flight had been dispatched with the FMC MEL'd.
summary: A crew operating an aircraft with an MEL'd FMS lost communications with Potomac Approach while vectored to DCA, causing them to encroach on P56 airspace. The First Officer initiated an unauthorized turn to avoid the restricted area after ATC failed to provide vectors due to a ground radio failure.

synopsis: A B717 First Officer selected the VERT SPD mode in order to increase climb rate as requested by ATC, then got distracted, so that the airspeed decayed and the LOW SPEED protection engaged a which added MCT power.
summary: During climb through FL310, the Pilot Flying selected VERT SPD to expedite climb, causing airspeed decay that triggered Low Speed Protection and MCT thrust. The Pilot Not Flying intervened to lower pitch and restore speed, resulting in no ATC deviation or safety incident.

synopsis: A day after landing a B767-300 ETOPS aircraft, a First Officer was informed the #3 Leading Edge Slat was found damaged, canted sideways, and not fully retracted.
summary: The crew of an ETOPS B767-300 landed and taxied at ZZZ1 without detecting a damaged Leading Edge Slat due to a lack of aural or EICAS warnings. The reporter notes that without these alerts or the Slat Protection System, the crew could not have identified the issue, raising safety concerns about the system's reliability.

synopsis: A CE-750 flight crew reported AHRS heading information was invalid on the LGA Whitestone climb. DG fast slave did not work, and all navigation information was inaccurate until the AHRS corrected itself at cruise altitude.
summary: During the LGA 4 Whitestone Climb departure, both AHRS units malfunctioned with 30-45 degree heading discrepancies, rendering the autopilot and DG fast slave inoperative. The crew relied on the magnetic compass to navigate after erroneous VOR and map data prevented accurate heading and course tracking until higher altitudes.

synopsis: A DHC8-300 developed a burnt rubber smell with smoke during taxi out so an emergency was declared, the engines shut down, and after Airfield Rescue and Fire Fighter inspections the aircraft restarted for a return to the gate.
summary: The crew smelled burnt rubber and saw smoke while taxiing, prompting an emergency stop on Taxiway Bravo. After shutting off bleeds and engines, fire rescue found no external fire, but the odor worsened during the return to the gate with bleeds remaining off.

synopsis: A pilot reported that his Company ordered a Mechanic to lubricate a B767-300 pack valve when he knew an engine bleed valve was the most probable cause of a repeat pressurization problem.
summary: The flight crew and maintenance personnel encountered a recurring left pack fault where mechanics allegedly falsified logbook entries to release the aircraft for revenue service despite knowing the issue was likely an engine bleed problem, not the valve. The reporter asserts that management coerced mechanics to perform superficial fixes rather than resolving the actual safety hazard.

synopsis: Air Carrier departure from Runway 15L at IAH voiced concern regarding traffic departing Runway 15R simultaneously without and ATC notification, the reporter recommended staggering departures in these types of operations.
summary: The pilot reported a simultaneous takeoff from IAH Runways 15L and 15R where their aircraft flew wingtip-to-wingtip until 400 feet. The reporter cited safety concerns due to the lack of traffic advisories and the risk of inadvertent turns into the parallel departure path.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An Airbus flight crew encountered a false localizer intercept when cleared for the ILS Runway 9 at MEM.
summary: Pilots on the Tammy Arrival experienced a false localizer capture while intercepting Runway 09, causing an unintended 20-degree right turn. The crew manually corrected the deviation, suspecting ground equipment interference from Tunica Airport as the cause.

synopsis: A Captain was informed that a right wing upper access panel, outboard of the spoilers, was missing from their MD-11 aircraft without any discrepancy noted in their pre-flight or post flight walk-around checks.
summary: The Captain reported that an MD-11 was found missing a 72x18 inch panel on the upper right wing after an uneventful flight. The crew detected no discrepancies during preflight or postflight inspections, and the cause of the panel loss remains undetermined.

synopsis: A Maintenance Controller was informed he had released a CRJ-200 aircraft for continued service with lightning strike damage that was more substantial than the information a Contract Maintenance Mechanic had provided to him.
summary: A CRJ-200 pilot reported a lightning strike, and a contract mechanic found a disconnected bonding strap and paint burns before releasing the aircraft. Later, line mechanics discovered additional damage, leading the reporter to conclude the initial external inspection was insufficient.

synopsis: A PA31 pilot diverted under emergency conditions to the nearest suitable airport due to gas fumes and liquid leaks behind the instrument panel.
summary: A VFR pilot en-route reported a fuel smell and liquid dripping from the instrument panel, prompting an emergency declaration and diversion to an airport with ARFF. The pilot executed a normal landing to the ramp with ARFF escort, deplaning passengers without further incident.

synopsis: When their right engine began losing power the instructor and student pilots declared an emergency, ultimately shut down the failed engine and returned safely to their departure airport.
summary: During a student training flight leveling at 5,500 MSL, the right engine failed after RPM dropped and the engine shook, prompting an emergency declaration and landing. Maintenance found fuel and oil present, though the pre-flight run-up showed a 150 RPM drop on the right magneto.

aircraft: M-20 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An M20 pilot filed IFR to AVP expressed his displeasure when he was denied direct routing through the CLT Class B due to arrivals and departures.
summary: A pilot flying IFR to AVP was vectored 60 degrees off course by Charlotte Approach to circumvent CLT airspace, adding significant time and reducing fuel reserves. The pilot attributed this circuitous routing to controller coordination issues and a perceived reluctance to handle transient general aviation traffic.

synopsis: A VFR-rated helicopter pilot reported he chose to declare an emergency and descend through the clouds when he was caught above an overcast.
summary: A non-instrument rated helicopter pilot declared a fuel emergency while returning to departure due to deteriorating VFR conditions and cloud cover. The pilot descended through clouds to 1,000 feet AGL and landed safely without incident.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described an over take event on final and subsequent loss of separation when go around instructions were issued, the reporter listing varying wind conditions accompanying thunderstorm activity as contributing to the event.
summary: An air traffic controller managing a Global Express and a Falcon during erratic winds and turbulence initiated a missed approach when the Global Express's ground speed increased unexpectedly, closing the gap to 2.8 miles. The controller attributed the near-miss to unpredictable wind shifts that rendered standard spacing techniques ineffective.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: SFO Controller described a below-MVA event when traffic on final for Runway 28L initiated a go around absent a landing clearing with traffic departing Runway 28R, the reporter assigning the wrong altitude/frequency to missed approach aircraft.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller at SFO cleared a CRJ for a missed approach on Runway 28L after the crew reported no landing clearance. The controller attributed the subsequent frequency error and altitude confusion to being distracted by the go-around and frequency congestion.

synopsis: ATL Controller described a potential conflict involving an RNAV departure routing, noting that equipment limitations prevented him/her from observing the initial wrong turn and suggesting additional and/or re-location of RADAR displays in the Tower.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared a B717 for the RAMBLN6 departure but the pilot mistakenly flew the COKEM5 route, resulting in a separation of less than 3 miles behind a preceding aircraft. The controller attributed the missed turn to limited visibility and RACD display limitations caused by equipment blocking the view and being slaved to an arrival sector.

synopsis: ZDC Controller described a very busy/complex traffic period noting last minute enroute restrictions for multiple Florida airports, adding the TMU's at all involved facilities were late in implementing flow requirements.
summary: ZDC and ZJX Traffic Management Units issued late trail and altitude restrictions for MIA, FLL, and MCO due to weather and volume, creating an unsafe, complex situation for controllers managing high airborne inventory. The reporter attributes the chaos to untimely restrictions that failed to account for existing traffic, forcing difficult vectors and conflicts.

synopsis: TRACON Controller acknowledged a loss of separation event when 'thinking' one descent clearance but in fact 'issuing' another.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a descent clearance to a C750 using a BE20's callsign, causing the BE20 to descend below 050 MSL while the C750 was at 040 MSL. This error resulted in lost separation between the aircraft, prompting the controller to recognize the need for improved situational awareness and verification of clearances.

synopsis: Enroute Controller working non-RADAR oceanic traffic described an unauthorized climb through occupied airspace, the reporter acknowledging using less than clear and concise phraseology with this international flight crew.
summary: An air traffic controller advised an A330 at FL320 that a climb to FL340 was possible at M0.76, but the pilot climbed without a clearance, triggering a trail probe with traffic at FL330. The controller attributed the incident to ambiguous phrasing and a language barrier, noting the pilot failed to verify the clearance before climbing.

synopsis: S46 Controller described a TCAS RA event between an IFR BFI departure aircraft and an unknown VFR aircraft operating nearby, the reporter listing less than complete communication between ATC personnel and the VFR aircraft.
summary: A C560 departing BFI received a TCAS RA while climbing to 2,100 feet due to an unidentified VFR target at 1,600 feet. The pilot descended to 2,100 feet, and the controller attributed the event to a lack of traffic advisories from BFI Tower prior to the frequency change.

synopsis: M03 Controller described a developing conflict when traffic issued the CRSON SID was navigating via the CASLN SID, the reporter noting that this was not the first instance of pilots confusing these similar SID names.
summary: An air traffic controller observed Aircraft Y deviating from the cleared CRSON1 departure to the CASLN1 departure, causing a conflict with Aircraft X during simultaneous departures from Memphis. The controller issued a heading and altitude change to Aircraft X to restore separation, attributing the incident to confusingly named Standard Instrument Departures.

synopsis: HCF Controller voiced concern regarding the on-going problems with 127.6 in certain areas, noting the problem has existed for a long period and should be resolved.
summary: An air traffic controller reported persistent communication failures on frequency 127.6 between AUNTI, BOARD, APACK, and BITTA sectors affecting non-RADAR aircraft checking into HCF. The poor audio quality forced the controller to repeatedly request IDENTs to confirm clearance receipt, causing significant distraction and wasted time during busy periods.

synopsis: Tower CIC described a confused intersection departure event caused by a breakdown of communications between the Ground Controller and Local Controller.
summary: A Local Controller cleared an Archer for takeoff from blocked intersection C8 due to poor scanning and missed Ground Controller coordination. Despite the clearance cancellation, the pilot departed, resulting in a runway incursion.

synopsis: A Line Captain describes why he believes MEL 28-02-01R should have been applied to their B737-800 aircraft for an inoperative Right Center Fuel Boost Pump. Maintenance Control had applied MEL 28-02-02R. Compliance with Airworthiness Directives, AD 2002-19-52 and 2002-24-51 that superseded their Aircraft Flight Manuals was also raised.
summary: The pilot disputed Maintenance and the Assistant Chief Pilot's issuance of MEL 28-02-02R for an inoperative right center fuel boost pump, arguing it conflicted with Airworthiness Directives and Flight Manual limitations. The pilot flew the aircraft as dispatched but planned to divert if the second pump failed, noting the risk of unusable fuel.

synopsis: An air carrier Captain reported receiving an altitude alert from Approach Controller and EGPWS on visual approach to ABQ. Escape maneuver was executed and a normal visual approach and landing followed.
summary: The flight crew received a visual approach clearance to Runway 26 at ABQ and descended below the 9,200-foot minimum vectoring altitude. This triggered an EGPWS terrain warning, requiring an escape maneuver before the crew stabilized the descent and completed the landing.

synopsis: B737 Captain laments the change in the title of the Two Engine Flame Out checklist to the Loss of Thrust on Both Engines checklist. The CFM56 engines on the B737 occasionally experience a significant delay in thrust response (up to 40 seconds) under certain conditions, which may be interpreted as a loss of thrust.
summary: A B-737 pilot reported that the renamed "Loss of Thrust in Both Engines" checklist may cause crews to unnecessarily shut down operating engines during known 40-second thrust response delays. The pilot argues this change complicates recovery for a condition where engines are running but thrust is temporarily unavailable, recommending a title change or added guidance.

synopsis: A Saab 340 flight crew, confronted with varying ITT readings opted to divert to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced right engine ITT fluctuations and a 50°C delta while en route at 8,000 FT in a Saab. They diverted to a known alternate for a precautionary visual landing, suspecting FOD ingestion or faulty ITT trimming as the cause.

synopsis: B757-200 First Officer reports a left hydraulic system overheat during climb out and the left engine driven pump is secured in accordance with QRH procedures. After reaching cruise an EICAS message for L Hyd Quantity and L Hyd Pressure is annunciated. The crew elects to continue to destination where alternate gear and flap extension methods are employed prior to landing. The aircraft is towed to the gate.
summary: The flight crew experienced a left hydraulic system failure during climb and cruise, leading to an emergency landing with alternate gear and flap extension. Although the aircraft landed safely, the crew faced difficulties with nose wheel steering and right reverser deployment due to the hydraulic loss.

synopsis: An MD-80 flight crew reported a malfunctioning FMS to ATC, and they flew VOR-based navigation to destination.
summary: Shortly after departure, the flight crew received an 'RNP' flag on both PFDs and reported FMS failure to LAX Center. The crew switched to VOR navigation, received a heading from ATC, and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: An MD11 First Officer is informed after the fact that an upper wing panel on an aircraft he flew was found missing on post flight.
summary: The pilot reported that a missing upper wing skin panel was discovered post-flight despite a normal preflight walk-around and uneventful flight. The pilot suspects the panel detached en route due to the difficulty of visually inspecting the wing's upper surface from the ground.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported having to reject takeoff at an uncontrolled airport due to opposite direction takeoff traffic. Reporter stated that all appropriate communications had been made on CTAF, but the other aircraft apparently failed to hear them.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff from Runway 01 after a Cessna entered Runway 19 at the departure end while the crew was accelerating. The incident occurred despite multiple CTAF calls and direct communication, prompting the Cessna to vacate the runway and the crew to complete rejected takeoff procedures.

synopsis: A B757-200 First Officer reported receiving a TE FLAP DISAGREE EICAS message on final approach. A go-around was executed, procedures run, and after consulting with Operations, a diversion plan was implemented.
summary: During final approach, the flight crew received a TE FLAP DISAGREE message when flaps stopped beyond 20 degrees instead of 25. The crew executed a go-around, diverted to a nearby airport with a longer runway, and landed uneventfully without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: A B757-200 flight crew reported directional control difficulties on initial takeoff roll, so takeoff was rejected and the aircraft returned to the gate for maintenance attention.
summary: During takeoff roll below 30 knots, the aircraft veered right unresponsive to rudder input until left brake application corrected the path. The Captain aborted the takeoff, and the aircraft returned to the gate for maintenance.

synopsis: A Maintenance Controller and two Aircraft Dispatchers report about improperly applying two Configuration Deviation List (CDL) deferrals on the Main Landing Gear (MLG) doors of an EMB-145 aircraft for lightning strike damage.
summary: A dispatcher and maintenance controller mistakenly issued two Configuration Deviation Lists for the same main landing gear system due to ambiguous manual wording. The aircraft flew four flights before another dispatcher caught the error, leading to an aircraft swap.

synopsis: MD11 flight crew experiences frozen rudder trim at FL360. Flight continues to destination for a normal landing with rudder trim still frozen. Just prior to engine shut down the trim is found to be free.
summary: During enroute flight at FL360, the crew found the rudder trim knob frozen, though primary controls remained functional. They landed safely without declaring an emergency, and the knob functioned normally after shutdown, with suspected ice buildup as the unconfirmed cause.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports not having an RII Inspection accomplished after replacing a sheared teleflex cable for the #2 Engine right reverser half on a DC-10 aircraft.
summary: Two mechanics troubleshooting a deferred DC-10 engine thrust reverser sheared a flexshaft and installed a replacement teleflex cable without performing the required RII inspection. The reporter admits failing to identify the installation as an RII task because the requirement was not explicitly listed in the Maintenance Manual.

synopsis: A Maintenance Supervisor reports their new Aerospatiale/Eurocopter AS350 Aircraft Maintenance Manuals (AMM) do not have a clear Maintenance illustration reference to help determine the correct orientation of a beveled washer during build-up of the Aft Flex coupling, compared to the old manuals for the Main Rotor Drive System (MRDS).
summary: A mechanic encountered confusion regarding the correct orientation of a beveled washer during the Aft Flex coupling build-up on an AS350 Main Rotor Drive System. The reporter attributed this to the current maintenance manual lacking the clear illustration found in previous revisions, which previously helped distinguish the curved face from the flat side.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: A C-525B flight crew suffered a right engine flame out as they descended from FL430. A subsequent restart attempt at a lower altitude was successful and they continued to a safe landing where they sought maintenance attention.
summary: The crew experienced a right engine rollback and failure during descent from FL430 to FL370. After a successful restart at FL200, they landed without incident, attributing the issue to a faulty fuel delivery unit.

synopsis: Unable to completely extend the main gear despite repeated attempts the pilot of a C210L landed with only the nose gear extended and ran off the side of the runway. The aircraft suffered minor damage.
summary: The pilot experienced a main gear failure to lock during the landing phase, likely due to hydraulic fluid issues. After unsuccessful manual extension attempts, the pilot executed a partial gear landing, resulting in a skid onto grass and minor stabilizer damage with no injuries.

synopsis: A C208B brake system failed after taxi-out resulting in a hard left turn, so the pilot used all available braking to bring the aircraft to a stop. Previous brake failures were reported.
summary: The pilot experienced a left brake failure while taxiing a 6,700-lb aircraft on Taxiway A in 19G33 winds, causing a 90-degree excursion. Although initial inspections showed no issues, master cylinders were replaced due to a history of unexplained brake failures, with final inspection results pending.

synopsis: A student pilot aboard a C-150 was unable to remain on the runway surface when landing in a crosswind. He struck and broke a runway edge light, but did no apparent damage to the aircraft. Concern about a Heavy Jet going around behind him contributed to reporter's decision not to go around when his loss of control might otherwise have caused him to do so.
summary: The pilot landed a general aviation aircraft on Runway 15 in a 180-degree crosswind, blew off the runway, and struck an edge light. The pilot attributed the incident to an inability to handle the crosswind and pressure from a following heavy aircraft's uncertainty about going around.

synopsis: Both of a CE750's AHRS malfunctioned after a LGA Runway 13 takeoff and required ATC vectors referencing the magnetic compass until the compass systems returned to normal at cruise operating independently.
summary: During SID climb, both AHRS units malfunctioned with conflicting headings, causing unreliable navigation and a deviation toward another aircraft at 34,000 feet. ATC issued a divergent heading to prevent conflict, and the crew eventually stabilized using the magnetic compass and a recovered right AHRS at cruise.

synopsis: A C182 pilot departing the pattern experienced an NMAC with a B-17 entering it from the opposite direction.
summary: A pilot climbing to 2,000 feet in Class D airspace encountered a B-17 performing an extreme forward slip upwind, leaving no time for corrective action. The reporter attributed the near-miss to limited visibility for both pilots and the Tower controller's failure to alert traffic about the unconventional maneuver.

synopsis: A BE20 engine failed after being shutdown for training at FL270, then restarted at which time a bang was heard followed by debris exiting the engine.
summary: During a training flight, an instructor simulating a right engine shutdown caused an immediate explosion and debris ejection when moving the condition lever to LOW Idle. The crew secured the engine, declared an emergency, and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: A PA28 pilot on a night IFR flight suffered the loss of all electrical and, thus, communications and navigation capability. Rather than proceeding to his destination using lost comm procedures he opted to take emergency measures and diverted to a VFR airport for a safe landing.
summary: A single-pilot night IFR flight lost all electrical power 50 minutes after takeoff. The pilot declared an emergency, received no ATC response, and landed safely at a nearby non-towered airport after reaching VFR conditions.

synopsis: A321 Captain reports being assigned Runway 13 for landing at FLL due to construction, which he rejects in favor of Runway 9L. Reporter is informed by ATC that his company had made a commitment that all aircraft arriving FLL could land Runway 13.
summary: The A321 pilot requested Runway 9L for arrival at FLL due to its 9,000-foot length but was assigned Runway 13 (6,930 feet) by MIA Approach. The TRACON Supervisor enforced a new program prioritizing hourly counts over safety, despite the pilot's concerns that landing on the shorter runway was not as safe as using the longer available option.

synopsis: A PA34 instructor was unable to restart an engine after an inflight shutdown demonstration so he diverted to a nearby airport where Maintenance was able to start both engines.
summary: A flight instructor and student experienced a right engine restart failure at 5,500 feet MSL during a feather demonstration, resulting in a single-engine landing at a non-towered airport. Mechanics later started both engines using a power boost, attributing the issue to a possible short.

synopsis: ZSE Controller described an unsafe condition report involving ERAM and dropping of flight plan data.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported that a C17 on IR326 lost its flight plan from ERAM and EDST shortly after point 'D', causing a scramble to coordinate with Chinook Approach. The controller attributed the issue to a recurring software error on this route and recommended grounding flights until fixed.

synopsis: ZMA Controller described a very confused operational event involving military airspace including the coordination with the controlling agency, noting the lack of coordination within the facility referencing these types of operations.
summary: Miami ARTCC controllers cleared aircraft into W174 without knowing a military controlling agency existed, causing altitude conflicts and operational disruption. The reporter attributes the confusion to a lack of pre-coordination, clear procedures, and defined paperwork regarding the military mission's status and controlling authority.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a below MVA event when handling an IFR aircraft as a VFR and issuing a descent to below MVA limitations. The reporter listed lack of vigilance as the primary contributing factor.
summary: An air traffic controller mistakenly cleared an IFR PA44 to descend to 8,000 feet while in a 9,000-foot MVA due to misidentifying the flight strip as VFR. The aircraft exited the restricted airspace and landed safely behind a Citation without incident.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a TCAS RA event during a training session with parallel approaches in use, the reporter noting that he should have continued to work the position after the initial TCAS RA in lieu of returning the position to the trainee.
summary: An OJT instructor and trainee at Final Center lost separation between CE500 and CE560 due to CE500's slow turns and altitude deviations, triggering a TCAS RA. The instructor later admitted that resuming the trainee's duties too soon caused a missed shallow turn, bringing CE500 too close to Aircraft Z on final.

synopsis: A B737-300 Captain reported that after takeoff 15-18 right aileron trim units were need to attain coordinated flight so Maintenance asked the crew to return to the departure airport.
summary: The crew discovered excessive right aileron trim requirements after takeoff, suspecting the aircraft was out of rig. They returned to the departure airport without declaring an emergency, landed safely, and swapped aircraft, noting the previous crew failed to report the issue.

synopsis: A corporate jet Captain reported an NMAC with a glider who was apparently flying at 11,000 FT directly on the LYNNX 8 arrival to BUR.
summary: The pilot of LYNXX 8, descending through 11,000 feet on arrival to BUR, avoided a collision with a non-transponder-equipped glider at the same altitude. The pilot executed an aggressive climb while the glider dove, passing 50 feet below, violating Mode C requirements above 10,000 feet.

synopsis: A CL300 Captain cleared for the SJC Fairground Visual Runway 30L was confused about the descent clearance because the Chart stated RECOMMENDED 5,000 FT prior to the MANDATORY 5,000 FT SJC 170 constraint and so he began the descent early.
summary: The flying pilot descended below 5,000 feet prior to the SJC 170 radial during the Fairground Visual approach to Runway 30L, confusing a recommended altitude with a mandatory one. The pilot corrected the descent after the reporter intervened, attributing the error to confusing chart wording that listed both recommended and mandatory 5,000 feet.

synopsis: A CRJ-90 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence on approach to DFW behind a B777 that resulted in 'significant roll.'
summary: The crew encountered significant wake turbulence roll from a preceding B777 during arrival at DFW, prompting ATC to provide additional spacing. No injuries occurred, and the crew recommended increased spacing and vertical separation behind the B777.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: After a late descent clearance from cruise into CRW, a Captain lowered the landing gear to regain the profile and at a high rate descended 900 FT below the ATC cleared 3,100 FT.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a high-rate descent on an ILS approach into CRW in IMC mountainous terrain due to a late descent clearance. The crew executed a 360-degree turn and recovered from a descent below 2,200 feet after the Captain struggled with pitch control and automation confusion.

synopsis: A CL604 pilot reported confusion regarding the correct name for 4A7 airport which is variously charted or referred to by ATC as: Hampton/Clayton County-Tara Field, Tara Field, Clayton County, Hampton, GA-Clayton Co-Tara. Most egregious is the fact the airport's AWOS advises the weather it provides is for Atlanta South Regional Airport, a name the reporter was unable to find associated with any US airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced confusion while approaching 4A7 due to conflicting airport names between the AWOS, ATC, and various charts. The AWOS identified the field as "Atlanta South Regional Airport," a name absent from all official publications, while other sources used "Tara Field" or "Clayton Co-Tara."

synopsis: The rudder pedal control of a C177RG nose wheel steering failed during landing which resulted in a wingtip contacting the runway and subsequently the aircraft exited the runway.
summary: During landing on Runway 34L, the aircraft turned left uncontrollably due to a mechanical failure in the nose wheel steering system. This caused the right wingtip to strike the pavement, damaging the strobe light and collapsing the oleo strut.

synopsis: A confused BE40 pilot departed on the TEB RUUDY FOUR and did not level at 1,500 FT prior to WENTZ so ATC notified him of the error at 2,000 FT.
summary: The pilot deviated from the RUUDY FOUR departure by leveling at 2,000 feet before crossing WENTZ Intersection, believing the restriction was 1,500 feet or above. ATC notified the pilot of the deviation but confirmed no issue was caused.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: After re-opening a closed runway, Tower Controller failed to note the runway as open on the ASDE-X programming and allowed an aircraft to land after an alarm was broadcasted. The reporter acknowledged his failure to use the checklist.
summary: An air traffic controller failed to update the ASDE-X status for Runway XXL after it reopened, causing a false alert for an A310 on final approach. The controller corrected the status and allowed the landing, though they acknowledged the aircraft should have been sent around.
