The controller disputed the clearance interpretation, assigned a new heading, and the aircraft eventually crossed BEKOL well above 16,000 feet.

synopsis: A tired flight crew was kept at too high an airspeed by ZBAA Approach Control until near the FAF. Flight crew had to scramble and work together to achieve stabilized approach criteria to avoid having to execute a go around.
summary: An experienced crew arrived at the FAF at 200 KTS with flaps 1 due to incorrect assumptions about ATC speed reduction and map markers. Although stabilized by 500 FT, the pilot attributed the initial error and subsequent rapid correction to fatigue.

synopsis: A B757-200 Captain reported a burning smell in the cockpit, so an emergency was declared and a divert to a nearby airport executed.
summary: During climbout, the flight crew detected burning fumes and visible smoke in the cockpit despite following the checklist and turning off ovens. After struggling with radio communications, they declared an emergency, diverted to a nearby airport, and made a normal overweight landing.

synopsis: Cleared for a visual approach to OKC, the flight crew of an A320 mistook PWA for OKC and began a descent to land there. Approach Control noted their track and altitude and brought the error to their attention.
summary: The Pilot Flying and crew visually misidentified Runway 17 at Wiley Post as Runway 17R at OKC during a visual approach. Tower controllers corrected the error by instructing a climb to 3,000 feet, allowing the aircraft to intercept the correct runway and land safely.

synopsis: A B767-300 returned to its departure airport when the outer pane of a passenger window cracked.
summary: The crew at 33,000 feet reported a loud bang and a jagged crack in the outer pane of cabin window 41A. They diverted back to the departure airport, following ATC clearance and FOM procedures to execute a normal approach and landing.

synopsis: Q400 Captain reported shutting down #1 engine due to high oil temperature. An emergency was declared and flight returned to departure airport.
summary: During climb, the flight crew encountered high oil temperature on engine #1 caused by over-servicing, leading to cavitation. After temperatures rose despite power reduction, the crew shut down the engine, declared an emergency, and returned safely to the departure airport.

synopsis: The Flight Crew of a CRJ-200 thought they had encountered wake turbulence during descent around 22,000 FT. Upon inspection after landing, they discovered the top half of the right engine cowling was missing and presumed lost enroute.
summary: During descent through 22,000 feet, the crew and a flight attendant experienced wake turbulence, but the flight continued to a normal landing. A post-flight inspection revealed the top half of the right engine cowl was missing.

synopsis: A medical helicopter flew a severely injured accident victim to the hospital where, upon removing the victim from the helicopter, they discovered he was carrying a handgun in his back pocket.
summary: A helicopter medical crew transported a patient from a motor vehicle accident scene to a hospital for rapid offload. During the transfer, hospital staff discovered a semi-automatic pistol in the patient's pocket, prompting a security response and a recommendation for increased crew vigilance regarding onboard weapons.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reports confusing NOTAM's and non-standard markings during an instrument approach and landing on Runway 12 at SMX.
summary: The flight crew descended for Runway 12 at SMX, expecting full length based on Dispatch advice, but encountered a barricade separating a black, unusable section from the gray active runway. The pilot adjusted the descent rate to land beyond the barricade, attributing the confusion to unclear NOTAMs and lack of tower warnings regarding the runway surface markings.

synopsis: Flight Crew describes a TCAS RA event while arriving into MIA caused by the climb rate of a departing aircraft leveling 1,000 feet below. The reporters aircraft climbed 250 feet to comply with the RA then returned to 8,000 feet.
summary: The flight crew encountered two TCAS Resolution Advisories while approaching MIA at 8,000 feet due to rapidly climbing departing aircraft. The crew complied with climb commands to 8,250 feet, notified ATC, and returned to altitude without loss of separation, noting that reduced climb rates on departure could prevent such alerts.

synopsis: A B737-800 First Officer's Display Electronic Unit (DEU) failed in flight so the crew diverted to a VMC airport where Maintenance determined that both DEU's had faults.
summary: The crew experienced multiple display failures enroute, including 'Display Source' and 'SPD LIM' flags, attributed to a suspected #2 Display Electronic Unit (DEU) failure. They declared an emergency and diverted to a VFR airport, where maintenance confirmed the #2 DEU failure and swapped units before releasing the aircraft.

synopsis: Two line mechanics report a B747-400 right wing gear door trailing edge was damaged after making contact with the right wing body gear door lock. Mechanics were checking the adjustments of the landing gear door proximity warning targets.
summary: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician and the reporter damaged the right wing gear door while adjusting a proximity sensor because the body gear door lock was not removed. The oversight occurred due to distraction during aircraft repositioning and time pressure from an upcoming departure.

aircraft: Cessna Aircraft Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A user pilot reported that an airport tenant had erected 70 foot high towers to the east of the approach end of a runway that has been closed for a number of years. He reported that the closed runway 'had been in continuous use by local pilots 'at their discretion' during high wind conditions...' which make the actual open runway unsuitable.
summary: Local pilots using closed Runway 26 at GVT during high winds narrowly missed an uncharted 70-foot tower and wire antenna array. The reporter states the hazard is not listed on charts or NOTAMs despite being higher than other charted items.

synopsis: A C182 Instructor reported a light jet flew below them at approximately 800 FT AGL in the vicinity of PMP airport, apparently enroute to another airport.
summary: A Cessna crew on a visual approach to PMP experienced a near miss with a light jet 100 feet below and 300 feet behind at 900 feet MSL. The jet likely departed FXE and switched frequencies without monitoring PMP CTAF, leaving no time for evasive action.

synopsis: BE-200 pilot shut down his malfunctioning left engine and declared an emergency while descending for landing.
summary: During the terminal phase at 2,000 feet, the pilot observed left engine yaw, muffled sounds, and red sparks from the inboard exhaust. The pilot declared an emergency, executed a precautionary shutdown of the left engine, and completed a single-engine landing without further issues.

synopsis: P180 Captain overshot clearance limit in climb when the primary horizontal stabilizer trim failed.
summary: During initial climb, the pilot encountered primary pitch trim failure near 1,600 FT MSL. Switching to secondary trim caused a 200 FT altitude overshoot, but the aircraft completed a normal descent and landing without further incident.

aircraft: Gulfstream Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: First Officer of a corporate jet reported they were vectored directly over traffic that was 400 FT below them, resulting in an RA.
summary: The DAL crew received a premature ATC turn clearance while at 4,000 feet, placing them directly above a descending aircraft and triggering a TCAS climb resolution advisory. The pilot executed the climb to 4,500 feet to resolve the conflict, attributing the event to the controller issuing a turn when vertical separation was insufficient.

synopsis: A C210 pilot reported confusion as to whether he was operating under IFR or VFR flight rules in the weather.
summary: The pilot requested IFR clearance and 4,000 feet after takeoff but was instructed to remain VFR. The pilot reported that staying VFR was impossible at that flight phase, despite receiving a squawk code and direct routing to JUREX.

synopsis: A flight crew, new to their C560XLS+, failed to comply with the required track, altitudes, and speeds while flying the RUUDY RNAV SID from TEB.
summary: Pilots of a new XLS+ departing TEB on the RUUDY RNAV SID experienced an FMS waypoint skip that caused them to exceed 250 KT and miss the 2,000 FT TASCA limit by 200 FT. The crew attributed the deviation to unfamiliarity with the new avionics and attempted to re-initialize the FMS instead of flying a heading.

aircraft: M-20 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Tower Controller described a non-compliance event involving the LUAW procedures noting the new requirements are less than efficient and changes should be considered.
summary: An air traffic controller at Local Control 1 issued a Line Up and Wait clearance to a Mooney before adequate runway spacing was attained for an inbound experimental aircraft. The controller failed to issue traffic information to both aircraft, violating national procedure, though the reporter deemed the safety impact limited.

synopsis: ZOB Controller voiced concern regarding the facility phraseology used to inform military aircraft of MOA entry instructions. The reporter noted that the phraseology is confusing for the pilots and indicates an altitude assignment, which is not the case.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported that Aircraft X climbed 1,000–2,000 feet above its block altitude while entering the Steelhead MOA after receiving a clearance to maintain a higher altitude only while inside the MOA. The controller attributed the deviation to confusing phraseology and recommended clarifying instructions to specify altitudes to maintain until entering the Special Use Airspace.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a conflict event between two successive IFR departure aircraft during reduced visibility when the first aircraft failed to turn as cleared. A supervisory report on the event provided an additional perspective.
summary: During IFR conditions, a Caravan deviated from its assigned 030 heading toward an MD80's departure path on Runway XXL, causing a Conflict Alert. The Local Controller, supervising OJT, resolved the situation by instructing the MD80 to turn left to heading 300 and the Caravan to turn right to heading 050, resulting in diverging courses without a TCAS RA.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a loss of separation event when assigning an altitude in conflict with another aircraft, the reports indicating the controller was thinking one altitude but in fact assigned another, perhaps a Mode C indication.
summary: An air traffic controller inadvertently cleared four F16s to FL270 instead of the intended FL280 due to a verbal error while managing non-functioning Mode C transponders. The controller misheard the pilots' report of FL270 as FL280, resulting in a handoff to the next sector at the incorrect altitude.

synopsis: TRACON Controller providing OJT described a probable loss of separation event when the trainee was late in correcting a head on situation, the reporter indicating the student lacks the ability to certify but continues in the training program because of management pressure.
summary: An ATC trainee cleared a King Air for a visual approach while it was on a head-on course with a Texan, creating a 5-mile, 400-knot closure. The supervising controller intervened to hold the King Air at 3,000 feet, preventing a loss of separation caused by the trainee's poor sequencing and scanning.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a conflict event when failing to note the release issued was from other that the expected runway resulting in an opposite direction operation, the reporter failing to note the runway change from a previous session.
summary: A Radar Approach Controller released a FA20 for departure without confirming the runway, assuming Runway 14 while the aircraft actually departed Runway 23. This caused a 500-foot, one-mile separation with a BE58, prompting immediate vectoring to avoid conflict.

synopsis: TRACON Controller voiced concern regarding the 'Maintain Visual Separation' phraseology and the read back requirements from flight crews, indicating flight crews responses often do not comply with the latest FAA requirements.
summary: An air traffic controller issued visual separation instructions to an Aero Commander and a CRJ7 during vectoring, but the Aero Commander provided ambiguous readbacks instead of confirming the instruction. The controller questioned whether "Roger" or "we won't hit him" constitutes valid acceptance of visual separation and requested clarification on required pilot readback procedures.

aircraft: Lockheed Corp Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: F-35 in emergency status descended slower than the enroute Controller anticipated, resulting in an airspace violation.
summary: An air traffic controller managed an F-35 test flight declaring an emergency during climb-out, issuing a clearance to 12,000 feet that risked a conflict with R-ZA. The aircraft landed safely, but the controller noted that short staffing prevented a D-side coordinator from assisting with the complex descent coordination.

synopsis: HCF Controller reported situation where aircraft target disappears unless equipment is in mosaic mode.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller experienced a radar data loss for Aircraft X during the approach to Runway 4L, requiring a switch to the Mosaic display to maintain contact. The incident, attributed to a Mode S equipment issue, caused operational chaos but was resolved through the controller's expertise, with all traffic handled safely.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: ZFW Controller reported military departures routinely climb VFR opposite direction to DFW arrivals creating conflict.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a TCAS alert on an MD80 inbound to DFW while crossing ISABL at 11,000 feet due to a head-on conflict with four F16s en route to Brownwood MOA. The controller attributed the incident to military aircraft departing VFR directly toward terminal arrivals and suggested procedural changes to prevent future conflicts.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ZNY Controller issues FL390 to aircraft believing he had issued FL400, resulting in airspace deviation.
summary: A non-radar controller in ZNY North Atlantic Airspace issued a conflicting CPDLC clearance to Air Carrier X, instructing it to maintain FL390 then climb to FL390. The pilot's uncertainty revealed the error, which the controller attributed to careless mistakes made while meeting time constraints.

synopsis: An A319's pushback was stopped immediately after it started because an Agent put the jetway up to the aircraft without warning to board another passenger. An alert Flight Attendant luckily disarmed the door.
summary: During pushback, ground agents moved the jetway toward the aircraft with a passenger on board without notifying the flight deck, causing the forward door to open and slides to disarm. The tug driver stopped the pushback upon noticing the jetway, preventing damage to the aircraft and jetway and avoiding potential injuries.

synopsis: A fatigued crew descending into RJAA was issued a runway change and the Captain, while getting the approach chart, engaged the autopilot, but not autothrottles, so the aircraft decelerated to 10 KTS below clean maneuver speed before recovery was initiated.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced an airspeed decay to near stall speed while leveling at 9,000 feet after a runway change, caused by failing to re-engage autothrottles. The crew recovered with a 100-foot altitude loss, attributing the error to fatigue, smooth flight conditions, and the distraction of the runway change.

synopsis: An A319 ECAM alerted L/G SHOCK ABSORBER, L/G DOORS NOT CLOSED, and L/G NOT UPLOCKED so the crew complied with the ECAM and returned to the departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced landing gear faults and communication failures after takeoff, forcing reliance on ACARS. They returned to the departure airport, declined a diversion request, and completed a normal ILS approach and landing.

synopsis: A B747-400 flight crew which departed only hours before the FMS database switchover time arrived at their destination to find the STAR assigned by ATC was not in their FMS database and their assigned ILS was marginally different in course details and the Missed Approach Procedure.
summary: Pilots reported that the FMC database lacked the cleared BULS1P STAR and contained outdated ILS Runway 33R data, including incorrect frequency and fixes. After receiving a direct clearance to PULUN, the crew completed an uneventful approach and landing despite the FMC discrepancies.

synopsis: An A320 ECAM alerted AUTO BRAKE FAULT BRAKES RELEASE so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The crew received an Auto Brake Fault ECAM message after takeoff, declared an emergency, and burned fuel to landing weight before landing. They coordinated with Dispatch and Maintenance via phone patch to manage the brake system failure.

synopsis: A B737 crew requested FL390 as the final altitude but became distracted and failed to set the MCP or FMC which resulted in climb to FL399.
summary: During climb, the flight crew was distracted by a cabin call and failed to verify the MCP altitude setting after being cleared to FL390, causing the aircraft to climb to FL400. ATC instructed a descent to the assigned FL390, which the crew executed without conflict, attributing the error to distraction and lack of strict SOP compliance.

synopsis: After a Q400 #1 engine oil reached 124C the QRH directed an engine shutdown. An emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The pilot flying and Captain managed a high oil temperature on engine #1 during climb, leading to an emergency shutdown and return to the departure airport. They executed a single-engine approach and landed safely on runway 15R after completing relevant checklists and declaring an emergency.

synopsis: An EMB145 FMS dumped the flight plan so the crew reentered the data from the PDC but entered an intersection which was not in the flight plan for the destination arrival.
summary: The crew reported that the FMS dumped the flight plan twice after takeoff, causing a missing en route intersection. After informing ATC of the FMS issues and verifying routing, ATC cleared them to fly direct to the intersection, prompting the crew to emphasize the need for accurate flight plan checks.

synopsis: A CRJ200 nose gear would not retract so the crew completed the GEAR DISAGREE emergency checklist, then declared an emergency and diverted to a nearby international airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a nose gear retraction failure shortly after departure, with the gear indicating down and locked. They diverted to a nearby international airport and landed safely after replacing the nose gear days prior to the flight.

synopsis: An EMB-145 EICAS alerted PACK 1 FAIL, and as the cabin altitude began rising the crew declared an emergency, descended to 10,000 FT, completed the QRH and diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: During cruise at FL250, a PACK 1 failure caused a pressurization loss, prompting the flight crew to execute an emergency descent to 10,000 feet and divert. The aircraft landed safely with fire services monitoring for hot spots due to a potential overweight landing.

synopsis: A B747F Flight Engineer reported that on two consecutive nights the same aircraft's #3 Engine EGT gauge indicated an abnormal start even with a replaced EGT harness, so the flight was canceled and he was later told the fan blades were worn out of limits.
summary: The pilot reported that after a #3 engine EGT malfunction on pushback, maintenance installed a cracked, unauthorized spare harness and cleared the aircraft despite fan blade wear. The pilot believes this intentional act by mechanics, who failed to order proper parts, created a catastrophic risk had the engine failed during a maximum weight takeoff.

synopsis: A B737 passed in the top of a thunderstorm where moderate turbulence injured two flight attendants and turned over the beverage cart so an emergency was declared and the flight diverted to a nearby foreign airport for medical attention.
summary: While diverting at FL340 in foreign airspace, the crew encountered moderate turbulence after passing through cloud tops, causing two flight attendants working with a cart to strike the ceiling and sustain injuries. The captain declared a medical emergency, diverted to a nearby airport, and landed safely, attributing the incident to ineffective HUD guidance for avoiding buildups.

synopsis: After departing RKSI on the SEL1C SID north, both the aircraft's GPS units indicated failure but returned to normal shortly thereafter. Days later the crew was informed North Korea was jamming GPS signals but no crew alert was issued.
summary: The flight crew experienced a temporary dual GNS failure while climbing through 3,500 feet on the SEL1C departure from RKSI, suspecting North Korean GPS jamming. The crew did not inform ATC, but the incident highlighted that a relevant FIR Boundary NOTAM regarding this threat was missing from their flight paperwork.

synopsis: A CRJ Captain struck the right winglet on a baggage cart at LAX after the First Officer and Marshaller both signaled to continue.
summary: The Captain and First Officer of an aircraft taxiing to a gate at LAX struck a baggage cart with the right winglet. The collision occurred due to misjudged clearance, visual distortions, and reliance on the Marshaller's signals despite the carts being in the safety zone.

synopsis: A pilot reported that during a minimum rest period after a 13+44 hour duty day, the Crew Scheduling Desk called to notify him about extending his rest which interrupted and prevented further rest so he called in fatigued.
summary: A fatigued pilot reported that Crew Desk interrupted their minimum rest layover by calling two hours early to notify of a departure delay. The pilot stated this unnecessary wake-up prevented further sleep, directly causing fatigue and highlighting a need for better Crew Desk guidance on notifying crews during minimum rest periods.

synopsis: An air carrier flight crew rejected there takeoff at 90-95 KTS when an EICAS CARGO DOOR warning illuminated.
summary: The flight crew aborted takeoff at 95 KTS due to an AFT CARGO DOOR EICAS warning, which maintenance later attributed to a deferred sensor. After a Chief Pilot inquiry regarding crew stress, the aircraft departed less than two hours later.

synopsis: Distracted by unanticipated holding and suffering from duty time related fatigue the flight crew of a very long range B777 failed to reset their FMS/ILS for their reassigned runway and flew through its extended centerline at ORD. An alert from ATC and a TCAS RA with respect to an aircraft on final to an adjacent parallel runway prevented more serious repercussions.
summary: A fatigued flight crew cleared for a visual approach to Runway 28 at ORD failed to notice the active ILS 27L remained selected. This oversight, attributed to fatigue, resulted in a TCAS RA with an aircraft on final to 27L before the crew manually corrected to land safely on Runway 28.

synopsis: A B777's weather radar antenna failed which caused the loss of both weather radars while flying to South America but the crew was able navigate around weather with some language difficulties.
summary: The crew lost both weather radars entering Georgetown airspace and failed to restore them via circuit breaker resets. Despite communication difficulties across four control areas, they avoided adverse weather and separation issues by following a dispatch-suggested route.

synopsis: An A321 Captain reported a strong dirty socks smell throughout the entire aircraft which did not dissipate after turning the engine bleeds and packs OFF, so the aircraft was deplaned and the flight canceled.
summary: During engine start, a strong odor resembling dirty socks permeated the aircraft, prompting complaints from flight attendants and passengers. The pilot shut down the engines and deplaned passengers, suspecting the smell originated from burning oil in the APU or engines.

synopsis: CRJ200 Captain describes the events leading up to a fatigue call to Crew Scheduling.
summary: A pilot on ready reserve reported fatigue after an unscheduled overnight duty disrupted their sleep cycle, despite the assignment being legal. Although the schedule was modified to remove subsequent legs, the pilot felt too tired to continue after the first flight and voluntarily called in fatigued to prevent unsafe operations.

synopsis: When dispatched with a deferred open right engine anti-ice valve the flight crew of an EMB-145 suffered an ITT over temperature prior to 80 KIAS on the takeoff roll. They rejected the takeoff, returned to the gate for maintenance and suffered a recurrence of the event after maintenance had discovered nothing in the aircraft's maintenance system recordings.
summary: The flight crew rejected two takeoffs due to an E2 overtemperature and ATTCS no margin warning on the second engine. Maintenance attributed the initial fault to a deferred anti-ice valve at a high-altitude airport, though the second abort occurred despite normal taxi readings.

synopsis: A CE560 alerted ADC #1 Comparator Monitor on takeoff because of an insect impact into the pitot tube. Maintenance Control requested the crew not document it because it was most likely a nuisance alert.
summary: During a ferry flight takeoff, pilots received an ADC #1 Comparison Monitor Alert caused by a bug strike in the left pitot tube. Despite Maintenance Control pressure to fly again, the crew wrote up the fault, preventing an illegal departure the next day when the backup aircraft was grounded.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain elected to declare a fuel emergency and divert to an alternate when weather deteriorated at his original destination.
summary: The pilot diverted to an alternate airport due to deteriorating weather and declared a minimum fuel emergency because the alternate was not on the flight release and fuel estimates were near the comfort level. The approach and landing were uneventful.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reports deviating around a thunderstorm on a North Atlantic Track using Captain's emergency authority when ATC cannot provide a clearance to do so.
summary: The Relief Pilot on a Pegasus aircraft over the North Atlantic exercised emergency authority to deviate and descend 300 feet after ATC denied a weather avoidance request. The crew encountered severe thunderstorms on their cleared track between SOORY and 44N50W despite receiving SIGMETs via HF radio.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reports requesting deviation for thunderstorms via CPDLC from RJJJ and begins the deviation just prior to receiving clearance to do so. After initially deviating left it becomes necessary to deviate right and another request is made. Again the deviation is commenced prior to receiving clearance and this time the request is denied.
summary: The crew deviated left and then right of course to avoid storms near ADNAP after RJJJ delayed CPDLC clearances. The pilot attributed the safety risk to radar limitations, communication delays, and the inability to reject the controller's "unable" message for the right offset.

synopsis: B757 flight crew experiences smoke in the cockpit one hour into flight and diverts to the nearest suitable airport. QRH procedures eliminate the smoke prior to landing.
summary: The flight crew experienced acrid odors and visible smoke originating from the instrument panel, likely linked to a recently replaced weather radar unit. They declared an emergency, diverted, and landed overweight after the smoke dissipated upon turning off the air conditioning packs.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: CL65 Captain experiences a Flaps Fail CAS message during climb out and continues to destination. An emergency is declared and a no flap landing ensues. The logbook indicated that the aircraft had experienced the same anomaly the day prior.
summary: The pilot reported a Flap Fail CAS message during climbout, requiring a flapless landing due to an improperly repaired failure from the previous day. The incident occurred after a 14-hour duty day, compensatory rest, and a flight extension beyond the scheduled release time.

synopsis: EMB170 Captain arriving ORD from the south describes a TCAS RA to descend generated by a skydiving aircraft at 14,000 FT, just as the skydivers exit the aircraft. ATC took responsibility for the close call, citing a new Controller on the position.
summary: During approach to Chicago ORD at 14,000 feet, the crew received a TCAS RA to descend due to a conflicting aircraft at the same altitude. The controller admitted fault for the conflict, which involved a parachutist bailout, and the crew safely descended to 10,000 feet with no injuries.

synopsis: EMB145 Captain receives a BAGG SMOKE warning shortly after takeoff. ATC is advised and the QRH is consulted resulting in the halon bottle being discharged into the cargo compartment. Flight returns to departure airport where the warning is found to be false.
summary: The crew received a 'BAGG SMOKE' warning at 800 FT MSL shortly after takeoff, discharged the cargo halon bottle, and returned to the departure airport. Fire crews verified no fire upon landing, allowing the aircraft to taxi to the gate for baggage transfer to a replacement aircraft.

synopsis: A medical helicopter pilot reported aborting a flight when he got a transmission chip light.
summary: The pilot encountered light turbulence during a patient transport flight, triggering a Master Caution and transmission chip caution light. The flight was aborted and returned to base with no further incidents.

synopsis: MD83 First Officer describes maintenance actions and delays that occur during preflight and pushback with the FAA observing. After pushback the flap lever becomes jammed and the aircraft returns to the gate and the flight delayed while another is sought. The times for the pushback and return to the gate were removed from the computer by the Dispatcher, much to the dismay of the reporter.
summary: The pilot reported excessive oil under engine #1 and a stuck slat handle during preflight, forcing a return to the gate and grounding the aircraft. The dispatcher subsequently deleted the flight's push and return times from the computer, erasing the official record of the air interrupt and crew presence.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports inability to extend trailing edge flaps during approach. A go around is initiated, an emergency is declared, and the QRH is consulted resulting in a no flap landing.
summary: The crew encountered flap extension failure and asymmetry during approach, prompting a missed approach and emergency declaration. After following QRH procedures, they executed a safe no-flap landing with ARFF standby.

synopsis: A B767 flight crew had a low airspeed condition during initial climb when VNAV is selected shortly after the autopilot is engaged. The autopilot engagement had caused the aircraft to pitch up to maintain V2 and VNAV had caused a power reduction at the same time. Autopilot was overridden to regain airspeed.
summary: During a 767/757 RNAV departure from EDDF, engaging the autopilot and VNAV near climb power selection caused an automatic nose-up pitch and airspeed bleed to approximately 150 KTS. The First Officer immediately overrode the autopilot to recover airspeed, preventing a stall while maintaining control throughout the rest of the flight.

synopsis: B737 Captain arrives at the aircraft to find a Mechanic working on the right service door handle which is reported to be loose. The Mechanic believes the problem is internal and cannot be quickly corrected. A supervisor believes it will be OK and is willing to sign the logbook, but the Captain does not think so and refuses the aircraft.
summary: A pilot refused an aircraft after a mechanic identified an unsafe right service door and refused to sign it off, despite supervisor pressure. The Captain subsequently grounded the aircraft, but the pilot was denied the opportunity to log a formal refusal for follow-on crews.

synopsis: DO228 flight crew reported aircraft damage at the gate resulting from the power cart not being disconnected before it was driven away from the aircraft.
summary: During the after-start flow, the aircraft jerked twice because the power cart drove away while the power line remained attached. The ramper realized the error, inspected the damage, and instructed the crew to shut down the engines before Maintenance was notified.

synopsis: A CL604 reported a TEB Runway 19 false glideslope at 2,000 FT prior to TUGGZ which resulted in an abrupt 400 FT altitude gain, most likely the result of departing aircraft taxiing to TEB Runway 24.
summary: During an ILS 19 approach at KTEB, the autopilot captured a false glide slope, causing an abrupt climb of 300–400 feet above 2,000 feet. The pilot attributed the erratic signal to taxiing aircraft interfering with the unguarded critical area and manually disengaged the autopilot to correct the altitude excursion.

synopsis: Mechanic was informed he failed to collar the Left Engine Start Circuit Breakers (C/B) he had previously pulled while prepping an EMB-145 aircraft for a Boroscope Inspection.
summary: A mechanic preparing a left engine for borescope inspection pulled the Engine Start Circuit Breakers but failed to install safety collars. The omission occurred because the mechanic became distracted by other maintenance tasks and did not return to the cockpit to secure the breakers as required by the Aircraft Maintenance Manual.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic was informed he had loaded an MD-11 NAV DATA update into a B757-200 aircraft. He had used a new type 409 Data Bus Loader and checked the current data date, but failed to notice the fleet type difference.
summary: A mechanic installed an incorrect MD-11 navigation database into a B-757 FMS while using a new Type 409 Data Bus Loader. The error occurred because the mechanic verified only the data date and missed the fleet type mismatch due to the loader's different formatting.

synopsis: The pilot of a 'manned mission' of the first QF-16 UAV was unable to pitch over from a maximum performance takeoff in a timely fashion to avoid exceeding his cleared altitude of 15,000 FT MSL by nearly 1,000 FT.
summary: The QF-16 pilot exceeded the cleared 15,000 FT altitude during a Functional Check Flight due to a misunderstanding of the unrestricted climb clearance and high climb performance. The pilot attributed the deviation to communication issues and emphasized the need to verify clearances precisely when managing multiple tasks.

synopsis: A B777 flight crew was advised of a low altitude alert by ATC on approach, causing some confusion in the cockpit.
summary: Pilots reported that ATC vectors kept them high until 7 miles out, followed by conflicting low altitude alerts during a visual approach descent. The crew continued the approach despite confusion over ATC instructions, resulting in an uneventful landing with no terrain or EGPWS issues.

synopsis: Student landed amphibious aircraft with gear extended on water, resulting in the aircraft flipping.
summary: A student pilot failed to retract the landing gear on amphibious floats while landing on water. The aircraft flipped upon contacting the water surface.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Instructor pilot in light aircraft described an NMAC at FFZ when he followed the wrong aircraft to the airport.
summary: A flight instructor and student in a training aircraft lost visual contact with the correct lead aircraft while sequencing for Runway 22R at Falcon Field. The instructor mistakenly followed a different airplane, resulting in a near mid-air collision that was avoided by an immediate left turn.

synopsis: A PC12 Captain reported losing all EFIS data for several minutes after a passenger accidentally turned off power to the system.
summary: A passenger entered the cockpit of a Pilatus aircraft and struck the overhead electrical panel, disabling all electrical power, EFIS, autopilot, and engine instruments. The pilot subsequently flew raw data NORDO using only a battery-powered standby attitude gyro while systems rebooted.

synopsis: BE36 pilot reported descending below clearance limit toward terrain on approach to MTN.
summary: The pilot descended below the cleared 2,500 feet MSL to 2,200 feet MSL while en route to MTN due to distraction by GPS distance and mist. Potomac Approach alerted the pilot to the altitude deviation, which was corrected safely despite the risk of controlled flight into terrain in poor visibility.

synopsis: A PA-32R pilot reported misreading the chart and descending to 200 FT AGL in the pattern at T31.
summary: The pilot misread the chart for Traffic Pattern Altitude while approaching Runway 17 at T31, descending to 1,000 MSL instead of the required 1,600 MSL. This error placed the aircraft only 200 feet above ground and surrounding homes, prompting the pilot to commit to a more thorough pre-brief to prevent recurrence.

synopsis: An SR-22TN pilot reported he diverted because of a rough running engine. No anomalies were found by the mechanic.
summary: A pilot in cruise flight experienced a sudden engine thump, vibration, and power decrease with normal MFD indications, prompting a precautionary landing at a nearby airport. The pilot executed a downwind landing on the opposite runway; a mechanic found no anomalies, and the aircraft will be ferried for further inspection.

synopsis: A C182 pilot struck a rubber cone with the prop while taxiing from parking.
summary: The pilot and a sport pilot passenger struck an orange cone placed by FBO personnel while taxiing, causing the cone to fly across the ramp. The crew attributed the incident to an inward-focused preflight that missed the hazard and subsequently drove to their destination for maintenance inspection.

synopsis: A C-206 carrying skydivers had engine trouble during climbout. The skydivers left the aircraft. The pilot landed at the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The pilot experienced engine sputtering one minute after takeoff during a skydiving operation. After unsuccessful troubleshooting of fuel and ignition systems, the pilot executed an emergency landing at the nearest field while skydivers exited safely.

synopsis: C182 pilot reports attempting to return VFR to home field located beneath the Class C ring of a nearby airport with a weather report of 800 scattered and 12,000 broken. Upon nearing destination it appears that the broken layer is actually 1,200 FT requiring an IFR clearance to reach the destination airport.
summary: A VFR pilot returning to a small private field under a Class C shelf encountered lower-than-reported ceilings and turned west to climb above the clouds. The pilot subsequently obtained a pop-up clearance into Class C airspace, executed a low approach, and landed safely after realizing the reported weather was inaccurate.

synopsis: A B767-300 aircraft required an air turnback after the left Main Landing Gear (MLG) door light remained on after takeoff. All three landing gear had been replaced
summary: A B767-300 pilot reported a left main gear failure after takeoff caused by a missing sequence valve hardware installed during a maintenance inspection six days prior. The crew extended the gear using the alternate system and landed safely, with corrective action involving hardware replacement per the Aircraft Maintenance Manual.

synopsis: The left nose tire assembly previously replaced on a B767 aircraft was missing an axle nut washer.
summary: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician replaced a damaged nose tire on a B767 during a heavy workload period and likely omitted the wheel spacer due to staffing shortages and fatigue. The technician torqued the nut and signed off the logbook, believing these factors caused the missing spacer.

synopsis: ZME Controller reported a restricted area within his sector was hot for 90 minutes without his knowledge. Reporter suggests an automation solution.
summary: An air traffic controller failed to notice that Restricted Area R-ABCD was active from the surface to FL300 for over an hour due to missing scope depiction and an ineffective ESIS display. The controller discovered the error only after a colleague's inquiry, highlighting a critical safety gap in the current notification system for restricted airspace status.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ELP TRACON issued an air carrier the MOLLY 2 STAR which caused confusion for the crew and a conflict for ATC but was in accordance with a ZAB letter of agreement.
summary: The crew accepted a late MOLLY 2 RNAV arrival clearance at 13,000 feet while approaching El Paso, but Approach Control vectored them to heading 110 and 6,000 feet after observing an initial turn northeast. The Ground Controller attributed the vector to the aircraft's direction, while the pilot cited poor Center-Approach coordination and heavy cockpit load from the late clearance as the cause.

synopsis: B737-500 Captain reported receiving a 'Terrain Alert' from ABQ Tower on approach to Runway 26. With no EGPWS warnings the flight continued to a normal landing.
summary: The flight crew, on a visual approach to Runway 26 in ABQ, received a "Terrain Alert" from Tower while on left base. Despite having no cockpit EGPWS or terrain alerts, the crew continued a stabilized approach and landed safely.

synopsis: A B767-300 flight crew departing had a conflict with a foreign air carrier A320 departing a parallel runway and making an unauthorized right hand turn. ATC advised and TCAS issued a 'Descend' RA. The reporter later learned the A320 flight crew was having communications problems with ATC prior to departure seemingly the result of a language barrier.
summary: The reporting crew experienced a near-miss during climb after a foreign Airbus A320 crew failed to comply with ATC clearances due to language barriers. The conflict triggered a TCAS descent resolution advisory, requiring the reporting aircraft to stop climbing and maneuver to avoid the intruder passing overhead.

synopsis: The First Officer aboard a CRJ addressed his concerns about First Class meals being boarded for an inaugural route flight and discovering that the weight and balance program for the aircraft was not programmed to accept the carriage of the heavier meals. The problem was exacerbated by the Captain's recent phone call from a Chief Pilot strongly encouraging 'timely' release and taxi from the gate for takeoff.
summary: During pre-departure for a new destination, the crew faced ACARS weight and balance errors regarding First Class meals on a Boeing 700. Under time pressure from the Chief Pilot, the Captain continued taxiing while the crew estimated meal weights instead of returning to the gate to resolve the discrepancy.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reported on descent they received a left engine oil pressure warning, likely as a result of a flameout. A restart attempt was unsuccessful and the flight landed after declaring an emergency.
summary: During descent through 11,000 feet, the crew experienced a left engine oil pressure warning and spool-down. After a failed relight attempt, they declared an emergency, completed single-engine procedures, and landed safely without further incident.

synopsis: B777 flight crew discovers airborne that they have departed with conflicting MEL's concerning Main Deck shut off valves. After consulting with Maintenance the flight continues to destination.
summary: The flight crew discovered conflicting Minimum Equipment List (MEL) items for air conditioning valves during cruise, rendering the aircraft non-compliant. Maintenance Control confirmed the conflict, causing a blocked-out departure due to improper airworthiness certification by maintenance personnel.

synopsis: A B747 First Officer reported the aircraft was refused because the number 3 engine sounded strange and the EGT erratic even after Maintenance replaced the EGT harness and inspected the engine.
summary: Pilots and mechanics involved a flight with an aircraft having erratic EGT indications on engine 3 due to broken harnesses. The crew rejected the flight after discovering a field-repaired, cracked harness and an abnormal engine sound, citing maintenance deception and pressure to fly an unsafe aircraft.

synopsis: MD-82 First Officer reported a 5 KT overspeed during an emergency descent for loss of pressurization.
summary: During an emergency descent for loss of pressurization, the aircraft exceeded maximum speed by approximately 5 KTS. A mechanic inspected the aircraft, noted no damage, and signed off the logbook entry.

synopsis: A B757 Flight Attendant reported that a non English speaking passenger was allowed to sit in an emergency exit row when he did not understand the questions regarding emergency exit operations.
summary: A flight attendant attempted to brief an exit row passenger who could not understand English instructions despite hand signals and Purser assistance. The reporter argues that passengers must speak English to safely perform emergency duties, disagreeing with current policies allowing non-English speakers in exit rows.

synopsis: A Technician reports he found an electrical harness that had become water saturated at a previous wire repair on an EMB-145 aircraft. The water saturation appeared to be one of the causes of a repeat discrepancy for a Parking Brake light that remained 'On' after the Parking Brakes were released.
summary: A mechanic found moisture in an EMB-145's brake harness during routine maintenance and recommended replacement, but the aircraft was returned to service after the harness was merely dried and the connector replaced. The reporter attributed this unsafe decision to pressure to return the aircraft quickly rather than ensuring full airworthiness.

synopsis: E190 First Officer reported losing #2 hydraulic system. After running the procedures a normal landing was executed.
summary: During climb, the crew received a HYD 2 EDP FAIL EICAS that did not reset, followed by HYD 2 LO PRESS and brake fault messages. They executed the QRH Hydraulic System 2 Loss procedure, landed uneventfully, and were towed to the gate.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot was on short final to CTAF X35 Runway 28 reported a near miss with an aircraft not making the FAA recommended CTAF position reports as it departed.
summary: The pilot of a C182 on short final for Runway 28 at X35 executed an emergency go-around after a Citabria taxied onto the runway and began takeoff without slowing or responding to radio calls. The incident, which reduced separation to 6–10 seconds, was attributed to the Citabria pilot failing to look before taxiing and likely having a non-functional radio.

synopsis: A B757 galley coffee maker exploded injuring a Flight Attendant after it spewed hot coffee grounds on her face, eyes, mouth, neck and chest.
summary: A Flight Attendant suffered burns when a coffee machine exploded in the galley during cruise. The crew stabilized the injury with medical guidance, declared an emergency, and landed at the destination where paramedics transported the injured crew member to a hospital.

synopsis: After extending the landing gear, two BE36 gear down lights did not function, so the pilot declared an emergency, had a nearby Tower verify the gear down, landed and after checking the gear proceeded to his destination airport.
summary: The pilot experienced two inoperative gear lights during the landing phase at a closed airport. After verifying gear extension via a low pass and manual extension, the pilot declared an emergency, landed for inspection, and subsequently departed to land safely at the destination.

synopsis: A King Air pilot reported a near miss at FL210 when ATC issued a climb clearance to FL230 then abruptly canceled the climb and ordered a descent after he was above FL210, but did not issue any traffic alerts.
summary: A King Air 200 pilot en route reported a near mid-air collision caused by conflicting ATC instructions to descend while climbing, compounded by an inoperative TCAS. The pilot executed the descent, resulting in a close pass with another aircraft that was never verbally alerted by the controller.

synopsis: A Mechanic working under supervision of another Mechanic, reports he failed to reinstall a fork bolt that secures the fork and strut assembly including the nose wheel pants on a Cessna 150 aircraft.
summary: A pilot and supervising mechanic omitted the nose wheel fork bolt during fairing removal on a Cessna, relying solely on the Service Manual. The aircraft was recalled before takeoff after the pilot consulted the Illustrated Parts Catalog, revealing the bolt's critical structural role and the mechanic's inadequate supervision.

synopsis: A Lead Mechanic working a B737-800 aircraft noticed 1/8 inch radial play at the Accessory Gearbox (AGB) Lower clevis mount on a NexGen CFM-56-7 engine. Although no wear limits could be found, he was told by company Engineering and their Engine Support desk he could defer the wear. The engine was replaced the following night for excessive bushing wear.
summary: A mechanic discovered excessive play in the #1 engine AGB lower clevis mount but found no limits in the AMM. Despite concerns, the mechanic deferred the defect under AMM 72-63-00-200 after Engineering and the Engine desk approved the action without an ERO.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot landing DVO reported a NMAC during final approach as he executed a go around to allow traffic spacing and then discovered this hand held radio transmitter failed but the receiver was OK.
summary: The pilot inbound to DVO Runway 13 observed a faster aircraft on downwind and descended to 700 feet AGL for a 360-degree turn to avoid conflict. The pilot later discovered their handheld radio was receiving but not transmitting, though the conflict was successfully avoided.

synopsis: Limited experienced Controller described a complex traffic event that eventually resulted in a go around, the reporter indicated the need for training on unusual traffic situations.
summary: An inexperienced air traffic controller managed a B737 requesting a 360 and a second B737 on a closed traffic pattern behind an A319. The second B737 failed to turn base, prompting a route change to Runway 19L without prior coordination with Final Sector, though the controller reported no loss of separation or vector below MVA.

synopsis: An A320 Captain's airspeed decreased toward V1s during descent, so he disconnected the autopilot and autothrottles to manually increase airspeed when the First Officer discovered the aircraft was overspeeding. They determined the Captain's airspeed was in error and the air data computer was at fault.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced conflicting airspeed indications during descent, causing the Captain to manually override autothrottles and autopilot. This confusion led to an overspeed, a missed 10,000-foot crossing restriction, and a delayed approach to runway 27L after switching to Air Data 3.

synopsis: An air carrier crew began an approach to their destination as thunderstorms were approaching and so after holding, declared minimum fuel and diverted to a nearby airport where an emergency was declared for low fuel.
summary: The relief pilot reported that the crew diverted due to thunderstorms and low fuel, declaring a PAN-PAN emergency to bypass ATC delays. After landing with 9,000 lbs of fuel, passengers and crew were held on the ramp for five hours because foreign customs refused deplaning at the divert airport.

synopsis: A B747 Captain discovered a delaminated L3 cockpit window during his preflight which Maintenance reluctantly changed causing a nearly five hour departure delay.
summary: The B747-400 pilot reported a cracked L3 cockpit window and vinyl deformation during preflight, which Maintenance initially misidentified as deferrable delamination before agreeing to replace it. This error, combined with poor communication from the crew desk regarding the 5-hour delay and lack of crew rest, resulted in the crew exceeding 19 hours on duty.

synopsis: An air carrier arriving RKSI reported the loss of GPS signals most probably due to jamming so the ILS was flown to touchdown.
summary: The pilot lost both GPS signals during a 12-mile intercept to final on runway 33R but completed the ILS approach and landing. Signals returned after exiting the runway, and a subsequent report confirmed GPS jamming in the ICN (RKSI) area as the cause.

synopsis: An EMB145's right engine failed on final so the pilots declared an emergency and continued the landing without incident. No abnormal indications of any kind noted.
summary: The pilot reported a Number 2 engine failure during an ILS approach over the final approach fix while in landing configuration. With no abnormal or fire indications, the crew declared an emergency, continued the approach, and landed safely without further incident.

synopsis: An EMB135 Captain reported fatigue and distraction contributed to the crew's failure to raise the flaps until FL 24.5 and about 242 KTS.
summary: The Pilot Not Flying on a multi-leg flight failed to monitor airspeed and flap position during climb due to distraction by ATC clearances and fatigue. Flaps remained extended to 9 until 24,500 feet, reaching 245 knots, before being retracted without structural damage.

synopsis: When reassigned to fly an early morning turn around following a fatiguing five day trip with disruptive sleep cycles the flight crew of an EMB-135 failed to note their PDC clearance cleared them only to 2,000 MSL although their assigned NEWARK SID off Runway 11 required a climb to 3,000 MSL with an intervening at or above altitude of 2,500 MSL. ATC reminded them of their revised altitude restriction when they checked in out of 2,300 for 3,000 and then cleared them to maintain 3,000.
summary: The fatigued Captain and First Officer departed EWR on Runway 11, climbing to 3,000 feet despite a PDC clearance for 2,000 feet due to the Captain missing the altitude change while managing logbook duties. Departure Control identified the deviation, confirmed no traffic conflict, and authorized the climb to 3,000 feet.

synopsis: A wide body aircraft departing FGSL turned right after takeoff and proceeded direct to TJJ as cleared prior to departure. Upon contact with DOULA control they were advised they were in 'prohibited' area.
summary: The flight crew departed FGSL following a clearance to climb to FL400 and turn right direct to TJJ. Doula Control subsequently reported the aircraft was in prohibited airspace, despite the crew adhering to the initial clearance issued by Ground Control.

synopsis: BK-117 pilot inadvertantly entered IMC, declared an emergency, received vectors for an ILS approach and, once established on the approach entered VFR conditions and returned to base. Pilot believes that low experience level with Night Vision Googles may have been a factor.
summary: The pilot entered unforecast IMC at 2,700 MSL while using Night Vision Goggles, likely due to low NVG experience masking cloud bases. After declaring an emergency and climbing to MSA, the crew executed an ILS approach, broke out into VMC, and returned to base safely.

synopsis: A Captain was informed by his First Officer that he saw speed tape along the leading edge of the right horizontal stabilizer during his walk around. The B737-800 aircraft had flown for 16-months without any follow-up inspection to a Temporary Repair (TR) using speed tape.
summary: A pilot reviewing a B737-800 logbook discovered speed tape on the right horizontal stabilizer from a 2011 temporary repair lacking required follow-up inspections. The aircraft had flown for over 16 months without re-inspection, prompting the pilot to insist on a new discrepancy entry and re-inspection of the repair.

synopsis: MD82 Captain during an emergency descent after loss of cabin pressurization, overspeed the aircraft.
summary: The pilot oversped the aircraft by approximately 5 knots during an emergency descent following depressurization. The narrative does not specify the aircraft type, altitude, or the cause of the depressurization.

synopsis: B737 Flight Attendant describes a gate return and the manual disarming of the slide by placing the girt bar in the storage clips. When the door is opened the slide pack falls from its' container but does not inflate.
summary: A flight attendant reported that while disarming the L1 door at the gate, the slide pack partially fell and the girt bar detached. The reporter speculates the girt bar popped from its clips and caught on floor brackets, causing the slide to drop from its container.

synopsis: An AA5 pilot suffered a close encounter with a flight of two A-10s in the pattern at GEZ.
summary: A single-pilot training flight at GEZ encountered two A-10s transiting the traffic pattern at or below 1,000 AGL without CTAF communication. The military aircraft maneuvered to avoid the trainer, but the pilot reported this unsafe practice of overflying civil airfields at pattern altitudes requires correction by military authorities.

synopsis: A helicopter pilot reported a line of four fairly new uncharted towers near 47' 09' 23'N 117 20' 30'W oriented east/west at about 3,150 FT MSL, about 350 FT AGL. All but the western most towers are correctly lighted.
summary: A pilot reported four uncharted towers near N 47°09'23', W 117°20'50' that were approximately 3,150 FT MSL and 350 FT AGL. The westernmost tower had a missing top light, and no reference to the structures was found on the Seattle VFR Sectional or in NOTAMS.

synopsis: A CE550 electrical system malfunctioned without flight station annunciations but after ATC reported weak and failing communicaitons the crew returned to the departure airport where generator and inverter resets restored normal electrical operations.
summary: The pilot reported that during the departure phase, radio communications became unreadable due to suspected electrical issues, prompting a return to the departure airport. The pilot flying restored power by resetting generators and inverters, allowing for a safe landing with no prior warning lights.

synopsis: A departing aircraft reported engine trouble and intent to land on a closed runway occupied by personnel. Tower Controller took action to remove personnel and informed the aircraft to 'proceed as requested.'
summary: An ATC controller cleared a PA28 pilot reporting engine problems to land on closed Runway 10 while personnel were present. The controller used "proceed as requested" instead of standard closed runway phraseology, believing the low-time pilot would not understand the latter.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports descending early during the ILS 35L at DEN in IMC. While troubleshooting a discrepancy between FMC position and raw data LOC, situational awareness is lost. ATC notices the early descent and questions the crew.
summary: Pilots on an ILS 35L approach to Denver lost situational awareness regarding distance after a false lateral deviation distraction, causing the pilot flying to descend early below 10,000 feet. ATC queried the descent, prompting the crew to level off, verify position, and complete a normal landing with no safety compromise.

synopsis: A B757-200 flight crew opted to cross the threshold of 28L at SFO high in order to assure clearance with the tail of a B747 which had been cleared to cross 28L and hold short of Runway 28R.
summary: A B747 landing on 28L flew slightly above the glideslope at 200 feet to clear the tail of another B747 holding short of 28R, which had crossed the 28L hold short line. The landing was normal with no incident, though the pilot recommended prohibiting such holds during 28L approaches.

synopsis: A320 First Officer reported losing green hydraulic system and a fuel boost pump on arrival. They declared an emergency and were towed to the gate.
summary: The crew experienced a green hydraulic system warning followed by a right main fuel tank pump pressure loss during arrival. They declared an emergency, managed the failures, and landed safely, but the aircraft required crash crew attendance and towing to the gate.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain missed the fact Tower frequency had been changed by NOTAM, noted that the item was 59 inches down the page.
summary: The crew at Denver switched to a Tower frequency that was out of service for Runway 8, causing a missed call from Ground while taxiing. The reporter attributed the error to critical NOTAM and ATIS details being buried in information overload and a lack of crew communication regarding the frequency change.

synopsis: An A319 flight crew declared and emergency and continued their arrival to a safe landing when the #2 engine failed, perhaps due to and Inlet Guide Vane failure.
summary: The crew experienced a #2 engine flameout with shuddering at 10,000 MSL on initial approach, prompting an emergency declaration and decision to land without attempting a relight. Ground inspection revealed no obvious damage, though the aircraft self-reported an Inlet Guide Vane failure.

synopsis: B717 Captain reports checking fuel just prior to descent for landing and finding all normal. During descent a fuel imbalance is annunciated with the left tank indicating 3,000 LBS less than the right. Thinking fuel leak an emergency is declared with a diversion to a closer airport. During approach the fuel imbalance disappears and the left tank again indicates the same as the right.
summary: During descent, the flight crew declared an emergency and diverted due to a master caution indicating a fuel imbalance and suspected leak. The issue resolved upon intercepting the final approach course when the left tank indication stabilized, revealing a fuel indication problem rather than an actual leak.

synopsis: An ERJ-190 Captain advised his FMS 'Profile Mode' display failed to properly display a programmed crossing restriction showing them to be on profile when they were, in fact, about 5,000 FT high.
summary: Pilots in cruise at FL370 missed a crossing restriction at RBA by 5,000 feet due to contradictory altitude data on the Honeywell FMS profile view. The controller accepted the deviation, but the crew attributed the error to unreliable equipment programming rather than pilot scan.

synopsis: An EMB-145LR flight crew intercepting the localizer inbound to CLE responded to TCAS Traffic and Resolution advisories with respect to an unknown aircraft departing from BKL.
summary: The crew received a climb Resolution Advisory while descending to 3,000 feet to intercept the 24R localizer due to a Burke Lakefront departure below. The pilot manually climbed to 3,200 feet to clear the conflict, noting ATC's lack of vigilance regarding the separation of arriving and departing traffic.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reports a rejected takeoff when three faint beeps are heard as the Captain is initiating the takeoff. Once clear of the runway the sound is traced to the Captain's cell phone which had been placed in airplane mode but was emitting a low battery warning.
summary: The Captain rejected takeoff at 50 KTS due to an unidentified alarm later suspected to be a low-battery phone warning. After verifying no aircraft abnormalities and allowing brakes to cool from 345 degrees, the flight continued without incident.

synopsis: A B767-200 flight crew oversped their flaps when performing a go-around during which the pilot flying (First Officer) inadvertently mismanaged the autoflight and autothrottle systems. A mix of cockpit instrument configuration in the carrier's fleet was a contributing factor.
summary: The crew executed a missed approach due to lack of landing clearance, but the First Officer inadvertently disconnected auto-throttles instead of engaging go-around mode. This caused an airspeed exceedance into the red band while flaps were extended, requiring manual speed reduction before a safe return and landing.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew approaching TOMAS Intersection at 8,000 FT arriving MROC in IMC receives an EGPWS terrain warning and executes the escape maneuver. A second approach flown in a similar manor produces no warning.
summary: The flight crew received EGPWS terrain warnings while descending through 9,000 and 8,000 feet in IMC during an ILS Runway 07 approach at MROC. They executed escape maneuvers, climbed to 14,000 feet, and later completed an uneventful landing after holding for weather and traffic.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 flight crew failed to properly program the altitude alert and the FMS to properly schedule a crossing restriction from ATC. They descended below the crossing and conflicted with aircraft below. ATC caught the error and a correction was made in a timely fashion.
summary: The pilot and First Officer descended to FL300 instead of the cleared FL330 due to FMS entry errors, complacency, and a jumpseater distraction. Center instructed a climb after the crew noticed the altitude pre-select error and traffic at FL320, prompting an immediate manual climb to FL330.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports he experienced a near fatality by a moving vehicle entering the Breezeway-Alley way from an International Gate, just adjacent to where the aircraft tire jacks were stored.
summary: A ground personnel member reported a near-fatal incident where a moving vehicle entered the breezeway near International Gate XX, adjacent to stored aircraft tire jacks. The reporter attributed the event to LD3 containers blocking the view of incoming traffic at the breezeway entrance.

synopsis: A Line Safety Mechanic reports about a congested and restrictive work environment in their Fire Bottle Shop. He raises concerns about adequate egress to escape from the release of Purple-K Fire Retardant during Servicing and Annual Checks of their 400 LB Fire Bottles.
summary: A Building Maintenance Mechanic servicing fire extinguishing bottles in a small, poorly ventilated shop reported a high risk of accidental Purple-K discharge due to congestion. Management seeks a larger location to ensure personnel safety but faces roadblocks finding available space.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Corporate aircraft's FMS had a stored route through ZAU airspace with an intersection named ARLYN instead of ARLIN which caused ATC to question the aircraft's routing.
summary: Pilots flying a stored flight plan with a misspelled intersection (ARLIN instead of ARLYN) received an incorrect heading from Chicago Center. The 56-degree course deviation occurred because the FMS database contained a typo, which the crew noted could be prevented by a published SID.

synopsis: EMB-120 Captain reported losing Green Hydraulic System. After consulting Dispatch the decision was made to continue to destination.
summary: The flight crew experienced a total Green Hydraulic System failure during cruise, losing gear, flap, and steering control after a prior unconfirmed leak report. They declared an emergency, extended the gear via free fall, and safely landed on a longer runway.

synopsis: B767-300 Captain reported he was dispatched with an incorrect MEL that resulted in an overheating hydraulic pump and resultant fluid leak.
summary: The flight crew and maintenance operated a cargo aircraft with an improperly deferred right engine hydraulic pump under an inapplicable MEL. This error caused severe overheating and fluid leakage, requiring pump replacement and revealing that the deferral did not cover a pump failing to generate pressure.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Single engine Part 135 pilot experiences engine failure shortly after takeoff and lands straight ahead on the 8,600 FT departure runway. Takeoff was initiated with the fuel selector to the right wingtip tank which indicated low but should have contained sufficient fuel, a hard landing results.
summary: The pilot experienced a complete engine failure at 300–400 feet AGL shortly after takeoff, likely due to fuel starvation despite the right tip tank gauge reading low. The pilot attempted to restart the engine and switch tanks but was forced to execute a hard landing on the remaining 1,000 feet of runway.

synopsis: An Instructor pilot noted a helicopter air taxied from the TMB fuel pit Spot 2 to Spot 1 and its down wash caused havoc with a line of parked aircraft as it flew over them.
summary: A helicopter pilot taxied and hovered between parked aircraft at a self-serve fuel area, causing tails to nearly strike the ground and shaking multiple airplanes. The reporter stated this unsafe maneuver should have been replaced by using the main taxiway and requesting clearance via Taxiway Alpha.

synopsis: A Champ 7ECA pilot landed after his engine quit while in the landing pattern and the aircraft had minor propeller damage. Water or icing suspected.
summary: The pilot reported an engine failure while on the right base leg for Runway 31, forcing a landing that resulted in minor damage and a bent propeller. The pilot suspected water ingestion or icing as the possible cause.

synopsis: B757-200 flight crew receives a status message during climb on an ETOPS flight indicating that the left fuel quantity fuel gauge has failed. Maintenance is consulted and the crew is informed they may continue on the over water flight. The crew continues, condition, but believes that some non-normal procedures could not be performed in this and that a fuel leak could not be detected.
summary: During climb to FL360, the crew experienced a blank left fuel quantity indicator and totalizer. Although Maintenance advised continuing ETOPS operations without restrictions, the crew expressed concern that critical QRH checklists could not be properly assessed without fuel quantity data.

synopsis: A319 flight crew experiences an engine 2 oil filter clogged message at FL380. Several minutes later slight vibration is noted and the crew elects to descend to FL310. During the descent N2 vibration increases to 4.5 units and the crew elects to divert to a suitable airport. Nearing the airport the oil quantity and pressure go to zero and the engine is shut down, a single engine landing ensues.
summary: The flight crew encountered an ENG 2 oil filter clog at FL380, leading to reduced thrust and an emergency diversion. At 13,000 feet, oil quantity and pressure dropped to zero, prompting an engine shutdown and a routine single-engine landing.

synopsis: B767-300 flight crew reported difficulty controlling cabin temperature. Maintenance suggested re-setting a circuit breaker that solved the problem.
summary: The flight crew experienced a loss of cabin temperature control during cruise on an aircraft dispatched with known air conditioning issues. They regained control after cycling a circuit breaker to reset the trim air system, as advised by maintenance.

synopsis: B757 Captain discovers that nose wheel steering is not functioning shortly after being cleared to taxi and calls for assistance. A ramp person arrives and apparently moves the steering bypass lever rendering the steering operational and departs without communicating with the Captain. Maintenance is called and three Mechanics arrive and verify the bypass lever is properly positioned then depart without signaling clear.
summary: The pilot reported a steering bypass issue during taxi that was fixed by a ramp worker and three mechanics who failed to provide "aircraft clear" signals or confirm personnel clearance. This non-compliance with safety protocols created a potential risk of serious injury to ground staff near operating engines.

synopsis: A B757 engine oversped at FL360 on an oceanic route so an emergency was declared, the Oceanic Off Track Procedures complied with and the flight diverted to a foreign airport.
summary: A B757 crew en route at FL360 diverted after the right engine surged to 111% N1, causing an uncontrollable overspeed. The Captain shut down the engine, declared an emergency, and landed single-engine at an alternate airport with no injuries.

synopsis: An A321 Captain noted that his experienced but First Officer failed to get landing clearance even after he strongly affirmed that he had when questioned about the clearance on final.
summary: During an ILS 9R approach below 3,000 feet, the Captain questioned landing clearance while the First Officer incorrectly confirmed it. The First Officer's lack of concentration and failure to monitor the tower frequency caused confusion during the flare, leading the Captain to add him to a no-fly list.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Dispatcher reported that he heard an aircraft declaring an emergency for an elevator trim problem but the company radio frequency bleed over was so strong that he had difficulty acknowledging the crew's emergency.
summary: A flight crew declared an emergency due to inoperative main pitch trim while attempting to contact Dispatch. Communication was initially hindered by frequency bleed-over, but the crew eventually confirmed their return to the departure airport without requiring dispatcher assistance.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier Captain reported executing a missed approach on the LAX 25L ILS at 1,800 FT after the glideslope failed and because the glideslope was not captured did not have the missed approach altitude set in the MCP ALT window.
summary: During an ILS approach to LAX Runway 25L in IMC, the crew lost the glideslope signal at 1,800–1,900 feet and executed a go-around. Because the MCP altitude was set to 2,600 feet per SOP, the aircraft climbed above the 2,000-foot missed approach altitude before ATC could assign a new clearance.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier First Officer reported that his Captain, the flying pilot, refused to execute a go around during an unstabilized approach.
summary: During an unstable approach into MIA Runway 9 in thunderstorms, the Captain overrode the First Officer's repeated go-around commands at 400 feet despite high speed and sink rate warnings. The aircraft landed safely, but the incident highlighted a conflict between the Captain's operational authority and the Operations Manual's go-around requirements.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic and Maintenance Controller report about their involvement with releasing an ERJ-175 aircraft and not accomplishing, or deferring, a sealant application procedure for new electrical bonding straps (jumpers) installed at the refueling control panel.
summary: A maintenance controller and mechanic deferred sealant on broken fuel panel bonding jumpers for an EMB-175 based on incorrect AMM interpretation. The reporter later identified this as an improper dispatch after reviewing the manual, noting the error resulted from relying on the controller's assurance without verifying the full procedure.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier departed MUHA Airport on the EPRIM1.TADPO Departure then EYW, but ZMA notified them upon check in that they were in an active military area, to squawk 7700 and given an exit vector.
summary: The crew entered an active military operating area southwest of TADPO after Miami Center claimed their flight plan was filed over MTH instead of EYW, despite receiving a clearance for EPRIM1.TADPO. Miami instructed the crew to squawk 7700 and deviate toward MTH before reclearing them direct to RSW upon exiting the airspace.

synopsis: A BE58 pilot filed IFR on a route he normally flew VFR and on this particular day was vectored around a non NOTAMed military airshow training session which he would not have known about if VFR.
summary: A pilot on an IFR flight east of Nashville received an 80-degree heading change from Approach to avoid military jet practice for an air show. The pilot noted no NOTAMs, TFRs, or MOAs existed for this activity and felt a NOTAM was necessary since they would have otherwise flown VFR.

synopsis: Tower Controller issues go around to ACR aircraft when twin Cessna does not hold short of runway.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a taxi clearance to a C340, which the pilot misinterpreted as an instruction to enter Runway 30L, causing a runway incursion with a B737 at 50 feet. The controller attributed the incident to the pilot's accent and their own failure to provide specific directional instructions or verify understanding.

synopsis: TRACON Controller providing OJT failed to note an incorrect read back that resulted in a below MVA event.
summary: A trainee Air Traffic Controller issued a descent clearance to a BE20, which was misread as 6,000 feet instead of 8,000 feet. The error was detected when the aircraft descended through 7,500 feet in an 8,000-foot MVA, prompting an immediate climb instruction to restore the correct altitude.

synopsis: Air Carrier was instructed to 'follow' traffic that was landing on a parallel runway confusing the flight crew, the reporter noting the clearance was unclear and a 'do not pass' instructions should have been issued if required by ATC.
summary: During descent on vectors for visual 26R, the crew received a conflicting instruction to follow a heavy aircraft landing on 26L, leading to a Climb RA. The crew executed the RA and landed safely while the other aircraft went around, attributing the conflict to the controller's agitated demeanor and ambiguous phrasing.

synopsis: Following a go around for a TE FLAP DISAGREE EICAS, the B757 Captain expressed frustration with the lack of training and flight crew communications to address new and revised Company procedures.
summary: During approach, the crew encountered a TE Flap Disagree EICAS message after selecting flaps 25, prompting a go-around at 900 feet MSL. Following the QRH, they declared an emergency and landed safely using the alternate flap system with flaps 30.

synopsis: An Air Carrier Captain comments about the unsafe CLT airport ground operations by taxiing aircraft, ground crew, ramp operations, and conflicts with aircraft pushed from concourse end gates onto ramp roadways.
summary: Ramp workers and Regional Jet operators at CLT engaged in unsafe taxiing and driving, including a Dash 8 cutting off the reporter. The reporter attributes these risks to a careless local attitude and suggests operational changes to prevent aircraft from intruding on ramp roads.

synopsis: An A320 Captain rejected the takeoff near V1 because his PFD airspeed indicated around 80 KTS while the First Officer's indicated near V1.
summary: The Captain rejected the takeoff on Runway 19R between 80 KTS and V1 due to a faulty airspeed indicator showing decreasing speed. The aircraft stopped safely, cooled brakes on the taxiway, and returned to the gate where passengers deplaned and the flight was cancelled.
