synopsis: While rushing their cockpit preparation due to a short airplane switch, the flight and ground Crews of an E-145 failed to coordinate their pushback communications and the Captain's attempt to bring the pushback to a stop by applying brakes while the tractor was pushing caused a massive failure of the tow bar.
summary: During pushback, the flight crew initiated movement without headsets after misinterpreting a ground handler's signal, causing the aircraft to move unexpectedly. The towbar subsequently failed and wedged against the nose gear, but the crew stopped the aircraft using wheel brakes, and maintenance confirmed no further action was required.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew missed a crossing restriction issued by ATC. First Officer, Pilot Flying, attributed the error to distraction caused by a conversation with the Captain.
summary: The Pilot Flying, while inbound to IAH at FL330, failed to initiate a descent for a HAMMU crossing clearance due to distraction from conversation. This resulted in crossing HAMMU at 10,800 ft and 290 KIAS instead of the cleared 10,000 ft and 280 KIAS.

synopsis: While conducting the first stages of an RNAV SID, the flight crew of a CRJ-200 suffered a short term track deviation when the First Officer (PF) was unable to display RNAV guidance on his PFD and navigation displays. The Captain, whose displays were normal, took over PF duties. They later determined that the First Officer's Nav Source Selector had been improperly selected.
summary: During initial climb, the First Officer's inadvertent selection of no navigation source on his selector caused FMS sequencing failure and lateral deviation on an RNAV SID. The crew resolved the issue by transferring the FCC to the Captain's side and correcting the selector to the white needle position.

synopsis: An A310 flight crew returned to their departure airport after receiving a Green Hydraulic System Overheat alert.
summary: The flight crew experienced a green hydraulic system overheat during climb out from VIDP, prompting an emergency return. They executed ECAM procedures to depressurize the system, landed overweight with 200 FPM vertical speed, and were towed to the gate with 2,000–3,000 feet of runway remaining.

synopsis: An instructor pilot flying an experimental Piper Pacer equipped with a tailwheel lost control on landing and ground looped the aircraft.
summary: The pilot reported a ground loop in an experimental tailwheel aircraft after landing caused by insufficient rudder-to-tailwheel spring tension and a failed copilot left brake. The outcome was a loss of directional control due to these mechanical failures.

synopsis: An Instructor pilot and his Student lost control of their aircraft when the left tire blew out during the landing roll. A ground loop followed when the Student pilot overreacted and the aircraft exited the runway suffering damage to a wingtip, landing gear, tail wheel and windshield.
summary: An instructor and student ground looped a taildragger aircraft off the runway during landing after a left tire burst. The student's hard right rudder input caused a sharp veer, resulting in damage to the landing gear, wingtip, tail wheel, and windshield, though both occupants were unhurt.

synopsis: Local Controller described an aborted takeoff event when he cleared a landing aircraft to cross the departure runway. The reporter acknowledged that he confused the two aircraft being controlled.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Air Carrier X for takeoff but failed to scan the runway while looking at radar scopes, causing an AMASS alert. The controller instructed the aircraft to hold, confirmed the pilot aborted the takeoff, and attributed the error to confusing the flight with a previous departure.

synopsis: ZID Controller voiced concern regarding the lack of training regarding contingency operations, describing a recent CMH's declaration of ATC Zero and the confusion that ensued.
summary: An air traffic controller assumed CMH Approach airspace during an ATC Zero event, causing confusion and delays while managing an inbound aircraft at 9,000 feet near DAY. The controller attributed the incident to a lack of specific training, checklists, and maps for handling contingency airspace transfers.

synopsis: ZMA Controller described an airspace incursion event listing human factor failures as the reason for the occurrence.
summary: Sector 46 controllers failed to coordinate a timely point out for Aircraft X climbing out of MIA airspace, resulting in the aircraft entering Sector 21 at 17,500 feet without a PVD. The incident was caused by communication errors and reverse coordination, prompting a recommendation to review point out procedures.

synopsis: PNE Controller in training described a crossing runway conflict event when coordination between Local and Ground was confused and/or incomplete, the reporter listing a loud air conditioner noise as a contributing factor.
summary: A Trainee cleared a Citation Jet to cross Runway 33 at C3 while a Saratoga was taking off, but the loud air conditioner prevented the Instructor and Ground from hearing the clearance. The Citation pilot queried Ground upon seeing the departing aircraft but did not cross the hold short lines.

synopsis: ZMP Controller voiced concerns regarding the functionality of ERAM equipment.
summary: An air traffic controller managing a Meridian en route to LBF encountered a known ERAM trackball pick failure while attempting a weather reroute. The controller resolved the routing manually but was distracted by the undocumented bug, noting that controllers were not briefed on this known system issue.

synopsis: A B737 First Officer responded incorrectly to a TCAS RA after he increased the aircraft's rate of descent when the resolution was to decrease the descent rate.
summary: During a descent from FL360 to FL340, the First Officer misinterpreted a TCAS Resolution Advisory and increased descent rate, causing the aircraft to descend below FL340. The Captain eventually took control to level off at FL334, attributing the error to TCAS display confusion, startle effect, and delayed intervention.

synopsis: While the reporter/Captain was in the cockpit preparing the A319 for departure, the aircraft was struck violently by a 'runaway tug.' A Maintenance Manager declared the event to have been 'no big deal' although he was not present when it occured. The reporter disagreed and had a maintenance inspection performed prior to accepting the aircraft for a revenue flight.
summary: A pilot reported that a runaway tug violently slammed the aircraft backward ten minutes prior to departure, causing the pilot to feel whiplash. Although maintenance inspected the aircraft and found no damage, the pilot criticized management's cavalier safety response and contacted an attorney.

synopsis: A widebody Captain addressed serious communications problems with Faleolo Control when flying in and out of NSTU (Pago Pago). The essence of the problem is that communication is essentially unavailable through any published or NOTAMed frequencies.
summary: The flight crew experienced severe VHF and HF communication difficulties with Faleolo Tower during descent and landing, compounded by an inability to manually dial the tower's phone number via SATCOM. The pilot attributed the issue to inoperative radios and restricted satellite phone functionality, noting that while the landing was normal, the situation posed a potential safety risk if other traffic had been present.

synopsis: A GLF IV noted spiking left engine TGT, unaccompanied by other engine instrument anomalies. The flight crew declared an emergency and diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: During cruise at FL400, the left engine TGT spiked twice without other parameter changes. The crew moved the power lever to idle, declared an emergency, diverted after burning fuel, and completed a normal landing.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported two wake vortex encounters that resulted in significant uncommanded roll while in trail of an A330 into MIA.
summary: The First Officer performed upset recovery maneuvers twice while descending on the Hiley Three Arrival into MIA due to wake turbulence from a preceding Airbus A330. ATC provided an offset and vectors to avoid further turbulence, resulting in no injuries or flight deviations.

synopsis: The flight crew of a B767-300ER abandoned their approach due to a LE ASSYM EICAS alert. They declared an emergency, completed appropriate checklists and landed uneventfully with 20 degrees of flap.
summary: The flight crew encountered a 'LE ASSYM' EICAS message during descent, declared an emergency, and diverted from final approach to complete the QRH. They landed normally with 20 flaps, requiring a full runway rollout due to higher speed, before taxiing to the gate with ARFF escort.

synopsis: A Stearman Pilot momentarily lost directional control on rollout following a normal landing and performed a ground loop, exiting and returning to the runway interrupted by brief ground contact with the lower right wingtip.
summary: The pilot reported that during rollout after landing, the aircraft swerved left due to inadequate rudder and tailwheel steering corrections. The airplane exited the runway at 30 mph in a three-point attitude, causing minor damage to the right lower wingtip before returning to the surface.

synopsis: CE560 Captain reports landing on Runway 36 at PSN and, knowing that Taxiway A is NOTAM'ed closed, turning off at the north end to find the taxiway blocked some distance south with no way to turn around. Not only does the airport not have any Taxiway signs, the airport diagrams of both the Commercial and Government charts also lack them.
summary: The pilot landed on Runway 36 at Palestine, TX, and entered a dead-end taxiway despite a NOTAM for Taxiway 'A' closure. The aircraft could not turn around due to narrow width, forcing a back-taxi to clear the runway because of missing markings and barricades.

synopsis: DHC2 pilot experiences engine failure at 2,000 FT when the tank suppling the engine is used up. After switching to the rear tank which is half full the engine does not restart and an engine out landing in wetlands ensues without damage.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine failure over wetlands and performed a forced landing after switching to a half-full rear tank without success. The aircraft sustained no damage, and the pilot noted an expired Class 3 medical certificate is being renewed.

synopsis: Small aircraft Instructor Pilot, unable to obtain handoff from a busy Regional Approach Controller for entry into the ADS Class D airspace, executed a 360-degree turn outside of the airspace before being cleared to enter a left base for Runway 15. Pilot was not handed off to the Local Controller until two miles inside the Class D airspace and noted the lack of information available as to the proper airspace entry procedure for this airport.
summary: A VFR pilot returning to Addison (ADS) with a student delayed entering Class D airspace due to confusion over whether Regional Approach's squawk assignment authorized entry without Tower contact. The pilot executed a 360-degree turn outside the boundary after the busy controller failed to respond to clarification requests, eventually receiving Tower clearance and landing safely.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Enroute Supervisor described an airspace infraction during an OJT session when both he and the Instructor were advising the Developmental both failing to note the developing problem.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller and Instructor conducting OJT with a developmental lost track of a northern overflight aircraft while focusing on vectoring a Class C arrival around slower traffic. The overflight entered the next sector without a handoff due to the team's tunnel vision on the training scenario.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: PHL Controller reported a possible runway separation error between a landing aircraft cleared to cross Runway 35 at Taxiway G and a departure cleared for take of from Runway 35 while still on Taxiway E.
summary: A Dash 8 taxiing for Runway 35 departure was cleared for takeoff while still on Taxiway E, violating post-sunset intersection departure procedures. The controller overlooked the Dash 8 due to distraction from a tower conversation while managing a CRJ2 exiting Runway 26.

synopsis: ZDV Controller described a loss of separation event listing similar call signs as the direct cause.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller issued conflicting descent clearances to two aircraft with similar call signs, causing Air Carrier XXXX to descend into close proximity with another aircraft. The controller attributed the near-miss and subsequent RA to the similar call signs and simultaneous transmissions, recommending distinct call signs to prevent recurrence.

synopsis: LAS Controller described a developing conflict event when traffic on final made an unexpected go around paralleling departure traffic form the same runway, the reporter listing the 'gear dragging' by the departure as distracting.
summary: An ATC controller and a B737 pilot experienced a TCAS RA during a go-around at LAS due to communication failures and conflicting instructions. The pilot initiated a self-separation maneuver after the controller failed to issue a heading change, resulting in a temporary conflict with a departing Airbus.

synopsis: ZDC Controller described a probable loss of separation event occurring immediately after a position relief. The reporter listed an on going data block drop problem near a common boundary with ZOB as the causal factor.
summary: A new controller descended Air Carrier X to FL210 in the BLR/EKN sector, causing a 200-foot and 4.07-mile separation loss with a slow-moving aircraft at FL250. The incident occurred because the second aircraft's data block timed out and disappeared from the scope during the controller's sign-in, a recurring issue with early handoffs from Cleveland that the briefing team failed to identify.

synopsis: Two pilots performing a preflight logbook review, report about a 'perfect storm' of Maintenance oversight, miscommunication, lack of attention to detail, an unresolved open maintenance item, and improper use of Logbook Corrective Action sign-off boxes on their B737-700 aircraft, involving a malfunctioning # 2 Display Electronic Unit (DEU).
summary: During preflight, the flight crew discovered an unresolved #2 Display Electronics Unit defect in the logbook that was not transferred to the computerized system, despite a prior Airworthiness Release and CAT III recertification. After consulting maintenance and dispatch, the crew obtained a new bite check confirming no faults before departing safely.

synopsis: While below 2,500 FT MSL flying the BRIJJ RNAV Visual Approach to SFO, an A319 flight crew received multiple ECAM warnings related to the possible failure of the air/ground squat switch. In addition their FMS failed leaving them without RNAV capability. They asked for and received a 'conventional' Visual Approach Clearance from the Tower and landed uneventfully.
summary: During an FMS visual approach to SFO Runway 28R below 2,500 feet, the crew experienced multiple ECAM messages and an FMC failure caused by air/ground sensor issues. They requested and received a visual approach clearance, landed safely, and reported a subsequent landing gear disagree fault to maintenance.

synopsis: When the flight crew of an A320 attempted to resolve a Green Hyd System 1 low pressure ECAM, they discovered a discrepancy between the ECAM Checklist and the more complete procedure in their Flight Manual as far as utilizing the PTU to extend the landing gear. They declared an emergency, landed safely and was towed to a gate after a 30 minute delay.
summary: During cruise, the crew received a Green Hydraulic Engine 1 low pressure ECAM and landed in ZZZ after declaring an emergency. They gravity extended the gear due to a perceived discrepancy between ECAM and AOM checklists regarding the Power Transfer Unit, resulting in no nose wheel steering or normal brakes.

synopsis: Following a procedural change, which in the past had the First Officer turn a B757 start switch OFF for single engine taxi, a Captain announced he was shutting down number one engine and the First Officer shut number two down out of habit.
summary: During ground taxi, the Captain and First Officer unintentionally shut down both engines due to miscommunication regarding new single-engine taxi procedures. The APU provided power for a successful engine restart, allowing the aircraft to taxi to the gate after a brief loss of electrical power and fuel vapor in the cabin.

synopsis: Following a B757 EICAS 'LE ASYMMETRY' alert, the Captain became confused by the new QRH Checklist format and the lack of training on it. He declared an emergency then landed with flaps 30 instead of flaps 20.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced an LE Asymmetry EICAS warning during approach, leading to a diversion. The Captain incorrectly executed the QRH procedure due to inadequate training on the new format, landing with Flaps 30 instead of the required Flaps 20, though the landing occurred without incident.

synopsis: Air Carrier taxiing to the gate after landing BOS taxied across the hold lines for Runway 4L, the reporter listing hold line identification difficulties as one contributing factor.
summary: The First Officer and Captain landed an aircraft at BOS and received unusual taxi instructions due to FOD and an intersecting landing. Distractions and a late frequency change caused the crew to nearly cross the 4L APPR hold line before stopping safely while another aircraft took off.

aircraft: Cessna Citation Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Citation Captain reports overshooting the turn to WENTZ on the RUUDY2 departure from TEB. The 260 course 'came alive' but the flight director did not indicate the turn until passing through the course. ATC issued vectors for the remainder of the departure.
summary: The flight crew departed TEB Runway 24 on the RUUDY2 procedure with the autopilot disengaged. A delayed flight director turn caused an overshoot of the 260-degree course, prompting ATC to issue a heading and altitude that removed the aircraft from the departure procedure for vectoring.

synopsis: EMB145 Captain reports being dispatched with an inoperative number one pack and experiencing cockpit temperatures up to 41 degrees C. During level off at 9,000 FT, airspeed is allowed to accelerate above 250 KTS.
summary: The flight crew operated with PACK 1 MEL'd, causing cockpit temperatures to reach 41°C and distracting them into an overspeed of 272 KTS at 9,000 FT. They corrected the speed, continued the flight, and later criticized the MEL allowance for extreme heat conditions.

synopsis: After the flight crew of a Citation Sovereign successfully resolved the failure of the nose gear to retract after takeoff, utilizing the associated check lists, they noted the last checklist item directed them to land as soon as practical. The crew questioned the decision by the company to continue to their destination rather than to return to their departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced gear vibration and conflicting lights during retraction, prompting a climb to 3,000 MSL and a checklist that confirmed all gear down and locked. They diverted to an alternate airport due to wind and runway length concerns, noting ambiguity in the "land as soon as practical" instruction.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew missed flaps set at 8 rather than the required flaps 20 until noted by the First Officer in the high speed segment of the takeoff. Judging that a rejected takeoff would be more dangerous than continuing the takeoff, the Captain set flaps to 20 and told the First Officer, pilot flying, to continue. Takeoff and climbout were normal.
summary: The flight crew missed the required flaps 20 setting for Runway 19R due to rushing during taxi and takeoff clearance. The First Officer identified the error at 80 knots, and the Captain extended flaps to 20 degrees above 100 knots, resulting in a normal takeoff despite a configuration warning.

synopsis: A Lead and two Mechanics were informed the Lock Spring bolt they had robbed from a removed A320 left-hand Main Landing Gear (MLG) and used to secure a Lock Spring on the Side Stay assembly on a new MLG was a Time Limited Part and should not have been reused. The Lead Mechanic was directed by his Supervisor to reuse old bolt.
summary: During an A320 main landing gear change, a mechanic stripped a new bolt and installed a used Time Limited Part from the removed gear. The Lead mechanic directed this substitution based on supervisor instructions, resulting in the unauthorized installation of a used part on the new gear.

synopsis: An M-7 pilot flying IFR in rain was unable to maintain power and requested ATC vectors to a nearby airport where a safe landing was accomplished.
summary: A pilot flying a Maule into IMC at 4,000 MSL experienced engine roughness and choking after activating carb heat in rain, limiting power to 1,500 RPM. Unable to maintain altitude, the pilot requested vectors to the nearest airport and landed safely with controller assistance.

synopsis: Pilot of a small aircraft had difficulty maintaining heading and altitude due to distractions caused by lack of proficiency with a KLN-94 GPS which was being used for navigation and instrument approaches at two airports.
summary: A pilot flying instrument approaches in a KLN-94 equipped aircraft exceeded heading and altitude tolerances due to GPS setup errors, a failed Nav/Com, and poor task management. The pilot initiated a missed approach after passing the FAF without proper setup and attributed the incident to overconfidence and inadequate pre-flight preparation.

synopsis: A CE550 Captain noted extreme aileron trim tab deflection after takeoff which could not be trimmed out so the flight returned to land where it was found the cockpit trim indicator was misaligned with the trim tab. Reportedly, Maintenance had completed overnight serving of air conditioning system and other inspections including the flight control system.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced an uncommanded right roll immediately after liftoff due to a misaligned left aileron trim tab, despite cockpit indicators showing neutral trim. They returned for an overweight landing, maintaining control with dual inputs, and discovered the physical trim tab deflection only after shutting down.

synopsis: ZHU Controller voiced concern regarding facility notification procedures regarding 'Restricted Airspace' limitations citing a recent example of an airspace incursion because of incomplete notifications efforts.
summary: An air traffic controller nearly descended an Aerostar into active live fire exercises in R6302C because ESIS displays omitted the activation for that sub-area. The supervisor attributed the error to a new supervisor failing to update all ESIS boxes, highlighting a breakdown in coordination procedures.

synopsis: A HCF Controller had a below MVA event with traffic on the LOC/DME BC at KOA executing a missed approach procedure turning in the wrong direction.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller observed an Orion P3 off course and below Minimum IFR Altitudes during a LOC/DME approach at KOA. The Controller issued a climb and heading to ensure terrain clearance but regrets failing to explicitly instruct the Tower to alert the crew of their low altitude.

synopsis: Loss of separation occurred when in-trail separation was allowed to deteriorate below requirements. The reporter acknowledged less than necessary diligence during this occurrence.
summary: An air traffic controller lost separation between a CRJ and an E120 on a STAR arrival after assuming the faster CRJ would descend for a visual approach. The controller vectored the E120 away after it caught up to the stationary CRJ, admitting the incident resulted from delayed action and incorrect assumptions about speed and handoff procedures.

synopsis: A SFB Controller is concerned the ambiguity of the LOA requirements between their facility and MCO TRACON contributed to a conflict when MCO turned a VFR aircraft into the path of an IFR departure.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller vectored a Sky Hawk on a 110 heading while clearing a B767 for takeoff, but Orlando Approach turned the Sky Hawk into the B767's flight path. The controller attributed the conflict to confusing Local Operating Agreement heading requirements between the facilities.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Enroute Controller assigned a D-Side witnessed a loss of separation when the RADAR Controller reportedly overlooked known traffic.
summary: A Radar controller descended a southwest-bound CRJ from FL360 to FL340, losing separation with a northbound Embraer at FL350. The controller overlooked the conflict due to complacency while manually managing spacing during a System Information Area outage.

synopsis: A ZJX Controller experienced an airspace incursion when the D-Side failed to point out traffic to an adjacent sector.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller working with a D-Side failed to hand off an Air Carrier deviating into R08 airspace. The aircraft entered R08 five miles deep before the point out was approved and eventually penetrated 20 miles due to the controller taking back the auto-flash instead of letting R08 manage the traffic.

synopsis: A SFO Tower Controller had a confused departure event when the wrong strip, with incorrect routing information, was passed along to Local Control with the Flight Crew responding to and with the wrong call sign.
summary: An Air Carrier XXXX flight departed Runway 01L using the incorrect call sign and clearance strip for Air Carrier YXYX. The error was discovered en route when the aircraft executed an unexpected right turn, revealing the crew had read back the wrong call sign and SID.

synopsis: A Ground Controller described an unauthorized runway crossing by a student pilot who apparently confused both the taxi instructions to the active runway and the hold short directives.
summary: A student pilot in a C172 crossed active Runway 23 while a C182 was departing, causing the C182 to abort takeoff. The incident occurred because the student failed to hear Ground Control's instructions to hold short, resulting in a pilot deviation and a Brasher warning.

synopsis: HCF Tower ASDE-X nuisance 'false' alarms are recurring. A number of recent suggestions provided at the facility level that might provide some relief are provided.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported an ASDE-X nuisance alarm during a Caravan's short approach to Runway 4L while a Sky Hawk cleared Runway 4R. The alarm triggered due to the Caravan's proximity to the Sky Hawk, though no conflict occurred, highlighting ongoing ASDE-X logic issues at the airport.

synopsis: A B767-300 diverted after a Landing Gear Green light illuminated in flight. On landing numerous EICAS alerts annunciated, including AIR/GRD DISAGREE, with various aircraft systems indicating the in-flight mode.
summary: The crew of a 767 experienced landing gear, slat, and air/ground system anomalies during cruise and landing, attributed to a known MEL item and recurring fleet issues. They diverted for maintenance, landed with hot brakes requiring fire/rescue standby, and reported similar events in other aircraft.

synopsis: A B757 Cabin temperature became uncontrollable while in cruise at FL370 so the flight diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: The crew diverted the aircraft to a nearby airport after the cabin temperature became uncontrollable, reaching 95 degrees in First Class and 92 in economy. The decision followed consultation with Maintenance Control and Dispatch, with Center coordinating the diversion.

synopsis: An A319 flight attendant crew reported an egg/sulfur smell near Row 18 prior to flight but Maintenance found no cause. During flight, the odor returned so the Captain diverted to an enroute airport and was later told the cause was an overheated cabin sidewall electrical light ballast.
summary: Flight attendants reported burning and electrical odors near Row 18 during cruise, prompting a diversion after maintenance failed to identify the source. The aircraft landed normally, but the crew deadheaded while maintenance could not locate the odor's origin before departure.

synopsis: An EMB145 EICAS alerted FLAP FAIL during climb after the aircraft had flown multiple flights with a FLAP LOW SPEED EICAS alert. An emergency was declared and the flight continued to its filed destination.
summary: The crew experienced a FLAP FAIL Master Caution during climb-out on an aircraft with a recurring MEL for FLAP LOW SPEED. They declared an emergency, landed safely on the longest runway, and attributed the failure to maintenance repeatedly deferring the core issue instead of fixing it.

synopsis: A Gulfstream IV with spiking TGT in the left engine diverted to a nearby airport with the engine at idle.
summary: The flight crew experienced a left engine TGT exceedance at FL400, spiking between 910-990 degrees. They declared an emergency, descended, and diverted to the nearest airport for an uneventful landing after reducing the throttle to idle.

synopsis: When their landing gear doors failed to retract after takeoff the flight crew of an MD82 elected to continue to ORD at reduced mach per their QRH procedure. When the doors failed to close as they had expected after gear extension for landing they performed a missed approach, declared an emergency and landed with the doors open and dragging on the runway.
summary: The flight crew encountered a persistent 'Gear Door Open' light after takeoff and failed to notify ATC of required reduced speeds. They declared an emergency, rejected a visual approach behind a B747 to manage fuel and wake turbulence, and landed with gear doors dragging on the runway before maintenance secured them.

synopsis: Following multiple maintenance delays and false starts for a 'red eye' flight, the First Officer of an A320 felt he would be physiologically impaired due to fatigue at their likely arrival time at destination and refused to fly due to fatigue.
summary: The pilot reported fatigue after multiple maintenance delays and an unrelated failure requiring a new flight plan and lower altitude operation. Concerned that continued delays would result in over 24 hours awake, the pilot contacted the Crew Desk to relieve themselves from duty.

synopsis: An A319 had a HYD G RSVR LO ECAM shortly followed by a FWS SDAC1 FAULT ECAM. Forecast weather at the destination led to a divert to a suitable alternate. After landing, the Green system reservoir was found to be over serviced.
summary: The crew diverted an aircraft at FL370 after HYD G RSVR LO and FWS SDAC1 FAULT ECAMs, citing forecast thunderstorms and windshear risks. They declared an emergency, gravity extended the landing gear, and landed uneventfully, though mechanics later found the Green hydraulic reservoir over-serviced.

synopsis: An A319 lost Green Hydraulic system pressure during climbout. The flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: During climbout, the crew lost the green hydraulic system after a stainless steel hose in the wheel well split. The first pilot flew the aircraft and handled radio communications while the captain completed the checklists.

synopsis: A B737-800 Captain was informed by the Tower of smoke coming from the right main gear after landing. CFR was requested. The out board tire was found to be deflated and the brake on that wheel locked.
summary: The flight crew landed with a locked right outboard brake that caused a tire to deflate, prompting a stop and fire response. Maintenance confirmed the brakes were cool, replaced the tire, and evacuated passengers via vans with no injuries.

synopsis: An MD11 encountered severe clear air turbulence at FL320 causing both overspeed and stick shaker activation and some loss of altitude. A lower altitude was immediately requested and granted by ATC. The flight continued to destination.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe clear air turbulence at FL320 west of London, causing two stalls and stick shaker activations. They descended to FL300 per London Control clearance, recovered the aircraft, and continued to destination after logging the event for inspection.

synopsis: DC-10 Captain reported wake turbulence encounter in trail of a B777 on arrival to MEM and suggested additional spacing might be a good idea.
summary: The crew encountered B777 wake turbulence while descending to 6,000 feet on the LTOWN arrival, causing a 15-degree bank and momentary stall warning. The pilot manually recovered the aircraft, attributing the event to insufficient separation and lack of wake turbulence notification from ATC.

synopsis: A B757-200 flight crew, dispatched with the right Generator deferred inoperative, rejected their takeoff below 80 KTS when they received a left generator drive EICAS message. Upon clearing the runway they received an equipment cooling EICAS message.
summary: The crew aborted takeoff below 80 KTS after receiving a 'LT GEN DRIVE' EICAS message while operating with a deferred Right Generator and continuous APU. Following an additional 'EQUIP COOLING' message, the aircraft returned to the gate and was taken out of service for maintenance.

synopsis: A B757-200 Captain reported receiving an EICAS alert for cabin over wing doors and associated slides shortly after takeoff. They returned to departure airport for maintenance attention.
summary: The flight crew received transient EICAS messages indicating emergency door and overwing slide faults just after rotation. Unable to confirm the specific doors during this critical phase, they completed the checklist, returned to the departure airport, and landed overweight at 208,000 lbs to prevent in-flight slide deployment.

synopsis: An A319 Flight Crew suffered the loss of their Green Hydraulic System, ran the appropriate checklists, declared an emergency and returned to their departure airport where they were towed off the runway and to their gate for maintenance.
summary: The crew experienced a green hydraulic system failure shortly after takeoff, triggering ECAM warnings and requiring alternate braking and no nose wheel steering for landing. Following an hour of preparation and emergency briefings, the aircraft landed safely and was towed to the gate for maintenance.

synopsis: A turboprop commuter aircraft was unable to get safe gear indications and requested a flyby of the Tower for a visual confirmation of the landing gear status. In attempting to manage the emergency request while maintaining traffic flow and separation the Local Controller cleared a B737 to LUAW on the runway about to be utilized for the flyby inspection. Due to taxiway closures and outbound traffic the Controller was unable to get the jet off the runway prior to the flyby and a facility ASDE-X alarm was triggered as the commuter aircraft passed overhead.
summary: During a circling approach, an aircraft declared an emergency due to a faulty nose gear indicator, prompting a low approach for visual inspection. The controller cleared the emergency aircraft and a departing B737 for the same runway, causing an ASDE-X alarm due to heavy workload and blocked taxiways.

synopsis: Some confusion reigned aboard a B767-300ER when the First Officer as pilot flying noted an EICAS GEN DRIVE FAIL message as they approached 80 KIAS and called out the light while beginning to pull back the thrust levers to reject the takeoff. The Captain assumed control and opted to continue the takeoff, pushing the throttles forward again until feeling RTO braking engage at which time the takeoff was rejected.
summary: The Captain and First Officer aborted a night takeoff on Runway 17R below 80 KTS after a right engine generator DRIVE light illuminated. The aircraft stopped safely with reverse thrust and manual braking, and ARFF inspection confirmed no brake overheating before returning to the gate.

synopsis: When a Flight Attendant discovered two walk around oxygen bottles without the tubing to the masks connected she was unable to get a Mechanic to correct the problem, in part because of a language problem. She, instead, attached them herself and advised the Purser and Captain.
summary: A Flight Attendant at ZSPD found disconnected oxygen tubing on wheelchair bottles before departure. Due to a language barrier with the Maintenance Technician, the Attendant connected the tubing herself, advised the Captain and Purser, and the flight boarded without further maintenance input.

synopsis: While en route the Flight Attendant/Reporter who had armed door 5L prior to departure on a B747-400 was advised it was no longer armed. When the reporter investigated she discovered the arming door would not remain in the armed position but, instead, would spring out of it when arming was attempted. Maintenance was advised and met the aircraft upon arrival.
summary: A Flight Attendant reported that Door 5L on the aircraft would not remain armed because the handle acted like a spring, returning to the disarm mode. Maintenance was notified, and a Mechanic inspected the door after landing, confirming the handle's faulty spring-like behavior.

synopsis: Two Inspectors and two Mechanics were involved with the Nose Landing Gear (NLG) Sliding Tube seals replacement and installation on an EMB-145 aircraft that required an air turnback after takeoff.
summary: Mechanics replaced nose gear seals on an Embraer, but the upper centering cam was installed 90 degrees out of alignment. This caused a gear retraction failure and air turnback, as the maintenance manual lacked a required extension and retraction check after the repair.

synopsis: Two Mechanics were informed by their Maintenance Manager that required Boroscope Inspections had not been accomplished after they had performed Engine Vibration Run Checks on both GE CF-34 engines for 'ENGINE EXCEEDENCE' EICAS messages. Aircraft, an ERJ-175, was released aircraft for service. It was later grounded and flights canceled.
summary: Two mechanics performed an engine run on an ERJ-175 to check Engine #2 vibrations but ignored an Engine #1 exceedence message, resetting the FADEC instead of following manual requirements for a borescope. The aircraft returned to service, causing flight cancellations five flights later when the fault was reported, though the subsequent borescope found no damage.

synopsis: An Inspector has safety concerns involving the use of High Pressure 'screw-on' type inflation tools (adapters)that are used to service aircraft tires on their Gulf G-200 aircraft, compared to the Brass High Pressure type 'push-on' type tire servicing equipment.
summary: A mechanic performing a preliminary inspection found a tire requiring service and identified that the service cart used an inappropriate screw-on inflation tool and had a leaking regulator. The reporter warned these conditions could cause catastrophic tire bursts, damage, or injury, recommending the return of brass chucks and a regular cart inspection program.

synopsis: An A330 aircraft had fuel quantity indication failures that did not show up as fuel faults in the Aircraft Condition Monitoring System (ACMS). Only after flight cancellation and repositioning of the aircraft did 2,000 LBS of missing fuel reappear. Technician believes water in the fuel tanks may be a factor.
summary: A mechanic and three pilots investigated a Left Inner Tank fuel indication discrepancy on an aircraft with an existing MEL for the high level detection system. The flight was canceled due to suspected improper sumping from short turn times, but fuel indications normalized after the aircraft was towed and re-sumped.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic inadvertently replaced the right side Air Cycle Machine (ACM) when the left side ACM was scheduled to be replaced on a B717 aircraft while trying to meet a morning departure schedule.
summary: Mechanic X replaced the wrong Air Cycle Machine (ACM) on a B717 during a routine overnight maintenance window due to misinterpreting the task card, fatigue, and excessive heat. The error was discovered the following night when the next shift realized the left ACM was scheduled for replacement instead of the right.

synopsis: C150 pilot reported power loss in pattern, declared an emergency, returned for an immediate landing. FBO opinion was that he mis-set the mixture, running full rich when he should have leaned a bit.
summary: A student pilot in a Cessna 150 experienced engine oscillation and loss of climb during a touch-and-go training flight. The pilot declared an emergency and landed safely; the Chief CFI attributed the issue to an overly rich mixture setting caused by warming temperatures.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A pilot using a SRQ AFD Airport diagram was unable to identify his hold short clearance point at the Taxiway D intersection with Runway 14/32 and consequently crossed Runway 4/22.
summary: The pilot inadvertently crossed a runway hold line while searching for a non-existent intersection on charts during taxi, caused by partial panel operation and a misunderstood clearance. The controller issued a revised clearance to a visible intersection, and the pilot departed without incident after later realizing the original instruction referred to a different intersection.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot taxied beyond the newly installed OWD Runway 35 hold short line because it was some distance from the runway end and he was not expecting it to be different from its previous location.
summary: The pilot taxied over a hold short line at their home airport and was reminded by the Tower Controller. The incident was caused by the pilot's expectation of the line's previous location, lack of recent experience, and personal distraction following a family death.

synopsis: A BE35 loss of battery took down the electrical system. An emergency return to departure airport was followed by a safe landing.
summary: The pilot experienced electrical instrument and radio failures at 1,000 feet AGL, squawked 7600, and declared an emergency. After manually extending the landing gear without green lights, the pilot landed safely following a visual fly-by confirmation, with post-flight inspection revealing a failed battery.

synopsis: A Bellanca Viking pilot made an immediate return and landing with Tower's assistance when engine oil began coating his windshield after takeoff. The oil filler cap had not been secured prior to takeoff.
summary: The pilot reported oil on the windshield after takeoff, caused by a loose filler cap that detached in flight. After requesting and receiving clearance to land on Runway 15, the pilot elected to land on Runway 6, executing an uneventful but mostly blind landing.

aircraft: Grumman Corp Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: The engine of a vintage Grumman war bird swallowed a valve and ATC provided generous assistance while vectoring the pilot to the nearest suitable airport where he made a safe landing.
summary: The pilot experienced a swallowed valve causing severe vibration, power loss, and smoke while en route to an air show. After declaring an emergency, ATC provided vectors and airport information, enabling a safe landing with no damage to the aircraft or personnel.

synopsis: While attempting to stretch his fuel to get to his destination ahead of forecast weather the pilot of a PA28-B ran out of fuel but was able to extend his glide just enough to reach the touchdown zone of his destination airport.
summary: The pilot bypassed a planned fuel stop due to an optimistic fuel assessment, causing an engine power loss during descent after clearing controlled airspace. Selecting alternate tanks briefly restored power, but the engine failed again just short of the threshold, resulting in a successful engine-out landing with no injuries.

synopsis: While in cruise at FL320 the flight crew of a Citation 550 suffered a rapid loss of pressurization. They declared an emergency and conducted an emergency descent to 10,000 MSL where they regained some pressurization control and, ultimately diverted to the location of their corporate maintenance facility. There they discovered the pressurization outflow valve had failed in the full open position.
summary: The flight crew in cruise at FL320 experienced a rapid cabin altitude rise due to a failed outflow valve. They declared an emergency, descended to 10,000 feet, and diverted to a maintenance facility after the cabin altitude reached 20,000 feet.

synopsis: Piper Cub pilot reported loss of power after takeoff, so he returned to departure airport.
summary: The pilot of a Continental A-65 reported insufficient climb performance after takeoff, requiring maneuvering between obstacles and over a river to gain altitude for a safe return landing. The pilot suspected a stuck valve caused the issue.

synopsis: A C-172S Intructor pilot and his student lost control of vertical performance during a touch and go departure when the electric flaps failed to retract to the selected 10 degree extension, appearing to stop at 20 degrees deflection. The Instructor assumed control and eventually managed to accelerate and climb to a safe altitude from where a safe approach and landing were completed.
summary: During a training touch-and-go, a flight instructor and student experienced a premature lift-off followed by poor climb performance due to flaps failing to retract from 30 to 10 degrees. The instructor declared an emergency, landed safely, and grounded the aircraft for a flight control failure after confirming the flap selector was ineffective.

synopsis: A PA-28-180 pilot reported engine roughness and loss of power after takeoff. He returned to departure airport for maintenance attention.
summary: The pilot of a Piper Cherokee PA-28-180 experienced intermittent engine roughness and RPM drops during climb and runup when using the right fuel tank. The pilot attributed the issue to potential fuel contamination or a delivery system fault in the right tank, returned safely, and grounded the aircraft for investigation.

synopsis: While attempting to avoid a line of thunderstorms and at FL410 using NEXRAD and on board Radar, A CE650 flight crew experiences a Radar failure and severe turbulence resulting in altitude excursions. An emergency is declared and the flight is cleared to FL450 then eventually down to FL390. Upon clearing the weather the RH Chip Detector illuminates and the crew elects to divert for maintenance.
summary: The Captain and First Officer encountered severe turbulence and lightning while navigating convective weather at FL410, causing autopilot disconnect, uncontrolled altitude changes, and on-board radar failure. Post-flight inspection revealed minor lightning damage and a pre-existing engine bearing defect, though no injuries occurred and the aircraft returned to service after repairs.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A small aircraft pilot incurred HWD Runway 28L after he did not recognize the runway hold short line on Taxiway A because of its distance from the runway and because it was perpendicular to the runway orientation.
summary: The pilot taxied past a perpendicular hold short line at Runway 28L while distracted by cockpit tasks, though remaining clear of the runway. The incident resulted from the unusual line placement and the pilot's unfamiliarity with the airport layout, leading to a hold position instruction from Ground.

synopsis: C414 pilot reports inadvertently entering a fire fighting TFR when his G696 with XM does not depict an increase in the dimensions of the airspace that occurs after takeoff.
summary: A pilot flying a VFR flight inadvertently entered a TFR at 13,000 MSL because XM satellite updates on the Garmin 696 did not reflect a recent increase in the TFR's altitude and area. Air Traffic Control confirmed no harm was done but noted the delay in XM data dissemination.

synopsis: A Contract Mechanic was directed to use an Engineering Order that allowed the use of Naphtha fluid, a highly flammable solvent, to clean their aircraft insulation blankets, including the blankets in the Electrical Equipment (E/E) compartment.
summary: A mechanic cleaning an insulation blanket in Aircraft X's E/E compartment used Naphtha per a printed Engineering Repair Order after the digital system failed. The mechanic observed a shiny residue and believes the solvent damaged the blanket's required burn rate.

synopsis: A Czech Aero Works pilot made a successful off airport landing after the engine quit because of fuel starvation at a low altitude with the selected fuel tank indicating four gallons when it was actually empty.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine stoppage at 3,000 feet MSL due to fuel starvation while cruising. After two restart attempts and using the electric boost pump, the pilot executed a safe farm field landing with no damage or injury, attributing the cause to inaccurate fuel gauges and an un-ported pickup.

synopsis: After landing a PA-22's brakes provided very little braking. While taxiing, ATC put another aircraft in conflict with it requring the pilot to take evasive action onto an active runway.
summary: The pilot reported little to no braking after landing on Runway 4, leading to a runway incursion on Runway 15 while avoiding a Cessna 172. The pilot attributed the incident to the controller clearing conflicting traffic despite being informed of the brake failure.

synopsis: PHL Controller described a potential go-around event during a Runway 27R/35 arrival operation utilizing Converging Runway Display Aid (CARDA) 'ghost target' procedures, the Controller listing various controller technique/s as problematic.
summary: An air traffic controller managed tight spacing between Air Carrier X and Y on intersecting final approaches to runways 35 and 27R, compounded by similar call signs. The controller prevented a potential double go-around by briefing both pilots to slow down and accept the risk, attributing the conflict to poor spacing by the OOD controller and inadequate facility training.

synopsis: Air Carrier taxiing for departure at LGA passed the ILS hold line for Runway 4 resulting in several ATC issued go arounds, the reporter noting more exacting information regarding this common procedure should be published.
summary: The pilot reported that at LaGuardia, their aircraft caused two arrivals to go around due to wingtip clearance issues on Runway 4. Although ATC eventually instructed them to hold short of the ILS line, the pilot noted this common practice was not clearly listed on the chart's key notes page.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier Captain reported transitioning onto SFO Taxiway A from Taxiway B when the clearance was to use F1 because the signage at the the Taxiway A, B and F1 confluence did not clearly identify Taxiway F1 when approaching from the West.
summary: The flight crew transitioned to an unassigned inner taxiway due to poor signage, radio congestion, and a weight and balance issue. They visually cleared adjacent areas before turning and realized the error only after reaching the inner taxiway, resulting in a successful but non-compliant transition.

synopsis: CRJ200 Flight Crew discovers that their aircraft is not pressurizing shortly after takeoff. A call from the Flight Attendant indicates that the door may not be properly latched although there are no indications on the EICAS and the Captain elects to return to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew and a flight attendant experienced a pressurization failure during climbout due to a missing pressurization flap on the main passenger door, which showed a green indication but allowed daylight and wind noise. The crew declared an emergency, returned for an overweight landing, and required maintenance to open the jammed door after arrival.

synopsis: After takeoff B737-800 passengers reported a spoiler up and the Generator OFF light alerted so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport where a left engine access panel was discovered missing.
summary: The crew experienced a left engine cowling separation and generator failure shortly after takeoff, causing vibration and a Master Caution. They declared an emergency, landed safely at the departure airport, and the aircraft was taken out of service after the cowling was found on the runway.

synopsis: A Line Inspector describes how he inadvertently deployed a door slide at Cabin Door 2-Right on a B-777 aircraft during verification of the slide installation.
summary: A mechanic performing a slide replacement inspection on a Boeing B777 at ZZZ Maintenance Hanger inadvertently deployed the slide. The deployment occurred when the mechanic moved the Door-2R handle slightly while the door was armed during an operational check.

synopsis: A CFII and his Commercial student were distracted and failed to note another aircraft on final when they were cleared for takeoff. Although the Tower believed he had subsequently canceled their takeoff clearance, neither pilot nor the pilot of another aircraft heard any such transmission. The landing aircraft was directed to make a go-around.
summary: A CFII instructor and student entered the runway without checking final, causing a go-around for an aircraft on approach. The instructor attributed the incident to his failure to scan for traffic and distractions from turbulence reports and the student's focus on IFR procedures.

synopsis: PA32 pilot rejected the takeoff at DZJ when another aircraft was found to be rolling out from the opposite direction. A crest half way down the runway and heat shimmers make sighting the other aircraft difficult and communications were never established.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff on Runway 8 after spotting an unannounced aircraft on the runway, likely obscured by heat haze. The other pilot failed to make radio calls or verify runway clearance before departing the airport without being contacted.

synopsis: A CE550 lost cabin pressure while climbing through FL370. Attempts to control the cabin pressure were unsuccessful and an emergency descent and diversion were made.
summary: The flight crew experienced a rapid cabin altitude increase and automatic oxygen mask deployment while climbing from FL360 to FL380 due to a pressurization failure. They executed an emergency descent to 10,000 feet and diverted, landing safely after the issue could not be secured.

synopsis: An M20 had engine failure at 500 FT after a touch and go. The Instructor quickly took control from the student and made a safe landing on an intersecting runway. The fuel tank feeding the engine was found to be empty with the fuel gauge indicating sufficient fuel but selected to a different tank.
summary: During flight instruction in a Mooney M20B at 500 feet AGL near Chino Airport, the engine stopped due to fuel exhaustion caused by inconsistent fuel selector and gauge switch settings. The instructor executed a safe emergency landing on Runway 3 with no injuries or damage.

synopsis: SFO Controller voiced concern regarding the flight characteristics and/or pilot techniques of the A320 with regard to SID compliance.
summary: An ATC observer reported a potential loss of separation in NCT airspace between an A320 and a B757, both departing Runway 1L on the PORTE3 SID. The A320 was described as flying incredibly slow and turning sharply, leading the observer to question whether the issue stemmed from aircraft performance or pilot error.

synopsis: B737-500 flight crew reports an altitude deviation during the RIIVR 2 arrival to LAX when they are given direct to RIIVR from over GRAMM and 300 KTS or better. Level Change was selected for descent to 14,000 FT then forgotten when 2,200 is set for the final approach fix altitude.
summary: During descent into LAX on the RIIVR arrival, the crew descended below 10,000 feet at 300 knots because the Captain selected Level Change instead of LNAV/VNAV. The First Officer's distraction by a flight director failure and crew complacency prevented timely detection of the mode error until ATC intervention.

synopsis: B757 Captain believes that the flight manual requirement to verify aircraft position on the NAV display prior to takeoff is not germane due to the position not being updated in the FMC until the EPR button is pressed for takeoff.
summary: A B757/B767 pilot reported that the flight manual's requirement to visually confirm the aircraft symbol on the assigned runway before takeoff cannot be met in non-GPS aircraft. The pilot stated the position update occurs only after takeoff begins, causing the symbol to be off the runway and forcing crews to violate the manual on most flights.

synopsis: The Flight Attendant in charge reports their B737-800 aircraft required an air turn-back due to a loud air noise coming from Forward Entry Door 1-Left immediately after takeoff. A First Officer had closed the door prior to departure. Flight Attendant noted the cockpit Door Warning Indicator did not show door was not properly closed.
summary: Cabin crew on a B737-800 heard a loud air noise after take-off, prompting a return to the departure airport. The reporter attributed the issue to a Boeing door design defect where the cockpit warning indicator fails to detect improper closure in the aft section.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports the left engine on a company B767-300 aircraft had shutdown on landing when the thrust reversers were deployed. A metal gasket he had installed between the fuel/oil cooler housing and the fuel 'In' tube connection to the fuel/oil cooler had failed.
summary: A mechanic replaced the left engine fuel flow transmitter and gasket, then performed a successful engine run. The left engine subsequently shut down during thrust reverser deployment on landing due to a failed fuel 'In' tube gasket, though the cause remains undetermined.

synopsis: Two Line Mechanics report that a B737-800 aircraft experienced moderate buffeting through the aircraft after departure, requiring an air turn-back. On landing, while going into reverse thrust, the #1 Engine Generator had fallen 'Off-Line' as the Outboard (O/B) fan cowl was blown off the same engine.
summary: A B737-800 experienced generator failure and vibration after takeoff, followed by the left engine outboard fan cowl blowing off during reverse thrust. The crew attributed the incident to the cowl not being properly secured due to high workload, distraction, and miscommunication during maintenance.

synopsis: A320 First Officer departing Runway 9L at ATL describes a rejected takeoff at 120 KTS when the Captain notices an aircraft crossing the runway ahead.
summary: The crew aborted takeoff at 120 KTS on runway 9L after observing an aircraft taxiing across on Taxiway DIXIE. The aircraft stopped off the runway at M14, and the crew was subsequently instructed to return to the gate.

synopsis: An instructor providing IFR training in a C-172 allowed himself to get distracted by taking student error notes on a new EFB. As a result, he allowed/participated in a minor track deviation until advised by ATC.
summary: An instructor supervising a student during an instrument approach noticed the student selected the wrong radial, but distraction from using an unfamiliar electronic flight bag delayed correction until the aircraft was nearly one mile off course. The incident highlighted how technology can divert attention from primary flying duties and student monitoring.

synopsis: AC690 pilot becomes distracted by a malfunctioning glide slope indication during approach and nearly lands gear up before going around. A landing gear circuit breaker had been pulled to silence the warning horn while practicing slow flight and was not reset.
summary: The pilot practicing an ILS approach in VFR conditions landed with gear up due to a frozen glide slope display and a pulled landing gear circuit breaker. This resulted in belly rivet contact before a go-around was initiated, caused by checklist sequence disruption and troubleshooting on final.

synopsis: CE550 First Officer experiences radio failure when attempting to contact Departure Control after takeoff. This was planned as a short flight and the crew elects to squawk 7600 and continue to destination.
summary: The pilot not flying and Captain experienced a two-way radio failure during departure and approach while flying to 5,000 feet. They squawked 7600, received vague clearances, and landed using light gun signals after troubleshooting electrical issues without restoring full communications.

synopsis: Flight Attendant describes a east coast to west coast round trip flight sequence that is scheduled to depart in the evening and return at dawn. The trip ends up being delayed six hours after the crew has checked in resulting in an 18 hour duty day.
summary: Cabin crew reported a trans-continental redeye flight where a 3.5-hour delay extended their duty to nearly 18 hours without rest or breaks. The crew stated they were physically ill and unable to evacuate the aircraft due to exhaustion, fearing disciplinary action if they rested.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A pilot reported missing the ASG Runway 18 Runway Critical Hold Short line which was located well before Runway's departure end.
summary: The pilot, cleared by Ground Control to taxi to Runway 18 via the West Taxiway, failed to identify the hold lines located approximately 400 feet south of the runway entrance.

synopsis: A BE300 on a test flight lost pressurization at FL270 because two sense lines on the pressure controller had been reversed during extended maintenance. The pilot had communications problems because of headset/oxygen mask incompatability.
summary: The pilot experienced a pressurization failure and oxygen mask deployment during climb after a major modification, caused by two crossed lines at the controller. The crew descended to 10,000 feet and returned to the departure airport, where a mechanic later fainted from oxygen exposure.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: SFO Controller described a confused flight plan event where an aircraft's call sign was mixed up during the taxi out to the departure runway. The reporter listed company similar sounding call signs as contributing to the incident.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller issued taxi and departure instructions to Air Carrier YXYX using the incorrect call sign Air Carrier XXXX, which the pilots failed to correct. The error was only discovered when the aircraft turned right instead of left, nearly causing a conflict with a departing B737 due to the similar-sounding call signs.

synopsis: ZTL Controller voiced concern regarding weather tools available to ATC and the wind reading inaccuracies that sometimes occur.
summary: Charlotte Meter Position controllers reported that the Integrated Terminal Weather System (ITWS) displayed winds 50 degrees off from actual METAR data, risking tailwind landings. Although the sensor was checked by the CWSU, the discrepancy persists, requiring further verification of the ITWS sensor or programming.

synopsis: ZMP Controller described an airspace incursion event listing the ERAM's 'actual' activation time for map displays as a contributing factor, noting the restricted airspace should be displayed ten minutes before activation.
summary: An air traffic controller at Toronto Center struggled to reroute a B747 away from scheduled military airspace because ERAM displayed the restriction only when active. The aircraft clipped the restricted area corner after delayed compliance, prompting a recommendation for earlier ERAM alerts despite the controller's belief that the outcome would not have changed.

synopsis: A320 Captain describes extreme fatigue after a series of late night flights.
summary: A pilot reported severe exhaustion during the cruise phase of a flight, causing an inability to recall recently read-back frequencies. The pilot attributed this dangerous state to an unsustainable schedule involving multiple night flights and minimal rest days over the preceding eleven days.

synopsis: B757-200 flight crew experience significant engine vibration climbing out of 6,000 FT and elect to return to the departure airport for an overweight landing.
summary: Pilots of a Boeing 757-200 experienced significant left engine vibration while climbing from 6,000 to 6,500 feet. After consulting Dispatch, they declared an emergency, returned to the airport, and completed an overweight landing without incident.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier Captain reported a conflict with another aircraft while taxiing on DEN Taxiway WB after ATC failed to issue taxi guidance to either aircraft.
summary: The pilot reported a runway incursion risk while taxiing eastbound on WB after landing on 16R, where a southbound jet on Foxtrot encroached into their path. The pilot believes Ground Control missed the conflict, and the situation was resolved only by the aggressive stopping actions of both flight crews.

synopsis: CRJ200 flight crew experiences compressor stalls, vibration, and high ITT shortly after takeoff. With the thrust reduced the symptoms disappear and the Captain elects to return visually to the departure airport with the engine operating at low thrust.
summary: During initial climb at 700 feet AGL, the crew experienced a left engine compressor stall causing loud bangs, vibration, and an ITT over 950°C. The Captain reduced thrust, declared an emergency, and returned for a visual landing at the departure airport, where emergency crews confirmed the engine was secure.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 flight crew reported a wake encounter following an A319 after takeoff at ATL that resulted in a course deviation. Reporters suggested allowing more spacing behind A319/320 aircraft.
summary: The pilot reported that heavy wake from an A319 caused a course deviation immediately after takeoff, requiring a left turn to intercept the departure path. The pilot attributed the incident to ATL Tower clearing the aircraft for takeoff before the preceding Airbus had lifted off, noting that A319/320 wake turbulence is comparable to heavy aircraft.

synopsis: B747 Captain reports discovering airborne, that his cargo load of 55,000 pounds is actually 55,000 kilograms while attempting to reach FL330. The flight descends to FL310 and is able to continue to destination.
summary: The flight crew experienced degraded climb performance and airspeed issues due to cargo weights being misinterpreted as pounds instead of kilograms. This unit error caused the aircraft to be overloaded, requiring a descent to FL310 and continuous monitoring before an uneventful landing.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic working on an A320 aircraft in a Hangar, reports that an overhauled Main Landing Gear (MLG) Upper Side Stay Spring attach pin was removed and replaced with the pin from the 'Off' (removed) MLG. Their MLG paperwork did not state the old attach pin was also a Time-Limited part.
summary: Maintenance crew swapped a Main Landing Gear Upper Side Stay Spring attach pin with the removed unit to avoid carrier charges, believing the pin was not a Time-Limited part. This decision followed vendor briefings stating that unserviceable parts are covered under the overhaul contract, though paperwork did not identify the pin as time-limited.

synopsis: PA44 pilot entering the traffic pattern on downwind reports a NMAC with a C172 in the pattern and also on downwind. The C172 pilot apparently had the PA44 in sight but the PA44 pilot did not see the C172 until they were very close.
summary: The reporter's aircraft and a Cessna experienced a near-miss at 2,600 feet MSL while entering the downwind for Runway 13. The reporter attributed the incident to poor visibility from haze and bright sun, noting the Cessna flew high and made insufficient traffic calls.

synopsis: While attempting to climb above weather the pilot of a UAV lost control of his aircraft at FL210 and lost altitude to 16,500 MSL before regaining control and restarting the climb.
summary: The pilot encountered severe weather while climbing from FL190 to FL250, causing an uncommanded descent from FL210 to 16,500 feet. After regaining control, the crew climbed to the amended clearance of FL290 to fly above the weather.

synopsis: A PA-32 pilot had a runway excursion after he lost control of his aircraft on landing for unknown reasons. No damage or injuries resulted.
summary: The pilot landed a single-engine aircraft on Runway 19 in VMC with westerly crosswinds, but the airplane unexpectedly veered right and became uncontrollable immediately after touchdown. The aircraft exited the runway, rotated 180 degrees, and came to rest on adjacent terrain with no injuries, though the pilot could not confirm if the cause was a gust, vortex, or complacency.

synopsis: A light sport aircraft pilot ran out of fuel on a 48 mile flight and conducted a safe off airport landing on a highway where he was given 91 octane fuel to complete his trip.
summary: The pilot of a small aircraft experienced fuel exhaustion due to 20-knot headwinds during a 48 NM flight, forcing a landing on a highway. After receiving 4 gallons of 91 octane from locals, the pilot flew to the destination, refueled with 100LL, and returned to the departure airport.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described an emergency descent event when the request for an immediate descent did not permit time for coordination with adjacent sectors prior to entry.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a B737 emergency descent from FL330 to 8,000 feet after the pilot requested an immediate return to the departure airport. The pilot's refusal to disclose the emergency nature prevented the controller from coordinating effectively with adjacent sectors or alerting other traffic.

synopsis: ZNY Controller voiced concern regarding the PHL arrival routing URET limitations.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a C750 landing at PHL required manual coordination because URET incorrectly displayed the VCN8 arrival instead of the required RNAV JIIMS1. This automation error forces extra HERT routing, increases controller workload, and risks future errors until the system is updated.

synopsis: MLI Controller voiced concern regarding a recent maintenance re-boot during normal working hours alleging these types of maintenance activities should be performed during Tower closure hours.
summary: While a CRJ2 climbed from 5,000 feet during a handoff to ZAU, maintenance rebooted the ARTS system, causing a loss of radar data. The aircraft subsequently received a TCAS RA and descended to avoid a non-communicating VFR Cessna, an incident the controller attributed to unsafe daytime maintenance scheduling.

synopsis: Local Controller cleared an aircraft for takeoff on a runway on which he had previously cleared an airport vehicle. Vehicle cleared the runway after hearing Controller issue clearance to the aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared a PA-31 for takeoff on Runway 2R while Vehicle X was approved on the same runway due to the controller failing to scan the shared hot box status. The controller attributed the near-miss to not verifying the hot box before issuing the clearance, noting the shared display for Runway 2R and Ski Strip 2 contributed to the error.

synopsis: According to a Center Controller an air carrier aircraft ignored heading assignments that the Controller issued for weather avoidance and then became confused and argued with the Controller.
summary: An air traffic controller and a pilot were involved during the arrival phase when the pilot refused to deviate right of course to avoid precipitation. The pilot ignored multiple instructions to turn right or fly heading 050, eventually deviating left into adjacent airspace before a supervisor ordered a course reversal.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier Crew departed SEA Runway 34R and received jet blast when barely airborne from a B747-400 which had not cleared the runway hold short lines to exit the runway.
summary: The flight crew experienced a strong engine blast from another aircraft while rotating on Runway 34R after the other aircraft had not fully cleared the runway at intersection E. The crew reported the incident to Tower, who confirmed the other aircraft was clear of the runway, and the takeoff continued normally.

synopsis: An A320 flight crew was unable to lower their landing gear, initiated a go around, successfully conducted a gravity extension procedure and returned for a safe landing. Their fuel remaining could have compromised more extensive trouble shooting had the gravity extension not proven successful. A previous identical failure some 11 days before was not annotated in the logbook or in the flight crew's maintenance briefing message provided for flight planning.
summary: The flight crew experienced a landing gear malfunction on final approach, requiring a go-around and successful gravity extension. They noted a missing maintenance record for a similar incident eleven days prior and credited an extra 1,000 pounds of fuel for providing adequate troubleshooting time.

synopsis: B767-300 Captain reported noticing an EICAS CARGO BTL 1 and DISCHRG light on, triggering a divert for maintenance action before they committed to their international over water leg.
summary: The crew received a cargo bottle discharge indication during flight and diverted to avoid ETOPS airspace due to an inadequate QRH. Maintenance found a loose cannon plug on the number one bottle pressure gauge, allowing the aircraft to land overweight and continue after repairs.

synopsis: Air Carrier Dispatcher reported confusion regarding a flight's status due to an ATC error in entering the destination airport, a track change due to Warning Areas becoming hot and a citizen, observing the flight on Flight Tracker, erroneously reporting that the flight was diverting due to a medical emergency.
summary: A flight following specialist observed a false destination change on Flight Explorer for Aircraft X, caused by a Center Controller entering incorrect data due to active military airspace. This error led to public confusion and a mistaken report of a medical emergency diversion, though the Captain confirmed the original destination remained unchanged.

synopsis: EMB170 Captain is informed just prior to pushback that the oil service door for the number one engine is open. Further investigation reveals that the oil cap is missing and a screwdriver is in the compartment. Maintenance was not being performed during this stop and indications are that the aircraft arrived in this condition.
summary: The Captain and a new First Officer discovered an open oil service door with a screwdriver inside on Engine 1 during pushback, despite no maintenance notification or logbook entry. The aircraft departed 1 hour and 45 minutes late after the missing oil cap was found and the door secured.

synopsis: EMB145 Captain reports being dispatched with pack one inoperative and noticing cabin altitude climbing rapidly as the aircraft passes through 16,000 FT during climb. Pack number two has tripped and cannot be reset and flight returns to departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a pressurization failure with Pack 1 MEL'd and Pack 2 failing during climb, causing cabin altitude to rise to 10,000 feet. They requested priority return to the departure airport after consulting the QRH and hearing a strange noise reported by the flight attendant.

synopsis: A Dash 8 flight crew succumbed to heat illness when they were unable to cool the cockpit and was ultimately unfit to fly the next day's flight when symptoms returned even following a layover.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced heat illness during cruise and approach in an older 100 model aircraft due to excessive cockpit temperatures that failed to cool despite system adjustments. Symptoms degraded their performance, leading to a request for medical evaluation upon landing, with the Captain later requiring hospital treatment.

synopsis: CE-680 First Officer reported noticing pitch trim indicator reading abnormally high in cruise flight. When autopilot was disengaged it was apparent the indicator was wrong and the trim was not actually moving out of the normal range.
summary: During cruise at FL410, pilots observed uncommanded pitch trim indicator movements while the autopilot remained engaged. They determined the stabilizer did not actually move, attributing the event to a faulty display indication, and continued to the destination without incident.

synopsis: EC135 Check Airman reports an inadvertent engine shutdown while on the runway of an uncontrolled airport at night. A complete electrical shut down is determined to be necessary to restart the engine but is deemed to risky on the runway. The helicopter is single engine air taxied to clear the runway and perform the shutdown and restart.
summary: During ground recurrent training, a pilot inadvertently shut down Engine #2 while executing a FADEC failure maneuver, causing a restart failure due to switch resets. The crew taxied the aircraft under single-engine power to a nearby ramp to avoid remaining dark on the active runway at night.

synopsis: PC-12 pilot reported NMAC with an inbound aircraft at CNM when the inbound was apparently using an outdated CTAF frequency.
summary: The pilot reported a Traffic Alert System warning after takeoff while climbing past 1,000 feet AGL, prompting a climbing turn to avoid a target. The conflict occurred because the other pilot was monitoring an outdated CTAF frequency instead of the current one.

synopsis: Dispatched with the right generator deferred inoperative the flight crew of an MD-83 rejected their takeoff when the APU failed. A subsequent relight of the APU was followed by a second takeoff attempt and a completed flight.
summary: The pilot rejected takeoff at 40 KTS after the APU, which was powering the right bus due to a deferred generator, shut down. Maintenance later determined the APU failure was caused by low oil, and the flight continued successfully after a restart.

synopsis: An air carrier that departed IWA following three aerobatic aircraft had to request a departure vector in order to maintain a comfortable separation from the aircraft maneuvering in the departure corridor.
summary: The crew departed Runway 12C immediately after three aerobatic aircraft, requesting a right turn to avoid their path. They climbed 10 degrees right of the runway past 10,000 feet, noting that standard clearance would have placed them dangerously close to the aerobatic box.

synopsis: B767-300 Relief Pilot describes the events leading up to a rejected takeoff at 130 KTS. When the First Officers sliding window comes open at 80 KTS and cannot be cranked closed the Captain rejects the takeoff.
summary: The crew aborted a 767-300ER takeoff at 130 KTS after the First Officer's window handle was found in the aft position and stuck. The aircraft stopped safely, but popped wheel fuse plugs required a 30-minute brake cooling delay before passengers deplaned.
