synopsis: B737 Captain reports noting a large pressure drop during a simultaneous test of the oxygen system, although the drop is normal when one system is tested at a time. Maintenance is called and the supply valve is found to be not fully open.
summary: Pilots discovered a partially open cockpit oxygen valve during preflight when simultaneous testing caused a pressure drop from 1300 to 150 PSI. Maintenance fully opened the valve, resolving the issue, though the pilots warned that the original test procedure could have missed this hazard during an actual depressurization event.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported being vectored toward mountainous terrain on arrival to MMTO.
summary: The pilot reported that Toluca Approach Control issued headings 140 and 135, placing the aircraft on a collision course with terrain while 20 and 10 miles from a mountain. The pilot refused the second heading, turned back to the PTJ VOR to intercept the ILS for Runway 15, and landed safely.

synopsis: MD11 Captain reports getting low during a visual approach in hazy conditions with the autopilot engaged and ostensibly programed to fly the GPS RNAV approach. Vertical speed had been used for descent and PROF had not been reengaged to follow the vertical path.
summary: The Captain and a new First Officer flew an MD-11 on a visual approach, descending below the FAF altitude due to the Captain's failure to re-engage PROF after an ATC descent clearance. Expectation bias regarding the procedure, distraction monitoring the First Officer, and hazy visibility contributed to the deviation, which was corrected before an uneventful landing.

synopsis: King air Captain reports a taxiway excursion due to a parking brake failure while discussing FMC programing with a new Copilot in the runup area.
summary: During a pre-takeoff check on a single-pilot certified aircraft with a new co-pilot, the pilot discovered an FMC programming error and conducted training, during which the aircraft rolled three feet into grass due to inadequate parking brakes. The pilot attributed the incident to poor brake design, lack of simulator training, and divided attention while mentoring the co-pilot.

synopsis: MU2 First Officer believes that an ongoing feud between Controllers and certain pilots is leading to arrival delays and an unsafe working environment.
summary: The pilot reported that during a visual approach, the Captain questioned unnecessary vectoring for a B737 and requested to speak with the supervisor. The supervisor later accused the crew of improper radio usage, which the pilot denied, attributing the conflict to a mistaken identity with another flight department.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reported landing on 22L when he was cleared for 22R, mentioning that recent re-paving on 22L was a factor.
summary: The pilot landed on Runway 22L instead of 22R at CHD, mistaking the recently repaved 22L for 22R due to complacency from frequent prior operations. The incident occurred because the pilot failed to verbally confirm the clearance or visually verify the runway on final approach.

synopsis: PA-46 pilot reported running off a wet runway when braking proved insufficient.
summary: The pilot of an IFR flight on a short runway overran the wet surface into overgrowth due to late airport detection, a high approach speed for crosswinds, and a rejected go-around. The aircraft sustained no damage and was pushed back, with the pilot citing poor decision-making regarding ILS use and altitude management as causes.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot reported a runway incursion at JLN Runway 31 after failing to recognize the runway critical hold line because of the line's distance from the runway approach end.
summary: The pilot overran the ILS hold position signage while taxiing to Runway 31 due to distraction from checking diagrams and scanning for traffic. The aircraft was stopped safely on the taxiway corner, and ATC waved off an aircraft on final approach.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a less than required landing separation event when the second aircraft refused ATC's go around instruction because of a minimum fuel situation.
summary: Local Control initially instructed a C182 on short final to go-around due to insufficient separation from a C172 on the runway, but cleared it to land after the pilot reported low fuel. Controllers deemed the landing safe despite the C172 being 2,700 feet down the runway, though the C182 pilot later claimed the runway was clear upon crossing the threshold.

synopsis: ZTL Controller voiced concern regarding an adjacent controller allegedly 'dressing-up' a Data Block to indicate procedures were being issued/followed when in fact had not, compromising airspace integrity.
summary: A Sector 32 controller accepted a CRJ2 handoff from Sector 50 with a data block showing descent to FL250, but the aircraft remained at FL270 without clearance. The controller expedited the descent to avoid crossing traffic, resulting in a six-mile miss, and suspected the data block was intentionally falsified.

synopsis: DEN Controller described a potential ground conflict event involving an aircraft under tow transitioning under a Runway 34R lander. The reporter suggested a reassessment of aircraft tail height clearance requirements.
summary: A CRJ2 under tow on Taxiway WB due to hydraulic issues appeared to be at risk of overflight by a CRJ2 on final to Runway 34R. Observers confirmed the landing aircraft passed behind with ample vertical clearance, prompting a request to reassess the 18.55-foot tail height limitation.

synopsis: P50 Controller described a loss of separation event when facility controllers misapplied pre-arranged coordination procedures, the reporter noting this was a repeat of a similar same type event earlier in the year.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported a loss of separation between an Air Carrier X jet and a Small Transport at the same altitude due to misapplied prearranged coordination procedures. The Navajo specialist incorrectly climbed the Small Transport to 10,000 feet instead of maintaining 7,000 feet, causing a conflict with the descending arrival.

synopsis: TRACON Controller reported a TCAS RA event, relating it to the failure of the Flight Data Controller being able to adjust information in the FDIO.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managed a B190, B737, and BE9L during departure and arrival phases, issuing visual separation after a Flight Data operator failed to amend the BE9L's flight plan due to FDIO system proficiency issues. The controller resolved the conflict manually, but reported that insufficient Flight Data staffing and training caused undue workload and delays.

synopsis: P80 Controller described a below MVA event during late night operations involving an arrival routed via an non-standard clearance. The reporter suggested all routing be pre-approved if other than LOA standards.
summary: An A319 crew and controllers were involved when the aircraft descended to 13,000 FT below the 13,400 FT MVA while on an uncoordinated direct routing to BONVL. The controller instructed the crew to maintain terrain separation, and the aircraft landed safely after the crew verified clearance using navigation displays and visual references.

synopsis: ZDC Controller described a loss of separation event when traffic descended without clearance during multiple weather deviations.
summary: An air traffic controller denied a 737's request to descend to 35,000 feet due to conflicting traffic and weather, but the pilot descended anyway, triggering a Conflict Alert and declaring an emergency. The controller handed off the aircraft after the pilot refused to hold, citing undisclosed factors for the unauthorized descent.

synopsis: A320 Captain experiences a dual FMGC lock up while attempting to 'clean up the box' during vectors for approach. This is the second occurrence the reporter has experienced recently.
summary: The Captain reported simultaneous FMS-1 and FMS-2 failures while cleaning up the box on approach to CLE. The reporter noted this was a recurring issue affecting multiple crew members and mechanics, suspecting a problem specific to certain airports.

synopsis: Intermittent static on the communication radios caused the flight crew of a commuter jet to return to their departure airport for maintenance.
summary: During departure, the flight crew experienced severe static on communication radios, likely caused by broken headset pieces left in the panel by ground personnel. The crew returned to the field without declaring an emergency after failing to identify the source or restore clear communications.

synopsis: B737 Captain experiences a lurch to the left when passing V1 during takeoff. Once safely airborne the crew believes a tire failure may have occurred and elects to return to the departure airport after declaring an emergency and burning down to maximum landing weight. Maintenance discovers a nose tire to be severely out of balance.
summary: The pilot reported a sudden left lurch at V1 caused by a severely unbalanced right nose tire, which was initially suspected to be a blowout. After declaring an emergency and burning fuel to 128,000 lbs, the crew landed with a nose-up attitude and vibration, later confirming the tire imbalance during a tow to the gate.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reports a NMAC with a C172 orbiting near the FAF for Runway 28L at PDX. Captain questions the advisability of allowing this aircraft to operate at this location and altitude regardless of its mission.
summary: A commercial crew on the PDX 28L ILS approach encountered a C172 police aircraft orbiting near LAKER NDB at 1,900 feet. The C172 turned into the commercial aircraft's path, triggering a climb RA and resulting in a 200-foot vertical separation at the closest point.

synopsis: An A320 flight crew and ATC at LAX had a conflict over where to hold short of Taxiway P when Westbound on H. The 'quasi' high speed entrance to P at H combined with the lack of any hold short markings were contributing factors.
summary: The flight crew held short of taxiway P on H after clearing runway 25L, but ATC urgently instructed them to move forward, claiming they were blocking the runway. The crew complied, suspecting either a controller error confusing taxiways P and T or inadequate pavement markings for the hold-short position.

synopsis: A320 Captain experiences a loss of airspeed indication and rejects the takeoff at 80 knots.
summary: The Captain aborted the takeoff at 80 KTS due to no airspeed indication on the PFD. The reporter attributed the event to a failure of onboard aircraft systems to provide airspeed information.

synopsis: CE560 Flight Crew describes a runway incursion at IWA.
summary: The flight crew crossed the hold short line of runway 30L while taxiing due to miscommunication regarding taxiway Bravo and distraction from anti-ice checks. ATC issued a stop command after the aircraft crossed the bars by approximately 20 feet, resulting in no traffic conflict.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot on a patient transport flight noted a loss of the air conditioning system followed by a burning smell, so performed a precautionary landing and transfer of the patient to another EMS unit.
summary: During a hospital transport flight, the crew reported air conditioning failure and a burning smell, prompting a precautionary landing after an 'S' turn revealed no visible smoke. The aircraft was secured for patient and crew safety while awaiting maintenance and EMS transfer.

synopsis: A310 flight crew experienced an engine failure and associated generator failure during landing roll at about 80 knots. The Tower reports fire and the engine is shut down and both fire bottles are discharged, although there is no fire indication in the cockpit.
summary: During rollout at 80 KTS, the pilot heard a loud pop and saw a #2 generator light and over-limit indication while Tower reported flames from the right engine. The crew exited the runway, shut down engine #2, discharged both fire bottles, and requested fire truck inspection before taxiing.

synopsis: B737-700 experienced NMAC on downwind at LAX from an aircraft who was not talking to ATC.
summary: Pilots flying a descent to 3,000 feet at LAX received a TCAS RA for uncontacted traffic while 9 DME from Runway 24R. They executed avoidance procedures, leveling off to a slight climb, achieving 400 feet of separation while ATC vectored them away from the conflict.

synopsis: B737-300 flight crew experienced loss of cabin pressure. They descended to 10,000 FT and diverted to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The crew, operating with an MEL requiring a bleeds-off takeoff, experienced a cabin altitude warning at 29,000 feet despite correct switch positions. They performed an emergency descent to 10,000 feet and diverted, noting they failed to complete the abnormal pressurization checklist to manually close the outflow valve.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported stick shaker and 'Airspeed Low' warnings on approach. After a go-around and completion of procedure another approach was executed, where the stick shaker was again alive, triggering another go-around. A third approach was successfully completed.
summary: The Captain and First Officer executed two go-arounds during approach due to false 'Airspeed Low' warnings and stick shaker activation, likely caused by a sensor failure. After declaring a fuel emergency to expedite handling, they completed a safe flaps 15 landing with 2.9 tons of fuel remaining.

synopsis: B767-300 flight crew experience an EICAS message for FWD EQUIP COOLING, followed shortly by a FWD EQUIP OVERHEAT message. QRH procedures are complied with and the flight continues toward Europe. Prior to leaving domestic airspace, another EICAS message for FIRE BTL 1 is displayed, with the FIRE BTL DSCH light is illuminated. The crew elects to return to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew returned to the departure airport during cruise after a #1 cargo fire bottle discharge and forward equipment cooling/overheat warnings. Although Maintenance Control suggested continuing, Dispatch and the captain disagreed, citing the inability to dispatch for ETOPS with the fire bottle discharged.

synopsis: After a go around and an unsuccessful completion of the QRH for a 'steer fail' CAS warning on final approach, the flight crew of an ERJ-170 elected to land and be towed to the gate for maintenance.
summary: The flight crew received a 'Steer Fail' CAS message during approach with gear down, executed a go-around to complete the QRH, and landed with failed steering. No emergency was declared; the aircraft was towed to the gate with minimal delay after maintenance was called.

synopsis: MD-82 flight crew reported TAIL COMP TEMP HIGH light shortly after takeoff. They ran the procedure, declared and emergency, and returned to departure airport.
summary: The flight crew observed a tail compartment temperature warning at 1,400 feet after takeoff, declared an emergency, and returned for an overweight landing of 133,000 lbs. Fire trucks detected no heat in the tail compartment, attributing the only detectable heat to the engines.

synopsis: MD-83 flight crew reported low oil pressure and quantity and rising oil temperature, so the engine was shut down and a divert accomplished to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The First Officer flying at FL330 declared an emergency due to high oil temperature and low quantity on Engine #1, diverting after the initial airport closed. Following QRH checklists, the crew shut down the engine, landed safely, and taxied to the gate after confirming only minor oil dripping.

synopsis: A Contract Line Mechanic reports that a Regional Jet aircraft had reported smoke in the cabin and flight deck on approach. During troubleshooting of the smoke, he noticed evidence of overheating at the left-hand ceiling ballast fixture and disconnected the electrical connectors at both ends of the fixture, but had failed to include the information when deferring the light assembly.
summary: A mechanic investigated smoke reported in the cabin and flight deck during final approach, finding overheating at left ceiling light fixtures in Rows One and Two. Although the MEL required no action, the mechanic disconnected and bagged the light connectors and ballasts to eliminate potential ignition sources.

synopsis: A Maintenance Controller reports that he instructed Line Maintenance personnel at Station ZZZ to decommission the #2 Engine Thrust Reverser per MEL 78-31 on a B757-200 ETOPS aircraft by capping the hydraulic actuator return line fitting at the engine firewall.
summary: Line Maintenance reported a leak in the #2 engine thrust reverser actuator return line on an ETOPS aircraft. Maintenance Control instructed them to decommission the reverser per MEL 78-31-00 and cap the firewall fitting to prevent fluid drainage.

synopsis: A Westwind 24 Captain reported that he failed to properly document a hydraulic problem in the maintenance log, citing the pressure of a long assignment away from home as a factor.
summary: The pilot experienced a nose gear unsafe light and hydraulic low pressure warnings on final approach, which resolved before landing. Post-flight inspection revealed a hydraulic leak from a pump plug caused by a prior undocumented repair following a fuel truck collision, attributed to the pilot's failure to log the maintenance.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: IFR Corporate aircraft on descent for DTN experienced a conflict event noting frustration with the ATC services provided given the known existing conditions.
summary: A pilot arriving at DTN on IFR was vectored by SHV Approach over the airport and cleared for a visual approach while unable to see the runway. The pilot was subsequently instructed to stop descending because another aircraft was on final 500 feet below, which the reporter attributed to poor controller planning.

synopsis: BE20 Captain reports avionics circuit breaker tripping during ILS approach in VMC. The approach is continued and the circuit breaker is reset and stays in long enough to communicate and declare an emergency.
summary: A pilot conducting an FAA check ride in an aircraft equipped with a G500 lost all avionics due to a tripped 30-amp circuit breaker while vectored for an ILS Runway 4 approach. After reducing electrical load to reset the breaker, the pilot declared an emergency, received light-gun signals, and landed safely.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported an NMAC with another light aircraft who was using the wrong CTAF frequency at TPF airport.
summary: A pilot flying a left closed pattern at TPF received a TCAS alert on left base for Runway 22 and executed a go-around after spotting a low-wing aircraft 300 feet ahead and 200 feet below. The other pilot, cleared for a visual approach by Tampa TRACON, had mistakenly used the VDF approach plate and transmitted on the wrong frequency.

synopsis: HS-125 First Officer reported severe turbulence encounter that resulted in 4,800 FPM uncommanded rate of climb from 32,000 FT to 33,800 FT before control was regained.
summary: The crew encountered unforecast heavy precipitation and severe turbulence west of MXQ VOR in IMC, causing autopilot and yaw damper disengagement and a 4,800 FPM climb. Control was regained at 33,800 FT, after which the Captain notified ATC of the deviation and filed a PIREP.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reports leaving his seat at FL240 to open the cockpit door for the Captain returning from his bathroom break.
summary: During the approach phase, the First Officer and Captain simultaneously swapped seats while a flight attendant remained in the cockpit, leaving both pilot seats unoccupied for approximately five seconds. The reporter attributed this deviation from standard security procedures to a momentary lapse in judgment, noting no emergency occurred during the brief interval.

synopsis: The single pilot of a CE560 was advised by departure Controller that he had climbed to 2,000 MSL prematurely while departing TEB on the RUUDY RNAV SID although he believed he had maintained 1,500 MSL to WENTZ as charted prior to climbing to 2,000 MSL.
summary: The pilot departed TEB on Runway 24 via the RUUDY 4 SID but received conflicting altitude instructions from the Departure Controller to maintain 1,500 feet until an unclear fix. The pilot attributed the confusion to last-minute clearance changes and noted no other aircraft were affected.

synopsis: Unfamiliar with the complex taxiway structure at RJTT, the Captain of a Falcon 900 mistook L-9 for Lima after crossing Runway 04 at T-6, thus encroaching on Runway 16R/34L. After holding the Falcon short, ATC directed a B-747 inbound to 34L to make a go around and then rerouted the Falcon to the departure end of the runway.
summary: The Captain of an aircraft taxiing at RJTT mistakenly entered high-speed exit L9 instead of Taxiway L due to a zoomed-out diagram and complex intersection markings. This caused a 747 on final to go around while the crew held short of Runway 34L until cleared to continue.

synopsis: A Mooney M20J pilot reported getting a low altitude alert from the CDW Tower on visual approach to Runway 4.
summary: A pilot flying a Mooney on a visual approach to Runway 4 at Caldwell received a low altitude alert at 2,000 feet MSL while descending slowly. Distracted by the alert and a passenger, the pilot arrested the descent, remained high, and executed a steeper-than-average final to land.

synopsis: King Air F90 Captain reported landing gear failed to extend, but alternate method did get the gear down. Normal landing ensued.
summary: The King Air F90 experienced a normal hydraulic landing gear extension failure during approach. The crew successfully extended the gear using the manual emergency procedure, executed an uneventful landing, and taxied to the ramp for maintenance.

synopsis: When a PA-28 pilot concentrated excessively on clearance from another aircraft when exiting the runup area for Runway 07 at VGT it unwittingly crossed the hold short lines for the runway. ATC cleared him to cross and then discussed the trangression with the pilot prior to takeoff. The reporter believed lack of sleep due to being in Las Vegas over night was a contributing factor.
summary: The pilot crossed a runway hold short line at North Las Vegas Airport while taxiing from the Runway 7 runup area to Taxiway Gulf. The incident was caused by fatigue and unfamiliarity with the airport markings, compounded by fixation on clearing another aircraft.

aircraft: M-20 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: M20 pilot reports landing just before an approaching thunderstorm then having to 'fly' his aircraft for 20 minutes in torrential rain and 55 KT winds while sitting on the ramp, with the engine running.
summary: A pilot flying VFR to pick up his daughter landed at an airport just as a microburst and lightning struck, causing 55-knot gusts that weather-vaned the aircraft on the ramp. The pilot attributed the incident to a false sense of security from recent weather encounters and goal-oriented judgment, though the aircraft sustained no damage.

synopsis: C182 pilot lost power and landed in a field after trying to troubleshoot some fuel system anomalies. Unclear whether the aircraft was out of fuel or if operator error caused power loss.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 182Q experienced an in-flight engine power loss during cruise at 11,000 feet, forcing an off-airport landing in a pasture with minor damage but no injuries. The pilot attributed the failure to potential fuel selector valve mismanagement after observing abnormally high fuel flow readings.

synopsis: C172 pilot reports landing at a military field due to a rough running engine.
summary: The pilot made an emergency landing at a military field due to engine misfiring.

synopsis: G550 First Officer laments the requirement to use oxygen continuously above FL410, especially when the comfort position of the mask is inoperative, believing that the Automatic Descent Mode (ADM) in the autopilot should eliminate the requirement for both pilots to be on oxygen.
summary: The flying crew removed their oxygen masks during high-altitude cruise on an extended international trip due to inoperative comfort positions causing headaches and fatigue. They descended to FL410 once adequate fuel reserves were met, while the PIC rested, and the reporter suggested rule changes regarding long-duration mask use.

synopsis: A C150 lost electrical power while a student pilot flew a cross country. He returned to the departure airport where a conflict developed with an air carrier and he executed a go around because of an unstabilized approach.
summary: A solo pilot experienced total electrical and radio failure 20 miles from departure, squawking 7600. Gusty conditions and lack of flaps caused a go-around at 10 feet, but the pilot landed safely on runway 17R after a second attempt.

synopsis: A Line Maintenance Lead Technician reports that a B757-300 flight crew took off after reporting a compressor stall during their initial takeoff roll, without returning to the gate for a Visual Inspection of their engines.
summary: A maintenance controller received a report of a compressor stall on Flight XXX, Aircraft X, and cleared the crew to restart engines after confirming no recent engine history. The controller noted the radio was garbled and the maintenance room was overcrowded, but the flight proceeded to takeoff without an aborted departure or fire.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A pilot back taxied on the closed section of LFT Runway 22L because of confusion about the actual runway length and the lack of runway closure barriers.
summary: The Pilot in Command and Co-Captain of a Learjet taxied onto a closed blast pad at Lafayette (LFT) during takeoff preparation for Runway 22L. The incident resulted from conflicting information regarding available runway length and a lack of NOTAMs for the temporary blast pad, leading to a potential pilot deviation investigation.

synopsis: A PA-31 lost pressurization at 15,000 FT, so the pilot declared an emergency and began a descent to 10,000 FT before ATC acknowledged because they were slow responding.
summary: The pilot experienced lost cabin pressurization at 15,000 feet and initiated an emergency descent to 10,000 feet after receiving no immediate response to their initial call. ATC acknowledged the emergency and cleared the descent at 14,700 feet.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ZJX Controller described a confused routing situation during multiple weather deviation procedures, the reporter indicated planning was absent with regard to weather re-routes.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller in ZJX Sector 71 reported that multiple Air Carrier aircraft inbound to CLT encountered severe turbulence and were routed into extreme precipitation due to delayed arrival closures and lack of coordinated weather avoidance plans. The controller noted that New York Center refused northeast traffic due to weather and frequency outages, forcing aircraft to accept uncomfortable routings or deviate while facing potential fuel issues.

synopsis: CNO Controller described an unauthorized Class D entry event during IFR conditions permitted by SCT controllers. The reporter noted that SCT controllers are in need of SVFR refresher information.
summary: A C177 pilot entered CNO Class D airspace VFR while weather was below minimums (4 miles visibility, 800 FT ceiling) without requesting SVFR. The Local Controller denied landing clearance, causing the pilot to divert to RAL, while the reporter attributed the incident to the Approach Controller's lack of SVFR knowledge and improper coordination.

synopsis: B757 First Officer reports a fatigue call after being unable to get proper rest for a flight departing 24 hours after arriving on a Red Eye flight.
summary: A fatigued pilot reported being unfit to fly after accepting a short-call assignment following an all-night flight from Hawaii. The pilot cited insufficient rest, having slept only five hours after being awake for over 24 hours, and criticized the airline's unsafe scheduling practices.

synopsis: A320 Captain lost his airspeed indicator on takeoff roll. Rejected takeoff executed and aircraft was returned to the gate.
summary: The Captain reported no airspeed indication on their side during takeoff. The crew aborted the takeoff and returned to the gate.

synopsis: Air Carrier with ZMA inbound to FLL experienced a conflict event reportedly resulting from a VIP TFR that was creating an overload situation for the Controller handling the flight.
summary: During cruise at FL380, an A319 crew encountered a TCAS alert and a B757 conflict due to Miami Center controller overload from VIP TFRs. The controller issued conflicting turns and descents, resulting in a near-miss where the B757 passed just above the A319 before separation was restored.

synopsis: A C-182RG pilot departing HND was given a Terrain Alert by ATC when he improperly maintained his climb rate at or above 481 feet per minute, rather than the 481 feet per mile as required for terrain clearance.
summary: The pilot departed HND and incorrectly maintained a climb rate of 481 feet per minute instead of per mile, triggering an altitude alert. The pilot corrected the issue with a shuttle climb, confirmed they never deviated from the routing, and attributed the error to misinterpreting the climb gradient requirement.

synopsis: PA-32 pilot on a VFR flight encountered unforcast weather on climb out and remained at low altitude in marginal conditions until able to climb to VFR On Top and proceed to destination.
summary: A non-instrument rated pilot departed in VFR conditions but encountered unexpected low fog and IFR conditions at 450 feet AGL shortly after takeoff. After ATC advised climbing above reported cloud tops at 1,300 feet, the pilot climbed to 900 feet, regained visibility, and completed the flight safely.

synopsis: A B737 aircraft failed to pressurize after takeoff. A rear service door was found to be improperly closed. They did not have a warning light in the cockpit.
summary: A newly hired pilot reported that a 737 failed to pressurize during climb due to an improperly closed right rear service door left by a caterer. The crew diverted for maintenance without declaring an emergency, later questioning the lack of cockpit door indicators and the legality of the dispatch paperwork.

synopsis: An aircraft on final had to execute a go around when an M20 pilot, unfamiliar with the airport and uncomfortable with radio communications, inadvertently crossed the runway hold short lines.
summary: The pilot mistakenly crossed Runway 34 hold short lines while taxiing to Runway 34, causing an aircraft on final to go around. The incident resulted from the pilot's error in crossing without clearance while rushing to depart VFR before worsening weather.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot reported a near miss on short final to RBW after making the recommended traffic reports which were not acknowledged by the other pilot.
summary: A pilot flying an ILS approach to Runway 23 at RBW reported a 200-foot separation with another aircraft on final, which neither crew saw nor heard. The other pilot later advised the reporter of the proximity and stated he executed a go-around.

synopsis: A B737-800 Flight Crew had some internal confusion on how to deal with an intermittent wheel well fire warning. They decided to divert as a precaution.
summary: During departure near FL250, a transient wheel well fire warning illuminated and sounded, extinguishing before the crew could complete the first checklist step. After consulting Company at FL340, the crew landed as soon as possible with no further complications, noting that missing dispatch frequencies caused distraction.

synopsis: Unresolved confusion between Clearance Delivery and the flight crew of a B757-200 as to the track by which the flight was to arrive at FIXIT waypoint resulted in a deviation.
summary: The flight crew departed LAX on the new FIXIT1 RNAV departure, mistakenly flying the procedure instead of following radar vectors due to a vague clearance and fixation on speed restrictions. This confusion arose from ambiguous instructions regarding "radar vectors to a SID" and a lack of specific heading assignments from Tower.

synopsis: An air carrier Captain was cleared to LAS Runway 25R via Taxiway C but taxied onto Taxiway Q from the East Ramp near Spot 1 because he was confused by a C painted on the taxiway which made it appear to him that Taxiway Q was Taxiway C.
summary: The flight crew mistakenly turned onto Taxiway Q instead of Taxiway C while taxiing for departure, relying on a black "C" sign they believed identified the correct taxiway. Ground Control corrected the error and recleared them via Taxiway R, resulting in no traffic conflicts.

synopsis: A SFO Air Carrier departure from the Runway 1 complex aborted take off due to an EICAS message and was directed by ATC to hold short of Runway 28R. ATC decision was questioned by the reporter given the circumstances.
summary: The flight crew aborted takeoff at 88 knots due to an R Eng Hi Stage EICAS message and exited onto Runway 28L after Tower instructed them to hold short of Runway 28R. The crew questioned receiving a crossing runway clearance during an abort, noting that an aircraft on Runway 28L was subsequently told to go around.

synopsis: While deviating around weather and in moderate precipitation an EMB145 flight crew encountered widely divergent airspeed indications among the Captain's, First Officer's and Standby airspeed indicators. They initially were aware only that the Captain's speed was gradually decreasing and, only after receiving a mach overspeed warning, did they cross check and notice the First Officer's was touching the Barber Pole. They wrote up the event but failed to note the maintenance response when they flew the airplane the following day--when it operated normally.
summary: During cruise at FL360, the crew encountered conflicting airspeed and altitude indications attributed to suspected water in the pitot systems while avoiding weather. After declaring an emergency and descending to FL200, all instruments eventually matched, and maintenance later found no water despite the initial belief.

synopsis: A Fractional jet flight crew observed parachute jumpers near UUU and took evasive action to avoid a collision while on vectors to a visual approach at EWB.
summary: A pilot and second-in-command flying a visual approach to EWB at 3,000 feet encountered tandem parachutists while vectored by ATC. The crew avoided a collision by manually banking left after the second-in-command spotted the jumpers, attributing the safe outcome to their vigilance despite conflicting ATC information.

synopsis: B717 Captain describes anomalous FMS operation that seems to occur only when the KRANN1 arrival to BOS is loaded. When the MANUAL track after KRANN is deleted the The FMS returns to normal operation.
summary: A Boeing 717-200 pilot reported that the KRANN ONE RNAV arrival into Boston caused uncommanded level-offs and FMS descent mode errors during climb due to a corrupt "KRA075" manual heading entry. Deleting this specific manual heading restored normal FMS climb and cruise operations.

synopsis: A Q400 Captain reported high workload after takeoff and failure to open the pneumatic bleeds, resulting in the aircraft's failure to pressurize. When bleeds were opened, normal operation resumed.
summary: The pilot forgot to turn on the bleeds after takeoff due to FMS programming errors and icing equipment selection. A cabin altitude warning occurred at 10,000 ft during descent, but the light extinguished after the bleeds were restored before reaching 7,000 ft.

synopsis: A CE-560XLS flight crew crossed the hold short line of Runway 31L at MDW when they were unaware the line was almost immediately after they turned left off the parallel Taxiway F.
summary: The pilot reported that while taxiing at MDW, the aircraft's nose crossed the hold short line for runway 31L immediately after turning left onto taxiway K. The pilot attributed the incursion to the unexpected proximity of the hold short line and suggested a clearance to hold short of taxiway K would prevent recurrence.

synopsis: A B1900 flight crew, after back-taxiing on Runway 14 and announcing their movements on CTAF at a non-towered airport, moved off centerline to avoid conflict with a Cessna that departed on Runway 32.
summary: The pilot back-taxied on Runway 14 while a Cessna departed Runway 32, creating a potential conflict due to a runway hump blocking visibility. The reporter attributed the incident to the Cessna pilot likely failing to realize that Runway 32 is the reciprocal of Runway 14.

synopsis: A Maintenance Inspector, Maintenance Supervisor, company Engineer and a Mechanic report drain holes were not drilled at a repair doubler on the lower surface of the Right-Hand Horizontal Stabilizer of a B737-800 aircraft prior to departure.
summary: Maintenance personnel discovered missing drain holes on a B737-800's horizontal stabilizer doubler after C-Check release, caused by an Engineering Authorization that deviated from the Structural Repair Manual without addressing the holes. The holes were drilled at the gate, the item was deferred, and the aircraft returned to service following clarification from Engineering.

synopsis: A PA31 pilot returned to land because a 'snap down' oil dip stick lock opened after takeoff allowing a passenger to detect the streaming oil.
summary: The pilot of a C208 reported a right engine oil leak at 1,000 feet caused by a failed snap-down dipstick that popped up during flight. The crew returned for a safe landing, evacuated passengers due to smoke, and grounded the aircraft, recommending a modification to screw-in dipsticks.

synopsis: A DA-40 pilot making an unplanned fuel stop at HTO, landed without a clearance. He was unaware of the presence of a temporary Control Tower.
summary: The pilot landed at HTO without contacting the temporary Tower, relying on CTAF and a release from Providence Approach that omitted the Tower's existence. The incident occurred because neither the temporary Tower nor Approach advised the pilot of the active temporary control in Class G airspace.

synopsis: Cessna 152 pilot transiting CNO airspace reported an NMAC with a helicopter climbing out of CNO. Reporter contends that more maneuverable helicopter should have maintained separation from the reported Cessna traffic.
summary: A pilot in cruise at 2,000 FT MSL northwest of Chino Airport encountered a departing twin-turbine helicopter that accelerated and climbed directly toward their aircraft. The pilot maneuvered to avoid a collision as the helicopter passed beneath them, attributing the hazard to the helicopter pilot's failure to slow down or maintain altitude despite having excellent visibility.

synopsis: A Line Maintenance Supervisor describes how assumptions and a lack of clear communications between himself and a Line Mechanic led to a B757-200 aircraft departing with the Emergency Slide Light inoperative at Door-4R.
summary: A ground supervisor reported that a B757-200 mechanic cleared a Door-4R arming issue by removing debris but failed to defer the resulting inoperative emergency slide light. The mechanic allegedly left the decision to dispatch the aircraft with the defect to the supervisor after consulting the flight crew, bypassing standard maintenance procedures.

synopsis: ZDV Controller described a weather deviation event when the separation required was questioned because both terminal and enroute procedures were involved.
summary: An air traffic controller intervened when Aircraft X deviated right toward Aircraft Y near Denver, creating a potential conflict. The controller issued a heading change and expedited climb to ensure separation, questioning which facility was responsible for maintaining the required 5-mile standard.

synopsis: ZOB Controller described a probable MOA incursion event involving an IFR aircraft electing to transverse the area, the reporter questioning the applicable procedures involved in this instance.
summary: An ATC trainee allowed an aircraft to traverse the active MISTY MOA after confirming no military traffic was present and IFR separation could be provided. Although the military desk later prohibited entry, the controller maintained the aircraft's course, questioning if a violation occurred given the continuous separation.

synopsis: LAX Controller voiced concern regarding a ground conflict resulting from the handling provided by 'Ramp Control;' The reporter suggested Ramp Controller operations be terminated for safety concerns.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported that Aircraft X ignored instructions to hold for an outbound Airbus on Taxiway 1 and taxied to its gate while communicating with the Company Ramp Tower. The controller warned this unauthorized movement created a potential collision risk with other aircraft, attributing the issue to ineffective ramp tower operations at LAX.

synopsis: Large transport aircraft being vectored for approach to BFI, responded to a TCAS RA and experienced an NMAC with 'pop-up' traffic that had just activated the aircraft's transponder.
summary: A BFI approach crew on a vector for 13R encountered a TCAS conflict with an unidentified aircraft that had just activated its transponder. The crew executed a TCAS climb, passing the target 100–200 feet above it, before ATC re-cleared them to their original approach vector and altitude.

synopsis: After accepting a B767-300 with a history of air/ground logic anomalies for a short turn-a-round sequence, the flight crew was confronted with a flap asymmetry condition for landing after the outbound leg. Their Maintenance Department was also receiving automated fault condition warnings that had previously been precursors to multiple previous flap and speedbrake anomalies. After completing a safe approach and landing the flight crew wrote the aircraft up as unfit for further flight.
summary: The flight crew of a Boeing 757/767 encountered recurring air/ground logic anomalies and an LE SLAT ASYMMETRY message during the approach phase. They declared an emergency, completed the checklist, and landed safely, subsequently refusing to fly the aircraft until the recurring fault was corrected.

synopsis: An A320's autothrottle transitioned to THRUST LOCK followed by the number one engine spooling back. The crew declared an emergency, but the engine returned to normal operation with no autothrottles.
summary: During arrival after thunderstorm deviation, the crew experienced autothrottle failure and a Number 1 engine thrust rollback, prompting an emergency declaration. Control of the engine was restored within one minute, but the autothrust remained inoperative for the remainder of the flight to ZZZ1.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A flight crew departing MSN failed to hold short of the Runway 3 approach critical line on Taxiway L5 prior to entering Taxiway A because they were not expecting nor did they see the hold lines at that location.
summary: The flight crew inadvertently crossed the Runway 03 approach hold short line while turning from Taxiway L5 to Alpha due to late ATC clearance, lack of markings, and the line's proximity to the turn. Ground Control confirmed the incursion but cleared the aircraft to continue taxiing to Runway 36 without requiring paperwork.

synopsis: EMB145 Flight Crew taking off with micro bursts in the area experiences a stall warning with stick shaker activation shortly after takeoff. The Capitan responds with maximum power and lowers the nose but the warnings continue as airspeed increases. After running the QRH procedure for Inadvertent Stall Protection Activation, the warnings cease and the crew elects to divert to a suitable airport for an uneventful landing. Maintenance discovers that the Captain's angle of attack vane is bent.
summary: During takeoff, the crew experienced inadvertent stall protection activation caused by a bent Captain's AOA sensor, initially misinterpreting it as windshear. They executed a stall recovery, diverted to ZZZ, and landed safely after maintenance confirmed the equipment failure.

synopsis: B767 international departure experiences compressor stall near V1. Flight continued takeoff, emergency declared, fuel dumped, and the flight returned to departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced a left engine compressor stall at V1 during departure, continued the takeoff, dumped fuel, and landed overweight without injury. The pilot attributed the stall to unknown causes, noted difficulties with emergency procedure tracking and VOR navigation, and recommended improved training and legal support for international operations.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Because they were flying in CAVU daylight conditions and were familiar with the area the flight crew of an unidentified Part 91 passenger flight aircraft chose not to respond to an apparently anomalous EGPWS 'Terrain' warning.
summary: During initial climb, a pilot received a single GPWS "terrain" warning while turning south at 2,000 feet MSL, likely triggered by an 878-foot tower. The crew did not take evasive action due to visual confirmation of clear terrain, and the flight continued without incident.

synopsis: A Maintenance Controller and Line Mechanic describe their involvement with a DHC-8-300 aircraft that returned to field after the Nose Landing Gear (NLG) would not retract. The aircraft was on a scheduled Maintenance Ferry Flight to replace a leaking hydraulic line to the Solonoid Valve at the Steering Actuator.
summary: A Maintenance Controller authorized capping a leaking nose gear hydraulic line on a DHC-8-300 for a ferry flight, causing the nose gear to fail to retract after takeoff. The aircraft returned safely using alternate extension, and the reporter concluded the line should not have been capped and the ferry should have been conducted gear down.

synopsis: Pilot of a small aircraft encounted a downdraft while flying by a National Monument site and descended lower than planned, but did not violate FAR restrictions.
summary: The solo pilot in a slow aircraft diverted from a planned route to investigate the Crazy Horse monument, encountering sinking air that reduced horizontal clearance to 1,500–2,000 feet. The pilot attributes the deviation from planned safety margins to poor planning and distraction by ground features, though no regulations were violated.

synopsis: PA-24 pilot lost his primary flight instruments shortly after takeoff because of a defective pitot-static system.
summary: During a flight test of new avionics, the pilot experienced primary instrument failure on departure due to a contaminated pitot tube and static leak. The pilot transitioned to backup instruments, deviated from assigned vectors, and landed safely without declaring an emergency.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot reported a JST Runway 23 incursion on Taxiway E because he did not expect the hold short line to be at such a great distance from the Runway threshold.
summary: The pilot inadvertently crossed the hold short line on Taxiway Echo while taxiing to Runway 23, stopping approximately 20 feet past the line. The Tower confirmed the incursion, noted it occurs frequently due to the line's distant placement, and cleared the aircraft for takeoff.

synopsis: A C150 lost engine power in the practice area. The Instructor assumed control, declared an emergency, and was able to safely return to the airport.
summary: The instructor pilot of a Cessna 150 declared an emergency during practice maneuvers after the engine ran rough and failed to maintain 2,600 feet MSL. The aircraft descended to 1,500 feet MSL where level flight was possible, resulting in an uneventful landing at the airport.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: An inexperienced Private Pilot in an unidentified tricycle gear airplane lost control and ground looped the aircraft while attempting to expedite his exit from the runway to facilitate the subsequent departure of an airliner holding short.
summary: The pilot ground looped the aircraft while turning left onto a taxiway at excessive speed after landing, caused by locking the right main tire due to poor braking. The incident resulted from self-imposed pressure to clear the runway quickly for a departing Airbus, compounded by the pilot's inexperience and the aircraft's directional instability.

synopsis: An A36 pilot landed off airport when the engine quit because of fuel starvation after the left wing fuel cap streamed fuel while the right tank was half full.
summary: The pilot experienced an abrupt engine power loss at 8,000 feet while descending for a visual approach, forcing a soft-field landing in sagebrush that folded the nosewheel. The incident was caused by fuel starvation from an empty left tank, despite the gauge indicating half full, leaving the pilot uninjured.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a VIP TFR incursion when facility briefings and coordination failed.
summary: A Radar instructor reported that a Citation Excel violated a Presidential TFR in Sector X while controllers were distracted drawing new CAP and ANCHORs. The violation occurred due to late briefings, excessive phone calls, and confusion regarding whether fractional operators were permitted in the restricted airspace.

synopsis: TRACON Controller providing OJT described a confused 'low fuel' event when inbound general aviation traffic indicated the need to fly toward the airport with all haste. The reporter listed the need for cleared communications between the pilot and ATC would have prevented this incident.
summary: A trainee controller managed a fuel-starved C206 and a following B737, issuing conflicting altitude clearances due to traffic and frequency congestion. The C206 pilot reported engine issues before recovering, while the supervisor noted the pilot delayed declaring an emergency despite critical fuel status.

synopsis: PDX Controller described a developing conflict event between a PDX Air Carrier arrival for Runway 28L and Cessna conducting a NDB Approach to TTD. The reporter noted the TRACON should have provided more spacing.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a potential conflict between a Cessna on an NDB approach to Troutdale and a B737 on final for Portland 28L at the same altitude. The controller attributed the close proximity to the B737 failing to maintain adequate separation or advise of visual contact during the Cessna's practice approach.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: ROA Controller described a below MVA event during a busy/complex traffic period when an incorrect altitude read back went unnoticed. The reporter listed poor RADAR coverage as an added distraction contributing to the incident.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller at Roanoke East RADAR issued a descent clearance to 5,200 feet to Air Carrier Y, but the pilot read back 2,500 feet. The controller failed to hear the incorrect readback due to high workload and poor radar coverage, resulting in the aircraft descending below the assigned altitude.

synopsis: MSP Controller described an ASDE-X go around command resulting in a potential conflict. The Controller indicated that controllers should have alarm overriding authority when involved traffic is obviously not a factor.
summary: An air traffic controller at MSP initiated a go-around for a CRJ on Runway 30L due to an ASDE-X alarm, despite the conflicting departing CRJ being clear of the runway. The controller reported that strict adherence to the computer logic unnecessarily placed the CRJ and an Airbus on converging paths when visual separation existed.

synopsis: TEB Controller described a conflict event between an IFR ILS 19 aircraft an an unknown VFR aircraft clear of restricted airspace. The reporter noted this type of event is common during Runway 19 operations because of the current airspace configurations.
summary: A Challenger 300 on an ILS approach to Runway 19 received a Resolution Advisory and descended to 1,900 feet to avoid an uncontrolled VFR aircraft squawking 1200. The pilot reported the target was too fast and close to see, attributing the conflict to unmonitored airspace north of Teterboro.

synopsis: A B737-300 flight crew experienced a loss of cabin pressure climbing through FL320. They declared an emergency, descended and diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: The crew experienced intermittent TCAS failure and a cabin altitude warning at FL320, triggering an emergency descent and overweight landing. Maintenance Control attributed the multiple system failures, including the pressurization fault, to a likely faulty air/ground sensor.

synopsis: An A320 flight crew experienced failed autothrust capability and, after analysing their capabilities and the weather, continued utilizing continued to their destination using manual flight and thrust controls.
summary: The crew at FL190 experienced an uncommanded idle retardation of engine 1 with Auto Thrust warnings, prompting an emergency declaration. After disconnecting the autopilot and manually verifying normal engine operation, they rescinded the emergency and completed a safe hand-flown approach.

synopsis: A B737-700 Captain discussed the problems he encountered upon losing both FMCs in RVSM airspace and subsequently finding several of the VORs by which they attempted to navigate an airways clearance were out of service although not NOTAMed to be so.
summary: The flight crew experienced a dual FMC failure over the Florida panhandle, losing area navigation and encountering multiple non-functional VORs. They completed a visual approach after ATC vectors, but maintenance deferred both FMCs under the MEL, allowing the aircraft to continue service without functional FMCs.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain noticed abnormal brake temperatures after arrival. Inspection revealed right inboard brake quick disconnect line not connected.
summary: The pilot reported abnormal BTMS readouts on the right main gear after arrival. Maintenance found the hydraulic line quick connect to the right inboard brake was disconnected, reconnected it, and the system operated normally for subsequent flights.

synopsis: Although it reset and operated normally, the flight crew of a B757-200 opted to return to their departure airport when their EICAS advised the right generator was off.
summary: The pilot experienced a standby gyro off flag during taxi and a Right Generator Off EICAS message after takeoff. After resetting the generator and completing checklists in the local area, the crew returned to the runway for an uneventful landing.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reports a loud vibrating, pounding noise passing FL230. When ATC communications become nearly impossible the crew elects to declare an emergency and return to the departure airport. At FL200 in the descent the noise disappears and a normal landing ensues.
summary: During climbout to FL300, pilots experienced severe vibration, deafening noise, and a burning electrical odor near the First Officer's right foot, causing radio communication loss. The crew declared an emergency, donned masks, and returned for an uneventful landing with no visual smoke or fire observed.

synopsis: CRJ-700 Captain reported acrid smell from APU after landing. At gate a momentary APU fire warning resulted in APU shutdown, but no fire found by CFR.
summary: Crew reported an acrid APU smell and bleed open caution during taxi, followed by a momentary fire warning and self-shutdown at the gate. Firefighters found no evidence of fire while passengers were deplaning, and maintenance was notified.

synopsis: A Captain and First Officer report about the need for clearer wording of MEL 74-1 when deferring Engine Ignition Systems Channel-A or-B on CRJ-700 aircraft. They had performed a Flight Crew Placard under the direction of Maintenance Control and departed with Channel-A Ignition inoperative on both engines.
summary: The Captain and Maintenance Control incorrectly applied MEL 74-1 to placard Ignition-A faults on both engines, believing one channel per engine was sufficient. The reporter attributes this error to a confusing MEL procedure that failed to explicitly prohibit deferring Ignition-A on both engines simultaneously.

synopsis: An E-140 flight crew declared an emergency and landed uneventfully following loss of their Number One Hydraulic System.
summary: The crew experienced a Hydraulic System 1 failure in flight, declared an emergency, and followed AOM procedures. They executed a normal landing with flaps 45 and were subsequently towed to the gate.

synopsis: An ERJ-135 Captain provided a detailed example of what he believes to be routine overly optimistic fuel burns planned for flights using the methodology applied by his airline to determine the fuel required. The fuel burnouts thus proposed may result in planned arrivals with fuel quantity caution lights illuminated.
summary: The pilot reported that company fuel planning failed to account for ATC vectoring and sequencing, resulting in actual burn exceeding planned estimates. Consequently, the pilot frequently requested additional fuel to avoid landing with reserves in the red warning range or insufficient fuel for a go-around.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew reported problem with nose gear. They declared an emergency and returned to departure airport.
summary: During climb through 14,000 feet, the crew received a nose gear disagree warning and returned to the departure airport for an overweight landing. Although the crew requested maintenance notification via ACARS, the local mechanic arrived unaware of the return, indicating the dispatcher failed to relay the message.

synopsis: B747-400 Captain reported noticing low oil quantity on three of his engines. Shortly after alerting company, #4 oil quantity and pressure dropped to a level low enough that the Captain declared an emergency and diverted to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The pilot reported low oil quantity and pressure on three engines while enroute at 33,000 feet, with Engine #4 subsequently dropping further. An emergency was declared, resulting in a safe diversion and termination of the flight at the nearest suitable airport.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew experienced flap failure on approach, and landed uneventfully after running the complex procedures.
summary: During descent, the Captain and First Officer experienced a flap malfunction where the flaps failed to extend. They declared an emergency, followed extensive QRH procedures, and subsequently landed uneventfully on the longest runway.

synopsis: Despite having been advised of recent anti-skid failures--one of which was on the proceeding flight but not written up because 'it was already in the logbook'--the flight crew of a DC-10 took the aircraft without maintenance attention and, upon landing approach were faced with yet another failure. Their problem compounded by poor decisions as to runway selection and flap settings, they suffered blown tires upon landing and required a tow to their gate.
summary: During an IOE landing with a known anti-skid history, the crew selected flaps 35 and early gear extension, resulting in an anti-skid failure and two blown tires after brake application. The reporter attributed the tire damage to insufficient braking speed and runway length, noting that the previous crew failed to write up the recurring anti-skid issue.

synopsis: Three commuter jets suffered conflicts with one another on the ramp at CLT when two CRJ's--cleared via ramp control subsequent to the reporter's ERJ-175--taxied aggressively to cut out the reporter's aircraft and gain prior access to the ramp 'spot' for receiving an ATC taxi clearance.
summary: An ERJ-175 and two CRJs experienced a taxiway conflict at CLT Ramp when the first CRJ failed to yield as instructed, causing both to stop. The incident resulted from poor communication and radio monitoring, though all aircraft eventually reached Spot 2 and the flight proceeded successfully.

synopsis: EMB-145LR First Officer reported Captain selected the wrong localizer frequency on approach to ORD that led to a small lateral deviation before the crew and ATC noticed.
summary: The Captain, acting as flying pilot, mistakenly tuned the localizer for Runway 27L instead of 27R while intercepting. The error was immediately identified by the flight crew and ATC, prompting a correction before the Approach Checklist was run.

synopsis: CE-560SL flight crew reported ACM overheat on takeoff on a very warm day. They ran the procedure, declared an emergency, and returned to departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced an ACM overheat and emergency pressurization activation during takeoff roll in extreme heat, likely caused by prolonged APU operation. They declared an emergency, landed with priority, and returned to the FBO after completing checklists on the ground.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported multiple laser strikes in the vicinity of SBGR airport, and commented on how common this has become at that airport.
summary: The flight crew of CGO1 departing SBGR encountered three separate green laser illuminations during climb between 2,000 and 8,000 feet AGL. Pre-flight briefing and operational measures prevented direct eye contact, though the crew noted multiple ground sources and suggested replacing sun shades with laser-absorbing versions.

synopsis: B777-200 flight crew experienced a track heading deviation immediately after takeoff while on the JTEEE1 RNAV SID off Runway 18C at MEM.
summary: The flight crew of a Boeing 777 departed Runway 18C with a PDC clearance for JTEEE1 but deleted waypoints from the FMC that matched the RNAV SID. A subsequent conflict arose when Departure cleared them to CHETO, a deleted waypoint, while the crew maintained they were cleared direct to JTEEE based on their PDC and ATC confirmation.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported lax security procedures by boarding agent at EWR.
summary: A gate agent in Newark failed to verify crew IDs before allowing access to the jetway, claiming they did not look like terrorists. The First Officer subsequently required the crew to exit with their luggage so he could manually record their names.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic working a chronic 'No-Start' and Engine Fuel Valve problem on a B767-300 aircraft describes the efforts of four mechanics and himself to locate a misplaced ratchet ring type wrench that was used during the reinstallation of an Engine J-Box cover.
summary: A mechanic reported losing a ratchet wrench while servicing an engine fuel valve and wiring harness. After extensive searches and six engine runs failed to locate the tool, the mechanic informed Maintenance Control and requested a post-ferry flight inspection to ensure the wrench was not inside the engine.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic was informed that a washer next to the axle retaining nut for the left nose tire was found not installed on a B767-300 aircraft, after he signed for the tire change.
summary: A mechanic on a B767-300 reported missing a washer next to the retaining nut while changing the left nose tire, despite using correct manuals and new tooling. The company discovered the error, but the aircraft suffered no damage or delay.

synopsis: A Maintenance Controller recommends changing their A321 MEL to 'disallow deferral' of Cabin L-2 Door storage compartment with emergency equipment, because all of the equipment is attached to a sliding drawer/door. Controller also notes the storage compartment is easily damaged and should be relocated or modified.
summary: A mechanic issued an MEL for an inoperative overhead bin door, interpreting a maintenance note regarding aircraft location incorrectly. The reporter recommends amending the MEL to disallow deferral of compartments containing permanently affixed emergency equipment, citing the risk of damage to the sliding drawer mechanism.

synopsis: Confused by the NACO Airport Diagram's format for display of Runway numbers and TDZ elevations, the pilot of a C172 made his initial approach to land at SUA to Runway 16 vice 12 as cleared. ATC alerted him and directed a go around after which he returned to land safely on Runway 12.
summary: A pilot misidentified Runway 12 on a confusing printed SUA diagram and attempted an approach to Runway 16 despite conflicting wind and heading indications. The controller instructed a go-around after the pilot reported a heading of 15, resulting in a safe stop-and-go on the correct runway.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A light aircraft pilot encountered severe wake turbulence while entering Washington, DC Leesburg SFRA because most aircraft use the JYO Runway 17 ILS localizer track for SFRA entry because the AML VORTAC is not available to define the areas boundaries when used with the DCA VORTAC.
summary: The report describes how JYO SFRA gate collocations with Runway 17 ILS concentrate traffic, creating head-on passing opportunities in turbulence near the 1,500 FT Class B floor. This occurs because the out-of-service AML VORTAC forces aircraft without DME to rely on ILS fixes instead of ground references.

aircraft: Challenger Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: CL60 flight crew reported the First Officer failed to remove the pitot covers on walkaround, citing the absence of red streamers on the covers as contributing.
summary: The copilot, pilot in command, and mission specialist failed to verify pitot cover removal after line personnel assisted with pin extraction. The aircraft aborted takeoff due to no airspeed indication caused by the covers remaining on the tubes, attributed to removed red streamers and checklist omissions.

synopsis: While preparing to depart a non towered airport, the pilot of a C-140 taxied onto the runway forcing a twin on short final to go around.
summary: A pilot taxiing a tailwheel aircraft at a non-towered airport delayed crossing the runway due to a stuck wheel, causing a light twin on final to go around. The incident resulted from the pilot's failure to adequately scan for traffic, an intermittent radio preventing callouts, and underestimating the twin's approach speed.

synopsis: BE40 flight crew experiences a dual engine failure at FL430 after starting a descent due to stick shaker activation while deviating around thunderstorms. The engines are unresponsive resulting in a flaps up dead stick landing at the nearest suitable airport.
summary: A Part 91 flight crew encountered severe turbulence and icing at FL450, causing both engines to flame out and the stick shaker to activate. The aircraft descended below the clouds, landed with emergency braking, and sustained brake smoke and tire damage, likely due to ice-coated engines preventing restart.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: On his first flight aboard his recently purchased Ercoupe the new owner encountered low oil pressure indications and diverted to the nearest suitable airport where he--along with an accompanying CFI who was performing a check out--landed on a closed runway. After adding oil and determining oil pressure was now normal, they took off and continued to their destination.
summary: The pilot and a CFI flying a 1946 Ercoupe 415C diverted due to low oil pressure caused by an incorrect oil level after an engine upgrade. They landed safely on a closed, unmanned grass runway without seeing the yellow 'X' marking, then topped off the oil and departed.

synopsis: A helicopter departed a DPA ramp and had near miss with an aircraft landing on Runway 28 after ATC cleared him for takeoff 'at his own risk' but did not report the approaching traffic.
summary: A helicopter pilot departing a ramp at their own risk encountered a small aircraft on final approach to Runway 28 at 100 feet. The pilot executed an evasive left turn after spotting the aircraft's shadow, attributing the near-miss to the controller's failure to provide runway status or traffic information.

synopsis: An E-145 flight crew declared an emergency and diverted to the nearest suitable airport when they received an EICAS air/ground fail message on takeoff.
summary: The crew experienced a momentary landing gear air/ground failure indication on takeoff that immediately extinguished. They declared an emergency and landed without incident on the longest runway at the nearest suitable airport.

synopsis: Two pilots aboard a Beechcraft Duchess were unable to extend their nose gear using either normal or emergency systems and landed with it retracted after making a flyby after which the Tower Controller confirmed the condition.
summary: The crew attempted to land with a retracted nose gear after extension failed during approach. They executed a controlled belly landing at their home airport, resulting in no injuries to the three occupants.

synopsis: When the normal landing gear extension system failed the pilot of a Commander 114 utilized the emergency extension procedure, was rewarded with three green lights, and landed safely.
summary: The pilot experienced a landing gear extension failure with no indicator lights during approach. After using the emergency checklist to successfully extend the gear and land, the pilot identified a tripped circuit breaker as the cause and flew the aircraft with the gear lever placarded.

synopsis: After his right tire blew out on touchdown a C-172 pilot opted to let the airplane slow to a stop without aggressive control inputs.
summary: The pilot of a single-occupant aircraft experienced a suspected right main tire blowout immediately after touchdown on Runway 18. The pilot maintained control without braking, allowing the aircraft to veer gently off the runway into a flat grassed safety area to avoid obstacles and a ditch.

synopsis: A M20 developed smoke and fumes after takeoff so the pilot secured all Master Electrical Switches and continued flying spending a short while under Class B Airspace with the transponder OFF.
summary: A pilot experienced smoke in the cockpit shortly after takeoff, turning off avionics and the master switch to isolate the issue. The flight continued without electrical systems, but the pilot inadvertently entered an area with parachute activity due to a lack of radio communication.

synopsis: TB9 pilot experiences alternator failure due to a tripped circuit breaker. It was thought that the circuit breaker was over heated due to the aircraft sitting in the sun and would remain set after cooling, which after intermittent periods of lost comm, it did.
summary: The pilot experienced an alternator failure and subsequent loss of radio communications shortly after departing PHL due to a heat-soaked circuit breaker. The pilot attributed the communication loss to low battery power and admitted to underestimating the resolution time and failing to inform ATC of the situation.

synopsis: Following his third closed circuit landing on Runway 10 at a non-towered airport the pilot of a C152 took precautionary evasive action for an aircraft landing opposite direction, the pilot of which had not followed recommended CTAF communication procedures.
summary: A pilot practicing short field landings at a non-towered airport encountered a silent aircraft on final approach for the opposite runway. The pilot taxied to the south side to allow the other aircraft to land, resulting in a minimum separation of 1,000 feet.

synopsis: A Citation First Officer and a C172 Instructor describe an incident resulting in a go around for the Citation when the C172 taxis onto the runway for takeoff. The C172 had been cleared for takeoff, but apparently took some time to do so.
summary: The pilot reported a runway incursion during a visual approach to ZZZ when a single-engine aircraft taxied onto the runway and lined up for takeoff. The crew executed a go-around after the controller admitted they had cleared the other aircraft for departure, believing it had already left the runway.

synopsis: A Sonex turned left off the runway during the takeoff roll because of torque and crosswind. Unable to stop, the pilot continued as his propeller struck sand and grass before liftoff.
summary: The pilot of a Sonex tailwheel aircraft lost directional control during a rolling takeoff due to torque, crosswind, and suspected wake turbulence from an AT-6. Unable to correct without differential braking or sufficient rudder authority, the aircraft struck a runway light, damaging the propeller but causing no injuries.

synopsis: A PA-18's tail wheel was discovered hard right after it flipped over at 10 KTS when the pilot applied full brakes to prevent the aircraft from entering trees following a landing.
summary: A student pilot and instructor in a PA-18 flipped the aircraft during a landing at a dirt strip after the tail wheel yawed right despite full left rudder input. The reporter attributed the accident to the tail wheel being hard over to the right, causing substantial damage with no injuries.

aircraft: Cessna Single Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A small light aircraft pilot attempting his first north to south crossing through the LAX Class B after taking off from SMO met with multiple conflicting ATC communications and clearances, ultimately confusing him to the point he forgot to contact Hawthorne Tower after completing the passage.
summary: A pilot overflying LAX experienced confusion regarding altitude clearances and a missing discrete transponder code due to conflicting instructions from SMO and LAX controllers. The pilot descended to 2,500 feet to enter Class B airspace but forgot to contact Hawthorne Tower after the controller admitted the oversight.

synopsis: C206 pilot taking off on Runway 06 at GUC reports detecting a business jet landing on Runway 24 as he is about to rotate. The takeoff is continued with a turn to the north and the reporter suggests that he may have been in error.
summary: The pilot departed Runway 06 at GUC without radio confirmation and discovered a landing aircraft at the far end during the takeoff roll. The pilot attributed the near-miss to poor vigilance and insufficient time between the departure call and rolling, choosing to continue the departure and bank left to increase separation.

synopsis: A RV8's nose wheel is suspected of causing the aircraft to depart the runway after landing when it veered hard right and neither braking, rudder nor aileron inputs could counter the turn.
summary: The pilot reported a hard right veer and runway departure during landing on Runway 26, causing slight aircraft damage after sliding into a ridge. The cause was unknown to the pilot, though they suspect a main gear toe issue despite finding no visible tire wear.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: C90 Controller described a severe weather event including numerous microbursts, the reporter questioning the FLM's decision to not initiate holding sooner.
summary: The pilot reported that Air Traffic Control sent eight or nine aircraft into a severe thunderstorm with 45-knot microbursts at ORD instead of holding them. This resulted in multiple missed approaches due to sudden wind shifts, which the pilot attributed to Flight Line Manager incompetence and a failure to recognize the danger.

synopsis: STL Controller described his/her reasoning for not complying with an ASDE-X commanded go around, the reporter noting the 'conflicting' traffic was observed completely clear of the landing runway.
summary: An ATC controller managed a Cherokee and an MD80 on final for Runway 30R, using an S-turn and early exit to maintain spacing. The ASDE incorrectly alerted a conflict as the MD80 flared, but the controller did not issue a go-around because the Cherokee was clear and the MD80 was too close to touchdown.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: CLT Controller described an unsafe situation with regard to supervisory runway configuration decisions and the resulting tailwind landing events.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that safety was compromised during a converging runway operation when the supervisor was overridden to continue operations despite increasing wind shear up to 30 knots and thunderstorms. The controller stopped departures but remained concerned about aircraft landing with a 12-knot tailwind and limited go-around room due to the weather.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ZOB Controller described an unsafe condition when a supervisor elected to close a D-Side position to accommodate controllers leaving the shift. The reporter noted that this would not have happened during other time/traffic periods.
summary: An air traffic controller at ZOB objected to combining GAM and ECK sectors during high traffic, citing fatigue and safety concerns. The supervisor temporarily worked the D-Side position while approving leave, which the controller deemed unsafe and unacceptable for end-of-shift operations.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reports being assigned a runway change from 7R to 25L approaching GEELA on the GEELA6 arrival to PHX. This results in quick changes to the FMC to stay on track but being below the MNSTR crossing restriction with no altitude assignment from ATC.
summary: Pilots on a GEELA arrival accepted a runway change without the new ATIS, resulting in an incorrect FMC transition and a descent below the MNSTR altitude restriction. The crew avoided an altitude deviation by quickly requesting a revised clearance, though they noted ATC should provide immediate heading and altitude instructions during such changes.

synopsis: B737-300 flight crew experiences an engine flame out as thrust is reduced to idle at the top of descent. No attempt to restart the engine is made and a successful single engine landing ensues.
summary: During descent at FL340, the crew experienced a #2 engine rollback and passenger-reported smoke, prompting an emergency declaration and fire checklist execution. The aircraft landed safely with one engine inoperative; post-landing inspections found no engine damage but noted hot brakes, while the PA system failed during passenger announcements.

synopsis: B737-700 First Officer reports auto flight anomalies during a noise abatement departure from SNA. The procedure is successfully flown manually but the crew does not understand what caused the flight director bars to retract from view, auto thrust to disengage, and LNAV to be no longer armed.
summary: During a noise abatement departure from SNA, the crew experienced an unexplained loss of TO/GA and LNAV modes during the takeoff roll. They manually flew the procedure, noting that the early cutback requirement significantly increased workload and created a potential safety hazard when combined with automation failures.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew experiences a cabin altitude warning horn at FL390 followed by an emergency descent and diversion to a suitable airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a cabin altitude warning at FL390 due to a suspected left engine bleed valve malfunction, forcing an emergency descent to 10,000 FT.
