An emergency is declared and descent initiated to 10,000 FT and the cabin altitude is noted to descend as the aircraft descends. The crew elects to return to the departure airport and the cabin altitude is noted to be below sea level at 3,000 FT. Manual pressurization is used to depressurize for landing.
summary: The flight crew experienced a cabin altitude warning at FL310, prompting an emergency descent to 10,000 feet with masks donned but cabin masks failing to deploy. After pressurization normalized, the crew held to burn fuel and landed unpressurized due to subsequent over-pressurization issues.

synopsis: MD11 First Officer reports an early starter disengagement during pushback with the fuel lever placed to off. Fire is reported by a ground observer and the Captain pulls the the fire handle and discharges both fire bottles.
summary: During pushback, the number one engine starter disengaged at 38%, causing flames and smoke reported by the ground mechanic. The Captain shut down the engine, discharged two fire bottles, and requested Fire/Rescue, which extinguished the fire before the aircraft was towed back to the gate.

synopsis: A310 Captain notes a high frequency vibration from the number one engine during initial climb. All indications are normal except for vibration monitor readings which are elevated. While considering a course action the crew received an EPR mode fault alert and the ATS lever kicked off. At about the same time Number 1 EGT fails and N1 RPM begins to increase uncommanded. Thrust is reduced manually and shortly after, the crew noticed that oil quantity and pressure on engine one bled to zero. The engine is shut down and flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced high-frequency vibration and an EPR mode fault on engine one shortly after takeoff, leading to uncommanded N1 climb and total oil loss. They declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport, and landed safely on runway 06 with no observed damage.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: First Officer as pilot not flying reports exceeding Vmo below 10,000 FT while attempting to enter a missing waypoint into the FMC. The Captain had used Vertical Speed on the MCP to descend quickly below a cloud layer then became distracted by the waypoint search.
summary: During the BOUNO FOUR arrival into HPN, the Captain selected Vertical Speed without PROF protection to descend below clouds, causing an overspeed to 344 KTS while distracted by a missing waypoint. The First Officer, preoccupied with inserting the fix, failed to monitor the autopilot until the overspeed clacker sounded, prompting the Captain to deploy speed brakes and restore normal parameters.

synopsis: Two tire shop mechanics were informed that four B747-400 main tire/wheel assemblies that were built-up in their shop, were found with incorrect wheel bearings installed on the inboard side.
summary: A mechanic reported that four B747-400 main tire/wheel assemblies built in July 2012 had bearings incorrectly installed on the inboard side. Two assemblies are currently in the shop while two remain in the system, with the error discovered only after notification from a lead.

synopsis: BE90 with ZOA descending into Chico experienced a TCAS RA, the pilot questioning the ATC service provided.
summary: A pilot descending to Chico reported a near mid-air collision with an opposing aircraft while Oakland Center was distracted by another flight. TCAS provided the only warning, resulting in a pass within 100 feet vertically and 1/4 mile horizontally after the pilot initiated a left turn.

synopsis: BE58 pilot landed at a non-towered airport and observed another aircraft land simultaneously on the opposite runway. Although all CTAF calls were made, the BE58 pilot heard no other transmissions due to having previously lowered the radio volume.
summary: The pilot, en route in a Cessna, landed on Runway 34 while unable to hear radio traffic due to accidentally lowering the communication volume. Although a Cessna landed on the opposing end of the 5,000-foot runway, both aircraft stopped safely without a close call.

synopsis: C182 pilot reports inadvertently entering SLC Class B airspace while attempting to avoid it using a paper TAC, iPad with Foreflight, and a moving map GPS. The vertical dimension of the Class B airspace was obscured on all three maps for various reasons.
summary: A pilot flying a Lancair southbound from OGD inadvertently entered Salt Lake Class B airspace between 7,600 and 10,000 feet while climbing to avoid weather. The intrusion occurred because zoomed-in GPS and folded sectional charts obscured the airspace shelf, leading to an unauthorized penetration of approximately 500 feet before clearance was obtained.

synopsis: C404 pilot experiences engine roughness and loss of oil pressure during initial climb. The engine is shut down and the flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: The pilot experienced a left engine failure shortly after takeoff due to zero oil pressure and loss of manifold pressure. The pilot secured the engine, returned VFR to the departure airport, and landed safely on the remaining engine.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A pilot crossed the APA Runway 34R hold short line on Taxiway A16 because it is so far from the runway and aircraft stopped there would block Taxiway A.
summary: A pilot unfamiliar with APA taxied a small aircraft past the A16 hold short line while moving from an unmarked run-up area, blocking the taxiway. The controller vectored an arriving corporate jet around after the pilot crossed the line, attributing the error to lack of local experience and confusing hold bar placement.

synopsis: The pilot of a C-182, after experiencing a close call with radio control modelers sharing--with permission--the use of the runway at L82 airport determined he would go elsewhere in the future for landing practice if the modelers were again present.
summary: A pilot practicing takeoffs and landings at Buttonwillow Airport (L82) encountered a person standing at the runway edge during rotation. The pilot continued the takeoff, becoming airborne at 100 feet with 200 feet horizontal separation, and subsequently decided to avoid the airport when model aircraft are operating.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A pilot departing a CLE area airport eastbound received a verbal route clearance which included KEATING (ETG) along J146 and confused it with the similar sounding, nearby KEATN Intersection.
summary: The flight crew experienced navigation confusion at CGF due to the similar pronunciation of intersection 'KEATN' and VOR 'KEATING' in their departure clearance. Ground Control resolved the issue by providing the 'ETG' identifier, allowing the crew to correct their FMS and complete the flight safely.

synopsis: A child in a BE-35's right seat accidentally turned the ignition key off and knocked it out. After loosing power the pilot declared an emergency and returned to land on a closed runway.
summary: The pilot reported an engine power loss and vibration after takeoff caused by a child unintentionally moving the ignition switch to an intermediate position. After declaring an emergency, the pilot landed safely on the closed Runway 24, and subsequent ground checks confirmed normal engine parameters.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A single engine pilot crossed the CAE Runway 29 Hold Short Line because he did not recognize it as a hold short line because it was so far from the runway.
summary: The pilot inadvertently crossed the Runway 29 hold short line by 25 feet while taxiing at Columbia Airport due to confusing markings in a hot spot area. Ground Control instructed a 180-degree turn to correct the position, and the flight departed safely after the incident.

synopsis: C172 Instructor pilot describes a possible runway incursion at BFI after becoming distracted due to an unnecessary delay initiated by the Tower.
summary: A flight instructor at BFI Runway 31L lost situational awareness due to frustration with ATC responses and cleared for takeoff while a Cessna was landing and a Citation X was on final. The instructor entered the runway, causing a runway incursion, before the Tower canceled the clearance due to a mistaken N-number identification.

synopsis: P80 Controller described a loss of separation event between an aircraft holding at UGB VOR and an IFR UAO departure. The reporter suggested improved RADAR coverage is a must in this area.
summary: An air traffic controller turned a departing C414 to avoid a C172 holding at the UBG VOR due to delayed radar contact caused by poor coverage and the C414's climb performance. The controller attributed the conflict to limited radar in the southwest quadrant and noted that climbing the C414 would have further reduced radar visibility.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain experiences a loss of A hydraulic system quantity and pressure in cruise and turns off the A system engine driven pump without consulting the QRH or informing the First Officer. Maintenance directs the crew to divert to a suitable airport where they are able to land normally with the A system pressurized although the nose wheel steering fails during taxi in.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a steady A hydraulic fluid loss during cruise, leading to an Engine Driven Pump failure and a subsequent diversion. Maintenance attributed the failure to the pump burning fluid internally, while the crew noted a temporary breakdown in coordination that was later resolved.

synopsis: B737-300 flight crew reports a loud bang from the nose gear area when the landing gear is extended but no other anomalies are exhibited. After a Tower fly by a normal landing ensues with taxi to the gate. Post flight reveals a hydraulic leak in the nose gear area.
summary: The flight crew heard a loud bang during nose gear extension but received three green indications and no hydraulic warnings. After a normal landing following a low-altitude flyby, a post-flight inspection revealed significant hydraulic fluid leakage from the nose wheel area.

synopsis: Flight crew reports being dispatched with a malfunctioning SAT gauge with the provision that TAT functions normally. During climb it is determined that normal climb thrust is not being produced by the ATS and that neither temperature gauge is providing accurate information. Flight continues to destination.
summary: Pilots flew an aircraft dispatched with a deferred TAT probe and suspected faulty SAT, resulting in slow climb performance and lost FMC fuel predictions. The crew manually computed go-around settings and noted the MEL lacked guidance for dual temperature errors, though autothrottles functioned normally.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reports unreliable crew oxygen pressure indication during climb and cruise. Maintenance indicated that the crew should continue to destination.
summary: The flight crew experienced unreliable crew oxygen indications during climb and cruise. Maintenance advised continuing to the destination despite the erroneous indication.

synopsis: A regional jet Captain reported high right engine oil temperature on climbout. QRH was run, engine shut down, an emergency declared, and the flight returned for a safe landing at departure airport.
summary: During climb out, the pilot observed the right engine oil temperature rising to 178 degrees, exceeding limits. After completing the QRH and declaring an emergency, the crew shut down the engine and executed an uneventful single-engine landing.

synopsis: Reporter stated a B767-300 had a loss of weather radar, and with weather forecast enroute was unable to continue. Emergency was declared for overweight landing and flight returned to departure airport.
summary: The crew declared an emergency due to weather radar failure and an anticipated overweight landing. They dumped fuel from FL290 to 6,000 feet, landed normally, and were escorted to the gate by ARFF with good coordination from all parties.

synopsis: MD-82 Captain reported his First Officer noticed binding and clicking in the elevator controls an approach. Aircraft was written up after landing.
summary: The First Officer experienced binding, a bump, and an audible click in the elevator controls near the neutral position during final approach after disconnecting the autopilot. The issue was not felt by the Captain, and maintenance was contacted after landing.

synopsis: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports how the aft side of #3 Slat on a B737-300 aircraft had been damaged by the slat actuator during removal of the slat rod end switch.
summary: A mechanic and an AMT damaged the #3 Slat back section while replacing the #3 Slat rod end switch. The actuator jerked forward and caused the damage when the AMT turned hydraulics on to retract the Leading Edge Devices further.

synopsis: A BE90 Captain is cleared to fly headings between 270 and 360 to deviate around weather. When it becomes necessary to deviate to the southwest, a different Controller on the same frequency approves that request. When the first Controller returns to the frequency, he admonishes the crew for deviating from the original clearance. An explanation is not provided due to time and frequency congestion.
summary: Pilots in cruise at 16,000 feet deviated south around a thunderstorm after receiving specific clearance from the first controller. A second controller questioned the deviation, citing original instructions, but the crew could not clarify due to high radio traffic and lack of handoff information.

synopsis: EA500 Captain reports communication difficulties with ATC while attempting to change destination or descend and and cancel IFR due to weather. A deviation below the ATC assigned altitude of 17,000 FT occurs prior to the Controller acknowledging IFR cancellation request.
summary: The pilot of an IFR flight to ECP, lacking onboard weather radar, requested a destination change to CEW to avoid severe thunderstorms but received no ATC acknowledgment. The pilot subsequently canceled IFR and descended below the assigned 17,000 feet to proceed VFR, attributing the issue to poor flight planning and delayed decision-making.

synopsis: PA28B-235 Instructor reported loss of control and runway excursion when student froze on the rudder pedals.
summary: A student pilot lost directional control shortly after landing, causing the aircraft to excursion off the hard surface onto grass. The reporter suspects the cause was student stiffness on the rudder pedals at touchdown.

synopsis: P50 Controller described a below MVA event involving a FFZ departure assigned a MESA1.MESA SID. The Controller claimed that the aircraft turned in the wrong direction, adding that pilots seem to misunderstand the published procedure.
summary: An EA50 pilot departed on the Mesa One SID but turned northbound instead of southwest, reaching 3,000 feet near a 4,500-foot MVA. The controller climbed the aircraft to 6,000 feet, but it entered the MVA at 3,000 feet before the pilot assumed terrain clearance responsibility.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ZJX Supervisor described a very complex traffic period with heavy/complex traffic and limited airspace availability due to weather. The reporter debated military operations/airspace vs. civil aviation needs.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller at Jacksonville ARTCC reported extreme workload during severe weather when aircraft deviated into Sectors 67, 68, 58, and 76 due to denied military warning area airspace. The situation required a Tier 1 Ground Stop and direct controller intervention to release airspace, highlighting failures in CAR40 procedures and lack of external support.

synopsis: A321 Captain experiences apparently false simultaneous SMOKE FWD CARGO SMOKE and SMOKE AFT CARGO SMOKE ECAM warnings accompanied by the fire bell in cruise. After some discussion the crew elects to divert to a suitable airport for an over weight landing. It is later learned that the aircraft has a history of false cargo smoke warnings.
summary: The flight crew diverted to ZZZ2 during climb due to simultaneous false forward and aft cargo smoke warnings, likely caused by a faulty system with no actual smoke or fire. They executed an overweight landing safely, and post-flight inspection confirmed no damage, though the aircraft has a history of this fault.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An aircraft taxied beyond the BOS Runway 4R Visual Hold Short Line on Runway 14/32 because the crew did not recognized it as the Runway Hold Short Line.
summary: The flight crew taxied past the Runway 14 hold short line after Tower instructed them to hold short of the visual hold short line, which coincided with the runway hold line. The reporter attributed the incursion to ambiguous phraseology and a need for greater vigilance regarding the airport diagram.

synopsis: CRJ700 First Officer describes an in-flight engine shut down for high oil temperature and return to the departure airport.
summary: The First Officer and Captain managed a right engine high oil temperature event between 7,000 and 8,000 feet, declaring an emergency and shutting down the engine. They returned for a smooth single-engine landing, with the crew noting the incident was handled well despite minor procedural sequencing issues.

synopsis: A DC-10 Captain reported losing automatic cabin pressurization control. After running the procedure the flight continued in manual pressurization mode.
summary: The crew received a cabin altitude warning at cruise and followed QRH procedures to manually control the cabin. The reporter suggested updating the checklist to allow cycling back to automatic mode to avoid running the system in manual for the remainder of the flight.

synopsis: A Maintenance Controller reports he scheduled a Special Maintenance Inspection to be accomplished on Number 3 Engine for an ENGINE INDICATING-ENGINE VIBRATION write-up at a station he thought would be the last flight cycle for an MD-11 aircraft. He was later informed the aircraft actually had two more stops in between and had overflown the deferral limits.
summary: A maintenance planner assigned a Special Inspection for an MD-11's engine vibration issue to a future stop, failing to account for two intermediate stops. Consequently, the aircraft overflew the inspection limit by one cycle before the engine was cleared for FOD damage checks.

synopsis: DA40-180 pilot reported he failed to close the rear passenger access door and it departed the aircraft on takeoff roll. Takeoff was aborted.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff after the rear access door blew off due to snapped hinge tabs, having been overlooked while the front canopy was partially open for cooling. Damage was limited to the door and its support rod, with no impact to the fuselage or tail.

synopsis: Phenom 100 Captain reports that his FMC incorrectly reads the HOMRR crossing restriction on the EAGUL5 RNAV to PHX as a hard altitude instead of 'at or below' as depicted. This makes the VNNOM crossing restriction impossible to achieve.
summary: The reporter identified a potential safety issue with the EAGUL5 arrival where passing HOMRR below 16,000 feet requires an unsafe descent rate to meet the 11,000 to 10,000 feet constraint within four miles. Avionics systems correctly calculate this as unable, prompting a request to alter the STAR for a more gradual descent.

aircraft: De Havilland Canada Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: DHC Chipmunk pilot describes loss of oil pressure on the third leg of a flight to OSH. The engine continues to produce power and the reporter is able to return to the departure airport. It is discovered that the oil filter screen is completely coated with metal particles. The filter is cleaned and reinstalled, the oil topped off, and the engine run up. When all appears satisfactory the reporter takes off and climbs over the field before continuing on to OSH.
summary: The pilot of a de Havilland Gipsy Major 10 engine aircraft experienced a total oil pressure loss due to a seized pressure filter screen containing ferrous debris. After declaring a Mayday and dead-sticking the aircraft to a safe landing, the pilot later discovered the jammed filter and decided to ground the plane for a full engine overhaul.

synopsis: Line Mechanic reports noticing the left-hand elevator was missing during a post flight walk around inspection on a Piaggio-180 aircraft. Mechanic suspects nuts backed-off. Hardware configuration issue.
summary: During a post-flight walk-around inspection, mechanics found the left-hand elevator missing. The reporter suspects that nuts backing off caused the elevator to depart from the horizontal stabilizer during flight.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a conflict event when a Trainee assuming Local Control cleared an aircraft for takeoff with traffic on very short final, the reporter noting that during the relief no one was looking out of the window.
summary: A Developmental controller cleared a Cardinal for takeoff on Runway 28L while a Husky was on short final, causing a near mid-air collision. The conflict resulted from the trainee's error during a position relief briefing, exacerbated by distractions and a lack of trainer awareness.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a near ground conflict event when, relying on input from the Ground Controller, the reporter issued a 'line and wait' clearance.
summary: Local Control cleared a King Air for takeoff on Runway 2L while a Navajo was landing, causing a runway incursion risk. The controller attributed the error to relying on the Ground Controller's position report and a misplaced flight strip instead of visually confirming the King Air's location at Bravo Taxiway.

synopsis: E10 TRACON Controller describes an unsafe event where ZLA failed to accept hand offs on aircraft that were normally accepted. The reporter noted that too much ZLA Controller interpretation currently exists regarding what should be an accepted standard.
summary: ZOA controllers reported that ZLA-16 refused handoffs of a B737 and A319 at FL330, forcing an unnecessary descent to FL290 despite no conflicting traffic. The reporter deemed this unsafe due to potential military activity in the airspace and cited inconsistent Letter of Agreement interpretations as the cause.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported failure of Captain's L1 window in climb. An emergency was declared and the flight returned to departure airport.
summary: During climbout between 14,000 and FL230, the Captain's L1 window shattered due to suspected stress, not a bird strike. The crew declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport, and performed an overweight landing of 136,800 lbs.

synopsis: CE-750 First Officer reported loss of hydraulic system A. They declared an emergency and diverted to the nearest suitable airport, where a hydraulic line failure was diagnosed.
summary: Pilots experienced a hydraulic system failure immediately after takeoff, causing gear asymmetry and requiring an emergency landing with emergency brakes. A ruptured hydraulic line in the nose wheel bay caused the failure, while outdated dispatch phone numbers delayed company contact.

synopsis: Air Carrier arrival was cleared for a Visual Approach to Runway 19 only to discover opposite direction traffic departing Runway 1 when transferred to the Tower, a significant communication error between the Tower/TRACON was listed as the causal factor.
summary: Pilots flying an aircraft on a visual approach to Runway 19 encountered a departing E145 from Runway 1 due to a communication breakdown between TRACON and Tower controllers. ATC issued immediate avoidance vectors, resulting in a near miss with 200 feet vertical and one mile horizontal separation before a safe landing.

synopsis: An EMB145 crew declared an emergency and returned to the departure airport after the Flight Attendant reported cabin smoke during the climb after takeoff. The smoke's odor was described as rubber or electrical in nature.
summary: The flight crew declared an emergency at 5,500 feet after a flight attendant reported cabin smoke between rows 12 and 17. The aircraft returned for an overweight landing on Runway 28, where rescue teams found no external issues before the flight deplaned at the gate.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer describes an engine failure during vectors for a visual approach. An emergency is declared, QRH procedures are complied with, and a single engine landing ensues.
summary: During a visual approach descent, the pilot flying experienced an uncommanded Engine 1 shutdown while hand-flying. The crew secured the engine, declared an emergency, and landed safely after briefly recovering from a low-power state that caused a slight yaw.

synopsis: A pilot recommends a revision to the Beech 1900-D MEL 22-2-2 'Yaw Damper Computer;' to clarify as to 'when' an 'O' Procedure for pulling and collaring the Yaw Damper Computer Circuit Breaker (C/B) should apply.
summary: The flight crew and Mechanic X encountered conflicting interpretations of MEL 22-2-2 regarding an inoperative Number 1 Yaw Damper Computer after landing. After initial confusion over the 'O' Procedure, the Chief Pilot and Dispatcher agreed to reset the circuit breaker, allowing the aircraft to depart with one computer inoperative.

synopsis: A Captain discovered his Company's EWR Runway 4L procedure called for a right turn to 010 after takeoff whereas the standard procedure calls for a more likely left turn.
summary: Pilots briefing the T-procedure for EWR Runway 4L identified a conflict between ACARS and company procedures regarding the turn direction to 010 degrees. The crew determined the company's left turn instruction was correct given the 039-degree runway heading.

synopsis: B737-800 First Officer discovers on third leg of his flight that the fuel system is malfunctioning, causing fuel spills and uncontrolled fuel transfer between wings. A Maintenance Supervisor suggests that this situation is not mechanically possible and the crew should take it flying and see what happens. The crew declines.
summary: The relief pilot reported that a fuel system failure caused uncontrolled wing-to-wing transfer and overflow during refueling, leading the entire crew to refuse flight. Maintenance personnel initially dismissed the issue, but the aircraft was grounded until a rescue flight arrived after mechanics confirmed broken valves and a lack of prior logbook entries.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports he inadvertently signed-off the Inspection block on a Work Card for the Nose Gear Tire Spin Down Brake pads on a B757-200 aircraft.
summary: A line maintenance mechanic on a B757-200 incorrectly signed a nose gear brake inspection work card requiring Quality Control approval. The reporter attributed this clerical error to the card's confusing format, which resembled standard line maintenance tasks lacking clear QC sign-off notations.

synopsis: Super Cub pilot reported ground looping his aircraft resulting in rear spar damage.
summary: The pilot ground looped a Super Cub on a grass glider strip after a full-stop landing, causing the left wing to strike the ground. Subsequent inspection by the pilot and an A&P mechanic revealed a bent rear spar and fabric damage on the left wing.

synopsis: PBI Taxiway R is restricted to non air carrier aircraft but the wingtip of an air carrier type aircraft on R will be beyond the Runway 10R Hold Short Line if the line were extended parallel to the runway.
summary: A pilot operating a 65-foot wingspan aircraft at PBI reported that using Taxiway R causes the wingtip to extend beyond the hold-short line. The pilot suggested implementing a specific wingspan restriction for the taxiway while allowing larger aircraft to access Runway 10R/28L via Taxiways L or T.

synopsis: C182 pilot in landing flare, encountered rotorwash turbulence from military H60 helicopters operating in the vicinity of the runway at a non-towered airport.
summary: A pilot landing on Runway 16 encountered significant turbulence from rotor downwash generated by hovering military H-60 helicopters. The pilot attributed the event to underestimating the downwash spread in calm winds and suggested improved UNICOM announcements and NOTAMs for such operations.

synopsis: PC12 Captain who also flys CE510 and CE525 aircraft, laments the current state of the ATC system with complex arrival and departure procedures make safe operations difficult for a single pilot crew.
summary: Pilots of PC-12 and CE aircraft reported confusion regarding speed restrictions, incomplete Garmin 530W arrival data, and conflicting RNAV interpretations with ATC at MEM. The reporter attributes these safety issues to unclear new procedures, poor chart design, and a lack of FAA guidance.

synopsis: M03 Controller voiced concern regarding the newly implemented ODP procedures noting unless M03 controllers and management hold ZME controllers accountable for STAR compliance, the procedure will not be successful.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that an E135 and a Beechjet on the LTOWN 6 RNAV arrival to MEM failed to meet STAR restrictions at COPEN due to ZME's lack of coordination. The controller attributed this to ZME's failure to enforce Optimum Descent Path requirements and criticized M03 management for not supporting controllers in enforcing these standards.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports the attitude indicator and the RMI sliding out of the instrument panel on takeoff for a ferry flight. Control is passed to the First Officer and the components are held in to prevent interference with the yoke;then properly secured prior to landing.
summary: During rotation on a ferry flight at 95 KIAS, the Captain's attitude indicator and RMI detached due to unsecured locking bolts. The Captain stabilized the panel to clear the yoke, and onboard maintenance secured it in-flight with no further action required.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported flaps failed on extension for landing. An emergency was declared and safe landing followed.
summary: The flight crew encountered a flaps locked/alignment fault while selecting flaps 2 for landing, prompting a hold and checklist execution. They landed on the longest available runway with fire trucks standing by, delaying brake application until below 90 KTS before exiting with over 2,000 feet remaining.

synopsis: A320 First Officer describes the circumstances leading up to a fatigue call to Scheduling.
summary: A reserve pilot experienced a 6 hour 40 minute delay due to APU failure and extreme cabin heat, leading to a late reassignment and reduced rest. The pilot reported fatigue caused by the delay, lack of rest quarters, and prior reduced rest, resulting in an inability to fly the subsequent morning departure.

synopsis: B757-200 flight crew reported low oil quantity in left engine. Engine was shut down and the flight diverted to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: During cruise at FL340, the crew observed zero left engine oil quantity and fluctuating pressure that eventually dropped to zero. They diverted 147 NM to a suitable airport, shut down the left engine per checklist, declared an emergency, and landed.

aircraft: Boeing Company Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reports a go around due to an unstabilized approach caused by windshear. A TE flap disagree EICAS message is displayed during the go around with the flaps locked at 23 degrees. After compliance with QRH procedures an uneventful partial flap landing ensues.
summary: The crew encountered a windshear alert and TE Flap Disagree EICAS at 500 feet during approach, causing a missed approach. After resolving the flap lockout via checklist, they completed an uneventful landing with 20 degrees of flaps.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain experiences excessive N1 vibration at FL350. After a discussion with Maintenance Control the Captain elects to continue to destination. The vibration diminishes as the aircraft descends for approach.
summary: The crew experienced high N1 vibration on engine one at FL350, which reduced during descent. After consulting Dispatch and Maintenance Control, they continued to the destination and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew is informed by ATC that one of their tires shed most of its' rubber during takeoff. Flight continues to destination and lands normally after declaring an emergency. The tire was found inflated but missing most of its' tread.
summary: The crew was unaware that the right main gear tire shed debris during takeoff until notified by ATC while climbing. They declared an emergency, continued to the destination, and landed without incident; the tire was later found inflated but missing most of its rubber.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported rejecting takeoff when N1 vibration exceeded normal limits.
summary: The crew rejected takeoff before 80 KTS due to an N1 vibration indication of 8.7, exceeding the Flight Operations Manual limit of 5.0. Maintenance performed Task 77-32-00-810-807-A, found no damage, and the aircraft taxied to the gate.

synopsis: A320 Captain believes that he erred in accepting an aircraft with ECS (Environmental Control System) anomalies. The cabin temperature cannot be controlled and much of the time is excessively hot.
summary: The Captain accepted the aircraft with a deferred hot air system despite prior excessive heat reports, resulting in severe cabin overheating and a passenger requiring oxygen during the flight. The crew struggled to control temperatures using ECS procedures, leading to an uncomfortable flight and concerns about the deferral decision.

synopsis: A Dispatcher's ability to communicate with a flight experiencing problems was compromised by dysfunctional new communications hardware.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that while managing a flight crew's declared emergency regarding a nose wheel steering ECAM alert after departure, the new communications system experienced numerous delays and lock-ups. The controller stated these breakdowns hindered timely information exchange and represent a significant safety issue requiring immediate repair or replacement.

synopsis: Pilot reports an MEL deferral of a Potable Water Quantity Gage was incorrectly applied on a B757-200 aircraft.The Potable Water tank was later found ruptured and leaking after repeated refills. Lack of adequate Maintenance troubleshooting, prior to deferring the Quantity Gage, was also noted.
summary: Flight crew on a B757-200 encountered a split flap condition on approach after a ruptured water tank leaked, caused by incorrectly applying an MEL for a quantity gage instead of troubleshooting the leak. The crew landed safely with Flaps 20, though the incident compromised safety due to maintenance complacency.

synopsis: CRJ-700 Captain reported diverting to nearest suitable in response to a bleed overheat that later was determined to be a false warning.
summary: The crew encountered a right bleed duct warning at 20,000 feet while using cowl anti-ice, prompting an emergency descent to 10,000 feet and diversion to the nearest airport. Maintenance later identified the cause as an open loop indication error, confirming the warning was false.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew was questioned by Approach Control when they had failed to program an 'expect to cross at' note on the WAVUN into their FMS while on descent into FLL and, as a result, failed to meet the restriction when it was given.
summary: The flight crew missed a DEKAL intersection restriction during the WAVUN.ONE arrival, causing them to be high and unable to comply with the 6,000 FT/250 KTS requirement. The crew notified Miami ARTCC immediately, but the controller berated them and failed to provide relief vectors until a second controller assigned a descent to 5,000 FT.

synopsis: An ERJ flight crew on the TEB RUUDY 4 climbed directly to 2,000 FT before WENTZ because the Captain was task saturated with the unfamiliar departure and weather avoidance.
summary: The Captain and First Officer departed TEB on a charter flight and climbed to 2,000 feet too early on the RUDDY 4 RNAV departure. The incident resulted from the Captain's incorrect takeoff briefing regarding the 1,500-foot crossing restriction, compounded by distraction from weather cells and unfamiliar procedures.

synopsis: MD-82 Captain reported right engine oil quantity went to zero after takeoff. Emergency was declared and flight returned to departure airport.
summary: The pilot reported that on departure, the right engine oil quantity dropped to zero. The crew executed the QRH procedure, declared an emergency, and returned to the departure airport.

synopsis: A pilot was cleared to pushed back to SPOT R-1 at MPTO but because it was not on his airport diagram did not know where the SPOT was.
summary: The flight crew received a pushback clearance to Spot R-1, which is not depicted on MPTO Commercial Chart pages. The tug driver located the spot, but the reporter notes this chart omission is a recurring issue with no corrective action taken.

synopsis: C414 pilot deviated from assigned altitude while dealing with a temporary loss of power related to fuel crossfeed valve malfunction.
summary: During cross-feed operation, a malfunctioning crossfeed valve caused temporary left engine power loss, resulting in a 400-foot altitude decrease for 30-40 seconds. The issue was resolved, power returned, and the pilot advised Center, who reported no problem.

synopsis: SA227 pilot reports narrowly missing an unlighted truck parked on his departure runway at night, after the Tower had closed.
summary: A pilot taking off from Runway 33 after tower closure encountered three maintenance personnel and an unlit truck on the active runway just after V1. The pilot aborted the takeoff path to clear the obstacle, attributing the incident to a lack of NOTAMs, simultaneous radio transmissions, and the absence of a 24-hour control tower.

synopsis: An EA50 pilot was assigned the TEB RUUDY 4 RNAV Departure which was different from his filed SID and subsequently he missed the waypoint constraints because the FMS did not load the SID.
summary: The pilot departed with an incomplete FMS flight plan due to a manual clearance mismatch, causing a missed waypoint and altitude deviation during climb. Air Traffic Control intervened with a heading change to avoid traffic after the pilot realized the navigation error.

synopsis: A CE-500 on the TEB 8 Departure failed to capture 6,000 FT because of an autopilot malfunction and additionally the First Officer failed to call approaching the assigned altitude.
summary: A two-person crew flying a Teterboro 8 departure overshot their 6,000 FT clearance to 6,500 FT because the autopilot failed to capture the altitude and the crew did not monitor or call out the deviation. The incident resulted from crew failure to recognize the autopilot error, lack of altitude callouts, and violation of sterile cockpit procedures.

synopsis: D21 Controller described an unsafe condition when communications equipment was operating intermittently, distracting the reporter.
summary: An air traffic controller at position A experienced transmitter and jack failures while managing a B737 and E135, causing missed transmissions and distraction. This led to the B737 descending below its clearance, resulting in a TCAS RA for the E135 due to the controller's inability to confirm readbacks or issue visual separation instructions.

synopsis: ZTL Controller described a loss of separation event when taking over communications for another controller without a complete briefing during late night operations as positions were being combined and operations changed.
summary: A West Departure controller incorrectly assumed track control of three aircraft while covering for a Gadsden colleague, relying on erroneous radar tags. This led to a loss of separation between two aircraft stacked 2,000 feet apart inbound to Atlanta due to misidentified call signs and altitudes.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: S46 Controller described an unsafe event when a military fighter participating in an air show transitioned very close to the TFR boundary in close proximity to departure traffic. The reporter voiced concern regarding the FAA's 'no transponder policy' issued to air show participants.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller observed a fighter jet flying within 3/4 mile and 600 feet of a departing Air Carrier near Seattle while the jet's transponder was off. The controller attributed the dangerous proximity to poor briefing, high speed, and the decision to turn off transponders, which prevented the carrier from seeing the jet.

synopsis: ZAB Controller described a loss of separation event when neglecting to properly scan the Data Block altitude information before assigning another altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller mistakenly believed an A320 was at FL340 instead of FL320 and cleared it to FL360, causing a conflict with a southbound aircraft at FL330. Both aircraft received resolution advisories, prompting the controller to issue a 30-degree right turn to separate them.

synopsis: BWI Controller described a 'false' ASDE-X alarm involving a Runway 33L landing and a non-existing target at a runway intersection, the reporter suggesting either refinement of the ASDE-X parameters or discontinuing use of the equipment.
summary: An E190 landing on Runway 33L rolled through a false ASDE-X target that subsequently disappeared. When a B737 landed on the same runway, the ASDE-X incorrectly alerted that the runway was occupied despite the E190 being visually and radar-confirmed clear, leading the controller to recommend eliminating the unreliable equipment.

synopsis: A B737-700 pilot reported deviating from ATC assigned speed to increase spacing behind a B757 that was causing some wake turbulence.
summary: The flight crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding B757 during the ERLIN 9 arrival into Atlanta and slowed to 170 KTS to avoid further encounters. The pilot attributed the subsequent speed management issues to overly conservative wake avoidance tactics and insufficient communication with ATC regarding speed restrictions.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported abnormal aileron vibration severe enough they decided to divert to nearest suitable airport.
summary: The First Officer reported a rhythmic airframe shudder during climb-out, correlating with right aileron vibration, which caused passenger concern. The crew diverted and executed an overweight landing after passengers observed the aileron fluttering, though the aircraft remained controllable throughout.

synopsis: An MD-82 flight crew, distracted by malfunctioning AC power, failed to note the Flight Director had defaulted to heading hold resulting in a deviation from their SID track.
summary: During climb through 9,000 to 10,000 feet in 40°C heat, the crew experienced intermittent AC power interruptions causing autopilot disengagement and bus cycling. The aircraft deviated 3 miles south of the SID course while the crew managed the electrical failure and leveled for traffic.

synopsis: The MTPP Runway 10 ILS glide slope directed an aircraft to land short of the runway in the bay.
summary: The pilot captured the glide slope from above in visual conditions, resulting in a high sink rate and a projected water touchdown 1.5 miles from the runway. The pilot manually took over at 800 feet to avoid a crash, and the event was duplicated on a subsequent flight.

synopsis: B757 Captain describes an inadvertent slide deployment that he was directly involved with.
summary: The Captain opened the armed 1L door during pushback preparations, causing a partial slide deployment due to poor illumination and failure to visually verify the lever position. Passengers were evacuated for 25 minutes, and the flight departed hours later after encountering a medical emergency and a false smoke alarm.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: CRJ-50 Captain reported rejecting takeoff at 85 KTS when his altimeter setting spontaneously changed from 30.01 to 29.89.
summary: The crew rejected takeoff at 85 knots when the Captain's altimeter setting spontaneously changed from 30.01 to 29.89 inches, causing a negative altitude flag. The cause of this malfunction was unknown.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: CRJ First Officer reports descending below the MSA during a visual approach which is challenged by ATC and corrected by the reporter.
summary: The First Officer, flying pilot, descended below the 2,900 FT MSA on base leg after being assigned a high altitude, prompting a Tower instruction to check altitude. The crew climbed back to the MSA, corrected a right-of-course deviation, and completed a stabilized visual approach to landing.

synopsis: EMB170 Captain reports an unsatisfactory aileron check after starting both engines using the Captain's yoke, but the check is satisfactory using the First Officer's yoke. Flight returns to the gate for maintenance, where the flight control anomalies are confirmed visually.
summary: The Captain reported resistance in the left aileron and incomplete right spoiler deployment on the MFD during preflight checks, while the First Officer's yoke operated normally. The aircraft returned to the gate for maintenance after the Captain noted the resistance persisted even with hydraulic pressure off.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: The MDW Commercial Airport Diagram and taxiway signage at the Taxiway P/Y Intersection are confusing and ambiguous. The charted P and Y should be placed further apart and the taxiway intersection signage positioned more accurately.
summary: The pilot reported a misunderstanding with Air Traffic Control regarding a taxi clearance to Runway 31C, where the controller incorrectly stated the aircraft missed Taxiway Papa. The pilot attributed the confusion to deceptive airport signage and chart placement, compounded by high task saturation and fatigue from operational delays.

synopsis: An Air Carrier First Officer refused to fly a four day, red eye, Atlantic crossing flight sequence scheduled to begin the same afternoon of the day on which he had just arrived from a previous four day sequence, the last two flights of which consisted of a Hawaii/West Coast flight followed by an all nighter to his home domicile in the Central time zone.
summary: A fatigued pilot reported being scheduled for an international flight to the British Isles without a relief pilot shortly after completing a four-day trip with night flying. The pilot notified Crew Scheduling due to extreme fatigue and was removed from the pairing to ensure safety.

synopsis: Air Carrier arrival to EWR being vectored over TEB experienced a TCAS RA apparently from a TEB departure aircraft, the reporter expressing concern regarding ATC's reported nonchalant comments.
summary: While being vectored at 3,000 feet over TEB for EWR Runway 22L, the crew received a 'CLIMB' RA due to a conflicting aircraft taking off from TEB. Both aircraft had been cleared to 2,500 feet, but the controller dismissed the conflict as non-problematic after the crew responded to the RA.

synopsis: Air Carrier landing SFO Runway 28R was issued a go-around on short final heading 265, the reporter observing traffic ahead, elected to turn right, and then noted rising terrain directly in front.
summary: During a visual approach to SFO 28R in fog, the crew executed a go-around and refused an initial heading 265 clearance due to a close climbing aircraft. Diverted attention to the traffic and rising terrain caused the crew to over-turn the subsequent heading 310 instruction by 30 degrees.

synopsis: B717-200 Captain reported loss of right hydraulic system during climbout. An emergency was declared and the flight returned to departure airport.
summary: During climb out, a hydraulic quantity low alert prompted an emergency return and overweight landing. A right main gear tire failure upon touchdown caused debris damage to hydraulic lines, flaps, and the right engine, requiring the aircraft to be towed back.

synopsis: ERJ-170 flight crew attempted passage through a narrowing path between thunderstorms, encountered severe turbulence and, with ATC clearance, descended to smooth, clear air.
summary: The flight crew encountered moderate to extreme turbulence, rain, and light icing while attempting to cross a closing weather gap at FL340. After requesting and receiving a descent clearance to FL320, the pilot manually controlled the aircraft through the 20-30 second event, resulting in no injuries or further issues.

synopsis: An aircraft taxied beyond the BOS Runway 4R visual hold short line on Runway 14/32 because the crew did not recognized it as the runway hold short line.
summary: The flight crew, while taxiing to cross Runway 4L, missed the visual hold short line for Runway 4R after turning onto Runway 14/32. The pilot attributed the error to unfamiliarity with the specific hold line marking and distraction from determining the transition route.

synopsis: BE1900 Captain reports failure of the left autofeather system to arm as takeoff power is applied and the takeoff is rejected. The reporter wonders if it is legal to issue a ferry permit in this situation when aircraft limitations require the autofeather system to be operational for all takeoffs and landings.
summary: The crew aborted takeoff due to a left autofeather failure to arm, a recurring issue previously cleared by company mechanics. The pilot returned to the gate for maintenance and questioned the legality of ferrying the aircraft with an inoperative autofeather, as limitations require it to be operable for all flights.

synopsis: MD82 flight crew experienced a cabin altitude alert climbing through FL280. With the system apparently operating normally and the outflow valve apparently fully closed, the crew initiates a descent. When the cabin altitude reached 13000 feet the primary controller automatically switched to standby and locked out and the cabin altitude began to descend. Flight continues to destination.
summary: The flight crew experienced repeated cabin altitude warnings during climb due to a faulty primary pressurization controller, despite the outflow valve appearing closed. The issue resolved when the system automatically switched to the standby controller, allowing the crew to descend and later climb to destination without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: A Line Avionic's Technician describes a simple check for determining how water mass accumulation on outer Alternate Static ports had contributed to a B737-800 aircraft Stanby Altimeter reading 600' feet higher than the Captain and First Officer Altimeters while on the ground. Technician noted the water accumulation at Static ports is well known.
summary: A mechanic and flight crew found a B737-800 standby altimeter reading 600 feet high due to rainwater in alternate static ports at the gate. The mechanic cleared the water by breaking surface tension, verified altimeters were within 20 feet, and confirmed airworthiness using maintenance manual tables without breaking into the system.

synopsis: Following an unspecified 'repair' the pilot of a PA28 attempted a takeoff despite a full power run-up test which resulted in significant RPM underperformance. Once airborne, the aircraft was unable to climb, an emergency was declared and an opposite direction landing on the takeoff runway was successful. The reporter advised he and 'other parties' were unaware of what RPM was expected during the static run-up.
summary: The pilot declared an emergency after the engine failed to produce adequate climb power from Runway XXR due to a mechanical issue. The cause was attributed to the crew's failure to notice the static run-up RPM was 2150 instead of the expected 2450 following repairs.

synopsis: As he was climbing to his cleared altitude of 10,000 MSL on autopilot, the pilot of a Turbine Legend Experimental aircraft was adjusting the aileron trim when the autopilot pitch and roll servos disconnected and the aircraft abruptly climbed to 11,100, rolled into a 30 degree left bank turn. The pilot recovered control and returned to his clearance.
summary: While climbing a Turbine Legend to 10,000 feet, the pilot applied left roll trim, causing the Dynon autopilot servos to disconnect due to exceeding 32 PSI. This resulted in an uncommanded 30-degree left bank and climb to 11,100 feet, which the pilot manually corrected before resuming the climb to 15,000 feet.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: The Airport Facilities Directory (AFD) does not indicate that on weekends APN is a Class D Airport and that ARTCC acts as Approach Control during that time.
summary: A VFR pilot landed at Alpena without clearance, assuming the Tower was closed based on AFD Monday-Friday hours and unresponsive Approach Control. The Tower later scolded the pilot, admitting they were open but using Center for Approach on weekends, a detail not published in the AFD or approach plates.

synopsis: Long EZ pilot experiences loss of engine power during descent in humid conditions. Carb heat does not solve the problem and the reporter elects to divert to a suitable airport. The engine continues to run and full power is restored once on the ground. Carb ice is strongly suspected.
summary: The pilot experienced significant engine power loss and a zero EGT reading on a GEM 602 monitor while descending to 5,000 feet in hot, humid conditions. Suspecting carburetor icing, the pilot diverted to an en route airport, landed safely with partial power, and restored full static power after adjusting the mixture and throttle on the ground.

synopsis: PA32 pilot experiences difficulty maintaining altitude and heading while being vectored to successive fixes on the RNAV to Runway 23 at CPK in heavy rain.
summary: A pilot flying a light aircraft into Newport News (CPK) in heavy rain and turbulence experienced severe altitude loss and unusual attitudes after ATC vectored the aircraft through convective weather and altered the approach sequence. The pilot attributed the near-accident to ATC prioritizing traffic separation over safety, forcing vectors that turned the FAF into an IAF and pushing the aircraft into dangerous conditions.

synopsis: Shortly after takeoff while doing pattern work, a BE35 pilot requested an immediate turn toward and landing on another, more expeditiously accessed, runway due to an engine oil leak which was obscuring his forward vision.
summary: A pilot experienced an oil leak from the cowl access door during pattern work, causing oil to accumulate on the windshield. After notifying Tower and receiving clearance for a right traffic return to the longest runway, the pilot landed and taxied to parking without declaring an emergency or assistance.

synopsis: C152 instructor pilot reports a conflict in the traffic pattern Aircraft Y enters on the downwind without announcing on the CTAF. When Aircraft Y is finally contacted the pilot elects to make a 180 degree turn to reenter and a NMAC occurs.
summary: A training flight on right downwind for Runway 20 encountered a Cessna 172 entering the pattern ahead without audible radio calls. The instructor executed a left descending turn to avoid a head-on conflict after the other pilot acknowledged the call and turned 180 degrees to fly downwind in the opposite direction.

synopsis: C172 pilot reports inadvertent entry into a fire fighting TFR when he fails to see the NOTAM in the list provided by DUAT's. His iPad with WingXPro also failed to display the TFR both before and after the event.
summary: The pilot missed Lake Isabella TFRs while relying on iPad WingXPro7 software during a sightseeing flight near Bakersfield. After climbing above 5,500 feet to view smoke and helicopters, the pilot confirmed two active TFRs via FSS and attributed the oversight to not thoroughly reading the DUAT briefing.

synopsis: The Captain of a government operated CL604 directed his First Officer to load the new FMS databases but failed to insure they had been activated prior to departure. A ramp inspection by a Standards Pilot upon arrival at their destination discovered the error. A contributing factor was the reporter's meager training and experience on the 604 model aircraft and its FMS, on his primary fleet, the CL601, the FMS automatically activates a new database after it is loaded.
summary: The pilot and co-pilot loaded a new FMS database on a CL604 but failed to activate it, leaving expired data active due to a design feature where downloads go to a secondary position. This occurred because the crew was unaware of the activation requirement and lacked adequate type-specific training.

synopsis: C172 pilot encounters a strong downdraft flying below storm clouds at 9,000 FT and looses 700 FT inadvertently. ATC questions the descent then assigns 7,000 FT as requested.
summary: A pilot en route on V113 at 9,000 feet encountered a downdraft while deviating from medium precipitation, losing 700 feet to 8,300 feet. After reporting the situation, ATC cleared the aircraft to descend and maintain 7,000 feet.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A pilot reported that he was unable to establish his aircraft outbound on the SEG VOR-A because the VOR signal outbound was unusable.
summary: The pilot could not establish the published approach procedure while VOR outbound due to temporary instrument problems.

synopsis: Mooney pilot reports a rough running engine shortly after takeoff and elects to land at RDM but is unable to contact the Tower prior to landing.
summary: The pilot reported an engine running rough shortly after takeoff, resulting in a safe landing at RDM despite being unable to contact the tower. The issue was resolved after the engine was cleared of carbon.

synopsis: Enroute FLM expressed his view on a recent operational decision that was questioned by higher management with regard to position management.
summary: An Operations Supervisor relieved a Sector 22 Controller who initially declined a D-Side, but minutes later the Controller requested one before a B737 and another aircraft lost separation and triggered TCAS alerts. The Supervisor attributes the event to resource limitations and management pressure, noting that a D-Side was immediately provided once requested.

synopsis: ELP Controller described a conflict event during combined operations in the Tower, citing equipment, procedural and other distractions as contributing factors.
summary: An Approach controller managing a combined TRACON and Tower position lost required separation between a military helicopter and a King Air while distracted by VFR traffic and equipment limitations. The controller failed to secure visual separation from the Tower due to unanswered calls and lack of supervisory support, resulting in a potential loss of separation.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a conflict event when failing to insure the planned sequence was provided to pattern traffic.
summary: An air traffic controller managed two helicopters requesting arrivals while a B717 descended through 2,500 feet. The controller failed to explicitly sequence the helicopters, causing Helicopter Y to pass overhead of Helicopter X, which the controller attributed to assuming visual contact and known plans.

synopsis: After taxiing into position for takeoff, B737-700 flight crew was informed by a ground vehicle of fluid leaking from the Number Two engine. Upon return to gate, a significant fuel leak is discovered.
summary: The flight crew held on Runway 22L after ground personnel identified a significant fluid leak from the #2 engine. The crew secured the engine, returned to the gate on one engine, and the aircraft was taken out of service for a confirmed fuel leak at idle.

synopsis: Although the reporter First Officer was opposed to doing so, the Captain of a B737-300 decided to complete their flight notwithstanding reports from other flights that there was a panel door open, possibly the external power panel door. Their Maintenance Department had advised them to do so as no damage would result.
summary: The crew received a report of a possible open external power door while cleared for takeoff. Maintenance advised departing as normal, but the First Officer later concluded they should have returned to the gate to avoid potential damage risks.

synopsis: Although they believe they programmed the FMS properly to comply with ATC's clearance to cross HALIE at 6,000 MSL the flight crew was surprised to find they had never left 10,000 MSL when ATC queried them about making the restriction. An acknowledged contributing factor was the flight crew's failure to monitor their flight path, anticipating that the FMS would do what they thought they had programmed.
summary: Two pilots descending an aircraft in the MDW area failed to meet a HALIE crossing restriction at 6,000 feet due to distraction during a discussion about VNAV, despite correct FMC programming. They manually deployed speedbrakes and requested a vector to 4,000 feet, noting the autopilot remained in VNAV PATH without switching to VNAV SPD or providing adequate warnings.

synopsis: B757 flight crew experiences the loss of the Left Hydraulic System fluid shortly after takeoff. After complying with QRH procedures an emergency is declared and flight returns to departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced a left hydraulic system fluid loss shortly after takeoff while turning to 270 degrees at 2,000 feet. They declared an emergency, returned for a normal ILS landing, and were inspected for brake smoke before being cleared to tow.

synopsis: Dispatcher reported a serious concern regarding 'maintaining an operational control' during certain time periods based upon workload.
summary: Air traffic controllers in Sectors 43/59 reported that high traffic volumes from thunderstorm-prone regions before 1500L require two desks to maintain operational control. The reporter identified this staffing need as a serious safety concern rather than a complaint about workload.

synopsis: After they were advised of tire parts on their departure runway the flight crew of an E145 declared an emergency, performed two precautionary fly-bys for evaluation by ground personnel and and landed at their destination with CFR standing by. The passengers were deplaned on the taxiway and bussed to the terminal.
summary: The First Officer reported that after ATC advised of a suspected tire separation, the crew declared an emergency and performed two low passes to visually confirm gear integrity. Despite a longer landing roll, the aircraft landed safely with no fire or immediate danger, allowing for normal deplaning.

synopsis: CL300 flight crew reports an uncommanded landing gear retraction at 200 FT during approach. A go around is initiated and a TCAS RA is annunciated on downwind but evasive action is not required. On the second approach the gear handle is verified in the down detent and an uneventful landing ensues.
summary: During an ILS approach at 200 FT AGL, the crew experienced an uncommanded landing gear retraction caused by a selector malfunction, prompting a go-around. After resolving the issue and verifying the gear was locked down, they completed a safe visual landing.

synopsis: AA5 pilot reports encountering heavy turbulence at 5,000 FT while attempting to use Nexrad to avoid the worst weather.
summary: The pilot encountered heavy turbulence between BRV VOR and TAPPA Intersection while deviating to avoid rain and updrafts. The pilot lost the GPS display for an unknown reason, attributing the situation to excessive reliance on Nexrad Radar and a delayed deviation request.

synopsis: General Aviation pilot voiced concern regarding ATC handling by N90, noting the Controller's reluctance in issuing a pop-up IFR clearance unlike in previous years.
summary: A pilot reported that NY TRACON controllers are increasingly refusing pop-up IFR clearances due to suspected practice requests and claims that Flight Service is now private. The pilot believes this reluctance to accept clearances for unexpected IMC or low ceilings compromises safety.

synopsis: After transiting through a Towered Airport's airspace at night, a BH206 pilot subsequently found that the radio in use was inoperative. Pilot noted that the red light gun signal used by the Tower would appear as green when using Night Vision Goggles (NVG).
summary: A pilot conducting a Night Vision Goggle flight experienced radio failure on the #1 radio while approaching ZZZ Tower, preventing communication and obscuring red light gun signals which appeared green. The pilot landed safely after contacting the tower via phone, and a mechanic later replaced the #1 radio antenna to restore operation.

synopsis: Bonanza pilot reports crossing the hold line for Runway 28L on Taxiway A, thinking it is an ILS hold line due to its distance from the runway.
summary: The pilot taxied past the runway hold short line, mistaking it for an ILS hold short line. This error occurred because the hold short line was located well before the runway threshold.

synopsis: A UPF7 pilot landed dead stick after the engine failed due to fuel exhaustion while entering the pattern.
summary: A Gold Seal Master CFI experienced an engine failure due to fuel exhaustion while entering upwind for Runway 18, resulting in a successful power-off landing on Runway 9. The pilot attributed the incident to inaccurate fuel gauges and a previous incomplete tank top-off, despite preflight calculations indicating adequate fuel.

synopsis: Decathlon pilot reports landing gear separation from the aircraft shortly after touching down on a paved runway. As the the aircraft slows it departs the runway to the left.
summary: The pilot reported that three seconds after landing, the left main gear of the 33-year-old aircraft failed due to existing cracks, striking the wing strut and fuselage. The pilot maintained control during the rollout but veered off the runway when the wingtip dipped before stopping.

synopsis: A single pilot reports noticing a 5-1/2 inch tear on top of the right wing with several rivets missing above the right Main Landing Gear (MLG) on a PA-28R180 aircraft.
summary: The pilot reported a landing gear malfunction on a midfield left downwind for Runway 17C, where the nose and right main gear initially failed to lock but subsequently indicated down. Post-landing inspection revealed a wing tear and missing rivets attributed by a mechanic to previous hard landings, rendering the aircraft unairworthy.

synopsis: ZAU Controller described a supervisory decision to change to DARC operations with weather moving coupled with other computer anomalies, the reporter suggesting supervisors heed controllers recommendations regarding DARC scheduling.
summary: Air traffic controllers at the Center operated in DARC mode during late-night weather despite worker recommendations. ETMS strip failures and a computer glitch causing beacon code swaps forced manual coordination and track cancellations, leading the reporter to suggest rescheduling computer maintenance during such weather events.

synopsis: BOI Controller reported vectoring below the MVA because of a slow climbing GA aircraft. The reporter listed the recent elimination of the DVA as a contributing factor.
summary: A C182 pilot departing Boise on the BOI2 SID struggled to meet the climb gradient and risked terrain below the MVA. The controller vectored the aircraft 20 degrees right to avoid terrain, allowing the pilot to reach the filed altitude safely, and recommended reinstating a Diverse Vector Area.

synopsis: ZAU Controller described a busy/complex and unsafe traffic period during DARC operations noting a number of factors that should be considered by supervisors prior to approving DARC procedures.
summary: Three controllers at ZAU managed a sector inundated with weather-avoiding traffic while operating in DARC mode due to computer failures and missing flight data. The lack of management support and tools led to airspace violations and a near-miss between two aircraft at 39,000 feet, creating a dangerous situation the reporter attributes to unnecessary system downtime.

synopsis: A B737-700 autopilot failed to capture the SNEAD 7 11,000 FT TARRK constraint event though it was in the FMS with FL190 in the MCP.
summary: The flight crew departed LAS on an RNAV departure and inadvertently climbed through the 11,000 FT TARRK restriction while in VNAV. The crew attributed the deviation to insufficient monitoring of the autopilot and failure to manually set the next restrictive altitude in the mode control panel.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reports being dispatched with an inoperative rudder PCU and encountering moderate to severe turbulence. The aircraft rolls excessively and he questions the role the inoperative PCU may be playing. VHF communication problems are also reported.
summary: The crew encountered moderate/severe turbulence at FL220 while managing a deferred rudder PCU issue and a VHF radio failure that caused communication loss with ATC. They exercised Captain's Authority to deviate from crossing restrictions, received vectors for a visual approach, and landed safely with no injuries or aircraft damage.

synopsis: Confused by multiple ramp taxi lines, construction and NOTAMs, the Captain of a B777 initially followed the wrong yellow ramp taxi line that did not provide adequate safety margins. An alert Ramp Controller advised of his error.
summary: A B777 crew at Denver International Airport mistakenly followed a commuter RJ on a solid yellow taxi line during a south ramp construction deviation. Ramp Control intervened to redirect the aircraft to the correct second yellow line, noting the original markings and instructions were confusing for wide-body aircraft.

synopsis: An ERJ-190 Captain reported that because of staffing issues, his trip departed six hours late, arrived at the hotel near sunrise and after a minimum rest they were scheduled to flying 5 legs fatigued.
summary: The pilot crew faced a six-hour delay and reduced rest before a five-leg day due to inadequate staffing requiring a Reserve Captain. The reporter states this preventable situation compromised rest quality and safety despite the crew remaining fit to fly.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 flight crew, after encountering weather avoidance vectors, ATC requests to keep their speed up for arrival sequencing. They receive conflicting vertical navigation guidance from their FMS and are unable to comply with the crossing restriction at ROCAB on the TAMMY RNAV STAR to MEM.
summary: The flight crew encountered difficulties meeting altitude and speed restrictions at the ROCAB waypoint during a complex RNAV arrival into Memphis while deviating for thunderstorms. Incorrect VNAV guidance on the MFD compared to the PFD required a manual descent rate increase to 4,000 FPM to comply with the 10,000-foot and 230-knot requirement.

synopsis: EMB145 Captain describes the factors that resulted in missing a crossing restriction during the GIBBZ1 RNAV arrival to IAD.
summary: A Captain and inexperienced First Officer deviated above the vertical path indicator during an enroute clearance change to a new IAD arrival with multiple crossing restrictions. The deviation resulted from the First Officer's slow descent rate and confusion over restrictions, compounded by the Captain's delayed monitoring, though they recovered without ATC intervention.

synopsis: A Dispatcher reported one of his international flights returned to their departure airport and landed overweight due to an equipment cooling anomaly. He cited their failure to declare an emergency as the factor requiring a report to be made.
summary: A dispatcher coordinated a diversion for a flight returning due to an equipment cooling issue. The aircraft performed an overweight landing without declaring an emergency, prompting a reminder that policy requires an emergency declaration for such landings.

synopsis: An SF-340 crew was notified by ATC that a tire tread separated during the takeoff roll confirming the vibration felt at V1, so an emergency was declared and the flight return to land.
summary: The flight crew experienced a tire tread separation during takeoff roll, resulting in a tire left on the runway. They returned for a safe landing, where inspection revealed the separated tread caused damage to the engine cowling.

synopsis: An A310's enroute ATC and ACARS communications were disrupted as the aircraft deviated around thunderstorms at FL290. Once clear of the weather, normal communication were reestablished.
summary: The crew lost all communications with ATC due to heavy static while deviating around thunderstorms at FL290. They suspect a bonding issue after attempting 121.5 and ACARS without success, and the Captain logged the incident upon landing.

synopsis: An AT502B landed off airport because the fuel quantity and fuel low lights are unreliable during maneuvering flight and on these flights fuel was limited because of large hopper loads. Complacency and Fatigue were factors.
summary: The pilot experienced an off-field landing due to fuel exhaustion during an agricultural application flight. The cause was attributed to pilot complacency and fatigue regarding fuel loading verification, compounded by difficult-to-see warning lights and erratic fuel gauges during steep turns.

synopsis: A B767 flight crew departed 10,000 MSL prior to crossing KRAIN when flying the ILS 25L to LAX. They believed the use of FMS and the Altitude Alert setting for each crossing restriction--as opposed to setting the final altitude in the 'descent ladder' in the altitude alert and allowing VNAV to navigate the intermediate crossings--was a contributing factor.
summary: The flying pilot descended early from 10,000 feet at LUVYN while using Flight Level Change instead of VNAV during the LAX arrival, causing a temporary altitude deviation to 9,700 feet. The crew corrected the error after ATC intervention, and the pilot attributed the incident to high workload from company procedures requiring manual VNAV reselections.

synopsis: A BE-76 engine lost power after takeoff so the Instructor took control, shut the engine down and returned to the airport. A Mechanic had failed to secure the magneto after preflight maintenance.
summary: During a training flight's initial climb, the student pilot experienced a left engine failure at 700 feet caused by a magneto detaching from its mounting screws. The instructor took control, feathered the engine, and landed safely, though the propeller windmilled until touchdown due to an incomplete shutdown.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports he had used a Transponder Manufacturer's Maintenance Manual instead of the Aircraft Manufacturer's Service Bulletin to identify and remove an electrical wire from connectors on #1 and #2 Transponders on a Challenger CL-604 aircraft.
summary: The Challenger 604 crew lost transponder contact with ZZZZ1 Control due to a wiring error where Pin-21 was removed from the wrong plug during a previous Service Bulletin compliance. The issue stemmed from conflicting plug orientation instructions between Bombardier and Rockwell Collins manuals, which was corrected after flight testing confirmed the fault.

synopsis: A pilot incurred RDG Runway 36 on Taxiway B between Runways 36 and 31 because he taxied beyond the Runway 36 line toward the Runway 31 hold short line.
summary: A Local Control supervisor and Ground Control trainee managed Aircraft X, which repeatedly crossed Runway 31 hold lines while taxiing for a VFR departure. The pilot, unfamiliar with the airport, failed to hold short despite correct readbacks, highlighting confusion at a known hot spot regarding standard hold markings.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a loss of separation event during weather deviations and vectors to clear restricted airspace.
summary: An air traffic controller managing severe weather and a Warning Area experienced a potential conflict between Air Carrier X at FL340 and Air Carrier Y climbing to FL360. The controller attributed the incident to a misunderstanding regarding altitude reporting and data tag resets, noting that a supervisor later confirmed the aircraft lacked adequate separation.

synopsis: ZOB Controller described an adjacent airspace incursion when the automated hand off feature initiated the hand off to the inappropriate sector without controller corrective action.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller in the LAN Sector stopped an E135 at 15,000 feet due to traffic, but automation incorrectly flashed the handoff to the wrong sector. This caused a potential conflict with a CRJ2, requiring the controller to intervene and stop the CRJ2 at 14,000 feet.

synopsis: A pilot reported to his Company that while jump seating on another carrier's B737-800 he learned about a loss of thrust control (LOTC) is affecting some of that carriers -800's, but the cause is unknown.
summary: A pilot reported hearing from another carrier's crew about uncommanded engine rollbacks to idle on Boeing 737-800s, which they mitigate by carrying a minimum of 23,000 LBS of fuel. The reporter noted that Boeing engineers are investigating the cause, which persists despite initial beliefs that it was a winter-only issue.

synopsis: A B737-800 with an engine bleed air trip history was at FL330 when the Left Bleed tripped. To get over weather, they climbed to FL380 where there second bleed tripped, so an emergency was declared and the flight descended to 10,000 FT with crew and passenger oxygen in used.
summary: The pilot flying and captain experienced repeated left and right bleed trip-offs on an unpressurized flight, causing cabin altitude to rise and requiring an emergency descent to 10,000 feet. The crew managed the depressurization by donning oxygen masks, deploying passenger masks, and executing a rapid descent before landing uneventfully.

synopsis: A B777 Captain reported that at some point after oceanic track entry, the ACARS dropped its initialization which prevented the aircraft from sending and receiving ACARS reports including Dispatch messages, fuel reports, and other critical communications.
summary: A pilot on a Boeing 777 cruise flight discovered ACARS failed to report position fuel due to a dumped initialization page, causing a loss of SATCOM communication. The pilot identified this as a recurring systemic issue affecting multiple aircraft, raising concerns about flight following and security message delivery.

synopsis: A Dispatcher reported that a Commercial Weather product used by his Company does not reference North Atlantic Air Traffic Agencies' SIGMET and Hazardous Weather reports causing miscommunication and confusion.
summary: A dispatcher reported that WSI SIGMET products lack official identification numbers issued by controlling authorities like Gander or Shanwick. This omission prevents crews and dispatchers from coordinating hazardous weather information using ATC-provided tags, which the reporter describes as frustrating and dangerous.
