synopsis: When they received a late 'descend via' clearance on the GIBBZ RNAV STAR to IAD, the flight crew of an A319 was unable to comply with the multiple altitude and airspeed restrictions and required ATC re-clearances to complete the arrival, citing the complexity of programming changes in a manner that satisfies the restrictions and the capabilities of the aircraft and the FMGS.
summary: Washington Center held the crew high on the GIBBZ1 arrival, causing an FMGS speed mode reversion and a late descent clearance. The First Officer's delay in correcting the speed and remaining in selected descent resulted in crossing MOSLE at 10,600 feet instead of the required 11,000 feet.

synopsis: A CE-560 pressurization failed at FL450 so an immediate descent was begun, an emergency declared, and while navigating around thunderstorms the crew diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a rapid cabin pressure climb at FL450 while avoiding thunderstorms, triggering an emergency descent to FL340 and then 10,000 feet. After consulting with the company, they diverted to a nearby airport and landed safely without further incident.

synopsis: When on the ILS 25L approach at LAX, the Captain elected to cross the intermediate segment fixes approximately 800 FT above the charted crossing altitudes. The First Officer advocated the need to cross at those altitudes, but the Captain disagreed, believing them to be minimum altitudes.
summary: The flight crew descended via ILS 25L using VNAV, crossing TAROC, DYMMO, and FUELER 800 feet above charted restrictions before correcting at GATTE. The reporter attributes the altitude deviations to VNAV limitations and suggests manual flying was necessary to meet crossing restrictions.

synopsis: An air carrier Captain reported his displeasure at what he believes to be unnecessary NOTAMed changes to crossing altitudes on the OLYMPIA STAR to SEA. He believes that anything other than emergency changes to airways procedures should be introduced via a chart revision.
summary: A pilot reported that frequent NOTAM changes to mandatory crossing altitudes and speeds on the OLM arrival into SEA create a safety threat. The reporter argues that burying these changes in scattered NOTAMs invites accidents and insists such modifications should only occur via revised approach plates.

synopsis: Mechanic reports he inspected, but did not notice a Horizontal Stabilizer (H/S) Pitch Trim switch had been installed 180-degrees from the proper position on an EMB-145 aircraft. An Operational Check of the Pitch Trim by another shift failed to notice the H/S moving in the opposite direction contributing to an inflight incident.
summary: A mechanic installed a First Officer's Pitch Trim switch 180 degrees incorrectly on an EMB-145, which the inspector failed to detect during sign-off. The error caused the horizontal stabilizer to move in the wrong direction during the subsequent operational check, prompting a manual discrepancy report and a request for updated warnings.

synopsis: A Maintenance Controller reported that a #2 DC Generator Caution light on a DHC-8-100 aircraft had illuminated in flight, was showing no loads and would not reset. The Generator was found to have left its mounting pad and sheared the Generator shaft. The V-Band clamp was in place, but reported cocked.
summary: A flight crew reported a #2 DC Generator fault, which Line Maintenance found had sheared its shaft and left its mounting pad due to improper securing. The generator, replaced the previous evening, was removed for inspection, and the Generator Control Unit was replaced.

synopsis: A C421 landing gear circuit breaker popped after takeoff, leaving the main gear down and locked but the nose gear out of the down position. After completing all checklists, an emergency landing was completed with the nose gear collapsing on landing.
summary: During a post-maintenance check flight in a C421, the nose gear circuit breaker popped upon retraction, leaving the nose gear unsecured and unresponsive to emergency extension attempts. The crew executed a nose-high landing, resulting in windmilling propeller damage after the nose settled on the runway.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot crossed the NEW Runway 36L hold short line on Taxiway B because the hold short point is so far from the runway it was not identified and he was confused by the signage when Taxiway F morphed into Taxiway B.
summary: The pilot crossed the hold short line for Runway 36L while searching for a run-up area due to confusing signage where Taxiway F blends into Taxiway B. The controller stopped the aircraft, directed a runway crossing, and reported a deviation, noting similar past incidents at that location.

aircraft: Cessna Single Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: The pilot of a C-162 was shocked when the cabin door appeared to burst open and disappear on a night flight. He declared an emergency and returned safely to his departure airport where he learned the door was still attached but had folded back out of reach. He also learned he had failed to secure a secondary latching mechanism installed as a result of a Service Bulletin addressing similar previous incidents.
summary: A pilot flying a Cessna 162 at night reported an emergency after the left door appeared to detach, though it was actually folded back due to an unlatched secondary latch. The pilot maintained control, landed safely, and attributed the incident to failing to secure the secondary latch despite a known Service Bulletin.

synopsis: A L-39 Canopy departed in flight climbing though 11,000 FT with air conditioning and indicating systems operating normally.
summary: During the climb of an L-39 ferry flight, the pilot and a mechanic experienced a cabin altitude warning followed by the left canopy separating after the pilot manually pulled it down. The pilot attributed the incident to improper canopy locking despite normal indicator lights and safely landed the aircraft, which was subsequently impounded for investigation.

synopsis: A B-737 flight test crew declared an emergency, donned oxygen masks, and returned to their departure airport due to recurring fumes in the cockpit.
summary: During a 737 first flight climb, the crew detected a rubber-like odor that persisted intermittently, prompting them to don oxygen masks and terminate flight checks. The crew declared an emergency for priority handling and landed uneventfully after reporting the fumes to Quality Assurance and Maintenance.

synopsis: PCT Controller experienced a loss of separation event between two arrivals to IAD. The reporter listed the new GIBBS RNAV STAR's track as contributing to the event.
summary: An air traffic controller lost separation between a Hawker and a CRJ during the CRJ's base turn on the GIBBZ RNAV arrival due to the aircraft's wider-than-expected path. The controller attributed the incident to the new arrival procedure's fix placement and airspace boundaries, recommending a westward shift of the SIYOB fix.

synopsis: M03 Controller described a near loss of separation event between two successive FNCHR1 arrivals. The reporter listed the OPD procedures and the unfamiliarity with same by the ZME controllers as likely causal factors.
summary: An ATC controller managing an MD11 arrival observed a B777 overtaking it with less than 4 miles lateral separation due to the B777 pilot's slow compliance with speed restrictions. The controller attributed the incident to ZME controllers' unfamiliarity with Optimum Descent Path procedures and a lack of management support for issuing immediate heading changes.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a loss of separation event claiming 'mental fatigue' was a contributing factor.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a potential conflict between an E145 at FL280 and a B737 at FL290 by issuing descent and turn instructions while the B737 climbed via TCAS. The controller attributed the situation to prolonged position time, high workload, and resulting mental fatigue.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a weather encounter that prompted an immediate descent because of hail and resulted in an emergency with aircraft damage.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored a Cessna 402 left of extreme precipitation, but the pilot encountered severe hail while descending through the weather. The aircraft sustained wing and nose dents plus a cracked ice viewing shield, yet the pilot landed safely without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: EMB-135 First Officer reports requesting he be removed from a flight due to the Captain's overweight condition causing a restriction to the yoke in the full up elevator direction.
summary: A First Officer reported restricted control travel and blocked emergency exit access during the second leg due to the Captain's extreme size. The First Officer requested reassignment or removal from the flight, but scheduling had no available trips.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: An MD80, cleared via the FRDMM RNAV STAR to DCA experienced excessive workload due to the complexity of the multiple airspeed and altitude restrictions required by the STAR. The workload was exacerbated by the inability of their FMS to both display and comply with the restrictions because it lacked the ability to program crossing altitude 'windows.' In addition, after having cleared them 'via' the arrival, Approach later cleared them direct to a waypoint beyond the waypoint whose altitude restriction constituted the flight's 'cleared' altitude. The Controller seemed unaware of their problem until precious comm time was taken to explain the fact they no longer had a cleared altitude.
summary: Pilots flying a new RNAV arrival enroute reported high workload due to FMS limitations in displaying bracketed altitudes. Confusion arose when ATC amended the clearance to bypass a fix, removing its crossing restriction, leading to unclear descent instructions from Potomac Approach.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A flight crew departed their ELP gate and cleared to taxi to Runway 8R when they expected a long taxi to Runway 26 and almost immediately entered 8R at K, surprised at how close the runway was to the terminal.
summary: The crew at ELP taxied past the Runway 8R approach hold short line due to high workload and confusion over a sudden runway change. Ground instructed them to contact Tower, which immediately cleared them for takeoff from that position, highlighting a need for better situational awareness and communication.

synopsis: B737-400 Captain experiences numerous anomalies during climb including loss of cabin pressurization, possibly caused by a faulty ground/air sensor. Plastic bags were found in the outflow valve on post flight.
summary: During climbout, a flight crew experienced autothrottle, transponder, and pressurization failures caused by debris in the outflow valve. The crew declared an emergency, descended to 10,000 feet, and diverted for an uneventful landing.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain notices the aircraft is not pressurizing early in the climb, just before the forward Flight Attendant reports a loud air leak at the forward entry door. Flight returns to the departure airport for an overweight landing.
summary: The flight crew and Number 1 Flight Attendant experienced a pressurization failure and loud air leak from the forward entry door at 4,500 MSL after takeoff. They declared an emergency, performed an overweight landing with normal approach parameters, and confirmed no hot brakes upon rollout.

synopsis: While 'descending via' the FRDMM RNAV STAR to DCA the flight crew of an MD80 lost both FMSs and their associated Map displays thus rendering them unable to comply with the RNAV procedure. ATC ultimately provided vector and altitude clearances to a successful visual approach. The logbook showed two recent FMC failures. When asked to fly another leg with both FMS systems deferred the Captain refused the aircraft and the flight was canceled.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a total FMS failure on an MD80 during the FRDMM One RNAV arrival into DCA. Citing cumulative fatigue, high workload, and maintenance history, the Captain refused the aircraft after it was placarded per the MEL, resulting in a canceled flight.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: MD80 Captain experiences compressor stalls on Number 1 engine, left yaw, and burning rubber smell at Vr. An emergency is declared and thrust is reduced on the malfunctioning engine. Flight returns visually with the number one engine at reduced thrust. Post flight reveals that one of the main gear tires has shed its' tread.
summary: The Pilot Flying experienced compressor stalls and left yaw on a heavy aircraft during takeoff in hot conditions, suspecting a left tire blowout. The crew returned for an emergency landing, secured the left engine, and taxied clear of the runway after ground personnel confirmed the tire was damaged but holding air.

synopsis: When the flight crew felt it necessary to override autoflight vertical navigation to meet the altitude and airspeed restrictions of the FNCHR RNAV STAR to MEM they momentarily descended below the crossing restriction an LOONR.
summary: During an RNAV arrival, the crew descended below the 9,000 FT restriction at LOONR after switching to Level Change mode while retaining 4,000 FT in the altitude window. The error resulted from an FMS Cost Index failing to meet speed restrictions and the crew's inexperience with the new procedure, requiring an immediate climb to correct the altitude.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports finding a Mid lavatory (lav) light lens bonded in place and no electrical wiring attached. Further trouble shooting located the 'Hot' (power on), electrical wires hanging between the Galley module and the inner fuselage.
summary: Mechanics on a B757-200 discovered a mid-lavatory light lens bonded in place with wiring missing and live between the galley and fuselage. After killing power, they rerouted the wires per WDM 33-26-21, restored function, and released the aircraft.

synopsis: When his single turbine engine quit at FL190 the pilot of a TBM-700 dropped into a conveniently located airport.
summary: The pilot reported an engine failure during flight, necessitating a diversion to the nearest suitable airport for a landing. The pilot stated the event occurred quickly and that no different actions could have been taken.

synopsis: BE33 pilot describes using XM weather in flight to determine that continuing to destination was not advisable and that deviating to TOL to spend the night was the best option.
summary: The pilot diverted from Akron back to Toledo Express due to deteriorating weather, specifically a 600-foot overcast ceiling and strengthening thunderstorms. The crew elected to stay overnight in Toledo to refuel and reassess conditions before continuing the flight the next day.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot made incorrect turn to initiate the VOR A approach to FUL due to misinterpretation of the GPS graphic display.
summary: The pilot and safety pilot executing a practice VOR A approach to FUL incorrectly turned left during the procedure turn by following a misleading GPS graphic instead of the published plate. SCT Approach controllers queried the deviation and corrected the pilot to the required right turn.

synopsis: A transient pilot was cleared to LZU Runway 25 via Taxiway D, hold short at W, but because of faded hold short lines he taxied beyond the hold line.
summary: A pilot taxiing at an unfamiliar airport passed the faded hold short line for Runway 25 due to an unusual clearance and reliance on ground markings. The pilot stopped upon seeing the runway marker, was cleared to cross by Ground, and reported no runway incursion or near miss.

synopsis: Confusion reigned at MEM when an A300 flight crew crossed LTOWN Intersection just as the airport was turning around to land to the north. When told to fly the 'North transition' the crew interpreted that to mean 'take the Northerly' track from LTOWN. ATC recognized the error and provided a clearance back to the 'Southerly' track appropriate for flights landing 'to' the north.
summary: The flight crew and Memphis ATC encountered confusion during the LTOWNE6 RNAV arrival due to non-standard "North transition" phraseology while the airport switched landing directions. The controller clarified the situation by issuing a direct clearance to rejoin the arrival, prompting a later bulletin to standardize terminology for these new procedures.

synopsis: ZDC Controller described a heavily impacted traffic period by weather conditions resulting in multiple airspace infractions due to deviation events. The reporter listed the lack of TMU interventions as problematic.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported an unsafe situation where an A321 deviated over 20 miles into New York Center airspace due to severe weather and failed Traffic Management Unit flow restrictions. The controller declared an emergency after coordination delays, eventually transferring the aircraft to New York Approach.

aircraft: Light Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: ZOA Controller described a probable MVA event when traffic departing FAT was restricted to 100 eastbound as per LOA. The reporter suggested needed changes to the procedure.
summary: An Air Carrier climbing eastbound from FAT to 100 failed to contact ZOA, remaining level near high terrain until the pilot reported visual contact and accepted a VFR climb. The controller attributed the incident to an unsafe handoff procedure requiring higher altitude clearance before transfer.

synopsis: A pilot crossed LOU Runway 33 after ATC cleared him twice to hold short. He acknowledged and then crossed Runway 33 anyway.
summary: A pilot taxiing from an FBO to hangars across Runway 33 received hold short instructions twice but crossed the runway after reading back "ROGER." The reporter attributed the incident to poor communication procedures by the pilot.

synopsis: Local Controller failed to issue missed approach instructions after an aircraft cleared via a visual approach lost sight of the airport, this all occurred when simultaneous approach procedures were suppose to be in place.
summary: An air traffic controller allowed an aircraft on a visual approach to Runway 1R to continue after the pilot lost sight of the airport at 1,500–2,000 feet. The pilot later regained visual contact and landed, but the controller concluded the approach should have been cancelled and the Monitor should have intervened.

synopsis: ZBW Controller indicated a probable loss of separation event noting facility sector combination protocols were contributory to this event, adding combination decisions should be made at the sector level.
summary: An air traffic controller in Sector 09 reported a loss of separation between an Air Carrier X flight at FL380 and a descending aircraft from Sector 08. The controller attributed the event to the premature splitting of Sectors 08 and 09, which increased complexity and constrained airspace during bad weather reroutes.

synopsis: Tower Controller reported a loss of separation when the Local Controller failed to secure a correct read back resulting in an overflight of traffic at an intersection.
summary: A Local Controller issued improper restricted low approach instructions to a Skyhawk without a readback, causing it to overfly a Lear at the runway intersection during a touch-and-go. The incident resulted from the controller failing to follow proper clearance procedures and not issuing a go-around when separation was lost.

synopsis: Enroute Controller noted the rapid descent of an aircraft squawking emergency. The reporter noted pilots should be more forth coming with information to ATC as to their status.
summary: A C750 en route at FL470 requested and received clearance to descend to FL430 before becoming unresponsive with an emergency beacon code and rapid descent. The aircraft landed safely after rapid depressurization caused deteriorated transmission capability, which also hindered Tower communications during the approach.

synopsis: After parking at the gate after a normal landing a B767-400ER developed a small fire on the left main gear brakes, apparently fueled by a fluid leak onto the hot brakes. The fire was extinguished by the time the flight crew exited the aircraft to inspect the problem.
summary: After a normal landing and taxi, ground personnel reported a left main brake fire while the crew observed smoking fluid leaking from the right rear main gear. The crew kept brakes set until mechanics confirmed the fire was extinguished, though no flames were seen by the pilots.

synopsis: A Companion Dog on an A320 became ill and loose boweled, requiring a potentially toxic cleaning agent to clean up. The crew refused aircraft for flight because of fumes.
summary: The pilot refused an inbound aircraft for passenger operations due to intense fumes from 'Aero Clean X-200' used to clean a dog's vomit and feces. The company's claim of no available replacements was false, resulting in an unnecessary two-hour delay once another aircraft was found.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reports the runway lights turning off right as the aircraft is in the flare. With sufficient light from landing lights the landing is successfully completed.
summary: During the flare phase of a night landing at LCH, runway lights turned off. The pilot used aircraft landing lights to execute a normal landing, deeming a go-around or radio call to restore lights unnecessary and distracting.

synopsis: Embraer 145 Captain experiences a Hydraulic System 1 overheat in cruise and elects to divert, although the company suggested they continue to destination. After landing and waiting three and a half hours for a replacement aircraft the crew flies three hours to destination. A fatigue call is used to prevent flying another two hour leg departing after midnight.
summary: The flight crew diverted due to a Hydraulic System 1 overheat caused by a failed engine-driven pump, burning fuel to test gear extension before landing with reduced braking. Post-landing fatigue from the emergency, a 3.5-hour wait, and scheduling disputes led the crew to call out fatigued after receiving a reduced rest period.

synopsis: A300 flight crew reports failure of the right main gear to extend during approach. A go around is initiated and the manual gear extension checklist is used to obtain a safe indication. A wind shift requires a runway change prior to landing and Maintenance tows the aircraft to the ramp due to inoperative nose wheel steering.
summary: During approach, the right main gear failed to extend, prompting an emergency declaration and manual extension. A thunderstorm shifted winds out of limits, forcing a landing on the west runway where the aircraft stopped with no nose wheel steering.

synopsis: A B767-200 departing Europe on an ETOPS flight had to divert for maintenance when multiple system components failed due to a faulty Circuit Breaker. The breaker had been worked on by Maintenance prior to departure as a result of an inoperative EICAS screen but was deemed ultimately to have been fixed.
summary: The crew experienced a faulty 115V AC BUS1 SEC2 circuit breaker that popped during preflight and again after takeoff, causing multiple system failures. They diverted to burn fuel to maximum landing weight before landing safely, with maintenance later confirming the breaker was the cause.

synopsis: An A321 flight crew declared an emergency and landed uneventfully at their destination when the Yellow Hydraulic System failed due to low fluid.
summary: During cruise, the crew received a HYD Y SYS LO RSVR ECAM and declared an emergency with Approach Control. The flight landed normally, though the right thrust reverser was inoperative due to the hydraulic system issue.

synopsis: When the left engine reverser and master caution lights illuminated shortly after takeoff the flight crew elected to return to their departure airport for maintenance attention.
summary: The crew experienced a left engine reverser light and master caution during rotation, leveling at 5,000 MSL to run the QRH. Despite maintenance advice to continue, they returned for an overweight landing due to safety concerns over water, finding the reverser pinned post-landing.

synopsis: Q400 flight crew reports a main cabin door seal failure resulting in no pressurization and a call from the forward Flight Attendant reporting the air leak. Flight returns to the departure airport for an overweight landing.
summary: The flight crew and flight attendant reported a main cabin door seal failure after takeoff, causing pressurization loss and water ingress despite the door appearing locked. The crew returned for an overweight emergency landing at 63,500 lbs, using TOLD cards due to a lack of maintenance contact.

synopsis: When an air carrier flight crew suffered the loss of multiple pitot static system ice protection systems shortly after takeoff they had to declare an emergency with ATC in order to avoid flying through icing conditions as they returned to their takeoff airport.
summary: The pilot experienced multiple pitot and static heat caution messages shortly after takeoff, leading to an aircraft malfunction. After declaring an emergency to escape icing conditions when ATC initially denied a descent, the crew received clearance to descend and returned safely to the departure airport.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: DHC8 Captain experiences failure of the landing gear to retract after being selected up. Maintenance was contacted and determined that the cause was the alternate release door was in the open position.
summary: The pilot reported that landing gear failed to retract after takeoff due to the alternate release door being left open. Maintenance performed a satisfactory evaluation flight, and the pilot attributed the error to a lack of concentration during preflight checklist duties.

synopsis: CE680 flight crew experiences a loud bang followed by a low vibration and rumbling during descent for landing. All indications in the cockpit are normal but the crew diverts for maintenance at the company's request. Post flight revealed that most of the bottom of the right engine cowling was missing.
summary: Two separate ferry flights experienced a loud bang and severe vibration during descent, leading to emergency diversions. Post-landing inspections revealed significant damage and missing cowling on the right engine, though the cause remained unknown to the crews.

synopsis: B737-400 Captain reported diverting due to loss of Captains displays and low ceilings at the destination. With Maintenance accomplished and additional fuel the flight departs for the original destination. One week later the Captain is informed that CFR was not available was not available during his departure in violation of company Operations specifications.
summary: The Captain diverted to an alternate due to dual display failures during initial descent above 10,000 feet. Although the crew landed and departed legally, they later learned the airport lacked required fire and crash rescue services for takeoff, a gap the pilot attributed to unclear dispatch authorization.

synopsis: When the MD83's TAIL COMPARTMENT TEMPERATURE HIGH LIGHT illuminated shortly after takeoff the flight crew declared an emergency and requested an immediate landing on the departure airport's longest Northbound runway. ATC advised they were unable to clear traffic for an immediate landing on that runway and cleared them to land immediately on a parallel runway instead. The reporter took umbrage at their refusal after the event was resolved.
summary: The crew experienced a recurring tail compartment temperature light and a right reverser failure during takeoff, prompting an emergency return. Although the landing was safe, the pilot criticized ATC for denying the requested longer runway, arguing that emergency authority should prioritize the Captain's safety decisions over traffic coordination delays.

synopsis: A MD-82 landing gear failed to indicate down and locked after extension on approach, so a go around was executed, an emergency declared, the QRH complied with and the aircraft returned to land with three green lights.
summary: The flight crew approached the destination without landing gear extension confirmation, discontinued the approach, and declared an emergency. After a go-around confirmed gear down and a second approach showed three green lights, the aircraft landed uneventfully with emergency equipment standing by.

aircraft: Boeing Company Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer describes the circumstances leading up to an engine overheat warning shortly after takeoff on a very hot day. The engine is shut down and flight returns to departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced an intermittent Engine 2 overheat light caused by a faulty detection switch and loop malfunction during taxi. Despite MEL clearance, the light illuminated steadily after lift-off, forcing an emergency shutdown of Engine 2 and a single-engine landing.

synopsis: An air carrier aircraft's #2 Center Fuel Tank pump MEL'ed fuel was part of the ZFW but, after an over board vent fuel leak, Load Planning decided the aircraft was overweight. Dispatch was reluctant to help because of workloads.
summary: The Captain reported a right wing fuel leak caused by an overpressure light, which stopped after transferring 500 lbs of fuel to the center tank. Subsequent dispatch communication delays and a 68 lb weight reduction requirement were resolved before a normal takeoff.

synopsis: A non-GPS B737-300 had a track deviation after takeoff on a RNAV departure after the Flight Director gave an incorrect turn command.
summary: The pilot flying of a Boeing 737-300 departed Runway 18L and deviated from an ATC clearance by following erroneous flight director commands while in LNAV mode. The incident resulted from automation reliance, autopilot engagement failure, and a lack of cockpit communication and cross-checking between the crew.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An MD-80 Captain refused to accept the GIBZZ RNAV STAR to IAD because his GPS equipped aircraft was not equipped with an FMS with full functional VNAV capability. He cited the complexity of the waypoint crossing restrictions as incompatible with flight safety.
summary: The MD80 crew rejected the GIBBZ1 RNAV arrival due to unsafe descent rates incompatible with their aircraft, initially requesting and receiving a DOCCS1 route change. When reassigned GIBBZ1 en route, they informed ATC they could not meet the vertical profile, resulting in assigned level-offs.

synopsis: A MD-80 #1 tire shredded between V1 and rotation causing compressor stalls so an emergency was declared and the aircraft returned to land overweight. The aircraft developed hot brakes which were cooled on the runway.
summary: The crew experienced left engine compressor stalls during takeoff, which ceased after reducing thrust to 80% N1. Following a high-speed landing with hot brakes, a suspected shredded tire was found to have thrown its cap into the engine, requiring maintenance inspection.

synopsis: When, following spacing victors, the flight crew of a B757-200 was re-cleared direct to FNCHR and to descend via the FNCHR RNAV STAR the flight crew failed to note a speed restriction previously programmed at ARG on the STAR was no longer an active part of their new clearance. As a result they failed to cross FNCHR at the charted 290 KTS.
summary: The pilot not flying missed a dropped 290 KTS speed constraint in the FMS after a direct clearance to FNCHR during descent into Memphis. This distraction caused the aircraft to arrive at FNCHR at 300 KTS, requiring a reclearance, though the flight concluded with an uneventful landing.

synopsis: Three Aircraft Maintenance Technicians (AMTs) report that four bushings had separated from the left Main Landing Gear (MLG) Axle Flange when the # 2 Inboard Brake was removed. The bushings had remained stuck to the removed Brake Assembly alignment pins and were not noticed until the A320 aircraft had departed.
summary: Mechanics replacing a difficult-to-remove brake on an A320 departed for ZZZ1 before discovering four axle flange bushings remained stuck to the removed assembly. The report attributes this to the bushings separating from the axle flange and notes the Aircraft Maintenance Manual lacks a specific inspection procedure for their installation.

synopsis: Two mechanics and one Inspector report about an Emergency Power Assist System (EPAS) bottle that was not re-serviced on a B777-200 aircraft after a slide replacement. The same slide also fell out of the slide pack the next day at the gate due to a foreign object.
summary: A mechanic replacing deployed door slides on an aircraft overlooked the final Maintenance Manual step to check the Emergency Power Assist System reservoir pressure due to complacency. This error was discovered at the gate, resulting in the aircraft being taken out of service.

synopsis: A C-560XL pilot expressed concern that recent RNAV SIDs and STARs are overly complex and complained that ATC issued them during periods of already high work loads, thus compromising the flight crew's ability to properly program, review, brief, and implement them and still maintain situational awareness with respect to their aircraft's track, performance, and compliance with the restrictions associated with their revised clearance. The reporter cited such procedures at MEM as pertinent examples.
summary: A pilot reported that new SID and STAR procedures at MEM create a safety of flight issue by requiring FMS programming during critical taxi and descent phases. The reporter attributes this to late runway assignments and complex charts, which increase cockpit workload and distract crews from external monitoring.

synopsis: BE58 pilot reported that a child passenger raised the gear handle on landing roll resulting in a partial gear collapse.
summary: During landing, a six-year-old passenger grabbed the gear handle, causing the landing gear to unlock on a runway bump. The aircraft stopped on the inboard and nose gear doors with minimal damage and no injuries.

synopsis: C206 pilot at 10,000 FT experiences communications failure followed shortly by a burning electrical smell and smoke. All avionics are shut down and the reporter commences an emergency descent to the closest airport. During the descent the smoke begins to dissipate and a safe landing ensues.
summary: The pilot of a patient transport aircraft experienced an intercom panel power supply failure causing smoke and audio loss while exiting Class B airspace at 10,000 feet. The pilot shut down avionics, diverted, and landed safely, later confirming the melted board caused the incident.

synopsis: Despite repeated maintenance attention to the cargo door warning micro switch prior to departure, the P-180 Flight Crew received a cargo door warning light 20 minutes after takeoff from a high altitude airport. After consultation with Maintenance they returned to their departure airport, opting to not comply with the checklist requirement that the aft mounted left engine be shut down due to its propiquity to the door.
summary: The crew experienced an intermittent baggage door annunciator light in cruise due to a faulty microswitch, prompting a return to the departure airport. Maintenance realigned the door per the manual, resolving the issue without an emergency declaration or pilot deviation.

synopsis: When the UAV's original route of flight was compromised by an active MOA, its flight crew received vectors around populated areas and to the vicinity of their recovery station.
summary: ATC vectored a UAV over populated areas to avoid military airspace, violating operational restrictions. The crew repeatedly requested alternative headings, and ATC adjusted vectors to avoid cities before handing off to Approach for an incident-free recovery.

synopsis: AgCat pilot reports departing with fuel gauge reading full, to run out of fuel 40 minutes into the flight. A safe landing on a highway ensues with minor damage to the aircraft. Fuel gauge was inaccurate.
summary: The pilot reported fuel starvation during agricultural operations after departing with a full tank indicated by a faulty gas gauge. The aircraft was safely landed on a highway with minor wingtip damage, refueled at a nearby farm, and subsequently took off safely.

synopsis: Glider pilot reports landing on Runway 2, at an uncontrolled airport, after electrical failure renders his radios inoperative. Runway 2 is currently being used for glider operations and is into the prevailing wind but a commuter turboprop elects to use Runway 20. The reporter pulls his aircraft as far off the runway as possible as the turboprop rotates just prior to the glider.
summary: A glider pilot with an electrical failure landed on Runway 02 while a tow plane departed, then held the glider clear as a twin turboprop commuter aircraft took off from Runway 20 and passed overhead at 50 feet. No damage or injuries occurred, and the pilot recommended all traffic take off into the wind to match glider operations.

synopsis: Light Sport Aircraft (LSA) pilot reports being cut off on the taxiway by a C150, which proceeds to takeoff without communicating on CTAF. The LSA pilot proceeds to takeoff also 150 feet behind the C150 and discovers that his aircraft is faster than the C150 requiring evasive action.
summary: A Thorp pilot followed a Cessna onto the runway without CTAF communication, overran it during climb-out, and side-stepped right to avoid collision. The reporter attributed the incident to the Thorp pilot's error in judging the Cessna as faster and the Cessna's failure to communicate.

synopsis: C182 pilot reports being intercepted by an F16 south of Chicago then informed after landing that he had flown through a TFR that was shown as expired on his GPS display.
summary: A pilot flying a general aviation aircraft near Chicago encountered three fighter jet fly-bys after relying on ADS-B data showing an expired TFR. The pilot contacted multiple ATC facilities, received a squawk code, and was later informed by Chicago TRACON that the flight had actually penetrated an active TFR due to outdated electronic data.

synopsis: C172RG pilot reports a belly landing when the landing gear fails to extend prior to touching down and the propeller contacting the runway. A visual approach was being attempted through a broken cloud layer.
summary: A VFR pilot approaching ZZZZ at 9,500 feet descended through broken clouds and received landing clearance. The landing gear failed to extend, and the pilot attempted a go-around but was too low, resulting in the propeller striking the ground.

synopsis: Local Controller described a conflict event between a VFR helicopter arrival and an unknown target suddenly appearing to the side of the helicopter.
summary: A VFR helicopter inbound from the northwest at 1,500 feet encountered an unknown target at the same altitude on its left. The pilot called traffic, prompting the other aircraft to take evasive action and descend immediately to approximately 1,200 feet.

synopsis: SCT Controller described a conflict event between a LGB Air Carrier arrival and a VFR King Air departing SNA seeking an IFR clearance, the reporter indicting a heads-up from SNA Tower would have eased the situation.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managed a King Air departing SNA and an Airbus on ILS approach to LGB when the Airbus received a TCAS RA and climbed unannounced. The King Air turned right to avoid the Airbus, which the controller attributed to a lack of prior coordination and communication from other towers.

synopsis: PCT Controller described a conflict event occurring after an aircraft was cleared for a visual approach on base, but failed to turn toward the airport to the correct runway.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored a Citation near a Premier that failed to turn for a visual approach to Runway 33R at BWI. The Premier crossed both final approach paths, forcing the controller to climb the Citation to 2,500 feet to avoid a collision before both aircraft landed safely.

synopsis: Enroute Controller provided a number of suggestions with regard to Traffic Management initiates prompted by weather, retsricted areas and airspace constraints.
summary: An air traffic controller and a military BE20 at FL280 encountered a weather cell between restricted areas, causing the aircraft to deviate and declare an emergency. The reporter attributes the incident to a lack of compliance with CAR 40 TELECON requirements and insufficient Traffic Management Initiatives to manage Special Use Airspace proximity.

synopsis: ZBW Controller described a conflict event between a VFR and an IFR inbound to ACK. The situation was complicated by a number of aircraft requesting IFR clearances.
summary: A Radar Controller and a pilot at Cape Cod missed a traffic alert between a VFR C402 and an IFR aircraft descending into ACK due to high traffic complexity and shared frequencies. The VFR pilot nearly collided with the IFR aircraft in clouds, prompting the IFR pilot to report the near miss after canceling his flight plan.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported that engine #1 overheat light illuminated on taxi out. Engine was shut down, fire bottle discharged, and flight returned to gate.
summary: During taxi out, the ENG 1 overheat light illuminated, prompting the crew to follow the QRH, declare an emergency, and return to the gate. While cockpit indications remained normal except for the light, external observers reported the engine appeared normal during the taxi.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew report accepting an aircraft that had a history of flap problems. On the first approach the flaps failed to extend when selected, but this is not detected by the crew until the EGPWS annunciates 'to low, flaps.' A go around is initiated, QRH procedures are complied with, an emergency is declared, and a flaps up landing ensues.
summary: The flight crew encountered a flap system failure during the approach phase, triggering a "Too Low Flaps" warning and necessitating a go-around. After troubleshooting failed, they declared an emergency and executed a successful high-speed, no-flaps landing with emergency services standing by.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported the T1 sign on FLL Taxiway B approaching Taxiway T1 east bound is missing.
summary: The pilot reported a missing Taxiway T1 sign along Taxiway Bravo eastbound approaching the T1 intersection at FLL. The reporter noted no sign has ever existed there and recommended installing one to properly mark the intersection.

synopsis: An ATL arrival was questioned by 'Ramp Control' regarding entry into the ramp area. The flight crew indicated that improvements in the charting depictions were needed reference 'ramp names/locations'.
summary: The flight crew entered the ramp without Ramp clearance while holding for another aircraft, causing a conflict with Ramp who stated they could not enter without communication. The crew stopped short of crossing vehicles after Ramp clarified the ramp's three-area division, a terminology not found on their ground charts.

synopsis: B757 flight crew experienced high vibration on the number two engine during climb and elected to return to the departure airport for an uneventful landing.
summary: During climb out at 13,500 feet, the crew observed high vibration on engine #2, with the indicator jumping from 0.3 to 3.0. After consulting Dispatch and Maintenance Control, they returned for an overweight landing.

synopsis: A320 First Officer experiences high N1 vibration (5 units) at FL350, which increases to 8 units in the next few minutes. As thrust is reduced for descent and landing at destination the vibration is reduced to 1.5 units and does not return.
summary: The First Officer reported high number 1 engine vibration and airframe rumble during cruise, which resolved after reducing thrust and descending to 26,000 feet. The crew suspects the issue relates to a previously signed-off drain mast leak, noting that a similar leak weeks earlier was caused by a failed internal O-ring.

synopsis: Airline flight crew reported #1 engine locked in idle thrust during climbout. Crew declared an emergency and returned to departure airport.
summary: During climb out at 12,000 feet, the #1 engine failed to respond to thrust inputs, causing a loss of climb performance. The crew executed a single-engine return to the departure airport using the Stalled Engine Checklist, resulting in an uneventful overweight landing with no ECAM warnings.

synopsis: CRJ200 First Officer reports uncontrolled pressurization of the the aircraft when the main cabin door is closed in preparation for engine start. The APU was inoperative and jetway preconditioned air was supplying the cabin. The emergency depressurization button is pushed to regain control but the damage is done and the crew requires medical attention.
summary: The flight crew experienced a rapid, dangerous cabin depressurization during door closure at the gate, likely caused by high-pressure ground air being connected while the main cabin door was closed. This resulted in severe physical symptoms for the crew, who were subsequently evacuated and sent to the hospital for medical evaluation.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: A Citation cleared to taxi north on M at DEN failed to hold short of ED as directed. ATC cleared them to make a 180 and hold short facing south.
summary: The flight crew inadvertently passed the hold short point for ED Taxiway while taxiing on M for Runway 17L. ATC instructed a 180-degree turn to reposition, resulting in no conflicts or safety concerns.

synopsis: When flying the FRDMM RNAV STAR to DCA an E-145 Captain advised the FMS NAV mode reverts to the ROLL mode when passing FNCHR and must be re-selected to continue to track the arrival. The reporter also cited excessive complexity of the many crossing restrictions required by the STAR which demand excessive attention by the flight crew during a critical phase of flight.
summary: A 145 crew descending on the FRDMM ONE RNAV arrival reported the autopilot NAV mode disengaging at FRDMM Intersection, requiring manual rearm to prevent deviation. The pilot attributed this to FMS software issues and noted the STAR's complexity causes excessive distraction for 145 crews.

synopsis: A CRJ had pre-programmed the 'landing north' transition on the FNCHR RNAV STAR to MEM and realized too late that the airport had switched to landing to the south, eliminating the long downwind track and lowering the appropriate crossing altitudes on the arrival. A modest failure to cross at the required altitude at one waypoint resulted.
summary: The flight crew returning to MEM loaded an outdated north transition RNAV STAR into the FMS, unaware of a traffic flow change to a south transition. This caused the crew to miss speed restrictions and arrive high on the profile, highlighting concerns about complex chart formats and the need for simpler procedures.

synopsis: G200 First Officer experiences a TCAS RA at TUGGZ FAF, with the Captain flying, during a visual approach to Runway 19 at TEB. Intruder was inside the Class D and not in contact with ATC.
summary: The flight crew on an ILS approach to Runway 19 received a TCAS Descend RA due to a small, non-transponder aircraft on a perpendicular path. The PIC complied with the RA, maintaining separation of approximately 300 feet horizontally and 0 feet vertically, and safely completed the landing.

synopsis: EC-135 pilot on night flight took evasive action to avoid another helicopter that was reported by ATC and detected by helicopter's TCAD.
summary: A medical helicopter crew executed a descending right turn to avoid a near mid-air collision with an unidentified air ambulance helicopter less than one mile away and 100 feet above. The reporter attributed the incident to the other pilot's failure to see and avoid despite the reporter's high-visibility lights and ATC warnings.

synopsis: B767 Flight Attendant describes departing on a planned seven hour flight then being informed upon arrival that she must fly another leg of five hours due to staffing issues.
summary: A flight attendant working ZZZ-ZZZ1 and ZZZ1-ZZZ2 without rest consumed moldy food and faced delays, resulting in extreme fatigue and a verbal confrontation with a CSR. The 12-hour-18-minute duty caused post-traumatic anxiety the following day.

synopsis: Two Line Mechanics report a right-hand Aft Overwing Escape Slide inadvertently deployed on a B757-200 aircraft while they were performing an MEL deferral procedure involving a Voltage Test of the Slide Squib connectors. The slide safety pin was not installed.
summary: Two mechanics attempting to defer a RH aft overwing slide squib on a non-ETOPS aircraft inadvertently deployed the slide while testing for voltage. The deployment occurred because they failed to pin the slide bottle after not reading the full AMM procedure.

synopsis: A PA28R-200 flight instructor took control of the aircraft on touchdown when the nose gear green light extinguished and the gear warning horn activated. He aborted the landing and went around while exercising positive and negative Gs in at attempt to lock the gear in place. A subsequent landing, however, repeated the warnings although the nose gear stayed in place when it was lowered slowly to the runway.
summary: During a training flight at a Class D airport, a nose gear unsafe indication occurred during the flare of an overhead approach to Runway 14. The instructor executed a go-around, landed with the nose wheel off the ground, and taxied to parking after the gear light reactivated on the landing roll.

synopsis: A Cessna Conquest pilot failed to recognize the remotely located hold short lines for a full length takeoff from Runway 28L at HWD.
summary: A pilot taxiing to Runway 28L at dusk passed the hold bars due to poor lighting and the bars appearing distant. The aircraft stopped in a run-up area past the hold bars and before a 45-degree turn, resulting in an inadvertent runway incursion.

aircraft: M-20 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Mooney M20T pilot reported that the landing gear would not retract after takeoff. While dealing with that distraction he entered restricted airspace.
summary: The pilot experienced a landing gear retraction failure after departure and turned down the radio volume to troubleshoot using the manual. While transiting a military control area without hearing ATC responses due to the low volume, the pilot eventually raised the gear and continued to the destination.

synopsis: C208 pilot reported engine failure in flight, resulting in safe return to departure airport.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine failure in flight and successfully landed at the departure airport.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) with Inspection Authority, reports a Piper PA28 Cherokee Six elected to land after the pilot reported the Lycoming IO-540 engine started making knocking noise. Two overhauled cylinders had been installed just ten flight hours earlier.
summary: A mechanic installed new cylinders with rocker arms on the wrong side due to an assumption about part numbers. After 10 hours of flight, the pilot heard a knocking noise and landed safely, leading to warranty repairs for the misalignment.

synopsis: Air Carrier being pushed back by 'Ramp Control' inadvertently entered an active taxiway without ATC approval.
summary: Ramp agents pushed the aircraft from an SFO gate onto an active taxiway without specific clearance, citing traffic avoidance. The crew contacted Ground to apologize for the incursion, which caused a brief delay for other aircraft.

synopsis: An air carrier pilot reported inadequate identification signs for Taxiways Bravo and Charlie at CHS.
summary: A pilot reported missing signage identifying Taxiway Bravo and the intersecting Taxiway Charlie when exiting Gate XX at CHS. The lack of signs occurred despite the taxiway locations being obvious on commercial airport diagrams.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported loss of trailing edge flaps on approach. The ran the procedure with no help, declared an emergency, and diverted to a nearby airport that featured longer runways.
summary: The First Officer flew an Airbus experiencing a locked trailing edge flap fault during approach, leading to an emergency declaration and diversion. While holding in a congested General Aviation area, the crew managed multiple TCAS advisories and traffic conflicts before executing an uneventful landing with abnormal configuration.

synopsis: B767 Captain is informed of a sweet burning smell in the cabin shortly after takeoff. The smell is very faint and quickly dissipates. One hour into the flight more vigorous smoke is detected in the cockpit and the flight diverts to the nearest suitable airport. The smoke began to subside and approximately five minutes later the EICAS displayed a RIGHT REIRC FAN message.
summary: The flight crew experienced intermittent smoke odors shortly after takeoff, followed by heavy cockpit smoke and a RIGHT REIRC FAN EICAS message one hour later. The captain declared an emergency, diverted, and performed an overweight landing, attributing the second incident to a burning right recirculation fan while the initial cause remained unknown.

synopsis: CRJ-700 flight crew descended from assigned altitude after misinterpreting ATC instruction, 'Cleared to intercept the approach' as clearance for the approach.
summary: Pilots misinterpreted an ATC clearance to intercept the GPS 19 approach as "cleared for the approach" at 4,000 feet, causing an early descent to 2,000 feet. The crew subsequently diverted to Runway 10 due to wind shear, attributing the incident to ambiguous phrasing and a failure to clarify the clearance.

synopsis: B717 had a wake vortex encounter at FL340 with an opposite direction B777 at FL350.
summary: The flight crew encountered wake turbulence from a B-777 passing 1,000 feet above at FL340, causing a 40-degree roll and momentary stick shaker activation. The pilot manually corrected the attitude, confirmed no injuries, and recommended offsetting tracks when passing heavy aircraft in light winds.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew reported loss of hydraulic system 3. Emergency was declared and a normal landing ensued.
summary: During descent, the Captain observed low hydraulic system 3 fluid and a gear disagree warning after lowering the gear. An emergency was declared, checklists were completed, and a normal landing was made without further incident.

synopsis: Air Carrier departing Runway 1R at SFO elected to slow the takeoff due to 'wake separation' based upon only time, the delay caused a go-around on Runway 28.
summary: The Captain reported that SFO Tower cleared their departure from Runway 01R too soon after a B757, ignoring wake turbulence separation and failing to mention an aircraft on final for 28R. The crew continued the takeoff roll to avoid conflicting with the landing aircraft, which subsequently executed a go-around.

synopsis: While inside JESTI navigating via the FNCHR RNAV STAR to MEM, Approach Control offered the flight crew of a B757-200 a more favorable runway for landing. When they programmed and executed the new runway the autoflight system turned off course and stopped their established rate of descent which resulted in a small track deviation and the failure to make the crossing restriction at LOONR.
summary: A newly IOE Captain and First Officer deviated from the vertical profile while accepting an ATC runway change from 36L to 36R. The crew crossed LOONR at 12,000 feet instead of the required 9,000–11,000 feet due to FMS reprogramming delays, requiring speed brakes to regain altitude before landing safely.

synopsis: An MD-11 flight crew was surprised when the aircraft entered a climbing right turn and the autothrottles advanced commensurately when the approach/land mode autoflight mode was selected. They disconnected the autopilot and autothrottles but gained nearly 1,000 FT before regaining flight path control.
summary: During a visual approach to 17R at 3,000 feet, the crew experienced an uncommanded high pitch and power right turn after selecting approach mode. The aircraft climbed to nearly 4,000 feet before the Captain manually disconnected the autopilot and autothrottles to regain control for an uneventful landing.

synopsis: An MD-11 Captain addressed concerns about the wording of an MEL regarding dispatch with the 'depressurization function' of a hydraulic system deferred rather than the Engine Driven Pump which was responsible for the 'function' failure. The Captain implies that MEL was utilized because deferring the pump would have required too much time to accomplish.
summary: The pilot reported a dispute with Maintenance Control regarding a deferred Engine Driven Pump 2R and the resulting Number 2 hydraulic system failure during the after-start test. The pilot concluded the Minimum Equipment List is poorly written because it fails to clarify that the system will fail in manual mode if the opposite pump fails.

synopsis: B767-300 flight crew reported rejecting the takeoff at about 120 KTS when the First Officer's airspeed indicator hung.
summary: The Captain and First Officer rejected a takeoff due to a large airspeed split caused by the First Officer's indicator stagnating at 90 KTS while the Captain's read 120 KTS. The aircraft stopped below V1, cleared the runway, and returned to the blocks for brake cooling and maintenance checks.

synopsis: C182T Pilot reported he could not disconnect his GFC700 autopilot, causing control difficulties. Pilot declared emergency and diverted to a suitable airport, where a safe landing was made using manual trim and power for control.
summary: The pilot and copilot experienced an uncontrollable climb in a G1000/GFC700-equipped aircraft after the autopilot failed to disengage despite multiple attempts. They declared a mayday, managed the descent using power and manual trim, and landed safely without flaps or yoke control.

synopsis: A NMAC occurred in the vicinity of MSN airport when the reporter's Lancair and a C-310, both VFR in MSN Class C airspace and in contact with Approach Control, received late traffic advisories from the Controller.
summary: A Lancair pilot under MSN Approach Control descending for Runway 03 executed an evasive climbing left turn after ATC advised of a converging Cessna 310. The pilot's action prevented a collision as the Cessna passed 300 feet behind and 100 feet below, allowing a normal landing to follow.

synopsis: While doing stop and go landings in a tundra tire equipped CC-11 homebuilt, the owner Student Pilot and the Reporter, providing instruction, lost control of the aircraft and groundlooped in a moderate gusty cross wind. The right tire was scuffed to the wheel rim and the right wingtip sustained some damage when it struck the ground.
summary: An instructor and student in a CC-11 homebuilt groundlooped on Runway 17 during stop-and-go landings in gusty crosswinds. The aircraft rolled over due to oversized low-pressure tundra tires acting as a pivot point, causing the right wingtip to strike the ground.

synopsis: Two homebuilts in loose formation inadvertently entered a TFR when they were distracted by abnormal vibrations in the engine of one of the aircraft. They declared an emergency and the ailing aircraft landed at the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The pilot of an RV-8 experienced intermittent engine vibration at 2,500 feet MSL while flying in trail of a CJ-6. After reducing throttle to stabilize the aircraft, the pilot declared an emergency, coordinated with Approach and Tower, and landed safely at the nearest airport.

synopsis: An Enroute Controller described a conflict that occurred when he tried to climb an aircraft between two minimally spaced aircraft. One of the involved aircraft experienced an engine problem requiring an immediate turn leading to the event.
summary: An air traffic controller attempted to climb an E145 between a C414 and an SF340A but lacked separation when the SF340A reported an oil leak from Engine 2. The controller delayed corrective action due to frequency congestion, eventually declaring an emergency to separate the aircraft after the SF340A diverted.

synopsis: A ZAB Controller described a possible 'Opposite Direction' rule infraction during operations at SAF. The reporter indicated the briefings regarding Opposite Direction operations were less than desired.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller and a Radar Developmental at Santa Fe encountered conflicting instructions regarding opposite direction approaches and runway clearances. Confusion arose when Tower requested clearances for runways differing from the ATIS broadcast, leading to unsafe situations caused by inconsistent briefings on new procedures.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a conflict where a VFR traffic failed to adhere to assigned VFR altitude/s.
summary: An air traffic controller observed a Piper climbing from 4,400 to 5,900 feet while a helicopter was at 6,000 feet on an IFR flight plan. The controller turned the helicopter south to avoid a merge, attributing the conflict to the Piper pilot's failure to report an inability to maintain the assigned 3,500-foot altitude.

synopsis: While descending via the KRANN RNAV STAR to BOS the flight crew of an air carrier aircraft suffered serious confusion and distraction when Approach Control changed their Runway from 22L to 27.
summary: The pilot reported an altitude deviation during the KRANN RNAV STAR arrival at Boston while transitioning to Runway 27. The error occurred because the pilot failed to program the 5,000-foot MCP altitude and was confused by the STAR chart, resulting in a 1,500-foot overshoot of the 11,000-foot crossing restriction at KRANN.

synopsis: A319 Captain reports an ECAM: F/CTL FLAPS FAULT/LOCKED, when flaps are selected to 2 during approach which results in landing with flaps up and slats 3. Difficulties are reported locating information in a redesigned flight manual and using an iPad EFB.
summary: The flight crew declared an emergency during a night visual approach after a flap fault locked the right flaps due to sheared torque tube bolts. They executed a high-speed landing with hot brakes after consulting paper manuals, as the iPad application proved unreliable for managing multiple non-normal charts.

synopsis: A B757-200 Captain addressed multiple issues affecting the operation of his flights including improperly cleared maintenance issues, refusal to complete maintenance actions, confrontation with passenger service personnel over delays for maintenance, and a general breakdown in teamwork between different agencies within the airline.
summary: The Captain and maintenance crew encountered a faulty temperature sensor and a misaligned door 4L on an aircraft prior to departure. The sensor was improperly installed, and the door required realignment after initial repairs failed, causing a flight cancellation before the aircraft departed safely the next day.

synopsis: The flight crew of an air carrier aircraft returned to their departure airport after receipt of an engine #2 overheat warning light. The event duplicted a return to the airport for the same reason by the previous flight crew the night before.
summary: The flight crew experienced a recurring false right engine overheat light on an aircraft previously returned for the same issue. After declaring an emergency and following the QRH procedure at 10,000 feet, the light extinguished, and the crew completed a normal landing with no further faults.

synopsis: A CRJ flight crew declared an emergency and returned to their departure airport when they were unable to pressurize the cabin. Maintenance discovered a cargo door was not sealing properly when closed.
summary: The flight crew experienced a pressurization failure during climb caused by an improperly sealed cargo door, triggering cabin altitude warnings and requiring oxygen mask use. After descending to 8,000 feet and receiving maintenance advice to climb, the crew returned to the airport for a safe landing at maximum weight.

synopsis: Forewarned by another flight crew, the pilots of an MD-82 found themselves barely able to comply with the altitude restrictions on the GIBBZ RNAV STAR to IAD by employing full speed brake extension and idle thrust. When queried by the flight crew ATC advised they had received previous similar complaints.
summary: The pilot reported that the GIBBZ ONE arrival at IAD requires aggressive descent with idle power and full speed brakes to meet eight altitude and two airspeed restrictions. The crew believes the procedure is unsafe for future winter conditions and diverts attention from essential duties, setting crews up for violations.

synopsis: Two pilots report about a recurring 'WARN ELEX' EICAS Status message on a B767-300 aircraft that had been written-up and signed-off multiple times without correcting the problem. Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) isolated the fault to a diode with high resistance, but also noted that one of the stick-shakers was probably inoperative the entire time.
summary: The Captain of a B767-300 halted operations after a mechanic's test revealed an inoperative stick-shaker caused by high resistance in Diode R843. The pilot reported that the aircraft had been repeatedly flown with passengers while maintenance attempted ineffective fixes without verifying related safety systems.

synopsis: An air carrier on the MTPP Runway 10 ILS encountered a brief windshear which caused a speed increase and a flap overspeed while the autopilot and autothrottles to disengaged to stabilize the aircraft.
summary: During an ILS 10 approach at MTPP at 4,000 feet with flaps 15, a gust caused airspeed to exceed 213 knots, triggering a red speed warning. The pilot disconnected the autopilot and increased pitch to reduce speed below 200 knots within 3-5 seconds.

synopsis: A B757-200 flight crew rejected their takeoff at about 60 KIAS when the Captain's airspeed indicator failed.
summary: During takeoff acceleration, the First Officer detected the Captain's airspeed indicator failure at 60 KTS, prompting a rejected takeoff. The crew exited the runway, completed checklists, and taxied back to the gate.

synopsis: B737 Flight Attendant describes preparations for an emergency return to the departure airport.
summary: During the climb phase of a Boeing 737 flight, the Captain declared an emergency due to a binding leading edge flap/trim and returned to ZZZ to burn fuel. The crew coordinated for a normal landing without executing the emergency checklist, resulting in an uneventful arrival and subsequent removal of the aircraft from service.

synopsis: A flight instructor training a student on touch and go landings on Runway 13 at F45 was alarmed when a C-172 crossed their runway westbound on Taxiway K as the student was applying takeoff power. The reporter cited this event as common at the non-towered airport and a demonstration of the need for an Air Traffic Control Tower to be opened.
summary: A Cessna 172 training a student on a touch-and-go at uncontrolled F45 encountered another Cessna 172 taxiing across Runway 13 without radio contact. The crossing aircraft was 1,500 feet down the runway at 10–15 knots, posing no collision risk, though the reporter cited high traffic volume and intersecting runways as safety concerns.

synopsis: RV4 pilot experiences engine failure during an attempted go around from a grass strip. A long landing results in a runway over run and minor damage.
summary: The pilot reported an engine quit during a go-around at a private grass airfield, causing the aircraft to roll off the runway end and strike a small berm. The pilot determined the damage did not constitute a reportable accident or incident under 49 CFR Part 830.

synopsis: A CE560XL departed on the TEB RUUDY 4. At the dogleg turn before WENTZ, the crew mentally connected the turn and climb so continued toward 2,000 FT early. ATC then cleared the flight to 6,000 FT.
summary: Pilots departing Runway 24 at TEB on the RUUDY 4 Departure mistakenly climbed to 2,000 FT MSL at an unnamed dogleg intersection instead of waiting for WENTZ. ATC noticed the early climb and issued a clearance to 6,000 FT, while the crew attributed the error to confusing the intersection and poor FMS monitoring.

synopsis: TRACON Controller handled an aircraft with gear problems. A go around was initiated. A flight crew reporter also provided additional perspectives regarding this incident.
summary: A Dash 8 crew encountered a faulty nose gear indication during a visual approach to Runway 28, prompting a go-around and emergency declaration. After manually extending the gear using the Alternate Landing Gear Extension checklist, the aircraft landed safely, though the pilot criticized the company for discussing the missed checklist while emergency crews were present.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported an overspeed at FL380 following a wake vortex encounter that could have disconnected the autothrottles.
summary: The Pilot Not Flying reported that autothrottles disengaged during level-off at 38,000 feet while encountering light wake turbulence. The crew attributed the disconnect to the turbulence, logged the event, and continued to the destination where maintenance inspected the aircraft.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier on an EWR ILS 22R Circle to Land 29, lost the Runway 29 runway lights in the city background lights, descended too early and executed a go around after an EGPWS TOO LOW OBSTACLE warning.
summary: During a circle-to-land approach at EWR, the crew lost visual contact with Runway 29 and descended below circling altitude while turning base. This triggered a GPWS "Too Low Obstacle" warning at 500 feet, forcing a go-around and climb to 5,000 feet before a successful subsequent approach to Runway 22R.

synopsis: A B757-200 received a GPWS terrain warning on a circling approach when it descended below procedure altitude. A climb to a safer altitude and a normal landing was made.
summary: The Captain of a Boeing 757 descended below intended altitude while circling to Runway 29 due to distraction from locating the runway. This triggered a GPWS obstacle warning, forcing a go-around and a subsequent landing on Runway 22R.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 left engine would not reduce thrust in response to throttle movement. Engine was shut down in accordance with procedure, an emergency declared, and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced uncommanded acceleration of the left engine at 7,000 feet, causing the aircraft to mistakenly detect a right engine failure. They declared an emergency, shut down the left engine per the QRH, and returned safely to the departure airport.

synopsis: Passengers and ground personnel noticed smoke coming from the left main gear of an EMB-145 while parking at the gate. Passengers were quickly deplaned and CFR crews responded promptly to the affected area, where a hydraulic leak was found.
summary: After landing and taxiing to the ramp, passengers and crew observed smoke from the left main landing gear. The aircraft was evacuated after the Captain identified leaking hydraulic fluid and visible fire, prompting an emergency response.

synopsis: When the right main landing gear safe light failed to illuminate the pilot of a C-402 executed a missed approach, accomplished the associated QRH checklists, did a fly-by with the Tower for a visual inspection and ultimately landed safely despite the light remaining extinguished.
summary: The pilot experienced a non-illuminated right main landing gear down light during visual approach for Runway 33R. After executing a missed approach and using the QRH to blow down the gear with nitrogen, Tower visually confirmed the gear was down, allowing for a normal landing.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An MD-80 Captain expressed his concerns regarding the complex descent profile on the FRDMM RNAV STAR into DCA, expressly addressing the difficulties of complying with the multiple and complex altitude and speed restrictions in an RNAV eligible aircraft which is not equipped with VNAV guidance.
summary: Pilots flying an MD80 without VNAV reported struggling to comply with the complex FRDMM ONE RNAV arrival into DCA due to numerous speed and altitude restrictions. The reporter attributed the high workload and reduced situational awareness to the procedure's excessive complexity, which forced both pilots to focus internally rather than scanning for traffic.

synopsis: Two mechanics report that after high powered engine runs, debris from the poorly maintained ramp surface damaged another aircraft.
summary: Two mechanics performed a high-power engine run on a designated pad, but debris from a deteriorating ramp behind the aircraft struck another parked aircraft. The reporter attributes the incident to the failing ramp surface and notes the extent of damage to the other carrier's aircraft is unknown.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A corporate pilot reported that after departing a Chicago area airport, an airborne weather reroute included PADDE intersection, but PADDY was inserted in the FMC. The track deviation was detected by ATC who then clarified the fix's spelling.
summary: The crew misinterpreted a rapid ATC reroute clearance, selecting fix PADDY instead of PADDE due to the controller's rushed delivery. This caused a 30-degree heading error, which was corrected after the controller clarified the phonetic spelling.

synopsis: General Aviation pilot on an RNAV Approach Runway 31 to SUN described some apparent confusion on the part of ATC regarding the minimums required for the procedure, adding the Controllers questions were very untimely.
summary: A pilot conducting an RNAV Runway 31 approach to SUN disputed the controller's refusal to land due to reported visibility below minimums, despite having the airport in sight. The controller issued an unsolicited Special VFR clearance, which the pilot found distracting during a critical flight phase, though the landing was completed uneventfully.

synopsis: TRACON Controller providing OJT described a reported NMAC when two military aircraft were directed to proceed to the 'initial point' for an 'overhead' arrival simultaneously, the reporter acknowledging a failure to intercede.
summary: A trainee controller sequenced two T-45s returning to Runway 19L incorrectly, ignoring the second aircraft's higher speed and straight-in position. This resulted in both aircraft arriving at the initial point simultaneously at 3,000 feet, forcing the second pilot to climb to 3,500 feet to avoid a reported near mid-air collision.

synopsis: C90 Controller experienced a loss of separation event claiming the new 'fusion' RADAR.
summary: An air traffic controller at C90 vectored an Airbus A320 off final approach to avoid loss of separation behind a heavy Airbus due to high winds and a scud layer. The controller attributed the maneuver to timing differences with the new fusion radar and wind conditions affecting the aircraft's position.

synopsis: N90 Controller described a probable loss of separation event when traffic on the ILS for LGA was changed to a Visual Approach because of altitude concerns. The aircraft then executed an uncoordinated 360 toward following traffic.
summary: An air traffic controller in the New York TRACON lost separation between an E190 and a B737 while managing arrivals at LGA after a weather closure. The E190 executed a 360-degree turn on the Runway 4 approach, colliding with the B737's path despite the controller's immediate corrective actions.

synopsis: BHM Controller described an event when an Air Carrier requested an opposite direction takeoff because of weather near the airport. The request was denied because of new 'opposite direction' procedures.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller denied Air Carrier X's request to depart Runway 6 to avoid precipitation, citing policy changes, and instead cleared the aircraft for Runway 24 with a north heading. The pilot filed a complaint regarding safety concerns but departed safely in visual meteorological conditions.

synopsis: ASE Controller described a TCAS RA event between a departure and arrival aircraft caused by a misunderstanding between the Approach and Local Controllers reference the term 'practice approach' and IFR vs VFR status.
summary: A Falcon pilot reported a TCAS RA during departure from Aspen while a Hawker arrived, caused by the controller misidentifying an IFR Cirrus as VFR. The Falcon descended to 9,200 feet to resolve the conflict, but the pilot criticized the controller's calm response and a voice on the frequency telling them to "grow up."

synopsis: During descent a B777 First Officer's PFD, ND, and CDU momentarily blanked twice then returned to normal. After landing, the autothrottles did an uncommanded disconnect.
summary: The First Officer reported that all PFDs and CDUs blanked momentarily twice during approach, followed by an unexplained autothrottle disengagement at touchdown. No EICAS messages appeared, and the crew briefed Maintenance upon landing.

synopsis: When they lost control of their pressurization at FL330, an EMB-145 flight crew declared an emergency, began an emergency descent and performed appropriate procedures and checklists as they descended to a safe altitude and then continued to their destination.
summary: During descent, the Captain observed cabin altitude in the amber range, which climbed to approximately 9,500 feet despite initial procedures. The crew donned masks, executed rapid depressurization and emergency descent checklists, declared an emergency, and continued to the destination without further incident.

synopsis: A Citation flight crew experienced an NMAC when ATC failed to note their conflicting flight paths with a CRJ that was also descending.
summary: Oakland Center cleared the crew to descend from FL340, then instructed a climb to FL330 while a CRJ was cleared to FL320, causing a near collision. The pilot executed an evasive left turn after visual identification, attributing the incident to the controller's altitude error and the aircraft's lack of TCAS II.

synopsis: An A319 had an AIR ENG 1 BLEED FAULT ECAM during climb after takeoff and then at FL390 an AIR ENG 2 BLEED FAULT ECAM so as the cabin depressurized an emergency was declared while descending and returning to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew and cabin crew experienced a rapid decompression at FL390 following dual engine bleed faults, causing an emergency descent to FL100. The reporter attributes the incident to a previously reported broken air pack and excessive heat, resulting in one passenger requiring medical oxygen and a return to the departure airport.

synopsis: CL300 pilot reports crossing the hold line for Runway 28L on Taxiway A while distracted by attention to a noise abatement sign in the same area.
