synopsis: Several maintenance discrepancies including an unsecured bolt on the top deck of a Bell 206 were missed during a final inspection. A Mechanic noticed the unsecured bolt after a check flight.
summary: During a main rotor mast change and AAIP inspection, mechanics missed a missing nut on the collective bolt, a missing chin bubble seal, and an incorrectly installed oxygen line due to poor tagging and shift handover failures. The aircraft was released for service and flown before the missing hardware was discovered, resulting in a near miss attributed to new team dynamics and communication gaps.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic found a Magnetic Chip Detector plug housing sheared-off flush with the Main Gearbox (MGB) transmission housing on a Bell 206L-1 helicopter. He had previously found two other Bell 206L-1 MGBs with the same condition.
summary: A pilot reported transmission oil seepage on a Bell aircraft during a demonstration assignment. A mechanic found the magnetic chip plug sheared at its base, likely due to improper installation torque, though the internal check valve prevented further leakage.

synopsis: A PA32-300 pilot rejected takeoff due to a loss of power. A Maintenance Technician later identified that the induction air flexible duct had collapsed at a bend in the duct.
summary: A Piper Cherokee 6 PA-32-300 aborted takeoff due to sudden power loss caused by a collapsed induction air duct. The failure resulted from a missing elbow assembly creating a sharp bend, likely due to a prior improper repair with non-certified parts.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A flight crew heard an ATC clearance to Beckley (BKW) but BUGME, 130 NM away on J91, was intended.
summary: The flight crew misheard an ATC clearance for direct to BUGME as Beckley (BKW) south of VXV, resulting in a deviation from the assigned route. Center corrected the error by instructing a turn to heading 360 and re-clearing the aircraft direct to BUGME.

synopsis: At FL270 a B737 Cabin Altitude Warning horn sounded so an emergency was declared and the flight descended to 8,000 FT. On this flight and the previous flight the Equip Cooling OFF light illuminated indicating a lack of air flow.
summary: The flight crew experienced a loss of pressurization above FL270 due to inoperative cooling fans, prompting an emergency descent to 8,000 FT and a safe landing. Post-landing, the crew discovered the outflow valve remained closed because the pilot not flying failed to open it below 1,000 FT, leaving the cabin pressurized at the gate.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An Airbus Captain described multiple anomalies apparently related to the failure of either one or both FMGCs per Maintenance. The flight crew ad libbed the use of the remaining navigation devices until in VMC on approach to their destination where they made a safe landing and turned the jet over to Maintenance.
summary: The flight crew experienced multiple FMGC failures during approach to IAD, causing erroneous flight director commands and loss of speed bugs. They completed the landing using raw data and manual procedures, attributing the issues to a likely software bug following a recent update.

synopsis: Previously cleared and programmed to descend via the CLIPR RNAV STAR to DCA the flight crew of an ERJ-190 was re-cleared direct to and to cross CLIPR at 12,000 FT vice TRISH at 12,000 FT as charted. They failed to reprogram the crossing restriction and a deviation ensued.
summary: The flight crew missed a CLIPR crossing restriction at 12,000 feet during the CLIPR 3 arrival to DCA after an ATC direct clearance deleted the TRISH restriction in the FMS. The crew attributed the error to monitoring the wrong VNAV path, high workload, fatigue, and a corporate culture prioritizing fuel savings.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: After being cleared to cross Runway 1 on Taxiway F hold short of Runway 33, Air Carrier Captain realizes that he has also crossed Runway 4 without a clearance.
summary: The pilot crossed Runway 4/22 without explicit clearance while taxiing at DCA after being cleared across Runway 1/19. The reporter attributes this error to the close runway proximity, lack of hold short lines, and the intersection not being designated as a hot spot.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer as Pilot Not Flying (NFP) reports a descent below the MEA after being cleared for the LDA DME Runway 25 approach to EGE in VMC. ATC issued a low altitude alert and the crew corrected.
summary: The pilot monitoring descended below the published route between Kremmling and VOAXA while flying an LDA DME approach into EGE. ATC issued a low altitude alert, prompting an immediate climb to 13,800 feet, which the crew attributed to failing to verify VNAV crossing restrictions.

synopsis: While descending in VNAV to cross ZIZZI at 16,000 FT, the flight crew of an E-145 had to manually return the aircraft to its programmed crossing restriction when the autopilot failed to capture the altitude. A known FMS software flaw, currently under review, may have been a contributing factor.
summary: The flight crew descended through an ATC-cleared 16,000 FT restriction while in VNAV with autopilot engaged due to an autopilot malfunction preventing level-off. The flying pilot immediately disengaged the autopilot to correct the altitude and notified ATC of the equipment failure.

synopsis: An EMB145 EICAS alerted PTRIM MAIN INOP after takeoff but the autopilot trim remained functional so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a PTRIM MAIN INOP warning during the turn to heading 360 after takeoff. After confirming backup trim and autopilot functionality, they declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport, and landed safely with no further incident.

synopsis: A strong odor was detected by a MD-80's pilots, flight attendants, and passengers after takeoff so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: During initial climb, flight and cabin crews detected a strong odor with no smoke, prompting the Captain to declare an emergency and return to the departure airport. The aircraft landed uneventfully, and post-flight inspections by rescue crews found no external cause for the odor.

synopsis: PA23 pilot experienced a loss of power just after takeoff and declared an emergency with the Tower. After securing the left engine the pilot is able to return and land opposite direction on the departure runway. 250 FT AGL is the maximum altitude attained during the flight.
summary: A pilot experienced a left engine power loss below 200 feet during initial climb on a VFR departure, declared an emergency, and landed safely on Runway 27R. After landing, the pilot requested a revised taxi clearance due to single-engine limitations, which Ground Control provided to reach the ramp where the aircraft was grounded.

synopsis: C172 Instructor pilot reports simulating an engine failure by placing the fuel selector to off. When the fuel selector is placed to both the engine does not restart and an off airport landing ensues.
summary: During an engine-out exercise in a student-provided C172 at 3,000 feet, restart attempts failed after the fuel selector was placed in the 'off' position. The pilot executed an off-field landing, resulting in nose wheel damage but no injuries to the occupants.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: An pilot approaching SGU IFR was told to expect a visual approach then deviated from the ATC assigned track because of weather and after approaching high terrain was given a climb clearance.
summary: The pilot en route to SGU deviated 20 degrees right to avoid thunderstorms while expecting a visual approach, inadvertently entering higher terrain. LA Center instructed a climb to 10,000 feet for clearance after the pilot realized they should have requested a new clearance before deviating.

synopsis: A G-IV flight crew--cleared to depart HPN via the WESTCHESTER SID, vector BAYYS on course--mistook 'BAYSE' for 'BAYYS' when cleared direct. ATC noted their error and provided corrective clearances.
summary: The First Officer and pilot misinterpreted a clearance for waypoint BAYYS as BASYE during departure from HPN. The confusion arose from similar waypoint names, causing the crew to fly toward the wrong location before Air Traffic Control corrected the route and issued a direct clearance to SEALL.

synopsis: APA Controller voiced concern regarding run up procedures and the inadequate signage for pilots regarding same.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X taxied to the A1 ramp instead of the designated north run-up area at APA due to incorrect charting. The controller instructed the pilot to move south to the correct location, noting that signage is needed to prevent future confusion when snow covers markings.

synopsis: B777 flight attendants and pilots detected an electrical odor in First and Business Classes so an emergency was declared and the flight diverted to an enroute airport for maintenance. The flight later continued on the same aircraft.
summary: Flight attendants and the pilot crew reported an electrical odor in the First Class galley and cockpit at FL380. The crew declared an emergency, diverted, and landed normally after fire rescue found no external fire indications.

synopsis: An A320 crew was notified after flight that the FMGC failure they had experienced in flight is believed caused by a 'bug' in a recent software update.
summary: The crew experienced multiple FMGC failures, likely due to a software bug, during the approach and landing phases. These failures caused navigation discrepancies, a missing speed bug, and a cabin pressure fault, forcing the pilots to rely on raw data and manual procedures to complete the flight safely.

synopsis: After previously diverting en route for an odor and with the Cargo Fan MELed, the flight continued to the filed destination where on approach the odor returned. So an emergency was declared and the crew donned oxygen masks for a short approach. Several flight attendants reported being ill.
summary: The crew diverted due to an electrical odor caused by an overheated cargo fan, which was deferred. On approach, the odor recurred in first class, prompting an emergency declaration, a normal landing, and medical treatment for three flight attendants suffering from headaches and nausea.

synopsis: An A321 diverted because the flight attendants reported physical symptoms including eye, sinus and throat irritation, foggy headedness, and headaches after detecting a dirty socks odor.
summary: Flight attendants reported a foul odor and physical symptoms like sinus burning and tremors during cruise, prompting the crew to follow the QRH Smoke and Fumes procedure. The pilots declared an emergency and made a precautionary landing where paramedics checked the affected crew members.

synopsis: A B737-700 returned to the gate during taxi after flight attendants reported a repeat detection of a strong electrical smell near the L1/R1 doors.
summary: The flight crew and cabin crew reported an acrid electrical smell near the L1/R1 doors after the aircraft arrived from the hangar. The aircraft returned to the gate under its own power during pushback after the smell intensified and cabin crew felt ill, though maintenance initially found no cause.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 Flight Crew addressed their concerns about ATC phraseology and their aircraft's autoflight system's capability to cope with the more complex aspects of the TAMMY RNAV STAR to MEM.
summary: The flight crew missed a "descend via" clearance while en route to MEM due to confusion over the "North Transition" and cramped approach plates. This resulted in an altitude deviation at ROCAB, requiring ATC to issue a heading and descent to 6,000 feet.

synopsis: While the First Officer was occupied by checklists during a very short taxi to Runway 8R at ELP the Captain taxied across the runway hold short line without a clearance. No conflicts resulted and the Tower cleared them for takeoff. The First Officer reported fatigue as a contributing factor.
summary: The crew taxied a short distance from the gate to Runway 8R without assigned taxiways, crossing the extended threshold due to confusing markings and fatigue. The Tower cleared them for takeoff despite the incursion, and the flight continued without further issues.

synopsis: A B737-800 Aileron Autopilot Actuator failed on final approach at flaps 1 causing the loss of System B Hydraulic Fluid so an emergency was declared, the airspeed adjusted and the flight continued to a normal no flap landing.
summary: The flight crew experienced a total loss of System B hydraulics during a visual approach, causing flap extension failure and loss of normal brakes. They declared an emergency, landed safely with flaps up using alternate brakes and one thrust reverser, and were towed to the gate after maintenance identified a failed autopilot aileron actuator.

synopsis: A MD-83 landing gear indicating system malfunctioned after takeoff so an emergency was declared, the QRH completed and, after an uneventful landing, a nose landing gear position fault was discovered.
summary: The crew experienced a malfunctioning nose gear light after takeoff, prompting a return to the departure airport. They declared an emergency after the light flickered during approach, completed QRH procedures, and landed safely with all gear indicators green.

synopsis: An MD-82 Oil Strainer Clog light illuminated then would not extinguish as oil pressure and quantity decreased so following the QRH the engine was shutdown and the flight diverted to an enroute.
summary: The flight crew at FL320 secured the right engine after the Oil Strainer Clog light illuminated and oil pressure and quantity dropped. The aircraft landed overweight at 134,000 LBS without incident.

synopsis: An MD-82 Captain believed a LAS TRACON clearance to intercept the GRANPA RNAV STAR at TRROP, cleared for the RNAV 19R approach was illegal.
summary: Pilots flying a TYSSN3 arrival into LAS received a clearance to intercept the 19R RNAV approach from the GRNPA1 arrival, which the crew deemed illegal due to missing transition points. After contacting the tower and supervisor, the crew was recleared for a visual approach to 19L and landed uneventfully, though they noted potential GPS loading risks.

synopsis: S-76B helicopter Second in Command (SIC) reported that the PIC, pilot flying, continued flight after experiencing brief engine power rollback in an aircraft that had a previous history of this problem. SIC advised against continuing the flight and later resigned rather than continue to fly with this PIC.
summary: The SIC reported that the PIC, a Part 135 Chief of Operations, ignored the SIC's recommendation to abort a flight after an S-76B experienced an Engine 1 power rollback and engine-out indications during hover-taxi. The PIC ordered takeoff clearance despite the SIC's safety concerns, leading the SIC to resign and report the incident to the company CEO and FAA.

synopsis: P180 flight crew experiences a hydraulic system failure as the landing gear is retracted after takeoff. The gear is extended using the Emergency Gear Extension Checklist and the flight returns to the departure airport. During the roll out without nose wheel steering or normal brakes, directional control is lost as the rudder becomes ineffective and the aircraft departs the runway at low speed.
summary: The Captain of a Piaggio experienced a hydraulic pump failure during gear retraction, requiring emergency gear extension and a return to the departure airport. Upon landing, the loss of nose wheel steering and brakes caused the aircraft to yaw and exit the right side of the runway into mud.

synopsis: A T310Q right engine lost power during climb after takeoff so the IFR pilot started a turn toward the departure airport. While enroute the engine quit, so without declaring an emergency he landed safely in an emergency condition.
summary: The pilot experienced a right engine failure and fuel pump malfunction while climbing through 8,000 feet, prompting a rapid descent to 6,000 feet. After realizing they remained on an IFR flight plan below clearance, the pilot cancelled IFR, feathered the engine on final, and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: Several Maintenance Technicians performed a gas path cleaning procedure on all four engines of a B747 under less than ideal conditions. Weather, equipment, pressure, changing plans and distractions plagued the process. The aircraft was released for service with the protective covers still installed over all of the generator cooling ducts. This caused all of the generators to fail in flight due to lack of cooling air. The flight crew safely landed the aircraft, but without the use of thrust reversers or anti-skid system. Several tires were blown.
summary: Maintenance crew performed gas path cleaning on all four engines at the blast fence but forgot to remove generator cooling duct covers before dispatch. The aircraft subsequently landed with all four generators failed and 13 deflated tires due to the blocked cooling ducts, though the crew remained unharmed.

synopsis: ZHU Controller described a restricted area incursion when intra and inter facility coordination was incomplete.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller relieving the Ocean East D-Side sector encountered an Airbus A319 deviating south due to weather while W174 military airspace was active but uncoordinated between Miami and Houston Centers. The pilot refused a turn into the active airspace, highlighting dangerous communication gaps and a need for procedural updates regarding military airspace status.

synopsis: LAS Controller experienced an ASDE-X event when Runway 25R landing traffic and rolling across Runway 19R activated the alarm due to departure traffic from Runway 19R, the less than clear ADW procedures were listed as contributory.
summary: An air traffic controller at LAS experienced a loss of separation while applying the new ADW procedure, resulting in an arrival and departure on the same runway. The controller attributed the incident to ASDE-X warnings and prior supervisor concerns, which caused them to fail to reiterate visual separation instructions to the departing B737.

synopsis: A B737-700 engine failed during climb so the QRH was complied with, an emergency declared and the flight diverted to an enroute airport.
summary: The crew experienced a Number Two engine failure during climb out at 12,000 feet. They declared an emergency and diverted to an en route airport to execute an ILS 24L approach.

synopsis: An A320 First Officer called in fatigued for airport standby on his third duty day because on the previous two nights he was not able to get fitful rest.
summary: A pilot called in fatigued for a field standby after completing a two-day trip with limited sleep due to noisy neighbors and malfunctioning hotel air conditioning. The pilot reported that coffee consumed to compensate for fatigue prevented rest during a layover and caused further sleep issues the following night.

synopsis: An A320 Dispatcher reported that the human generated noise in the dispatch office was so high that he had difficulty on a phone patch with a flight discussing an FMGC issue and so he demanded people sitting close by be quiet.
summary: Approximately 30 minutes after departure, the crew experienced FMGC 1 failures and struggled to communicate with Maintenance via phone patch due to loud background noise in the Dispatch office. Although the noise was reduced, constant communication could not be maintained throughout the call.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Captain reported MCP, FMC programming, and briefing complete for a descent into the DFW area, but after receiving clearance to 13,000 FT he became distracted with other tasks and failed to engage NAV, thus missing the altitude constraint.
summary: The pilot flying failed to initiate a descent to cross CQY VOR at 13,000 feet after entering the restriction into the FMS, mistakenly assuming VNAV was active while the aircraft remained level at FL240. ATC queried the non-compliance and issued a subsequent clearance to cross ORVLL at 9,000 feet, which the crew executed without further issue.

synopsis: A PA-31 turbo failed which caused an oil leak. The pilot shut the engine down and diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: The pilot experienced a right engine turbo failure en route, indicated by low manifold pressure and backfiring, which led to oil leakage and reduced fuel flow. The pilot followed the engine shutdown checklist, contacted ATC, and safely landed single-engine at a nearby airport.

synopsis: An air carrier flight crew erred in their descent calculations and were unable to comply with the crossing speed restrictions on the MONAA RNAV STAR to MEM.
summary: The pilot flying a descent from FL240 on the MONAA RNAV STAR to MEM failed to plan for speed restrictions, missing 250 KTS at MONAA and 210 KTS at ZAMET. ATC subsequently cleared the crew to pilot's discretion to 4,000 FT, removing them from the STAR to allow recovery.

synopsis: When cleared for the FNCHR RNAV STAR to MEM and directed to maintain 270 KTS by ATC the FMS failed to comply with the 250 KTS restriction at JESTI despite ATC's subsequent clearance removing the assigned speed.
summary: The flight crew encountered a speed restriction issue while executing the FNCHR 1 RNAV STAR. A distraction caused a delay in monitoring the FMS, resulting in the aircraft crossing the JESTI waypoint more than 10 knots fast despite manual intervention.

synopsis: A B757 EICAS alerted L HYD QTY then, L HYD SYS PRESS. The QRH was completed and an emergency was declared at the destination airport where alternate flap and gear extension checklists were completed prior to landing with no nose wheel steering.
summary: The crew experienced a left hydraulic quantity and pressure warning during climb, causing loss of nosewheel steering and alternate flap/gear extension delays. They declared an emergency, landed safely, and were towed after maintenance identified a component material failure in the left wheel well.

synopsis: After the flight crew was cleared for the MONAA RNAV STAR to MEM, they reprogrammed the 'at or below FL230' at JYSON to 'at FL230/' As they approached JYSON they realized they would be unable to comply with the 'between 6,000 and 10,000 FT at 250 KTS' restriction at MONAA only 16 NM beyond JYSON.
summary: The pilot not flying changed an FMS "at or below" restriction to a hard altitude at JYSON while descending on the MONAA RNAV STAR to Memphis. This error caused the aircraft to cross MONAA at 290 knots instead of the required 250 knots, requiring ATC to issue a pilot discretion descent.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 350 suffered a track deviation departing TEB when she either failed to load the departure procedure in the GPS/MFD or had inadvertently deleted it. ATC provided vectors to resolve the error.
summary: The pilot departed Teterboro with the Departure Procedure accidentally deleted from the GPS, causing a deviation until ATC issued immediate vectors. The pilot attributed the error to not loading the chart and implemented procedural changes to prevent recurrence, noting no safety risk occurred.

synopsis: A B767-300 departing TTPP misunderstood the meaning of their ATC clearance to proceed direct to LOGAN after takeoff and turned toward it fix prior to completing the Obstacle Clearance procedure which requires runway heading to 4,100 FT before proceeding on course. Difficulty understanding the Controller was cited as a contributing factor.
summary: The flight crew at TTPP received a difficult-to-understand clearance to proceed direct to LOGAN immediately after takeoff, causing an unsafe initial turn. The crew corrected the course to runway heading until 4,100 feet after realizing the clearance conflicted with terrain avoidance procedures.

synopsis: When the left engine failed to restart after a training engine failure exercise the instructor pilot declared an emergency and the pilot in training performed a successful landing at their airport of departure.
summary: During a single-engine checkout in a Beech Duchess at 3,000 feet, the left engine failed to restart after a planned exercise. The instructor declared an emergency, and the pilot executed a single-engine landing at the base airport with no perceived damage.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: CL65 First Officer describes a generator failure in cruise and the use of the APU generator to take its' place. During descent an APU oil temperature EICAS message is received and the QRH states 'land at nearest suitable airport.' The Captain believes that since the aircraft is already descending the destination airport is the best choice and the First Officer disagrees believing that an airport directly below (aircraft at FL280) is the nearest suitable.
summary: The First Officer and Captain disagreed on the nearest suitable airport after an APU oil temperature warning occurred at FL280. The Captain elected to continue to the destination citing runway length, while the First Officer later concluded an immediate descent to the closer airport was safer due to potential APU fire risk.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot reported that a newly installed white strobe light on a tower near LEW airport is so bright that it has an adverse affect on Night Vision Goggle (NVG) operations in the area.
summary: A single-pilot NVG helicopter operator reported that a new white strobe on a tower one mile east of LEW causes distraction during all flight phases. The reporter stated the bright light adversely affects NVG operations, especially in high moisture weather, and requested a daytime-only sensor.

synopsis: A BE-55 pilot reported dual engine failures because of fuel starvation after a right tank fuel cap was either left unsecured during preflight or a cap seal deterioration leak. A single engine was restarted before landing where a runway excursion and wingtip damage occurred.
summary: The pilot and a passenger flew a Baron B-55 for sightseeing when both engines failed at 2,000 feet due to fuel exhaustion from improper crossfeed usage and a leaking right fuel cap. The pilot landed on one engine but ran off the runway, striking a fencepost with the wingtip.

synopsis: PA28 pilot on IFR flight plan at 10,000 FT reports encountering thunderstorms and turbulence. A course reversal is initiated prior to advising Center and several altitude deviations occur.
summary: The pilot filed IFR to 10,000 feet MSL but encountered severe turbulence and thunderstorms, leading to a deviation from course without timely notification to Cleveland Center. The incident involved altitude excursions of 500 feet and precession errors, attributed to inadequate onboard weather support, prompting a return to base.

synopsis: Pilot of an Experimental-Homebuilt aircraft took off, refueled at an intermediate stop and continued to a short layover at his destination before departing with the intention of returning to the airport where he had refueled. After passing an airport enroute, the pilot became concerned about his fuel state since air show practice was taking place at the destination airport. ATC interrupted the practice activity and the Pilot landed without incident.
summary: A pilot flying a Kitfox encountered a closed runway due to aerobatic practice and was instructed to circle while low on fuel. The pilot landed safely but faced FAA inspection for lacking a medical certificate and operating limitations, attributing the incident to poor flight planning and NOTAM awareness.

synopsis: A landing helicopter passed within 50 FT above a taxiing PA-32 causing the pilot of the aircraft to have trouble maintaining control in the rotor wash.
summary: A pilot taxiing to Runway 28 reported that an inbound helicopter hovered over the taxiway at approximately 50 feet, creating severe rotor wash that nearly lifted the aircraft. The pilot attributed the incident to the helicopter's low altitude over the taxiway and criticized the controller for lack of alertness.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a loss of separation event when an adjacent TRACON lost RADAR, declared ATC ZERO, and resulted in an IFR arrival and IFR departure not being separated. The reporter suggested additional training on unusual events.
summary: During an ATC zero event, a TRACON controller assumed ZZZ1 airspace and inadvertently failed to separate a helicopter on ILS approach from a departing Challenger. The controller attributed the loss of separation to confusion over tower status, unclear departure clearances, and insufficient training for non-radar airspace transfers.

synopsis: Air Carrier inbound to the gate area at LGA experienced confusion with regard to communications between Ramp Control, Ground Control and Company.
summary: The First Officer at LGA mistakenly contacted Company Operations instead of Ramp Control while taxiing after landing on Runway 22. Operations inadvertently cleared the aircraft to the gate, causing confusion with Ground Control and Ramp Control regarding the clearance source.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A flight crew on STL Taxiway F reported missing the Runway 12L entry on Taxiway S and so incurred Runway 6/24.
summary: The pilot flying crossed the Runway 6/24 hold short line instead of turning onto Taxiway S for Runway 12L due to unfamiliarity with the layout and a rushed clearance. The Tower Supervisor canceled the takeoff, and the crew returned to the correct runway after the pilot admitted fault for not verifying the route.

synopsis: An A-320 flight crew experienced an NMAC with an MD-80 during initial approach to TNCA. The reporter alleges the MD-80 flight crew purposely mis-stated their position and shut off their transponder to gain an arrival advantage.
summary: The crew of a jet approaching Aruba (BEA) executed a TCAS avoidance maneuver after an MD-80 appeared below them during a non-radar ILS approach. The reporter attributes the near-midair collision to the MD-80 crew allegedly falsifying their position and disabling their transponder to gain priority.

synopsis: Air Carrier with ZAU described a very confused communications event involving four digit call signs and attempts to communicate with ATC.
summary: The flight crew received a clearance intended for a different aircraft with a similar call sign while climbing to FL190. After the controller admitted the error and instructed a return to the previous frequency, the crew contacted Departure Control and received corrected vectors to 090 and 16,000 feet.

synopsis: A B737-800 pilot noticed that on two separate engine runs at two different Maintenance stations, only one of the stations used a protective cage around the inlet of their CFM-56 engine. Mechanics were trouble shooting a recurring oil leak.
summary: Pilots and mechanics at ZZZ, ZZZ1, and ZZZ2 observed oil leaks on a B737 right engine during gate runs. The reporter recommends mandating protective cages to prevent fatalities, citing a 2006 incident where a mechanic was ingested while checking for leaks without a cage.

synopsis: A DC-10's right aft and left forward nose gear doors had brackets and hinges fail in flight which allowed those two doors to open with no indication except for an unusual vibration.
summary: The flight crew experienced loud noise and vibration below FL200, suspecting ADG deployment, but maintenance later found open nose gear doors with broken brackets, links, and hinges. No cockpit alerts were received, and the crew recommended an engineer investigation into the failed parts and inspection procedures.

synopsis: While practicing night landings at a Towered airport the pilot of a C-172 suffered an electrical failure and the associated loss of comm capability. He remained in the pattern and made a pass above the runway alerting the Tower as to his problem and on the subsequent pass was given light signal clearances to land and to taxi in.
summary: The pilot experienced a total electrical failure during the night approach to Runway 17R, losing all radios, cockpit lighting, and landing lights. After squawking 7600 and landing without flaps based on ATC light signals, the pilot taxied slowly using a flashlight and towed the aircraft to the hangar for maintenance.

synopsis: C172 Student and Instructor experience a NMAC with a Cirrus in Class B airspace while being vectored for an ILS approach for a satellite airport. The Cirrus pilot was not talking to Approach Control.
summary: An instructor and student in a practice ILS approach within Class B airspace experienced a traffic conflict while descending from 2,500 to 2,000 feet. The near-miss with a Cirrus aircraft was attributed to delayed manual descent, distraction from read-backs, and the other pilot's failure to use lights or communicate.

synopsis: Citabria pilot reports running out of fuel in his newly purchased aircraft and landing on a highway just short of his destination. The flight was planned for 3.5 hours and the 36 gallon tank ran dry at 3 hours and 35 minutes.
summary: The pilot of a Citabria 7GCBC experienced an engine failure due to fuel exhaustion during the cruise phase while avoiding thunderstorms. The pilot executed an off-airport landing on a state highway with no damage to the aircraft or property.

synopsis: Tower Controller described confusion regarding the application and clearance for a 'Contact Approach' vs. a 'Special VFR' request.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller issued a Contact Approach to a C310 VFR pilot in low visibility smoke, later realizing the clearance was incorrect as the procedure applies only to IFR aircraft. The pilot should have requested a Special VFR clearance instead, prompting the controller to review rarely used procedures.

synopsis: ZMP Controller describes a conflict between a CRJ200 departing MOT and a UAV operating in an MOA at FL200. MOT Departure had not restricted the CRJ to stay below FL200 until cleared to climb by ZMP but had instead cleared the CRJ to climb in accordance with the LOA without regard for the UAV.
summary: A ZMP controller handed off a climbing commercial airliner to Minot Approach, where it entered unsafe proximity with a stationary unmanned aircraft. The controller attributed the conflict to Minot Approach's lack of training and failure to maintain positive separation between the two aircraft.

synopsis: SAT TRACON Controller experienced an airspace incursion indicating that unfamiliarity with the new 'fused' RADAR system as a contributing factor.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller and trainee vectored a PAY2 aircraft for ILS 30L but issued a breakout climb to 3,000 feet and left turn to 210 degrees when the aircraft was too high and fast. The aircraft entered APK airspace one mile early because the controller failed to assign a higher altitude of 3,500 feet, a situation complicated by recent difficulties adapting to new fused radar mode.

synopsis: PHX Controller described a IFR/VFR conflict between an Air Carrier arrival and a VFR helicopter departure on a prescribed VFR route claiming unfamiliarity with the new 'Electronic Flight Strips' contributed to the event, adding that the subject VFR route should be re-designed to increase procedural separation.
summary: An air traffic controller at PHX Tower forgot a departing helicopter while managing a landing King Air during testing of malfunctioning electronic flight strips. The controller attributed the oversight to inconsistent system training and recommended moving VFR helicopter routes further from arrival paths to prevent conflicts.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller reported a loss of separation between two aircraft. A contributing factor was the erratic display on his newly introduced 'Fusion' radar and his lack of familiarity with its capabilities.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that the new 'Fusion' radar displayed erratic target jumps and tag switching while the main sensor was out of service. This caused a loss of 3 miles lateral separation with a P180 due to unexpected turn rates, leading the controller to conclude the system is unreliable.

synopsis: MKE Controller voiced concern regarding the parachute activity at C89 airport noting a recent conflict between the jump aircraft and an IFR overflight, the reporter describing the parachute activity as dangerous.
summary: An air traffic controller managing high workload reported a skydiving aircraft descending near C89 came within one mile of an E145 at 12,000 feet and a BE36 on approach to ENW. The controller deemed the skydiving activity in this airspace extremely dangerous and unsafe due to conflicts with arrival and departure traffic.

synopsis: ZAU Controller was alerted to a TCAS RA experienced by an Air Carrier arrival when the ceiling altitude for a parachute aircraft was miscommunicated.
summary: An Air Carrier at 14,000 feet and a VFR Beech 65 conducting parachute jumps experienced a potential conflict when the Beech reported 13,300 feet while the Carrier was 100 feet low. The Carrier followed TCAS climb instructions after initially being advised the traffic was below, prompting a recommendation to move jump operations to less congested airspace.

synopsis: ZAU Controller described an unsafe situation due to the functionality of ERAM which is unlike prior equipment, the reporter emphasized that controllers must not 'remove strips' for aircraft under their control.
summary: An air traffic controller managing a VFR Cirrus descent during an ERAM run lost the aircraft's data block after another controller removed the flight strips. The controller recovered the track using ESDT, noting that ERAM allows flight plan data to return to the Center, unlike the old NAS system.

synopsis: SCT Controller described a near loss of MVA required standards, the reporter claiming the 'Fusion' RADAR system provided erroneous information regarding separation, prompting a turn which caused the event.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored a PA28 away from a C182 due to erroneous radar data indicating a loss of separation. The faulty target tracking caused the controller to maneuver the PA28 toward higher terrain, though actual separation was never lost.

synopsis: Two A300 flight deck overhead panels were in locations other than typical as identified during the preflight setup. This condition was addressed verbally to the Local Maintenance technicians, who then proceeded to reposition the panels. It was reported that no logbook entry was made, and it appears that no maintenance manual was referenced.
summary: During cockpit preparation, the pilot and Captain noticed the secondary gear down and cockpit voice recorder panels appeared swapped. Two mechanics arrived, confirmed the swap was usual, physically exchanged the panels, and promised a logbook entry that was never made, leaving the crew uncertain if the configuration was an irregularity.

synopsis: Uncommanded deviations in the yaw axis during late stages of the takeoff roll resulted in a rejected takeoff performed by the flight crew of an unidentified air carrier aircraft.
summary: During takeoff, the aircraft yawed left twice, prompting the Captain to abort. The crew taxied to the gate after confirming no fire, though emergency services reported brake temperatures reached 650 degrees and flight attendants were thrown in their seats, with no injuries.

synopsis: As the reporter's A320 was on short final a B-737 cleared to depart the same runway prior to their landing rejected their takeoff but failed to clear the runway completely. When asked to expedite clearing the resultant jet blast struck the A320 as they flared causing momentary destabilization from which the reporter recovered and landed safely.
summary: The pilot landed behind a B-737 that had aborted takeoff and was clearing Runway 33L. The landing aircraft encountered severe jet wash in the flare, causing a momentary deviation, which the pilot attributed to the B-737 accelerating or operating on a single engine.

synopsis: CRJ-700 First Officer reported 'Nose Wheel Steering Inop' and 'Gear Disagree' warnings after takeoff. Crew declared an emergency and returned to departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a 'Nose Wheel Steering Inop' caution and 'Gear Disagree' warning immediately after takeoff and gear retraction. They declared an emergency, followed QRH procedures, and returned to the departure airport.

synopsis: A Lear 35 Captain reported losing hydraulic pressure on climbout. Flight continued to destination, and upon landing the drag chute was deployed but departed the aircraft. Aircraft was stopped with emergency braking after some initial difficulties.
summary: During climb-out, the crew experienced a total hydraulic failure, forcing an emergency gear extension and landing without flaps or normal braking. The drag chute detached after deployment, and the pilot struggled to engage the emergency brake lever, but the aircraft stopped with 1,000 feet of runway remaining.

synopsis: MD-83 Captain reported losing First Officer CADC on takeoff roll, so the takeoff was rejected and the flight returned to the gate.
summary: During takeoff roll, the First Officer's airspeed indicator failed and auto-throttles disconnected due to a lost CADC, prompting a rejected takeoff at 80 KTS. The crew exited the runway, returned to the gate for maintenance inspection, and logged the event after confirming brake temperatures remained below 205°C.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reported losing #1 Hydraulic System. Flight declared emergency and diverted to nearest suitable airport.
summary: During stable cruise, the crew received an amber ED1 hydraulic 1 low pressure indication and diverted to the nearest suitable airport. They declared an emergency during descent, completed a visual approach without issues, and ended the emergency after clearing the runway.

synopsis: BE-400XP flight crew found the First Officer's O2 mask was installed incorrectly after maintenance, potentially rendering the mask unusable.
summary: The flight crew accepted an aircraft out of maintenance for a reposition flight, unaware the co-pilot's oxygen mask harness was installed upside down. The error was discovered upon arrival when the mask fell out, potentially preventing quick donning, though no leaks were detected.

synopsis: Hawker 850 flight crew reports exceeding 1,500 FT prior to WENTZ on RUUDY 4 departure from TEB while attempting to use VNAV with 2,000 FT set in the altitude preselect (MCP).
summary: The Captain and First Officer overshot the 1,500 FT constraint on the RUUDY 4 departure from TEB while using VNAV with a 2,000 FT preselect. The crew attributed the deviation to delayed flight director response, manual power adjustments, and a distracting ATC frequency change, subsequently deciding to avoid VNAV for this procedure.

synopsis: Captain describes his efforts to have Maintenance remove erosion tape from the HF antenna on the vertical stabilizer of a B737-800 aircraft, due to tape was peeling off and potentially cover Elevator Pitot System in flight. Maintenance Supervisor disagreed. Captain refused aircraft.
summary: The pilot refused an aircraft during preflight due to peeling HF antenna erosion tape that could block the Elevator Pitot System. Maintenance deferred the repair citing safety risks, causing a 3-hour 44-minute delay until a replacement aircraft was found.

synopsis: MD-83 Captain reported turning down an aircraft that had multiple persistent electrical issues that were deferred instead of resolved.
summary: The pilot refused the aircraft at the gate due to multiple electrical failures, including repeated 150-amp ground power and battery charger circuit breaker trips, an inoperative APU generator, and MEL-listed cargo heater and recirculation issues. The reporter believed these recurring faults indicated a larger underlying problem requiring the aircraft to be removed from service rather than continuing revenue flights.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported encountering wake vortex 11 miles in trail of a B747 on approach to LAX, resulting in turbulence and roll. One Flight Attendant reported back pain as a result.
summary: During descent through 15,000 feet on the RIIVR2 arrival into LAX, the crew encountered wake turbulence from a B747 eleven miles ahead, causing a 10-degree roll. A flight attendant fell to the floor and reported mid-back pain but declined immediate medical assistance.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported turbulence from a wake vortex encounter in cruise flight that resulted in a minor back injury to a flight attendant.
summary: During cruise near BUF with autopilot engaged, the flight crew encountered wake turbulence causing a single bump despite clear skies and no reported traffic. The Purser reported a possible back injury from the event but continued duties without difficulty.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports about the disagreement he had with a Maintenenance Supervisor involving a lightning strike burn mark on the external skin of a B777-200 Nose Landing Gear (NLG) door. Mechanic also raises his concerns about a performance driven management culture versus aircraft safety.
summary: A mechanic identified a lightning burn mark on a B777-200 nose gear door, but Supervisor X incorrectly claimed it was a paint chip and attempted to remove the mechanic. While other mechanics concurred with the burn finding, the supervisor refused to acknowledge the damage, citing a management performance culture that undermines mechanic independence.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported NMAC in the traffic pattern.
summary: The pilot reported a near mid-air collision on final approach due to congested ATC and four light aircraft. After being instructed to turn right, the pilot evaded an unseen aircraft crossing their path by pulling up and banking away.

synopsis: BE20 First Officer questioned an experienced Captain's decision to cancel IFR, operate the aircraft in a less than professional manner, and violate VFR cloud clearance criteria apparently motivated by a case of 'get-there-itis.'
summary: A right-seat pilot reported that a Captain on a King Air B200 charter flight cancelled IFR to scud run through a 500-foot cloud gap at 500 feet AGL. The maneuver triggered TAWS warnings and involved flying near terrain and power lines due to the Captain's complacency and pressure to reach the destination.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: C-525 Captain reported NMAC that he felt could have been avoided with better ATC technique.
summary: The pilot reported that Air Traffic Control issued a crossing altitude placing their aircraft directly above a training aircraft on approach. The controller initially claimed 500 feet separation was sufficient but subsequently diverted the other aircraft, prompting the pilot to contact the manager regarding unsafe separation planning.

synopsis: B767 Captain describes a tire failure at 160 KTS during the takeoff roll. The takeoff is continued and when the flaps are retracted a 'TE flap disagree' is annunciated and a pronounced rolling tendency is noted. An emergency is declared, fuel is dumped, and when the gear is extended an unsafe indication is noted for the right main gear. After landing a large hole is found in the right wing directly above the right main landing gear strut.
summary: The Captain reported a right main gear tire blowout during takeoff, causing flap asymmetry and gear extension failure. The crew managed the emergency by dumping fuel, manually controlling the aircraft, and executing a rough landing with a 4-foot hole in the right wing root.

synopsis: A BE200 pilot was unable to find OLIIN waypoint on J2 on government charts downloaded to an iPad. Clearance delivery advises that OLIIN has replaced CIE which is to be decommissioned. The fix was located on a second iPad downloaded from a different source.
summary: The pilot received a departure clearance referencing the OLIIN intersection, which was missing from one set of government charts but present on another. After a 15-minute delay and an amended clearance excluding OLIIN, the crew flew the revised route and reported the chart discrepancy to authorities.

synopsis: DA40 Flight Instructor reports taking control of the aircraft from his student during landing when speed becomes to low. The nose is allowed to drop causing the nose gear to seperate from the aircraft.
summary: A student pilot on approach dropped below recommended speed, causing the nose gear to fracture when they relinquished controls after the instructor's command. The instructor executed a go-around, confirmed the gear loss via low passes, and completed a soft field landing with no injuries or serious damage.

synopsis: Enroute Controller initiated 'no gyro vectors' to an aircraft that was experiencing difficulties complying with assigned headings, the reporter recommending more pilot training to prevent future occurrences.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller and trainee managed a PA32 pilot who lost directional control due to vertigo while departing. The pilot climbed from 4,000 to 6,000 feet and descended below assigned altitude before completing a visual approach, requiring recurrent training on partial panel procedures.

synopsis: Upon taxi into the gate Air Carrier flight crew note EICAS indications that the right engine is shutting down although the fuel control switch is still on with fuel flow indicated with EGT rising and N2 decreasing. The engine is secured with the fuel control switch and Maintenance is informed.
summary: The pilot reported that after landing and taxiing to the gate, the right engine oil pressure dropped to 40 PSI, triggering EICAS warnings and an EGT rise. The pilot shut down the right engine and observed an oil leak from the cowling, prompting a maintenance call and debrief.

synopsis: An air carrier Dispatcher was unable to establish a flight crew/Dispatch/Maintenance Control communication link request from a domestic flight. Ultimately, the Captain gave up the attempt due to the distraction being more of a problem than was the reason for which the patch was requested.
summary: A dispatcher attempted a three-way phone patch between the Captain and Maintenance Control, but the connection repeatedly failed due to poor radio quality and dropped lines. The Captain eventually continued to the destination, while the dispatcher required assistance from colleagues to manage workload changes caused by updated weather forecasts.

synopsis: A B737-700 flight crew inadvertently taxied past the Runway 35 hold short line. Confusion over the location of the hold short line on Taxiway Papa vice Alpha contributed to their error.
summary: The pilot not flying crossed the Runway 35 hold short line on taxiway Papa while taxiing for takeoff. The incursion occurred because the pilot mentally dismissed the actual line, expecting it to be located closer to the runway as it is on taxiway Alpha.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported entering a cargo net discrepancy in the logbook prior to departure and informing Maintenance. The Captain was then chastised by the Maintenance Controller for making the entry at a non maintenance base.
summary: A pilot reported a missing cargo door net hook after loading, but Maintenance Control suggested delaying the log entry to move the aircraft to a station with maintenance. The pilot refused, logged the discrepancy, and incurred a 50-minute delay for local contract maintenance to repair the Airbus.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 descending via the FNCHR RNAV STAR to MEM in calm wind conditions experienced what the flight crew believed to have been long term severe wake turbulence from a preceding aircraft.
summary: Pilots descending via the FNCHR1 arrival encountered severe wake turbulence from a preceding heavy B737 at 16,000 feet due to calm winds and close vertical proximity. The crew eventually deviated 10 degrees left to escape the turbulence, attributing the event to "descend via" procedures forcing both aircraft onto the same flight path.

synopsis: EMB145 First Officer experiences a RUDDER SYS 1-2 INOP EICAS message during climb. QRH procedures are accomplished but only Rudder System 1 is returned to normal operation. Maintenance indicates that the crew should return to the departure airport, which is accomplished, although at the time they are closer to their destination.
summary: During climb, the crew received a RUDDER SYS 1-2 INOP message; System 1 recovered but System 2 remained inoperative. Despite being 30 minutes from destination, Maintenance Control ordered an air return due to being busy, resulting in a safe landing, aircraft swap, and subsequent departure.

synopsis: EMB-145XR First Officer described seeing and smelling thick smoke on initial climb. Flight declared an emergency and returned to departure airport.
summary: The crew encountered thick cockpit smoke at 2,000 feet after takeoff, prompting an emergency return and overweight landing. A malfunctioning oxygen mask microphone hindered communication between pilots and the flight attendant, though the crew managed the situation using hand signals and partial mask removal.

synopsis: A Dispatcher related concern regarding routine and frequent computer related outages primarily related to communications with the flights for which he is responsible.
summary: An air traffic controller experienced a simultaneous failure of communications, plotting, and ACARS systems while assisting a pilot with landing data. The company ordered an exit from all computer systems for IT repairs, leaving the controller unable to communicate with the aircraft during the incident.

synopsis: Dash 8-100 Captain reported smoke and odor emanating from windshield heat terminal bar. Power to window was shut off and smoke and odor disappeared.
summary: The crew detected an electrical odor and slight smoke from the right windshield terminal bar while approaching the destination. They turned off the windshield heat, which stopped the smoke, and landed safely after confirming a similar prior incident with Maintenance Control.

synopsis: CE-750 First Officer, pilot flying an arrival using VS to meet published altitude and speed restrictions, is confronted by the Captain regarding the use of VNAV instead of VS. Captain engaged the VNAV mode without informing the First Officer. First Officer re-engaged VS and landed without further incident.
summary: The SIC pilot flying an arrival descent reported that the Captain engaged VNAV without consent, causing an unintended speed increase to 340 KTS. This resulted in a 20 KTS speed restriction exceedance at the next fix before the SIC regained control and corrected the speed.

synopsis: CE-560XL Captain reported loss of both his and First Officer heading information. Flight declared an emergency and diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: During an enroute ferry flight descent through FL400, the Captain and First Officer experienced a dual heading failure indicated by 'HDG FAIL' annunciators. After completing the checklist and declaring an emergency, the crew descended in VFR conditions and landed without incident.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew experienced compressor stall on Number One Engine on initial climb. Engine was shut down, flight declared an emergency and returned to departure airport.
summary: The pilot experienced repeated loud bangs and N1 RPM fluctuations in Engine One at 1,500 feet AGL, identifying a compressor stall. After declaring an emergency, the crew shut down the engine, dumped 55,000 pounds of fuel, and executed a coupled auto-land ILS approach.

synopsis: Two Maintenance technicians were flown to an outlying station to repair a maintenance defect. After they completed the work, and returned to the home station, they were advised that the work they performed should have been verified by an Inspector.
summary: Two maintenance technicians removed and reinstalled a squealing left overwing emergency exit door on a chartered aircraft during a road trip. They later learned an Inspector should have been present for the installation, as the Duty Manager incorrectly assumed one was not needed.

synopsis: PA28 flight instructor experiences a loss of engine power after becoming airborne with a student at the controls. The instructor assumes control, but with insufficient runway remaining and insufficient power to climb, an of runway landing ensues with minimal damage and no injuries.
summary: During a student training touch-and-go, the aircraft suddenly lost power and RPM shortly after takeoff, causing a loss of lift. The pilot executed a shallow left turn to avoid housing and performed a soft field landing in the clearing area with no injuries or damage.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A private pilot reported operating near a disabled aircraft that was just off the runway and questioned whether that was legal or advisable.
summary: A pilot on final approach to Runway 34 at CGE observed an unoccupied, damaged ultralight aircraft on a turn-off and initially executed a go-around. After landing and taking off again, the pilot concluded the situation was unsafe and resolved to divert to another airport in the future rather than operating near an inoperative aircraft.

synopsis: C210 pilot reported he landed with green landing gear light but the gear had apparently not extended.
summary: The pilot reported a landing phase incident where the landing gear failed to deploy despite a green gear light. An FAA Inspector observed the event and advised that the cause appeared to be a mechanical malfunction.

synopsis: PA-44-180 instructor reported the aircraft departed the runway, causing minor damage, when power was cut to simulate an engine failure.
summary: During a multi-engine training takeoff, an instructor simulated an engine failure, but the student failed to release controls, causing the aircraft to exit the runway and destroy a light. The resulting minor damage to the propellers was repaired within days, leading the instructor to conclude that simulating takeoff failures on a student's first flight is unsafe.

synopsis: Starduster II pilot reported his right main landing gear collapsed when the aircraft swerved after landing.
summary: The pilot reported that while landing a Starduster II, the aircraft swerved and the right main landing gear collapsed, causing it to slide to a stop. The pilot attributed the incident to deciding not to go around when the swerve began, resulting in a bruised passenger leg.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A pilot read back a clearance to cross 50 northwest of APA at 15,000 FT but the the crew leveled at 16,000 FT because of high terrain knowledge and was then notified by ATC that the descent clearance was to 17,000 FT.
summary: During initial descent, the crew misread a clearance to cross at 15,000 feet instead of 17,000 feet due to controller oversight of their incorrect readback. The Captain leveled at 16,000 feet upon spotting terrain, and ATC later instructed a climb to 17,000 feet after frequency congestion prevented earlier clarification.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Tower Controller described a developing separation problem on final. Controller noted the TRACON Controller's application of 'Visual Separation' as questionable.
summary: A Tower controller reported an unsafe operation where an Approach controller sequenced a Dash 8 and CRJ2 with less than one mile separation, incorrectly assuming the Dash 8 could provide visual separation. The controller cleared both aircraft to land, noting the incident resulted from inadequate Approach sequencing and visual separation application.

synopsis: Tower Controller described an unsafe situation involving a conflict between military aircraft and a local law enforcement aircraft that was conducting surveillance maneuvers.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a near mid-air collision between a sheriff's C182 and two C130s in Class D airspace when the C130s changed lead aircraft and climbed into the C182's path. The controller issued traffic alerts and turned both aircraft to avoid a head-on conflict, leaving the C182 pilot rattled and prompting a change in the surveillance flight's route.

synopsis: A flight crew refused to fly a B737-800 after a logbook entry stated 'potable water failed EPA testing, needs disinfected' but did not contain a sign off after the required 48 hour compliance period.
summary: The Captain and First Officer initially refused an aircraft with a potable water MEL discrepancy due to missing logbook documentation of required disinfection and retesting. They accepted the aircraft only after Maintenance Control confirmed the work was completed and recorded on a non-routine card held at the maintenance base.

synopsis: A pilot reported that the MDW Runway 31C Hold Short Line is difficult to see at night and in the rain. Better lighting and/or more contrasting markings in that area are needed.
summary: A pilot reported difficulty seeing runway hold short markings while approaching Runway 31C at MDW for takeoff due to poor lighting and heavy rain. The reporter recommends improved markings and lighting at the airport to address this safety concern.

synopsis: B737-300 Captain experiences a cabin altitude warning horn approaching FL350. A descent is initiated and upon reaching FL250 cabin altitude has descended to 5,000 FT. There were no indications of a pressurization controller or pack malfunction, but the duct pressure on the right side was near zero.
summary: During climbout at 33,500 feet, the flight crew experienced a cabin altitude warning at 11,000 feet caused by near-zero right duct pressure. The crew descended to stabilize pressurization, but the aircraft was taken out of service after the dispatcher remained unaware of the incident due to unclear communication.

synopsis: CRJ-700 flight crew noted high Fan Vibe gauge readings during climb and, after descending and slowing the aircraft, stabilized the engine within limits. After considering the aircraft problem and destination weather, crew elected to divert. Captain noted that the Fan Vibe issue was difficult to locate in the QRH.
summary: The flight crew diverted after the right engine fan vibration spiked during climb, causing audible noise and requiring a descent to FL300. Although Maintenance Control cleared continued flight, the crew elected to land precautionarily due to deteriorating destination weather and concerns about engine performance during a potential go-around.

synopsis: B757-200 crewmember reported WX radar failed during climb out. Since thunderstorms were forecast enroute the flight declared an emergency and returned to departure airport.
summary: During climb out while deviating for weather, the crew experienced WX WEAK followed by WX FAIL on both HSI screens. Due to night conditions and scattered thunderstorms, they declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport, and landed at normal weight.

synopsis: A B737NG Captain expressed concern about the proper interpretation of an MEL regarding malfunctioning flight crew alerting systems.
summary: The flight crew and maintenance personnel encountered an inoperative engine system annunciator light during the before taxi phase. Maintenance reset circuit breakers and performed a lights test, placarding the light inoperative despite the crew's concern that the MEL requirements for verifying associated panel lights were not fully met.

synopsis: Although technically legal to do so, B737-800 Captain advised ATC the flight was unable to descend 'via' the GIBBZ RNAV STAR to IAD due to a deferred FMC component and requested an alternative arrival. His decision was based on excessive flight crew workload associated with the complex RNAV STAR's multiple speed and altitude restrictions.
summary: The crew declined a 'descend via' clearance for the GIBBZ1 arrival to IAD due to a placarded First Officer FMC and workload concerns. This caused confusion with Washington and Potomac controllers, resulting in vectors to the DOCCS1 arrival, though the landing remained uneventful.

synopsis: B737-800 Check Captain describes a low fuel situation arriving LAX due to delays for a runway closure and a go-around caused by an aircraft departure on the landing runway. Gate arrival fuel is 4,000 LBS.
summary: An IOE Captain and crew on a Boeing 737 experienced a runway incursion risk at LAX due to a departing aircraft, forcing a go-around and minimum fuel declaration. The flight landed safely with 4,000 lbs of fuel after ATC vectors and a low fuel warning on final approach.

synopsis: A300 flight crew experiences speed and altitude anomalies during the EAGUL5 RNAV arrival to PHX landing west. The altimeter was set to local when cleared to descend via, prior to FL180.
summary: The flight crew descended below the FL240 restriction at PAYSO and crossed VNNOM 500 feet high due to Profile Mode autopilot errors and distraction while troubleshooting FMS speed targets. They manually recovered the aircraft and completed an uneventful landing after ATC issued a runway change.

synopsis: After they were vectored off the TRUPS RNAV STAR to DCA for spacing the flight crew of a B737-800 assumed that a clearance 'direct to TRUPS, resume the STAR' included the clearance to resume descent on the arrival. ATC disagreed, believing they should have maintained their last assigned altitude independent of the STAR restrictions.
summary: During the TRUPS ONE arrival, a controller intervened at 10,400 feet to clear the crew to 9,000 feet after they descended toward 8,000 feet without a specific altitude assignment. The pilot attributed the confusion to the lack of a verbalized maintain or descend via clearance when resuming the RNAV STAR.

synopsis: IA1125 First Officer reports the Captain missing the crossing restriction at DYLAN on the PHLBO3 RNAV arrival to EWR while the First Officer is evaluating the Class B airspace. ATC issues vectors.
summary: During an IFR arrival to EWR, the crew descended via the PHLBO3 arrival but crossed the DYLAN intersection at 10,800 feet instead of the required 8,000 feet. The deviation occurred because the pilot flying relied on VNAV after the glide slope disappeared while the first officer was distracted by a Class B airspace request, leading to a loss of situational awareness.

synopsis: A BE-20 pilot shut an engine down on approach to a Class B airport but declined to declare an emergency.
summary: A pilot flying a single-engine aircraft into a Class B airport descended below the assigned 6,000 feet to 5,700 feet while securing a failing right engine. The pilot declined to declare an emergency despite high workload and sunset conditions but successfully landed after being vectored for the localizer.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain notices number one engine oil quantity dropping during takeoff and rejects above 100 KTS.
summary: The pilot rejected the takeoff at 100 KTS due to rapidly falling number one engine oil quantity dropping from 40% to 30%. The aircraft stopped safely on the dry runway and returned to the gate for maintenance to prevent potential engine failure.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reports erratic fuel flow indication on the left engine and rejects the takeoff below 90 KTS.
summary: The crew aborted takeoff twice due to erratic fuel flow on the left engine, first at 90 KTS and again below 85 KTS. After maintenance inspection and sign-off, the aircraft departed and completed the flight without further incident.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain experiences autopilot disengagement at 75 FT during an auto land approach in VMC. A firm manual landing ensues after a small bounce. Maintenance determines that the Captain's radar altimeter failed at 75 FT causing the autopilot disengagement.
summary: During a practice auto-land at SEA, the autopilot and autothrottle disengaged at 75 feet due to a Captain's Radar Altimeter failure, causing a manual takeover and a bounced landing. The event resulted in no injuries or hard landing indications but highlighted the risks of transferring control near touchdown.

synopsis: EMB145 flight crew experiences a Bleed 2 Leak during initial climb. QRH procedures are complied with and the engine bleed valve is closed, but no valve closed annunciation is displayed. Engine 2 is shut down and the flight returns to the departure airport after declaring an emergency. The bleed leak message remains on until just before landing.
summary: The crew received a Bleed 2 Leak message during climbout, declared an emergency, and shut down Engine 2. Ground personnel inspected the aircraft after landing and cleared it for taxi to the gate on Engine 1, though the leak message remained active.

synopsis: B737-400 Captain reports failure of the left main gear to extend during approach. A go-around is initiated and the gear is successfully extended using the alternate extension method. An uneventful landing and taxi to the gate ensues.
summary: During approach, the left main gear failed to extend, prompting a missed approach, emergency declaration, and successful alternate extension per the QRH. After a low fly-by confirmed the gear was locked, the crew completed a normal landing, though the cause remained unknown and maintenance inspected the aircraft.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 flight crew diverted to a nearby airport when the left engine oil pressure began fluctuating and the CAS oil warning illuminated.
summary: During climb, the crew experienced a left engine oil CAS warning with fluctuating pressure between 25 and 30 PSI. Following QRH procedures and contacting Maintenance Control, they diverted to a nearby airport and completed required logbook entries.

synopsis: CRJ-700 First Officer reports evacuating the aircraft during taxi due to smoke in the cockpit and cabin. The crew is informed a day later that no logbook entry was made.
summary: The Captain and First Officer evacuated the aircraft on a taxiway due to smoke but failed to log the incident in the maintenance log. This omission resulted from task saturation caused by extensive post-emergency inquiries and paperwork from company, fire, and station personnel.

synopsis: A Falcon 2000 flight crew declared an emergency and diverted to a nearby airport due to an illuminated wheel well overheat light.
summary: During climbout, the crew observed a Left Wheel Well Overheat light, declared an emergency, and diverted to the nearest suitable airport. The aircraft landed normally after following the emergency procedure.

synopsis: MD82 Captain describes a TCAS RA event during a visual approach to an uncontrolled airport. After maneuvering for the RA a 360 degree turn is required to get back on the approach path.
summary: An MD80 pilot on a visual approach to Runway 26 executed multiple TCAS vertical speed commands and a 360-degree turn to avoid a small aircraft loitering in the approach path. The conflict occurred because the other pilot, despite acknowledging traffic calls, failed to remain north of the highway and performed maneuvers that prevented divergence.

synopsis: While in their descent a Beech 1900 flight crew suffered an NMAC with a VFR Beech Baron.
summary: The crew of a descending aircraft, with TCAS inoperative, avoided a collision with a Beechcraft Baron spotted 20 feet below after ATC issued a traffic advisory. The Baron passed left to right, and the subsequent handover between controllers resulted in the new controller being unaware of the incident.

synopsis: After Maintenance at their originating airport declared several suspect brake wear indicators to be 'well within limits' and signed off the logbook the flight crew of an MD-83 once again wrote them up as below limits at an intermediate stop and Maintenance there took the aircraft out of service until the brakes could be changed, stating they were '...not well within limits.'
summary: The Captain and First Officer reported brake wear indicator discrepancies on an MD-83 during preflight at two stations. A maintenance technician initially cleared the aircraft despite apparent limits, but the flight was cancelled at the second station when brakes were confirmed below limits and required replacement.

synopsis: While distracted by unassociated maintenance considerations during his preflight, the Captain of an MD-83 failed to notice a missing switch cover until at cruise.
summary: The Captain performed the preflight alone while addressing maintenance issues and missed a missing white cover on the Captain's Stick Shaker Push to Inhibit switch during the Stall Warning test. The discrepancy was logged after level off, and the switch cover was replaced at the destination.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reports misunderstanding his IFR clearance departing CON. An ATC question about maintaining terrain clearance northbound is interpreted as just that, a question and not a clearance to maintain runway heading after takeoff.
summary: A pilot departing Concord Runway 35 on an IFR flight misinterpreted a controller's terrain clearance question as permission to use the published ODP instead of flying northbound. The pilot executed the ODP turn, was vectored back to heading 210 for traffic, and clarified the misunderstanding with no loss of separation.

synopsis: CE680 First Officer reports crossing WENTZ below the RUUDY 4 depicted altitude due to a traffic advisory although the traffic was at 1000 feet.
summary: The pilot flying departed on the TEB RUUDY 4 SID and descended to 1400 feet to maintain visual separation from opposite-direction traffic, deviating from the required 1500 feet. The pilot acknowledged that prioritizing visual separation over the published procedure was an error, though no separation violation occurred.

aircraft: MD-90 Series (DC-9-90) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: When the Maintenance technicians identified a defective part in a MD90 hydraulic system, they discovered that a replacement part was not available, and the system was not deferrable. They then identified a comparable part on the aircraft that was installed in a deferrable system. They swapped the units, and deferred the affected system per an approved MEL. The plan worked well until several days later when the inoperative accumulator, now installed on the thrust reverser, developed an external leak. The released hydraulic fluid contaminated the APU inlet.
summary: Mechanics swapped a serviceable thrust reverser accumulator for a faulty elevator/rudder accumulator on an MD90 to resolve a hydraulic air issue. Five days later, the deferred accumulator leaked hydraulic fluid into the APU inlet, causing cabin odor and haze, which required part replacement and APU maintenance.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a conflict when traffic conducting a survey operation agreed to maintain visual separation with an inbound air carrier, but continued on the grid pattern requiring the air carrier to initiate evasive action/s.
summary: A South Local Controller reported a near-midair conflict between a PA31 survey aircraft and a B737 arriving for Runway 12L. The PA31 accepted visual separation but failed to maneuver, forcing the B737 to descend rapidly to avoid collision, prompting the controller to relocate the survey grid.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a conflict event listing multiple human factors that may have contributed to the apparent lapse in vigilance.
summary: A fatigued air traffic controller failed to recognize a conflict between a B737 at FL380 and a descending Citation, resulting in a loss of separation estimated at 3.5 miles. The controller attributed the error to sleep deprivation and mental disengagement, requiring immediate corrective vectors to restore safe separation.

synopsis: Approach Controller cleared two aircraft to a 'T' fix on an RNAV procedure only to later discover that the 'T' fix was removed from the approach on a recent procedural change.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared two aircraft for RNAV 4L approaches using a non-existent T fix ABCDE due to unannounced changes in the approach plates. The controller discovered the error later and notified management, noting that no facility personnel or briefing items had indicated the significant chart update.

synopsis: Local Controller and Ground Controller described an aborted takeoff event when an aircraft observed a mower crossing down field. Failed coordination between Local and Ground reportedly led to the occurrence.
summary: A Local Controller cleared a Challenger for takeoff while a Ground Controller had authorized a mower to cross the runway, causing the aircraft to abort. The incident resulted from obscured tower views, combined controller duties, and a failure to coordinate the mower's immediate crossing status.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer describes a number 1 engine flame out at 11,000 FT during descent. An emergency is declared while the failed engine self starts and shuts down two times during the descent and landing.
summary: The flight crew experienced a Number 1 engine flameout at 11,000 feet during night arrival, followed by cabin light failure and a second failure after throttle advancement. The engine self-started twice, allowing the crew to complete the approach and land safely with emergency vehicle escort.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reports that Spot 8 near Concourse D at LAS is not located where it is depicted on the Commercial Chart diagram.
summary: The pilot taxied to Spot 8 instead of the assigned Spot 7 due to a discrepancy between the commercial chart and actual gate locations. After realizing the error, the crew continued taxiing under a new runway clearance to ensure safety.

synopsis: CL600 Captain experienced a stall fail caution message climbing through FL350. In compliance with QRH procedures the left PTCT switch is turned off. One minute later continuous ignition came on, the warbler sounded and the stick shaker activated. Flight returned uneventfully to departure airport after declaring an emergency.
summary: During climb through 35,000 feet, the crew received a stall fail caution and turned off the left PTCT switch per QRH. One minute later, continuous ignition, warbler, and stick shaker activated with conflicting airspeed cues at 280 knots, prompting an emergency declaration and return.

synopsis: EMB145 First Officer reports the EICAS displayed L/G Air Ground Fail message during initial climb. After complying with QRH procedures crew elects to return to the departure airport. Many anomalous EICAS messages and stick shaker activation are reported during taxi in and shut down at the gate.
summary: During climb-out, a First Officer and Captain experienced an EICAS L/G Air Ground Fail message causing false ground logic, leading to a gate return. Post-landing, a stick shaker activated below 10 knots, and switching to GPU power caused multiple system failures and an inoperative gust lock.

synopsis: ERJ-170 Captain reported that the aircraft started to drift to the right while taxiing after one engine was shutdown. Nosewheel steering was inoperative and Captain subsequently noted that the First Officer had turned the hydraulic pump off.
