Cabin altitude remains below 11,000 FT and masks do not drop but Flight Attendant's report personally using oxygen bottles on their own initiative.
summary: Pilots and cabin crew experienced a rapid cabin altitude climb exceeding 1,000 ft/min at FL310 due to pressurization failure. The crew descended to 10,000 ft using manual pressurization, avoiding passenger oxygen mask deployment and returning safely without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: B767-200 flight crew reports being dispatched with an existing placard for the equipment cooling valve. The valve was confirmed closed during preflight and the circuit breaker collared in compliance with MEL procedures. After takeoff the aircraft will not pressurize and the flight returns for an overweight landing. Maintenance confirms that the equipment valve is now open.
summary: The crew declared an emergency and executed an overweight landing after the aircraft failed to pressurize due to an outboard equipment cooling valve opening despite a pulled circuit breaker. Maintenance later confirmed the valve was open, and the pilot suspected an intermittent short to ground caused the malfunction.

synopsis: MD80 First Officer notes loss of engine indications for the right engine after reaching cruise altitude. After consulting with Maintenance Control the flight diverts to a suitable airport.
summary: The pilot reported that upon reaching cruise altitude, right engine instrument readings went blank while EGT, N1, and N2 remained normal. The crew contacted Maintenance Control and ATC and diverted to the nearest suitable airport.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reports failure of the right engine anti-ice valve to open during descent. The Captain instructs the First Officer to squawk the emergency code but 7500 is entered in error. After ATC inquiry the correct code is inserted and the flight continues to destination with the right engine at idle due to vibration experienced during the descent.
summary: The crew encountered a right engine anti-ice valve failure during descent in icing conditions, causing high vibration. Intense workload led to an inadvertent transponder code 7500 entry instead of 7700, which was corrected after ATC inquiry, resulting in an uneventful single-engine landing.

synopsis: A Maintenance Technician found it difficult comply with a MD-11 MEL procedure and elected to remove the harness and store it in the flight deck closet. He suggests a revision to the MEL be considered.
summary: A mechanic deferred a faulty #5 tire pressure sensor on an MD-11 during pushback after finding the MEL procedure for securing the harness unsafe. The mechanic removed and capped the sensor coupling, stored the harness in the flight deck, and recommended updating the MEL to specify safe deactivation steps.

synopsis: A Falcon 900 autopilot failed to capture 1,500 FT on the TEB RUUDY 4 SID so the Captain disconnected the autopilot and manually returned to the SID altitude constraint.
summary: During a TEB departure on Runway 24, the autopilot failed to capture the 1,500 FT altitude at WENTZ, causing the aircraft to climb to 1,740 FT. The pilot manually corrected the altitude within 20 seconds before ATC cleared an immediate climb to 6,000 FT.

synopsis: While flying VFR, a PA28 pilot notices that the generator has apparently failed and a turn is made to return to the departure airport. During descent airspeed is noted to be near the red line but slowing produces a mushy feeling in the flight controls. The airspeed indicator is ignored and the aircraft is successfully flown to a safe landing by feel alone.
summary: The pilot experienced total electrical failure and an unreliable airspeed indicator during VFR cruise. Flying by feel without radios or a transponder, the pilot landed safely despite the airspeed indicator reading 110 KTS at stall warning and 70 KTS at a full stop.

synopsis: C210 pilot experiences a NMAC at 4,500 FT shortly after level off while setting prop and throttle. A hard right turn is made to avoid collision.
summary: A VFR pilot in a single-engine aircraft at 4,500 feet near 5C1 observed a light twin heading directly toward them. The pilot executed an immediate hard right turn to avoid a potential collision, losing sight of the other aircraft shortly after.

synopsis: A BE40 Captain, distracted by the turbulence and weather, failed to level at 1,500 FT during a TEB RUUDY 4 Departure and climbed non stop to 2,000 FT.
summary: The pilot departed TEB on Runway 24 via the RUUDY 4 departure and encountered windshear on rotation. Distracted by the windshear, the pilot missed the 1,500-foot crossing restriction at WENTZ Intersection and climbed to 2,000 feet instead.

synopsis: Rotor of an A-119 helicopter preparing to depart from a highway accident scene was struck by a truck while still on the ground. Damage was inflicted on all four rotor blades.
summary: The EMS helicopter pilot reported that while starting up at an accident scene, a 26-foot rental truck struck the rotor system after the highway was reopened to traffic. This collision damaged all four rotor tips and rendered the aircraft unairworthy because the scene commander ignored the medic's request to keep the road closed.

synopsis: BE35 pilot reports engaging the autopilot and GPS without verifying the waypoint after being cleared to join V107. The aircraft attempts to turn back to the previous fix (VOR) before it is detected by both ATC and the reporter.
summary: During an IMC climb to 6,000 feet, the pilot engaged GPSS before the GPS sequenced to the next leg, causing a near-360-degree turn. The pilot disengaged the autopilot and corrected the heading after realizing the automation was attempting to rejoin the previous inbound leg.

aircraft: Bell Helicopter Textron Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A Helicopter departed MJD and after passing R-4403 at 750 FT had a near miss with a UAV painted white and very difficult to detect against the background.
summary: A pilot departing MJD on Runway 18 encountered a small, white, untransponder-equipped drone at 750 feet while flying 120 knots. The drone blended into the sky and was not detected by traffic alert systems, forcing the pilot to overtake it without time for evasive action.

synopsis: A single pilot departed on the TEB RUUDY 4 but failed to program the Garmin 530 to include the Departure and had a track deviation which ATC corrected with a vector away from conflicting traffic.
summary: A single-pilot flight departing TEB deviated from the RUUDY 4 SID because the pilot failed to enter the procedure into the active Garmin 530 flight plan after activation. The Departure Controller vectored the aircraft right to 320 degrees to prevent a possible loss of separation with landing traffic, an error attributed to pilot workload and reliance on a pre-stored plan.

synopsis: A pilot maneuvering during acrobatic flight in a high performance aircraft may have entered the V81 confines near CO15 while not communicating with ATC but monitoring the training area frequency 122.75.
summary: A pilot performing aerobatics near Kelly Airpark maneuvered to avoid an unseen aircraft passing over 2,500 feet below and west. The pilot attributed the lack of separation awareness to the other aircraft's silence on 122.75 and the failure of the TIS system to issue a traffic advisory.

synopsis: PCT Controller voiced concern regarding current visual approach 'turn on' restrictions as applied to visual approach procedures. The reporter noted the procedure is costly and introduces several safety concerns.
summary: An air traffic controller managing visual approaches to parallel runways 15L and 15R received a TARP alert for loss of separation after issuing a 200-degree heading to a Galaxy jet. The controller reported no actual unsafe situation occurred, attributing the alert to unnecessary 30-degree intercept restrictions that increase workload and operational costs.

synopsis: ZMP Controller described a questionable IFR clearance issued to an aircraft in difficulty encountering IMC conditions but not IFR qualified. The Controller indicated that actions taken were to get the pilot out of a dangerous situation.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller assisted a VFR pilot in IMC who was halfway through IFR training and flying 500 feet above ground. The controller issued a temporary VFR on Top clearance to raise the aircraft to 3,300 feet before reverting it to VFR status to avoid danger.

synopsis: PCT Controller described a TARP recorded separation event involving the mandated thirty degree turn on for visual approaches.
summary: The Final Controller reported a TARP loss of separation alert while managing visual approaches for Aircraft X and a B737 to parallel runways 15L and 15R. The controller stated the operation was safe but argued that the 30-degree intercept requirement unnecessarily increases workload for runways spaced over 4,300 feet apart.

synopsis: En route Controller described a loss of separation event when an inbound aircraft declared an emergency and failed to adhere to descent instructions.
summary: An A320 at FL270 and a G-IV descending to 13,000 feet experienced a conflict when the G-IV climbed back to FL234 after being cleared to FL240. The G-IV subsequently declared an emergency due to a right engine flame-out and requested a direct route to the airport.

synopsis: An aircraft descending on the PDX Runway 28R approach took evasive action to an EGPWS TERRAIN warning at 5,300 FT and was advised that they were over a 4,300 FT peak.
summary: During descent to PDX Runway 28R in IMC, the crew received an EGPWS terrain warning at 5,300 feet and executed an escape climb to 7,400 feet. Post-flight investigation confirmed the aircraft was over a 4,300-foot peak, with ATC confirming no loss of separation from other traffic.

synopsis: A B757 EICAS alerted RH WINDOW OVHT followed by the windshield outer pane cracking so an emergency was declared, the QRH completed, and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: During climb, a pilot reported a right window overheat alert on an aircraft, causing the outer pane of the right forward windscreen to shatter. The crew declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport, and performed an uneventful overweight landing.

synopsis: A B767-300 Right Landing Gear indicator did not illuminate with the gear down. Assuming a light malfunction, the Captain executed a go around, declared an emergency, set the flaps to 25, and with no warning sounds landed uneventfully.
summary: The flight crew executed a precautionary go-around and declared an emergency on a Boeing 767 approach due to a missing right main gear down indication. After a normal landing, ground crews visually inspected the gear, confirming the aircraft was safe despite the faulty indicator.

synopsis: M20 pilot reports turning direct to HAAYS after passing RUUDY on the RUUDY4 departure from TEB. ATC advises him of his error.
summary: The pilot departed TEB on the RUUDY 4 procedure and mistakenly turned toward HAAYS Intersection before receiving vectors. ATC corrected the heading mismatch, and the pilot maintained visual separation from traffic without further action.

synopsis: CE560 Captain reports climbing to 2,000 FT early on the RUUDY4 departure from TEB.
summary: A single-pilot high-performance jet departed TEB on the RUUDY 4 SID, climbing to 2,000 feet before passing the WENTZ fix instead of maintaining 1,500 feet. The pilot attributed this altitude deviation to confusing the procedure with a previous non-RNAV departure and failing to note the specific climb fix.

synopsis: B757 flight crew descending into BWI experiences a sudden 5 NM map shift and resultant track deviation that is questioned by ATC. The error is verified visually during approach and again at the gate using the map display, fix page, and the IRS latitude and longitude. The system is MEL'd for the return flight.
summary: The flight crew experienced a 5-mile northwest ADI map shift and IRS drift on all three units while passing RAVNN on the RAVNN3 arrival at BWI. ATC provided radar vectors for a visual approach to Runway 15R, and Maintenance Control issued an MEL for subsequent flights under Non-RNAV restrictions.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a reported opposite direction infraction between a aircraft practicing a missed approach procedure and an FAA Flight Check aircraft that initiated a go around, the reporter questioning the operational requirements of the 'Opposite Direction' procedures.
summary: An OJTI and a trainee on Local Control cleared a CRJ200 to land Runway 06 while a C182 executed a missed approach for Runway 24, creating an opposite direction conflict. The reporter attributed the event to insufficient training on opposite direction procedures and a misunderstanding that the non-landing C182 did not constitute an opposite direction situation.

synopsis: ATL Controller described a conflict involving a 'Ramp Controller' area alleging the Ramp Controller issued inappropriate taxi clearances to aircraft about to enter FAA controlled taxiways.
summary: A ground controller reported that a DC-9 ignored instructions to wait and entered a ramp mouth while two MD-88s were exiting, causing a dangerous pass. The controller attributed the incident to Ramp X's failure to hold aircraft and management's reluctance to enforce safety protocols.

synopsis: SCK Controller experienced a loss of legal separation with regard to the new 'Opposite Direction Procedure' with a departing aircraft and another on a 'Circling Approach', the reporter not realizing the new directive applied to this event.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller at Local Control cleared Aircraft W for takeoff from Runway 11L while Aircraft X was on an opposite direction approach to circle to land, creating a conflict. The controller attributed the error to misinterpreting new opposite direction rules and failing to break off Aircraft X sooner.

synopsis: A First Officer called in fatigued after being scheduled for an early morning show trip following thirteen hour duty day with sixteen hours awake.
summary: A pilot requested removal from a pairing due to fatigue caused by an 18-hour waking day, sleep deprivation, and operational delays on a B787. The pilot cited inadequate rest, meal delivery issues, and a subsequent scheduling call as reasons for being unfit to perform duties for the next assignment.

synopsis: A Dispatcher was unable to contact a Company aircraft using the new digital phone system after the crew requested a Dispatch/Maintenance phone patch.
summary: Air traffic controllers attempted a SELCAL phone patch with Dispatch and Maintenance using a specific frequency on the new digital system, but the call failed three times. The patch succeeded only after the flight contacted Commercial Radio to establish the connection.

synopsis: An air carrier First Officer had a habit of setting his altimeter's barometric pressure by 'spinning' the set knob but inadvertently set a 1.00 difference causing an altitude deviation because the autopilot did not capture the MCP altitude.
summary: The pilot flying reported that during approach, the First Officer's altimeter was incorrectly set to 31.12 instead of 30.12, causing the aircraft to descend below the 12,000-foot clearance. The pilot manually stopped the descent, corrected the setting, and attributed the error to complacency and insufficient checklist verification.

synopsis: A DHC-8-200 Captain declared an emergency and returned to the departure airport after the Number 2 Engine began surging during climb after takeoff.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a surging Number 2 Engine during climb out, prompting an emergency declaration and priority landing clearance from ATC. They determined an engine shutdown was unnecessary due to the minor fluctuation rate and completed a normal landing.

synopsis: Pilot reports nose gear tires on aircraft have been found damaged, deflated or with low tire pressures that Maintenance believes is caused by improper use of towbarless type tugs by ramp personnel.
summary: During pushback, the right nose wheel tire deflated due to improper alignment with a lift-type tug's claw device, which lifted the tire off the rim. Maintenance confirmed the ground crew failed to position the aircraft correctly, causing the tire to lose pressure and requiring replacement before departure.

synopsis: A MD-80 TAIL COMPARTMENT OVERHEAT warning alerted after takeoff but after the memory items were complete, the light did not extinguish until the right thrust lever was retarded per the QRH. An emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: During climb in an MD80, a tail compartment overheat warning persisted until the right engine was retarded to idle, prompting an emergency return and overweight landing. The crew completed checklists and landed safely with no smoke or cabin incidents, though the reporter noted the event was unusual for the ambient temperature.

synopsis: During descent when a MD-82 Left Hydraulic System was selected to HI/ON/CHECKED, the Master Caution and LEFT HYD LOW PRESS lights illuminated. An emergency was declared, the QRH completed and a normal landing followed.
summary: During approach, the First Officer selected hydraulic pumps to HI, causing left system pressure and quantity to drop to zero. The crew declared an emergency, performed the checklist, and landed safely without incident.

synopsis: A B757 with the Left PACK MEL'ed had a temporary loss of cabin pressurization as the descent out of FL350 commenced after the EICAS alerted RIGHT PACK INOP and RIGHT PACK OFF and while the QRH procedure was completed.
summary: A B757 crew operating with one pack inoperative lost the remaining pack shortly after Top of Descent from FL350, causing temporary cabin depressurization. The crew followed QRH procedures and landed safely.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A flight crew failed to notice that the lightly printed PDC changed the DFW LOWGN4 RNAV to the BLECO4 and so after being cleared to the BLECO intersection the crew asked for vectors because it was not in the FMS.
summary: The crew missed a revised BLECO4 departure segment on the PDC due to a faint ACARS print while operating a LOWGN4 departure. Although cleared direct to BLECO, no deviation occurred because the initial waypoints matched the original plan.

synopsis: A C172 Traffic Watch Pilot reported the loss of electrical, so he squawked 7600, returned to his departure airport. The pilot was given light signals to land and taxi to parking.
summary: During a VFR flight in Charlie airspace, the pilot experienced an alternator failure causing radio and flap issues. After squawking 7600 and landing via light gun signals, the electrical system recovered upon touchdown, likely due to a faulty connection.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Corporate aircraft on a GPS approach to SLN had a near miss in IMC with an aircraft climbing VFR in the clouds but not communicating with anyone.
summary: The pilot reported a TCAS conflict during an IMC GPS 17 approach to SLN, requiring a right turn and climb to avoid a VFR aircraft flying in IMC. The other aircraft passed 300 feet below, and Tower acknowledged the traffic but provided no vectors or contact.

synopsis: A109 helicopter pilot experienced an over torque on engine start but did not notice the Exceedance Alert until the second start after a patient had already been loaded for transport. Pilot completed the mission, but later had second thoughts about flying without a maintenance inspection and release.
summary: The pilot experienced a 109% transmission torque exceedance during engine start but elected to continue the flight with a patient on board after incorrectly determining the event was within limits. The pilot attributed the decision to self-imposed mission pressure and admitted they should have grounded the aircraft for maintenance inspection instead.

synopsis: A PA-44-180 electrical system surged during a practice instrument approach go around resulting the loss of both generators and smoke in the cockpit so the flight landed at the nearest airport.
summary: During a training flight's missed approach, the pilot and students experienced an electrical surge causing alternator failure, a popped circuit breaker, and smoke. The crew shut down non-essential equipment, notified ATC, and diverted to the nearest airport due to the burning smell and visible smoke.

synopsis: A Breezy engine lost power because of a blocked fuel line so the pilot landed the aircraft on a deforested pipeline area with no aircraft damage or injury.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Breezy experienced erratic engine performance at 1,000 feet AGL due to a suspected fuel line blockage from mixing 100LL and autogas. He executed a precautionary landing in a pipeline clearing, resulting in no damage to the aircraft or occupants.

synopsis: S46 Controller expressed concern regarding the operational characteristic of 'FUSED' RADAR, noting the targets 'jump' making it difficult to insure proper instructions are issued.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored a B737-900 behind a B737-800 for dual-dependent ILS approaches to Runways 16L and 16R. Separation was lost when the controller misjudged distance and turn rate due to FUSED radar target hopping and wind, forcing a break-off maneuver.

synopsis: PCT Controller voiced concern regarding the thirty degree intercept rule during Visual Approach procedures noting BWI with one downwind does not benefit from the new requirements.
summary: An air traffic controller at BWI cleared a Citation Excel for a visual approach to Runway 15L, but the aircraft turned 210 degrees to join final, causing a recorded loss of separation. The controller attributed the incident to the labor-intensive 30-degree intercept rule, which complicates operations at the busy airport.

synopsis: A B737-300 engine shutdown from fuel starvation at FL350 while the engine was being cross fed with the high tank pumps ON and the crossfeed valve open. The flight diverted to a nearby airport and the engine was restarted prior to landing.
summary: The Captain initiated a high-altitude crossfeed to burn center tank fuel, causing Engine #1 to roll back and the aircraft to roll left. The crew diverted, shut down and successfully restarted the engine, landing safely; the Captain attributed the incident to crossfeeding at high altitude with a minor imbalance.

synopsis: An A319 was released at the departure station with a belly fuselage fastener loose but at the next station was grounded until the fastener could be replaced and secured. The previous release was deemed illegal.
summary: A pilot discovered a missing fastener on a belly panel during a walk-around, which Maintenance Control initially deferred via a configuration deviation. A subsequent Maintenance Controller and Representative identified the deferral as illegal per the AMM, holding the outbound flight to replace the fastener immediately.

synopsis: B767-300 First Officer's backpack strap caught on and tripped the DC Standby Bus circuit breaker which ultimately resulted in the flight continuing without autothrottles.
summary: The First Officer's backpack strap snagged the DC Standby Bus CB, causing a power interruption that forced the left engine EEC into alternate mode. Consequently, autothrottles were lost, but the flight continued and landed safely after both engines were placed in EEC ALT MODE.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reported receiving a stick shaker on very short final from a preceding C130 wake vortex. Captain continued the approach to a normal landing.
summary: The First Officer reported a stick shaker on short final caused by C-130 wake turbulence from a practice go-around. The Captain landed safely, deciding to continue due to low altitude and runway length, while the First Officer deemed intervening more dangerous.

synopsis: G200 First Officer questions whether the hold short line for Runway 33 has been crossed as the crew taxi's to that runway via Taxiway A at DET.
summary: The pilot and PIC taxied a general aviation aircraft to Runway 33, crossing Runway 25 while debating the presence of hold short lines. The PIC stopped the aircraft due to uncertainty about crossing the lines, but they received a takeoff clearance before confirming whether a runway incursion occurred.

synopsis: A B737-700 number two engine bleed, which tripped on takeoff, was reset during climb but tripped again as the aircraft entered possible icing so the flight returned to the departure airport for the second BLEED trip maintenance of the day.
summary: The crew experienced a recurring right bleed trip light during climb after a delayed departure due to a previous PRSOV replacement. Entering icing conditions without the right air conditioning pack and with limited fuel, the pilot returned to the departure airport due to a suspected bleed or sensing system malfunction.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported a wake vortex encounter on approach to PHL that resulted in a hard landing. The reporter suggests perhaps a different ATC procedure could help avoid future incidents like this one.
summary: The flight crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding Airbus A320 while on a visual approach to Runway 35 at PHL, despite slowing to 142 KTS as instructed. The crew attributed the firm touchdown to timing that placed them in the wake during flare, prompting a logbook entry and a request for ATC guidance on intersection crossing intervals.

synopsis: BE400 First Officer reports slightly overshooting the initial level off altitude on departure from Runway 24 at TEB.
summary: The flight crew inadvertently overshot the initial level-off altitude during the RUUDY4 departure from Runway 24 at TEB but quickly corrected to 1,500 feet. No ATC query occurred, and the crew only learned of the error later from the Director of Safety.

synopsis: B1900 flight crew experienced a loss of the cabin pressurization controller and rapid pressure changes resulting in extreme ear discomfort. Flight crew noted a lack of checklist guidance for the problem they encountered.
summary: Pilots reported abnormal pressurization on a post-maintenance flight where the cabin altitude dropped 3,000 feet below zero during descent and surged 9,000 feet upon landing, causing extreme ear pain. The crew attributed the issue to recent pressurization system work and a lack of checklist guidance for this specific anomaly, resulting in a 24-hour medical grounding.

synopsis: PA-28 instructor pilot reported he and his student encountered wake vortex from an MD-88 departing another runway that caused a roll resulting in a wingtip strike.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot experienced a left wing drop during a crosswind landing on Runway 5 at Melbourne International in gusty winds. The instructor attributed the incident to suspected wind shear and wake turbulence from a departing MD-88, resulting in a wingtip strike and full stop landing.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Two fixed wing aircraft in formation on a photo mission in the New York City SFRA had a near miss with a sightseeing helicopter at about 1,400 FT over the Hudson River.
summary: Two aircraft flying in formation for aerial photography in the Hudson River VFR corridor encountered a helicopter that turned into their path. The pilots executed evasive maneuvers to avoid a collision, though ATC later reported a possible deviation for exceeding the 1,300 FT altitude limit.

synopsis: M98 Controller was advised of a 'Wake Remnant' separation error, the reporter noting that this separation criteria should not be a controller evaluation criteria.
summary: An air traffic controller received a wake remnant error report for a B767 and CRJ visual approach, citing failure to ensure the CRJ was on a 270 track rather than heading. The controller disputed the error, stating they maintained appropriate separation and did not believe wake turbulence was a factor.

synopsis: D01 Controller described a go around event during simultaneous approach procedures when one controller elected to alter the simultaneous procedures leading to the go around.
summary: A Monitor 2 Controller canceled a B737's ILS approach to 35R after the Final Controller ordered a pull-out during a shuffle procedure. The reporter attributed the go-around to the Final Controller's aggressive attempt to save time and fuel, noting that standard SIMOS procedures would have prevented the issue.

synopsis: Tower CIC described a conflict event when traffic conducting opposite direction operations initiated a go around and experienced a TCAS RA, indicating intra-facility ATC communications coordination as contributory.
summary: A Tower Controller reported a conflict between a C182 executing an early missed approach and a CRJ going around on opposite directions. The controller attributed the incident to a lack of coordination and communication regarding the IFR status and simultaneous maneuvers.

synopsis: A B737-300 Captain diverted because of a very loud, unusual noise apparently coming from beneath the floor, left side just after of the leading edge, forward of the emergency exit.
summary: The flight crew diverted due to an unexplained noise and vibration near the left wing floor, despite normal system indications. They declared an emergency for an overweight landing as instructed by Dispatch, landing safely without incident.

synopsis: The Captain of an RNAV equipped Boeing found himself with more questions than answers when ATC attempted to minimize the workload associated with the complex GIBBZ RNAV STAR by giving clearances direct to down-line waypoints, bypassing multiple intervening fixes with complex crossing restrictions. Among the questions were uncertainty as to the status of 'descend via' procedures and the effect of being cleared to GIBZZ 'at' an assigned--but unpublished--altitude on their need to comply with the prior STAR crossing restrictions at MOSLE, MONNK and BMICH.
summary: Pilots flying at FL370 on the GIBBZ1 arrival descended to approximately 10,700 feet after receiving conflicting clearances and VNAV path deviations. The reporter attributes the altitude error to imprecise phraseology regarding "descend via" clearances and the complexity of the arrival's numerous restrictions.

synopsis: ATC initiated alterations to the GIBZZ RNAV STAR may have contributed to an altitude deviation for a Boeing flight crew when the autoflight system failed to arrest their descent at 11,000 per the MCP altitude window and the active FLCH mode.
summary: The flight crew received a late descent clearance to cross MOSLE at 11,000 feet while in VNAV PATH. The aircraft overshot the altitude to 10,750 feet despite ALT CAP mode, requiring manual intervention to correct the descent.

synopsis: A B767-300 EICAS alerted LE FLAP ASYM EICAS when flaps 1 was selected. This aircraft had a previous history of this anomaly so the crew was prepared for it, had the equipment standing by and completed the abnormal landing.
summary: The flight crew encountered a LE FLAP ASYM EICAS message during flap extension on approach, prompting a landing on a 12,001-foot runway per Dispatch guidance. Despite prior warnings of potential system failures, the aircraft landed safely with normal reverse and autospoiler operation, followed by a brake check and fire truck inspection.

synopsis: A321 Captain discovers during preflight that the aircraft had a ELAC 1 Pitch Fault and ELAC 2 Pitch Fault a day earlier and that it is the same aircraft that he experienced the same problem several weeks earlier. The maintenance sign off was ground test OK, but a detailed review of the previous flight control failures was conducted at the reporters suggestion and the Pitch Trim Actuator was replaced.
summary: The pilot identified recurring ELAC pitch faults on an aircraft previously signed off with no faults. Maintenance replaced the Pitch Trim Actuator after a detailed review, resulting in an uneventful flight.

synopsis: When the C560-XL's FMS appeared unlikely to comply with the imminent charted 9,000 MSL crossing at EDDNA on the MAIER RNAV STAR to PHX, ATC intervened and provided vectors and altitudes to complete the arrival. The aircraft's VNAV path control had shown an occasional tendency to err on previous flights but had alternately appeared to function as intended.
summary: The non-flying pilot reported a VNAV malfunction during the MAIER FIVE arrival to PHX where the aircraft failed to descend on the computed glide path despite correct automation settings. ATC issued a new altitude and turn, and the pilot attributed the deviation to an undetermined equipment fault rather than operator error.

synopsis: A B737-NG overflying DFW 40 SM south at FL370 had 111.75 selected on the VHF radio heads and the APP MODE engaged causing a twenty five degree roll right. DFW ILS 17L/35R frequency is 111.75.
summary: Pilots en route near DFW at FL370 experienced a 25-degree right roll when the FMC switched from LNAV to APP mode without input. The cause was both VHF radios tuned to 111.75, matching the DFW ILS frequency, resulting in minimal heading deviation before correction.

synopsis: The reporter indicates that he notified company personnel that a step in the Service Bulletin procedure has not been accomplished.
summary: Maintenance personnel partially complied with an Alert Service Bulletin on three Part 135 aircraft by omitting required paint application despite log entries claiming completion. Management ignored reports of this discrepancy, returning the aircraft to service and necessitating a repeat inspection before the paint can be applied.

synopsis: CRP Controller described a loss of separation event when a military training aircraft made an unanticipated turn for a TACAN Approach arc, the reporter indicating the military does not hold the training aircraft accountable.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managed a BE20 and T34 during approach procedures when the BE20 deviated eastbound from the RYNOL fix instead of joining the arc westbound. This uncoordinated deviation caused a 2.98 NM separation loss, which the controller mitigated by climbing the T34 to 3,000 feet and issuing a heading change the BE20 pilot ignored.

synopsis: Tower Ground Controller described an emergency event when Local Control cleared an aircraft off a parallel runway with emergency equipment trying to get to the emergency aircraft followed by complete confusion regarding vehicle runway clearance reports.
summary: Ground Control and Local Controllers managed an Alert II emergency for an air carrier landing on Runway 24R with a burning smell. An ARFF vehicle entered Runway 24L without clearance while a departing aircraft began its takeoff roll, causing a potential runway incursion due to continued departures during the emergency response.

synopsis: ATL Controller described a probable ground conflict event when traffic was permitted to land, uncertain that the previous landing was in fact totally clear of the runway, the reporter critical of the 'make it work' philosophy that reportedly exists in the Tower.
summary: Local Control-1 instructed a C501 to turn around on the runway while an A320 was on final, causing a near collision as the A300 landed. The reporter attributes the incident to a lack of space for the GA jet's turn and a controller culture that discourages timely go-arounds.

synopsis: ZOB Controller described a loss of separation event when failing to note conflicting traffic prior to issuing a descent. The reporter stated the TCAS RA resolution provided compounded the conflict.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller in Sector 68 lost separation between an E170 at FL320 and an A320 at FL330 due to delayed instruction reception and conflicting TCAS Resolution Advisories. The A320 climbed into the E170's path after receiving a climb RA, resulting in a loss of separation on the next radar update.

synopsis: ZFW Controller described an airspace infraction when an adjacent sector refused a hand off, claiming separation was not yet established between two aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller in the DAL HI sector reported that BILEE HI initially refused a handoff of a Challenger 300 descending to FL280 due to perceived separation issues with a B737 at FL330. The controller stated this refusal caused a distraction and risked deviation, noting that BILEE HI eventually accepted the handoff after the Challenger was cleared below the B737.

synopsis: MCI Controller described his/her first session with FUSION RADAR and noted the difficulty and unfamiliarity with the characteristics especially reference turn on vector assignments. Reporter suggested additional training be provided.
summary: An air traffic controller struggled with the FUSION display during a busy arrival phase, causing separation issues and requiring aircraft to break off final approach. The controller attributed the incident to an inability to interpret the FUSION presentation compared to STARS, noting a lack of adequate training on the system's differences.

synopsis: S46 Controller providing OJT described a below MVA event listing multiple distractions as contributing factors.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller and a Developmental Controller issued incorrect missed approach instructions to a C172, causing the pilot to turn westbound into a 4,000-foot MVA while IMC. The controller diverted attention to other traffic, allowing the aircraft to enter higher terrain before issuing an immediate climb and vectoring it to lower altitudes.

synopsis: ZMA Controller experienced a loss of separation event when departure traffic from both PBI and MIA TRACON's conflicted with no time to issue separation vectors. The reporter suggested alternate procedures.
summary: Miami Approach's late hand-off of an LJ31 FXE departure caused a loss of lateral separation with a BE40 BCT departure. The controller stopped the BE40 at 10,000 feet and turned the LJ31 left to 290 degrees as the LJ31 climbed through 10,800 feet.

aircraft: Challenger Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: ZNY Controller described an airspace incursion claiming that the TMU failed to correct a bad routing that led to the event.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a Challenger entered Sector 73 without coordination due to an uncorrected bad routing from TMU. The controller attributed the error to TMU's failure to catch invalid routes despite previous studies identifying the problem.

synopsis: Tower Controller voiced concern regarding the behavior of one of the locally based CFI's and stated the CFI frequently questions ATC directions.
summary: An air traffic controller lost composure on frequency after a C172 pilot failed to comply with instructions to avoid a near mid-air collision with a C152 during a single-runway configuration. The controller attributes the incident to the pilot's repeated non-compliance and editorializing, and intends to refuse future service to this individual.

synopsis: ZLC Controller described a failed communications attempt with GPI Tower by an IFR inbound on the LOC Approach. The reporter was unable to explain the failed communications.
summary: An Air Carrier landing on Runway 2 at Glacier Park International Airport landed without Tower clearance after Tower failed to respond on 124.55 or via telephone. The pilot cancelled IFR with Center, and Tower later confirmed the arrival was safe despite the communication failure.

synopsis: B737-700 encountered wake vortex departing LAS that caused a deviation from the departure track.
summary: Pilots on a COWBY 4 departure encountered severe jet wash over RBELL, causing a 30-degree left bank while the autopilot failed to correct the course. The deviation resulted from simultaneous radio congestion and turbulence, leading the crew to manually correct the heading and proceed to ROPPR without TCAS alerts.

synopsis: B737-700 First Officer reports being cleared via the CADIT 6 RNAV via PDC but on Runway 8L the crew is cleared by the Tower to turn left to 070 at the middle marker. The crew is not able to identify the middle marker and is instructed to turn by the Tower.
summary: The flight crew departing Runway 8R at ATL on the CADIT SIX departure could not hear or see the middle marker indications. The crew criticized the procedure's reliance on "best judgment" and the potential delay in tuning radios as unacceptable for a congested airport.

synopsis: A B737-700's left engine failed during climbout with a loud bang, so an emergency was declared, the Checklist completed and the flight returned to land overweight.
summary: During departure at 5,000 feet, the crew experienced a loud bang and Number 1 engine failure, followed by a second bang and left roll 12 miles from the airport. The pilots executed emergency checklists, aborted a restart attempt, and completed a smooth overweight single-engine landing.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: The SAN POGGI TWO RNAV requires PGY NAVAID to be operational if an aircraft is non-GPS equipped, but a crew had not seen chart note until ATC questioned their GPS capability since PGY was non-operational.
summary: The pilot of a non-GPS aircraft departing San Diego on the POGGI 2 departure initially misinterpreted conflicting chart notes regarding required navigation aids for the IPL transition. An air traffic controller questioned the routing, prompting the pilot to request and receive a radar vector to avoid a potential non-compliance with the published procedure.

synopsis: A B737-800 Master Caution Light and Master Warning HYD illuminated in cruise with the System B quantity indicating zero so the QRH was completed, an emergency declared and the flight diverted. CRM and crew coordination issues developed on final.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced a System B hydraulic failure in cruise, leading to an emergency diversion. The Captain's incorrect checklist execution and poor communication caused increased workload and flight control issues, but the First Officer managed the diversion and landing safely.

synopsis: A B757 Captain reported the control column stiff on takeoff, but binding during land which required significant force to overcome in the flare.
summary: The pilot reported stiff control column resistance during takeoff rotation and a temporary stoppage during the landing flare. Significant additional back pressure was required to free the column, allowing a normal touchdown, and the issue was logged for maintenance.

synopsis: An A300 engine VIB ECAM alerted 3.8 during climb, so after troubleshooting, considering the flight time ahead and the proximity to Maintenance. The flight crew declared an emergency and returned to the departure airport.
summary: During climbout, the crew received a left engine N1 vibration advisory of 3.8 units and declared an emergency to return due to the abnormal indication and high landing weight. They performed an overweight landing with increased airframe vibration on descent, and the APU failed to start both in flight and on the ground.

synopsis: EMB170 Captain describes a TCAS target climbing towards his aircraft after having received a descent clearance. When ATC is questioned they reply that there is no target at that location and altitude.
summary: The flight crew at FL290 observed a TCAS target climbing from below while cleared to descend, but Boston Center reported no such traffic. The crew questioned the discrepancy, and subsequent investigation revealed the aircraft does not save TCAS data, leaving the cause of the phantom target unconfirmed.

synopsis: An EMB-145 departed in icing conditions and both engine BLEED OVERTEMP warning messages appeared during climb, so an emergency was declared. The QRH was completed and the flight returned to the departure airport for an overweight landing.
summary: The Captain, returning from medical leave, experienced dual bleed overtemperature warnings shortly after takeoff due to anti-ice system issues. The crew declared an emergency, held to manage engine temperatures, and executed a safe overweight landing to prevent catastrophic engine damage.

synopsis: A BE-400 Master Caution light illuminated along with the Right Thrust Reverser Arm and Unlock lights so the checklist was completed and the engine was shutdown during descent to preclude full deployment.
summary: During descent, a pilot and co-pilot experienced a Master Warning followed by Right Thrust Reverser Arm and Unlock lights. They shut down the right engine as a preventive measure and completed a successful single-engine visual approach and landing.

synopsis: A MD-83's right engine failed to maintain takeoff EPR, so the Captain rejected the takeoff but failed to extend the spoilers on an older model aircraft without autospoiler/autobrakes.
summary: The pilot flying rejected takeoff at 90 knots on an MD-80 due to a right engine EPR failure and lagging acceleration. Although the Captain deployed reversers, speed brakes were not manually extended because the rapid deceleration left no time to stow reversers and deploy spoilers before exiting the runway.

synopsis: An aircraft with RAAS alerted ON TAXIWAY during takeoff on a runway overrun suitable for takeoff, but not landing so the Captain initiated a slow speed reject but ignored the warning on the subsequent takeoff.
summary: The crew received an 'on taxiway' alert at 25 knots during takeoff, rejected, and later continued after a second alert. An ACARS message regarding a crew member caused significant distraction and safety concerns throughout the flight due to fears for family members.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reports descending early during arrival into SKBO in VMC due to misunderstanding what the First Officer read back to the Controller. An EGPWS warning is triggered. The First Officer was on his second trip after IOE and was having difficulty with foreign accents.
summary: The Pilot Flying descended early due to miscommunication with a task-saturated new First Officer, triggering an EGPWS warning while approaching the BOG VOR. The crew maintained visual terrain clearance and continued the approach, attributing the incident to scheduling a novice crew member for a challenging international trip.

synopsis: A310 Captain reported problem with slats 1 and 2 that became 'stuck' when extended for landing. Procedure provided no relief and flight landed uneventfully.
summary: The pilot reported that slats 1 and 2 stuck upon lowering, and recycling the Slat Flap Lever failed to resolve the issue. The crew extended the red tabs and landed the aircraft uneventfully.

synopsis: CRJ700 flight crew experiences a number two generator off message during a visual approach and elects to continue. The First Officer is asked to review the QRH and inadvertently turns off the number one generator while attempting to comply with the reset procedure causing the ADG to deploy. The APU is started and the flight continues to a normal landing.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway XR, the First Officer accidentally switched GEN 1 OFF instead of GEN 2 while running the QRH, causing the ADG to deploy. The Captain continued the landing safely, attributing the error to the First Officer's distraction and a lack of a "confirm and off" step in the checklist.

synopsis: Air Carrier departure from FLO experienced a conflict with a helicopter, both aircraft were advised of one another but ATC failed to hear an incorrect read back by the helicopter resulting in the conflict.
summary: During takeoff from Runway 19 at FLO, a helicopter turned left into the aircraft's path, requiring the pilot to maneuver to avoid a collision within a few hundred feet. The reporter attributed the incident to a takeoff clearance issued with traffic in the departure corridor and the controller's failure to correct the helicopter's erroneous readback.

synopsis: A Maintenance Technician overlooked the note in the Structural Repair Manual and deferred damage that required Boeing approval. At some point later this information he was advised of this information and the aircraft was repaired.
summary: A line mechanic deferred a fuzzy aileron trailing edge and released the aircraft after overlooking a critical area note in the Structural Repair Manual. The damage was later found to be within the critical area, requiring Boeing contact, due to the mechanic focusing only on the allowable damage table.

synopsis: P180 First Officer reported engine fire warning for right engine. Crew declared an emergency, shut down the engine and diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: During initial descent, the crew declared an emergency after an 'Engine Fire' warning for the right engine, shut down the engine, and deployed the extinguisher. They diverted to a suitable airport, flew a VOR approach near minimums, and evacuated the aircraft upon landing.

aircraft: Light Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Flight crew observed a 'Baggage Door' warning after takeoff, secured the left engine as per the QRH and returned to land.
summary: The flight crew experienced a false 'Baggage Door' master warning shortly after rotation, prompting an emergency return and left engine shutdown per the QRH. Post-landing inspection confirmed the false indication, noting the aircraft had a history of this specific discrepancy.

synopsis: G450 First Officer reports overshooting the 1,500 FT initial level off altitude on the RUUDY4 departure from TEB. The autopilot was engaged at 900 FT and was unable to make to make the level off precisely.
summary: The pilot departed TEB Runway 24 on the RUUDY4 departure and engaged the autopilot at 900 FT to level at the WENTZ 1,500 FT restriction. The autopilot overshot the altitude by 100 FT, requiring manual correction, which the pilot attributed to over-reliance on expected autopilot performance.

synopsis: A BE-18 tail wheel became unlocked in flight, so that after landing the pilot lost control of the aircraft and both wing tips struck the ground while he recovered.
summary: The pilot experienced a left tail swing after touchdown that could not be corrected with differential power or braking, forcing a go-around. During the second landing, both wing tips struck the ground due to the continued lack of directional control.

synopsis: Small aircraft pilot reported an NMAC in the pattern at MRI when another aircraft deviated from his clearance.
summary: The pilot reported a traffic conflict in the Runway 25 left traffic pattern when upwind traffic turned early to crosswind. This deviation caused both pilots to take immediate avoidance action, which would not have been necessary had the other aircraft maintained proper spacing.

synopsis: Small aircraft instructor pilot reported an NMAC with another small aircraft in the pattern at MRI.
summary: A student pilot and instructor flying a training aircraft on final approach to Merrill Field Runway 7 experienced a near mid-air collision with another aircraft that ignored instructions to follow behind. The other pilot, reportedly distracted by a military aircraft, intercepted their path at 250 feet separation, forcing an immediate evasive dive to avoid impact.

synopsis: A J3 ATP rated pilot under instruction with an instructor lost control of the aircraft, ran off the runway and gently struck and broke a PAPI light which caused propeller damage.
summary: During a tailwheel training landing in a Piper J3 Cub, the student pilot and instructor experienced a ground loop on the runway due to excessive drift and loose tailwheel steering linkage. The aircraft struck a PAPI light with the propeller, causing minor damage, which the instructor attributed primarily to pilot error in recognizing lateral limits.

synopsis: SR22 pilot reports inadvertently entering a TFR for a sports event. DET Tower had issued an advisory prior to TFR entry then issued instructions to exit quickly. The TFR was not included in the preflight briefing and did not show up on the moving map display.
summary: A pilot conducting a sightseeing flight inadvertently entered a TFR over Ford Field while transitioning Detroit Class D airspace because the restriction was missing from the flight briefing, ATIS, and Avdyne moving map. Detroit Tower detected the intrusion and instructed the pilot to turn west and northwest to exit the TFR.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot of a small aircraft attributed a runway incursion to failure of the geo-referenced, tablet display he was using for taxi.
summary: The pilot's tablet locked up after taxi clearance, causing distraction that led to a hold-short line violation and a missed clearance readback. The pilot attributed the error to over-reliance on the new device and a lack of backup planning, though no incident occurred.

synopsis: AUS Controller described an airspace incursion event in a complex corner of airspace abutting both Center and IAH TRACON airspace. The reporter listed the failure of the automated hand off function as contributory to the problem.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a Cessna Centurion en route to DRT failed to automatically hand off to ZCH due to suspected radar automation issues in a specific airspace corner. The controller manually re-routed the aircraft and coordinated with SAT and ZCH, recommending equipment upgrades to resolve the recurring handoff failures.

synopsis: ZOB Controller described some confusion encountered when 'contingency' plans were not reviewed and/or followed during an ATC ZERO event by an adjacent facility. Reporter also questioned the Supervisor's operational knowledge base.
summary: Air Traffic Controllers reported that a Supervisor assumed Johnstown Approach airspace during an ATC ZERO event without verifying critical details like ATIS codes or VFR tower status. The Supervisor neglected contingency checklists and dismissed the need for specific information, leading to concerns about his operational knowledge and decision-making abilities.

synopsis: An RNAV equipped air carrier flight crew was uncertain whether their clearance direct to BSV, cleared for the Runway 1 ILS to CAK required them to fly a course reversal at BSV. ATC was unresponsive to their request for clarification and they opted not to fly the reversal. They then descended from the 3,000 FT MEA from BSV to BULIT prior to being 'established' on the Localizer per the Tower Controller.
summary: Pilots descending into Akron (CAK) experienced confusion after being cleared direct BSV for the ILS 1 approach without explicit instructions on the course reversal. The crew descended below the assigned 3,100 feet while attempting to resolve the clearance ambiguity, prompting Tower alerts to maintain 3,000 feet before they intercepted the glideslope and landed.

synopsis: A B737-300 First Officer became distracted with takeoff performance calculations during engine start and failed to detect and stop an engine overtemp on start so the aircraft returned to the gate for maintenance.
summary: During pushback, the First Officer experienced task overload while managing engine start and runway changes, causing an Engine 2 EGT exceedance of 749 degrees. The Captain aborted the start, leading to a 30-minute delay for maintenance, attributed to analog gauge limitations and distraction from radio duties.

synopsis: B757-200 flight crew reported they struck a large bird or birds, possibly Canadian geese, while climbing through 15,000 feet. With indeterminate damage to nose and right engine, they declared an emergency and returned to departure airport.
summary: The pilot reported a severe bird strike by Canadian Snow Geese at 15,000 feet, causing substantial damage to the nose, right engine, and systems, leading to an emergency return. Post-flight inspection confirmed blade separation and compressor stalls, with the pilot noting the impact occurred just below the cockpit window.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported effective loss of Number 2 engine when the thrust lever was driven to idle by a 'Thrust Lever Position Disagree' fault during the approach.
summary: The pilot reported a 'Thrust lever position disagree' fault during ILS intercept that caused thrust to idle with slats extended, degrading the aircraft to single-engine operation. The crew landed uneventfully with Engine Number 2 at idle, following all applicable procedures.

synopsis: Air carrier arrival to ORD voiced concern regarding the ATC handling reference speed assignments and transfer of communication instructions.
summary: The flight crew approached ORD on an ILS 27L, executing a go-around due to excessive speed and a loss of separation caused by conflicting speed instructions and premature frequency switching. The pilot attributed the incident to unclear ATC handoff procedures and misleading company publications regarding when to contact Tower.

synopsis: Both B737-800 pilots simultaneously used the oxygen system on preflight, as per a new company procedure, and found very low mask pressure, so a maintenance check found the crew oxygen bottle valve nearly closed.
summary: During pre-flight on a Boeing 737, simultaneous oxygen checks by the crew revealed a pressure drop from 1,500 to 300 PSI caused by a closed oxygen valve. Maintenance opened the valve, restoring normal pressure, though the reporter noted a potential catastrophic outcome if oxygen had been required.

synopsis: A MD11 Captain rejected the takeoff at 60 KTS when the Master Caution alerted Pitot and AOA heater failures.
summary: The Captain rejected takeoff at 60 KTS on Runway 16R after simultaneous Pitot and AOA heat failures triggered a Master Caution. Maintenance replaced the MSC Controller, allowing a successful second takeoff to the destination.

synopsis: A B767-300 Air Data Computer and Mode Control Panel both malfunctioned after a heavy maintenance check and the aircraft did not level at an intermediate altitude on the SID.
summary: During a ferry flight climb after heavy maintenance, the crew overshot a 7,000 FT clearance to 7,300 FT due to an Air Data Computer failure and a faulty Mode Control Panel altitude window. The autopilot failed to level the aircraft, requiring manual intervention to descend back to the assigned altitude before a safe return landing.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot departing SQL reports inadvertently entering a TFR over a football stadium. The TFR did not appear in a DUAT's briefing and did not show up on the Garmin 696 with XM Radio in-flight TFR display.
summary: The pilot departed San Carlos and likely violated a Stanford Stadium TFR at 2,000 feet because the restriction was absent from DUATS briefings, ATIS, and Garmin 696 displays. NorCal TRACON advised vectors to clear the area, prompting the pilot to acknowledge that relying solely on standard FAA sources was insufficient for sporting event TFRs.

synopsis: A BE36 autopilot and COM1 malfunctioned in flight where the pilot momentarily lost control in weather, near his destination, but was able to contact ATC on COMM2 and fly an ILS.
summary: A pilot flying IFR at 5,000 feet experienced an autopilot malfunction in heavy IMC and turbulence, causing the aircraft to deviate and dive. After regaining control, the pilot lost radio contact with ATC for 11 minutes before re-establishing communication, completing an ILS approach, and landing safely.

synopsis: C90 Controller described a very complex traffic period with an extreme crosswind factor and the potential for multiple go-arounds. The reporter was very frustrated with this on-going problem.
summary: An air traffic controller reported unsafe conditions at ORD during a west flow C90 operation with 36-knot crosswinds after a hurricane. The controller criticized the reactive runway configuration change process, which delayed action until pilot refusals occurred, resulting in congested airspace and a near-miss on Runway 32R.

synopsis: A B767-300 EICAS alerted L ENG ANALOG N2 and L ENG CONTROL, then high oil temperature and low oil pressure lead the crew to shut the engine down, declare an emergency, and return to the departure airport.
summary: During departure at 7,000 feet, the crew experienced a left engine surge followed by EICAS messages and oil pressure/temperature anomalies. They declared an emergency, returned to land, and secured the left engine for five minutes before taxiing to the ramp without further issues.

synopsis: A B757 outflow valve failed to regulate pressurization at FL380 so after the EICAS alerted CABIN ALTITUDE the crew declared an emergency, descended to 10,000 feet, and returned to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a cabin altitude warning at FL380 due to a malfunctioning outflow valve that failed to modulate or close. After descending to 10,000 feet to lower cabin altitude, they returned to the departure airport for a precautionary landing without deploying passenger oxygen.

aircraft: Embraer Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer discovers via BUF ATIS that coupled approaches to Runway 5 are not authorized. During the hand flown approach irregularities in the LOC are noted. Upon breaking out at 400 feet the localizer indicates the aircraft is to the right of centerline but in fact the aircraft is 100 feet to the left of centerline.
summary: The crew flew an ILS Runway 5 approach into Buffalo while the localizer signal was intermittent and inaccurate, causing a significant deviation from the centerline at 400 feet. The pilot attributed the unsafe conditions to a known but un-Notam'd equipment issue and a failure to select the available Runway 32 approach.

synopsis: An EMB-145 EICAS alerted LOW HYD LEVEL 2 at cruise so crew briefed emergency procedures in advance of the arrival and when the quantity indicated zero, declared an emergency and completed the approach well prepared for any eventuality.
summary: The crew managed a Hydraulic System 2 failure during cruise and approach after fluid quantity dropped to zero, causing total pressure loss. They declared an emergency, landed safely, and taxied to the gate, attributing the successful outcome to the Captain's proactive briefing and effective crew coordination.

synopsis: Following a double engine change for smoke in the cabin, Maintenance personnel were unaware that engines received after overhaul could require testing on-wing prior to release for service.
summary: Maintenance technicians replaced both engines on an aircraft at 20,000 FT due to smoke caused by faulty #2 carbon seals. The newly installed left engine failed to reach takeoff power due to temperature limiting, requiring a second replacement because the manufacturer shipped the engines without performing required ground performance runs.

synopsis: A PC-12 engine was malfunctioning after takeoff so the pilot declared an emergency and returned to the departure airport for maintenance.
summary: The pilot declared an emergency during climb-out due to a rough-running engine and returned to the departure airport. After turning 180 degrees to join right downwind, the aircraft landed safely without incident, and maintenance is currently evaluating the suspected mechanical trouble.

synopsis: A SA-226 pilot reported discovering a fractured outboard main landing gear drag link after the right main landing gear warning light illuminated at the gate.
summary: The pilot landed a freight aircraft in snowy conditions and later discovered the right main gear outboard drag link had sheared. The missing part was found 3,000 feet down the runway, and further damage was identified inside the gear well.

synopsis: Falcon flight crew experiences confusion at SFO after receiving instructions to taxi via Taxiways C, Z, and B. A turn is initiated at C1 and a runway incursion results at the approach end of Runway 10L.
summary: Pilots at SFO confused taxiway signage while taxiing to Runway 01L, causing them to inadvertently cross the departure end of Runway 28R. The incident resulted from a lack of signs indicating the transition from Taxiway Charlie to Zulu, leading the crew to rely solely on heading indicators.

synopsis: A PA-31T engine malfunctioned at 300 FT after takeoff so the engine was feathered but the flight continued to cruise altitude and diverted to the crew's home base where a broken throttle cable was found.
summary: The pilot reported a left engine torque loss at 300 feet AGL during takeoff, caused by a broken throttle cable. After a failed air restart, the crew diverted to their home airport, landing safely on one engine while maintaining 185 knots ground speed.

synopsis: SCT Controller described a below MVA event when ONT Tower failed to transfer radio communication on a departure as requested.
summary: An Air Carrier X pilot climbing to 4,000 feet near ONT entered a 5,300-foot MVA due to delayed communication transfers and an initial right turn instruction. The controller corrected the error by issuing a left turn and immediate climb after the aircraft passed the turn point.

synopsis: IAD Controller described a probable loss of separation incident likely involving multiple events, the reporter detailing a number of suggestion to resolve some existing confusion and noting the continued erosion of experience levels at ATC facilities.
summary: PCT and IAD Tower controllers lost separation between a Piper PA34 and Embraer 145 departing IAD Runway 30 due to uncoordinated non-RADAR release of a P180 from JYO. The incident resulted from failure to block airspace, ambiguous "control for turns" communication, and conflicting heading assignments violating the LOA.

synopsis: Air Carrier holding well clear of Runway 12L for departure observed an aircraft on final issued go around instructions by ATC because of an occupied runway alarm.
summary: A Boeing 737 crew held short of Runway 12L at Hobby Airport, but faulty ground sensors falsely indicated runway encroachment. This caused Tower to order a landing twin to go around, though the crew was subsequently cleared to taxi and take off after the controller acknowledged the equipment error.

synopsis: A320 Captain experiences lost communication on departure due to a stuck mic that is annunciated by ECAM as 'VHF1 EMITTING'. The problem transfers to VHF2 when that radio is selected and eventually clears on its' own.
summary: The flight crew experienced simultaneous VHF1 and VHF2 emitting failures just after takeoff, resulting in a total loss of communication. They squawked 7600, used a third radio on 121.5, and followed QRH procedures until the radios recovered at level-off.

synopsis: A Q400 crew was notified their flight's pressurization malfunction and CABIN PRESSURE Warning may have resulted because circuit breakers were popped prior to or during preflight and went undetected.
summary: The flight crew experienced a cabin pressure warning at 12,000 feet during climb, prompting a descent to 8,000 feet and a normal landing at the filed destination. The cause was a pressurization malfunction, possibly due to popped circuit breakers that may have existed before departure or occurred in flight, though the reporter did not personally observe them.

synopsis: Experimental aircraft instructor with student on first flight for both experiences aileron binding shortly after takeoff and elects to return for a precautionary landing. During the landing flare the aircraft is stalled just above the runway causing damage to the left main gear.
summary: An instructor and student in an experimental Mustang II experienced stiff ailerons and low airspeed ten minutes after takeoff, likely due to a mechanical binding. They returned to the airport but inadvertently stalled on final approach, striking the left gear and causing damage.

synopsis: A VEZE nose gear collapsed on touchdown because the worm gear extension teeth were stripped.
summary: The pilot of a canard pusher experimental aircraft reported a nose gear collapse on touchdown caused by a stripped hand-cranked worm gear. The pilot shut down the engine, coordinated with ATC to clear the runway, and pushed the aircraft to the hangar.

synopsis: A CE-560 pilot reported a wake vortex encounter inbound to LAS 8 miles in trail of a widebody aircraft that resulted in a 50 degree roll.
summary: The flight crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding widebody transport while descending from 12,000 to 8,000 feet on the TYSSN 3 arrival to LAS. The upset caused a 50-degree bank with autopilot engaged, prompting TRACON to level the aircraft at 9,000 feet before a visual approach to Runway 19R was completed without further incident.

synopsis: An MD-88 Captain, new to the airplane, had difficulty programming the FMS for a change in their arrival clearance to ATL and a track deviation resulted.
summary: The pilot flying on an MD-88 during the HONIE 8 arrival drifted right of course while reprogramming the FMS for a runway change and ILS PRM approach. The delay was caused by the aircraft's slow FMS processing speed and the pilot's developing familiarity with the system, though no traffic conflict occurred.

synopsis: After having been previously cleared to cross BRNDN waypoint on the GIBBZ RNAV STAR at FL270 vice the published FL290, the Flight Crew of a Falcon 900 were cleared to 'descend via' the STAR and were uncertain if that clearance required them to climb back up to FL290 to comply with the charted crossing.
summary: The crew descended below the published FL290 crossing restriction at BRNDN while executing a "Direct BRNDN" clearance before receiving a "Descend via" instruction. The pilot attributed the confusion to ambiguous STAR coding and FMS logic, ultimately crossing at the previously cleared FL270 without traffic conflict.

synopsis: A King Air (BE-9T) high pressure fuel pump failed in cruise so the pilot feathered the engine and diverted to an airport with long runways and emergency equipment.
summary: A pilot returning from simulator training experienced a right-hand engine high-pressure fuel pump failure in cruise. The pilot secured the engine, changed destination to an airport with longer runways, and landed uneventfully after ATC declared an emergency.

synopsis: OAK Tower Controller described a failed coordination event that resulted with a construction crane being raised near the final for Runway 27R requiring a landing aircraft to maneuver on short final.
summary: Tower controllers failed to notice a construction crane blocking the final approach for Runway 27R because it was erected early and blended into the background. A jet had to maneuver around the obstruction due to incorrect NOTAM timing and poor communication between the construction crew, Airport Authority, and Tower Management.

synopsis: D10 Departure Controller described a conflict event reportedly resulting from the flight crew confusing the ATC facility name 'Regional Departure' with a 'resume departure' instructions.
summary: An A319 pilot departing DAL misinterpreted the controller's "Regional Departure" identification as a clearance to "resume departure," causing a deviation that required immediate corrective turns and level-offs. The pilot attributed the error to a language issue and failure to read back the clearance, while the controller noted the facility name frequently causes this confusion.

synopsis: CHS Controller described a conflict event when indicating to a visual approach aircraft to 'maneuver as necessary' due to altitude resulting in a conflict with a succeeding aircraft
summary: An OJTI on West RADAR intervened when a trainee's non-directive clearance caused Aircraft X to turn outbound, creating a conflict with Aircraft Y descending on final. The OJTI attributed the incident to the trainee's task saturation and the failure to provide specific maneuvering instructions.

synopsis: A CRJ-701 EICAS alerted 'SLATS FAIL' during the initial flap extensions for landing so the QRH procedure was complete and the landing accomplished slats zero, flaps 45.
summary: During arrival at 6,000 feet, the crew received a 'Slats Fail' caution after selecting Flaps 8, leaving slats at 0. They followed QRH procedures to land safely with Flaps 45, requested ARFF as a precaution, and taxied to the gate with flaps extended per maintenance instructions.

synopsis: During a windshear go around in turbulence and heavy rain, an A319 engine failed so the flight diverted to a nearby airport but ATC vectored the aircraft too close and another go around was executed before landing.
summary: During an A319 go-around for windshear, Engine 2 went idle and autothrust failed, causing a diversion and emergency landing. The crew suspects an electrical reset issue, noting a passenger later reported arm numbness upon deplaning.

synopsis: An ECD-EC135 helicopter compass precessed nearly ninety degrees while parked on a hospital roof for 27 minutes but because this particular aircraft had no compass slew installed to correct the heading error, the aircraft was rendered non-IFR capable.
summary: A pilot reported severe HSI precession on a helicopter parked on a hospital roof, likely caused by rooftop turbines rather than MRI equipment. The aircraft lacks a synchronization panel to manually correct the gyro, rendering the HSI useless and compromising IFR capability and safety.

synopsis: After the landing gear was extended and Flaps 20 set, a B757 EICAS alerted L HYD SYS PRESS and associated system failures were displayed so the crew continued the approach to a normal landing but requested ARFF assistance to the gate.
summary: The First Officer flew a Boeing 757 on short final when a left hydraulic system failure occurred, causing loss of nose wheel steering. The crew completed a normal landing, declared an emergency, and were towed to the gate with an ARFF escort after inspecting hydraulic fluid leakage.

synopsis: A MD-83 Fuel Low Light illuminated at FL320, but without a departure station fuel slip the crew was uncertain about the quantity indicated so an emergency was declared and the flight diverted for fuel and maintenance.
summary: The crew of a DC-9 at FL320 declared an emergency after a false Fuel Low Light illuminated due to inaccurate fuel quantity indications. Maintenance confirmed the tanks held 700 LBS less than indicated, prompting a diversion and subsequent fuel system placarding before the flight resumed.

synopsis: A PA-32-350 pilot made a precautionary land after loosing power because an exhaust pipe apparently became partially separated from the engine.
summary: The pilot experienced a partial engine failure during cruise, declared an emergency, and landed at an enroute airport after descending to 11,000 feet. Post-landing inspection suggested a partially loose exhaust pipe as the likely cause, though a mechanic has not yet confirmed the issue.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: C525 Captain approaching WENTZ at 1,500 FT (RUUDY 4 from TEB) attempts to engage the autopilot without success. During this time the altitude drifts up to 1,700 FT prior to WENTZ and is corrected back to 1,500 FT, but TASCA is crossed at 1,500 FT instead of the 2,000 FT published.
summary: The pilot departing TEB on the RUUDY 3 departure could not activate the autopilot at 1,500 FT while leveling at WENTZ. This distraction caused an altitude deviation to 1,700 FT before manual correction, though the autopilot functioned normally five minutes later.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot reports lost comm during flight to M21 after being instructed to contact Campbell Approach on 118.1. Fort Campbell is too far away to be contacted and the approach chart lists Evansville Approach as the controling agency which it no longer is. A solution is suggested.
summary: An H60 helicopter pilot lost communications with Indianapolis Center and Fort Campbell Approach while descending for the M21 RNAV 24 approach due to inadequate radio range and outdated chart frequencies. The pilot continued VFR to OWB, attributing the incident to poor coordination between facilities and a lack of usable published frequencies for the approach.

synopsis: A Cessna Citation was released for service following engine work performed under less than ideal conditions. The flight crew later indicated that the right throttle would creep from the full power setting. Maintenance personnel then detected that they had inadvertently hooked the throttle input lever on the wrong side of a cable attach lever.
summary: Mechanics incorrectly installed the right engine fuel control unit input rod during night maintenance in adverse weather, causing the throttle to auto-retard on climbout. The fault was corrected per the manual, and the aircraft returned to service without recurrence.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a taxiway landing event during the sunset time frame and landing to the West, the Controller indicating difficulty in recognizing the exact aircraft location.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller issued traffic instructions to a J-3 and C172 during sunset at an XXL/R airport. The J-3 pilot misidentified Taxiway X as the runway due to an optical illusion caused by the sun and tower height, resulting in a landing on the taxiway.

synopsis: R90 Controller expressed concern regarding the limited frequency coverage with aircraft operations at CBF, the reporter recommending the installation of a RTR/RCO at CBF.
summary: Air traffic controller reported that a B350 departed uncontrolled CBF airport and climbed through Omaha Charlie airspace without establishing radio contact, triggering a Brasher warning. The controller attributed the violation to the lack of a remote RTR/RCO at CBF, a known issue for a decade.

synopsis: ZDC Controller described a loss of separation event listing the current required phraseology related to climb instructions as as contributing to this event and recommending changes to the current procedure.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a CRJ-200 climbing westbound near an A320 at FL370. The CRJ-200 failed to maintain a 1,000 FPM climb rate, prompting a left turn and descent to FL360 to avoid separation loss before being transferred to ZID.

synopsis: ZSE Controller described a confused relief effort when the relieving controller utilized the exact opposite procedure regarding data block illuminations, the reporter suggesting a common facility procedure be adopted.
summary: An air traffic controller missed a handoff and mismanaged a NORAC transfer due to conflicting data block highlighting methods with the relieving controller. The incident caused a Sector 13 call and a frequency check error, prompting a request for standardized tracking procedures and an all-aircraft dwell toggle function.

synopsis: ATL Controller described a near serious conflict event when departure traffic failed to comply with the issued route, the Controller suggesting more exaggerated turns to affect separation more quickly and be more easily identified by ATC.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller observed Air Carrier X deviating left from a straight-out RNAV departure heading due to an FMS malfunction. The controller intervened to prevent a potential mid-air collision with another aircraft, prompting the pilot to correct course immediately.

synopsis: SNA Controller voiced concern regarding the current, but ever changing, 'opposite direction procedures' and interpretation of same by SCT TRACON.
