summary: A flight attendant reported that the Captain diverted the aircraft due to a critical system alert but instructed the cabin to prepare for a normal landing, withholding the true emergency nature of the situation. This communication failure prevented proper cabin preparation despite the severity of the potential catastrophic failure.

aircraft: Embraer Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) questions why an RII Inspection is required when their Base Maintenance technicians replace an Electric Driven Hydraulic Motor Pump (EDMP) on their ERJ aircraft, but not required for an on-call Maintenance Provider Technician at an Outstation.
summary: A Company Aircraft Technician reported a discrepancy in Required Inspection Item (RII) requirements for replacing Electrical Motor Driven Hydraulic Pump brushes between Routine Overnight maintenance and AOG outstation repairs. The reporter requested adding the task to the RII list or removing it from Job Card 29-10-04 to ensure proper oversight by certified personnel.

synopsis: C172 flight instructor reports visually clearing downwind, base, and final before taking the runway at an uncontrolled airport. While preparing to takeoff a C152 flies overhead and lands in front of the reporter, then taxies clear of the runway.
summary: A pilot and student on the runway hold line were nearly struck by a radio-equipped Cessna 152 landing 500 feet ahead. The Cessna 152 was high and left of centerline, placing it above the pilot's line of sight, but the crew elected not to execute a go-around.

synopsis: When the associated hydraulic system improperly remained pressurized after landing gear retraction the flight crew of a C550 made a precautionary return and landing at their departure airport. Although they had not declared an emergency they were met by airport officials inquiring as to their well being and aircraft status. The reporter felt such efforts were unnecessary.
summary: Pilots reported a malfunctioning microswitch causing false hydraulic and gear lights shortly after takeoff, prompting a precautionary return and normal landing. The crew attributed subsequent unnecessary emergency calls by the Airport Authority to a communication breakdown regarding their status.

synopsis: BE9 pilot experiences a gradual power loss at 16,000 feet resulting in lost communications and the decision to return VFR to the departure airport. During descent electrical power is regained and Center is contacted, allowing the flight to continue to destination.
summary: The pilot experienced a gradual electrical failure at 16,000 feet, losing communications and squawking 7600 before turning back to the departure airport. Power was restored at 14,500 feet, allowing the pilot to contact Center and resume the flight to the destination.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot reports a NMAC with a large kite at 900 FT AGL in rural eastern Pennsylvania.
summary: During cruise at 1,300 feet MSL, a pilot avoided a large kite flying at 900 feet AGL after a passenger spotted it in overcast conditions. The kite passed within 50 feet of the aircraft, posing a significant hazard due to its invisible tether and automated reel system.

synopsis: ZTL Controller voiced concern regarding the continued failure of Area 4 controllers to comply with established procedures.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Hampton Sector 27 controllers descended aircraft into Macon airspace without coordination, violating the rule that sectors must coordinate before using airspace they do not own. The reporter cited repeated uncoordinated descents into their stratum as unsafe, noting that Sector 27 claimed Macon approval despite lacking proper communication.

synopsis: TRACON Controller using ARTS 11 Limited RADAR voiced concern regarding the outdated equipment, indicating this subject equipment is unsafe.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that the ARTS II radar display at a lower-level facility is unreadable and outdated, utilizing 1960s equipment. The controller stated this condition poses a safety risk and urged an immediate upgrade to prevent potential disasters.

synopsis: Enroute Supervisor described a developing head on event involving two Air Carriers and weather deviations, the reporter eventually directing the Controller to turn both aircraft saving separation.
summary: A Flight Lead Monitor intervened when Air Carrier X slowed its climb to FL366 while approaching head-on traffic at FL360, prompting the Radar Controller to issue degree turns instead of assigned headings. The incident highlighted that the Controller's pleasant tone failed to convey urgency and that weather deviations complicated climb clearances near head-on traffic.

synopsis: DAB Controller voiced concern regarding the time lag in the Fusion RADAR system, making the identification of aircraft positions less than desired.
summary: An air traffic controller at DAB reported that RADAR lag in the new Fusion system obscured Aircraft Y's turn from downwind to base leg while vectoring Aircraft X. The controller attributed this safety risk to the system's inability to display turn rates and a lack of compatible ADS-B equipment in local training aircraft.

synopsis: Local Controller approved a vehicle runway crossing of the active and then cleared an aircraft for takeoff forgetting about the vehicle crossing.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared a C172 for takeoff on Runway 31 while forgetting an authorized crossing by a Learjet due to simultaneous communications and distraction. The pilot reported the Learjet ahead, prompting the controller to cancel the clearance before the C172 began its roll.

synopsis: An air carrier Captain reported that the CLT Runway 5 ILS glide slope has significant fluctuations especially near KECKS.
summary: Pilots reported an unstable ILS glide slope for Runway 5, with deviations of up to 1.5 dots occurring near KECKS. The reporter attributed the issue to equipment instability rather than interference, noting no vehicles or aircraft were operating on parallel runways.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A Dash 8 Captain provided a lengthy description of a long and physically debilitating day on the job which he believed rendered him unfit to fly the next day due to fatigue. He expanded his comments to address attempts by his managers to intimidate him into not doing so.
summary: A Dash-8 crew experienced multiple delays, a malfunctioning PTT switch, and an in-flight windshield smoke emergency caused by burned heating wires, leading to a diversion and extended maintenance wait. The Captain subsequently called in fatigued due to the cumulative stress and lack of company support, citing a need for better fatigue recognition programs.

synopsis: A C208 pilot returned to his departure airport when the engine oil pressure dropped into the yellow after takeoff.
summary: The pilot reported abnormal oil pressure indications in the yellow range at 1,000 feet AGL during climb after takeoff. The aircraft was vectored back by Departure for a safe landing, with the gauge remaining in the yellow through taxi to the ramp.

synopsis: EMB-120 Captain on a ferry flight declared an emergency shortly after takeoff and returned to departure airport after experiencing abnormal flight control response that may have been related to previous ground damage.
summary: The pilot flying an EMB-120 ferry flight after a ground strike and wingtip replacement encountered severe control difficulties and excessive yaw forces during climb. Lacking a briefing on expected abnormal handling characteristics from maintenance, the crew declared an emergency and returned to the origin airport for a safe landing.

synopsis: An A321 Flight Attendant crew reported a foul smelling odor and, after consulting with Maintenance, the #2 pack was secured. Then the flight descended to 10,000 feet and with both Packs OFF finally diverted to a nearby airport, where the flight attendants sought medical treatment.
summary: During climb, foul odors prompted the crew to secure the #2 pack, divert, descend to 10,000 feet, and secure the #1 pack while opening the ram air valve. The aircraft landed safely, but four flight attendants sought medical attention, with one ending her trip due to symptoms.

synopsis: EMB-145 continued approach to landing after observing a Cessna aircraft come to a stop past the hold-short line of an intersecting taxiway on the same runway.
summary: A pilot on final approach to Runway XXR observed a Cessna taxiing past the hold short line due to radio confusion regarding takeoff clearance. Although the Cessna stopped 15-20 feet from the runway, the pilot landed but later regretted not executing a go-around.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reports a loud noise and vibration from the nose gear as it is being raised after takeoff. A 'STEERING INOPERABLE' caution is annunciated and is cleared using QRH procedures. During approach at the destination airport, the caution reappears when the gear is extended and cannot be cleared. A go-around is initiated followed by an uneventful landing with a tow to the gate.
summary: The flight crew experienced a recurring 'STEERING INOPERABLE' caution during gear extension on departure and approach, causing a go-around and emergency declaration. After landing on the long runway, ground steering reset attempts failed, requiring the aircraft to be towed in.

synopsis: When the outer pane of First Officer's windshield shattered as they were at FL230 on their way to FL390 the flight crew of a B737-700 elected to return to their departure airport for maintenance and a fresh jet.
summary: During climb at FL230, the First Officer's forward windscreen shattered near the heating element electrical lead, likely due to an internal failure rather than impact. The crew deemed the aircraft un-airworthy despite QRH guidance and diverted to the departure airport, where passengers were transferred to another aircraft.

synopsis: While on a visual approach to Runway 2R at PDK a C560XL flight crew received and complied with an EGPWS obstacle warning.
summary: During a visual approach to PDK Runway 2R, the crew received a GPWS 'Obstacle' warning while inside southern towers. They climbed to extinguish the warning, executed a missed approach, and subsequently completed a normal landing on Runway 2R, though the cause of the warning remained unknown.

synopsis: When their stabilizer electric trim failed at cruise the flight crew of a B737-800 completed the associated QRH procedures and landed at their destination utilizing flaps 15 and manual control of the stabilizer trim.
summary: During cruise, the crew encountered an unresponsive electric stabilizer trim after the 'Stab Out of Trim' light illuminated. They declared an emergency, used the manual trim wheel per the checklist, and completed an uneventful Flaps 15 landing.

synopsis: MD11 Relief First Officer attributed landing without clearance to flight crew's fixation on stabilizing the approach.
summary: The Reserve First Officer observed a hand-flown ILS approach where the Captain was initially high and fast, causing crew fixation on stability and task saturation. This distraction led to uncertainty about whether landing clearance was received, though the landing was uneventful.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot reports NMAC with a light twin during landing at GLS. The light twin pilot reportedly was not using the CTAF and saw the helicopter ahead and elected to expedite his approach and land under the helicopter.
summary: During a Part 91 flight check at GLS, a helicopter on short final to Runway 35 encountered a Mexican-registered multi-engine aircraft taxiing on the runway at 50 FT AGL. The collision was avoided because the other pilot, rushing for a patient transport, failed to monitor the correct CTAF frequency and landed behind the helicopter without hearing its position reports.

synopsis: BH 206 instructor pilot reported NMAC with a light aircraft in the pattern at DTO.
summary: During a training GPS/RNAV 18 approach at DTO, a CFII in a helicopter lost sight of a higher Cessna due to clutter, creating a collision course. The pilot executed evasive deceleration at 1,000 feet AGL to achieve 300 feet separation, noting that late Tower instructions to break off were ineffective.

synopsis: The reporter indicated that even with the 100 flight hour periodic inspections, the rivet had failed since the last check.
summary: A mechanic removed both magnetos for scheduled replacement and discovered a sheared rivet head from the left magneto's impulse coupling inside the engine accessory case. The broken part was found in the scavenge oil sump with no engine damage, prompting a recommendation to mandate replacing all riveted couplings due to potential failure despite passing inspections.

synopsis: PCT Controller experienced a loss of separation event when failing to note the incorrect runway assignment scratchpad information in the data block.
summary: An IAD Final Approach Controller lost separation between a CRJ-900 and a GLF2 due to conflicting scratchpad runway information and a failure to issue visual separation instructions. The controller amended the CRJ-900's heading to follow the GLF2 but lacked the required 45-degree divergence, resulting in a separation loss.

synopsis: ZBW Controller voiced concern regarding the lack of training received reference ATC Zero events, noting the lack of check lists and/or requirements.
summary: The Controller In Charge managed Sectors 15 and 16 after Bangor Approach lost all radar, reverting to VFR tower capabilities. While monitoring three arrivals, the reporter observed a Citation Mustang turning too closely into a lead King Air, noting a lack of specific training or checklists for such ATC Zero events.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described an emergency event when the aircraft in question lost instrumentation need for flight.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored a PA-28 and C172 near the OMN VOR when the PA-28 pilot declared a Mayday due to a failed turn coordinator. The controller provided emergency separation and vectoring until the PA-28 stabilized VFR on top at 3,500 feet.

synopsis: After being cleared comply with a crossing restriction below the transition altitude on descent, the flight crew of a CRJ-700 determined they would be unable to comply and were recleared to maintain FL180. Because the flying pilot had already set his altimeter to the local pressure setting they initially leveled several hundred feet low.
summary: The Captain prematurely changed the altimeter setting while descending on the PASLY RNAV STAR into BNA, causing the aircraft to be 300 feet low. This occurred because the crew anticipated crossing the transition altitude instead of following the checklist, though ATC subsequently issued a lower clearance.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 Captain reported his continued concerns regarding the complexity of Optimized Descent Profiles into MEM and contributed a proposed flight crew do's and don'ts checklist to simplify compliance.
summary: A flight crew flying the LTOWN RNAV STAR into Memphis struggled with the complex Optimized Descent Profile due to infrequent practice, cluttered charts, and distracting VNAV guidance. The pilot reported that the procedure was labor-intensive and recommended a specific checklist to ensure future compliance and safety.

synopsis: UH60 flight crew experienced two altitude excursions after disconnecting the stabilator from the auto mode due to a Flight Path Stabilization caution light. ATC advised of a Pilot Deviation due to the proximity of an accompanying helicopter in trail and 1,000 feet above the reporter's aircraft.
summary: The pilot experienced airspeed and flight path stabilization faults while flying IFR at 11,000 feet, requiring manual stabilator control that caused an uncommanded climb to 11,400 feet. This deviation from assigned altitude occurred due to changed handling characteristics and communication delays, resulting in a pilot deviation call from ATC.

synopsis: DA20 pilot reported having no throttle response on final approach, and since the throttle was at 'Full Open' he elected to secure the engine via the mixture control to complete his landing. He landed short of the runway in the grassy area with no damage to the aircraft. A Maintenance Technician reported a post landing inspection revealed that the throttle control arm had spun on the air/throttle shaft.
summary: A pilot flying a Diamond DA20 at night experienced a stuck throttle during a VFR approach to ZZZ, forcing an engine shutdown via mixture control and a grass landing short of the runway. Post-landing inspection revealed the throttle control arm had spun on the shaft due to a loose self-locking nut, causing no aircraft damage.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: While on a right base for for Runway 25R at DVT, pilot is instructed to orbit north of the center line of the Runway. A left turn is initiated resulting in a NMAC with another aircraft on base for Runway 25R.
summary: A pilot landing at Deer Valley Airport misunderstood a Tower instruction to orbit north of Runway 25R, executing a left turn that caused a near miss with another aircraft on base for Runway 25L. The incident resulted from confusion over the orbit phraseology during the approach phase.

synopsis: PA44 instructor pilot reports shutting down the right engine at 5,500 feet for training then being unable to restart it after three tries. An emergency is declared but during descent a fourth attempt to restart is successful and the emergency is canceled.
summary: During single-engine training, the pilot and student shut down the right engine, which failed to restart despite starter use and increased airspeed. After declaring an emergency and descending, a fourth restart attempt succeeded, allowing them to cancel the emergency and land safely.

synopsis: Enroute Controller failed to utilize proper RADAR termination phraseology with an emergency aircraft, distracted by a complicated re-route effort.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller vectored a PA-46 reporting a single-engine emergency to a visual approach but became distracted by a complex re-route request. The controller incorrectly terminated radar service for the emergency aircraft using improper phraseology, though the pilot landed safely.

synopsis: A B737-700 experienced significant vibration in the right engine which became excessive and illuminated the oil filter bypass light when thrust was reduced to idle per the vibration checklist. The flight crew declared an emergency, shut down the engine and diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: The crew experienced increased vibrations and grinding noise from Engine 2 at FL380, which worsened during descent to FL360 and triggered an oil filter bypass light. Following a QRH-guided shutdown and diversion, post-flight inspection revealed obvious internal engine damage despite no visible exterior issues.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports taking evasive action for a TCAS RA during descent into BUR. Clouds obscured visual contact with the other aircraft until the first TCAS resolution had been enunciated.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring and Captain on a Boeing aircraft approaching BUR received a TCAS RA while IMC due to a non-communicating Stearman scud running nearby. They manually descended to 4,000 feet and turned right, avoiding a collision with the other aircraft by approximately 200 feet vertically and 500 feet horizontally.

synopsis: B717 Captain reports hearing and feeling a bump during final approach to TPA. Upon taxi in to the gate a RT HYD QTY LOW alert is annunciated and the ground crew indicates something is amiss with the right gear. Post flight inspection reveals a large bird wedged in the right main landing gear.
summary: The flight crew experienced a bird strike on final approach to TPA RWY 01L, causing a hydraulic line rupture in the right main landing gear. A shore bird lodged in the bogey sprayed fluid, triggering low quantity alerts and requiring engine shutdowns after landing.

synopsis: Captain reports about their Scheduling Department's effort to have him taxi their CRJ-200 aircraft to a company hangar with a running fuel leak from the right inboard wing area near the aircraft's main wheel well.
summary: The flight crew refused to taxi an aircraft with an active fuel leak from the right main gear wheel well, despite repeated scheduling pressure. The leak persisted after failed maintenance attempts, and the crew declined to operate the aircraft due to fire risks, especially after finding the APU running unattended near the leak.

synopsis: A Check Airman conducting initial operating experience with a new First Officer on a CRJ-700 was distracted by other duties as the First Officer, who was flying a visual approach to BHM, got distracted, overturned to final and triggered a low altitude alert from the Tower and a momentary EGPWS warning. An appropriate profile to an uneventful landing was quickly re-established and no go around resulted.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway 6 at BHM, the Captain and First Officer descended below 2,500 feet due to the Captain's poor monitoring while managing checklists. This resulted in a low altitude alert and GPWS warning, which were resolved after the Captain corrected the flight path before the First Officer completed the landing.

synopsis: CE-750 flight crew reported wake vortex encounter on arrival into BOS in trail of an Airbus. Aircraft rolled in response and one passenger, not wearing a seatbelt, reported back and neck pain.
summary: During descent into BOS, the crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding Airbus at 8,000 feet, causing abrupt rolls and bumps. One passenger sustained neck and back injuries while unbelted despite the seat belt sign being on, though they refused medical attention.

synopsis: A B737-800 pilot experienced wake vortices from an A380 while en route.
summary: A B-737-800 crew encountered heavy-moderate turbulence at cruise, likely from an A380 that crossed 6 minutes prior at an estimated 1,000 feet above. The pilot reported no injuries but questioned the adequacy of standard A380 separation minima given the unexpected wake turbulence at night.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant questioned whether a developmentally disabled female should fly unaccompanied. It was ignored and at an intermediate stop the passenger slipped out beyond security before being found.
summary: A flight attendant reported that a disabled, disoriented passenger boarded without proper evaluation and wandered off during a mid-continent stop. The crew located her at baggage claim and escorted her back to the aircraft, noting that Operations failed to assess her ability to travel independently.

synopsis: BE35 pilot reports fuel venting from a fuel tank cap just after takeoff. An emergency is declared and an abbreviated pattern is flown to the departure runway. Ninety percent of the fuel in that tank had vented in the short flight.
summary: The pilot declared an emergency after takeoff when avgas vented from one of four fuel tanks due to a fuel cap locking mechanism issue. The aircraft returned for a normal landing, and a certified mechanic adjusted the cap after 90% of that tank's contents had vented.

synopsis: A Learjet 31 pressurization duct connection failed while climbing through FL360 because the glue connecting a pressurization duct had not completely cured following an extensive maintenance overhaul.
summary: The First Officer of a Learjet 31 experienced an abrupt cabin pressure loss during climb to FL430, likely caused by the aft pressure bulkhead failing. The crew executed an emergency descent to 12,000 feet, stabilized the cabin, and returned safely to the departure airport for repairs.

synopsis: BE36 pilot reports a muffled bang during cruise at 7,000 feet followed by increased exhaust noise and the smell of exhaust fumes. Fearing a compromised exhaust system, an emergency is declared and vectors requested to the nearest suitable airport. Post flight revealed the fuel sump door had opened in flight.
summary: A pilot on an IFR flight at 7,000 feet declared an emergency after a fuel sump door opened, causing exhaust fumes and noise. Despite two unanswered requests for the Tower frequency, the pilot landed safely with fire trucks present, and the aircraft was repaired the same day.

synopsis: A Repair Shop Mechanic describes the events that led to the discovery that unapproved chrome cylinders had been installed on a Grumman AA1 aircraft's Lycoming 0-235-C2C engine, approximately 24 years earlier.
summary: A mechanic and an owner-mechanic discovered that an engine repair station reinstalled LW-11633 cylinders, which are unapproved for the O-235-C2C engine, causing continued high oil consumption. The error occurred because the wrong cylinders, originally installed 24 years prior, were not identified by part number during removal or repair.

synopsis: Tower Supervisor voiced concern regarding a TRACON's interpretation of the 'opposite direction' mandate that is continuing to cause confusion.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a safety concern when a PA31 was on a two-mile final for Runway 26 while a Cessna 402 was over the Runway 8 outer marker for a circle-to-26 approach. The controller believed the TRACON Operations Manager misunderstood missed approach protection procedures under 7110.65, prompting a recommendation for clarification and refresher training on opposite direction operations.

synopsis: D01 Controller described a conflict event when arrival traffic was not transferred from ZDV in a timely manner resulting in a conflict with VFR glider traffic.
summary: The reporter, an ATC controller, attempted to warn ZDV about a VFR glider at 17,500 feet conflicting with Air Carrier X, but ZDV failed to act until the aircraft were two miles apart. Air Carrier X executed a TCAS RA, passing within 200 feet of the glider, which the reporter attributed to ZDV's inaction and the glider's presence in the area.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: P80 Controller voiced concern regarding PDX Tower's failure to hold all departures when directed due to previous departures route/heading confusion.
summary: An Air Carrier X DH8D departed Portland on a radar-vectored SID but incorrectly turned right into the jet corridor instead of left to TIMEE. The Departure Controller halted all departures at 6,000 feet after the ATCT delayed holding, resolving the conflict once the aircraft corrected its heading.

synopsis: SCT Controller described a conflict event involving Air Carrier traffic inbound to ONT on the ILS 26L and VFR traffic crossing the ILS path, the reporter recommending ONT's Class C be expanded to reduce same type events.
summary: An air traffic controller issued traffic to an A320 on ILS 26L into ONT descending from 3,400 feet regarding a VFR aircraft without a transponder crossing the final. The controller declined a vector offer, noting the VFR aircraft was at 2,200 feet and recommending Class C airspace extension to prevent future conflicts.

synopsis: EWR Controller described a go around event, the Controller questioning the 'wake remnant' separation standard, noting no rules are currently described in any ATC Directives.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored Air Carrier Y to a go-around and issued heading and altitude instructions to separate it from departing Air Carrier X due to a preceding aircraft blocking Runway 4R. The controller cited limited airspace and wake turbulence concerns as the cause for these maneuvers and requested clearer regulatory guidance on wake remnant separation.

synopsis: PCT Controller experienced a loss of separation event when leaving the RADAR control position to modify a flight plan, the Flight Data Controller otherwise engaged in another location.
summary: An air traffic controller at BELAY lost track of Aircraft X after leaving the scope to amend data while the Flight Data Controller was distracted. This caused a conflict with Aircraft Y, requiring immediate traffic advisories and turns to separate the aircraft, which the controller attributed to unsafe data entry practices and leaving a non-acquired track.

synopsis: B737-300 Captain experiences a loss of cabin pressurization at FL340. Oxygen masks are donned and QRH procedures are complied with during descent. After leveling at 10,000 feet and after considering passenger distress and fuel status, the crew elects to continue to destination.
summary: The flight crew at FL340 initiated an emergency descent after a cabin pressurization warning and oxygen system activation. They continued to the original destination due to adequate fuel and no passenger distress, attributing an odd odor and mist to the passenger oxygen generators.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Airline Captain believes that the Expressway visual Approach to Runway 31 at LGA should have some fixes with suggested altitudes (like the River Visual to 19 at DCA) to aid pilots that do not fly into LGA on a regular basis.
summary: The Pilot Flying reported safety concerns regarding the Expressway visual arrival to LGA Runway 31, noting that the lack of waypoints and visual references makes maintaining a stabilized approach difficult. The pilot suggested adding altitude and position checkpoints to improve situational awareness and efficiency for this procedure.

synopsis: OAK Air Carrier arrival for Runway 11 selected an incorrect localizer frequency resulting in a failed intercept requiring additional ATC vectors and an eventual go around event.
summary: The crew failed to set the correct ILS frequency on approach to OAK Runway 11, causing the aircraft to miss the localizer. ATC canceled the approach, issued urgent descent instructions to avoid traffic, and vectored the aircraft for a successful second ILS attempt.

synopsis: An Embraer 145 Captain reports encountering wake vortices while on descent into IAD.
summary: During descent into IAD on the GIBBZ One arrival, the crew encountered significant wake turbulence from a preceding B737, causing abrupt rolls up to 45 degrees and an autopilot failure due to overpowering control inputs. The pilot manually recovered, slowed to 230 KTS, and logged the event for precautionary flight control inspection, with no injuries or further anomalies.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reports failure of the aircraft to pressurize after takeoff and is informed shortly by the Lead Flight Attendant that the forward entry door is not sealed properly with a gap along the bottom of the door. Crew elects to return to the departure airport after burning down to landing weight.
summary: During initial climb, the flight crew and cabin crew identified an unsealed L-1 door causing excessive cabin climb rates and noise, despite no door annunciators illuminating. The crew declared an emergency, burned fuel to reduce landing weight, and returned for a normal landing; maintenance attributed the issue to the 737 door cam lock design.

synopsis: MD82 Captain detailed the factors that contributed to both crew members missing the wrong altitude set in the altitude window which resulted in an altitude deviation on a SID.
summary: The flight crew deviated 1,000 feet below the 8,000-foot SID altitude because both pilots incorrectly set 10,000 feet in the altitude window during preflight. The reporter attributes the error to a failure to carefully read the SID and follow the checklist, noting that standard safety layers like ATC questioning and ACARS data were absent.

synopsis: A Maintenance Supervisor reports an Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) discovered that the left and right engine fire bottle cartridges had been installed at incorrect locations, allowing the left engine bottle 'A' to be discharged to the right engine and the right engine bottle 'A' to be discharged to the left engine in the event of an engine fire. The ERJ-170 had been flying for several years in that configuration.
summary: A mechanic discovered during a Fire Bottle Job Card that fire bottle cartridges were installed in incorrect locations on an Embraer aircraft, allowing cross-discharge between engines. The reporter attributed this to ambiguous maintenance procedures and excessive wiring slack, creating a risk of total fire protection loss.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports about the lack of any specific reference in the B777 Maintenance Manual (M/M) providing guidance on what to do 'after' fluid penetration into the forward Main Equipment Center (MEC) tunnel and lower lobe areas has occurred. Mechanic noted the B767 M/M does provide detailed instructions for similar galley spills.
summary: A mechanic on a B777-200 discovered a dried coffee stain in the forward avionics bay caused by a galley leak into the lower lobe. The report notes that while the B767 manual provides spill guidance, the B777 Maintenance Manual lacks specific procedures for this scenario.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air Carrier departing DFW voiced concern regarding the 'Coded Taxi Routes' used for his company, noting inconsistency of use by ATC and cockpit workload as complicating factors.
summary: A pilot at DFW Airport reported safety concerns regarding inconsistent coded standard taxi routes issued by Ground Control. The pilot stated these clearances force heads-down taxiing, increase runway incursion risk, and shift controller responsibilities to the cockpit, leading the pilot to refuse such clearances.

synopsis: LAS Air Carrier departure voiced concern regarding an ATC instruction to 'sight' another departure from a parallel runway, the reporter claiming the subject separation is the responsibility of controllers.
summary: A pilot departing LAS received a takeoff clearance requiring them to keep a preceding aircraft in sight while managing critical takeoff duties. The pilot reported this as an unsafe, impossible task that overloads the crew and questioned the lack of clear guidance on duration and required actions if visual contact is lost.

synopsis: PA28 pilot notes fuel streaming from the wing tank fuel drains after checking fuel during preflight. The drains are opened and closed again stopping the fuel flow and the reporter departs. The tanks are filled to capacity of 48 gallons at the first fuel stop but after 2.5 hours of flight the left tank appears empty and the right tank shows 5 gallons. Still thinking high fuel consumption the aircraft is fueled and returned to the FBO where the next renter finds the right tank empty in the morning.
summary: The pilot preflighted a rental Piper Archer and observed fuel leaking from both wing petcocks but proceeded with the flight. Despite abnormal fuel consumption and gauge readings, the pilot continued flying until the next renter discovered the right tank had emptied due to the unresolved leak.

synopsis: TB20 pilot discovers failed throttle linkage at 9,000 feet and with ATC assistance a successful emergency landing is accomplished with the engine shut down on short final. A bolt was found to have fallen out of the throttle linkage. A rebuilt engine had been installed approximately eight months ago.
summary: A pilot flying IFR at 9,000 feet experienced throttle unresponsiveness due to a missing bolt in the linkage, prompting an emergency landing. A mechanic replaced the bolt with a cotter pin, certified the aircraft, and the pilot resumed the flight after ground checks.

synopsis: C172 pilot reports becoming disoriented in IMC and being assisted by NCT with vectors to a safe landing.
summary: The pilot lost control and became disoriented while flying in clouds on a vector heading, causing an unintended descent to 3,000 feet. NORCAL Approach amended the clearance to VFR, allowing the pilot to divert to the Embassy Suite checkpoint and land safely.

synopsis: ZOB Controller described a conflict event when issuing a 'direct' clearance when a more positive method of separation should have been used.
summary: An air traffic controller managing Air Carrier X at FL380 and Air Carrier Y at FL360 issued a direct route clearance that caused Air Carrier X to turn northwest into Air Carrier Y's path. The controller attributed the conflict to assigning a direct route instead of a specific heading until Air Carrier X descended below Air Carrier Y.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: MYF Controller described a conflict event involving an arrival VFR aircraft, the reporter claiming the procedures with SCT need to be revised to more clearly define routes/procedures and coordination to be used in these types of situations.
summary: A pilot approaching Runway 28L reported a 200-foot vertical separation conflict with a climbing aircraft due to undefined coordination procedures between facilities. The pilot also executed a go-around after the tower released traffic on the active runway, attributing both incidents to new controllers learning their job.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew encountered a main landing gear extension problem and executed a missed approach. The Emergency Checklist was accomplished and Maintenance Control contacted. Company reserve fuel policy did not allow for a Tower fly-by landing gear inspection and an uneventful landing was accomplished.
summary: During final approach, the crew encountered a gear disagree warning where main gear failed to deploy due to a suspected electronic signal failure. After successfully extending the gear manually with a jammed release handle, the crew landed safely despite low fuel reserves limiting troubleshooting time.

synopsis: Air Carrier on initial climb experienced a digital flight guidance failure on both systems resulting in a return to the departure airport.
summary: The pilot flying departed ZZZ for SJC when both digital flight guidance computers failed at 3,000 feet, causing a loss of automation and navigation displays. The crew declared an emergency, returned to ZZZ for an overweight landing, and maintenance grounded the aircraft due to multiple system failures.

synopsis: A B737-800 flight crew inbound to Nashville was cleared to fly the SWFFT RNAV STAR, but because they were not 'cleared via' and had not received an 'independent' descent clearance, did not descend to cross SWFFT as charted. Approach Control ultimately provided descent clearance and vectors as necessary.
summary: The flight crew, while descending from cruise to BNA, experienced confusion and a delay because Center cleared them direct SWFFT without specifying the "North Transition" or issuing a descent clearance. Consequently, they remained at FL240 until Approach Control intervened to clear them down to 5,000 feet, resulting in an uneventful landing.

synopsis: Pilot reports finding a Flap Control Rod protruding a few inches from the top of Number 3 Flap Canoe fairing on a B747-400 aircraft during a post flight walk-around inspection. Maintenance noted damage of unknown origin had occurred to Number 3 and Number 4 Flap Control rods on both flap track assemblies.
summary: A B747-400 landed with MEL items including a removed Number 4 flap canoe fairing. Post-flight inspection revealed a protruding flap control rod on the Number 3 fairing, leading mechanics to find damage to Number 3 and 4 flap track assemblies of unknown origin.

synopsis: MD-82 Captain reported loss of cabin pressurization after takeoff. Emergency was declared and flight returned to departure airport.
summary: The flight crew of a DC-9 experienced a total loss of pneumatic pressure and cabin pressurization shortly after takeoff. They declared an emergency, burned fuel, and landed overweight at 140,000 lbs with a smooth touchdown and no injuries.

synopsis: MD10 Captain experienced engine fire warning so he declared an emergency and returned to departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced a false fire warning on the Number 2 engine during climb due to a deferred fire detection loop and a flickering fuel lever. They declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport with the engine at idle, and landed safely after fire/rescue inspection confirmed no actual fire.

synopsis: A commuter departure encountered a flock of circling birds, one of which was struck by the right wing damaging the slat system. The flight crew declared an emergency and diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: The flight crew encountered a flock of turkey vultures shortly after takeoff from ZZZ, resulting in a bird strike on the right wing slat that triggered multiple system failures. The crew declared an emergency, diverted to a nearby airport, and landed safely after maintenance identified a slat dent and broken skew sensor.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reported the Flight Attendant called them during sterile cockpit on short final stating the jump seat became inoperative. Flight Attendant sat in lavatory during landing.
summary: During short final, a flight attendant reported a stuck jump seat to the cockpit crew, forcing the attendant to land from the lavatory. The incident highlighted the need to inform pilots of cabin malfunctions during high-workload sterile cockpit phases.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew on approach received multiple aural and ICAS warning indications and elected to abandon the approach. In VMC they circled and landed without incident.
summary: During an RNAV approach, the pilot experienced false gear warnings and a VNAV slope jump at 2,000 feet, causing the FMS to display incorrect runway distance. The pilot leveled off, broke out of weather at 1,500 feet, and landed safely after suspecting a map shift or radar altimeter issue, though maintenance found no faults.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew reported loss of First Officer air data computer on takeoff roll. Captain continued takeoff since they were near V1, and after selecting the Captain's ADC they returned to departure airport.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced multiple airspeed and flight director failures during takeoff and initial climb due to a faulty Captain CADC. After switching to the First Officer's CADC to restore instruments, they returned to the departure airport for an uneventful landing.

synopsis: A CE560 Captain flew the TEB RUUDY 4 with the VNAV engaged as an experiment and, after following the left turn guidance, was directed right by ATC to return to the departure track.
summary: The pilot and co-pilot departed TEB on the RUUDY 4 procedure, but the autopilot's v-bars incorrectly commanded a left turn at 400 feet instead of the required right turn. The pilot followed the erroneous display until the tower controller corrected the heading, attributing the deviation to misplaced trust in the navigation system.

synopsis: FA10 flight crew climbing through FL380 reported severe airframe vibration of unknown origin, so they declared an emergency and diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: During a climb to FL400, the crew experienced severe airframe vibrations that persisted despite reducing power and airspeed. After descending to FL300 resolved the issue, the flight diverted to a nearby airport because passengers refused to continue, resulting in an uneventful landing.

synopsis: PA32 pilot on a VFR flight obtained ATC permission to climb into Class A airspace to avoid cloud tops and icing conditions.
summary: The pilot encountered icing and high cloud tops during departure, prompting a request to enter Class A airspace up to FL225 to maintain VFR. After 15 minutes, cloud tops lowered, allowing a safe descent and landing with the aid of ATC PIREPs.

synopsis: P28A pilot reported he took evasive action and dove to avoid an aircraft he perceived to be a collision threat.
summary: A pilot on an IFR flight at 4,000 feet reported a near-midair collision with a VFR aircraft at 4,100 feet while under Dover control. The pilot executed a rapid descent to 3,200 feet to avoid the other aircraft, which was not at a proper VFR cruise altitude and took no evasive action.

synopsis: While airborne using XM weather, a PA32 pilot discovers that his destination is IFR and below minimums. The forecast the night before was for VMC at the ETA and no alternate was filed. Reporter diverts to a suitable alternate.
summary: The pilot departed with four passengers in VFR conditions but discovered IOW weather was below minimums and no alternate was filed. The crew diverted to MLI for a safe landing after the pilot realized he had failed to check destination weather before takeoff.

synopsis: IAH Controller described a confused call sign event involving similar sounding four digit flight numbers.
summary: Air Carrier ABCD pilots departed with an incorrect beacon code matching Air Carrier EABC, causing a call sign confusion on ASDE-X that went unnoticed until 70 miles from the airport. The reporter attributes this ongoing safety issue to similar call signs and inadequate crew awareness of flight plan discrepancies.

synopsis: Aircraft lost Flight Director Command bars and had multiple warning indications during the takeoff roll. RTO was initiated by the Captain and aircraft returned to the gate. First Officer spent considerable time attempting to locate the QRH page referencing an RTO event, only to discover it had been eliminated from the QRH.
summary: During a maximum power takeoff in cold weather, a hydraulic and anti-ice failure triggered an automatic RTO after the crew exceeded 80 knots. The First Officer missed the speed callout and later struggled to locate the RTO checklist, which is no longer in the QRH, delaying assistance to the Captain.

synopsis: Upon receiving a Cabin Altitude Warning light and aural warning the flight crew of a B737-500 declared an emergency and initiated an emergency descent.
summary: During climb to FL300, a cabin altitude warning prompted the Captain to initiate an immediate emergency descent to 10,000 feet while the First Officer ran checklists. The crew landed safely but noted the rapid descent prevented proper analysis of the pressurization issue before executing the checklist.

synopsis: Crew received multiple flight instrument failures and warning indications during take-off, and executed an abort.First Officer could not locate the QRH page referencing an RTO.
summary: The Captain rejected a max power takeoff after a Number 2 generator trip caused multiple system cautions and flight director loss. Aggressive auto-braking generated smoke and a burning rubber smell, but fire crews found no tire damage, allowing the aircraft to return to the gate.

synopsis: B737-500 flight crew had a Cabin Altitude Warning horn activation during climb out at FL290. Flight crew responded as per the checklist.
summary: The flight crew experienced a cabin altitude warning while climbing through FL280 and FL290 on a second leg of an aircraft with known pressurization issues. They executed an expeditious descent to 10,000 feet, where the system stabilized, allowing them to land safely without passenger oxygen mask deployment or injuries.

synopsis: An MD-82's ailerons jammed three times during flight so the aircraft was removed from service, ferried to a maintenance station and the crew later discovered three previous similar anomalies on the aircraft. A servo fault and lack of lubrication are believed to be the causes.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced three aileron jams at 23,000 feet while the autopilot was engaged, requiring manual force to break the binding. Although the crew completed the flight without declaring an emergency, the reporter noted the aircraft had three prior logbook entries for this issue and criticized the lack of QRH procedures.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant reported that their B737-900 seat bottoms cushions were not flotation devices but a passenger noted that the pre-takeoff PA announcement stated that the seat cushions were flotation devices.
summary: A flight attendant incorrectly stated that seat cushions were flotation devices during the takeoff announcement on a new aircraft type. The error occurred because she failed to incorporate updated information from the preflight bulletin into her announcement script.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported their wingtip fence made contact with a parked aircraft during gate arrival.
summary: During taxiing at 2-3 knots, the flight crew followed three marshallers and struck the tail cone of a parked EMB-190 with their left wingtip fence. The crew stopped the aircraft, shut down the left engine, and requested a tug, reporting no injuries.

synopsis: A C-207 pilot landing at night with strong gusty crosswinds on a lighted but questionably maintained gravel airstrip in Alaska lost control of the aircraft and exited the left side of the runway, striking runway edge lights with the aircraft and/or the propeller while doing so.
summary: The pilot landed a single-engine aircraft at an uncontrolled airport in strong northeast crosswinds. Premature touchdown on the left runway side caused a bounce, and subsequent drift into the snow embankment resulted in the aircraft striking runway edge lights before stopping.

synopsis: C152 pilot experienced a radio failure after takeoff and landed at another airport without receiving any light signals from the Tower. After obtaining a handheld radio, the Pilot departed, lost communication again and landed at the original departure airport without receiving any light signals. Pilot was subsequently advised by ATC that he should have called the Tower via phone after the first landing.
summary: A solo VFR pilot experienced a complete radio failure while returning to the airport, unable to transmit or receive ATIS or Tower communications. After circling for light signals without success, the pilot landed safely and later learned from the controller that coordinating via cell phone on the ground is a safer alternative for future radio emergencies.

synopsis: ATC cleared a MQ-9 into restricted airspace believing it was under their control but the pilot was notified by Range Control after entry that the area was active so he exited immediately.
summary: The MQ-9 pilot requested and received clearance from Center to enter a Restricted Area but was informed by Range Control that the airspace was active and not under Center's control. The pilot immediately turned around and exited the airspace without further incident.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Recip Eng
synopsis: A pilot, taxiing on BFI Taxiway A in dark wet conditions, detected an orange construction barrier on the taxiway centerline. After diverting, thought he avoided it but was informed at his destination that his propeller struck the barrier.
summary: The pilot, while taxiing a propeller aircraft in dark, wet conditions, swerved to avoid an unannounced construction barrier after looking inside to set radio frequencies. Post-flight inspection revealed no aircraft damage, though Operations later confirmed the barrier was sliced, attributed to distraction and perceived familiarity.

synopsis: GSP Controller voiced concern regarding the tower blinds, claiming they are inadequate and also indicted the fly problem is distracting and needs to remedied.
summary: Air traffic controllers reported that inadequate tower blinds and a structural roof defect allowed excessive sunlight and hundreds of flies to enter the facility. The resulting visual glare and distracting buzzing noise impaired operations, prompting the crew to manually clean and spray pests while requesting a new roof and blinds.

synopsis: TEB Controller described a runway incursion event by an airport vehicle during a take off, the reporter electing not to cancel the take off clearance given the departures speed and runway location.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft X for takeoff on Runway 1 while a TEB airport vehicle entered the runway and performed a 180-degree turn. The controller did not cancel the takeoff due to the wet runway and the aircraft's advanced departure roll, citing a need for better vehicle operator training.

synopsis: Two pilots report their B737-700 aircraft MEL does not list the AUTOBRAKES, TCAS or RTO Systems as possibly affected by a deferral of the Left Inertial Reference Unit (IRU). Captain's suggestion to verify that all three systems are functioning prior to dispatch was also raised.
summary: The crew departed ZZZ in a B737 with an inoperative left IRS under MEL 34-35, but en route experienced TCAS, autobrake, and speed trim failures. Maintenance grounded the aircraft, replaced the left IRU, and confirmed the MEL was incomplete regarding these associated system failures.

synopsis: A Captain and First Officer report about the misinterpretation and confusion they and Maintenance Control had with a previous MEL 22-5-01 deferral for a Mach Trim System failure on their B737-300 aircraft. The aircraft had flown with a dual channel Mach Trim failure but had been deferred as a single channel failure.
summary: The flight crew misinterpreted MEL 22-5-01 for a single-channel Mach Trim failure, incorrectly believing the Recall test was not required before each flight. Despite doubts and conflicting advice from Maintenance Control, they departed without the required warning lights, resulting in a ground delay and MEL change to 22-5-02 for a dual-channel failure.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported a wake vortex encounter following a B737-900 on arrival to IAH that resulted in a slight injury to a flight attendant.
summary: During descent behind a B737-900, the crew encountered moderate wake turbulence that injured a flight attendant's shoulder and neck. The crew slowed to 210 knots to increase spacing after a second light turbulence event and landed safely on Runway 26L.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported left main gear light remained out after gear extension. They ran appropriate checklists, declared an emergency, and landed normally.
summary: The flight crew encountered a left main landing gear light failure on final approach, prompting a go-around at 1,000 feet and an emergency declaration. After executing checklists and pressing the light fixture to illuminate it, they performed an uneventful landing and stopped straight ahead on the runway.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier aircraft encountered severe turbulence on approach, executed a missed approach and diverted to a distant alternate.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence and wind shear during the approach to ZZZ, causing an airspeed excursion and autopilot disengagement. They aborted the landing, declared an emergency, and diverted to a northern alternate airport, landing safely with 5,000 lbs of fuel remaining.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported a ground conflict in SFO when he was cleared to cross 28L at Tango at the same time another Airbus was clearing the runway at Delta. Reporter feels that is a dangerous clearance.
summary: The First Officer stopped their aircraft before crossing Runway 28L at SFO after seeing an Airbus rapidly approaching on the runway. The near collision occurred because Tower instructed an expedited crossing while another aircraft was clearing the runway, leaving insufficient space for both operations.

synopsis: B757 flight crew had an engine failure turning onto final approach. Flight crew requested vectors off the approach and ran the Engine Failure Checklist. Engine restarted on its own and flight crew continued on a visual approach to uneventful landing.
summary: The flight crew experienced a right engine failure at 3,000 feet while intercepting a VOR approach, indicated by a pop, whine, and EICAS warnings. The engine restarted automatically, allowing the crew to land safely on the right runway using flaps 20 and an ILS backup.

synopsis: A B737 FMS dropped a WYNDE 4 RNAV segment immediately after FNT and proceeded to a DEWIT Intersection which was not on the flight plan. ATC caught the deviation and cleared the flight direct GRR.
summary: The flight crew experienced a momentary FMC malfunction en route to ORD near the FNT VOR, causing the EMMMA intersection to disappear and the aircraft to deviate toward DEWIT. Air Traffic Control vectored them to GRR to rejoin the arrival, resolving the deviation with no separation issues reported.

synopsis: B737 flight crew experienced wake turbulence on arrival to SFO following an A319. They took evasive action and missed a crossing restriction as a result.
summary: The flight crew experienced significant wake turbulence from a preceding Airbus A319 during a visual approach to San Francisco Runway 28R at 7,000 feet. To escape the turbulence, they offset right and slowed, inadvertently descending below the 6,000-foot restriction before ATC assigned a new offset and 180 knots.

synopsis: An EGLL gate auto-stop parking system failed so that a ground worker had to command a B757-200 emergency stop to prevent an engine from contacting the jetway.
summary: The Captain of a B757-200 taxiing at LHR overshot the gate by 25 feet due to a malfunctioning automated parking system and lack of stop line visibility. A ground worker triggered an emergency stop, preventing the left engine from striking the jetway, leaving the aircraft for investigation.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported flaps failed at zero degrees on approach. Appropriate checklist was run, ATC notified, and a normal landing ensued.
summary: The flight crew experienced a flap failure at zero degrees during final approach. They followed the QRH, notified ATC, and landed safely before taxiing to the gate to alert Maintenance.

synopsis: CE-750 flight crew reported loss of Hydraulic System A on descent. Crew ran the checklists, declared an emergency, and landed safely, coming to a stop with the emergency brake system.
summary: During descent at 15,000 feet, the crew received a HYD VOL LOW A EICAS message indicating 16% hydraulic fluid and declared an emergency. After completing checklists, they landed normally using the Emergency Brake System and discovered fresh hydraulic fluid leaking from two wicks on the right fuselage.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An MD-80 First Officer reported difficulties complying with the late stage crossing restrictions while descending via the KAYLA RNAV STAR to STL. Changes to their assigned landing runway from northwest to southeast were reported as primary contributing factors.
summary: The flight crew experienced task management overload while descending into STL on the KAYLA arrival due to three FMS changes caused by runway switches. This resulted in being 2,000 feet high at two waypoints, requiring an immediate faster descent to correct the altitude deviation.

synopsis: DHC6 pilot with minimal experience in type on a skydiver mission, ran the aircraft out of fuel, got the jumpers out, feathered the engines, and made a successful dead stick landing.
summary: A pilot with less than 20 hours in type experienced a dual engine flameout at 12,000 feet during a skydiving climb after switching fuel tanks due to fluctuating left engine flow. All jumpers exited safely, and the aircraft landed safely following an emergency spiral descent.

synopsis: JAX TRACON Controller described a loss of separation event when anticipated visual separation could not be provided by CRG Tower.
summary: An ATC controller managing Aircraft X on an ILS to CRG requested visual separation from CRG Tower for a conflicting NRB helicopter, but the tower could not see either aircraft due to low cloud bases. The controller immediately issued a break heading of 210 and 3,000 feet to resolve the proximity conflict caused by the airports' close proximity and weather limitations.

synopsis: B737-300 flight crew reported loss of cabin pressure in descent, possibly associated with an unannuciated pack trip. Cabin altitude never exceeded 14,000 feet and the flight landed without further incident.
summary: During descent, the flight crew experienced abnormal air mix valve positions and a cabin altitude warning, prompting a rapid descent to FL200. The crew managed the pressurization issue using checklists without declaring an emergency, as cabin altitude remained below 14,000 feet and passenger masks did not deploy.

synopsis: A B757-200 flight crew was informed they may have operated a flight with an improper deferral a week after the flight.
summary: The pilot and two mechanics addressed an illuminated STBY BUS light during pre-flight by performing MEL procedures and verifying standby power with the STBY BATT switch. The pilot later learned the deferral may have been improper, though the crew believed the aircraft was safe and airworthy at the time of departure.

synopsis: An ERJ-170 diverted because of a very strong chemical odor in the cabin which was first detected during preflight but became very strong in flight. Three of the four crew members became ill.
summary: The flight crew and cabin crew experienced a chemical odor and physical illness during the climb and cruise phases due to suspected fume contamination from Pack 1. The crew diverted the aircraft, landed safely, and reported that three crew members and two maintenance technicians felt ill, while no passengers complained of symptoms.

synopsis: EC135 pilot reported excessive HSI precession after landing on a hospital rooftop helipad and attributed the problem to the hospital Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) equipment and/or machinery on the roof. The helicopter was not equipped with a gyro magnetic compass synchronization control panel to correct the problem.
summary: A pilot reported severe HSI precession on a rooftop hospital pad, likely caused by exhaust turbines, while the aircraft lacked the manual slew panel needed to correct the error. This equipment deficiency rendered the HSI useless, compromising IFR capability and creating a significant safety risk for navigation and situational awareness.

synopsis: MD-82 flight crew reported a Flight Attendant called with smoke in the cabin. They declared an emergency and returned to departure airport where a defective light ballast was determined to be the probable cause.
summary: Ten minutes after takeoff, flight attendants reported smoke from an overhead bin, prompting the crew to declare an emergency and return to the departure airport. Maintenance later determined the cause was an overheated light ballast, and no injuries were sustained.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A Taylor Craft BC-12 engine failed at 700 FT turning final so the aircraft was turned directly to the airport, but landed short with no injuries to the pilot or instructor.
summary: The pilot flying lost engine power at 700 feet while descending for a full stop landing. Following the CFI's instruction to turn toward the runway and maintain 60 knots, the aircraft landed short of the airport property with no injuries.

synopsis: PVD Controller described a lost communications event noting this type of radio coverage limitation has been problematic for some time.
summary: A UH60 pilot and air traffic controllers experienced repeated radio communication failures during an IFR practice approach to IJD due to poor frequency coverage. The controller maintained contact by coordinating a point-out and changing frequencies, eventually issuing missed approach instructions after multiple failed attempts to reach the aircraft.

aircraft: MD-90 Series (DC-9-90) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: SJC Controller described a coordinated Visual Approach to Runway 12R that was noticeably off course, NCT advised the aircraft appeared to making the approach to Moffett.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller issued a landing clearance to Air Carrier X for Runway 12R at SJC after the aircraft was found low and off-course, only to discover the pilot was aligned with the wrong airport, Moffett Field. The controller attributed the error to a TRACON Controller issuing a visual clearance without verifying the aircraft was on the proper final approach.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: PVD Controller observed numerous false targets when maintenance was being conducted on one of the RADAR sites. The reporter indicating ATC must be assured prior to any release that maintenance activities will not interfere with RADAR returns.
summary: A Radar Controller at PVD observed false targets with beacon codes and altitudes caused by maintenance at adjacent BDL and QVH sites. The issue was resolved by switching to ESL mode and disabling external feeds, though it increased workload and required manual handoffs during light traffic.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew experienced surging/overspeed/overtemp on both engines on climbout from a high altitude airport. Number 2 engine spontaneously failed, so after running the checklists the flight declared an emergency and returned to departure airport.
summary: During climbout through 12,000 feet, autothrottle anomalies caused engine surges, overspeeds, and overtemps on both engines, leading to an insidious failure of engine #2. The crew declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport, and executed an uneventful single-engine landing after stabilizing the aircraft.

synopsis: CE-560 flight crew reports a normal brake failure when the landing gear is extended due to the power brake circuit breaker was tripping. A go-around is initiated, checklists are completed, and a normal landing ensues with braking supplied by the emergency braking system.
summary: The crew experienced a popped power brake circuit breaker during gear extension, triggering LO BRAKE PRESS and ANTISKID INOP warnings. They executed a missed approach, landed using emergency brakes on the longest runway, and were towed to the FBO without incident.

synopsis: BE400 flight crew reports missing the turn from Taxiway S to Taxiway B southbound due to fatigue and the cluttered Commercial airport diagram.
summary: The pilot missed a taxiway turn at EWR while taxiing to Runway 4L due to fatigue, inexperience, and a confusing commercial airport diagram. ATC provided amended instructions to rejoin the route, resulting in a brief stop with no traffic delays.

synopsis: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) suggests a revision that would add another Block Decision Step to Boeing's Fault Isolation Manual (FIM) for B767 aircraft. The revision would reduce the required additional tests for Rudder Ratio Changer Module faults that commonly appear after initial aircraft power-up.
summary: A mechanic troubleshooting a Rudder Ratio Changer Module fault on a B-767 found the Fault Isolation Manual lacks a decision block for transient power-up faults. The reporter suggests adding a check for recent recurrence or power-up status to avoid unnecessary testing when the fault clears after initial system power.

synopsis: PA28 instructor with student on visual approach to 71J reports a NMAC with an Apache helicopter which passes 200 feet below the reporter. The reporter was executing a 360 degree turn at the time to loose altitude and gain spacing on other traffic.
summary: A pilot and student conducting an IFR training flight to 71J executed a right 360-degree turn during a visual approach to Runway 12. An Apache helicopter passed within 200 feet below the aircraft during the maneuver, then briefly paralleled their path before resuming its course.

aircraft: Bell Helicopter Textron Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An ATC miscommunication as to the landing traffic's direction of taxi after landing resulted in a conflict with a departing helicopter piloting expecting the landing aircraft to turn away rather than toward his direction of takeoff.
summary: The pilot held on Taxiway Charlie while a TBM exited Runway 23R, but the controller incorrectly instructed that the TBM would turn right onto Foxtrot. The TBM actually turned left, creating a head-on conflict that the pilot avoided by applying power and rotating right after realizing the error.

synopsis: SAV Controller described an unsafe equipment condition with regard to an overdue aircraft and difficulty in trying to secure recorded information from existing the RADAR equipment because of duplicate beacon codes.
summary: Savannah controllers and ZJX initiated an overdue search for a DA42 due to a false target caused by duplicate beacon codes in the Mode S-ARTS system. The aircraft was never actually in the airspace, but the erroneous data activated a flight plan and triggered an Alert, highlighting an unresolved technical issue requiring Tech Ops intervention.

synopsis: ATL Controller described multiple confused landing attempts by a general aviation aircraft who was apparently unfamiliar with the ATL operation, resulting in the go around of an Air Carrier.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managed a Cherokee attempting to land at ATL, which missed Runway 8L and nearly conflicted with a B757 on Runway 9R. The controller issued go-arounds, diverted a B737, and halted departures due to the pilot's poor situational awareness and heavy traffic.

synopsis: CLE Controller described a loss of separation event claiming the new 'Fusion' RADAR software sometimes displays inaccurate ground speeds.
summary: An air traffic controller at CLE reported a potential separation loss between a BE40 and an EA50 during approach to CGF, caused by relying on inaccurate ground speed data from the new FUSION radar system. The controller mistakenly believed visual separation was established without proper coordination, attributing the error to false speed displays and a lapse in procedure.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier crew realized after taking the runway that only one engine had been started and so exited the runway to start the engine before completing a normal takeoff.
summary: The Captain and First Officer aborted a takeoff at IAD after discovering Engine 1 was off due to the start/stop selector being in the stop position. The reporter attributed the error to complacency and fatigue following a long duty day, though the flight was completed normally after a safe restart.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier made an emergency stop to avoid a fuel truck at the intersections of ORD Taxiways A and F.
summary: During taxi to Runway 28ZV, a refueling truck cut in front of the aircraft at the intersection of taxiways A and F, forcing an emergency stop. The truck also nearly struck an approaching Express Jet, prompting the pilot to recommend retraining ground personnel on yielding to aircraft.

synopsis: A DHC-8-300 Master Caution and Cargo Smoke alerted during engine start so an emergency was declared. The aircraft returned to the gate and after passengers deplaned a faulty smoke detector was discovered.
summary: After starting Engine Two, a SMOKE warning light illuminated, prompting the Captain to request fire equipment and return to the gate. Although the Flight Attendant reported no visible smoke, the crew deplaned passengers in an orderly manner upon meeting ground crew.

synopsis: BE400 Captain experiences brake failure after landing. Initial brake application is successful in slowing the aircraft to near taxi speed, but the second application had no effect and emergency braking is used to stop the aircraft. The reporter also laments the lack of taxiway designations at RAC and reports an unrelated issue, that at ROG airport the beacon is not located at the point depicted on both the Commercial and NOS airport diagrams.
summary: The SIC of a Part 135 aircraft experienced total brake failure during the landing roll at Racine after normal deceleration, requiring emergency brakes to stop the aircraft. The crew attributed the failure to a recurring issue noted in the logbook where previous repairs did not address the anti-skid system.

synopsis: CE560 Captain discovers during taxi that a company designed visual engine out procedure from EGE, which must be entered into the FMC manually, has a waypoint name that is the same as an FAA waypoint. This is corrected by entering Lat/Long, the same as the other waypoints in the procedure which are not in the FMC data base.
summary: During a 121.440 check at EGE, the crew discovered a waypoint name conflict in the FMS Visual Engine Out Procedure where the database fix was 90 NM from the intended location. The First Officer corrected the error using LAT/LONG coordinates, revealing a systemic ambiguity between FAA and company waypoint naming conventions.

synopsis: A B757-200 right hydraulic system failed in flight so the QRH was complied with, an emergency declared and the flight landed uneventfully at its filed destination.
summary: The crew experienced a right hydraulic system failure at altitude. They completed the QRH procedure, declared an emergency, and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: A B757-200 Captain reported a split elevator condition detected because of the unusual aileron trim, then verified by the PFD indications.
summary: The 757 crew experienced a split elevator condition during cruise, requiring increased aileron trim for coordinated flight. The reporter attributed the issue to improperly rigged flight controls fighting each other, which increased fuel burn, and documented the discrepancy for maintenance.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: After landing, a crew was cleared to back taxi on HLG Runway 21 and exit at the end, but because of poor lighting, fatigue, and unfamiliarity they exited at Taxiway B then entered Runway 16/34 before turning right onto Taxiway D.
summary: The flight crew inadvertently entered Runway 16/34 while taxiing at night at HLG after landing on Runway 21. The pilot attributed the runway incursion to dark conditions, poor lighting, and lack of local knowledge, noting they only learned of the event after company notification.

synopsis: A BE-1900 engine fire warning alerted as the takeoff was barely begun so an emergency was declared, the aircraft stopped on the runway, the emergency checklist completed and the aircraft evacuated.
summary: The flight crew of a Boeing 757 experienced a left engine fire while holding for takeoff after a preceding 757 departure. The Captain executed fire suppression procedures, and the crew evacuated two passengers before emergency services arrived.

aircraft: McDonnell Douglas Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reports departing with a deferral for Fuel Tank 1 Aft Pump Inoperative with direction to run the FSC in Auto and to add 2,000 LBS of fuel as MEL Penalty. During the next two and one half hours of flight multiple valve and pump anomalies are observed and corrected by placing the FSC to manual then back to auto, then finally leaving it in manual. When an alert is received for trapped fuel in number three tip tank the crew elects to divert.
summary: The crew encountered multiple fuel system alerts and pump failures on an aircraft operating with a Fuel Tank 1 Aft Pump MEL. Suspecting Fuel System Controller trouble, they switched to manual mode, declared an emergency due to trapped fuel, and diverted to ZZZ for a safe landing.

synopsis: B777 Captain reports that one of his company's aircraft auto tunes the frequency for ILS X [Z] 25R at EDDF when the ILS Y 25R is selected in the FMC. Manual entry is required to over ride.
summary: Pilots reported that selecting the ILSY 25R approach on this specific aircraft caused the ILSX 25R frequency to auto-tune. After cycling approaches failed to resolve the unique fault, the crew manually selected the correct frequency.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier crew flying IMC at 2,000 FT MSL on a left downwind to a LGA Runway 13 ILS executed the escape maneuver to 3,500 FT MSL after the EGPWS alerted 'TERRAIN PULL UP.'
summary: During an ILS 13 approach to LGA at 2,000 feet in IMC, the crew received a GPWS terrain warning and executed a climb to 3,500 feet. Maintenance later found no fault with the radar altimeter, though the crew noted a high terrain point of 1,900 feet on final.

synopsis: A B767-300 in oceanic airspace, encountered continuous weather at FL330, experienced an unusual blue static discharge/lightening event which disrupted all digital equipment, several for an extended period, and was then forced to divert for repairs.
summary: A Boeing 767 crew encountered severe turbulence and a static discharge event in oceanic airspace at FL330, causing momentary total cockpit power loss and permanent MCP failure. The crew hand-flew the aircraft, declared a Mayday via CPDLC, and diverted for a normal landing after maintenance reset the systems.

synopsis: A DHC8-100 Captain rejected the takeoff when the LOW OIL PRESSURE WARNING light illuminated and after returning to the gate Maintenance discovered the oil had not been serviced for three days resulting in the quantity being three quarts low.
summary: The pilot rejected takeoff at 80 knots after the Number 1 engine oil pressure light illuminated due to the engine being 3 quarts low on oil. Maintenance had not checked oil levels for three days, which the mechanic identified as the probable cause for the warning.

synopsis: A300-600 Captain reported loss of Blue hydraulic system at cruise. Flight declared an emergency and continued to destination for a normal landing.
summary: During cruise, the crew received a HYD SYS LO PRESS ECAM alert and lost BLUE HYD SYS QTY. They declared an emergency via ACARS, coordinated an early arrival with ATC through Operations, and completed an uneventful approach, landing, and taxi to the gate.

synopsis: A Maintenance Controller reports how a Repetitive Inspection deferral requirement was not continued for a fuel seepage leak at the right inboard (I/B) fuel tank, inboard aft spar area on an A300 aircraft.
summary: A maintenance technician incorrectly configured a fuel leak deferral on a layover aircraft, failing to set the system for required weekly re-inspections. This data entry error caused the tracking system to skip intermediate checks until the next C-Check, delaying proper monitoring of the spar area leak.

synopsis: BE1900 pilot reports accumulating ice at 16,000 FT that is successfully shed by the boots through several cycles before becoming unable to shed the ice. Climbing to FL180 results in less ice formation and a right engine bleed failure. During descent for landing the cabin altitude warning light comes on but is ignored due to the descent rate as well as an early level off at 13,000 FT vice the cleared altitude of 12,000 FT noted by ATC.
summary: The single-pilot Captain of a BE1900 experienced a possible altitude deviation during descent to SLC while managing ineffective de-ice boots and a cabin altitude warning. The pilot attributed the confusion between 11,700 and 13,000 feet to simultaneous distractions from the pressurization warning, icing concerns, and rapid descent.

synopsis: RV6 pilot experiences a sudden loss of oil pressure at 2,500 FT with visible oil on the windscreen and the smell of hot oil in the cockpit. With no airports nearby an emergency landing is preformed on a country road. Post flight reveals a kinked breather hose causing pressure to build up in the crank case and blow out the crank shaft seal.
