summary: The pilot not flying aborted the takeoff at 60 KTS because the right engine failed to maintain 1.59 EPR and rolled back twice despite throttle adjustments. The aircraft returned to the gate with no other issues reported.

synopsis: Level at 4,000 FT after takeoff, an SF340 Captain experiences pressurization anomalies causing ear pain in the passengers. The crew elects to return to the departure airport where the Dump Valve Circuit Breaker is found to be tripped.
summary: During initial climb at 4,000 feet, the aircraft depressurized with a cabin rate exceeding -2,000 feet per minute and a differential of 5.2. The crew executed an air return after a deadheading Captain reported passenger pain, later discovering a popped pressurization Dump Valve Circuit Breaker.

synopsis: Despite having programmed and verified all altitudes and speeds when assigned the ANCHR RNAV STAR to DEN the flight crew of an A319 was compelled to override the FMGC descent path commands to comply with charted crossing restrictions.
summary: The flight crew encountered autopilot non-compliance with published altitude restrictions during a modified RNAV arrival into Denver. The aircraft crossed waypoints high despite FMS programming, forcing manual intervention and increasing workload, which the pilots attributed to flawed new procedures.

aircraft: Cessna Twin Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Light Twin Captain experiences a complete electrical failure at 700 FT AGL after takeoff. After climbing to a safe altitude, flight returns to the departure airport for a no flap landing after emergency extension of the landing gear.
summary: During an IOE night departure at 700 feet, the crew experienced a complete electrical failure. They executed a no-flap emergency landing with extended gear, and the reporter suggested equipping aircraft with handheld com/nav units to mitigate recurrence.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reports near collision with a tug pulling carts during taxi in under Marshaller's direction.
summary: During a night tow-in taxi in inclement weather, a tug driver with five carts nearly struck the aircraft's forward left side after the marshaller signaled an emergency stop. The tug driver maneuvered to avoid contact, missing the aircraft by 15 feet, reportedly due to high speed and failing to see the aircraft until the last minute.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reports accepting a visual approach to Runway 19R at ICT from the east and descending early, causing an EGPWS alert with the towers in sight that likely caused the warning.
summary: The Captain descended to 2,000 feet during a visual approach to 19R at ICT, triggering an EGPWS obstacle warning due to nearby towers. The crew executed a shallow climb to resolve the conflict, attributing the event to an aggressive descent profile and early acceptance of the visual clearance.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier at 3,300 FT descending on a right downwind for visual to TYS Runway 23R, received an EGPWS PULL UP command from known antennas in the descent flight path.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced a GPWS Obstacle Warning and Pull Up command while descending to 3,000 feet for a visual approach to TYS 23R. The reporter attributes the alert to a delayed base turn, which was corrected by stopping the descent, allowing for an uneventful landing.

synopsis: An A300 Air Data Computer failed in cruise at FL320 which resulted in the Captain's airspeed and Flight Director loss as well as an altimeter error, so control was transferred to the First Officer and the flight descended out of RVSM airspace.
summary: The crew experienced a Captain's PFD and altimeter failure at FL320, likely caused by an ADC malfunction, which triggered a momentary erroneous altitude report to ATC. After switching to standby instruments and Autopilot 2, they informed Center they were no longer RVSM capable and were cleared to descend to FL280.

synopsis: An RV-8 developed an oil cooler leak during flight which was only discovered after landing because of oil puddles. The cooler was a year old with in service time of 10.5 hours.
summary: The pilot flew the aircraft for 37 minutes to warm oil before discovering a ruptured oil cooler during post-flight pushback. The failure, which caused significant oil loss without triggering abnormal pressure readings, likely occurred in the final minutes of flight due to an undetectable defect.

synopsis: A B767 developed a Center Hydraulic System leak and, in order to conserve fluid, turned the pumps OFF at cruise but declared an emergency. They turned them back ON for a normal landing using the remaining fluid.
summary: The crew received a low hydraulic quantity warning in the C system en route and turned off center pumps to conserve fluid. Despite very low indications, all systems operated normally during approach and landing, and the aircraft was cleared after a Fire and Rescue inspection.

synopsis: TRACON Controller working all positions combined on a mid shift experienced a loss of separation event, noting the quick combination of positions in this case was not a good idea.
summary: An air traffic controller working a combined TRACON position during night operations lost separation between a Learjet 45 and a Cessna 208 while managing multiple aircraft. The controller attributed the incident to combining positions and having only one person working the mid-shift.

synopsis: C90 Controller described a loss of separation event during simultaneous approach procedures and hazy weather conditions making sighting traffic and the airport difficult for the flight crews.
summary: An air traffic controller lost separation between Aircraft X and Aircraft Y during a visual approach at ORD in hazy conditions. The controller attributed the loss of separation to turning Aircraft X left instead of right to save distance, acknowledging they should have initiated an instrument approach sooner.

synopsis: Tower Controller cancelled a takeoff clearance after observing a sweeper entering the runway, the reporter noting the Ground Controller was inexperienced working snow removal operations and failing to coordinate with Local.
summary: A new Ground Controller cleared a sweeper vehicle onto Runway 15 immediately after an aircraft received takeoff clearance, forcing Local to cancel the departure. The reporter attributes the runway incursion to the controller's lack of specific snow removal training and recommends mandatory refresher classes.

synopsis: A MKE Controller voiced concern regarding the MVA requirements in the local area when various RADAR sites are being used. He recomends more detailed briefings for the controllers regarding the applicable requirements.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a CRJ inbound on a visual approach to Runway 31 was below the correct Minimum Vectoring Altitude of 2,700 feet due to confusion over updated video maps and a lack of briefing. The incident was compounded by a disabled Low Altitude Alert system, raising concerns about terrain collision warnings not triggering for the aircraft.

synopsis: A B737-700 #2 Generator Control Unit (GCU) and Generator malfunctioned in flight illuminating the #2 Transfer Bus Off and Generator Drive Lights as well as creating electrical fumes in the aircraft so an emergency was declared and the flight diverted safely to a nearby airport.
summary: During cruise at FL410, the flight crew experienced a #2 generator failure and fumes, prompting an emergency diversion. Maintenance later identified a fried #2 GCU and replaced the generator, while the crew successfully managed the event through coordinated checklists and communications.

synopsis: A B737-700 #2 Engine surged to well over 100% at climb power so the Captain immediately completed the Engine Limit/Surge/Stall QRH procedure and the flight diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: During climbout at 12,000 feet, the #2 engine surged, exceeding N1 and N2 limits. The crew executed immediate action items and checklists, stabilized the engine, and diverted to a nearby airport due to an unavoidable engine malfunction.

synopsis: An A300 Master Caution alerted AFT CARGO LOOP FAULT A, followed by a Master Warning CARGO SMOKE. Both alerts extinguished but an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: During climb through FL200, the crew received a cargo smoke warning and diverted back to the departure airport. The warning extinguished before checklist completion, but the crew continued the precautionary emergency return and made a normal landing with no actual smoke detected.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier flight crew, distracted while viewing a meteor shower, turned to heading 360 when ATC's call was actually to climb to FL360. ATC detected the error.
summary: The Pilot Flying and First Officer descended to FL360 instead of turning to heading 360 after ATC issued a traffic avoidance instruction. The error resulted from misinterpreting the clearance due to low cockpit lighting, meteor observation distractions, and a breakdown in Crew Resource Management verification procedures.

aircraft: McDonnell Douglas Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Pilot of a medical helicopter noted a vibration in the cyclic during cruise flight, diverted and performed a roll-on landing at an airport. Pitch change link had failed.
summary: During a patient transport cruise at 2,000 feet, the helicopter experienced vertical vibration and cyclic feedback caused by a failed lower bearing on the black pitch change link. The pilot declared an emergency and executed a safe roll-on landing to Runway 18.

synopsis: An Air Carrier landing Runway 13 at LGA experienced a TCAS RA with unreported helicopter traffic.
summary: An A319 crew received a TCAS climbing Resolution Advisory while on a visual approach to LGA Runway 13 due to a helicopter 300 feet below that was not visually acquired. The crew executed the climb to avoid conflict, resumed the approach, and landed safely, attributing the incident to the restrictive visual approach path over the Hudson River.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports that a crane he was moving after an engine change on a B717-200 aircraft struck the trailing edge wing box near the right wingtip. Brakes were ineffective on crane.
summary: A mechanic maneuvering a crane after an engine change struck the right wing's trailing edge due to ineffective brakes and a crowded hangar path. The incident caused minor damage to the wing box, which the reporter attributed to marginal equipment condition and limited maneuvering space.

aircraft: Cessna Twin Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Cessna pilot is advised after landing that he has violated a TFR located over a coal ash pond. The TFR NOTAM was not noticed on a list provided by WSI nor seen on the GPS moving map display with XM.
summary: A pilot violated a 1-mile radius, 3,000-foot TFR while photographing a coal ash pond in West Virginia. The reporter attributed the violation to either a failure in TFR dissemination by WSI/XM or missing the NOTAM, concluding that relying on technology without calling Flight Service was the cause.

synopsis: A CE501 pilot reported attitude indicator failure with auto pilot engaged in IMC. Recovery from the steep turning descent was initiated using the turn needle and the aircraft was climbed to VMC before diverting to a VMC airport.
summary: The pilot experienced a rapid dive and abnormal instrument readings after engaging the autopilot and changing altitude pre-select during climb. The pilot disconnected the autopilot, manually recovered the aircraft from the dive, and landed safely at a VFR airport due to a failed attitude indicator.

synopsis: C182 pilot reports a total electrical failure in IMC at night over mountainous terrain. With ATC assistance the reporter is able to land safely.
summary: A pilot flying a Cessna 182 at night in mountainous IMC experienced a total electrical failure and oxygen depletion while climbing to 15,000 feet. The pilot attributed the incident to complacency regarding route familiarity and the decision to conduct a single-engine night flight in IMC, ultimately surviving by maintaining VFR and descending below assigned altitude.

synopsis: TUL Controller described an unsafe event during side visual approaches to parallel runways when traffic failed to follow the thirty degree intercept instruction, causing a conflict.
summary: A C650 pilot ignored a 150-degree intercept instruction during a visual approach to Runway 18R, flying directly in front of a BE1900 on a parallel approach. The unsafe situation occurred because pilots were unaware of the new 30-degree intercept rule and had not been briefed on the updated clearance phraseology.

synopsis: An A320 Lead Flight Attendant notified the Captain of an aft galley burning plastic smell. After the First Officer investigated, an emergency was declared and the flight diverted to an enroute airport.
summary: The Pilot Not Flying and First Officer managed a strong burning plastic smell in the aft galley during cruise, leading to a precautionary diversion after cabin power was cut. The crew attributed the event's smooth resolution to effective CRM, though they noted the new Flight Manual format delayed accessing checklists.

synopsis: An A320 First Officer expressed concerns about the newly initiated RNAV STAR procedures at DEN, believing them to be excessively complicated and demand capabilities the state of the art FMGC installed on his aircraft was unable to provide. In the instant case it was necessary to disconnect the autopilot twice and the autothrottles once to avoid non-compliance with crossing restrictions.
summary: A crew flying an A320 into Denver reported that new RNAV STARs caused confusion and distractions due to conflicting notes and vector changes. The aircraft's advanced FMGC could not comply with complex speed and altitude restrictions, forcing the pilots to disconnect automation and hand-fly to avoid exceeding limits.

synopsis: CL300 flight crew reports not noticing the crossing restriction at ROPPR on the BOACH 5 RNAV from LAS. A TCAS RA is generated and the crew takes evasive action. A runway change prior to departure may have contributed to the error.
summary: The pilot departed Runway 19R on the BOACH 5 RNAV departure and climbed above the 7,000 FT restriction at ROPPR, triggering a TCAS RA due to conflicting traffic. The incident resulted from the pilot incorrectly assuming an unrestricted climb clearance instead of adhering to the published altitude limits.

synopsis: EC130 pilot flew VFR to a patient pick up point, but upon departure after a 13 minute turnaround, encountered inadvertent IMC. Pilot climbed to Enroute Safe Altitude, regained VFR conditions and diverted to an alternate hospital.
summary: The pilot of an EC130 B4 helicopter entered IMC shortly after departing a Fire Department pad due to rapidly deteriorating visibility. The crew executed an emergency climb to 3,800 feet, regained VFR conditions, and diverted to a hospital without contacting ATC.

synopsis: A B737-800 autopilot twice transitioned from VNAV Path to CWS Pitch without command and the during the first event at FL360 began a dive loosing 300 FT before recovery was affected.
summary: The pilot reported that turbulence caused the autopilot to drop out of VNAV and revert to CWS Pitch, resulting in a 4,000 FPM dive and 300-foot altitude loss. The pilot manually stopped the descent, and a similar mode reversion occurred later without altitude deviation.

synopsis: B737-800 First Officer reported autopilot dropped out of VNAV and started a sharp descent on two occasions.
summary: During turbulence, the autopilot pitch mode reverted from VNAV to CWS Pitch, causing a 4,000 FPM dive. The Captain (PF) disconnected the autopilot to stop the descent after losing 300 feet; a similar mode reversion occurred later without altitude deviation.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports replacing a faulty component on an EMB-135 aircraft with a part identified by their Parts Computer System as being 'Interchangeable with' the part he removed. The new part was interchangeable, but not 'Effective' for the aircraft. Mechanic noted the Illustrated Parts Catalog (IPC) had the correct information, but was not used to verify.
summary: A mechanic installed an incorrect part on an aircraft overnighting at ZZZ1 gate after relying on a flawed parts system that listed it as interchangeable. The error occurred because the mechanic failed to verify part effectivity in the Illustrated Parts Catalog before installation.

synopsis: LAN Controller voiced concern regarding the lack of taxiway signage at Taxiway 'Charlie.' The reporter noted that this concern has been elevated to the airport for two years with no action taken.
summary: Air traffic controllers at LAN reported that landing aircraft on Runway 10R frequently miss the unmarked exit to Taxiway 'C' and nearly enter an intersecting runway. The airport refuses to install signage due to the exit angle, creating a persistent runway incursion risk despite two years of warnings.

synopsis: A BE35 pilot with minimal actual IFR experience was surprised when a refresher flight with a CFII in actual conditions proved more demanding than his previous Instrument Proficiency Checks utilizing 'foggles' to merely simulate IMC.
summary: A single-pilot pilot practicing hand-flying in actual IMC with a CFII deviated from IFR clearances during an initial turning climb. The pilot attributed the poor execution to the significant difference between actual IMC and simulated conditions, noting that LPV guidance later improved performance.

synopsis: An IFR BE-1900 and a VFR Caravan had a near miss at about 5,200 FT after the Caravan pilot reported the BE-1900 in sight but took no evasive action.
summary: A pilot descending from 6,000 feet received a TCAS traffic alert for a VFR Caravan climbing nearby. The pilot executed a climbing right turn, passing 200 feet above the Caravan, which reportedly made no evasive maneuvers.

synopsis: Student pilot in a PA28 reported landing on the nose gear, losing control, and departing the runway. No damage reported.
summary: The pilot landed a nose-wheel aircraft at 65 KIAS, lost directional control due to wheelbarrowing and braking, and veered off the runway into grass. After a mechanic inspected the undercarriage and cleared the aircraft, the pilot returned to base with an instructor two hours later.

synopsis: P180 Captain describes a comment by ATC during the TEB8 departure. The comment was 'thought you were going to make your turn earlier' before the hand off to the next Controller.
summary: The flight crew departed TEB on the TEB8 departure after selecting it over the RUUDY 4 option. ATC remarked that the crew should have turned earlier, but the crew verified their FMS and autopilot were correct and continued without urgency or conflicts.

synopsis: A C208 pilot reported cabin contamination as TKS propeller anti-ice fluid enters the cockpit as a vapor in the nearly 500 degree engine compressor bleed air used for heating which is cooled by ambient air also exposed to the anti-ice fluid entering the lower cowling.
summary: A commercial pilot reported inhaling toxic TKS fluid fumes in a single-engine turboprop during icing conditions when the anti-ice and heating systems operated simultaneously. The fumes entered the cockpit via engine bleed air and cabin leaks, causing physical symptoms that resolved only when the heat was turned off.

synopsis: A330-300 First Officer reported slowing below assigned speed on final at EGLL following a wake vortex encounter.
summary: ATC assigned 160 KTS to 4 DME, but the Captain slowed to 155 KTS at 6 DME due to a wake turbulence encounter. After ATC queried and chastised the crew for the speed deviation, the aircraft completed a normal landing with no further issues.

synopsis: TRACON Developmental described an airspace incursion event during a training session when traffic and complexity increased beyond his/her capabilities.
summary: During a training session, a trainee controller issued an IFR clearance to a King Air departing ZZZ1, allowing it to approach an active MOA within 1.5 to 2 miles. The instructor admitted failing to take over or request assistance during high traffic, though Center confirmed no aircraft were in the MOA and no separation loss occurred.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: ZOA Controller noted an enroute aircraft approximately ten miles off course potentially leading to a loss of separation. After questioning the pilot, Military GPS interference was identified as the causal factor.
summary: Air Traffic Controller observed Air Carrier X at FL340, 10 miles south of course due to military GPS jamming. The controller alerted the pilot, preventing a potential conflict with an eastbound aircraft at FL325-350 that was laterally separated by 7 miles.

synopsis: ZAU Controller voiced concern regarding an ERAM dropped data block, recommending a return to the HOST RADAR system.
summary: An air traffic controller lost the data block for Aircraft X during descent due to a transponder code error causing an ERAM failure. The controller coordinated with adjacent sectors and reset the transponder to restore the track, noting the system's inability to display unrecognized codes is unsafe.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a probable loss of separation event when trying to relieve a controller who was overwhelmed, the reporter suggesting increased FLM coverage and delaying position take overs during these conditions.
summary: A relieving Air Traffic Controller observed a Radar North Controller issue conflicting vectors to a BE36 and TBM8, resulting in a loss of 1,000-foot vertical separation at 5,000 feet. The situation resolved naturally without intervention, though the reporter attributed the conflict to the relieved controller's poor sector management and inadequate supervision by the CIC.

synopsis: An ERJ crew on the DCA FRDMM 1 Arrival was deleting duplicate FRDMM FMS waypoints and failed to begin the descent which caused the aircraft to cross MORLL at FL211 instead of FL200.
summary: The flight crew, distracted by deleting duplicate FRDMM fixes in the FMS during the FRDMM 1 arrival, failed to set a proper descent rate and crossed MORLL at FL211 instead of the required FL200. ATC confirmed no violation occurred, and the crew attributed the error to FMS design requiring duplicate fix removal.

synopsis: Air Carrier night time arrival into COU landed with one side of the runway lights inoperative. ATC indicted a loss of some lights but was unsure of the exact location.
summary: Pilots conducting a night visual approach to Runway 20 at COU encountered asymmetric runway edge lights, with the left side dim or out while the right side remained bright. Despite the malfunction and high workload, the crew continued to a stabilized landing, later identifying the lighting failure as the primary threat.

synopsis: An A300 Captain reported unreliable pitot static instruments in icing and turbulence at FL220, but both pilots' instrument indications returned to normal at about 14,000 FT descending.
summary: The crew experienced unreliable airspeed and system failures at FL220 in turbulence, causing a 350-foot altitude deviation, followed by an uncommanded right turn during the final approach to Runway 5R. The pilot attributed the second event to a potential maintenance issue and simultaneous distraction during checklist duties, resulting in a hand-flown landing.

synopsis: C182 pilot discovers on a flight to MBO that his G1000 data pack does not include the area east of the Mississippi River. Jackson International airport Class C airspace is entered without clearance during landing.
summary: A pilot flying a Cessna with a G1000 lost GPS data while approaching Bruce Campbell Field in Mississippi due to an incomplete data pack. The pilot failed to contact Jackson Tower, resulting in a polite verbal warning upon landing.

synopsis: Scout pilot reports being intercepted and followed to his destination by a State Trooper. On the ground the reporter is accused of flying too low.
summary: A pipeline patrol pilot experienced a close encounter with a State Trooper helicopter while entering the traffic pattern at an uncontrolled airport. The trooper aggressively approached the aircraft, then confronted the pilot on the ramp, demanding identification and questioning weapon possession.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: K90 Controller suggested utilization of the ASR-9 RADAR system in lieu of CENRAP operations when the ASR-8 RADAR system is scheduled out of service, noting the ASR-9 operation maintains a higher degree of safety.
summary: An air traffic controller advised a Flight Line Manager against using CENRAP procedures on the ASR-8 radar during its scheduled outage. The controller recommended utilizing the ASR-9 system instead to maintain separation criteria and display accuracy, arguing it offers greater safety and efficiency.

synopsis: B737-300 First Officer reported loss of MCP in climb, leading to a decision to return to departure airport, where they made a safe overweight landing.
summary: During climb at 29,000 feet, the crew experienced a frozen Mode Control Panel and fuel totalizer MEL, forcing a return to the departure airport. They navigated thunderstorms with ATC assistance and performed an overweight landing, though the Captain refused to declare an emergency despite the First Officer's disagreement.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported getting the cabin altitude warning horn on climbout, at which point they realized the engine bleeds were off.
summary: During climb, the crew triggered an altitude warning at 11,000 feet due to engine bleeds being off and APU bleed on. After the First Officer corrected the bleed configuration, cabin altitude dropped below 10,000 feet, allowing the crew to resume climbing despite reported pressure to rush engine start procedures.

synopsis: A B737-700 Oil Filter Bypass light illuminated during climb. After completing the QRH procedure the engine was shut down, but no emergency was declared as the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: During climb through FL260, the crew experienced a Number 1 Engine Oil Filter Bypass light, shut down the engine, and returned to the departure airport without declaring an emergency. The aircraft landed uneventfully, though the issue had been reported on the previous flight but could not be duplicated by maintenance.

synopsis: Air Carrier pilot voiced concern regarding the FAA's failure to re-certify the ILS CAT II/III ILS system at BWI after runway maintenance had been completed, noting the significant disruption caused by this event.
summary: Pilots flying from ZZZ to BWI diverted to ZZZ1 due to low visibility and the unavailability of the Runway 10 CAT II/III ILS following maintenance. The crew managed safe passenger disembarkment at the congested ZZZ1 ramp without injury, though the event caused significant schedule disruption and increased operational risks.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A pilot reported that his clearance on the DTW PALACE FIVE included a transition on V116 at ZEGBI to BAGEL, but because the SID did not depict ZEGBI he was confused about where the transition would occur.
summary: The flight crew encountered a discrepancy where the filed routing waypoint ZEGBI was missing from the PALACE FIVE Departure clearance, though it appeared on the Low Altitude Enroute Chart. Both pilots verified the en route charts matched the filed routing and continued the flight without further incident.

synopsis: A B737-300's flaps failed to extend beyond 1 before landing, so delay vectors were taken but the QRH procedure was not completed before landing because the Captain wanted to get on the ground.
summary: During descent, the crew encountered a flap malfunction indicating position 1 instead of 5. The Captain elected to land without completing the QRH, resulting in brake cooling issues and a post-landing debrief acknowledging the need for greater assertiveness and checklist adherence.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported they got ECAM for 'BRAKING - AUTO BRAKE FAIL' on final. They elected to declare an emergency, go around and review the procedures, and landed normally with alternate brakes.
summary: The crew experienced an Auto Brake Fail ECAM at 3,000 feet on final, declared an emergency, and landed using alternate brakes after reviewing worst-case performance. The aircraft was towed to the gate following a fire truck inspection.

synopsis: An EMB-145 flight crew misread the 6,000 MSL crossing restriction at CORRA on the SWFFT RNAV STAR to BNA and descended more than a thousand feet below until queried and reassigned 5,000 by Approach Control. The reporter cited the saturation and complexity of the STAR chart as a contributing factor.
summary: The pilot misread the CORRA crossing restriction as 4,000 feet instead of 6,000 feet while descending on the SWFFT ONE RNAV STAR to Nashville. The error, attributed to a confusing chart layout and task saturation, caused an unintended descent to 4,700 feet before the pilot climbed and ATC assigned 5,000 feet.

synopsis: A Q400 pressurization malfunctioned during climb after takeoff and then failed climbing through FL185 so the crew descended and returned to the departure airport. While addressing this issue after takeoff the flaps remained at 10 were until 195 KTS.
summary: The flight crew experienced a pressurization failure and missed the acceleration height callout due to distraction, resulting in a flap overspeed and subsequent return to the departure airport. They landed overweight at 62,500 lbs after Maintenance Control advised continuing despite the recurring pressurization issue and unclear SOPs regarding emergency landings.

synopsis: A-320 fails to comply with the complex altitude and airspeed restrictions on the KOHOE RNAV STAR to DEN. The reporter believes the problems to be systemic to the A-320 autoflight systems and backs that opinion up by citing previous similar problems when attempting to comply with similar RNAV STAR arrivals at PHX and DEN.
summary: The flight crew encountered gross FMS errors during a managed descent on the KOHOE ONE RNAV STAR into Denver, where the system incorrectly calculated altitudes and speeds for "at or below" constraints. Pilots avoided violations by manually selecting Vertical Speed and speed modes to meet restrictions, noting the FMS failed to properly profile descents for soft constraints.

synopsis: After programming the ILS to Runway 19C at IAD some 150 NM out the flight crew of a CRJ-700 was surprised as they approached SUNYJ where the transitions to north or south operations emanate to find the wrong transitions and approach selected. In their haste to correct the programming the pilot flying disconnected the autopilot and the aircraft descended 700 FT below their cleared altitude.
summary: The pilot and First Officer experienced an FMS sequencing error and altitude deviation while enroute to IAD on the GIBBZ STAR. The pilot attributed the incident to task saturation and distraction while manually correcting the FMS discontinuity, resulting in an inadvertent descent to 6,300 feet before recovery.

synopsis: A B767-300'S FWD EQPT COOLING SUPPLY FAN was MEL'ed and after takeoff the FWD EQPT COOLING VALVE failed to close, thus preventing pressurization and equipment cooling so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The crew and maintenance encountered equipment cooling and lavatory issues after a B-Check, leading to an overweight emergency landing due to pressurization failure and cooling overheat. Maintenance later found the cooling valve was stuck open and incorrectly advised the crew that the condition was normal, causing the event.

synopsis: A B757 EICAS alerted LT HYD SYS PRESS so the crew completed the QRH first securing the engine driven pump, then as the fluid loss continued, secured the left electric hydraulic pump to slow fluid loss conserving it for the emergency landing.
summary: The crew managed a left engine hydraulic leak during cruise and descent by shutting off pumps, which caused slow gear and flap extension and PTU engagement. They declared an emergency, landed with 20 flaps on the longest runway, and taxied to the gate without ground assistance.

synopsis: An Avionics' Technician reports finding an electrical wire bundle chafing inside a P320 Ground Service/ Handling Power panel at the door hinge area, in the Main Equipment Center, on a B777-200 aircraft. Additional wires for an IFE power cut-off switch Service Bulletin (SB) and seat modifications increased the bundle size raising concerns about arcing and possible fire.
summary: A mechanic inspecting a B777-200 during a C-Check at ZZZ Dock-1 found wire interference with an electrical bundle inside the P320 panel during an IFE switch installation. The mechanic reported a potential arcing or fire hazard to the Lead Mechanic to ensure the issue was addressed.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot providing instruction at PVU described a near miss when ATC's instructions resulted in a conflict with other pattern traffic.
summary: A pilot and student in a small aircraft experienced a near-miss with a twin aircraft while executing a left 270-degree turn to final for Runway 18. The pilot initiated a hard left bank and called for a go-around after the twin appeared only 30 yards away, resulting in the twin landing full-stop and the pilot landing full-stop on Runway 18.

synopsis: A DA900EX developed cockpit smoke from an unknown source so an emergency was declared and the flight diverted to a nearby international airport.
summary: The crew declared an emergency due to unexplained cockpit smoke, and ATC vectored them to a suitable airport where the smoke cleared on final approach. The aircraft landed safely but was detained by government officials for 23 hours while exit visas were arranged, leaving the aircraft awaiting repairs.

synopsis: CLT Controller described an incorrect turn taken by an IFR departure when the wrong departure runway had been programed in the FMS, noting this was not an isolated event.
summary: A CRJ2 departing Runway 36C flew toward Runway 36R's initial waypoint because the pilot failed to update the FMS after a runway change. The controller issued a heading of 290 to avoid a CRJ9, noting that RNAV procedures and FUSION radar limitations contributed to the deviation.

synopsis: C90 reported a probable loss of separation event when two air carriers being vectored for parallel runways, one with equipment issues, failed to properly acknowledge a 'maintain visual separation' instruction.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported a loss of separation between Air Carrier X and Air Carrier Y during vectoring for parallel runways 9R and 10. The incident occurred because Air Carrier Y's pilot failed to execute instructed heading changes due to equipment issues, preventing the required visual separation.

synopsis: PHL Controller reported a possible loss of separation when traffic on final failed to respond appropriately to a visual approach clearance.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a heavy aircraft and a trailing A320 on final approach in windy conditions after the A320 pilot deviated to rejoin the localizer. The controller issued a visual approach clearance with visual separation instructions, but the pilot failed to provide a proper readback, prompting the controller to consider using ILS approaches instead of visual approaches in the future.

synopsis: PIT Controller described an unsafe condition when an air carrier taxied from the ramp to a de-icing area without contacting Ground resulting in a developing conflict with a fire truck.
summary: Air Carrier X taxied from the ramp to Deice Pad C without contacting Ground Control, forcing a fire truck to stop to avoid a collision. The pilot attributed the incident to confusion over taxi instructions and a lack of explicit clearance limits from Ramp Control.

synopsis: An Approach Controller reported one of several instances of complaints from flight crews about the complexity of the newer, 'optimized' RNAV STAR procedures into BNA. In this particular instance, the STAR in question was the RYYMN.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that an E135 pilot complained about safety margins while flying the RYYMN RNAV arrival, citing excessive heads-down automation work. The controller attributed potential conflicts to mixing RNAV and non-RNAV aircraft with differing speeds and altitudes, suggesting segregated arrival posts.

synopsis: TRACON Supervisor (FLM) receiving training reported a loss of separation event, noted the training provided on the position has been very sporadic and not in keeping with a reasonable chance to learn the sector.
summary: A trainee Flight Line Manager on the arrival position failed to slow Air Carrier Z, causing potential separation loss with Air Carrier Y and X due to sporadic radar training. The instructor intervened to prevent a worse situation, resulting in Air Carrier Z overshooting final and requiring expedited descent for Air Carrier X.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: EWR Controller elected not to issue mandated ASDE-X go-around instructions after positively observing the landing traffic had cleared the runway. The reporter claimed faulty ASDE-X logic as a contributing factor.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a night landing on Runway 29 and departure from Runway 22L while Runway 22R was closed due to a disabled aircraft. The controller ignored an ASDE-X alert for a go-around after visually confirming the preceding aircraft had cleared the runway, citing faulty system logic and the landing aircraft's critical flight stage.

synopsis: SCT Controller described a MVA event involving a BUR IFR departure and traffic inbound to VNY. The reporter acknowledged waiting for the NVY prior to issuing the BUR departure release would have been a better option.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller issued a 310-degree heading and 6,000-foot clearance to a CRJ7 departing Burbank Runway 33, causing the aircraft to climb below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude due to weather. The controller acknowledged the error, noting they should have denied the heading or delayed the departure to avoid the terrain conflict.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew describe last minute changes to the passenger count and bag loading that results in an inaccurate load sheet and an incorrect takeoff trim setting.
summary: Pilots reported that an -800 series aircraft experienced delayed rotation and excessive stick forces during takeoff due to incorrect stabilizer trim settings caused by weight and balance errors. Multiple passenger and baggage configuration changes led to a loading discrepancy that compromised controllability, requiring additional runway distance to lift off.

synopsis: After entering a new cruise ALT of FL320 vs FL340 on the PROG Page, an A319 Captain reports the autothrottles pulled back to idle and speed bug unexpectedly dropped to 221 KTS. Initial attempt to bug the speed up has no effect and the autopilot and autothrust are disengaged to return the aircraft to normal speed and correct an altitude overshoot. Once stabilized the autothrust system functions normally.
summary: The crew experienced an unexpected speed drop to 221 KTS and idle thrust after changing the FMGC cruise altitude to FL320. Manual intervention caused an 8-12 second engine spool delay and an inadvertent +400 FT altitude deviation before stabilizing at FL320.

synopsis: A B737 1L door seal did not seat properly and therefore the aircraft could not pressurize. The flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced a failed 1L door seal causing pressurization loss and air return. After leveling at 10,000 feet with the seal still unseated, they returned to the departure airport where the door was found closed but the seal remained unseated.

synopsis: A B777 EICAS alerted CTR TANKS LOW, but the right center tank would not turn off. The circuit breaker was pulled but because that procedure was not authorized, the Duty Manager diverted the aircraft and removed the crew.
summary: During cruise, the crew could not shut off a right center fuel pump despite an empty tank, fearing overheating. After pulling a circuit breaker to stop the pump, the crew was ordered to divert, declare an emergency, dump fuel, and was subsequently removed from the trip.

synopsis: An A300 Captain's window shattered at FL350 in cruise so an emergency was declared and the First Officer made the landing as blizzard conditions approached the airport.
summary: The Captain's windshield shattered at FL350 just prior to descent due to weather conditions. The crew declared an emergency, and the First Officer landed the aircraft safely without further incident.

synopsis: A CRJ200 attempted a climb to FL360 but because the aircraft was heavy with the temperature ISA +11, it could not climb above FL350 and an emergency was declared for an immediate descent after a stall warning.
summary: The pilot reported that during a climb to FL360 in heavy conditions, the aircraft lost airspeed and triggered the stick shaker due to being behind the power curve. The crew descended to FL340 after declaring an emergency, attributing the incident to inadequate attention to minimum published airspeeds for the high altitude and temperature.

synopsis: Air Carrier described a confused communications event with ATC, listing that the company practice of assigning similar four digit call signs within the same area at the same time is directly impacting safety.
summary: During cruise to IAH, Flight ABC and Flight ABG experienced a frequency confusion due to similar call signs, requiring Houston ATC to intervene. The pilot attributed this recurring safety threat to company marketing policies assigning similar flight numbers in the same area.

synopsis: DFW Tower issued a low altitude alert to an aircraft on the VOR Runway 31L approach during a night approach in gusty, turbulent weather conditions.
summary: The pilot flying a visual approach to Runway 31L at night received an altitude alert from DFW Tower at 1,400 feet and climbed to 2,000 feet. The pilot attributed the alert to rapidly rising local pressure while continuing the approach in moderate turbulence and windshear.

synopsis: An EMB145 crew did not set the correct barometric altimeter setting and realized, after ATC asked them to verify their altitude, that they were 500 FT low.
summary: During descent, the crew mistakenly set altimeter 29.56 instead of the correct 29.06 due to low light, turbulence, and icing, causing a lower-than-assigned altitude. After ATC queried the altitude, the crew reset the altimeters and immediately climbed to the assigned 12,000 feet, continuing to the destination without incident.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An aircraft approaching CAK in changing weather conditions was 700 FT low on approach because of an incorrect barometric altimeter setting which was detected first by a low radar altitude, then by ATC.
summary: Pilots vectored for ILS 23 into CAK descended to 3,100 FT but realized they were low due to an incorrect altimeter setting of 30.35 instead of the correct 29.35. After ATC confirmed the clearance and setting, the crew reset their altimeters and climbed back to 3,100 FT.

synopsis: A CRJ200 Dispatcher twice used the SELCAL system to contact a flight crew during a critical, sterile flight environment period to relay non-essential crew scheduling information.
summary: Dispatchers sent two non-essential SELCAL ACARS messages regarding crew scheduling during taxi and approach, overpowering ground instructions and violating sterile cockpit rules. The crew verified safety but criticized the abuse of the dispatch link for non-flight-related activities.

synopsis: CE680 Captain reports a runway incursion taxiing from the FBO ramp via Taxiway B to Runway 19 at FRG. Westbound Taxiway B is followed instead of northbound B.
summary: The pilot of an aircraft at FRG entered Runway 19 while taxiing via Bravo due to distraction from severe weather, FMS errors, and an ELT alarm. The incursion occurred because the pilot misinterpreted a location sign and failed to verify the runway sign before crossing hold short lines.

synopsis: During descent, a B767-300 RT BLD DUCT warning alerted then extinguished after the QRH procedure was completed, but as a precaution an emergency declared for landing.
summary: During descent at FL250, the crew experienced an RT BLD DUCT warning with anti-ice systems active. After following QRH procedures and declaring a precautionary emergency, they landed safely with the right engine bleed, crossover, and wing anti-ice off, followed by a maintenance log entry.

synopsis: A B767-300 Left Hydraulic System quantity decreased to 0.15RF so an emergency was declared and the flight diverted to an airport for an overweight landing where another aircraft was available to continue the flight.
summary: The crew diverted and declared an emergency due to a left hydraulic quantity indication of 0.15RF just prior to coast out. They performed a soft overweight landing at 327,000 lbs with 200 FPM vertical speed, after which passengers and cargo were transferred to a replacement aircraft.

synopsis: A Captain questions whether the Illustrated Parts Catalog (IPC) may be showing the wrong Part Number (P/N) for their MD-83 series aircraft after two occurrences where he noticed incorrect Fuel Quantity Indicators had been installed on the same airplane.
summary: The pilot reported that an incorrect Fuel Quantity Indicator was installed on an MD-83 during pre-departure checks, a recurrence of an issue found five days prior. The pilot suspects the Illustrated Parts Catalog lists the wrong part number for this aircraft type.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air Carrier landing MEM and cleared for a visual approach adjusted his flight track to follow traffic. The reporter was questioned by ATC and the flight crew informed the subject turn-away from the airport was not authorized.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway 27 at MEM, the pilot turned right to maintain separation from preceding traffic after ATC cleared them to follow. A controller subsequently reprimanded the crew for turning away from the airport and vectored them out of the approach, though the pilot maintained that visual clearance transfers separation responsibility to the flight crew.

synopsis: When ATC deleted their speed restriction at MNSTR on the GEELA RNAV STAR to PHX the flight crew of a B737-700 was uncertain of how to do so in the FMC while retaining the crossing window above 15,000 and below 16,000. They opted to exit VNAV PATH and continue their descent in speed intervene mode in anticipation the FMC predicted crossing would comply with the restriction. It didn't and they crossed the waypoint 800 FT low.
summary: During descent into PHX, the flight crew deleted a speed restriction at MNSTR, which inadvertently removed the associated altitude constraint, causing an early descent to 14,200 feet. The pilot attributed the deviation to FMC limitations and selecting Speed Intervention instead of maintaining VNAV PATH or manually entering the altitude floor.

synopsis: For reasons unknown the FMS on their B737-700 dropped out of VNAV while descending on the RIIVR RNAV STAR, Runway 24R at LAX. The aircraft descended about 400 FT below the crossing restriction at MINZA.
summary: The flight crew descended via RIIVR Arrival 24R but the aircraft failed to level at 10,000 feet, descending to approximately 9,650 feet because VNAV disengaged. The pilot used CWS pitch to stop the descent, re-engaged VNAV, and completed an uneventful approach and landing.

synopsis: A B737-500 flight crew was unable to comply with an ATC directed crossing restriction. The restriction was noted as an 'expect to cross at...' fix on the arrival plate.
summary: The pilot forgot to load the COACH crossing restriction at 11,000 feet into the FMC, resulting in the aircraft being high at 9,000 feet. Although the crew requested relief from Center, the clearance was unclear until Houston Approach verbally verified the restriction was removed, allowing an uneventful landing.

synopsis: A B737-300 suffered a close encounter with a light aircraft while on approach to ONT. TCAS and ATC gave conflicting resolution advisories and the flight crew appropriately follows those from TCAS. The vertical separation was approximated at 200 feet but no horizontal estimate was provided.
summary: The crew of an aircraft on final approach to ONT 26R received a TCAS RA to descend while ATC instructed a climb due to a nearby general aviation aircraft. The pilots followed the TCAS RA, resulting in a safe pass with the GA aircraft approximately 200 feet above them, after which the approach was resumed.

synopsis: While climbing through FL300 and returning to the departure airport after a missed approach, a B737-500 pressurization failed but during the descent was recovered using MAN AC so the cabin did not exceed 12,000 FT.
summary: The crew diverted a Boeing 737 due to weather, then experienced a cabin altitude warning while climbing to FL350. They descended to 16,000 feet, managed the pressurization issue without declaring an emergency, and landed safely, resulting in the aircraft being taken out of service for inspection.

synopsis: A320 flight crew experiences a Green Hydraulic system low pressure followed by a reservoir low level ECAM climbing out of 10,000 feet. An emergency is declared and the flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: During departure, the crew encountered Green hydraulic low pressure and reservoir warnings, causing a loss of nose wheel steering. They declared an emergency, returned for an uneventful landing, and were towed to the gate after fire services confirmed hydraulic fluid leakage.

synopsis: An ERJ-190 flight crew declared an emergency and returned to their departure airport after receiving amber level vibration from the left engine.
summary: The flight crew experienced a left engine LP vibration indication of 4.6 at 100 KIAS during takeoff, limiting N1 to 60%. They returned for a precautionary engine-out landing, and maintenance later identified a chip detection message.

synopsis: EMB145 First Officer reports a track deviation after being cleared direct to a fix and entering it into the FMC but failing to select NAV on the FGCP. ATC detects the error and issues headings to the reporter and another aircraft to avoid conflict.
summary: During cruise, the flight crew failed to engage LNAV after loading a new STAR, causing the aircraft to maintain an incorrect heading instead of tracking direct to OZZZY. This deviation required immediate ATC intervention to avoid traffic, stemming from a lack of cross-checking navigation mode selection after route changes.

synopsis: EMB145 First Officer reports calling for the flaps to be retracted at the appropriate time but a radio transmission from the Tower interrupts the process and the flaps remain at 9. A flap over speed ensues.
summary: During the departure climb of an E145, the crew failed to retract flaps after takeoff due to an interrupted flow and fatigue, resulting in sluggish acceleration and an ATC inquiry. The First Officer eventually noticed the 9-degree flap extension on the EICAS and retracted them at 250-260 KIAS, allowing for a safe landing.

synopsis: DHC200 Captain experiences a fuel leak during climbout via the fuel gauge and visually from the left wing. Flight returns to departure airport for an uneventful landing and taxi to the gate.
summary: During climbout, the pilot observed a rapid fuel drop and visible leaks from NACA vents and hinges on the Number 1 side. The crew returned for a visual approach, landed without incident, and expedited deplaning without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: CE750 flight crew reports apparently accepting a clearance for another flight departing TEB on the RUUDY 4 departure and starting a climb to 6,000 FT direct to ELVAE.
summary: During initial climb from TEB on the RUUDY 4 SID, the crew mistakenly accepted a clearance for ELVAE and 6,000 feet intended for another aircraft. ATC later corrected the error, instructing the crew to climb to 10,000 feet and fly heading 270, attributing the confusion to high workload and prior deviations from published departures.

synopsis: BE400 Captain as the pilot not flying in the right seat hears the trim warning sound and notes the pilot flying struggling to level off at 2,000 FT. The autopilot/trim disconnect switch is pressed and held by the pilot not flying as the pilot flying detects the trim switch 'hat' is stuck in the nose up position. The remainder of the flight is uneventful and Maintenance can find no faults.
summary: During the third leg to PWK, the PIC hand-flew while the First Officer noticed the pitch trim stuck nose-up at 1,900 feet. The First Officer disconnected the autopilot/trim, allowing the aircraft to briefly reach 2,300 feet before returning to the assigned 2,000 feet; subsequent checks found the trim system operational.

synopsis: An MD83 engine failed just after rotation with snow falling. The crew was vectored for an ILS but an incorrect ILS frequency necessitated a go around. The second attempt was successful. Once on the ground the fire department reported visible damage to the left engine.
summary: The flight crew experienced a left engine failure with loud bangs immediately after rotation during a snowy departure. They returned for an overweight landing after ATC provided an erroneous ILS frequency, forcing a go-around before a safe landing and ARFF inspection.

synopsis: A B737 First Officer reported detecting a leaking right engine bleed valve after engine start. Maintenance deactivated the valve and placed it on MEL. On the next leg, in a different aircraft, the same problem arose and the Captain chose to ignore it, despite some insistence from the First Officer.
summary: The First Officer reported that the Captain ignored repeated indications of a leaking right engine bleed valve on a replacement aircraft, despite similar issues in Houston. The Captain refused to return to the gate for maintenance, dismissing the 20 psi reading as unlikely, and flew the aircraft to destination without incident.

synopsis: B767-300 First Officer reports a RT BLD DUCT LEAK msg descending through FL250. QRH procedures are complied with and flight continues to destination for an uneventful landing.
summary: The Relief Pilot experienced a Right Bleed Duct Leak message while descending through FL250. After executing QRH procedures to isolate the right bleed, pack, and AC, an emergency was declared, resulting in an uneventful landing.

synopsis: When they failed to properly configure their avionics for the RNAV Approach to Runway 11 at EWR while operating in heavy rain a turbulence the flight crew of a widebody initiated a go around and diverted to JFK following receipt of an EGPWS 'Terrain' warning and a low altitude alert from the Tower.
summary: The crew flying an RNAV/GPS 11 approach to Newark in severe weather and turbulence failed to engage PROF mode, causing an unstable descent and GPWS terrain warning. The Captain initiated a go-around after a delayed autopilot setup, and the flight diverted to JFK due to the altitude bust caused by high workload and adverse conditions.

synopsis: An A300 First Officer reported crossing DYLAN high on the PHLBO 3 RNAV arrival due to strong tailwinds and turbulence. The Captain was the pilot flying using LNAV and VNAV. The autopilot was disconnected in an attempt to make the restriction.
summary: The Captain manually flew an Airbus during a night IMC descent into EWR after disconnecting the autopilot to avoid crossing the DYLIN restriction 1,500 feet high due to Profile mode failing in heavy rain and tailwinds. The crew reported crossing DYLIN 500 feet high, maintained separation, and received a vector to final approach.

synopsis: Two maintenance controllers and a Lead Mechanic report about the need for clarification of MELs 27-92-02C and 27-64-01A, when applied to ECAM 'F/CTL Spoiler Fault' displays that occur during engine starts, on their A321 aircraft.
summary: A mechanic incorrectly applied MEL 27-92-02C for an ECAM 'F/CTL SPLR FAULT' due to high workload and confusion with a past incident. The MEL was later reclassified to 27-64-01A, and the aircraft was swapped for maintenance where a successful SEC-3 reset cleared the fault.

synopsis: A B777-200 aircraft suddenly rolled backwards from a terminal gate during preparations for tow. A lavatory truck was still connected to the aircraft.
summary: A B777-200 rolled back at the gate while the reporter rode brakes after releasing them, with a lavatory truck still attached and the assessment form incomplete. The driver reported the rollback and asked to check on the lavatory technician's safety.

synopsis: BE40 Captain reports exceeding the SID mandated altitude by 500 FT during a Runway 24 departure from TEB due to a caution light distraction.
summary: During departure from Runway 24 at TEB, caution lights distracted the pilot flying, causing a 500-foot deviation from the SID altitude. The pilot immediately corrected the error, received an ATC 'ident' request, and the crew agreed to improve CRM to prevent future distractions.

synopsis: G200 Captain reported a wake vortex encounter shortly after takeoff from VHHH that resulted in a roll and a track deviation from the assigned SID.
summary: The pilot departed Hong Kong on Runway 7R using the BEKOl3A departure and encountered suspected wake turbulence shortly after takeoff. This caused a sharp 60-degree left bank and course deviation, which the pilot corrected while maintaining terrain visibility.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: General Aviation pilot describes tall trees on both approaches to 1S6, which the Airport Board refuses to address.
summary: A pilot reported that tall fir trees at Priest River Airport (1S6) infringe on landing approaches, while local officials neglected safety issues like non-functional lights and lack of fuel. The pilot attributed the deteriorating conditions to unqualified board members and received an unhelpful response from an FAA representative.

synopsis: Air Carrier on a Visual Approach to MHV was restricted by ATC at an altitude that required a go around. The restriction to clear other unknown airspace.
summary: Air Carrier X pilots encountered conflicting altitude instructions from Approach Control during a visual approach to MHV, where ATC restricted descent below 7,000 FT due to protected airspace. Confusion over clearance requirements led to an unstabilized approach, a missed approach, and a subsequent IFR cancellation to circle land on Runway 30.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A corporate aircraft expediting taxi for night takeoff incurred HNL Runway 8L at Taxiway E as the First Officer was heads down and the Captain confused by the signage.
summary: The flight crew at HNL crossed hold short lines for Runway 8L during a night taxi due to time pressure, poor markings, and lack of situational awareness. The Captain stopped the aircraft after realizing the deviation, which was attributed to confusing airport layout and inadequate lighting at the hot spot.

synopsis: LR40 Captain reports an airborne conflict with a DA42 during a visual approach to BZN. Tower called the traffic and TCAS commanded an RA climb without showing the traffic or announcing a TA first.
summary: While descending on a high right downwind at 8,500 feet, the crew received a TCAS Resolution Advisory for a DA42 crossing at 7,700 feet after Salt Lake City Center failed to provide traffic advisories. The crew executed an immediate climb, passing within 500 feet horizontally of the other aircraft, and later questioned a potential radar blind spot.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: A turboprop pilot requested 360 gallons of fuel departing Canada but was fueled with 360 liters instead. This error was confirmed when airborne and the reporter diverted for fuel. Illness, fatigue, and maintenance delays were cited as factors.
summary: The pilot requested 360 gallons of fuel but was inadvertently fueled with 360 liters due to a unit confusion at the Canadian FBO. After discovering the discrepancy during climbout, the pilot diverted to Columbus (CMH) to refuel, citing fatigue and prior maintenance issues as contributing factors to the delayed recognition of the error.

synopsis: A C172 pilot became disoriented approaching OLM due to low clouds and visibilities. The Tower was eventually contacted and provided the information necessary for the reporter to become reoriented.
summary: A pilot flying a VOR/ADF-equipped aircraft southwest of OLM became disoriented in deteriorating weather and low clouds due to delayed corrective action and poor navigation equipment usage. After contacting the tower for assistance, the pilot was guided to a safe landing within the Class D surface area.

synopsis: A Maintenance Quality Assurance Manager for a Cargo Operator report the lack of updated information in Cessna's 208 Series Airframe Illustrated Parts Catalog (IPC), Service Bulletins, Avionics Installation Manual and Wiring Manuals. Data from 1997 for Avionics Master Switches, CM3589-30, still had not been incorporated in the revised 2011 IPC Manual resulting in an incorrect part installation.
summary: A mechanic discovered incorrect Avionics Master Switch part numbers on a Cessna C-208 after replacement, noting that Cessna had updated the part in 1997 without revising manuals. The outcome was that the mechanic installed the recognized part while highlighting that manufacturers are not required to update documentation promptly.

synopsis: DA40 pilot experiences a rough running engine at 7,500 FT, switches fuel selector from the right tank to the left, and diverts to the nearest airport. Low fuel and an inaccurate fuel gauge is determined to be the cause.
summary: A pilot flying VFR at 7,500 feet declared an emergency due to engine sputtering caused by low fuel and a faulty sensor. After landing safely, refueling, and verifying the issue with a mechanic, the pilot completed the flight without recurrence until an A&P confirmed the defective fuel sensor days later.

synopsis: BE33 pilot reports a NMAC in the traffic pattern at PDK.
summary: A pilot flying VFR through Atlanta Class B airspace experienced a near-miss with a Waco aircraft while on right downwind for Runway 20R at PDK. The pilot attributes the conflict to the Waco flying opposite direction, potential radar misidentification by the tower, and the Waco lacking Mode C transponder.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a loss of separation event during a go around, the ATC instructions confused when a Supervisor countermanded previously coordinated headings between the Tower and TRACON.
summary: A Local Controller issued a conflicting 070 heading to Air Carrier X after a Supervisor's ambiguous instruction during a go-around caused by Air Carrier Y's slow roll. The reporter attributes the resulting loss of separation to the Supervisor's uncoordinated intervention and the controller's failure to question the unsafe heading.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a failed coordination event between facility controllers and the pilot of an aircraft inbound to a non-towered airport that resulted an ALNOT and Search and Rescue intervention.
summary: Commander 114 landed at ZZZ but failed to cancel its IFR flight plan due to pilot distraction during parking in rain. Air Traffic Controllers initiated a search and rescue after missing the cancellation during a handoff briefing, though the aircraft was found safe on the ramp.

synopsis: PSC Controller described multiple runway incursion events involving snow removal operations noting the vehicle operators are in need of additional training.
summary: Airport vehicle operators Snowplow 1 and Airport 2 entered Runway 30 and other control surfaces without ATC approval during snow removal. The reporter attributed these unauthorized incursions to a lack of training and recommended remedial instruction for the operators.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reports loss of Green Hydraulic System pressure at FL340 due to loss of Green System fluid. Crew elects to continue to destination and lands normally after using alternate means of landing gear extension.
summary: During cruise, the Captain observed a decreasing Green Hydraulic System fluid level that triggered a Low Quantity ECAM. The crew followed procedures, consulted maintenance, and executed a normal landing using gravity gear extension before being towed to the gate.

synopsis: CRJ200 flight crew discovers that the right engine is unresponsive to thrust lever movement when attempting to retard thrust for descent. An emergency is declared, the engine is shut down, and a single engine landing ensues.
summary: The First Officer and Captain encountered a jammed right thrust lever at 98% N1 during descent, preventing speed control. They followed the QRH to secure the engine at 14,000 feet, declared an emergency, and completed a safe single-engine landing.

synopsis: Despite a forewarning from Maintenance regarding the possibility of residual air conditioning odors due to cleaning of the engines the previous night, the flight crew of an ERJ-170 elected to return to their departure airport after takeoff due to the level of contamination and the fact that the associated haze had appeared to trigger a lavatory smoke alarm.
summary: Pilots and cabin crew experienced a strong odor and a false lavatory smoke indication shortly after takeoff due to residual fumes from an overnight engine cleaning. The crew declared an emergency, returned to the airport, and landed safely with no injuries or evacuation required.

synopsis: As they awaited their gate after arrival the flight crew of an ERJ-170 experienced a shorted windshield heat event that blazed momentarily and spider webbed the Captain's windshield.
summary: While parked at the gate, a spark from the Captain's side lower windshield heat strip caused flames and spider cracks in the laminated glass. The crew deselected the heat, consulted Maintenance, and taxied to the gate without further incident.

synopsis: DASH 8-100 Captain reports descending too low during a visual approach and receiving a 'Too Low, Gear' EGPWS warning and climbing up to 1,000 FT from about 600 FT.
summary: The pilot flying descended below the intended altitude during a visual approach to an uncontrolled airport due to distraction from pointing out ground features, violating sterile cockpit procedures. An EGPWS "Too Low, Gear" warning at 600 FT MSL prompted an immediate climb to 1,000 FT, allowing a safe interception of the glidepath and normal landing.

synopsis: MD83 Captain experiences a cargo fire warning at cruise altitude and complies with QRH procedures. Flight diverts to a suitable airport where the warning is determined to be false.
summary: During cruise, the crew received a false FWD CARGO FIRE warning, discharged the fire bottle, and landed enroute. Maintenance inspection of the forward cargo compartment revealed no indication of fire.

synopsis: IAH Controller experienced confusion with regard to similar sounding call signs noting the problem is becoming more serious with no resolution in sight.
summary: Local West controller cleared Flight ABC for takeoff, but the pilot read back as Flight ABG when switching to North Departure. The controller verified the call sign change with other facilities, attributing the confusion to poor company communication regarding flight number changes and similar-sounding call signs.

synopsis: ZMA Controller voiced concern regarding the actions taken by the TMU during very busy and complex traffic periods, noting FLM's should counterman TMU decisions when warranted.
summary: An air traffic controller managing heavy traffic and weather reported that departing traffic from the TMU sector compromised spacing between a CL60 and C560. The controller attributed the conflict to TMU failing to provide adequate in-trail spacing and ignoring sector-specific arrival restrictions.

synopsis: ZMA Controller experienced a loss of separation event when traffic and weather introduced complications difficult to overcome, the reporter listing the lack of pre-planning between management and the TMU as a causal factor.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managing a trainee issued conflicting headings to a Gulfstream and a B737 near a weather line, triggering a conflict alert. The controller attributed the near-miss to insufficient spacing and poor pre-planning between management and the Traffic Management Unit.

synopsis: ZMA Controller experienced a loss of separation event during a very busy and complex traffic period citing Traffic Management shortfalls as contributory.
summary: A busy Miami Center controller and a Gulfstream pilot reported a loss of separation between a C560 and CL60 at FL350 due to excessive traffic volume and weather deviations. The pilot also experienced a TCAS alert during a hurried descent to 28,000 feet, attributing the safety compromise to flow control inaction and controller stress.

synopsis: When they received a cabin altitude warning climbing through FL320 the flight crew of a B737-500 declared an emergency, descended to a safe altitude and diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: During climb through 32,000 FT, the flight crew experienced a cabin altitude warning at 10,000 FT with no abnormal lights. After completing emergency checklists and descending to 10,000 FT, they diverted and landed safely due to the unknown cause of the pressurization issue.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier First Officer did not commence the GPWS escape maneuver while on a RNAV Runway 28R approach to BOI in night VMC conditions.
summary: During a night arrival to BOI, the First Officer expedited descent due to turbulence and offset the flight path to avoid terrain, triggering a 'Caution Terrain' warning after gear extension. The pilot immediately corrected the flight path, and the aircraft landed without incident.

aircraft: Embraer Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Two pilots report noticing during the cruise phase on an Embraer ERJ-145 series aircraft;that the Gust Lock Thrust Lever Bar had been installed upside down (backwards). A notch on the bar was incorrectly positioned at the thrust levers, allowing number two thrust lever to be increased more than number one thrust lever.
summary: The First Officer discovered during cruise that a mechanic had incorrectly installed the Elevator Gust Lock thrust lever bar following maintenance. The bar was reversed, allowing the Number Two engine thrust lever to advance further than the Number One, a discrepancy not caught during preflight checks and reported upon arrival.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier crew reported a rejected takeoff on MMPB Runway 35 because a Mexican Air Carrier aircraft entered the runway as they were just past 80 KTS.
summary: The crew aborted takeoff at 80 knots on Runway 35 after a Mexican carrier aircraft ignored hold-short instructions and entered the runway. The incident occurred due to poor visibility of the intruder until its landing lights were seen, resulting in a safe 4,000-foot stop and subsequent normal departure.

synopsis: B737NG flight crew experiences an engine failure at FL340. Indications are that the spar fuel valve has closed uncommanded. Attempts to restart the engine during descent are unsuccessful and the flight diverts to a suitable airport.
summary: The crew experienced a Number 2 engine flameout and rollback at FL340 due to a closed spar valve preventing fuel flow. They declared an emergency, diverted to ZZZ, and executed an overweight single-engine landing with no abnormalities found.

synopsis: A DHC-8-200 on a test flight developed a fuel imbalance which the Mechanic on board could not balance and so on return to the airport a ground observer commented that something was hang from or coming from the left wing.
summary: During a maintenance check flight, the crew observed a 400-pound fuel imbalance on the left tank that persisted despite transfer attempts. Although no leak was detected in-flight, ground personnel reported an object hanging from the left wing on short final, resulting in an unsatisfactory flight completion.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic describes his efforts to determine the cause of a Left Engine Oil By-pass Light that illuminated on a B737-700 aircraft prior to landing. Aircraft was released the following day, but required an air turnback, resulting in an engine change.
summary: A mechanic on a B737-700 investigated a left engine oil bypass light during an overnight check but could not duplicate the fault or remove the scavenge filter bowl. The aircraft was released to service per Maintenance Control instructions, but it later required an engine change, leading the mechanic to regret not delaying the flight to force filter removal.

synopsis: A Maintenance Controller reports how miscommunication and misunderstanding between himself and a B737-700 flight crew led to a takeoff departure with both Engine Electronic Controls (EEC) in the Alternate Mode. Number 2 Engine Control Light had illuminated after pushback.
summary: A maintenance controller incorrectly deferred an illuminated Number 2 Engine Control Light on a B737-700 by misinterpreting the crew's report and MEL requirements. The aircraft departed with the light extinguishing before lift-off, but the controller later realized the error and arranged for the aircraft to be returned for repairs.

synopsis: Two Maintenance Base mechanics report how a false indication of applied torque to a seat row locking shear pin contributed to a B777-200 coach passenger seat coming loose from a floor track in flight.
summary: Two mechanics installing upgraded economy seats on a B777-200 reported that debris and carpet in the seat track caused a shear pin to give a false torque indication. This resulted in a seat coming loose during a subsequent trip, requiring repair at a line station.

synopsis: On a clear, calm day the pilot of a Globe Swift suffered loss of flight control shortly after lift off and the airplane banked to the left and impacted the ground. The pilot exited the aircraft and was uninjured.
summary: The pilot reported that during the initial climb after takeoff, the aircraft suddenly pitched left and became unresponsive to controls at 50 to 75 feet. The pilot attempted to flare and reduce throttle before impact, after which the aircraft came to rest and emergency services arrived.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Airbus A320 Series ECAM alerted left overwing emergency open after takeoff so the flight immediately returned to land at the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew returned to the departure airport shortly after takeoff due to an ECAM warning indicating an open left overwing emergency exit. The decision to land immediately was made because the aircraft was near company maintenance, whereas continuing to the destination would have left them without support.

synopsis: EMB-145XR F/O reported after departure cabin began to depressurize at FL240. Crew ran the QRH, declared an emergency, and returned to departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a rapid cabin altitude rise to 10,000 feet at FL240, triggering an emergency descent and oxygen mask deployment. They manually controlled pressurization to stabilize the cabin, returned to the departure airport, and landed 400 lbs over structural weight without injury.

synopsis: G-200 fractional Captain reported noting after takeoff they got a 'CABIN DOOR' warning and the aircraft did not pressurize. Flight returned to departure airport.
summary: The pilot flying returned to the departure airport after a 'cabin door' warning and rapid cabin pressurization rate indicated a door issue. The aircraft landed safely at maximum landing weight, though ground air brakes failed to deploy, requiring passenger assistance until recovery crews arrived.

synopsis: B1900D flight crew reported noticing an electrical smell followed by failure of the Captain's EADI. An emergency was declared and the flight diverted to nearest suitable airport.
summary: During cruise, the Captain detected a greasy odor followed by melting plastic and a flickering EADI, suspecting a potential cockpit fire. The crew declared an emergency, landed at ZZZ, and safely unloaded passengers with professional support from ATC, fire, and ground agents.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew reported Captain's window outer pane shattered. An emergency was declared, and the flight diverted to a nearby suitable airport.
summary: During cruise at FL390, the Captain's outer windshield shattered, reducing visibility and safety margins in icing conditions. The crew declared an emergency, descended clear of thunderstorms, and diverted to the nearest suitable airport due to snow and ice at the destination.

synopsis: After engine ground runs, flight checks and several hours of troubleshooting for a recurring Caution FLI/No Tq (torque) indication on a Eurocopter helicopter, an Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) notices a cannon plug to the Stepper Motor on Number 2 Engine was not seated all the way. Same issue happened before with same results.
summary: A mechanic troubleshooting a "Caution FLI/No Tq" on Engine 2 during maintenance found a cannon plug to the Stepper Motor was not fully seated. After securing the plug, the aircraft passed all checks and was released for return to service.

synopsis: A Cessna 421 entered an uncommanded pitch over at 8,000 FT with the autopilot engaged. The pilot recovered at about 2,000 FT after the autopilot circuit breaker was pulled.
summary: The pilot reported an uncommanded nose-down dive at 8,000 feet after engaging the autopilot, caused by a failure of all disconnect switches. A passenger pulled the circuit breaker to disengage the system, allowing recovery at 2,000 feet and a safe diversion landing.

synopsis: When the right engine of their PA-31 started to surge and display increasing oil and cylinder head temperatures the flight crew performed an in-flight shutdown, declared an emergency with ATC, and diverted to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The pilot and co-pilot experienced right engine surge and rising temperatures after climbout, prompting a precautionary shutdown and emergency declaration. A mechanic later determined the cause was a partially failed right magneto, and the aircraft landed safely.

synopsis: A C550 crew hit the grass during a go around after encountering wake vortices during landing in OKC.
summary: Two experienced pilots flying a light aircraft encountered severe wake turbulence from a preceding Airbus A330 during final approach, causing a violent roll and buffet at 100 feet AGL.
