summary: During climb through 12,000 feet, both AC tie bus relays tripped, triggering stick shaker activation and emergency power. The crew returned to the departure airport, burned fuel to reduce landing weight to 108,000 lbs, and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: A Q400 crew, during a cold and windy enroute stop, decided not to check a report from the ground crew of a 'flap' sticking out of the cargo door. During the subsequent climb out toward mountainous terrain they experienced pressurization problems, but fortunately were able to reroute and stay at an altitude at which pressurization below 10,000 MSL could be maintained. Maintenance determined the un-investigated flap was a fully deployed cargo door depressurization flap.
summary: The Captain departed with a misaligned forward cargo door flap after ground personnel dismissed the issue. This caused a cabin pressurization warning at 12,700 feet, requiring a descent to 10,000 feet, and maintenance later confirmed the flap was fully open and out of adjustment.

synopsis: An FAA Inspector, boarding the CRJ-200 for an enroute check, discovered the aft cabin bulkhead louvers and the louver guard adjoining the cargo compartment were damaged rendering the jet unfit for service until properly repaired or replaced. The inability to seal off the cargo compartment would have compromised the safety of flight in the event of a cargo compartment fire.
summary: During an enroute turn, an FAA Inspector discovered a damaged aft cabin bulkhead exhaust louver guard and non-flush case, likely caused by ground loading. The reporter concluded this airworthiness issue could have endangered the aircraft in a cargo fire and recommended updating flight attendant preflight manuals to include checking for flush louver cases.

synopsis: An ERJ-170 flight crew deiced four times before the aircraft remained acceptably clear of snow and he determined after the fact that during the first deice cycles heavy snow was falling for which no holdover time exists. During the final deice cycle the Deice Crew acknowledged the aircraft did not remain clean during the first three cycles, but they failed to alert the crew.
summary: The flight crew experienced deice fluid failure during heavy snow while taxiing to Runway 3, causing a return to the gate. The failure occurred because snow intensity reached heavy levels with no holdover time, a condition the crew missed due to outdated ATIS visibility reports.

synopsis: FAA Inspector points out worn skid shoes and missing shoe attach bolts to EC135 pilot.
summary: During a post-landing ramp check, an FAA Inspector found missing bolts and worn skid shoes on the aircraft, which the pilot had missed during preflight. The aircraft was grounded immediately due to the damage, which the pilot attributed to difficult visibility and heavy training use.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 'R AOA' Caution Message alerted after takeoff, but the Captain mistakenly ran the L and R AOA HEAT which directed that the aircraft remain clear of icing so the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew diverted to the departure airport after mistakenly selecting the wrong QRH checklist for an AOA heat caution in icing conditions. This error, caused by high workload and turbulence, led to an unnecessary return based on the false assumption that AOA heat failure prohibited flight in known icing.

synopsis: An MD-11 developed two separate electrical system malfunctions while taxiing for takeoff. On the first takeoff attempt the Electrical System Controller failed, on the second attempt an IDG failed.
summary: The flight crew aborted takeoff on Runway 08 due to an 'ELEC Alerts' level two alert caused by a faulty Electrical System Controller and IDG. After disconnecting the IDG and deferring both items per MEL, the aircraft departed and arrived at its destination without further incident.

synopsis: An Air Ambulance pilot reported that at 2,000 FT, seven miles southwest of POM, his helicopter's Garmin 530 and 430 simultaneously lost the GPS signal with both displays indicating no satellite signal for several minutes.
summary: A helicopter pilot reported simultaneous loss of reception to both Garmin 530 and 430 GPS receivers while flying eastbound at 2,000 feet MSL, 7 miles west of the POMONA VORTAC. The aircraft was straight and level with the autopilot engaged and coupled to the Garmin 530 at the time of the incident.

synopsis: A Corporate HS125 First Officer discussed his Captain's confusion and unfamiliarity while taxiing at and departing from BOS.
summary: The First Officer corrected the Pilot in Command's failure to engage NAV coupling on the BLZZR 1 departure from BOS Runway 9R below 1,000 feet, which caused a course deviation. The PIC attributed the error to task saturation from taxi confusion, adverse weather, and unfamiliarity with new procedures.

synopsis: A Falcon 20 engine failed during climb so an emergency was declared and the checklist completed. The crew then restarted the engine, undeclared the emergency and continued to their filed destination.
summary: The crew declared an emergency during departure due to a Number 2 Engine failure but successfully restarted it and canceled the emergency. Upon arrival, they grounded the aircraft for maintenance to further diagnose the problem.

synopsis: An Air Ambulance pilot reported the simultaneous loss of his Garmin 530 and 430 GPS signals while landing on a hospital helipad but the signals were reacquired with 10 minutes with normal operations during departure.
summary: The pilot experienced lost GPS reception on GARMIN 530 and 430 units with only one satellite available while landing at an LA hospital rooftop helipad. A shutdown and restart ten minutes later restored reception without issue, and no loss occurred during departure.

synopsis: LAX Controller voiced concern regarding the long existing VFR corridor that crosses over LAX Airport and the potential traffic conflicts resulting from same.
summary: A Grumman AA1 transitioning southbound through LAX Class Bravo at 900 feet was redirected to the flawed Mini Route, where it overtook a C172. The controller resolved the conflict by assigning an unauthorized 2,000-foot altitude, highlighting the route's design flaws and safety risks.

synopsis: L30 Controller expressed concern regarding the recently initiated 'point out' procedures involving VGT operations.
summary: A pilot flying an SR22 IFR into VGT was not handed off to LSV because the controller failed to recognize the aircraft's IFR status. The controller attributed the error to a flawed SOP requiring MED to coordinate the handoff instead of the sector working the aircraft.

synopsis: A B737-300 FWD Cargo Fire bell and light alerted at cruise so the fire bottle was discharged which put the warning out for about six to seven minutes. After the fire system alerted again, the crew diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: The crew experienced a forward cargo fire warning at cruise, discharged a bottle, and saw the light extinguish for six to seven minutes before it reactivated. They subsequently diverted to an airport 90 miles away.

synopsis: An A321 Number 2 brake was seen overheating after landing but cooled before the next takeoff only to overheat again during taxi and takeoff so the airborne brake cooling procedure was employed. At the next destination the fire trucks inspected the 325C brake and then followed the aircraft to the gate.
summary: The flight crew experienced a suspected dragging left main brake causing high temperatures during taxi, takeoff, and landing. They operated with gear down, requested fire trucks as a precaution, and landed safely before maintenance inspected the gear.

synopsis: A B777 engine failed at FL220 after departure so an emergency was declared, the QRH completed and flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced a left engine failure shortly after engaging the autopilot while climbing past FL220. They returned to the departure airport for a smooth single-engine landing at maximum weight, noting a need for improved training on emergency checklist flows.

synopsis: A B747-200 crew reported that at FL360 the Flight Engineer was feeding engines 1/2 from the fuel tank 1 and engines 3/4 from the tank 4 when engines 2 and 3 shutdown. The engines were restarted descending through FL290.
summary: During climb to FL360, Engines 2 and 3 rolled back while the Flight Engineer performed non-standard crossfeed to balance tanks. After unsuccessful rapid restarts at FL350 and FL310, the crew descended to FL290 where a successful restart stabilized the engines, allowing the flight to continue.

synopsis: A G200 First Officer flying his first TEB RUUDY 4 Departure overshot the WENTZ Intersection 1,500 FT altitude by 200 FT because he had no experience with the power verses pitch requirement during the high pitch angle climb.
summary: The pilot flying departed Runway 24 at TEB on the RUUDY4 departure and deviated 200 feet above the 1,500-foot crossing altitude at WENTZ due to insufficient pitch reduction. The pilot corrected the altitude immediately and attributed the excursion to inexperience with the procedure and inadequate coordination of thrust and pitch.

synopsis: An A320 encountered turbulence during the climb at 17,000 FT so maximum continuous thrust was set to expedite the climb which caused an EGT overtemp so after reducing thrust the flight returned to the departure airport for a precautionary landing.
summary: The pilot flying encountered chop while climbing through 14,000 feet and advanced thrust to MCT, causing Engine 1 EGT to exceed limits and fuel flow to rise 600 LB/hr above Engine 2. The crew reduced thrust, returned to the departure airport, and landed safely, though Engine 1 parameters remained elevated during taxi.

synopsis: An A320 Engine 2 Reverser Fault ECAM alerted and even though the Flight Manual directed a diversion the crew knew is was not necessary. Dispatch and the Duty Manager confirmed the procedural error so the crew continued.
summary: During cruise, the pilot received an Engine 2 Reverser Fault ECAM and found the Flight Manual's "Land as soon as possible" procedure incorrect based on experience. After consulting maintenance and technical managers, they agreed the procedure was poorly written, no diversion was required, and the flight continued to destination.

synopsis: A B737-400 nose gear ground/air sense squat switch failed to the ground mode preventing aircraft pressurization and other systems from functioning so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: A Check Airman and First Officer experienced autothrottle lock, TCAS failure, and MCP malfunctions after departure, causing an uncontrollable cabin climb. They declared an emergency, descended to 10,000 feet, and returned for an uneventful landing with cabin altitude remaining below 7,000 feet.

synopsis: A B737-400 Cabin Altitude Warning sounded and the autothrottles stopped working at FL310 because the nose gear air/ground sensor partially failed so an emergency was declared and the flight diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: The crew experienced autothrottle failure and a rising cabin altitude at FL310, forcing an emergency descent to 10,000 FT. They diverted after aircraft systems incorrectly indicated ground status, preventing ACARS communication, though high-flow oxygen kept cabin altitude below 14,000 FT.

synopsis: EMB145 First Officer experiences wing anti ice failure during approach in icing conditions. An emergency is declared and the warning light extinguishes at 500 FT AGL on the approach.
summary: During the downwind leg in moderate icing, the crew received wing anti-ice failure and inoperative warnings at 55% N1. They declared an emergency to exit the icing conditions, noting the unusual persistence of the warnings at high power settings until reaching 500 feet AGL.

synopsis: PA31 pilot reports failure of the nose gear to retract after takeoff and also to extend to the down and safe position. The flight returns to the departure airport and the 'Emergency Gear Extension' checklist is employed to successfully extend the nose gear prior to landing.
summary: The pilot reported a nose gear actuator failure during takeoff where the gear remained midway up and would not lock down. After performing an emergency extension in IMC, all three gears indicated down, allowing a safe landing.

synopsis: B767-300 flight crew reports right main gear tire failures after landing. The only indication in flight had been a momentary anti-skid advisory message and the crew elected not to use auto brakes during the landing.
summary: The flight crew experienced vibration during landing rollout below 100 KTS due to shredded and flat right main gear tires, following an intermittent in-flight antiskid advisory. The aircraft taxied to the gate for inspection, where the tire damage was confirmed and a runway FOD check was requested.

synopsis: A300 Captain reports loss of Green Hydraulic System fluid during descent for landing. The fluid level had indicated low prior to departure and was serviced. An emergency is declared and a normal landing ensues after gravity gear extension.
summary: The flight crew observed low green hydraulic fluid preflight and received an ECAM warning during descent, prompting an emergency declaration and manual gear extension. Maintenance later identified a leak in the Number 1 Engine pylon, which caused the fluid loss and gauge fluctuations.

synopsis: After observing a loss of Hydraulic System A quantity and pressure during flap retraction following takeoff the B727-200 flight crew declared an emergency and returned uneventfully to their departure airport.
summary: The crew encountered low Hydraulic System A pressure and quantity during flap retraction after departure, prompting an emergency return. Although the QRH did not address the fluid loss stabilization, the crew successfully executed a normal ILS approach and landing with stable systems, eventually canceling the emergency.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reports a Green Hydraulic System overheat ECAM just prior to start of descent. ECAM actions are complied with and crew lands normally after extending the gear via gravity extension, with a tow to the gate.
summary: The crew managed a Green Hydraulic System overheat during descent by shutting off the Engine 1 pump and PTU, then manually extending the landing gear. They declared an emergency due to lost nose wheel steering, executed a normal landing, and were towed to the gate.

synopsis: B737-700 experienced wake vortex encounter on takeoff from SNA behind an A320 that resulted in a roll and course deviation.
summary: The crew encountered moderate wake turbulence from a preceding A320 at 800 feet AGL during the noise abatement profile at SNA, causing a 20-30 degree right deviation. SOCAL Departure issued a heading to re-intercept the track, and the flight concluded without injuries or further issues.

synopsis: MD11 Captain experiences a number one hydraulic system failure over the North Atlantic. After coordination with Dispatch and Maintenance Control flight continues to destination for an uneventful landing with a tow to the gate.
summary: The flight crew experienced a sudden loss of Number 1 hydraulic system pressure and fluid at FL300 during cruise over the North Atlantic. They diverted to an alternate airport, declared an emergency, and executed a safe landing despite delayed ATC speed restrictions and deferred thrust reversers.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician and an Inspector report about an EMB-120 aircraft that 'returned to field' after pilot experienced an abnormal 'roll' characteristic after they had signed-off a right outboard flap installation and Operational Check.
summary: An A&P mechanic incorrectly installed the right outboard flap actuator on an EMB-120 during a routine overnight check, allowing the rod end to ride on the shoulder rather than engaging the bosses. This error caused an abnormal roll during takeoff, forcing the pilot to return to the field due to the flap remaining extended while others retracted.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A corporate jet pilot reported that ATC issued a terrain alert along with a heading and altitude change after the flight crew began navigating to DEJAY Intersection in mountainous terrain instead of to DEWAY.
summary: Part 91 pilots repositioning from UDD misread a clearance for the DEJAY intersection instead of DEWAY, causing SOCAL to issue a terrain warning and new climb instructions. The reporter attributes the confusion to two similarly named intersections in the same airspace, which nearly resulted in a terrain collision.

synopsis: The flight crew of an MD11 experienced difficulty complying with the crossing airspeed restriction at ROCAB on the TAMMY RNAV STAR to MEM when they had previously been cleared direct to TAMMY thence descend via the STAR.
summary: The crew of an MD-11 flying the TAMMY RNAV STAR to Memphis potentially exceeded the 230 KIAS restriction at ROCAB due to conflicting ATC clearances and automation prioritizing altitude over speed. The pilot attributed the issue to expedited "shortcut" clearances and ambiguous speed instructions, recommending clearer routing and earlier descent notifications.

synopsis: LR35 Captain notes the failure of the right main landing gear down light to illuminate after gear extension during approach. A go around is initiated and the Tower advises that the gear appear to be down. To make sure the emergency landing extension checklist is run and the gear is blown down followed by a safe landing.
summary: During a visual approach, the flight crew noted a missing right main landing gear 'down' light. After a low approach confirmed gear extension visually, the crew executed the emergency extension checklist using the nitrogen bottle and landed normally with fire trucks standing by.

synopsis: An HS-25 Captain failed to level at 1,500 FT at the WENTZ Intersection on the TEB RUUDY 4 because VNAV was not selected for the guidance.
summary: The flight crew departed Runway 24 on the RUUDY 4 departure and likely crossed WENTZ above the assigned 1,500 feet due to VNAV not being selected. The controller acknowledged the deviation but advised the crew not to worry, stating everything was OK.

synopsis: Two C172 pilots attempted to return to their departure airport in the Denver area at night with an inoperative magnetic compass. Following a highway which they thought was headed north, they land in Texas with low fuel.
summary: Two pilots flying a general aviation aircraft at night became lost after relying solely on road navigation following a frozen magnetic compass failure. They landed in Texas due to poor flight planning and lack of ATC contact, attributing the incident to pilot negligence and equipment failure.

synopsis: The pilot of a C-210 suffered total electrical failure while on an IFR flight plan in VMC. Efforts to minimize the use of electronic equipment preserved sufficient battery power to inform the Tower of the aircraft's arrival and light signals from the Tower were utilized for landing and taxi.
summary: The pilot experienced an electrical failure and altimeter/transponder discrepancies during IFR cruise at 7,000 feet, causing a loss of all electrical power. After declaring an emergency and conserving battery, the pilot hand-pumped the landing gear and landed safely on Runway 27.

synopsis: DA50EX flight crew on approach to BFI reported wake vortex encounter in trail behind a B757 on approach to SEA that resulted in porpoising and roll. Captain decided to go around and there was some confusion when they realized they were above missed approach level off altitude.
summary: A pilot flying a Boeing 757 approach in IMC at Seattle initiated an early go-around due to wake turbulence, inadvertently climbing above the 1,500 FT missed approach restriction. The pilot attributed the altitude deviation and brief loss of separation to fatigue, counter-intuitive local procedures, and excessive ATC communications that distracted the crew.

synopsis: After diverting to an enroute airport due to the failure of their left generator the flight crew of a C-550 began to cross a runway--believing they had been cleared to do so--but were stopped by Ground/Tower advising they had not been cleared. The pertinent transmission may have been partially blocked.
summary: The crew diverted due to a left generator failure and landed safely, but later crossed Runway XX without clearance after misinterpreting a blocked ATC transmission. The aircraft was subsequently stopped by Tower for holding short before being cleared to proceed to the ramp.

synopsis: LJ31 flight crew experiences a dual inverter failure at FL330 rendering all primary flight instruments inoperative. With ATC assistance, the crew elects to divert to a suitable airport for maintenance.
summary: The flight crew diverted to ZZZ after both inverters failed at 33,000 feet, causing a loss of primary flight instruments and navigation capability. ATC provided vectors for the descent to 27,000 feet, and the aircraft landed safely in visual meteorological conditions.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A pilot executed a go around at 300 FT when he realized he was lined up to land on the F82 taxiway adjacent to Runway 35 because during his dusk approach he did not distinguish the difference until he saw a taxiing aircraft.
summary: A pilot inbound for Runway 35 at dusk mistakenly aligned with an adjacent taxiway due to dark skid marks resembling runway markings. The pilot executed a go-around after realizing the error, confirmed by another pilot, and subsequently landed safely on Runway 35.

synopsis: Varieze pilot experiences fuel starvation on downwind while doing timed fuel burn measurements of the header tank. An emergency is declared and a dead stick landing ensues.
summary: The pilot of a Varieze experienced an engine stoppage on downwind at 850 feet after switching from a dry header tank to main tanks during a fuel burn test. An emergency was declared to land ahead of a Piper, resulting in an uneventful landing with no safety issues.

synopsis: An A320 Captain expressed concern about the proposed implementation of iPads as the sole flight deck source of information and data currently provided through paper documents and publications. The reporter believes an extended period of vetting, with the paper documents retained as backups, should be required to insure reliability and provide flight crew with adequate opportunity to gain facility and confidence in their use.
summary: An airline pilot with 48 years of experience warns that rushing to implement iPads as the sole flight deck reference without backup paper manuals is unsafe. The reporter urges delaying full implementation until extensive line pilot testing and evaluation confirm the technology's feasibility to prevent potential accidents.

synopsis: A PA-28 engine quit because of fuel starvation forcing an off airport landing after the student pilot selected the crossfeed to CLOSE because that aircraft had no selector detent before the OFF position.
summary: A student pilot inadvertently turned the fuel selector valve to OFF during a Cherokee flight, causing engine power loss and an off-airport landing on a dirt road. The incident resulted from the valve's lack of a detent stop, the student's unfamiliarity with the aircraft configuration, and the instructor's failure to verify the switch position.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a possible taxiway landing event listing the visibility form the new Tower as problematic.
summary: A tower controller lost visual contact with a Mooney Allegro on final for Runway 29R due to ground clutter and later observed it rolling out on Taxiway A. The controller could not determine if the aircraft landed on the taxiway or exited the runway early but chose not to question the pilot.

synopsis: Tower Controller expressed concern regarding the Supervisor's failure to assign a CIC when leaving the Tower for a break, the reporter listing some complicating operational restraints adding to the uncertainty.
summary: An air traffic supervisor left the tower cab for over 20 minutes without assigning a Combined Information Coordinator, leaving new controllers to manage a busy departure push alone. The reporter states this violation of SOPs creates a dangerous safety risk due to the lack of backup support during unusual or busy situations.

synopsis: A300 Captain reports a lightning strike that knocks out several aircraft systems, including the First Officer's airspeed and attitude information. Dispatch is contacted and a diversion is suggested for the required maintenance but the planners do not agree and the flight continues to destination.
summary: During climbout, lightning struck the aircraft, causing temporary loss of airspeed, attitude, and autopilot systems before a permanent instrument failure occurred three minutes later. Although the crew noted severe winter storms at the preferred diversion airport, Planning ignored this input and directed the flight there despite the weather risks.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 flight crew declared an emergency and returned to their departure airport when they were unable to retract all three landing gear after takeoff.
summary: The flight crew experienced a landing gear disagreement during retraction, causing the right main gear to oscillate. They declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport with gear down for a safe landing, and terminated the trip due to fatigue.

synopsis: EMB145 flight crew experiences a TCAS RA at FL230, with the intruder 500 FT above and descending and superimposed on another target 1,000 FT below. The RA is complied with but once clear the target has vanished and ATC advises that they are not aware of any other target.
summary: The pilot reported a TCAS Resolution Advisory during descent from FL330 to FL230, commanding a 2,000-2,500 ft/min descent to avoid an unseen intruder 500 ft above. The crew lost 400-500 ft before clearing the conflict, suspecting a spurious transponder signal caused the false alert.

synopsis: While climbing out of FL280 a MD83 crew noticed the oil quantity on the right engine went from 12 quarts down to eight. The crew diverted to a nearby airport where Maintenance later advised a seal had broken allowing oil to escape close to the starter.
summary: The First Officer reported a right engine oil leak during climb from FL280, causing an emergency diversion. Maintenance later determined a broken seal near the starter allowed oil to escape, resulting in a landing with three quarts remaining.

synopsis: A Check Airman conducting initial First Officer line training aboard an B777 was compelled to take unilateral action with respect to his initial departure when ATC first insured they were cleared via the JTEEE RNAV SID prior to takeoff, then gave them a 'non JTEEE compliant' vector heading with their takeoff clearance and then was unable to provide a proper clearance to return to the SID and continue on their flight planned/PDC cleared route after takeoff. The reporter advised this was only one of many such experiences since the recent implementation of the new RNAV SIDs at MEM.
summary: A 777 Check Airman reported communication issues with Memphis Departure Control during a 777 departure on Runway 36C. Conflicting clearances regarding the JTEEE1 RNAV SID caused confusion, leading the crew to deviate from the published route to maintain aircraft control and safety.

synopsis: B737 Flight Attendant reports discovering walk around oxygen bottles without the plastic tubing connected to the bottles on numerous occasions, during preflight. Maintenance is called to correct the problem.
summary: A flight attendant discovered an unconnected aft right main cabin oxygen bottle during pre-flight checks and reported it to the Captain and Maintenance. A mechanic corrected the issue, but the reporter noted this is a chronic fleet-wide problem caused by inadequate training and inspection procedures.

synopsis: B737-800 Flight Attendant reported multiple instances during preflight of finding walkaround O2 bottles with mask and tubing not connected.
summary: A flight attendant discovered an unconnected oxygen walk-around bottle during pre-flight checks and reported it to the Captain, who requested Maintenance to fix the issue before boarding. The flight departed safely, but the reporter attributes the recurring problem to a lack of training and unclear procedures regarding tubing connections.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A pilot was unable to contact VPS TRACON as directed before takeoff from DTS and so was counseled after calling for takeoff clearance after becoming airborne.
summary: A pilot at Destin experienced radio reception failure while attempting to contact Departure Control for takeoff clearance as instructed. Unable to communicate on the ground, the pilot took off in VMC and established contact at 300 feet, attributing the issue to line-of-sight limitations and a lack of published alternate procedures.

synopsis: An AA5A Instructor pilot and his student made an emergency off airport landing when the ammeter pegged high followed quickly by burning electrical odors in the cockpit. No injuries to the occupants nor damage to the airplane were incurred.
summary: While cruising at 4,000 MSL, the pilot and student experienced an ALT light, high ammeter reading, and burning smell, prompting a master switch shutdown. They executed a precautionary off-field landing with no injuries or damage to the aircraft or property.

synopsis: The Chief Pilot of a cargo/freight/passenger air carrier operation operating Shorts SD3 aircraft resigned his position and alleges the company, due to lack of parts and resources, has failed to maintain their aircraft in an airworthy condition.
summary: The former Chief Pilot reported that a Part 121/135 carrier operating Shorts SD3 aircraft continued flying with multiple inoperative systems, including fire fault and GPWS tests, due to lack of funds for repairs. The pilot resigned citing safety concerns, alleging the use of automobile gas and an engine seizure that grounded passenger operations.

synopsis: C90 Controller described a go-around event claiming a previous inbound who was sent around because of spacing issues slowed to below assigned speed to the Outer Marker and caused a subsequent go around.
summary: A B737-800 pilot slowed early on the ILS Runway 10 approach at O'Hare, creating excessive spacing that forced an A330 to collapse and subsequently go around. The controller attributed the incident to the B737-800 deviating from speed restrictions without advising ATC.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a developing conflict event when the Center Controller failed to take timely action on two aircraft converging.
summary: An Approach controller reported that a Center controller handed off a descending B737 directly toward a climbing B737 departure, creating a conflict. The Center controller initially refused to take responsibility or issue a turn, eventually maneuvering the aircraft only after the separation became dangerously close.

synopsis: B767-300 First Officer is informed after the fact that the Weight and Balance calculations for a flight he flew were incorrect. The error occurred when the operations representative added up the various bin loads and passengers on board incorrectly then provided that incorrect information to the flight crew to preform Weight and Balance calculations.
summary: The flight crew, including the Captain, First Officer, and Relief Pilot, operated a live trip with inaccurate weight and balance calculations caused by an Operations Representative's incorrect load forms. The error went undetected because the crew relied on the representative's zone weight totals, which prevented the onboard computer from flagging the illegal loading.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported engine surge that drove a decision to return to departure airport. Workload caused a slight delay in running the checklists.
summary: The Captain experienced a Thrust Instability Event during climb on an overwater flight and recovered the engine from memory. Although all actions were correct, the QRH checklist was delayed due to workload and surprise, prompting a commitment to better checklist discipline in the future.

synopsis: A MD-83 HDG COMP flag annunciated after takeoff but the QRH did not have an applicable procedure so the Captain selected R ON AUX which cleared the fault. The Captain noted that the carrier's diverse MD-83 fleet creates equipment and publication knowledge problems.
summary: The pilot reported a 10-degree heading discrepancy and AHRS comparator flags after takeoff due to a lack of specific QRH procedures for the aircraft's three-AHRS configuration. The crew resolved the issue by selecting the AHRS Revisionary Switch to 'R ON AUX,' which cleared the annunciation but highlighted gaps in documentation and equipment configuration management.

synopsis: B737-800 experiences Master Warning and Hydraulic (HYD) warning lights when the gear is retracted after takeoff with the hydraulic pressure dropping to 2750 PSI then recovering. The discrepancy had been previously written up and signed off by Maintenance, but the crew elects to continue to destination and not depart until the problem is corrected. Eventually a loose connection to the bleed air system, providing head pressure to the hydraulic reservoirs is found and corrected.
summary: The Captain rejected a B737 after repeated hydraulic warnings during rotation and gear extension, caused by a bleed air leak in the reservoir head pressure line. Despite initial maintenance sign-offs, the Captain refused departure until the leak was found and repaired, preventing potential hydraulic failure under high demand.

synopsis: A C172 pilot had a near miss with another aircraft on short final for LVK Runway 25R after a Tower mandated go around because high speed traffic was descending for the same runway.
summary: The pilot reported a near mid-air collision with Aircraft Y during a go-around and approach to LVK, caused by a trainee controller issuing conflicting runway instructions and poor traffic management. The pilot attributed the incident to inexperienced personnel handling too much workload, resulting in a late runway change from 25R to 25L.

synopsis: MXS pilot experiences a catastrophic engine failure at 8,500 FT and is able to glide to a suitable airport and land on a closed runway. There was insufficient time to contact the Tower via radio prior to landing.
summary: The pilot ferrying an MXS experienced a catastrophic engine failure at 8,500 feet MSL. After shutting down avionics, the pilot visually cleared the area, dodged runway barriers, and landed safely without contacting Tower due to the emergency.

synopsis: After both primary hydraulic systems failed during descent the flight crew of a Learjet 60 declared an emergency, performed appropriate checklist actions and diverted uneventfully from their destination airport to a nearby airport with superior runways and facilities.
summary: During descent, the pilot flying deployed spoilers for an ATC speed restriction, causing a total loss of primary hydraulic pressure. The crew declared an emergency, diverted to a nearby airport, and landed safely using the back-up braking system.

synopsis: C90 Controller expressed concern regarding the use of Runway 28 when simultaneous arrival operations are being conducted.
summary: An air traffic controller monitoring parallel approaches at ORD observed an A319 failing to check in on the monitor frequency while an E145 descended nearby and a departure was cleared from Runway 28. The controller could not verify the A319's frequency status until after the departure took off, citing a systemic safety issue regarding simultaneous departures and arrivals without a dedicated monitor frequency.

synopsis: Frequent flight crew confusion and resultant altitude deviations when flying the MNZNO RNAV SID from ABQ has convinced the reporter of the need to develop unique phraseology when clearing flights 'via' the procedure. Her suggestions included deleting the 'published' altitude constraints, instead clearing flights to cross all constrained fixes at altitudes 'greater than' the published restrictions. Her preferred method, however, was to give 'old school' heading, altitudes and clearances direct to a fix.
summary: An air traffic controller reported confusion among flight crews regarding altitude restrictions on the MNZNO RNAV SID at ABQ, leading to readback errors and pilot safety concerns. The controller resolved the issue by issuing traditional heading and altitude clearances instead of the SID, recommending this method for mixed aircraft types.

synopsis: B757 Captain operating in the Colombia ATC system noted the ATC English skill levels couple with increased traffic volume has made the Colombian ATC system unacceptable.
summary: The pilot reported multiple ATC errors at BOG/SKBO, including incorrect taxiway instructions, uncoordinated climb-out traffic at FL200, and conflicting frequency clearances. The reporter attributed these unsafe conditions to deteriorating ATC performance, poor English skills, and increased traffic levels in Colombia.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant's concerns about a hot mirror in a passenger lavatory and an off and on electrical odor in the cabin of her B757 precipitated events that culminated in a diversion to the nearest suitable airport when the mirror started 'pulling off' the lavatory wall.
summary: During enroute flight at FL360, a Flight Attendant reported an electrical burning odor near a lavatory mirror. After pulling breaker P9 for the adjacent entertainment screen and signs failed to stop the odor or prevent the mirror from peeling, the Captain diverted to the nearest airport.

synopsis: A BE1900 flight crew operating into a remote gravel airstrip during strong gusting cross/tailwinds lost control after touchdown and ground looped off the downwind side of the runway, collapsing the nose gear.
summary: The pilot landed a VFR flight on Runway XX in strong crosswinds and blowing snow, causing the aircraft to slide right, twist 90 degrees, and collapse the nose gear. No injuries occurred, but the pilot attributed the loss of control to stacked negative factors including low visibility, a slick runway, and an unstabilized approach.

synopsis: A321 flight crew missed a crossing restriction while descending via an RNAV arrival and attributed the error to a cockpit discussion which distracted them from monitoring the automation.
summary: The crew descended via an RNAV arrival and requested speed relief from ATC. After the Captain adjusted altitude to meet a restriction, the aircraft inadvertently entered Vertical Speed mode due to crew distraction, causing them to cross an intersection 1,000 feet below the 15,000-foot restriction without ATC intervention.

synopsis: ATC's late airspeed change to a crossing restriction as the flight approached QUENY on the EAGUL RNAV STAR to PHX, compounded by an FMC programming error, resulted in the deletion of both the speed and altitude restrictions and allowed the A321 to descend 250-300 FT below the required 9,000 MSL.
summary: During a descent into PHX on the EAGUL 5 RNAV STAR, the pilot deleted altitude and speed restrictions after an ATC clearance change, causing the aircraft to descend below 9,000 FT. The crew manually arrested the descent 250–300 FT below the restriction, attributing the error to rushed procedures from last-minute ATC deviations.

synopsis: An A321 diverted after an unbearable odor was detected in the cabin making the entire crew ill and requiring hospital emergency care treatment because of carbon monoxide poisoning.
summary: During a scheduled ferry flight converted to a live flight, fumes caused illness to the crew and passengers, prompting an emergency diversion. The reporter attributes the incident to a lack of flight deck indications and company pressure to operate the aircraft despite known maintenance issues and missing parts.

synopsis: When they were vectored off the GIBBZ RNAV STAR, by which they had previously been cleared to 'descend via;' the flight crew of an ERJ-170 were uncertain as to their cleared altitude. Difficulty communicating with the busy Controller forced a brief level off at an intermediate altitude until a new clearance could be provided.
summary: Pilots descending on the GIBBZ1 RNAV into IAD were vectored off the arrival with a 020 heading but received no specific altitude clearance. The crew leveled at 11,000 feet after failed radio attempts until ATC later instructed a descent to 6,000 feet, highlighting a need for explicit altitude assignments when vectored off a "descend via" clearance.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Flight crew complying with TCAS RA 'Descend' command received an instruction from ATC to climb due to terrain. Crew, observing that terrain was not a factor, delayed climb until TCAS 'Clear of Conflict' was received.
summary: Enroute at 7,000 feet, a TCAS Resolution Advisory blocked ATC instructions and commanded a descent. The controller then issued a conflicting climb clearance for terrain, which the crew ignored based on EGPWS data before returning to 7,000 feet once the conflict cleared.

synopsis: CL605 First Officer reports leaving 1,500 FT for 2,000 FT prior to crossing WENTZ on the RUUDY 4 when the magenta VNAV altitude above the IVSI changed from 1,500 to 2,000. The pilot-not-flying Captain pointed out that WENTZ had had not yet been crossed.
summary: The pilot flying inadvertently climbed to 1,620 feet after misinterpreting a VNAV altitude change as waypoint passage during the RUUDY departure. The pilot not flying corrected the error by disconnecting the autopilot and descending back to the assigned 1,500 feet.

synopsis: A flight crew using a new EFB software package commented about distractions caused by the lack of its usability and the First Officer overshot an assigned altitude while searching for a DH after a runway change.
summary: The First Officer manually flew the aircraft below the assigned 1,800m altitude while distracted by a runway change and difficult EFB software. The crew corrected a maximum 150-foot deviation after an altitude alert, attributing the error to high workload and inadequate EFB training.

synopsis: An engine fire during initial climb caused the flight crew of a Q400 to discharge both fire retardant bottles, shut down the engine, declare an emergency and return for a landing and evacuation on the runway.
summary: The crew experienced an engine fire during climbout, leading to hypoxia and communication difficulties after donning oxygen masks. They returned and landed single-engine with the fire light still illuminated, resulting in an uninjured deplaning attributed to a sterile cockpit violation and a standby attitude indicator anomaly.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reports that the AWOS at C75 gave inaccurate information, which was also relayed to him by ZAU. The result was arriving at the airport above a solid under cast with insufficient fuel to go elsewhere. The decision was made to enter the layer and land, which was successful.
summary: A pilot flying VFR to Marshall County (C75) landed through an overcast layer after receiving incorrect clear weather reports from AWOS, Flight Watch, and Chicago Center. The pilot discovered the AWOS was inaccurate, a known issue the airport manager failed to fix, and requested a NOTAM to warn other operators.

synopsis: Corporate jet inbound to PDK voiced concern regarding the questionable ATC handling provided by one ZTL Controller with respect to weather avoidance.
summary: Pilots arriving at PDK reported an Approach Controller aggressively vectored them into visible thunderstorms despite their objections, later ordering a 180-degree turn. After a second controller assisted with navigation, the original controller returned to enforce a 200 KTS speed restriction in Class B airspace before the crew landed safely.

aircraft: Fairchild Swearingen Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Tower Controller working a late night shift allowed an aircraft to land on a closed runway according to the AMASS equipment, the reporter offering several suggestions to improve the equipment functionality.
summary: An air traffic controller approved a landing for Air Carrier X on Runway 18R despite an unnoticed "closed" status on the AMASS system. The controller visually confirmed the runway was clear and allowed the landing, concluding the system alert was a false positive caused by an erroneous data entry.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air Traffic Controller reports about a developing aircraft separation issue between CRJ and Drone.
summary: A GFK Approach controller cleared a departing CRJ onto a course that converged with a descending drone in a TFR, creating a conflict. The reporter stopped the CRJ at 11,000 feet and turned it away, attributing the unsafe situation to the controller's confusion over phraseology and inability to ensure separation.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Tower Controller described a go around event when communication with an arrival was not established. The reporter later realized the appropriate frequencies were not selected after positions were combined.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller working Local North, Center, and South lost radio contact with a business jet on final for Runway 27, likely due to failing to select the Local South frequency on the touch screen. The aircraft ignored light gun signals and Guard frequency clearances, initiated a go-around, and subsequently established contact with Local West.

synopsis: ZMA Controller reports a botched handoff from ZJX resulting in a late point out to military controllers at Sealord.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that an A320 handoff from ZJX lacked the required BAHAA HIBAC TRV clearance, causing the aircraft to get within one mile of Sealord before being pointed out. The controller attributed the incident to ZJX failing to provide the correct flight plan per the Letter of Agreement.

synopsis: During a turn at an intersection while taxiing to the gate following a landing in icing conditions, the flight crew of a B757-200 was unable to stop the lateral movement of the nose toward the edge of the taxiway. Judicious use of reverse, forward, and differential thrust successfully avoided an excursion and permitted careful taxi to the ramp.
summary: The flight crew experienced a loss of directional control on Taxiway N due to nil braking action while exiting the runway. They recovered alignment using differential thrust and reversers, taxied to the ramp without damage, and maintenance confirmed no gear or FOD issues.

synopsis: A319 Captain performing post maintenance test flight experiences porpoising as the aircraft accelerates to 290 knots. The left elevator is visibly moving on the flight control synoptic page. Airspeed is reduced, an emergency is declared, and flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: During a test flight exiting a 2 S check, the crew experienced increasing porpoising and left elevator oscillation above 10,000 feet at 290 knots. They declared an emergency, returned to land safely, and attributed the failure to a probable left elevator servo or actuator issue.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew experiences a TCAS RA while leveling off at assigned altitude. The target aircraft was assigned and altitude 1,000 feet above and no action was required by the pilot flying as the autopilot leveled the aircraft 1,000 feet below.
summary: Pilots climbing south of RESPE waypoint to FL320 encountered an unannounced aircraft on TCAS, triggering a Resolution Advisory. The crew attributed the conflict to an ATC oversight in failing to provide traffic advisories, though no collision occurred.

synopsis: EMB-145LR flight crew reported trailing edge flaps failed when commanded to Flaps 22. They executed a go-around, ran the procedure, declared an emergency, and executed a safe landing.
summary: During approach, the crew received a 'Flap Fail' message at Flaps 9, prompting a missed approach and emergency declaration. The Captain took over as pilot flying for a successful no-flap landing on the 11,000-foot runway with no issues.

synopsis: A B737-800 returned to land after takeoff because a strong dirty socks odor was detected in throughout the aircraft. Maintenance stated an engine wash was completed the previous night so the odor may be a chemical residue.
summary: The flight crew and cabin crew detected an oily odor shortly after takeoff, prompting an emergency return to Runway 36 with packs and bleeds turned off. Mechanics later reported an overnight engine wash, which the crew suspects caused chemical residue to enter the cabin via the bleed air system.

synopsis: While attempting to turn off the end of the slippery runway in a strong crosswind the flight crew of an A300 was unable to stop the aircraft nose from sliding to the left. The crew believed they had left the hard surface and called for a tow.
summary: The flight crew lost directional control while turning onto a slippery taxiway in light snow, despite using full tiller, differential braking, and thrust. The aircraft stopped off the surface without damage and required two tugs and sand to be towed to the ramp.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic suggests that an investigation should be conducted to determine where a failure to quarantine and properly handle unserviceable galley ice cart containers had occurred, after noticing that a large puddle, extending from an aft galley ice cart to the lavatory and the aft right entry door on an A320, had started to ice over.
summary: During routine overnight maintenance on an A320, a cabin crew member discovered a water leak from an aft galley ice cart. The leak was caused by an unserviceable container, marked multiple times as broken and wrapped in a trash bag, which had been improperly installed by a catering vendor.

synopsis: SR22 pilot reports sighting a possible UAV 1,000 FT below and opposite direction in SDF airspace. ATC is advised but they claim no knowledge of the aircraft.
summary: A pilot flying VFR on top at 10,000 feet observed a small, powered unmanned aircraft at 9,000 feet while being vectored by Louisville Approach. The controller reported no radar contact, and a post-flight debrief dismissed the sighting as a glider, which the pilot rejected due to the aircraft's power and altitude.

synopsis: The pilot examiner of a Columbia 400 took evasive action on short final when the aircraft in front of them dove for the runway during an assumed go-around. They were restricted by a crane in the area, but were able to maneuver around it and return for a safe landing.
summary: A Columbia 400 examiner and examinee faced a conflict with a Tencam student pilot who unexpectedly dove and climbed near the runway threshold. The incident resulted in a blocked landing and go-around path due to tight airspace, speed disparity, and failures by the student, tower, and crew to recognize the hazard.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Recip Eng
synopsis: An pilot reported a near miss at 2,000 FT while in the UGN traffic pattern with no traffic alert from ATC.
summary: A pilot on an IFR flight to UGN experienced a TCAS alert and visual sighting of a single-engine aircraft 300 feet away during a visual approach to Runway 5. The pilot attributed the near miss to a lack of traffic advisories from the Tower, though no collision occurred.

synopsis: LAS Controller expressed concern regarding the current prop departure procedure, i.e. the issuance of headings, adding formalized procedures should be published for LAS propeller aircraft.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller at LAS failed to solicit a VFR climb request from an IFR light twin pilot during a congested departure phase. Although no separation or terrain issues occurred, a deviation was recorded due to the missed instruction required by the local LOA.

synopsis: Tower Controller chronicled a poor braking action landing event when the exact nature and location of the poor braking was confused and another aircraft was cleared to land, shortly after the runway was closed.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller at ZZZ managed arrivals on Runway 12L during snow and low visibility, issuing a "NILL" braking report to a CRJ after a preceding A320 reported poor conditions. The CRJ landed safely, but the controller noted the complexity of the situation and recommended a dedicated local coordinator for busy traffic.

synopsis: N90 Controller expressed concern regarding the release procedures used for JFK Tower and the interaction of the TMU vs. the departure sectors.
summary: The JFK Departure Controller stopped 31L departures due to volume, but JFK Tower or the TRACON TMU released Southwest traffic without approval. This caused an airspace deviation into the reporter's sector, highlighting the danger of releasing traffic without sector coordination.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a NMAC between a traffic pattern arrival and a departing aircraft, the reports indicating the arrival aircraft was a student pilot who entered the pattern incorrectly.
summary: A solo student pilot flying a C172 entered the wrong downwind and base leg, causing a near mid-air collision with a departing C172. The student failed to comply with initial ATC headings, eventually avoiding the conflict, though the departing pilot reported a NMAC and the reporter attributed the event to inadequate flight school training.

synopsis: Tower CIC Controller described a loss of required runway separation event when traffic landed with landing clearance, listing additional fly in workload as a causal factor.
summary: A Local Control controller missed a Diamond aircraft's calls during a busy training session and flight event, allowing the pilot to land without clearance while another aircraft began takeoff. The controller attributed the near-miss to high workload, lack of Local Assist staffing, and visual obstructions, noting the Diamond exited the runway just as the departing aircraft started its roll.

synopsis: ZMA Controller described a potential loss of separation event claiming similar sounding call signs was the primary causal factor.
summary: Air Traffic Control managed two MD88s at FL280 with similar call signs, assigning a speed restriction to the trailing aircraft and descending the lead aircraft to FL260. The controller noted the confusion caused by the similar call signs and the initial failure of the lead aircraft to read back the descent clearance.

synopsis: An A320 Captain discussed his concerns with respect to his airline's, in his opinion, rush to implement the availability of aircraft operational content solely by 'pad type' hand held electronic devices. He believes their use as the sole on board procedural resource should be proceeded by extensive testing and evaluation of the average line pilots' facility in its use.
summary: An airline pilot warned that rushing to implement iPads as the sole flight deck reference without paper backups is unsafe. The reporter urged more training and evaluation using line pilot data to prevent potential accidents caused by this premature implementation.

synopsis: Q400 flight crew reported engine fire after takeoff, and after discharging bottles the fire light remained on. Crew felt pressure to get aircraft on the ground as quickly as possible, and some SOP deviations may have occurred.
summary: The crew experienced an engine fire during climb, leading to a return where communication was disrupted by tangled oxygen masks and headsets. They landed with flaps 35 to manage energy, noting they deviated from standard procedures, including checklist order and sterile cockpit rules, due to the emergency.

synopsis: While flying approaches in icing conditions the flight crew of a CRJ-200 suffered anomalous flight control response and received a yellow warning flag, the purpose of which they were unaware. Three approaches were abandoned at their destination and, although the symptoms returned again, a final and successful approach and landing were accomplished at a diversion airport.
summary: The crew experienced erratic handling and autopilot aileron trim disagree flags during multiple approaches in icing conditions, leading to three go-arounds. They diverted to ZZZ, declared minimum fuel and an emergency, and landed safely after maintenance identified the trim disagreement as the cause.

synopsis: The pilots of an Embraer 145 received an erroneous low fuel warning during climb and observed one fuel quantity indicator going to zero. The crew turned towards the departure field, ran the low low level checklist, and made a safe landing.
summary: The crew received a false FUEL LOW LEVEL 1 warning with wing tank 2 indications dropping to zero while climbing through 12,000 feet on departure. They executed an emergency return and landed uneventfully after confirming the indication was erroneous.

synopsis: EMB145 flight crew reports rejecting a takeoff after Vr due to failure to rotate. The aircraft is successfully stopped on the runway and taxied back to the gate.
summary: The First Officer aborted takeoff at rotation speed due to excessive yoke backpressure and failure to achieve normal rotation on a de-iced aircraft. The crew returned to the gate for maintenance inspection after a high-speed abort, attributing the issue to abnormal handling despite following all procedures.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 402 discovered the left brake ineffective during the landing roll-out. He was able to slow the aircraft but contacted one runway end light prior to stopping.
summary: The pilot reported a left brake pedal failure during landing rollout, requiring aerodynamic braking and right brake use to stop the aircraft. The plane hit an end light, but all passengers deplaned without injury.

synopsis: The pilot of a B737-800 experienced a loss of control during takeoff roll. He observed a differential acceleration of the engines that caused a drift that he could not control with rudder pedal input, differential braking or tiller command. Once the takeoff was rejected, he regained control but was hesitant to taxi since he did not know the cause.
summary: During takeoff, asymmetric engine acceleration caused a left drift, followed by a nose wheel steering failure that rendered the tiller inoperative and caused the gear to smoke. The pilot rejected the takeoff, regained steering control, and requested a tow after a mechanic identified the nose wheel steering had momentarily entered bypass mode.

synopsis: The pilots of a MD10 received a window shield heat alert and consulted the checklist, which stated to turn off the window heat. Shortly after, the Captain's window shattered, obscuring his vision. The crew consulted the checklist for a cracked or arcing window. They elected to divert to a suitable airport due to the icing restriction. The First Officer made an uneventful landing.
summary: During cruise at 35,000 feet, a Level 1 left windshield heat failure caused the captain's window to arc and shatter, obscuring forward view. The crew declared an emergency, diverted to a nearby VFR airport to avoid icing, and the First Officer landed safely.

synopsis: An A300 flight crew, dispatched with their EFBs MEL'd and both FMC updates deferred, descended below the 9,000 MSL constraint at LOONR while descending via the FNCHR RNAV STAR to MEM. Contributing factors included a vector off the DAWGG STAR, then recleared via the FNCHR and increased flight crew workload due to Dispatch with out of date FMS databases and MEL'd EFBs.
summary: Pilots reported increased workload due to deferred FMS and EFB databases caused by maintenance delays. While descending on a re-cleared RNAV STAR, the crew descended below the 9,000-foot crossing restriction at LOONR before reaching the waypoint.

synopsis: B757 First Officer experiences a Cabin Altitude EICAS warning message at FL400. An emergency is declared, descent initiated, and a diversion to a suitable airport is planned.
summary: The flight crew received a Cabin Altitude EICAS warning at FL400, prompting an emergency descent to 10,000 FT and a diversion. They deviated 30 degrees from course, informed ATC, and completed the diversion with no further events after stabilizing.

synopsis: A CRJ200 experienced a wake turbulence event when vectored behind a DC10 on approach to JFK.
summary: Pilots flying an ILS 4R approach behind a DC-10 experienced severe wake turbulence exacerbated by 42-knot headwinds. Despite requesting spacing, ATC instructed a speed increase which the crew refused to maintain safety, eventually landing without further disruption.

synopsis: A CE-750 suffered a fuel spill following a 'top off' fueling.
summary: During preflight, a fueler reported fuel ejecting overboard after fueling stopped and the float check was completed, creating two six-foot fuel pools. The aircraft was moved away from the spill, and a subsequent float check on the next leg showed no anomalies.

synopsis: As they climbed through only 11,500 FT MSL the flight crew of a DHC-8 were alerted by a CABIN PRESS warning light. They declared and emergency, descended to 10,000 FT MSL, resolved their problem and continued to their destination after verifying sufficient fuel on board to do so.
summary: The flight crew experienced a cabin pressure warning above 11,500 feet during climb, prompting an emergency descent to 10,000 feet. After resolving the pressurization issue via checklists and confirming fuel sufficiency with Dispatch, the aircraft continued to its destination at 10,000 feet.

synopsis: An A320 flight crew complied with all appropriate checklists, declared an emergency, and landed safely after encountering a malfunctioning flap/slat extension system.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a slat lock and wingtip brake ECAM warning while descending for an ILS approach. They declared an emergency, followed QRH procedures, and landed safely with 7,600 pounds of fuel after the Captain had previously added fuel due to concerns over insufficient load.

synopsis: In response to anti-skid and brake failure warnings on final approach the flight crew of a CE-560XLS executed a go-around, followed the appropriate QRH procedures, declared an emergency and landed safely using max reverse thrust and emergency brakes to a full stop.
summary: During final approach, the crew encountered an 'ANTISKID INOP' light and a popped 'PWR BRKS' breaker, followed by a 'LO BRAKE PRESS' light. After a go-around and QRH review, they declared an emergency, landed on Runway 28 using emergency brakes, and noted a discrepancy between the popped breaker and the QRH procedure.

synopsis: Two B737-800 flight attendants required medical treatment after exposure to a 'chemical smell' during descent for landing. The pilots detected no odor in the flight station.
summary: During approach, flight attendants reported breathing difficulties and a chemical smell, prompting the crew to request medical and crash rescue services. Upon landing, four flight attendants were hospitalized for medical attention while passengers disembarked, though the flight deck reported no odor or air quality issues.

synopsis: A Cabin Flight Attendant reports that Blue Water fluid from a previous overflow spill in the Aft Lavatory toilet on their B737 aircraft had continued to seep out from under the galley carts, saturating cabin flooring and carpets under the aft three rows of passenger seats.
summary: A missing toilet paper roll holder caused a toilet backup on the previous flight, saturating the aft galley and seats 23–25 with overflow during taxi and takeoff. Hazmat crews cleaned the area, but the aircraft continued operating with soaked carpets requiring replacement.

synopsis: When their B737NG experienced a deafening decibel level air leak at the left forward entry door during initial climb the flight attendant reporters did their best to cope as the flight returned to their departure airport. Their request to be relieved of further duty for the day, however, was met problematically by management, advising that such relief would be allowed only if logged negatively in their personnel records.
summary: Flight attendants reported a pressurization loss and deafening noise from an L1 door leak during climbout, forcing an air turn back to the departure airport. The Captain requested crew replacement due to communication failure and stress, but supervisors delayed support and offered a choice between continuing duty or calling in sick.

aircraft: Embraer Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) was informed that an Embraer aircraft was unable to engage the Aileron Trim System during a flight test after he had accomplished an Aileron Control Cable rigging Task Card.
summary: A mechanic over-tensioned an Embraer's aileron control cables during rigging by failing to cross-reference load charts when using an alternate tensiometer. This error caused stiff ailerons and trim system failure during a subsequent Functional Check Flight, forcing the aircraft to return to base.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports he noticed lightning strike damage on the lower fuselage body fairing of a B777 aircraft prior to departure schedule. He documented the discrepancy, but was threatened with an investigation by his Maintenance Supervisor after he refused to alter his logbook write-up to indicate chipped paint.
summary: A mechanic at a terminal gate documented a suspected lightning strike on a fuselage fairing but was ordered by a supervisor to alter the logbook entry to "chipped paint." The mechanic refused based on their judgment, resulting in a threatened investigation by management who disputed the damage assessment.

synopsis: C172 pilot reports having his left wingtip bumped by the right wingtip of another C172 taxiing out of the runup area. The Tower is advised and eventually the other aircraft returns to the runup pad where minor damage is found to have occurred to both wingtips.
summary: A student pilot in Aircraft Y clipped the wingtip of stationary Aircraft X while taxiing from the runup pad due to insufficient clearance awareness. Although initial inspections found no damage, a later FSDO inspection revealed a bent shield on Aircraft X and gouges on Aircraft Y, rendering the latter potentially unairworthy.

synopsis: Pilot reports having experienced the following shortly after take-off in a C-421 Cessna: an onboard AC Electrical failure, loss of all system verification lights, Landing Gear, Flaps, Electric Trimmer tab, Nav screens 530 and 430 Sandel displays, DME, Transponder, Avidyne Select buttons flashing constantly and major problems forcing an override of an erratic Autopilot System.
summary: The pilot of a single-engine aircraft experienced a total electrical and avionics failure shortly after departure, causing erratic autopilot behavior and loss of navigation. The pilot manually extended the landing gear using a high-speed technique and executed a high-speed landing without flaps, avoiding conflict with another aircraft during the approach.

synopsis: While departing TEB to the north on the TEB 8 departure, DA2000 Captain reports climbing slowly and reaching 2,000 FT after turning to 280 degree heading.
summary: The pilot and first-time SIC departed in a PROLINE4 aircraft, where engaging VNAV instead of FLCH caused a climb rate decrease. This resulted in turning to heading 280 beyond the 2.3 NM noise abatement limit before reaching the required 2,000 FT, prompting ATC to advise they were below altitude.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental aircraft was operating in the vicinity of Class D airspace. When he contacted the Tower Controller to request transition through the airspace, he was advised of an IFR departure from that airport. When he could not acquire the aircraft visually, the Tower suggested a 360 degree turn for separation. When he completed that orbit, he observed the traffic, and descended. He estimated that the aircraft passed over him within 300-500 FT.
summary: A VFR pilot transitioning a Class D airspace was instructed by Tower to perform a right 360-degree turn to separate from an IFR Cessna 172 departure. The C172 subsequently passed 300 to 500 feet above the pilot, who noted that an initial left turn would have provided better separation.

aircraft: M-20 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: M20 pilot at 4,000 FT with ZMA reports sighting a possible drone opposite direction at 3,500 FT near JANGL Intersection.
summary: A pilot approaching restricted airspace R2901E observed an unreported drone at 3,500 feet while Miami Center had cleared the area as cold. The pilot was subsequently handed off to a controller who reported a target at 1,200 feet behind the aircraft.

synopsis: Following a nose gear collapse, the pilot of a Beechcraft V35 suspects that he may have reached for the landing gear handle instead of the flap handle during a touch and go.
summary: During a touch-and-go in a retractable aircraft, the pilot collapsed the nose gear while attempting to retract flaps, likely due to mistakenly moving the gear lever instead. The pilot attributes the error to muscle memory from Cessna training and notes that forward motion forced the wheel into the well once the lock broke.

synopsis: Two helicopters, a MD500 and an AS350, had a near-miss in Class D Airspace after the Tower Controller initially pointed out mutual traffic but provided no updates and the MD500 TCAS did not display traffic.
summary: The PIC of a police helicopter and an EMS AS350 pilot nearly collided in Class Delta airspace while on opposite courses at 1,900 FT MSL. The incident occurred because neither pilot visually acquired the other, the Garmin 530 failed to display traffic, and ATC provided no follow-up updates as the aircraft converged.

synopsis: An R182 lost electrical power in a night landing pattern, but continued his final approach and landing as he could hear but not respond to ATC so he knew a departing aircraft was holding short.
summary: A Cessna R182 pilot experienced a total electrical failure during night stop-and-go training, losing lights, flaps, and radio contact. The pilot executed a go-around due to a King Air on the runway, landed without flaps or lights, and taxied to a parking area after crossing Runway YY to avoid blocking active taxiways.

synopsis: ZBW Controller voiced concern regard a new arrival fix for CYUL noting it is too close in spelling and enunciation, causing confusion even with vigilant readback hearback efforts.
summary: A pilot reported that an aircraft flying the CARTER1 STAR into CYUL incorrectly crossed the ABCOT fix at 110 instead of the new EBDOT fix. The pilot attributed this error to the similar spelling and enunciation of the two fixes, recommending a name change for EBDOT.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a likely runway separation event when forgetting that an airport vehicle was still on the runway end when departure traffic was cleared for takeoff, the reporter recommending vehicle procedures.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller cleared Air Carrier X for takeoff from Runway 13/31 without detecting an operations vehicle at the far approach end due to distance and terrain. The vehicle was a non-factor as the aircraft rotated with over 5,000 feet remaining, though the controller noted the need for better surface surveillance and official runway closures during long inspections.

synopsis: When their flaps wouldn't extend to the 35 degree landing setting the flight crew of an MD-11 executed a go around, conducted appropriate checklists, declared an emergency, landed uneventfully, had the brakes tested for heat by CFR and taxied to parking.
summary: The flight crew experienced a flap extension failure to 35 degrees during landing, prompting a go-around and emergency declaration. They successfully executed a flap 28 landing with normal cockpit indications and no brake issues.

synopsis: An A321 diverted after the flight attendants reported unknown fumes which were later detected by the flight crew who then declared an emergency and completed the Smoke/Fume QRH procedure.
summary: During cruise, pilots and cabin crew detected suspected electrical fumes, causing illness and prompting an emergency diversion. The crew flew fast to the nearest airport, accepted a runway change for speed, and landed safely with EMTs meeting them at the gate.

synopsis: Cleared for an RNAV Visual approach to Runway 8L at ATL, the autoflight system of their CRJ-200 failed to turn the base leg. The flight crew disconnected the autopilot, advised ATC, and flew an ILS backed up approach to an uneventful landing. ATC advised other aircraft had experienced similar failures.
summary: The flight crew experienced an FMS sequencing failure on the RNAV Visual approach to Runway 8L at Atlanta, causing an overflight of the CWOWN fix. The controller vectored the aircraft to the localizer, allowing the crew to manually fly the approach and land safely.

synopsis: Despite Maintenance Control's belief it was an indicator problem, an EMB-145 flight crew declared a precautionary emergency due to the illumination of the 'Brake On' light climbing through 10,000 MSL. The subsequent landing with CFR standing by was normal.
summary: During climb at 10,000 feet, the crew reported a 'Brake On' light illumination, likely caused by a sensor fault. They declared an emergency, landed normally with functional brakes, and terminated the emergency after clearing the runway.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot expressed concern about an inadequately lit construction crane in close proximity to a hospital helipad.
summary: A helicopter pilot reported a new 300-foot tower crane near a Florida hospital heliport poses a night approach hazard due to inadequate lighting and lack of NOTAMs. The pilot fears collision or go-around impacts, noting that FSDO and ATC have not yet resolved the issue despite the crane company's ability to install more lights.

synopsis: A Lear 55 pilot shut down the left engine and discharged one extinguishing bottle in response to a fire warning shortly after takeoff. The flight returned to the departure airport where Maintenance determined there was no fire and the warning was the result of a faulty fire detection loop.
summary: Pilots experienced a false left engine fire warning at 4,000 feet during climb, prompting an emergency shutdown and extinguisher discharge. The aircraft landed safely at the departure airport with no injuries or damage; the cause was identified as a faulty fire warning loop.

synopsis: An observant flight instructor training in a Cessna 172 was handed off to the second Tower Control frequency and turned to the parallel runway following a touch-and-go. While turning downwind he heard a radio call from another aircraft on downwind making 360 degree turns. He observed the aircraft at his altitude and on a collision course, so he took over control from his student and executed an evasive maneuver. He was concerned that the Tower was unaware of the situation, and that the other aircraft did not see them. They re-entered the traffic pattern and made a safe landing.
summary: A flight instructor and student in a Cessna 172 experienced a near mid-air collision on downwind while training, caused by a Cessna making an unannounced 360-degree turn. The instructor executed an aggressive climbing turn to avoid the other aircraft, which the reporter attributes to high controller workload and sequencing errors during a runway change.

synopsis: Aircoupe pilot, using a notebook computer GPS 'indicator;' attributed an error in the reported distance the airport to a GPS malfunction.
summary: A pilot on final approach to a Class D airport reported an inaccurate distance of 10 miles based on a laptop GPS, later discovering they were actually 5 miles out. The Tower verified the position and cleared the landing without incident, though the pilot noted the error highlighted risks of over-reliance on single electronic resources.

synopsis: PA30 pilot reports a runway incursion at MYNN after being instructed to follow the Challenger to Runway 30. The Challenger switches to the Tower and is cleared for takeoff without stopping and the reporter, still on Ground, follows it onto the runway. The hold short line is reported to be faint and the runway signs are well off the taxiway.
summary: The pilot and crew of a Challenger aircraft inadvertently crossed a hold short line on Taxiway L at MYNN while following another Challenger. The pilot attributed the runway incursion to overemphasizing the follow instruction, poor line visibility, distracting vegetation, and a narrow runway appearance, subsequently executing a 180-degree turn.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports he had been on-duty for 50-hours, slept for 7-hours, then was on-duty for another 30-hours. Their Maintenance Supervisor works crews on 24-hour shifts with little time off for rest due to low manpower. A dangerous environment exists, as personnel are making mistakes due to fatigue.
summary: A mechanic for Air Carrier X reported working 50-hour duty shifts with only 7 hours of sleep, followed by 30-hour shifts, due to a supervisor scheduling crews for 24 hours with little rest. The reporter stated this unrelenting schedule causes fatigue, leading to mistakes during aircraft troubleshooting and creating a dangerous situation.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ORD Controller described a go-around event when it became unclear if snow removal vehicles were in fact clear of the landing runway.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Operations Vehicles X and Y failed to coordinate with ATC while clearing Runway 9R, causing two arrivals to go around. The incident resulted from the snow team's refusal to communicate their status and their unauthorized return to the runway without clearance.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a loss of required wake turbulence separation claiming the Feeder Controller failed to provide a workable feed given the final airspace constraints.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported unsafe stacking of a B777 at 8,000 FT and an A320 at 9,000 FT over a VOR, causing proximity issues and unstable approaches. The controller attributed the loss of approved separation and high approach speeds to improper stacking procedures instead of vectoring aircraft into trail.

synopsis: M03 Controller described a loss of wake turbulence separation when the frequency transfer to MEM Tower was uncertain, the reporter suggesting new RECAT identifiers/information for the Data Blocks.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller working ARF during mid-inbound operations mistakenly believed an A310 (Air Carrier X) was cleared to Memphis Tower while a B777 (Air Carrier Y) was on final. The controller realized the A310 was less than the required 4 miles behind the B777 due to RECAT wake turbulence standards, attributing the error to confusion over the "B" weight category display.
