synopsis: Tower Controller declined to issue a ASDE-X mandated go around to an emergency fuel aircraft on short final, noting the ASDE-X alarm likely occurred because of an emergency vehicle approaching the runway at a very fast speed.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a low-fuel Beechcraft 99 emergency on final for Runway 25L when a County Operations vehicle on intersecting Runway 1R triggered an ASDE-X "GO-AROUND" warning. The controller ignored the alert to allow the aircraft to land, citing a lack of discretion in the system despite the fuel emergency.

synopsis: An EMB-140 flight crew failed to comply with the 6,000 FT MSL crossing restriction at BUTTS on the ALDAN RNAV STAR into RDU. Task saturation due to multiple crossing restriction restraints, in particular above/below windows, was cited as the primary contributing factor.
summary: The flight crew missed the 6,000-foot crossing restriction at the BUTTS fix while descending via the ALDAN arrival into RDU. The pilot attributed the error to task saturation from complex RNAV altitude gates, unfamiliarity with the procedure, and a mistaken assumption of early vectoring.

synopsis: When they broke out high after being forced into a stressful RNAV approach in bad weather due to ATC limitations and an out of service glide slope, the flight crew of an E135 opted to make a steep, unstabilized descent to land in lieu of performing a go around and remaining airborne in the inclement conditions. The reporter remonstrated himself over the decision to do so despite landing safely.
summary: The flight crew executed an RNAV 22L approach at LFT at night in thunderstorms with the glide slope inoperative. The pilot descended too high, misjudged the visual path due to rain, and landed unstably, attributing the unsafe condition to poor leadership in continuing the approach instead of executing a go-around.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate pilot voiced concern regarding the term 'converging' on several approach procedures noting the term is less than clear in it's meaning and flight crew requirements.
summary: A pilot reported a safety concern regarding the "Converging" ILS approach at PHL, noting crew confusion over the term and FMC limitations containing only one approach version. The reporter warned that executing the standard missed approach during a "Converging" clearance could lead to a collision with another aircraft's flight path.

synopsis: CRJ200 Captain arriving PHF on the DRONE 1 arrival reports evading a drone maneuvering at 4,000 FT and visible on TCAS.
summary: During arrival into PHF, the flight crew encountered an unidentified aircraft at 4,000 feet while descending. The crew avoided a TCAS Resolution Advisory by maneuvering away from the target, which they identified as a drone operating erratically in violation of altitude restrictions.

synopsis: BE400 flight crew reports rejecting a takeoff at low speed due to the Captain having red lines through heading and pitch readouts on his PFD. The AHRS 1/2 button was in the 2 position and switching back to the 1 position solved the problem.
summary: The Pilot Flying aborted a takeoff from Runway 6 at TEB after red lines appeared on the Primary Flight Display due to the AHRS 1/2 button being set to position 2. The crew resolved the issue by switching the button to position 1, attributed the cause to an insufficient pre-takeoff instrument scan, and successfully departed later.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier jet FMS database listed only the DFW BOWIE 2 propeller arrival so the flight crew requested vectors for their arrival.
summary: The flight crew reported a potential FMS database error on the BOWIE 3 arrival to DFW, where the system incorrectly provided a propeller-specific procedure instead of the jet arrival. They requested and received vectors from Regional Approach for the ILS to Runway 36L, noting the issue may affect all aircraft.

synopsis: A B737NG flight crew opted to try and climb above turbulence at their cruise altitude of FL380 and were cleared to FL400. Climbing through FL390 they encountered even greater turbulence and the aircraft could climb no higher, in fact entered an uncommanded descent. The crew declared an emergency and descended to FL350 for the uneventful remainder of their scheduled flight.
summary: The flight crew encountered heavy turbulence while climbing to FL400, causing an uncontrolled descent to FL350. The Captain hand-flew the aircraft after declaring an emergency, and the flight continued to destination without injury.

synopsis: An Embraer Phenom 100 CAS alerted ENG 1 & 2 TT0 HTR FAIL in icing conditions. The pilot descended out of icing and reported that the CAS alert indicated actual ice accumulation with the heaters enabled.
summary: The pilot of an Embraer Phenom 100 encountered rime ice and received ENG TT0 HTR FAIL messages caused by ice buildup on functional TT0 probes. The pilot descended to FL350 to exit icing conditions and landed uneventfully, though the report highlights safety risks regarding unreliable temperature data and potential engine damage.

synopsis: A private pilot in a Cessna 182 began his takeoff roll at an uncontrolled airport and then observed a commercial carrier jet taxi across the runway in front of him. He was able to abort his takeoff and maneuver behind the jet at high speed. The commercial carrier jet crew did not make any common traffic frequency announcements.
summary: A C182 pilot aborted a takeoff roll after a commercial jet entered the runway without announcing intentions on the common traffic frequency. The pilot swerved behind the jet to avoid a collision, but the jet crew never acknowledged the event or communicated their crossing.

synopsis: ZOB Controller described a confused situation when required to take over Lansing TRACON airspace due to an ATC Zero event, the reporter claiming additional training is needed for these types of occurrences.
summary: Cleveland Center Area 1 controllers, covering Lansing Approach airspace during an ATC Zero event, faced an unsafe situation when a GRR arrival descended unexpectedly due to an unknown Letter of Agreement between GRR and Lansing Approach. The reporter attributes the risk to a lack of training and coordination, recommending updated checklists and specialist briefings.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a less than authorized separation event when a emergency aircraft elected to circle the airport of intended landing to ensure a safe landing.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a BE35 declaring an emergency due to engine vibration and oil pressure issues while en route at 10,000 feet. The controller prioritized the emergency landing over increasing separation from a nearby C177, resulting in a safe landing with no injuries despite a 3-mile, 700-foot proximity.

synopsis: LGB Controller described a loss of required runway separation when a go-around clearance was ignored by a landing aircraft. The reporter claimed that a lack of English proficiency was the causal factor.
summary: A Cessna landing behind another Cessna that had not promptly exited the runway landed despite a go-around attempt due to the pilot's lack of English comprehension. This resulted in the second aircraft landing within 3,000 feet of the first.

synopsis: ZID Controller voiced concern regarding the interference being received on 121.5/243.0 at FLM work station.
summary: Air traffic controllers at the IND remote site reported unauthorized music transmissions on the 121.5/243.0 emergency frequencies at their FLM workstation. The controller attributed these interruptions to an unknown source and requested the frequency be cleared of non-ATC transmissions.

synopsis: The pilots of a B737 experienced an engine failure in cruise at 24,000 FT. They declared an emergency and diverted to another airport where a safe landing was made.
summary: During cruise, the crew experienced a loud bang and left yaw due to Engine 1 failure, characterized by zero oil, no N2 rotation, and rising EGT. The aircraft diverted, landed safely, and post-flight inspection revealed turbine debris, though the sequence of oil loss versus turbine failure remains undetermined.

synopsis: A Q400 oil pressure began fluctuating in cruise so the crew diverted assuming an indication issue because other indications were stable. However, they shut the engine down on landing because of RPM fluctuations.
summary: The crew experienced fluctuating Number 2 engine oil pressure and RPM during cruise at FL250, triggering a Master Warning and PTU cycling. They diverted and landed safely, later concluding they should have shut down the engine earlier per the checklist rather than assuming it was only an indication problem.

synopsis: An EMB-145 EICAS alerted FLAP FAIL as flaps 9 were selected for landing so the crew completed the QRH, declared an emergency, and landed without incident.
summary: The flight crew experienced a flap failure on downwind for Runway 23 while descending to 2,600 feet, triggering an EICAS caution. They completed the QRH, declared an emergency, and safely landed with flaps zero, noting that limited fuel restricted diversion options.

synopsis: A Check Airman reported the pilot flying had descended well below the visual glide slope on the Runway 28 charted Visual BRIJJ approach to SFO before being alerted by the pilot not flying. The descent was arrested and the landing completed.
summary: The flight crew descended below the visual glide slope with four red PAPI lights while approaching Runway 28 in scattered low clouds. The pilot not flying alerted the pilot flying, who reduced the descent rate, leading to a post-incident debrief on refusing visual approaches in marginal conditions.

synopsis: The pilots of an MD10 have identified foreign material inside the crew oxygen masks that would interfere with its operation.
summary: The First Officer discovered a dry cleaning cloth in his oxygen mask mouthpiece and noted that tucked head straps prevent auto-inflation. The reporter advises pilots and maintenance to ensure masks are free of debris and straps are not tucked to guarantee proper inflation.

synopsis: A First Officer with little experience in type reported that the Captain descended to 6,000 feet before JOULES intersection and lined up for DEN 17L instead of 17R, but corrected to final as ATC questioned the aircraft's altitude.
summary: A downgraded Captain and inexperienced First Officer descended below 8,000 feet minimums during a visual approach to Denver, mistakenly intercepting the wrong runway localizer. The crew corrected the lateral error after ATC queried their 1,000-foot altitude, attributing the incident to the Captain's lack of recent flight time and the crew's unfamiliarity with the airport.

synopsis: C172 Instructor and student pilot attempting to land in turbulence, low level windshear and gusty wind, bounced off the runway twice, executed a go-around, entered IMC, encountered icing and declared an emergency. After receiving vectors to an alternate airport, the pilots lost radio communication, but were able to land visually.
summary: An instructor and student pilot encountered severe windshear, turbulence, and rapid icing while navigating scattered snow walls during a checkride. After declaring an emergency and experiencing a radio failure, they executed a rough landing at an alternate airport.

aircraft: Cessna Single Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A Cessna C-162 aircraft non-flying pilot reports how the lack of a clear read-back by the pilot flying to a Tower Controller for runway crossing clearance contributed to a near miss with another aircraft taking off. Snow piled high on side of runway completely blocking vision from taxiway also a factor.
summary: The pilot flying a Cessna C-162 attempted to cross Runway XX at Foxtrot despite a hold-short instruction due to distorted radio transmission and a non-standard read-back. The pilot not flying stopped the aircraft just before a takeoff, preventing a collision caused by communication failures and blocked visibility from snow berms.

synopsis: Tower Controller voiced concern regarding the TRACON issuing a visual approach to an inbound with no prior coordination noting a developing conflict with pattern traffic.
summary: Local Control reported a conflict between a Beechjet on an unapproved visual approach and a Super King Air 350 departing Runway XX. The King Air deviated northeast off its SID without TRACON coordination, creating a potential collision risk with the descending Beechjet while visual separation was applied.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a developing conflict event when clearing an aircraft for a visual approach only to discover the aircraft was following the wrong aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that an MD88 on a visual approach cut off a B737's traffic while instructed to follow it, causing a conflict. The controller attributed the incident to issuing a "follow" clearance with ambiguous traffic descriptions while another aircraft was already turning base.

synopsis: Tower Controller described an unsafe situation when helicopter operations were difficult to observe due to the location and height of the Tower.
summary: An instructor and trainee controller cleared a C172 for takeoff on Runway 21R while an R22 helicopter was landing, causing a potential conflict. The C172 aborted after the instructor's "hold short" call was blocked by the pilot's readback, though the helicopter was airborne with over 3,000 feet of separation.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 nose gear did not extend when the landing gear was selected down so the crew declared an emergency, complied with the checklist, and landed safely after the nose gear extended. This was a repeat problem.
summary: The flight crew experienced a nose gear indication failure on approach, triggering a Gear Disagree warning despite the gear being down and locked. After cycling the gear and performing a fly-by, they landed safely with nosewheel steering failure, attributing the issue to a recurring problem previously reported at another airport.

synopsis: A CRJ-900 Captain reported that two upper wing service panels were missing, one off each wing, after an overnight landing gear pivot point service. The aircraft had previously flown several flights that day.
summary: The Captain and First Officer discovered missing inspection panels on both wings during a post-flight walk-around after the aircraft was shut down. Maintenance Control confirmed the panels were removed overnight for gear pivot point service, noting that escape path markings made them difficult to detect from the ground.

synopsis: An international B767 crew departed after multiple distractions caused by a weather related departure delay with engine shutdowns, then discovered after hours of flying that the APU had remained operating.
summary: The flight crew left the APU running during a rushed preflight checklist after multiple runway changes caused by thunderstorms. The oversight was discovered en route, resulting in increased fuel burn, but the APU was shut down and the flight continued safely to its destination.

synopsis: In descent the pilots of a B767 noticed a fuel smell in the cockpit which was confirmed by the flight attendants to also exist in the cabin. The Captain declared an emergency and received a clearance direct to the destination airport. The pilots donned their oxygen masks and performed the checklist for fumes. A safe landing was performed and the aircraft was checked by Airport Fire Rescue. A fuel leak was confirmed on the right engine which ceased when the Captain pulled the engine fire handle.
summary: The flight crew encountered a strong fuel odor and haze during descent after a hold, declaring an emergency and isolating the right pack to dissipate fumes. Upon landing, fire rescue confirmed a right engine fuel leak, which stopped after the fire handle was pulled, and the aircraft was towed to the gate.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) suggests that FAA should revise Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2000-15-15 to include inspection of the Horizontal Stabilizer Jackscrew (J/S) shaft for an out of round, or elliptical run-out movement. His company engineering had released an MD-83 aircraft for service with an excessive, visible, wobble of the Horizontal Stabilizer Jackscrew (J/S) that was noticed during a B-Check.
summary: An A&P mechanic performing a B-Check on an MD-83 discovered a .070-inch horizontal stabilizer jackscrew run-out, exceeding the .004-inch limit. Although a replacement was planned, an engineer issued a Line Engineering Order to allow the excessive run-out due to parts unavailability, which the mechanic deemed unairworthy.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 206 mistook a freshly plowed field adjacent to a private airstrip as the runway. His landing was successful but the nose wheel dug into the soft ground and caused the aircraft to flip over. The pilot was uninjured but the aircraft received some damage.
summary: The pilot landed a single-engine aircraft on a freshly tilled field mistaken for the runway due to similar dimensions and glare, causing the nose gear to dig in and flip the plane. The pilot escaped uninjured, and the aircraft sustained damage to the right wing, propeller, and vertical stabilizer.

synopsis: The downloaded flight plan dropped out of a Falcon 900EX Honeywell NZ-2000 FMS after takeoff even though the crew manually entered a revised flight plan was and verified it after entry at the gate.
summary: The pilot reported that after manually entering clearance changes into the Honeywell FMS, the system reverted to the original filed plan, causing the aircraft to deviate from ATC vectors. The crew attributed this to a glitchy FMS, noting a prior leg where the flight plan had also unexpectedly dropped out.

synopsis: The pilot of an RV8 observed electrical smoke in the cockpit. He secured the electrical master switch and turned towards the closest airport. He transmitted his situation and intentions from his handheld radio on 121.5, but was unable to receive a response. He landed successfully and established communication clear of the runway.
summary: A pilot experienced electrical smoke in the cockpit at 9,500 feet during cruise, shut off the electrical master, and landed at a nearby airport. Two-way communication was delayed because the tower could not decipher blind 121.5 calls, though the landing was uneventful.

synopsis: The pilots of a Westwind experienced an elevator trim control malfunction. With the help of the non flying pilot, they made a successful landing.
summary: The pilot in command declared an emergency during climb out after the elevator trim control malfunctioned, rendering the elevator unresponsive and slow. With assistance from the non-flying pilot, the crew returned the aircraft and landed safely.

synopsis: A DC-3A pilot reported a ground loop on landing as he attempted to expedite clearing the runway for landing traffic.
summary: The pilot of a 71-year-old aircraft attempted an exaggerated turn to exit the runway on A-7 taxiway, causing ineffective braking and a stop short of the exit. The right engine quit and back-fired due to a rich idle mixture, prompting a false fire response, but the pilot eventually exited and departed uneventfully.

synopsis: Enroute Controller provided a descent to an aircraft experiencing a cracked windshield, the reporter noting he should have declared an ATC emergency for the aircraft and provided an immediate descent.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a B737 at FL340 with a cracked windshield and muffled transmissions by descending it to FL290 and turning it away from an E145. The controller noted the situation was borderline emergency despite the pilot not declaring one, and recommended the pilot declare an emergency.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A VGT Controller issued mutual traffic to an IFR jet inbound and a single engine in the landing pattern but the jet missed his traffic by 150 feet after he descended for landing but did not have his traffic insight.
summary: An ATC controller reported that an IFR small jet descended below its 3,500-foot restriction before landing clearance was issued, resulting in a 150-foot vertical separation with a single-engine aircraft. The controller attributed the incident to the pilot's non-compliance and his own failure to verify the jet had the traffic in sight.

synopsis: F11 Controller described an unsafe condition involving SFR departure procedures noting the addition of a Local Control position coupled with more runway procedures require the need of new LOA revisions.
summary: A King Air and a BE33 departed Sanford's parallel Runways 27R and 27C on different frequencies and radar scopes, creating a safety issue due to outdated procedures and a flawed Letter of Agreement. The reporter states these conditions caused numerous close calls by shifting separation responsibility to satellite controllers instead of the Tower.

synopsis: SMO Controller described a loss of separation event during marginal weather when spacing judgement was flawed, the reporter noting the published approach chart could be a contributing factor.
summary: An air traffic controller at SMO released a C172 for departure while a Citation and a twin Cessna were on final, resulting in likely lost separation when the twin Cessna executed a missed approach. The controller attributed the error to forcing the release under pressure and noted that the airport's confusing circling approach plate contributes to frequent missed approaches.

synopsis: A B737-300 Forward Cargo Fire Bell alerted at 9,000 FT on departure, so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport where the flight crew had maintenance and fire crews keep the cargo closed until all passengers were removed.
summary: During climb out, the flight crew declared an emergency due to false forward cargo bay fire indications and returned for a priority landing. Fire crews confirmed no fire after all passengers disembarked, though they initially misunderstood the QRH requirement to delay opening the cargo door.

synopsis: A B747 Captain complained that ZDC is frequently modifying the constraints of the GIBBZ RNAV STAR in ways that make it impossible to comply, specifically changing the 'At or above FL240' at HESEE to a hard crossing just 5.7 NM beyond a previous hard crossing of FL270 at PHOOW.
summary: A pilot reported that ATC issued unattainable altitude clearances on the GIBBZ ONE RNAV arrival HVQ transition, specifically requiring a descent from FL270 at PHOOW to FL240 at HESEE within 5.7 NM. The pilot stated the procedure is flawed because descending 3,000 feet in that distance at 280 knots is impossible even with speed brakes fully extended.

synopsis: A B757 flight crew descending via the GIBBZ RNAV STAR to IAD had to request vectors after GIBBZ because their ND did not display the tracks after GIBBZ associated with their landing runway.
summary: The flight crew encountered an FMC discontinuity after the GIBBZ arrival fix and received a heading from ATC. The controller attributed the error to a missed, hard-to-locate routing insert that does not load into the FMC, which the crew felt was exacerbated by recent procedure changes.

synopsis: A B717 had an engine compressor stall on takeoff during a Function Check Flight so the flight returned to the departure airport with both engines operating.
summary: Pilots conducting a post-maintenance Functional Check Flight experienced a right engine compressor stall shortly after takeoff during a left turn, causing a loud bang, yaw, and smoke. The crew returned for a safe landing after alerts extinguished, noting the event highlights the need for day VMC conditions during FCFs.

synopsis: An EMB-170 EICAS alerted 'FLAP FAIL' while climbing through FL180 with the flaps already retracted so the crew continued to their destination, declared an emergency after the flaps failed to extend and completed a normal, abnormal landing.
summary: The flight crew of Aircraft X continued to destination after a 'Flap Fail' caution occurred during climb due to a deferred flap skew sensor. They safely landed with flaps retracted and slats extended after declaring an emergency, attributing the successful outcome to simulator training and MEL planning.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A First Officer mistakenly followed a flight director left turn command after a TEB Runway 24 RUUDY 4 takeoff, but the Captain alerted him so that he turned to the correct heading as ATC took note of the error.
summary: During departure from TEB Runway 24 on the RUUDY 4 procedure, the pilot flying followed erroneous command bars at 400 feet AGL, turning 20 degrees left before the pilot not flying corrected the course. ATC questioned the deviation, which was attributed to a mistake, and the flight continued without further difficulty.

synopsis: A CRJ-900 crew reported that two upper wing service panels were missing, one of each wing, after an overnight landing gear pivot point service. The crew flew the initial flight after the service but were notified long after about the event.
summary: Maintenance personnel left an unsecured wing inspection panel on the aircraft, which later detached and was ingested by Engine 2, causing damage. The Captain and First Officer detected no anomalies during their preflight, flight, or postflight inspections, and the issue was only discovered by a subsequent crew after two additional legs.

synopsis: A MD-80 TAIL COMPARTMENT TEMP HI light illuminated climbing through FL210, so the QRH was completed, an emergency declared and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The crew encountered a 'TAIL COMPARTMENT TEMP HI' light while climbing past FL210, prompting an emergency return to the departure airport. After the light extinguished, they exceeded 250 knots below 10,000 feet for a quick landing, resulting in an overweight landing and the aircraft being taken out of service with no heat signature found.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 crew preparing for takeoff on DTW Runway 22L first dealt with an AUTO PACK FAIL prior to takeoff, then an 'EFIS COMP MON' alert for a heading issue. After takeoff the crew determined both PFD 1 and 2 headings were off about 25 degrees but errors were cleared with QRH completion.
summary: The crew deferred a left pack failure on the ground, then encountered an EFIS COMP MON message and incorrect heading indications during departure from Runway 22L. The pilot flying initiated a turn in the wrong direction due to faulty displays, causing a lateral deviation that was corrected by cross-checking the standby heading and slewing the instruments.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reported a damaged O-Ring seal for an Air/Oil Cooler line on #2 Engine had caused an inflight diversion of a company Q-400 aircraft, due to a steady loss of oil pressure and oil quantity.
summary: Mechanics X and Y missed an oil pressure check step and cut an O-ring during #2 engine oil cooler installation, causing an in-flight oil leak and pressure loss. The aircraft diverted, and the engine was removed to replace the damaged line after FDR data confirmed the procedural error.

synopsis: An M20 pilot deadsticked to a safe landing at a nearby airport when the engine failed while switching tanks. A malfunctioning fuel tank selector valve was reponsible.
summary: During descent, the pilot switched the fuel selector from left to right, causing engine failure due to lost fuel pressure. A safe landing on Runway 18 occurred with no injuries, later attributed to the selector handle separating from the stem, leaving the valve stuck in the off position.

synopsis: A Global 700 autopilot disconnected on the TEB Runway 24 RUUDY 4 Departure at 1,300 FT due to turbulence and the pilot descended from 1,800 FT to cross WENTZ at 1,500 FT.
summary: The pilot of a Global departing Teterboro Runway 24 encountered moderate turbulence and strong winds at 1,300 feet, causing the autopilot to disengage. The pilot manually flew the aircraft, which overshot the assigned 1,500-foot altitude to 1,900 feet before descending and re-engaging the autopilot without loss of control or conflict.

synopsis: After landing on the right parallel runway, an older M-20 pilot was cleared to hold between the runways, but failed to fully clear the right parallel until prompted by the Local Controller. Pilot cited the lack of a nap prior to flight as a contributing factor.
summary: A retired pilot over 60, deprived of a pre-flight nap due to terminal noise, lost focus while exiting a runway after landing in a quartering tailwind. He stopped short of the required hold-short lines, attributing the error to age, distractions, and fatigue, before complying with tower instructions to correct his position.

synopsis: Cessna 206 departed the runway during a routine landing.
summary: The pilot of a C206 with a STOL kit experienced a violent left veer and steering failure upon nose wheel touchdown on a paved runway. The aircraft exited onto grass to avoid a go-around, triggering the ELT, and was later grounded by an A&P for suspected nose gear linkage and lubrication issues.

synopsis: A Falcon 2000 First Officer became distracted by a radio call and did not make the TEB 8 SID 2.3 DME turn, but did turn at 2.5 DME when alerted by the non flying Captain.
summary: The pilot flying failed to turn at 2.3 DME to heading 280 because the captain was distracted by a radio call. The turn was initiated late at 2.5 DME due to fatigue and distraction, with no other traffic present.

synopsis: Cessna 172 pilot experienced a crosswind landing where the left tire departed the wheel.
summary: The pilot of a rented aircraft experienced a tire blowout on the left main gear during landing on Runway 22L due to a crosswind gust. The incident caused the rim to strike the runway, resulting in a bouncing landing, propeller damage, and a bent nose gear before the aircraft was towed to the hangar.

synopsis: Local Controller elected not to issue a go around after receiving an AMASS alert noting the target activating the alert was behind the aircraft in question and no other runway traffic was observed.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller on Local Control West received a false ASDE alert to send a landing B757 around during rainy IFR conditions. The controller kept the aircraft on the runway, attributing the error to the system detecting a target behind the aircraft's actual position.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew, after encountering wake from preceding B757, deviated from assigned speed on arrival to LAX to avoid further wake turbulence.
summary: The pilot flying an ILS 24R approach at LAX slowed 20 KTS and flew high on the glideslope to avoid wake turbulence from a preceding 747. The reporter attributed the risk to ATC prioritizing standard spacing over safe separation despite low visibility and multiple wake turbulence cautions.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports having their right winglet removed during pushback by the left wingtip of a B737 to their right as it begins to taxi away from the gate. This event occurred during darkness with cockpit windows partially obsecured with snow.
summary: During a night pushback in snow, the flight crew and tug driver collided with an adjacent B737, severing the reporting aircraft's right winglet. The incident was caused by reduced visibility from snow-covered windows and the tug pushing the aircraft too close to the other plane while it was turning.

synopsis: The Captain and Dispatcher describe the radio and intercom issues on an A321 after the pushback crew disconnected the headset. The problem returned when the throttles were advanced for takeoff, so the crew performed a slow speed reject. After troubleshooting, the Flight Deck to Ground Interphone system was deferred as inoperative. However, when the next station replaced the headset jack and the system reactivated, the problem returned. The system operated normally after the Audio Management Unit was replaced.
summary: The flight crew experienced loud static squeals in the intercom and radios during pushback and takeoff attempts caused by a faulty headset jack and Audio Management Unit. After multiple runway exits and a 3.5-hour delay, maintenance replaced the Audio Management Unit to resolve the issue, though the crew clarified that no rejected takeoff occurred as takeoff power was never set.

synopsis: Citation X flight crew descended below assigned crossing altitude.
summary: During descent on the JAIKE THREE arrival, the crew descended 400 feet below a crossing altitude after the FMS dropped all programmed altitudes upon runway selection. The pilot flying disconnected the autopilot to return to 13,000 feet, and ATC confirmed no traffic conflict existed.

synopsis: C560XL cabin failed to pressurize, resulting in an uneventful return to the departure airport.
summary: During initial climb-out, the crew encountered a cabin climb rate of 4,000 FPM and leveled at 5,000 feet in a holding pattern. After determining the aircraft was not pressurizing, they returned to the airport without further incident.

synopsis: While taxiing on intersecting runways for takeoff, an MD-83 flight crew experienced a close encounter with a Cirrus on final to a runway they had been cleared to hold short of. Fatigue induced complacency and familiarity were cited as contributing factors.
summary: The flight crew mistakenly crossed Runway YY while taxiing, causing a near-midair collision with an approaching Cirrus and a flight attendant injury due to sudden braking. The pilots attributed the error to complacency from repetitive taxi instructions and a failure to verify hold-short clearances at the intersection.

synopsis: A TBM-850 pilot, in daylight VMC, received a low altitude alert from the Tower when he failed to transition from monitoring a GPS generated 'required rate of descent' to visually monitoring the PAPI adjacent to the runway of intended landing.
summary: The pilot descended on a visual approach to SQL using GPS Vertical Speed Required, neglecting to level off at 1,000 feet to intercept the VASI. The Tower issued a low altitude alert, prompting the pilot to correct the descent.

synopsis: Distracted by a cracked cockpit window while at FL270, and anxious to reduce pressurization differential, the pilot of a PA-46 failed to arrest his descent at FL240 as cleared.
summary: During a demo flight at FL270, a pilot's side window cracked, prompting an emergency descent. The pilot descended below the assigned FL240 clearance due to distraction by the emergency and poor communication, later receiving clearance to 6,000 feet.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: A pilot stated that some Alaska airport ATIS verbal recording rates are too high for the information to be recorded and at select airports some critical information cannot be written down after listening twice.
summary: A pilot reported that prerecorded ATIS broadcasts at several Alaska facilities are read too quickly, preventing accurate transcription of critical data like runway conditions and altimeter settings. This communication failure hinders safe flight decisions, and despite prior complaints, the excessive verbal speed remains uncorrected.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described an airspace incursion event when an adjacent Controller failed to follow proper procedure claiming he/she observed no traffic and entered the airspace, the reporter questioning the younger Controller's safety culture.
summary: Two F-16s en route to ZZZ entered Sector XX airspace without coordination from Sector YY, where a controller used a "look and go" method despite limited data. The reporter attributes this safety breach to a culture where younger controllers incorrectly accept uncoordinated airspace use, causing unexpected traffic conflicts.

synopsis: When it was necessary to shut down one engine due to zero oil pressure and quantity, a B757 flight crew diverged from their oceanic track and returned to their departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced zero oil pressure and quantity with a rapid EGT rise during cruise. They shut down the engine, diverted from their oceanic track, and returned to the departure airport.

synopsis: Air Carrier aircraft experienced a loss of engine oil quantity and pressure, resulting in engine shut down.
summary: The crew experienced a rapid drop in Number 1 engine oil quantity to zero at FL310, prompting a precautionary shutdown and return to the departure airport. After dumping fuel to reach maximum landing weight, the Check Airman performed an uneventful single-engine landing despite a fuel imbalance.

synopsis: At FL380 B757 EICAS alerted AIRSPEED UNRELIABLE, MACH/SPEED TRIM, and RUDDER RATIO in an area of moderate icing. The crew, assumed pitot icing, descended to FL350 where the alerts ceased.
summary: The flight crew encountered moderate icing at FL380, blocking pitot tubes and causing unreliable airspeed and EICAS warnings. They descended to FL320 with anti-ice systems active, resolving the issue as airspeed indications stabilized near FL350.

synopsis: During initial climb, the B757's left engine lost power, an emergency was declared and flight returned to the airport.
summary: The crew experienced a left engine compressor stall and thrust loss at 600 feet AGL shortly after takeoff, causing an emergency return. Although the engine recovered, a second stall occurred at 800 feet AGL, leading to an overweight landing with emergency services standing by.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reports failure of a fuel truck driver to yield at Spot 8 during initial taxi for takeoff.
summary: The flight crew stopped their aircraft at PHL while taxiing to Runway 27L after a fuel tanker truck cut a corner and passed within 15 feet of the nose. The near-miss occurred because the driver left the designated roadway, creating a blind spot that prevented seeing the aircraft.

synopsis: During takeoff, aircraft experienced an electrical malfunction, declared an emergency, and returned to land.
summary: The pilot experienced a cycling number 1 transfer bus failure during takeoff, causing instrument and navigation mode failures. After burning fuel in a holding pattern, the crew declared an emergency and returned for an uneventful overweight landing.

synopsis: Light twin Captain reports engine failure shortly after takeoff. Noticing high fuel flow to the engine, the aux fuel pump is turned off and the engine regains power. Flight returns to departure airport.
summary: The pilot experienced a right engine surge and power loss during climb-out caused by a malfunctioning auxiliary fuel pump flooding the engine. After turning off the pump to restore power, the pilot returned to the field and landed normally.

synopsis: Gulfstream V Captain discovers SAV runway lighting after Tower closure is set to only illuminate one of the two runways, this information is not readily available to flight crews via ATIS or NOTAM. This resulted in a go around when Runway 19 lights could not be activated, followed by a visual approach to the lighted Runway 10.
summary: The crew attempted an RNAV (GPS) Runway 19 approach at SAV at night but could not activate the runway lights despite following standard procedures. They executed a missed approach and landed on Runway 10 after learning the tower pre-selects one runway for lighting at night without issuing a NOTAM or ATIS notification.

synopsis: B747-400 Captain experiences autoflight failures during departure that are largely overcome by using the center autopilot to fly to LAX. When approach mode is armed the center autopilot and autothrust become inoperative and a go around is initiated. The second approach is successfully hand flown in raw data to a normal landing.
summary: The flight crew experienced repeated autopilot, flight director, and auto-throttle failures during departure and arrival at Los Angeles. They successfully executed a missed approach and landed using raw data after automation failed again during the ILS approach to Runway 25L.

synopsis: Cessna 208B veered left during initial taxi, indicating the crew had no nosewheel steering coming within feet of a service vehicle.
summary: Two pilots experienced a loss of steering and braking while taxiing a loaded aircraft, nearly colliding with a service truck. The crew attributed the incident to suspected brake line corrosion from long-term parking on a slope, though a subsequent mechanical inspection found no abnormalities.

synopsis: ZSE Controller described a near terrain clearance infraction with a departure being handed off from P80, the reporter questioned the absence of a MSAW alarm and the handling by P80.
summary: P80 controllers failed to assign a Citation C560 the required 15,000 feet departure clearance, allowing it to level at 6,000 feet in IMC near rising terrain. R-Side controllers intervened to climb the aircraft, preventing a potential terrain impact, while noting that MSAW did not activate as expected.

synopsis: Two pilots report about the Crew Oxygen System on their B737-700 aircraft that would not give a proper test after they had flown the aircraft for five legs. Contract Maintenance had reported the oxygen bottle valve handle was not open.
summary: A B737-700 crew reported that a contract mechanic found the oxygen bottle valve not fully open three days after replacement, despite normal pressure readings during five prior legs. The pilot suspects the valve was only partially opened during installation, noting no flight deck procedure exists to detect this condition.

synopsis: B737 crew oxygen was discovered to be in the 'off' position subsequent to conducting a flight.
summary: The Captain and First Officer of Aircraft X were informed that the crew oxygen valve was found off, potentially following a maintenance bottle change two days prior. The pilots suspect the valve was inadvertently closed down-line or missed during preflight, prompting a commitment to more rigorous system checks.

synopsis: A319 flight crew cleared to 'descend via' the Las Vegas TYSSN THREE Arrival by Center and subsequently vectored off the arrival by Approach Control, continued descent in accordance with the arrival restrictions until advised by Approach to stop descent.
summary: During descent into Las Vegas on the TYSSN 3 arrival, the crew descended via the procedure to 8,000 feet after being vectored off the route by Approach Control. The reporter attributed the ambiguity to a breakdown in controller communications and lack of amended altitude clearances when the aircraft was removed from the arrival.

synopsis: EMB-145EP flight crew reported loss of Number 2 hydraulic system. An emergency was declared and they returned to departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced a HYD2 LO QTY advisory after rotation, followed by an engine-driven pump failure and total loss of Hydraulic System 2 at FL260. They returned to base, landed safely with ARFF escort, and identified a leaking drain as the cause.

synopsis: EMB145 flight crew experiences a rudder overboost message during climb and QRH procedures are complied with allowing the flight to continue. Maintenance will be required prior to the next departure and the First Officer has difficulty contacting Maintenance and conveying this information to them. Eventually the crew is directed to return to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew received a rudder over boost message during climb and faced significant delays contacting Maintenance Control and Dispatch. They declared an emergency and returned to the departure airport for a normal landing, noting that slow company communication created uncertainty regarding whether to continue or return.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 descended into IMC at about FL350 and lost all air data computer information, resulting in the loss of numerous systems and leading to an airframe overspeed. A diversion was made to a nearby airport where all systems returned to normal in VMC conditions.
summary: The flight crew experienced a total Air Data Computer failure in IMC at FL350, causing unreliable airspeed and autopilot disconnection. They maintained control using pitch and power during an emergency descent until instruments recovered at 12,000 feet, resulting in a safe landing despite probable airframe overspeed.

synopsis: Shortly after encountering significant turbulence while deviating for weather, the flight crew of a CRJ-200 had to shut down the left engine due to its failure to spool up, accompanied by high ITT, following a descent.
summary: The crew encountered severe turbulence enroute, deviating 500 feet above assigned altitude with ATC approval. Later, during descent to 4,000 feet, the right engine flamed out with an ITT spike upon throttle advance, forcing an emergency landing after failed restart attempts.

synopsis: B757 flight crew and two of the flight attendants describe the events leading up to a return to the gate and an evacuation that follows when smoke is detected coming from the wheel well by ground personnel. The Captain had intended that passengers leave promptly through the 2L entry door, but some of the crew and passengers used the escape slide at the 4L door.
summary: A flight attendant reported a hydraulic pump failure and smoke on the left wing during taxi, causing the aircraft to return to the gate. Following emergency announcements and passenger movement to the rear, the attendant armed the door and deployed the slide to evacuate the aircraft.

synopsis: A B-17 Flying Fortress flight crew on a media flight may have briefly entered the local area Class B while investigating an aurally perceived power plant anomaly. After landing they determined an exhaust stack from the Number 4 engine had departed the airframe.
summary: The pilot and co-pilot in a B-17 experienced an engine noise and a Class B airspace incursion during a local media flight. Post-flight inspection revealed the Number 4 engine lost its Number 3 cylinder exhaust stack and the cowl flap was burned.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a loss of separation event when a SVFR helicopter on a rescue mission was less than the required distance from an IFR inbound with minimum fuel. The reporter suggested a new LOA would have assisted in this case.
summary: Local Control and Approach controllers managed a conflict between an SVFR news helicopter assisting a rescue and a low-fuel IFR twin Cessna in Class D airspace with low visibility. Without a Letter of Agreement for reduced separation, controllers relied on terrain and procedural constraints to allow both aircraft to land safely despite potential regulatory non-compliance.

synopsis: B737-300 Captain taxiing to the runway at BWI reported having to make a sudden stop to avoid a collision with another Company aircraft.
summary: The pilot executed an emergency stop during taxi to Runway 15R to avoid a collision with a company aircraft emerging from a blind spot on Taxiway P. The incident resulted from conflicting ATC clearances, the pilot's slow taxi speed, and the other aircraft's failure to confirm its sequence.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reports a vigorous autopilot pitch up as the aircraft is capturing the assigned altitude of 6,000 FT. The autopilot is quickly disconnected by the FP and the aircraft returned to 6,000 FT. Shortly before and during this event the Captain was testing the TCAS and deleting CLB-2 from the autothrust system.
summary: During a climb from 4,000 to 6,000 feet with Autopilot B engaged, the aircraft pitched up 20 degrees and lost airspeed upon altitude capture, coinciding with a TCAS failure and FMC key issues. The crew manually recovered the aircraft, but Autopilot B and TCAS remained inoperative and were subsequently MEL'd.

synopsis: A B737-700 First Officer reported a series of flight crews flew an aircraft with the crew oxygen system not energized but he is certain that he successfully tested the oxygen system prior to his first flight on that aircraft.
summary: The pilot reported that an aircraft he flew was later found to have an oxygen bottle turned off, despite his normal five-second F.I.G. test showing no abnormal gauge drop. He suggested extending the test duration to ten seconds or having both pilots test simultaneously to better detect such issues.

synopsis: Air Carrier complained about the new dispatch software which reportedly increases workload and fails to complete required actions.
summary: Dispatchers reported that the Dispatch Decision Support (DDS) system caused safety issues by omitting runway data from weight and balance closeouts due to flawed weather logic. The reporter manually corrected ACARS transmissions for airborne flights and added runway weights for pending flights, attributing the error to DDS malfunction.

synopsis: Dispatcher voiced concern regarding a new software program designed to reduce fuel loads claiming the attention required of this new system detracts from more important duties.
summary: A company fuel reduction program caused weight and balance irregularities, forcing the dispatcher to manually calculate landing performance. The reporter attributes this safety issue to an unexplained program built by inexperienced personnel, which delays flight releases and hinders flight progress monitoring.

synopsis: EMB145 First Officer describes an electrical fume event with a pressurization anomaly at FL250 requiring descent and diversion to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The flight crew diverted an aircraft with an MEL on Pack 2 after detecting electrical fumes and a pressurization failure at FL250. The simultaneous issues increased workload, prompting a descent and non-emergency landing with priority ATC handling.

synopsis: C402 pilot reports landing long at high speed with a strong crosswind and being unable to stop on the runway due to brake failure. Aircraft is taxied back on the runway and to the gate.
summary: The pilot experienced brake failure during landing on Runway 14 in gusty winds, resulting in a runway overrun of 10–20 feet. The aircraft was safely stopped off the runway end, passengers were offloaded, and the pilot attributed the incident to soft brakes and late throttle reduction.

synopsis: A B737NG flight crew was surprised when, while at cruise, the flaps extended to the one degree detent, apparently the result of resistance to fully engage the zero degree gate during retraction.
summary: Pilots reported an uncommanded flap extension to 1 degree during cruise above FL200, accompanied by a LE FLAPS TRANSIT light and handle resistance at the 0-degree detent. The crew suspects the handle never fully seated, causing migration, and Maintenance inspected the system after landing.

synopsis: An A300 flight crew declared an emergency and returned to their departure airport after receipt of an Avionics Smoke warning accompanied by the smell of electrical fumes. A circuit breaker involved with an associated system had not been pulled when deferred prior to departure.
summary: During enroute climb, the crew encountered avionics smoke and fumes caused by an overheated Field Limit Computer System 2 due to a deferral that did not require pulling circuit breakers. The crew declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport, and landed safely after fire services inspected the aircraft.

synopsis: A Technical Support Lead Mechanic reports about an ongoing problem with electronic tablets that are suppose to help Maintenance personnel access MEL's, Aircraft History and Aircraft Maintenance Manuals (AMM). Lack of WiFi features and inability to print Wiring Diagrams for troubleshooting purposes were also noted.
summary: A mechanic at Air Carrier X reported that intermittent tablet performance and difficult wiring diagrams create human factors issues at stations without maintenance. The reporter suggested enabling WiFi or adding printers to improve access, though security concerns currently prevent WiFi activation.

synopsis: At an intermediate stop, a B206 pilot turned off the anti-collision and position lights to conserve battery power and then took off without turning them on.
summary: During a night EMS helicopter departure, the pilot failed to turn on anti-collision and position lights due to fatigue and altered start procedures. The aircraft flew for three minutes under Class C airspace with lights off before the pilot noticed the error and corrected it.

synopsis: The pilot of a SR22 turned towards higher terrain as he attempted to reload the departure procedure. He was operating below the minimim vectoring altitude so the Air Traffic Controller advised the pilot to reverse course until able to become established on the departure route.
summary: The pilot departed with an IFR clearance but failed to load the SID into the Garmin 430 due to distraction, causing a deviation toward high terrain below minimum vectoring altitude. ATC vectored the aircraft 180 degrees to avoid a potentially fatal collision, attributing the error to the pilot's hesitation and lack of GPS verification.

synopsis: PA32 pilot experiences landing gear collapse after landing on a clear calm day, with all gear indicating down.
summary: The pilot reported a landing gear collapse on touchdown after a normal approach with three green lights and no warnings. An eyewitness observed the nose gear failing first, followed by the right main gear, resulting in no injuries while the cause remains under investigation.

synopsis: Ground Controller described a ground conflict event involving Ground Control and Ramp Control, indicating that Ramp issued push back clearance to the wrong aircraft.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managed a taxiing Air Carrier X aircraft that misidentified its gate as 25 instead of 29 while communicating with Ramp Control. The controller coordinated with the Flight Line Manager and Air Carrier Y to resolve the confusion, allowing the aircraft to pull back and proceed safely.

synopsis: ZMA Controller described a loss of separation event between two aircraft by being transferred from ZJX caused an overtake speed differential, the reporter recommending that altitude be used until in-trail separation can be assured.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported a loss of separation between an E55P and a CL60 in ZJX airspace due to poor vectoring and speed control by the previous sector. The controller corrected the situation by issuing descent and turn clearances after misinterpreting a bad beacon code as ground speed, noting that vertical separation would have prevented the event.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a loss of separation event during staggered ILS approaches, listing distractions and training as contributing factors.
summary: An experienced Final Controller and a trainee managed a near-miss between an Airbus A319 and a CRJ-200 during staggered ILS approaches when the trainee delayed a turn and base leg traffic descended slowly. The controller executed emergency turns and descents to separate the aircraft, which triggered TCAS maneuvers, attributing the incident to distraction and inadequate trainee supervision.

synopsis: ACT Tower Controller described an incursion into a non-movement area when clearing an aircraft holding short of Runway 1 for takeoff on Runway 32 with specific instructions to taxi via B2 and B3.
summary: An air traffic controller issued taxi instructions to a C414 for Runway 32, but the pilot misinterpreted them, taxied across a non-movement area, and took off without clearance. The controller did not cancel the departure due to safety concerns and instead coordinated with Radar Approach after the aircraft became airborne.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a loss of terrain separation event when traffic cleared via conventional navigation failed to navigate properly and was off course causing the terrain issue.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a P-3 Orion pilot deviated from a cleared ILS 26 approach by descending below 6,000 feet and flying off course. The controller attributed the incident primarily to poor pilot navigation, though admitted a delay in communication occurred because the controller failed to switch the aircraft to the correct frequency.

synopsis: P50 Controller voiced concern regarding the Tower wake separation techniques used with subsequent departures claiming the procedure is unsafe and results in wake turbulence encounters.
summary: A CRJ2 pilot reported moderate wake turbulence from a preceding departure while on Departure frequency. The controller attributes this recurring hazard to PHX Tower's use of visual separation and 6,000-foot airborne clearances, warning that this unsafe procedure risks a future accident.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a traffic pattern conflict event when less than clear procedures in a new LOA with the TRACON introduce confusion as to how and who was responsible for sequencing etc.
summary: Tower controllers and pilots of a C182 and T38 experienced a close call on final for Runway 34L due to sequencing confusion under a new LOA. The T38 overtook the slower C182 with less than one mile separation, forcing an immediate go-around after the controller failed to confirm the T38 received a break-off instruction from Approach.

synopsis: TRACON Controller voiced concern that, at times, aircraft departing with required wake separation request to deviate for wake avoidance, indicating that during heavy departure pushes this can be a separation problem.
summary: An ATC controller reported that a B737 pilot requested a course deviation for wake turbulence while following an A319 on departure under visual separation. The controller stated this frequent request increases workload and creates a safety situation during major departure pushes.

synopsis: P50 Controller expressed concern regarding the visual separation techniques used by PHX Tower and the resulting wake turbulence concerns.
summary: An air traffic controller at PHX intervened when an A319 overtook and outclimbed an A321 on parallel northbound departures, losing visual separation. The controller stopped the A321's climb and turned the A319 to restore safe separation, citing unsafe visual launches on same-direction SIDs.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a near separation loss, claiming the facility 'flash through' procedures are dangerous and should be terminated.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller assigned an A320 to descend from FL310 to FL290 using an interim altitude procedure, but the pilot reported a PC12 at FL290 ahead. The controller halted the A320 at FL300 to avoid a potential loss of separation, attributing the near-miss to the dangerous "flash through" interim altitude practice.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a confused navigation event when an aircraft experienced icing and had difficulty complying with ATC clearances.
summary: An air traffic controller failed to issue a clearance limit to a C182 pilot experiencing GPS issues and icing while confused about the approach. Despite the controller's distraction from internal disagreements and the pilot's deviations, the aircraft landed without incident.

synopsis: B737-400 Captain is informed during takeoff that his First Officer has no airspeed indication and the takeoff is rejected.
summary: The First Officer reported a failed airspeed indicator at 80 knots, prompting the Pilot Flying to execute a rejected takeoff below 90 knots with armed but inactive auto brakes. Maintenance replaced the faulty indicator and confirmed brake cooling before the aircraft taxied to the gate and departed.

synopsis: An Air Carrier flight crew, given a vector direct to MALNR and cleared to 'descend via' the MALNR RNAV arrival to RDU, descended to the published crossing altitude for MALNR. Post-flight call to ATC revealed that descent was not authorized since they were not on a published segment of the arrival.
summary: The flight crew descended via the MALNR ONE RNAV Arrival while on a direct routing off the published course after receiving a "descend via" clearance from Washington Center. Post-flight review confirmed the descent was premature because the direct routing removed them from the profile, caused by a misleading clearance and crew inexperience with Optimum Profile Descent procedures.

synopsis: A319 Captain is informed of an ATC delay during taxi out and elects to shut down both engines with the APU providing power to conserve fuel. The APU shuts down and cannot be restarted requiring the aircraft be towed back to the gate.
summary: The crew taxied to the runway end, shut down engines, and experienced an APU auto shutdown followed by a total aircraft power loss eight minutes later. The aircraft was towed back to the gate, the APU was deferred, and the flight continued to the destination.

synopsis: DHC8-300 flight crew reports being struck by lightning during approach, causing the loss of both DC generators. Flight continues to a normal landing with TRU's supplying DC power.
summary: Pilots reported a lightning strike while being vectored for an ILS approach, causing the loss of both DC generators. They executed the emergency checklist, landed safely using the AC system, and criticized Dispatch for pressuring crews to fly into deteriorating weather.

synopsis: MD80 flight crew experienced an AC Crosstie Lockout, Left Generator OFF, and L AC Bus OFF indications during descent for landing. An emergency is declared and as much of the QRH procedure as possible for the failure is accomplished prior to landing.
summary: During descent on arrival, the crew experienced left generator and AC bus failures with autopilot disconnect. The Captain declared an emergency, flew the visual approach, and landed safely while the First Officer managed abnormal and landing checklists.

synopsis: During approach, the pilot flying disconnected the autothrottles to expedite speed reduction, and aircraft slowed undetected to below reference speed.
summary: The pilot flying a final approach disconnected autothrottles to comply with a Tower speed reduction but forgot to re-engage them, causing an airspeed decay and momentary stick shaker activation. The pilot attributed the incident to breaking established habit patterns and failing to communicate the autothrottle disconnection to the crew.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: A pilot reported that the BRW PAPI is located on the runway's right side, but a Commercial and NOS charts for BRW indicate it is located on the left side.
summary: A pilot approaching Runway 07 at Barrow airport (BRW) found the PAPI located on the right side, contrary to Commercial Charts and NOS plates showing it on the left. The reporter recommends updating these charts to reflect the correct PAPI location.

synopsis: A300 flight crew reports an engine failure during taxi out with smoke and possible engine fire. Crew elects to evacuate the aircraft as the fire crew arrives on the scene, and the logbook entry for the event is forgotten.
summary: During taxi, the crew experienced a generator fault followed by an engine failure and smoke from the left engine, prompting a ground evacuation. Firefighters extinguished the smoke, and the crew was transported to a new aircraft for a transload and trip continuation.

synopsis: An A330 flight crew heard a muffled sound, felt a pressure change and noted the cabin altitude begin to climb rapidly. They declared an emergency, descended to a safe altitude where stable pressurization was regained and continued the short remaining distance to their destination.
summary: The flight crew experienced a rapid cabin altitude increase at FL380, likely caused by a ruptured duct or bleed issue, prompting an emergency descent to 10,000 feet. Despite some oxygen masks failing to deploy, the aircraft landed uneventfully with no visible damage after maintenance confirmed closed outflow valves.

synopsis: EMB175 Captain reports failure of slats to extend when selected during approach. After QRH procedure (return flap lever to previous position) the flaps and slats extend normally. Maintenance can find no faults. The anomaly repeats on the next leg with the same outcome. This time Maintenance detected possible faults in the Flap/slat computer or the flap lever.
summary: During approach, slats failed to deploy on the first attempt twice but extended after QRH checklist procedures. Maintenance identified possible electrical faults in SF-ACE one or the slat/flap lever, and FDRs were pulled for NTSB reporting.

synopsis: BE400 Captain reports failure of fuel pumps in the fuselage to shut off when the tank is empty. The abnormal checklist is consulted and the pumps are secured via pulled circuit breakers. The flight diverts to a suitable airport.
summary: The crew diverted and declared an emergency when fuel transfer pumps failed to shut off after the fuselage tank emptied, causing erratic annunciators. They secured the pumps via circuit breakers and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew experiences level two alerts during approach for SEL ELEV FEEL MAN and SEL FLAP LIM OVRD. At the same time the Captain detects low airspeed and alerts the flying First Officer before determining that the Captain's airspeed is in error. A go-around is initiated and the QRH consulted, which leads to the Unreliable Airspeed checklist and CADC switching. A near normal approach and landing ensues.
summary: During an IMC approach, a Captain and First Officer experienced autopilot disconnects and airspeed discrepancies caused by a faulty #1 CADC. While managing the emergency, the crew briefly descended 250–300 feet below 4,000 feet due to distractions before completing a safe landing.

synopsis: Near mid-air collision by two single engine aircraft on parallel approaches.
summary: While on short final for Runway 34R, a Mooney aircraft cleared for Runway 34L drifted into our flight path within 100 feet. The First Officer executed a go-around to avoid collision, and the aircraft subsequently landed safely after the Tower Supervisor investigated the Mooney's deviation.

synopsis: CRJ200 Captain detects erratic oil pressure during climbout and elects to return to the departure airport. The oil pressure warning is flashing during approach and comes on steady after landing and the engine is shut down. Maintenance discovers O-rings were omitted on an air turbine starter change the day prior.
summary: The crew experienced erratic left engine oil pressure on climbout through FL190, returned to the departure airport, and landed normally. A mechanic attributed the issue to excessive oil loss caused by missing O-rings during an air turbine starter change the previous day.

synopsis: A B737-800 FMS reverted to the full DFW BYP RNAV arrival beginning at LIT after ATC changed the landing runway to 35R as the aircraft approached STONZ and the crew attempted to change the landing runway.
summary: The Pilot Not Flying on a DFW arrival inadvertently created an FMS discontinuity by selecting a duplicate waypoint after a runway change, causing a one-mile deviation. The Captain disengaged the autopilot to correct the course, attributing the error to a known database anomaly and rushed verification.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew experiences a LE FLAPS TRANSIT amber light on and a split flap indicator when flaps 1 is selected during approach. While consulting the QRH the LE FLAPS TRANSIT light extinguishes resulting in approach and landing with LE flaps extended and TE flaps up. Fuel was a consideration as the flight had diverted for weather.
summary: During a weather divert approach at 5,000 feet, an Operating Experience trainee First Officer and Captain encountered a LE FLAPS TRANSIT light and split flap needles while selecting flaps 1. The crew declared an emergency, performed asymmetry procedures, and executed an uneventful trailing edge flaps up landing before maintenance cleared the aircraft for departure.

synopsis: An MD-11 flight crew successfully resolved anomalous airspeed indications during an arrival in IMC.
summary: During descent in rain and mist, the crew encountered an airspeed miscompare and CADC #1 failure after disconnecting the autopilot. They followed the QRH checklist, selected CADC 2, and landed uneventfully, though maintenance later attributed the issue to moisture in the pitot static system.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier was advised by ATC of a track deviation near CJS when the GPS was engaged and indicated on track. The flight crew suspected GPS DOS but ATC had no indication of interference.
summary: The Pilot Flying drifted 8 miles south of course while navigating GPS direct to CJS VOR at FL340, likely due to RAIM loss and distraction from paperwork. ATC provided a heading correction, and the crew noted that limited First Officer display access hindered deviation detection.

synopsis: A330 Flight Attendant describes a loss of cabin pressure during during descent. The cockpit crew was apparently aware that the masks were about to drop and informed the cabin.
summary: Flight attendants assisted passengers during a cabin decompression where oxygen masks deployed, though some masks failed to drop and French-speaking passengers faced communication barriers. Despite hyperventilation and shaken travelers, the crew maintained professionalism, resulting in no major incidents and positive passenger feedback upon deplaning.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports about a bio-hazard concern involving the removal of contaminated passenger seat cushions that brush up against passengers and flight attendants during the boarding process as Maintenance tries to remove the seat cushions from the aircraft.
summary: Maintenance personnel reported a bio-hazard risk during boarding when flight attendants allowed passengers to board while soiled seat cushions containing bodily fluids were being replaced. This practice forced mechanics to work in narrow aisles near passengers, causing physical contact with contaminants and passenger distress to avoid delays.

synopsis: After a Captain's pitch trim switch had been replaced on a company ERJ-170, two Maintenance Supervisors and a Contract Maintenance Technician describe the human factor issues that contributed to their missing a required CAT-2 statement that was not entered in the logbook.
summary: A Maintenance Supervisor and Technician failed to document a CAT II pitch trim switch replacement on an ERJ-170 during a work package review, releasing the aircraft out of service. The error resulted from human factors like distraction and complacency, as the critical component was not identified at receiving inspection.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports he let himself get out of sequence during a removal/replacement of Number 4 Main Tire wheel assembly by temporarily installing the Wheel Dust/Anti-Skid Transducer cap bolts only finger tight until he had down-jacked a CRJ-200 aircraft. He was attempting to help speed up passenger boarding and minimize a delay.
summary: A mechanic servicing Flight Y's Number 4 main tire after a cord exposure on Flight X admitted to deviating from procedures by lowering the aircraft before fully torquing and safety-wiring the wheel cap bolts. The mechanic notified management to inspect the aircraft upon arrival at ZZZ1, acknowledging the procedural error caused by rushing to minimize delays.

synopsis: A B757-300 ETOPS aircraft returned to field due to Number 2 Engine shut-down for a low oil pressure indication. The engine oil cap was not re-installed after an overnight Maintenance Check.
summary: A mechanic servicing a B757-300 ETOPS aircraft added oil to both engines and installed the caps, unaware that the Number 2 oil cap was missing. This oversight followed a previous incident where the same aircraft returned to field due to an engine shutdown caused by a loose Number 2 oil cap.

synopsis: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports he mistakenly mis-identified a Yellow System hydraulic line hose coupling for a Green NORMAL Hydraulic System hose coupling, causing only the Yellow hydraulic line to be stowed for an MEL deferral of an A320 Brake Temperature Indication. High temperature condition recurred due to brake was still active on landing.
summary: A mechanic mistakenly stowed the Yellow hydraulic line instead of the Green line while deactivating the brake system for an overheat MEL. This error caused the brake to remain active, resulting in a recurring overheat condition upon landing and a subsequent flight delay.

synopsis: ATC denied an EMB 170 flight crew landing clearance at an airport with a closed Tower due to a previously landed air carrier crew not closing their flight plan. The EMB 170 crew declared a fuel emergency rather than divert from a field in VMC with a clear runway.
summary: The pilot held for 23 minutes because ATC could not close a preceding flight's plan, preventing approach clearance. The pilot declared an emergency to accept a visual approach, landing safely after the preceding crew was finally contacted to close their plan.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: A CE-525 flight crew flying the RNAV (GPS) Runway 30 approach to BCB had to maneuver to avoid a helicopter which was unknown to the TRACON prior to switching the flight to UNICOM.
summary: The pilot maneuvered to avoid a helicopter while conducting an RNAV approach to Runway 30 at BCB in VMC after receiving no traffic advisories. The near collision occurred because the helicopter was not initially visible on TCAS or communicated on CTAF, though the pilot later heard an RA while visually maintaining separation.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A Flight Instructor resigned from the flight school where she was working because, after having an electrical system malfunction at night, she felt the school's poor aircraft maintenance program put instructors and students at risk.
summary: An instructor, student, and observer experienced a total electrical failure during an instrument training flight in a Cessna 150, causing loss of radios, lights, and instruments. The aircraft landed safely on Runway YYL using visual cues, and maintenance later attributed the failure to a bad master solenoid and battery.

synopsis: After an IFR BE36 pilot suffered reduced power and loss of airspeed after passing through a light snow shower he received a clearance to the nearest suitable airport. While doing so he inadvertently descended 1,000 FT below his cleared altitude of 3,000 MSL.
summary: The pilot experienced suspected propeller icing and performance loss while approaching a Class C airport at 7,000 feet. While managing the diversion and avionics, the pilot inadvertently descended to 2,000 feet due to anxiety, poor task management, and insufficient vigilance in visual conditions.

synopsis: When a Lear 25 pilot turned the right engine nacelle heat OFF after leveling and accelerating at FL410 it flamed out so during descent toward FL200 he restarted the engine and returned to FL410.
summary: The pilot turned off nacelle heat switches at FL410, causing an EPR increase and immediate right engine flameout. The crew descended to below FL250, restarted the engine per checklist, and completed the flight normally with the aircraft remaining in full control.

synopsis: An IAI ASTRA Right BLEED AIR LEAK light illuminated and did not extinguish with checklist procedures so the engine was shutdown, an emergency declared and the flight diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: During cruise, the crew encountered a persistent right 'BLEED AIR LEAK' light, prompting a right engine shutdown and emergency declaration per checklist. The light extinguished eight minutes later, and the aircraft landed uneventfully at a nearby airport with a long runway after receiving ATC vectors.

synopsis: Maintenance Technician forgot to remove MD11 center gear pin and aircraft flew subsequent leg with center gear down.
summary: A mechanic performing a PS-1 check failed to remove the center nose gear pin while servicing tires and lubricating regulators, mistakenly believing all pins were removed. The aircraft subsequently launched with the pin installed, preventing the nose gear from retracting until the pin was removed and an inspection completed.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a conflict event when traffic cleared for an approach to Runway 34L but flew through the final for Runway 34L and 34C resulting in a declared NMAC. Pilot error was listed as the causal factor.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller cleared a B737 for a visual approach to Runway 34L, but the copilot mistakenly lined up for Runway 34R, causing the aircraft to cross two active finals. This deviation forced both the B737 and a trailing aircraft to go around, resulting in a reported near mid-air collision.

synopsis: Ground Controller observing an Air Carrier taxiing at high speed and cutting taxiway corners, issued a 'stop' instruction when the aircraft missed a turn and was about to enter the active runway.
summary: An air traffic controller observed Flight X rapidly accelerating and cutting corners while taxiing toward Runway YY instead of turning onto Taxiway J. The controller issued repeated stop commands, causing the aircraft to halt before it crossed the hold short line, after which the crew corrected their path without further incident.

synopsis: An MD11 center gear failed to retract on takeoff. The flight continued to destination at reduced speed for a normal landing. Post flight revealed the center gear pin is installed.
summary: During takeoff, the center gear primary position light remained red due to a forgotten center gear pin. The crew followed Non Alert procedures, continued to destination, and executed a normal landing without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: MD-11 center gear failed to retract.
summary: The First Officer and Captain continued flight after the center gear handle was moved up but lights remained red due to a forgotten center gear pin. They completed a Non-Alert checklist, landed normally with all gear indications correct, and did not declare an emergency.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 EICAS alerted HYD 3 LO PRESS and IB GND SPLRS when the landing gear were retracted so an emergency was declared, the QRH completed and the aircraft returned to the departure airport where the passengers were deplaned on a high speed taxiway.
summary: The flight crew experienced a HYD 3 LO PRESS and IB GND SPLRS message after take-off while retracting gear, prompting an emergency return to Runway 18. The aircraft landed safely, and a hydraulic leak was observed on the left wing.

synopsis: A B737-700 flight crew suffered TCAS TA and RAs while on vectors for landing Runway 19L at SNA.
summary: During the downwind leg of a 19R approach into SNA, a commercial crew received a TCAS Resolution Advisory to climb after ATC instructed a turn toward a VFR light twin. The aircraft climbed approximately 300 feet to avoid a close encounter with the twin, which was flying just a few hundred feet below, before landing safely.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 rudder trim deflected full left with the autopilot engaged, so the QRH was completed, the rudder re-centered and the flight continued but the Captain refused the aircraft for further service after Maintenance found no faults.
