synopsis: Following a modest ground conflict between departing and taxiing aircraft on and/or crossing Runway 15 at BTV the Ground Controller discussed his belief that recent modifications to the intersecting Runway 19 have contributed to increased frequency of such events.
summary: A Developmental controller training on Local Control issued conflicting taxi instructions to a King Air and a CL30 at an intersection, causing the King Air to deviate from its assigned taxiway. The reporter attributes the confusion and resulting safety hazard to a poorly planned 400-foot displaced threshold extension on Runway 19 that intersects Runway 15.

synopsis: A B737-500 flight crew suffered a pressurization failure, initiated an emergency descent and, when level at 10,000 feet with adequate fuel reserves, elected to continue to their destination rather than divert.
summary: The flight crew experienced an uncontrolled cabin pressure rise at FL360, triggering an emergency descent to 10,000 feet and automatic oxygen mask deployment. They continued to their original destination despite severe weather at a potential diversion airport and landed safely with EMTs meeting them at the gate.

synopsis: When chronic fuel pump problems resurfaced enroute the flight crew of an A319 was forced to land short of their destination due to insufficient accessible fuel. A substitute aircraft was utilized to complete the scheduled flight.
summary: The crew experienced CTR tank pump sequencing failures and a tripped Pump 1 circuit breaker during climbout, likely due to a faulty breaker noted by maintenance. With insufficient fuel to reach the destination, they coordinated with dispatch and ATC to land safely and obtain a replacement aircraft.

synopsis: A B767-300 that had recently come out of maintenance for problems with air/ground logic had a repeat LND GEAR MONITOR EICAS message during cruise and a LE SLAT ASYM EICAS message upon arrival at their destination. The flight crew declared an emergency and after landing was towed to the gate.
summary: The crew of an aircraft with known air/ground logic issues continued to destination after receiving 'LND GEAR MONITOR' and 'LE SLAT ASYM' messages. They executed a precautionary emergency landing with locked-out thrust reversers and manual braking, requiring a tow to the ramp to prevent brake overheating.

synopsis: A line flight crew, reassigned to a flaps/slats extended maintenance ferry, encountered difficulty and resistance from their Dispatcher with respect to the required fuel load and expected aircraft performance at the mandated restricted airspeed and altitude. When ultimately airborne the Dispatcher's prognostications were proven inadequate and the flight crew refused to continue without a fuel stop. Calculations of the fuel remaining during that stop predicted the useable fuel remaining would have been approximately 700 pounds less than that required to complete the journey non-stop.
summary: The flight crew ferrying an aircraft with inoperative slats discovered a fuel planning error by Dispatch, which failed to account for specific ferry limitations and increased fuel burn. The crew diverted to an intermediate station because the initial release lacked sufficient fuel to reach the destination non-stop.

synopsis: An ERJ 145 Captain addressed flaws in the manner by which his airline computes required fuel for legs from ORD to ZZZ.
summary: The pilot reported a flawed dispatch release for an Embraer flight from ORD to ZZZ that underestimated reserve fuel requirements for the Shelbyville crossing. The crew arrived with less fuel than planned due to the unrealistic reserve calculation, prompting a request for revised releases with higher fuel allowances.

synopsis: A B767-300 westbound for Hawaii had to return to its departure airport when both the normal and standby sources of EGT for the right engine failed prior to entering ETOPS airspace.
summary: The flight crew diverted to the departure airport during climb to FL340 after both primary and standby right engine EGT indicators failed, violating ETOPS requirements. They executed an overweight emergency landing at 320,000 pounds with Flaps 30 and autobrakes set to position three.

synopsis: When faced with a Brake Control Fault message enroute to an airport with short runways the flight crew of an ERJ-170 elected to divert to an airport with superior facilities. The decision to divert was made in part due to their inability to communicate effectively with Dispatch and Maintenance to determine the extent of the failure's threat to stopping distance, a subject of great importance given the modest runways at their destination. In the reporter's words '...essentially, we were on [our] own.'
summary: The flight crew diverted during climb out due to a Brake Control Fault and lack of maintenance input regarding degraded braking performance on short runways. The crew noted previous logbook entries for the same fault and found ACARS communication volume unmanageable while handling the emergency.

synopsis: Despite experiencing an unusual popping noise and feeling some slack in the ailerons the flight crew of a CE-560 elected to continue to their destination as superior prevailing wind direction and velocity predicted less exposure to possible handling problems than did those existing at their departure airport.
summary: The pilot reported a "pop" noise and increased control play in the yoke during a left turn after departure. The crew elected to continue to the destination due to gusty crosswinds and aircraft weight, noting the yoke drifted left only during level cruise with the autopilot engaged.

synopsis: CE560 Captain reports track and altitude deviations during the RUUDY 4 RNAV departure from TEB due to improper flight guidance setup prior to departure.
summary: The crew, feeling rushed by an early passenger, deviated 150 feet above the assigned 1,500-foot altitude during the RUUDY 4 departure after the autopilot followed the Captain's outdated ILS settings instead of the First Officer's NAV mode. The reporter attributed the error to failing to synchronize flight director modes and rushing the checklist.

synopsis: Confusion over the wording of a pressurization MEL item caused the flight crew of a C-750 to takeoff, expecting the baggage compartment ISO (Isolation valve) to close automatically at 1.0 psi differential pressure. When it did not do so they returned to their departure airport for maintenance.
summary: The flight crew departed with a deferred baggage door seal discrepancy, relying on MEL procedures that did not explicitly require manual isolation valve activation. During climbout, a cabin altitude warning occurred because the faulty door switch prevented automatic isolation, forcing a return to the departure airport after the crew manually closed the valve.

synopsis: PA31 pilot reports climbing early on the TEB 8 departure due to faulty DME equipment aboard his aircraft.
summary: A pilot departing TEB on the Teterboro Eight departure experienced a DME failure at 1,700 feet, causing a false indication of being inside the climb area. After the DME reset, NY Departure issued a climb clearance to 6,000 feet, prompting the pilot to rely on VOR radials as a backup.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: MD80 flight crew experiences loss of oil pressure on the left engine during climb passing FL190. The engine is shutdown and flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: During climbout at FL190, the pilot observed a left engine low oil pressure light and zero gauge reading. The crew leveled at FL200, consulted the QRH, shut down the left engine, declared an emergency, and returned for landing.

synopsis: DC10 flight crew experiences a Gen Drive 2 Fault upon taking the runway and taxiing clear the fault disappears. On the next attempt the fault returns and the takeoff is rejected at 20 KTS and the crew returns to the line for maintenance. CSD was low on oil.
summary: The flight crew rejected takeoff twice due to an intermittent Gen Drive 2 Fault alert appearing at 20 KTS during the roll. The aircraft returned to the gate for maintenance, which revealed the CSD required 4-5 quarts of oil.

synopsis: A300 Captain laments being dispatched with the First Officer's EFB MEL'ed and removed from the aircraft requiring all performance calculations to be done by the Captain while airborne.
summary: The Captain and First Officer faced a deferred First Officer EFB with no available performance laptop, forcing non-standard data entry from behind the Captain's seat. This caused operational delays during taxi and prevented the First Officer from calculating updated performance data for flaps 20 while holding in severe windshear conditions.

synopsis: B767-300 Flight Attendant reports that although the FAOM requires that carts not block access to jump seats, the standard First/Business Class service does just that.
summary: A flight attendant reported that company meal service procedures park carts blocking three of six jump seats in the Business/First Class cabin. This restriction prevents one of four crew members from securing a seat during turbulence, violating the FAOM requirement that carts must not restrict jump seat access.

synopsis: B737-800 Flight Attendant reports the lead Flight Attendat becoming ill and unresponsive during flight. Oxygen is administered and the flight continues to destination with three working flight attendants.
summary: During flight, Flight Attendant #1 became ill and unresponsive, requiring First Aid and oxygen from Flight Attendant #2. With only two crew members remaining, Flight Attendant #2 managed the cabin and forward door while assigning Flight Attendant #4 to the rear, as no medical assistance was received via paging.

synopsis: Maintenance Technician reports being assigned to an aircraft with an elevator feel EICAS message in flight. Reporter suspects that a pitot cover was left on the right pitot tube and mostly disintegrated in flight.
summary: The inbound B757 pilot investigated an elevator feel EICAS message and suspected a pitot cover caused the issue after a partner reported seeing one. Inspection confirmed the tube was clear, the item was signed off, and the flight departed without delay, though the pilot recommended against installing covers for same-day flights.

synopsis: While flying a cross country at the request of the airplane's owner, and in hopes of building flight time, a commercial pilot of a PA-32 stumbled into icing, IMC, GPS failure and loss of indicated airspeed enroute. Many errors of omission and commission were part of the tale. Assistance from ATC prevented an even more distressing outcome.
summary: The PIC and an instructor flew a passenger-carrying flight in marginal conditions where icing caused a pitot tube blockage, resulting in zero indicated airspeed and a 700-foot altitude loss. The crew diverted to a towered airport after GPS failure, attributing the incident to "get there itis," inadequate preflight checks, and unverified pitot heat functionality.

synopsis: C172 instructor pilot on downwind at PRC reports a NMAC with another C172 entering the pattern under Tower control. Reporter informs the Tower and initiates a right 360 to reenter the downwind.
summary: A flight instructor and student in a training aircraft on downwind encountered a conflict when another aircraft with an inoperative transponder descended into their path. The instructor executed an emergency 360-degree turn, attributing the incident to poor controller sequencing and the lack of early traffic detection due to the other aircraft's failed transponder.

synopsis: C172 vectored for a visual approach to Runway 15 at DET reported that the runway was very difficult to identify because of numerous burned out runway lights.
summary: A pilot approaching Detroit City Airport at 3,000 feet could not visually acquire the runway due to numerous burned-out lights. Despite the poor visibility, the pilot used functional PAPIs and Tower assistance to execute a safe landing on Runway 15.

synopsis: Helicopter instructor pilot reports a NMAC with a RV4 that had preformed a touch and go behind the helicopter then over flew the helicopter on the upwind.
summary: An experimental RV4 entered the S50 traffic pattern non-standardly, flying over slower departing traffic without visual contact and forcing a training aircraft to slow below 50 KIAS. The pilot attributed the risk of mid-air collision to the RV4's erratic speed, lack of CTAF coordination, and improper pattern entries.

synopsis: A line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports his station has a large number of mechanics that do not have line experience and training with direct supervision is very poor. They are led to believe that they can sign-off their work based on just the possession of an Airframe/Powerplant (A/P) license. Issues with electronic signatures were also raised.
summary: A pilot reported that inexperienced mechanics at an Air Carrier Line Maintenance Station were incorrectly issuing Airworthiness Releases based solely on A/P licenses due to poor training and misleading electronic signature screens. The reporter attributed this safety risk to a lack of fleet-specific formal training, inadequate supervision, and system failures to block unqualified personnel from signing off work.

synopsis: BOS Controller described a conflict event between an air carrier departure and a VFR tour aircraft, the reporter acknowledging more specific instructions should have been issued to the tour aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller approved a city tour for a pilot who subsequently flew eastbound, opposite to the assigned Runway 27 departure. The controller instructed the pilot to descend and maintain visual separation from a departing air carrier after the pilot failed to acknowledge the conflicting traffic.

synopsis: Tower Controller reports a possible conflict between an A320 departing Runway 27 at BOS and an SR22 flying over the downtown area.
summary: Local Control West and East controllers managed an Airbus departure and a SR22 city tour near Runway 27. The SR22 moved closer than expected, prompting a traffic advisory, but the SR22 pilot maintained visual separation, resulting in no loss of separation.

synopsis: Tower CIC described an over-take event resulting in a loss of separation. The reporter indicated the RADAR Controller failed to take into account several factors.
summary: A Tower CIC observed an E190 rapidly overtaking an E145 on final approach due to high tailwind and the West RADAR controller's lack of situational awareness. The CIC instructed the Local Controller to order an immediate breakout, which was executed after a delay while both aircraft were in IMC conditions.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a loss of separation event when traffic issued a heading initially turned the wrong direction, the reporter acknowledging several oversights on his part during the event.
summary: An air traffic controller managing a B737 on base in low RVR conditions issued conflicting turn instructions due to fatigue and failure to verify the aircraft's heading. This resulted in potential loss of separation with a departing aircraft, though the controller noted divergence may have occurred.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a NMAC between a departing aircraft and another near by aircraft. The reporter noted that more specific instructions should have been issued to the departure.
summary: Air Traffic Control cleared a departing Diamond for takeoff while a Baron was on downwind, but the Diamond turned right early instead of continuing straight for half a mile. The controller, distracted by sightseeing traffic, failed to notice the deviation, resulting in a near mid-air collision when the Diamond entered the Baron's flight path.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller described an alledged error during light traffic and side-by visual approach procedures where one aircraft failed to use call signs when instructed to maintain visual separation.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller in Sector X reported that a B737-800 acknowledged a visual separation clearance from an A321 without using its call sign during a visual approach. The controller argued this was a non-event because both aircraft maintained visual separation, attributing any potential deviation to the A321 pilot's failure to advise ATC if sight was lost.

synopsis: A ZDV Controller described a loss of separation when traffic inbound to D01, one via a new RNAV STAR and another on a 'Legacy' STAR conflicted.
summary: A Denver Center controller reported a loss of separation between a Dash 8 and a B737 descending via RNAV STARs into Denver. The incident occurred because the controller transferred the B737 to Approach without stopping it at the gate fix, violating LOA procedures intended to maintain positive separation over converging traffic.

synopsis: A B737-700 First Officer reports a ground air conditioning hose being sucked into the number one engine as the the jetway was moved toward the aircraft.
summary: During night pushback, the crew ingested an unchained air conditioning hose into engine one while taxiing to the gate. The Captain immediately shut down the engine after debris was thrown, and the agent confirmed the hose was not secured.

synopsis: A commercial pilot reported passenger control on the ramp during boarding at EYW needs increased supervision. Passengers are frequently unescorted while transitioning aircraft movement areas.
summary: A flight attendant reported that unescorted passengers boarding in EYW wandered across the ramp near regional aircraft with spinning props. The reporter warned that these passengers, unaware of the hazards, risked a serious accident due to a lack of supervision while aircraft were ready to taxi.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported wake vortex encounter that provided enough distraction Tower was not called for landing clearance.
summary: SCT Approach vectored the crew onto final within 1.5 miles of a heavy B777, causing wake turbulence and a loss of Tower communication verification due to low sun and maneuvering. The crew landed safely but attributed the incident to ATC vectoring too early and close to the heavy, alongside their own distraction preventing clearance confirmation.

synopsis: When the right engine failed to accelerate for takeoff the Flight Crew of a B737-400 rejected the takeoff and returned the aircraft to Maintenance.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff below 60 knots due to the right engine lagging and failing to exceed 54% N1 or 1,800 pph fuel flow. After a failed run-up on a remote taxiway, the aircraft returned to the gate for maintenance and passengers were rebooked on another flight.

synopsis: Crew experienced engine abnormalities, incurred a slight altitude deviation and returned to land.
summary: During climb to FL180, the crew heard loud noises from Engine 1 and received an Eng 1 Control Fault, causing auto-pilot disconnect. While executing the QRH, the aircraft deviated 300 feet above FL180 for two minutes before the Captain declared an emergency.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 Captain, flying his first ever RNAV Visual approach to Runway 26R at ATL, tuned, but did not display, the ILS as a back up to the RNAV driven 'snowflake.' Confusion reigned until he was 'feeling low' on the approach and reverted to visual perception to arrest his excessive rate of descent, restabilize and complete the approach and landing.
summary: The pilot flew an RNAV Visual Approach 26R and descended below the standard glide path using snowflake guidance while distracted by altitude restrictions and a missing ILS overlay. The crew corrected the descent by disconnecting the autopilot and setting Flaps 45 after realizing the aircraft was below 1,000 feet above airport elevation.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A pilot taxiing westbound on the Ramp 1 taxiway north of Terminal A at night, taxied north off the taxiway centerline to avoid fuel trucks and discovered a large unpaved, unlit, and unmarked area, but was able to avoid taxiing on it.
summary: The pilot at CVG deviated from the taxi line to avoid fuel trucks and encountered an unpaved dirt area lacking edge or hazard markings. The pilot recommends installing cones with flashing red lights to delineate this area for better visibility, especially at night.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain experiences a pitot system failure at cruise altitude resulting in unreliable airspeed and altitude indications on his PFD. An emergency is declared and flight diverts, with pitot system indications returning to normal upon exiting IMC.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring and First Officer experienced erroneous airspeed and altitude indications in cruise due to suspected pitot-static icing. They declared an emergency, descended to VFR conditions using backup instruments, and landed normally after indications returned to normal.

synopsis: MD-82 began to loose cabin pressurization, executed an emergency descent and landed safely.
summary: The flight crew experienced a cabin altitude warning at FL300, triggering an emergency descent to 8,000 feet due to difficult manual pressurization control. After manually deploying oxygen masks and detecting a smoke-like odor, they landed safely with no injuries, later attributing the gauge confusion to rapid cabin altitude changes.

synopsis: An A320 had an intermittent Flap/Slat Locked indication in cruise, followed shortly by an intermittent COND AFT CRG ISOL VALVE warning. Maintenance Control suggested cycling the flap/slat control circuit breakers, to no avail. New ECAM's appeared, including nose wheel steering disconnect message, a BRAKES HOT, and an AIR PACK 1 OVHT. The AIR PACK 1 OVHT ECAM was complied with and the others were cleared by cycling the FWC (Flight Warning Computer) circuit breakers. A landing at destination with normal flap operation was made.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced intermittent flap, cargo, and other system warnings during cruise, likely caused by Flight Warning Computer faults. Maintenance Control incorrectly advised cycling prohibited flap circuit breakers in flight due to a communication error, though the crew landed safely after extending flaps normally.

synopsis: While taxiing to the gate a B757-200 Captain noted high and rising EGT and falling oil pressure on the left engine. They shutdown the engine and contacted Maintenance at the gate.
summary: During taxi to the gate, the pilot observed left engine oil pressure warnings and rising EGT, prompting an immediate engine shutdown using the checklist. The aircraft taxied to the gate without declaring an emergency, and maintenance was notified.

synopsis: B737 First Officer describes a fatiguing trip paring that is FAR legal but should not be.
summary: A pilot reported three WOCL incursions during a fatiguing trip involving early report times and a double-duty red-eye. The pilot attributed the errors to extreme fatigue caused by the schedule, noting recovery took two days after the trip ended.

synopsis: B717 Captain experiences a hydraulic low quantity alert during approach and goes around. An emergency is declared and the emergency gear extension handle is used to lower the gear. Aircraft is towed to the gate.
summary: The crew received a HYDR QTY LOW alert on approach, executed a go-around, and landed with gear doors open after raising the emergency gear lever. Maintenance identified leaking hydraulic fluid and a possible broken line, resulting in no injuries or aircraft damage.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: Civil Jet on a go around from Runway 4 at HHF experienced a loss of contact with ATC, the reporter suggesting amended communications procedures with ATC.
summary: The flight crew experienced a loss of ATC contact after a go-around from Runway 4 at HHF, requiring a climb to 10,000 feet to establish communication with Albuquerque Center. The aircraft landed safely at AMA, but the incident was reported as a deficiency in missed approach communication procedures.

synopsis: Air Carrier being handled by ZDC described a confused descent clearance involving the 'descend via' phraseology but with an intermediate vector off the procedure, the reporter suggesting additional training is needed for ATC.
summary: A pilot and student flying to RDU received contradictory ATC instructions to descend via the ALDAN 1 arrival while performing a 360-degree turn off the procedure. The reporter attributes the confusion to improper "descend via" phraseology used while the aircraft was in heading mode, suggesting controllers need better training on avionics and arrival procedures.

synopsis: While being vectored for approach in IMC to MYR at 2,000 FT AGL, a CRJ-200 flight crew responded appropriately to a GPWS terrain warning. The reporter checked their altimeter settings, which were correct, and could find no other apparent cause for the warning.
summary: The pilot reported a false GPWS terrain warning while IMC at 2,000 feet during vectors to ILS 36 near MYR. After climbing to 3,500 feet for the escape maneuver and confirming correct altimeters with no local terrain, the crew continued the approach and landed safely.

synopsis: A319 Captain reports the inability of the First Officer to raise the landing gear handle after takeoff. Shortly after that a cascade of ECAM malfunctions and INOP Systems on the Status Page including First Officer TAT, AP 1+2, A/THR, CAT 2, ANTI SKID, N/W STRG, NORM BRK, AUTO BRK, L/G RETRACT. After some discussion flight returns to the departure airport. This aircraft had a long history of similar anomalies which Maintenance believed were caused by a leaking (nitrogen) main landing gear strut. The Captain declines a request to ferry the aircraft.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a cascade of system failures and gear retraction issues shortly after takeoff due to a known right main landing gear strut pressure fault. They declared an emergency, performed a low-pass to confirm gear alignment, and landed safely, subsequently declining a ferry flight request due to safety concerns regarding the recurring fault.

synopsis: A319 Captain is informed after gate arrival of a piece of tape over a passenger oxygen panel in the cabin. Maintenance became aware of the issue due to an Internet posting of a photo taken by a passenger. No write ups or MEL's could be found concerning this panel.
summary: After landing, a mechanic informed the flight crew about tape on a cabin oxygen panel in row 13 DEF, which a passenger had photographed and posted online. Maintenance removed the tape, applied an MEL, and blocked the row, though the crew found no prior logbook entries or knowledge of the issue.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported possible wake vortex encounter in trail of an Airbus that led to a low altitude stick shaker.
summary: The pilot reported a right wing drop below 50 feet during the landing flare, likely caused by wake turbulence from a preceding Airbus and updrafts. Recovery actions led to a Stick Shaker activation under 10 feet, but the aircraft landed without incident.

synopsis: CRJ900 Captain is informed that the right engine chip detector light was illuminated in the aft equipment bay. Maintenance Control is contacted and they do not deem it necessary to take any action prior to flight.
summary: The First Officer and Captain discovered an illuminated right engine chip detector light during a walk-around that could not be reset. Maintenance Control was unhelpful and questioned the crew's aircraft type, delaying the dispatch of a mechanic to resolve the safety issue.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: DHC8 First Officer reports loss of the right hydraulic system during approach. A go around is initiated, the QRH is consulted, an emergency is declared and a normal landing ensues.
summary: During approach, the crew experienced a right hydraulic isolation valve caution and loss of number two hydraulic quantity after gear extension. They executed a go-around, declared an emergency, and completed a normal landing after accepting vectors for another ILS approach.

synopsis: DHC8-200 Captain reports the nose landing gear attempting to retract uncommanded during taxi. The aircraft is stopped and the passengers deplaned to a bus before the aircraft is towed to the gate.
summary: The flight crew aborted takeoff after hearing a loud noise and observing nose gear warning lights indicating a gear malfunction. They coordinated with ground operations to deplane passengers via a people mover on the taxiway before the aircraft was towed to the gate for maintenance.

synopsis: B767-300 Flight Attendant describes an unanticipated encounter with turbulence and difficulties securing the cart and finding a jumpseat.
summary: A flight attendant serving snacks before landing encountered severe, unforecast turbulence that caused beverage carts to overturn and spill hot liquids. The lack of cart tie-downs trapped the crew member, resulting in burns and bruises while they struggled to secure equipment and reach a seat.

synopsis: A Maintenance Supervisor and a contract Maintenance Inspector report that a Cessna CE680 flight crew at FL430 experienced a sudden stoppage of oxygen (O2) flow in mid-breath, even though the crew O2 bottle pressure was 1500 PSI. Maintenance found the composite type Crew Oxygen Bottle shut-off valve not fully opened.
summary: During cruise at FL430, a Cessna CE-680 crew experienced sudden oxygen flow stoppage in both masks due to the bottle regulator shut-off valve not being fully open. Maintenance corrected the issue by reseating the valve and replacing the safety wire, attributing the failure to incomplete valve seating during a prior scheduled maintenance visit.

synopsis: Pilot on short final reports a NMAC with a PA28 departing opposite direction and passing overhead.
summary: A pilot landing on Runway 21 at E80 experienced a near miss with an aircraft departing Runway 3 that was not heard on the local CTAF. The incident occurred because the pilot failed to monitor the correct frequency or adequately screen the airport, requiring a rapid descent to maintain clearance.

synopsis: After a precautionary shutdown of the Number Two Engine for a low oil pressure indication, an H25B flight crew encountered numerous communication difficulties with Mexican Air Traffic controllers which the crew attributed to non-standard phraseology associated with the emergency.
summary: The First Officer of a Hawker 700 reported a low oil pressure warning at FL350, leading to a precautionary shutdown of Engine Two and a diversion. The crew attributed the primary risk to poor communication and coordination among multiple controllers who struggled to understand English requests for emergency services and approach clearances.

synopsis: M20 pilot experiences a popping noise shortly after takeoff and turns back to land opposite direction on the departure runway. The landing gear is not extended and a gear up landing ensues.
summary: The pilot departed Runway 27, turned back to Runway 09 after an engine popping noise at 1,400 feet, and landed with high airspeed. The aircraft skidded to a stop because the landing gear was not lowered, requiring the FBO to lift and tow the plane.

synopsis: Learjet 45 flight crew experienced a primary pitch trim failure on an RNAV departure, declared an emergency, regained control with secondary trim, and returned to base.
summary: The flight crew experienced a primary pitch trim failure during the takeoff phase while executing an RNAV SID. They declared an emergency to avoid SID constraints, recovered control using secondary trim, and returned to base successfully.

synopsis: AC90 pilot reports a NMAC with a helicopter on short final to Runway 24 at PMP and continues to landing. Animosity develops between the reporter and PMP Controllers which later spills over to FMY Controllers.
summary: The pilot reported a near-midair collision with a helicopter on short final at Pompano Beach and subsequent unprofessional ATC interactions during departure and arrival at Fort Myers. The pilot attributed the events to controller anger, poor communication, and a refusal of approach services, concluding that ATC behavior was unsafe and unprofessional.

synopsis: SR22 pilot reports a double bounce landing and go around resulting in a propeller strike. A safe landing ensues.
summary: The pilot reported a propeller strike during a go-around after a high flare caused by distractions, including a jammed microphone and self-imposed pressure in gusty crosswinds. Following a successful second circuit and emergency inspection, the aircraft landed safely on the third attempt.

synopsis: LR35 Captain is confused by the NUAL8 departure from Runway 16R at VNY and an HSI that is not set to show DME. The aircraft is maintained on runway heading at 1,700 FT well past the 2.2 DME, alarming himself and the Controller involved.
summary: The pilot departed VNY on the NUAL8 departure and mistakenly monitored Time to Go instead of DME due to an HSI knob setting, causing a delayed climb past the 2.2 DME fix. This error triggered a terrain advisory from SoCal, though the crew safely climbed to 6,000 MSL in VFR conditions.

synopsis: PA-44 student pilot with instructor, experiences a right landing gear failure while landing with a left crosswind.
summary: A student pilot and instructor in a Piper PA-44-180 experienced a right main landing gear collapse during a touch-and-go landing in gusty crosswinds. The reporter attributes the accident to a faulty gear component, as pre-flight checks and in-flight verifications confirmed the gear was down and functional prior to the failure.

synopsis: After in flight loss of a critical system aircraft proceeded to destination and landed.
summary: The pilot continued to the destination after an electrical failure occurred 30 minutes prior to landing, choosing to avoid an unfamiliar field. Although the transponder's Mode C status was uncertain, the pilot entered the Mode C veil for landing without entering or under-flying Class B airspace.

synopsis: PA-44 departed the runway during landing.
summary: The pilot and student landed a twin-engine aircraft on Runway 04 in crosswinds, experiencing a hard right pull suspected to be a flat tire. The aircraft veered off the runway onto Taxiway C, where the right main gear collapsed, bending the propeller and damaging the undercarriage, though both occupants remained unharmed.

synopsis: A PA-44 pilot verified three green gear down lock lights and completed the landing checklist but the nose gear collapsed on landing causing some damage but no injuries.
summary: During a standardization flight in a Seminole on an ILS 31 approach, the nose gear collapsed after a normal touchdown. This collapse reduced clearance, causing the propellers to strike the runway surface.

synopsis: PA-44 nose gear collapsed during landing.
summary: During a standardization flight on a simulated engine failure ILS approach, the nose gear collapsed at touchdown despite verified down and locked indications. This caused propeller strikes on both engines and a 1,000-foot runway slide before the aircraft stopped right of centerline.

synopsis: Aircraft experienced abnormal flight characteristics immediately after takeoff.
summary: Cabin crew reported loud bangs and lurches shortly after takeoff, suspecting a nose gear issue, while passengers later reported flames over the wing. The captain identified a bird strike, diverted the flight, and landed normally without incident.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An MD-80 Number 1 Flight Attendant sequentially describes the events in the cabin following an in-flight decompression and the confusion encountered with activating the jumpseat O2 masks.
summary: A flight attendant on an MD-80 overheard pilots report a cabin pressure loss during cruise and initiated landing preparations. The crew deployed oxygen masks, managed passenger safety, and landed safely after Fire and Rescue inspected the aircraft and confirmed the hot oxygen cylinders were secure.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: After an MD-80 pressurization failed and the passengers' oxygen masks deployed, a Flight Attendant was unable to lower a single row of passenger oxygen masks which had failed to activate.
summary: During descent, a cabin pressure loss triggered oxygen mask deployment, but masks at seats 32A/B failed to open despite crew attempts to manually release them. Passengers shared masks from the row ahead, and the flight landed safely before the crew reported the malfunction.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: TRACON Controller described an 'aircraft in distress' event when an IFR qualified pilot requested IFR handling but was unable to comply with ATC instructions.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored a small aircraft pilot who became disoriented and descended below the 80 MVA while attempting an IFR pick-up in IMC. The pilot, admitting limited recent IFR experience, diverted to a Class D airport where he regained VMC and landed safely.

synopsis: PHL Controller witnessed an ASDE-X conflict alert that was unheeded by the Local Controller. The reporter notes this type of no-action event is on-going and very dangerous.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller at PHL observed an ASDE-X alert for converging E190 and CRJ2 landings on runways 27R and 35, yet the Local East Controller took no action. The reporter deemed this standard operation dangerously tight, warning that simultaneous go-arounds could cause a mid-air collision and noting management has not formed a study group to address the issue.

synopsis: DAL Controller described a runway incursion event by a departing general aviation aircraft that failed to stop at the Runway 13R hold line. The reporter indicated that the location of the hold line was problematic.
summary: Local Control reported a BE36 taxiing across a non-standard VFR hold short line for Runway 13R while a GLEX was on final approach. The controller ordered the BE36 to turn back, attributing the incursion to poor hold short line design and FAA policy misunderstandings.

synopsis: A B737-700 had an engine fail in flight as indicated by vibration, high EGT and decreasing N1, so an emergency was declared, the QRH completed and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a Number 2 engine seizure with high EGT and vibration while climbing from FL360 to FL370. They declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport, and landed uneventfully after securing the engine and completing the QRH checklist.

synopsis: 1. Reporter corrects a log book entry, aircraft seat returned to service. 2. Reporter experiences an ECAM alert and MASTER WARNINING during off-gate engine start, returns to gate, determined with Maintenance personnel that it is an indication fault and applies MEL.3. Reporter speculates how his personal illness may have affected his judgment process.
summary: The crew returned to the gate after an Engine 1 Low Oil Pressure Master Warning during start, despite normal parameters, causing a two-hour delay for maintenance testing. The flight continued to destination with the warning recurring, attributed to an inoperative pressure transducer, while the pilot noted potential judgment issues due to recent illness.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew described a ground conflict with a high speed taxiing aircraft requiring sudden braking, causing injury to standing and unsecured flight attendants.
summary: During a ramp departure, the crew executed an emergency stop to avoid a high-speed aircraft misjudged by ATC, causing two flight attendants to fall and sustain minor injuries. The pilot in command successfully prevented a collision, though the incident highlighted potential risks to cabin crew during taxi maneuvers.

synopsis: A MD-11's Number 3 Engine failed while being vectored for landing so an emergency was declared but ATC asked for a 10 minute landing delay before closing the runway for their arrival and post landing inspection.
summary: During an MD-11 approach with no autothrottles, Engine 3 experienced a low RPM alert and high EGT, prompting a shutdown using the Low RPM checklist. The crew landed after a brief ATC delay, taxied to the ramp following a fire department inspection, and noted that severe damage checklist usage and speed control without autothrottles were areas for improvement.

synopsis: MD80 Captain experiences a compressor stall on the left engine during climb. The engine is shutdown and the flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: During climbout at 15,000 feet MSL, the left engine stalled and was shut down per procedures. The crew declared an emergency for single-engine operations and returned to the departure airport for an uneventful landing.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A high performance aircraft Captain flying the TEB RUUDY 4 Departure started the climb early from 1,500 FT because a CDI heading change made him think he was at WENTZ.
summary: The pilot deviated from the 1,500-foot level-off prior to WENTZ Intersection by climbing early to 2,000 feet due to misinterpreting the CDI track change. The reporter attributed this loss of situational awareness to high workload, fatigue, and excessive external scanning during a heavy departure from TEB.

synopsis: ZNY Controller described a probable loss of separation event when accurate wind data was not entered into the system creating the potential for separation errors, the reporter suggesting increased training in this area.
summary: An air traffic controller in Sectors 87/89 identified that erroneous wind data over 200 KTS corrupted aircraft profiles, potentially causing loss of separation. The controller manually corrected the wind data to resolve conflicts after the Flight Line Manager failed to address the system error immediately.

synopsis: TRACON Controller providing OJT described a TCAS RA event involving a Corporate Jet arrival on a visual approach and a Medevac helicopter departing a near by hospital.
summary: An OJT instructor and trainee on the Arrival Position observed a potential conflict between a descending LJ55 and a Medevac helicopter. The helicopter pilot executed an evasive descent to 1,600 feet after seeing the LJ55, prompting the instructor to conclude that the trainee failed to apply necessary altitude restrictions or vectors.

synopsis: A B737-300 Captain lamented the training deficiencies at his airline that he believes ill prepares flight crews to effectively conduct complex terminal area RNAV procedures.
summary: During descent to STL, the pilot flying changed the FMC without verbalizing, causing a VNAV disconnect and route discontinuity. The pilot not flying managed the altitude while the pilot flying corrected the FMC, though the crew attributed the error to inadequate training on FMC automation and RNAV procedure changes.

synopsis: Despite the flight crew having verified their parking safety area was clear of clutter, a B737-700 ingested a large quantity of the ground air conditioning hose into the left engine while they awaited the connection of ground power.
summary: The flight crew parked the aircraft with the left engine running, but the plane vibrated and went dark after an immediate engine shutdown. The pilot later observed that the left engine had ingested a large quantity of the yellow aircraft air conditioning hose.

synopsis: Air Carrier conducting an LDA PRM 28R approach to SFO described a go-around event by parallel traffic on Runway 28L. ATC claimed the reporter's aircraft passed parallel traffic causing the event.
summary: Pilots flying an LDA PRM 28R approach into SFO slowed to final approach speed early due to a simultaneous PRM 28L aircraft observed on TCAS. Although SFO Tower later claimed the pilots passed the other aircraft, the crew maintained minimum speed and reported the other aircraft was slightly behind upon visual contact, resulting in no wake turbulence issue.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reports a TE FLAPS DISAGREE EICAS during approach and goes around. QRH procedures are complied with resulting in a flaps 20 approach and landing.
summary: The flight crew experienced a 'TE DISAGREE' EICAS warning during approach, prompting a go-around and checklist completion. They subsequently executed a flaps 20 approach and landed uneventfully after debriefing with maintenance at the gate.

synopsis: An ERJ-170 flight crew suffered momentary loss of control and loss of altitude when they encountered likely wake turbulence during arrival vectoring.
summary: During a visual approach at 7,000 feet, the crew experienced violent vibration and an uncommanded 35-degree roll, causing a descent to 6,000 feet. The pilot attributed the event to either wake turbulence from a descending Airbus or a potential flight control malfunction, though no system alerts were present.

synopsis: The First Officer of a CRJ-200 experienced glide path and airspeed control issues on a visual approach during which the ILS glide slope, tuned for a back up, was providing erratic information. The Captain belatedly took control but the resulting touchdown ended with the right wing tip contacted the runway. No injuries resulted.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced a gusty approach with fluctuating glide slope and wind shear, resulting in a hard landing where the right wingtip contacted the ground. The Captain took control at 100 feet to manage speed and altitude, but the aircraft sustained right wing damage upon touchdown with no injuries.

synopsis: B737-800 crew discovers a fuel imbalance during cruise flight that cannot be corrected with QRH procedures. Crew diverts to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: During cruise, the crew experienced an uncommanded fuel imbalance that could not be controlled. They followed the QRH, declared an emergency, and diverted the aircraft.

synopsis: A B767-200 unscheduled STAB TRIM light, Master Caution and aural warning alerted at 60 knots during takeoff so the takeoff was rejected and the aircraft returned to the gate for maintenance.
summary: The crew aborted takeoff at 60 knots after the unscheduled Stab Trim light, Master Caution, and aural warning illuminated. The aircraft returned to the gate for a maintenance inspection.

synopsis: A CE560 flight crew suffered an NMAC with what they believed to be a Piper Cherokee while being vectored for an approach at ATC's minimum vectoring altitude in hilly terrain. ATC was unaware of the other aircraft.
summary: The pilot not flying reported a near miss with a climbing Piper Cherokee while cruising at 7,300 feet in clouds under Atlanta Center control. The reporter attributed the incident to high terrain, potential radar coverage gaps, and IFR conditions that prevented visual detection of the traffic.

synopsis: A320 Captain experiences a TCAS RA at 5,000 feet approaching SNA.
summary: The pilot received a TCAS Resolution Advisory to climb at 5,000 feet while being vectored by ZLA. The report does not specify the aircraft type, the cause of the conflict, or the outcome of the maneuver.

synopsis: SFO Controller described an unsafe condition citing the continued use of similar sounding four digit company call signs during the same time frame with identical routings.
summary: A Ground Control controller identified a potential safety risk when an Air Carrier pilot transposed their call sign during taxi clearance. The controller corrected the error, noting that similar call signs could lead to wrong strip handling and loss of separation during busy departure periods.

synopsis: ZID Controller voiced concern regarding the 'shared airspace' between G57 and G44, the reporter claiming the shared airspace issue is unsafe.
summary: The pilot reported that Danville Sector could not accept a handoff until coordinating with Eon Sector due to shared airspace. The reporter described this known coordination delay as an unsafe condition requiring immediate resolution to prevent an accident.

synopsis: P50 Controller witnessed a side by departure event with the Tower providing visual separation, the reporter noting speed assignments should be published on the SID to minimize various speeds utilized by different aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller observed an A321 and a CRJ9 departing Phoenix side-by-side with only a few hundred feet of separation while the faster CRJ9 overtook the A321 below 8,000 feet. The controller attributed the close proximity to pilots selecting their own climb speeds and recommended publishing specific speed restrictions on departure procedures.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a loss of separation between two different Air Carrier aircraft when each altered their airspeed without due recognition by the controller, the reporter providing some excellent insight to the event.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a potential separation compromise between an arriving A319 and a departing Falcon 2000 due to unanticipated speed changes in turbulence. The controller failed to monitor the increasing closure rate, allowing the Falcon to overtake the slowing A319 before visual separation was established.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain is informed as he takes the runway, by the pilot behind him that flames were coming out of the engine. Both engines are shut down with no more flames reported and the APU is started. After inspection by the fire crew the good engine is started and the aircraft is taxied back to the gate.
summary: The Captain reported flames from Engine 1 during takeoff roll, prompting an immediate stop and shutdown. After fire crews and maintenance confirmed no fire or damage, the aircraft taxied to the gate, deplaned passengers, and was taken out of service for an oil leak check.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew experiences a left bleed trip passing FL320 for FL400, which is successfully reset. Bleed trip reoccurs at FL400 and cannot be reset, resulting in the left pack being turned off in compliance with QRH. The right pack then trips and an emergency descent is initiated. During the descent both packs are reset successfully but the crew elects to divert for maintenance.
summary: The Pilot Flying and First Officer experienced repeated left and right pack trip-offs during climb to FL400, causing rapid cabin altitude rise and requiring oxygen mask use. They declared an emergency, descended to 10,000 feet, and diverted after successfully resetting the packs mid-descent.

synopsis: An A320 First Officer reported specific and generalized problems with respect to conducting RNAV STAR operations into DEN. His summation states: 'THIS IS NOT WORKING!'
summary: Pilots flying into Denver encountered conflicting ATC clearances and airspeed anomalies during the descent on the TELLR1 arrival. The FMGC failed to maintain required speeds, forcing manual flight and speed brake use to meet altitude constraints.

synopsis: Dispatcher voiced concern regarding the functionalities of the current decision making tool providing a number of examples of the limits encountered.
summary: A dispatcher identified that the dispatch system incorrectly recommended no alternate for an A319/320/321 flight despite high crosswinds and ground delays. The reporter attributed this to the system's failure to account for operational limits and fuel requirements, creating a risk of illegal flights and distracting from safe operational control.

synopsis: CRJ-700 Captain reports being dispatched on a ferry flight with the right IGD deferred. At FL210 the left engine oil temperature is noted to be high and rising. When the oil temperature cannot be reduced the engine is shut down and the flight diverts to the nearest suitable airport. Maintenance determines that the high temperature was caused by a faulty probe.
summary: The crew diverted to ZZZ after the left engine oil temperature reached 190°C during climb, triggering an emergency shutdown. Mechanics later identified a faulty oil temperature probe as the cause, and the crew successfully managed the single-engine landing despite FMS workload constraints.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: A pilot reported the INT Runway 33 hold short line on Taxiway A was a greater distance from the runway than expected and the crew nearly missed seeing it.
summary: The flight crew, operating an aircraft with an inoperative landing light in total darkness, nearly crossed a hold-short line while taxiing southbound on Taxiway A. The copilot applied brakes after identifying the faded lines as a hold-short marking, stopping just short of the intersection.

synopsis: A MD-80's right engine failed during the climb, so an emergency was declared, the QRH completed and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: During climb on the last leg, the crew experienced a right engine failure with severe damage, indicated by a loud bang and high EGT. They secured the engine using the QRH, returned to the departure airport, and landed safely with effective crew coordination.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier crew exited MFE Runway 13 onto Runway 18/36 believing that they were exiting on Taxiway C.
summary: The flight crew mistakenly turned onto Taxiway C instead of Runway 36 after landing at MFE due to the close proximity of the two. The captain stopped the aircraft, assessed the situation, and safely exited the runway to avoid conflict with landing traffic.

synopsis: An MD-82 Captain was alerted by the outbound First Officer preflighting the aircraft he flew in that there was a substantial hydraulic fluid leak at the left main gear. The reporter returned to the flight deck and entered an appropriate write-up in the AML.
summary: After landing and taxiing to the gate, the First Officer reported a hydraulic leak near the left landing gear. The Captain inspected the area and found a significant leak from the left main landing gear strut seal, leaving a fluid trail, which was then logged as a discrepancy.

synopsis: An A321 Captain returned to the departure airport after the entire flight attendant crew reported a lightheaded, drunken feeling and with a headache while experiencing the dirty socks odor. Paramedics assessed the Flight Attendant reporter with high blood pressure. The reporter felt ill the entire next day.
summary: During an A321 flight, cabin crew experienced dizziness, headaches, and a "dirty sock" odor caused by an unidentified gas leak. The Captain diverted the aircraft back to the departure airport for medical evaluation after the crew self-administered oxygen and reported symptoms.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports about improper maintenance practices he was directed to follow under threat of losing his job, after a B767-300 aircraft arrived with a SLAT ASYM EICAS message and LEADING EDGE light illuminated.
summary: A mechanic repairing a B767-300's faulty slat proximity switch used an open flame to seal splices in a flammable zone after being pressured by engineers and management. The mechanic was subsequently suspended pending termination, despite claiming they followed available documentation and felt forced to deviate from safety standards to keep their job.

synopsis: An IMC PA-28 pilot began an early descent after he misidentified a final approach but was told by the TRACON to remain at 2,000 FT because of obstacles. Fatigue, anxiety and lack of proficiency were identified as part of the reporter's problem on two previous unsuccessful approaches.
summary: The pilot misidentified the final approach fix during a third LDA 33 attempt, descending below the cleared 2,000 feet to 1,200 feet due to fatigue and anxiety. An ATC alert prompted an immediate climb, averting a terrain incursion, leading the pilot to commit to increased simulator training and better alternate selection.

synopsis: A CE-560XL encountered severe turbulence at 11,000 FT while descending on the FERNANDO 5 Arrival into Southern California, but damage was not discovered during a post flight airframe inspection nor did any occupants sustain injury.
summary: During a charter descent on the FERNANDO 5 arrival near PIRUE, severe turbulence disengaged the autopilot and caused a 400-foot altitude deviation. The crew requested a turn toward the coast and a descent to 8,000 feet, landing uneventfully with no aircraft damage after a maintenance inspection.

synopsis: A Lead Mechanic reports how company policy of requiring 'brakes-Off' on aircraft at domestic and international terminals, has contributed to multiple incidents in one month, of aircraft that 'weather-vaned' off the gates due to windy conditions. B737NG aircraft appear to be more susceptible.
summary: Two maintenance technicians moved an empty aircraft with brakes off when a wind gust caused it to weather vane and excursion 25–40 feet laterally. The aircraft was removed from service for inspection, and the reporter attributes the incident to the carrier's "brakes off" gate policy in windy conditions.

synopsis: A Quality Assurance Inspector reports about two events involving a Eurocopter AS-350 that experienced an inflight Hydraulic System Failure Warning Annunciation, requiring a shutdown of the aircraft's single hydraulic system and an emergency landing. Maintenance troubleshooting noted the hydraulic system was functioning properly, but the 'On/Off' Hydraulic System toggle switch detent on the Pilot's Collective handle was malfunctioning.
summary: The AS-350 helicopter crew experienced a hydraulic system failure annunciation during flight, prompting an emergency declaration and a successful landing. Maintenance found no visible signs of failure, though the aircraft had experienced the same issue the previous week.

synopsis: BE35 pilot is informed of a NMAC by the other aircraft involved while climbing to 2,000 FT 5 miles south of HOT. The other aircraft was never sighted by the reporter.
summary: During a Hot Springs airport open house, a pilot flying a club sightseeing route climbed eastbound over Lake Hamilton and was informed by an unknown aircraft that he had passed 200 feet below it. The reporter assumed the other aircraft was on a 45-degree downwind entry descending to 1,500 feet MSL, but the flight continued without incident.

synopsis: Enroute Controller voiced a safety concern regarding the similar sounding four digit call signs utilized by an Air Carrier company, frequently at the same time.
summary: An air traffic controller in Sector X vectored three Air Carrier X flights (ABCA, ACCA, ACAA) for airport sequencing. The controller recommended the airline change departure times or call signs to resolve recurring frequency congestion caused by simultaneous morning arrivals.

synopsis: Enroute controller voiced concern regarding the TRACON's handling of an emergency aircraft with regard to priority, often failing to afford priority to emergency and Medevac operations.
summary: An Air Carrier pilot declared an emergency due to cockpit smoke while descending to 16,000 feet. The Center controller eventually cleared the aircraft direct to a fix, but TRACON subsequently turned it west to sequence behind another inbound, delaying the priority handling.

synopsis: N90 Controller described a go-around event at a non-towered airport when current information regarding a runway closure NOTAM was not recognized by the reporter and flight crew.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared a Gulfstream V for an ILS approach to closed Runway 14 at JFK due to outdated Integrated Display System data and an incomplete briefing. The pilot executed a missed approach after airport operations intercepted the aircraft for vehicles on the runway, attributing the incident to multiple communication and information failures.

synopsis: A B737-300 Captain discovered the Standby Hydraulic/Rudder System inoperative after inadvertantly performing the system preflight check which had been removed as a preflight requirement about six months prior.
summary: A B737 captain discovered a complete Standby Hydraulic System failure during an originating preflight while performing a removed standby rudder check. Contract Maintenance found the electric standby pump lacked power, raising concerns about how long the aircraft had flown without this system since the check was deleted from procedures.

synopsis: An EMB-145 number 1 Engine Bleed Leak System alerted after takeoff so an emergency was declared, the checklist completed and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The Captain and First Officer declared an emergency and returned for an overweight landing after a Number 1 Engine Bleed Leak indication occurred post-takeoff. The aircraft touched down at less than 300 FPM, passengers deplaned, and maintenance was notified.

synopsis: A B747-400 First Officer commanded a rejected takeoff after 50 knots when he realized that the right air data computer had failed.
summary: The First Officer reported an Air Data Computer failure causing erratic airspeed indications during takeoff below 80 knots. The crew executed a rejected takeoff without activating autobrakes, exiting the runway after the Captain responded to the First Officer's prompt.

synopsis: A B767-300 fueling valve did not completely close after refueling so left tank fuel continuously transferred into the Center tank requiring the crew to repeatedly re-balance the fuel tanks.
summary: The flight crew managed an in-flight fuel transfer issue on a Boeing 767 caused by a fueling valve that failed to fully close. After multiple re-balancing attempts, they continued to an uneventful landing and recommended adding specific guidance to the QRH for this scenario.

synopsis: A MD-11 developed a nearly 75 KT difference between airspeed indications after an hour of IMC flight at FL350 but upon descent the Captain, First Officer, and Standby airspeeds again agreed and autothrottles and autopilot came functional. Maintenance changed the number 1 CADC.
summary: During cruise in IMC, the crew experienced autopilot and autothrottle disconnections with erratic airspeed indications, including a 50-knot difference between pilots. They declared an emergency, descended early to FL250, and landed after airspeeds normalized below 15,000 feet.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 rolled violently 40-45 degrees right and the L FLT SPLR EICAS alerted after the flight spoilers were fully extended during descent. Full left aileron started a partial recovery with wings level after spoiler retraction.
summary: During descent in IMC, the pilot extended flight spoilers to slow, causing a violent 45-50 degree right roll. Retracting the spoilers corrected the flight, but the left spoiler remained inoperative, requiring aileron input during landing and taxi.

synopsis: An overhead panel in the cabin of a CRJ-900 had been removed and replaced during installation of WiFi wiring. When it was replaced it was secured with the incorrect screws and, upon a subsequent landing, the panel fell out and struck a passenger in the head causing a painful and bloody, but not serious, injury.
summary: A cabin crew member reported that an overhead panel dislodged upon landing impact due to improper screws used after WiFi installation, striking a passenger in Row 3C. The passenger received medical treatment and was cleared to continue, while a mechanic secured the panel and inspected others.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports that a Supervisor failed to warn and inform Maintenance personnel when he turned on a B737-400 aircraft's Hydraulic System and moved flight controls. Supervisor did not follow the 'Warning' notice in their Job Card prior to performing a scheduled CAT-2 upgrade Certification Check.
summary: A supervisor performing a CAT-2 certification check activated hydraulics without warning mechanics, violating Job Card XXX4003 Step 7. Although flight controls moved, the mechanics avoided injury by staying clear of potential moving parts.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician Trainer was informed, after training several new mechanics on DHC8-300 Engine Rigging, that he, the trainees and Quality Assurance failed to notice a Condition Rod from the # 2 Engine nacelle quadrant to the Mechanical Fuel Control Unit, had been installed on the opposite side of the MFC Condition arm.
summary: A mechanic training new staff on engine rigging incorrectly installed a condition rod on the opposite side of the Mechanical Fuel Controller. The error went undetected for two months until a heavy check, when the rod was repositioned correctly.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) was informed that all four flight crew Oxygen (O2) mask microphones on a B777-200 aircraft were found not connected to the back side of their stowage boxes. Lack of adequate Maintenance turnover communications between shifts and the need for more Avionics's Operational Checks prior to aircraft release were noted.
summary: A maintenance technician completed an Engineering Order on a B777-200, discovering four unconnected oxygen mask microphones during a shift turnover. The reporter attributed the issue to poor maintenance crew handovers and a lack of operational checks before aircraft release.

synopsis: A MD-11 EICAS alerted LEVEL 2 FCC 2B DATA FAULT so after conferring with Dispatch and Maintenance an emergency was declared while returning to the foreign departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced a Level 2 FCC 2B Data Fault while intercepting a 6R offset in foreign airspace below RVSM. The Captain declared an emergency, coordinated a return to the departure airport, and landed uneventfully, attributing the event to a mechanical failure.

synopsis: An amphibian aircraft, experienced a hydraulic pump failure after takeoff and with partially retracted landing gear, the pilot successfully landed on grass at the departure airport resulting in minor damage.
summary: The pilot and co-pilot experienced a hydraulic failure preventing landing gear retraction on an amphibious flying boat due to a blown O-ring in the main actuator. They landed on a grass area with tower assistance, resulting in minor damage to the right wing float and hull paint but no injuries.

synopsis: A SR-22 pilot departed with the towbar attached and returned to land after first hearing the propellers strike the towbar, then seeing the rotating propeller tips delaminated after towbar contact.
summary: The pilot took off with the towbar still attached after moving the aircraft from a hangar, causing a propeller strike at 500 feet. The composite propeller was damaged, but the pilot returned for a safe landing where the towbar released upon ground contact.

synopsis: HCF Controller voiced concern regarding the less than clear opposite direction operations practiced by the MKK Tower and the apparent lack of understanding by the HCF Controllers.
summary: An OJT instructor and trainee at MKK managed a DA40 approach and an Air Carrier departure during confused opposite-direction operations. The trainee approved visual separation despite the carrier not seeing the DA40, prompting a supervisor to verify the unsafe situation and the instructor to request facility retraining on non-radar procedures.

synopsis: Enroute Controller failed to remember the very low altimeter settings and non availability of FL180, resulting in a loss of separation.
summary: An air traffic controller in Sector X lost separation between a Turbo Commander at FL170 and an E145 at FL180 due to assigning an unusable altitude during low altimeter settings. The controller failed to use visual separation despite the E145 pilot reporting the other aircraft in sight, resulting in a separation loss of 8-9 miles.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a conflict event when traffic on a missed approach conflicted with departure traffic that turn unexpectedly in the wrong direction, the reporter suggested new missed approach procedures be developed.
summary: Local 1 controller managed a B737 departure from Runway 4L while a second B737 on Runway 4R executed a missed approach, turning left instead of the standard right. The controller separated the aircraft by expediting the departure's climb and restricting the missed approach, attributing the conflict to procedural flaws, the unexpected left turn, and potential language barriers.

synopsis: PDX Controller described an opposite direction take off from VUO, the reporter suggesting a Tower be opened at VUO to reduce these types of events.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller at uncontrolled VUO advised a Pitts pilot on final for Runway 8 of a departing Sonex on opposite Runway 26, causing the Pitts to execute a go-around. The controller attributed the incident to confusing CTAF procedures and recommended establishing a control tower to safely manage traffic near PDX.

synopsis: LAS Controller described a go around event while utilizing a back up RADAR system, claiming that the lack of familiarity and training deficiencies were both casual factors.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared a B737 for takeoff while an A320 was three miles out on final, but the A320 disappeared from the backup radar before initiating a go-around. The controller attributed the resulting close proximity to the backup radar's reduced accuracy and requested refresher training on its limitations.

synopsis: NCT Controller described a conflict event between traffic off SFO and OAK, the Controller listing the failed auto acquisition of the SFO traffic and non compliance of LOA procedures by SFO Tower as causal factors.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller and a B757 pilot reported a loss of separation between a B757 and a B737 near SFO caused by the B757's failure to auto-acquire on radar, delayed tower notification, and a non-standard heading clearance due to VOR outage. The conflict resulted in a TCAS RA, with the B757 pilot estimating 200 to 500 feet vertical and 0.5 to 1 mile lateral separation at closest point.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ZTL Controller voiced concern regarding management's decision not permit overtime when know increased traffic volumes and weather impacts were forecasted.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported that during a high-traffic weather event at ATL, management denied requested overtime, leaving the sector understaffed for over two hours. This resulted in unsafe conditions, including extended holding patterns, fuel concerns, and compromised separation due to a lack of certified controllers to manage the workload.

synopsis: Local Controller described an aborted take off apparently due to prop wash from an aircraft departing another runway.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft X for takeoff from Runway 18 while Aircraft Y held on adjacent Runway 14 with props running. Strong easterly winds combined with Aircraft Y's prop wash caused Aircraft X's left gear to lift, forcing an aborted departure and taxi back for brake cooling.

synopsis: Local Controller providing OJT described a loss of runway separation event when an aircraft on short final failed to comply with go around instructions.
summary: An OJTI and trainee on Local Control issued a late go-around to a PA32 behind a C172 on Runway 32 due to lost separation. The PA32 pilot acknowledged but refused the instruction, landing safely within 1,500 feet of the C172, citing that a go-around was too late and landing was safer.

synopsis: A B737-300 flight crew, cleared to descend via the WAHUU RNAV STAR to DEN noted the charted crossing at SAYGE in the FMS database was different from that published on their commercially provided aero chart.
summary: Pilots on a WAHUU Arrival into DEN discovered a discrepancy between their FMS and charts regarding SAYGE altitude restrictions. After ATC confirmed the chart data, the crew manually entered FL180 to avoid a potential major altitude deviation caused by the inaccurate FMS database.

synopsis: A baggage tractor driver, hurrying because he had no accurate way to determine the time relative to the scheduled departure time of flights to which he was delivering bags, attempted to take a turn at too high a speed and was ejected from the vehicle. The unmanned baggage vehicle continued uncontrolled and struck two lavatory trucks and several baggage carts.
summary: A luggage distributor lost control of a tractor while rushing due to an inaccurate scanner time, causing the vehicle to strike two Lav trucks and dollies. The incident occurred when the operator pressed both pedals simultaneously during a turn and was not wearing a seatbelt.

synopsis: A MD-11 takeoff was rejected because of a momentary ANTI-SKID FAIL alert but after clearing the warning and conferring with Maintenance, the flight departed but the crew realized later Maintenance should have cleared the log book.
summary: The flying pilot and Captain rejected takeoff at 80 knots due to an intermittent Level 2 anti-skid failure Master Caution. After consulting local maintenance and an ACP, they departed successfully but later realized they should have blocked in for a formal 'p' write-up per the FOM.

synopsis: A B767-300, cleared to climb to FL310 received TA and RA advisories triggered by an opposite direction flight.
summary: The flight crew received a TCAS Level Off Resolution Advisory while climbing to FL310 due to opposite-direction traffic at FL290, despite ATC reporting no conflict. The crew manually leveled at FL302 to clear the conflict, after which the opposing aircraft took no action and the controller expressed surprise at the RA.

synopsis: An A319 Captain, contacted maintenance to replace a total of 25 bulbs in the aircrafts EXIT signs, the MEL allowing a maximum of 16 burnt out bulbs.
summary: The Captain reported multiple inoperative cabin exit sign bulbs exceeding MEL tolerances during pre-departure, causing a 10-minute delay for repairs. A maintenance technician made inappropriate comments regarding the write-up, though the aircraft departed only eight minutes late after the lights were fixed.

synopsis: An EMB-145's retraction/extension hydraulic lines were catching on the auxiliary gear drag brace washer and preventing the nose gear from extending so an emergency was declared and the aircraft landed uneventfully following a post maintenance Functional Check Flight.
summary: During a post-MBV functional check flight, a loud bang and LG/LEVER DISAGREE message occurred during gear extension, causing a missed approach. Maintenance identified hydraulic lines catching on the auxiliary gear drag brace washer as the cause and recommended rerouting the lines.

synopsis: The pilots of an Embraer 135 identified an airspeed anomaly followed by crew alerting messages, they suspected a frozen pitot-static line to the Air Data Computer. After descending a few thousand feet the system returned to normal. Later, Maintenance personnel confirmed that frozen water was found in the pitot-static line.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced airspeed and altitude data loss at FL370 due to frozen pitot-static lines. After losing 400 feet while requesting a descent to FL340, the system recovered, and maintenance later found freezing water in the line.

synopsis: An MD-82 flight crew diverted to the nearest suitable airport in response to unreliable airspeed/mach indications on both pilots' flight instruments.
summary: The crew declared an emergency and diverted at FL330 due to unreliable airspeed indications caused by a discrepancy between Captain and First Officer instruments. After autothrottle and autopilot disconnects, they flew using pitch and power settings cross-checked with the standby airspeed indicator.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reports not being instructed to join the localizer during approach to LFPG and overshooting before turning back to intercept. LFPG has a special rule about joining the localizer without being instructed to do so, which the crew had forgotten.
summary: The flight crew overshot the localizer for Runway 26R at LFPG while distracted by a QRH check, failing to apply the airport's 70-degree intercept rule without ATC instruction. They corrected the deviation by turning back to intercept from the south, resulting in no traffic conflict.

synopsis: Two B747-400 pilots report a First Officer's PFD and ND failed on final approach with a very strong electrical odor in the flight deck. They also noted they did not have enough time to advise the flight attendants or run the Smoke/Fumes Checklists.
summary: During approach at 2,500 feet, the First Officer's PFD and ND failed with an electrical burning odor, prompting an emergency declaration and uneventful landing. The crew donned oxygen masks but could not run smoke checklists or brief flight attendants due to the immediate need to land.

synopsis: CRJ-700 flight crew reported EICAS message 'Elevator Split' in climb. QRH directed landing at nearest suitable airport, so they returned to departure airport.
summary: During climb through 6,000 feet, the crew received an elevator split caution, followed the QRH to land at the nearest airport, and returned to the departure airport. They declared an emergency and landed safely.

synopsis: During a flight crew bathroom break, an A319 Captain notices the Mid and Aft-cabin EXIT location signs were dimly lit. Numerous light bulbs were found inoperative in EXIT location signs, including the left and right overwing EXIT marking signs. Concern about Maintenance overlooking the EXIT marking and EXIT location signs was also noted.
summary: Flight crew discovered multiple inoperative bulbs in mid-cabin, aft-cabin, and overwing exit signs during a flight and after landing. The reporter attributes the issue to maintenance routinely overlooking these items on 7-day checks and recommends moving inspections to daily checks.

synopsis: EMB190 First Officer describes receiving a Slat Fail caution message during initial climb. QRH procedures are complied with and the crew elects to return to the departure airport due to the long runways. The flight had been dispatched with a flap motor on MEL.
summary: During initial climbout at 3,500 feet, a slat failure occurred, likely contributed to by an existing MEL for slow flap retraction. The crew diverted to a long runway, managed icing and turbulence, and landed safely with fire services standing by.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier crew being vectored for the SBN Runway 9R ILS received an EGPWS terrain warning at 2,600 feet and because they were IMC executed the escape maneuver even though they believed there was no threat west of the airport.
summary: The flight crew received a GPWS terrain warning while being vectored for the SBN 9R ILS at 2,600 feet in IMC. They executed an escape maneuver to 3,000 feet, suspecting a false alarm due to the lack of high obstacles, and subsequently completed the approach without further incident.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 in IMC at FL370 lost all air data computer information, resulting in the loss of all altitude, indicated airspeed, and VSI indications. A diversion was made to a nearby airport and while descending through FL240, Air Data Computer 1 systems returned to normal.
