summary: A pilot inbound to Tucson Ryan Airport at 2,200 feet AGL reported a Cessna passing underneath from right rear to left front while on a left base for Runway 6L. The pilot attributed the close call to not seeing the low-wing aircraft from below and noted the Tower subsequently cleared them for Runway 6R.

synopsis: C414 flight crew note flickering hydraulic flow lights in cruise and attempt to extend the landing gear unsuccessfully. The emergency extension bottle 'T' handle is then pulled, also without success. After several hours and many consultations a belly landing ensues. After the aircraft is lifted from the runway, an FAA Inspector is able to activate the emergency extension system on the second try using extra force.
summary: A pilot and passenger flew a Cessna 414A VFR when hydraulic flow lights flickered and the landing gear failed to extend despite multiple emergency procedures. After burning fuel and consulting mechanics, they executed a gear-up landing; post-incident inspection revealed a hydraulic leak and a stuck emergency handle that required a sharp strike to release.

synopsis: Tower Controller described an ATC declared emergency event when a VFR aircraft encountered IMC conditions, was unfamiliar with SVFR procedures and required controller assistance to locate the airport.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller declared an emergency for a C172 pilot who could not maintain VFR when weather deteriorated to 2 miles visibility and 700 feet ceiling. The controller guided the pilot to the shoreline and cleared a safe landing on Runway 20 or 23 after the pilot regained visual contact.

synopsis: Air Carrier described a TCAS RA between himself and a Lear who was reportedly maintaining Visual Separation with him.
summary: During descent into Tower Controlled Airspace, Approach Control cleared a Learjet to climb through the reporting aircraft's 10,000 FT altitude while claiming visual separation, despite the reporting crew never calling traffic in sight. This conflicting clearance caused a TCAS RA conflict and a dangerous near-miss, which the reporter attributes to Approach Control's error and the Learjet crew's actions.

synopsis: A B767-300 Forward Recirculation Fan failed in flight causing very strong chemical odor/fumes so, after donning oxygen masks, an emergency was declared and the flight diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: At FL390, both pilots experienced strong chemical fumes affecting their lungs, prompting an emergency declaration and oxygen use. They diverted to a nearby airport, requested fire and rescue, and executed a visual approach while running the smoke and fume checklist.

synopsis: When a windshield sun visor fell from its hanger on a B767-300ER in cruise at FL390 it struck the right engine fuel control, causing it to move to the cutoff position and shutting down the engine. The flight crew promptly returned it to the run position and the engine restarted. A loss of 300 feet during the episode went unnoted by ATC and the flight continued to destination.
summary: During cruise flight, a window shade fell onto the right engine fuel control in light turbulence, inadvertently shutting down the engine. The crew corrected the fuel control, restored power, and returned to FL390 with a maximum altitude loss of 300 feet.

synopsis: An EMB-145 flight crew experienced an NMAC with a VFR general aviation aircraft while on descent to EWR.
summary: FQM3 crew inbound to Newark received an RA at 6,000 feet due to a VFR aircraft descending to their altitude. The First Officer climbed per RA instructions while ATC issued a late turn, as the threat involved uncontacted GA aircraft ignoring altitude clearances.

synopsis: While descending IFR to 6,000 a CE-560XL flight crew responded to TCAS TA and RA alerts due to a conflict with a VFR Aero Commander allegedly at 5,500 MSL while requesting an IFR clearance.
summary: While descending to 6,000 feet, the crew received a TCAS RA after a Twin Commander, cleared below 5,500 feet, appeared at 5,800 feet one mile away. The pilot climbed to 6,400 feet to avoid a conflict, noting the intruder would have been within 200 feet vertically had the maneuver not occurred.

synopsis: SF340 Captain reports a TCAS RA to descend after flap retraction at an uncontrolled airport. The descend RA is repeated followed quickly by an EGPWS warning to, don't sink.
summary: The Captain and First Officer, unfamiliar with this uncontrolled airport, received a short void time and took off despite TCAS traffic alerts. They experienced conflicting TCAS descent and EGPWS climb warnings due to nearby traffic, highlighting the difficulty of avoiding conflicts without radar or air traffic control.

synopsis: DHC-8-200 flight crew on a ferry flight experiences a cabin altitude warning light at FL190 and initiates an emergency descent and declares an emergency. During descent the #1 and #2 engine manual caution lights illuminated and torque indication was blank. Crew elects to divert to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: Flight crew enroute at FL190 declared an emergency and diverted after a cabin pressurization warning and engine manual lights illuminated. Despite blank torque gauges, the aircraft responded to power inputs and landed safely without incident.

synopsis: When an air taxi CE-402 lost the emergency exit door in flight the Captain declared an emergency and diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: During VFR cruise, the Row 2 emergency exit door opened, prompting the pilot to declare an emergency and divert to a nearby airport. After confirming no passenger injuries, the aircraft landed safely with no further incident.

synopsis: An A319 Flight Attendant became very ill then drove herself to a hospital following exposure to a complex odor resembling burnt plastic and electrical with a hint of nail polish.
summary: A Flight Attendant on an Airbus 319 reported a burnt plastic odor after takeoff, which the Captain attributed to the flight deck upon landing. The crew refused to fly the aircraft, but the Attendant later suffered severe neurological symptoms and disorientation, which she believes were caused by toxic fumes rather than the trash bin as the mechanic claimed.

synopsis: A C-172 departing a remote airfield suffered an NMAC with a commercial fixed wing aircraft inbound, opposite direction to the same runway.
summary: A pilot departing Runway 07 from a remote airport encountered a commercial twin on a direct approach to Runway 25 near a VOR at 1,500 MSL. The pilot attributed the near-miss to the carrier likely monitoring Center instead of CTAF and both aircraft flying opposite headings on the same runway.

synopsis: Piper Cub pilot reports loosing control during landing resulting a runway excursion and impact with a building.
summary: While landing a Piper Cub J3, the pilot encountered fluctuating quartering tailwinds that caused a right yaw uncorrectable by rudder or brake. Rolling left to correct resulted in the right wingtip and spinner striking a building, bringing the aircraft to rest.

synopsis: C150 student pilot in the traffic pattern experiences a rough running engine and low RPM. The pilot sets up for an off airport landing but at 100 FT the engine recovers and a normal landing ensues.
summary: The pilot executed a precautionary landing after the engine ran rough with very low RPM. The engine cleared up 100 feet above the field, allowing a continued landing with no injuries or aircraft damage.

synopsis: Falcon 50 First Officer reports a takeoff with the center engine fuel computer light on. When the thrust is advanced the engine 2 fail light comes on and the First Officer calls for a reject which is ignored. Once safely airborne the Captain agrees to return for maintenance.
summary: A First Officer aborted takeoff after an Engine 2 fail light illuminated, despite the Captain ignoring the call and dismissing earlier fuel computer light concerns. The aircraft returned to the airport with fire trucks dispatched, and the First Officer later concluded the Captain had deceived the crew about maintenance clearance.

synopsis: BE36 pilot is advised to check altitude during a night visual approach to Runway 20 at HFD. The reporter had descended to 800 FT MSL several miles to the northwest of the field.
summary: A fatigued pilot on a night visual approach to HFD Runway 20 lost sight of the airport due to complacency and navigated too far north, triggering a low altitude alarm. The pilot confirmed visual contact with Tower, received clearance, and landed safely without further incident.

synopsis: ZAU Controller described an unsafe event when an adjacent Controller amended data block information not under hiS control.
summary: A ZAU controller reported that a MIE controller improperly amended a CRJ2's data block to FL210 while the aircraft remained in ZAU airspace at FL230 near head-on ERJ traffic. The reporter attributed the error to unauthorized data block changes in another facility's airspace and recommended reverting to HOST procedures.

synopsis: NCT Controller was questioned regarding an alledged 'wake remant' separation loss, the Controller claiming no tools are avaialble to controllers to identify these types of occurrences.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported a separation alert between an A380 and a B737-800 departing SFO, which playback attributed to A380 wake remnants. The controller disputed this cause, stating they lack tools to track historical altitudes or wake data and rely only on real-time information.

synopsis: A First Officer describes an in-flight event involving a decreasing Oil Quantity Indication on the Left Engine of a B767-200 aircraft while over water, the loss of their APU and the decision process to return to their departure airport. Oil quantity returned to normal after engine shutdown. False readings from Left Engine oil quantity sending unit.
summary: The crew of an ETOPS flight turned back from the North Atlantic after the left engine oil quantity indication dropped to 11 quarts at FL370. Maintenance later confirmed a false reading caused by a blocked vent, as actual oil levels remained sufficient for an uneventful return.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reports descending early on the RNAV Runway 28 to MTPP. The clearance direct IRDAS is received late and the transition from IRDAS is not selected in the FMC eliminating two step down fixes and results in a terrain warning.
summary: Pilots flying into MTPP received a garbled ATC clearance direct to IRDAS, bypassing the expected SAVAR transition. This caused a route discontinuity in the FMC, leading to an early descent and a GPWS warning that was resolved by climbing before completing a safe landing.

synopsis: When the flight attendants reported a smoke filled cabin immediately after takeoff the flight crew of a CRJ-900 declared an emergency and returned to their departure aiport where they landed safely.
summary: The pilot declared an emergency immediately after takeoff due to smoke and an electrical burning smell reported by flight attendants. The crew returned to land safely at 2,000 feet AGL, where the smoke dissipated, allowing passengers to deplane without evacuation.

synopsis: After receiving a clearance to fly a heading to intercept an airway, a G4 flight crew interpreted a subsequent heading as an intercept also. Controller advised that the second heading was not an intercept.
summary: The flight crew and air traffic controllers experienced a communication misunderstanding during a frequency change while joining airway A699. The crew initially turned to heading 010 based on a conflicting instruction, requiring a subsequent correction to heading 360 after the new controller clarified the clearance.

synopsis: A student pilot lost control of a PA-28 during landing after initially landing on the nose wheel. The aircraft departed the runway surface and settled nose low in the grass.
summary: A student pilot soloing a PA-28-161 at ZZZ airport executed a nose-wheel landing during a touch-and-go, causing the aircraft to porpoise, lose control, and veer off the runway. The nose gear sheared off and the propeller struck the runway, but the pilot sustained only minor injuries.

aircraft: Cessna Aircraft Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: The private pilot on a touch-and-go took evasive action after a helicopter crossed the departure end of the runway. ATC had mentioned the touch-and-go traffic but it is possible that the helicopter pilot did not see the correct aircraft.
summary: A pilot on short final executed a go-around after a helicopter crossed the departure end of the runway. The pilot turned right to pass behind the helicopter because the helicopter crew had the wrong aircraft in sight and failed to see the pilot's aircraft.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) describes some of his observations and safety concerns involving recent tow bar disconnections that have occurred during towing of B737-800 aircraft and the difficulty viewing the same aircraft when using large tow tractors.
summary: A LOSA observer reported a B737-900ER towbar shear bolt failure during a high-speed hangar tow, causing erratic nose gear movement. The incident was attributed to using an incompatible towbar and a TUG GT50H tractor, which the reporter claims are unsafe and unsupported by the manufacturer.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: IAD Controller expressed concern regarding PCT's alleged failure to consider weather and other traffic factors during a significant thunderstorm/lightning event, noting PCT's performance was unsafe.
summary: The Tower Controller reported that PCT cleared three aircraft for simultaneous visual approaches to Runways 19L, 19C, and 19R despite thunderstorms and windshear. The Controller warned that a go-around would force aircraft into weather, but PCT ignored the request for staggered approaches, creating an unsafe situation where the reporter's aircraft landed safely by luck.

synopsis: B767 First Officer is informed by the flying crew upon returning from the third break, that the left hydraulic system has failed and the flight is continuing to destination.
summary: A flight attendant on break joined the cockpit during arrival at 20,000 feet over Pennsylvania after the crew lost the left engine hydraulic pump and left hydraulic quantity over Canada. Following checklist completion and maintenance conferences, the crew safely landed at the destination and taxied to the gate.

synopsis: B757 Captain experiences a configuration warning after takeoff with an EICAS message 'CONFIG GEAR NOT DOWN'. After cycling the gear with no change, the Captain elects to return to the departure airport.
summary: The pilot reported a red configuration light and "config gear not down" EICAS message after takeoff. After an unsuccessful gear recycle at 4,000 feet, the crew returned for an uneventful landing, and the aircraft was taken out of service.

synopsis: A B757-200 diverted to a suitable airport after shutting down the left engine due to what turned out to be a false overheat warning.
summary: The crew experienced a false left engine overheat indication at FL380, prompting an emergency descent to FL280 and diversion. Maintenance later identified a faulty computer controller in the detection system as the cause of the erroneous warning.

synopsis: A pilot describes why he believes the current MEL practice of deferring both Cargo Door Warning Lights on their Fairchild SA-227 aircraft is an unsafe practice. They fly single pilot operations.
summary: A pilot reported a persistent cargo door light and received two Minimum Equipment List (MEL) deferrals from maintenance despite concerns that the door might not be properly secured. The pilot departed with the unairworthy MEL due to pressure from mechanics and fatigue, fearing the door could detach and damage the tail.

aircraft: Cessna Single Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Cessna pilot using both TIS-B and TAS for traffic avoidance reports erroneous target information from the TIS-B. The TIS indicated traffic at 1:30 coming toward the reporter and TAS indicated traffic at 7:30 going away on the same heading. The TAS traffic was visually confirmed.
summary: A Cessna pilot descending southwest of CMH received false Traffic Advisories from Garmin TIS-B while Avidyne TAS correctly identified traffic. The TIS-B misplotted ADS-B locations, creating a high collision risk as evasive action based on its data would have led to the actual traffic.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Small Transport pilot reports being cleared for the visual approach to PDK by Atlanta Approach then issued a heading by the Tower for traffic. The reporter stops descent at 2,500 FT and on a southerly heading passes over antennas depicted as 2,049 FT on the RNAV 3R approach chart. After landing during taxi, a late hold short clearance requires a sudden stop.
summary: The pilot reported two safety issues at PDK: a visual approach vector toward terrain without altitude restrictions and a near runway incursion during taxi. The pilot attributed these events to ATC workload and training controllers, noting that visual conditions prevented an accident.

synopsis: PA32 pilot was alerted by ATC of a large heading deviation while on an IFR clearance and experiencing turbulence in the cloud tops. The pilot then noticed a strong left turning tendency, and needed to add significant opposite control input to maintain course. With ATC assistant flight was diverted to the nearest airport and landed safely.
summary: A pilot encountered turbulence while climbing to 10,000 feet, after which the autopilot deviated from course and the aircraft required constant right aileron input to maintain heading. The pilot diverted to a nearby airport for a safe landing; inspections found no physical damage, with a stuck autopilot servo suspected as the cause.

synopsis: Maintenance Technician is informed after the fact that he and a helper installed a B737-700 brake on a B737-800 and signed it off. The part number was not correct and was detected after the aircraft had been released for flight.
summary: Two mechanics installed an incorrect 737-700 brake assembly on a 737-800 during a service check because they failed to verify the part number against the Aircraft Maintenance Manual. The error was discovered the following night, requiring the brake to be replaced with the correct part at another station.

synopsis: Pitts pilot is informed enroute by GKY Tower of a TFR to the north of the field and deviates to the south and west. The onboard GPS with XM gave no indication of a TFR in the area.
summary: A VFR pilot received conflicting TFR information from GKY and GPM while transitioning near a stadium, noting the dynamic TFR was not displayed on current XM GPS data. The pilot altered heading to avoid the area and suggested improving dynamic TFR availability on GPS and maps to prevent potential violations.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a conflict event when an air carrier delayed a descent, likely due to weather, and then turned tighter than expected, adding to the problems were communications difficulties.
summary: Two air traffic controllers in Sector X managed a Stratolifter and a Medium Large Transport, but poor frequency conditions and a tight turn by the Stratolifter caused a Conflict Alert. The Transport subsequently went NORDO for 5–10 minutes while controllers struggled to issue clearances due to static and communication delays.

synopsis: After failing to restrict airspeed below the SFO Class B airspace while departing SJC on the SAN JOSE SID, A B767-300 Captain addressed the fact that none of the published procedure pages for SJC provide the information necessary to determine either the confliction details of the airspace or even a note advising of its existence and the resulting need to restrict standard aircraft acceleration SOPs.
summary: The flight crew departed SJC on the SJC 9 SID without noting a company requirement to maintain clean maneuvering speeds until clear of Class B airspace. Upon reaching 5,000 feet, they exceeded 250 knots until ATC reminded them of the airspace, prompting an immediate speed reduction to 220 knots.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An air carrier flight crew flying out of FLL was surprised to learn that Runway 13/31 had been decommissioned and the new East West runway was not yet open, making it a one runway airport.
summary: The flight crew at FLL discovered Runway 13/31 and Taxiway B were closed during taxi, despite Ground Control initially stating only the runway was decommissioned. The reporter attributes this confusion to inadequate operational messaging regarding the airport's single-runway configuration, which was not clearly reflected in NOTAMs or flight releases.

synopsis: CRJ200 flight crew experience a catastrophic engine failure climbing through 11,500. The Captain assumed control of the aircraft, declared an emergency and turned toward the airport as the cockpit quickly filled with smoke. The First Officer commenced the smoke removal checklist and eventually got the packs off and the aircraft depressurized just before landing. The passengers and crew evacuate after stopping on the runway.
summary: During climb to FL230, the First Officer reported a loud bang, N2 vibration, and ITT spike on the left engine, followed by dense cockpit smoke. The Captain declared an emergency, landed safely, and evacuated all six passengers and crew with no injuries, attributing the event to a catastrophic left engine failure.

synopsis: A B717 declared and emergency and returned to their takeoff airport following repeated compressor stalls from the right engine.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced two compressor stalls in the right engine at 800 feet AGL during climb. They declared an emergency, returned to land safely with the engine at idle, and maintenance will investigate the cause.

synopsis: DHC-8-300 Captain notes a PASS DOOR warning light illuminated during during approach passing 5,000 FT. The Emergency Checklist is consulted and the flight continues to a normal landing.
summary: During approach at 5,000 FT MSL, the pilot reported a PASS DOOR warning light illumination. The crew executed emergency checklists, notified passengers, and advised ATC before landing without incident.

synopsis: A B737-800 flight crew flew two legs before discovering their flight crew oxygen bottle pressure well below minimum upon completion of their final leg. The pressure gauge had been reading abnormally high which did not trigger further assessment earlier.
summary: Pilots flew a multi-leg trip with a faulty crew oxygen gauge pegged high, unaware the actual pressure was critically low at 300 PSI. Maintenance later identified a loose connection causing the false indication, leaving the crew potentially without oxygen during the flight.

synopsis: MD82 flight crew experiences a CADC failure shortly after takeoff and returns to the departure airport after declaring an emergency.
summary: The First Officer experienced a CADC #2 failure shortly after takeoff, prompting an emergency declaration and a return for an ILS approach via ATC vectors. The aircraft landed normally under maximum weight, with the reporter attributing the issue to aging electrical and pneumatic connections.

synopsis: An MD-82 suffered a pressurization problem climbing out of approximately 11,500 MSL. They declared an emergency, conducted appropriate QRH checklists and returned uneventfully to their departure airport.
summary: During climb through 11,500 feet, Master Warning and Cabin Altitude warnings illuminated. The crew descended to 10,000 feet, executed QRH procedures, declared an emergency, and landed safely on Runway 8 ten minutes later with no further complications.

synopsis: B757 flight crew experiences left engine surging shortly after takeoff. An emergency is declared and the flight returns to the departure airport with the left engine at idle.
summary: During climb out, the left engine surged and thumped, prompting the Captain to take control, declare an emergency, and return for an uneventful landing with the engine at idle. The cause was identified as left engine surging on climb.

synopsis: Corporate aircraft departing ABQ experienced a TCAS RA with an arrival aircraft, the reporter suggesting the close proximity of arrival and departure navigational fixes could be one causal factor.
summary: During initial climb to 9,000 feet departing Runway 21, the crew received a TCAS alert while turning northwest near ASTAH Intersection due to an approaching airliner near STIKI. The pilot reduced climb rate, and both aircraft received a "monitor vertical speed" Resolution Advisory, which the reporter attributes to the proximity of these two intersections.

synopsis: A CL30 which departed on the TEB 8 Runway 1 SID did not capture the 2,000 FT set in the MCP and so overshot by about 350 FT at which time ATC issued a higher altitude.
summary: During the TEB 8 departure, the pilot flying engaged the autopilot at 1,000 FT MSL and failed to anticipate the 2,000 FT level-off, resulting in a 350 FT altitude overshoot. The reporter attributed the incident to the pilot flying being behind the aircraft, poor judgment, and reluctance to follow standard operating procedures.

synopsis: ZMP Controller voiced concern regarding the recent performance of frequency 132.90, the reporter providing a number of equipment and/or procedural solutions to the problem.
summary: An Air Carrier X aircraft at 16,000 feet near the MBS135007 fix could not hear the controller's transmissions on frequency 132.90 at TVC. The controller attributes this to degraded equipment performance or interference and recommends changing frequencies or procedures to improve coverage.

synopsis: MMU Controller described a reported NMAC when traffic on a visual approach to Runway 23 to MMU encountered VFR departure traffic from CDW, the reporter claiming N90 controllers consistently fail to coordinate as required.
summary: A C750 on a visual approach to MMU Runway 23 encountered a VFR departure from CDW, triggering a Resolution Advisory that forced a climb to 2,200 feet. The reporter attributes the conflict to N90 failing to coordinate the visual approach with CDW Tower before transferring the aircraft to MMU.

synopsis: A B737-300 flight crew suffered pressurization failure at FL370, initiated an emergency descent and descended to 10,000 feet where they continued to destination. Maximum cabin altitude reached was approximately 12,500 feet and passenger O2 masks did not deploy.
summary: During cruise at FL370 in IMC, the flight crew experienced a cabin altitude warning and executed an emergency descent to 10,000 feet due to pressurization system failure. The crew managed the situation using checklists and standby mode, landing safely with minor passenger discomfort, though the pilot noted difficulties with oxygen mask donning and obscured pressurization gauge readings.

synopsis: When a B757 flight crew was cleared to 'descend as if you were 'descending via' the GIBBZ RNAV STAR to IAD' while, in actuality, deviating well north of the published track, then were switched over to another Controller without receiving a requested clarification as to what was expected of them the Captain refused to descend below a previously cleared hard altitude and felt compelled to submit this report.
summary: Pilots flying a Gibbz One arrival to IAD deviated north for weather and received a confusing clearance to "descend as though on the arrival" while off-course. They questioned the instruction, contacted Approach Control to clarify their last hard altitude of 11,000 feet, and received a proper descent clearance before landing.

synopsis: This Boeing 737 crew received EEC ENG and EEC ALT Master Caution warnings after engine start and returned to the gate for maintenance attention. After Maintenance sign-off, the flight again departed, and during takeoff and climb they now noticed airspeed indicator discrepancies and received an IAS Disagree message, and returned to their departure airport.
summary: During a red-eye departure, the crew experienced an IAS Disagree message and inconsistent airspeed indications between the Captain and First Officer after takeoff. Unable to resolve the unreliable airspeed via maintenance contact, they returned to the departure airport for an overweight landing, where maintenance cleared a blocked pitot-static system.

synopsis: Dispatcher reports difficulty with the communication capabilities of his dispatch computer system which he believes is symptomatic of wider problems with the system.
summary: Air traffic controllers attempted to alert airborne flights of a dispatch computer outage via ACARS, but the system failed to reach all sector flights and incorrectly messaged others. This communication failure highlighted a wider system issue that the reporter believes increases the risk of an incident.

synopsis: Dispatcher reports that several times a day the controlling WSI forecast gets knocked out of the Dispatch program by the NWS forecast.
summary: A pilot reported that the controlling WSI weather forecast was repeatedly replaced by the NWS forecast on their display. The pilot had to contact WSI to request a TAF re-transmission to restore the correct forecast.

synopsis: A Dispatcher reported that his new dispatch computer software normal connectivity failed which required that an alternated login method was needed but ACARS was then no longer available.
summary: A dispatcher experienced a two-hour connectivity failure in the primary dispatch software, preventing ACARS message reception for about 10 minutes. The issue was resolved by switching to a test-mode backup method, while the dispatcher instructed flights to use Commercial Radio for necessary communication.

synopsis: Baggage handler suggest that the aircraft lavatories should not be serviced while the rear compartment is being loaded and unloaded due to the high winds present at PHOG and the likelihood that the ground crew will get sprayed.
summary: Baggage handlers reported exposure to biohazardous waste while servicing lavatories on a B757 during offloading and loading operations. Management's decision to allow simultaneous servicing, combined with wind shifts and truck liquid buildup, caused hazardous spray exposure to unprotected employees.

synopsis: Ground crewman supervising an aircraft tow reports a broken tow bar hitch approaching the gate. Before the aircraft can be signaled to set brakes the nose tires run over the towbar popping both tires.
summary: A ground handler guiding a pushback tractor reported a towbar hitch failure that caused the towbar to separate while the aircraft was being towed to the gate. The aircraft subsequently ran over the detached towbar, damaging both nose gear tires before the flight deck could set the brakes.

synopsis: An EMB-145 flight crew experienced a Bleed Over-Temp and Wing Anti-Ice Fail warning while entering icing conditions, and returned to their departure airport for maintenance inspection. The Anti-Ice system ground checked normal, and the flight again was dispatched. When entering icing conditions for the second time and activating the Anti-Ice system, they again had the same failure and the same Master Caution warnings as before.
summary: The flight crew returned to the departure airport due to a Wing Anti-Ice failure in icing conditions. They descended through a cloud break to 10,000 feet to avoid ice and executed a safe overweight landing despite thunderstorms and windshear advisories.

synopsis: A319 pilot reports that the CCLYD way point on the BRYCC1 departure from DEN is misspelled. The FMC spells it as CCYLD and the Commercial Chart shows CCYLD. (CCLYD is correct.)
summary: The pilot reported a misspelled waypoint in the MCDU flight plan for the BRYCC1 departure, where CCLYD was entered as CCYLD. The flight plan requires reissuance to correct the spelling according to the departure plate.

synopsis: B777 flight crew reports a runway excursion at LAX when instructed to exit Runway 6R at E8. A wet runway and bright terminal lights during night conditions were conducive to the Captain mistaking old taxiway lines for the desired exit. The aircraft is stopped in a paved area, not intended for taxi, without damage to the aircraft or airport property.
summary: The crew of an aircraft landing on Runway 6R at LAX mistakenly turned onto an old, visible taxiway marking instead of E8 due to wet pavement, terminal glare, and misleading old stripes. The aircraft stopped safely with no damage after an IRO intervention, though the tail remained on the runway until a tug assisted in repositioning.

synopsis: A First Officer reports about a recurring runaway overheat of their L2 window on a B737-800 aircraft that was previously signed-off. Pilot noted the Overhead P5 Window Heat switch would not shut off electrical power to the window. He also questions whether or not the recent use of RAM mounts on the windows are a contributor to the overheat conditions.
summary: During preflight on a B737, the L2 window overheat light re-illuminated after maintenance reset, requiring a mechanic to pull the Cannon plug to stop heating. The aircraft was taken out of service due to a suspected faulty Window Heat Controller or window, with the reporter attributing the issue to stress from an attached RAM mount.

synopsis: The crew of an MD-82 experienced a left engine compressor stall just prior to level off and smoke almost immediately appeared in the cockpit and cabin. The QRH was consulted, Dispatch contacted, and an emergency declared with ATC. The aircraft, with both engines continuing to operate, diverted to a suitable airport and landed uneventfully. ATC initially issued a NOTAMED out-of-service runway, but when questioned by the alert flight crew another runway was assigned.
summary: The crew experienced a left engine compressor stall with cockpit smoke at FL330, prompting an emergency diversion. Although Approach initially assigned a NOTAMed ILS, they corrected the clearance, allowing an uneventful landing with the engine operating throughout.

synopsis: B757-200 flight crew reports smelling strong electrical smoke in the flight deck at FL390. The flight attendants also report an odor at the 2L and 2R doors. After a few minutes of looking the crew elects to divert to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The flight crew and cabin crew detected a strong electrical smoke odor in the cockpit and near doors 2L and 2R while en route at FL390. Unable to locate the source, the Captain declared an emergency, diverted to ZZZZ, and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: A330 Captain experiences failure of the landing gear to retract after takeoff followed quickly by failure of the Green hydraulic system. Maintenance can offer no solution and the flight returns after burning down to landing weight. Upon touchdown the Green hydraulic system restored itself to normal. Maintenance had been performed on the Green system prior to departure.
summary: The flight crew experienced landing gear retraction failure and Green hydraulic low pressure on takeoff due to suspected maintenance errors. After holding to burn fuel, the system restored itself on landing, allowing a normal taxi to the gate.

synopsis: An EMB-140 Captain, while at the gate and just prior to pushback and engine start, was notified by the Agent in charge that a fuel leak had been detected emanating from the #1 engine. It was noted that the leak was one drop per second with the fuel pump on, and slowly dissipated with the fuel pump in the off position.
summary: Ground crew reported a substantial fuel leak from Engine 1 prior to pushback, prompting the pilot to stop the operation. The leak, suspected to be caused by the fuel pump pressurizing the system, slowed when the pump was turned off, leading to a maintenance log entry and delayed departure.

synopsis: A Q-400 descended below the crossing restriction at RAYNI when cleared to descend 'via' the MARNR RNAV STAR to SEA. A late descent clearance, a previous clearance to disregard speed restrictions and maintain maximum forward speed and the resultant demands that exceeded the capability of the autoflight system were contributing factors.
summary: During descent into SEA, the First Officer descended 300 feet below the charted 12,000-foot restriction at RAYNI while hand-flying after switching from VNAV to vertical speed mode. The pilot attributed the deviation to FMS programming deficiencies, high workload, and inadequate altitude awareness, though the aircraft was corrected before landing.

synopsis: A319 Captain reports returning to the gate to replace a defective Blue Hydraulic pump. During the next takeoff attempt an ECAM for Brakes System 1 fault is displayed and the takeoff rejected at very low speed. The brake system is reset and the next takeoff produces the same result and the flight returns to the gate for Maintenance. After a full reset the next takeoff produces the same result and the flight returns to the gate with the crew out of duty time.
summary: The flight crew experienced repeated ECAM Brakes System 1 faults upon advancing power levers during three takeoff attempts, causing aborted departures and runway exits. After unsuccessful resets and maintenance checks, the crew returned to the gate and ended their duty due to exceeding duty time limits.

synopsis: An A319 taxied to the end of LAX Taxiway E and was admonished for failing to hold short at the specified hold short sign but the crew did not see a sign nor is a hold short note printed on the airport diagram as it is for Runway 25R.
summary: The First Officer and Captain held short of Runway 24L while finishing the Before Takeoff checklist, prompting an irritated Tower query about an uncharted hold line. The crew reported no prior knowledge of this procedure, noting the hold line is absent from charts and Ground Control clearances.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reports being cleared via three different routes by ATC while awaiting a wheels up time. Once cleared for takeoff the crew is cleared direct to a fix on the second route. After some discussion with ATC the second route re entered in the FMC, but an error is made causing a track deviation later in the flight.
summary: The crew entered three routes during taxi, causing ATC confusion when a fix from the second route was assigned. The Captain missed an airway entry while re-entering the second route, leading to a departure from the planned course and requiring ATC vectors.

synopsis: B747-400 flight crew experienced an autothrottle malfunction and the aircraft approached a stall before they recognized the loss of airspeed and took corrective action.
summary: During approach, an autothrottle malfunction caused airspeed loss and a near-stall. The crew recognized the issue, and the approach continued normally.

synopsis: With the First Officer flying, an MD-82 crew experienced an AC power interruption during initial climb, with the intermittent loss of the First Officer's Nav Display and PFD, as well as the added distraction of ringing Lav Smoke Alarm chimes. While concurrently leveling at 5,000 feet, a momentary slat overspeed of 5 KTS occurred. The PNF Captain misunderstood the PF First Officer and assumed his flight instruments had returned to normal, and directed him to continue flying the aircraft while he accomplished the QRH, declared an emergency, and commanded a return to the departure airport.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced multiple AC power interruptions, smoke alarms, and instrument failures during departure from ZZZ, causing autopilot disconnect and a slat overspeed at 5,000 feet. They declared an emergency, returned to ZZZ for a normal landing, and logged the incident after power issues recurred on rollout.

synopsis: An MD-82 flight crew rejected their takeoff at 120 KTS when they observed a wheel not turning warning.
summary: During takeoff on Runway XXR, the wheel-not-turning light illuminated at 120 KTS, prompting the Captain to reject the takeoff and stop the 137,000-lb aircraft. A flat left inner tire was found, requiring fire department inspection and brake cooling before the aircraft was towed to Gate X for deplaning.

synopsis: A B737-800 flight crew declared an emergency and landed safely following the failure of flats and slats to extend.
summary: During initial approach, the flight crew experienced a failure of flaps and slats to extend after selecting flaps 1. They declared an emergency, followed QRH procedures, and landed uneventfully with slats only, followed by normal post-landing checks.

synopsis: A DC-10 crew rejected two takeoffs for what they believe were valid windshear warnings but were successful on the third attempt.
summary: The crew rejected two takeoff attempts at 80 KTS due to cockpit windshear indications in 15 to 25 KTS downwind gusts. A successful departure occurred on the third attempt, and the reporter requested better windshear monitoring equipment with ATC.

synopsis: When the left thrust lever of their B757-200 appeared to stick in place at cruise thrust as they started their descent the flight crew applied increasing leverage until it broke loose and functioned normally thereafter. Maintenance found a notepad had slipped into the pedestal.
summary: During descent from FL400, a notepad in the throttle quadrant jammed the left thrust lever, causing asymmetric thrust. The crew manually freed the lever after failed autothrottle disconnection attempts, and mechanics confirmed the foreign object interfered with the clutch microswitch.

synopsis: The flight crew of a B737-800 declared an emergency and returned to their departure airport when the right side leading edge devices extended at FL340.
summary: The crew experienced uncommanded starboard leading edge extension at FL340, triggering an emergency descent to FL200 and a return for an overweight landing. Manual speed brake deployment was required as they failed to deploy, though ground inspections showed the devices appeared normal.

synopsis: An A319 had to be towed to the gate after suffering the loss of nose wheel steering.
summary: After landing, the flight crew received a 'WHEEL N/W STRG FAULT' ECAM while turning on Taxiway Alpha, resulting in a total loss of nosewheel steering. The aircraft was subsequently towed to the gate by a supertug after the QRH checklist failed to resolve the issue.

synopsis: A DC-10 flight crew suffered recurring failures of display units and FMCs during their descent to a safe landing in VMC. Heavy rains at the ramp prior to their departure may have entered the aircraft before takeoff as ramp personnel noted water dripping from the underside of the aircraft as they taxied in the ramp following the incident.
summary: The crew experienced dual FMC and display unit failures during descent through FL190, likely caused by rainwater contamination in the electronics bay from heavy thunderstorms at departure. They declared an emergency, flew a visual approach using standby instruments, and landed safely before mechanics confirmed water dripping from the aircraft.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew received a Level 2 GEN BUS 1 FAULT at FL390. The QRH directs deployment of the ADG and land at the nearest suitable airport. Numerous anomalies are detected during descent and approach, and the aircraft goes completely dark during the landing roll out.
summary: The crew experienced a Level 2 GEN BUS 1 fault at FL390, deploying the ADG and diverting to ZZZ. Erratic airspeed indications, false stick shaker activations, and total cockpit power loss occurred, but the flight was completed safely using the HUD.

synopsis: When they received a Master Caution and 'L Engine Oil Pressure Low' warning at rotation the flight crew of a DC-9-30 continued the takeoff and returned to the airport. While flying the pattern to land the left engine oil quantity approached zero, the autospoiler system failed to arm and one left antiskid light illuminated. They elected not to declare an emergency and to not to shut down the engine until after landing.
summary: Pilots experienced low oil pressure and quantity warnings immediately after rotation, prompting an immediate return to the airport. They landed with manual spoilers and no thrust reverser power on the left engine, then shut down the engine on the ground due to near-zero oil quantity.

synopsis: An Avionics Technician describes some of the factors that contributed to a B757-200 air turnback with the Forward Nose Compartment access door still open. He had been troubleshooting the Weather Radar System and no one realized the Nose Compartment Door Indication System switch had failed prior to departure.
summary: Two mechanics troubleshooting a B757-200 weather radar failure were distracted by poor lighting and a service attendant, leading them to leave a nose compartment access door open. The aircraft was dispatched with the door open and subsequently turned back due to this un-airworthy condition.

synopsis: Maintenance Technicians are assigned to taxi a CRJ200 from the hangar to a gate with the APU generator inoperative. After engine start the ground crew disconnects the tug before hydraulic pressure can be established resulting in no brakes and uncontrolled aircraft movement. The engine is shut down but the aircraft continues to roll and comes into contact with the hangar door.
summary: Pilots and ground crew lost control of a CRJ200 during a battery start taxi after the tow team disconnected the tug prematurely due to miscommunication. With no hydraulic brake pressure, the aircraft accelerated, struck hangar doors, and stopped without injury.

synopsis: MD-88 Captain reported wake vortex encounter inbound to ATL that resulted in enough roll to cause the autopilot to disconnect. When he slowed to increase spacing he was chastised by ATC.
summary: The flight crew experienced two autopilot disconnections and aircraft upsets while intercepting the ILS at ATL in IMC behind a B757. The pilot reduced speed below the ATC clearance to avoid wake turbulence, causing a controller dispute, but the flight landed uneventfully.

synopsis: When the landing gear doors failed to retract on a PA-31 the pilot extended the gear, made a fly-by for the Tower to confirm the gear was down and landed safely.
summary: The pilot experienced a recurring red in-transit light and open inboard doors during gear retraction after takeoff. After troubleshooting and low passes confirmed the gear was down and locked, the aircraft landed safely with no defects found post-flight.

synopsis: Hawker 800 Captain experiences an autopilot failure, without warning, at precisely the time the aircraft needed to level off and turn to a fix. An overshoot occurs which is quickly corrected. Infrequent flying on short trips was cited as a factor in the incident.
summary: Pilots of a Hawker 800 climbing to 14,000 feet experienced an undetected left AFCS hard failure while receiving a direct clearance to Solberg VOR. The aircraft overshot to 14,350 feet due to task saturation and infrequent flying before the crew manually corrected the climb and resumed the descent.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reports starting his engine and setting the parking brake to discover the seat height needs adjustment. While head down making the adjustment aircraft movement is detected and the brakes are quickly applied. The aircraft narrowly misses two aircraft parked on the ramp during the undetected movement.
summary: The pilot reported that a light GA aircraft rolled forward on the ramp while they adjusted their seat, narrowly missing a parked aircraft. The incident occurred because the parking brake failed to hold the aircraft, leading the pilot to shut down and manually reposition the plane.

synopsis: A C-208 instrument rated pilot got trapped by unexpected weather and an autopilot deferred inoperative enroute to OGG. In technical violation of company policy which required either an SIC or an autopilot, he obtained an IFR clearance to complete the flight.
summary: A single-pilot VFR flight en route to OGG encountered deteriorating weather and an inoperative autopilot due to an MEL, forcing a transition to IFR. The pilot obtained an IFR clearance and landed safely, citing the weather and lack of a second crew member or working autopilot as the cause.

synopsis: P32 pilot inadvertantly flew into IMC, notified ATC and, after receiving vectors to clear adverse weather, resumed VFR flight.
summary: A pilot flying an IFR-certified aircraft entered IMC conditions while operating VFR after encountering rapid weather deterioration. Memphis Center provided radar assistance and a heading change to avoid heavy weather, allowing the pilot to exit the clouds and return to VMC safely.

synopsis: Student helicopter pilot with instructor on visual approach to PAE, reports a NMAC with a BE35 overtaking at 1.5 miles on final. The reporter had been apprised that he was number two for landing but the position of number one was not determined until the NMAC. A controller change occurred during the approach.
summary: An R22B helicopter pilot reported a near-midair collision with a Beech Bonanza during the final approach to Runway 16L at Paine Field. The Bonanza overflew the helicopter 5 feet left and 25 feet above, prompting a diversion and straight-in landing, attributed to a controller change and delayed traffic position requests.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Cessna pilot reports being illuminated by a green laser on a 1.5 mile final to TUS, causing momentary loss of night vision. The student continues the approach to landing. Two air carrier aircraft landing ahead of the reporter were also illuminated.
summary: A pilot and student flying a training aircraft into TUS were illuminated by a ground-based green laser on final approach, joining two other air carrier reports within 15 minutes. The laser temporarily impaired the pilot's night vision, but the student safely landed the aircraft, though the proximity to the runway posed a significant accident risk.

synopsis: PA44 pilot discovers late that the OBS has not switched automatically from GPS to LOC during an ILS approach, resulting in a significant course deviation and a go around. The second attempt is successful with the OBS manually switched to LOC.
summary: A pilot practicing an ILS 23 approach to BUF deviated right due to a GPS malfunction showing incorrect location. The aircraft was vectored for a second successful approach, highlighting the need to manually verify GPS-to-OBS switching since the single unit did not auto-switch to the localizer.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ZAB Controller expressed concern regarding ATC assignments made by MMZT controllers noting the same altitude was given to multiple aircraft, the reporter claiming continued systematic ATC problems along the Southern border.
summary: An air traffic controller reported two aircraft descending from Mexico to TUS at FL220 without altitude restrictions from MMZT Center. Aircraft Y entered with a bad code and violated airspace at FL261, highlighting a systemic issue with border handoffs and clearance issuance.

synopsis: B737-700 First Officer reports requesting CSFF removal by the de ice crew to discover that the entire wing is being deiced. The de ice crew is redirected to de ice just the inner wing where the frost is located.
summary: The flight crew requested limited CSFF deicing on the wings at Denver, but the ground crew sprayed the entire wing despite explicit instructions. The pilot attributed this error to the ground crew's lack of training on CSFF procedures and failure to follow flight crew directions.

synopsis: B757 Captain experiences a high frequency vibration during climb and initial cruise requiring three units of right rudder trim to level the wings. Later a 'Spoilers' EICAS message displayed. The crew and Dispatch are unable to locate landing performance data for this anonaly and the crew elects to divert to a longer runway.
summary: The flight crew experienced high-frequency vibration and a Spoilers EICAS message during climb, requiring right rudder trim. Due to unavailable landing distance data for the abnormality and limited runway length at the destination, they diverted to an airport with a longer runway to ensure a safe landing.

synopsis: EMB145 flight crew receives a LG AIR/GND FAIL EICAS message after rotation and the gear lever will not move to the up position. The Captain asks the First Officer to push the down lock release button and select the gear to the up position, which is successful and the LG AIR/GND FAIL message goes away. The crew later discovers that a QRH procedure exists for the gear handle will not move to the up position and that pushing the down lock release button is not part of it.
summary: The flight crew experienced a Landing Gear Air/Ground Fail EICAS message during climb, using the downlock release button to retract the gear. They later realized they incorrectly followed the Air/Ground Fail checklist instead of the Gear Lever Cannot Be Moved checklist, prompting a request to link these procedures in the QRH.

synopsis: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) questions how a Digital Flight Control System (DFCS) Test for a Dual Channel Mach Trim System could have passed with all four Mach Trim Circuit Breakers (C/Bs) 'Open' (pulled). The B737-700 flight crew returned to the gate after noticing the C/Bs were still pulled, even though a Mach Trim MEL had been signed-off.
summary: A mechanic performing a DFCS BIT check on a B737-700 with a Mach Trim MEL failure did not realize Mach Trim circuit breakers were pulled, though the system passed tests. The aircraft returned to the gate after the crew discovered the pulled and collared breakers, which the mechanic noted should have been listed in the MEL write-up.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot reports discovering after landing that he had been operating in a TFR. A 496 Garmin GPS with TFR information was in use during the flight and did not show the TFR.
summary: An ENG pilot flew a helicopter near a state border for a bank robbery flyover at 1,700 feet MSL without checking for Temporary Flight Restrictions (TFRs). The pilot later discovered an active TFR that was not displayed on the Garmin 496 GPS, prompting a commitment to manually verify TFRs before future flights.

synopsis: CE650 Captain reports exceeding 1,500 FT prior to WENTZ on the RUUDY 4 departure from TEB and exceeding 200 KTS below the Class B.
summary: The pilot departed TEB Runway 24 and inadvertently climbed through 1,800 feet into Newark Class B airspace while turning from WENTZ to TASCA. This occurred because the pilot misidentified the autopilot mode as 'ALT' instead of 'ASEL', causing the aircraft to continue climbing after the altitude preselect was changed to 2,000 feet.

synopsis: Local Controller described a confused go around and unsafe routing event, claiming the two supervisor's in the cab were not engaged to the developing problem and offered little assistance.
summary: A Local Control East controller managed a BE1900 departure and an A319 go-around while two distracted Flight Line Managers failed to coordinate. The resulting confusion caused a loss of separation, forcing the BE1900 to stop at 8,000 feet until the A319 turned westbound to resolve the conflict.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: D10 Controller expressed concern regarding the STARS equipment, providing examples of how the STARS functionalities can lead to an unsafe condition.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that STARS system failures prevented departing ARTS IIIE aircraft from auto-displaying to Dallas South and auto-handing off to DR1. This caused aircraft to appear as limited data blocks or disappear entirely, creating a serious safety risk during prearranged coordination climbs.

synopsis: D10 Controller described an unsafe condition involving the STARS equipment displaying 'ghost targets.' The reporter suggested a return to the ARTS III equipment until this anomaly can be corrected.
summary: An air traffic controller observed a "ghost target" on the STARS radar system while managing a Regional Jet climbing from 9,500 to 17,000 feet. The controller identified the target as a system error rather than actual traffic, noting that such false displays pose a significant safety risk by potentially triggering unnecessary evasive maneuvers.

synopsis: An Airbus Captain reported a fuselage marker beneath door 1L for Ramp Agent jetway parking guidance but continued inconsistent jetway parking adjacent the aircraft may lead to passenger injury during loading and deplaning.
summary: A pilot safety observer reported inconsistent jetway placements relative to new markings under Airbus 1L doors, noting variable gaps and step-downs. The reporter suspects this lack of standardization creates a fall hazard and questions the absence of Safety Management System oversight or proper agent training.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: CE525 Captain experiences a generator failure enroute on a ferry flight and is instructed to divert and pick up a replacement aircraft. During arrival the engine with the failed generator begins to vibrate and fails. The crew elects to divert to a nearby airport with a longer runway.
summary: The crew diverted after a right generator failure, then declared an emergency upon arrival due to right engine vibration, power loss, and smoke. The aircraft landed safely, was evacuated after liquid leakage was observed, and towed to the FBO with no fire detected.

synopsis: CE750 flight crew departing PHX Runway 25R on the MAXXO 2 departure report a conflict with an Airbus departing the same runway on the same departure just before the CE750 departure. The very different performance characteristics of the two aircraft resulted in a conflict at 9 DME during the turn to 140 degrees.
summary: A Boeing 757 crew missed a transponder switch to TA/RA due to a distraction, preventing an alert during a PHX departure behind an Airbus. The 757's faster climb caused a conflict when the Airbus turned into their path, forcing the 757 to climb to 8,300 feet to maintain 400 feet vertical separation.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reports that a large metal structure is being constructed off the approach end of Runway 10 at BWI that would increase the damage to an aircraft landing short of the runway.
summary: A pilot reported observing a massive metal structure under construction below the Runway 10 approach lights at BWI. The reporter expressed concern that this rigid structure could severely damage an aircraft if it descended below the glide slope, citing a past B747 incident at SFO where non-breakaway lights caused major damage.

synopsis: B747 flight crew reported departing with an MEL requiring the left outflow valve to be deactivated and secured in the closed position. During climb the left outflow valve was displayed in an un-commanded open position on the ECS page. Out of FL190 the cabin altitude is at 9,500 FT and climbing. An emergency descent is initiated and after discussion with the company, fuel is dumped down to landing weight and the flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: The crew of an aircraft with a deactivated left outflow valve experienced an uncommanded valve opening during climb, causing cabin altitude to exceed 10,000 feet. They descended to 8,000 feet, jettisoned fuel to reach maximum landing weight, and landed safely after coordinating with ATC and company.

synopsis: Two technicians and a Line Lead Mechanic describe how their local Airport Operations Department policy of allowing Ground equipment vehicles to park exceedingly close to aircraft parking lines and overhanging designated vehicle lanes, had contributed to the Left wingtip of their MD-82 aircraft striking a Ground vehicle during his taxi to a Terminal Gate.
summary: Three mechanics taxied an MD-82 from a cargo ramp spot to a gate due to a lack of tow personnel and time pressure. The left wingtip struck a parked panel truck during a right turn because the wing's arc traveled farther left than perceived and ground vehicles congested the area.

synopsis: GA5 pilot on an IFR flight had a partial communication failure, but heard clearance for an ILS approach and landed successfully. Pilot discovered that the radio problem was due to failure to engage the alternator on startup.
summary: The pilot experienced a total radio failure during an IFR approach due to a drained battery caused by starting the engine with the alternator switch off. After receiving a Coast Guard clearance and descending to 650 feet, the pilot landed safely using a portable GPS.

synopsis: BAE125 Captain reports a NMAC during visual approach to Runway 16R at VNY. A turboprop on right base was maneuvering to land on Runway 16L and passed over the BAE125 alarming the reporter and his passengers. The Tower had no comment.
summary: A pilot reported a near-midair collision risk while descending for a visual Runway 16R approach at VNY after being held high. A Piper Mirage or Malibu appeared on TCAS 300 feet above and passed close by, leaving passengers shaken, though the Tower appeared unaware of the proximity.

synopsis: King Air Captain experiences a left generator inoperative light on, that was followed by flickering of the PFD and MFD displays on both pilot and co-pilot sides. The Captain instructs the First Officer to lower the landing gear which apparently kills the entire electrical system. The electrical system is successfully reset and flight continues to destination.
summary: During initial climb, the pilot experienced fuel gauge discrepancies, generator failure, and display flickering, causing a temporary loss of electrical power and communication. After resetting the generators, power was restored, but the crew continued to destination despite temporary compass and PFD alignment issues.

synopsis: A PC-12 training flight at an uncontrolled airport experienced a critical near-miss while conducting a circling approach to a runway not favored by the existing wind conditions. No communication was heard from the opposing aircraft on the CTAF frequency until after the event.
summary: A flight instructor and upgrading pilot conducting a VFR circling approach at an uncontrolled airport executed a go-around to avoid a C172 on a collision course. The reporter attributed the near-miss to the other aircraft not monitoring the CTAF frequency and the quartering tailwind conditions.

synopsis: LR45 pilot reports exceeding 1,500 FT prior to WENTZ on the RUUDY 4 departure from TEB when the altitude alerter is changed from 2,000 FT to 1,500 with the autopilot engaged. The altitude is quickly corrected back to 1,500 FT from 1,700 FT.
summary: The pilot departed Teterboro on the RUUDY departure for Runway 24 and attempted to capture 1,500 feet at WENTZ. Despite disconnecting the autopilot and applying nose-down pressure, turbulence and a high climb rate caused the aircraft to overshoot to 1,700 feet before leveling.

synopsis: DA-42 instructor and student landed with minimum fuel after electing to bypass a planned fuel stop in order to return to departure airport on time.
summary: A flight instructor and student landed a Cessna 172 with minimum fuel after the instructor skipped a planned refueling stop to proceed direct. The instructor later discovered the fuel gauges were inaccurate, showing 3 gallons per tank while the aircraft actually contained only 1.4 gallons total.

synopsis: Noting a noise and vibration after takeoff, a DA20 instructor pilot declared an emergency and returned to base. Student pilot had left chocks hanging on boarding step.
summary: A student and instructor experienced severe vibration during a training flight because chocks hung on the pilot's side boarding step were striking the fuselage. The instructor declared an emergency and landed safely; post-flight inspection confirmed the chocks caused the noise and vibration, but no aircraft damage occurred.

synopsis: PA-28 pilot reports momentarily losing control of his aircraft during a hand flown ILS approach in turbulent IMC. A go-around is initiated and vectors to the RNAV approach the same runway are received to a successful landing. Fatigue and lack of pertinent Pireps were cited as contributing factors.
summary: The pilot hand-flying an ILS approach to Runway 2 at COU in turbulent IMC conditions experienced an uncommanded left bank and nose-down attitude 2.5 miles beyond the final fix. After regaining control and executing a missed approach, the pilot noted that unreported weather difficulties from a preceding King Air could have improved situational awareness.

synopsis: Pilot of a light single engine aircraft reported NMAC with a King Air in the Oshkosh pattern area. Reporter mentioned he would have appreciated a heads-up from ATC.
summary: A pilot conducting touch-and-goes on Runway 18 at Oshkosh had a close encounter with a King Air on Runway 9 base, estimated 100–300 yards apart. The pilot attributed the incident to high workload and fixation on Runway 9 traffic, while noting the single controller failed to issue traffic advisories despite the busy environment.

synopsis: BE-36 pilot reports losing control during a crosswind landing resulting in a runway excursion on the downwind side of the runway. No damage occurs and the aircraft is taxied to parking.
summary: The Pilot in Command of an aircraft landing on Runway XXL in 18-knot crosswinds veered off the left side into grass due to a strong gust and delayed go-around decision. The aircraft stopped on a taxiway 2,000 feet away with no damage, attributed to wind, late go-around, and possible premature rudder removal.

synopsis: PA-44 Maintenance Technician reports adjusting a nose gear down micro switch to correct an intermittent down indication on the previous flight. The right hand nose gear door linkage was disconnected to facilitate easier adjustment of the switch and not reattached, which resulted in a jammed nose gear on the next flight.
summary: A mechanic inspected a nose gear down light switch after a prior flight reported flickering, suspecting a missing linkage rod caused a bind. The aircraft landed safely, and the issue was resolved by adjusting the micro switch and reinstalling the rod, with the reporter attributing the incident to a missed final inspection.

synopsis: LAX Controller described a confused event when an automated departure run down to the TRACON failed because of an apparent 'dupe ID;' the reporter's corrective actions resulted in an arrival aircraft losing data block information.
summary: An air traffic controller at LAX lost the data tag for an inbound flight while attempting to resolve a duplicate call sign conflict with a departing B757-200. The controller mistakenly removed the arrival's control track, believing it had landed, which left the inbound aircraft airborne without an associated data tag.

synopsis: A80 Controller described an unsafe condition involving a 'special mission' aircraft transitioning the finals when full triple simultaneous approach procedures were being conducted.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported a close call between a B757-200 on visual approach to Runway 28 and a Cessna 206 photo mission aircraft at 4,500 feet. The controller attributed the conflict to misapplying visual separation with a wake turbulence aircraft and criticized the approval of VFR photo operations in the final approach airspace.

synopsis: ZOB Controller described a confused event when an air carrier was cleared for a visual approach to CKB, but started to line up with 4G7, the reporter noted an actual wrong airport landing occurred in the recent past.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored a CRJ-200 for a visual approach to Clarksburg (CKB), but the pilot descended rapidly and climbed back up after realizing they were aligned with nearby airport 4G7 instead. The controller noted that a landing at 4G7 would have been unsafe due to insufficient runway length for the aircraft.

synopsis: A321 Captain experiences a hard left turn as takeoff thrust is added. The takeoff is rejected and the aircraft is taxied back to the gate. Maintenance found one brake puck on the #3 wheel (right side) still engaged and dragging and they found heavy discoloration and high heat on the #2 brake assembly (left side).
summary: The pilot rejected takeoff after the aircraft pulled sharply left due to a dragging or locked #2 left brake, which caused a strong rubber odor and heavy discoloration. Maintenance confirmed the fault after the crew stopped on the pavement at 30 knots and returned to the gate.

synopsis: A CE-560EP crew was unable to fully extend the flaps during landing, declared an emergency, and diverted to another airport, landing safely. The First Officer deviated from Company Policy by moving the flap handle to the previously selected position when the flaps did not position to Flaps 15 setting, and the Captain (PF) did not immediately object to the unauthorized action.
summary: During the approach phase, the Pilot Flying and Pilot Monitoring experienced a hydraulic pressure light flash and stuck flaps after the PM moved the flap lever back to position 7. The crew diverted and declared an emergency, attributing the incident to the PM's unauthorized lever movement and the PF's delayed intervention due to fatigue.

synopsis: MD-83 Captain experiences a high oil temperature indication during descent. Reducing thrust to idle produces an immediate 90 degree temperature reduction and adding thrust returns the temperature to 199 degrees. An emergency is declared and the approach is conducted with the left engine at idle.
summary: The pilot reported a high left engine oil temperature while descending from FL220, which fluctuated with throttle changes. An emergency was declared to land with one engine at idle, resulting in an uneventful approach and landing.

synopsis: MD-82 pilot reports a pronounced roll when slats are extended, followed by the right hydraulic quantity going to zero. An emergency is declared and the crew is able to land normally with full flaps and slats.
summary: During arrival at 10,500 feet, slat extension caused a roll and right hydraulic quantity dropped near zero. The crew declared an emergency, completed the checklist, and landed safely with gear down and flaps 40 before maintenance inspected the aircraft.

synopsis: B737 flight crew experiences a ground conflict with another aircraft crossing left to right and the Captain stops abruptly injuring two flight attendants.
summary: The Captain abruptly stopped the aircraft during taxi out to avoid a crossing commuter aircraft, injuring two flight attendants who were moving with service carts. The flight returned to the gate where medical personnel removed the injured crew, and the reporter attributed the injuries to the attendants not being seated during taxi.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: During cruise flight at FL340 an MD-80 crew noticed that 2 circuit breakers had opened followed by an electrical burning smell. An emergency was declared followed by a landing at a diversionary airport.
summary: The pilot reported that at 34,000 feet, two circuit breakers popped and an electrical burning smell occurred due to malfunctioning forward cargo compartment heaters. An emergency was declared, resulting in a diversion and landing with no further issues.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain is informed of Lithium batteries loaded in lower forward cargo compartment, which only has Halon as the fire suppression agent and is not effective against Lithium battery fires.
summary: The reporter noted that 31 kg of lithium batteries were loaded in the lower forward cargo compartment, where Halon fire protection is ineffective against such fires. They recommended loading all lithium batteries on the main deck to utilize argon/foam systems for controlling thermal runaway.

synopsis: TRACON Controller providing OJT described a loss of separation event when a second departure turned inside the previous departure causing the conflict, the reporter acknowledging a failure to intercede in time.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller and Trainee managed a Falcon 2000 and Citation X departure where differing turn radii reduced separation to 1.84 NM and 400 FT. The Controller attributed the near-miss to delayed intervention during training, noting that immediate positive control and traffic alerts were required to maintain safety.

synopsis: MMU Controller described a TCAS RA event when traffic on a visual approach to MMU conflicted with VFR traffic likely operating in the vicinity of CDW, the reporter suggesting a work group be formed to address the issue.
summary: An IAI Gulfstream G200 on a visual approach to Runway 23 at MMU received a Resolution Advisory and climbed to 2,200 feet to avoid a C172 at 1,400 feet. The pilot attributed the conflict to inadequate traffic information exchange between MMU, N90, and CDW regarding VFR departures in the arrival path.

synopsis: ZMP Controller voiced concern regarding the inaccurate 'suffix' filing by corporate type aircraft with regard to RVSM equipment.
summary: A Learjet 45 checked into Kansas City Center at FL410 as negative RVSM with a /G suffix, despite a filed altitude of FL430. The controller climbed the aircraft to FL430 and corrected the suffix, noting that pilots often fail to notify controllers of negative RVSM status during climbs.

synopsis: SCT Controller was notified of a loss of separation that had been discovered during a post event review long after the fact, the reporter claiming the tools available to the Controller are not as precise as those used during the post event reviews.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a potential pilot deviation where an A320 on a non-RNAV departure from LAX Runway 25 appeared to turn north of its assigned heading before correcting. The controller attributed this to a possible procedural issue and recommended reviewing departure procedures to prevent future simultaneous departures or ensure turns are completed before handoff.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a conflict event when the facility manager, providing OJT, discouraged the use of assigned altitudes by VFR Tower controllers in Class D airspace.
summary: An Air Traffic Manager and Trainee at ZZZ Class D airport managed a Learjet 45 and Grumman AA5 merging on approach, triggering a collision alert. The Trainee issued a safe turn to the AA5, while the Manager's incorrect call sign and refusal to assign altitudes nearly caused a conflict with an AA1 on short final.

synopsis: Tower Controller voiced concern regarding the issuance of a runway crossing clearance through a third party.
summary: A ground controller refused a tractor's request to cross Runway 6 after the vehicle lost radio contact, despite pressure from the CIC and airport security to relay the clearance. The controller reported this practice as unsafe and requested a policy change requiring direct tower contact or an escorted crossing for all runway vehicles.

synopsis: Air carrier described an aborted take off when observing a truck entering the departure runway, the incident apparently a runway incursion by an airport vehicle.
summary: During takeoff on Runway XL, the crew aborted after a yellow pickup truck entered the runway from the left. The First Officer initiated the rejection, the Captain assumed control, and the aircraft stopped safely before the truck, which exited the runway.

synopsis: A319 Captain discovers low crew oxygen pressure during descent and elects to declare an emergency with ATC to expedite the descent. A normal landing ensues. Pressure had been normal during preflight.
summary: The crew discovered low crew oxygen (270 PSI) during descent and declared an emergency, descending to the Minimum Safe Altitude and then 10,000 feet per QRH guidance. The flight landed without incident after briefing passengers and deciding against obtaining emergency oxygen bottles due to proximity to the airport.

synopsis: Air carrier inbound to MEM assigned the Tammy 4 STAR encountered confusion with regard to the 'descend via' clearances issued by ATC.
summary: Pilots descending via the Tammy arrival into Memphis were cleared to 3,000 feet by one controller but questioned by the next for being below 4,000 feet. The pilot attributed the confusion to poor ATC clearances regarding the descent profile and frequency change.

synopsis: Two Boeing 777's, proceeding to the same destination and on the same and routing, were alerted to an impending mid-air collision by their respective TCAS RA's, and both aircraft followed their TCAS avoidance commands. Both aircraft had lost communications with ATC.
summary: Two B777s on the PIRA5 arrival into Sao Paulo lost ATC separation due to communication failure and identical GPS tracks, triggering a TCAS RA. The crew executed a climb to FL220 to avoid the trailing aircraft, later establishing contact with Approach after switching frequencies.

synopsis: A MD-82 First Officer rejected the takeoff at about 90 knots following two right engine compressor stalls and later the crew was told the engine would be replaced.
summary: The crew rejected takeoff on Runway 35R at 90 knots after hearing loud pops and suspecting a right engine compressor stall. The aircraft stopped safely with half the runway remaining, and the right engine was later replaced despite no visible damage found during inspection.

synopsis: A B-757 crew reported a rejected takeoff at 80 kts because of a +/_ 0.1 EPR fluctuation.
summary: The Pilot Flying and Pilot Monitoring experienced a left engine surge with +/- .1 EPR fluctuation between setting Standard Power and 80 KTS. The Captain rejected the takeoff at 80 KTS.

synopsis: Two Mechanics report about a repair procedure to a B767 Cabin Floor Beam that was originally approved by company Midnight Engineering, but later considered to be 'Out of Limits' by their Dayshift Engineering. An electrical harness for the Aft Galley Chiller had burned through the harness and damaged the floor beam at Fuselage Station (Sta.) 1562.
summary: A B767 in ZZZ hangar required floor beam repair after a chiller harness burned through the structure during troubleshooting. Engineering initially approved the repair as within limits, but later determined it was out of limits, causing the aircraft to be ferried for proper repair and resulting in a flight cancellation.

synopsis: BE58 pilot initially attributed airspeed and altitude indication anomalies to environmental effects, but upon further assessment concluded that a static leak inside the pressure vessel was more likely.
summary: The pilot experienced inaccurate airspeed and altitude indications during IMC climbs in a 58P due to suspected partial pitot ice blockage and a static leak following recent maintenance. Continuing two flights with this degraded equipment resulted in pilot error, leading to the aircraft being grounded for inspection.

synopsis: SR22 pilot reports turning on to a vehicle road at DFW after receiving clearance to taxi from spot 1 Juliet. Help from airport personnel is required to turn the aircraft around.
