summary: A pilot taxiing a general aviation aircraft at DFW mistakenly entered an unmarked road instead of Taxiway Juliet, causing the right main wheel to stick in the grass. Airport personnel assisted in pulling the aircraft out, and the pilot recommended adding signage to distinguish the road from taxiways.

synopsis: BE35 pilot cancelled IFR clearance prior to landing and subsequently had to get clearance for an approach to an alternate field. Pilot failed to see NOTAMS regarding runway restrictions at the destination airport.
summary: The pilot cancelled an IFR clearance prematurely while circling to land at an airport with two closed runways, forcing a missed approach due to deteriorating weather. The incident resulted from poor preflight planning, missed NOTAMs, and cancelling the clearance before landing.

synopsis: Transitioning to takeoff from a touch-and-go landing, C182RG pilot inadvertantly raised the gear handle. Aircraft settled onto the runway and skidded to a stop.
summary: The pilot inadvertently retracted the nose gear during a touch-and-go transition, causing the nose to settle on the runway and skid until the aircraft stopped. The incident resulted in no injuries or property damage, attributed to the pilot reaching for the gear lever instead of the throttle.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: Corporate departure from Runway 36L at NEW experienced a near miss from an unobserved and unreported target shortly after takeoff resulting in a climb above assigned altitude.
summary: A Cessna 525B pilot departing Runway 36L at New Orleans Lakefront received a TCAS II "Climb" Resolution Advisory at 1,500 FT MSL due to a target aircraft within 400 FT vertical separation. The pilot executed the climb to 2,200 FT, received a "clear of conflict" message, and descended back to the assigned 2,000 FT while notifying New Orleans Approach.

synopsis: A HS125-800A crew determined an airframe vibration was originating from the Number two engine so they declared an emergency, shut the engine down using the Engine Vibration Emergency Checklist and diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: The crew experienced sudden airframe vibration at FL400, suspecting the rear of the aircraft. After determining Engine 2 power changes affected the vibration tone, they declared an emergency, secured the engine, and completed a non-eventful single-engine landing.

synopsis: A C-172 instructor reported he and his student, the flying pilot, landed in gusty conditions and departed the runway after a 21 knot gust turned the aircraft but no damage was found after the aircraft was towed back to the runway.
summary: An instructor and student in a training aircraft rolled off the runway and down a hill during a gusty crosswind landing due to a sudden left gust while the student retracted flaps. The aircraft stopped in the grass without damage, and post-incident checks confirmed the throttle and systems were functioning normally.

synopsis: ZOA Controller described an unsafe airspace situation when coordination concerning MOA airspace was not briefed properly and unclear as to it's operational usage.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared an F-18 into the HUNTER MOA while managing overlapping military airspace with AV-8s and a stationary ALTRV. The controller attributed confusion regarding IFR clearances and separation to inadequate briefings, conflicting MOA boundaries, and the unauthorized use of a stationary ALTRV.

synopsis: ZBW Controller experienced a loud tone in his/her head set only to discover that an assigned frequency had been released to maintenance.
summary: An air traffic controller working R46 heard a tone on frequency 126.22, which was released to maintenance but incorrectly activated by the OMIC desk. The controller attributed the incident to miscommunication regarding the frequency status and recommended system updates to prevent future occurrences.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: TRACON Controller assigned an altitude below the MVA when vectoring to clear weather, the aircraft never actually descending below authorized altitudes.
summary: An air traffic controller assigned Aircraft X to FL50 while rerouting it north to avoid precipitation, failing to update the altitude for the new route's Minimum Vectoring Altitudes. The aircraft descended below the MVA before the controller issued a corrected altitude, an error attributed to fatigue during the final hour of the shift.

synopsis: Tower Controller voiced concern regarding Supervisory instructions not to issue a SFVR clearance when the airport was above VFR minima even though cloud clearance was apparently a factor.
summary: A Mooney pilot departed VFR after a Flight Line Manager instructed Local Control to revoke an SVFR clearance, causing the aircraft to fly closer than the required 500 feet from low clouds. The reporter attributes this to the FLM's lack of instruction on cloud clearance differences between VFR and SVFR flights.

synopsis: Tower Controller expressed concern regarding an Air Carriers questions during a go around instruction, the reporter noting these questions should be ask at a later time.
summary: Air Carrier X was instructed to go around on final after a following aircraft failed to timely confirm visual contact with a company aircraft. The pilot argued against the directive, prompting a reminder that compliance with safety instructions is mandatory and non-essential questions should wait.

synopsis: ZLC Controller described a loss of frequencies event when the military, coordinated to 'jam' GPS signals only, were also jamming radio communications.
summary: Air traffic controllers in ZLC, ZLA, and ZOA sectors experienced up to 10 minutes of lost communications due to military frequency jamming affecting 30 to 40 aircraft. The lack of a specific mission sheet for frequency jamming caused significant delays in resolution, prompting a recommendation for updated procedures.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports receiving a line check from an FAA Inspector that needs a refresher course in cockpit etiquette.
summary: A pilot reported that an FAA Inspector entered the cockpit without prior crew permission and later sat in the First Officer's seat during cruise, manipulating the yoke and thrust levers. This caused the autopilot to disengage and created a significant distraction, though the pilot re-engaged the system and the flight concluded normally.

synopsis: Air Carrier departure from LAS expressed concern regarding ATC's use of 'anticipated' separation on successive Air Carrier departure aircraft.
summary: The pilot refused a takeoff clearance from LAS Tower on Runway 25R because the preceding aircraft was still on the runway during its takeoff roll. The controller issued the clearance twice while the preceding jet was still accelerating, forcing the pilot to delay acknowledgment until the aircraft rotated to avoid a runway incursion.

synopsis: A pilot reports that in all the years he has flown for his air carrier, he has never experienced anything remotely as disorganized or troubling in terms of getting appropriate maintenance performed and correct maintenance documented on their merged air carrier's A319/320 aircraft. Lack of maintenance experience and training was apparent at certain Stations.
summary: A pilot at ZZZ intervened when a mechanic with limited A320 training incorrectly deactivated the #1 Flight Augmentation Computer instead of the #1 Yaw Dampener and issued a false maintenance release. The pilot halted the departure, corrected the deferral procedure, and ensured a proper release was issued before the delayed flight departed safely.

synopsis: A321 Captain notes that the requirement for the hill to be visible departing Runway's 28L/R on the CUIT4 from SFO has been deleted and replaced with a minimum climb gradient. His company issued airport briefing page does not discuss this issue and he does not believe his aircraft is capable of the climb rate required. The SFO9 is requested instead.
summary: The A321 crew declined the CUIT4 SID due to a procedural change substituting a minimum climb gradient for visibility requirements, which was not published on the airport advisory. They elected to fly the SFO9 SID straight out, as the aircraft likely could not meet the required gradient at 205,000 lbs with a turn.

synopsis: An EMB-135 electrical system began malfunctioning after takeoff and finally only STBY POWER was available so an emergency was declared and the flight diverted to an enroute airport for maintenance.
summary: The flight crew experienced a progressive electrical failure during climb, where Generator 2 overloaded and caused other generators to trip offline, eventually leaving the aircraft on standby power. They diverted to an airport, landed safely, and later confirmed Generator 2 was faulty while other generators were restored.

synopsis: A B-737-800 crew completed the QRH, declared an emergency and diverted after the FILTER BYPASS warning light alerted.
summary: The crew experienced a 'Fuel Bypass' warning light on the left engine during cruise. They followed the QRH, declared an emergency, diverted, and landed uneventfully before terminating the emergency with Tower.

synopsis: MD82 pilot reports loss of left hydraulic system fluid during arrival. Maintenance is consulted and a normal landing ensues.
summary: The crew experienced a complete loss of hydraulic fluid in the left system while in the terminal area. They executed the QRH, consulted maintenance, alerted ARFF, and landed the aircraft.

synopsis: A MD-11 LVL 1 'REV 2 PRESSURE FAULT' and a Red 'U/L' in the #2 N2 gauge alerted after takeoff and as the QRH was completed the crew prepared to return but the alerts extinguished so the crew continued to the filed destination.
summary: The flight crew experienced a Level 1 'REV 2 Pressure Fault' and a Red 'U/L' indication on the #2 engine N1 gauge during initial climb at 400-500 feet AGL. After returning to the departure airport, the alerts cleared at 11,000 feet, prompting the crew to safely continue to their filed destination.

synopsis: A B-737 crew reported a compressor stall at 600 FT after takeoff so they returned to the departure airport where Maintenance determined the cause was an engine malfunction and not a bird strike.
summary: During departure at 600 feet AFE, the crew experienced a loud bang and right yaw, followed by passenger reports of flames from engine 2. Although no instrument anomalies were detected, the crew returned for an overweight landing, and maintenance later determined the cause was likely a compressor stall.

synopsis: EMB-145XR crew had two sequential aborts at about 40 knots because of EICAS Caution of 'Rudder SYS1 INOP'. On the first abort the crew consulted the QRC and QRH, and then consulted Maintenance for guidance on procedures and log book entries. After the second takeoff attempt with the same warnings at about 40 knots, the crew decided to return to the gate and was issued another airplane.
summary: The crew aborted two takeoffs at 40 knots due to a Rudder SYS1 INOP EICAS caution. After a second identical failure, they returned to the gate for maintenance, resulting in an aircraft swap and a duty day exceeding 15 hours.

synopsis: A C-208B Captain reported a brake failure as she was attempting to hold short of a taxiway where prior entry permission was required as a result of frequency congestion could not communicate the aircraft's condition.
summary: The pilot experienced total brake failure while taxiing on Hotel Taxiway, causing an uncontrolled turn toward Charlie. After a communication breakdown with the Tower controller, the pilot regained control, returned to Apron 6, but was unable to report the brake failure before the incident concluded.

synopsis: A pilot reports about an A321 aircraft that somehow had been allowed to fly revenue flights between 15 and 30 days with an existing right-hand Outboard Brake not functioning and the Autobrakes on MEL. Replacing the Brake Steering Control Unit (BSCU) did not correct the discrepancy, deferral had continued. Concerns also raised about chronic major system faults not being fixed.
summary: The First Officer reported an A321 with a suspected inoperative right outboard brake flew multiple legs over 30 days despite recurring high temperatures on compensating brakes. Maintenance performed ineffective bleeding instead of grounding the aircraft, leading to a flight delay and the crew's concern that operational pressure compromised safety processes.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reports being confused by their taxi clearance and the Romeo taxi lines south of the west ramp at IAH.
summary: The crew misidentified taxiway RC as RB due to poor lighting and signage while taxiing for a 15L departure, causing a near collision with an A320 on WB. The incident resulted from confusing ramp markings, multiple radio frequencies, and the A320's failure to yield, highlighting the need for improved lighting and streamlined ATC procedures.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain detects an electrical burning smell during climb and elects to divert to a suitable airport. After some searching, a malfunctioning light socket in the galley is found and replaced allowing the flight to continue to destination.
summary: The flight crew diverted due to an electrical smell caused by a shorted galley light bulb socket that arced and produced smoke. Mechanics replaced the socket, allowing the flight to continue three hours late after ground inspections found no other abnormalities.

synopsis: An ERJ-170 crew noticed the Number 2 engine Amber EICAS High Temperature warning during cruise flight at FL350 and took the appropriate actions. The oil temperature continued to increase despite their efforts, and the engine was shut down per the emergency checklist. An Emergency was declared with ATC, and the flight diverted to a familiar airport. During the approach the crew received a 'FUEL 2 LO LEVEL' alert, but in the interest of safety continued and landed uneventfully.
summary: During cruise at FL350, the crew encountered a rapidly rising Engine 2 oil temperature, prompting a QRH-directed shutdown and emergency diversion. The aircraft landed safely on Runway 8 with a subsequent low fuel warning, and post-landing inspection revealed no visible engine damage.

synopsis: EMB-170 First Officer experiences high engine oil temperature shortly after level off in cruise. The QRH is consulted and the oil temperature is brought back to within limits. Flight continues to destination.
summary: The crew encountered a high #2 engine oil temperature indication at cruise altitude, which they resolved using the QRH checklist and continued to the destination. The reporter attributed the event to an unknown cause but identified ambiguous wording in the QRH and AOM regarding "abnormal parameters" and "transient" temperature limits as a safety concern.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew experiences smoke and sparks emanating from the transponder during descent. The transponder is turned off and the smoke begins to subside. An uneventful landing ensues.
summary: During descent from FL400, smoke and sparks emerged from the transponder panel, prompting the crew to turn the unit off, don oxygen masks, and request a high-speed direct descent to the IAF. The aircraft landed safely without declaring an emergency, though the pilot later noted that declaring one would have secured the necessary ATC support more effectively.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reports a left aft entry door light on at FL370. The cabin crew finds the door handle slightly raised and moves it to the closed position extinguishes the light. The door warning light returns and the handle is found slightly raised again and elects to divert for maintenance.
summary: While level at FL370, the AFT entry door light illuminated despite normal pressurization. Although cabin crew closed the slightly raised handle, it rose again, prompting a diversion per QRH procedures with dispatch concurrence.

synopsis: An MD-10 aircraft suffered a Hydraulic System Number 3 failure and subsequent autopilots disconnect, resulting in a 700 feet altitude deviation before the Captain regained control. The autopilot would not stay engaged, requiring the Captain to hand-fly the airplane. A slat disagree indication was overcome, [and] then the nose wheel failed to extend normally and was extended with the alternate system. The next challenge was Hydraulic System Number 2 High Temp indications followed by both pumps shutting down. After landing both hydraulic systems Number 2 and Number 3 returned to full pressure, but during taxi-in the aircraft was reported as slow to respond.
summary: The crew experienced a HYD 3 failure at FL380 causing autopilot disconnect and nose gear extension issues, requiring alternate gear extension. Subsequent HYD 2 overtemp alerts occurred during approach, but the aircraft landed safely with all systems recovering, though steering remained sluggish on the taxiway.

synopsis: While practicing instrument flying in VFR conditions, the pilot flying became disoriented and entered restricted airspace. When this was pointed out by ATC, the pilot exited the airspace but also descended 1,000 FT prior to becoming re-established at his cleared altitude.
summary: An IFR-rated pilot entered a restricted area and lost 1,000 feet of altitude while disoriented during a procedure turn in IMC. The controller vectored the aircraft for an ILS approach, resulting in a safe landing and the pilot's recognition of a need for additional training.

synopsis: Sport Cub instructor pilot reports his student losing control due to a wind gust during a wheel landing. The instructor cannot react quickly enough and the aircraft departs the runway with the right wing tip contacting the ground.
summary: During landing rollout, a wind shift caused the aircraft to veer and depart the runway, resulting in the right wing tip contacting the ground. A mechanic applied a temporary patch to the damaged wing tip, and the aircraft was returned to service.

synopsis: BE35 pilot landing reports a critical ground conflict with a C172 taking off in the opposite direction. The C172 pilot was hugging the runway edge allowing the two aircraft to pass unscathed. Numerous position reports had been made by the BE35 pilot on the CTAF with no response.
summary: A pilot flying an RNAV (GPS) 5 approach to Runway 5 landed and encountered a Cessna 172 taxiing in the opposite direction on the runway. The near-miss occurred because the Cessna pilot failed to transmit position reports or acknowledge the landing aircraft's four reports, despite both having operational radios.

synopsis: C182 pilot reports momentary loss of control when a parachute instructor and his tandem student exit the aircraft, apparently due to the drogue chute catching on the horizontal stabilizer.
summary: The pilot reported that after a skydiver exited at 8,500 feet, the aircraft entered an uncommanded nose-low turn due to a drogue chute damaging the horizontal stabilizer. The pilot declared an emergency, landed safely, and attributed the damage to the chute deploying early after being trapped beneath the flap lever.

synopsis: The C-172 pilot of record on an IFR flight plan failed to note his assistant pilot's course and altitude deviations until advised by ATC.
summary: A second instrument-rated pilot flying under the reporter's IFR plan deviated from assigned altitude and heading. Socal Air Traffic Control alerted the crew, prompting an immediate correction of the flight path.

synopsis: The pilot of a glider tow aircraft was informed that while he was landing an automobile was forced to apply the brakes while traveling along the road adjacent to the grass landing strip. His standard approach was observed by the Airport Manager and it was determined to be safe.
summary: A glider pilot on short final for a grass runway caused a car to brake when the tow rope alarmed the driver while crossing a road. The Airport Manager observed adequate clearance, but the pilot plans to raise the approach to 200 feet over the fence to increase safety margins.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Wilga 80 pilot reports exhausting fuel in one tank and being unable to restart the engine when fuel is switched to the remaining tank. An off airport landing is undertaken resulting in propeller damage.
summary: The pilot ran out of fuel in one tank and could not restart the engine after switching tanks, forcing a precautionary landing in a field. Insufficient flaring during the roundout caused the wooden propeller to strike the ground, delaminating one blade.

synopsis: An RV-6 pilot landed off airport because of fuel starvation after taking off with no fuel quantity indicated because previous experience told him he should have enough fuel to fly to a nearby airport.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine failure shortly after takeoff due to fuel exhaustion, despite gauges indicating sufficient fuel. The pilot successfully executed an off-airport landing on a highway with no damage, attributing the incident to relying on previous experience rather than visible fuel levels.

synopsis: Two different points of view involving a refused handoff event, both Center controllers believing their actions were appropriate.
summary: A CRJ-700 climbing to FL340 to avoid turbulence was vectored into the reporter's airspace by a Sector XY controller who refused to coordinate a descent to FL320. The reporter accepted the handoff only after OMIC intervention, citing the transferring controller's unprofessional refusal to comply with airspace requirements.

synopsis: D10 Controller described a 'Ghost Target' event while vectoring an aircraft to the ADS Airport. The reporter noted the STARS equipment should be shut down until the cause of these false targets can be fixed.
summary: An air traffic controller vectoring a King Air for an ILS approach at ADS Airport observed a false radar target with no altitude data crossing the airport. The controller held the King Air to monitor the ghost target, which disappeared after the aircraft crossed paths, causing significant distraction and prompting a request to shut down the system.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: D10 Controller described a 'Ghost Target' event while using the STARS system, the reporter noting continued events involving the STARS equipment.
summary: An air traffic controller at DFW Arrival 3 observed a "Ghost Target" at 6,000 feet with no data block between ILS approaches for runways 18R and 17C. The unidentified target, showing "flight not stored," traveled southbound at 540 knots before disappearing, prompting the controller to warn of potential collision risks and demand a system shutdown.

synopsis: A B737-700 flight crew reported an EGPWS Predictive Windshear Warning (PWS) while on short final for STL Runway 12L, but because daylight VMC conditions existed without convective activity, the approach was continued.
summary: During final approach to Runway 12L at STL, the crew received an erroneous PWS windshear warning at 500 feet AGL with no convective activity. The radar entered test mode five seconds later, but the Captain elected to land, and maintenance attributed the false warning to a known, unresolved issue at the airport.

synopsis: A B767 EICAS alerted ENG FUEL FILTER (L) at 800 feet after takeoff so after completing the QRH the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The 767 crew received an ENG FUEL FILTER (L) warning at 800 feet after liftoff from ZZZ. They completed the QRH procedure and elected to land back at the departure airport overweight.

synopsis: After a B737 landing gear was selected down both GREEN and RED indicator lights were ON and when TOO LOW GEAR warning sounded at 500 feet a go-around was executed. Upon returning for a second approach all indications were normal.
summary: The pilot and First Officer experienced a momentary gear warning horn and conflicting red/green gear lights while descending on final to Runway XXL. They executed a missed approach at 500 feet AGL, completed the Gear Disagree checklist, and landed normally on the second attempt without further warnings.

synopsis: An EMB-145 alerted MASTER CAUTION for MAIN PITCH TRIM INOP followed shortly by a BACKUP PITCH TRIM INOP so an emergency was declared and, while on a delay vector, the crew was able to restore the Backup Pitch Trim before the emergency landing. Maintenance determined the Main Pitch Trim fault was a computer fault, not mechanical in origin.
summary: During initial descent, the Captain received MAIN and BACKUP PITCH TRIM INOP warnings, declared an emergency, and landed using backup trim after QRH procedures. Maintenance later determined the issue was a computer problem, not a flight control malfunction.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician performing RII inspections describes his efforts to release a B767-300 aircraft after a B-Check and a damaged slat replacement. He failed to note a logbook entry by a Line Maintenance Supervisor that did not include his High Frequency Eddy Current (HFEC) inspection.
summary: A Maintenance Inspector discovered out-of-limits damage on a replacement B767-300 slat during a hangar inspection, halting installation. The aircraft was eventually released after the Inspector failed to identify incomplete documentation regarding the off-wing repair and HFEC inspection in the logbook.

synopsis: A pilot reported departing SBP Runway 15 with calm winds and having a near-miss with a fixed wing pilot departing Runway 33 who did not utilize CTAF communications procedures. Both pilots side stepped to avoid a collision.
summary: The reporter and a non-radio-equipped low-wing pilot departed SPB simultaneously on Runways 15 and 33 due to the other pilot's failure to use the calm wind runway or communicate. Both pilots executed evasive sidesteps, maintaining visual separation of approximately 250 feet before departing in opposite directions.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A Stinson V-77 pilot reported no injury or damage following a ground loop during landing. Maintenance examined the aircraft prior to departure the same day.
summary: The pilot of a Stinson experienced a ground loop on the runway and taxied to the end of runway 31C. An A&P mechanic inspected the aircraft at the FBO, found no damage, and the pilot departed the same day.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: An instructor observing his Student Pilot's first solo flight witnessed the student land on LGU Runway 28, then as the student back taxied on Runway 10 another aircraft land over his student's aircraft on Runway 28 which the student has partially exited.
summary: A student pilot on his first solo flight taxied back on Runway 28 while another aircraft was on short final. The second pilot descended to 10 feet above the student's tail before landing 700 feet down the runway, and both pilots steered away to avoid an accident.

synopsis: A Piaggio P180 took an apparent lightning strike on a propeller while IMC at FL360 and subsequently all EFIS data was lost. While troubleshooting, the aircraft entered a descending turn which the pilot arrested using his Standby Gyro, then diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: A pilot flying at FL360 in IMC experienced a total loss of EFIS and multifunction displays, likely due to turbulence, leading to an uncommanded steep descending turn. After recovering using a standby gyro, the pilot diverted and landed safely at ZZZ with one passenger.

synopsis: An Aircraft Inspector at a Contract Maintenance Repair Station reports that a sequence of Task Card steps had been broken due to a lack of proper tooling during installation of a V2500 Engine on a Customer's A320 aircraft. He missed a required step to verify the proper installation of a retainer assembly at the Forward Engine Mount.
summary: A QC Inspector at a repair station missed verifying the Retainer Assembly installation on an Airbus A320-200's V2500 engine due to a broken task card sequence requiring hoist removal. The error resulted from a standard station deviation and staffing constraints, prompting a process correction.

synopsis: Tower Controller described an emergency event that resulted in an unexpected runway entry by the emergency trucks.
summary: Air Traffic Control reported that Airport Operations and ARFF vehicles entered Runway XX without clearance to follow a Dash 8-400 landing with a blown tire. The controller criticized the unsafe practice of closing the runway while the aircraft was still rolling out at 100 knots without prior coordination.

synopsis: A B737-300's right wing Leading Edge Transit Lights did not extinguish after takeoff, but because of normal flight control feel, the flight continued to its destination with the 300KTS/.65 Mach constraint. The flight did exceed the FL200 constrain for a period of time before descending to FL190.
summary: During initial climbout, the flight crew failed to observe a 20,000-foot altitude restriction in the QRH for unretracted right wing leading edge flaps, climbing to FL270 before realizing the error. They descended to FL190 after recognizing the oversight, attributing the incident to focusing on airspeed limits while neglecting the altitude limitation.

synopsis: A B767 right engine developed a compressor stall at rotation but continued to operate normally, so the flight returned to the departure airport for an overweight landing.
summary: During takeoff rotation, the right engine experienced a compressor stall. The crew continued the takeoff and returned to ZZZ for an overweight landing.

synopsis: Following an APU air start before landing, an EMB-145 APU Fire Warning alerted with the APU RPM hung at 55%, so an emergency was declared, the warning ceased when the QRH was completed and after landing no sign of a fire was found.
summary: The flight crew experienced an APU fire warning during the final approach to ZZZ after the APU hung at 55% while starting. They executed the QRH checklist, declared an emergency, landed normally with Fire and Rescue standing by, and taxied to the gate after a negative fire inspection.

synopsis: An ERJ-170 engine oil temperature was detected in the amber range and after completing the QRH the temperature remained high so the engine was shutdown, an emergency declared and the flight diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: The crew experienced a rising oil temperature in the amber range during cruise, prompting an engine shutdown per QRH. They declared an emergency, diverted, and landed safely with no external damage observed by emergency vehicles.

synopsis: A B737-800 Flap Asymmetry Fault activated at flaps 1 selection so an emergency was declared and the flight diverted a nearby airport for an uneventful no flaps landing. The event was this aircraft's seventh such event.
summary: The Captain and First Officer declared an emergency during the approach phase due to a split flap and flap disagreement, despite normal overhead panel indications. They diverted to an alternate airport for a safe landing, later discovering maintenance had seven prior undocumented flight control write-ups.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 CAS alerted ANTI-ICE DUCT so the crew completed the QRH and closed the 14th stage bleed before returning to the airport for maintenance because of nearby icing and thunderstorms.
summary: The crew experienced an Anti-Ice duct warning and thrust reverser arming failure during climb and final approach due to an incomplete QRH and insufficient ground maintenance. They diverted to the departure airport, applied a malfunction procedure, and landed safely while managing nuisance warnings and weather avoidance.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 205 lost engine power on base leg during a VFR approach to an uncontrolled airport, attempts to restart the engine using failed. The aircraft was landed power-off and tail-low, resulting in a tail strike with the runway. After refueling the aircraft the engine started and ran normally. Fuel usage had been calculated using the aircraft electronic fuel totalizer, providing the pilot with the assumption that at least 8 gallons remained onboard.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine power loss on base leg due to fuel exhaustion despite calculating sufficient fuel based on the electronic totalizer. The aircraft sustained cosmetic tail damage during a forced landing, but the engine restarted after refueling, confirming the tanks held approximately nine gallons.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot on short final to CTAF CBE Runway 23 executed a go-around after a near miss with an aircraft whose pilot failed to employ recommended CTAF communications reporting.
summary: A pilot practicing touch-and-goes at CBE initiated a go-around after spotting a Cessna 200 feet below and left on final to Runway 23. The other pilot apologized for being on the wrong frequency, and the reporter attributed the near-miss to a missed visual scan and lack of radio monitoring.

synopsis: A80 Controller described a go-around event at 4A7 after clearing an arrival for a visual approach, the reporter acknowledging the SAIDS was listing the subject closed.
summary: An air traffic controller accepted a Turbo Commander 690 handoff for a visual approach to 4A7, but the pilot later reported the airport was closed due to a runway closure listed on SAIDS. The controller issued a clearance to FFC, and the pilot landed without incident, though the controller noted a failure to verify NOTAMs.

synopsis: ZDC Controller described a near airspace infraction when a ZNY Controller had incorrectly advised a pilot of the status of R4001.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored a Piper PA-31 away from active restricted area R4001 after the pilot, relying on incorrect inactive status from a neighboring controller, entered the airspace. The incident highlighted a critical error in the restricted area activation process where the neighboring facility's status board incorrectly displayed R4001 as inactive.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ZMP Controller described a holding event for ORD claiming that holding in ZAU's airspace much closer to ORD was more reasonable.
summary: An air traffic controller reported holding aircraft 300 miles from ORD while ZAU had an unused sector 200 miles closer, causing one aircraft to divert due to fuel. The controller attributed the issue to ZAU not opening all sectors and Command Center policy denying assistance unless all sectors were active.

synopsis: An A319 crew was alerted by ECAM to a flap extension fault during a visual approach when the flaps locked in position between 1 and 2. Following procedure, recycling the flap handle did not correct the problem, a go-around was initiated, an emergency was declared, and the aircraft returned to land uneventfully.
summary: During a VFR approach, flaps locked between positions 1 and 2, triggering an FCTL ECAM fault. After a go-around and emergency declaration, the crew stabilized at 9,000 feet and completed an uneventful landing with flaps left in position 3.

synopsis: A319 flight crew receives a confusing PDC which they interpret incorrectly and insert the wrong SID in the FMGC. This is quickly straightened out after departure with no appreciable track deviation.
summary: Pilots reported confusion after a PDC listed the BUNZZ 2 route but remarked "CAPITAL 8 DEPARTURE," causing them to load the wrong procedure. Although no deviation occurred, the conflict forced a high-workload FMGC reprogramming shortly after takeoff when cleared direct to TIICE.

synopsis: A319 Captain reports being dispatched with an MEL for a root fillet fairing which states the flight control position indicator in the cockpit was unreliable and contained a long and potentially dangerous preflight check.
summary: The pilot discovered a discrepancy between the flight plan's MEL item for a root fillet fairing and a more critical, unlisted MEL item regarding an unreliable flight control position indicator. The reporter concluded the aircraft should not have been in service for three days due to this dangerous oversight.

synopsis: A319 Captain experiences stuck flaps between position 1 and 2 during approach and goes around. QRH procedures are complied with expeditiously due to a low fuel situation and a partial flap landing ensues.
summary: During a visual approach, the crew experienced a trailing edge flap extension failure between positions 1 and 2, triggering an ECAM and go-around. Compounded by minimum fuel from weather deviations, they rushed checklists and landed safely at high speed with partial flaps, arriving with 3,500 LBS of fuel.

synopsis: B767-300 flight crew experiences a LE Slat ASYM EICAS message while selecting flaps 25 during appraoach. A go around is initiated and QRH procedures are complied with before returning for landing.
summary: The flight crew received a Leading Edge Slat Asymmetric EICAS message while selecting flaps 25 on final approach. They executed a missed approach, completed the emergency checklist, and landed the aircraft without incident.

synopsis: A B767 Flight Attendant called the flight station to report four of the six flight attendants were ill and lightheaded, so the Captain diverted and the aircraft was met by parametics. The flight was canceled and the crew flew the aircraft home empty.
summary: While cruising at FL360, four flight attendants became lightheaded and sleepy, prompting the flight crew to divert for an overweight landing. A passenger doctor suspected odorless CO2 exposure, leading to the crew's recovery and the aircraft's ferry return after maintenance inspections.

synopsis: A330-200 Captain experiences an engine failure leveling at FL360. An emergency is declared and flight returns to departure airport after dumping fuel.
summary: The crew experienced a Number 1 engine failure at FL360, indicated by zero EPR, oil pressure, and N3 readings. They declared an emergency, performed fuel dumping and checklists, and executed a successful single-engine landing.

synopsis: Corporate jet departing VNY Runway 16R issued a Newhall 8 SID with a left turn experienced a TCAS RA, the reporter suggesting that due to the airspace involved, the NEWHALL SID should be modified.
summary: The Citation Excel pilot encountered a TCAS TA during the NEWHALL 8 departure from VNY 16R while turning left to 110 degrees below 1,700 feet. The pilot attributes the conflict to the departure's heading clashing with LAX airspace and recommends discontinuing the left turn to prevent future TCAS alerts.

synopsis: An air carrier flight crew utilized Captain emergency authority to complete the approach and landed without a clearance at SVMC when the Tower did not respond on the published frequency. After landing he learned that they have been using an unpublished and not NOTAMed Frequency 118.9.
summary: The flight crew landed safely without clearance at Maracaibo after losing radio contact with Tower and Approach due to the tower using an unpublished frequency (118.9). The crew exercised emergency authority following a delayed handoff and inability to raise any published frequencies.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew misunderstands a taxi clearance at MSY and believes that Taxiway E turns into Taxiway D, when in fact D is the diagonal, due to the location of the D near Taxiway E on the airport diagram. An electronic display of the airport diagram was being used for taxi and the assumed route had been highlighted.
summary: The flight crew misread the airport diagram at MSY during taxi out, confusing a labeled 'D' on Taxiway E with the actual Taxiway D. Ground Control detected the error and issued a re-clearance, prompting the crew to recommend a chart fix and hotspot note.

synopsis: C340 pilot on an IFR flight requested lower altitude to avoid icing conditions, but did not receive immediate clearance to descend. After noting ice on the prop spinners, the pilot advised ATC and was given clearance to descend.
summary: A pilot flying an IFR flight at 15,000 feet encountered light icing after entering clouds while awaiting a descent clearance. The pilot reported the conditions to ATC, received a descent to 11,000 feet above freezing, and landed safely, noting that earlier or firmer requests could have prevented the incident.

synopsis: A DA20 instructor pilot and his student in the traffic pattern experienced an NMAC with a Piper Seneca that had taken off after them but passed overhead 100 FT while on downwind.
summary: A Piper Seneca departed and turned early south, passing 100 feet above the reporting aircraft on right downwind for Runway 13. The pilot pitched down to avoid collision, noting Tower provided no alert despite the conflict, claiming radar showed the Piper passing behind.

synopsis: ZOB Controller described a conflict event between VFR traffic and a military aircraft operating in the BAX ALTREV, the reporter noting his concern regarding military operations in the subject airspace.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported a near-midair collision between a Cessna 421 and an A-10 at 3,000 feet near BAX Airport while the A-10 operated VFR in IMC within a stationary ALTREV. The controller attributed the unsafe proximity to the A-10's failure to monitor frequencies and the vague rules of the ALTREV, which allowed reckless maneuvers near the approach corridor.

synopsis: ZBW Controller described an unsafe condition when traffic being transferred to his/her frequency contained inaccurate data block information activating a false 'Conflict Alert'.
summary: A transferring controller failed to update the data block or verbally inform the receiving controller that a B737-700 was stopped at FL230 instead of descending to FL190. This caused a Conflict Alert with an ERJ175 climbing to FL230, which the reporter attributes to unsafe pre-loading of data blocks.

synopsis: B757 Captain experiences a left AC bus failure at rotation. A great deal of air conditioning fog is present and initially concerning but begins to dissipate. An emergency is declared, the AC bus is restored and the crew diverts to a suitable airport.
summary: The crew experienced a left AC bus failure and cockpit fog at rotation, prompting an emergency return. They determined the fog was likely A/C condensation, restored power, and executed an uneventful overweight landing despite an inoperative flap gauge.

synopsis: An A300 returned to their departure gate when the flight crew noticed smoke and odors during initial taxi. No report of findings.
summary: The flight crew and a jump seater detected smoke and a strong odor in the cockpit and supernumerary area shortly after engine start and during taxi. After shutting down the aircraft, fire services assisted, and the crew exited normally following a clearance to return to the gate.

synopsis: Dispatcher is informed of a diversion by one of his flights due to a smoke indication in the cargo compartment but failed to send the crew a message that the flight plan had been amended as required by current policy.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a flight diverting to ZZZ due to a cargo smoke indication and emergency declaration. The controller failed to send a message confirming the amended flight plan, noting that previous system behavior had implicitly notified the crew.

synopsis: During initial climb the Captain of a CL600-2D24 triggered the GPWS system with an unnoticed 1,000 FT FPM descent at 250 KTS. The aircraft had reached 1,000 FT AGL and the First Officer had begun reconfiguring the aircraft for climb when he noticed the deviation and notified the pilot flying just as the GPWS activated. The condition was then immediately corrected and a normal climb profile established.
summary: During a hand-flown RNAV departure in IMC, the Captain lowered the nose to accelerate, causing a descent that triggered a GPWS "Don't Sink" warning. The First Officer attributed the incident to the Captain's failure to scan instruments while rushing to reach 250 KTS and recommended requiring autopilot use for such departures.

synopsis: A Captain and First Officer report about multiple write-ups and Maintenance sign-offs for speed tape that required several re-applications on the Right Engine cowl of a CRJ-200 aircraft. The First Officer noted the speed tape could have been ingested causing issues with engine performance or operation, including the Cowl Anti-Icing System.
summary: Flight crew on a CRJ-200 reported recurring peeling of speed tape on the right engine cowl, which an FAA inspector noted may have been ingested. The crew also logged an obscured registration certificate, attributing these issues to inadequate temporary repairs and rushed preflight checks.

aircraft: Cessna Twin Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Light Twin Captain reports a B767 under tow passing in front of his aircraft close enough that the wing passes overhead, alarming passengers. The taxi clearance is then misunderstood requiring a 180 degree turn to get back on the cleared route.
summary: The pilot landed at BOS on Runway 4L and stopped on Taxiway Quebec while waiting for ground clearance. A B767 under tow passed over the pilot's wing without contact, and the pilot later admitted to taking a wrong taxi route due to rushing.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Captain briefed the taxi procedure from the DEN Freight Ramp to the runways including the A hold point, but did not see the hold point on the taxiway and suggested a better chart depiction.
summary: The flight crew missed the A hold point while taxiing out from DEN behind traffic, expecting it further up the taxiway based on ramp pages. The crew contacted Ground without issue and continued the flight, noting the ramp pages poorly depicted the hold point's actual location.

synopsis: After accomplishing a company Engineering Order (E/O) for the installation of an improved lower hinge assembly on the flight deck door of multiple ERJ-170 aircraft, an Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) realizes he had misinterpreted one of the maintenance steps and failed to install a required roll pin.
summary: A mechanic performing an Engineering Order on three ERJ-170s in the hangar may have incorrectly installed a roll pin on the flight deck door hinge due to confusing part nomenclature. This error potentially left the door insecure and the Airworthiness Directive non-compliant, prompting a recommendation to inspect and correct the installation immediately.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A pilot landed on ACT Runway 14 and after missing Taxiway B-3 entered the area beyond the runway's end where he was given a 180 degree turn to Taxiway B-3 and advised of a runway incursion in the non-movement area.
summary: Pilots taxiing a landing aircraft at Waco Airport on Runway 14 inadvertently entered the non-movement overrun area due to unclear signage and charting. This resulted in a reported runway incursion violation, despite the crew stopping before crossing adjacent Runway 19 and complying with subsequent controller instructions.

synopsis: ZMP Controller described an equipment issue when no information was available via the ERAM on an aircraft arriving from Canadian airspace, the reporter suggesting more same type functionalities between US and Canadian equipment.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller at ZMP received an Air Carrier X aircraft from ZWG without a flight plan in ERAM, delaying data entry for 40-50 NM due to the international plan's length. The controller noted this routine lack of data may stem from non-standard remarks and recommended improved system functionality or earlier notification from NAVCANADA.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described an unsafe event when visual separation advisories were not applied correctly by an adjacent controller.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller intervened when a BE35 overtook a PA-28 at the same altitude after the transferring controller incorrectly reported visual contact. The controller issued avoidance vectors because neither pilot had the other in sight, resolving the unsafe proximity before the aircraft resumed navigation.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a near loss of separation event when assuming climbing traffic had reported an 'expected' altitude but in fact stated a different altitude.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller in ZZZ Center Sector 29 misheard Aircraft X's check-on altitude as FL190 instead of FL180 due to expectation bias. The controller prematurely cleared the aircraft to FL290, creating a potential separation conflict with another aircraft at FL190 before correcting the climb to FL180.

synopsis: ZLC Controller voiced concern regarding variances in the MIA's between ZLC and ZLA, the reporter suggesting a national standard be adopted to prevent this type of confusion.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported a false Minimum Safe Altitude Warning (MSAW) alert for a Cessna 182 level at 140 feet in ZLA airspace. The alert triggered at 148 feet due to incorrect polygon display settings, despite the actual Minimum IFR Altitude being 125 feet.

synopsis: ZTL Controller described a conflict event between an IFR departure and VFR traffic occurring shortly after a handoff was received from BHM TRACON. The reporter believes the TRACON Controller was remiss in not provided better traffic advisories.
summary: The R-Side Controller managed a B737-800 departing Birmingham that nearly merged with a VFR aircraft squawking 1200 at unverified altitude 096. The pilot criticized the late traffic warning and unverified altitude, while the controller attributed the unsafe situation to insufficient coordination by Birmingham Approach.

synopsis: TPA Controller described an unsafe condition with regard to the parachute operations conducted at X49 and the potential conflicts with other VFR/IFR traffic, noting more accurate reports from the jump aircraft is imperative.
summary: An ATC controller managed a C182 parachute operation and an SR22 IFR flight near South Lakeland Airport. The C182 pilot falsely reported "2 minutes prior to jump," causing a delay that placed the SR22 dangerously close to the jump zone, highlighting a recurring issue with inaccurate jump timing reports.

synopsis: A320 flight crew experiences a Green Hydraulic System failure due to fluid loss climbing through FL180. Crew elects to divert to a suitable airport and lands normally after gravity extending the landing gear.
summary: During climb out through FL180, the crew experienced a complete loss of green hydraulic fluid, resulting in lost nose wheel steering, reverser one, and green brakes. The Captain diverted, declared an emergency, and performed an overweight landing with alternate gear extension, exiting via the high-speed taxiway before being towed in.

synopsis: The Dispatcher's first three releases were in error due to automatic modification made by the computerized dispatch system.
summary: A dispatcher reported that a computer likely autocalculated a flight to SFO twice, altering the optimized route and removing the SJC alternate. The dispatcher corrected the error after the Captain noticed the discrepancy, preventing an illegal and potentially dangerous release.

synopsis: Dispatcher reports that his dispatch computer does not alert in a timely manner when flight delays will cause two aircraft with the same flight number to be in the same airspace.
summary: The pilot of outbound flight 123 reported that Dispatch View failed to alert them of a conflicting inbound flight 123 until four minutes prior to arrival. This system error created a risk of two identical callsigns operating simultaneously in sterile cockpit conditions, requiring manual coordination to ensure safety.

synopsis: Another Dispatcher report describing deficiencies in their new and improved dispatch computer programs.
summary: The Captain and Dispatcher identified a contradiction in the Sabre flight plan where page one stated M1 cleared terrain, but page five stated it did not. They verified the error, confirmed M1 cleared terrain, and departed without issuing a new flight plan.

synopsis: Q400 flight crew experiences a tire failure during takeoff and elects to continue to destination for landing. A normal landing ensues with a tow to the gate.
summary: The flight crew experienced significant vibration during takeoff rotation caused by a blown right main tire and suspected gear door damage. They declared an emergency, burned fuel, performed an alternate gear extension, and landed safely on the runway for a tow to the gate.

synopsis: CRJ200 flight crew reports being cleared to line up and wait on Runway 27R at ATL, then noting an 'EFIS COMP MON' caution message....and 3 red flags on Captain's PFD. The crew taxies clear of the runway and the problem disappears. The next attempt at takeoff is successful. The Captain believes the rebar in the new runway extension is causing interference with the aircraft compass system [AHRS].
summary: The flight crew held on Runway 27R at Atlanta when rebar in the new runway addition caused an EFIS COMP MON caution and red flags on the Captain's PFD. They exited the runway without advancing thrust for takeoff, the fault cleared, and they departed shortly after without further abnormalities.

synopsis: DHC-8-300 Captain notes a small amount of smoke coming from the First Officer's windshield heat terminal and turns it off. No other problems are reported.
summary: During descent, the flight crew observed smoke from the First Officer's windshield heat terminal. The Captain turned the heat off, stopping the smoke within five seconds with no further overheating indications.

synopsis: G-200 Captain reports confusion and questionable ATC practices during arrival and approach to TNCM.
summary: The flight crew and a single Juliana ATC controller managing multiple positions experienced confusion during the approach to Princess Juliana International due to non-standard 15 DME arc instructions and last-minute clearance changes. The crew safely landed after manually correcting course deviations and managing conflicting altitude and vector instructions without published procedure support.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reports that the CLT 1 SID is poorly depicted and greatly confusing to crews that are not familiar with it. The 1.6 DME turn when departing runway 18C is depicted on the north side of the VOR and it should be on the south side. The FMC also appears to initiate the turn early. (Corrected in the June chart revision).
summary: The flight crew departed CLT on Runway 18C and executed an early turn to 200 degrees based on incorrect FMS coding and chart graphics. Investigation revealed the procedure requires a turn south of the CLT VOR, though no ATC concern or traffic conflict occurred.

synopsis: BAE125 Captain reports confusion over the altitude to be maintained initially on the missed approach from the ILS 19 at TEB. The flying First Officer believes the climb is to 3,000 feet but the Captain helps him return to 1,500 feet.
summary: The crew executed a missed approach on ILS 19 at TEB due to low weather, inadvertently climbing above 1,500 feet before TROVA due to ambiguous missed approach instructions. High workload, unforecasted weather, and a low-time First Officer contributed to the deviation, which was corrected after ATC issued a climb to 2,000 feet.

synopsis: A300 First Officer reports a sudden pitch over passing an airspace fix on a STAR, causing the speed to increase to 230 knots from 210 knots. Other A300 crews have reported similar anomalies at the same location.
summary: During an arrival into ZZZ, an Airbus crew reported an abrupt nose-down pitch and speed increase to 230 knots at 9,100 feet while in Profile mode. The pilot corrected the speed using Level Change, noting the cause was unknown but similar events had been reported by other crews at this location.

synopsis: An A300 flight crew followed their ECAM procedures, declared and emergency and diverted following a loss of fluid in the green hydraulic system.
summary: The flight crew experienced fluctuating green hydraulic quantity indications and low ECAM warnings during cruise at FL360. They diverted to a nearby airport, declared an emergency, and landed normally before being towed to the gate by maintenance.

synopsis: A320 flight crew on climbout passing FL260 reports receiving ECAM for COMPRESSOR VANE ENGINE 2. The company wants the crew to continue to destination, then on to maintenance. The Captain declined and the crew diverted to a suitable alternate. During descent the engine compressor stalls and the engine is shut down. A single engine landing ensues.
summary: During climbout past FL260, the crew received an Engine 2 Compressor Vane ECAM and diverted to ZZZ. Upon descent with thrust levers near idle, a compressor stall occurred, forcing an Engine 2 shutdown and emergency declaration, followed by an uneventful landing and inspection.

synopsis: When vectored to a short final for the ILS 18R at DFW, restricted to not below 250 Knots by Approach Control, the flight crew of a CRJ-200 opted to ignore an EGPWS terrain warning as they were leveling at the FAF altitude less than five miles from the fix. The warning went away promptly as they leveled and the approach was successfully completed.
summary: The pilot reported an EGPWS terrain warning during a tight ATC vector to 2,400 feet for the ILS 18R approach, caused by a high descent rate and proximity to a nearby tower. The crew identified the alert as a nuisance event and continued the approach without deviation.

synopsis: EMB170 First Officer reports EICAS messages for BRK LH Fault and BRK RH Fault when the gear is extended during approach. A go around is initiated, the QRH is consulted and a normal landing ensues after declaring an emergency.
summary: The pilot monitoring reported brake fault EICAS messages during a visual approach, prompting a go-around and emergency declaration. After completing the QRH and coordinating with maintenance, the crew landed safely on the long runway with crash/fire/rescue standing by and taxied to the gate.

synopsis: An air carrier flight, eastbound over the Pacific Ocean, suffered a single IRS failure and eventual loss of the Captain's flight instruments. The flight continued utilizing the First Officer's instruments and IRS data.
summary: During cruise, the crew managed a left IRS navigation error and subsequent failure that caused Captain's instrument loss. After declaring an emergency and receiving radar vectors, they restored instrumentation via checklist and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reports confusion departing CLT on the CLT1 departure, with the chart depicting a turn at 1.6 DME north of the VOR and the text indicating a turn to 200 degrees 1.6 DME south when departing Runway 18C.
summary: The flight crew departed runway 18C on the Charlotte One departure and turned to heading 200 at 600 feet, believing the chart depicted the turn before the CLT VOR. A manager later confirmed the turn should have occurred 1.6 miles after the VOR, meaning the crew turned too soon due to a confusing chart depiction.

synopsis: After deferring the boost pump for the right engine, the flight crew of a BAE-125 experienced an inflight shutdown of the engine, which they subsequently restarted. They later discovered they had been unaware of the second page of the AML deferral procedure which directed opening the crossfeed valve, which they had failed to do.
summary: During an enroute reposition flight, the crew experienced a right engine failure after unintentionally missing a second page of the MEL procedure for a deferred fuel boost pump. The engine was successfully restarted following an emergency declaration, though the crew attributed the incident to incomplete maintenance logbook review under time pressure.

synopsis: Air carrier pilot reports difficulty downloading his weekly EFB update and later requires the use of paper charts due to the corrupted database.
summary: Pilots experienced Electronic Flight Bag software corruption at MIA, leaving no chart database available for departure. The crew borrowed paper charts to fly, suspecting server or data issues caused the failed updates and highlighting a lack of backup plans for widespread corruption.

synopsis: A300 Captain reports inability to control airspeed/thrust via MCP during approach. Vectors off the approach course are requested and after several minutes MCP operation returns to normal.
summary: The pilot reported that during final approach, the aircraft's airspeed remained locked at 250 knots because the speed/mach control knob would not move from the preselected setting. After executing a left 360 to manually slow the aircraft, speed control was restored after three minutes, allowing for a normal landing.

synopsis: An MD-11 flight crew, cleared via the Molokai SID from PHNL from Runway 8R, was chastised by ATC for not turning right to 140 degrees in a timely fashion despite completing the turn prior to the HNL 3.6 DME as charted.
summary: The Captain flying a Runway 8R departure at HNL followed the Molokai Four SID by turning right within 3.6 DME, but ATC questioned the lack of an immediate turn. The pilot attributed the confusion to ambiguous chart wording and PDC phrasing regarding when the turn must commence.

synopsis: An A320 flight crew refused their aircraft and canceled the flight when fuel gauge discrepancies occurred followed by the discovery of significant amounts of water in the fuel.
summary: The crew and maintenance personnel encountered a 2,000-pound fuel gauge discrepancy on the left inboard tank during the Before Start Checklist. Water contamination and a faulty fuel processor caused the error, leading to a Class 2 navigation refusal after maintenance failed to resolve the issue.

synopsis: B777 flight crew describes the crew actions after several bird strikes at 500 FT AGL on departure. An EGT over temperature is noted initially and the crew elects to return to the departure airport. Fuel is dumped but approaching weather leads the crew to terminate that process and land overweight.
summary: The flight crew encountered a bird strike shortly after takeoff, causing a right engine EGT over-temperature indication. They declared an emergency, diverted, and performed an overweight landing with the right engine shut down for inspection.

synopsis: Boeing 737-700 crew, level at FL400, entered holding instructions into FMC and when 'ENTER' was activated the airspeed bug decreased to 206 knots and the engines rolled back to flight idle. Engines were slow to respond to the pilot's manual throttle movement, and did not fully recover to 'normal' operation until FL380-370.
summary: At FL400, the First Officer entered holding instructions, causing autothrottles to idle and airspeed to decay despite throttle advances. The crew descended immediately as engines remained at 40-50% N1 until passing FL370, after which they recovered and operated normally.

synopsis: When cleared off the Mount Vernon visual to circle to land on Runway 33 the flight crew of a commercial fixed wing aircraft suffered a NMAC with helicopter that had been directed to make a right 360 to clear the approach path.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway 33 at Washington National, a helicopter turned into the jet's flight path despite Tower instructions to maintain visual separation. The pilot executed a missed approach with a climbing right turn to avoid a collision, estimating the helicopter was only a few hundred feet away.

synopsis: CRJ-700 Captain experiences a nose wheel 'STEERING INOP' message while making a sharp turn on to the runway for departure. The takeoff is delayed while the steering is reset and an aircraft on final is instructed to go around.
summary: The pilot reported a STEERING INOP message after a tight turn on the runway, causing a private aircraft on final to go around. The crew reset the nose wheel steering by turning it off and straightening the wheel, then departed without logging the event or contacting maintenance.

synopsis: DHC8-100 Captain experiences a SMOKE Master Warning Light as the nose wheel is lowered to the runway after touch down. The aircraft is stopped on a taxiway and the passengers are evacuated. ARFF can locate no fire or smoke. The aircraft is towed to the gate by Maintenance.
summary: The flight crew received a SMOKE Master Warning Light during the landing roll-out, prompting an immediate evacuation after completing the smoke checklist. Fire crews inspected the aircraft and found no smoke, after which maintenance took control.

synopsis: Hawker 900 Captain experiences a false localizer signal during a night visual approach to Runway 33L at BWI. The Tower reported no faults with the localizer and the the crew could find no faults with the aircraft or the set up.
summary: During a night visual approach to BWI RWY 33R, the crew encountered conflicting localizer indications guiding them toward parallel RWY 33L despite correct equipment setup and no failure flags. The pilots safely landed by prioritizing visual references over the erroneous instrument guidance, though the specific cause of the signal deviation remains undetermined.

synopsis: During a night CAT I landing in minimum weather conditions at a non-controlled airport, the crew neglected to remotely activate the airport runway lighting system and touched down without runway lights. At the Captain's call of runway in sight at about 200 feet AGL, it was realized that the runway was not lit and the First Officer, the PNF, attempted to activate the lights by keying the mic button seven times but moved the stab trim switch instead. The lights were eventually activated after touchdown.
summary: During an approach to minimums at a closed uncontrolled airport, the First Officer forgot to activate runway lights and accidentally pressed the stab trim button instead of the microphone. The crew landed with lights off, which illuminated only after touchdown, prompting the reporter to admit they should have executed a go-around.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reports inability to contact his Dispatcher directly to advise of a weather diversion to an airport other than the filed alternate.
summary: The flight crew enroute to a destination with bad weather attempted to divert to ZZZ but received no response from Dispatch via ACARS or unreliable internet phone. With only ten minutes of hold fuel and a thunderstorm on final, they declared an emergency, landed at ZZZ for fuel, and continued to the original destination.

synopsis: B757 flight crew experiences a flap disagree EICAS message during approach when flaps 30 are called for by the Captain above flaps 30 speed and quickly corrected. The flap handle is moved to the 30 position by the First Officer then back to 25, resulting in a flap disagree. A go-around is initiated, the QRH is consulted and a flaps 20 landing ensues.
summary: During a visual approach, the pilot monitoring extended flaps to 30 while exceeding the 162 KIAS limit, triggering a flap disagree and go-around. The crew managed the abnormal flap configuration and landed safely, attributing the incident to high speed restrictions and distraction.

synopsis: CRJ200 Captain discovers the left engine is not responding to thrust lever movement during descent and is holding a steady 72% N1. The engine is shut down following QRH procedures and a single engine landing ensues.
summary: During descent to 6,000 feet, the left engine failed to respond to thrust lever movements, remaining fixed at 72% N1. The crew executed the thrust lever jammed QRH procedure, shut down the engine, and landed safely in VMC.

synopsis: As they began their taxi from the gate the flight crew of a B737-700 received frantic alerts from the flight attendants of flames emanating from the exhaust of the left engine. Investigation determined the engine control light had illuminated and the engine had performed an auto shut down. Emergency equipment was dispatched and the flight returned to the gate.
summary: The flight crew experienced an amber ENG CONTROL light and a reported engine one fire during taxi, based on flight attendant observations of flames. Maintenance later attributed the incident to a fuel leak rather than a tail pipe fire, resulting in the aircraft returning to the gate for a swap.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports an unacceptable FOD situation in the gate area prior to aircraft arrival. Ramp personnel are asked to correct the problem but are unwilling to do so in a timely manner. The Captain then picks up the FOD on his own.
summary: A pilot found over 70 pieces of FOD in the gate safety zone after a ramp agent refused to perform a walk-down due to apathy. The pilot personally cleared the debris, citing a lack of leadership, training, and supervision as the cause for the hazardous conditions.

synopsis: The Captain of an A321 failed to note when his First Officer, new to the airline, loaded the route in the FMS incorrectly. A track deviation ensued.
summary: The Captain and a new First Officer deviated four miles from their filed route after the First Officer incorrectly entered the flight plan into the FMS. The error was discovered after passing FKN, requiring a controller clearance to Salisbury to return to the correct course.

synopsis: The crew of a DHC-8-400 sent erroneous information through ACARS and received takeoff data in reply, then discovered after takeoff that the weight and balance system not only failed to detect and indicate the incorrect input, but also did not discover and indicate the obvious weight discrepancy.
summary: Flight crew discovered a 14 lb aft cargo limit exceedance after ACARS failed to flag two weight and balance errors, including a 314 lb input mistake. Maintenance determined no inspection was needed as major weight limits were not exceeded, though the crew requested an investigation into the ACARS system failure.

synopsis: CE650 First Officer reports a runway incursion at SDF while attempting to cross Runway 35R on taxiway G but veering left and incurring Runway 29.
summary: The crew, fatigued after 10 hours, inadvertently entered Runway 35R at night due to poor lighting and a misleading airport diagram where pavement shading resembled Taxiway G. Ground control alerted them to the incursion, allowing the crew to exit the runway safely before reaching Runway 29.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain experiences the loss of a single IRS on an over water flight, just past the mid point, and continues to destination.
summary: The crew encountered a left IRS position shift and subsequent failure causing loss of the Captain's PFD during cruise. They declared an emergency, followed QRH procedures, and executed an uneventful landing after verifying position with the right IRS.

synopsis: The pilot of a Eurocopter elected to return to base following a bird strike that resulted in a fractured nose between the windshield and chin bubble.
summary: During a night enroute flight, a bird struck the aircraft nose, breaking the structure between the windshield and chin bubble and entering the cabin. The pilot returned to base without further incident.

synopsis: MD83 flight crew reports a hard landing. The winds were reported as steady at 18 knots and were in fact gusting to 25, which may have contributed to the incident.
summary: Pilots reported a hard landing during a visual approach to Runway 30 in gusty winds not advised by the Tower. The aircraft struck the ground hard due to wind shear and insufficient speed, causing minor cabin damage and two passenger injuries, though no structural damage was found.

synopsis: When dispatched with an inoperative APU it was necessary to start the B737-800 using a ground power cart. The flight crew inadvertently started the right engine first contrary to the non-normal procedure because the start cart must be positioned in front of the right engine. The ground crew reminded them and they shut down the right engine, started the left engine and then pushed back prior to restarting the right utilizing crossbleed pneumatics.
summary: The flight crew and Crew Chief experienced a near-miss during gate engine start with an inoperative APU when the start cart was positioned in front of the number two engine. The engine was shut down immediately, confirmed undamaged, and the crew subsequently started the number one engine first before completing the pushback.

synopsis: An MD-82 flight crew declared an emergency diverted to a nearby airport and landed overweight but uneventfully when acrid odors permeated the cockpit and passenger cabin.
summary: The flight crew diverted an aircraft from FL280 after an acrid odor appeared in the cockpit and cabin, likely caused by galley or recirculation issues. They landed overweight at a nearby airport to minimize exposure time, deviating from standard procedures to get the jet on the ground quickly.

synopsis: When the Captain/PNF became task saturated programming a runway change while descending via the TAMMY RNAV STAR to MEM, he failed to reset his altimeter passing FL180. The altitude alert warning sounded when the PF leveled at 16,000 feet while the Captain's altimeter read 15,700 feet.
summary: During a descent on the Tammy Four RNAV arrival, the Captain deleted waypoints and failed to select the correct transition, causing a navigation issue resolved by manual entry. Additionally, the Captain's altimeter was set to QNE instead of QNH at FL180, triggering an altitude alerter before being corrected.

synopsis: Confusion reigned when an air carrier flight crew, descending via the LTOWN6 RNAV STAR to MEM misunderstood their landing runway assignment. As a result they were unable to comply with the 10000/230K restriction over COPEN.
summary: The flight crew descended via the LTOWN 6 North transition after a runway change to 18L, failing to meet the 10,000-foot restriction at COPEN. Memphis Approach vectored them off the arrival to 5,000 feet, while the pilot attributed the error to cockpit noise and late ATIS updates.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports finding bolts that attach a hinge support to a bearing block just aft of a mixing unit, on a EC-135 Eurocopter, were not torqued or cotter pinned. Pilot had noted the EC-135 had a 1 to 1 hop in all axis of flight that had been getting worse.
summary: During reassembly of a Eurocopter EC-135 main rotor hub, mechanics installed but failed to torque or cotter pin two bolts securing the hinged support to the bearing block. The aircraft flew a maintenance flight and a patient flight before a pilot reported a vibration, leading to the discovery of the loose bolts and a missing nut between the transmission and mixing unit.

synopsis: A corporate flight crew began a visual approach descent without clearance from ZTL because they heard 'Expect the Visual' and began a descent when they felt they would have normally.
summary: The pilot flying and Chief Pilot descended below 7,300 feet enroute to the airport after misinterpreting an "expect visual" clearance as an actual visual approach clearance. This premature descent occurred because the crew failed to report the airport in sight, though no traffic conflict or separation loss resulted.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot entered ORL Class D Airspace at MCO TRACON's direction and was confronted by a combative ORL Tower Controller for entering the airspace without his clearance even though MCO cleared him in.
summary: A VFR pilot approaching Orlando Executive was vectored by Approach into Class D airspace without prior Tower coordination due to radio congestion. The pilot complied with Approach's descent and downwind instructions but was later questioned by Tower for entering without clearance, which the pilot attributed to improper Approach procedure.

synopsis: PA-28R pilot began to lose communications while within the Washington SFRA, he advised ATC in the blind and exited the SFRA to land at a nearby diversion airport.
summary: The pilot experienced an in-flight electrical failure during VFR cruise caused by a faulty alternator field wire, resulting in lost avionics and communications. After securing non-essential loads, the pilot executed a NORDO visual approach to a diversion airport and landed safely.

synopsis: SR20 pilot reports calling Ground for an early morning taxi for takeoff and getting no response. After several more attempts the reporter assumes the Tower is not yet open and uses CTAF procedures to depart. Once airborne the Tower calls and asks who just departed without clearance. The headset was found to be defective.
summary: The pilot departed Runway XX without authorization, assuming the Tower was closed after receiving no radio response due to a faulty headset. The Tower contacted the aircraft at 700 feet AGL, and the pilot acknowledged the error while noting the Tower heard transmission attempts on tape.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: A Cessna CJ3-25B crew mistook ATC's revised heading clearance, given during takeoff, for an altitude change and climbed on a heading not intended or expected by ATC, creating a conflict with another aircraft. The reporter states several missed opportunities for ATC to notice the misunderstandings during the flight crew's read-back of the clearance instructions and particulars.
summary: The flight crew received an amended altitude clearance during the takeoff roll, which they read back without correction. Departure controllers later reported a conflict because the crew climbed to FL200 instead of following a missed heading instruction, though the crew believed the clearance was correct based on the Tower's lack of correction.

synopsis: Columbia 400 pilot reports confusing instructions and questionable handling during a practice ILS approach to Runway 6 at LOZ. The reporter was apparently expected to return to ZID frequency after the approach but this was not clearly conveyed to the reporter.
summary: A pilot practicing an ILS approach at LOZ remained 3,500 feet above the glide slope after Indy Center cleared them to fly the published missed approach while remaining VFR. The pilot incorrectly assumed Flight Following had ended and failed to cancel the plan, causing Lexington Approach to search for the aircraft.

synopsis: CE560 First Officer reports difficulties and errors attempting to communicate with ATC late one night while during taxi and takeoff from EWR.
summary: The PIC and co-pilot experienced confusion during taxi and takeoff at Newark due to non-standard frequency changes by Ground and Tower controllers. The co-pilot missed switching frequencies, resulting in a takeoff clearance on the wrong frequency and subsequent verbal reprimand from Departure.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A MD-80 First Officer supervised refueling at a foreign station with the Fuel Valves in the MANUAL OVERRIDE position which caused an overfilled right main fuel tank to vent out the left wing vent. The fuel system was thought to be faulty but not entered in the Maintenance Log until arrival in the U.S.
summary: During refueling, fuel vented from the right main tank through the left wing vent because the First Officer used manual override valves instead of the auto system.
