The Captain stopped the spill, but later incorrectly logged the cause as an auto system malfunction and flew with an open maintenance deferral.

synopsis: An experimental aircraft engine throttle was blocked at low power setting by a passenger's watch, unbeknown to the pilot who prepared to land on a beach after passing low over a populated area but at the last minute the throttle block was removed and they climbed.
summary: During a descent from 2,000 to 1,000 feet MSL, the pilot could not advance the throttle above 40 percent due to a passenger's watch stuck in the control. The pilot descended toward a beach landing but regained full throttle control at idle, allowing a safe return to flight without landing.

synopsis: A C172 passenger accidentally activated the portable fire extinguisher under the pilots seat with his foot creating what appeared to be a fire. But the extinguishing agent was quickly identified and the flight returned normally to the departure airport.
summary: A pilot conducting a personal sightseeing flight experienced smoke in the cockpit caused by a passenger accidentally activating the fire extinguisher. The pilot diverted back to the departure airport, confirmed the non-emergency, and landed uneventfully after the cabin self-ventilated.

synopsis: BE-36 pilot tired from a long day of flying and overly dependent on his moving map display, made multiple errors of judgment and execution when taxiing for takeoff at FDK. Ground Control was instrumental in the aircraft's eventual arrival at the departure end of the active runway.
summary: A fatigued pilot on the third flight of the day at FDK entered Runway 30 without clearance due to false assumptions about markings and over-reliance on a lagging moving map. Ground control provided progressive guidance to return the aircraft to the departure end, resulting in a runway incursion with no further incident.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot flying the TRI Runway 23 LOC approach had a CFIT when he descended early below the FAF crossing altitude because he failed to debrief the approach after being told the ILS was out of service.
summary: The pilot, diverting to TRI, descended below the minimum altitude before the FAF on a LOC Runway 23 approach due to cockpit distractions preventing an approach briefing. This caused a terrain alert and a missed approach, which the pilot attributed to unfamiliarity with the airport and poor situational awareness.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A small transport pilot encountered severe turbulence and descended up to 3,000 feet from his assigned altitude while flying south of and parallel to a line of Midwestern thunderstorms.
summary: A pilot flying an aircraft equipped with stormscope and onboard radar encountered severe turbulence and icing while descending from FL270 to FL230 near thunderstorms. The autopilot disengaged, causing a 2,000 to 3,000-foot altitude deviation below FL230, which the pilot attributed to insufficient distance from convective activity.

synopsis: ZMP Controller voiced concern regarding the functionality of the ERAM equipment processing flight plan information.
summary: ZMP and ZAU controllers experienced an ERAM software error where ZAU returned an incorrect flight plan with pref routing for an aircraft crossing their boundary. This caused a route display mismatch that confused the ZMP controller, requiring coordination to resolve the discrepancy and highlighting a critical risk of future operational errors.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: TRACON Controller described the total failure of RADAR, Radio and all facility electrical inputs, the reporter improved attention to local 'contingency' plans.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller working a combined sector experienced a total power failure at ZZZ, causing loss of radar, radios, and lighting. The controller issued a blind transmission advising aircraft to maintain VFR and contact the tower until power was restored and full radar service resumed.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A single axle aircraft Captain refused to fly the aircraft into MDW with a 270 foot stopping margin on the active wet runway so his company had a Management Pilot fly and upon arrival the airport was clear and dry.
summary: The flight crew refused a return flight to MDW in a fully loaded single-axle aircraft due to an unsafe 270-foot wet runway stopping margin. Despite Dispatch and Chief Pilot pressure to proceed, the crew deplaned passengers, were deadheaded on the flight, and later landed safely on a dry runway after a Check Airman took command.

synopsis: An air carrier crew continued the takeoff at ORD with the incorrect takeoff runway in the FMC after ATC issued several taxi route changes along with three runway changes.
summary: The flight crew experienced multiple runway changes and distractions at ORD, leading the First Officer to incorrectly enter Runway 32R/T10 into the FMC instead of the assigned 32L. An FMC runway disagree warning occurred during the takeoff roll, but the Captain elected to continue the departure due to the aircraft's light weight and familiarity with the runway.

synopsis: A DH-8-400 First Officer's windshield shattered at FL250. So the crew completed the QRH, declared an emergency, descended to 14,000 feet and continued to the filed destination.
summary: During cruise at FL250, the First Officer's windshield shattered. The crew followed the QRH, descended to 14,000 feet, slowed to 190 knots, declared an emergency, and continued to the filed destination.

synopsis: An ERJ crew descending on the RAVNN Arrival overshot then climbed back to the 9,000 feet OTT constraint after noticing the altitude constraint and name are reversed from all others on the right flight path.
summary: Pilots descending on the RAVNN arrival missed the OTT fix crossing restriction of 9,000 feet due to confusing chart placement, descending to approximately 8,600 feet before correcting. The crew attributed the error to the restriction being listed on the opposite side of the fix name compared to other points on the chart.

synopsis: Because the FMGC was not maintaining the LAX RIIVR TWO Arrival profile after GRAMM, an Airbus Captain set the cruise altitude to 1 resulting in all arrival altitude constraints dropping which then required that he fly the arrival manually.
summary: During the RIIVR TWO arrival into LAX, the Captain attempted to reset the Airbus FMGC altitude constraints by changing the cruise altitude, which caused the system to drop all constraints. While manually calculating descents and navigating in heading mode, the Captain drifted off the arrival path due to over-tasking, though no altitude restrictions were missed.

synopsis: When weather forced a B737NG flight crew to deviate from the HAWKZ RNAV STAR to SEA they were unable to 'descend in compliance with the descent path of the complex procedure as requested by ATC. When they so advised ATC they were given the same clearance.
summary: The flight crew deviated right of the HAWKZ RNAV STAR for weather but received a clearance to maintain the arrival's descent profile while off-course. The crew reported this clearance was invalid because maintaining the profile is impossible when not flying the arrival path.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports a runway incursion at Taxiway E and Runway 28 at BWI. Taxi instructions were to taxi via A, P1, U to Runway 28. The turn onto A was never executed.
summary: The flight crew executed a taxi clearance to Runway 28 but missed a turn onto Alpha taxiway due to distraction by a departing aircraft. This error caused them to enter Runway 28 via Echo taxiway, resulting in a runway incursion with no other traffic present.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports an airborne conflict with a C208 dropping skydivers. ATC was in contact with both aircraft and issued last minute heading and altitude instructions to the reporter to avoid collision. A TCAS TA was annunciated.
summary: During climb, a pilot deviated from ATC clearance to avoid a Cessna Caravan conducting skydiving operations, resulting in less than 1,000 feet vertical and 2 miles horizontal separation. The pilot attributed the Traffic Advisory and near-miss to ATC human error for assigning conflicting headings and altitudes despite awareness of the jump aircraft.

synopsis: After replacing both nose tires on an ERJ-190 aircraft, a Line Mechanic realizes he installed tires that were not 'Effective' for the aircraft. Mechanic noted that only a single letter at the end of the tire Part Number (P/N) marked the difference between the ERJ-170 and -190 nose tires.
summary: A mechanic installed incorrect nose tires on an ERJ-190 during a quick gate turn due to time pressure and failing to create a material request first. The non-effective parts were discovered later, requiring the next maintenance station to replace them with the correct tires.

synopsis: The pilot of a Learjet 35A mismanaged his onboard navigational equipment and lost situational awareness, culminating in heading and course deviations. ATC noticed his difficulty and provided radar vectors until he regained orientation and was able to proceed to his destination all by himself.
summary: The flight crew entered the destination airport as the current location in the FMS on the ground, causing incorrect GPS positioning and an unintended left turn during the en route phase. ATC intervened to provide a corrective heading after the aircraft attempted to navigate to a waypoint based on the erroneous flight plan.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Stinson 108 student pilot reports swerving during his third landing and having the instructor take control. The instructor initially corrects then ground loops the aircraft causing a runway excursion and propeller damage.
summary: During a Stinson 108 tailwheel landing, the instructor took control to correct a swerve but ground-looped the aircraft after his foot slipped off the rudder pedal due to unfamiliarity with the cockpit layout. The incident resulted in a propeller strike with no other damage.

synopsis: A B767-200 was given vectors to avoid a UAV and received an RA.
summary: The flight crew on a PAR approach at 11,400 feet received a TCAS RA after a non-communicating UAV descended toward their altitude during a vector. The Captain manually executed the climb and descent advisories to avoid the UAV, which was visually spotted less than one mile away, before returning to the approach.

synopsis: When cleared to exit the General Aviation ramp at STL the pilot of a Small Transport aircraft taxied onto K1 prior to contacting Ground Control. The Ground Controller reprimanded the pilot for entering a movement area without a clearance. Reporter stated there were no airport markings or signage that depicted movement vice non-movement areas when departing the GA ramp.
summary: A pilot repositioning an empty aircraft from the General Aviation ramp to the Main Terminal Charlie gates taxied into the movement area without clearance, believing the area was non-movement due to missing markings. The pilot apologized to the Controller and later received updated procedures from the Chief Pilot regarding FBO exit protocols.

synopsis: EA50 pilot experiences erroneous airspeed indications and stall warnings at FL380 while IMC above a thunderstorm. A descent and diversion is executed with ATC approval and the pitot static system returns to normal passing 17,000 feet.
summary: The pilot of an Eclipse aircraft encountered erroneous airspeed and stall warnings at FL380 due to moisture freezing in the pitot-static system after entering IMC. The autopilot disconnected, requiring manual flight and a descent to FL260, while the pilot noted missing static covers and design flaws in the drain system contributed to the failure.

synopsis: Enroute Controller voiced concern regarding the HIBAL weather balloon release procedure claiming not enough information is provided to the controllers with reference to the launches.
summary: An air traffic controller at position R91/65 reported receiving insufficient data regarding a HIBAL launch near the PHX arrival corridor. Supervisors dismissed the controller's safety concerns about the lack of specific balloon details, despite the potential proximity to aircraft on J2/J18 routes.

synopsis: B737-300 flight crew distracted by an ATC runway change, overlooked the After Start Checklist and neglected to extend the Slats/Flaps.
summary: The flight crew re-ran the Before Push Checklist after an ATC runway change, causing them to skip the subsequent checklist. The Captain discovered an incorrect flap configuration during a throttle burst while taxiing, prompting a stop to complete all flows before a safe takeoff.

synopsis: Dispatcher described unintended consequences when trying to change a flight number to avoid duplication in the ATC system.
summary: An air traffic controller filed a STUB originated flight with a changed call sign but failed to cancel the original strip. The pilot contacted Clearance Delivery using the original flight number, causing a discrepancy that the controller resolved by instructing the pilot to continue operations under that number.

synopsis: B767 flight crew discovers enroute that there is no pre planned escape route in their manuals for loss of pressurization over high terrain along their route in South America.
summary: The flight crew operating over high terrain on route VVC UB689 BOG UG447 SPP found no Terrain Critical Depressurization Procedure in the Planning guide. Dispatch could not provide alternative publications, so the crew proceeded on their cleared route with caution while discussing contingency plans for mechanical failures.

synopsis: B747 flight crew began to taxi before receiving a salute from the guideman, still connected to the aircraft by his headset.
summary: After a 17-hour duty day and non-standard pushback, the crew lost awareness of the guideman and rolled one foot before stopping. The Captain halted the taxi upon seeing a person near the nose, waited for them to clear, and then continued.

synopsis: B757 flight crew took evasive action from an unseen TCAS RA target at 5,600 FT near SAX VOR descending for a EWR approach.
summary: Pilots received conflicting TCAS RAs while being vectored by NY Approach near SAX VOR at 6,000 FT. A descent clearance to 5,000 FT toward VFR traffic triggered a climb RA, forcing a climb back to 6,000 FT to avoid a potential 400 FT separation breach.

synopsis: A319 Captain experiences uncomfortably hot temperatures in the cockpit and forward cabin during climb. With the the Hot Air valve turned off uncomfortably cold temperatures result and the crew elects to divert to a suitable airport. This was a chronic issue with this aircraft according to the maintenance history.
summary: The crew experienced uncontrollable cabin temperature extremes and a burning electrical/oil odor during climb and descent due to a chronic aircraft issue. After resetting pack circuit breakers failed, they declared an emergency, diverted to ZZZ, and landed overweight while mechanics confirmed a lingering oily smell at the pack intake.

synopsis: A B737 captain expressed general umbrage toward the recently initiated 'OPD' RNAV STARs to DEN. In the specific incident referenced they had been cleared direct to cross QUAIL as charted (Between FL220 and FL200) on the ZPLYN RNAV STAR, thence to descend via the STAR. Subsequently they were recleared via the BOSSS RNAV STAR via direct to QUAIL and to cross as charted, between FL190 & 17,000, but were unable.
summary: The flight crew encountered FMC programming conflicts during descent on the BOSSS arrival due to conflicting altitude restrictions between the transition and STAR. This caused high workload and an inability to descend and slow as requested, resulting in a vector for a downwind leg and resequencing.

synopsis: EMB145 Flight Crew experiences the loss of the First officer's airspeed indication at FL370. An emergency is declared and the flight continues to destination for a normal laneding. During descent all pitot static systems return to normal.
summary: The flight crew encountered unforecast severe icing at 37,000 feet, causing ice detector failure, inaccurate airspeed/altitude readings, and autopilot disconnect. After declaring an emergency to descend, instruments normalized, and post-flight inspection found no defects despite suspected ADC and ice detector issues.

synopsis: CE680 flight crew experiences an MCDU failure in cruise flight and elects to divert for maintenance. Shortly after the failure an electrical burning odor is detected and the crew elects to divert to a closer airport. A very busy descent and approach results in an overshoot while attempting to intercept the localizer. A normal landing ensues.
summary: During cruise, the crew diverted due to a flickering #2 MCDU and burning odor, then cleared for a visual approach to 19L. They overshot the centerline but corrected after ATC reconfirmed clearance, attributing the error to crew saturation from rapid changes.

synopsis: An air carrier crew descended below FL240 10 miles prior to AXXEL because the chart note describing the common restriction at CASOT, AXXEL and KELNE is printed some distance from the waypoints and not clearly associated with the them.
summary: The crew descended below FL240 while executing the LTOWN SIX RNAV arrival into MEM due to distraction and cluttered chart notes. The First Officer noticed the deviation at 23,500 feet, and the Captain immediately climbed back to FL240 without ATC intervention.

synopsis: DHC8-100 First Officer is informed by the Captain during landing of jammed ailerons in the left wing down direction. The First Officer is asked to try it for himself and initially feels resistance when rolling to the left but repeated attempts result in the resistance disappearing.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring reported a control yoke jam during rollout after a normal landing. The jam occurred at 15-20 degrees left deflection, required approximately 15-20 lbs of force to clear, and the aircraft was subsequently inspected and approved for a ferry flight.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: MD80 flight crew reports fuel decreasing in both wing tanks and the center tank during cruise when only the center tank should be decreasing. The QRH procedure for fuel not feeding from the center tank is employed to ensure most center tank fuel is used before turning the wing tank pumps back on.
summary: During cruise, the crew observed simultaneous fuel depletion in all three tanks on a DC-9, suspecting low center tank pump pressure. They executed the QRH procedure for "Fuel Not Feeding from Center Tank" to empty the center tank before using wing fuel, resulting in an uneventful landing.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reports being cleared for a night takeoff at SBGL then noticing an aircraft at the far end of the runway just prior to V1. The Captain elects to continue the takeoff and easily clears the other aircraft. The Tower Controller was speaking Portuguese to the local pilots and English to this U.S. crew.
summary: The flight crew departed SBGL at night on Runway 28 after being cleared for takeoff while another aircraft remained at the runway end. The Captain continued the takeoff to avoid a high-speed abort near V1, clearing the stationary aircraft safely, though the Tower admitted the preceding aircraft had not vacated before issuing the clearance.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reports a compressor stall climbing through 10,000 feet that results in high N2 vibration and high ITT. The thrust is reduced to idle and the flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced a loud noise, vibration, and odor shortly after climbing through 10,000 feet, triggering left engine N2 vibration and red ITT EICAS indications. They declared an emergency, returned, and landed safely after reducing thrust to idle and deciding against a full engine shutdown.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Maintenance Inspector reports receiving emergency exit light batteries and installing them in an aircraft. He is later informed that the batteries should not have been accepted due to the MPM requirement that the batteries not be off charge for more than seven days, which they were. The RII inspection notes did not contain this requirement.
summary: A mechanic installed an emergency battery pack for a B717 that had been off charge for over seven days, violating MPM shelf life requirements due to outdated Receiving Inspector notes. The battery was installed to correct the issue, and the inspector began rejecting eight other non-compliant batteries while requesting updated documentation.

synopsis: Citation jet departing ATL Runway 9L on the Atlanta Six SID experienced some confusion when ATC instructed the aircraft to initiate a turn at the Middle Marker after the take off clearance was issued.
summary: The flight crew received a non-standard clearance to turn at the Middle Marker after takeoff on Runway 9L while executing a high-performance climb to avoid wake turbulence. Because the marker beacon is ineffective at 4,000 feet, the crew turned late, prompting ATC to advise that such clearances should use known fixes or altitudes instead.

synopsis: C172 pilot reports being aware of the requirement to turn on transponder upon receiving taxi clearance at SLC, but then forgetting to do so. ATC provides a reminder.
summary: The pilot forgot to activate the transponder after receiving taxi clearance at SLC, despite pre-flight review of the new ASDE-X requirement. Ground control reminded the pilot to comply, and the incident was attributed to outdated habits from prior operations before the rule change.

synopsis: DA40 instructor with student on an IFR flight plan report an NMAC with an Aeronca just after breaking out at 800 FT AGL on the ILS 3 to MGJ. A missed approach is executed by the DA40. The Aeronca had no radio and no transponder.
summary: An IFR instructor and student in a DA40 encountered a non-responsive Aeronca near the runway during an ILS approach at MGJ in IMC. The DA40 pilot executed a right bank to avoid collision, then initiated a missed approach after the Aeronca landed, attributing the near miss to the other aircraft's lack of radio and transponder.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: General aviation pilot reports encountering a flock of geese during the flare for landing at 26N. After several impacts a successful go-around is initiated. The next landing is uneventful although the aircraft is found to have dents in the rudder on post flight.
summary: The pilot executed a go-around during final approach after a flock of geese struck the aircraft, causing windshield obstruction and runway misalignment. The subsequent inspection revealed a torn beacon and dented rudder, leading the FSDO to ground the aircraft as unairworthy.

synopsis: Cessna 172 instructor pilot reports that a local ATC Controller's mumbling, indistinct, and rapid speech on Tower, Ground Control, and ATIS communications causes confusion and requires many pilots to have to ask for a repeat of radio transmissions.
summary: A pilot reported that a Tower and Ground Air Traffic Controller frequently uses unclear, mumbled, and fast speech, forcing crews to request repetitions. This communication issue creates a safety hazard during high workload and dense traffic conditions by causing uncertainty and increasing stress for both ATC and flight crews.

synopsis: After departure the pilot of a C172S was not able to maintain the required climb performance because of downdrafts in mountainous terrain, and additionally failed to stay in contact with ATC. Upon reaching cruise altitude the Departure Controller informed him that he had descended below the MVA.
summary: The pilot experienced degraded climb performance and airspeed loss due to a downdraft during climbout in mountainous terrain. The pilot failed to inform ATC of the inability to maintain a safe climb, resulting in a deviation below Minimum Vectoring Altitude.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a loss of separation event due in part to vectoring traffic for an instrument approach on a tight downwind.
summary: Air Traffic Control lost IFR separation between two aircraft on VOR Runway 23 practice approaches when a tight downwind-to-final turn caused lateral conflict. The controller resolved the situation by turning the trailing aircraft to heading 070 to restore safe spacing.

synopsis: ZOA Enroute Controller voiced concern regarding the lack of coordination and information provided regarding a balloon launch.
summary: An air traffic controller managing R14 without a D-Side struggled to warn pilots of untracked balloons due to delayed, vague, and erroneous information from the Supervisor. This lack of accurate data caused pilot confusion and safety concerns while F18s requested headings to avoid the balloons, highlighting a dangerous situation exacerbated by poor coordination.

synopsis: ZAN Controller described a confused event when an issued NOTAM reflected incorrect information regarding airport status apparently due to confusion regarding ATC control authority.
summary: An Air Carrier X pilot inbound to DUT for a GPS12 approach found a conflicting NOTAM stating the runway was closed due to CDB Radio's closure, despite work in progress. The pilot contacted ENA Radio and learned the runway was actually open, highlighting that NOTAMs were incorrectly changed solely because the controlling facility closed.

synopsis: The crew of a B767 was delayed at the gate after receiving push back clearance because it was discovered that the cargo had been loaded improperly and unsafely.
summary: The flight crew cancelled pushback after ramp agents failed to move the aircraft due to improperly loaded cargo cans that could shift aft and compromise the center of gravity. The delay required unloading and reloading the cargo, a recurring issue the Captain attributes to serious ramp training deficiencies.

synopsis: A B757 Captain reported unusually high stick forces required at rotation due, he believes, from faulty weight and balance calculations by load planners.
summary: The flight crew reported that despite verifying trim settings via ACARS and FMC, the aircraft was difficult to rotate and balance during takeoff. The pilot had to apply excessive control force and additional nose-up trim to lift the nose and level off, describing the aircraft as feeling out of balance.

synopsis: A First Officer describes why he refused to accept an ERJ-170 aircraft that included an uncontrollable overheated cabin, a very cold flight deck, an MEL Maintenance Procedure (M) improperly applied to Number 2 Pack with a plastic bag zip tied over the Ram Air Valve inlet and a Number 1 Pack that was noisy with a burning electrical smell inside and outside the cabin.
summary: The flight crew refused to operate an ERJ-175 after discovering a zip-tied Ram Air Valve inlet, a burning Number One Pack, and a faulty Number Two Pack temperature sensor with over 140 recorded faults. These conditions violated the MEL requirements for the aircraft to fly below FL310 with specific pack configurations.

synopsis: During descent the crew of an ERJ-170 missed a crossing altitude clearance by 10,000 feet, and was subsequently vectored and descended by ATC to regain the approach profile.
summary: The flight crew missed a descent clearance during arrival due to fatigue from interrupted sleep the previous night. ATC queried their altitude, vectored them away, and they resumed the arrival without incident after the crew recognized their mental fog.

synopsis: The crew of an EMB-145LR in cruise flight experienced a loud external clunking noise of undetermined origin accompanied by a shaking of the aircraft. An emergency was declared and as a precaution they diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a loud clunking noise and shaking in the front of the aircraft during cruise with no EICAS indications. They declared an emergency and diverted to an unplanned airport, landing safely with no further abnormalities.

synopsis: EMB145 Captain reports diverting for maintenance when the aircraft he is flying begins to produce a loud noise in the cabin as it had on the previous flight and as reflected in the maintenance history.
summary: The deadheading Captain and Flight Attendant, along with the operating crew, experienced a loud, irregular cabin noise above 10,000 feet despite normal EICAS and pressurization indications. The crew diverted the aircraft due to the persistent noise, noting that prior ground maintenance checks failed to replicate the issue.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain as the NFP reports the aircraft nose beginning to lift prior to V1. The flying First Officer trims the nose down and rotates at Vr. The trim setting remained in the green band the entire time.
summary: The First Officer flying a Boeing 737 experienced nose wheel float during takeoff roll, likely due to an aft center of gravity from a light passenger load. The crew corrected the issue with forward yoke pressure and trim, moved passengers forward, and landed safely, though the Chief Pilot was unreachable for follow-up.

synopsis: B757 First Officer experiences a terrain warning approaching KELSO during the RNAV Runway 08 approach to MDPP and takes evasive action.
summary: A B757/767 crew executing an RNAV (GNSS) RWY 08 approach at MDPP triggered a terrain warning due to high speed and configuration, forcing a missed approach. The pilot attributed the event to unacceptably tight procedure tolerances and recommended removing the approach, citing it as unsafe compared to the VOR 26 option.

synopsis: EMB-190 Captain reports using the published runway length for takeoff performance calculations with a NOTAM in effect shortening the runway by approximately 1,300 feet. This NOTAM should have been in the performance data base and the full runway length selection should not have been allowed. The takeoff was uneventful and the error was detected airborne.
summary: The First Officer loaded takeoff data for Runway 12, but the Performance data system failed to block the full length selection despite a NOTAM shortening the runway by 1296 feet. The system provided valid data without requiring the "FULL" code, yet the takeoff was completed uneventfully.

synopsis: Musketeer pilot reports switching to the full fuel tank prior to takeoff then having the engine quit at 900 feet AGL. The fuel selector is placed back to the left tank and carburetor heat is applied. The engine immediately catches and a precautionary landing ensues.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine stoppage at 900 AGL during climbout from SEG while using the right fuel tank. The engine restarted after switching to the left tank, and the mechanic attributed the temporary fuel starvation to a suspected right tank issue.

synopsis: General Aviation aircraft expressed concern regarding ATC handling during maneuvers to avoid weather. The reporter noted ATC's poor grasp of the flight situation.
summary: During descent to 7FL6, the pilot maneuvered visually through rain showers while Daytona Beach Approach assigned a fixed heading of 170, claiming the pilot could not choose their own path. The pilot safely landed but later complained to the supervisor about the controller's lack of situational awareness and inappropriate interference with safe flight conduct.

synopsis: PA44 Student Pilot raised the gear handle on takeoff, but the gear remained down with three down and locked indications. Instructor Pilot took control of the aircraft, lowered the gear handle and, after a fly-by for visual verification, landed without incident.
summary: A pilot and student experienced a landing gear malfunction during departure when the gear failed to retract due to an improperly installed squat switch. Despite indicator discrepancies and a 'gear unsafe' light, the gear remained down and locked, resulting in a safe landing after maintenance consultation.

synopsis: C182 pilot reports loosing control at touchdown and swerving off the runway. No damage or injuries occur and the aircraft is taxied to the FBO.
summary: The pilot, flying a straight-in approach to Runway 24 behind a B737, experienced a left veer and skid off the runway upon touchdown. The pilot attributed the incident to a high approach and excessive speed, noting no aircraft damage was found during post-flight inspection.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: ZAB Controller described an airspace incursion claiming an ERAM anomaly contributed to the event.
summary: An air traffic controller managing a B737 at FL290 experienced a radar track loss when the aircraft shared a beacon code with a VFR flight, causing the target to disappear from the ERAM scope. The controller manually recovered the track and rerouted the B737, attributing the incident to a potential system glitch or interface issue between ERAM and the HOST system.

synopsis: ZSU Controller described a go around event when the Tower sent an A320 around that was following a DHC6, the TRACON Controller indicating the Tower ignored the TRACON's direction.
summary: An air traffic controller in the R1 Sector reported a coordination failure with Tower regarding a VFR DHC6 and an IFR A320 on approach to Runway 10. Although no separation was lost, the controller attributed the incident to Tower's unprofessional attitude and lack of cooperation, stating that safety is being compromised.

synopsis: M03 Controller described a loss of heavy jet separation event claiming FUSION equipment was a contributing factor.
summary: An air traffic controller using the FUSION system reported difficulty determining spacing between a B752 and a PC12 on parallel finals due to target wobbling. The controller inadvertently released the PC12 with 4.99 miles separation instead of the intended 5 miles, resulting in a minimum spacing of 4.86 miles.

synopsis: ZMP Controller suggested the elimination of the TVC Transition on the WYNDE4 STAR, noting frequent route confusion when this procedure is issued.
summary: Aircraft X deviated from its filed flight plan by flying the TVC segment of the WYNDE4 arrival without clearance after passing SSM. The reporter states this unauthorized transition has occurred routinely for two years and demands the TVC transition be eliminated from the arrival procedure.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a weather deviation event resulting in the flight crew declaring an emergency, the air carrier pilot expressing extreme dissatisfaction with the ATC handling on his departure.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller training a trainee denied a B747's request for a left weather deviation during departure due to conflicting traffic and wake turbulence, prompting the pilot to declare an emergency and squawk 7700. Although no separation loss occurred, the pilot later complained to the FAA about the controller's decision and airport procedures.

synopsis: A320 Captain reports receiving a release after diverting with a substantial change in ZFW while almost no actual change occurred. Load planning is contacted and the correct ZFW, almost 29,000 pounds heavier, is supplied.
summary: The crew diverted to OKC and discovered a 28,000-pound Takeoff Gross Weight discrepancy between the initial and new flight plans. After Load Planning corrected the Zero Fuel Weight, the flight was re-dispatched on RLS03 and completed uneventfully.

synopsis: A ramp serviceperson awaiting the opening of the main cabin door witnessed the passenger agent who had marshaled the commuter aircraft into the gate performing a walk around while the right engine was still operating, contrary to their operations manual.
summary: A passenger agent performed a walk-around with engine two running while the nose gear was chocked and the main cabin door was open. The reporter identified this as a serious safety infraction violating the Operations Manual, which requires engine shutdown before approaching the cargo pit.

synopsis: Baggage tug driver reports a collision between a bag cart he is pulling and a belt loader, causing damage to the aircraft that is being loaded.
summary: A ground handler pulling baggage carts struck a belt loader's bumper, damaging the aircraft threshold during loading. The incident, caused by a sharp turn without guide men, resulted in the aircraft being taken out of service for repairs and passengers being rebooked.

synopsis: An A300 flight crew elected to return to their departure airport for maintenance when the landing gear failed to retract after takeoff and the increased fuel burn to destination precluded continuing.
summary: The flight crew experienced a landing gear retraction failure during climb-out, prompting a return to the departure airport following ECAM procedures. Maintenance later questioned why the crew did not switch gear systems, but the crew explained the specific ECAM alert dictated a different procedure due to gear positioning issues.

synopsis: A320 Captain experiences an ECAM Status message during approach indicating both normal and alternate brakes are inoperative. A go around is initiated. After go around the ECAM message has changed to AUTO BRK FAULT and a normal landing ensues.
summary: During approach at 1,500 feet AGL, the crew encountered ECAM warnings for normal and alternate brake inop, prompting a go-around. After the ECAM updated to an auto brake fault, the crew completed a normal landing and reported the issue to maintenance.

synopsis: EMB145 First Officer reports a takeoff warning when power is advanced for takeoff and the takeoff is immediately rejected. The Takeoff Configuration Test button had been pushed prior to taking the runway with Takeoff OK enunciated. Nothing can be found out of position and the second attempt is successful.
summary: The flight crew aborted a takeoff at low speed due to a false 'TAKEOFF BRAKE' warning triggered after pressing the TAKEOFF CONFIGURATION button. Maintenance reset the brake system, and the crew subsequently completed a successful takeoff to destination.

synopsis: Multiple distractions, fatigue and administrative equipment breakdowns contributed to the flight crew of a CRJ-700 losing situational awareness during taxi for takeoff at ORD.
summary: A fatigued First Officer and Captain at ORD rushed due to computer delays, causing the Captain to misidentify runways 22L and 28R while the First Officer multitasked. This loss of situational awareness led to a runway incursion where the aircraft crossed hold short lines before Tower intervention and a back-taxi correction.

synopsis: The crew of a Boeing 737-800 was given confusing taxi instructions by Ground Control referencing non-standard markings and procedures that could not be deciphered with the onboard resources available to them on the flight deck.
summary: The flight crew of an Air Carrier aircraft misinterpreted non-standard taxi markings at Salt Lake City, leading to a ground controller intervention after they deviated from the assigned route to Runway 34L. The incident was caused by a lack of charted information regarding the airport's unique colored lines and spot numbers, highlighting a need for standardized markings.

synopsis: DHC8-200 Captain experiences an over torque just after takeoff and elects to shut the engine down and return to the departure airport.
summary: During a ferry flight departure at 400 feet, the pilot experienced a #1 engine torque spike to 116% and yaw, prompting an immediate shutdown and feathering after the First Officer failed to feather it. The crew declared an emergency, requested ILS vectors to complete checklists, and landed single-engine without incident.

synopsis: B777 flight crew reports ATC confusion when an extra flight section uses the same flight number with the addition of an Alpha, on a flight from Europe to North America.
summary: Dispatch assigned similar call signs to two flights, causing ATC confusion and CPDLC login failures across the North Atlantic. Controllers forced a call sign change to the tail number, resulting in persistent identification errors from departure to arrival.

synopsis: An A300 dispatched with the #1 Pack MEL'ed, received a #2 PACK TEMP ADV while climbing and elected to return to the departure airport because they were unable to control the #2 pack.
summary: During climb through 17,000 feet, the crew received an uncontrollable #1 pack overtemp advisory despite following the QRH. They returned to the departure airport and landed safely, noting the pack was already deferred.

synopsis: A B757 EICAS alerted LE SLAT DISAGREE and TE FLAP ASYM after flaps 25 was selected on approach at about the same time as a light to moderate turbulence event. A go-around was executed, the QRH completed and an uneventful landing followed.
summary: During approach, the crew encountered LE Slat Disagree and TE Flap ASYM EICAS messages after selecting flaps 25, possibly triggered by rapid wind changes and airspeed fluctuations. They executed a go-around, completed QRH procedures with gear down, declared an emergency, and landed safely with flaps 20.

synopsis: During the takeoff roll, a B737 nose wheel vibration and something striking the aircraft belly lead the crew to suspect a nose tire failure which ATC confirmed. So, at their destination an emergency was declared and a normal landing completed.
summary: The flight crew experienced a suspected right nose wheel tire failure during takeoff, evidenced by loud noise and debris on the runway. They declared an emergency, continued to their destination, and landed normally with no further issues.

synopsis: When an A320's throttles were set to MAN/FLEX, a Master Caution and 'DING' alerted but the Captain continued the takeoff after the FMC dropped the V speeds because the First Officer did not fully finish the runway change input from SFO 28L to 28R.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a loss of V-speeds on the PFD during takeoff from SFO Runway 28R after the First Officer likely entered the runway change incorrectly. The Captain continued the takeoff at TOGA power, deciding it was safer than aborting at speeds well above V1.

synopsis: An Air Carrier crew took evasive action responding to a TCAS RA at FL340 eastbound near OMEKA Intersection after Gander erroneously issued a climb clearance to a westbound aircraft.
summary: The flight crew received a TCAS RA while climbing toward FL370 after another aircraft, cleared by Gander Radio to climb then return to FL340, intruded on their path. The crew executed a climb in response to the RA, establishing visual contact as the other aircraft descended, and subsequently reported the conflict to ATC.

synopsis: ORD Departure Control asked a B737 if the O'HARE 7 250 KT restriction had been removed and the First Officer responded 'We thought so;' but because of weather and a busy departure he could not actually remember.
summary: The flight crew exceeded the 250 KTS speed restriction while climbing on the O'Hare 7 Departure due to high workload from multiple reroutes, maintenance, and weather issues. The crew could not definitively recall if the speed limitation was released, though the Center Controller confirmed the Departure Controller had not explicitly cleared them for normal speed.

synopsis: Similar call signs and a language barrier between ATC and the flight crew of two aircraft resulted in a military interception of the reporters' flight. The propriety of the flight was established with the intercept pilot and the flight was completed uneventfully.
summary: Air Carrier X Flight ABC was intercepted by a fighter jet south of VESAN while in French airspace at FL320. The pilot attributed the incident to potential controller confusion caused by similar call signs (ABC and ADC) and unclear communications, though the flight remained in contact with ATC throughout.

synopsis: While in icing conditions after takeoff, an EMB-145 CAS alerted WING ANTI-ICE FAIL and BLEED TEMP so the crew declared an emergency and returned to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew declared an emergency shortly after takeoff due to wing anti-ice failure and bleed temperature messages, landing at the departure airport. Post-flight communication delays caused Dispatch to amend the flight plan late, prompting a procedural update to amend plans regardless of flight status.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 tire failed on takeoff FOD'ing an engine so the crew declared an emergency and diverted to a nearby airport. The Dispatcher was not made aware of the divert reason until the crew was on the ground because of the short flight.
summary: A dispatcher learned after landing that a flight diverted due to a tire blowout and engine ingestion on takeoff. The dispatcher could not amend the release or send fuel numbers because the aircraft landed before the emergency was reported, though a record history was filed.

synopsis: A B717 VIA (Versatile Integrated Avionics) #1 failed in flight with numerous failures including the Captain's airspeed, stall warning, autopilot and autothrottles. An emergency was declared while the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: During climb through 10,000 feet, a #1 VIA failure caused multiple system alerts, unreliable airspeed, and loss of autopilot, prompting an emergency return to the departure airport. The crew landed safely with fire trucks following, noting the QRH provided insufficient guidance for the extensive failures.

synopsis: A B717 Via (Versatile Integrated Avionics) 1 failed in flight resulting in the loss of critical flight information so an emergency was declared and the flight continued to its filed destination.
summary: The crew experienced a VIA 1 failure and false system alerts at FL330, causing loss of FMS navigation. They declared an emergency, followed a visual approach to 27R with fire trucks standing by, and landed safely; maintenance later confirmed the VIA 1 failure and an unidentified internal fault.

synopsis: During a late night taxi to the gate after landing, the Captain elected to shutdown the Number 2 engine while the First Officer was performing the After Landing checklist. When the First Officer reached to shut down the Number 2 engine, he mistakenly shutdown the Number 1 engine. The crew recovered by stopping the taxi, starting the APU and restarting the Number 1 engine, followed by a successful taxi to the gate.
summary: The Captain and First Officer, fatigued after an 11-hour duty day, accidentally shut down both engines on the taxiway because the Captain prematurely cut Engine 2 while the First Officer mistakenly cut Engine 1. They recovered by starting the APU and one engine to taxi to the gate, attributing the error to rushing, poor lighting, and fatigue.

synopsis: An EMB-145 returned to the departure airport after the pilots and Flight Attendant heard a banging sound in the aircraft's forward section while at cruise. A previous maintenance test flight for the banging was negative.
summary: The flight crew experienced a recurring banging noise near the nose gear bay during climb and cruise on an aircraft recently returned from maintenance without resolving a prior similar report. The crew diverted back to the departure airport, landing safely, and attributed the issue to inadequate maintenance testing that failed to simulate actual cruise conditions.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain experienced uncontrollable pack overheat, declared emergency and returned to departure airport.
summary: The crew declared an emergency due to an uncontrollable pack overheat and returned to the departure airport. They executed an overweight landing of 167,000 lbs.

synopsis: An Air Carrier crew departed on the ORD7 and accelerated to 300 knots because they had zoomed in on the iPad looking at the altitude restrictions and missed the speed constraint because it would outside of the selected viewing area during the brief.
summary: Pilots flying the ORD7 departure failed to observe a 250 KIAS restriction below 10,000 feet while using an iPad, causing the aircraft to accelerate to 300 KIAS. After ATC queried the speed, the crew slowed to 250 KIAS, attributing the error to missing the restriction due to zooming in on the digital chart.

synopsis: During a gusty crosswind approach, the pilot of a BAE-125-850 carried additional airspeed into the landing. This resulted in floating longer than expected prior to landing and the subsequent slow excursion from the runway into the overrun area. No damage or injuries occurred, and the crew was able to turn and taxi normally to the ramp.
summary: The pilot overran the runway by 10 feet at under 20 knots during landing rollout due to excessive approach speed (REF+15) in gusty winds causing a late touchdown. No damage occurred, and the aircraft taxied to the ramp after a 180-degree turn.

synopsis: B757 Captain describes two single engine returns on the same aircraft when an engine cannot be restarted in flight during a maintenance test flight after Contractor Maintenance.
summary: Two functional check flights on the same aircraft after contractor maintenance resulted in single-engine returns due to an engine valve discrete during inflight restart attempts. Replacing the Fuel Flow Governor failed to fix the issue, prompting engineering to evaluate the fuel pumps while praising the technical crew chiefs' assistance.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew describes an arrival and approach to Runway 5R at MMMX that does not go as depicted or briefed.
summary: The flight crew flying the DATUL2A STAR into Mexico City received rapid ATC clearances that placed them 700 feet below route minimums before being vectored for a no-comm conflict. The crew climbed to meet transition requirements and landed uneventfully, noting that the chaotic sequence of instructions created an unsafe situation.

synopsis: B767-300 Captain experiences a LE SLAT ASYM EICAS message during initial climb. An emergency is declared and flight returns for an overweight landing after complying with QRH procedures.
summary: The flight crew received a LE SLAT ASYM EICAS message after takeoff and declared an emergency. Following unsuccessful QRH troubleshooting, they dumped fuel to enable a safe but overweight landing.

aircraft: Embraer Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reports a TCAS RA arriving SJC from the south at 5,000 FT. Climbing slightly and turning to avoid VFR traffic.
summary: The pilot received a visual approach clearance and was advised to level at 5,000 feet due to climbing VFR traffic. A Traffic Alert and Resolution Advisory occurred, prompting a slight climb to resolve the conflict before a normal landing was completed.

synopsis: A Boeing 737 Captain decided to continue the takeoff when at approximately 110 knots a door warning master caution illuminated. Shortly thereafter, at a speed reported to be no higher than 140 knots, screams were heard emanating from the cabin, the cockpit chime sounded, and the Captain elected to command an abort. Upon inspection, no faults were found other than some tire damage from the high speed rejected takeoff.
summary: The Captain and First Officer performed a high-speed rejected takeoff at 140 KIAS after a main cabin door opened one foot and the master caution illuminated. The aircraft returned to the gate for inspection, which found no door faults but required replacing a damaged main landing gear tire, causing a five-hour delay.

synopsis: During takeoff, an A-319-132 crew noticed the absence of 'MAN FLEX' in the FMA by 30 knots accompanied by a warning chime, a master warning, and an ECAM 'Eng 2 Thrust Lever Disagree' indication. A low speed rejected takeoff was accomplished and the aircraft was returned to the gate for maintenance action.
summary: The First Officer aborted takeoff at 30 knots after the MAN FLEX mode failed to appear and an Eng 2 Thrust Lever Disagree warning illuminated. The crew exited the runway and returned to the gate for maintenance.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer arriving SVVA reports an airborne conflict with departing traffic after being cleared for the ILS approaching the VAL VOR.
summary: The flight crew encountered conflicting VFR traffic while executing a course reversal holding pattern at the VAL VOR during an approach to Runway 10 at SVVA. They manually descended and turned to avoid the traffic due to communication difficulties with Approach Control, then completed the approach and landed safely.

synopsis: A B767 flight crew declared an emergency and proceeded to an appropriate airport when one hydraulic system failed late in their journey.
summary: The enroute aircraft lost one hydraulic system due to fluid loss, prompting an emergency declaration to Center. Approach provided priority vectoring for descent and landing, after which the aircraft stopped on the runway and was towed to the gate.

synopsis: While approaching to land and upon initial configuration of aircraft, the Boeing 737-800 crew received a Master Caution warning and FLT CONT light. The yaw damper had also disconnected and could not be reset. An emergency was declared and all of the appropriate steps were accomplished prior to executing an all flaps up landing at about 180 knots. Aircraft was then taxied to the gate uneventfully.
summary: The pilot reported a flight control malfunction at 9,000 feet during downwind, where the yaw damper disengaged and flaps failed to extend due to asymmetry. After declaring an emergency and executing the all-flaps-up landing checklist, the crew landed safely on Runway 17C and taxied to the gate.

synopsis: An MD82 Captain on an unpressurized ferry flight encountered an opposite direction Citation and responded to TA and RA warnings as well as directives from the First Officer based on visual contact.
summary: During an unpressurized ferry flight at 10,000 feet, the crew received a climb RA and turned left to avoid a Cessna Citation, conflicting with ATC's right turn instruction. The near-miss occurred near a sector border where the aircraft were on different frequencies, and the other pilot appeared unaware of the conflict.

aircraft: McDonnell Douglas Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An air carrier aircraft in cruise at 10,000 MSL on an unpressurized ferry flight suffered a close encounter with an unidentified opposite direction aircraft in a climb.
summary: The crew of an unpressurized aircraft at 10,000 feet received conflicting RA climb commands and ATC right-turn instructions while climbing near a sector border. The First Officer spotted the intruder, prompting the Captain to execute a left turn and descent to avoid a close pass with the other climbing aircraft.

synopsis: An MD-11 enroute from the Philippines to mainland China temporarily lost contact with control as they approached the Hong Kong FIR. An assist from a company flight restored contact.
summary: Pilots en route to RPLC lost contact with Manila Control at SABNO and failed to switch to Hong Kong Control. They regained contact eight minutes later after another aircraft alerted them on guard, prompting a discussion on proactive frequency switching and boundary awareness.

synopsis: CRJ200 Captain reports performing a preflight in the morning and noting three gear pins in the storage closet. After takeoff the left main gear will not retract. Upon returning a fourth gear pin is found installed in the left gear, without a flag attached.
summary: The flight crew discovered a left main gear pin installed after takeoff, causing a gear disagree warning and a return to land. The reporter attributed the incident to a missed pin during the pre-flight inspection and recommended improved maintenance checklists and flagging procedures.

synopsis: A PA-32 pilot flying over the Sierra Nevada mountains encountered mountain waves severe enough to lift him into Class A airspace. He descended out of the incursion when the wave subsided and the terrain below became less of a concern.
summary: A pilot flying a normally-aspirated Piper Lance VFR westbound over the Sierra Nevada inadvertently entered Class A airspace above 19,000 feet while climbing in mountain waves. The pilot immediately descended after realizing the entry, attributing the incident to insufficient preflight planning and situational awareness regarding altitude limits.

synopsis: Reporter described communication problems at ABY that do not allow aircraft and vehicles on the ground to hear each other on the CTAF. In this instance, a near collision with an airport operations vehicle occurred during takeoff. Both the pilot and the vehicle operator announced their intentions on the CTAF, but neither was heard by the other.
summary: A pilot taking off from Runway 22 at an uncontrolled airport narrowly missed an airport operations truck crossing the runway due to mutual CTAF communication failure. The Control Tower Supervisor found the CTAF unreliable, prompting a NOTAM and FAA investigation into the communication issues.

synopsis: C414 pilot reports a loss of power in the right engine during a maintenance test flight for a newly installed left engine. The engine is shut down and the flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: During a maintenance check flight to break in a new left engine, the pilot experienced right engine power loss at 8,500 feet and returned to the airport. The engine was shut down per checklist, and a safe landing was achieved after maintenance identified a blown prop accumulator as the cause.

synopsis: An RV-6A pilot, utilizing an iPad for navigation on a VFR cross country entered a TFR enroute despite his belief the tablet had been properly updated to display restricted airspace immediately prior to his departure.
summary: A professional pilot flew directly through a firefighting TFR near SBA Class C airspace because the Foreflight app on his iPad failed to display the restriction despite an internet connection. The pilot was unaware of the violation until contacted by SBA Approach, attributing the incident to an unexplained technical glitch preventing the TFR update.

synopsis: Despite regular and specific observation of a normal landing gear extension, the pilot of a Cessna 421 suffered the collapse of the left main gear during landing roll out.
summary: The pilot landed a single-engine aircraft after verifying gear down, but the left gear collapsed during rollout at the 2,000-foot marker, causing the propeller to strike the ground. The aircraft skidded into a grassy area with no injuries, and the pilot attributed the failure to insufficient preflight and annual gear inspections.

synopsis: A mis-rigged elevator trim following major maintenance, which resulted in full nose down trim when indicating in the 'takeoff' range, contributed to the inability of the pilot of an M20 to remain airborne after lift off. Upon abandoning the takeoff and attempting to land on the remaining runway one prop blade struck the runway.
summary: During a ferry flight for annual inspection, the aircraft bounced and porpoised after takeoff due to uncalibrated trim set to full down despite cockpit indicators showing takeoff position. The pilot regained control with one propeller tip grazing the runway.

synopsis: When a failed glideslope indicator prevented landing at their destination the pilot of a CE421 elected to divert to an airport other than the planned alternate because it had ceilings that would not require a glideslope. The longer diversion made the fuel situation critical and ATC wasn't sufficiently responsive to their needs. An emergency was then declared.
summary: The pilot of a six-person aircraft declared a fuel emergency after a glideslope failure and subsequent ATC delays prevented a timely landing. The reporter attributed the unsafe situation to inadequate assistance and undue delay while managing minimum fuel and equipment failure.

synopsis: VFR C172 inbound to a Towered airport, described a conflict event when communications between pattern traffic and ATC was confused and not clear.
summary: A Cessna pilot on a straight-in approach to Runway 26 encountered a converging Cherokee after the controller misidentified the Cessna as the Cherokee to following traffic. The pilot broke off the approach and landed safely, attributing the near-midair collision to complacency and assuming the controller managed separation.

aircraft: Grumman Corp Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: The pilot of a Grumman Avenger declared an emergency when his engine failed to restart after switching to the center tank following the anticipated depletion of fuel from the left tank. While setting up for an emergency landing his trouble shooting lead to selecting the right tank and the engine immediately returned to life.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine failure at 6,500 feet due to a dry left tank and an improperly engaged fuel selector switch. After declaring an emergency and gliding toward the airport, the engine restarted once the selector was physically moved to the right tank, allowing for a safe landing.

synopsis: A Dispatcher reported that a non-GPS equipped B757-200 he became responsible for after shift change, was issued an RNAV departure which was NOTAMed GPS only by either ATC or the Dispatcher.
summary: A relieving Dispatcher identified a NOTAM prohibiting a non-GPS aircraft from using an RNAV departure, contradicting the Captain's claim of ATC clearance. The original Dispatcher admitted he did not plan or file that specific departure, though the Captain had signed the release.

synopsis: SJC Controller observed an apparent early turn by a corporate jet off Runway 30 assigned a SJC9 SID resulting in a conflict with a previous departure aircraft.
summary: A Gulfstream V departing San Jose Runway 30 on the SJC9 procedure climbed rapidly and turned early, passing close to a preceding CRJ900. While ATC suspected a pilot deviation, the Gulfstream crew maintained they turned at the correct FMS point and remained in visual contact with the aircraft ahead.

synopsis: TRACON Controller providing training failed to note that the trainee did not issue a turn on vector, resulting in a conflict with parallel traffic, a new arrival procedure was cited as contributing to the error.
summary: A pilot and trainee on an aircraft at 4,000 feet experienced a loss of separation with Aircraft Y due to ATC errors in vectoring and altitude assignments. The crew initiated evasive action before a TCAS RA, leveling at 3,400 feet with no injuries, attributing the incident to poor ATC situational awareness and conflicting instructions.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: D10 Controller described a STARS aircraft display anomaly.
summary: An air traffic controller observed a VFR aircraft 7-8 NM northeast of ADS at 1,600 feet displaying erratic STARS symbols and double-printed altitudes. The controller confirmed the display anomaly with ADS Tower and reported the issue to management.

synopsis: ZNY Controller described a probable airspace error when incorrectly transmitting a data communication, datalink.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a descent clearance for a B767 from FL340 to FL310 but accidentally pressed VHF instead of SEND while using Ocean21. Consequently, the aircraft crossed the LPAZ boundary at the wrong altitude, a mistake attributed to the ATOP system interface.

synopsis: SCT Controller described a developing conflict with LAX departures when one aircraft failed to turn as required, the reporter listing 'Fusion' RADAR as one contributing factor.
summary: An air traffic controller observed a B737-800 failing to turn to the required 220-degree heading at SMO 160R while a B737-700 departed on a conflicting 250-degree track. The controller issued a southbound turn to the B737-800 to restore separation, attributing the error to frequent pilot non-compliance and potential difficulties with the Fusion system.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew read back the takeoff clearance and started their takeoff roll from Runway 31C at MDW, ATC directed an aircraft on final for Runway 4R to go-around. Flight crew suspected the takeoff clearance may have been intended for an aircraft lined up and awaiting clearance for takeoff from Runway 4R, thus precluding the use of the runway for the go-around aircraft.
summary: The pilot reported that at MDW, the tower controller inadvertently cleared their aircraft for takeoff on runway 31C instead of a crossing aircraft on 4R. The controller quickly recovered by instructing the aircraft on final to go-around and re-clearing the pilot, resulting in a safe departure with no near-miss.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports an emergency vehicle crossing their runway as they are about to touch down. The approach is continued to landing as the vehicle is moving quickly. The Tower Controller sited a communication error as the cause of the incident.
summary: During the final approach, an emergency vehicle rapidly crossed the runway at midfield while the crew was below 100 feet. The pilot flying landed uneventfully after the vehicle cleared, and the Tower Controller attributed the incursion to a communication error with the truck.

synopsis: A B737-700 left bleed tripped four times climbing to FL380 and the pack was turned OFF. Shortly thereafter the right bleed tripped several times and finally with both bleeds OFF an emergency was declared and the flight diverted but not before the cabin exceeded 14,000 FT causing the masks to drop.
summary: The flight crew experienced repeated left and right bleed trips and pack failures during climb and cruise, leading to an emergency descent and diversion. Cabin altitude exceeded 14,000 feet, causing passenger oxygen mask deployment, but the aircraft landed uneventfully after maintenance took over at the gate.

synopsis: When the B737-700 flight attendants reported smoke in the cabin the flight crew immediately donned oxygen masks, initiated the immediate action and follow up checklist items during which the smoke dissipated. They declared an emergency but, since the smoke had dissipated and the source appeared to be contained, continued to a safe landing at their destination where they canceled the emergency and turned the aircraft over to Maintenance.
summary: During cruise at FL300, the crew encountered cabin smoke and executed QRH procedures, including isolating the right pack and turning off galley power. The smoke dissipated, allowing the aircraft to land safely at ZZZ with no injuries after declaring an emergency.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported a wake vortex encounter on descent into BNA that provided enough distraction they missed a crossing restriction.
summary: The flight crew encountered wake turbulence on the SWFFT 1 arrival into BNA, causing an autopilot disengagement and a 25-degree bank. The First Officer recovered control, but the crew crossed LENSE at FL260 instead of the required FL240 due to an MCP setting error, prompting a revised descent clearance from ATC.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew and the Dispatcher involved report a go-around at ABQ due to severe turbulence on approach to Runway 26. The crew continues on a westerly heading to avoid the weather and eventually requests direct to their alternate, but does not proceed as cleared continuing to discuss options. ATC questions the crew, but by this time flights are getting in and the crew elects to land at ABQ and does so safely.
summary: The crew executed a go-around on approach to ABQ due to severe turbulence and weather, causing a 20-minute communication gap with Dispatch. After coordinating with ATC and receiving a favorable PIREP, the flight successfully landed on a second attempt with no injuries.

synopsis: A B757 Captain voiced his displeasure with the inability of his Dispatcher to provide him with a flight plan release that did not contain a SID for which his aircraft was not eligible due to lack of GPS navigation, the apparent stumbling block being the intransigence of the airline's recently introduced flight planning software.
summary: A pilot reported that new flight planning software caused Dispatch to file an illegal GPS-required RNAV SID for a non-GPS aircraft. This triggered a conflict with ATC, forcing the pilot to bypass Dispatch to secure a legal clearance, resulting in significant delays and passenger dissatisfaction.

synopsis: B767-300 Captain reports accepting an aircraft for the first flight after the winglet modification and finding the NAV database is out of date with the standby database even older. The reporter asks that the database be replaced and a lengthy delay ensues.
summary: The crew and maintenance encountered an expired NAV database and a fuel pump fault on a post-modification aircraft, causing significant delays. The database issue stemmed from maintenance oversight regarding expiration dates, while the fuel pump fault required a return to blocks after the crew could not complete the required DMP steps.

synopsis: A B717 left engine compressor stalled at about 120 KTS on takeoff so a high speed reject was completed, and the aircraft returned to the gate accompanied by Airport Rescue and Fire.
summary: The flight crew aborted takeoff at 120 KTS due to a left engine compressor stall that caused a loud bang, left veer, and visible flames. Fire trucks inspected the aircraft as a precaution, and the crew noted overheated right brakes before switching to a replacement aircraft.

synopsis: During climb through FL280 the crew of a EMB-145LR began to notice a rumbling, fluttering, and slight knocking in the flight controls that seemed to increase with altitude. An emergency was declared and the aircraft was diverted to a nearby airport. As they descended the abnormal condition diminished and eventually ceased.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced flight control fluttering and rumbling while climbing through FL280 in VMC, suspecting a high-speed or high-altitude issue. They diverted and declared an emergency, but symptoms resolved below FL200, and post-flight inspections revealed no abnormalities.

synopsis: A MD-80 pilot declared an emergency and executed a high speed approach after flight attendants reported a rubber burning odor in the cabin.
summary: The flight crew responded to a rubber burning smell reported by cabin crew by executing the Smoke/Fumes Checklist and declaring an emergency. They requested Airfield Rescue and Firefighters and exceeded 250 KTS below 10,000 FT to expedite the descent.

synopsis: A B767-300 EICAS alerted R OIL FILTER so the crew complied with the QRH, shut the engine down, declared an emergency and diverted to an enroute airport.
summary: The flight crew enroute at FL400 in a Boeing 767 received a continuous 'R OIL FILTER' EICAS alert. They performed the QRH procedure, shut down the engine, declared an emergency, and completed an uneventful approach and landing.

synopsis: A B757 returned to its departure airport when the flight crew received and EICAS ELEV FEEL message.
summary: The 757 crew received an 'ELEV FEEL' EICAS message after takeoff and requested maintenance advice from Dispatch. Dispatch instructed a return to the departure airport, where the crew landed below maximum weight and logged the event.

synopsis: MD83 Captain experiences a Tail Comp Temp Hi light shortly after takeoff. An emergency is declared, QRH procedures are complied with and the flight returns safely to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew declared an emergency shortly after takeoff when the Tail Comp Temp Hi light illuminated below 1,000 feet AGL. They returned for an immediate landing with ARFF standby; the light extinguished in flight, and maintenance inspected the tail area after the aircraft cleared the runway.

synopsis: A MD-11 crew suspected the First Officer's CADC was intermittently malfunctioning during an IMC descent near thunderstorms after IAS appeared on both PFDs, the autothrottle, autopilots (2) and Captain's Flight Director failed. Finally an emergency was declared after the EICAS alerted WSHEAR DET FAIL, SEL ELEV MAN and SEL FLAP LIM OVRD. Systems returned to normal at about 10,000 FT.
summary: The crew encountered multiple airspeed and autopilot failures during a weather-diverted descent and hold at FL240, caused by an unreliable First Officer CADC. They declared an emergency, manually stabilized the aircraft using standby instruments, and completed the approach after repeated system alerts.

synopsis: An aircraft descending on the MEM LTOWN6 had an uncommanded descent while the aircraft was beginning the turn at CLARK toward DIGLE because the DINKE constraint compliance required rapid FMS calculations and automation response.
summary: During the LTOWN6 arrival, the crew experienced a rapid pitch-over and acceleration to 240 KIAS while descending to CLARK with autopilot and autothrottles engaged. The pilots manually disconnected automation and used speedbrakes to correct the deviation, attributing the event to imprecise Profile mode performance on this arrival.

synopsis: A LJ36 flight crew failed to receive positive gear retracted indications after takeoff. After multiple recycling and Tower flybys they elected to remain in the area to burn fuel to max landing weight and land. The landing was completed but the nose gear was cocked some 80 degrees from straight ahead. The aircraft was towed to the ramp.
summary: The pilot reported that after takeoff, the nose gear unsafe light remained illuminated with doors open and the wheel assembly misaligned. An emergency was declared, and the aircraft landed safely with no injuries, though the nose tire was found at an 80-degree angle to the centerline.

synopsis: A C550 crew inadvertently crossed an active runway forcing another aircraft's go around because, after reading back their taxi clearance, they followed what they believed was the cleared route for takeoff.
summary: The flight crew crossed an active runway while taxiing, causing another aircraft to go around. The Ground Controller attributed the incident to a pilot deviation resulting from the crew following what they believed was the correct taxi route.

synopsis: A C-172RG landing gear did not extend for landing so the instructor and student burned fuel down, completed all checklists and made a successful gear up landing.
summary: During a training flight, a simulated engine failure led to a landing gear malfunction where the gear failed to extend after retraction. Despite troubleshooting with checklists and the emergency pump, the crew prepared for a gear-up landing after confirming no gear down indication.

synopsis: An M-7 landed with faulty emergency brakes locked and had a prop strike during the sudden stop.
summary: The pilot reported that the aircraft touched down with locked brakes due to a faulty emergency brake release, resulting in a propeller strike.

synopsis: An A320 crew declared an emergency and returned to the departure airport after flight attendants reported smoke in the cabin and in the after landing confusion may have crossed a parallel runway without clearance.
summary: Following an emergency return due to cabin smoke, the flight crew crossed Runway 30R without the First Officer recalling a specific clearance, while the Captain believed one was issued. The reporter attributes this confusion to high task loading and simultaneous communications with the Tower and crash-fire-rescue on different frequencies.

synopsis: A Military helicopter pilot reported a near miss with a glider at 9,200 FT over 0E0 after making three CTAF position reports approaching the airport.
summary: A VFR aircraft overflying airport 0E0 at 9,200 feet MSL had a near miss with an unreported glider at the same altitude. The glider was climbing and turning left, prompting the pilot to descend rapidly to 8,000 feet after making blind radio calls on CTAF.

synopsis: After attempting to demonstrate a Zero-G maneuver and possibly going into Negative-G regime, a PA-28R pilot noted that the elevator trim felt tight, but controls were otherwise normal. Maintenance personnel subsequently advised that the battery became dislodged and acid had spilled onto the control cables.
summary: A pilot performing a zero-G maneuver at 3,000 feet experienced tight trim controls caused by negative G-forces dislodging the rear battery. Spilled battery acid corroded the control cables, leading the pilot to cancel future attempts and note a lack of proper guidance in the POH.

synopsis: C172 pilot reports discovering airborne that a sporting event TFR is in effect and is aided by an N90 Controller. TFR's had been specifically checked prior to departure with none reported.
summary: A pilot planning a VFR flight down the Hudson was told no TFRs existed but later discovered an active TFR at X Stadium. The pilot received radar service to divert west and noted that Flight Service dissemination of scheduled game events needs improvement.

synopsis: A11 Controller described a conflict event involving IFR and VFR traffic complicated by local procedures and airport locations.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported a potential conflict between a C207 requesting descent from 2,200 feet and an A319 on final to Runway 15 at Anchorage. The controller denied the descent and issued traffic advisories, noting the C207 initially did not see the A319 due to scattered clouds, though the A319 descended to 2,000 feet and passed safely ahead.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ZJX Controller voiced concern regarding the lack of timely and accurate information referenced the status of R2903, the reporter listing several communication breakdowns within the facility.
summary: A D15 Controller at Ocala Sector discovered R2903 was active to FL320 after a Supervisor failed to verify the status with Missions Sector. The reporter cited a communication breakdown and the Supervisor's lack of urgency as causes for potential unsafe aircraft proximity or airspace violations.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a helicopter off field landing event, the reporter indicating he should have been more insistent on IFR handling regardless of the pilots requests.
summary: An air traffic controller working Arrival, Departure, and Satellite positions lost contact with a VFR helicopter that refused vectoring for an approach despite having only 2 miles visibility. The controller attributed the incident to failing to insist on IFR procedures or an approach when the pilot could not see the Class D airport.

synopsis: DEN Ground Control issued a B737 crew clearance to the gate after it landed on 16R then issued it an emergency stop after the aircraft taxied into the Runway 34R Runway Safety Clearance Zone while a BE1900 on a Runway 34R final executed a go around.
summary: The flight crew crossed the hold short line for Runway 34R at DEN while taxiing during a runway change, failing to see an approaching Beech 1900 due to distraction and lack of hold short instructions. The controller urgently ordered a stop, and the Beech 1900 subsequently executed a go-around.
