summary: A pilot reported three A330 incidents where battery-only power on the ground caused VHF 1 failure, preventing evacuation checklist completion and rescue coordination. The reporter requested a new FOM policy for ground communication loss to address this documented safety gap.

synopsis: A320 First Officer describes errors made during taxi out and takeoff from JFK after a continuous duty overnight, during which minimal rest was obtained.
summary: A fatigued flight crew on a continuous duty period missed the Breezy Point climb procedure during departure from JFK due to taxi errors, frequency changes, and rushing tasks. The aircraft inadvertently entered LGA airspace before ATC corrected the heading, with the pilot citing insufficient rest and compounded distractions as the cause.

synopsis: An EMB-145 EICAS alerted HYD 2 LOW QTY followed by ENG 2 PUMP FAIL while at cruise so an emergency was declared and the flight continued to the filed destination for an uneventful emergency landing.
summary: The crew experienced a Hydraulic System 2 failure enroute due to a belly leak, resulting in lost flight controls and braking capability. They declared an emergency, landed safely with reduced braking effectiveness, and were met by ARFF.

synopsis: An EMB-145 Captain rejected the takeoff after the EICAS alerted E2 ATTCS NO MARGIN meaning the Alternate Takeoff Thrust Control System (ATTCS) has no margin for ITT or N2 to attain higher thrust should it be triggered.
summary: The flight crew aborted takeoff at 60 knots due to an EICAS "E2 ATTCS NO MARGIN" message on an aircraft with an existing Engine 2 MEL. The pilot attributed a slight delay in reaction time to the pre-existing MEL, though the aircraft was safely stopped and returned to the gate.

synopsis: A B737 Captain reports the EGPWS RAAS is a safety hazard because it interferes with important communications in untimely circumstances.
summary: A 737 crew holding short of runway XXR could not hear a Tower takeoff clearance because the Runway Awareness and Advisory System (RAAS) activated. The pilot reported that the RAAS volume prevented communication, describing the system as a safety hazard that frequently blocks critical instructions.

synopsis: A B767 crew detected an electrical burning odor taxing out but could not verify it. After leveling at cruise, the odor returned so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport where Maintenance found the Forward EE Compartment fan had failed.
summary: The flight crew detected an electrical burning smell during takeoff preparation and again 22 minutes into the flight, prompting an emergency return for an overweight landing. Maintenance identified a seized forward EE Equipment Cooling fan with a popped circuit breaker as the cause.

synopsis: An MD-11 nose wheel steering began leaking on short final draining Hydraulic System 1 fluid and causing a HYD-1 alert so the Captain landed and had the aircraft towed to the ramp.
summary: The Captain took control during short final after Hydraulic System 1 failed, landing the aircraft with a nosewheel fluid leak. The crew stopped on Taxiway S, where maintenance pinned the landing gear and towed the plane following a probable unpreventable steering mechanism failure.

synopsis: An EMB-145 Captain realized that FL350 was not an authorized cruise altitude with a pack inoperative so he descended to FL250 in compliance with the MEL.
summary: The Captain realized during cruise that the aircraft was cleared to FL350 despite a Pack 1 MEL limiting altitude to FL250. The crew contacted ATC to descend to FL250, and the flight continued without incident.

synopsis: CE560 Captain experiences frozen elevator trim during initial descent from FL410. The Jammed Elevator Trim emergency checklist was complied with and the crew landed on the longest runway at their destination. The trim remains frozen after engine shutdown.
summary: During descent through FL390, the flight crew encountered a frozen elevator trim system, likely due to cold temperatures, which rendered electric and manual trimming ineffective. The pilots manually controlled the aircraft, completed the emergency checklist, and landed safely on the longest runway without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: When someone failed to actuate the autofiling to enroute ATC centers function of flight plans by dispatchers a number of trans-Pacific flights departed without ATC coordination, causing pilots, ATC, and dispatchers to play catch up.
summary: Flight Planning Support disabled the autofiling function, removing AFTN addresses from dispatch releases and preventing flight plans from reaching enroute ATC centers like RJJJ. This caused a significant workload increase for the PM Dispatcher, who had to manually re-file plans for flights already enroute.

synopsis: After landing on ZGSZ Runway 16 and taxiing on R the crew turned the incorrect direction for Route 1 at Runway 15/44 because the Route 1 and 2 signs appeared reversed and the crew did not see the airport route chart.
summary: The flight crew, after landing, turned right onto Runway 15/33 following taxi signs for Route 1, contradicting the Parking Stands Diagram which showed Route 1 as a left turn. The controller questioned the maneuver, revealing a conflict between the signage and the diagram that caused the incorrect taxi path.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reports that his EFB using Commercial 1 charts does not depict taxiways and holding points that are routinely used by Ground Controllers at OMDB.
summary: The flight crew landed at OMDB and experienced a taxi delay because the Commercial 1 EFB chart failed to depict instructed holding points KC and KA. The crew stopped to verify locations, causing ground congestion, and subsequently reverted to Commercial 2 paper charts due to the EFB's inadequacies.

synopsis: B777 crew reports landing on Runway 9 at MEM and being instructed to roll to the end then left off and Taxiway V to the gate. Once clear the crew is told to stop by the Tower and advised that Taxiway V is not suitable for B777 aircraft. Wing walkers and a follow me truck are provided and taxi to the gate is completed.
summary: A B777 crew at MEM turned left onto Taxiway Victor after landing on Runway 9, violating a wingspan restriction. ATC stopped the aircraft, and it was escorted to the gate by wing walkers due to unclear chart markings regarding the taxiway limitation.

synopsis: A320 Captain reports departing MIA without a revision to their PDC issued via Departure ATIS. ATIS requested via ACARS is Arrival ATIS and did not contain the revision.
summary: The flight crew departed MIA on an Airbus and was instructed by Departure Control to hold a heading instead of flying the RNAV departure. The crew reported the clearance was not received via PDC or Tower, noting they had inadvertently selected Arrival ATIS via MCDU instead of the Departure ATIS containing the amendment.

synopsis: A319 First Officer reports the holding pattern created by his aircraft at FL310 has a 23 NM diameter. The aircraft is slowed from 260 KTS to 220 KTS with no change in the pattern. The flight path is finally tightened up using the heading knob but the depicted pattern remains unchanged.
summary: The flight crew encountered an oversized holding pattern on the FMS while enroute at FL310 due to a suspected software bug. They manually tightened the turn to correct the pattern before receiving a direct clearance, noting this issue had occurred previously on an A319.

synopsis: EMB145 First Officer describes a smoke and fume event while at cruise altitude. QRH procedures are very effective at eliminating the smoke and the flight diverts to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The flight crew diverted an aircraft en route at cruise altitude after experiencing cockpit and cabin smoke with a burning odor, likely triggered by a noise heard mid-fuselage. They landed safely at ZZZ without injuries, though the crew criticized ground operations for delayed gate assignment and pressure to duplicate the fault immediately.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reports being cleared via the TWF1 departure from SLC with an added speed restriction of 230 KTS. Passing SHOLZ at 10,000 FT the crew is issued an unrestricted climb to FL230. Passing 17,000 FT the crew is admonished for exceeding 230 KTS.
summary: During an RNAV departure from SLC, a controller's ambiguous clearance to cancel restrictions caused confusion over speed limits, leading to conflicting instructions and increased pilot workload. The Center Controller later apologized for the errors, which stemmed from non-standard phraseology and redundant PDC data conflicting with the published procedure.

synopsis: MD80 Captain experiences an engine failure at 5,000 feet on departure. The engine is shut down and the flight returns safely to the departure airport. Both engines had exceeded EGT limits on the previous departure and had been allowed to continue without any inspection required.
summary: The pilot reported a right engine failure during climb-out, likely caused by prior over-temperature events under the MTO program without a required maintenance inspection. The crew executed an emergency return and landed safely with no injuries, though the aircraft was later grounded for inspection.

synopsis: MD11 flight crew departing LFPG on the Oaple 3A RNAV departure is informed by ATC that they are off course. The crew can detect no errors and their map display shows they are on course.
summary: The flight crew departed LFPG on Runway 27L via the OPALE 3A RNAV departure, maintaining NAV mode and tracking the magenta line. Departure Control incorrectly advised they were 1.5 miles off course, but the crew confirmed their position was correct, concluding the controller was mistaken.

synopsis: The lead Flight Attendant reports discovering a passenger who has been designated a 'customer of size' sitting in the emergency exit row, although the passenger does not appear to fit the classification. The Flight Attendant manual is not clear on the subject and the passenger is allowed to remain. After the flight it is determined that the COS designation is the determining factor and the passenger should have been moved.
summary: A pilot and flight attendants discovered a "Seat Reserved" sign for a Customer of Size (COS) in an overwing exit row during pre-takeoff checks. Although the passenger did not need a seatbelt extension, the crew allowed him to remain there due to manual ambiguity, later confirming that COS designation prohibits exit row seating.

synopsis: B747 Flight Attendant reports falling while descending the steps from the upper deck due to a failed light on the third step from the bottom. Other flight attendants reportedly fell or stumbled during the same flight.
summary: Multiple flight attendants, including the reporter and Purser, fell down the aircraft stairs during the cruise phase due to missing lighting on step two. This caused them to misjudge the step count and fall three steps, resulting in injuries to the neck, back, and knees, though the issue was deferred after the flight.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: While flying to SLC a light twin aircraft lost reception on both GPS receivers and while resetting them climbed through his assigned 15,000 FT altitude.
summary: A pilot flying to SLC inadvertently deviated 500 feet above the assigned 15,000 feet altitude during climb. The deviation occurred because the pilot lost situational awareness while troubleshooting a dual GPS failure.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A Ercoupe pilot flying out of a high altitude Arizona airport intending to sight see over even higher terrain found himself barely able to avoid ground obstacles while in mountainous terrain and unable to maintain altitude.
summary: A pilot conducting a VFR sightseeing flight in a mountain valley encountered a sudden sinkhole of air, forcing a low-altitude escape that resulted in a near-miss with a snow road reflector post. The pilot attributed the incident to a lack of flight briefing and insufficient safety margins regarding performance factors.

synopsis: C182 pilot climbing out over the airport with skydivers experiences a partial loss of engine power and glides back after declaring an emergency.
summary: The pilot experienced a partial loss of engine power at 6,000 feet while climbing over the airport. After declaring an emergency, the pilot idled the engine and landed without incident, resulting in no damage to persons or property.

synopsis: EMB500 pilot reports descending below the MEA after passing RLG on the LDA DME Runway 25 at EGE due to terrain depiction clutter on the chart. ZDV issues a low altitude alert and the altitude is corrected.
summary: The pilot, descending into Eagle on the LDA 25 approach, received a low altitude alert after initially setting 12,900 feet instead of the required 13,800 feet. The error occurred because terrain depictions obscured the altitude on the approach plate, but the pilot corrected the altitude and continued the flight uneventfully.

synopsis: General Aviation pilot described multiple contact attempts with ZJX. The reporter suggested more ATC radio equipment be installed in Southwestern Georgia.
summary: A pilot flying a Garmin G1000-equipped aircraft from Jacksonville to Tupelo missed a handoff to Atlanta Center due to poor radio reception on Jacksonville Center frequencies. The pilot eventually contacted Atlanta Center after hearing a Guard frequency call, attributing the communication failure to insufficient transmitter coverage in Southwestern Georgia.

synopsis: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports he installed an incorrect Centralized Fault Display Interface Unit (CFDIU) in an A320 that had chronic, intermittent fault messages. The CFDIU had passed all required Operational Tests. The merged air carrier's Illustrated Parts Catalog (IPC) was found to be confusing with incorrect reference data.
summary: A technician installed an incorrect Centralized Fault Display Interface Unit on an A320 due to confusing Illustrated Parts Catalog notes and unfamiliarity with merged carrier manuals. The error was later identified, the wrong part was replaced, and the company corrected the manual system.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic reports how his lack of knowledge of a reference in the Fault Isolation Manual (FIM) for cockpit window pressure squeals, contributed to his not performing a proper cabin High Pressure Differential Pressure Check on a B757-200 aircraft. The Captain's left sliding window area had chronic pressure squeals.
summary: Mechanics inspected a B757-200 after a pilot reported a squeal at the L-2 window at 17,000 feet. During a pressurization check, they inadvertently over-pressurized by 2 PSI, but a subsequent Boeing-approved inspection at another base found no damage.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a MVA infraction when issuing a descend to an emergency Air Carrier with a possible cabin fire. The reporter did not expect the rapid descent toward the diversion airport.
summary: A B757 crew declared an emergency and diverted due to electrical smoke from a galley oven, while the ATC controller admitted to allowing a rapid descent through a 10,200 MVA block. The crew turned off galley power, landed safely, and reported the smoke dissipated with no external smoke observed by ATC.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier Captain grabbed a toddler who nearly fell through the opening between the rubber jetway bumper and the aircraft door frame because the gap between the two was too wide.
summary: A flight attendant stopped deplaning after a toddler fell into a widening gap between the aircraft and jetway at the main cabin door. The attendant caught the child, prompting a recommendation to limit the gap to one inch on both sides of the door to prevent future falls.

synopsis: A B737-700 inbound to BUR suffered a close encounter with a C210 conducting an MAP from VNY. The C210 had failed to follow the published MAP. Avoidance directives from ATC were in conflict with those from TCAS.
summary: A B737 crew executing an ILS approach to BUR received a TCAS 'descend' RA after ATC issued conflicting climb instructions due to a C210's incorrect missed approach from VNY. The crew prioritized the RA over ATC commands, avoiding a collision with the C210 which had descended into their protected airspace.

synopsis: A B737-700 flight crew, cleared by a PDC to depart ABQ on the '...MNZNO departure, maintain 9,000 FT...' was re-cleared after takeoff to 'climb to FL200' by Departure Control. This clearance was given prior to YUGLO which is restricted to be crossed 'at or below 9,000 FT. Confusion ensued as the flight crew was uncertain whether departure's clearance relieved them from the restriction at YUGLO.
summary: The flight crew departed ABQ on the MNZNO RNAV SID and climbed to 9,300 feet after ATC cleared them to FL200 without "climb via" verbiage. The crew descended to 9,000 feet after confirming with ATC that published restrictions still applied, citing confusion over whether the clearance deleted SID altitude limits.

synopsis: B737 First Officer as the pilot flying takes over ATC communication also so the the Captain can discuss a door issue a Flight Attendant. Passing through 10,000 FT the cabin altitude warning horn sounds. An emergency is declared and the flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: The Pilot Flying and Captain experienced a cabin altitude warning shortly after takeoff while discussing a door issue with no overhead lights. They descended to 10,000 feet, declared an emergency, and returned for an overweight landing after completing checklists.

synopsis: LAS Air Carrier arrival voiced a complaint regarding ATC's runway assignment noting the tail wind factor that caused a go around.
summary: The crew of a Boeing 737-700 executed a go-around at LAS due to an 18-knot tailwind on Runway 7R, which exceeded limits despite Tower clearance. After landing on Runway 19L, the crew turned onto the wrong taxiway due to unfamiliarity and poor signage before correcting the error.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reports a go around at TBPB when both the localizer and glide slope fail during the ILS approach to Runway 9 in IMC. The crew is able to land visually on the next approach.
summary: The pilot experienced a loss of ILS glide slope and azimuth in IMC conditions while on approach to TBPB. The crew elected to go-around and subsequently completed a visual approach to land.

synopsis: MD11 flight crew experiences the loss of the number three hydraulic system while configuring for landing. A go-around is initiated, the QRH is consulted and the gear is manually extended.
summary: The pilot lost the #3 hydraulic system while configuring for landing, necessitating a go-around. Following QRH procedures, the crew manually extended the landing gear.

synopsis: During descent for landing a B767-200 developed a cabin dirty socks odor which was detected by both flight attendants and passengers.
summary: A deadheading crew member and passengers on a return flight detected a moldy, acidic odor in the cabin 20 minutes prior to landing. The flight attendant informed the captain, leading to a rapid landing with no reported illness or adverse reactions among occupants.

synopsis: A Maintenance Manager was informed the Nose Gear Safety pin was not being installed in the Nose Landing Gear (NLG) overcenter link during tow movement of their Gulfstream G-200 aircraft. FBO Contract Maintenance and Ramp Service providers were not aware of the Gulfstream Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM) nose gear pin requirement.
summary: A Maintenance Manager reported that FBOs and aircrews at ZZZ and ZZZ1 are not installing the required nose safety pin (P/N 23122-000-00) on Gulfstream G200 aircraft during towing, contrary to the Maintenance Manual. The reporter identified this non-compliance as a safety issue requiring communication to FBOs and crews or a manual revision.

synopsis: C172 pilot experienced a runway incursion at LGB. Reporter stated confusing signage was a contributing factor.
summary: A pilot landing a C-172 on Runway 30 at Long Beach (LGB) turned left onto the displaced threshold of active Runway 25L due to ambiguous signage and lack of double yellow lines. The Tower corrected the pilot, highlighting a runway incursion risk caused by the airport's complex layout and frequent simultaneous runway operations.

synopsis: ZAB Controller described an unsafe condition during extensive flow control limitations for LAX, the reporter noted the variances of several flow measures and the pitfalls of each effort.
summary: An air traffic controller managing LAX arrivals reported spacing conflicts between an A320, two CRJs, and other traffic due to TMU scheduling errors and freeze horizon limitations. The controller attributed the excessive vectoring and a near-miss point-out on a B737 to incompatible time-based metering and miles-in-trail restrictions.

synopsis: D10 Controller voiced concern regarding the continuous, and sometimes false, Conflict/Low Altitude Alerts that are occurring with the new STARS system.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a false Conflict Alert between an E135 descending to 3,000 feet and a VFR aircraft at 2,000 feet within the Bravo airspace. The controller attributed the alert to the new STARS system, noting that frequent false alarms cause controllers to ignore warnings, potentially missing real conflicts.

synopsis: B757 flight crew holding short of Runway 28L at SFO reports a ground conflict with an A330 landing 28L. The B757 crew is cleared to cross before the A330 arrives at the same taxiway. An Airbus on final is issued a go-around.
summary: The First Officer reported a potential runway incursion at SFO while taxiing to cross Runway 28L after landing, where an A330 was still on the landing roll. The crew stopped just short of the runway because the A330 likely overshot its exit point, and the Tower failed to identify the conflict or inform the crew of the traffic.

synopsis: The flight crew of a B737NG conducted a high speed rejected takeoff when the 1L cabin door opened approximately one foot during the takeoff roll.
summary: A 737NG crew rejected takeoff near MATOG weight after a door warning and loud screaming indicated the 1L door opened one foot at 110 KTS. The Captain executed a smooth RTO, cleared the runway, and returned to the gate with maintenance standing by.

synopsis: A321 Captain describes an encounter with unexpected moderate to severe turbulence at FL330 causing the aircraft to climb 900 FT before returning to assigned altitude.
summary: The flight crew encountered unforecast heavy turbulence west of GLD while deviating for weather, causing autopilot disengagement and a 900-foot altitude deviation. Although the First Officer notified ATC, no injuries occurred, and the aircraft returned to FL330 after the event.

synopsis: An EMB-145 flight crew returned to their departure airport for maintenance when advised by a deadheading pilot that fuel was leaking, apparently from a tank vent on the right wing tip.
summary: During climb, a jumpseater reported fuel venting from the right wingtip, prompting an emergency return and overweight landing. Maintenance later found a detached flapper valve allowed fuel into the vent system, though the leak stopped before landing and no further issues occurred.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported a passenger had a heart attack shortly after takeoff, an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport. Captain stated the flight attendants were utilizing unique to the flight attendant group language to describe the situation which resulted in an inaccurate assessment of the needs between the flight crew and ATC.
summary: Shortly after takeoff, the captain declared an emergency and returned to the airport after flight attendants used an internal code phrase indicating an immediate landing was required. The crew later discovered the cause was a passenger having a heart attack, though the initial lack of specific communication led the pilot to suspect a fire or airworthiness issue.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An MD80 flight crew returned to their departure airport after receipt of a Tail Comp Temp High warnings.
summary: The crew declared an emergency on departure from ZZZ after the Tail Comp Temp High light illuminated. Following a QRH completion and return to ZZZ, they declined to continue to ZZZ1 due to accumulated delays and maintenance issues.

synopsis: Two Line Aircraft Maintenance Technicians (AMTs) report about a company CRJ-700 aircraft that had to divert in flight due to oil quantity loss on Number 1 Engine. They had previously removed the Engine Driven Hydraulic Pump (EDP) on the Accessory Gear Box (AGB) and had been 'pushing' to meet a morning departure schedule.
summary: Two mechanics deferred a hydraulic pump on a CRJ-700 but omitted installing a required spline plug due to poor communication, stress, and inexperience. This error caused engine oil leakage, forcing an emergency landing at ZZZ1.

synopsis: An SA227 pilot diverted to the nearest suitable airport on battery power after suffering the failure of both AC generators.
summary: The pilot experienced a dual generator failure during IFR climbout and could not restore power despite reset attempts. The aircraft diverted to the nearest airport on battery power and completed a normal landing with no other abnormalities.

synopsis: C172 pilot reports a possible Class C incursion due to loss of GPS signal to his iPad at 3,000 FT south of SNA.
summary: A pilot flying south along the coast feared entering SNA Charlie airspace after an iPad backup GPS lost signal in haze, prompting an immediate descent and turn away from shore. The pilot landed without incident but added a checklist item to ensure at least one operational GPS is available, noting uncertainty about an actual airspace violation.

synopsis: Luscombe pilot reports a groundloop during landing resulting in a runway excursion that causes damage to the right gear and wing.
summary: A solo pilot flying a Luscombe in hot, thermally active conditions experienced a ground loop after landing, causing the right gear to collapse and the wingtip to bend. The pilot attributed the incident to unpreparedness for local summer weather extremes and remained uninjured.

synopsis: C150 pilot discovers that the ceiling is much lower than reported on a flight to CKB. On the return flight an attempt is made to climb over the clouds resulting in carburetor ice and a descent through a small hole to VMC below. The engine returns to normal but the reporter elects to divert to a suitable airport.
summary: A pilot en route to CKB experienced carburetor icing at 11,300 feet, forcing a descent to maintain VFR below clouds. Washington Center lost radar contact and questioned the pilot's IFR status, though the pilot remained in VMC and resumed normal flight after engine recovery.

synopsis: PHL Controller described a IFR/VFR glider conflict event near CKZ Airport, the reporter noting the glider activity at this location and on V3 is frequently problematic.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller issued an immediate left turn to a Hawker climbing to 4,000 feet near PTW VOR to avoid a glider operating at the same altitude. The Conflict Alert activated as the glider was barely moving over the VOR, prompting the controller to divert the Hawker while the pilot simultaneously executed a TCAS climb.

synopsis: HTS TRACON Controller described a MVA event when trying to identify a VFR aircraft operating at low altitudes due to low ceiling. The reporter listed CENRAP equipment/operations as a contributing factor.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managing a C501 and SR22 near HTS/HTW during a CENRAP operation lost radar contact with the SR22 due to low clouds and inaccurate pilot position reports. The controller eventually located the SR22 near large antennas and issued an IFR clearance, noting that reverting to full radar coverage would have been the appropriate solution.

synopsis: ZJX Controllers described a restricted area spill out resulting in a conflict event. The reporters claimed the airspace location is problematic and should be relocated.
summary: Air traffic controllers lost separation between a CRJ-700 and two F-16s near active AR600 airspace when the fighters deviated from their KC-135 tanker to follow the commercial jet. The incident occurred because controllers initially misidentified the F-16 flight as a single aircraft and the fighters operated outside their cleared track.

synopsis: SCT Controller described several false target events claiming that the FUSION RADAR continually produces target that do not exist, lowering the confidence of the pilots receiving the false traffic information.
summary: An air traffic controller issued traffic alerts to a B737 on ILS Runway 25L approach for false targets generated by the FUSION radar system due to a failed San Diego sensor. Switching to single sensor mode eliminated the false targets, which the controller attributed to FUSION's inability to handle multiple sensor inputs safely.

synopsis: A rushed B737-300 crew made a BLEEDS OFF takeoff with an MEL'ed Left pack but should have used APU air and the right pack for a pressurized BLEEDS OFF takeoff.
summary: The Captain departed unpressurized with the left pack MEL'd and an operating APU, incorrectly assuming a bleeds-off takeoff was required. This configuration error triggered Auto Fail and Standby lights after takeoff, forcing a level-off at 8,000 feet to run checklists before continuing to the destination.

synopsis: A320 Captain experiences an airborne conflict with a military helicopter at 900 FT during a River Visual to Runway 19 at DCA. TCAS RA states to monitor vertical speed with the helicopter 200 FT below the A320.
summary: During a night River Visual approach to DCA, a pilot reported a military helicopter passed 200 feet below their aircraft at 900 feet. The controller admitted the helicopter was flying 700 feet, higher than the normal 300–400 feet, causing a TCAS alert and a near-miss before the airliner landed safely.

synopsis: After being informed by an inbound Captain of the need to use the Fire Handle to shut down the Left Engine on a B777 aircraft, the outbound Captain was assured by Maintenance Control, Dispatch and a Maintenance Supervisor that no write-up existed. The Maintenance Release had to be broken during taxi out to address the engine shut down discrepancy.
summary: The Captain of a B777-200 reported a previous left engine shutdown issue that was initially missed in the Maintenance Release. Dispatch and Maintenance Control admitted the write-up was overlooked, delaying departure until a corrected release confirming the repair was received at XB:54 pm.

synopsis: DHC 8-300 flight crew believes they have a fuel leak in the left engine and elects to shut it down before continuing to destination. The combination of an aux fuel pump light that failed to extinguish when the pumps are turned off, uneven fuel consumption and a possible fuel odor in the cabin lead the crew to this conclusion.
summary: The crew suspected a fuel leak due to an illuminated aux pump light, fuel imbalance, and a cabin fuel odor, prompting an in-flight engine shutdown and emergency landing. Post-landing, the aircraft experienced sticking brakes requiring high torque to move, and the crew pulled the CVR circuit breaker to preserve data, though no leak was found by ground personnel.

synopsis: MD82 First Officer receives a cabin altitude warning at FL330 and after verifying cabin altitude above 10,000 feet and climbing an emergency descent is initiated. During descent manual control of the cabin is gained, but the crew elects to divert to a suitable airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a cabin altitude warning at FL330 with the cabin climbing above 10,000 feet. After donning oxygen masks and executing QRH procedures, they manually controlled the cabin during descent and diverted following Dispatch concurrence.

synopsis: An A310 number two engine BLEED LEAK ECAM alerted, so they complied with the checklist, declared an emergency, and returned to landing. During the return, a LOWER ACCESS panel door light ECAM alerted, but the crew determined after landing the two ECAMs were not related.
summary: The flight crew declared an emergency after receiving an engine bleed leak warning and an ECAM alert for open lower access panels during approach. They landed safely, shut down the second engine for inspection, and found the panel handle dislodged, concluding the two issues were unrelated.

synopsis: A300 flight crew reports being dispatched with an MEL for an inoperative Yellow Hydraulic System overheat light. Climbing through FL250 the light illuminates with associated ECAM warning and the Yellow System is shut down. During cruise the Green System quantity is noted to be decreasing and eventually triggers a low level light and ECAM warning. The Green System is shut down and the flight diverts. During descent the Yellow System overheat light extinguishes allowing that system to be used for approach and landing.
summary: The Captain and crew experienced a Yellow hydraulic reservoir overheat light during climbout after an incorrect MEL deferral, followed by a Green hydraulic low quantity warning. They declared an emergency, diverted, and landed safely with manual gear extension after recovering the Yellow system.

synopsis: A B757 mid-galley oven fan failed causing a great deal of black smoke in the cabin, but not knowing the cause inflight an emergency was declared and the flight diverted.
summary: Two flight attendants managed a possible oven fire in the mid galley during flight, where the left oven released dense black smoke due to a compromised fan igniting charcoal-like residue. The crew cut power, declared an emergency, and landed safely, though the attendants later sought medical evaluation for smoke inhalation.

synopsis: SR22 pilot reports an 'Eng Sensor not communicating' message on his MFD during descent with autopilot engaged and altitude capture active. During troubleshooting the autopilot descends 500 feet below selected altitude before detection.
summary: The pilot descended from 8,000 to 6,000 feet but overshot to 5,580 feet after autopilot capture failed due to spurious MFD messages. Distracted by the alerts, the pilot corrected the altitude after ATC intervention and grounded the aircraft for maintenance.

synopsis: General Aviation aircraft inbound to ADS reported confusion with the 'blanket Class B Clearance' issued by ATC to all aircraft inbound to ADS.
summary: A VFR pilot arriving at Addison Airport received a blanket Class B clearance and a traffic alert for a closing aircraft at the same altitude. The pilot executed an immediate right turn to avoid the traffic, reporting the incident due to the controller's workload and non-specific clearance.

aircraft: MD-90 Series (DC-9-90) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Following an engine borescope inspection, the Maintenance personnel neglected to reinstall a borescope plug.
summary: Two inexperienced mechanics performing a borescope inspection on an aircraft with a heavy work package missed reinstalling a plug due to fatigue, poor lighting, and pressure to meet a first flight deadline. The error was discovered later when thrust reverser panels were found open, despite a prior engine run showing no leaks.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: General aviation pilot describes the circumstances leading up to a NMAC five miles west of PHOG at 2,500 feet.
summary: A pilot flying westbound at 2,500 feet encountered a Stationair 50 feet below and right due to garbled Tower transmissions and inaccurate Approach traffic advisories. The pilot climbed 100 feet to avoid collision, attributing the near miss to communication failures and insufficient visual separation.

synopsis: A321 First Officer reported a wake vortex encounter on the EAGUL arrival into PHX that resulted in deviation from a crossing restriction.
summary: The pilot encountered wake turbulence from an A321 while descending on the EAGUL arrival into PHX. Disconnecting the autopilot to maintain control may have caused the aircraft to be high on the 10,000 to 8,000 feet altitude constraint at ESDEE, though the flight continued uneventfully.

synopsis: ELP Controller described an MVA infraction when failing to note an incorrect read back on an altitude assignment.
summary: An air traffic controller issued an incorrect heading of 345 degrees instead of 245 degrees to a Citation Excel on the SAMMR arrival, causing the aircraft to enter a 085 MVA at 080. The controller attributed the error to distraction from multiple simultaneous communications and recommended changing the arrival descent floor to 085.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a loss of separation event and provided a number of recommendations to lessen the chance of future same type occurrences.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller in Sector XX failed to maintain separation between an Eclipse 500 climbing to FL230 and a Beechjet 400 at FL190, resulting in a loss of separation to 4 miles and 500 feet. The controller attributed the incident to an incomplete scan, misidentifying the Eclipse, and failing to notice the overtaking situation amidst complex traffic and MOA congestion.

synopsis: A B737 right main gear viewing port was unusable because a thick Velcro cover could not be removed to permit gear down-lock verification.
summary: The pilot could not visually inspect the right main gear through the cabin floor view port due to a thick fiberglass cover attached with strong Velcro. Maintenance required a metal tool to remove the cover after landing, prompting a request for crew notification and an easier removal method.

synopsis: Inbound OAK air carrier described an event where similar call signs were in use on the same frequency, clearances were not verified and general confusion resulted.
summary: During descent into OAK, a pilot queried a controller after receiving an incorrect descent clearance due to confusion between similar call signs. The controller mistakenly issued instructions intended for another aircraft, causing the crew to level off at 16,800 feet before being cleared back to the original arrival path.

synopsis: Two pilots report about the left nose wheel folding under and collapsing during a hard right turn after pushback, using only Number 2 Engine power. The flight crew had to stop their single engine taxi out due to the B737-700 aircraft had continued turning left towards the Terminal, regardless of tiller position.
summary: During a single-engine taxi, the Captain attempted a tight right turn, causing the nose wheel tire to collapse and the aircraft to veer left. The incident resulted in a minor injury to a flight attendant, a two-hour delay, and a subsequent tire replacement due to the Captain's inexperience with the procedure.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 Captain took his company's management to task for the non-user friendly nature of their Company Operations Manual(s). His indictment was precipitated by being advised by his flight attendants that a deferred overhead bin had been sealed with tape and the PBE and Fire Extinguisher stored therein were, thus, rendered inaccessible. The manuals were so poorly written that Maintenance was able to interpret them to state it was permissible to dispatch revenue flights with the emergency equipment neither accessible nor, itself, deferred. He refused the aircraft.
summary: The Captain and Maintenance Control discovered a deferred overhead bin taped shut containing required fire extinguisher and PBE equipment, which had flown for two days without proper deferral of the equipment. A technician repaired the bin after the Captain refused to depart until the emergency equipment was correctly addressed, highlighting gaps in the MEL and Operations Manual.

synopsis: A320 flight crew returned to their departure for a precautionary landing due to an inflight vibration during departure climb. Post landing aircraft inspection revealed the fueling bay door was open.
summary: The flight crew experienced severe vibration during climb on an A320, caused by a partially open fueling bay door. They returned to the departure airport for a precautionary landing, where ground inspection confirmed the door was separating and damaged.

synopsis: An EMB-145 flight crew declared an emergency and returned to their departure airport when they were unable to raise the landing gear handle and received a landing gear air ground fail EICAS message.
summary: The pilot reported that after takeoff, the landing gear handle failed to move up, triggering an EICAS air/ground failure message. The crew declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport for a normal landing without thrust reversers, and attributed the issue to potential preventable maintenance.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 flight crew overcame transmitter problems with their primary ATC radio by using some creative troubleshooting. Once on the ground they assured the problem was repaired and not passed on to the next crew.
summary: During cruise and descent into ZZZ, the First Officer's yoke intercom failed, causing a stuck hot mike on Radio 1 that jammed the approach frequency. The crew managed communications by using Radio 2 and identifying with ATC, then deferred the faulty First Officer's microphone to Maintenance after rejecting an initial deferral of only the yoke unit.

synopsis: A BK117 pilot on a maintenance assessment flight encountered a chip warning in the Number Two Engine. He performed appropriate preparatory procedures, shut down the engine and performed a run-on landing on the grass between the runway and parallel taxiway at the departure airport.
summary: During a maintenance test flight, the pilot received an Engine Two chip warning, attempted to burn it, and returned for a One Engine Inoperative landing. The pilot shut down Engine Two over the runway and performed a run-on landing to the grass with no injuries or damage, though no chips were found on the detector plugs.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Recip Eng
synopsis: A C182 jump aircraft near 2B1 was not detected on a small transport aircraft TIS and they had a near miss as the C-182 climbed over PEAKE Intersection.
summary: The pilot and First Officer encountered a C182 jump plane at 4,500 feet while enroute south of 2B1, passing within 250 feet laterally. The close call resulted from the jump plane's non-standard noise abatement pattern and potential radar or transponder issues that prevented ATC from issuing traffic advisories.

synopsis: An MD82's AUTO Cabin Pressure Controller failed at FL330, flight crew declared an emergency and while descending the First Officer stabilized the cabin in Manual Control. After leveling at FL240 the flight diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: The crew experienced lost cabin pressurization at FL330, triggering a warning. They descended to FL240, stabilized pressure using manual control, and elected to divert after consulting flight attendants and Dispatch.

synopsis: B737-800 First Officer inadvertently bumped the flap handle while entering data into the FMC during cruise, causing it to move out of the 'up' detent.
summary: During cruise at FL390, the First Officer accidentally brushed the flap lever while entering a fix, causing a momentary extension to Flaps 1 and a slight aircraft bump. The pilot immediately returned the lever to Flaps 0, and the event was reported to Dispatch and Maintenance with no overspeed warnings or transit lights illuminated.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Shortly after takeoff an MD80 flight crew and flight attendants detected an acrid burning rubber odor, so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure where Airport Rescue and Fire Fighters detected no heat spots.
summary: The flight crew detected an acrid burning rubber smell on climbout, declared an emergency, and returned for a visual approach to Runway 18R. The odor dissipated before landing, and ARFF found no heat signatures, allowing the aircraft to taxi to the gate and offload passengers.

synopsis: A B737-800 flight crew, distracted by sluggish pitch response, failed to turn in a timely manner when flying the National SID off Runway 1 at DCA and briefly entered P-56 while correcting. The aircraft had been fueled to 33,000 LBS of fuel vice the flight plan required 18,000 LBS.
summary: The Pilot Not Flying reported that a new First Officer flying a heavy Boeing 737 failed to maintain the National 3 SID course, violating P-56 airspace. The deviation was attributed to the pilot's preoccupation with trimming a sluggish, heavy aircraft caused by excessive fuel load and VIP departure pressure.

synopsis: A MD11's number three engine flamed out with no secondary indications, checklist was complete, an emergency declared and the flight landed uneventfully.
summary: During arrival descent, the crew experienced a Number 3 engine flameout with no vibrations or fire indications. After unsuccessful restart attempts, they landed safely, and maintenance cleared the aircraft to taxi after confirming no damage.

synopsis: The crew of a Boeing 757-200 unexpectedly encountered moderate to severe turbulence and lightning while in cruise at FL350, resulting in, among other things, altitude deviations. A strong electrical burning smell permeated the flight deck, and several random emergency and EICAS lights illuminated, suggesting a possible lightning strike.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence and lightning at FL350, causing altitude excursions, electrical odors, and multiple system failures including gear and altitude indications. Maintenance grounded the aircraft for inspection of potential lightning strike and overstress damage, though the crew landed uneventfully without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: B737-300 Flight Attendant reported failure to lower girt bar into place on departure because of a distraction. The error was discovered in flight.
summary: A Flight Attendant in the 'A' position failed to lower the girt bar while arming the door, leaving the red flag visible until the 'C' Flight Attendant corrected it above 10,000 feet. The error occurred due to momentary distraction during ground training, prompting the reporter to commit to improved focus on arming procedures.

synopsis: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) describes his injuries, including hearing loss, after an oxygen supply servicing hose separated at the Crew oxygen external servicing port on an EMB-145 aircraft.
summary: A mechanic servicing an aircraft's crew oxygen system suffered hearing loss and arm injuries when a defective hose disconnected at 1,800 PSI. The incident also dented the aircraft, prompting maintenance action and a recommendation for routine hose inspections and life limits.

synopsis: Upon arriving at company hangar, a Maintenance Manager discovers a SAAB 340B+ (plus) aircraft resting on a bottle jack (axle jack) with both left Main wheels removed. Jacking procedures in Technical Manual (TM) Chapter 07-10-00 were not followed.
summary: A Maintenance Manager discovered a SAAB 340B in the hangar resting on a bottle jack with both left main wheels removed. The crew was directed to place the aircraft on main jacks to ensure a safe, level condition, as the initial setup violated defined jacking procedures.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A flight crew on the BONVL 7 Arrival was transitioned to the HHOOD RNAV but not given an arrival runway at PDX. The crew was reluctant to descend because the FMS programming could not be completed without the Runway.
summary: The flight crew en route to PDX experienced confusion after being recleared to the HHOOD1 arrival with minimal briefing time, leading to an altitude deviation below FL240. The crew attributed the incident to the sudden arrival change, unclear STAR format, and lack of runway information, resulting in ATC issuing vectors to manage the descent.

synopsis: A90 Controller described a technical loss of separation event during simultaneous parallel runway operations involving heavy separation, the reporter recommending possible revised procedures.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managed parallel approaches for a B752 and A319 on Runways 4R and 4L, where the B752 overtook the A319 by 0.25 miles despite wake turbulence restrictions. The controller allowed the approach to continue, noting a TCAS RA occurred but concluding no unsafe situation existed due to visual separation and glide path differences.

synopsis: ZMP Controller described an unsafe condition relating to the confusion regarding who is authorized to change Data Block information and when those changes can be made.
summary: The receiving controller entered a climb altitude for Air Carrier Y after approval, leading to a dispute with the transferring ZAU 75 controller over ERAM data block procedures. This distraction caused the transferring controller to neglect a required pointout for Air Carrier X, which subsequently clipped the receiving sector without coordination.

synopsis: ZDV Controller described a below MIA/MVA event and the disagreement between controllers involved with regard to routing and procedure, the reporter suggesting that improved Radio/RADAR coverage would help prevent future events.
summary: An ATC controller reported a conflict with a Sector 22 controller regarding a BE36/G aircraft at 9,000 feet unable to climb to the V86 MEA of 11,000 feet. The controller requested a direct routing to RAP to comply with the 9,300-foot MIA, but the other controller argued, leaving the aircraft in poor radar and radio coverage.

synopsis: LAX air carrier departure described a developing conflict with parallel runway departure traffic after takeoff, the reporter suspecting the conflicting aircraft may not have changed database after a last minute runway change.
summary: The pilot reported a near-midair conflict with another carrier during simultaneous takeoffs from parallel runways 24L and 24R. The reporter suspects the other aircraft failed to update its navigation database or received an incorrect clearance, causing a drift that triggered a resolution advisory.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier aircraft on the LAS SUNST RNAV Arrival missed the IPUMY 230 KT speed restriction as the pilot attempted to slow the aircraft in turbulent, ground heated air.
summary: Pilots on the SUNST arrival encountered moderate turbulence and ground heating while descending through FUZZY, causing them to exceed the 250 KTS restriction and reach 274 KTS. They eventually met the IPUMY altitude restriction at 11,000 feet but required an ATC clearance to slow further to 210 KTS to manage the speed.

synopsis: A Dispatcher reported that he was notified that he had worked a flight that had conflicting deferred items.
summary: A dispatcher took over a flight already airborne that was released with conflicting deferred items: an APU and a right engine high pressure shutoff valve. Maintenance and Dispatch missed that the MEL prohibits dispatching both items simultaneously, an error discovered the next day.

synopsis: A Ground Service employee reported that during passenger deplaning the loading bridge rose without being commanded until it came in contact with the bottom of the aircraft door. The deplaning was suspended until the loading bridge was repositioned. Maintenance was contacted to check the aircraft for possible damage.
summary: A ramp agent reported that a passenger loading bridge rose into the aircraft door during deplaning. The agent stopped passengers, lowered the bridge 8-10 inches, and a Maintenance Supervisor examined the aircraft.

synopsis: A gate agent operating a jet bridge reported the inbound aircraft nearly contacted the bridge because ramp personnel had used the wrong stop line.
summary: The pilot reported that marshaling to lead line A positioned an engine directly under the jet bridge, requiring the bridge to be raised to avoid a collision. Ramp agents subsequently stopped the pilot's attempt to maneuver the aircraft and initiated a pushback to the correct stop.

synopsis: MD-11 First Officer reported loss of Number 3 Hydraulic System in flight. They ran the procedure, contacted company, and continued to destination where a manual gear extension was performed, followed by a safe landing.
summary: The crew experienced a Number 3 hydraulic system failure requiring manual gear extension, but the center gear failed to extend. After exhausting troubleshooting options, they landed safely with no visible damage following a fire crew inspection.

synopsis: An air carrier flight crew descending into SEA via the MARNR RNAV STAR descended below the at or above 12,000 FT restriction at MARNR. The deviation was the result of the incompatibility of the aircraft's FMS to deal with the complexities inherent in the 'state of the art' STAR.
summary: The crew descended below the 12,000 FT crossing restriction at RAYNI during the MARNR 3 arrival after the Captain switched the autopilot from VNAV to VS mode. This deviation occurred due to FMS programming changes for a runway switch and crew distraction, which removed vertical path protection and allowed an uncommanded descent.

synopsis: Corporate aircraft responded to a TCAS RA on final for IAD 19L and executed a go-around, the pilot questioning ATC for allowing helicopter operations near the landing runway.
summary: The flight crew encountered a helicopter mapping for a subway on final approach to runway 19L, triggering a TCAS climb resolution advisory and a missed approach. The pilot attributed the conflict to the helicopter's presence at 1,000 feet AGL and criticized the Tower's slow response to move the traffic.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier landing PVU described a confused visual approach and landing event when ATC seemed to be surprised, very busy and confused with the aircraft involved, ATC reportedly listed lack of communications with the TRACON as a causal factor.
summary: During a CA IOE visual approach to PVU Runway 13, the crew and a Cessna experienced a traffic conflict due to a lack of coordination between Approach and Tower. The single controller, overwhelmed by staffing issues and field maintenance, was unaware of the IFR arrival until a TCAS advisory prompted immediate evasive action by both aircraft.

synopsis: A B777 right engine surged during climb at FL260 with fuel flow and EGT remaining above normal so fuel was dumped as the flight returned to the departure airport for an uneventful landing.
summary: During climbout from FL260 to FL320, the crew experienced two right engine surges with elevated fuel flow and EGT, prompting a return to the departure airport. The aircraft required a fuel dump to meet maximum landing weight before making an uneventful landing.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported the inbound Captain failed to make a logbook entry documenting a brake fault and a delay resulted.
summary: The inbound Captain failed to write up a cleared autobrake fault, causing Maintenance to later discover a significant brake temperature split and initiate MEL procedures. This omission resulted in a departure delay while the brake system was investigated and repaired.

synopsis: Air Carrier landing CLT described a confused descent clearance event most likely resulting due to same Company similar sounding call signs, the reporter acknowledging that his Company needs to correct the problem.
summary: A Company ABED crew descended to 9,000 feet per CLT Approach instructions, but the controller later stated they should have been at 10,000 feet. The pilot attributed the altitude discrepancy to a controller error caused by confusion between similar-sounding call signs, Company ABCD and ABED.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported receiving caution messages on flight spoilers, ground spoilers, and spoilerons deployed. They performed a Flaps 20 landing on the longest runway at their destination.
summary: During climb, the crew received simultaneous caution messages for flight, spoileron, and ground spoiler deployment. Following QRH procedures, they performed a Flaps 20 landing on the longest available runway at the destination.

synopsis: CE-560XL flight crew experienced a Cabin Altitude warning during climb at 15,000 FT. They declared an emergency and returned to their departure airport.
summary: The pilot in command reported a cabin altitude warning and master warning at 15,500 feet during climb, causing an immediate return to the departure airport. The pilot attributed the event to potential distraction or fatigue while reviewing MEL procedures for a cabin door light, resulting in an uneventful landing and subsequent MEL of the ACM.

synopsis: A B737 Captain strongly expressed his dissatisfaction, supported by multiple personal examples of operational issues, with the lack of response from his Company and the FAA to numerous reports he and other pilots have submitted regarding the disfunctionality and the reduced safety resulting from use of the HAWKZ RNAV STAR into SEA.
summary: A pilot reported that the HAWKZ arrival into SEA caused high workload and safety risks due to conflicting speed clearances, runway changes, and tailwinds. These factors disrupted VNAV, triggered LNAV/VNAV disconnects, and created holding pattern errors, leading the pilot to recommend discontinuing the procedure.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported a wake vortex encounter on arrival into DEN that resulted in a Flight Attendant injury.
summary: The pilot reported moderate wake turbulence near Denver just before gear extension, which caused a flight attendant to cut her head. The pilot initially filed a severe turbulence report due to a mistaken recollection of company definitions but later corrected it to moderate after reviewing the manual.

synopsis: B757-200 flight crew noticed 'smoky' odor in cockpit at FL370. Crew confirmed odor with flight attendants, declared an emergency, and diverted. Area wildfires found to be the cause of odor.
summary: The crew of an aircraft en route at FL370 smelled smoke, declared an emergency, and diverted to ZZZ after ATC confirmed similar reports from one other aircraft. They landed overweight following a descent to FL240, suspecting local wildfires as the cause.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported they rejected their takeoff when the Number 2 Engine would not spool up beyond 1.15 EPR.
summary: During a FLEX takeoff, the crew aborted after the right engine failed to spool past 1.15 EPR while the left advanced normally. The rejection was caused by the engine failure, an ECAM message, and the Captain's difficulty maintaining directional control due to the thrust asymmetry.

synopsis: During taxi for takeoff the B757 Captain declared an emergency and returned to the gate after the aft cabin developed strong fumes making passengers and flight attendants ill.
summary: Cabin crew reported strong fumes in the rear causing sickness to passengers and crew, prompting a request for medical assistance. The Captain declared an emergency to expedite taxiing to the gate and prepare for a potential evacuation.

synopsis: Eurocopter pilot reported Number 1 ENG FAIL light illuminated with no corroborating indications, so he continued to destination. Reporter stated he had seen this same false indication on this aircraft previously.
summary: The pilot reported a false Number 1 ENG FAIL light on the CAD and VEMD during departure, a repeat of symptoms from two days prior. The lights extinguished on approach to the hospital, the aircraft was secured, and the fault was logged for maintenance troubleshooting.

synopsis: In cruise at FL280, MD-82 flight crew detected 'burning electrical' odor after turning on engine heat. Flight attendants reported same odor in the cabin. Crew declared an emergency and diverted to ZZZ where odor was attributed to massive forest fires in the area.
summary: The pilot reported a burning electrical odor in the cockpit and cabin at FL280 near ZZZ1 after activating engine anti-ice, prompting an emergency diversion to ZZZ. The crew suspects the smell originated from regional forest fire smoke rather than an aircraft fault, noting that prior awareness could have prevented the unnecessary diversion.

synopsis: B757 First Officer flew a trip after becoming aware of an irritation in one eye, but with no affect on vision. After the trip a piece of metal was extracted from the eyeball.
summary: A pilot flew a leg with a metal fragment in their eye, reporting no vision issues or impact on duties during the uneventful flight. The object was removed at an emergency room, resulting in the pilot being grounded for the subsequent flight.

synopsis: The flight crew of a CRJ-200 departed with the Right A/C Pac deferred and bleed air supplied to the left Pac by the APU. Once airborne, the APU was secured and the crew attempted to establish bleed air to the Left Pac without success. With no pressurization or conditioned air available, the aircraft returned to the departure airport and made an uneventful overweight landing.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a failure of the right pack and isolation valve during climb, causing cabin overheating and pressurization loss. They returned to the departure airport for an overweight landing to avoid severe weather and extreme cabin temperatures.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 206 experienced a strong wind gust during landing resulting in a bounce and subsequent nose gear damage.
summary: The pilot experienced a hard landing and nose gear damage during the landing phase due to strong wind gusts causing a bounce and over-correction. The pilot attributed the imperfect reaction to personal performance degradation from a long day of flying in adverse weather.

synopsis: M20E pilot reported landing gear-up because of distractions dealing with an engine problem.
summary: The pilot experienced rough engine operation and partial power during climb, possibly due to a plugged injector, and returned for a gear-up landing. The landing occurred because the pilot failed to follow the landing checklist, resulting in the gear not extending before touchdown with no injuries.

synopsis: M20J pilot reported probable prop governor problem resulting in an oil leak that coated the windshield.
summary: During cruise, a pilot encountered oil spraying on the windshield and smoke, likely caused by oil leaking from a faulty prop governor onto hot exhaust parts. The pilot declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport, and landed safely despite reduced visibility.

synopsis: During takeoff following a refueling stop, the pilot of a Piper PA32 experienced a loss of power due to the failure to properly install the fuel caps. The return to the field was sucessful, however the pilot neglected to lower the landing gear, resulting in a gear-up landing.
summary: The crew experienced partial power loss and altitude reduction during takeoff due to fuel venting from missing fuel caps. They returned for an emergency landing but failed to extend the landing gear.

synopsis: G200 flight crew experiences thrust reverser and brake failures during landing that result in a runway excursion causing minor damage to the aircraft. The aircraft had a history of proximity switch failures and issues with the brakes wear indicators.
summary: During a Part 135 line check in a G200, the crew experienced a runway overrun due to suspected WOW switch failure that disabled antiskid and limited thrust reverser effectiveness. The aircraft departed the runway end 10-15 feet with no injuries, though tire marks indicated a lack of braking on the right main and outer left wheels.

synopsis: A C404 Pilot declared an emergency then landed with the nose gear retracted after extensive attempts to lower it failed. Only minor damage to the nose and bent propellers were noted.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 404 experienced a nose gear extension failure on final approach despite cycling the gear, using emergency nitrogen, and performing G maneuvers. The aircraft landed safely on the main gear with the nose touching down, resulting in minor damage to the props and lower nose.

synopsis: Small aircraft pilot reported the runway/taxiway surface markings at the intersection of Runway 6/24 and Taxiway A at ISM are faded and need to be repainted. The reporter also noted signage at that location is too close to the movement surfaces and difficult to see from an aircraft that sits in a nose high attitude.
summary: A pilot reported that faded pavement markings at the Runway 6/24 and Taxiway Alpha intersection and signs placed too close to the ground were difficult to see from a nose-high aircraft. The reporter recommended repainting the markings and relocating the signs further from the pavement.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reports encountering thunderstorms during an IFR flight to MYAM and deviating with ATC assistance to avoid the heaviest weather. On board ADS-B weather was not displaying any weather east of MYGF.
summary: The pilot flying an IFR flight to Marsh Harbor encountered towering cumulus clouds and heavy precipitation, requiring multiple altitude changes and a deviation from the assigned heading. After losing radio contact in IMC, the pilot broke out of clouds at 3,000 feet, received a relayed IFR cancellation, and landed safely.

synopsis: C172 pilot reports using the UNICOM frequency to make position reports during approach to DKX with no traffic heard. During the landing flare an aircraft was noticed on the takeoff roll in the opposite direction and a go-around on the left side of the runway initiated. The departing aircraft rejected the takeoff and an aircraft behind on final goes around, side stepping to his right resulting in a head on NMAC situation.
summary: A pilot and safety pilot executing a visual approach to Runway 26 initiated a go-around due to an aircraft taking off from the opposite end. A second aircraft on final then turned right into their flight path, passing 100 feet below, caused by confusion over UNICOM versus CTAF frequencies and simultaneous use of both runways.

synopsis: ZJX Controller voiced frustration with Sealord military operations and their unwillingness to released airspace when weather factors demand immediate action.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller at Sector 68 coordinated a B757's weather deviation and descent into active military warning areas after Sealord approved the point-out. Sealord later panicked and ordered the descent stopped at FL300, despite previously stating the live-fire exercise was active up to and including that altitude.

synopsis: An aircraft departed LAX Runway 24L and passed directly over another aircraft which, contrary to ATC's instructions, did not hold short after landing on Runway 24R.
summary: The flight crew executed an aggressive takeoff on Runway 24L after another aircraft crossed the runway without holding short as instructed. The reporter attributed the incident to the other carrier's failure to monitor radio instructions and clear the runway, while noting ATC may have missed the lack of response.

synopsis: A B737NG autoflight system transitioned to LEVEL CHANGE (LVL CHG) and began a descent after the crew began programming the FMS's to exit holding and continue a RNAV arrival descent upon passing the holding fix at the holding altitude constraint.
summary: The flight crew holding at FUZZY at 16,000 feet experienced an unexpected descent to 15,400 feet after ATC changed the arrival to Runway 25R. The autopilot switched to Level Change mode when the FMC converted a hard altitude constraint to a soft one, which went unnoticed because both crew members were focused on reprogramming the flight management computer.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier jet was cleared to taxi from the BUR passenger terminal across Runway 8 to Taxiway A and reported light twin departed on Runway 8 overflying them by 200 FT. Ground lost track of the Tower's light twin clearance.
summary: While crossing Runway 08 under Ground Control clearance, the crew encountered a departing Piper Twin climbing out 200 feet above them. The reporter attributes the near-miss to a miscommunication where Ground failed to coordinate with the departing aircraft, compounded by a 737 obstructing the crew's view of the runway.

synopsis: Experimental aircraft pilot reports losing control during landing in a strong crosswind, resulting in nose gear collapse and damage to the prop and lower cowling.
summary: The pilot landed on Runway 03 in 90-degree crosswinds gusting to 18 MPH. A gust lifted the right wing, causing an angled landing that collapsed the nose gear and damaged the propeller and lower cowling with no injuries.

synopsis: The pilot of a Beechcraft BE35 flying at 3,100 feet was warned of obstacles ahead on his flight path by ATC. He also received warning of the impending catastrophic conflict with the towers ahead by his onboard terrain guidance equipment.
summary: The pilot cancelled IFR to fly VFR to a new destination but failed to identify the correct Maximum Elevation Figure on charts. This resulted in flying at 3,100 feet, insufficient for four towers, requiring an altitude increase to 3,800 feet after terrain guidance and Approach alerted the pilot.

synopsis: A B747 Cargo Fire Warning alerted at cruise, so an emergency was declared and the flight diverted to an enroute airport where a false warning was confirmed by the Airport Rescue and Fire Fighters.
summary: The flight crew diverted an aircraft from FL330 due to intermittent Aft Cargo Fire warnings caused by a failed smoke detector. They performed an overweight landing, discharged Halon, and evacuated passengers, though fire crews found no evidence of fire.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reports a very noisy and rough running engine with reduced power during a cross country flight. Reporter is able to return to the departure airport safely.
summary: The pilot of a PA28-180 declared an emergency over water after an exhaust manifold broke, causing backfiring and power loss. An A&P later attributed the failure to an exhaust leak creating an overly lean condition and blowing exhaust gas into the carburetor.

synopsis: A Repair Station Aircraft/Engine Inspector (IA) reports about a summary of errors that contributed to five out of six incorrect cylinders being installed on a Continental IO-550B Engine. The Beech A36 Bonanza had flown approximately 100 hours and one year when an Oil Analysis discovered high aluminum content in the oil.
summary: During an annual inspection, a Parts Manager, Installer, and Inspector failed to verify cylinder kit applicability, resulting in the installation of incorrect parts. The aircraft flew for 100 hours before oil analysis and a third-party repair revealed piston wear caused by the non-airworthy engine.

synopsis: A B737-700 Captain believes the crossing altitude depicted at BAMDE waypoint (at or above 3,000 feet), on the AMYLU RNAV STAR for arrivals to Runway 21 at CHS, is inappropriate and should be a hard altitude to prevent arriving aircraft from being too high to continue the approach.
summary: Pilots reported an error in the AMYLU RNAV STAR into CHS where the BAMDE transition's "at or above" altitude restriction caused an FMC discontinuity. This prevented proper descent, forcing the crew to execute a 360-degree turn to lose altitude before intercepting the RNAV RNP Z approach to runway 21.

synopsis: An A320 ECAM alerted HYD G LO PR on landing and with the resultant loss of nose wheel steering the aircraft veered left and was uncontrollable.
summary: The flight crew experienced a loss of nose wheel steering and a HYD G LO PRESS warning while taxiing after landing on 22L. They stopped the aircraft using brakes and were towed to the gate after airport personnel observed hydraulic fluid leaking.

synopsis: When a line of thunderstorms forced the CRJ-200 flight crew to divert from their destination they were unable to contact their Dispatcher to coordinate doing so. Only after landing at their diversion airport and while awaiting access to their gate did an ACARS message arrive from Dispatch.
summary: The flight crew diverted to BMI due to impenetrable thunderstorms after failing to reach Dispatch via ACARS or ATL Radio. The pilot cited the lack of dispatcher oversight and delayed release amendment as the greatest threat, noting the amendment arrived only after landing.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 Captain reported the significant bump on CLT Runway 18L at the intersection of Runway 23 is apparently becoming more pronounced over time forcing a nose strut bouncing motion.
summary: The flight crew reported significant nose bouncing during a heavy-weight takeoff on Runway 18L at CLT caused by a deteriorating bump at the intersection with Runway 23. Although control was maintained, the pilot recommended repairing the runway surface to prevent the need for manual back-pressure.

synopsis: C172 instructor experiences a loss of engine power while practicing power off stalls with his student. An emergency is declared with Approach Control and a safe landing ensues.
summary: A pilot and student experienced an engine power loss during power-off stall practice. After declaring an emergency, Approach Control and Tower provided an urgent runway clearance, allowing for a safe landing once power was restored.

synopsis: Low oil pressure indications and a failing pressurization system convinced a Convair 580 flight crew to divert to a nearby airport. Although the right engine was shut down as a precautionary measure, no emergency was declared.
summary: The crew experienced cabin decompression and a low oil pressure warning while enroute near ZZZ, despite normal oil temperature and quantity. The Pilot Flying initiated a preventative engine shutdown, and the aircraft diverted to ZZZ for a safe landing without declaring an emergency.

aircraft: M-20 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Tower Controller providing OJT described a loss of separation between an IFR arrival and an IFR departure when the final traffic executed a missed approach due to weather.
summary: An ATC controller permitted a BE33 to depart on a 2-mile final behind an M20P in low ceilings, resulting in a 300-foot vertical and 2-mile lateral separation when the M20P missed approach. The controller attributed the incident to failing to apply visual separation rules and not ensuring the M20P was in sight before authorizing the departure.

synopsis: LEX Controller described a possible vector into weather due to equipment problems with no maintenance available to correct the problem, allegedly due to budget constraints.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored a PA-23 into severe thunderstorms due to a radar weather display limited to 12 NM by an unreported equipment failure. The aircraft subsequently lost significant altitude to 1,400–1,600 MSL, well below the 2,500 FT minimum safe altitude, nearly resulting in a loss of the aircraft.

synopsis: A330 First Officer reported encountering wake turbulence in trail of a B747 on final to EDDF, stating that in his opinion five miles is not enough separation.
summary: The pilot encountered wake turbulence from a 747 five miles ahead on final approach to Runway 25L at EDDF while at 4,000 FT MSL. The crew climbed to 4,400 FT MSL and remained above the glideslope for a normal landing, noting that five miles is insufficient separation for a 747.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported mistakenly selecting flaps 10 when flaps 5 were called for, leading to an overspeed.
summary: The First Officer inadvertently selected Flaps 10 instead of Flaps 5 during final approach at 4,073 feet, causing an 8-knot overspeed. The reporter attributed the error to fatigue after six consecutive duty days and limited visibility of flap gate settings from the Captain's seat.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) was informed that the ARDROX-185L chemical solution he used to accomplished a compressor wash on two Arrius 2B2 turbine engines installed on an EC-135T2 helicopter, was not on their approved Chemical List.
summary: A mechanic performed an engine compressor wash on an EC-135T2+ using ARDROX-185L, which was later identified as unapproved by a trainer. The incident resulted from the mechanic failing to verify the specific chemical against the approved list before mixing and applying it to the Arrius 2B2 engines.

synopsis: C172 instructor pilot discovers that her aircraft will not climb after rotation. The aircraft is placed back on the runway and the takeoff rejected. A business jet is allowed to land while this is occurring.
summary: A flight instructor and student aborted a takeoff on a 4,400-foot runway after the aircraft failed to climb out of ground effect despite normal rotation speed and attitude. The pilot landed straight ahead, stopping just before the runway end, and subsequently exited via taxiway A11 after the preceding business jet had cleared.

synopsis: When the engine failed on the PA-18 while banner towing over a populated seashore the pilot was forced to ditch off the beach on water covered with a reef and rocks. The aircraft flipped over on touchdown but the pilot was not seriously injured.
summary: The pilot of a PA-18 Super Cub towing a banner at 550–560 feet experienced complete engine power loss one hour and fifteen minutes after takeoff. The aircraft was forced into a controlled water landing on a reef, flipped, and leaked fuel and oil, though the pilot evacuated uninjured.

synopsis: Tower Control reporters describe a go-around event and developing conflict when a B777 on flair elected to go-around because previous landing traffic was not clear of the runway.
summary: A B777 on short final initiated a go-around due to perceived runway traffic, conflicting with a VFR transition aircraft. The Local Controller issued a heading that reduced separation, while the reporter attributed the event to training distractions on Ground, ASDE inaccuracies, and single-runway complexity.

synopsis: A Dash 8-300 flight crew returned to their departure airport when they noted a chronic fuel venting problem was recurring.
summary: The Captain observed a fuel leak from the left NACA vent during the after-takeoff phase while the First Officer completed checklists. The crew returned for a normal landing, shut down engine number 1 for inspection, and found no fuel evidence before deplaning.

synopsis: When neither the Dispatcher nor the Captain noted the MELed IDG, combined with a previously noted APU MEL declaring it unable to provide electrical system redundancy, the flight was released with only a single source of electrical AC power.
summary: Maintenance deferred an IDG without notifying the crew, and the Captain and reporter failed to realize that combining this with a previous APU MEL rendered the aircraft unairworthy. The flight departed due to poor communication between Maintenance and Dispatch and unclear MEL guidance regarding multiple deferrals.
