synopsis: A Flight Attendant working as a Purser, describes her efforts to address cabin egress safety issues after being informed that a section of the cabin floor Emergency Lighting strip was missing on their outbound B757 aircraft.
summary: The Purser and cabin crew reported a missing emergency lighting strip on a B757-200, which a mechanic dismissed as normal design after comparing it to another aircraft. Despite the crew's safety concerns and evidence of intact strips on other planes, the Captain accepted the mechanic's assessment, allowing the flight to proceed with the defect.

synopsis: Two Line mechanics report how interruptions and a verbal altercation during a right Main Landing Gear (MLG) tire change resulted in the axle nut tang washer not being installed on a B737-800 aircraft.
summary: Two mechanics missed installing a washer during a Number 3 main tire change on a B737-800 A-Check due to frequent interruptions and verbal altercations from lead mechanics. The Maintenance Supervisor generated a maintenance item for the missing washer, attributing the error to lost task focus and complacency.

synopsis: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) realizes he improperly ordered an inboard Slat Disconnect Sensor for a CRJ-900 aircraft through the parts computer ordering system of their merged Air Carrier's inventory program, instead of using their own parts ordering system. He noticed the incorrect serviceable tag after returning from a field trip.
summary: Mechanic X and Mechanic Y mistakenly ordered a CRJ-200 Slat Disconnect Sensor for a CRJ-900 due to a mental lapse while rushing to another airport. The error resulted in the aircraft being placed Out of Service (AOS) after the wrong part and serviceable tag were identified upon return.

synopsis: The pilot of a Glastar homebuilt elected to turn directly to a nearby open field where he landed safely after his engine lost substantial power shortly after takeoff.
summary: The pilot experienced a partial engine power loss at 200 AGL after takeoff and executed a 90-degree turn to land in an adjacent grass area without contacting the tower. Maintenance found no cause for the power loss, and the landing was uneventful.

synopsis: Despite the failure of the No. 1 alternator the pilot of an SR-22 opted to continue the IFR cross country anticipating the No. 2 alternator and the batteries would provide adequate electrical power. Prior to destination all electrical power was lost and the pilot opted to divert to an uncontrolled airport where he landed safely and called ATC to report the event.
summary: The pilot reported a dual alternator failure and total electrical loss on an IFR flight southwest of Atlanta, causing altitude encoding and radio communication failures. The crew diverted to an uncontrolled field, broke IFR clearance, and landed without electrical equipment or flaps to avoid congestion at the busy destination.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA32 landed for fuel, and as a precaution removed the engine cowling to inspect the engine. Others assisted him in re-installing the cowling, but not having been latched properly, came loose just after takeoff and sustained damage, but did not depart the aircraft. The pilot immediately returned to land, and grounded the aircraft to await the necessary repairs.
summary: The pilot landed for fuel and engine inspection, then took off with a right cowling that dislodged immediately after rotation due to two unengaged latches missed during a distracted preflight. The pilot executed a go-around and landed safely, grounding the aircraft for repairs.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: After pushback an Air Carrier Captain began taxiing on the ramp thinking he was on Taxiway B and because of the lack of signage, his airport unfamiliarity and incomplete ATC taxi instructions did not know to transition to Taxiway B.
summary: The flight crew mistakenly taxied on the ramp instead of Taxiway B at EWR after misreading charts and unclear markings. They corrected the error by notifying Ground Control, attributing the incident to poor situational awareness, unfamiliarity, and inadequate taxi instructions.

synopsis: A Dispatcher reported that one of his flight's crew ACARSed him about a galley smoke event and diverted as a result, then he was unable to communicate with the aircraft the remainder of the flight.
summary: A dispatcher received an ACARS declaring a cabin smoke emergency from a flight but failed to receive subsequent messages. The crew diverted due to smoke from a forward galley oven, and the dispatcher reported being unable to provide support because additional ACARS transmissions were not received.

synopsis: At cruise an A300 ECAM alerted HYD G PUMP LO PR followed by HYD G RSVR LO LVL so during approach the gear was lowered manually and towed to the gate after landing.
summary: The Captain experienced HYD G PUMP LO PR and HYD G RSVR LO LVL ECAM messages, declaring an emergency to Approach Control for a wide pattern to manually crank the gear. The aircraft landed without incident and was towed to the ramp by Maintenance.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a conflict event when the military was reluctant to allow entry into several restricted areas for air carrier deviation requests.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller and trainee lost separation between Air Carrier X and Air Carrier Y at FL330-340 due to high workload, overlapping data blocks, and military traffic conflicts. The incident triggered a TCAS alert and Conflict Alert, resulting in a 20-degree turn clearance to increase separation.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a pilot filed NMAC event while vectoring successive departure aircraft, one aircraft vectored behind a heavy B747, reporter claiming appropriate separation existed.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored Air Carrier X behind a heavy Air Carrier Y to resolve a tie at an arrival fix, resulting in X passing through Y's wake turbulence with over 5 miles separation. The controller reported that Air Carrier X complained about the wake encounter and recommended Center review the LOA with the TRACON.

synopsis: Glider pilot reported NAMC events involving two air carrier aircraft inbound to the DFW area, the reporter suggesting more positive ATC separation procedures.
summary: A glider pilot thermalling at 3,800 feet MSL south of DFW reported two airliners passing within half a mile in Class E airspace. The pilot attributed the unsafe proximity to DFW Approach's lack of caution regarding the nearby TSA glider port.

synopsis: A C414 pilot failed to remove the yoke gust lock during preflight and so rejected the takeoff when he could not rotate, then ran off the runway end but did not cause significant damage.
summary: The pilot attempted takeoff at a high-altitude airport with the yoke lock still installed, obscured by a new iPad mount. The aircraft failed to lift off, overran the runway, and struck a navaid light, resulting in no injuries or aircraft damage.

synopsis: A B737-400 Captain rejected the takeoff when the Captain's airspeed, altimeter and IVSI indicated OFF because his ADC failed possibly because of no air conditioning when parked on the ramp in high temperature.
summary: The crew rejected takeoff at 100 knots after the Captain's airspeed, altimeter, and IVSI failed due to an Air Data Computer malfunction. The reporter attributed the equipment failure to a hot aircraft with no APU and poor air circulation caused by a lack of ground air.

synopsis: A B757-200 began loosing oil at FL350 on an Atlantic Track and diverted to an ETOPS alternated with the engine running at idle and oil pressure in lower green band.
summary: The crew diverted to an ETOPS alternate after the right engine oil quantity dropped to zero and pressure decreased on a North Atlantic track. They declared an emergency, offset left, and landed uneventfully using single-engine procedures due to a right engine oil leak.

synopsis: CRJ700 flight crew is issued holding instructions descending through 16,000 FT for an 11,000 foot hold as depicted on the arrival but does not note that the FMC has defaulted to one and a half minute legs when one minute legs are required below 14,000 FT. ATC takes note and issues a revised clearance.
summary: The flight crew holding at HOLEY while descending to LGA inadvertently exited protected airspace because the FMS defaulted to 1.5-minute legs instead of the published 1-minute legs. This occurred because the aircraft was above 14,000 feet when the hold was entered, causing the system to fail to adjust leg length for the assigned 11,000-foot altitude.

synopsis: A widebody Captain took exception to his airline's policy of scheduling long range overwater flights with only a single relief pilots on flights which routinely exceed 12 hours of flight time, in apparent violation of FAR flight time limits and their labor contract. He noted that, when he was ordered to fly the trip despite his concerns, his managers and/or an FAA representative were unable to provide a copy of an alleged LOA with the FAA they had cited to justify the assignment.
summary: A fatigued three-person crew reported making significant errors during a West Coast to RJAA flight after Operations denied a request for an additional crewmember. The crew was ordered to fly despite fatigue concerns, with management citing a disputed FAA Letter of Agreement that was never produced.

synopsis: An Air Carrier pilot noted that his EFB moving map own ship symbol was not visible after landing and so he nearly exited ZGSZ Runway 15 at Taxiway E6 which was closed. Poor E6 signage location also caused confusion because the sign is near Taxiway E7.
summary: The pilot nearly exited Runway 16 onto closed Taxiway E6 at ZGSZ due to high workload, missing EFB position data, and poor signage. ATC warned the crew, who corrected the error and exited via Taxiway E7 without entering the closed taxiway.

synopsis: A DC-10 CARGO FIRE LOWER alerted three times with the TRI tone but no flashing discharge switch so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport but no sign of fire was seen.
summary: During climbout through FL 180, the crew received intermittent 'Cargo Fire Lower' warnings without observing a flashing discharge switch or smoke. They declared an emergency, returned for a visual approach, and landed with no fire signs found by fire crews or maintenance.

synopsis: A First Officer describes the extreme workload of a two man flight crew operating nearly 8 flight hours at night between the Middle East and Asia while communicating with controllers in poor English, at times on two frequencies.
summary: A two-crew flight from OMDB to Asia encountered excessive workload due to substandard radio and radar in Kolkata, Dhaka, and Yangon sectors. The pilot reported that complex ATC instructions requiring dual radio management are unsafe without a Radio Flight Officer and better company communication.

synopsis: DC-10 flight crew reported they lost an engine after takeoff that they feel was probably due to failure to complete checklist and mismanaged fuel pumps.
summary: The flight crew of a DC-10 operating with an inoperative fuel gauge experienced an engine rollback at 15,000 feet, likely caused by missed fuel pump checklist items due to distractions and glare. The crew executed an engine fire checklist and returned for a safe landing, suspecting pilot error in the manual fuel procedure.

synopsis: SCT Controller described a conflict event when an IFR release from LGB was delayed and plans to handle a VFR aircraft failed to materialize. The reporter suggested airspace changes that might prevent future occurrences.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managing an A320 departure and a C172 near LGB issued a turn that caused the A320 to receive a Resolution Advisory from a VFR aircraft at 2,800 feet. The controller attributed the conflict to airspace design limitations and admitted to assuming the VFR aircraft's altitude and intent without verification.

synopsis: The pilot of a C182 attempted to remain clear of Class B airspace by the use of his iPad for navigation guidance. He was advised that he had entered Class B airspace by several miles. Later when he compared his iPad chart depiction to a paper chart, he realized that when he zoomed in on his iPad, the altitude was not visible.
summary: A pilot flying a rented aircraft at 5,500 feet violated Class B airspace near ZZZ2 due to a recent airspace configuration change. The violation occurred because the pilot's Foreflight app displayed the TAC chart at a zoom level that hid the new 5,000-foot shelf altitude, leading to an undetected incursion.

synopsis: During pushback, while utilizing a new procedure, the Captain misunderstood the ground crew and thought the pushback was complete, and set the brakes. When the ground crew attempted to move the aircraft forward to the intended parking spot, the tow bar shear pin broke. The aircraft was returned to the gate for a Maintenance Inspection.
summary: During an experimental silent pushback, the Captain mistakenly set the brakes while the tug pulled the aircraft forward to a taxi spot, shearing the tow bar's shear pin. The crew returned to the gate for a nose gear inspection, resulting in an aircraft swap and removal from service due to maintenance requirements.

synopsis: Baron 58 pilot reported after takeoff he noticed airframe buffeting that he traced to vibration in the right trailing edge flap. He returned to departure airport for a zero flap approach.
summary: The pilot experienced altimeter and VSI bouncing, yoke buffet, and right flap vibration during the departure climb in low overcast. Suspecting the flap might detach if extended, the pilot elected to return for a no-flap ILS landing, which was completed uneventfully after notifying ATC and Maintenance.

synopsis: B737-800 First Officer reported airspeed, elevator feel differential, and EEC anomalies. First Officer airspeed was deemed most reliable and flight continued to destination after declaring an emergency.
summary: The crew experienced erratic airspeed indications, an elevator feel light, and EEC reversion during departure and descent. After the Captain's airspeed dropped 50+ knots at 11,000 feet, the First Officer took control, declared an emergency, and landed safely using the First Officer's accurate airspeed.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported they received a microburst alert from Tower on final approach and the Captain elected to continue the approach contrary to company guidelines and First Officer recommendation.
summary: The Captain continued a localizer approach despite a Tower microburst alert indicating a 35 KT loss, landing uneventfully. The Captain later admitted fatigue, inexperience with ground-based alerts, and confusing "alert" with "advisory" caused this violation of company guidance requiring a mandatory go-around.

synopsis: A B737-800 Captain's Airspeed dropped to about 200 KTS as the aircraft entered clouds at about 10,000 FT but the First Officer's airspeed remained normal at 250 KTS. Descending through about 5,000 FT, the airspeed was again normal.
summary: The Captain experienced a sudden Captain PFD IAS drop from 250 to under 200 KTS at 10,000 FT during an RNAV arrival, likely due to an intermittent IAS DISAGREE issue. The crew transferred controls to the First Officer, declared an emergency, and landed safely on Runway 16 after the Captain's IAS normalized below 5,000 FT.

synopsis: A B737-800 IAS and MASTER CAUTION alerted near rotation speed on takeoff because of a 20 KT to 50 KT left to right airspeed indicator difference so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The pilot flying experienced an IAS DISAGREE warning with 20 to 50 KT discrepancies near rotation, prompting a manual flight and overweight landing on ILS 34. The crew declared an emergency, requested AARF equipment, and landed safely for tire and brake inspection, noting a history of similar airspeed issues.

synopsis: A Lead Aircraft Maintenance Technician reports the left-hand (L/H) main landing gear (MLG) oleo strut on a CE-560XL aircraft had collapsed, allowing the L/H MLG casting to come in contact with the single main gear tire. The right MLG oleo had also collapsed. Reporter expressed concern for a catastrophic failure of the single main tire and aircraft safety.
summary: A Lead Technician and two mechanics discovered collapsed main gear oleos on a Cessna 560XL during a post-maintenance check, causing tire contact with the gear casting. The oleos leaked after servicing, prompting a recommendation for a mechanical stop to prevent catastrophic tire failure if collapse occurs in flight.

synopsis: Enroute Controller, distracted by other than normal duties, issued an altitude below MVA requirement, correcting same quickly.
summary: An air traffic controller managing a temporary tower during firefighting operations mistakenly cleared a King Air F90 to descend to 140 in a 150 MIA. The controller halted the descent after realizing the error, confirming the pilot had visual contact with the terrain.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a conflict event at FL350/370, claiming one of the aircraft was slow to respond when given an instruction contributing to the occurrence.
summary: An air traffic controller failed to adequately scan traffic before clearing an A319 from FL350 to FL370, causing a conflict with Air Carrier Y at FL360. The controller issued emergency turns and descents, resulting in a minimum separation of five miles and 1,000 feet, attributing the risk to poor traffic scanning and delayed pilot compliance.

synopsis: Experimental light twin pilot reports water contact while circling at low altitude to view sea life. The right propeller is damaged and the right wheel is missing. Aircraft is flown to a nearby airport and landed safely with minimal additional damage.
summary: The pilot of a twin-engine experimental aircraft descended to 30–50 feet to photograph a shark, lost control due to distraction and high sink rate, and struck the water, losing the right wheel and engine. After landing on one engine, a ground loop occurred due to crosswind and missing gear, resulting in aircraft damage but no injuries.

synopsis: BE55 pilot at 2,500 FT reports turning without clearance from NCT to avoid terrain north northeast of OAK due to the perception that terrain was a factor. Reporter was receiving vectors from NCT in day VMC.
summary: The pilot reported that NORCAL ATC vectored the aircraft toward higher terrain with a clearance of at or below 3,100 feet. The pilot turned left to avoid mountains after receiving no further instructions, resulting in a reprimand from the controller for deviating from the vector.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Business jet flight crew reports landing at NQX Runway 25 while attempting to land at EYW Runway 27.
summary: The crew landed at the wrong airport during a visual approach to Key West Runway 27 due to faded runway numbers, faded markings, and a lack of DME verification. The aircraft was stopped and cleared after the error was realized, with the pilot citing distraction and poor situational awareness as contributing factors.

synopsis: A321 pilot reported wake vortex encounter at FL340 from preceding Airbus that was two to two and one half minutes ahead.
summary: The pilot encountered wake turbulence at FL340 while en route to LOMIA, causing a 10 to 15-degree right roll. The disturbance was attributed to a preceding company Airbus 15 miles ahead, with no loss of control or clearance deviation reported.

synopsis: Air Carrier reported a high speed abort instruction from the Tower on a limited distance wet runway, reportedly an automated ATC alarm was the reason the instruction was issued by ATC.
summary: The flight crew aborted takeoff at approximately 100 knots on a wet runway after Tower issued an abort command due to a Ground RADAR conflict alarm. Although no actual conflict existed, FAA procedures required the controller to act on the alarm, resulting in a rejected takeoff, a go-around for a following aircraft, and a subsequent return to the gate for inspection.

synopsis: Q400 First Officer reports an unsafe nose gear indication after not getting the gear lever completely up on the first try. The alternate gear extension procedure is used to lower the gear and an uneventful landing ensues at the departure airport.
summary: The pilot failed to fully retract the landing gear handle during climb, causing nose gear unsafe lights to remain illuminated. The crew returned, performed alternate extension, and landed safely; maintenance later found nose gear door damage attributed to the poor handle grip.

synopsis: Dash 8-300 Captain reported a fuel truck nearly hit his aircraft on the ramp at CLT.
summary: A pilot taxiing an aircraft reported a fuel truck driven directly toward the radome, stopping only 25–50 feet away after the pilot activated lights. The truck swerved to avoid collision, and the pilot attributed the near-miss to the driver's distraction.

synopsis: B737-800 First Officer reported he dropped some AAA batteries that went under the floor in the rudder pedal area.
summary: During cruise, a pilot dropped three AAA batteries that bounced into the underfloor area beneath the First Officer's left rudder pedal. Despite a one-hour search with a mechanic after landing, the batteries remain missing, and the incident was logged and reported to Dispatch.

synopsis: An A300 flight crew descending via the FNCHR RNAV STAR to MEM, landing north transition, was advised to expect Runway 27 just prior to passing FNCHR. The pilot not flying, believing the 'landing south' transition would need to be programmed ASAP to provide guidance for the pilot flying, quickly programmed Runway 27--expecting the transition to program simultaneously--but, when activated, the FMS dumped all data beyond FNCHR and the autopilot kicked off. When they attempted to manually program and fly direct to JAMLA ATC noted their deviation and provided vectors for Runway 27.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced an FMS dump and autopilot disengagement during the FNCHR RNAV STAR arrival due to a late runway change and incorrect transition selection. The Captain attributed the deviation to fatigue-induced task saturation and poor communication, noting that immediate ATC notification would have prevented the error.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports about damage to the keel beam area of a company B737-800 aircraft when a left Main Landing Gear (MLG) was deflated. Contributing factors were heat, noise, lack of communications, distraction when Shift Manager started talking with the crew and maintenance work being accomplished during the MLG deflation.
summary: Two mechanics servicing a B737-800's landing gear after jack removal damaged a panel and intercostal when lowering the aircraft onto a ladder left in the wheel well. The incident was caused by a forgotten tool, distractions from the Shift Manager, and incomplete distribution of work cards.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a loss of separation event involving several aircraft. The reporter indicated the pilot started an unauthorized climb after being advised of the Controllers' plans.
summary: An Air Carrier X pilot climbed from FL360 to FL365 without a clearance, losing separation with two aircraft at FL370 and triggering a TCAS RA. The controller attributes the incident to the pilot misinterpreting a standby instruction as an expedite clearance and failing to read back or verify the altitude change.

synopsis: F11 Controller described a very confused traffic period when facility personnel failed to comply with SOP directives and set up a potential loss of separation event.
summary: An air traffic controller managing a busy arrival sector faced potential separation loss after East Departure assigned two aircraft to the wrong runway complex without coordination. The reporter attributes the incident to uncoordinated "valet parking" by inexperienced controllers, a failure to follow SOPs, and a neglected safety culture.

synopsis: A pilot approaching PHX Runway 7R commented on a bright TV style commercial billboard whose content changed during a dusk VMC approach, interfered with visual ability and was a distraction because it was brighter than the approach lights.
summary: A pilot reported that a bright lighted billboard located right of the extended centerline and abeam the approach end causes severe distraction during low visibility night approaches. The reporter recommends relocating the sign to prevent it from shining in pilots' eyes below 100 feet on final approach.

synopsis: When their yaw damper failed on approach the flight crew of a B737-700 was distracted and, unable to establish a stabilized approach to the short runway at their destination, performed a missed approach. A second approach suffered the same inability to stabilize at which time the First Officer noted abnormally high 'low speed' stall indications on the MASI [Mach Air Speed Indicator] and realized the flaps had not extended as commanded. They diverted successfully to an airport with longer runways.
summary: The crew experienced a yaw damper failure and abnormal MASI indications during approach, leading to two go-arounds. After the Captain initially dismissed the issues, the First Officer diagnosed a flap failure, prompting a diversion to complete the no-flaps checklist.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reports loss of cabin pressurization at FL220 after being dispatched with the left engine bleed inoperative and the APU powering the left pack to 17,000 feet. When the APU bleed air is turned off the problems begin. Crew returns to the departure airport and discovers that Maintenance performed the MEL procedure on the wrong engine.
summary: The flight crew and maintenance personnel were involved in a pressurization event during cruise at 22,000 feet caused by maintenance incorrectly applying MEL procedures to the good engine. The crew executed an emergency descent to 10,000 feet with oxygen mask deployment, stabilized the cabin, and returned to the departure airport.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported a loss of blue hydraulic system shortly after takeoff due to a pump failure. Flight returned to departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a low Blue Hydraulic Pressure ECAM alert shortly after takeoff due to an electric pump failure resulting in 0 PSI. They completed the checklist, contacted Maintenance and Dispatch, and returned to the departure airport for an uneventful landing.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reported an airborne conflict resulting in an RA and an altitude deviation.
summary: During the arrival phase, a crew operating an aircraft with a speed restriction received a TCAS RA while being vectored off the HAMMU1 arrival. The conflict was resolved by descending to 11,000 feet, though the pilot noted an error in pressing the TCS button instead of the autopilot disconnect during the maneuver.

synopsis: EMB-145LR Captain reported flaps failed in 0 degree position on approach. Crew declared an emergency and landed on the longest available runway.
summary: The flight crew experienced a flap failure at 0 degrees while being vectored for a visual approach at night. They declared an emergency, completed the QRH, and executed a high-speed landing on the longest available runway without further abnormalities.

synopsis: A pilot reported how scheduling changes, hotel issues and calls from crew scheduling disrupted his rest period.
summary: A flight crew member reported that scheduling changes reduced their overnight rest from 14 hours to a short duration, compounded by repeated calls from scheduling. The reporter identified the lack of sleep as a safety threat caused entirely by these scheduling errors and reassignments.

synopsis: The pilot of a DHC 8-100 was advised that the fleet's navigation database expiration date had gone unnoticed and they were required to defer the system per the Minimum Equipment List procedures.
summary: The flight crew operated two DH8 legs with an expired RNAV database because Maintenance missed the update and the Captain initialized the sole unit before the First Officer could verify it. Dispatch later ordered the unit MEL'd, forcing a return flight without RNAV capability.

synopsis: Dash 8-200 Captain reported a significant number of SOP violations during pre-departure activities, some of which had safety implications.
summary: The pilot reported that ramp personnel loaded three bags behind the left wing after the Number 2 engine started, triggering a cargo door warning light. The incident was caused by baggage being added after paperwork was completed without notifying the crew, alongside broader failures in ramp coordination and professionalism.

aircraft: McDonnell Douglas Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reports a taxiway incursion at MMTO due to a vague clearance and depiction of the A taxiway on the airport diagram.
summary: The pilot reported a taxiway discrepancy after landing where Tower instructed a join to taxiway A, which was not depicted on Jepp charts as ending at the runway. The pilot attributed the confusion to inaccurate commercial charts and unclear ATC instructions regarding the specific join point.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported communication difficulty that led to a runway incursion that he later traced to interference from a power splitter.
summary: A Cessna 172 pilot taxiing at TRK crossed an active glider runway due to poor situational awareness and radio interference from a Scosche dual charger. The pilot acknowledged the close call was caused by the charger's emissions, rushing, and unclear signage, though no collision occurred.

synopsis: A B737-700 Left Bleed tripped at FL400, but did not reset following the QRH. Ten minutes later a successful reset was accomplished but the bleed tripped again, so the flight continued single pack.
summary: Pilots enroute at FL400 experienced a Number 1 Bleed Trip Off, operated single pack, and attempted a reset that temporarily restored two-pack operation before the fault recurred. The aircraft arrived safely, but the pilot reported the incident to clarify QRH guidance on repeated reset attempts and ensure maintenance received full details.

synopsis: A B737-700 First Officer entered the Zero Fuel Weight (ZFW) in the FMC instead of the Takeoff Weight (TOW). After rotation the Captain added full power due to a sluggish aircraft feel and an ADI Stall indication. An inoperative EFB requiring a paper weight and balance contributed to the error.
summary: The flight crew entered Zero Fuel Weight instead of Takeoff Weight into the ACARS PERF function due to an unfamiliar interface and interruptions, resulting in reduced thrust and sluggish elevator control during takeoff. The crew corrected the error by applying maximum thrust after becoming airborne, attributing the incident to inadequate procedure review and confusing system design.

synopsis: After landing the Captain of a B757 is informed by the 2L Flight Attendant that a piece of aircraft flew off during approach. Post flight reveals a 12X20 inch piece of the inboard left slat to be missing.
summary: The flight crew reported a missing 12x20 inch piece of the upper left inboard slat after an uneventful landing, prompted by a cabin crew observation. Maintenance confirmed the structural failure of the leading edge honeycomb, noting no evidence of a bird strike.

synopsis: All four B747 pilots failed to recognize the foreign airport's 997 Hector Pascal altimeter and allowed 29.97 QNH to remain in the altimeter, despite ATC's repeated correction, which made the aircraft about 500 FT low on approach.
summary: A military charter crew misinterpreted an ATIS altimeter setting of 997 as inches instead of hectopascals during a night approach. Although the controller noted a transponder altitude discrepancy, the crew verified their setting, intercepted the ILS, and landed safely after realizing the unit error post-landing.

synopsis: A B757 EICAS alerted L HI STAGE BLEED during takeoff so the QRH was completed and the crew continued to FL370 single pack where the aural and light CABIN ALT WARNING alerted. An emergency was declared and the flight descended to a divert airport.
summary: The crew continued takeoff after a left high stage bleed caution, but single pack operation failed to maintain cabin altitude, triggering a red warning. They declared an emergency, descended, and diverted to a safe landing with manual pressurization assistance.

synopsis: During an approach, a DHC 8-400 IOE Captain allowed the aircraft's pitch to get excessively high and after assistance from the Check Airman he released the yoke which caused a blown tire and nose strut damage during the hard landing.
summary: During an IOE visual approach to Runway 31, the IOE Captain failed to correct a high pitch attitude near 100 feet, prompting the reporter to take control and push the nose forward. This resulted in a hard landing that blew a nose tire and caused undetected nose strut damage, though the aircraft was safely taxied to the gate.

synopsis: An A319 Captain on the LAS KEPEC3 near CLARR Intersection reported taking evasive action from a series of gliders while descending VMC from 13,000 FT to 8,000 FT. Some gliders had transponders, some not.
summary: During a VMC descent south of LAS, the pilot deviated from an ATC vector to 080 after TCAS indicated multiple climbing gliders, turning back to 010 to avoid a head-on conflict. The crew subsequently visually observed a non-squawking glider passing closely below and to the right before continuing safely to land.

synopsis: An EMB-145 EICAS alerted FLAPS FAIL when the Flap 9 was selected, so the QRH was completed, an emergency declared and an uneventful landing followed.
summary: During descent for a visual approach to runway 26L, the crew experienced a flap failure where the system remained at position 0 despite selecting Flaps 9. After declaring an emergency and receiving vectors, they executed a fast, no-flap landing on runway 22 and deferred maintenance troubleshooting to the next morning.

synopsis: After departure a CRJ-200 radio altimeter indication began fluctuating affecting the GPWS so, after resetting circuit breakers at Maintenance's advise, the aircraft returned to land with the faults continuing.
summary: The flight crew encountered fluctuating radar altimeter readings and GPWS alerts just after takeoff. Following unverified instructions from Maintenance Control to pull circuit breakers in flight, the crew returned to the departure airport due to the intermittent fault and a breakdown in communication.

synopsis: A DHC-8-300 autofeather remained armed after takeoff with the switch was de-selected during the after takeoff flow, so the flight returned to the departure airport but the system deactivated prior to landing.
summary: The pilot noticed the auto-feather system re-armed with the amber 'Arm' light illuminated during the after-takeoff flow despite the switch being deselected. The crew returned to the departure airport for maintenance, where the indication extinguished itself upon arrival.

synopsis: CL300 Captain reports a runway incursion while attempting to hold short of Runway 30R at SJC. The taxi instructions were to cross Runway 30L (at B) and angle to hold short of 30R at A. The hold line for 30R was crossed while attempting to locate Taxiway A.
summary: The flight crew at SJC crossed the hold short line for Runway 30R while taxiing after receiving non-standard instructions to angle across from Runway 30L. The pilot attributed the incursion to confusion over the taxiway sign location, complacency, fatigue from a long duty rotation, and distraction from schedule changes.

synopsis: A MD-83 Captain reported that he, and his entire crew became ill during preflight after a very strong odor was detected and hydraulic fluid loss were observed with the right pack ON.
summary: The flight crew and passengers experienced symptoms of hydraulic fluid vapor exposure after the APU and AC packs were activated on an aircraft with low hydraulic fluid. Two flight attendants were hospitalized, and the crew advised maintenance to investigate the odor source before future boarding.

synopsis: A King Air C90 E90 pilot noticed fuel leaking from the top of the right engine nacelle, so he declared an emergency, diverted to a nearby airport and after an uneventful landing Maintenance discovered a gasket separation was allowing the leak.
summary: During cruise, the pilot observed fuel leaking from the right nacelle due to a separated gasket. The crew declared an emergency, diverted to the nearest airport, and landed uneventfully before being towed to maintenance.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: During downwind approach pilot experiences a rough running engine and advises the Tower of the issue and the need to land opposite direction on the active runway, which is approved. Engine quits on short final and a safe landing ensues.
summary: The pilot experienced intermittent engine power loss and a complete engine failure on short final while landing Runway XR with three people and 9 gallons of fuel. The cause remains undetermined pending a mechanic's engine checkout.

synopsis: ZLC Controller described a momentary MVA infraction when issuing turn instructions to avoid a developing conflict with VFR traffic.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored Aircraft X for landing at JAC while managing VFR traffic, triggering a pilot-initiated RA. The controller issued a right 360 and climb to FL130 to maintain separation, resulting in the aircraft briefly clipping the Minimum IFR Altitude corner by a few hundred feet during the climb.

synopsis: Tower Supervisor described a reported NMAC in the traffic pattern when a student pilot with apparent limited English skills failed to extend upwind as instructed and conflicted with traffic entering downwind.
summary: A Ground Controller and Flight Line Manager reported a near-midair incident involving a student C152 and an RV7 on right downwind at a Class Delta airport. The C152 pilot misinterpreted repeated instructions, turning left toward the RV7, which maneuvered to avoid the student aircraft despite the controller observing no unsafe proximity.

synopsis: IAD Controller described an on going unsafe condition chronicling several late frequency changes from PCT making landing/takeoff decision very difficult.
summary: A Local Controller reported multiple incidents where PCT failed to transfer arriving aircraft to Tower frequency before entering airspace, causing unauthorized landings and near-loss of separation. The controller attributed these safety risks to PCT's inability to manage combined final positions and comply with separation restrictions.

synopsis: ZTL Controller voiced concern regarding the AVL Tower hours of operation, providing examples of flawed coordination regarding the ILS in use resulting in go-arounds and diversions.
summary: An R44 controller cleared a CRJ7 for an ILS Runway 34 approach at AVL, but the crew lost the localizer and never received the glide slope, forcing a fuel diversion. Subsequent arrivals also missed approaches or diverted due to signal issues and weather, which the reporter attributes to unsafe ARTCC limitations in mountainous airspace and insufficient AVL ATCT operating hours.

synopsis: A B737-700 Captain, cleared to taxi to Runway 14 at JAX via Romeo and November, reported the lack of taxiway identification of Romeo exiting the ramp and at several subsequent intersections enroute to the departure end of Runway 14.
summary: The flight crew reported missing taxiway markings for Romeo and November while taxiing to Runway 14. They notified Ground Control, which requested a formal report to have the signage repaired to prevent potential runway incursions.

synopsis: A B737-700 APU was discovered powering the aircraft at cruise, so it was turned OFF which put both engine generators online tripping the autopilot. The APU was restarted for autopilot power, but when the aircraft began load shedding both engine generators were restored for normal electrical operation.
summary: During climb through FL320, the Captain turned off the APU while it was powering the aircraft, causing autopilots to disengage and load shedding to occur. The crew resolved the issue by restoring main generator power after realizing they had inadvertently operated on sole APU source due to missed checklist items and distractions.

synopsis: An EMB-145 departed with both FMC's inoperative and had difficulty navigating on airways defined by LVOR's and airway intersections needing radial and DME information for description.
summary: The crew, operating with MELed FMSs, deviated laterally during departure after the Captain misinterpreted a DME distance for a turn point. The error resulted from fixating on the DME number while lacking recent conventional navigation practice, requiring ATC radar vectors to recover.

synopsis: Air Carrier Dispatcher describes a one plus hour computer outage and the difficulties encountered trying to work without it.
summary: An air traffic controller experienced a total computer system failure during operations, preventing flight following and locking screens while backup laptops also failed. A dispatcher used a personal hotspot to restore access, but the controller reported exhaustion from the rushed workflow implemented after the one-hour incident.

synopsis: A MD-83 Instrument Comparator began alerting after takeoff so following numerous inflight realignment attempts, the autopilot disengagement and ND faults, an emergency was declared with a request for a no gyro vectors to the departure airport.
summary: Following multiple maintenance delays, the crew experienced a Heading Comparator failure and autopilot disconnect during climb through FL22-FL23. They declared an emergency, hand-flew using the standby compass, and returned to the departure airport for a safe landing before removing themselves from duty.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew departed on YSSY SYD 4 departure with an ATC assigned heading, but the Captain engaged the autopilot with NAV active on the SYD 4 and turned the wrong direction before catching the error and correcting it.
summary: The crew experienced an incorrect left turn after takeoff at SYD due to selecting NAV early while expecting a 155 track instead of the cleared 170 heading. The error was immediately corrected manually, attributed to expectation bias and reduced situational awareness caused by heavy rain.

synopsis: A B737-800 developed an elevator flutter with a frequency of about 3 oscillations per second with climb power applied, an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced continuous elevator oscillation during climb above the cloud deck, which ceased at 14,000 feet but resumed with climb power. They declared an emergency, leveled at FL240, and returned for an overweight landing.

synopsis: The Captain of a Boeing 717-200 reports that after an aileron change the aircraft was given a pre-flight inspection, a flight control functional check, and a flight check. No deviations were noted, and the aircraft was signed off and returned to service. Reporter stated the ailerons became 'unbussed' at some point during the flight.
summary: Two pilots performed a Flight Control Functional check after an aileron change, confirming the ailerons were bussed together before returning the aircraft to service. The reporter states the ailerons later became unbussed at an unspecified time after the aircraft was signed off.

aircraft: Medium Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reports being dispatched with both FMSs inoperative and discovering enroute that the VOR at their destination is also inoperative. Flight is able to continue in VMC with Radar vectors from ZLC.
summary: The crew departed with both FMS units MEL'd and failed to notice a NOTAM indicating the BOI VOR was out of service. They continued to BOI using VOR navigation and VFR conditions, landing safely after realizing the error over BKE VOR due to not thoroughly reviewing NOTAMs.

synopsis: CRJ700 Captain experiences nose wheel steering failure during taxi off the runway after landing, requiring the aircraft to be stopped quickly to prevent departing the paved surface. The nose wheel steering is eventually reset electrically, but a tug is required to push the aircraft back from the taxiway edge before a turn can be made.
summary: The Captain reported that nose wheel steering disengaged during a sharp 90-degree runway exit turn, causing the aircraft to drift toward the runway edge. After stopping and failing initial resets, maintenance successfully re-engaged the system, allowing the crew to taxi to the gate following a tug assist.

synopsis: In an apparent mast moment indicator check, a BK117 pilot was distracted by another helicopter landing nearby and momentarily exceeded the mast moment limit.
summary: During a maintenance flight on the ramp, the pilot experienced a mast moment exceedance while the aircraft was light on skids with five mechanics and near-full fuel. The pilot attributed the event to momentarily looking away at a nearby landing aircraft and a slight tailwind, noting that a hover or tie-down procedure would have eliminated the risk.

synopsis: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician noticed during a Pre-Departure Check on a B777-200 aircraft, the Captain's seat forward limit switch was broken off. The front rail stops were also not correctly positioned. Unclear procedures and drawings in the Aircraft Maintenance Manual allowed for misinterpretation of installation.
summary: A mechanic inspecting a B777-200 during an ETOPS pre-departure check found the Captain's seat front rail stops mispositioned and the forward limit switch broken. The mechanic placarded the seat power functions inoperative per MEL 25-1a, attributing the issue to unclear seat installation instructions.

synopsis: An aircraft Inspector and a Maintenance Technician report a right Main Landing Gear (MLG) on a Curtiss C-46 aircraft had collapsed while taxiing during a final positioning left turn under differential power.
summary: A Curtiss C-46 experienced a right main landing gear collapse while taxiing to park on the ramp in ZZZ, causing a prop strike and wing contact. The Maintenance Inspector reported no injuries, with the cause currently unknown and under investigation.

synopsis: BMG Controller voiced concern regarding an unsafe working condition involving sun shades currently in the Tower Cab and the limited visibility encountered.
summary: Air traffic controllers at BMG Tower reported that inconsistent window shade tints caused aircraft to become invisible in the traffic pattern, particularly on bright days. This visibility loss led to a near-miss where a taildragger was instructed to turn away from an unseen aircraft, creating a dangerous situation requiring controllers to raise shades or move positions to maintain visual contact.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate jet flight crew reports a disagreement over the proper altitudes to fly on the RUUDY 4 departure from TEB, with the junior Captain deferring to the senior Captain. WENTZ is crossed above 1,500 FT climbing to 2,000 FT and noted by ATC.
summary: Two fatigued captains on a TEB departure disagreed on the RUUDY 4 RNAV initial altitude, with the junior pilot deferring to the senior captain's incorrect 2,000 FT setting. The aircraft climbed past the required 1,500 FT restriction to 2,000 FT before ATC intervention, attributed to crew fatigue and poor CRM.

synopsis: Lancair pilot reports an inadvertent entry into a TFR in his local area due to not checking NOTAMs and an inoperative GPS map display.
summary: A pilot conducting personal flight testing on a Garmin GDL 39 inadvertently entered a TFR because the unit failed to warn of proximity after the XM weather antenna was disconnected. The pilot attributed the incident to not checking NOTAMs and disabling available equipment that would have provided the necessary alert.

synopsis: G1159 First Officer reports descending early on the VOR DME or GPS-B approach to VNY, resulting in an EGPWS terrain warning.
summary: During a Part 91 positioning flight to VNY, the Pilot Flying descended below the assigned 3,400 feet before the final approach fix due to unclear communication with the Pilot Not Flying. This resulted in a terrain warning, requiring an immediate climb to 3,400 feet before accepting a visual approach.

synopsis: BE58 pilot is informed of a heading error on departure by ATC which is due to a malfunctioning compass system. In level VMC flight the compass eventually corrects itself and the flight continues to destination.
summary: The pilot experienced significant heading lag during the FRG 4 departure climbout, causing a 60-degree deviation from the cleared 030 heading. The pilot diverted to VFR conditions while the compass corrected, and the aircraft will undergo avionics inspection to determine the cause of the gyro spool-up delay.

synopsis: A23 pilot reports confusion between himself and the Tower when cleared for an intersection takeoff on Runway X, with the Tower intending to say Runway XX. An aircraft on short final goes around and the reporter rejects his takeoff.
summary: The pilot and ATC were involved during taxi and takeoff when the pilot was cleared for the wrong runway due to a controller error and confusing frequency cross-talk. The pilot aborted takeoff upon seeing an aircraft on final, resulting in a go-around for the landing traffic.

synopsis: HS125 Captain experiences unreliable airspeed indication climbing through 3,500 FT resulting in an overspeed upon leveling at 8,500 FT. Post flight reveals that a small bird may have impacted the Captain's pitot tube.
summary: During climb and cruise, the Captain's airspeed indicator fluctuated due to a bird carcass blocking the pitot tube, causing a 40-knot discrepancy with the Co-pilot's instruments. The crew completed a normal landing using alternate data, and maintenance removed the obstruction, grounding the aircraft for Pitot Static and RVSM re-certification.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reports being over taken in the pattern by a light twin departing after the reporter, causing a NMAC.
summary: The departing pilot reported a near mid-air collision with a green and white twin that overtook them in the crosswind leg at Sundance. The reporter attributed the incident to the twin pilot's garbled radio calls, failure to maintain proper separation, and incorrect pattern entry.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cirrus SR22 declared an emergency and landed safely after experiencing a loss of engine power.
summary: The pilot reported a partial engine failure in flight causing loss of power, indicated airspeed, and altitude. ATC vectored the aircraft to the nearest airport for a safe landing with no injuries or damage.

synopsis: BE23-24 pilot experiences electrical failure and lands at his Tower controlled destination airport without communication.
summary: A solo pilot flying a Beech Musketeer Super III experienced a total electrical failure, including radio and GPS loss, caused by two alternator wires parting during flight. The pilot successfully executed a short-field landing at the destination airport without communication and later repaired the wiring.

synopsis: RV-9 pilot reports loosing power ten minutes after takeoff from a fuel stop. The engine continues to make power and a landing on a highway is delayed in hopes of landing at an airport. Before that can happen the engine begins to run normally again and the flight continues to destination.
summary: The pilot experienced engine RPM decay and roughness ten minutes after departure, suspecting fuel contamination. After declaring an emergency and attempting a highway landing, the engine recovered, allowing the pilot to climb to 11,500 feet and continue to the destination.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew and the LAS Tower Controller involved describe an airborne conflict between the Air Carrier going around from a Runway 25L approach and a Coporate jet departing Runway 19R. The Corporate jet crew is instructed to stay low but responds to a TCAS RA and goes high requiring the Air Carrier crew to go under.
summary: Air Carrier X crew executed a go-around on Runway 25L due to excessive tailwind while a Corporate jet departed intersecting Runway 19R. The Corporate jet received a Resolution Advisory and climbed hard to pass overhead, avoiding a collision with the descending Air Carrier X aircraft.

synopsis: Tower Controller described the complexities of handling an emergency aircraft inbound opposite direction to the normal flow of traffic and the coordination/communications difficulties encountered.
summary: A Local controller managed an A330 emergency diversion while launching departures, but TRACON stopped departures early without coordination, causing delays. The A330 landed long, blocking Intersection E, and required a doctor, revealing poor communication and staffing issues during the event.

synopsis: ZSE Controller described a MOCA/MVA event when an aircraft rerouted to avoid higher terrain then failed to answer attempts by ATC to establish communications.
summary: An Air Carrier X C320 at 12,000 feet became NORDO while crossing the Mt. Adams MIA of 14,300 after requesting a reroute from an ATC controller. The aircraft eventually turned to avoid the mountain in a subsequent sector, though the cause of the communication loss remained unknown.

synopsis: ATL Controller voiced concern regarding operations conducted with weather all around and no consideration given to the possibility of go-around's.
summary: Ground controller and Local controllers at ATL faced safety concerns during simultaneous ILS PRM approaches and departures in heavy precipitation. Despite Ground warnings that a 190-degree departure heading offered no go-around escape, supervisors and Locals proceeded, compromising safety until departures could resume safely.

synopsis: N90 Controller described a TCAS RA event while vectoring an IFR aircraft to HPN, the reporter noting that current airspace design is problematic and should be changed to prevent future occurrences.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managing three positions issued a traffic alert to Air Carrier X on a visual approach to HPN when a VFR aircraft climbed to 1,800 feet. The carrier responded to a Resolution Advisory by climbing to 2,300 feet, entering a departure path, which the controller attributed to dangerous airspace design around HPN.

synopsis: B737 flight crew is informed after a ferry flight that the crew oxygen bottle was turned off for the flight.
summary: The ferry pilot reported that the next crew discovered the B737 crew oxygen valve was shut off after a night ferry flight. The pilot attributed the error to potential distraction from an unfamiliar airport and non-standard operations, admitting they likely missed the gauge drop during the preflight check.

synopsis: The pilots of a B737-300 observed an N1 overspeed condition of the #2 engine and elected to return to the departure airport. A successful landing was completed.
summary: The Pilot Flying reported a runaway #2 engine N1 spike to 107% at FL 240 while deviating in VMC, causing a left yaw. The crew executed the Engine Limit/Surge/Stall checklist, returned to the departure airport, and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: A B737-700 pressurization system malfunctioned so the crew declared an emergency and diverted. During the descent the O2 masks dropped and three personal oxygen bottles but were used but not reported to Maintenance.
summary: The Captain diverted the aircraft due to a pressurization issue, resulting in an emergency descent and oxygen mask deployment. Post-landing, the pilot learned Maintenance had used three POBs without reporting them to Dispatch, though no FAR or procedure violations occurred during the event.

synopsis: A320 flight crew experiences an ECAM alert for BCL1, immediately followed by BCL2, losing essential DC power while in cruise. Many pages of ECAM's are complied with until finally the RAT is deployed, which cleared most of the ECAM's and repowered the ess DC bus. Flight continues to destination but after touchdown the ground spoilers would not deploy, after the RAT died, communications were lost, and the airplane went through multiple rapid BIT checks, including fire/detect cycles including lights and alarms. The engines would not shut down normally at the gate and the fire buttons had to be used.
summary: During cruise, an A320 crew experienced dual BCL failures and essential DC power loss, deploying the RAT to restore power before continuing to destination. After landing, the aircraft failed to recognize ground status, preventing spoiler deployment and normal engine shutdown, requiring fire buttons to stop the engines.

synopsis: A320 First Officer experiences a Green Hydraulic system failure at FL320 and the crew elects to continue to destination.
summary: The crew experienced a total Green hydraulic system failure at FL320, requiring gravity gear extension and an emergency landing. Despite two TCAS RAs and sluggish handling on final approach, the aircraft landed safely and was towed in by airport operations.

synopsis: A320 Captain experiences a Green Hydraulic system failure during taxi in after landing resulting in loss of nose wheel steering. After stopping on the taxiway the aircraft is towed to the gate.
summary: The flight crew experienced a loss of nose wheel steering and green hydraulic low pressure while taxiing after landing, causing the aircraft to veer left. They stopped the plane with brakes, and airport personnel observed hydraulic fluid leaking before the aircraft was towed to the gate.

synopsis: Air carrier pilot describes a rolling delay caused by a rejected takeoff due to low power and a lack of English speaking mechanics. The company sends mechanics to correct the engine malfunction and the flight departs the next day.
summary: The crew aborted takeoff due to a number 2 engine failure to spool-up, causing a hard right veer. Maintenance later identified a cracked anti-ice solenoid switch and damaged cannon plug, requiring repairs before a successful departure the next day.

synopsis: Widebody flight crew and the jetway operator involved describe a jetway contact with the aircraft that causes damage to the pitot tubes.
summary: During preflight checks, a malfunctioning jetway struck and bent the left pitot tube, causing further damage when an operator attempted to retract it. Maintenance declared the aircraft inoperative due to the impact, requiring a third operator to reposition the jetway for deplaning.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew detects smoke during cruise (approaching top of descent) which the flight attendants believe is coming from an oven. An emergency is declared and the flight proceeds to the destination airport at best forward speed. It is necessary to remind ATC that they are an emergency aircraft to prevent vectoring for traffic. The jetway operator does not show up until five minutes after the aircraft arrives at the gate.
summary: The flight crew and cabin crew experienced smoke from a first-class galley oven while cruising at FL400, prompting an emergency descent to ZZZ. Although the crew expedited the landing and applied fire extinguishers, they faced delays from ATC routing and a five-minute wait for the jetway driver upon arrival.

synopsis: A B757 Captain advised that the FMC database on both fleets failed to display the airspeed crossing restrictions at TXMEX and CRVZA published on the TXMEX RNAV STAR into IAH.
summary: The pilot discovered missing hard speed constraints at TXMEX and CRVZA while crosschecking the TXMEX RNAV STAR into Houston. The dispatcher reported that flight planning software only supports Mach speeds, prompting a recommendation to inform database producers to include the missing knots in the next revision.

synopsis: A pilot flying on Canadian Airway NCA20 noted that the MORA's were 22,000 feet and lower, but his B737 did not have escape route guidance in the event of pressurization loss or other events requiring a descent.
summary: The pilot flying and pilot monitoring on a Boeing 737 en route to ANC found no engine-out or cabin depressurization guidance in the Operations Manual or charts for high-terrain areas near position DB. Consequently, they improvised diversion strategies, noting the aircraft lacks the escape route warnings available on widebody types.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reports being assigned 250 KTS during descent then slowing as he nears the airport without advising ATC. Approach advises that 250 KTS was assigned and should be maintained.
summary: The flight crew, operating a twin-engine aircraft with one failed MCDU, slowed to 210 KTS while being vectored off the Johns Arrival into CLT. The pilot attributed the subsequent ATC speed query to task saturation and confusion over whether the "maintain 250 KTS during descent" clearance applied after the aircraft was configured for approach.

synopsis: An air carrier Captain refiled a route to his planned destination prior to three flights to avoid weather because his Dispatcher refused to file or increase fuel even with known weather along the filed route.
summary: A pilot reported four flights where Dispatch filed routes through strong thunderstorms without contingency fuel or alternative plans. The pilot repeatedly contacted ATC to obtain new clearances and fuel, noting that Dispatch refused assistance, increasing workload and causing delays.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier crew departed on the CLT DEBIE 6 departure and the First Officer followed the #2 FMS Flight Director command off track because the flight plan was entered in the #1 FMS but not verified in the #2 FMS.
summary: During the DEBIE 6 departure from Runway 18C, the crew experienced a lateral deviation after arming LNAV because FMS 2 contained an incorrect flight plan while the pilot monitored the Aerodata page. The crew corrected the course after identifying the FMS discrepancy and receiving a new heading from ATC.

synopsis: A B737-800 Captain, cleared ro descend via the HAWKZ RNAV STAR to SEA, reported excessive ATC intervention with route shortening direct routes and large scale variations in assigned airspeeds.
summary: The pilot reported unsafe procedures during the HAWKZ 2 RNAV arrival while landing north, where a direct clearance to FOOTT Intersection caused a 2,200 FT profile deviation. Subsequent airspeed changes from 300 to 210 KTS by Center and Approach, attributed to sequencing conflicts, required excessive heads-down time before a normal landing.

synopsis: A B757 Number 2 EGT exceeded temperature parameters as the throttles were moved to begin taxi so the engine was shutdown, an emergency declared, the QRH completed and the aircraft returned to the gate.
summary: The pilot reported an EGT exceedence on Engine 2 during taxi, prompting the Captain to shut off its fuel. After ARFF inspection and a runway change distraction, the crew returned to the gate and requested maintenance.

synopsis: A DC-10 First Officer failed to verify the Number 2 Fuel Pump ON before start which caused on engine rolled back to idle climbing through FL190. Not knowing the cause, the Captain shut the engine down, declared an emergency and returned to the departure airport.
summary: The First Officer failed to verify the Number 2 fuel pump was on during engine start due to MEL confusion and distraction, causing the engine to roll back to idle at FL190. The crew followed QRH procedures, shut down the engine, and returned to the departure airport.

synopsis: Wide body flight crew reported wake vortex encounter in trail of an Airbus on final approach to MEM that was strong enough to trigger a go-around.
summary: The crew encountered uncontrollable wake turbulence from a preceding Airbus at 320 feet AGL on final approach, causing a go-around at 280 feet. The pilot attributed the event to RECAT spacing limitations in quartering headwinds and successfully landed after receiving vectors.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported a wake vortex encounter in trail of an A380 that resulted in a 90 degree roll. Reporter stated he was not advised he was following a heavy.
summary: A CRJ900 crew encountered severe wake turbulence from an A380 during final approach, causing rapid snap rolls to 90 degrees at 600 feet. The First Officer recovered control, and the aircraft landed safely with no injuries, though the pilot reported the separation was insufficient.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 First Officer reported a track deviation after he failed to select an MCP heading and engage the NAV mode because of distractions from a new hire jumpseat pilot and a just completed IOE Captain.
summary: A pilot, a new Captain, and a training jumpseater experienced a navigation error during climb after takeoff when the aircraft turned left instead of right to heading 090. The deviation resulted from crew distraction caused by disjointed discussions and inexperience, requiring ATC to issue a new heading to correct the course.

synopsis: A B777 Captain parked on the ZBAA ramp described a communication's situation in which the crew was unable to contact the Company, Operations, or ATC but a passenger was texting Operations and determined they were released to taxi.
summary: Pilots at Beijing encountered pushback confusion due to an inoperative PA system, poor radio links, and unclear ATC phraseology. Although the crew fixed the PA issue, they could not verify clearance status until a passenger relayed information from Operations, highlighting severe communication breakdowns.

synopsis: An A320 ECAM alerted HYD B SYS LO PR followed shortly thereafter by HYD B RSVR LO LVL so an emergency was declared, the QRH completed and an uneventful landing followed at the destination airport.
summary: The flight crew encountered HYD B SYS LO PR and HYD B RSVR LO LVL warnings at 37,000 FT, prompting an emergency declaration and direct routing to the destination. They landed safely on runway 16R after following non-normal landing procedures and coordinating with maintenance and ATC.

synopsis: A B757-200 right cockpit window cracked with a loud bang so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure.
summary: The First Officer reported a right front window crack and loud bang at FL300 during climb out, prompting an emergency return to the departure airport. The crew executed QRH procedures for an overweight landing, which was uneventful with normal brake temperatures, resulting in flight cancellation.

synopsis: A B717 crew executed a go-around after a MCDU NAVAID UNTUNEABLE alert and on the go-around were cleared to 3,000 FT but climbed to 4,800 FT. The second approach was successful after the LOC frequency was verified.
summary: The pilot flying initiated a go-around at 3,000 feet due to a 'NAVAID UNTUNEABLE' message and turbulence, inadvertently climbing to 4,800 feet by following training instincts instead of ATC's instruction to maintain 3,000 feet. The crew subsequently completed a successful ILS approach after verifying the localizer.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier departed DEN with FMS programmed for the incorrect RNAV because an early rise hours before with no time for breakfast and then the First Officer did not see the PDC clearance change. ATC caught the error later.
summary: The flight crew departed OMA to DFW but failed to cross-check an amended PDC, loading the STAKR1 departure instead of the assigned SPAZZ1. Confusion arose because both procedures shared identical initial fixes, though ATC radar vectors prevented a lateral deviation.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A corporate aircraft departed ZZZ Runway XXR and took evasive action visually and using TCAS from a B737 after that aircraft's crew executed a go around from Runway XY because of winds.
summary: The pilot reported a near-miss during climb-out from Runway XXR with a B737 performing a go-around at less than 400 feet AGL. Confusing "stay low" instructions from the Tower led the crew to maintain climb power, resulting in an 800-foot vertical separation when TCAS issued a "Monitor Vertical Speed" resolution advisory.

synopsis: A Dispatcher realized after the fact that an A320 with an MEL restricting extended overwater flights, was routed with a flight segment over the Gulf of Mexico.
summary: A dispatcher released a flight from MMUN with an inoperative portable ELT (MEL 25-61-01A) on a route violating the 162 NM overwater restriction. The error occurred because the dispatcher and crew assumed the MEL only restricted ETOPS operations and failed to read the specific Operations Procedures.

synopsis: A Dispatcher discovered after the fact that the B757-200, dispatched with ACARS and HF Comm MEL's communications systems in actuality only had a single functioning long range communication system. ATC was enlisted to provide info/data relays if required.
summary: A pilot reported that an international flight with MEL'd HF/SATCOM and ACARS lost SATCOM capability due to incorrect software, leaving only single HF. The cause was the MEL failing to indicate that the ACARS software issue also rendered SATCOM unusable.

synopsis: A widebody inbound to ZGGG from the northeast and cleared for the ILS to Runway 20R was unable to receive the localizer and deviated from course. ATC provided ameliorative handling.
summary: Pilots flying into ZGGG received late arrival and runway clearances after passing IGONO, causing FMS autotuning failure and localizer off flags. The crew manually re-intercepted the ILS 20R multiple times amidst high ATC workload and frequency changes before landing uneventfully.

synopsis: B777 Captain is instructed to taxi to and hold short of Runway 10 on Taxiway N at VDIP. After stopping initially at the ILS hold point and with VMC, taxi is continued toward the runway on Taxiway N. The Tower expected the crew to hold at the ILS hold line.
summary: The flight crew taxied past the ILS Runway 10 critical area hold point believing it was inactive, but the Tower subsequently ordered them to hold for an aircraft on final. The reporter noted that the airport diagram does not depict this critical area or hold short point.

synopsis: An A319 flight crew discovered that the takeoff performance data provided by the company's new flight planning/dispatch program was not based on current meteorlogical information. The reporter believes discrepancies such as this, if common, could be hazardous.
summary: Pilots discovered during a departure that ACARS provided incorrect takeoff performance data based on outdated weather, differing from the current ATIS. The First Officer identified the error, which caused significant V-speed changes and highlighted a serious accident risk if such errors occurred on short runways with heavy aircraft.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Captain noted that PHL Ramp personnel and controllers operate with less than standard concern about potential main line and RJ aircraft conflict and collision events.
summary: The Captain reported a near-collision risk at PHL while parking, caused by an adjacent regional jet being aggressively pushed back under their wing in tight quarters. The Ramp Supervisor dismissed safety concerns by claiming another carrier controls the ramp, and the Tower Controller used non-standard "Copy that" phraseology.

synopsis: When, midway through the climb, several flight attendants and a passenger complained of physiological reactions to an obnoxious 'body odor' smell, primarily in the area of the aft galley and lavs, the transatlantic flight was turned back to the departure airport where several individuals were taken to the hospital for examination. Both reporters stressed the recurring nature of such events.
summary: During climb through FL210, a pilot declared an emergency due to odors sickening three flight attendants and a relief pilot, resulting in a heavy weight landing. The crew attributed the issue to unaddressed aircraft odors, while maintenance previously dismissed similar reports as condensation without logging a write-up.

synopsis: CRJ700 flight crew reports having their takeoff clearance canceled at 80 KTS after requesting a weather deviation when airborne. The non flying Captain asks for clarification without response from the Tower and the takeoff is rejected at 120 KTS.
summary: The First Officer and Captain rejected a takeoff at 120 KTS on a wet runway after Tower canceled clearance due to a weather cell and then experienced a communications failure. The crew aborted smoothly, waited for brake cooling, and departed later after maintenance confirmed no inspection was needed.

synopsis: EMB145 Captain experiences LG AIR/GROUND FAIL on takeoff which prevents the landing gear from retracting. QRH procedures are complied with, an emergency is declared and flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced an LG AIR/GROUND FAIL immediately after takeoff, preventing landing gear retraction and subsequent spoiler/thrust reverser deployment. They returned to land safely using brakes only, suspecting a recent strut repack may have caused the sensor failure.

synopsis: MD-83 Captain experiences a Tail Compartment Temp High light climbing out of 6,000 FT. QRH procedures are complied with, an emergency is declared and flight returns to the departure airport with the left engine at idle per the chicklist.
summary: The pilot reported a tail compartment high indication at 6,000 feet, isolating a bleed leak to the left engine likely caused by previous ducting work. With no passengers on board, the crew declared an emergency, returned for a right traffic pattern, and landed with emergency vehicles standing by.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant working the aft cabin of a B747-400 aircraft reports that meal service cart tie-downs were missing at main cabin doors 5-left (5L) and 5-right (5R). Concerns raised for passenger and flight attendant safety due to carts left temporarily unattended and not tied down during meal service.
summary: A flight attendant reported a FAR violation on a Boeing 747 during meal service when full carts were left unattended at doors 5L and 5R due to missing tie-downs. The reporter stated this unsafe practice, required to serve a full cabin, could have caused injury during turbulence, though no injuries occurred.

synopsis: PA28 pilot on an IFR flight plan reports being distracted by a radio problem and allowing his heading to drift off course by 45-50 degrees before correcting.
summary: A low-time IFR pilot flying a friend in the evening lost heading control by 45–50 degrees during a handoff to Fayetteville due to distraction from a minor communication equipment issue and radio setup. The pilot corrected the course and landed safely, attributing the incident to inexperience and committing to recurrent training.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot reports being bumped on the main skid by a landing C140 as the helicopter is air taxied over the grass to parking. There is no damage to the helicopter and slight damage to the top of the aircraft's wing. The aircraft pilot lost control during the landing roll and departed the runway. The C140 pilot believes the rotor wash caused the loss of control.
summary: A Robinson R44 helicopter pilot and a Cessna 140 pilot were involved at an uncontrolled airfield when the Cessna's left wingtip contacted the helicopter's right skid during the Cessna's landing rollout. The Cessna pilot lost directional control due to a locked right brake and rotor vortices, causing the aircraft to drift left under the hovering helicopter, though no damage was found.

synopsis: Astra Captain reports discovering during arrival briefing that his FISEL 5 STAR is out of date in his iPad when compared to the First Officers iPad. Post flight revealed that both iPad's had current databases. The database provider described the problem as a glitch that was easily correctable.
summary: During the arrival brief for a FISEL arrival into FLL, the pilot not flying had a more current STAR on their Commercial 1 Flight Data iPad than the pilot flying. Tech support attributed the discrepancy to a software glitch that required deactivation and reactivation, noting there was no way to identify the outdated charts.

synopsis: A Piper Cub pilot, thinking he was out of gas, landed and determined there were still 11 gallons aboard in a wing tank.
summary: The pilot failed to properly position the fuel petcock during cruise, resulting in landing with only 11 gallons of fuel in the wing tank. The aircraft was subsequently restarted and flown back to the airport.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot reports a NMAC with a PA28 at 2,000 FT near PDX.
summary: The pilot reported a near mid-air collision with a white Piper Cherokee while cruising at 2,000 feet AGL and 140 knots. Both aircraft executed evasive maneuvers to avoid impact, and the pilot attributed the encounter to the lack of TCAS equipment.

synopsis: C182 pilot reports a rough running engine with zero oil pressure and the decision to land in a cornfield. No damage and no injuries were reported.
summary: A Cessna 182 pilot and student experienced zero oil pressure and engine vibration during a training flight, forcing a precautionary landing in a cornfield. The pilot shut down the engine at 200 feet to prevent catastrophic failure, resulting in a safe landing with no aircraft damage.

synopsis: DC9 Captain reports being advised of a low altitude warning by the Tower during a sidestep visual maneuver to the parallel runway. The descent rate is decreased and a normal landing ensues.
summary: Pilots on a visual approach to Runway 23R received a low altitude warning from Tower while navigating rapidly changing weather. They slowed their descent rate to maintain the glide slope using visual lighting and landed without further incident.

synopsis: Champ pilot experiences a rough running engine after an extended down time waiting for parts. The fuel selector, throttle and mixture are all manipulated without immediate effect. Suddenly engine power increases dramatically and the aircraft cannot be controlled before contact with the hangar door occurs.
summary: A pilot taxiing a 1946 Aeronca Champ after an annual inspection experienced an engine surge following fuel cutoff cycling, causing the aircraft to overrun brakes and strike a hangar door. The pilot attributed the incident to an inadvertently activated fuel shutoff with ambiguous handle position, leading to delayed power recovery.

synopsis: Airframe and Powerplant Technician reports an inadvertent flight after starting the engine with the throttle full open. A successful landing ensues on the second attempt.
