synopsis: MD82 flight crew reports a 'WHEEL NOT TURNING' light during takeoff and rejects at 100 knots. The aircraft is taxied back to the gate where the left inboard brake indicates hot.
summary: The Captain aborted the takeoff at 100 knots after the 'Wheel Not Turning' light illuminated. Post-incident checks revealed the left inboard brake temperature reached 310 degrees, while other brakes remained below 200 degrees.

synopsis: A Wide Body freighter aircraft encountered severe turbulence at FL380 crossing the Andes Mountains into Santiago, Chile which resulted in altitude deviations of plus and minus 800 feet along with high and low speed warnings caused by airspeed fluctuation of 45 knots.
summary: The crew encountered severe turbulence at FL380 over the Andes, causing airspeed fluctuations of ±45 knots, altitude deviations of ±800 feet, and stick shaker and overspeed warnings. Although ATC and maintenance were notified, no log entry was made for the overspeed warning, prompting a suggestion for improved weather forecasting.

synopsis: A MD-11 number three engine vibration indicated 5.0 with an Amber Box after takeoff so following trouble shooting the crew returned to the departure airport for maintenance with the engine at idle.
summary: During climbout at 6,000 feet, the crew observed a Number 3 engine EVM amber box indicating 5.0, which correlated with vibration returning above 40% N1. After consulting maintenance, they kept the engine at idle, landed, and shut it down on the ramp.

synopsis: An ERJ-145 flight crew initiated an emergency descent, declared an emergency with ATC and, ulimately, returned to their departure airport following the loss of both air conditioning and pressurization packs.
summary: The flight crew experienced a dual pack valve closure at FL 350, causing rapid cabin altitude increase and an emergency descent to 10,000 FT. The aircraft returned to the departure airport with manual pressurization control, though the specific cause of the valve closures remained undetermined.

synopsis: C210 pilot reported encountering turbulence from a departing Airbus that affected his landing roll out directional control.
summary: The pilot reported that after landing past the touchdown point, the aircraft encountered wake turbulence from a preceding departing Airbus. This caused the aircraft to roll and veer left then right while slowing down on the ground.

synopsis: An A321 Captain rejected a TOGA power takeoff after the left engine turbine section failed which triggered an ENG 1 FAIL ECAM.
summary: During a maximum weight takeoff, the Captain rejected the roll after a loud bang and left turn indicated left engine failure. Maintenance later confirmed destroyed turbine disks, but fire crews found no external damage, allowing the crew to taxi back and reposition passengers on a replacement aircraft.

synopsis: An airline crew Captain advised the signs identifying high speed exits ZH and ZJ from Runway 22L at EFHK are misplaced and easily confused.
summary: The pilot exited Helsinki Runway 22L onto taxiway ZH instead of the instructed ZJ due to confusing signage and Tower issuing clearance instructions during rollout. The crew corrected the error with no traffic conflict, noting that issuing turnoff instructions prior to landing would reduce workload.

synopsis: A B757 crew declared an emergency, and diverted to a nearby airport after completing the Smoke, Fire or Fumes Checklist for an odor and white smoke in the cockpit.
summary: Pilots at FL400 encountered light smoke from behind the instrument panel, declared an emergency, and diverted. They completed the Smoke, Fire, and Fumes checklist, which cleared the smoke, allowing a normal landing; maintenance later focused on equipment cooling fans and filters, though the cause remains unknown.

synopsis: Smoke developed from a B777 Business Galley ceiling and a Flight Attendant concerned for her safety was told to remain at her station in case of an evacuation.
summary: A flight attendant refused to re-enter an aircraft with a repaired engine crack after smoke filled the galley, citing safety concerns. A supervisor then intimidated the crew member with threats of job loss regarding a direct order, prompting the attendant to request a union representative.

synopsis: An A330 ECAM alerted ENG 1 SLOW TO RESPOND in flight, but the Maintenance Control Computer displayed ENG 1 CTL SYS FAULT which indicated a Fuel Metering Unit fault so the aircraft returned to the departure station. Subsequently, no test flight was flown, but a revenue flight crew reported normal operation.
summary: Maintenance Control and the flight crew reported an A330 Engine 1 slow response and FMU fault during cruise, causing a return to the departure airport. After replacing the FMU, a verification flight was conducted despite documentation restrictions, and the engine subsequently operated normally to the destination.

synopsis: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports about his Air Carrier's continued practice of releasing B767-300 aircraft with Main Cabin Door window viewports completely obscured by moisture condensation due to window heater panel failure. No Cabin Door window visibility requirements exists when deferring heat panels under B767 MEL 56-XX.
summary: A mechanic refused to defer a B-767 at ZZZ in August 2013 after the forward right cabin door window was fogged with condensation. The Technical Manager approved the condition under MEL 56-XX, but the mechanic argued the MEL must be revised to explicitly prohibit such visibility obstructions.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports that a Required Inspection Item (RII) was missed after a Green System hydraulic line was replaced on an A300 aircraft. The hydraulic hose for the all speed aileron had previously ruptured in flight, requiring an air turn back.
summary: A300 maintenance technicians replaced a ruptured Green System hydraulic hose but missed the required Return to Inspection (RII) due to human error and time constraints. The aircraft departed before the oversight was discovered, leading to a hangar return for rework and immediate RII training for all technicians.

synopsis: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports about a Part Power Stop (PPS) that was inadvertently engaged on a B757-200 aircraft engine after a Fuel Flow Governor replacement. Technician also noted the lack of a positive lockout mechanism to properly secure the PPS.
summary: Maintenance personnel replaced the Fuel Flow Governor on a B757-200 Engine 2, but the engine failed to start reliably. The reporter attributes the issue to the inadvertent engagement of the Part Power Stop during troubleshooting, noting the lack of a positive lockout mechanism.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Light aircraft pilot reported he struck another aircraft's rudder with his wing while taxiing.
summary: The pilot struck the rudder of a parked Piper with their left wing while taxiing on a grass taxiway. The pilot attributed the incident to miscommunication with a marshal on a scooter who failed to assist with wing clearance.

aircraft: Light Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Turboprop First Officer reports announcing intentions to depart Runway 5 at AND airport then learned that a Baron is rolling out opposite direction.
summary: Two pilots on an on-demand flight entered Runway 5 at a non-towered airport while a Baron was landing on the opposite end, Runway 23. The crew attributed the runway incursion to operational pressure and complacency regarding slow traffic, noting they could not see the Baron due to the runway's depressed ends.

synopsis: C-45 pilot took off on a Special VFR clearance and encountered deteriorating conditions in which he was unable to maintain Minimum Safe Altitude and remain clear of clouds. Pilot climbed through overcast into VFR conditions.
summary: An instrument-rated pilot departed VFR under Special VFR clearance in deteriorating weather, inadvertently entering IMC while searching for a cloud break. The pilot climbed 500 feet to exit the clouds into VMC, attributing the incident to overconfidence and a lack of viable contingency plans.

aircraft: Cessna Single Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: The student pilot on a solo cross country flight experienced gusty winds during landing resulting in damage to the nose landing gear of the Cessna 162.
summary: A student pilot soloing a training aircraft experienced a hard landing with nose gear separation due to a gusty wind flare at 2,500 feet. The pilot stopped the aircraft on the runway without injury after initial communication difficulties with the Tower.

synopsis: The multi engine check ride almost went awry until the examiner and applicant were advised over the radio to go-around due to their landing gear not being extended.
summary: During a commercial multi-engine checkride, the pilot and examiner missed gear-down callouts due to distractions from navigation issues, traffic, and fatigue. The aircraft nearly landed gear-up before a radio warning prompted a successful go-around.

synopsis: A Piper tri-pacer pilot did not see an aircraft that reported to be in the area, so he reported taking the runway for departure. As he was beginning to climbout, he heard the other aircraft report going around and observed the aircraft climbing above him. He did not hear the other aircraft report on base or final and had not seen the aircraft prior to taking the runway.
summary: A single-pilot Piper tailwheel aircraft departed the runway while a training aircraft was on final approach, resulting in a close call at approximately 200 feet. The pilot attributed the incident to the training aircraft's failure to make required radio position reports on base and final, despite the pilot's visual scan and familiarity with the airport.

synopsis: An Aviat Husky right main tire failed on landing which resulted in a runway excursion, left float damage, a cracked forward bracing strut and a damaged PAPI.
summary: The pilot reported that a Husky pulled hard right upon nose wheel touchdown, veering into soft grass and striking a PAPI light due to compromised steering. The aircraft sustained damage to the right front tire, left float, and strut, but there were no injuries and the plane was taxied for inspection.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported striking a wingtip on landing after a circle to land approach.
summary: The pilot executed a tight visual approach circle to de-conflict traffic, resulting in an uncommanded roll and wingtip scrape on touchdown. Post-flight inspection confirmed flap track damage, which the pilot attributed to their own error in circling too close to the runway.

synopsis: While the flight crew of a GLF 200 was managing a battery overheat and a return to their departure airport the PF, a temporary contracted airman, descended 150 FT below their cleared altitude.
summary: The PIC and a contracted Captain SIC experienced a recurring L BAT RED CAS message during climb from FXE, prompting a return. While descending to maintain 1,500 FT, the PF deviated below altitude due to distraction from the abnormality and intermittent FMS, though the PIC corrected it before landing.

synopsis: PA23 pilot experiences a nose gear collapse during the takeoff roll. The aircraft is stopped on the runway with no injuries.
summary: The pilot reported a nose gear collapse during the takeoff roll. The pilot cut engine power, notified the Tower, and evacuated the aircraft with all passengers unharmed.

synopsis: A BE-33 pilot flying IFR to RAP declared the runway in sight after breaking out of the clouds. A low altitude alert from the RAP ILS made him realize he was making a visual approach to a similarly aligned runway at RCA some seven miles closer than RAP.
summary: The pilot mistakenly identified Ellsworth AFB as destination RAP while breaking out of clouds at 5,400 feet during a vectored VOR 14 approach. After a terrain warning and tower correction, the pilot executed a 360-degree turn to avoid a Bellanca on final, landing safely despite initial confusion caused by similar runway alignment.

synopsis: M20 pilot reports inadvertently drifting right after takeoff from Runway 13L, into the path of a departing business jet off Runway 13R.
summary: A pilot departing a Mooney from Runway 13L at Boeing Field drifted right into Runway 13R's path due to a sudden wind gust and high nose attitude obscuring visual references. The pilot corrected after a tower warning, narrowly avoiding a collision with a business jet that had just departed the adjacent runway.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot of a tailwheel aircraft experienced a left brake failure while S turning during taxi, departs the taxiway causing some damage to the aircraft.
summary: The pilot reported that while taxiing for departure, the left brake failed during a right turn, preventing a left steer away from a 6-foot embankment. The pilot shut down the engine and went over the embankment, damaging the runner bottom and bending the right wing tip, though no engine or prop damage occurred.

synopsis: C172 pilot departing Runway 36 reports a near collision with an Air Tractor landing Runway 27. An early rotation allows the C172 to overfly the Air Tractor at the intersection. No communications were heard on the CTAF from the Air Tractor pilot.
summary: A C-172 pilot departing Runway 36 at TIP nearly collided with an Air Tractor landing on Runway 27 due to restricted high-wing visibility and the other pilot's failure to announce on UNICOM. The C-172 rotated and banked left to avoid the intersection, missing the Air Tractor by an unknown margin.

synopsis: A B737 flight crew, cleared to the ramp via taxiways N, C, V1 after landing on Runway 32 was unable to read the Taxiway V1 sign as they approached it on Taxiway C.
summary: The flight crew missed the intersection of Taxiway C and V1 at PIT due to a lack of visible markings and a congested airport diagram. They stopped to confirm the clearance, then corrected their path by turning onto Taxiway V to reach the ramp via V1.

synopsis: A B737 Captain failed to release the parking brake before he initiated gate pushback resulting in sheared tow bar bolts and the nose wheel turning to an unusual angle.
summary: The Captain initiated pushback without verifying brake release, causing the tow bar pin to shear and the nose wheel to cock left. Maintenance inspected the aircraft after the incident, which the pilot attributed to rushing and losing situational awareness.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported he had dangerous goods loaded on his aircraft and multiple procedural violations were noted.
summary: The Captain discovered 250 lbs of undocumented dry ice on board after Operations and Load Planning falsely claimed the quantity was under 2.5 lbs. This discrepancy caused a preflight delay and resulted in the offloading of five large HAZMAT boxes upon landing.

synopsis: B747 flight crew experiences a flap drive failure while attempting to extend flaps to 5 during approach. An emergency is declared and a partial flap landing ensues.
summary: During descent, the crew experienced a failure of the outboard trailing edge flaps to extend to the commanded position 5, triggering EICAS messages. They declared an emergency, executed checklists, and landed safely with uneventful touchdown, leaving flaps extended for maintenance assessment.

synopsis: An IFR arrival into MVY reported an apparent traffic conflict observed on TCAS and issued by ATC, the ATC report indicated that the conflicting target was likely a 'false target' sometimes experieced with the RADAR system.
summary: A Gulfstream IV pilot and an air traffic controller were involved during approach to MVY when a radar false target triggered a safety alert and unauthorized turn instruction. The incident resulted from the controller misidentifying a persistent false radar return as an aircraft, violating the Letter of Agreement while issuing the clearance.

synopsis: While being vectored for an approach at BOS the flight crew of a B737-800 responded to a TCAS RA with an aircraft with which they never had visual conrtact. ATC advised there was no apparent traffic conflict. The First Officer was upset with the response which he believed failed to address what he believed to have been a near collision.
summary: During a night approach into Boston, the crew received a TCAS Resolution Advisory at 3,000 feet while being vectored to final. The pilot maneuvered to avoid an unseen aircraft climbing into their path, attributing the conflict to Air Traffic Control's failure to identify the traffic or provide adequate separation.

synopsis: A310 Captain experiences low engine oil quantity upon reaching FL350 with all other parameters normal. When oil pressure fluctuation is noted the decision to divert is made and an emergency is declared. With good oil pressure the engine is operated throughout the approach and landing. During roll out the oil pressure light illuminates and the engine is shut down.
summary: The crew diverted to ZZZ and declared an emergency after receiving a low oil advisory on Engine 1 while approaching FL350. They landed with the engine at idle and shut it down post-rollout due to a subsequent low oil pressure alert.

synopsis: An Air Carrier crew was notified during flight that they had passed through North Korean airspace without proper diplomatic clearance because a Dispatch training error had occurred.
summary: The pilot reported that the crew flew through North Korean airspace per their flight plan and ATC clearances, but Dispatch later claimed a training error caused missing overflight permits. The Duty Officer attributed the incident to human error despite the flight release listing specific Korean overfly authorizations.

synopsis: While climbing out of an uncontrolled airport the pilot of a PA31 initiated a descent to avoid an inbound, opposite direction B737. The reporter had heard no traffic or position advisories from the inbound Boeing.
summary: During an ATP check ride climb, the pilot experienced a near miss with a descending B-737 due to the jet's failure to report position and a lack of ADS-B coverage. The pilot manually descended to avoid the conflict, attributing the incident to missing position reports and insufficient ADS-B alerts.

synopsis: An Enroute Controller observed a loss of separation involving two departure aircraft climbing into the enroute environment.
summary: A Center controller observed a loss of separation between two aircraft less than 3.5 miles apart, attributing the incident to the Approach controller's poor attitude and inadequate response. The reporter cited a procedural flaw allowing Approach to climb departures beyond their airspace as a secondary cause that enabled the overtake.

synopsis: TRACON developmental described a probable MOA airspace incursion when failing to anticipate the turn radius of an IFR departure that was increasing speed rapidly.
summary: An East Radar trainee controller issued a conflicting 270-degree heading instead of 090 to a departing Air Carrier X aircraft, causing it to drift toward an active MOA. The controller attributed the near incursion to high ground speed, insufficient turn planning, and lack of experience.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported deviating from cleared track on approach to LAX. Wake vortex concerns and haze were contributing factors.
summary: During a visual approach for training, the crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding Boeing 777, causing a slight overshoot of Runway 24R. The Pilot Monitoring briefly mistook Runway 24L for 24R while checking the AIII mode, requiring an immediate correction and ATC re-intercept instructions before a safe landing.

synopsis: B757 Captain reports being dispatched with one fire detection loop in the right engine deferred. During climb the right engine fire warning light and bell activated and stopped two times. EICAS status indicated both fire loops failed and the crew elects to return to the departure airport.
summary: The crew departed with a deferred right engine fire detection loop. During climb through 25,000 feet, intermittent fire warnings occurred, and a status message indicated both right engine loops were inoperable, prompting a return to base.

synopsis: Q400 flight crew reports a #1 Bleed Hot Caution light during approach that cannot be reset. During taxi in Maintenance is advised of the problem and they request that the crew do a ground reset procedure which requires an engine runup. Operations was advised but the rampers do not get the message and the engine is runup with a belt loader behind the engine and a Ramper in the cargo hold.
summary: The flight crew attempted an unsuccessful ground reset for a #1 Bleed Hot Caution light while taxiing, inadvertently running the engines with a belt loader and ramper in the danger zone. This caused four bags to blow off the loader and cargo net dents to the fuselage due to miscommunication regarding engine shutdown.

synopsis: An EMB-145 Captain reported excessive amounts of yoke movement were required to accomplish a desired pitch axis change.
summary: The pilot reported sluggish pitch control with 4-6 inches of yoke travel before elevator response during a visual approach with Runway 27 ILS backup. The pilot compensated for the reduced effectiveness to land safely, noting the same issue occurred on this aircraft one month prior despite maintenance initially claiming no record.

synopsis: While reversing after landing the flight crew of a CRJ-700 experienced a right engine flame out and noted high ITT as they turned off the runway. The shut the engine down, completed checklists, and taxied to their gate.
summary: The crew experienced a right engine flameout and ITT exceedance immediately after thrust reverser deployment during landing. They shut down the engine while exiting the runway, citing the malfunction and sun glare on displays as primary threats, though the aircraft taxied safely to the gate.

synopsis: B777 flight crew experiences a strong tailwind on short final during approach in turbulence and rain to Runway 02L then elects to go around at low altitude. The Controller issues a heading and altitude but the flying Captain inadvertently selects LNAV due to fatigue and turbulence. The Controller then issues vectors for landing Runway 02L and repeats the runway designation several times when queried by the crew, before finally realizing his mistake and stating Runway 20R. A normal landing ensues.
summary: Fatigued pilots executing a go-around at WSSS in thunderstorms inadvertently selected LNAV instead of Heading Select, causing an unintended left turn. Subsequent ATC confusion regarding the approach runway was resolved after multiple queries, allowing the crew to land safely on 20R.

synopsis: A flight crew reported they experienced abrupt yawing motions in a CRJ-200 aircraft that created an unstable flight path. The First Officer noted the rudder pedals would move along with the direction of yaw as though someone was pushing on them. Rudder continued to kick left and right during descent. No QRH procedure available for uncommanded rudder movement.
summary: The flight crew experienced uncommanded rudder movements at FL310 caused by a faulty Yaw Damper-1, which remained undetected by EICAS until after landing. They diverted to a nearby airport, slowed to Vmo, and landed safely while maintaining manual control of the aircraft.

synopsis: Luscombe pilot reported 'refueling' his aircraft without actually pumping any fuel after failing to flip the pump reset lever. An engine failure due to the dry tanks ensued.
summary: The pilot of a Luscombe aborted a takeoff due to low fuel and later experienced fueling difficulties at ZZZ caused by obstructed pump instructions and bulky hoses. Despite these issues and a previous radio clarity concern, the pilot managed the situation and completed a normal landing.

synopsis: C172 pilot performing night landings reports hitting a coyote at touchdown causing the right gear to break off and the aircraft to depart the runway.
summary: A pilot striking a coyote during a night landing caused the right main gear to break off, forcing a runway excursion onto grass. The aircraft was recovered with only gear damage, and the pilot classified the event as an incident not requiring an NTSB report.

synopsis: C172 pilot reports a NMAC west of ORD Class B at 3,000 FT with another aircraft closing from the 7:30 position. Evasive action is taken by diving and turning but the other aircraft continues on heading and altitude apparently unaware of the situation.
summary: A pilot cruising at 3,000 feet MSL near Sandwich, IL, observed an unidentified aircraft on a collision course at the same altitude. The pilot executed an immediate 400-foot dive and right bank to avoid impact, then returned to the home airport after the other aircraft continued its original path.

synopsis: C421 pilot experiences engine roughness at 12,000 FT and requests vectors to a suitable airport. At 6,000 FT low oil pressure is indicated and with the engine shaking badly it is shut down. A safe landing ensues.
summary: The pilot experienced engine roughness at 12,000 feet and requested a descent to ZZZ. At 6,000 feet, low oil pressure and severe shaking caused the pilot to feather the propeller and land safely without incident.

synopsis: TRACON developmental described a loss of separation event when communications between the reporter and another developmental in the tower cab fail to address the impending situation.
summary: A Local Control controller and Final Approach controller managed a potential conflict between a departing B350 and a Hawker on downwind. The incident occurred because Tower approved the Hawker's descent without advising Final of the B350, requiring immediate heading changes to de-conflict the aircraft.

synopsis: Local Assist Controller described a near loss of separation event between two departures that were assigned the same route due to the Ground Controller failing to identify same.
summary: A Ground Controller failed to notice two flight plans for a Phenom 300, causing it to be cleared for takeoff on a conflicting course with an A319. Departure Controllers executed evasive actions to separate the aircraft after the Phenom 300 overtook the Airbus, an incident the reporter attributes to the Ground Controller's negligence and a system failure to flag duplicate flight plans.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described a near loss of separation event when reliance upon an automated procedure was not followed up by needed human coordination to insure everyone was on the same page.
summary: A Radar North controller and a Radar West controller experienced a potential conflict involving a climbing P46T and a descending BE55 due to failed verbal coordination and assumptions about automated point-outs. The Radar North controller issued a climb to 6,000 without confirming the BE55's descent, requiring the Radar West controller to vector the BE55 to maintain separation.

synopsis: SMO Controller voiced concern regarding the GPS Approach procedure to Runway 21 describing a recent event that included a missed approach and potential conflict with LAX traffic.
summary: An ATC controller issued missed approach instructions to a P46T on a GPS approach to Runway 21 at SMO, but the pilot became overwhelmed by simultaneous coordination with LAX and SCT. The pilot failed to read back the assigned altitude and turned toward LAX, highlighting the serious risks of the current approach procedure due to airspace conflicts.

synopsis: C90 Controller described an unsafe condition when coordination regarding a flight check aircraft was incomplete and uncertain.
summary: A trainee Air Traffic Controller on the Feeder position allowed aircraft FLCXX to request a route conflicting with southbound departures after a Supervisor approved it without full coordination. The trainee subsequently diverted FLCXX away from departure traffic after the South Departure position reported being unaware of the operation.

synopsis: A Medium Large Transport aircraft and a service vehicle, parked at a gate in BWI, were dramatically rocked by jet blast from an MD-80 powering up to enter an uphill approach to another gate.
summary: A Flight Attendant reported that jet blast from an MD-80 taxiing uphill to Gate X-X at BWI nearly flipped a provisioning truck servicing their aircraft. Ground Control dismissed the incident as occurring in an uncontrolled area, prompting the crew to notify the Chief Pilot to address the safety hazard.

synopsis: EMB135 Captain describes the events leading up to the First Officer falling out of the main cabin door when the loading bridge is moved without his knowledge.
summary: The First Officer fell while backing out of the cockpit as ground agents prematurely removed the jet bridge, despite the Flight Attendant's attempt to stop him. The reporter attributes the incident to excessive gate noise hindering communication and recommends procedural changes to prevent agents from moving the bridge until both pilots are seated.

synopsis: A B717 flight crew rejected their takeoff following a loud and compressor stalls warnings followed by airframe vibration. They returned to the gate where the aircraft was taken out of service.
summary: The flight crew aborted takeoff on Runway XXR due to a right engine compressor stall and airframe shudder at 100–110 knots. After exiting the runway, a left brake overheat warning appeared, leading to a gate stop and subsequent tow to the hangar for inspection.

synopsis: EMB145 First Officer laments the lack of ATC action to prevent TCAS RA's during simultaneous visual approaches to Runways 16L and 16R at DEN.
summary: The monitoring pilot reported a near mid-air collision at Denver while on a visual approach to Runway 16L when an Airbus overshooting Runway 16R descended onto their aircraft. TCAS issued multiple descent RAs due to less than 200 feet separation, while Approach Control failed to intervene or stop the Airbus's descent.

synopsis: EMB-170 captain reports loss of Hydraulic system 1 in cruise due to loss of hydraulic system fluid. Crew diverts to a suitable airport with a long runway due to loss of some systems. A safe landing ensues.
summary: The crew experienced a total loss of Hydraulic System 1 fluid and pressure enroute at cruise, causing reduced braking and compromised spoilers. They declared an emergency, diverted to ZZZ, and landed with sluggish wheel brakes before being towed to the gate due to overheating.

synopsis: EC135 pilot is informed by his Medic that the stretcher seat belts have been removed and are being washed and that new belts have been installed. The pilot informs the Medic that the stretcher seat belts can only be changed by specially trained personnel and requires logbook documentation.
summary: A pilot discovered that a medic and flight nurse had improperly removed, washed, and reinstalled aircraft stretcher seatbelts without authorization or logbook entries. The pilot corrected the issue by inspecting the equipment, documenting the maintenance, and notifying management to improve medical crew training on these procedures.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reports being distracted during a night approach, by a very bright sign on the roof of a parking garage just to the left of Runway 4R at LIT.
summary: The pilot flying reported that an extremely bright sign on a parking garage left of Runway 4R at LIT distracted the crew during a night final approach. The reporter stated this compromised flight safety and recommended reducing the sign's intensity by 50% at night.

synopsis: A Lead Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports finding 50 Passenger Oxygen Canisters that were 'Out of Date' on a company B777-200 aircraft. AMT noted the B777 was not the first aircraft in recent past that came out of a Heavy C-Check from a foreign maintenance facility with the same discrepancy.
summary: A mechanic found 50 expired oxygen canisters on a B777-200 after a Heavy C-Check at a foreign facility. The reporter attributed the issue to inadequate training and recommended domestic maintenance to ensure accountability, resulting in the removal and replacement of the canisters.

synopsis: A Maintenance Control Manager explains why an MEL deferral of Number 2 Autopilot on a DC-10 aircraft was allowed with a Number-2 Flight Control Computer (FCC) fault.
summary: Maintenance Control Manager and an Aircraft Maintenance Technician investigated a Number 2 Flight Control Computer fault during an Auto Flight System check. The issue resulted from misinterpreting a deferrable test fault as a failed component, leading to an incorrect Autopilot Minimum Equipment List deferral.

synopsis: BE35 pilot reports autopilot failing to capture the localizer during an ILS approach then entering an unusual attitude. The autopilot is disconnected and the aircraft returned to assigned altitude but the ILS is unsuccessful. A second attempt is also unsuccessful along with a GPS approach and the reporter returns to his home airport in VMC. The HSI is found to have a course selection anomaly.
summary: The pilot flying to LBE experienced an autopilot failure and unusual attitude while attempting an ILS 23 approach due to a Sandel 3308 HSI course pointer malfunction. After losing 500 feet and failing to capture the approach, the pilot climbed to 7,000 feet, exited IMC, and landed in VFR conditions.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reports engine failure during approach due to fuel starvation. A successful dead stick landing ensues.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine power loss on final approach while feeding from the right tank, causing fuel pressure to drop to zero after switching to the left tank. This resulted in a successful dead stick landing, and subsequent refueling revealed the tanks held significantly less fuel than the calculated 17-gallon capacity.

synopsis: SR20 pilot reported encountering wake vortex on departure from SMO in trail of a G200. When he deviated to avoid the wake ATC became concerned and issued a vector to stay clear of LAX traffic.
summary: The pilot departed SMO behind a Gulfstream 200 on an IFR flight, deviated left to avoid wake turbulence, and was subsequently vectored back into the wake zone by Departure. The pilot attributed the incident to unfamiliarity with procedures, pressure to maintain IFR release time, and lack of communication regarding the deviation.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA28 was preparing for a mid-field takeoff from a runway over 10,000 FT long. When he felt rushed to begin his takeoff, he inadvertently turned towards the arrival end of the runway rather than towards the departure end. The arriving and departing aircraft performed right banking turns to alleviate the traffic conflict.
summary: The pilot, cleared for takeoff on Runway XXR while another aircraft was on short final, mistakenly turned right onto the runway instead of left due to the runway designation and ATC urgency. Both aircraft banked right to avoid a collision during the takeoff roll.

synopsis: BE35 pilot reports a loss of GPS signal at 5,000 FT in the vecinity of RFD. Discussions with other local airmen indicate that there may be a source of interference in this area near SIMMN Intersection.
summary: The pilot experienced two GPS and primary navigation outages lasting up to five minutes during flight, reporting the loss to RFD Approach. Service was restored within ten minutes, and the pilot suspects local interference after another pilot reported similar issues in the same area.

synopsis: C172 pilot experiences a NMAC with a glider near MEV at 8,200 FT.
summary: A pilot flying a high-wing aircraft at 8,200 feet near Minden Airport experienced a near mid-air collision with a glider while briefly looking down to retrieve a sectional chart. The glider, on a converging course from the right and slightly higher, passed within inches of the pilot's aircraft due to limited visual detection caused by the aircraft's design and the glider's flight path.

synopsis: JFK Controller described a go-around event when traffic cleared for takeoff delayed longer than expected and separation collapsed, the reporter noted the departing aircraft should have informed ATC of any expected delays.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller at JFK managed a conflict between an A320 holding on Runway 31L and a B767-200 on final approach after the A320 failed to commence takeoff. The controller ordered the A320 to exit and the B767 to go around, noting that the A320 should have notified ATC immediately if not ready.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described an unsafe condition when weather factors, re-routes, workload and poor supervisory/TMU decisions led to a loss of separation.
summary: An air traffic controller in Sector XX faced an unsafe situation when unrealistic 15-mile in-trail spacing was imposed on high-volume ZZZ and ZZZ1 arrivals. The controller issued traffic alerts and descent instructions to prevent a loss of separation between a B737-800 and an A319, attributing the near-miss to poor flow management and ignored safety concerns.

synopsis: Tower Controller witnessed a pilot declared NMAC when traffic on a right and left downwind conflicted turning base to follow traffic on final, the reporter indicated the instructor should have taken Local sooner.
summary: A developmental controller training on LC1 lost situational awareness, causing Aircraft X and Aircraft Y to come into close proximity during a VFR pattern. The controller issued a left 360 to Aircraft Y, prompting Aircraft X to report a near miss and consider a go-around.

synopsis: ZLA Controller relayed concerns expressed by flight crews overflying a solar farm south of LAS. Flight crews have noted the facility causes nearly blinding reflection.
summary: An air traffic controller in Las Vegas Sector 6 and 37 reported that an air carrier pilot found a solar farm nearly blinding and distracting during northeast-to-southwest flights. Management declined to take action, instructing the controller to have the pilot file a safety report instead.

synopsis: ZDC Controller voiced concern regarding the misunderstanding of a 'Descend via' clearance with specific applications to the IVANE 1 STAR, one event resulted in an airspace incursion and unsafe condition.
summary: An A321 at FL240 on the IVANE1 arrival to CLT descended to FL220 and violated South Boston Sector airspace after receiving a "DESCEND VIA" clearance. The controller attributed this unsafe situation to inconsistent arrival usage and a lack of recent training for both pilots and controllers regarding descent procedures.

synopsis: A B737-700 flight crew departing BUR was distressed when, after advising them of two helicopters in the general vicinity of their SID departure path and, after confirmation of visual contact by all flight crews involved, the Tower cleared them for takeoff. The reporter elected to make an NMAC report due to their in-flight proximity to the helicopters.
summary: A Boeing 700 pilot departing BUR Runway 15 delayed a turn to 210 degrees and maintained V2+20 to avoid a near mid-air collision with two helicopters at 1,200 feet AGL. The pilot attributed the risk to Tower's expedited clearance and lack of radar visibility, noting a TCAS TA occurred during the climb.

synopsis: Air carrier on the RAVNN STAR into BWI missed a crossing restriction due to miscommunications within the cockpit and also listed unsolicited ATC 'shortcuts' as contributing to the event.
summary: During the RAVNN 3 arrival, the crew crossed SABBI approximately 3,000 feet high while in VNAV PATH due to unsolicited shortcuts and poor monitoring. The Pilot Monitoring attributed the deviation to inadequate communication and monitoring, noting that radio congestion prevented early notification to Approach.

synopsis: A B757 Captain reported a blinding reflection that lasted several minutes from an apparent solar array in the vicinity of EED.
summary: Pilots on J6 in the EED area reported a blinding reflection from a solar array WSW of LAS that resembled laser illumination. The glare occurred while glancing toward the array's vicinity and persisted for several minutes.

synopsis: EMB145 Captain experiences control column vibration climbing through FL310. After discussions with Maintenance an emergency is declared and the flight returns to the departure airport. The aircraft had a history of elevator vibrations but this information was not relayed to the crew while airborne.
summary: During climb above FL310, the pilot experienced severe control column vibration caused by an elevator control surface failure, prompting an emergency return. The pilot reported that Dispatch falsely denied prior knowledge of this recurring issue on the aircraft, which Maintenance later confirmed had occurred before.

synopsis: A Citation 560 air conditioning compressor caught fire during preflight on ground power at the gate, the flight crew extinguished the fire using the aircraft's walk around halon bottle.
summary: During preflight with the GPU and air conditioner powered, the Captain and First Officer observed sparks and smoke from the AC compressor, which then erupted into flames. The crew extinguished the fire using a cockpit Halon extinguisher, and the Fire Department confirmed the unit was out before maintenance was notified.

synopsis: CE750 Flight Crew reports discovering a fuel leak on the bottom of the right wing during preflight.
summary: During preflight, the crew discovered a fuel leak and apparent corrosion on the underside of the right wing near a riveted area. Maintenance control classified the discrepancy as a fuel stain, and the aircraft was written up.

synopsis: A BE-400XP flight crew on final approach utilized innovative actions to halt a runaway stabilizer trim and land safely.
summary: During final approach at 1,000–1,500 feet AGL, the pitch trim failed while the autopilot was disengaged. The Captain held the trim switch and the crew switched to emergency trim, allowing them to control the aircraft, land safely, and notify maintenance.

synopsis: After completing the appropriate MEL tasks to depart with an inoperative No 2 fuel boost pump inoperative the flight crew of a BAE-125 suffered a flame out at FL410 and diverted to the nearest suitable airport for maintenance.
summary: The crew departed with an inoperative No. 2 boost pump per MEL, but the right engine flamed out at FL410. The aircraft diverted and landed single-engine; the crew suspects fuel starvation but found no procedural errors.

aircraft: Piper Single Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Two General Aviation pilots operating in the pattern of a Tower controlled airport experienced a Near Mid Air Collision when they could not make visual contact. One pilot mistook the pattern altitude and the other misunderstood the runway instructions.
summary: A PA-15 pilot flying at 1,200 feet instead of the required 1,500 feet pattern altitude experienced a close call when another aircraft flew within a wingspan overhead during downwind. The pilot attributed the incident to his incorrect altitude and the other pilot's confusion regarding runway assignments.

synopsis: Air carrier maintenance personnel installed the incorrect engine fuel control unit for the affectivity due to confusion over configuration and service bulletin status.
summary: A maintenance supervisor incorrectly instructed mechanics to install a -12 fuel control unit on a post-service bulletin JT8D engine due to misidentifying the bleed valve. This error, caused by the supervisor's lack of system knowledge, resulted in a slow spool discrepancy discovered a week later, requiring replacement with the correct -15 unit.

synopsis: C172 pilot reports announcing his intentions to cross the active runway on CTAF then noticing a twin turboprop accelerating towards him during the crossing.
summary: A Skyhawk pilot crossing Runway 22/4 at Bar Harbor encountered an unseen aircraft moving toward them due to terrain blocking the view of the arrival end. The pilot safely cleared the runway after noting the other aircraft made no radio call and was not visible until the crossing began.

synopsis: TRACON Controller described an unsafe event when releasing an aircraft from an uncontrolled airport only to find two flight plans were filed off different airports and the wrong departure was being considered for the release.
summary: An air traffic controller mistakenly held a Cessna 152 departing ZZZ due to confusion with a flight plan filed from ZZZ1 while vectoring a Cessna 172. The controller realized the error during a frequency handoff, attributing the incident to strip management issues and duplicate flight plans in the system.

synopsis: Center controller reported B737 had a wake vortex encounter with an A380 that in the B737 pilot's words 'felt like [we were] hit by a truck.' Controller noted the B737 was about 13 miles in trail and separated by 1,000 feet, and wondered whether the separation standards should be increased for Super Aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a B737 at FL390 encountered moderate clear air turbulence 20 miles behind an A380 at FL400 on a converging course. The controller attributed the event to wake turbulence from the A380, which passed 13 miles ahead and 5 miles laterally, and suggested increased separation standards.

synopsis: A RNO Tower Controller and a C182 pilot each present their version of an uncoordinated entry into the Class C airspace resulting in an airborne conflict.
summary: A disoriented C182 pilot and a PA28 inbound to Reno experienced a less than 0.5-mile same-altitude proximity due to Approach Control delays, incorrect transponder codes, and a late handoff to Tower. The Tower controller issued immediate traffic alerts and a left turn to the PA28, allowing the C182 to land safely after receiving a clearance.

synopsis: Local Controller voiced concern regarding the use of firearms for 'wildlife control' near the operating areas, suggesting no firearms be allowed in the airport environs.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported that Operations personnel entered the runway safety area with a rifle to shoot birds while an A321, B717, and Cessna 172 were operating nearby. The controller deemed the practice unsafe because the rifle was pointed toward the active runway, causing birds to scatter onto the surface during aircraft approaches and departures.

synopsis: ZDC Controller described an airspace infraction when a 'descent via' clearance was apparently misunderstood by an RDU air carrier arrival, the reporter noted pilots need improved training on these procedures.
summary: A B737-800 pilot violated LIB airspace by crossing the ALDAN waypoint at 13,800 feet while descending via the ALDAN1 arrival to RDU. The controller attributed this deviation to the pilot's lack of proper training on flying "descend via" clearances.

synopsis: ZLC Controller described an unsafe condition concerning sector splits and failure to open D-Sides, noting that even attempts to 'split' sectors can sometimes increase workloads significantly due to coordination requirements.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller working Sector 40 during a departure push requested a D-Side assistant three times after Sector 42 opened, but Management ignored the requests. The reporter states this staffing decision compromised safety by increasing workload across multiple sectors without operational necessity.

synopsis: SFO Controller described a duplicate flight number event with both an arrival on final and an airborne departure having an identical flight number.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a B737-700 departure and an inbound B737 arrival on 28R sharing identical callsigns without issuing cautionary advisories. The controller acknowledged failing to detect the duplicate callsigns on radar and strips, noting the airline should use stubbed callsigns for such scenarios.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reports being vectored for weather during arrival to MCO then executing two missed approaches due to microburst alerts from the Tower. The decision is made to divert to their filed alternate and is informed it is closed due to weather. The crew then decides to divert to the nearest suitable alternate and lands with 3,600 LBS of fuel.
summary: Pilots encountered multiple microburst alerts during arrival at MCO, forcing missed approaches and a divert due to thunderstorms. They declared minimum fuel, then diverted to Melbourne with low fuel without declaring an emergency, landing safely with 3,300 LBS.

synopsis: An air carrier Captain reported new flight crew meals are being boarded in plastic containers that are unsuitable for heating in the aircraft convection ovens, shrinking severely and threatening to be combustible. A flight manager's response to the reporter's concerns was dismissive.
summary: A pilot reported that flight attendants are placing plastic meal trays and roll packaging directly into aircraft convection ovens, causing the plastic to melt. The reporter identified this as a potential fire hazard and criticized the Duty Captain for failing to address the safety concern.

synopsis: A320 Flight Crew reports altitude and speed deviations during departure with the Captain hand flying and not precisely following the flight director commands.
summary: During climbout, the Captain hand-flew the aircraft, ignoring flight director commands and accelerating to 270 KTS between 3500 and 3800 FT. The Pilot Monitoring intervened to correct the speed and a subsequent 180 FT altitude overshoot at 5000 FT, attributing the deviations to workload management and automation issues.

synopsis: B767 flight crew experiences an intermittent stuck mic during descent, approach and missed approach before regaining communications and landing normally.
summary: The crew experienced a stuck microphone causing intermittent communications during descent and localizer intercept. They squawked 7600 and discontinued the approach until communications were restored, receiving clearance to land from Approach and normal contact with the Tower.

synopsis: CRJ-700 Captain experiences fan vibration climbing to FL360 and elects to stop at FL280 and reduce thrust until vibration is below the caution range. Flight continues to destination and lands uneventfully.
summary: The crew experienced increasing left engine fan vibration during climb to FL280, reaching 1.8 mils. They reduced thrust and leveled at FL280 per QRH procedures, maintaining controlled vibration to continue to destination and land uneventfully without shutting down the engine.

synopsis: B717 First Officer reports informing crew scheduling that he is too fatigued to take another flight at the end of his scheduled trip pairing.
summary: A fatigued pilot reported making errors on the final leg, such as turning off pack switches instead of hydraulic switches, due to only seven hours of restless sleep. The pilot subsequently notified scheduling via ACARS that they were fatigued after landing.

synopsis: DHC8-200 Captain reports stopping his aircraft during marshalling into the gate after sensing that he was passed the normal stop point. The Marshall had been looking at the CRJ200 line instead of the Q200 line.
summary: The pilot stopped the aircraft during parking because the Marshaller failed to signal a stop at the correct line, risking a collision with a GPU. The Marshaller later admitted he was focused on the CRJ-200 line instead of the Q200 line, while a Ramper assisted in stopping the aircraft.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Recip Eng
synopsis: Captain reports contacting the wing tip of another company aircraft with his rudder while being marshalled into a parking spot.
summary: The pilot taxied a Company aircraft into a tight parking spot between fuel trucks and another aircraft without wingwalkers. The pilot stopped after observing the rudder trim tab move, suspecting a wing strike, and shut down the engine while passengers were unloaded.

synopsis: A B767-300ER flight crew abandoned their approach and made a fly-by of the Tower for an inspection of the nose gear after the safe light failed to illuminate when the gear was extended. When it appeared to be down they declared a precautionary emergency but landed safely.
summary: The pilot reported a missing nose gear down indication upon extension, prompting a go-around for a visual inspection by the Tower. An emergency was declared, allowing the First Officer to fly while the pilot managed communications, resulting in an uneventful landing.

synopsis: B777 Captain reports loss of the right pack shortly after takeoff. Pack reinstatement is attempted before noting that the right engine bleed valve and right isolation valve are also closed. Fuel is dumped and the flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: Shortly after takeoff, the crew experienced right pack and engine bleed loss, closing associated valves and losing wing anti-ice. They declared an emergency, jettisoned 43,000 lbs of fuel at FL300, and landed uneventfully below maximum landing weight.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew reports rejecting a takeoff at 110 KTS for a number three engine fire warning. The aircraft had a history of false and incomplete fire warnings. Autobrakes did not disengage with manual braking as expected requiring autobrake switch to be selected off, which contributed to hot brakes.
summary: The crew rejected takeoff at 110 KTS due to a Level 3 Engine 3 fire alert and Master Warning, which cleared upon power reduction. Subsequent brake overheat alerts occurred, likely caused by delayed release of max braking, while distracting Tower communications hindered the return to the ramp.

synopsis: The single augmented flight crew of a B777-200, at the end of a 12 hour flight to ZGGG including avoiding typhoon weather, failed to reset their altimeters in a timely fashion as the passed the Transition Level and descended below their cleared altitude. Fatigue and metric altimetry at low transition levels were cited as contributing factors.
summary: A fatigued crew on a long-haul flight to Guangzhou descended 300 feet below the cleared 2,400 meters due to missed altimeter setting changes during arrival procedure switches in typhoon conditions. The pilot manually arrested the descent after the aircraft bottomed out between 7,500 and 7,600 feet, attributing the error to high workload, communication challenges, and fatigue.

synopsis: CRJ200 Captain reports being cleared to descend to FL180 with the First Officer flying. As the aircraft nears FL180 the altimeter settings begin to flash and the First Officer sets QNH of 30.14 resulting in a level off below FL180. The Captain tells the First Officer to climb back to FL180 then takes the controls when the First Officer does not respond.
summary: The Captain took control after the First Officer descended below FL180 due to an altimeter setting error while leveling off. The crew recovered the aircraft after losing approximately 150 feet, attributing the incident to procedural errors and confusion regarding the FL180 transition.

synopsis: B737 crew experiences a fuel imbalance upon leveling off at FL390 while feeding both engines from the center tank, with the left tank being low. With the cross feed open and the left tank pumps off the imbalance continues to increase. Flight returns to departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced rapid fuel loss in the left main tank at FL390 while the center tank was feeding the engines. They returned to the departure airport, reducing left engine thrust to idle to slow the leak, suspecting a fault in the left main tank.

synopsis: B747 Captain experiences the failure of the number one hydraulic system in cruise due to loss of hydraulic fluid and the confusion that reigns while trying to interpret the QRH procedure for this failure. Eventually it is determined that the aircraft can continue to destination.
summary: The flight crew encountered a HYD QTY LOW 1 warning at FL310, leading to confusion over a poorly written QRH checklist that falsely suggested an immediate diversion. Although the aircraft landed safely, poor communication regarding ground support caused a runway delay and a ground stop.

synopsis: B767 First Officer reports EFB difficulties requiring a password login any time a page is changed.
summary: Pilots reported that company-issued Electronic Flight Bags (EFBs) continually dumped, causing loss of displayed documents and requiring password re-entry. This occurred during document changes or paging, creating significant distraction during emergencies or irregular procedures.

synopsis: While following the checklist for a possible fuel imbalance the flight crew of a B777 noted it provided only for an actual imbalance or fuel leak, ignoring possible sensor or gauge faults. If the source of the error is a sensor/indicator fault the procedure runs the risk of a self induced actual imbalance.
summary: The flight crew encountered a fuel imbalance indication caused by sensor contamination rather than an actual leak. They reported that the current checklist fails to address sensor failure, risking a self-induced imbalance if followed without verifying gauge accuracy.

synopsis: Air Carrier pilot reports that some jetways at his base have been modified to mate with regional jets and the result does not mate well with mainline jets, leaving an opening to the left of the cabin door that a child could fall through.
summary: A pilot reported a safety hazard at a jetway equipped with an RJ extension, which creates a 1.5x3 ft gap beside the cabin door for mainline aircraft. Despite previous concerns raised with a gate agent and the chief pilot, the issue remains unresolved, posing a risk of children falling to the ground.

synopsis: A ramp person reports that his company's practice of marshalling aircraft from a catering truck during a lightning storm is unsafe since chocks are not installed and the aircraft may roll if the Captain releases the parking brake.
summary: The reporter observed a galley truck parking an aircraft without chocks or a push tractor during a lightning ground stop. This unsafe practice caused a previous incident where an Airbus rolled back five feet while passengers exited, stopping only when the door hit the loading bridge.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier Captain executed a go-around on the SFO LOC DME 28L at minimums (460 FT) and because no other approach was available the flight diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: The crew diverted to an alternate airport due to low ceilings at SFO and declared a low fuel advisory while on the LOC DME 28L approach. The pilot attributed the event to inadequate facilities at San Francisco, noting that a go-around would have critically reduced fuel reserves.

synopsis: A321 Captain reports a galley access panel coming loose in the cockpit during landing and becoming a projectile.
summary: During landing rollout, a loose Chiller Access Panel became a projectile in the flight deck, striking the center instrument pedestal and narrowly missing the pilots. The panel was not detected during pre-flight inspections, and while it could have engaged the parking brake at 140 KTS, no injuries or obvious compartment abnormalities were found.

synopsis: CRJ900 crew experienced an engine failure during climb and after the engine is secured, returns to the departure airport.
summary: During climb through FL230, the crew experienced a right engine flameout with oil pressure loss and shuddering. While ATC vectors and communications distracted the crew during checklist execution, they successfully secured the engine and completed a single-engine landing.

synopsis: B757 flight crew experiences a right engine flameout passing 12,000 FT in the descent. An emergency is declared and the engine successfully restarted before landing.
summary: During descent at 12,000 feet, the right engine flamed out following a master caution and loss of utility buses. The crew declared a Mayday, successfully restarted the engine, and completed an uneventful landing.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reports confusing signage, a cluttered Taxi diagram as well as the Controllers lack of concise instructions contributed to a Taxiway incursion after landing at ZBAA.
summary: The flight crew at PEK mistakenly turned onto Taxiway M3 instead of Z4 due to cluttered charts, confusing signage, and unclear ground controller instructions. The controller corrected the error after the crew reached Z3, resulting in no safety issues.

synopsis: A B757 Flight Attendant reported returning to the gate because of fuel fumes resulting in illness and an aircraft change. The next flight an impending pack failure resulted in additional noise and fumes.
summary: Cabin crew reported burning odors and loud vibrations during ground operations and flight, attributing the issues to failing air compressor bearings and bleed air valve problems. Despite prior reports of over-fueling and APU odors, maintenance dismissed the complaints before confirming the mechanical faults at the destination.

synopsis: A flight crew experienced a very bright, intense light from three solar complexes which interfered with their ability to scan for traffic while climbing westbound between 6,000 and 12,000 feet along J60/V12 southwest of NATEE Intersection.
summary: Pilots climbing from 6,000 to 12,000 feet MSL after a VFR departure from BVU were momentarily blinded by intense sun reflections from a solar power plant near Primm. The glare prevented scanning for traffic in that direction, creating a temporary flight hazard.

synopsis: IFR inbound to OAK elected to climb above the ATC assigned altitude to the published MEA when experiencing communications problems, the reporter noting MVA's should be available to pilots for safety clarity.
summary: A pilot flying an RNAV-equipped aircraft from SNS to OAK accepted a clearance below the published MEA, then climbed after a lost communication assumption caused by a frequency error. The supervisor advised against the unauthorized altitude change, while the pilot concluded that publishing Minimum Vectoring Altitudes would improve safety by allowing pilots to verify terrain clearance independently.

synopsis: CE560 Captain experiences loss of engine oil pressure during initial climb. The engine is shut down and the flight diverts to a suitable airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a left engine oil pressure loss at 6,500 feet due to failed carbon seals, triggering a precautionary shutdown. They diverted to a nearby airport and completed a normal single-engine landing with no further issues.

synopsis: SR22 Pilot atrributed track deviations and loading the wrong departure procedure to unfamiliarity with the aftermarket flight management system installed in the aircraft.
summary: A pilot ferrying a Cirrus SR22 with unfamiliar Avidyne R9 avionics from North Las Vegas entered the wrong departure procedure due to fixation and limited training. This caused an incorrect autopilot turn and deviation from the assigned route, requiring manual correction and additional controller instructions to rejoin the correct path.

synopsis: PA31 pilot experiences a right engine failure in cruise and diverts to a suitable airport. Dual drive Bendix Magneto, installed 20 minutes earlier, failed causing complete power loss.
summary: The pilot lost the right engine due to a dual drive Bendix Magneto failure shortly after a fresh overhaul, causing complete power loss. The aircraft diverted and landed uneventfully; the cause was a faulty ground in the mag case that failed both primary coils.

synopsis: RV8 pilot reports losing control of his aircraft during landing in a crosswind and departing the runway causing some damage to the aircraft and an airport sign.
summary: The pilot reported that during a crosswind landing on RWY XXR, the aircraft weather-vaned into the wind and departed the runway surface. The right wing and fuel tank were damaged after striking a taxiway sign while traveling through gravel before coming to rest on asphalt.

synopsis: Experimental pilot reports discovering on the takeoff roll that a Citabria that he thought had left the runway is taking off in the opposite direction. Evasive action is taken by the reporter, steering off the left side of the runway and becoming airborne shortly thereafter.
summary: The pilot reported a runway incursion while lining up for takeoff on Runway XX when a Citabria entered the runway without radio communication. The pilot veered left to avoid a collision, executed a steep takeoff, and landed safely with no injuries or damage.

synopsis: M20 pilot experiences a near collision departing Runway 19 at 1G5, with another aircraft departing Runway 27.
summary: The pilot departing Runway 19 at Medina Municipal Airport nearly collided with another aircraft crossing from a run-up pad onto Runway 27. The near-miss occurred because the crossing pilot failed to check the active runway or monitor CTAF, while the departing pilot was fixated on the runway surface.

synopsis: G-V flight crew reports missing a crossing restriction during descent due to what they believe is a flaw in the FMS software.
summary: The Gulfstream V crew received altitude restrictions from Fort Worth Center but failed to meet the CQY Vortac limit due to a Honeywell 6.0 software bug causing incorrect VPath calculations. After passing CQY at 9,400 feet, the pilot discontinued VNAV use until the software is updated.

synopsis: A float plane inbound to the Lake Union waterstrip north of SEA experienced an NMAC with another aircraft. Both had been broadcasting on CTAF, but did not have visual contact with one another.
summary: The pilot of a wheeled aircraft sightseeing near Lake Union flew 80 feet below and 100 feet in front of the reporting pilot's aircraft while crossing the final approach. The reporter attributed the near miss to the other pilot's lack of situational awareness in the busy uncontrolled traffic pattern and subsequently declined further flight for the day.

synopsis: IND Controller described a conflict event when an IFR departure from EYE failed to comply with the published departure procedure resulting in a potential conflict with a IND departure.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported a potential loss of lateral separation between a departing light jet from Eagle Creek (EYE) and a heavy aircraft from Indianapolis (IND) due to the pilot misunderstanding the departure procedure and turning right immediately. The controller issued traffic alerts, causing both pilots to execute Resolution Advisories, and recommended clarifying the ambiguous EYE Runway 3 departure instructions.

synopsis: S46 Controller described a conflict between a BFI departure and a SEA arrival aircraft. The reporter provided additional examples of potential conflicts when 'Split Flow' procedures are utilized, and recommended some procedural changes to BFI departures.
summary: A B737 on final at Seattle and a King Air departing BFI experienced a collision alert during unsafe Split Flow procedures due to converging courses and insufficient divergence. The pilot reported a loss of 1,000 feet separation and cited procedural flaws where visual separation was not provided by towers.

synopsis: A B737-700 captain expressed concern that a noise abatement policy at BNA requires aircraft to land on Runway 31 at night. The runway has no centerline, approach or touchdown zone lights and no visual glide path guidance and the reporter characterizes its use for visual approaches at night as a 'black hole' approach.
summary: A pilot reported that ATC forced a night landing on unlit Runway 31 at BNA due to a noise abatement policy, bypassing better-lit Runway 02s. The pilot warned that the lack of glide path guidance on this "black hole" approach creates a risk of landing short.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported wake vortex encounter at FL390 when an Airbus A380 crossed their path at FL400. The wake encounter resulted in a sharp roll to the left and then right.
summary: A pilot reported encountering heavy wake turbulence at FL390 while cruising, caused by an Airbus A380 crossing ahead at FL400 in quartering tailwind conditions. The event resulted in no injuries or damage, prompting ATC to document the encounter and review vertical separation procedures for tailwind scenarios.

synopsis: B757 First Officer experiences a jolt at FL340 accompanied by autopilot disengaging, flight directors disappearing and an EICAS message for the R Rec Fan. A strong burning smell is reported by the lead Flight Attendant and the crew dons oxygen masks and diverts to the nearest suitable airport. The smell dissipates during descent and an overweight landing ensues with normal taxi to parking.
summary: During cruise at FL340, a jolt and "R Rec Fan" EICAS message coincided with a burning smell and power loss, prompting the crew to divert to ZZZZ1. The aircraft landed overweight without further incident after the smell dissipated during descent.

synopsis: Following a 'jolt' of the aircraft, temporary loss of some autoflight systems and an EICAS R REC FAN message the flight crew of a westbound transatlantic flight declared and emergency, initiated an emergency descent and diverted safely to a nearby airport.
summary: During cruise at FL340, a jolt and "R REC FAN" EICAS message triggered an autopilot disconnect and smoke in first class, prompting an emergency descent to ZZZ2. The crew managed the descent and communications, resulting in an uneventful overweight landing after the fumes dissipated.

synopsis: B757 First Officer experiences two engine over temps in a row at 800 AGL with a maintenance inspection in between, and suggests the engine may be defective and should not be repeatedly signed off by Maintenance.
summary: Pilots experienced repeated left engine over-temperature indications at 800 AGL during takeoff on two consecutive legs, requiring immediate power reduction to VNAV. Maintenance dismissed the recurring issue as normal for the location, but the crew expressed safety concerns regarding potential engine failure and the adequacy of current maintenance limits.

synopsis: CE-560XLS Captain reported loss of cabin pressure while cruising at FL400. The pressure loss was slow enough to allow the aircraft to descend to 10,000 FT before they met the cabin altitude. Reporter mentioned air duct couplings as a probable cause.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna CE560XLS at FL400 detected a cabin pressure loss caused by a loose air duct coupling, prompting an immediate descent to 10,000 feet and a diversion. No emergency was declared, and the aircraft landed safely after ATC provided vectors, with the root cause identified as a disconnected coupling allowing pressurized air to escape.

synopsis: G-200 Captain reported on takeoff from 36U he had not properly briefed the second segment climb requirements and got a GPWS TERRAIN alert.
summary: Two pilots departed a loaded aircraft from Runway 4 at 36U on the COOLI3 departure, triggering a GPWS terrain warning due to rapid closure rate while visually clearing a ridge. The pilot later discovered the crew failed to verify the required 10.9% second segment climb gradient, which the FMS showed was only 4%.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A flight crew executed two missed approaches to PDK Runway 21L because of a localizer discrepancy which ATC said occurs occasionally. No warnings were given to the crew who ultimately landed off the RNAV GPS Y Runway 21L approach.
summary: Pilots executing an ILS 21L approach into PDK experienced full right localizer deviation near CHAMB, prompting two missed approaches. After successfully landing via RNAV (GPS), Tower attributed the ILS failure to known temporary equipment issues.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: The Captain of a turboprop twin landing Runway 14 at BFD using CTAF procedures encounters a Biplane taking off on Runway 23. Maximum braking is applied by the Captain to stop short of the intersection and avoid the Biplane. Neither pilot heard the other although both state they were using CTAF procedures.
summary: The pilot reported a near collision during landing on Runway 14 at BFD when an aircraft departed Runway 23 without radio calls. The pilot executed maximum braking to stop short of the crossing runway, attributing the conflict to obscured visibility from trees and the other pilot's failure to hear transmissions.

synopsis: A B737-800 flight crew, distracted by informal training and indoctrination of the new First Officer, failed to note the jet had not begun a programmed descent in a timely manner. During the hasty descent a short duration Vmo overspeed occurred.
summary: The Pilot Flying oversped a Boeing 737 during a descent to FL180 due to a strong tailwind and delayed manual intervention after VNAV failed to capture the profile. The pilot attributed the three-second overspeed warning to his own inattention following a three-week vacation and the First Officer's recent return to the cockpit.

synopsis: B767 Captain on visual approach to Runway 28R reports a TCAS RA caused by the aircraft on the visual to Runway 28L. The reporter speeds up and continues the approach to landing.
summary: The Captain flying a visual approach to Runway 28R received a TCAS climb RA near SAMUL but ignored it to avoid the preceding RJ aircraft. He accelerated to 150 knots for lateral separation, landed safely, and reported that SFO ATC had pushed visual separation limits too far.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported Number 1 engine oil filter bypass light illuminated shortly after takeoff. Engine was shut down and flight returned to departure airport.
summary: Shortly after takeoff, the crew shut down engine one due to a steady Oil Filter Bypass light. They declared an emergency, landed safely at the departure airport, and pulled the voice recorder circuit breaker.

synopsis: Distracted by on the job training the flight crew of a B737-800 failed to initiate their descent in a timely manner. During the descent they exceeded Vmo for a brief period.
summary: During a training descent from FL350 to HOGGS at FL180, strong tailwinds caused a brief 2 KIAS overspeed at FL190 despite ATC-approved speed increases. The Captain immediately corrected the descent rate and speed, then reported the incident to Maintenance upon arrival at JFK.

synopsis: MD-11 Captain reported flight control anomalies during go-around and subsequent landing. Reporter could not be reached for follow up comments.
summary: During approach, the crew executed a go-around due to a runway incursion by a preceding 757. Subsequent flight control difficulties, attributed to a suspected LSAS pitch hold mode, required manual intervention to level off and land safely.

synopsis: A Machinist Technician describes the extent of damage he noticed that had been caused by a Heavy Maintenance Contract Repair Station vendor's improper machining of four forward mount bore holes on the Right Engine pylon of an A330 aircraft. The entire pylon required replacement due to the unrepairable damage and potential for an in flight failure of the pylon engine mount.
summary: A mechanic at ZZZ identified unsafe corrosion and improper machining on an A330's right engine pylon mount performed by a contract vendor in ZZZ2. The aircraft was grounded and flown to the vendor for a pylon replacement after engineers determined the original repair violated Structural Repair Manual limits and compromised structural integrity.

synopsis: CE750 Crew experience the loss of hydraulic system A when the landing gear is selected up after takeoff. The main gear retracts but the nose gear remains extended. The crew elects to continue the relatively short flight to destination with the nose gear extended. An emergency is declared prior to landing and the aircraft is towed to the hangar after using emergency brakes to stop.
summary: The flight crew experienced a nose gear failure and hydraulic system warnings on departure due to a suspected leak in the nose compartment. They completed emergency checklists, declared an emergency, and landed safely using emergency brakes and flaps 15 before being towed to the hangar.

synopsis: Aeronca Instructor pilot, performing a tailwheel checkout for a private pilot, reports a landing gear failure on the seventh landing all of which had been very smooth. The aircraft is stopped on the runway with no other damage reported.
summary: During the seventh landing of a checkout flight in an Aeronca TAC65, the left landing gear broke, causing the aircraft to veer left and stop with the wing low. The failure occurred despite a clean pre-flight inspection and smooth previous landings, resulting in gear damage but no injuries.

synopsis: Aviat Husky pilot reported an NMAC with a light twin on approach.
summary: The pilot, flying a single-engine aircraft on short final to 28R, executed a go-around after a twin-engine aircraft switched runways and appeared 150 feet below. During the subsequent climbing 360-degree turn, the pilot encountered a Champ on downwind within 1,000 feet, noting no traffic advisories were provided by the controller.

synopsis: After landing a BE76 student pilot's right knee apparently moved the gear handle up and because of a failed 59-63 knot gear safety interlock, the nose gear retracted with the handle movement damaging both propellers and nose.
summary: A student pilot and instructor in a BE-76 experienced nose gear retraction during landing rollout when the student's knee inadvertently moved the gear lever. The reporter attributes the incident to a worn safety detent and a defective speed-sensitive retraction switch that failed to prevent the gear from retracting at 40 KTS.

synopsis: An A320 Captain expressed his disgust for the IVANE RNAV STAR into CLT advising its complexities exceeded the capabilities of his autoflight system, compelling it to exceed required airspeeds in order to attempt to comply with the associated altitude restrictions. Further difficulties were provided by the demands of ATC to comply with the published restrictions and/or to reassign airspeeds, vector or otherwise interfere with the flight crew's efforts to comply with the published constraints of the arrival. They ultimately refused the IVANE and requested and were assigned the MAJIC, a less complex, non RNAV STAR.
summary: The pilot reported unsafe conditions while flying an Airbus on the IVANE RNAV STAR due to FMS "too steep path" alerts, turbulence, and conflicting ATC speed assignments. The pilot exercised discretion to request and receive a clearance for the MAJIC STAR, resolving the operational issue.

synopsis: An A319 flight crew suffered an altitude deviation while descending on the IVANE RNAV STAR to CLT but with an assigned speed, forcing them to operate their autoflight systems in a non-standard manner.
summary: The Captain and First Officer descended below the 11,000 FT constraint at GIZMO while flying the IVANE RNAV STAR to CLT. The Captain attributed the deviation to ATC speed restrictions disrupting managed descent and simultaneous chart review by both pilots.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reported receiving an RA on approach to ATW.
