synopsis: B717 Captain reports an ANTISKID R FAIL alert exiting the runway after landing. Upon gate arrival the number four tire is found to be deflated. The aircraft had previously experienced the same fault/failure sequence.
summary: The First Officer landed normally on Runway 22 at LGA, but an ANTISKID R FAIL alert appeared after exiting the runway. A deflated Number 4 tire caused a flight cancellation, likely due to the brake locking up, a recurrence of a previous issue at this airport.

synopsis: EMB-175 Check Airman is instructed to fly a revenue trip with an aircraft that had been written up for high LP vibrations, with maintenance deferred and told to comply with QRH procedures which results in only 75% N1 in cruise.
summary: The Captain flew a revenue flight with a Deferred Maintenance Instruction for high LP vibrations, limiting climb to FL270 despite a FL350 plan. The pilot reported discomfort due to unknown single-engine performance and questioned the safety of operating with degraded engine capabilities.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reports an overly loud RAAS warning requiring the crew to ask the Tower to repeat the last transmission.
summary: The flight crew, while taxiing to runway 10L, missed a Tower transmission because the Runway Awareness and Advisory System (RAAS) audio override masked the controller's call. The crew requested a repeat, but the controller issued a disregard, leading the pilot to conclude the RAAS creates a communication hazard.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain departing Runway 14L at ORD reports a conflict with an Airbus landing Runway 22R. The Airbus is sent around by the Tower.
summary: The flight crew took off from Runway 14L intersection U2 while an Airbus executed a go-around on intersecting Runway 22R, passing within 500 to 600 feet laterally and 150 feet vertically. The crew reported this as their closest encounter during intersection operations, attributing the proximity to simultaneous movements despite complying with all tower instructions.

synopsis: A B757 oil temperature rose during climb after takeoff and after smoke entered the aircraft the Captain declared an emergency, completed the QRH and returned to the departure airport.
summary: The First Officer reported a high left engine oil temperature during climbout, followed by cockpit smoke at 27,000 feet. The crew donned oxygen masks, turned off the left engine bleed to clear the smoke, and returned to the departure airport for a normal landing.

synopsis: B777 flight crew reports a main battery overheat and discharge causing multiple system failures and fumes in the cabin and flight deck. Flight diverts to a suitable alternate.
summary: The crew diverted to ZZZZ airport after the main battery overheated and discharged, causing toxic fumes and multiple system failures. The aircraft landed overweight without incident but required towing due to APU and nose wheel steering failures.

synopsis: B757 Captain notes high oil temperature during climb which is brought back into the green by reducing thrust slightly on the left engine. Shortly thereafter the cabin and cockpit begin filling with smoke. The left engine bleed valve is closed eliminating the smoke and the flight returns to the departure airport. The lead Flight Attendants perspective of this event is also provided.
summary: During climb, the flight crew and cabin crew experienced thick smoke caused by engine oil leaking into the air conditioning system. The pilots closed the left engine bleed valve to clear the smoke, declared an emergency, and returned for a normal landing, leaving two shaken flight attendants unable to continue the trip.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports getting low on the RIIVR 2 arrival into LAX when asked to slow. The MCP is switched from VNAV to level change and 250 set in the speed window to slow more rapidly and VNAV is not re-selected in a timely manor.
summary: The pilot flying used Level Change to slow the aircraft during the River Arrival into LAX because VNAV was ineffective. The pilot failed to re-engage VNAV before the next crossing restriction, causing the aircraft to descend 500–600 feet below the required altitude.

synopsis: An A319 First Officer flying the IVANE 2 RNAV Arrival with his ND MELed reported the FMS defaulted to V/S as the Captain, pilot not flying, change the arrival runway from 36R to 36C which then allowed the aircraft to descend below the MAJIC altitude constraint.
summary: During a MANAGED descent on the IVANE TWO arrival into CLT, the First Officer changed the FMS runway selection, causing an uncommanded switch to V/S mode and a 400-foot descent below the 13,000-foot MAJIC restriction. The crew attributed the deviation to the FMS mode change, a MEL'd NAV display, and the Pilot Flying being distracted while searching for approach plates.

synopsis: EMB190 Captain reports being dispatched with Bleed System 1 on MEL then developing a Bleed System 2 leak. Flight descends to 10,000 FT and uses APU bleed air to continue to destination.
summary: The crew, operating an aircraft with Bleed System 1 on MEL, encountered a Bleed 2 leak in icing conditions at FL260. This caused a loss of pressurization, forcing an immediate descent to 10,000 FT where the APU was used to maintain cabin pressure for the remainder of the flight.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reports that the note with the ATIS frequency for SJT stating that the 128.45 is for ASOS when the Tower is closed is incorrect according to the Tower Controller.
summary: A pilot approaching San Antonio (SJT) found the ATIS on 128.45 lacked weather despite chart notes indicating ASOS availability when the tower is closed. The tower confirmed funding for the broadcast was unapproved, rendering chart and briefing information incorrect and potentially hindering weather access for non-ACARS aircraft.

synopsis: During the takeoff roll with an inoperative APU, an EMB-145 EICAS alerted ATTCS NO MARGIN so the takeoff was rejected and the flight returned to the gate for maintenance.
summary: The crew aborted a Runway 36 departure after receiving an ATTCS No Margin EICAS message while using TO-1 thrust with engine bleeds off due to an APU MEL. Maintenance attributed the event to high temperatures and engine bleed requirements, suggesting APU repairs to prevent recurrence.

synopsis: BK117 pilot experienced a Transmission Chip Detector warning in cruise flight and returned to base. Warning was determined to be an indicator malfunction.
summary: During cruise at 130 KIAS, a pilot experienced a flickering 'XMSN CHIP' light and master caution, prompting an aborted flight and uneventful return. The pilot followed procedures without declaring an emergency, attributing the event to an unforeseen maintenance malfunction.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reports being unable to stop prior to the end of the runway during landing at a relatively short high altitude airport.
summary: The Captain and First Officer hand-flew a visual approach to Runway 19 in gusty conditions, resulting in a late touchdown and excessive float. The aircraft stopped with the nose wheel 5-10 feet into the safety zone due to delayed manual braking and the decision not to use medium auto-braking.

synopsis: A320 flight crew experiences an unstable glideslope during approach to Runway 16L at SEA. It is ultimately determined that the Tower is crossing aircraft to depart Runway 16C which is causing the instability.
summary: During an ILS 16L approach at 6,000 feet, the crew experienced a spurious glideslope jump caused by aircraft crossing the critical area on Taxiway C. The pilots managed the resulting climb to 6,260 feet and continued the approach after the controller confirmed the interference.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier on a visual approach to BZN Runway 12 took evasive action during a near miss with an antique military trainer at about 1,000 FT above the airport.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway 12 at BZN, the crew executed evasive maneuvers to avoid a VFR antique military trainer that was 50–100 feet below and 300–500 feet ahead. The near collision resulted from the other aircraft's inaccurate position report, failure to follow straight-in instructions, and lack of a transponder during a radar outage.

synopsis: A320 Captain experiences a dual MCDU failure during arrival. Vectors are requested while the reset procedure is performed successfully.
summary: The crew experienced a simultaneous FMGC and ND display failure at 13,000 feet, prompting a request to maintain altitude instead of descending to 7,000 feet. Navigation was restored within minutes, allowing the arrival to resume, and the FMGC and IRU drift issues were reported to maintenance.

synopsis: B757 flight crew experiences an MCP failure at FL400 resulting in erratic autopilot and autothrust operation and failure of the horizontal stabilizer trim. Flight diverts to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The pilot reported a total Mode Control Panel failure at FL400 causing autopilot and autothrottle to cycle, resulting in uncommanded pitch and roll excursions. The crew declared an emergency, diverted without pitch trim, and manually wrestled the aircraft to a landing with continued control excursions.

synopsis: CRJ-700 flight crew reports being instructed to do the Spoileron (SPOST test) to force a fix for a problem that started with an ADC1 failure during preflight. After the fourth test the flight crew calls a timeout and a Contract Mechanic continues testing under the direction of Maintenance Control. After the tenth unsuccessful test the aircraft fills with smoke and is shut down.
summary: Flight crew and a contract mechanic attempted over ten forced SPOST tests to resolve an ADC1 failure, as directed by Maintenance Control. This repeated resetting caused acrid electrical smoke to fill the cabin, prompting the Captain to shut down the aircraft and evacuate the crew due to safety concerns.

synopsis: A low bang emanated from an EMB-145 nose area electrical compartment with the loss of electrical power as the aircraft prepared for departure. The aircraft was shut down, Maintenance reset systems and the flight departed, but the crew declared an emergency and diverted after the same event occurred during climbout.
summary: The flight crew experienced a loud bang and electrical smoke in the cockpit during climb, prompting an emergency diversion and precautionary landing. Although maintenance initially cleared the aircraft after a gate incident, the electrical fault recurred post-landing, suggesting the initial reset failed to resolve the underlying issue.

synopsis: CRJ200 Captain reports being dispatched with a pack inoperative then losing the second pack during descent at 11,000 FT. Flight continues to destination with the cabin unpressurized below 5,000 FT.
summary: During descent to 11,000 feet, the left pack failed while the right pack was deferred, causing rapid cabin pressurization loss. The crew descended to 3,000 feet after ATC clearance, attributing the event to recurring maintenance issues with the aircraft's pressurization system.

synopsis: C208 pilot reports entering severe turbulence at low altitude and losing control during the brief encounter, with large excursions in airspeed, altitude and heading. A normal landing ensues at destination.
summary: The pilot encountered severe turbulence while descending through 2,900 feet enroute, causing temporary loss of control over pitch, bank, and airspeed. The aircraft recovered without structural damage, though a step ladder shifted into the cargo compartment, and the flight landed safely on a contact approach.

synopsis: B737-800 First Officer experiences the failure of the weather radar shortly after takeoff. An emergency is declared and the flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: The pilot reported that aircraft radar failed shortly after takeoff, prompting an emergency declaration and return for landing. The aircraft landed uneventfully at 155,000 lbs after complying with all appropriate checklists.

synopsis: B737 flight crew notes an FDC NOTAM apparently instructing them to maintain runway heading to 2,000 FT departing Runway 1L at SFO on the PORT 5 departure. ATC advises this is not correct and that the procedure is a revision to the obstacle departure procedure only.
summary: The flight crew departed SFO Runway 28L on the PORTE 5 Departure but followed a confusing FDC NOTAM to fly runway heading to 2,000 feet instead of turning at 420 feet. ATC had no knowledge of the NOTAM, causing confusion, though no traffic conflict occurred.

synopsis: B737 Captain experiences a right engine fire warning during descent with the First Officer flying. The engine is shut down in accordance with QRH procedures and the flight continues to destination for a single engine landing. The Captain believes the warning was false as the B loop had been deferred prior to the first flight of the day.
summary: The First Officer managed a false Number 2 engine fire warning at FL250 caused by a previously deferred faulty B-loop detection system. The crew declared an emergency, shut down the engine, and landed uneventfully after fire crews inspected the aircraft.

synopsis: The flight crew of a B737NG discovered the commercially provided chart for the ILS Rwy 35 SA CAT I at MSP published an erroneous LOC frequency, 110.3, in the briefing portion of the page. The plan view of the approach, however, displays the correct frequency, 110.95. Worth of note, however, is that the identifier, IBMA, is correct in both locations and, thus, an alert flight crew could be expected to note the incorrect identifier had they tuned 110.3 per the briefing text.
summary: The flight crew identified a conflicting localizer frequency for MSP ILS 35 SA between the briefing strip and plan view during cruise. They verified the correct frequency via ATC and FMC, noting the error posed no issue during their visual approach but could cause confusion in IMC.

synopsis: A B737-300, with a Number 2 Fire Detection Loop MELed, had an engine fire indication so after a fire test failed, the engine was shut down with the emergency fire checklist, an emergency declared followed by an emergency landing.
summary: The crew received a false Number 2 engine fire warning with one detection loop deferred. Following the checklist, they shut down the engine and discharged one fire bottle, but ground response confirmed no actual fire before taxiing to the gate.

synopsis: An EMB-145 crew realized after the fact that having followed jet traffic to ORD Runway 32L may not have been what ORD Ground had intended.
summary: The pilot and First Officer at ORD misinterpreted a Ground clearance to "follow" an MD80, causing them to taxi onto Taxiway Bravo instead of the intended route to Runway 32L. The error resulted from ambiguous instructions, rapid changes, and insufficient crew cross-checking while the First Officer was occupied with pre-takeoff flows.

synopsis: After arriving at Runway 13 for takeoff, a CRJ200 Captain is advised that his departure gate is closed due to weather and to taxi onto Runway 13 and exit at AA. The crew cannot find the taxiway due to poor lighting and a lack of signs, requiring some assistance from ATC.
summary: Pilots taxiing a jet at LGA at night mistakenly turned onto a non-taxiway area while attempting to locate Taxiway AA due to poor signage and lack of edge lights. The crew stopped the aircraft after realizing the error, and ATC subsequently directed them to the correct hold short position.

synopsis: A B777 autothrottle system malfunctioned as the EICAS alerted AUTOPILOT with an audible warning. The aircraft accelerated beyond 250 KTS toward 300 KTS, which required disconnecting all autothrottle automation to regain control.
summary: During initial climb after takeoff on runway 02R, the autopilot and autothrottles failed to comply with speed limits, advancing throttles to mechanical stops and accelerating the aircraft to 300 KTS. The crew manually disconnected all automation to regain control and reduce speed to 250 KTS after ATC requested a speed restriction.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 EICAS alerted PAX DOOR during the takeoff roll, so the Captain rejected the takeoff and returned to the gate for maintenance.
summary: The flight crew aborted takeoff after receiving a PAX DOOR RED warning and triple chime, indicating a passenger door was sensed open. The aircraft taxied to the gate for maintenance after the door status on the EICAS changed from red to green.

synopsis: CRJ-700 flight crew reports unintentionally exceeding 250 KTS below 10,000 FT after an emergency descent.
summary: During an emergency descent for a bleed duct leak, the crew descended below 10,000 feet at over 250 knots to clear a normal cabin altitude message. The overspeed resulted from high workload and distraction while managing QRH procedures and ATC communications during the diversion.

synopsis: A PA-28 Instructor reported taking evasive action from another PA-28 near AVENT intersection while both aircraft were conducting training and initiating the FFZ GPS B approach.
summary: Two training aircraft conducting identical Deer Valley 1 Departures from Runway 25L experienced a near mid-air collision at 4,200 feet due to unexpected climb rates and high cockpit workload. The conflict occurred while both crews were changing frequencies and managing approach procedures, requiring immediate evasive turns to avoid impact.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Flight Attendant reports a galley cart coming out of the stowed area during takeoff. It is corralled with the aid of a passenger in 1C and returned to its' normal position passing 10,000 FT in the climb.
summary: A cabin crew member reported that a galley cart dislodged during takeoff on their first post-training flight, likely due to an unlatched latch left open by commissary staff. The crew member and a passenger secured the cart against the bulkhead without injury, and the flight continued normally after reaching 10,000 feet.

synopsis: C172 flight instructor reports an NMAC at DED with another C172 entering the traffic pattern midfield. The instructor elects to take evasive action and depart the pattern after being alerted by TIS-B then sighting traffic 100 FT behind and closing.
summary: During a training flight at Deland Airport, an instructor and student in a C172 encountered a conflict when an unknown aircraft entered the downwind for Runway 23 at high speed and closed to within 100 feet. The instructor took control, executed a steep climb escape maneuver, and departed the pattern to avoid a collision.

synopsis: CE550 Captain at FL300 is informed of opposite direction traffic at FL310. At about the same time the other aircraft states that they are descending for a TCAS RA. The CE550 was not TCAS equipped and remained level and is informed by ATC that Mode C has failed.
summary: A non-TCAS-equipped crew at FL300 observed an opposite-direction aircraft receiving a TCAS descent Resolution Advisory while ATC reported missing their Mode C data. Despite all three altimeters indicating 30,000 feet and recent RVSM certification, the crew descended under ATC instruction with 1,000-foot callouts.

synopsis: C208 flight crew reports rejecting a takeoff for low torque. Upon returning to the line the crew is informed that Maintenance is aware of the problem although no logbook entries have been made. The engine is 'repaired' and the flight departs three hours late.
summary: The Pilot Flying aborted takeoff after the aircraft failed to produce maximum torque, revealing a known maintenance issue that had not been documented or communicated to the crew. Maintenance adjusted the torque settings, allowing the flight to depart three hours late, though the crew expressed concern over the lack of prior disclosure and company pressure to alter the incident report.

synopsis: RV6 pilot reports an NMAC approaching Ocean City at 2,200 FT with a low wing aircraft. The other aircraft took evasive action and both aircraft were on ACY Approach.
summary: A pilot flying to 26N reported a near mid-air collision with a Piper that ignored ATC turn instructions while banking toward the reporter at 2,200 feet. The other aircraft passed within 50 yards, and the reporter attributed the incident to the second pilot disregarding clearances and apparent confusion.

synopsis: RV10 pilot reports electrical failure in IMC. Due to a recently installed glass panel with battery backup ADAHRS and an iPad with foreflight, a safe landing ensues at a divert airport.
summary: The pilot experienced an electrical system failure causing communications loss in IMC. After weather deteriorated at the departure airport, the pilot diverted to ZZZ, using a glass panel battery backup and iPad to navigate and land safely.

synopsis: EA50 pilot is instructed to hold for release from an uncontrolled airport and call back in ten minutes. When released birds are encountered on the roll and the takeoff is rejected, resulting in a blown tire and stopping in the overrun.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff after bird strikes damaged the left engine and tail while holding at the runway end due to a 10-minute clearance delay. The aircraft stopped in the overrun with blown and locked tires, which the pilot attributed to wildlife becoming comfortable during the wait.

synopsis: CE500 Captain experiences Emergency pressurization coming on at FL370. Oxygen masks are donned, descent is initiated and 7700 is squawked before discovering that the ACM can be reset by selecting a warmer temperature.
summary: The flight crew at FL370 initiated an emergency descent and squawked 7700 after the emergency pressurization system activated due to an overheated ACM ejector. No cabin depressurization occurred, and the crew reset the system to continue the flight to destination.

synopsis: C150 instructor pilot experiences IFR conditions after taking off on a VFR flight and quickly returns to the departure airport to wait for better weather.
summary: An instructor and student attempted a VFR departure in deteriorating weather, encountering lower-than-expected clouds shortly after takeoff. They executed an unsafe low-altitude return to land safely, later departing successfully after waiting for improved conditions.

aircraft: Diamond Aircraft Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air Ambulance crew reports being cleared for the visual approach to Runway 17L but the flying First Officer believes that 17R is the clearance and continues to believe so until short final when the Tower changes the clearance to 17R. Extreme fatigue was cited as a factor by both pilots.
summary: Two fatigued air ambulance pilots inadvertently landed on the wrong runway (17R instead of 17L) due to mishearing clearances and exhaustion from a punitive 24-hour on-call schedule. The error was corrected by the controller just before landing, resulting in no incident despite the crew's fatigue-induced confusion.

synopsis: The pilot of a C150 lowered the volume on the communication panel to better hear the engine during mixture adjustment, but then neglected to recognize it resulting in the inability to hear Tower communications. He concluded that the Tower was closed and landed without a clearance.
summary: A pilot climbing to 5,500 feet diverted due to deteriorating weather and failed to contact the tower because he had turned the radio volume down to monitor engine mixture and forgot to restore it. He landed treating the field as non-towered, only discovering the volume error during shutdown after an FBO employee directed him to call the tower.

synopsis: An experienced pilot was distracted by conversation with a passenger and neglected to remove the tow bar during pre-flight. This was discovered when attempting to reposition into the hangar after the flight. The tow bar was found off the runway with no damage to the aircraft.
summary: The pilot failed to remove the tow bar before taxiing and departing due to distraction. The bar was found 1,800 feet from the runway end with a bent spring, but the aircraft sustained no visible damage.

synopsis: PA22 pilot reports a NMAC arriving OCF after being cleared for a left base entry for Runway 18 by the Tower, with Cirrus cleared for the option on 36 off an instrument approach. The Cirrus departs initially to the north but as some point turns southeast bound coming dangerously close to the reporter. The Tower indicates the Cirrus is talking to ZJX.
summary: A VFR pilot landing on Runway 18 reported a near-miss with a Cirrus departing Runway 36 that entered the pattern in the wrong direction. The pilot attributed the incident to the Cirrus being transferred to JAX control without a specific heading and potential procedural issues regarding traffic separation.

synopsis: DHC8-100 Flight Attendant describes another passenger head collision with the top of the door frame while deplaning.
summary: A college-aged passenger bumped his head while deplaning due to a low airstair clearance, distraction from his iPhone, and fatigue. He sustained no injuries and left the aircraft.

synopsis: DHC8-100 Flight Attendant describes another passenger head collision with the top of the door frame while boarding.
summary: A passenger wearing a baseball cap struck his head on the airstair door frame while boarding because he was looking down and had limited visibility. He sustained no injuries and later acknowledged the low clearance issue when disembarking.

synopsis: A Glasair/Sportsman 2+2 left rudder became inoperable in flight. The pilot discovered cables rubbing on the side of the pulley hangers and the retainer guides which caused the left rudder cable to shear.
summary: The pilot of an experimental Glasair Sportsman 2+2 experienced left rudder failure on base leg due to a sheared cable caused by rubbing on pulley hangers. The aircraft landed safely, but the manufacturer has delayed inspection despite the pilot's concerns about potential systemic failures.

synopsis: A B737 crew on the OAK PNX 3 Arrival was cleared via the RNAV Z 29 but did not begin the approach at BUSHY because they did not believe that the BUSHY IAF should be termed a transition from the arrival.
summary: Pilots approaching OAK experienced confusion when ATC incorrectly referred to the BUSHY initial approach fix as a transition on the PXN 3 Arrival. The crew clarified the lack of RNAV Z 29 clearance, resulting in a vector and visual approach after ATC admitted the misunderstanding.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew reported anomaly that caused multiple false overspeed warnings. They chose to declare an emergency and returned to departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced repeated erratic airspeed indications and autothrottle retardation during climb and cruise, causing overspeed warnings. They declared an emergency, returned to base flying manually, and maintenance identified PSEU and autothrottle faults.

synopsis: LR-45 Captain experiences an ITT exceedance on short final and lands safely after securing the engine with the landing assured.
summary: The pilot reported an engine failure on approach below 1,000 FT MSL after ITT climbed red, causing the aircraft to shake and yaw right. The crew executed memory items, secured the right engine, and landed safely without declaring an emergency due to time constraints.

synopsis: MD-82 Captain reported wake vortex encounter six miles in trail of a B747-800 on arrival to ORD that resulted in a 40 degree roll. ATC stated there should not have been an encounter based on the flight paths.
summary: A crew flying a B747-800 on vectors for Runway 28 at ORD encountered wake turbulence while descending from 5,000 to 4,000 feet, causing a 40-degree left roll and autopilot disconnect. Although the aircraft was recovered and landed safely, an ATC review later indicated the flight paths should have prevented the encounter.

synopsis: The flight crew of an MD-11, inbound to ZSPD, line selected the wrong RNAV STAR associated with their final assigned runway. Doing so autotuned the incorrect ILS frequency and a short lived track deviation resulted.
summary: The crew approached ZSPD with conflicting flight plans for Runway 34, then switched to Runway 35R after detecting an incorrect localizer frequency during the Approach checklist. The pilot flying intercepted the correct localizer visually, and an uneventful landing occurred, though the reporter cited confusing chart transitions and late ATC runway assignment as contributing factors.

synopsis: CRJ-900 First Officer experiences a STEERING INOP caution message just after takeoff and is informed by the Captain that it is likely a nuisance alert. The crew continues to destination and elects to not declare an emergency or brief the flight attendants and passengers. An emergency is declared for the crew by ATC when a longer runway is requested and the reason for the request provided. During roll out it is discovered that the steering is truly inoperative and a tow to the gate is required.
summary: The flight crew continued to destination after a STEERING INOP caution, selecting runway XYL over the longer XYR to utilize high-speed turnoffs. Although the Captain initially treated the message as a nuisance, steering was confirmed inoperative on rollout, requiring a tug for taxiing after ATC declared an emergency.

synopsis: BE-36 pilot reports a track deviation due to errors entering his cleared route into his GPS and lack of familiarity with a new glass panel flight display.
summary: The pilot, flying a single-engine aircraft with a new Aspen glass panel, navigated toward terrain after incorrectly programming the GPS and failing to engage the autopilot on ATC vectors. The incident resulted from unfamiliarity with the new system and a failure to verify heading changes or request assistance when lost.

synopsis: After keeping his amphibious float equipped Husky in the water for four to five weeks the aircraft is flown to an airport where it is discovered after landing that the brakes do not work. Minor damage to the aircraft results.
summary: The pilot of a new amphibious float-equipped aircraft lost braking effectiveness after a 1.5-hour flight due to submerged brakes from weeks of water storage. The aircraft struck a hangar wall while exiting the runway, causing minor damage to the float bumper and the structure.

synopsis: ZAN Controller described a near loss of separation when intending to issue one altitude but in fact issued another caught by a fellow controller and corrected.
summary: An air traffic controller issued an incorrect holding altitude of 050 to an ATR42 descending to 060 while a Metro climbed to 050 due to fatigue and task saturation. A certified supervisor and D-Side colleague identified the error before separation was lost, preventing an incident caused by understaffing and expectancy bias.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports ingesting a goose at V1 during takeoff with the First Officer flying. Loud compressor stalls are heard from the left engine and the Captain assumes control at approximately 100 FT AGL but the positive rate call is not made and the gear is not retracted. After the engine is shut down the gear is noticed and retracted. Flight returns for a single engine landing.
summary: The Captain and First Officer of a B737-700 ingested geese into the left engine near V1, causing compressor stalls and visible flames. They executed emergency checklists, shut down the engine, and landed safely on one engine after declaring an emergency.

synopsis: A B737-800 had a dual ADIRU fault in icing conditions during descent which resulted in both engine EEC's reverting to the Soft Mode and the Captain's airspeed falling to about 120 KTS with a buffet alert and aural low speed warning.
summary: During a descent in weather, the Captain experienced a false low airspeed warning and buffet alert caused by an ADIRU fault affecting both EECs. The First Officer maintained control using correct indications, and the crew restored accurate data by switching EECs to hard alternate mode before landing.

synopsis: EMB-145LR First Officer reported wake vortex encounter in trail of an A310 on approach to IAH that resulted in a roll. When the Captain applied corrective controls they got a Yaw Damper Fail message.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway 26L at George Bush Intercontinental Airport, the crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding slow Airbus A310, causing a rapid right roll and a Yaw Damper Fail EICAS message. The pilot flying corrected the roll, and maintenance inspected the aircraft after a successful system restart at the gate.

synopsis: An air carrier inbound to EWR ILS 4R lost contact with ATC and flew through the LOC, eventually re-establishing contact with ATC, a high and fast vector by ATC only added to the LOC transition.
summary: The flight crew reported that New York Approach changed their frequency too close to the EWR Runway 4R localizer while they were at 220 KTS, causing a loss of communication due to congestion. This resulted in the aircraft passing the localizer without interception instructions, nearly forcing the crew to squawk 7600 before ATC eventually provided a new heading and frequency.

synopsis: A DHC-8-100 developed a burning odor at the gate with ground power plugged in but the Captain, working with Maintenance Control, could not find the source while troubleshooting and causing the Flight Attendant to become ill. When emergency vehicles arrived investigate the engine run, the Captain walked into a stationary propeller causing an injury.
summary: The Captain and Flight Attendant experienced fumes on a propeller aircraft at the gate, leading to the Captain sustaining a head injury from a propeller blade while the Flight Attendant became ill. The Captain attributed the fumes to an unknown source and the injury to poor visibility and rushing while assisting Maintenance Control.

synopsis: During post flight inspection a CE-560XLS Captain discovered an area of frost on the bottom of the tail cone which lead him to believe that ice had formed inside of the tailcone during flight after the aircraft was exposed to rain the previous night.
summary: The pilot reported frost on the tail section after a flight in rain, suspecting internal ice formation that melted during the flight. No flight control abnormalities occurred, but the pilot recommended Cessna add a drain hole to prevent future ice accumulation.

synopsis: A B777-200 Captain was advised by VIDP Approach Control that his lateral track did not conform to the SAM 6F RNAV STAR by which they had been cleared. The reporter, however, disagreed-citing their FMS track was precisely following the FMS magenta line which, in turn, exactly matched the route described on their commercially published aero chart.
summary: The crew flying an inbound jet to VIDP on the SAM 6F RNAV STAR reported that while the autopilot navigated the procedure, Approach Control assigned a heading and questioned the arrival. The crew concluded that their company jets were not flying the correct procedural ground track and agreed to contact Company Standards for investigation.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain experiences a duct overheat warning climbing through FL200. The bleed system is shut down and the flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: During climb through 20,000 feet, the flight crew received a left duct overheat warning, causing bleed system shutdown and slow depressurization. They descended to 8,000 feet, returned to the departure airport, and landed safely after completing non-normal checklists.

synopsis: Corporate jet departing SUS experienced a TCAS TA/RA with a preceding C172 departure and then with a STL inbound, the reporter listing ATC's 'first come first serve' procedure as problematic.
summary: The G-550 crew reported multiple traffic alerts during departure from SUS due to ATC releasing three aircraft in quick succession. The Cessna 172 drifted and climbed unexpectedly, causing conflicts that required the G-550 to maneuver to avoid both the Cessna and inbound 3,000-foot traffic.

synopsis: C177 pilot experiences an oil leak shortly after takeoff with oil dripping on his leg. The Tower is notified and the reporter is able to make 180 degree turn and land opposite direction on the departure runway. Post flight revealed that the oil line that supplies the oil pressure gauge had broken off at the fire wall.
summary: The pilot experienced a broken copper oil pressure tube at the firewall shortly after takeoff, causing oil to flood the cockpit and drop pressure to zero. The aircraft returned to Runway 24L for an immediate landing and shutdown, with inspection confirming the tube failure emptied the engine's oil into the cabin.

synopsis: PA28 Instructor Pilot experiences a power failure at 50 FT AGL with the student at the controls. The Instructor takes control and successfully lands on airport property with no damage to airport or aircraft. Fuel starvation is suspected.
summary: An instructor and student experienced total power loss at 50 feet AGL during takeoff, likely caused by a butterfly clip stuck on the cowling during fuel sumping. The instructor safely landed the aircraft on grass with no damage, though the exact cause remains unknown.

synopsis: BE36 pilot discovers an error in the CTAF provided by his G430 during approach to CLM. Frequency shown is 123.0 while current frequency is 122.975. A go-around results due to miscommunication with an aircraft on the runway.
summary: The pilot, cleared for a visual approach to Runway 08, executed a go-around after observing a floatplane crossing the active runway. The incident resulted from a Jeppesen chart error listing the incorrect CTAF frequency, which the pilot failed to cross-check before landing.

synopsis: PHL Controller detailed the difficult task of breaking up a flight when no prior coordination/requests were made by the flight.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managed a flight of three T-34s en route to TEB when two aircraft broke formation without prior notice, deviating from assigned altitudes and routes. The controller issued new clearances and codes to separate the scattered aircraft, noting that poor pilot coordination and incorrect altitude readbacks nearly caused a loss of separation.

synopsis: ZTL Controller described a loss of separation when two company aircraft accepted the wrong ATC clearance causing the separation loss, one reporter claiming the subject company pilots frequently confuse their call signs.
summary: Air Traffic Controllers issued a stop-at-FL300 clearance to Air Carrier X, but Air Carrier Z read it back, causing Air Carrier X to climb through FL304 while passing Air Carrier Y at FL310. This miscommunication resulted in a loss of vertical separation between the two aircraft due to the wrong pilot acknowledging the clearance.

synopsis: TRACON Controller was cited for a 'technical' separation loss during visual approach procedures when a pilot failed to acknowledge a clearance by using his/her callsign.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a visual approach clearance to an SR22 behind a descending B737 but failed to notice the SR22 pilot omitted their callsign in the readback. The controller accepted full responsibility for the oversight and suggested eliminating visual separation procedures to prevent similar reliance on pilot compliance.

synopsis: A320 First Officer reports the forward cargo door opening while the engine on that side is being started. The ground crew is queried and the crew informed that a late bag is being loaded.
summary: During pushback, while the second engine was starting, the forward cargo door opened to load a bag. The door closed before the engine stabilized, creating a risk of serious injury or engine damage.

synopsis: A flight crew lifted off ISN Runway 29 with less than 1,000 FT remaining and discovered after the fact that passenger and baggage weight was heavier than calculated and other flap/runway options should have been considered.
summary: The flight crew experienced an extended takeoff roll on Runway 29 at ISN, estimating only 1,000 feet remaining, likely due to underestimated passenger weights and communication errors in manual data entry. The pilot attributed the unsafe margin to reliance on Dispatch for non-ACARS flights and a lack of available performance charts to verify the weight and balance calculations.

synopsis: An EMB-145 was dispatched with PACK 1 MEL'ed and an EICAS advisory message PACK 1 VALVE CLSD. When PACK 2 failed the message was PACK 1-2 VALVE CLSD but the crew missed the subtle change so when the CABIN, CABIN aural alert sounded as the cabin climbed, an emergency was declared and the flight descended safely.
summary: On the fifth leg of a long duty day, a fatigued crew missed a subtle EICAS change indicating both air conditioning packs were closed, triggering an emergency descent from FL250 to 9,000 feet due to cabin altitude warnings. The crew attributed the event to fatigue and poor monitoring, noting that better recognition of the pack failure could have prevented the descent.

synopsis: Instructor pilot experienced a NMAC in the pattern when instructions from the Tower resulted in two aircraft being at the same place at the same time.
summary: An instructor and student pilot in a Cessna executed a go-around after Air Traffic Control issued conflicting traffic information, resulting in a near-midair collision with another Cessna 50 feet below. The reporter attributes the incident to ATC's failure to provide adequate separation and their own reliance on incorrect radio reports.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot reports over torquing the gearbox during a practice NVG landing due inability to see the ground approaching, then flying back to base.
summary: During a simulated medical pickup using NVGs, the pilot overtorqued the helicopter after overlooking the landing light switch and misinterpreting the torque warning. The pilot delayed checking the circuit breaker until landing three minutes later and failed to notify Dispatch immediately.

synopsis: PA28 pilot on a practice missed approach with instructor experiences lost communications with ATC. A new Garmin GTN-650 touch screen was being used and it is believed that an inadvertent touch caused the departure frequency to be swapped to the Tower frequency.
summary: A student pilot and instructor practicing instrument approaches in a Garmin GTN-650 equipped aircraft lost contact with Approach Control for eight minutes. The radio inadvertently switched to the Tower frequency due to an accidental touchscreen input, though no safety issue occurred as the instructor maintained visual contact.

synopsis: A PA-28 140 lost power during the takeoff roll and as the pilot rejected the takeoff the aircraft exited the runway end without sustaining any damage.
summary: The pilot experienced a loss of power during takeoff, preventing the aircraft from becoming airborne. The pilot power-slid to stop, but the aircraft exited the runway end into grass with no reported damage to the propeller or landing gear.

synopsis: The pilot of a Light Sport Aircraft encountered stronger than forecast headwinds that led to fuel exhaustion while on short final. The aircraft dropped 20 feet onto the runway.
summary: The pilot encountered strong headwinds and turbulence, with fuel gauges indicating sufficient fuel for the destination. Prior to touchdown, fuel feed to the engine stopped, causing the aircraft to drop 20 feet.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a traffic pattern conflict when allegedly the TRACON's sequencing resulted in one aircraft being on top another on final.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a near-midair conflict between a C172 and a C560 inbound for Runway 16L, diverting the C560 to Runway 16R. The controller attributed the situation to a TRACON sequencing error regarding the C172's entry type and noted the C560's speed prevented further separation.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew is informed by a ramp agent after gate arrival that the elevator appears damaged. The damage likely occurred two legs prior during either pushback or initial taxi when a bump is felt and an apparent nosewheel steering anomaly is detected. A careful inspection after the first leg did not detect the elevator damage.
summary: During pushback, the flight crew used hand signals due to faulty headsets, resulting in the aircraft's elevator striking a terminal stanchion. The damage was discovered later by ground crew, grounding the aircraft after the crew initially attributed taxi anomalies to nose wheel issues.

synopsis: A B757-200 right engine oil temperature rose into the yellow band, but continued into the red band after completing the QRH, so the engine was shut down, an emergency declared and the flight descended into its filed destination.
summary: The crew experienced right engine oil temperature excursions at FL380, triggering a shutdown after temperatures spiked into the red band with thrust. They elected to continue to their filed destination rather than divert to an unfamiliar airport, completing the flight safely.

synopsis: A319 Captain experiences an EGT exceedance when FLEX power is selected for takeoff. The takeoff is rejected and the engine shut down. Maintenance suspected variable stator vanes to be the culprit in this incident.
summary: The flight crew rejected takeoff due to an EGT over limit on Engine 2 caused by a vane position controller/actuator failure. Mechanics confirmed a mechanical or electrical fault prevented the engine from spooling up, resulting in a normal taxi to the gate.

synopsis: An EMB-145 CAS alerted both PITCH TRIM channels failed so an emergency was declared and the flight diverted. The crew had no autopilot, pitch trim or speedbrakes, and excessive back pressure was required to remain stable as they slowed to a very high Vref speed.
summary: The Pilot Not Flying reported a dual pitch trim failure on a VFR flight at FL220, compounded by previous unresolved stabilizer faults. The crew diverted to a nearby airport, declared an emergency, and landed safely despite high approach speeds and excessive control forces.

synopsis: An EMB-145 crew returned to the departure airport after a flight control vibration was felt and a low frequency tone was heard during climbout in left turns.
summary: During climbout, the crew experienced control column vibration and loud noise while banking left, prompting a return to the departure airport due to a suspected flight control issue. Effective workload management and communication between pilots, the flight attendant, and dispatch facilitated a smooth and safe air return.

synopsis: An EMB-145 EICAS alerted Pitch Trim Main Fail and Pitch Trim Backup Fail but using the QRH the Back Up channel was recovered so the flight continued to the filed destination without the autopilot.
summary: The Pilot Flying experienced dual pitch trim failures while climbing through FL300. After resetting systems and descending to FL270 to exit RVSM, the crew hand-flew the remaining 600 miles to a safe visual landing with the backup trim channel.

synopsis: An ERJ-170 pilot on a visual to SFO 28L reported taking TCAS RA evasive action from an aircraft on 28R which did not slow as directed by ATC.
summary: During a visual approach to SFO Runway 28L, the crew received a descent Resolution Advisory at 1,100 feet due to a conflicting aircraft on the parallel 28R approach. The crew descended below 1,000 feet and the glideslope, cleared the conflict, and successfully landed.

synopsis: A B737-800 Captain failed to turn right on an initial heading to their alternate after exiting holding so the First Officer took control in repose to ATC's concern about the wrong direction toward traffic.
summary: Two pilots holding over SMO at 14,000 feet diverted to an alternate but deviated from a left-turn clearance due to an unexecuted FMC fix and active holding pattern. The First Officer manually corrected the course after automation confusion and task saturation, resulting in no loss of separation and an uneventful landing.

synopsis: A DC-10 crew MELed an engine anti-ice system after leaving the gate when the ANTI-ICE DISAG light came on because they thought it was an indication error and after takeoff the fault self corrected.
summary: The flight crew received an ENG 1 A-ICE DISAG alert while taxiing and initiated a Crew MEL using MEL 30-22-04 after Maintenance suggested returning to the gate without specifying the correct MEL. The crew departed with the anti-ice on, but later realized they likely used the wrong MEL instead of the flagged MEL 30-22-01 due to poor communication with Maintenance.

synopsis: A321 landed without clearance after an earlier wake vortex encounter distracted the flight crew.
summary: The Captain, acting as pilot not flying, landed a jet at JFK without a clearance after mistakenly selecting the wrong frequency and missing the Tower's reply. This error occurred because the Captain was distracted by a technical discussion regarding wake turbulence from a preceding B747.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported an altitude deviation on IVANE2 arrival to CLT.
summary: The flight crew of an Airbus experienced an inadvertent descent below the 13,000 FT MAJIC crossing restriction during the IVANE2 arrival to CLT. The reporter attributes the event to the FMS dropping the altitude constraint after an ATC climb clearance and managed descent selection, compounded by crew fixation on a false speed discrepancy message.

synopsis: An Airbus crew on the PHX MAIER 5 noticed they were at 6,200 FT prior to KARDS after the ALT button failed to engage VNAV and while climbing to 7,000 FT were told by ATC to maintain 7,000 FT but became confused and again began a descent after KARDS.
summary: The flight crew descended below the STAR altitude on the Maier 5 arrival due to high workload, weather avoidance, and failure to verify VNAV engagement. They incorrectly resumed descent after crossing KARDS at 7,000 feet, violating a "climb and maintain" clearance issued by Approach Control.

synopsis: B717 Captain reported the APU shutdown suddenly at the gate after arrival, generating a smokey smell, so the aircraft was evacuated through the already open forward entry door.
summary: The Captain and flight attendants experienced an APU auto-shutdown with smoke in the aft cabin after switching from APU to ground power during post-landing deplaning. The crew evacuated remaining passengers, secured the APU, and coordinated with fire services, which confirmed no fire before maintenance cleared the aircraft for flight.

synopsis: B737 Captain notes a fuel imbalance after leveloff, which cannot be corrected with the crossfeed valve. The valve circuit breakers are found tripped and reset, after discussion with Maintenance Control, but trip again when the valve is opened. Flight diverts to a suitable airport.
summary: The crew encountered a fuel imbalance after leveloff when the crossfeed valve failed to open due to a tripped circuit breaker. After resetting the breaker caused a second trip, they diverted and landed safely, attributing the issue to a mechanical valve failure.

synopsis: Air Carrier pilot reports being inadvertently crossing Taxiway E without clearance to do so. The reporter does not believe a hold short clearance was issued by the Tower, although this taxiway is an extension of Runway 8R and treated as part of the runway by the Tower.
summary: Pilots taxiing to Runway 8R via Taxiway Kilo inadvertently entered Taxiway Echo, which intersects the runway centerline, because Tower issued no hold short instructions. The controller requested future compliance, and the crew suggested ATC clarify hold short points at Kilo to prevent runway incursions.

synopsis: B757-200 flight crew described operational complications arising from flying the aircraft with multiple MELs.
summary: The crew flew an aircraft with four flag MEL items, including inoperative autopilot and autothrottle, and declared an emergency when stab trim failed at 12,000 feet. They hand-flew the approach and landed safely, attributing the incident to the combined effect of the MELs and pressure to operate without spares.

synopsis: A300 First Officer experiences a generator fault during climb that will not reset. When the APU will not start the flight returns to the departure airport for maintenance.
summary: During climb, the pilot reported a Generator 2 fault that would not reset and an unsuccessful APU start attempt per the QRH. The aircraft returned to the departure airport for maintenance.

synopsis: B777-200 First Officer reported Flight Attendant noticed a smell of smoke about two hours into a transoceanic flight, so they declared an emergency and returned to departure airport.
summary: The flight crew detected burning plastic fumes from a previously repaired cabin printer at Door 2L during cruise at FL350. Suspecting an unresolved maintenance issue, the Captain initiated a PAN PAN diversion back to the departure airport while executing the Fumes Irregular checklist.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain experiences an iPad based EFB failure in cruise and wonders what happens when both iPad's fail.
summary: A pilot reported that at cruise altitude, their iPad lost all data access despite normal operation two hours earlier. The device displayed a dim screen with 73 pending transfers, and a hard reset failed to restore functionality.

synopsis: B757 Captain reports leading edge flaps stuck between five and up during departure. Maintenance Control is contacted and flight returns to departure airport using normal flap extension methods to an overweight landing.
summary: The flight crew encountered stuck leading edge slats between flaps 5 and up after takeoff. They declared an emergency, returned for a 219,000-pound overweight landing, and executed a normal landing using the normal flap extension system.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain is issued a release with a deferral for escape slide lighting which the MEL allows for daylight operations only and the flight is scheduled out before sunrise. The Dispatcher states that the company uses civil twilight as daylight in accordance with ICAO definitions. The Captain does not believe this definition of daylight meets the letter of the MEL and departs at sunrise.
summary: The Captain delayed departure until sunrise due to an MEL deferral for inoperative over-wing slide lights restricting operations to daylight. Despite Dispatch and Maintenance citing civil twilight as sufficient, the Captain insisted on actual daylight for slide visibility, overriding pressure to depart in darkness.

synopsis: B747-400 Captain reported difficulty loading certain waypoints into the FMC on a flight departing YSSY.
summary: During preflight, pilots encountered FMC route discontinuities and missing waypoints (30S63, 15N42) that could not be entered by name or short coordinates. They resolved the issue by manually entering full latitude/longitude coordinates, attributing the delay to an FMC database problem rather than corrupted uploads.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reports entering transposed numbers for a NRS (National Reference System) waypoint into the FMC, resulting in a track deviation detected by ZDV.
summary: The pilot transposed a cleared fix (KD54S) into the FMC as KD45S, causing a significant deviation. Denver Center queried the aircraft five minutes after passing CLEVE, prompting the crew to correct the error and receive a revised clearance.

synopsis: B777 flight crew describes the steps taken to correct a fuel filter EICAS message that returns after takeoff and results in a return to field for an overweight landing.
summary: Flight crew experienced recurrent left engine fuel filter EICAS messages during taxi and climb on an ETOPS flight, leading to two returns to the gate. Maintenance replaced the filter and pressure switch, but the issue persisted, forcing a second overweight landing due to safety concerns over potential fuel failure.

synopsis: A320 First Officer reported a course deviation on ILS arrival that was caused at least in part by fatigue and personal problems.
summary: The First Officer, fatigued by personal issues, over-managed the approach by switching to NAV mode instead of arming the localizer, causing a missed intercept. The crew manually re-intercepted the course after overshooting toward a parallel runway, attributing the error to over-thinking and slow reaction.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported taking off overweight because the First Officer was rushed in his calculations.
summary: The Captain and First Officer departed from intersection 17L on a Boeing aircraft using incorrect performance data due to rushing. This resulted in an overweight takeoff with a delayed rotation and excessive runway usage.

synopsis: MD80 Captain reports entering the flight plan waypoint ADIME as ADINE which goes undetected until turning toward the incorrect waypoint.
summary: The Captain and First Officer of a DC-9 at ORD incorrectly loaded waypoint 'ADINE' instead of 'ADIME' into the FMS due to a data entry error and checklist interruption. The crew deviated from course during climbout, received a vector from ATC to correct the path, and reported no loss of separation occurred.

synopsis: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) was informed that a flight crew noticed a pressure drop and low oxygen flow during an Oxygen (O2) Mask preflight check on a B737-900 aircraft. Technician noted the Crew O2 pressure did not require servicing during his Overnight Service Check. The carbon fiber composite crew O2 bottle valve handle was found not fully opened.
summary: Line maintenance performed an overnight service check on a B737-900 oxygen system, passing the flow test before the flight crew reported no mask flow. Maintenance found the oxygen bottle full but not fully opened; opening it restored flow with no delay, prompting a recommendation for additional training.

synopsis: The pilot of an RV-10 placed himself and his rated pilot passenger in a difficult situation when he elected to take the runway between landing traffic that had not yet cleared the runway, and traffic on final approach. The pilot was also observed to not utilize effective sterile cockpit practices.
summary: The Pilot Flying departed a fly-in-breakfast without proper separation, ignoring traffic on final and rollout. The reporter attributed this runway incursion to the PF's lack of situational awareness and unwillingness to wait for safe clearance.

synopsis: The pilot of a C182 was advised that his altimeter mode C altitude did not agree with his reported altitude. This was confirmed by comparing his G1000 altitude indicator against the back-up altimeter. The pilot then recognized that the altimeter barometric reading in the Kollsman window differed greatly from the local pressure. He surmised that he inadvertently adjusted the co-located barometric correction knob while attempting to adjust the autopilot course knob.
summary: The pilot inadvertently rotated the G1000 barometric setting knob while adjusting the course knob, causing a 2,000-foot altitude discrepancy between the primary and backup altimeters. This error triggered altitude alerts and Mode C conflicts with ATC, leading the pilot to cancel IFR and descend to the correct altitude.

synopsis: During the takeoff roll the pilot of a PA-28 noticed a lack of effectiveness when applying a right rudder correction. The takeoff was aborted, but the limited right brake effectiveness caused the aircraft to contact a runway threshold light and depart the runway surface. Maintenance was unable to find a mechanical problem and speculated that the brake became overheated during taxi and run-up.
summary: The pilot aborted a takeoff due to unresponsive right rudder and brake pedals, resulting in the aircraft overrunning the runway and breaking a threshold light. Maintenance found no mechanical faults but speculated the right brake had overheated during prior taxi and run-up operations.

synopsis: An instructor pilot and two students in a Phenom 100 identified a strong electrical smell during climbout. When they attempted to contact the Tower Controller, they were unable. When they made contact on the second radio, they declared an emergency and landed safely. Indications are that the Number 1 communications radio failed for an unknown reason.
summary: During a training flight in a Phenom 100, an instructor and two students detected a strong electrical smell and lost COM 1 while on the upwind leg. The crew declared an emergency, squawked 7700, and landed safely; maintenance is now investigating the cause of the smell and radio failure.

synopsis: The pilot of a BE-76 heard a loud bang after making a final flap extension in preparation for landing. He then observed the left flap was not connected at the outer hinge point. He was able to maintain control of the aircraft and landed safely. During the post flight inspection, he noted that fresh paint on the outboard flap hinge had not been disturbed by the installation of mounting hardware.
summary: The pilot reported that while on left base for Runway XX Left, the left wing flap folded inward after a loud bang during flap extension. Inspection revealed a missing bolt on the outer hinge following a recent 100-hour maintenance inspection, though the pilot landed safely without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported multiple autoflight anomalies on approach, perhaps related to FCC failure.
summary: During a PRM approach to ATL, both flight directors failed and the autopilot disengaged at 5,500 feet, likely due to FCC B or MCP failure. The First Officer hand-flew the aircraft through multiple system malfunctions before control transferred to the Captain, who re-engaged automation for a visual landing.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: MEM Tower described an unexpected go around event that caused concern regarding a possible loss of wake turbulence separation with a converging arrival aircraft.
summary: A pilot flying a heavy aircraft on a visual approach to Runway 36L executed a go-around due to a long landing, placing the aircraft in close proximity to another heavy on final for Runway 9. The controller turned the aircraft right to minimize wake turbulence exposure, and the other aircraft landed safely after being advised of the potential hazard.

synopsis: A90 Controller described a probable loss of wake separation when a 'large' aircraft was permitted to land on Runway 33R, the reporter suggested that 'large' aircraft be prohibited from using Runway 33R.
summary: A pilot reported that a large DH8 landing on short Runway 33R required early speed reduction, causing excessive compression and overlooked wake turbulence for a following H25A less than 4 miles away. The reporter concluded that large aircraft should not use Runway 33R due to these safety risks and lack of operational efficiency.

aircraft: Embraer Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Three Controllers and two pilots reported on an altitude deviation resulting from similar call signs which involved four aircraft converging on the same fix. Controllers recognized the problem and separated traffic.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller and two pilots involved a [Company] X90 and X19 during departure and climb phases due to a frequency change and altitude clearance miscommunication. The error caused X90 to climb into conflicting traffic, requiring immediate descent and turns to avoid a collision with a Kingair and B737.

synopsis: ZLC Controller voiced concern regarding the lack of proper coordination regarding a rocket launch area noting every aspect of the coordination procedure was flawed.
summary: The ZOA OMIC released mission airspace without sector controller consent or proper coordination, forcing a commercial flight to take a significant vector to avoid the restricted area. The reporter states this non-coordinated activation violated safeguards and occurred with insufficient notice, creating a critical safety issue.

synopsis: Confusion reigned when ATC--in an effort to maintain separation between a BE-190 on the SUNNS STAR to PHX and a B737 on the KOOLY RNAV STAR (both of which STARs include waypoint SQUEZ)--mixed 'descend via' phraseology with altitude assignments different from those on the STAR charts themselves.
summary: An air traffic controller and a B737 crew experienced a speed and altitude conflict during the KOOLY RNAV STAR arrival to PHX due to the pilot misunderstanding a "maintain" clearance as a "descend via" instruction. The controller diverted the jet to avoid a conflict with a preceding B190, highlighting a discrepancy between ATC expectations and pilot interpretations of mandatory speed restrictions.

synopsis: The Air Carrier flight crew observed several parachutes in close proximity during approach to a major metropolitan airport. When they inquired with ATC, they received the response that the jumpers had not been cleared to jump.
summary: During a visual approach descent at 4,000 feet, the crew encountered two parachutists passing within 150 to 400 feet on the right side. ATC admitted the jumpers were not cleared to jump and should have been held until the aircraft cleared the area, despite no ATIS or NOTAM warnings.

synopsis: A B737-700 nose wheel steering metering valve apparently malfunctioned as takeoff thrust was set which caused the aircraft to veer off centerline and resulted in a low speed rejected takeoff.
summary: During takeoff roll in thunderstorms, the crew aborted after the nose wheel yawed right and chattered despite TOGA application. Company Safety attributed the event to a faulty nose wheel steering hydraulic metering valve, resulting in the aircraft being pulled from service for maintenance.

synopsis: B737-300 Captain is informed after landing that the flight attendants were unable to contact the cockpit during flight and accuse the pilots of ignoring them.
summary: Pilots reported that flight attendants were upset after claiming their call attempts were ignored during cruise, though the crew heard no chime due to high cockpit noise or a low-volume system. Maintenance checks found the call system functional, and pilots concluded the attendants failed to follow proper emergency door access procedures.

synopsis: After experiencing some difficulty programming a clearance to descend to FL240 the Captain of a B737-700 realized that, instead of descending, the aircraft had climbed from approximately FL276 to FL300 where it had leveled.
summary: The flight crew descended from above FL310 to FL240 but inadvertently climbed to FL300 after VNAV failed to engage and an incorrect FMC altitude entry was made. The pilot corrected the deviation using Vertical Speed, noting that better monitoring of FMC entries would have prevented the error.

synopsis: B737-300 First Officer experiences a loud steady noise shortly after takeoff and a Master Caution for Forward Cargo Door light and the aircraft will not pressurize.
summary: The First Officer flew a takeoff where a loud noise, Master Caution, and forward cargo door light indicated a pressurization failure. The Captain coordinated a return to the field, and the First Officer completed a normal approach and landing with no other issues.

synopsis: The Pilots of a A320 described a green hydraulic system fluid loss accompanied by a yellow hydraulic system overheat. An emergency was declared and a successful landing was completed at the departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced green hydraulic loss and yellow system overheat during climbout, causing gear door vibration and loss of nose wheel steering. They declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport, landed safely, and were towed to the gate after emergency personnel inspection.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported he had set the parking brake handle to the 'On' position while waiting in line for takeoff, but the aircraft still rolled forward, he used foot brakes to stop the aircraft. While cycling the parking brake handle multiple times, he noticed the lack of brake pressure on the Yellow Hydraulic System Triple Indicator. Aircraft was taxied back to gate.
summary: The pilot reported that while taxiing for takeoff with the parking brake set, the aircraft rolled despite the handle being in the 'On' position. The pilot stopped the aircraft using foot brakes, cycled the handle with no pressure indication, and returned to the gate for a mechanical logbook entry.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An A319 on the CLT IVANE 2 crossed MAJIC Intersection at 12,000 FT because the FMGC dropped the 13,000 FT constraint even though it was verified during the preflight.
summary: The First Officer descended via the Ivane2 procedure and crossed the MAJIC intersection at 12,000 feet instead of the required 13,000 feet due to high task load. The pilot attributed the error to distractions caused by the Electronic Flight Bag and fatigue, requesting a supervisor call.

synopsis: A B737-700 flight crew arriving LAS from the west as dusk was turning to night was cleared for a visual approach to Runway 7R. During their descent they received a low altitude alert from ATC as they crossed terrain as high as 8,600 MSL.
summary: Pilots on a KEPEC arrival into LAS accepted a visual approach to Runway 7R at night and descended below published altitudes, triggering a low altitude alert from ATC. The crew leveled off to verify terrain clearance, attributing the incident to poor depth perception in darkness and a lack of published visual approach guidance for that runway.

synopsis: An ERJ-170 Captain intervened by extending full speed brakes during descent below 10,000 FT at 270 KTS because the First Officer, as the flying pilot just off IOE, was trained not use full speed brakes.
summary: The Pilot Not Flying intervened during descent below 10,000 feet when the First Officer failed to maintain 250 KIAS while using autopilot Vertical Speed mode and partial speed brakes. The reporter attributed the event to the First Officer's reliance on automation and incorrect training regarding speed brake usage and descent mode priorities.

synopsis: CRJ700 flight crew describe the events leading up to a go around from a flaps 8 landing on a maintenance ferry flight.
summary: During a maintenance ferry flight with flaps restricted to 8 degrees, the First Officer caused an unstable approach with oscillations, prompting the Captain to execute a go-around. The crew landed safely after ATC assistance, attributing the incident to the First Officer's handling errors and delayed decision to abort the approach.

synopsis: A light weight MD-11 developed hot brakes during taxi in because of brake usage but was constrained from taxiing into the assigned gate with less than all engines operating.
summary: The MD-11 crew reported Level 2 hot brakes (573°F) on arrival after using brakes to control taxi speed at a gate prohibiting single-engine taxi. The pilot attributed the overheating to the prohibition forcing brake usage on a lightweight aircraft, noting similar incidents and a previous tire failure at nearby gates.

synopsis: A CRJ-900 CAS alerted L BLEED DUCT with the L DUCT MON MEL'ed and simultaneously the right bleed closed. So with a depressurizing aircraft an emergency was declared, a descent commenced and at 10,000 FT the flight returned to their departure airport.
summary: The flight crew encountered a left bleed duct warning at 17,000 feet, causing the right bleed to close and leaving the aircraft unpressurized. They declared an emergency, descended to 10,000 feet, and landed uneventfully at the departure airport after completing abnormal checklists.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant described feeling ill after several legs with the cabin temperature very hot and that other Flight Attendant was vomiting during the encounter.
summary: Two flight attendants on a multi-leg flight suffered severe heat-related illness despite maximum cooling efforts, with one vomiting and the other developing a fever and rash. The reporter was hospitalized for heat exhaustion and dehydration, but a doctor later diagnosed toxic chemical exposure exacerbated by the high cabin temperatures.

synopsis: A Lead Mechanic describes his safety concerns after elimination of Lead Mechanic positions on the second taxi-tow crew slots for days and afternoon shifts. He also adds historical relevance to the benefits of having Lead Mechanics directly involved with the taxi-tow crews and not be assigned to a remote desk away from the actual aircraft movement.
summary: A Lead Mechanic reported that ZZZ management eliminated second Lead Mechanic slots for taxi-tow crews to save money, violating General Procedures Manual requirements for onsite oversight. The reporter warned this change increases the risk of aircraft damage and incidents during ground movements at hangar and gate locations.

aircraft: Alon; Inc Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An ER Coupe D engine would not accelerate above idle while recovering from slow flight/stall practice so the instructor landed in a nearby corn field resulting in minimal aircraft damage and a blown tire.
summary: An instructor and student in an ER Coupe experienced a throttle cable failure at 2,600 feet MSL during slow flight training, causing the engine to remain at idle. They glided to a safe landing on a farm with minimal aircraft damage and no injuries.

synopsis: A BE-76 student had difficulty holding back pressure to climb after takeoff, so the instructor took control, declared an emergency and land safely where a disconnected elevator trim was found.
summary: The flight instructor took control of a BE-76 during the climb after the student pilot could not maintain back pressure due to a loose elevator trim wheel. The instructor landed safely on Runway 17 with no damage or injuries.

synopsis: A non current IFR pilot on an IFR flight plan for currency declared an emergency because of an SR-22 oil pressure warning and discovered his lack of currency after landing.
summary: A pilot conducting a local IFR training flight encountered an oil pressure warning during cruise and returned to the home airport after declaring an emergency. The pilot later realized they were not in compliance with FAR 61.57 for IFR currency, having mistaken a March flight review for an IPC.

synopsis: T75 Controller expressed concern regarding the descent profiles of the various aircraft based upon equipment, noting that those differences result in highly variable altitudes and speed differentials.
summary: An E145 descending via the AARCH1 STAR flew significantly lower than a trailing A319 due to inadequate V-NAV, causing an altitude differential that required speed restrictions and potential clearance changes. The controller attributes this recurring issue to aircraft limitations creating unsafe overtakes and recommends amending the STAR with new altitude constraints.

synopsis: TRACON Controller providing OJT described a loss of separation when traffic increased significantly, positions were combined, and complexity increased. The reporter noted facility 'combined sectors' for training, as one causal factor.
summary: During on-the-job training in combined sectors, a trainee descended a Mooney from 7,000 to 5,000 feet, causing a loss of separation with a Navion at 6,000 feet. The reporter attributes the incident to excessive workload from combined sectors, insufficient staffing, and distractions from the trainer's questions.

synopsis: Two pilots report that a Flight Attendant sustained hot water burns when she lifted the handle on the aft #2 coffee maker during the brewing process on their B737-700 aircraft.
summary: During cruise at FL410, a flight attendant was burned by hot water from the aft #2 coffee maker after lifting its handle while brewing. The crew initially attributed this to operator error but later logged the equipment for maintenance, which replaced the unit due to coffee grounds.

synopsis: While flying but not 'cleared via' the KOOLY RNAV STAR to PHX the flight crew of a B737-700 was given ambiguous airspeed and altitude clearances with which they were unable to comply. The controller reprimanded them for not complying with speed restrictions even though he had altered the STAR altitude restrictions.
summary: Pilots descending on the KOOLY RNAV STAR received conflicting ATC clearances regarding altitude and speed restrictions, preventing compliance with both published criteria and specific vectors. The crew attributed the resulting confusion and deviation to negligent ATC instructions that failed to override published speeds when altering the arrival profile.

synopsis: A Captain violated the SFO Class B speed restriction below 8,000 FT while departing SJC after he instructed the First Officer to remove the Class B rings which were installed to prevent such a violation.
summary: The Pilot Not Flying and Captain of a Boeing 700 departed SJC, climbing under SFO Class B airspace. Despite the PNF's warning, the Captain accelerated to 250 KTS at 6,200 FT, violating the 200 KTS speed limit required below the Class B floor.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier crew programmed and briefed a SFO PORTE 5 Runway 28L departure but because of preflight distractions did not reprogram for a Runway 1L which resulted in a track deviation when LNAV was selected after takeoff.
summary: The First Officer departed Runway 1L with the FMC incorrectly programmed for Runway 28L, causing the aircraft to overshoot the 350 radial. NorCal queried the deviation and vectored the crew to heading 280 to rejoin the proper departure procedure after the error was identified.

synopsis: Air carrier departure from SNA, on the noise abatement rapid climb, experienced a TCAS RA with traffic assigned above with minimal IFR separation.
summary: During a noise abatement departure, the crew received a TCAS RA at 4,100 feet MSL due to converging Pilatus PC-12 traffic. The Pilot Flying disengaged the autopilot to follow RA guidance, climbed out of the assigned altitude, and reported the event to SoCal.

synopsis: An MD-11 flight crew cleared to fly an RNAV approach mistakenly modified the line selectable procedure when cleared direct from their transition route to the FAF. When doing so the crossing restriction at the FAF was deleted and the aircraft descended directly toward the DA(H). A low altitude alert was transmitted by the Tower and the flight returned to their clearance and completed the approach and landing.
summary: The pilot flying descended below the 3,000-foot crossing restriction at ZZZZZ after the FMS disregarded altitude limits following a direct clearance. The crew corrected the descent to 2,450 feet MSL and completed a stabilized approach despite a conflict over noise concerns versus altitude safety.

synopsis: An MD-11 returned to its departure airport following the failure of the Captain's CADC.
summary: The Captain experienced unreliable airspeed and Flight Director indications shortly after gear retraction, likely due to a recently replaced CADC. Control was transferred to the First Officer, and the crew returned to the departure airport following a Loss of Airspeed Suspected checklist, resulting in an uneventful landing.
