synopsis: A ZID Controller and the flight crew involved describe a track deviation due to a misunderstanding of the amended PDC.
summary: An E170 crew navigated direct GVE instead of via J42 after misinterpreting an amended PDC stating "TXK J42 MEM then as filed" as a direct clearance. The reporter attributed the deviation to the confusing amendment format, which also caused a similar incident with a Hawker aircraft.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a multiple loss of separation event involving a landing and departure aircraft, the reporter recommended some RADAR training be provided for Tower controllers to prevent future occurrences.
summary: Local Control 1 failed to properly execute a squeeze play between a Challenger 300 and two B737-800s on Runway 19L, causing the arriving B737 to go around while the departing B737 was still rolling. Subsequent errors in frequency handoff and lack of visual separation instructions resulted in a loss of separation between the two B737s.

synopsis: ZMP Controller described an unsafe condition involving the closure of RST Approach and the need to vector an inbound aircraft through weather. Reporter suggested the Approach Control be kept open for a few minutes to provide improved service to late arrivals.
summary: RST Approach transferred an E135 to ZMP Sector 07 during a thunderstorm while the aircraft was within five miles of the airport. The reporter recommends RST remain open until the aircraft lands safely to ensure better radar coverage and immediate weather awareness.

synopsis: A pilot reports he had to stop his taxi while being marshalled into a gate because a Ramp Agent with an external ground power cord had crossed through a Safety Zone in front of their B737-700 aircraft, so he could plug in a power cord.
summary: A Ramper walked through the Safety Zone while the aircraft was taxiing to the gate, forcing the pilot to stop. The Ramper later admitted the action, claiming the aircraft was not deep enough in the zone to warrant staying clear.

synopsis: After landing and on the ramp while awaiting an occupied gate the flight crew of a Boeing 737 received an AFT CARGO fire alarm. The applicable checklist was accomplished down to the EVACUATION line as the Captain concurrently queried the flight attendants as to the condition in the cabin. While no smoke or fumes were reported, an emergency was declared and the aircraft positioned on the nearest avaliable gate as ARFF was summoned. The passengers were evacuated off the aircraft (sans personal effects) through the forward door.
summary: After landing, the crew received a false aft cargo fire warning while taxiing to a gate. The Captain declared an emergency, evacuated passengers, and coordinated with ground staff, but no fire was found, resulting in a three-minute departure delay.

synopsis: EMB145 First Officer discovers a nav accuracy error during the takeoff roll. Once airborne it is found that neither GPS receiver is tracking any satellites. Five minutes into the flight GPS1 acquired a position and the remainder of the flight was normal.
summary: The crew departed Runway 34R on an RNAV departure with the FMS using inaccurate DME/DME data due to a lack of GPS signals. This caused a 0.5 NM course offset during takeoff, which was mitigated when ATC issued a direct clearance after the crew identified the GPS failure in flight.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew reports smoke in the cockpit when the bleed system is switched to the engines from the APU after takeoff. The smoke checklist is complied with and the flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced smoke in the flight deck after switching from APU to engine bleeds following takeoff. They executed emergency procedures, declared an emergency, and landed safely, though the root cause remained undetermined despite a prior Air Cycle Machine replacement.

synopsis: Sticking buttons on the FMS keypad of a CRJ-700 caused the FMS to not sequence to the ILS. The pilots became distracted and did not immediately recognize that the aircraft failed to maintain the proper heading.
summary: During the ILS approach, a deferred FMS keypad issue caused a key to stick, preventing sequencing and distracting both crew members. This distraction led to an unauthorized right turn, requiring ATC to re-vector the aircraft before a normal landing.

synopsis: A300 First Officer notices that fuel was being burned from the outer tanks with fuel still in the inner tanks. Trim tank fuel is manually transferred to the center tank then fed to the engines allowing the flight to continue to destination.
summary: The flight crew encountered an abnormal fuel feed sequence where outer tanks burned before inner tanks, with no ECAM warnings. They manually transferred trim tank fuel and used manual feed procedures to burn center tank fuel, confirming sufficient outer tank fuel remained for a safe landing.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reports accepting an aircraft out of heavy maintenance after a seating configuration change and flying their first leg. Prior to the next leg it is discovered that the weight and balance data has not been change to reflect the new configuration.
summary: The flight crew operated an aircraft from ORD to YYZ following heavy maintenance and seat reconfiguration, unaware that engineering tables were outdated. Upon taxiing for the return leg, Load Planning halted departure due to missing configuration data, revealing the previous flight likely departed with improper weight and balance information.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain is informed by his First Officer that the cabin is climbing slowly. The QRH is complied with and an emergency descent is initiated. The cabin altitude reaches 14,600 during the descent and the masks drop. Maintenance discovers a failed baggage door seal.
summary: The flight crew at FL310 initiated an emergency descent after cabin altitude climbed to 14,600 feet, causing oxygen masks to drop. Maintenance later identified the cause as a two-foot section of the bag door seal being blown out.

synopsis: While being vectored for an ILS in VMC conditions the crew of a Boeing 737 was given a heading of 120 degrees and the pilot flying, utilizing the autopilot and autothrottle functions, mistook the IAS selector for the heading select dial and set 120 knots. When the airspeed had decayed to about 135 knots, well below the 10 degree selected flap minimum maneuver speed, the PF noticed the deteriorated energy state and immediately restored power and airspeed back to 170 knots.
summary: Two pilots vectored for a localizer approach accidentally selected 120 knots instead of a 120-degree heading due to a control input error and lack of cross-verification. The aircraft slowed below minimum maneuver speed, but the Pilot Flying recovered airspeed to 170 knots, allowing an uneventful landing.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports being issued a reroute from LGA via LGA4 heading 359 for vectors to JFW, WAVEY ... except WAVEY is spelled WAVIE and the error is not detected and a track deviation results.
summary: The flight crew misidentified the waypoint WAVIE as WAVEY during an LGA departure re-route, causing an FMC navigation error and ATC "off course" alerts. The crew corrected the spelling after ATC provided the phonetic clarification, resolving the deviation without further incident.

synopsis: MD-80 Captain experiences an electrical malfunction approaching V1 and the takeoff is continued. Once airborne control is transferred to the First Officer whose PFD is functional. The Captain has lost his PFD, ND, FMS, DFGC along with autopilot and autothrust. DFGC is switched to position 2, eventually allowing autopilot and autothrust to be engaged and the emergency power is turned on restoring comm 1 and the Captain's PFD. An emergency is declared and the flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: The pilot experienced multiple avionary failures, including blank displays and inoperative radios, during takeoff and climb due to tripped VHF Nav 1 and FMS-1 NPU circuit breakers on the DC emergency bus. The crew returned for an uneventful overweight landing after switching to DFGC 2 and using emergency power to restore partial communications.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reports receiving an amended PDC stating SUMMA7 BKE KU90I- which would have required a course reversal to accomplish but was not detected until the aircraft made the turn at BKE.
summary: The flight crew inserted an amended PDC clearance into the FMS but failed to verify the flight plan, discovering waypoint KU90I was behind them after passing BKE. They deviated to the next waypoint, KU27M, to avoid a 50 NM detour, and ATC accepted this routing without further clarification.

synopsis: B737 flight crew experiences a flap overspeed and blow up from 30 to 25 during approach. Flaps 25 are selected then 30 (successfully), then 40 but not until 500 feet on the approach. A normal landing ensues behind a departing B747.
summary: During a visual approach to SFO Runway 28L, the crew experienced flap blowback from 30 to 25 due to overspeed while slowing for a departing B747. Despite reaching 40 degrees by 500 feet, they elected to land rather than go around behind the lifting 747, later logging a possible flap overspeed.

synopsis: A319 Captain reports entering Alpha Floor during localizer capture for Runway 5R at MMMX, with the autopilot initiating an aggressive bank. Both autothrust and autopilot are turned off and the approach is completed manually.
summary: During an ILS approach to Runway 5R at Mexico City, the autopilot aggressively banked while autothrottle lag, triggering Alpha Floor. The Captain disconnected automation, exited Alpha Floor, and manually completed a visual approach for an uneventful landing.

synopsis: B757 Captain reports going around after a last minute change to the approach clearance, but does not retract the spoilers until level off when noticed by the IRO.
summary: The flight crew executed a go-around during an ILS 22L circle-to-29 approach due to restricted visibility and lack of preparation. During the hand-flown missed approach, the captain failed to stow speedbrakes, causing poor acceleration until the First Officer identified and corrected the error.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain describes an incident with gate agents boarding passengers after the agents had been told not to board until instructed to do so. The Chief Pilot becomes involved and eventually the passengers are removed so that multiple NEF logbook write ups for the cabin can be checked. The reporter states that the agents' actions amount to interference with a flight crew in the performance of their duties.
summary: The Captain reported that gate agents boarded a CRJ-200 despite an open maintenance card, preventing proper review of 56 non-essential function items and causing paperwork errors. The flight continued after in-flight nose wheel steering and display cool cautions, but the aircraft was removed from service post-landing due to the interference and maintenance issues.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew reported wake turbulence encounter departing ATL in trail of an MD-88.
summary: The crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding MD-88 at rotation, 600 FT, and 1,500 FT, causing hard left rolls and a momentary stick-shaker. The First Officer countered the rolls, and ATC issued a heading of 070 to rejoin the departure, resulting in an uneventful remainder of the flight.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew reports rejecting a takeoff after 80 knots for a RUD SYS 1 INOP EICAS message.
summary: The flight crew aborted takeoff between 80 and 110 knots after a RUDDER SYS 1 INOP message appeared on the EICAS. The aircraft safely exited the runway, and the crew returned to the gate for an aircraft swap with no injuries or emergency declaration.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew reports being dispatched with a R Pack deferral and MLG Bay OVHT deferral, with the OVHT deferral requiring the MLG to be left down for 10 minutes after takeoff. After ten minutes, when the gear is selected up passing FL210, the left pack shuts down. An emergency descent is initiated and the flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: The crew departed with MLG bay overheat and right pack MELs, leaving the left gear down until FL210. Upon retracting the gear, the left pack shut off causing rapid pressurization rise, forcing an emergency descent and return landing.

synopsis: CRJ-700 Captain is informed by a Flight Attendant that a passenger has gotten his finger stuck in a small opening underneath the armrest. The flight diverts and is met by Maintenance and EMS and the finger is successfully extracted from the armrest.
summary: A passenger lodged his finger in an armrest opening, prompting an initial non-emergency response that escalated to a diversion when distress occurred. Maintenance removed the armrest to free the finger, allowing the flight to continue to the destination after the passenger signed a waiver.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew notes that their aircraft has been over fueled. After passenger boarding it is noticed that the fueling door is open and the aircraft is being defueled without coordinating with the flight crew. An altercation develops between the Captain and the Fueling Supervisor and the police are summoned.
summary: During boarding, an unauthorized fuel truck defueled the aircraft, causing fuel imbalance and low pressure warnings. A fueling supervisor entered the flight deck, ignored crew commands to stop, and required police intervention to leave, creating a high-risk safety situation.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reports discovering during preflight that the 'SPD BRK AUTO STOW' circuit breaker on the P6 panel is pulled and collared. Maintenance is called and it is determined that an MEL that was cleared by Maintenance over a month ago was not properly accomplished.
summary: The pilot discovered a collared 'SPD BRK AUTO STOW' circuit breaker during preflight, revealing the load alleviation system had been disabled for over a month after a previous MEL clearance. Maintenance reconnected the SAC and reset the breaker, noting no cockpit indications existed while the system was inoperative.

synopsis: B757 First Officer rolling out on Runway 27 at MEM reports another aircraft fly by in front of her, approaching Runway 18L.
summary: The Pilot Flying reported that Tower issued a confusing "stop on runway" then "disregard" instruction during landing on Memphis Runway 27 while another aircraft executed a go-around on Runway 18L. The pilot attributed the incident to Tower sequencing errors and frequency differences that caused confusion, though no collision occurred.

synopsis: Two Aircraft Maintenance Technicians (AMTs) were informed the end caps they had installed and removed during accomplishment of a Work Card for an Air Conditioning (A/C) Pack High Temperature run (burn) on an MD-82 aircraft were not installed in the correct location for the pack run.
summary: Two mechanics performed a Pack Run on an MD-82, during which the reporter installed temporary caps on sense line 'T' fittings before the test. The reporter recommends adding red-streamer caps to the work kit to improve visibility and prevent confusion during future maintenance.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) and two pilots report about the confusion surrounding an MEL deferral of an Emergency Lights 'Unarmed' light not illuminating during a preflight lights test procedure on a B757 aircraft, with the Emergency Lights switch in the 'Armed' position.
summary: Flight crew and maintenance personnel investigated a 757 emergency light indicator that failed to illuminate during the overhead test. Although maintenance initially signed off the condition as normal, the aircraft was later found to have a faulty assembly, suggesting it was unknowingly dispatched in an illegal state.

synopsis: M20 pilot reports a throttle failure during a practice VOR approach with an instructor on board. The power is fixed at 15 inches MAP. The engine is shut down on final but the resulting approach is high and fast resulting in a bounced landing and a prop strike. The engine had been recently overhauled.
summary: A student pilot and instructor experienced a throttle cable disconnection during a VOR approach practice, causing loss of engine response. The resulting forced landing involved a bounce and minor prop strike, as a go-around was impossible without throttle control.

synopsis: BE35 pilot on approach to D39 via RNAV Runway 13 approach, is informed by ATC that he is two miles off course between MIBOE and CAMEY. Garmin 530w showed airplane was tracking properly as did 2 onboard portable GPS units. Vectors are issued and the next attempt is successful with the GPS units in agreement with ATC Radar.
summary: The pilot flying an RNAV 13 approach at D38 was told by ATC to be two miles off course, contradicting three onboard GPS units. ATC canceled the clearance and issued vectors, but the pilot later confirmed via flight history that the aircraft was actually on course, highlighting a radar-GPS discrepancy.

synopsis: LR55 flight crew reports becoming stuck when the right main gear leaves the paved surface during a 135 degree turn from a high speed exit to the parallel taxiway. Darkness and fog contributed to the incident. A tug is required to extract the aircraft.
summary: The flight crew exited the aircraft onto Taxiway A3 and turned right onto Taxiway A, where the right main gear departed the pavement into soft mud due to poor visibility, a sharp turn, and distraction from the after-landing checklist. The aircraft was extracted by a tug with no damage to the airframe, though one taxiway light was knocked over.

synopsis: CL601 flight crew reports a NMAC with a Paraglider while on left base for Runway 10L at FLL. The Tower reported the traffic and so did TCAS before it was sighted. Evasive action is taken causing an unstabilized approach and landing.
summary: The CL601 crew encountered a high-altitude paraglider while being vectored for a visual approach to Runway 10L at FLL, forcing a deviation through the final approach course. Although radio contact was weak and the crew believed they lacked landing clearance, the Tower confirmed the clearance was issued, resulting in a safe landing.

synopsis: PA24 pilot reports inadvertent disengagement of the autopilot altitude hold function. The aircraft drifts 500 above assigned altitude before ATC queries the reporter and the deviation is corrected.
summary: The pilot inadvertently bumped the unguarded Alt Hld button on the S-Tec 50 autopilot while reading a chart, causing an uncommanded 500-foot climb to 10,500 feet in IMC. The deviation occurred because the small, sensitive buttons lacked audible warnings and the visual annunciator was obscured by the control horn and GPS.

synopsis: M20 experiences an attitude indicator failure during approach through broken clouds but does not inform ATC, resulting in deviations that ATC finds unacceptable.
summary: A pilot flying a Mooney M20J on an IFR approach to VRB experienced a failing attitude indicator that caused autopilot oscillation and an unintentional descent below 4,000 feet. The pilot regained control using secondary instruments but was later cited for a possible pilot deviation due to not notifying ATC of the instrument failure immediately.

synopsis: N90 Controller described a VFR/IFR conflict claiming the current design of the Class B contributed to the event.
summary: An SR22 pilot climbing from FRG entered the path of an unseen A380, forcing JFK final controllers to descend all arrivals below the Class B. The reporter attributes the conflict to airspace not designed for VFR operations and requests lowering the Class B floor or increasing the Belmont area ceiling to 4,000 feet.

synopsis: ZJX Controller described an airspace infraction when an adjacent sector manipulated the data block without any verbal coordination.
summary: An air traffic controller observed an Air Carrier X aircraft climbing from 11,000 feet to FL230 into their sector without a point-out from the adjacent Charleston/Florence sectors. The controller reported that the handoff was incomplete, recommending that controllers finish point-outs by advising the receiving sector of climbing aircraft to ensure safety.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports rolling back after parking at the gate with chocks in. The brakes are applied and the ground crew tugs the aircraft back to the spot. The company briefing page indicates that at this gate and another the company uses at this airport require the parking brakes to remain set at all times.
summary: The flight crew released the parking brake at Gate XXX while performing the checklist, causing the aircraft to roll backward and displace a chock. The incident resulted from the crew overlooking a briefing page notice requiring brakes to remain set at specific gates.

synopsis: B737 Captain laments the low fuel reserves routinely mandated by his company.
summary: A flight crew operating a Northeast Corridor route reported that the new Low Fuel policy resulted in arriving with low fuel lights and 3.9 tons remaining. The pilot attributed this unsafe outcome to the policy's requirement for minimal fuel loads, which forces crews to declare emergencies or return to the gate for minor delays.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports a track deviation departing FLL due to missing a revised segment in their PDC.
summary: The pilot of a Beechcraft departing FLL failed to enter a PDC route change from RAJAY to ZQA into the FMC due to misinterpreting the clearance and rushing. ATC intercepted the aircraft en route to RAJAY, clarified the correct ZQA clearance, and noted that multiple aircraft had missed this specific PDC update.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reports receiving an ACARS message that an aircraft on the current ATC frequency has a stuck mic. A radio check by the Captain using his PTT switch clears the problem.
summary: The flight crew experienced a suspected stuck microphone while transiting Cleveland Center airspace, causing ATC to lose contact until the Captain deselected the Push-To-Talk switch. The incident was attributed to a poorly engineered yoke switch that activated both ICS and VHF simultaneously without visual indication.

synopsis: A distracted B737 crew landed with Flaps 15 in gusty winds as the GPWS TOO LOW TERRAIN warning alerted at 400 FT after a task saturated the First Officer failed to hear the Captain's Flaps 30 request.
summary: The flight crew landed a gusty wind approach to Runway 35R with flaps at 15 degrees instead of the briefed 30, triggering a GPWS "too low terrain" alert. The error resulted from distraction by ATC traffic calls and wind updates, causing the crew to miss the flap extension callout before landing safely.

synopsis: B767-300 flight crew reports a 'mushy' feeling elevator during a flight control check prior to departure, but with full elevator movement available the crew elects to depart. Once airborne the same mushy feeling prompts the crew to return. Maintenance discovers a broken inner spring in the elevator feel system to be the cause.
summary: The flight crew experienced a mushy pitch control anomaly caused by a failed inner spring in the elevator feel system, which was detected during pre-flight checks but not indicated by EICAS. Despite the abnormal feel, they declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport, and landed safely with no further issues.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reports an unstabilized approach due to a flap anomaly. With the flaps selected to 3 and verified, the flying Captain calls for Flaps Full and the First Officer notes the flap indication to be 1+F. Flaps 1 through Full are reselected by the First Officer with the flaps responding normally. During this time autothrust responds with a large thrust increase and the Captain responds by disconnecting, with thrust levers to idle, then inadvertently selects reverse thrust. This is quickly corrected and the reversers do not deploy.
summary: During a visual approach, the First Officer reported flaps retracting to 1+F, causing autothrust to increase power, while the Captain inadvertently selected reverse thrust while disengaging autothrust. Maintenance found no defects after the flight, though ECAM messages appeared upon landing.

synopsis: EMB145 flight crew experiences an altimeter failure during descent causing the autopilot to disengage. Heading mode is selected while the QRH is consulted and NAV is not selected until after a track deviation occurs.
summary: The crew experienced an altimeter failure and autopilot mode reversion during descent from 8,000 to 6,000 feet, causing an inadvertent course deviation. They corrected the heading after realizing they forgot to re-engage navigation mode following the QRH procedure, and ATC recleared them to rejoin the arrival.

synopsis: BE400 flight crew reports being unable to rapidly identify Runway 4 after landing Runway 10 at BWI and the Tower issues go around instructions to the following B737. The flying Captain had slowed on final to maintain 5 miles in trail, reducing separation with the following B737.
summary: Pilots landing a jet on Runway 10 at BWI at night were instructed to exit onto Runway 4 while maintaining speed, but missed the unmarked intersection due to a lack of lead-off lights. The controller subsequently ordered the following aircraft to go around, and the crew attributed the incident to insufficient spacing and poor runway markings.

synopsis: MD-83 Dispatcher describes a charter flight with a passenger load that exceeds the MZFW. Assumptions are made that allow the flight to depart. Post flight research reveals that the weight and balance was not properly calculated.
summary: A dispatcher and captain incorrectly adjusted weight and balance for a departing charter flight by removing 16 lbs per passenger to compensate for 104 unaccounted checked bags. This error, combined with underestimated passenger weights, caused the aircraft to depart approximately 3,000 lbs heavier than calculated.

synopsis: An MD-83 was dispatched under MEL 24-04A because of an AC CROSS TIE fault with the APU continuously operating but while taxiing in after landing when the right engine was shutdown the Right AC BUS lost power.
summary: The flight crew shut down the right engine on taxi with the APU running per MEL 24-04A, causing the right AC bus and First Officer gauges to fail. The pilot questioned whether a previous inoperative AC crosstie placard was appropriate given the APU's consistent failure to power the right bus, raising concerns about potential single-generator operations if an engine had failed in flight.

synopsis: A flight attendant crew did not hear any pre-takeoff or pre-landing cockpit announcements but apparently the PA was operable because a flight crew PA announcement allowed cell phone usage on the ground.
summary: Cabin crew reported that pilots failed to provide prepare for takeoff and landing announcements due to ATC distractions and poor communication. This resulted in a flight attendant being unable to reach their jumpseat before takeoff and requiring a Federal Air Marshal to assist them.

synopsis: After realizing that a #1 Engine mount change was only partially completed on a DHC-8-100 aircraft that had already departed, an Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) recommends that all Maintenance personnel should ensure that any sign-offs for removal and replacement of assembled components are actually complied with.
summary: During Routine Overnight Maintenance, mechanics failed to replace all engine mount components as required, leaving new parts in the box while signing off on old ones. This improper maintenance was discovered after the aircraft dispatched when a supervisor reviewed the turn-in parts.

synopsis: Two Aircraft Maintenance Technicians (AMTs) were informed that a wash nozzle had not been removed from the inlet of #2 Engine on an MD-82 aircraft, after completing an Engine Wash Card.
summary: Two mechanics performed an engine wash on an MD-82 but failed to remove the wash ring from the #2 engine inlet due to distraction, lack of communication, and assuming the other had completed the task. The error was discovered seven days later, prompting recommendations for improved checklists and visual verification procedures.

synopsis: M20 pilot reports confusing Runway 17L for Taxiway F at DWH airport after being cleared to cross Runway 17L, causing an aircraft to go-around. When cleared for takeoff the baggage door opened requiring a rejected takeoff and stopping to latch the door.
summary: The pilot inadvertently entered a runway after a wrong turn due to missing signage, then aborted takeoff when a baggage door opened. The controller reported the incident because an approaching aircraft was sent around, though the pilot questioned the necessity of the go-around.

synopsis: B757-200 Captain reported wake turbulence in cruise at FL360 from an A380 at FL370. Captain stated he would have liked a point out from ATC.
summary: The flight crew encountered moderate wake turbulence from an A380 at FL360 while flying into the sun, causing a brief, severe jolt with no injuries. The pilot attributed the incident to ATC failing to provide traffic advisories or increased separation for the super-category aircraft.

synopsis: A Private Pilot reports the engine on his Diamond DA-20C1 Eclipse aircraft quit suddenly at 12,000 FT MSL after previously experiencing a momentary engine vibration. Emergency declared. Aircraft would not restart until on the ground. FBO Maintenance could not determine cause.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine shutdown at 12,000 feet following a vibration shortly after maintenance released the aircraft for a propeller issue. An emergency landing was executed at ZZZ after restart attempts failed in flight, though the engine started on the ground; maintenance found no cause despite replacing the propeller and servicing spark plugs.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Corporate aircraft descending on the VALRE Arrival to HPN took evasive action to a TCAS RA during a near miss at about 7,500 FT.
summary: During a VFR arrival descent through 8,000 feet, the crew received conflicting ATC instructions followed by a TCAS double RA requiring a climb to avoid a C-172. The aircraft cleared the traffic by only 200 feet after the First Officer manually followed the RA commands, prompting the pilot to report the encounter was too close for comfort.

synopsis: C172 pilot experiences a NMAC while on approach to Runway 34 at GKY with another aircraft of unknown type, but very fast.
summary: During an ILS approach to Runway 34 at GKY at 2,400 feet MSL, a pilot reported a dark, bullet-shaped object with a trailing light passing rapidly close to the left wing. The pilot could not determine the object's specific dimensions or identity.

synopsis: B717 crew experiences a dual MCDU lockout shortly after takeoff which cannot be corrected. The flight diverts to a suitable airport for maintenance, then continues to destination.
summary: The crew experienced a dual MCDU lockout shortly after takeoff, causing total navigation loss and autopilot failure. They declared an emergency and diverted to VFR weather, landing safely before maintenance fixed the issue for the flight to continue.

synopsis: Several flights after performing a Number 6 bearing Oil Supply Tube Flow Check on a GE CF6-80C2, Number Two engine, an Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) was informed the MEL deferral he created for the borderline high pressure oil reading was out of compliance.
summary: A mechanic deferred a Number 2 engine oil supply tube flow check after recording 31 psi, which was within the deferral range per the task card. Later, a maintenance reviewer deemed the aircraft out of compliance based on the logged 31 psi reading while the aircraft was out of the country.

synopsis: A Contract Maintenance Technician describes his efforts to have a Main Landing Gear (MLG) tire replaced on a EMB-145 aircraft and not just signed-off as 'within limits' by one of the Air Carrier's mechanics. The MLG tire had sustained a deep puncture by metal debris that had cut through multiple plies.
summary: A contract mechanic found an out-of-limits Main Landing Gear tire puncture on an EMB-145, but Maintenance Control instructed him not to log it and directed Air Carrier mechanics to sign it off without measuring. The mechanic documented the discrepancy and warned the crew, yet the aircraft was reportedly released for revenue flight despite the damage exceeding allowable limits.

synopsis: Light twin pilot cleared to land Runway 28 reports another aircraft taking off Runway 10 and turning away. The Tower issues a go-around but uses an incorrect call sign and the reporter lands on Runway 28.
summary: A pilot landing on Runway 28 at APA observed a conflicting departure on Runway 10 and ignored a Tower go-around instruction issued with an incorrect call sign. The pilot continued the landing, attributing the conflict to simultaneous opposite-direction operations and emphasizing the need for correct call signs and runway separation.

synopsis: A B737-700 at FL400 encountered a 35 KT headwind increase which resulted in an airspeed decaying to 210 KTS so the First Officer applied emergency power during a descent, finally getting ATC clearance to FL380.
summary: Pilots encountered an unforecast windshear at FL400, causing a 35-knot headwind loss and airspeed decay to 210 IAS. They executed high-altitude stall recovery procedures, descended to FL380, and stabilized the flight without exceeding aircraft limitations.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports a rushed pushback and engine start where the ground crew departs without removing the nose wheel steering bypass pin. The flight waiting for the gate notes the flag attached to the pin and informs the reporter. The ground crew is recalled and the pin is removed before taxiing is attempted.
summary: The Captain and First Officer pushed back a Company aircraft under time pressure while fatigued, failing to verify the nose gear bypass pin removal. The ground crew left the pin installed, requiring a return to the gate for removal before the flight continued uneventfully.

synopsis: A B737 flight crew, maintaining an assigned airspeed of 160 knots with 15 degrees of flap on a long final failed to select landing flaps at 1,000 AGL per stabilized approach criteria requirements. High surface winds had increased their planned Vref to that same 160 knots which delayed their observation. Landing flaps were, however, in place for landing.
summary: The pilot reported that high workload, tight spacing, and ATC speed restrictions distracted them from extending flaps to 30 degrees by 1,000 feet AGL. Although the approach remained stable with flaps at 15, the pilot attributed the missed configuration call to these distractions and the airspeed matching the landing target.

synopsis: The flight crew left the aircraft to perform post flight duties during a very short ground turn around time and after returning to the flight station found the aircraft in a shutdown condition.
summary: Pilots discovered an APU gate team had reconfigured cockpit switches, including turning off IRUs, battery, and standby power, and disarming exit lights while passengers boarded. This unauthorized access during a short turn created a safety of flight issue by undoing the crew's completed setup.

synopsis: Three B747 pilots describe an approach with the final flaps not selected until 500 FT when prompted by the GPWS. The flying First Officer was new to the aircraft having completed IOE two months prior without a landing since.
summary: During a visual approach, the First Officer reported a GPWS "too low flaps" warning at 500 feet because landing flaps were not selected. The Captain extended flaps from 20 to 25 degrees instead of executing a go-around, resulting in an uneventful landing despite bumpy conditions.

synopsis: A fatigued flight crew, complacent by virtue of returning to their home domicile failed to note the PF's ILS was set to the inbound course reciprocal failed to intercept the localizer and experienced a modest traffic conflict with traffic for a parallel runway.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway 18, the First Officer selected an incorrect inbound course of 003 instead of 183, causing the aircraft to penetrate parallel runway airspace. The crew attributed the error to fatigue and complacency, resulting in a near-miss with traffic that required ATC intervention but no formal write-up.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reports being cleared initially for the SEAVU2 to Runway 24R at LAX then being changed late to Runway 25L via a broken transmission requiring clarification. After landing a telephone call to ATC reveals that Runway 25L had always been the runway assignment and the crew did not hear correctly.
summary: Pilots on a descent into LAX on the SEAVU2 arrival experienced a high and fast approach after a garbled transmission and a misunderstood runway clearance. The crew later learned from the supervisor that the initial controller had cleared them for Runway 25L, not 24R, but delayed instructions caused them to cross the localizer before stabilizing for a safe landing.

synopsis: An EMB-145 flight crew conducted an uneventful zero flap approach and landing at their remote destination when the flaps failed to extend.
summary: The pilot flying reported a FLAP FAIL caution during descent below 10,000 AGL with low fuel, prompting an emergency declaration and a no-flap landing. The crew successfully executed the approach and stopped within 3,500 feet using full brakes and reverse thrust, with the aircraft never entering an undesired state.

synopsis: An EMB-145 EICAS alerted AUTOPILOT, YAW DAMPER, RUDDER SYS 1 and 2 during climb out so the QRH was completed leaving only RUDDER SYS 2 alerting so an emergency was declared and the flight continued to its filed destination.
summary: The flight crew experienced multiple EICAS failures, including Rudder Sys 1-2, during climb out and manually flew the aircraft. They declared an emergency, coordinated with ATC for a wind-favored runway, and completed an uneventful landing at their filed destination.

synopsis: CE680 Captain reports a communication mixup departing SDM late at night after a long duty day. Several radio communications to ATC are attempted and apparently completed using the CTAF while listening on the ATC frequency. The crew believes the assigned altitude is 11,000 FT and ATC stating 10,000 FT, resulting in an altitude deviation.
summary: A fatigued pilot and SIC on a corporate flight departing San Diego Brown Municipal Airport mistakenly communicated with ATC on the CTAF frequency while climbing. The crew initially read back a clearance to 11,000 feet but leveled off at 10,000 feet after ATC correction, attributing the communication and altitude discrepancies to fatigue after 12.5 hours of duty.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reports taxiing to Runway 11 at Taxiway A1 and learning later that Taxiway A1 was closed by NOTAM. It is also noted that Taxiways A1 and A2 appear to be separated by turf or dirt which does not actually exist.
summary: The pilot taxied to Runway 11 in fog and held on Taxiway A1, which was NOTAMed closed but lacked visual closure indicators. The crew realized the airport diagram incorrectly depicted a grassy island, though they believe they occupied the pavement ATC intended.

synopsis: An MD-80 arriving at its destination with minimum fuel was directed to go-around due to an airport emergency. They declared a fuel emergency and received appropriate special handling, arriving at the gate with fuel remaining of 2,700 LBS.
summary: The flight crew declared a low fuel emergency during a go-around on final approach due to an airport emergency. They landed with 3,400 LBS and arrived at the gate with 2,700 LBS after a delay caused by the airport emergency.

synopsis: M20 pilot reports a conflict with an LSA pilot landing on an intersecting runway. The LSA pilot does not use his radio due to incompatibility with his hearing aids. Previous conflicts are alleged.
summary: The reporting pilot nearly collided with another pilot landing simultaneously on intersecting Runways 9 and 23. The other pilot failed to monitor CTAF due to hearing aid interference and a history of unsafe operations, crossing the intersection 1,000 feet ahead of the reporter.

synopsis: BE20 pilot reports electrical failure shortly after takeoff with loss of G1000 and communications. The electrical failure is not initially detected but when discovered it is determined that the generators were never turned on after engine starting with a ground power cart.
summary: During climb-out, the pilot experienced total electrical failure and display loss after failing to activate generators post-startup, causing battery depletion. The pilot manually extended gear, navigated with a wet compass, and landed safely after resetting generators, attributing the error to distraction, checklist non-compliance, and a faulty avionics backup battery.

synopsis: C402 pilot experiences a right main gear collapse during taxi in after landing.
summary: The pilot landed and taxied at 5–7 mph on Taxiway D when the right gear collapsed. The pilot immediately shut down both engines, confirmed no fuel or oil leaks, and contacted the local FBO for assistance.

synopsis: C172 pilot preparing to land reports a NMAC with a departing Cessna that had been instructed to cancel takeoff clearance. When the departing Cessna does not respond, the reporters landing clearance is canceled.
summary: During a training flight to IXD, the pilot on short final for Runway 18 was forced to go around after a Cessna departed despite a canceled clearance. The pilot aggressively slowed to avoid a mid-air collision when the aircraft were 300 feet apart in trail.

synopsis: TRACON described a developing conflict, the reporter providing a detailed self analysis of 'what actions should have been accomplished'.
summary: An air traffic controller lost separation between a climbing SF34 and a descending DH8A due to frequency congestion and a missed readback of the altitude clearance. The DH8A pilot maintained visual separation to prevent a conflict, while the controller admitted fault for poor departure sequencing and communication.

synopsis: B757 flight crew experiences high EGT and engine surging climbing out of 4,000 FT. Checklist procedures are complied with, an emergency is declared and the flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: During climb out at 4,000 feet, the crew experienced a left engine surge, high EGT, and vibration, prompting an emergency declaration and return. The aircraft landed smoothly at 206,000 lbs with the engine running, after which the crew shut down the left engine at the gate.

synopsis: MD11 flight crew reports the sound of circuit breakers tripping as the aircraft rotates and loss of the First Officer's airspeed and altitude indication. An emergency is declared and flight returns to departure airport with no further issues. Seven circuit breakers are found tripped on post flight.
summary: The flight crew experienced seven circuit breakers popping immediately after rotation, causing First Officer PFD airspeed and altimeter failures. They declared an emergency, returned to the airport, and landed safely; post-flight inspection confirmed the popped breakers affected systems including engine ignition, air data, and hydraulics.

synopsis: MEM air carrier arrival expressed concern regarding the RECAT Wake Turbulence Separation being utilized.
summary: The flight crew arrived at MEM and queried ATC regarding RECAT wake turbulence standards after being sequenced 3.5 NM behind a Heavy MD-11. The crew reported that reduced spacing compromises safety and criticized ATC's potential refusal to grant additional spacing requests based on these new standards.

synopsis: CL300 flight crew reports not making their crossing restriction on the ADDEL 1 into HND due to an improper FMC entry.
summary: The flight crew flying the ADDEL ONE RNAV arrival into HND crossed FUZZY Intersection at approximately 17,000 feet instead of the cleared 16,000 feet due to misinterpreting the FMS display. The crew expedited descent to comply with the clearance, noting no conflict with other aircraft and attributing the error to insufficient cross-checking of the FMS against the ATC clearance.

synopsis: The Captain of an ERJ-170, following his second TCAS RA in busy terminal areas incident within a week, took vocal exception to ATC permitting 500 foot vertical separation between IFR and VFR traffic in VMC conditions.
summary: The crew received a TCAS RA to descend below 10,000 feet while flying near ORD due to a Citation at 10,500 feet. The pilot attributed the conflict to ATC allowing high-speed closure rates with less than 1,000 feet of vertical separation.

synopsis: DA2000 flight crew and a Maintenance Control Technician describe a MEL misunderstanding that results in the aircraft being dispatched inappropriately. An auto slats light had illuminated during engine start, indicating that the Auto Slat System was inoperative but the MEL was for the auto slats light being inoperative. The light extinguished during taxi out.
summary: A crew and maintenance controller misinterpreted MEL 27-17, releasing a DA2000 with an illuminated Auto Slats light for flight when the relief applied only to a light failure. The aircraft departed with passengers, but the Assistant Chief Pilot later confirmed the flight was safe as speed restrictions were observed.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain experiences a RAAS alert after being cleared to line up and wait, which completely blocks the next transmission from the Tower.
summary: The flight crew, while lining up for takeoff, missed a Tower clearance due to the Runway Awareness and Advisory System (RAAS) masking the transmission. The crew requested a repeat to discover the missed takeoff clearance, attributing the communication loss to the RAAS during this critical phase.

synopsis: After experiencing a Gen 2 OFF EICAS message, CRJ-900 Captain inadvertently secured the Number 1 Generator without using a checklist or enlisting the aid of the First Officer who was conversing with the cabin. ADG deployed and aircraft landed without further incident.
summary: During descent below 11,000 feet, the Pilot Flying inadvertently reset the wrong generator switch while the First Officer spoke to a flight attendant, causing a total electrical loss and automatic Air Driven Generator deployment. The crew managed the situation without declaring an emergency and completed a normal landing, attributing the error to overconfidence and failure to follow established two-person procedures.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew departing before Tower opening departs on a taxiway, being unaware that the pilot controlled lighting system only activates the runway lights for the runway in use when the Tower closed.
summary: The flight crew took off from Runway 19 believing runway lights were active, but they were actually blue taxiway lights because the crew missed a NOTAM stating only the tower's active runway had pilot-controlled lighting. The crew continued the takeoff due to adequate visibility, and the flight was completed safely.

synopsis: B737 Check Captain reports being assigned holding then having to declare minimum fuel during vectors for approach. On final below 1,000 FT, winds are noted at 15 KTS gusting to 20 on the tail. With ATIS winds of calm and a storm in the departure path the approach is continued to landing.
summary: The crew held at RADDY due to thunderstorms, declared minimum fuel, and landed on Runway 16R despite discovering an unexpected 15-knot tailwind on final. Although they touched down safely with planned stopping distance, the pilot noted that an earlier diversion to the alternate would have avoided the uncomfortable fuel and weather situation.

synopsis: Without notice, a Cargo Maintenance crew removed the chocks before an external airstart. The aircraft then began rolling with the first engine start because the brakes were also not set.
summary: During an external air start with a deferred APU, the aircraft began rolling after the Number 1 engine start because chocks were removed without cockpit knowledge. The pilot attributes this incident to miscommunication between ground maintenance and the flight crew regarding the tug connection and chock status.

synopsis: A DC9-30, departing a busy uncontrolled airport during a 'fly in' event, inadvertently exited the paved taxiway while attempting a turn to back taxi down a runway for takeoff and got bogged down in the rain softened grass. The aircraft had to be unloaded before it could be returned to the hard surface.
summary: The Captain and First Officer taxied a fully loaded freight aircraft off the taxiway into soft, wet grass at an uncontrolled field during a fly-in event. The incident occurred when the Captain executed a sharp turn while distracted by traffic monitoring, causing the left main gear to sink and entrench the aircraft on an active runway.

synopsis: A Maintenance Controller describes the confusion that led to an MEL deferral of a #2 Slat Overhead and Transit light intermittent in flight report, when in fact #3 Krueger flap was the discrepancy. The B737-300 aircraft was later removed from service for repairs.
summary: A pilot reported an intermittent slat light, but maintenance found no fault and issued an MEL for the wrong component due to a read-back error. The pilot subsequently grounded the aircraft for repair after discovering the log entry incorrectly listed a Krueger flap instead of a slat.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) describes how confusion and unnecessary shifting of job assignments contributed to discrepancy and corrective action information not being entered in a Q-400 logbook for damage found on a wheel half, during a wheel hub build-up.
summary: A mechanic working on a Q-400 hub scratch repair failed to log the corrective action due to excessive stress and frequent interruptions while being pulled between multiple projects. The reporter attributes this documentation error to management practices that prevented task completion, increasing the risk of future incidents.

synopsis: A Maintenance Manager describes his efforts to discourage a Captain from pulling the wheel chocks from an Embraer EMB-505 aircraft during pre-departure operations. Pilot disregards request, ignoring the safety concerns of Maintenance personnel and company Station safety policy.
summary: Before departure, a Captain ignored a Lineman's safety warning and pulled wheel chocks while the Ground Power Unit cord was still connected. This violated local policy designed to prevent aircraft rolling and GPU damage caused by inadvertent brake release during pre-flight checks.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports an A300 aircraft returned to gate after aborting a takeoff roll due to an engine thrust reverser pressurized fault indication on their ECAM for #1 Engine. Technician noted he had failed to remove an electrical connector from the directional pilot valve pressure switch on #1 Engine that was a requirement to defer a High Pressure Bleed Valve (HPBV) fault.
summary: A mechanic at a one-man station failed to remove an electrical connector during thrust reverser deactivation on an A300, causing a pressurized fault on takeoff roll. The aircraft returned to the gate due to the incomplete MEL procedure, which the mechanic attributed to distractions and rushing to avoid delays.

synopsis: A PA31-350 pilot diverted to a nearby airport when his instrument lighting began to fail, followed by intensifying heat and smoke emanating from the Circuit Breaker Panel.
summary: During cruise, the pilot encountered smoke and an intense glow from the co-pilot's circuit breaker panel, which appeared to be melting and flaming. The pilot pulled a breaker, declared an emergency, and landed safely, after which the glow dissipated once systems were powered down.

synopsis: B767 First Officer reports a NMAC at FL350 near ROLUT in Brazilian airspace. The approaching target was detected by the reporter at FL360 and ATC was queried. The reporter is issued a descent to FL350 and the other aircraft is instructed to remain at FL360 but descends. The TCAS RA showed conflicting information initially, with the voice calling for a descent and the display indicating a climb. Several RA reversals occur resulting in the NMAC. The Controller involved accepted responsibility for the initial conflict.
summary: Pilots on an augmented crew flight at FL360 in Brazilian airspace encountered a head-on conflict with another aircraft on the same level. The incident resulted in a near miss with 100 feet vertical separation after the other aircraft descended without clearance, causing conflicting TCAS commands and requiring immediate evasive maneuvers.

synopsis: ZOA Controller voiced concern regarding NAVCAN's reported policy of not providing certain ATC services to companies that fail to pay their ATC bills, noting that the policy causes confusion.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managing oceanic sectors encountered a B747 routing dispute with Vancouver Center due to unpaid NAV CANADA fees. The aircraft entered Vancouver airspace despite a reroute clearance because the pilot's flight computer could not accept the new coordinates, forcing Vancouver to assume control.

synopsis: Local Controller described a potential loss of runway separation event when internal Tower coordination failed and an aircraft was cleared for takeoff without insuring a vehicle was clear of the runway.
summary: A Local Controller cleared a Canadair regional jet for takeoff from Runway 13 while survey vehicles were still on the runway, causing the jet to begin its roll just as the vehicles exited. The controller attributed the incident to a lack of situational awareness and failure to scan the runway or heed the active memory aid light bar.

synopsis: A B737-700 Left Pack Tripped Off during climb but reset. It tripped again at cruise, followed by the Right Pack Trip, so an emergency was declared and the flight diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: During climb out, both air conditioning packs tripped off, prompting the flight crew to don oxygen masks and execute an emergency descent. The aircraft diverted and landed overweight at 134,000 lbs without incident after brake inspections.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain describes a VNAV disconnect descending through FL180 with a high barometric setting that he believes reveals a basic flaw in the B737 auto flight system.
summary: During descent to cross BEARR at 17,000 feet, the crew's VNAV disconnected after resetting altimeters, causing the aircraft to cross the intersection 300 to 500 feet high. The pilot attributed the event to abrupt VNAV path computation transitions and usability issues with the FMC's narrow tracking window.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports misreading a revised PDC, which results in a track deviation noted by ATC.
summary: The flight crew misread a Pre-Departure Clearance (PDC) during departure, inadvertently flying the HBU transition instead of the cleared TEHRU transition due to similar formatting. ATC vectored the aircraft to the correct route, and the crew later reported that the PDC layout frequently causes this specific routing error.

synopsis: The flight crew of an A320 diverted to the nearest suitable airport following receipt of high vibration indications and compressor stalls from the right engine.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a #2 engine compressor stall and subsequent overheat at FL340, prompting an emergency diversion. They executed a single-engine visual landing with fire trucks standing by, shut down the engine on the ground, and found no fire despite momentary fire detection faults.

synopsis: MD11 flight crew reports not selecting final flaps until below 1,000 FT on final.
summary: The flight crew recognized the aircraft was not in the normal landing configuration at flaps 28 during a visual approach below 1,000 feet AGL. They selected flaps 35 and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: An A319 flying the TYSSN RNAV STAR was leveling at 10,000 FT ALT CONSTRAINT * for SUZSI and began slowing to 210 KTS. As the 8,000 FT PRINO constraint was selected, the FMGC transitioned to VERT SPD and began a descent which the crew arrested.
summary: Pilots descending into Las Vegas via the Tyssn arrival experienced an unexpected mode change from ALT CONSTRAINT to VERTICAL SPEED near a 10,000 FT crossing restriction. The aircraft descended to approximately 9,500 FT before the crew manually restored altitude, likely caused by simultaneous approach activation and waypoint crossing.

synopsis: CRJ200 First Officer describes some auto flight anomalies that are common and may be attributed to FMS and or autopilot design.
summary: During the HYPER 4 arrival, the FMS entered sequence inhibit mode at 5,000 feet, causing confusion and a rapid descent to meet the HUSEL restriction. Later, strong tailwinds on base caused the autopilot to deviate half-scale from the localizer during the visual approach to Runway 1R.

synopsis: Fatigue played a part when a B737-700 First Officer failed to back up his autoflight mode selections with raw data based mental calculations with respect to a two phase descent clearance from ATC. A traffic conflict resulted requiring the crew to manually override their expedited descent and climb in order to avoid the crossing traffic.
summary: The pilot reported that during cruise descent, reliance on VNAV without mental math caused a delayed altitude change, resulting in an autopilot failure to descend and a subsequent dip to FL314. The pilot attributed the incident to poor altitude planning and fatigue, which led to a manual climb to recover the assigned FL320.

synopsis: After departure a B737-400 Captain, the flying pilot, lost communications so the First Officer assuming flying but his airspeed malfunctioned so he added power overspeeding N1, but could not communicate the problems to the Captain. Both pilots detected smoke and fumes so the Captain assumed flying, declared an emergency and returned to the departure airport.
summary: The crew encountered pitot static failure, headset communication loss, and cockpit smoke during climb with flammable cargo. They declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport, and landed safely with fire services standing by.

synopsis: B747 flight crew experiences a track deviation while proceeding direct to the next waypoint. The aircraft is turned 90 degrees to the desired track when queried by ATC about their heading. Post flight maintenance reveals an intermittent autopilot fault.
summary: During cruise at FL360, the flight crew experienced an uncommanded right turn while the left autopilot was engaged in LNAV/VNAV mode, caused by an intermittent autopilot mode operation error. The crew manually corrected the deviation, switched to the right autopilot, and continued to the destination after maintenance logged the fault.

synopsis: A B737-800 Master Caution alerted Engine Driven Hydraulic Pump #2 Low Pressure, so the QRH was completed, an emergency declared and after landing at the departure airport, the emergency crew reported a fluid leak from the engine so it was shutdown.
summary: The pilot declared an emergency and returned to the departure airport after the Engine Driven Hydraulic Pump #2 Low Pressure light illuminated passing FL200. Rescue and Fire Fighters reported fluid leaking from Engine #2, leading to its shutdown and a taxi to the gate.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew inadvertently left Number Two engine running at the gate.
summary: The Captain shut down engines 1 and 3 after a three-engine taxi but missed engine 2 due to habit pattern reliance. The First Officer discovered engine 2 still running while calling for a crew bus and subsequently shut it down.

synopsis: The pilot of a CRJ-900 was unsure if the Engineering Authorization document submitted by Maintenance Control personnel was complied with on the cargo door issue observed on the aircraft. He elected to write up the discrepancy again to ensure that the issue had compliance.
summary: The flight crew discovered missing cargo door weather seals on a -900 during preflight, leading to a 45-minute delay while maintenance applied speed tape based on an Engineering Authorization Document. The pilot later realized the missing seals were a CDL item requiring logbook entry, concluding the aircraft was flown without the required CDL due to confusion over documentation.

synopsis: DC9 Captain does not believe his cargo load has been weighed accurately and using some assumptions, increases the weight by 4,000 LBS. No accurate method of weighing the freight could be found and the estimate turns out to be conservative.
summary: A pilot encountered a cargo weight discrepancy at departure due to missing scales and inaccurate shipper data. The pilot conservatively estimated the load at 10,500 lbs, which proved safe as the actual weight was 8,130 lbs, though the shipper had originally underreported it.

synopsis: Company shop personnel are finding it difficult to determine the procedure for ascertaining product shelf life.
summary: A QA audit identified expired shrink tubing because the company's shelf-life program was uncontrolled, prompting a supervisor to mandate adherence to vendor expiration dates. New sign-off sheets were implemented to verify dates, though concerns remain regarding non-packaged material and cut tubing where shelf life cannot be established.

synopsis: A Columbia 400 pilot had a track deviation after takeoff because he misunderstood his clearance then had a carbon monoxide warning for which he took environmental clearing procedures for while using oxygen, but believes the warning was false.
summary: A private pilot misunderstood an IFR departure clearance, flying direct to a VOR instead of the assigned departure route, requiring ATC to issue a corrective left turn. During the climb, a carbon monoxide alarm activated briefly, causing temporary cognitive difficulty, though the pilot attributed the clearance error solely to a failure to request clarification.

synopsis: An L-39 instructor reported both the normal and emergency brakes failed on landing so the aircraft departed the runway end without sustaining damage or causing injury.
summary: During an L-39 training flight, the aircraft overran Runway 27 by 80 feet after both normal and emergency brakes failed to stop the student pilot's landing. The instructor attributed the overrun to a rear seat emergency brake failure and the slow application required due to the lack of anti-skid, resulting in no damage.

synopsis: A Maintenance Technician repositioned switches in the flight deck to conduct a test procedure, and assumed that the pilots would recognize it and change them back to the normal position.
summary: A mechanic reset a circuit breaker to fix a First Officer's FMC annunciator fault but left the autopilot disengage and FMC switches in the test position. The mechanic assumed the pilots would restore the switches, noting that incorrect switch positions not covered by checklists could cause problems.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a conflict event between an IFR and VFR aircraft, the reporter noting multiple chances were available to the controller to prevent this event but none were taken.
summary: Air Traffic Controllers and the pilot of Aircraft X experienced a potential loss of separation during departure due to delayed traffic advisories and a failed left-turn plan. The pilot initiated a TCAS-influenced descent to 2,500 feet to avoid conflicting traffic, resolving the situation without a Resolution Advisory.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a loss of separation event when coordination regarding an opposite direction operation was confused between the RADAR and Data controllers.
summary: Two air traffic controllers in combined sectors XX and XY lost separation between a departing CL30 and an arriving GLF4 at ZZZ1 due to miscommunication regarding a SYD release. The error resulted from the D-Side assuming the GLF4 was slow and failing to clarify the release target, causing a 2.02-mile lateral and 900-foot vertical proximity.

synopsis: ZAU Controller experienced a loss of separation event when handling heavy ORD arrival traffic was complicated due to weather deviations, the reporter claiming the Supervisor and TMU failed in their responsibilities.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported that a Supervisor and TMU failed to reroute ORD arrivals around weather, causing a Conflict Alert between an A320 and Phenom 100 while holding. The controller attributed the unsafe environment and near-miss to management's inaction and contradictory instructions during the arrival phase.

synopsis: PCT Controller experienced a loss of separation during staggered approach procedures the reporter commenting on the need for additional spacing tools for controllers if tenths of mile are going to determine a separation loss.
summary: An air traffic controller managing staggered approaches for a DC-9 and ERJ-145 to Runways 1C and 1R lost separation due to wind shear and ARTS display limitations. The controller issued a break-out clearance when the DC-9 failed to slow sufficiently, resulting in a 1.94-mile separation instead of the required 2 miles.

synopsis: SCT Controller observed a conflict event involving two air carrier aircraft departing LAX, the north complex aircraft routed south and a south complex aircraft routed north.
summary: A witness reported that LAX Tower cleared an A320 south while a CRJ-900 departed north under visual separation without notifying MANR. The MANR controller hesitated to turn the A320 south, avoiding a potential mid-air collision caused by the lack of communication regarding the CRJ-900's position.

synopsis: A B737-300 FMC transitioned from LNAV to HDG SEL after a down track fix was selected and activated but the pilot did not see the error until ATC questioned the aircraft's track.
summary: The pilot reported that while executing a direct route fix in LNAV, the autopilot unexpectedly reverted to HDG mode without warning, causing a deviation from the cleared heading. The pilot manually re-engaged LNAV to correct the flight path and recommended adding a visual warning light to alert crews when the system disengages from selected modes.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Line Check Airman (LCA) with a student and two relief pilots did not want to have either himself or his student relieved during a 15 hour duty day with 10:30 flight time. A Relief Pilot contended a FAR violation occurred so the LCA acquiesced.
summary: A First Officer intervened during a Line Check Airman's IOE trip when the LCA refused to rest a student pilot who had been in the control seat for eight hours. The LCA eventually agreed to fly the final leg in non-instructional mode after the First Officer cited safety concerns and fatigue risks, though the LCA required a formal letter explaining the decision.

synopsis: A321 First Officer reports descending early on the IVANE 2 RNAV arrival to CLT, crossing MSTRD below FL260, after an approach procedure change.
summary: Pilots reported that during the IVANE arrival to ILS 36R, the aircraft descended through the MSTRD altitude between FL240 and FL250 after the procedure was changed to RNAV 36R. The reporter attributes these frequent altitude deviations to a poorly written arrival procedure.

synopsis: EMB-135 Captain reports RIC has LED taxiway lights which are too bright, creating a hazard, and Controllers are reportedly unable to dim.
summary: A pilot reported that non-dimmable LED taxi lights at RIC create a hazard during night operations by preventing dark adaptation. The pilot stated that controllers confirmed the lights cannot be dimmed, describing the excessive brightness as an unnecessary risk that could contribute to an accident chain.

synopsis: EMB-170 First Officer experiences a TCAS descend RA approaching ORD at 10,000 feet and 300 knots, caused by a Citation at 10,500 feet that ATC forgot to mention.
summary: The crew received a TCAS RA to descend below 10,000 feet while between ESSPO and ORD due to a Citation at 10,500 feet that ATC failed to mention. Consequently, the aircraft could not slow to 250 knots below 10,000 feet while resolving the conflict with the target 200 to 400 feet away.

synopsis: B777 flight crew discovers that their EFB terminal chart database has expired and Maintenance cannot provide a current database, requiring the EFB to be MEL'd. The MEL requires the availability of charts from another source, in this case iPads. Once airborne it is discovered that all three iPads need to be updated.
summary: The flight crew departed with deferred aircraft EFBs and used personal iPads for terminal charts, later discovering available updates post-takeoff due to high workload and unclear notification. Dispatch confirmed via ACARS that the charts used were current despite the delayed update alerts.

synopsis: Forced by airport construction to back taxi on Runway 32 to utilize the full remaining length of 14 an air carrier flight crew taxied beyond the temporary displaced threshold prior to reversing course. The Tower reminded them of their technical 'violation' and cleared them for takeoff.
summary: The pilot back-taxied Runway 14 at RAP due to construction and a closed taxiway, turning around on the wrong side of the displaced threshold. Tower corrected the error and cleared the aircraft for takeoff, prompting a request for better barricades and an airport page.

synopsis: A319 Flight Crew reports descending below the LTOWN crossing restriction on the LTOWN 6 RNAV arrival to MEM. The crew had been cleared direct LTOWN but for unknown reasons the managed descent was lost after selection or was never selected.
summary: The Captain and First Officer descended below the LTOWN 6 arrival profile to 7,800 feet while distracted by an EFB software failure and ATC vectoring. The crew attributed the deviation to being high initially, ATC clearing a direct fix, and the distraction preventing proper monitoring of altitude constraints.

synopsis: Pilot reports they could not control the cabin pressurization in the Auto or Manual mode during initial climb in a CRJ-200 aircraft, air turnback was accomplished. Maintenance later discovered the Inboard and Outboard Avionics Cooling Exhaust valve electrical connectors were previously crossed. No EICAS message of valve position faults.
summary: During climb from ZZZ, the crew encountered a cabin altitude warning and lost pressurization control due to maintenance wiring the inboard and overboard cooling valve cables backwards. The flight returned to ZZZ for an unpressurized landing after maintenance corrected the valve connections.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A DHC-8 crew detected a momentary torque increase when the throttle was reduced and a momentary decrease with a throttle increase. Maintenance cleared the discrepancy as could not duplicate but the aircraft returned after takeoff for the same behavior.
summary: Pilots reported erratic torque indications on the #2 power lever during climb, prompting a return to the departure airport after maintenance initially signed the aircraft airworthy despite a mechanic's refusal. The reporter attributed the unsafe release to a communication breakdown between mechanics, where a second mechanic signed off the aircraft without resolving the original concern.

synopsis: A B737-800 autothrottle disconnected on final prior to 1,000 FT but went undetected the until 1,000 FT, about 7 KTS below VRef, and during recovery the aircraft went above glideslope and finally landed long.
summary: The Captain executed a sidestep from Runway 09L to 09R during a VFR LOC approach. At 1,000 feet, autothrottles disengaged causing airspeed decay; the pilot manually recovered speed and landed slightly long, noting a go-around would have been more prudent.

synopsis: After takeoff both B777 yoke controlled nose down trim inputs failed, although the ALT Trim continued to function, so an emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The pilot reported a loss of electric nose-down trim at 800 feet after takeoff, with no EICAS messages or circuit breaker issues. The crew hand-flew the aircraft, dumped fuel, and returned to the departure airport for an uneventful landing where trim functioned normally post-flight.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier on approach to CLE 6L was issued 8,000 FT traffic then in a descent to 8,000 FT took evasive to the traffic's TCAS RA but given no warning from ATC except after the fact with, 'Yeah, I figured that would happen.'
summary: During a descent to 8,000 feet while being vectored to the 6L localizer, the crew received a TCAS Resolution Advisory due to traffic 300 feet below. The pilot attributed the event to the Air Traffic Controller's failure to correct the conflict despite prior warnings, noting the controller's dismissive attitude after the alert occurred.

synopsis: A319 flight crew experiences an ECAM for AFT CARGO DOOR climbing through FL220. The crew determines that the pressurization may be abnormal and elects to don oxygen masks and perform an emergency descent. Flight diverts to the nearest suitable airport for an overweight landing.
summary: The flight crew received an aft cargo door ECAM warning and abnormal cabin climb rate while climbing through FL220, prompting an emergency descent and return to ZZZ. A mechanic confirmed the door indication, but the specific cause of the seal breach could not be determined after the door was opened for baggage handling.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reports forgetting to shut down the second engine after gate arrival due to multiple distractions. The running engine is detected by the First Officer during his walk around.
summary: The flight crew allowed three children into the cockpit while distracted by passenger assistance requests, resulting in Engine 2 remaining running during deplaning. The pilot attributed this safety deviation to high workload and distractions that caused a failure to complete the parking checklist before exiting the flight deck.

synopsis: The pilot of a CRJ-200 was concerned about the information he received from Maintenance personnel that appeared to contradict the Flight Manual.
summary: During descent, the crew received a transient Low Fuel Pressure caution that cleared after 3–4 minutes. Maintenance advised marking it as entered in error based on a supplement the pilot later found only covered landing and taxi, creating conflicting guidance between manuals.

synopsis: B737 flight crew is informed by the flight attendants that there is a fuel smell in the cabin. Since a fuel leak on the number one engine had been detected prior to departure and deemed to be acceptable by Maintenance, the left bleed and pack are shut down and the smell begins to dissipate. The aircraft is taken out of service after landing.
summary: Flight attendants reported kerosene fumes in the aft cabin due to a known serviceable fuel leak on Engine 1. The crew adapted the QRH to shut off the left bleed air and pack, dissipating the fumes before a safe landing and subsequent aircraft removal from service.

synopsis: B737-700 First Officer reports the Captain making rapid changes to the FMC without waiting for verification before executing. A track deviation occurs on the EAGUL 5 arrival due to an incorrect entry.
summary: During the EAGUL 5 arrival into PHX, the Captain executed unverified CDU changes causing a discontinuity and an unintended 180-degree turn. The First Officer intervened by selecting heading mode to correct the course, highlighting a need for mandatory cross-verification of all CDU entries.

synopsis: Confusion and a lengthy track deviation ensued when the flight crew of a B757-200 failed to execute their holding pattern in a timely fashion and were unable to re-establish compliance with their holding clearance. ATC provided vectors for a subsequent approach.
summary: The flight crew entered a holding pattern at OTT incorrectly when the FMC turned left instead of right, causing a loss of situational awareness. The controller subsequently vectored the aircraft south to RAVNN after the crew failed to regain proper holding airspace while troubleshooting the automation error.

synopsis: A B737-700 flight crew took exception to the manner in which center tank ballast fuel, required when a boost pump is inoperative, is accounted for in performance and flight planning programming.
summary: The crew encountered weight and balance calculation errors while operating under an MEL for an inoperative right center fuel tank boost pump. Discrepancies between the load sheet, weight and balance calculator, and FMC required non-standard procedures to correct gross weight and flight performance data.

synopsis: B737-300 Captain experiences a track deviation after being cleared direct to a waypoint and selecting LNAV. LNAV did not engage or dropped off after selection and was not detected by the crew until after the waypoint had been passed.
summary: The pilot and First Officer experienced an LNAV disengagement during climb after departing on a 030 heading to avoid weather. The system failure occurred while the crew was distracted by incorrect arrival charts, causing the aircraft to overshoot the FORPE waypoint before ATC provided a vector to reposition.

synopsis: When the flight crew of a B737-300 failed in their first attempt to rebalance fuel from wing to wing they recycled the boost pumps and crossfeed valves for a second try following which the right engine flamed out. Although they were later able to restart the engine they still opted to divert to a nearby airport.
summary: During cruise at FL360, the Captain's fuel crossfeed attempt caused an Engine 2 rollback, prompting a descent to FL240 and diversion. The crew restarted the engine with starter assist and landed safely, attributing the event to fuel system risks during high-altitude crossfeed procedures.

synopsis: A B757 flight crew descending at dusk for a visual approach to Runway 19L at LAS responded to an EGPWS terrain warning.
summary: The Pilot Not Flying on a visual approach to LAS Runway 19L triggered an EGPWS "too low, terrain" warning due to a modified base leg descent near a 3,993 MSL hill. The crew climbed to clear the terrain and landed safely, attributing the event to the removal of EGPWS checks from the approach checklist.

synopsis: ATC advised an air carrier flight crew assigned the ALDAN RNAV STAR to RDU that they had improperly crossed SBV below 17,000 FT, stating crossing was restricted to at or above 17,000. The reporter determined that both the government and commercially provided aero charts clearly restrict crossings at SBV to at or below 17,000 and at 280 KTS.
summary: The flight crew descended via the ALDAN RNAV STAR to 10,000 FT based on their charts, but ATC advised they should have crossed SBV at or above 17,000 FT.
