summary: During enroute cruise at FL400, the Number 2 engine rolled back to 60% N1, causing autothrottle disengagement. The pilot reduced power to stabilize the engine, which recovered normally, and the reporter suggests investigating potential high-altitude, low-temperature engine icing.

synopsis: Inadvertently selecting APP mode vice VOR/LOC to intercept the localizer while on autopilot resulted in a glide slope capture and a climb out of their cleared altitude for a B737NG flight crew.
summary: The Captain accidentally armed APP mode instead of LOC during a visual approach at 5,500 feet, causing the aircraft to climb 500 feet above altitude. The First Officer eventually intervened to disconnect the autopilot, allowing the Captain to correct the flight path and complete the approach with a slight overshoot.

synopsis: CLT Air Carrier arrival initiated a go around on short final when departing traffic became a factor, the reporter claiming CLT Tower controllers frequently misjudge arrival/departure separation requirements.
summary: The pilot executed a go-around at 100–200 feet AGL at CLT after Tower cleared a Dash 8 for takeoff with insufficient spacing from the landing aircraft. The reporter attributes this unsafe operation to controllers frequently misjudging spacing, resulting in wasted fuel and stress.

synopsis: Three weeks after the 'event' the FAA sought retribution from a B-777 flight crew for exceeding 250K below 10,000 on arrival at their destination. The source of their information was a routine review of the AML in which the flight crew had written up anomalous behavior of the autoflight system while operating with the autopilot engaged in LNAV and VNAV modes. The anomalous behavior described consisted of turning the wrong way at a waypoint and exceeding 250 knots below 10,000 feet. Both anomalous actions were immediately resolved by the crew and, again, written up in the AML.
summary: A relief pilot on a Boeing 777 arrival reported an uncommanded turn and 250-knot exceedance below 10,000 feet caused by an FMS automation failure. The pilot manually corrected the deviation, landed safely, and cited a known Boeing technical issue as the cause.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported a NMAC with a light aircraft during a visual approach to PSP. Reporter believes the light aircraft transponder was malfunctioning, and no RA was received.
summary: During a visual approach descent, the pilot and First Officer encountered a Cirrus aircraft at 9,500 feet after Approach reported conflicting traffic at 4,400 feet. The pilot attributed the 5,000-foot altitude discrepancy to a malfunctioning transponder on the other aircraft, which passed 50–100 feet above their flight path without triggering a TCAS alert.

synopsis: B757 Flight Attendant reported heavy smoke in the cabin that led to a landing at an alternate airport.
summary: Flight attendants reported heavy cabin smoke and engine smoke during an overwater descent, causing passenger distress and visibility issues. The crew managed the emergency, assisted passengers with life vests, and diverted to an airport for a safe landing where they deplaned after 30 minutes.

synopsis: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports he did not document or inform his Air Carrier Management personnel about loose 'smoking' rivets on the Left and Right Engine Exhaust Nozzles on their MD-83 aircraft, due to fear of losing employment.
summary: An AMT performing a cargo task on an MD-83 observed loose, smoking rivets on both engine exhaust nozzles but did not report them due to fear of employment retaliation. The mechanic alleges that management creates a hostile environment by threatening staff and falsifying sign-offs to suppress maintenance defect reporting.

synopsis: VFR aircraft in communication with Phoenix TRACON was questioned with regard to transitioning SDL Class D without contacting SDL.
summary: The pilot departed DVT Airport eastbound and communicated with Phoenix Approach, which noted a possible airspace deviation and instructed contact with SDL Tower upon landing. The pilot subsequently contacted SDL Tower after landing and reported a friendly conversation with the controller.

synopsis: PA23 pilot reported taking off on a parallel taxiway because of lack of situational awareness and time pressure.
summary: A pilot rushing to depart from an intersection on Taxiway Y mistakenly took off from the taxiway instead of Runway XXR due to overconfidence and lack of situational awareness. The pilot realized the error upon rotation, sidestepped to align with the runway, and avoided a collision as no traffic was present.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Inspector reports finding hat bushings missing from the rudder hinges on a CRJ-200 aircraft, three months after the aircraft returned from a Heavy Maintenance Check at a Contract Repair Station. While performing an RII Inspection of the rudder Power Control Units (PCUs), he noticed the United States flag paint lines did not line up with the paint lines on the rudder.
summary: During a routine inspection of a CRJ-200, maintenance personnel discovered missing top hat bushings on rudder hinges installed by a subcontract repair station in July 2013. This recurring issue, attributed to the vendor's incomplete installation, prompted the filing of discrepancy forms under the carrier's surveillance program.

synopsis: ZMP Controller acknowledged an airspace infraction when confused regarding sector consolidation, the reporter expressing concern regarding a lack of 'team atmosphere and support' evidenced in this and other events.
summary: An air traffic controller conducting annual certification mistakenly attempted a handoff to Sector 02 instead of Sector 14 for Aircraft X at FL230 due to confusion over new airspace boundaries. The controller attributed the error to a lack of team atmosphere and suggested team building to improve communication within the facility.

synopsis: Assisted by approach control, a SAAB 340 experiencing hydraulic system problems conducted a flawed missed approach procedure at ZZZ and diverted to ZZZ1 where they landed safely but were unable to taxi off the runway.
summary: An ATC controller managed a Saab executing a missed approach at ZZZ that deviated from the published procedure toward higher terrain. The pilot declared an emergency due to low hydraulic pressure, landed safely, but could not taxi off the runway.

synopsis: BJC Controller described a conflict event between an IFR aircraft and a VFR aircraft that had drifted into Class B airspace, the Controller suggesting that VFR aircraft request ATC services in the subject airspace.
summary: A Denver Approach controller issued a traffic alert to a VFR Cessna at 7,600 feet drifting into Class D airspace near ALIKE, warning of a southbound BE20 at 8,000 feet less than a mile away. The Cessna pilot reported the traffic in sight and was approved to transition through the airspace without further incident.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported ENG #1 compressor vane ECAM after takeoff, with no other issues they continued to destination. At top of descent the #1 engine rolled back and showed a high EGT, so the engine was shut down and non-eventful single engine landing ensued.
summary: The crew experienced an Engine 1 compressor vane warning on climbout, followed by an engine stall and failure at top of descent with EGT reaching 835 degrees. They shut down Engine 1, declared an emergency, and landed uneventfully with the First Officer flying.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported jet blast encounter from a departing aircraft on Runway 9 at BOS while landing on Runway 4. Reporter cited split Tower frequencies as contributing.
summary: A pilot reported experiencing a momentary jet blast jolt from a departing aircraft on Runway 9 while on short final to Runway 4L at BOS at night. The encounter occurred due to split tower frequencies preventing visual detection and communication, though the aircraft landed without incident.

synopsis: MD-83 Captain reported loss of cabin pressure at FL290. Unable to control cabin pressure the flight declared an emergency, descended to 10,000 feet and continued to a safe landing.
summary: The flight crew initiated an emergency descent from FL290 after the cabin altitude warning light illuminated and masks dropped due to an inability to maintain cabin pressure. They declared an emergency, descended to 10,000 feet, and landed safely with no passenger injuries.

synopsis: EMB-145XR Captain reported he was dispatched with engine 1 anti-ice valve inop. Shortly after takeoff they received a #2 bleed leak warning. Flight returned to departure airport.
summary: The crew departed with an Engine 1 anti-ice MEL and encountered a Bleed 2 leak and anti-ice failure at 11,000 feet in icing conditions. After isolating the leak, the captain elected to land overweight at 47,500 pounds rather than hold for over an hour to burn fuel, citing potential aircraft damage and task saturation.

synopsis: After an engine start problem, a Phenom 300 Captain reported he was uncomfortable with company operation's suggestion to perform a maintenance procedure he did not see in the book.
summary: The pilot reported a Phenom 300 right engine start failure during preflight, which Maintenance resolved after checking the ignition system. The pilot criticized MCC for suggesting crews pull the battery to reset the GCU, arguing this unapproved procedure masks a maintenance irregularity and creates safety risks.

synopsis: During an RNAV coupled approach this Bombardier Q400 crew descended slightly below a VNAV waypoint crossing restriction.
summary: The flight crew descended below minimum crossing altitudes at Waypoint Y after modifying FMS constraints and receiving a revised cruise clearance. The deviation occurred due to high workload, poor cockpit lighting, and a failure to cross-check current altitude against upcoming restrictions until ATC queried the aircraft.

synopsis: B767-300ER flight crew reported they got low on a night visual approach to SEA in part because the Pilot Flying was using vertical speed mode.
summary: The Captain and First Officer descended below the ILS glideslope on a visual approach to RWY 16C while using vertical speed mode. The First Officer manually leveled at 1,600 feet to intercept the glideslope, and the Captain attributed the deviation to the autopilot mode selection and insufficient monitoring.

synopsis: Flight Attendant (F/A) reports a Circuit Breaker (C/B) popped for a meal cart in the aft galley on a B767 aircraft in flight. C/B was reset on direction from flight deck, but a strong electrical odor came from the power cord to meal cart, Flight Attendant pulled C/B. Maintenance later replaced the electrical cord.
summary: A cabin crew member reset a popped circuit breaker for an aft galley meal cart, causing a strong electrical odor from the cord. The crew pulled the breaker again, logged the fault, and the power cord was replaced the next day due to faulty equipment.

synopsis: A First Officer reports that he and the Captain flying a C-560XLS aircraft noticed that pressurization air had ceased to flow from the overhead vents while in cruise flight. No Annunciator lights illuminated, indicating a loss of pressurization source. A non-emergency abbreviated descent was accomplished. Maintenance found a large composite cold air duct that had split open approximately 16' inches long, that looked like it had been cut with a razor blade.
summary: During cruise at 40,000 feet, the flight crew experienced a loss of cabin pressure due to a cracked duct line, causing the cabin altitude to climb. They executed an aggressive descent to 38,000 feet and made a precautionary landing without declaring an emergency, as the outflow valve closed and pressure stabilized.

synopsis: A pilot took off for a short flight from VPZ Runway 27 which was NOTAMed closed, but he had not checked NOTAMs and noted he monitored ASOS which the airport was prohibited from using as an airport status notification tool.
summary: The pilot test-flew an aircraft after annual inspection and took off from Runway 27, which was NOTAMed closed for surveying but not announced on ASOS. The pilot landed safely on Runway 18 after learning of the closure via UNICOM, noting that ASOS does not include NOTAM information.

synopsis: Two pilots in a Cessna T210 were forced to conduct a gear down off field emergency landing when they experienced sudden engine failure at about 2,000 FT AGL.
summary: The pilot and owner experienced an engine power loss at 2,000 feet AGL during cruise after the owner incorrectly moved the mixture to cut off. Despite restart attempts, the aircraft required an emergency landing parallel to a highway, resulting in a nose-first impact that collapsed all three landing gears.

synopsis: DAL Controller described a runway incursion event involving an aircraft taxiing to Runway 13L, the reporter claimed multiple same type occurrences and the existing hold lines are problematic and need adjusting.
summary: Local Control cleared an Eclipse 500 for takeoff from Runway 13L after the aircraft passed a new hold short line near the old line. The controller noted wet conditions and believes the hold line does not meet published requirements.

synopsis: The time required for the B737-700 flight crew to program an ATC assigned approach/runway change prevented them from initiating a descent required by their RNAV STAR assignment.
summary: A late ATC clearance change to the RNAV Visual 19R approach caused a delay in descending to the next altitude while the crew manually programmed FMC altitudes. ATC queried the descent status, and the crew quickly returned to profile.

synopsis: A Captain and First Officer report about a burning oil smell in the flight deck and cabin of a NexGen B737 aircraft shortly after takeoff. An emergency was declared and an air turnback accomplished. Maintenance noted that a Borescope Inspection had been accomplished on the CFM-56 engines the night before.
summary: Two separate crews reported smoke or burning odors shortly after takeoff from ZZZ, prompting emergency returns to Runway XXL. The first crew suspected an engine issue confirmed by maintenance, while the second crew struggled with checklist confusion and communication before executing an overweight landing.

synopsis: Three pilots describe their efforts to determine the actual fuel quantity on board an MD-11 aircraft during cruise flight after fuel indications in Number 1 and Number 2 Fuel Tanks became erratic while Number 3 Tank quantity was unknown due to being deferred 'inoperative.' Emergency was declared due to critical fuel status, aircraft diverted.
summary: The crew of an MD-11 operating in manual fuel mode due to an inoperative Number 3 tank indicator diverted to ZZZ1 after erratic fuel readings and a suspected leak caused critical fuel levels. They declared an emergency, landed safely, and suspected the fuel quantity indications were incorrect.

synopsis: Captain reports getting a Stick Shaker on their MD-11 aircraft during takeoff after 'Flaps Up' was called for and 'Flaps Up Allow' was displayed while slats were showing extend, with 'No Up Allow.'
summary: The First Officer flying a takeoff in light rain experienced a stick shaker after slats failed to retract despite a "Flaps Up Allow" message. The crew re-extended the slats, which resolved the issue, though a second shaker occurred before the slats fully extended for the remainder of the flight.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported he was advised by aft Flight Attendant of smoke in the cabin. The Captain asked for CFR response and the smoke that appeared to be from a ballast quickly dissipated.
summary: During taxi after pushback, the crew reported heavy smoke from the aft ceiling, presumed to be a ballast fire. The aircraft returned to the gate where maintenance confirmed the ballast fire, and the affected flight attendant was removed from duty due to smoke inhalation.

synopsis: A Q-400 flight crew diverted to the nearest suitable airport when the aft galley door came unlocked during flight.
summary: The flight crew received a fuselage door warning at top of climb indicating an unlocked galley service door, causing a brief pressure bump. Following checklist procedures, they diverted to the nearest airport, ZZZ, for an immediate landing after the flight attendant confirmed the door status.

synopsis: When the DHC-8 flight crew and Flight Attendant all detected strange odors and haze the flight diverted to a nearby airport. After landing the Flight Attendant advised the conditions in the cabin were unchanged the Captain ordered an evacuation.
summary: The flight crew encountered smoke and a blue haze while descending from FL190 due to icing, prompting an emergency landing and subsequent evacuation on the runway. The reporter attributes the incident to the operator's practice of flying aircraft without proper checkout, noting this was the fourth similar event.

synopsis: The flight crew of an HS-125 performed an inflight shutdown, declared and emergency and returned to their departure airport following receipt of a 'bang', vibration and high ITT from the left engine.
summary: During climb from FL380 on a passenger flight, a bang and vibration caused Engine 1 ITT to spike to 900°C, indicating failure. The crew shut down the engine, declared an emergency, and returned for an uneventful one-engine-inoperative landing; post-flight inspection revealed the N1 fan would not rotate.

synopsis: During cruise flight at FL380 in the vicinity of convective activity, the crew of a Boeing 747-8F experienced the loss of engine power to about 60% N1 on two separate occasions, on different engines, about 20 minutes apart.
summary: The flight crew encountered convective activity at FL380, experiencing two separate 15-second thrust reductions on Engines 2 and 4 due to suspected ice crystal formation. The reporter attributes these events to known engine issues in such weather and argues that current procedures placing the burden on pilots to avoid these conditions are unacceptable.

synopsis: When a Flight Attendant advised they had no galley power on the B767-300ER the flight crew investigated and found the BAT BUS DISTR circuit breaker near the First Officer's seat and flight bag was open. When closed, after consultation with Maintenance, the problem was resolved and the flight continued to its destination.
summary: During climb out, the flight crew found an open BAT BUS DISTR circuit breaker on the P6-1 panel causing galley power loss. After resetting the breaker, systems returned to normal, likely because the First Officer's seat belt accidentally bumped the switch.

synopsis: An MD80 taxiing to the gate after landing at ORD had to stop abruptly for an E-145 being taxied by Maintenance, which taxied in front of their cleared path at a high rate of speed.
summary: The pilot reported a near-midair collision while taxiing on Taxiway EE at ORD with an E-145 moving west on Taxiway D at excessive speed. The conflict occurred because the E-145, reportedly moved by a distracted mechanic, failed to yield despite being on a different ground frequency, requiring the pilot to brake aggressively to avoid impact.

synopsis: Two pilots report an EICAS Message appeared for a Right Wing Slide accompanied with an Emergency Doors light illuminating during climb. Cabin flight attendants confirmed Right Overwing Slide on their B767-300 aircraft had deployed in flight. Emergency declared and air turnback accomplished. Post flight inspection confirmed inflight slide deployment and departure from aircraft.
summary: During climb through FL250 on a departure from ZZZZ, the crew received a Right Wing Slide EICAS caution and heard a banging noise from the right overwing area. The flight attendants confirmed the slide had deployed but remained attached, prompting an emergency declaration and an uneventful return to land.

synopsis: After suffering multiple electrical anomalies the flight crew of an A300, Maintenance and Operations agreed to divert for maintenance assessment. Following maintenance action they departed but were promptly faced with repeats of the prior problems and returned for more comprehensive maintenance.
summary: During cruise, simultaneous failures of pitch trim, ATS, flight director, and standby pitot heat caused a diversion. After maintenance, the same issues recurred on the return leg, forcing an uneventful turn back without an emergency declaration.

synopsis: A310 First Officer experiences a left window heat fault at FL350 and the heat is turned off and the QRH consulted. Before the heat is turned back on the window cracks. Flight descends to FL230 and continues to destination.
summary: While cruising at FL350, a Left Window Heat fault caused the left front windscreen to crack after the crew reset the switch. The crew descended to FL230, followed the cracked window procedure, and landed without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) was informed correct software had not installed when he replaced a Data Loading Routing Unit (DLRB) on an A320 aircraft.
summary: A mechanic installing a Data Loading Routing Box on an A320 discovered the correct software was missing. The reporter attributes this to not recalling the software requirement and suggests verifying paperwork, revision dates, and the IPC for future installations.

synopsis: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) was informed that corrosion was found on the lower aft fuselage skin, just aft of the Lavatory Motor exhaust port on a B737-800 aircraft. He had previously accomplished an A-Check and walk around inspection on midnight shift using a flashlight.
summary: A mechanic performing a midnight A-Check on a B737-800 at ZZZ airport missed corrosion on the left aft fuselage during a flashlight-assisted walk-around. The reporter attributes the oversight to dark conditions and the gray paint color of the affected area.

synopsis: RV6 pilot reports an engine failure following a touch and go on a 6,700 foot runway. The decision is made to land straight ahead, touching down on the last ten feet of runway. The aircraft comes to a stop about 100 yards past the end of the runway, resting on the cowl and a wing tip. No injuries are reported.
summary: During climbout after a touch-and-go, the pilot experienced an abrupt engine power loss between 300 and 500 feet AGL with zero throttle response. The pilot executed an off-field landing 5 degrees off the runway centerline, causing the aircraft to tip onto its cowling and wingtip 75–100 yards past the runway end.

synopsis: A Lead Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) describes his company's maintenance repair facility work environment for their corporate S-76 helicopters. He lists a lack of: proper maintenance record keeping, lack of shift turnovers, tool control, tool calibration requirements, fuel sampling, hardware part numbers and storage of flammable materials.
summary: A mechanic reported safety violations on Sikorsky S-76 helicopters involving missing hardware, uncontrolled tools, and improper storage of flammables. The mechanic resigned after management lectured him for storing extra bolts in his desk and failed to address the lack of tool control and hardware disposal procedures.

synopsis: Air carrier departure described an engine failure during the climb to flight levels and the actions taken by the crew and ATC during the return to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a left engine failure with an N2 section failure while climbing through FL180 on departure from ZZZ. They declared an emergency, aborted a restart attempt, and executed a safe single-engine landing at ZZZ.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew experiences a fuel imbalance after attempting to use 500 LBS remaining in the center tank and forgetting to turn the crossfeed off when no fuel can be used. When the imbalance is noted the fuel pumps for the low wing are turned off but the imbalance appears to grow worse. The flight diverts to a suitable airport but Maintenance can find no discrepancy.
summary: The crew diverted and declared an emergency after a fuel imbalance increased to 1,400 LBS during cruise despite crossfeed attempts. Although preflight hydraulic fluid was found under engine two, post-flight maintenance found no discrepancies, and the cause of the imbalance remained undetermined.

synopsis: A319 Captain experiences a loss of directional control when thrust is set for takeoff and the takeoff is rejected below 15 KTS. The left engine did not accelerate at the same rate as the right engine according to the First Officer and the jumpseat rider. A second attempt is successful although the number one engine vibrates noticeably during climb with N1 vibration indicating between 1.8 and 2.6.
summary: The Captain rejected takeoff at 10–15 knots after the aircraft veered left due to suspected asymmetrical thrust from a lagging number one engine. Although vibration was felt during the subsequent flight, the crew completed the trip after accommodating nine passengers who disembarked.

synopsis: A First Officer reports about a Yaw Damper that failed shortly after takeoff, followed by a Rudder System-1 and Rudder System-2 'INOP' EICAS message on their EMB-145 aircraft. Flight crew declared an emergency due to loss of Rudder Flight Control System and returned to departure airport.
summary: During takeoff, the crew experienced a Yaw Damper failure followed by Rudder System (1) and (2) inoperative EICAS messages. They declared an emergency, returned to the airport, and landed safely due to effective crew coordination and checklist execution.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain experiences a NMAC with a business jet while on vectors to intercept Runway 36L localizer. The business jet on vectors to intercept Runway 36C localizer overshot intruding into 36L. TCAS announced the developing conflict and issued a descend RA.
summary: The pilot and First Officer of an aircraft approaching CLT for Runway 36L received a TCAS Resolution Advisory to descend due to a conflicting Gulfstream. The crew manually executed a steep descent and turn to avoid the collision, while ATC later vectored the Gulfstream to Runway 36R; the reporter attributed the conflict to delayed ATC traffic advisories.

synopsis: DHC 8-200 Captain experiences a flickering smoke warning at 16,000 FT. The crew elects to divert to the nearest suitable airport after declaring an emergency. During descent the Flight Attendant reports that there is no smoke in the baggage compartment, but the diversion is continued. A loose smoke detector cannon plug is found to be the cause.
summary: During cruise at 16,000 feet, the flight crew experienced a flickering SMOKE warning, declared an emergency, and diverted. A mechanic later determined a loose Number 1 baggage smoke sensor cannon plug caused the false warning, and the aircraft landed without incident.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Captain experiences a bird strike during takeoff and rejects at 78 KTS. Significant damage to the number one engine fan blades is noted on post flight.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff at 78 KTS due to a bird strike, returning to the gate. Post-flight inspection revealed significant damage to the Number 1 engine fan blades.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain and the Dispatcher involved describe a return to field due to a steering inop caution message received at cruise altitude. Landing is uneventful and the aircraft is towed to the gate.
summary: The non-flying pilot and crew experienced a persistent NOSEWHEEL STEERING INOP caution during climb on the second leg. They declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport, and landed on the longest runway before being towed off by a tug.

synopsis: A Line Mechanic was informed that cannon plugs to the squibs on a Cargo Fire Bottle were found not connected on a CRJ-200 aircraft approximately twenty days after he had installed the fire bottle. Flight crew had reported the Squibs Test had failed during their Pre-flight Check.
summary: A line mechanic replaced cargo fire bottle squibs under time pressure and reported completing all checks correctly. Twenty days later, flight crew found the squibs failed preflight checks because both cannon plugs were disconnected, though the mechanic could not recall making a specific error.

synopsis: AT6 instructor pilot reports a runway excursion while attempting to 'assist' his student with a wheel landing. The student and instructor end up fighting over the controls and the runway excursion ensue, with minor damage to the aircraft.
summary: During a T-6 training flight, an instructor and student lost directional control on landing due to conflicting control inputs while attempting a wheel landing. The aircraft swerved off the runway, scraping the wingtip and striking a taxiway light, causing minor damage to the fairing and flaps.

synopsis: BE350 First Officer reports a critical ground conflict with a landing B737 after being cleared to cross Runway 36R at Taxiway R. A collision is avoided by a quick stop and it is later determined that Controller error was responsible for the close call.
summary: Ground ATC mistakenly instructed the pilot to cross Runway 36R while a B737 was landing, causing the pilot to brake hard to avoid a collision. The controller later admitted the clearance was intended for another aircraft, and the incident was attributed to a controller mix-up.

synopsis: Pilot experiences an engine failure in cruise and a safe emergency landing on a golf course. No damage or injuries are reported.
summary: The pilot of a 582 experienced a Rotax engine power loss during cruise. After three unsuccessful restart attempts, the pilot executed a safe, uneventful landing on a golf course with no injuries or damage, followed by towing the aircraft for repairs.

synopsis: PA-28 instructor pilot reported encountering severe turbulence that led to an airspace incursion.
summary: A pilot and student in a Piper Arrow encountered severe turbulence and downdrafts during an IFR training flight, forcing a diversion to ZZZ1 due to altitude loss and student distress. Upon returning to ZZZ, they entered restricted airspace while battling extreme turbulence and disorientation before receiving vectors to complete the flight safely.

synopsis: PC-12 pilot reported losing directional control after landing in a crosswind, resulting in a runway excursion and some damage to the aircraft.
summary: A PC-12 pilot skidded off Runway XXR during a gusty landing due to a flat left tire and instinctive braking, causing the aircraft to veer onto rocky tundra. The incident resulted in fuselage, rudder, and flap damage from flying rocks, requiring gear replacement and towing to the hangar.

synopsis: LAS Controller described a near runway intersection conflict event prevented by pilot action/s after noting a departure aircraft rolling.
summary: A Local Assist and pilot at LAS reported a runway incursion risk on Runway 25R caused by inoperative ASDE-X radar, which forced the assistant to turn away from the operation. The controller cleared the pilot to cross while another aircraft was taking off, but the pilot stopped short of the runway, preventing a collision.

synopsis: BE400 Captain experiences runaway aileron trim climbing through 15,000 FT. With the left aileron trim active and the right trim off, trim returns to normal, but the crew elects to return to the departure airport.
summary: During climbout at 15,000 feet, the crew experienced a roll trim runaway while the autopilot was engaged. The Captain disengaged the autopilot, switched to hand flying, and stopped the runaway by isolating the trim system, allowing for a safe emergency return and landing.

synopsis: B737 flight crew member reported loss of cabin pressure while enroute. The flight elected to deviate to a nearby suitable airport.
summary: The flight crew managed a slow cabin altitude increase on a Boeing 737 enroute, likely caused by a mechanical failure following recent pneumatic system maintenance. They diverted to a nearby airport, landed safely, and returned unpressurized after ground tests failed to restore pressurization.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) was informed by the Manager on Duty that a Crew Oxygen bottle capillary line was found incorrectly installed on an EMB-145 aircraft. The discrepancy was noted during a Fleet Campaign Directive (FCD) inspection when the aircraft was at a Paint Shop facility.
summary: A mechanic replaced a broken crew oxygen capillary line on an EMB-145 during a C-Check, but a subsequent Fleet Campaign Directive at a paint shop found the line incorrectly installed with loose threads and tape. The mechanic believed the installation was correct, though documentation indicated otherwise.

synopsis: A Maintenance Controller in training reports that a company CRJ-200 aircraft was not able to pressurize after a Contract Maintenance provider had de-activated the Avionics cooling Inboard Shut-Off Valve to the 'Closed' position and the Overboard Exhaust SOV to the 'Open' position. Procedure was opposite from what the MEL required. Aircraft diverted.
summary: A pilot failed to send the carrier's Supplemental to on-call maintenance, causing them to incorrectly deactivate SOVs on a CRJ-200. The error left the Overboard SOV open, preventing pressurization and forcing a diversion.

synopsis: Single engine turboprop pilot reports setting up the EFIS for a visual approach and mistakenly setting selected altitude to 0 instead of 'OFF.' This results in an early descent and a low altitude warning from ATC.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway 11 at LFT, the pilot mistakenly set the selected altitude to 0 instead of OFF, causing the flight director to command an excessive descent. ATC issued a low altitude warning at 850 feet, prompting the pilot to climb to 1,000 feet AGL before completing a normal landing.

synopsis: During cruise, a B737-700 flight crew notices a fuel imbalance with #2 Engine fuel tank 700 LBS lighter. They discovered the fuel Crossfeed Valve Circuit Breaker (C/B) popped, but were unable to verify the valve's position. Imbalance increased to 1,300 LBS, crew declared an emergency and diverted.
summary: The flight crew at FL410 diverted due to a rapidly increasing fuel imbalance caused by a popped crossfeed valve circuit breaker. Although a flight attendant reported misty spray during flap extension, rescue confirmed no leak, and maintenance released the aircraft after repairs.

synopsis: During descent with the thrust lever at idle only a B737-300's nose gear red disagree light illuminated, then during approach the Configuration Warning alerted with the gear extended, flaps greater than 5. The landing gear circuit breaker was discovered tripped, and the system returned to normal with its reset.
summary: During a visual approach, the flight crew initiated a go-around after an intermittent gear warning horn and a single red nose gear light appeared despite the gear feeling down. The cause was a tripped circuit breaker, which the crew reset to restore normal indications before completing an uneventful landing.

synopsis: During an ERJ-175 landing roll out in rainy, windy conditions, the right main wheel anti-lock, anti-skid sensor prevented brake application symmetrical with the left brake, and in hydroplaning conditions, the aircraft exited the left runway edge.
summary: The crew landed on runway 27L in strong crosswinds and standing water, causing the aircraft to veer left after deploying thrust reversers and engaging autobrakes. Despite manual braking and anti-skid activation, the aircraft veered off the left side with the nose and left main gear in the grass before stopping safely.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 crew descended to 7,000 FT because of a non emergency dual Pack failure and when completing the UNPRESSURIZED FLT PROCEDURE the aircraft pitched over in an uncommanded descent when RAM-AIR was selected.
summary: During cruise at FL260, a flight crew managed a right pack failure and unpressurized descent to 7,000 feet. Opening the Ram-Air Valve caused an uncommanded 1,500 FPM descent while the autopilot remained engaged, requiring manual pitch mode selection to level the aircraft.

synopsis: EMB-145EP First Officer reported Tower informed them of a fuel leak shortly after takeoff. Flight returned to departure airport for a precautionary landing.
summary: The flight crew observed a fluid leak from the right wing during takeoff and executed a precautionary return to the departure airport. After confirming faster fuel consumption in the right tank, they landed safely, and a Fire Inspector cleared the aircraft for taxiing to the ramp.

synopsis: Light twin pilot reported an NMAC with another light aircraft on a visual approach to MYEF.
summary: The pilot and first officer of a VFR aircraft descending to Runway 12 at MYEF executed an evasive go-around after another aircraft descended through their altitude on final approach. The near-miss resulted from a misunderstanding of the pilot's ground speed call and the other crew's failure to verify position visually or via radio before continuing the approach.

synopsis: B767-300ER Captain reported loss of center hydraulic system near top of climb. Flight declared an emergency and returned to departure airport.
summary: The flight crew lost Center Hydraulic System Pressure just before top of climb, prompting an emergency return to the departure airport. They executed an overweight landing at 341,500 LBS with a sink rate of 100 FPM.

synopsis: DA10 Captain reports an altitude deviation during vectors for a visual approach due to an autopilot capture anomaly that is well known.
summary: Pilots flying a 30-year-old aircraft descended below their assigned 3,000 feet MSL during a visual approach vector due to the autopilot unexpectedly disengaging altitude capture. The crew arrested the descent at 2,550 feet MSL, attributing the deviation to unreliable autopilot behavior and a missed checklist item to verify altitude capture.

synopsis: BE-350 Captain reported he was cleared to cross CLT Runway 36R but as he entered the runway he saw a landing aircraft cross their path so he quickly stopped the aircraft.
summary: The pilot reported that while taxiing at CLT, Ground Control instructed a "Without Delay" crossing of Runway 36R just as a B737 landed, causing the Pilot Flying to slam brakes. The crew crossed the runway after the landing aircraft passed, and a subsequent Tower review confirmed the crew complied with all instructions.

synopsis: AMA Controller described a VFR pattern conflict when an inbound military aircraft failed to comply with published/assigned 'initial procedure' altitudes resulting in a conflict with traffic on base.
summary: Aircraft X descended below its cleared 055 altitude, creating a conflict with Aircraft Y at 050, and later refused vectors due to minimum fuel, forcing Tower to declare an emergency and re-route Aircraft Z and Y. All three aircraft landed safely after Tower issued climb and turn instructions to resolve the conflicts.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a conflict event involving a helicopter operating a photo mission and an Air Carrier arrival, the reporter suggesting improved and standardized procedures for handling helicopter photo operations.
summary: The Local Controller reported a near-miss between Air Carrier X and a photo helicopter on Runway 19 final due to the Helicopter Controller's failure to coordinate the helicopter's entry into the corridor at 1,600 feet. The aircraft converged within one mile with zero vertical separation before the helicopter turned away, prompting the implementation of a new Corrective Action Plan.

synopsis: ZFW Controller experienced an airspace infraction when internal coordination requirements increased the workload significantly, the reporter arguing that a D-Side would be more helpful than 'splitting' the sector.
summary: An air traffic controller working alone in the Turkey sector lost focus on a BE30 landing at MAF due to simultaneous complex tasks, poor frequency reception, and bad rides. The controller failed to coordinate the aircraft's descent to FL240 until it had already crossed the 61/82 boundary, attributing the error to high task complexity without a dedicated D-Side controller.

synopsis: ZDV Controller described an unsafe condition event when several air carriers were encountering severe turbulence but controller efforts to give exit clearances were not approved, reported due to government liability.
summary: An air traffic controller managed two aircraft encountering severe turbulence between FL260 and FL280 during climb out of Denver. The controller requested route deviations to avoid the turbulence but was denied by supervisors due to liability concerns, resulting in no turns being authorized despite the hazardous conditions.

synopsis: ZID D-Side Controller witnessed a loss of separation by the R-Side, listing 'brightness' settings as a causal factor.
summary: A D-Side controller observed a conflict alert between Air Carrier X and Air Carrier Y while the Radar Controller's scope brightness was too low for the observer to see data blocks. The Radar Controller issued turns to delay the conflict point, prompting the observer to recommend preventing low scope brightness and increasing platform lighting to ensure effective safety monitoring.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reported the Captain rejected a takeoff attempt because of directional control issues related to the nose wheel steering tiller not centering.
summary: During takeoff, the Captain aborted due to an inability to center the aircraft despite full left rudder. Post-flight maintenance revealed the nose wheel tiller failed to self-center, holding a 10-degree right deflection when released.

synopsis: MD-83 flight crew reported left engine loss of power shortly after takeoff, the result of a probable compressor stall. Flight declared an emergency and returned to departure airport with affected engine at idle thrust.
summary: The pilot reported a loud bang and left yaw at 800 AGL during takeoff, causing the left engine to rollback. The crew declared an emergency, returned for a safe landing, and taxied single-engine to the gate with no visible engine damage.

synopsis: A300 Captain describes a loss of GPS during arrival to ELP. After the fact a NOTAM is discovered describing the outage.
summary: The flight crew experienced intermittent GPS signal loss during descent into ELP while flying the SAMMR 2 RNAV arrival, causing confusion with Albuquerque Center regarding arrival restrictions. The crew attributed the event to an obscure, verbose FAA NOTAM regarding GPS unreliability in the area that was not included in their preflight paperwork.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported they were notified by a Flight Attendant that a passenger had pointed out missing skin in the area of Number 2 Engine. Flight declared an emergency and returned to departure airport, where postflight inspection revealed the Number 2 Engine cowl had departed the aircraft in flight.
summary: The flight crew and cabin crew reported that a right engine cowl separated in flight at 5,000 feet, exposing wires and pipes. The crew declared an emergency, returned for an overweight landing, and post-flight inspection confirmed the missing cowl and damage to the vertical stabilizer.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain experiences interference in his Bose X headset possibly caused by a cell phone.
summary: A pilot reported consistent electrical interference in their Bose X headset during taxi, takeoff, climb, and landing phases when passengers used cell phones. The pilot attributes the beeping noise to passenger devices and warns that expanded electronic device allowances could increase cockpit interference.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reported receiving a GPWS terrain alert while on vectors for an approach to ROA. Reporter feels this was controller error.
summary: The crew flying into ROA received a GPWS "Too low terrain" warning at 5,200 feet while being vectored over mountains after a conflict with a departing aircraft. The pilot executed an escape maneuver, and the controller appeared confused before the flight resumed the ILS approach without further incident.

synopsis: An A320 flight crew enroute suffered the loss of AC BUS 1 and elected to divert to an airport with longer runways due to the resulting partial loss of spoilers and reverse thrust. ATC declared an emergency for them when they requested CFR as a precaution.
summary: The Captain and First Officer diverted an A320 from cruise at FL350 after an AC Bus 1 fault caused automation loss and hydraulic system failures. They landed safely at a longer runway with fire trucks deployed after ATC declared an emergency, despite the crew not formally declaring one.

synopsis: A B737-800 encountered the wake vortices of a B737-900 on approach into ORD.
summary: Pilots on approach to ORD reported a controller confusion regarding runway assignment (27L vs 28C) and headings, resulting in a wake turbulence encounter with a preceding 737-900. The event required autopilot disconnect and power addition due to insufficient separation, which the controller initially dismissed despite it being their responsibility.

synopsis: B777 First Officer reported losing fire detection on right engine 2 1/2 hours into a long international flight. They elected to declare an emergency and divert to a nearby airport.
summary: The crew received right engine overheat and fire detection messages at cruise, leading to a loss of fire detection on that engine. Concerned about the time lapse and limited diversion options, they diverted to a nearby airport for a precautionary engine inspection by fire and rescue.

synopsis: When a A319 shed the left engine cowling during takeoff the flight crew returned to the departure airport for maintenance.
summary: A flight attendant reported a loud bang and missing engine housing on the right side during takeoff, causing a precautionary return to the departure airport. The reporter, a mechanic who had recently serviced the IAE V2500 engine cowls, attributed the incident to potential latch failure and recommended new inspections and run-up procedures.

synopsis: BE36 pilot reports losing control during landing in strong gusty winds, departing the runway and striking two fence posts.
summary: The pilot diverted to ZZZ due to strong crosswinds and landed on Runway 28 after a severe gust caused a rightward drift and nose yaw upon power reduction. The aircraft skidded off the runway, crossed a taxiway, and struck two fence posts with no injuries reported.

synopsis: The instructor pilot in Beech Texan II was distracted looking for the airport as the student failed to arrest their descent at the MDA. ATC issued an altitude alert and they recovered back to the MDA.
summary: An instructor and student pilot in a TEXII descended to 580 FT MSL, 80 FT below the 660 FT MDA, during an RNAV 23 approach due to the student's incorrect MDA belief and the instructor's external scan. The Tower alerted the crew, prompting a climb to MDA before a successful circle-to-land maneuver was completed.

synopsis: The pilot of a VFR PA-28 failed to take appropriate corrective action when overtaking a Cessna 172 and passed just 100 FT over the Cessna.
summary: A pilot flying westbound from PWK at 1,800 MSL overtook a descending Cessna 172 at 1,700 MSL with only 100 feet vertical and minimal horizontal separation. The pilot admitted failing to follow standard overtaking procedures by not passing to the right with adequate clearance.

synopsis: A C421 Captain experienced an engine failure at FL190 and diverted to the nearest suitable airport after shutting the engine down.
summary: The pilot experienced a right engine failure at FL190, declared an emergency, and diverted to ZZZ. After receiving clearance to descend to 8,000 feet, the crew secured the inoperative engine and completed an uneventful visual approach and landing.

synopsis: An instructor pilot and an instrumented rated pilot getting an IPC check were surprised when Potomac TRACON failed to hand them off to FDK Tower for a practice ILS approach. An NMAC with an inbound Seneca resulted plus the accusation from the Tower of a Class D violation.
summary: A CFII and PIC conducting an IPC practice ILS 23 approach at FDK entered Class D airspace without a handoff from Potomac TRACON to Tower. Confusion over non-standard clearances and lack of inter-facility coordination resulted in a near mid-air collision with a Piper Seneca, forcing a missed approach.

synopsis: When, while at cruise, the unexplained loss of several inches of one prop blade resulted in uncontrollable vibration of the C172-R the pilot was vectored to a nearby airport where he landed safely. There was no visible evidence of a bird strike.
summary: The pilot experienced a loud noise and shuddering at cruise when the oil access door opened and the dipstick ejected. After declaring an emergency and landing safely, the crew discovered several inches of the propeller were missing, with no evidence of bird strike.

synopsis: As he was descending toward his airport of intended landing a BE33 pilot experienced an NMAC with a same direction low wing single.
summary: A VFR pilot descending to 2,600 feet for landing at ARR sighted a low-wing single-engine aircraft at 2,500 feet just left of the wing. The pilot stopped the descent to avoid a collision, suspecting the other aircraft was obscured by their own wing and was not mentioned in Tower traffic advisories.

synopsis: BTR Controller described an unauthorized runway entry by mowers due to confusion regarding runway closure status.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared a VFR Mooney for takeoff from Runway 4R while mowers, mistakenly believing the runway was closed due to outdated internal sheets, crossed it. The aircraft passed between the mowers after the controller broadcast a stop command, highlighting a communication failure between airport operators and the tower regarding runway status.

synopsis: Tower Controller described a required go-around event when he/she failed to properly scan for arrivals before issuing a takeoff clearance with traffic on short final.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared a Citation for takeoff from Runway 26L but failed to see a Cessna 140 on short final for the same runway. Ground Control alerted the tower, allowing the controller to order the Cessna to go around before the Citation departed, preventing a runway incursion.

synopsis: A B737-700 crew experienced compressor stalls on climbout and return to the departure airport. The aircraft had been signed off as airworthy after a previous flight had experienced compressor stalls.
summary: The crew experienced loud bangs and yaw during climbout in an aircraft previously grounded for right engine stalls and fuel leaks. They returned to the departure airport for a normal landing, noting the aircraft was released without a test flight despite prior similar emergencies.

synopsis: EMB-190 Captain reports being dispatched on a maintenance ferry flight with with the Number 2 bleed system on MEL. Passing through FL250 a Number 1 BLEED LEAK message is annunciated on the EICAS. QRH procedures are complied with and the flight diverts to a suitable airport.
summary: The crew diverted a reposition flight with four souls on board after a Number 1 BLEED LEAK occurred at FL250 while the Number 2 BLEED was on MEL. They declared an emergency, descended to 10,000 feet, and landed at ZZZ where station personnel and maintenance met the aircraft.

synopsis: When cleared to cross MAYOS at FL220 (vice the charted 'between FL260 & FL220') on the IVANE RNAV STAR to CLT, the Pilot Not Flying of an A321 failed to program the change in the FMS and, as a result, was unable to comply with the more restrictive clearance. The reporter took umbrage with the frequency with which ATC modifies OPD (Optimized Profile Descent) STARs rather than clearing flights to descend 'via' them.
summary: The Monitoring Pilot and First Officer flying an RNAV STAR failed to cross MAYOS at FL220 because they misinterpreted a hard altitude clearance as a standard descent window. This error occurred when ATC issued step-down altitudes that conflicted with the FMS-loaded Optimized Profile Descent, causing the crew to be too high to meet the restriction.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 First Officer initiated a rejected takeoff when he noted another CRJ encroaching on their runway at high speed.
summary: The First Officer aborted takeoff after observing a CRJ taxiing onto the runway shortly after thrust advance. The crew stopped safely on the taxiway, completed cooling procedures, and departed 15 minutes later.

synopsis: Captain reports that after takeoff, at 400 FT, he noticed the left EPR became erractic and oscillating including the left N1 tach, followed by several bangs. Throttle reduced to idle and banging noise stopped. Air turnback accomplished. Left engine inlet bullet found separated from engine and resting in the inlet nacelle.
summary: The flight crew experienced a left engine compressor stall shortly after takeoff due to a detached engine bullet. They declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport, and landed safely with the left engine at idle before maintenance confirmed the detached bullet caused the event.

synopsis: A B737-800 flight crew inbound to a short runway suffered asymmetrical trailing edge flap extension at less than landing flap settings. They elected to divert to a major nearby airport with longer runways.
summary: The Captain and First Officer diverted an aircraft on final approach due to a trailing edge flap asymmetry and a continuous landing gear warning horn. They landed safely at a nearby airport with gear down, citing fatigue and the emergency as reasons to end their trip.

synopsis: A DC-10 Captain took exception to the manner in which PDC clearances are formatted in MIA, citing the 'assignment' of two different SIDs on the PDC for their flight.
summary: A pilot reported that Miami ATC assigned two conflicting departures, HITAG and WINCO, on a single Pre-Departure Clearance without standard asterisk highlighting. The reporter described this non-compliant procedure as a dangerous violation waiting to happen.

synopsis: MD11 flight crew reports the autopilot turning the aircraft to the right when the heading bug is turned to the left. The autopilot is eventually turned off and the aircraft manually flown to the desired heading. The autopilot is then successfully reengaged. During the hand flown approach the aircraft handles strangely and after landing the number two hydraulic system fails.
summary: The crew experienced autopilot and flight control failures during a left turn from heading 020 to 330, causing the aircraft to turn right despite correct inputs. A subsequent complete Hydraulic System 2 failure led to a precautionary shutdown of Engine 2 on the ground due to a right wing hydraulic leak.

synopsis: A helicopter and an aircraft suffered an NMAC as the helo crossed the runway on one of which the airplane was taking off.
summary: A helicopter crossed both runways at 700 feet while an airplane took off from Runway 13, forcing the airplane to maneuver right to avoid a collision. The incident resulted from miscommunication regarding clearance and the aircraft operating on different radio frequencies.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot near 05S at 3,000 FT reports a NMAC with a single engine Cessna. The approaching Cessna was obscured by the cockpit structure and not detected until the TIS alerted.
summary: A helicopter pilot in cruise at 3,000 FT near Vernonia received a Garmin 530 traffic alert for a converging Cessna 50 FT above. The pilot executed a course and altitude change to ensure separation, noting the alert was critical due to limited cockpit visibility and the absence of a second crewmember.

synopsis: BE36 pilot reports inadvertent entry into GEU Class D airspace while attempting to pick up an IFR clearance after departing GYR VFR. Departure Control could not be contacted on the frequency assigned and it was noted prior to departure that all three primary GPS receivers were showing no signal.
summary: The pilot departed Goodyear on a north heading after accepting a last-minute routing change, inadvertently entering Glendale Class D airspace due to GPS failure, incorrect frequency advice, and lack of notification that Luke AFB was closed. The pilot eventually contacted Luke Departure and was vectored to the destination without further incident.

synopsis: PA60-601P pilot reported loss of right engine at cruise flight, which was distracting enough he landed gear up.
summary: The pilot experienced a right engine failure at 25,000 feet and descended to land after unsuccessful restart attempts. Due to distraction during the emergency, the pilot forgot to lower the landing gear and landed wheels up.

synopsis: An ARTCC Controller expressed consternation at the failures of some flight crews to fail to maintain their assigned airspeed of 300 knots at TEDDY waypoint on the BULLZ RNAV STAR, instead slowing to 250 knots as published on the arrival.
summary: Pilots flying the BULLZ RNAV STAR into ORD reduced speed to 250 knots at TEDDY intersection without clearance, despite being assigned 300 knots. The reporter attributes this confusion to conflicting published speed restrictions and recommends removing them to improve safety and efficiency.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain experiences a dual bleed trip as thrust is reduced to begin descent from FL410. Oxygen masks are doned and QRH procedures are complied with. The bleed trip is reset passing FL250 and the passenger oxygen masks do not drop. Flight continues to destination at 10,000 FT.
summary: The flight crew experienced dual engine bleed trips and rapid depressurization shortly after descending from FL410, prompting an emergency descent to 10,000 feet. Pressurization was restored at 25,000 feet, and the aircraft landed uneventfully after the crew completed checklists and coordinated with ATC and cabin crew.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier Captain reported stopping immediately after exiting Runway 19 onto Taxiway E after landing at night, because confusing barricades made it appear that the Taxiway was closed 50 FT to 100 FT after exiting the runway.
summary: The flight crew encountered dimly lit barricades on Taxiway E at night while taxiing to the gate, requiring an emergency stop to avoid collision. Although ATIS mentioned construction, the reporter attributed the hazard to poor lighting and the taxi line's alignment with the barricades, noting skid marks from previous incidents.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported dual bleed failure leading to loss of pressurization. Flight declared an emergency.
summary: The crew declared an emergency at 41,000 feet due to a loss of pressurization caused by a dual bleed failure.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported abnormalities with the primary electric pitch trim system. They declared an emergency and returned to departure airport.
summary: During a VFR takeoff, the Captain and First Officer experienced main electric trim failure and speed brake warnings due to a loose cannon plug on the stabilizer trim. The crew managed the aircraft using manual trim, returned to the departure airport, and landed safely after maintenance confirmed the faulty connection.

synopsis: DHC8 flight crew experiences failure of the number two hydraulic system while holding short with the parking brake set. The aircraft begins to move and is stopped with with the normal brakes. The aircraft is taxied clear of the taxiway and shutdown and the passengers are bussed to the terminal.
summary: During taxi, a crew experienced a Number 2 hydraulic system failure causing the aircraft to roll forward despite the parking brake being set. The crew stopped the aircraft using toe brakes, taxied to a ramp, and shut down after firefighters chocked the wheels due to fluid leaks and smoke from the right main gear.

synopsis: A Captain notes that after two consecutive icing encounters and two consecutive Horizontal Stab (HStab) Ice Fail annunciations on two different flights, the normal Ground Test used by Maintenance is not 'robust enough' to find the cause of the HSTAB Ice Fails that have occurred in flight, on a Beechjet BE-400XP aircraft.
summary: The flight crew encountered an HStab Ice Fail annunciator while descending in icing conditions to ZZZ1, executing emergency procedures for a safe landing. The crew concluded that standard ground tests failed to detect the recurring fault, recommending escalated maintenance troubleshooting before the aircraft re-enters icing.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain experiences a GPS malfunction prior to taxi which is reset by the First Officer. After takeoff the crew and ATC both note the aircraft was not following the RNAV departure. VOR navigation is used to continue to destination.
summary: The crew experienced an undetected GPS failure shortly after takeoff, causing FMS navigation errors during the RNAV departure. They switched to VOR navigation after ATC queried the deviation, as the GPS could not be synchronized despite maintenance resets performed before the flight.

synopsis: A B757 Flight Attendant became flustered and distracted by a passenger demanding a prohibited alcoholic beverage during a tire change delay after landing, then deployed a slide while intending to check the tire change progress.
summary: During taxi after landing, a tire blowout caused a delay, leading to a confrontation with an intoxicated passenger. A distracted Flight Attendant opened the aircraft door to verify maintenance work, causing the emergency escape slide to deploy and creating an unsafe situation on the tarmac.

synopsis: A Q400 Flight Attendant discovered one of the aft galley portable oxygen bottles empty and a short while later, after the Captain verified her discovery, the second bottle was found empty.
summary: During Q400 pre-flight, a cabin crew member found a portable oxygen bottle gauge reading empty, but later discovered a second bottle was depleted after being turned on, likely by the Captain. The cause of the initial empty bottle remains unknown, though the crew noted a lack of training on galley oxygen equipment.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A single engine civilian pilot complained that Navy aircraft pilots were operating in an unsafe manner at a civilian airport during night operations.
summary: A pilot reported a near-midair conflict while landing on runway XX in dark, gusty conditions involving Navy aircraft performing unauthorized right-hand patterns at high speeds below pattern altitude. The pilot attributed the safety risk to the Navy planes ignoring standard procedures in uncontrolled airspace, noting that TRACON controllers could not monitor them.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reports an inadvertent TOGA selection by the flying First Officer, approaching minimums, followed quickly by deselecting autopilot and autothrust. The approach is continued to landing in marginal VMC with some glideslope excursions and the flight director indicating go-around.
summary: During a night IMC ILS approach, the Pilot Flying inadvertently selected TOGA and disengaged automation, causing flight director climb commands and a GPWS SINK RATE warning below 100 feet. The Pilot Monitoring took control to execute a nominal landing, attributing the event to over-reliance on automation and a need for better training on IMC-to-VMC transitions.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier Captain added 1,100 LBS of fuel and landed with the flight plan calculated fuel remaining but would have been at Company minimum fuel if not for the extra fuel upload. The company fuel planning software is flawed.
summary: The Captain added 1,100 LBS of fuel to a 4-hour flight to BWI due to concerns over Dispatch's fuel planning algorithms and mountain wave activity. The flight arrived with 5,100 LBS, avoiding a "Minimum Fuel" declaration that would have likely occurred with the original plan.

synopsis: A B777 left engine LOW OIL PRESS alerted at cruise shortly after takeoff, so an emergency was declared, fuel dump begun, the QRH completed and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The Relief Pilot assisted the flight crew during a return to the departure airport after the left engine showed zero oil quantity and low pressure at FL350. The aircraft completed a normal single-engine landing following fuel dumping and checklist procedures, with no further incident reported.

synopsis: An A320 Captain described his company's new Training Phase implementation and its negative safety impact on taxi out workload because of increased checklists, distractions with tasks better completed at the gate, heads down operation and single pilot taxi at busy airports.
summary: The Captain of an Airbus A320 reported that new Standard Operating Procedures shift critical preflight tasks to the taxi phase, increasing pilot workload during busy ground movements. The reporter believes this change degrades safety by forcing heads-down work during taxi, potentially causing mistakes or violations before takeoff.

synopsis: Flight crew was instructed to accomplish another disconnect of an Integrated Drive Generator (IDG) on their A321 aircraft after they noticed the IDG on the ECAM Electrical Page was pulsing. The IDG had previously been deferred and considered disconnected.
summary: The A321 crew encountered a rising IDG temperature during cruise, peaking at 155°C, and were instructed to disconnect the unit again. The temperature subsequently dropped, though the IDG was later found reconnected in ZZZ.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer is informed during descent that the PDX VOR has been decommissioned although no mention is made on the ATIS and no specific NOTAM has been issued. It is also noted that company engine out procedures use the PDX VOR.
summary: During descent into PDX, the Pilot Monitoring discovered the PDX VOR was inoperative and learned from Approach it was decommissioned. The crew noted that single-engine missed approach procedures and arrival briefings incorrectly relied on this VOR, while ATIS and release paperwork failed to report its deactivation.

synopsis: Captain reports he heard yelling from the ground crew and realized their EMB-145 aircraft was rolling forward beyond the gate, even though the parking brake handle was pulled and set.
summary: The pilot reported that after parking at gate ZZZ and setting the emergency brake, the aircraft moved forward despite the brake being engaged. The pilot stopped the plane using foot brakes, requiring a pushback, and attributed the incident to a malfunctioning emergency brake.

synopsis: A B757 crew was unable to hear ATC on the overhead speaker because selecting overhead cockpit speaker and interphone muted radio calls and as a result the flight was NORDO with conflicting traffic.
summary: During climbout on a B757, the crew failed to hear ATC traffic alerts because selecting the interphone inhibited the cockpit speakers. This communication loss occurred while climbing to FL390, resulting in a near-miss with another aircraft before the crew corrected the switch settings and received a vector.

synopsis: After the gear would not retract, an A300 crew switched to System 1 which allowed the gear to retract but ADC2, all pilot heaters, autopilot 2 and autothrottles failed possibly the result of the air/ground switch 2 failure.
summary: The crew experienced a gear retraction failure in system 2, which resolved upon switching to system 1 but triggered faults on ADC2, pitot heats, autopilot 2, and autothrottles. Unable to clear these faults, they returned to the departure airport for an eventful approach and landing, suspecting a ground air shift fault.

synopsis: A pilot entered R5311C at 6,500 FT below the GTN 750 GPS depicted 12,000 FT floor but that GPS did not depict the lower R5311 A/B areas along with their respective restricted altitudes.
summary: An experienced pilot inadvertently flew through restricted area R5311 below the 12,000-foot minimum altitude because the GPS display failed to clearly distinguish the separate R5311A, B, and C designations shown on paper charts. The pilot was notified by ATC on Guard and later contacted by restricted area authorities, prompting a recommendation to improve chart clarity to prevent future violations.

synopsis: B757 First Officer reported an MD-80 clearing a runway just missed his wingtip as he taxied by.
summary: The crew parked on Taxiway K while waiting for a congested Ramp frequency, causing an MD-80 exiting Runway 27R to pass within yards of their nose. The crew proceeded to their gate only after the MD-80 cleared the alleyway.

synopsis: Three controllers and an air carrier pilot describe the confusion after a helicopter is cleared through the final approach corridor but is in conflict with the air carrier who switched frequencies late and did not hear ATC's alert.
summary: A radar trainee cleared an air carrier for a visual approach to Runway 22 while a VFR helicopter crossed the final approach course. The helicopter turned toward the jet, causing a near midair with one mile lateral separation, attributed to the controller failing to ensure separation before issuing the visual clearance.

synopsis: B737 First Officer laments his company's new fuel policy that is exacerbated by flight plans with unrealistic altitude assumptions, resulting in low arrival fuel.
summary: The pilot reported that a flight plan filed for 40,000 feet conflicted with lower published STAR altitudes, increasing fuel burn and creating a tight arrival fuel situation under the new policy. The reporter attributed this pressure to inaccurate flight plan altitudes and called for larger fuel policy error windows.

synopsis: B777 flight crew reported loss of oil quantity and pressure in left engine. After consulting with Maintenance and Dispatch the engine was shut down, and emergency declared, and the flight returned to departure airport.
summary: The flight crew returned to the departure airport after the left engine oil quantity dropped to zero and pressure fell extremely low while cruising at FL350. They shut down the engine, dumped fuel to reach maximum landing weight, and executed a normal landing with emergency services standing by.

synopsis: A320 Captain experiences brake and steering faults prior to departure and Maintenance replaces the BSCU. After landing at destnation the same faults return and the aircraft is towed to the gate.
summary: The crew experienced Brake System 1 and N/W STRG faults, returning to the gate for BSCU replacement and facing a fuel delay before departure. Post-landing, steering failures and erroneous inputs forced a stop short of a parallel runway, requiring a tug tow to the gate.

synopsis: MD11 flight crew experiences a takeoff warning for flaps although the flaps are correctly set at 10 degrees. The takeoff is rejected at 90 KTS and the flight returns to the gate for maintenance.
summary: Pilots rejected takeoff at 90 KTS due to a false 'Flaps' warning caused by an erroneous flap transmitter signal while set to flaps 10. The aircraft returned to the gate for maintenance on a repeat item, and the subsequent takeoff with flaps 15 was uneventful.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reports that all the fixes necessary to fly the ILS36R at CLT do not load unless the HEKAM transition is selected when loading the ILS. Crew crosses HEKAM at 4,000 FT per ATC and starts descent to 3,000 FT not realising that two more fixes need to be crossed at 4,000 FT before descent is commenced. Glideslope was out of service.
summary: The crew of an aircraft conducting an ILS 36R approach at CLT experienced high workload and task saturation when the autopilot failed to capture the localizer due to a missing HEKAM fix in the FMS. The reporter attributed this to an unselected transition, incorrect altitude assignments by ATC, and the subsequent need to hand-fly while manually entering fixes.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reports being issued a low altitude warning by CLT Tower during a LOC approach to Runway 36R. The minimums had been raised by NOTAM from 1,080 to 1,220 FT, which the crew did not recall.
summary: The flight crew descended below the published MDA on the LOC 36R approach at CLT because they missed a NOTAM raising the minimum to 1,220 FT. This oversight occurred despite IMC conditions and a Tower low altitude alert, though the crew continued to a normal landing.

synopsis: DHC8-100 flight crew reports smelling exhaust like fumes during climb and cruise. The Flight Attendant and passengers do not notice any fumes but the crew elects to divert.
summary: The flight crew detected exhaust-like fumes during climb and cruise, causing physical symptoms that led to an emergency diversion. After donning oxygen masks and completing the smoke checklist, the aircraft landed safely, and the crew was medically evaluated and released.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported the Captain's windshield shattered at FL370. Flight declared an emergency and diverted to a nearby suitable airport.
summary: During cruise at FL370, the Captain's outer windshield shattered after a suspected arc caused a loud pop, resulting in zero forward visibility. The crew declared an emergency, descended to 10,000 feet with ATC coordination, and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: Flight Attendant notifies flight crew that fuel was leaking from Left tank shortly after takeoff. Captain offered video of left wing taken by passenger and concluded fuel leaking just outboard of outer flap panel. Emergency declared and the EMB-145 aircraft returned to field. Maintenance inspection revealed a flapper valve leaking.
summary: A flight attendant reported a fuel leak shortly after takeoff, prompting the captain to declare an emergency and return to the airport. The leak, caused by a faulty flapper valve, stopped at 10,000 feet, allowing for a safe landing and remote parking.

synopsis: An A319 crew became distracted while comparing the FMS track of the ORD TRIDE ONE RNAV Arrival, ILS 10C which indicated GIBNS direct BAIRY while the paper chart indicated GIBNS, JUKIC then heading 090. The crew failed to begin a descent for a crossing restriction.
summary: The flight crew descended late into ORD while distracted by an FMS chart discrepancy, failing to meet a clearance to cross VINCA at FL330. ATC re-cleared them to FL330 after they reported being high, and the crew acknowledged they should have prioritized aviating.

synopsis: EMB145 flight crew experiences a MAIN PITCH TRIM failure at rotation. After climbing to a safe altitude QRH procedures are complied with and the flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced a Pitch Trim Main Fail with the trim stuck at 8 degrees up shortly after takeoff, causing a nose-up tendency. They followed QRH procedures, declared an emergency, and returned for a safe landing with fire truck escort.

synopsis: When the CL600's nose gear collapsed after landing the flight crew was unable to arrest an excursion off the left side of the runway.
summary: During landing, the aircraft veered left and departed the runway after the nose gear collapsed. The crew evacuated the empty aircraft on the grass with no injuries reported.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: The pilot of a Liberty XL2 encountered turbulence in instrument conditions that caused a momentary loss of control. He was able to apply full power and flight control inputs to regain control and return on course.
summary: The pilot encountered severe turbulence and zero visibility while intercepting the ILS at 6,000 feet, causing a rapid descent and left wing drop. The reporter attributed the incident to unfamiliarity with the aircraft's handling characteristics in adverse weather.

synopsis: A Citation single pilot on a night time final approach to LVK appeared to have encountered an aircraft, also on final, which was operating without a transponder, no external lights and compromised communications capability.
summary: The pilot on final approach to Runway 25R received TIS alerts for an aircraft with an inoperative transponder, no lights, and garbled radio. The unlit aircraft, which the tower could not see, landed immediately behind the pilot after orbiting in darkness due to suspected weak electrical systems.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports that a B767 aircraft lost oil in # 2 Engine in flight, approximately eight months after a cloth parts bag had been installed, but not removed. The bag was used to cover the # 6 bearing cavity drain opening for the scavenge oil return line. Flight diverted.
summary: During maintenance on a B767's #2 engine, a parts bag left in the #6 bearing scavenge area caused oil loss and a flight diversion in November 2013. The incident resulted from using improper equipment to cover the scavenge opening during the March 2013 maintenance.

synopsis: B737-300 flight crew report a master caution light at 14,000 FT caused by a generator off light and a CSD low oil pressure light. Believing the oil pressure light is for the Number One Engine, it is shut down and the flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: The crew mistakenly secured the #1 engine at 14,000 feet after misinterpreting generator and oil pressure lights as an engine failure. They landed safely but realized post-landing that they had run the wrong checklist due to rushing.

synopsis: An air carrier Dispatcher was surprised when a CRJ-700 flight crew diverted to a nearby airport after sending an ACARS message advising only 'IFSD.'
summary: A CRJ-700 crew diverted due to engine oil quantity dropping below 15%, requiring an in-flight shutdown. The dispatcher initially misinterpreted the crew's "IFSD" ACARS message, highlighting a communication disconnect caused by ambiguous acronyms during the emergency.

synopsis: ATC assigned the ATL Runway 9L KOLTT RNAV after the crew briefed the Runway 8L ERLIN RNAV and during the descent to 9,000 FT a track deviation occurred while the crew hurriedly entered the FMS arrival change which generated numerous route discontinuities.
summary: The fatigued flight crew deviated from course while loading an unexpected Runway 9R ILS PRM approach during descent from 12,000 to 9,000 feet. Confusion over FMS waypoint discontinuities caused the deviation, though no controller query occurred and the landing continued without incident.

synopsis: Prior to intercepting the LGA Runway 13 ILS localizer, a B737-800 Captain selected the APP mode and as the glideslope indicatored passed through centered climbing, the aircraft unexpectely pitched.
summary: The Captain engaged approach mode at 3,000 feet while three miles from PAYMI, causing the aircraft to climb to 3,300 feet as it attempted to capture the glideslope. The pilot disengaged the autopilot to correct the deviation, attributing the event to premature mode selection before localizer capture.

synopsis: An A300 flight crew suffered a CFTT incident when the autoflight system malfunctioned and the aircraft failed to arrest its descent at 3,000 MSL as cleared prior to intercepting the ILS.
