summary: During a First Officer requalification ILS approach, simultaneous ALT capture and LAND arming caused autopilot mode confusion and an unrecognized descent to 2,000 feet. The Captain took control, triggered a GPWS obstacle alert, and manually recovered the aircraft for a safe landing.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier executed a missed approach on the FWA Runway 23 GPS approach and entered extreme turbulence so an emergency was declared because altitude could not be maintained as the flight turned to exit the embedded cell.
summary: The flight crew executing a GPS approach to Runway 23 at FWA encountered extreme turbulence after a missed approach, causing an inability to maintain the assigned 3,000 feet. They declared an emergency, requested 5,000 feet, and turned west to exit IMC and evaluate diversion options.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 Flight Attendant reported the Captain told her to prepare for an emergency landing, but no evacuation preparation, because an engine with a malfunctioning thrust reverser would be shutdown prior to landing.
summary: Cabin crew prepared for a potential evacuation after the Captain reported a stuck left thrust lever requiring a single-engine landing and diversion. The aircraft landed normally at the alternate airport, where fire trucks and EMTs met the flight at the gate.

synopsis: A PA-28 student pilot lost control of the aircraft after touchdown when a gust lifted the right wing which resulted in the aircraft exiting the runway.
summary: During a precision landing on Runway 24, a gust of wind lifted the right wing after touchdown, causing the aircraft to exit the left side of the runway into the dirt. The pilot applied brakes and taxied the aircraft to the parking area with no further damage reported.

synopsis: A Falcon 900 encountered wake vortices from an A320 departing LAS.
summary: The pilot departed Runway 25R at LAS behind an A320, maintaining visual separation and a steep climb to avoid wake turbulence. Despite these precautions, the aircraft encountered mild suspected wake turbulence at 7,000 feet, which the pilot attributed to using a single runway and departing immediately without a delay.

synopsis: Four Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports about working conditions at an FAR 135 repair facility that included fatigue, complacency, the lack of an Inspection Department and the lack of adequate maintenance procedures that eventually led to one of their pilot's performing a precautionary landing of a Bell 206L helicopter.
summary: A Bell 206L helicopter experienced an unusual noise and precautionary landing after a transmission replacement due to loose Main Drive Shaft bolts. The reporter attributes the error to the installing mechanic's incomplete fastener installation, driven by fatigue, complacency, and high production pressure at the maintenance facility.

synopsis: MD11 flight crew experiences 'ENGINE 2 VIB HI' during engine start. It is decided that ice may be the cause, but no action is required other than a runup. Before a runup can be accomplished the vibration ceases and the flight departs. Maintenance discovers compressor blade damage during post flight inspection.
summary: The flight crew experienced a Level 1 Engine 2 High Vibration alert during engine start after overnight freezing fog exposure. Although vibration levels normalized allowing for departure, post-flight maintenance inspection revealed seven damaged compressor blades.

synopsis: EMB145 Captain is informed of white smoke coming from the Number One Engine after shut down at the gate. Maintenance determines that this is normal and the flight is dispatched on the final leg of the day. Upon shut down thick white smoke is observed coming from the rear of the same engine and the problem is entered in the logbook. Next morning the engine is runup with Maintenance present, and again on shut down thick white smoke is observed this time with small flames. The Engine Fire on the Ground Checklist is accomplished, ARFF is summoned and the flight is canceled.
summary: After a fatigued crew and maintenance technician cleared a smoking Number 1 Engine following a six-leg duty day, flames erupted from the engine rear during a next-day ground runup. The crew executed emergency procedures, discharged the fire bottle, and cancelled the flight, though no EICAS fire warning was received.

synopsis: A crew entering the cargo ramp at night nearly turned onto the old Taxiway BB because the taxiway signage was located near the old taxiway and there were no Xs painted on the old taxiway indicating it was closed.
summary: The Captain initiated an early turn onto a closed taxiway at ORD while taxiing to the cargo ramp due to misleading ground markings, signage, and an outdated airport diagram. The aircraft was stopped by the First Officer and subsequently towed to the ramp without damage or ATC disruption.

synopsis: An ATR-72 Maintenance crew which had not attended the Airport Authority training, taxied from a company ramp with Ramp Tower permission, but did not contact Ground Control and were stopped by a security vehicle enroute to a maintenance hangar.
summary: Two mechanics taxiing an aircraft requiring inspections from a gate to a hangar received conflicting instructions from Ramp Tower and ATC, leading to an airport deviation. The incident occurred because Ramp Tower failed to direct them to contact ATC, resulting in an illegal taxi and a requirement to complete airport authority training.

synopsis: A student pilot on a solo flight in a PA28 experienced a runway excursion following a landing that was too fast.
summary: A student pilot on a solo flight landed flat and fast at 70 KTS, causing the aircraft to swerve left. The pilot overcorrected to the right and departed the runway, resulting in no injuries or damage.

synopsis: The pilot of a C172 performing pipeline inspections experienced a rough running engine and elected to land in a field. He later found that the fuel selector was in a position between both and right, but was unsure how this occurred. He ran up the engine and took off successfully.
summary: The pilot performed a precautionary landing in a cow pasture due to a rough-running engine while patrolling at 400 feet. The fuel selector was found between tanks, but the engine ran normally on the ground, and the aircraft landed safely at a nearby airport with no damage.

synopsis: A Pitts pilot bounced the aircraft during landing and the instructor was unable to salvage the landing, resulting in a ground loop and damage to the landing gear.
summary: A student pilot bounced a Pitts S-2B landing during dual instruction, causing the instructor to take control and ground loop the aircraft, damaging the landing gear. The incident created a runway hazard for nearly two hours due to delays in locating recovery equipment and unclear airport management reporting procedures.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew is informed by ATC shortly after takeoff that fuel is venting from the left wing tip. The crew elects to return to the departure airport and does so uneventfully.
summary: During climbout, the flight crew observed significant fuel venting from the left wing and a 280 LB tank imbalance, prompting a return to the airport. The aircraft landed safely, and maintenance found no external damage but required an interior fuel tank inspection.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot is informed during a VFR departure that his Mode C transponder is not working and attempts to recycle are ineffective. A few minutes later an NMAC occurs and the reporter cannot initially understand why the TCAS did not alert. Post flight reveals a tripped Altitude Encode circuit breaker which had caused both failures.
summary: A pilot and nurse crew experienced two near-misses while flying a helicopter near Boulder and Erie after a popped Altitude Encode circuit breaker caused Mode C and TCAS failures. The pilot attributed the first missed traffic alert to a blind spot and the second to the equipment failure, which was discovered post-landing and reset to restore normal operation.

synopsis: A DC-10 Engine 3 Oil Pressure exceeded the high limit and subsequently N2 rolled back to zero, so the engine was shutdown, an emergency declared and the flight diverted.
summary: The crew declared an emergency and diverted after Engine 3 oil pressure exceeded limits and N2 RPM dropped to zero. They performed an uneventful engine-inoperative approach and landing, finding no external evidence of malfunction upon taxiing to the ramp.

synopsis: CRJ-700 First Officer reported that a tin of mints placed between the flap and thrust levers rolled back on takeoff and lodged in the rudder trim causing an EICAS message and rejected takeoff.
summary: The Captain placed an Altoids tin between the flap and thrust levers during takeoff preparation. The tin rolled down the console, jammed the rudder trim, and caused a delayed EICAS message.

synopsis: A Beech Sierra B-24 pilot reported that on the third landing with an instructor during re-qualification training, the nose gear collapsed and separated from the aircraft on runway centerline.
summary: A pilot and flight instructor in a Beech Sierra B-24 experienced a nose gear collapse during the third touch-and-go landing on Runway 9R. The gear assembly sheared off, causing the aircraft to skid to a stop with no injuries reported.

synopsis: Two pilots report they were unclear what an EICAS Status message POWER XFR UNIT (PTU) display meant, when the message appeared after observing a previous L HYD ENG PUMP EICAS message on their B757-200 aircraft. They were getting ready to enter an ETOPS category flight and were concerned about ETOPS safety requirements and legality.
summary: The pilot reported a Left Hydraulic Engine Pump failure on a B757 during cruise, questioning if the Power Transfer Unit activated to support the Hydraulic Motor Generator for ETOPS. The crew continued the flight, concluding that while flight safety was not compromised, the ambiguity regarding PTU status potentially compromised ETOPS safety.

synopsis: A B737NG flight crew descended to 550 feet AGL six miles from the airport, versus recommended 1,800 feet MSL, while conducting a RIVER VISUAL approach to Runway 19 at DCA. Following receipt of an EGPWS Terrain warning they climbed and re-established the profile to a safe landing.
summary: A fatigued, inexperienced crew flying a River Visual 19 into DCA descended too low, triggering a GPWS alert due to misjudged position and potential VNAV setup errors. The Pilot Flying climbed to 900 feet AGL, while the Pilot Not Flying mistakenly silenced the terrain warning, resulting in an uneventful landing after the crew acknowledged their lack of situational awareness.

synopsis: A B757-200 flight crew, cleared to cross JENFR at 4,100 FT and, shortly after, cleared for the ILS 30 at OAK descended below the restriction when the PF entered the glideslope intercept altitude in the altitude alert window while operating in FLCH mode vice VNAV as intended.
summary: The flight crew descended below the 4,100-foot restriction at JENFR while on pre-final vectors after switching to FLCH mode and setting a lower MCP altitude. The autopilot was disconnected to level off at 3,850 feet, an error attributed to FLCH ignoring MCDU restrictions and a missed mode change by the PM.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: An instructor and student inbound to SRQ had a near miss with a departing aircraft after beginning an early descent to pattern altitude without clearance.
summary: A pilot with a student descended from 2,100 feet to 1,400–1,600 feet on downwind for Runway 14 at SRQ without authorization, creating a 100-foot conflict with a departing aircraft. The pilot corrected the altitude after Tower intervention, attributing the incident to the inbound instructor's failure to wait for descent clearance.

synopsis: A very experienced pilot landing at an uncontrolled airport with an inoperative radio experienced a near collision with an aircraft taking off from the crossing runway.
summary: A pilot with an inoperative radio landed on the wind-favored runway without checking for traffic. The pilot nearly collided with another aircraft taking off from a crossing runway that the wind was not favoring.

synopsis: An instructor and student announced their intentions and began to takeoff at an uncontrolled airport, then observed another unannounced aircraft landing on a crossing runway. The instructor pilot estimated that the aircraft came within 10 feet of a collision.
summary: A Piper 28-161 instructor and student nearly collided with a Cessna 150 during takeoff on a crossing runway at an active training airport. The near miss occurred because the Cessna pilot had an inoperative radio and failed to announce his pattern entry, while the Piper crew could not see the crossing final approach.

synopsis: CE560 pilot, on a visual approach, went heads down to use FMS heading command and turned inside traffic. Pilot followed ATC headings to clear traffic and landed without further incident.
summary: A single-pilot maintenance flight experienced a visual approach cancellation due to FMS heading command malfunction and difficulty identifying distant traffic in dusk conditions. The pilot corrected the heading manually after ATC intervened for turning inside traffic, then completed the approach without further incident.

synopsis: TRACON Controllers described a loss of separation event claiming the Fusion RADAR equipment was one causal factor.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported a loss of separation to 2.08 NM between a King Air 200 and a 737-800 during final approach due to the new Fusion RADAR's target update method distorting speed perception. A second incident involved a 737-800 and Medevac King Air 200 where separation decreased to 3 NM after the controller misjudged turn rates and failed to adjust vectors for spacing.

synopsis: A loss of separation event occurred when pronunciation of navigational fix HANAA was apparently incorrectly entered in the FMS as HANNA by the flight crew and an unexpected turn was initiated.
summary: An Air Carrier X flight and two military jets experienced a near-midair conflict during departure due to the crew entering waypoint "HANNA" instead of "HANAA" in the flight management system. The error caused the aircraft to deviate toward the military traffic, requiring ATC to issue a safety alert and vector the flight away.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew experiences airspeed and altitude anomalies on the Captain's displays during climb. Crew elects to maintain an intermediate altitude in VMC and continue to destination also VMC. During descent the Captain's instruments return to normal.
summary: During climbout in IMC, the crew experienced degraded air data displays and EEC soft altitude mode due to a suspected DEU failure. They maintained control using cross-checks with ATC, continued to the destination in VMC, and landed uneventfully after instruments restored at 13,000 feet.

synopsis: A BAE-125-850XP flight crew returned to their departure airport when a noticeable and increasing vibration and rumbling noise occurred shortly after takeoff.
summary: The flight crew experienced a vibration and rumble after takeoff, prompting a return to the departure airport. Maintenance identified a failed starter generator with metal debris as the cause, though the crew could not confirm the vibration originated from an engine.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier aircraft was pushed back from LAX to the North Spot where its main gear tires settled into a rut which then required 52% N1 to break away for taxi.
summary: The flight crew experienced a taxi issue at the North Spot between Terminals 7 and 8 where the aircraft settled into an asphalt rut. Although 40% N1 was insufficient to move the aircraft, 52% N1 on both engines was required to break free, prompting a recommendation to repair the rut or adjust pushback stopping points.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 EICAS alerted SLATS FAIL the Flap/Slat 1 was selected, so an emergency was declared, the QRH completed and an uneventful landing completed.
summary: The flight crew experienced a slats fail caution and zero indication while selecting flaps one during approach in IMC. They executed the emergency checklist, declared an emergency with ATC, and landed safely in a modified configuration.

synopsis: A CE-750 flight crew, flying the LOC DME (BACK CRS) to Runway 12 initiated a missed approach when ATC advised of a low altitude alert. Reporters advised they had entered the FMS displayed altitude at ASONE of 2,990 MSL which was lower than the MDA(H) of 3,120 MSL.
summary: The crew flying a LOC BC 29R approach set an FMS altitude of 2,990 feet at the ASONE fix, which was below the 3,120-foot MDA. Tower issued a low altitude alert, prompting an immediate climb and missed approach due to the conflicting FMS data.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported executing a go-around after encountering moderate turbulence and wake vortex on approach to ANC.
summary: The crew encountered severe turbulence and suspected wake turbulence from a B757 while approaching runway 7R at 2,000 feet, prompting a go-around with significant altitude and airspeed deviations. They diverted to FAI, landed safely with no injuries, and attributed the event to moderate turbulence combined with wake turbulence.

synopsis: A EMB-145 lost the Essential DC Bus 1 in flight, so the crew declared an emergency and continued to the filed destination with multiple avionics and equipment failures.
summary: The Pilot Not Flying and Captain experienced an Essential Bus 1 failure during cruise, causing instrument panel power loss, communication outages, and a nose gear indication failure. They declared an emergency, diverted to the longest runway, and executed a safe landing after confirming the nose gear was extended despite the lack of indication.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: CRJ flight crew reports an inadvertent button push while attempting to select heading on the FCP resulting in autopilot disconnect and the loss of 700 FT. GPWS and ATC both announce the deviation and the Captain returns to 6,000 FT. Both pilots cited a long fatiguing day as contributing to the error.
summary: Fatigued pilots on a multi-leg day inadvertently disconnected the autopilot while fixing a Comm 1 frequency error during an ILS 11L approach. This distraction caused a descent below 6,000 feet, triggering a GPWS 'Too Low Terrain' alert, but the crew recovered by climbing back to the assigned altitude and completing a safe landing.

synopsis: A B757 First Officer discovered a fuel truck plastic coated grounding wire, without a grounding clip attached to the aircraft ground point during fueling, but not properly grounding because plastic will conduct static electricity.
summary: During B757 preflight and passenger loading, a pilot discovered the fuel truck grounding clamp was attached to the aircraft but disconnected from the wire, leaving only plastic sheathing at the connection. The pilot stopped fueling, and the operator replaced the faulty wire with a functional one from the truck's front bumper.

synopsis: King Air 200 pilot is advised by ATC to check altitude during descent to the first two stepdown fixes on the RNAV Runway 18 at LIT. At LNAV minimums the runway is sighted off to the left and a normal landing ensues. Post flight analysis reveals that the approach may not have been correctly activated and the display scale was too high to detect the error.
summary: The pilot flying an RNAV 18 approach at Little Rock received multiple altitude alerts while the KLN 90 GPS needles remained aligned. The pilot realized the equipment was faulty when the runway appeared off-course, but landed safely after visually acquiring the runway.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: CL-65 Captain reported encountering significant wake turbulence in trail of an A320 departing from ATL.
summary: The pilot encountered wake turbulence from a preceding A320 shortly after departing ATL, causing a right roll despite full left aileron input. Company data confirmed the aircraft banked 17.5 degrees right at 230 feet AGL with minimal speed loss before the pilot stabilized and engaged the autopilot at 754 feet.

synopsis: IFR arrival to TEB described a very confusing event when the status of the landing runway and the associated ILS was uncertain, the reporter claiming ATC's handling created a hazardous situation.
summary: A pilot flying an ILS 6 approach to Teterboro encountered hazardous conditions when airport operations closed the runway and disabled ILS and lights without coordinating with NY TRACON or the Tower. The pilot diverted to a visual approach to Runway 1 after losing the localizer signal, landing safely despite the uncoordinated actions.

synopsis: A private pilot reports the Attitude Indicator, Turn Coordinator, and HSI all showed red Xs for a second or two and then all three displays on the G1000 PFD went to black just after rotation, on a Cessna C-182T aircraft.
summary: The pilot experienced a temporary failure of the G1000 PFD attitude, turn, and HSI displays during rotation, causing a return to the runway request at 100 feet AGL. The displays recovered at 400 feet AGL, allowing a safe landing with no emergency declared due to functioning standby instruments.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: An instructor pilot reported he stopped his aircraft on CTAF airport VNC Runway 5 about 200 feet from an air carrier twin which landed on Runway 13. The air carrier crew apparently made only one position call out on final which failed to mentally register with the task saturated instructor.
summary: A training aircraft and a transport aircraft stopped with 200 feet separation at an intersection of Runways 05 and 13 at VNC. The reporter attributed the near-miss to their assumption the transport used Runway 05, the transport's single 5-mile call-out, and their own distraction while training a student.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A corporate jet autoflight system failed to generate a glideslope on the HND GPS-B approach, so the pilot selected V/S and descended 700 feet below the IF to FAF segment minimum altitude where the GPWS TERRAIN warning alerted at which point he executed a go-around.
summary: The pilot flying a GPS-B approach to HND misread the minimum altitude between HAKID and JEXIX, descending 700 feet below the prescribed limit. This error triggered a ground proximity alert, forcing a missed approach before a successful second attempt.

synopsis: Seaplane pilot reports a near collision with a boat while attempting a river landing. The intended landing area had appeared clear but the reporter surmises that a very fast boat had intentionally obstructed the landing. A go-around is initiated and the reporter returns to his airport.
summary: A pilot executing a water landing on a river at 45 knots spotted a boat directly below at 10 feet altitude and applied full power to avoid a collision. The pilot concluded the boat moved into the clear landing area from behind, prompting a return to the airport and a commitment to better scan for approaching vessels.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air taxi crew landed on AVQ Runway 30 after proper CTAF arrival communications then after touchdown saw a military helicopter hovering over the runway centerline halfway down but were able to swerve around the dark aircraft.
summary: The First Officer reported that a military helicopter hovering on the active runway centerline blocked their landing on Runway 30. Due to poor visibility and lack of radio response, the crew executed an evasive drift to the right during rollout to avoid a collision.

synopsis: B737-400 Captain reports an engine failure in the traffic pattern while conducting flight testing of in flight systems not related to the engine failure. The failed engine is secured and a single engine approach and landing ensues.
summary: During a VFR flight test at 200 feet AGL, the crew experienced an Engine 1 N1/N2 rollback and high EGT while turning base. They secured the engine, performed a single-engine landing, and towed the aircraft for inspection with no injuries or damage reported.

synopsis: ZMP Controller voiced concern regarding the decision to permit an air carrier, limited to only one frequency, to transit multiple airspace environments and land at a busy east coast airport.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller in Sector 30 reported that Air Carrier X, en route to ZZZ1, had radio equipment limited to 134.57 and 121.5, frequencies the sector could not use. The controller stated this created an unsafe situation and excessive workload, arguing the aircraft should have diverted to repair the malfunction before proceeding to the busy destination.

synopsis: Enroute Controller experienced a loss of separation detected by automation, the reported estimating the separation loss at less than fifty feet.
summary: An air traffic controller lost separation while climbing Aircraft Y through Aircraft X at FL270 due to an 8-second calculation error. The controller attributed the incident to radar resolution limits and pilot reporting delays, noting the lateral separation was reported as 4.96 NM.

synopsis: A Captain was unable to select BDL VORTAC in the FMS and after querying ATC learned that the BDL VORTAC had been decommissioned, but not yet removed from some commercial airway and approach charts.
summary: Pilots entered the decommissioned BDL VOR into the FMC while cleared to Bradley, triggering a "Not in NAV database" message. The controller confirmed the VOR was removed eight months prior and re-cleared the aircraft to the airport, prompting a request to update approach charts.

synopsis: MD-11 was incorrectly refueled after maintenance deferral of a fuel quantity indicator. Flight crew noted fuel imbalance in flight that exceeded the aircraft limitation, but landed without incident.
summary: The flight crew deferred a fuel quantity fault on an MD-11, but maintenance likely over-fueled tank 1, causing a significant imbalance. This resulted in excessive aileron trim during climb and approach, though the crew completed the flight safely without transferring fuel.

synopsis: An A320 developed a strong odor after takeoff, so the Captain asked the flight attendants to confirm cabin odor then returned immediately to the departure airport where paramedics suggested medical treatment for the crew.
summary: The flight crew detected a strong chemical odor shortly after takeoff, prompting an immediate return to the departure airport. The incident resulted in an overweight landing and required hospital treatment for all crew members and several passengers due to chemical inhalation symptoms.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: A80 Controller described an unsafe condition while providing PRM services to ATL, noting the tailwind factor was of concern but no one was willing to initiate a runway change to align with the existing wind conditions.
summary: A PRM-O controller reported an unsafe East operation at ATL with tailwinds up to 13 knots on a wet runway, where pilots experienced difficulty flaring and rolling to the runway end. Despite the controller declaring the operation unsafe and a pilot diverting to hold, supervisors ordered the controller to stop objecting, resulting in no runway excursions but significant safety concerns.

synopsis: B737-300 First Officer reported encountering wake turbulence on arrival to LAX that resulted in a 45 degree roll.
summary: During the SADDE arrival at 7,000 feet, the aircraft rolled left to 45 degrees despite autopilot engagement, causing a 400-600 foot altitude loss. The pilot attributed the event to wake turbulence from an unknown aircraft ahead of the preceding Boeing 767, noting calm winds and topography likely prolonged the wake's presence.

synopsis: Two pilots report all three Radio Management Panel (RMP) frequency display windows went blank in flight and they were unable to change radio frequencies on their A320 aircraft.
summary: The crew experienced a system malfunction where all three Radio Management Panel frequency windows went blank, preventing frequency changes. After resetting the panels, VHF-3 was restored, allowing normal communication and a safe landing at ZZZ1.

synopsis: A B717 EICAS alerted ENG LEFT COMPRESSOR STALL in conjunction with two loud bangs, vibration and loss of engine thrust so the Captain rejected the takeoff at 120 KTS, had the aircraft inspected and returned to the gate.
summary: During takeoff, the crew experienced a left engine compressor stall with loud bangs, vibration, and thrust loss. They aborted at 120 kts, stopped on the runway, and returned to the gate after fire department inspection and engine shutdown.

synopsis: MD83 flight crew experiences a 'DC EMER BUS OFF Light' during climb out. The Emergency Power Switch is selected to on to reinstate emergency DC power and the flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a DC emergency bus failure and subsequent anti-skid system failure ten minutes after takeoff. They declared an emergency, returned for a visual approach, and executed an overweight landing on the 13,000-foot runway before taxiing to the gate uneventfully.

synopsis: A B767-300ER flight crew opted to return to their departure airport for maintenance when both the R ENG HPSOV (pneumatic High Pressure Shut Off Valve) and the L ENG PRV (pneumatic Pressure Regulating Valve) EICAS warnings illuminated.
summary: The crew experienced left and right engine bleed air faults on a Boeing 767 during takeoff and cruise. They diverted back to the departure airport, using the APU for pneumatics and landing uneventfully below maximum weight.

synopsis: An IMC Fighter on final to LMT Runway 32 was advised about VFR helicopter traffic on final but did not detect the aircraft visually until clear of clouds then flew beneath the helicopter while avoiding it.
summary: A military fighter pilot on an ILS approach to LMT Runway 32 in IMC visually acquired a helicopter one mile outside Class D airspace and aggressively maneuvered to avoid a collision. The reporter attributes the near-miss to air traffic control failing to de-conflict the IFR flight from the visual traffic despite radar and tower awareness.

synopsis: N90 TRACON Controller described a loss of separation event between two air carrier arrivals when the first, cleared for a visual approach, made an unexpected turn causing the event.
summary: A B737-800 cleared for a visual approach to Runway 22 unexpectedly turned back toward the LDA-A final course, losing separation with a CRJ-200 being vectored behind it. The reporter attributes the incident to the B737-800 failing to fly the most direct route to the runway as expected.

synopsis: B737 Captain with new First Officer reports a terrain warning while on a wide left downwind visual approach at 6,000 FT for Runway 25L at LAS. The Captain had advised 6,000 FT until past the ridge at 4,609 FT, but the warning was activated and a climb to 6,500 FT initiated.
summary: A new First Officer flying a visual approach to Runway 25L requested 4,900 feet despite the Captain noting 4,609-foot terrain. The crew received a terrain warning and climbed to 6,500 feet, while ATC provided no altitude restrictions or warnings.

synopsis: Captain reports finding the Standby Hydraulic System Pump indicating normal operation, but the Standby Low Pressure Light remained illuminated when he performed an Optional Preflight Check on a B737-900 aircraft. Maintenance found Hydraulic Supply Line to Standby Pump partially disconnected. Unknown how long aircraft had been flying without a functional Standby Hydraulic System.
summary: During preflight, the pilot discovered the Standby Hydraulic System pump was running but not generating pressure due to a partially disconnected supply line at the reservoir. Mechanics reconnected the line, verified system operation, and cleared the aircraft for flight, though the duration of the prior failure remains unknown.

synopsis: A First Officer reports that a company B747 aircraft has chronic unwanted fuel transfer problems in flight that have been written up 10+ times in the last three months. Fuel is disappearing from Main Tank #1 when it should not be, and after depleting the Center Tank, Main tank #3 decreases faster than Main tank #2.
summary: A B747 flight crew reported a chronic unwanted fuel transfer issue where fuel disappeared from Main tank #1 and Main tank #3 depleted faster than Main tank #2 despite matched engine flows. The reporter attributed this to inadequate maintenance troubleshooting and a maintenance history display that masks recurring fuel system defects with non-essential cabin items.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A fractional crew executed a go-around while approaching Runway 31L at BFI after a TCAS RA from a small helicopter landing on Runway 31R. Aircraft comes in conflict with a B737 departing nearby SEA while on the Tower issued missed approach procedure.
summary: The pilot flying a visual approach to Runway 31L at BFI executed a missed approach after a TCAS RA from a helicopter, then descended on Tower instruction to avoid a climbing B-737. The reporter attributes the conflict to aggressive helicopter operations and poor controller separation, noting the Tower's unhelpful response during the emergency.

synopsis: A B767-300ER ultimately returned to their departure airport after experiencing EICAS pneumatic system bleed anomalies on both engines.
summary: The flight crew experienced left and right engine bleed air EICAS messages during takeoff and cruise at FL340. After declaring an emergency and diverting, they returned to the departure airport and landed uneventfully following maintenance advice that the right engine issue was likely an indication problem.

aircraft: Boeing Company Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An air carrier Captain, flying the ILS Z RWY 36 approach at SEQM expressed confusion over whether the charted 18,000 feet MEA over QIT and the QIT 177/6.0 DME should be flown as a flight level or an altitude since FL180/18000 are the transition FL/ALTs.
summary: Pilots reported confusion regarding a crossing altitude on the SEQM ILS Z Runway 36 approach at QIT VOR, where the plate specified 18,000 feet but the transition level was FL180. Citing regulations for flight levels above the transition altitude, they crossed at FL180 with QNE settings, though they noted no inquiry from Quito approach.

synopsis: B757 Captain experiences a generator failure enroute and the APU is started to take its place. Thirty minutes later the APU shuts down and an emergency is declared. Flight returns to departure airport.
summary: During cruise at FL340 on an ETOPS flight, the left generator failed, followed by an APU fault and shutdown. The crew declared an emergency, diverted, and landed uneventfully after consulting Dispatch and Maintenance.

synopsis: CRJ700 First Officer experiences a L WING OVHT warning EICAS message and an aural Left Wing Overheat passing through 2,000 feet MSL. An emergency is declared and the flight returns to the departure airport for an overweight landing.
summary: During initial climb through 2,000 FT MSL, the crew received a Left Wing Overheat warning in icing conditions. They declared an emergency, returned for an overweight landing, and deplaned passengers to meet maintenance.

synopsis: When an EMB145 flight crew received a low altitude alert from the Tower while on approach they discovered the QNH setting from Approach Control was inaccurate. They then set the correct setting and continued without further incident.
summary: The flight crew received an incorrect altimeter setting from Approach while in moderate turbulence during approach to runway 31R. This error triggered a low altitude alert, but the crew verified the instruments, corrected the setting, and continued without further incident.

synopsis: EMB145 Captain reports a SPOILER FAIL master caution with a spoiler open indication on the EICAS at FL340. The Emergency Checklist is consulted and flight diverts to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The crew experienced an uncommanded spoiler deployment at FL340, triggering a SPOILER FAIL caution. They declared an emergency, descended to the nearest airport, and landed uneventfully with emergency vehicles standing by.

synopsis: The First Officer aboard a CE-680 repeatedly reminded his Captain to maintain their assigned altitude as the Captain appeared uncertain of the autopilot vertical navigation functions. Several modest deviations were initiated and arrested without comment from ATC.
summary: The First Officer reported that the Pilot in Command caused multiple altitude deviations below the assigned 3,000 feet during the approach to Runway 8 due to improper autopilot mode management. The PIC repeatedly selected vertical speed mode after the system auto-transitioned to altitude select, resulting in descents to 2,750 feet before corrections were made.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A small jet on the JQF Runway 2 GPS encountered turbulence near ECEGA at 2,500 FT which pitched the aircraft over triggering the GPWS terrain warning so a go-around climb was executed until the warning ceased.
summary: During a GPS approach to Runway 2 at JQF, moderate turbulence caused a pitch-down at 2,000 FT, triggering a GPWS obstacle warning. The crew climbed to 3,600 FT, executed a go-around, and successfully completed a subsequent approach.

synopsis: An Aircraft Inspector reports about the failure of 50 Passenger Service Unit (PSU) oxygen masks' doors that would not open on an A330 aircraft during a 'Manual Mask Release' Check. A second test noted that 38 different PSU doors failed to open. The wide body aircraft has a 2-5-2 passenger seat row configuration. Each PSU unit has either three or six masks.
summary: During a passenger oxygen manual mask release operational check, over 50 masks failed to drop. After replacing solenoids, the inconsistent failure pattern persisted across cabin zones, leading to an Engineering Order due to suspected fleet-wide issues.

synopsis: Lear 35 First Officer reported problems with the gear indicator lights that were eventually resolved, resulting in a normal landing.
summary: During approach, the crew encountered a left main gear indication failure on an aircraft with recent gear issues. After unsuccessful emergency extension attempts, the crew diverted, confirmed all three gear were down and locked via visual low pass, and landed safely.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 3 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier crew stopped rapidly on MIA Taxiway Whiskey to avoid colliding with a fast moving foreign carrier's A330 on Quebec. Ground Control gave no traffic warning or acknowledgment of the conflict.
summary: During taxi at MIA, the crew stopped to avoid a fast-moving Airbus crossing their path on Quebec after the First Officer was programming the FMC for a runway change. The reporter attributed the near collision to a lack of Ground Control monitoring and poor coordination between North and South ground controllers.

synopsis: EMB-145XR flight crew reported encountering wake vortex in climb that resulted in an altitude deviation.
summary: While climbing to 17,000 feet, the crew encountered wake turbulence or windshear causing buffeting, a left wing-low condition, and autopilot failure. The pilot flying regained control, inadvertently climbed to 17,400 feet, then returned to 17,000 feet before ATC cleared the flight to FL280.

synopsis: While at cruise a B757 left generator tripped and then the APU also auto shutdown after starting, so with on a single generator an emergency was declared and the flight diverted to an enroute airport.
summary: During cruise at FL350, an electrical fault caused autopilot disengagement and left AC system failure, prompting the crew to divert after communication difficulties and APU issues. The Pilot Flying manually flew the aircraft to a safe landing at an enroute airport following an emergency declaration, with no further incidents reported.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reports a near collision with a tug pulling carts during taxi from the gate. Hard braking is used and the tug driver swerves at the last second to avoid collision. A Flight Attendant is injured and the flight returns to the gate for medical assistance.
summary: During taxi, the flight crew applied maximum brakes to avoid a collision with a baggage tug driven by an employee reading a paper. The abrupt stop injured a flight attendant performing cabin safety checks, requiring medical evacuation and a return to the gate.

synopsis: A B737 on vectors for a EWR visual took evasive action in response to a TCAS descend command which then reversed to climb because the traffic was below and climbing. During the abrupt reversal a flight attendant was injured.
summary: During descent to 3,000 feet near GRITY, the crew received a TCAS Resolution Advisory that initially commanded a descent before instantly changing to climb, avoiding a twin turboprop passing 300 feet below. The aircraft climbed to 3,500 feet to clear the conflict, landed safely, and a flight attendant reported a crew member injury while taxiing.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew reported wake turbulence encounter on departure that resulted in airspeed fluctuations above 250 KTS.
summary: The crew experienced wake turbulence and airspeed fluctuations above and below 250 KTS below 10,000 FT during a minimum spacing takeoff behind a company aircraft. After taking corrective action, ATC issued a heading of 180.

synopsis: CRJ200 Flight Attendant describes a cabin smoke event about three minutes after takeoff and the subsequent return to the departure airport.
summary: A flight attendant reported smoke filling the cabin shortly after takeoff, originating from under seats in the aft and mid sections. The crew landed safely without using fire extinguishers, and while ground crews inspected the aircraft, the specific cause of the smoke remained unknown.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: An instructor in the LAL Runway 5 closed traffic pattern took evasive action during a near miss with a light twin which departed Runway 9.
summary: An instructor and student in a tailwheel aircraft nearly collided with a departing light twin at LAL while in a right traffic pattern for Runway 5. The instructor executed an evasive climb and turn after spotting the twin climbing into their path, attributing the conflict to pattern selection and divided attention.

synopsis: G-IV flight crew experiences airspeed, altitude and AOA anomalies descending to 10,000 FT. This results in stick shaker activation, Mode C readout error along with autopilot, flight director and yaw damper EICAS messages. Eventually the Captain's PFD is transferred to the number two DADC and the stick shaker circuit breaker is pulled. A normal approach and landing ensues, with the number one DADC returning to normal passing 5,600 FT in VMC.
summary: Pilots experienced a Number 1 AOA probe icing event at 11,000 FT, triggering stick shaker activation and DADC miscompare warnings that caused ATC to issue conflicting descent stop commands due to erroneous altimeter data. The crew managed the situation by switching to the Number 2 system, pulling the Number 1 circuit breaker, and landing uneventfully after the advisory cleared at 5,600 FT.

synopsis: PA28 pilot on a night VFR flight encountered IMC and requested an ASR approach due to faulty navigation equipment.
summary: The pilot of a Piper Arrow II entered IMC while VFR in Class C airspace due to deteriorating weather and an inoperative VOR. After climbing out of clouds, the pilot requested an IFR clearance and executed a VOR approach to Runway 7L, landing safely after ATC provided radar vectors and a visual approach clearance.

synopsis: LSA pilot reports running out of fuel due to the left fuel tank cap not being secured properly during a fuel stop and the crosswind at the destination being too strong, requiring a diversion to an alternate.
summary: The pilot refueled a single-engine aircraft at ZZZ but failed to secure the port fuel cap, causing fuel loss and an engine failure en route. The pilot declared an emergency, glided to a field, and landed safely after striking a wire fence.

synopsis: When faced with deteriorating engine oil pressure during a return to his departure airport an SR22T pilot learned an important lesson about declaring an emergency in a timely fashion in order to obtain the priority handling from ATC commensurate with his situation.
summary: A pilot flying VFR from ZZZ experienced dropping oil pressure while climbing through 6,000 feet, eventually reaching 2 PSI on short final. After declaring an emergency and being cleared to land behind a departing King Air, the pilot acknowledged they should have declared the emergency earlier.

synopsis: G550 Captain experiences a TCAS RA at 3,000 FT while being vectored for the ILS at TEB. The initial RA is to descend and is then reversed to a climb, then an increase climb. The reporter was in IMC and did not see the intruder and ATC did not provide a traffic advisory.
summary: A Gulfstream G550 pilot vectored for ILS 19 at TEB in IMC received a TCAS descent RA that immediately reversed to climb commands, peaking at 3,800 feet. The pilot followed the conflicting instructions without visual contact or ATC traffic advisories, suspecting a software issue with the aircraft's Certification F equipment.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: A C525 lost pressurization at FL410, so the single pilot declared an emergency and descended to 10,000 FT.
summary: The pilot experienced sudden depressurization at FL410 and declared an emergency. After descending to FL210 and then 10,000 feet following emergency drills, the flight was completed without further issues.

synopsis: CRJ-700 flight crew reported deviation from Whitestone track due in part to wake vortex encounter.
summary: A departing aircraft on the La Guardia 4 Whitestone transition experienced jet wash while turning to heading 040 at 2.4 DME from LGA. After confirming the turn with ATC, the crew received a new heading assignment.

synopsis: AA5B pilot reported losing power shortly after takeoff and landing straight ahead in a field, resulting in some damage to the aircraft.
summary: The pilot experienced a 75% engine power loss at 200 feet AGL during climbout, forcing a landing in an upsloped field to avoid trees. The pilot suspects a carburetor malfunction, noting similar roughness in cold, moist conditions previously resolved by carb heat, resulting in left wing and landing gear damage with no injuries.

synopsis: CE680 First Officer reports a low altitude alert from ATC during a visual approach. An incorrect altimeter setting was being used and also resulted in a speed above 250 knots below 10,000 feet. The short ferry flight and fatigue were cited as factors.
summary: Pilots on a short maintenance ferry flight violated the 250-knot speed limit below 10,000 feet and received a low altitude alert due to using the wrong altimeter setting. The reporter attributed these errors to fatigue, complacency, and distraction during the final leg of a long day.

synopsis: C182 pilot taxiing south on Runway 18 reports an LSA taking off to the north over the C182 pilot. The C182 pilot had announced his intention to back taxi on Runway 18 to an exit on CTAF, but no response was heard, nor was a takeoff announcement broadcast.
summary: A pilot back-taxiing on Runway 18 at Fallbrook Airpark observed another aircraft enter and take off from Runway 36 without radio calls. The pilot stopped at the runway edge as the other aircraft rotated and climbed over them.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A business jet departed OAK on the OAK 6 and during a high climb rate ascent was unable to level off after an amended climb clearance so the pilot took evasive to avoid the near miss traffic also under ATC control.
summary: The pilot of a jet climbing from OAK encountered a TCAS RA after NORCAL issued conflicting turn instructions that directed the aircraft toward a single-engine plane. The pilot followed TCAS commands to avoid a collision within 500 feet, attributing the incident to air traffic control turning the jet into the oncoming light aircraft.

synopsis: PCT Controller described an NMAC event acknowledging a failure to correct an incorrect readback. Controller listed the 'descend via' phraseology as problematic.
summary: An air traffic controller missed a Citation V's incorrect readback of a 9,000-foot restriction, allowing the jet to descend to 8,300 feet and pass only 300 feet above Aircraft Y. The controller attributed the near-miss to ambiguous phraseology regarding altitude restrictions during a "descend via" clearance.

synopsis: VNY Controller described an NMAC involving a departing aircraft and a Helicopter transitioning overtop the airport. The Controller suggested changes be made to existing crossing procedures.
summary: An air traffic controller issued traffic advisories to a helicopter crossing south of its requested Saticoy Street point, placing it below a departing Cessna 172. The controller attributed the proximity to the helicopter deviating from the designated crossing location and recommended updating operational brochures to clarify crossing points.

synopsis: B737-800 First Officer reported losing LOC capture on approach to SFO for unknown reasons.
summary: The pilot flying hand-flew an ILS approach to SFO Runway 28L after encountering wake turbulence from a preceding B747. The aircraft unexpectedly lost localizer capture and defaulted to heading select mode at 700 feet, but the pilot manually recovered the course for a safe landing.

synopsis: The flight crew of a CE-680 declared an emergency and returned to their departure airport when smoke and/or haze filled the cabin and cockpit shortly after takeoff. Shortly before landing the pilot not flying closed an unspecified Left Side Bleed Valve and the smoke started to dissipate. The aircraft was evacuated on a taxiway after exiting the runway.
summary: During climb, a pilot and co-pilot encountered cabin smoke originating from the lavatory, prompting an emergency return. Shutting off the APU and left bleed valve stopped the smoke, allowing a normal landing and taxiway evacuation with no injuries to the two crew or five passengers.

synopsis: At FL430, owner of a GIII hit his head on an electrical gang bar in the cockpit causing loss of electrical power and cabin decompression. Electrical power restored at 16,000 FT and aircraft landed without further incident.
summary: The aircraft owner struck his head on a cockpit gang bar at FL430, causing total electrical failure and depressurization. The crew performed an emergency descent to 16,000 feet to restore power, using iPads for navigation while the owner suffered hypoxia before a safe landing.

synopsis: SCT Controller described a conflict event when right downwind traffic for the south complex was crossed in front of straight in traffic for the north complex.
summary: An air traffic controller failed to restrict straight-in traffic or issue visual separation while a CRJ crossed in front of a B737 on downwind. The CRJ passed the B737 with only 500 feet of separation, though the B737 pilot reported no conflict.

synopsis: Tower CIC witnessed a conflict event involving departing traffic and an aircraft on a missed approach, the reporter noted the Local Controller failed to ensure separation.
summary: A CIC controller observed a PA28 on a missed approach passing within 200 feet of a Remos departing Runway 9 after the Local Controller cleared both aircraft simultaneously. The incident resulted from a lack of separation awareness and confusion regarding the legality of using a missed approach to separate intersecting runway operations.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reports that both the government and commercial charts depict the Runway 33L PAPI at BOS to be on the left side of the runway. In fact it is on the right side of the runway.
summary: The flight crew on an ILS 33L approach at BOS discovered the PAPI was located on the right side of the runway, contrary to charts showing it on the left. After verifying their setup was correct, they contacted Tower, who was unaware of the discrepancy, prompting a recommendation to update the charts.

synopsis: A Dash 8-400 encountered wake vortices from a heavy Airbus on approach to EWR.
summary: Pilots flying a jet during approach encountered severe wake turbulence from a preceding heavy Airbus, causing autopilot disconnect and an altitude deviation to 2,730 feet. The crew manually recovered the aircraft and notified ATC, who provided no comment on the deviation or traffic separation.

synopsis: During landing neither F-20 normal nor alternate brakes operated normally so near the runway's end, the Captain turned the aircraft off the runway across a muddy grass area, contacting several taxi lights and the re-entering a taxiway where it stopped with little apparent damage.
summary: The flight crew experienced insufficient braking on Runway 6 after landing, despite deploying airbrakes and attempting both primary and secondary brake systems with antiskid disarmed. To avoid a runway-end drop-off, the Captain turned right off the pavement, damaging taxi lights before stopping on a parallel taxiway with no obvious aircraft damage.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reports that the wind velocity and direction reported by SVMI Tower is rarely accurate.
summary: The First Officer departing SVMI in December 2013 observed a strong westerly tailwind on Runway 10, contradicting the Tower's reported 090-degree easterly wind. The crew adjusted performance data for the tailwind and departed safely, though the reporter noted that landing aircraft lacked this critical wind information.

synopsis: B757 Captain experiences a left AC Bus failure at FL350. The QRH is consulted and a generator reset is attempted without success. Flight diverts to a suitable airport.
summary: The crew experienced a left generator failure and bus isolation during cruise, triggering multiple EICAS messages. After unsuccessful reset attempts and contacting maintenance, they declared an emergency and diverted for a normal landing with the equipment still inoperative.

synopsis: Following deicing of the B737-800 at the gate an alert passenger advised a flight attendant the wing was still covered in ice. The attendant informed the Captain who checked, agreed with the passenger and refused the aircraft until it was de-iced properly.
summary: The Captain discovered ice on the wings after a passenger reported it, despite the deicing crew claiming completion. The aircraft required a second deicing because the crew failed to verify the surface was clear or provide required fluid and personnel details.

synopsis: MD11 flight crew reports descending below the FAF altitude at REEBO during the LOC Runway 27 approach to SAN due to inattention and not using the PROF autoflight function. The Tower and the pilot not flying both take notice and the approach path is corrected to the PAPI's and a visual approach clearance is issued.
summary: The pilot flying a non-ILS localizer approach to San Diego Runway 27 failed to engage the PROF mode, causing a late configuration and descent below the 1,800-foot crossing altitude at REEBO. After the tower reported the aircraft low, the crew climbed, intercepted the glidepath, and completed a normal landing.

synopsis: After failing to completely retract or extend the nose gear, the single pilot Beech King Air elected to land in an emergency condition at his departure airport. During the landing roll-out the nose gear collapsed and the aircraft slid to a stop, still on the hard surface of the runway.
summary: The sole pilot experienced a nose gear collapse during landing after the gear failed to retract and manual extension attempts were unsuccessful. The aircraft skidded 600 feet off the runway centerline but came to a stop with no injuries.

synopsis: A Lead Technician and Line Technician are informed that a Cessna C-404 aircraft they had replaced a left pneumatic pump on had declared an emergency, shut down the Left engine due to low oil pressure and diverted. Working outside in snow, cold, dark with very little lighting, heavy workload and lack of communication contributed to one bolt and nut not be properly tightened.
summary: Two mechanics replaced an inoperative left pneumatic pump on a Cessna at ZZZ but failed to tighten one of four nuts due to cold, darkness, interruptions, and poor communication. The loose nut caused an oil leak, forcing the pilot to declare an emergency, shut down the left engine, and divert to ZZZ1 for repairs.

synopsis: A Captain and First Officer report a very loud squeal sound and vibration could be heard and felt throughout the cabin as their B737-800 ETOPS aircraft climbed through 17,000 FT. Emergency declared and aircraft returned to departure airport. Cabin pressurization had remained normal.
summary: The flight crew returned to ZZZ after a loud squeal and vibration from Door 1L occurred during climb, despite a prior ground pressurization test. An emergency was declared, resulting in an overweight landing and a subsequent aircraft swap to complete the flight.

synopsis: B777 First Officer reports a taxiway incursion at RJAA while attempting to comply with taxi instructions to the gate after landing. A complicated taxi route, poor signage and construction were cited as factors.
summary: The crew inadvertently passed Taxiway C while taxiing at RJAA at night due to poor signage and new construction. Ground controllers cleared them to continue straight on S4 and turn left on R to the gate, with no safety issues reported.

synopsis: B757 flight crew experienced a TE Flap Disagree on final approach when selecting Flaps 25. Flaps stayed at 20 and crew landed at adjusted speed without incident.
summary: During an ILS approach in VMC, the crew received a TE FLAP DISAGREE message after selecting Flaps 25, as the gauge indicated Flaps 20. They landed safely with Flaps 20, and the flaps automatically extended to match the lever position while parked at the gate.

synopsis: An A320 crew on the DEN 35L ILS took evasive action in response to a TCAS DESCEND command with lower abeam traffic on the 35R ILS, but the command reversed to the correct CLIMB command after about 10 seconds. A go-around was initiated at that point.
summary: A flight crew conducting an ILS approach to Runway 35L at Denver received conflicting TCAS Resolution Advisories due to an aircraft on the parallel Runway 35R approach. The crew followed the commands, initiated a go-around to regain a stabilized profile, and noted that Tower did not acknowledge their TCAS callouts.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew descended below the glideslope inside the Final Approach Fix, but corrected back to the glideslope after discovering that the VNAV was in pitch mode.
summary: During an ILS approach to Runway 22, the crew descended below the glideslope because VNAV was in pitch mode despite the approach being selected. The First Officer identified the error, allowing the Captain to add power and re-intercept the glideslope for a visual landing, attributing the deviation to complacency and failure to verify automation on the PFD.

synopsis: The flight crew of a B757-200 was forced to take lateral, low altitude evasive action with reference to a helicopter hovering at the far end of their takeoff runway. Tower had advised of the helo's presence, holding for clearance to cross, but the flight crew did not have it in sight until after lift off.
summary: The Pilot Not Flying reported a close encounter with a Robinson helicopter at 500 feet AGL after takeoff, attributing the risk to the controller's clearance and the Captain's delayed response. The pilot executed a 10-degree right bank to increase lateral and vertical clearance, resulting in a final separation of less than 1,000 feet.

synopsis: Upon entering icing conditions on final approach, B737 flight crew received Engine Thermal Anti-Ice inoperative indication for the Number Two Engine and continued the approach to an uneventful landing.
summary: During an ILS approach at 2,500 feet, the crew encountered icing and activated engine TAI, but the Number Two Engine TAI displayed a disagreement indication that persisted after cycling. Citing low fuel and the necessity to descend through the thin cloud deck regardless, the pilots elected to continue the approach with the TAI inoperative rather than execute a go-around.

synopsis: A B737-800 Captain and First Officer discovered their oxygen mask pressures at 0 PSI during the preflight mask test and maintenance discovered the oxygen bottle valve not fully open after the bottle had been replaced the previous night.
summary: During preflight, pilots found crew oxygen pressure dropped to zero when testing masks, despite a bottle replacement the previous night. Maintenance identified the crew oxygen valve was not fully open, corrected it, safety wired it, and signed off the logbook.

synopsis: A Captain and First Officer report about snow melting from the top of freight cans loaded in the Forward Cargo pit on an A300 aircraft contributing to excessive water accumulation flowing forward into the Avionic's Compartment. A red ECAM 'AVIONICS SMOKE' message appeared prior to landing. The loss of # 1 and # 2 Generator Control Units (GCUs), including the APU GCU, occurred after landing without any associated Alerts or ECAM messages.
summary: The flight crew experienced an 'AVIONICS SMOKE' warning during descent caused by water from melting snow on cargo cans, which shorted generator control units and smoke detectors. Although the aircraft landed safely, all electrical power was lost upon engine shutdown, requiring maintenance to replace damaged units.

synopsis: SR22 pilot became disoriented on approach in IMC when PFD began displaying erroneous attitude information. After entering stall buffet and receiving ATC and aircraft low altitude alerts, pilot regained control by using standby attitude instruments, returned to VFR and, with ATC assistance, preceded to an uneventful landing at an alternate field.
summary: The pilot experienced PFD flickering and conflicting attitude/heading indications during an ILS approach, leading to an autopilot-induced stall. After disconnecting the autopilot and using standby instruments to recover, the pilot executed a missed approach and safely landed at an alternate airport using GPS.

synopsis: A C182 pilot flying a RNAV/GPS approach was cleared to maintain 1,500 FT until glideslope intercept but continued his descent to 800 FT thinking he would fly into the glideslope while descending.
summary: The pilot descended to 800 FT while cleared to 1,500 FT during an RNAV/GPS approach, prompting a query from Approach Control. The pilot admitted to commencing the descent too early before fully intercepting the glideslope.

synopsis: Enroute Controller described a below MIA event involving an aircraft encountering icing and a controller issuing an incorrect routing.
summary: A C172 pilot en route VFR requested IFR due to mist and diverted for trace rime icing. The aircraft entered a terrain alert volume, experienced mountain wave turbulence causing an uncontrolled descent, but the pilot regained control and completed a visual approach after being vectored clear.

synopsis: A B737-700 Left Engine failed at idle during descent for landing but because the aircraft was high, a go-around was begun, the engine shutdown, an emergency was declared, the QRH completed, and an uneventful landing followed.
summary: During a visual approach at 3,500 feet, the crew experienced severe shaking and engine limits after selecting Flaps 15, leading to an emergency shutdown of the number one engine. Maintenance suspects a shaft separation caused the imbalance, though the crew observed flames and soot despite a normal post-landing inspection.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A pilot at CTAF IWS believed the next arrival aircraft was on base but after getting into position and holding for the previous arrival to clear the runway, another unseen aircraft executed a go-around over him.
summary: A pilot holding short of Runway 15 at non-towered IWS entered the runway while another aircraft on final executed a go-around upon seeing them. The incident, caused by the pilot's failure to detect the final approach aircraft amidst busy traffic, ended without collision.

synopsis: During climb through FL200 both B737-700 engine EEC's transitioned to the Soft Alternate Mode with the Captain's airspeed indicating stall and an inaccurate transponder #1. ADIRU 2 data was functional and indicating an overspeed. Descending out of FL180 all systems returned to normal.
summary: During climbout through FL200, both EECs switched to soft alternate mode, causing conflicting airspeed indications and an overspeed warning. The crew managed the unreliable airspeed, leveled at FL280 after correcting a transponder setting, and completed the flight after systems normalized below FL180.

synopsis: A B737 departed SNA and ATC questioned if they were flying the cancelled DUUKE2.TRM SID after the First Officer folded the PDC in such a way that masked the revised clearance, STREL1.TRM.
summary: The Captain and First Officer departed on the DUUKE2 transition instead of the PDC-issued STREL1 because the First Officer folded the PDC, hiding the routing change. Departure corrected the error shortly after takeoff, and the Captain maneuvered the aircraft back to the STREL1 track, remaining within one mile of the intended path.

synopsis: An EMB-145 flight crew was flummoxed by inappropriate EGPWS call-outs while at high flight levels and a tendency for the aircraft to initiate uncommanded turns to the right. Upon landing nearly full left aileron was required to maintain wings level on approach, despite a crosswind from the right.
summary: The pilot reported a right turn off course on autopilot and false terrain warnings during descent, followed by significant left aileron trim required to maintain straight flight on final approach. Maintenance identified sticking flight controls, leading to an aircraft swap and a logbook entry for the unwanted autopilot turn.

synopsis: A PA-30 pilot thought that he switched from the empty AUX fuel tank to a MAIN, but the selector position was not fully in MAIN so the right engine quit. The pilot declared an emergency and ATC vectored him to a nearby airport.
summary: A solo pilot flying a PA30 Twin Comanche under IFR experienced a right engine failure at 6,000 feet due to fuel starvation caused by a fuel selector valve not fully engaging the main tank. The pilot declared an emergency, was vectored to a nearby airport, and landed safely on Runway 30L.

synopsis: A PA-31 pilot collided with a tree at a remote airport after he misread the RNAV GPS Approach plate and descended to minimums nearly 3 miles from the airport. A go-around was executed, an emergency declared and the flight diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: The pilot misread the approach plate, causing the aircraft to descend too low and encounter a tree during the approach. The pilot executed a missed approach, diverted to a nearby airport, and landed safely with no injuries or significant damage.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reports three missed approaches to Runway 22 at LGA, due to oscillating localizer indications on the first two ILS approaches and CDI oscillations on the third (VOR) approach.
summary: The pilot reported severe localizer oscillations on the ILS Runway 4 approach at LGA, causing two missed approaches and a diversion to ALB. The issue was isolated to the ground-based ILS 4 localizer, as subsequent approaches to Runway 19 at ALB and Runway 22 at LGA functioned correctly.

synopsis: An A319 Flight Attendant crew all detected a wet, dirty socks odor in the forward galley area. The Captain was notified and diverted to a nearby airport where the flight was canceled while the pilots ferried the aircraft to a maintenance base.
summary: Flight attendants reported a wet, dirty sock smell to the Captain, prompting a diversion and six hours of maintenance testing. The flight was subsequently canceled, with cabin crew sent to a hotel and cockpit crew ferried to a maintenance base.

synopsis: An SD-360-300 had a right main landing gear unsafe indication when the gear were lowered, so an emergency was declared, a Tower fly by confirmed gear down, but after landing and stopping on the runway the right gear collapsed.
summary: The Pilot in Command and First Officer of a Shorts 360-300 experienced a right main gear unsafe indication during an ILS 30 approach. Despite completing emergency checklists and a visual low approach, the right gear collapsed on landing, requiring a safe evacuation after the aircraft touched down.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A light twin approaching PHK IFR had a near miss with a VFR aircraft while ZMA was extremely busy with English as a second language pilots on training missions.
summary: Pilots flying IFR to F45 received a descent clearance to 4,000 feet from ZMA while 47 miles from PHK. An ADS-B advisory revealed a VFR aircraft climbing below them, prompting a shallow descent that resulted in a 300-400 foot vertical and 100-foot horizontal separation, which the pilots attributed to controller overload and lack of traffic advisories.

synopsis: PA46 pilot experiences tire failure at rotation speed and elects to reject the takeoff after becoming airborne. Directional control is lost and the aircraft departs the runway causing some damage.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff after a right tire blowout caused the aircraft to veer off the runway into uneven construction ground. The incident resulted in minor damage to the right main gear and aileron, attributed to the aircraft being marginally overweight due to improper pre-flight weight and balance calculations.

synopsis: A MD-11 crew experienced asphyxia during an extended predeparture de-icing with both packs OFF, the outflow valve closed and 14,000 LBS of dry ice on board.
summary: Flight crew and a jumpseater experienced asphyxia symptoms during a one-hour Type 1 de-icing delay caused by a truck breakdown and heavy snow. The incident occurred with packs off and the outflow valve closed, leading to the Captain shutting down the aircraft and opening doors to ventilate the cabin.

synopsis: After takeoff a B737-800 Captain's PFD and HUD lost altitude, airspeed, vertical speed, FMA annunciations, the autothrottle/autopilot would not engage and the yaw damper disengaged. An emergency was declared and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: During climb-out, the Captain lost all PFD and HUD indications while the First Officer lost Flight Director cues, causing autothrottle and autopilot disengagement without fault alerts. The Captain declared an emergency and returned to the airport uneventfully, citing an uncertain cause involving the IRS or FCC.

synopsis: The First Officer of a cargo flight noticed his carbon monoxide monitor alerting at a 0.5 to 0.7 level during de-ice operations with the Packs OFF and dry ice onboard. The crew used oxygen for about 20 minutes until the Packs were ON again.
summary: The flight crew experienced a rising CO2 alarm during de-icing with packs off, requiring them to wear oxygen masks for 20 minutes. After turning packs on, the alarm cleared, and they resumed the flight following advice from the Duty Officer, though exact exposure levels remain unknown.

synopsis: Cessna 414 pilot describes his efforts to regain aircraft control after a violent and sudden pitch down, without any change in his control input. Full back pressure efforts by himself and a ride-along Mechanic were required to pull the aircraft out of the dive. Subsequent inspection revealed, the Right Elevator Trim Tab actuating rod had separated from the tab and jammed the tab in a nose down condition.
summary: The pilot and a mechanic passenger experienced a violent pitch-down dive at 3,000 feet during a visual approach after an engine overhaul. The incident was caused by a broken or fouled trim cable that left the right horizontal elevator stuck in the down position, though the aircraft landed safely.

synopsis: RV-7 pilot reports inadvertent entry into R3002 due inability to see the individual A, B, C areas of R3002 on his moving map display. R3002B was active.
summary: A pilot flying VFR north of Columbus, GA, inadvertently entered restricted airspace R3002 between 4,000 and 8,000 MSL because the Dynon SkyView display obscured the third layer of restrictions. The pilot later contacted Atlanta TRACON and concluded that avoiding the MOA or establishing VHF contact with Columbus ATC would have prevented the incursion.

synopsis: CE-510 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence on approach to LAX in trail of an MD-80.
summary: The Citation Mustang pilot encountered wake turbulence from a preceding MD-80 while on a visual approach to LAX Runway 25L. The pilot attributed the encounter to TRACON instructions to maintain 180 knots at 2,600 feet, which resulted in the aircraft being tossed before the pilot disconnected the autopilot and recovered.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: A C525 pilot flying solo was cleared to 3,000 FT but read back 2,000 FT, a TRACON low altitude alert sounded the Controller recleared the pilot to 2,600 FT.
summary: An air traffic controller and pilot experienced a descent clearance misunderstanding during an ILS 19 approach, causing a low altitude alert at 2,100 feet. The controller attributed the error to a misheard readback of 3,000 feet as 2,000 feet, while the pilot noted the TAWS did not warn despite the altitude preselect being set to 2,000 feet.

synopsis: MD11 flight crew receives a 'Fuel Qty/Used Chk' Level 2 alert. It is determined that a fuel leak may exist in the number one engine and it is shut down and the flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: The RFO and Captain responded to a Level 2 fuel alert during cruise by shutting down Engine #1, declaring an emergency, and dumping 75,000 pounds of fuel. They returned to the departure airport for an uneventful two-engine landing, suspecting a fuel leak downstream of the shutoff valve.

synopsis: MD82 Captain reports the First Officer's compass failure during taxi out on a ferry flight after the aircraft had sat for two days in the rain. Before any remedial action can be taken the problem cleared and the flight departed. Passing 5,000 FT the problem returns and EFIS switching has no effect, and the flight returns to the departure airport. Maintenance attempts to dry out the avionics with hot air with apparent success, but on taxi out the problem returns again.
summary: The crew experienced recurrent Navigation Display compass failures and autopilot disengagement shortly after takeoff due to suspected moisture from a two-day rain delay. They declared an emergency to return for an overweight landing, but the issue recurred on the second taxi, forcing a final return to the gate for maintenance.

synopsis: DC-10 Captain at FL360 reports very loud electrical arcing sound emanating from the avionics bay under the flight deck, followed shortly by blue-white smoke with a very strong ozone smell. Flight diverts to the nearest suitable airport and lands safely. Post flight reveals that the Number Three Avionics Bay Exhaust Fan Motor internally shorted and self-destructed with the fan not operating.
summary: The flight crew experienced electrical arcing and smoke from a shorted Number 3 Avionics Exhaust Fan Motor at FL360, prompting an emergency descent to ZZZ. Maintenance confirmed the fan self-destructed while off due to inadequate circuit breaker protection, though the crew successfully landed the aircraft without fire.

synopsis: A320 Captain reports a TCAS RA approaching BIL at 7,000 FT with a VFR departure, both talking to ATC. ATC makes no attempt to prevent the conflict and the A320 climbs 4,500 FT at TCAS direction.
summary: A pilot approaching Billings (BIL) at 7,000 feet in VMC experienced a TCAS climb resolution advisory due to a VFR aircraft climbing into their path. Although ATC controlled both aircraft, the controller failed to prevent the conflict, resulting in a 400-foot vertical separation.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reports a taxiway incursion at IAD due to distractions and deficiencies in the Airport Diagram.
summary: The pilot reported a taxi conflict on Taxiway Delta while exiting Spot 80, caused by a head-on aircraft with taxi lights on and a third aircraft on Taxiway Y. The pilot paused to avoid a collision, attributing the confusion to visual distractions, a recent concourse change, and unclear airport diagram markings.

synopsis: MD-83 First Officer notes high EGT on the right engine during climb and thrust is reduced and the QRH consulted. The right CSD oil temperature is then discovered to be high and the QRH directs a disconnect. While discussing the situation the aircraft noticeably shook and yawed to the right slightly and the crew elects to return to the departure airport with the right engine at idle.
summary: During climb, the crew encountered high EGT and CSD oil temperature on the right engine, followed by a loud bang and yaw. They declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport, and landed safely with the right engine at idle after following QRH procedures.

synopsis: B737-800 First Officer reports receiving an aircraft from Maintenance with ice on the wings and the flaps full down and a note not to move the flaps until the aircraft has been deiced. After de icing the flaps are set for takeoff and the flight departs. Once airborne the aircraft requires significant rudder and aileron trim to fly straight. A trip to the cabin by the First Officer reveals that the right TE flap is not fully retracted and that two spoilers are partially extended. An emergency is declared and the flight returns to the departure airport for flaps up landing.
summary: The pilot reported that after deicing, the right trailing edge flap and two spoilers failed to retract during takeoff despite no cockpit indications. The crew declared an emergency, returned, and landed safely using the all-flaps-up procedure, discovering significant damage to the flap linkage.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reports discovering during preflight that the crew oxygen system is not functional. Maintenance discovers that the valve is turned off and safety wired in that position, and had likely been that way for over a month. The Captain believes that the late discovery is the result of no training on how to preflight the system.
summary: The Captain and First Officer discovered the cockpit oxygen system was inoperative during preflight because the bottle valve was safety-wired closed and the regulator was leaking.
