The incident resulted from the controller's failure to maintain a proper scan during radio communications, leading to an uncoordinated descent.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: PCT Controller reports of coordination problem between two controllers which leads to aircraft having to be re-sequenced.
summary: An air traffic controller in the DCA feed sector coordinated a nonstandard aircraft but issued an ineffective sequence, leaving the aircraft too high for approach at 3,000 feet. The controller rejected the feeder's suggested 270 heading and instead assigned a 160 heading back into final, creating a conflict with traffic 25 DME out.

synopsis: B757 Captain reports a TCAS RA approaching KADDY on the arrival to LAS. Evasive action is taken.
summary: During the TYSSN 3 arrival to LAS, the crew received a TCAS RA to climb due to a Cirrus VFR aircraft reported at 11,500 feet but displayed at 11,800 feet. The crew climbed to 12,500 feet to resolve the conflict, advised LA Center, and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: When cleared to hold '...west, as published at FL370...' at GVE the flight crew of a CRJ-700 entered the pattern utilizing standard 1.5 minute legs. Center took exception, advising that 'as published' restricted outbound legs to 10NM.
summary: The flight crew holding at GVE at FL370 was advised by ATC that their 13 NM FMS hold exceeded the 10 NM limit for a published hold. The crew reprogrammed the FMS to 10 NM, and the reporter noted that ATC should specify desired holding distances to prevent such discrepancies.

synopsis: The flight crew of a CRJ-700 failed to comply with the crossing restriction at ARGAL on the KAROO RNAV STAR to RDU.
summary: During the KAROO arrival into RDU, the Captain descended 500 feet below the charted altitude at ARGAL by selecting an incorrect vertical speed to meet the final restriction. The crew immediately climbed back to the correct altitude, and the incident was attributed to setting a single descent rate rather than programming individual altitude floors sequentially.

synopsis: A pilot reported the SDP (PASD) CTAF and pilot controlled lighting frequency was recently changed per the latest published Alaska supplement and Alaska Terminal procedures. Despite the frequency change on the published charts to 122.8, pilots wishing to control runway lighting must use the previous frequency of 122.3.
summary: Pilots reported a discrepancy at Sand Point (PASD) where the published CTAF and lighting frequency changed to 122.8, but the equipment still operates on 122.3. No NOTAM has been issued despite reports to Anchorage Center and Kenai FSS, leaving aircraft without the intended FSS monitoring on the new frequency.

synopsis: Just as they were about to intercept the localizer in IMC the flight crew of an MD-83 suffered the loss of first the Captain's PFD, ND, autothrottles and MCP panel and, after passing control to the First Officer, his PFD and ND failed as well. A go-around was initiated on standby instruments during which they encountered a windshear alert warning accompanied by associated significant performance degradation. An ATC assisted diversion to another airport for a fuel mandated downwind emergency landing was nearly an anticlimactic conclusion.
summary: The Pilot Flying and First Officer experienced simultaneous primary flight instrument failures and a windshear warning during an ILS approach in IMC, forcing a go-around and escape maneuver using standby instruments. They diverted to an alternate airport with emergency fuel, landing opposite the active runway after recovering from the shear and instrument loss.

synopsis: When Master Caution GEN 2 OFF illuminated after takeoff, CRJ-200 Captain inadvertently selected GEN 1 for reset thereby deploying the ADG. Flight crew returned to departure airport for uneventful landing.
summary: The pilot inadvertently reset the wrong generator switch at 1,000 feet AGL, causing an inadvertent ADG deployment and multiple caution messages. The crew returned to the departure airport for a safe landing after correcting the error and completing the appropriate checklists.

synopsis: A319 Captain reports that the Airbus FMGC will ignore MEA and airspeed requirements on the HHOOD 2 to Runway's 28 at PDX if left to its own devices.
summary: A pilot reported a potential terrain conflict on the HHOOD 2 RNAV arrival to PDX where the Airbus FMGC descended below the 7,200 FT MEA between HHOOD and BLRUN. The system ignored the 240 KTS restriction at SHAFR to achieve 6,700 FT, causing the aircraft to fly 500 feet below the minimum enroute altitude if following the VNAV path.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain describes problems viewing saved PDF's on his iPad since the change from OS6 to OS7, with pages taking up to 30 seconds to come into focus.
summary: A pilot reported that upgrading an iPad to OS7 caused 25-30 second delays when viewing Sabre-generated flight plan PDFs, unlike other files. The reporter attributed this issue to the Sabre software, noting it could hinder timely access to critical information like NOTAMs and weather if physical copies are unavailable.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported being issued holding instructions to hold at PEEKO on the back course to Runway 10 at OME, right turns with the First Officer flying. After 20 minutes of holding they are cleared for the LOC DME (BACK CRS) Runway 10. After commencing the procedure turn and starting descent the crew is advised by ATC that they are north of course heading towards high terrain and to climb to 6,000 FT being completely confused the Captain asks to start over from the VOR, which is accomplished successfully.
summary: The Captain and First Officer lost situational awareness while holding at PEEKO for a LOC DME approach to Runway 10, causing them to drift north of course and requiring an emergency climb to 6,000 feet. The incident resulted from the Captain's distraction, poor CRM, inappropriate navigation aid selection, and potential fatigue or compass discrepancies.

synopsis: B737 Captain on the ILS 16R to PAE reports a NMAC with a C172 just inside JUGBA. The C172 was talking to the Tower and the B737 was talking to Approach. A TCAS RA is received and complied with along with a turn away from the traffic.
summary: Aircrew on an ILS 16R approach at PAE received a warning of a non-communicating Cessna 172 crossing the path. An RA occurred when the C172 turned toward the aircraft, prompting a descent and turn to avoid the traffic, which appeared less than 500 feet away.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot reports of RA and airspace/traffic problems associated with the Class Bravo airspace at Phoenix.
summary: Pilots descending into KSDL on the JCOBS2 arrival received a descent to 7,000 feet from Phoenix Approach, resulting in a TCAS Resolution Advisory due to a climbing VFR aircraft. The reporter attributes the conflict to the controller's failure to maintain lateral separation from VFR traffic outside Class B airspace.

synopsis: The pilot of a C172 returning to base suffered a rough running engine which forced a safely conducted off airport landing. When he sumped the tanks and gascolator he discovered water in both. After appropriate ameliorative, testing and planning measures the flight back to base was conducted without further incident.
summary: The pilot experienced engine roughness during descent to traffic pattern altitude due to water in both fuel tanks and the gascolator. After a safe off-airport landing, the pilot purged the water, verified airworthiness, and returned to base without further incident.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot thinks he has clearance to cross an active runway, then while crossing, questions if he really did.
summary: A pilot and student holding short at taxiway D for a Runway 12R crossing clearance mistakenly began moving after hearing the Ground Controller say, "No need to respond, I acknowledge your patience." The pilot stopped upon realizing the phrase was not a crossing instruction, attributing the error to complacency and confusing standard acknowledgments with clearances.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot is told to fly published missed approach procedure while executing a go around from a visual approach. This along with a minor mechanical problem adds confusion for the pilot.
summary: A pilot executing a visual approach to Runway 9 at KSAN initiated a go-around due to a flap in-op light. The tower controller incorrectly instructed the crew to fly the published missed approach instead of issuing a heading and altitude, causing communication confusion until supervisors acknowledged the error.

synopsis: A C208B instructor reported the TKS fluid vaporization increases in high OAT conditions and the effects are not dissipating after repeated exposure. The reporter became nauseous and vomited after flight.
summary: Two pilots on a training flight in a TKS-equipped Caravan experienced severe respiratory distress and nausea after activating the anti-ice system in extreme heat. The reporter attributes these health effects to TKS fluid dripping into the cabin vent intake, causing hazardous vapor contamination.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: N90 Controller makes a request to change airspace related to IFR operations and VFR Helicopter operations.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a 600-foot vertical separation loss between Aircraft X at 2,500 feet and Aircraft Y at 1,900 feet over Manhattan during a visual approach to Runway 31. The controller attributed the conflict to Tower airspace restrictions allowing VFR traffic at 2,000 feet up the LGA 230 radial instead of the 240 radial.

synopsis: ZJX Controller describes situation where coordination between ATC facilities is not correct and finds this out from the pilot while exiting a warning area.
summary: ATC received two fighter groups from Double-Shot Approach that were incorrectly coordinated as a single formation with less than standard separation. The controller re-established separation after the pilots clarified they were two distinct flights, noting the error caused unnecessary distraction during high-traffic conditions.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reports an EGPWS 'Caution Obstacle' warning during a night visual approach to Runway 31L due to an overshoot to the left. The flying First Officer corrects to centerline and continues to a normal landing in violation of company SOP.
summary: During a night visual approach to Runway 31L at DAL, the First Officer overcorrected for a tailwind, triggering a GPWS obstacle caution. Although the crew continued the landing, they acknowledged violating company procedures by not executing a mandatory go-around.

synopsis: While exiting EWR Runway 29 at W2 after landing, an air carrier crew missed the Taxiway Y sign on Taxiway RM and entered Taxiway A. Reportedly, the signage is confusing or not visible.
summary: The flight crew misinterpreted a Taxiway Yankee sign at Newark after crossing a concrete block, inadvertently entering Taxiway Alpha instead of holding short of Uniform. The pilot attributed the error to non-standard sign placement and plans to request clarification from Ground in the future.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports difficulty complying with a circle to land clearance at LGA resulting in ATC issuing a climb and vectors for another approach. It was night with rain showers and the crew was new to the airport. The second attempt was successful.
summary: The pilot flying and pilot monitoring at LGA lost visual contact during a night ILS Runway 04 circle-to-31 approach due to rain, city lights, and an incomplete briefing on DME sources. This caused them to exit circling airspace, prompting ATC to vector them for a climb and re-approach, which they completed safely.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports receiving a Takeoff Warning Horn for flaps and rejecting the takeoff at 15 knots. A loose cannon plug in one of the flap indication circuits was found to be the cause.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff at 15 knots due to a configuration warning horn caused by a loose flap indication cannon plug. The incident resulted from the pilot's failure to verify flap position during pre-taxi checks due to complacency and rushing.

synopsis: After departure a B737 bleeds and packs would not operate to pressurize the aircraft. After troubleshooting at 8,000 FT they returned to the departure airport where Pressurization Control Computer in the E&E was found unracked.
summary: The crew experienced a main pressurization controller failure and loss of engine bleed pressure during climb, forcing a return to the departure airport. Maintenance later found an un-racked computer in the EE compartment caused the issue, which was resolved by re-racking the unit.

synopsis: EMB145 Captain receives a No Takeoff, configuration warning on EICAS at 45 knots and rejects the takeoff. A spoiler indication circuit breaker was found tripped along with a spoiler fail message on the EICAS. Flight returns to the gate for an aircraft swap.
summary: The Captain aborted takeoff at 45 knots after a No Takeoff configuration warning and a spoiler fail message appeared due to a popped spoiler indication circuit breaker. The crew taxied clear, logged the fault, and swapped aircraft, suspecting a false spoiler indication caused by an electrical short.

synopsis: Confused by ATC's initial approach clearance to the ILS 4R at LGA, the an air carrier flight crew struggled with the Tower's subsequent clearance to cross GRENE at 2700 (as published), cleared for the ILS to Runway 4R.
summary: Pilots flying an ILS 04 approach to LGA received conflicting clearances to stay on the glideslope and cross GRENE at 2,700 feet. The crew descended below the glideslope to meet the restriction but missed it by approximately 700 feet due to the confusing sequence of instructions.

synopsis: A CE560 First Officer encountered wake vortices from an A340 while landing at ORD.
summary: A pilot flying a small jet encountered wake turbulence from an Airbus A340 at 300 feet AGL while approaching Runway 10C at O'Hare. The aircraft pitched down and rolled left, requiring a go-around after the pilot struggled to disconnect the yaw damper and manage thrust.

synopsis: When a series of behavioral hints and suspicious events before, during and after their transatlantic flight brought into question the Captain's fitness for flight, the flight attendants made it clear that, in their opinion, he was not fit to fly the return flight.
summary: Flight attendants reported that the Captain appeared extremely ill during the flight and struggled to move upon arrival, yet they were not briefed on his condition until after landing. The crew expressed concern that the Captain was unfit to fly and criticized the decision to withhold this information from them during the flight.

synopsis: Pilot reports renting a Citabria with a previous write up concerning the fuel selector and is assured by the desk that the selector has been checked and released by Maintenance. After takeoff intermittent power loss is noted and the pilot returns to the departure airport after notifying the Tower of his problem and intentions.
summary: The pilot experienced intermittent power loss of 300-500 RPM during the initial climb and crosswind turn in a pleasure flight. Despite a pre-flight fuel selector squawk being cleared by maintenance, the pilot suspected fuel starvation, executed a short approach, and landed safely with no damage.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: CE525 Captain reports landing long at an unfamiliar airport and not being able to stop before the end of the runway.
summary: The pilot, on their first landing at this airport, cancelled IFR and landed long due to a shortened final approach and delayed descent. The aircraft overran the runway, rolled into grass, and entered a pond because a go-around was deemed unsafe once the pilot realized they would not stop.

synopsis: C172 pilot reports a harrowing flight through a thunderstorm encountered in the last ten minutes flight, despite all efforts to avoid heavy weather using ADS-B, ASOS and ATIS. A successful landing in 50 knot winds ensues.
summary: The pilot of a C172 with two passengers encountered severe turbulence and a sudden downdraft while approaching EDE in a thunderstorm, despite prior weather monitoring. The aircraft was lifted off the runway by 53 MPH surface winds upon landing, requiring a second landing and careful taxiing to a hangar to avoid flipping.

synopsis: PA18 pilot reports taxi out to Runway 13 using CTAF radio procedures and notes a BE58 going the other way without communicating. The takeoff is announced on Runway 13 and the takeoff initiated. Once airborne the BE58 is sighted below departing on the intersecting runway.
summary: The pilot reported a near mid-air collision with a Beechcraft Baron while departing RWY 13 after the Baron crossed the intersecting runway without making any CTAF position reports. The Baron had obtained ATC clearance but failed to announce its movements, creating a conflict at approximately 400 feet AGL.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZOB Controller reports to work and before shift starts another controller gives a briefing to no one, and then leaves the room. Controller reporting to work has to start work before officially being at work.
summary: A controller left an unmanned sector with a dummy jack plugged in and the frequency not selected to speaker before their shift ended. The relieving controller had to locate a handset to issue a descent clearance, causing a communication delay that frustrated the pilot and created an unsafe situation.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported encountering wake turbulence in trail of another B737NG on descent to PHX.
summary: During descent on the EAGUL Five arrival into PHX, a B737NG encountered unexpected wake turbulence from a preceding B737NG, causing significant banking. The event resulted in a flight attendant sustaining a neck injury, which the pilot attributed to strong headwinds delaying wake dissipation despite 20-mile separation.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reports a navigational error entering the NATS at 47N50W after a reroute is issued by Gander. The three new waypoints required are entered with a leading 'N' instead of a trailing 'N' producing a waypoint that is accepted by the FMC but a half a degree north of the desired latitude. This error is detected by Gander and the cause is known.
summary: The flight crew entered oceanic waypoints with a leading 'N' instead of trailing, causing a 30 NM north deviation during the enroute phase. Gander Oceanic detected the error and directed a course correction, which the crew executed after correcting the FMC format.

synopsis: An A320 series Captain noted that exiting SFO Runway 28L, Taxiway T left edge lights are inoperable which makes early identification of that taxiway difficult.
summary: A pilot reported missing taxiway edge lights on the left side while exiting SFO Runway 28L onto Taxiway T. The absence of lighting made it difficult to distinguish Taxiway T from the nearby Taxiways D and K.

synopsis: Flight crew reports discovering a biohazard shipment onboard at an intermediate stop which has no paperwork. The shipment is left behind.
summary: During unloading, the Captain found unlabeled boxes with biohazard placards and no shipper's declaration. Due to conflicting advice on paperwork requirements, the Captain left the boxes behind.

synopsis: A pilot was unable to raise the nose landing gear after departure due to the installation of a non-standard landing gear pin that was not removed by maintenance personnel following the replacement of the nose landing gear tires.
summary: A mechanic substituted a 6-foot socket extension for a nose gear safety pin during maintenance, causing a false "Gear NOT UPLOCKED" indication at FL210. The crew declared Minimum Fuel, continued to the destination, and landed safely after discovering the extension in the gear slot.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain as flying pilot reports loss of the First Officer's airspeed indication at FL340 along with lightening and a burning smell. Captain elects to divert to an alternate and an emergency is declared. During descent the pressurization system failed and the First Officer's airspeed indicator begin working.
summary: The crew diverted from FL340 due to a frozen First Officer pitot tube and lightning, causing airspeed loss, autopilot failure, and pressurization failure. They descended below 10,000 feet where the pitot unfroze, then landed uneventfully at ZZZ1 with an ADC failure attributed to freezing conditions and convective weather.

synopsis: A Captain questions Maintenance Control on the legality of using an MEL deferral for Maintenance lights on a CRJ-200 aircraft as an acceptable practice for also allowing a Circuit Breaker (C/B) to be 'Opened' and collared without any Maintenance Procedure or reference in the MEL. Pilot also concerned about possible wire harness chafing and electrical shorts not identified as cause of inoperative lights.
summary: The flight crew deferred an open circuit breaker using a remotely associated MEL after Maintenance Control cited General Maintenance Manual 2 8.3, despite concerns about a probable electrical short. The captain and first officer flew with hesitation, fearing the practice exploited procedures and risked harness chaffing or further system failures.

synopsis: EMB145 Captain experiences low hydraulic quantity in system number one during cruise and continues to destination. On short final an EICAS Brake Degrade message is displayed, discussed and a normal landing ensues. When the parking brake is set a loud hissing noise is heard and rapidly declining hydraulic system two quantity is noted. With the chocks in the engine is shut down and the parking brake is released. A large puddle of hydraulic fluid is reported around the right main gear.
summary: The flight crew experienced a hydraulic leak during cruise that worsened on the ground, causing a loss of all hydraulic systems and emergency brakes after setting the parking brake. The reporter attributes the rapid fluid loss to the emergency air brake bottle pushing fluid out and recommends more frequent inspections and full system topping.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer on a visual approach backed up by the localizer, overshot the runway by lining up on a parallel runway. A slow to intercept autopilot was a factor in not recognizing the error.
summary: The pilot accepted a visual approach for Runway 16L but mistakenly identified the parallel runway, causing the localizer to swing opposite and the autopilot to initiate an incorrect turn. The pilot disconnected the autopilot, corrected the course, and landed safely, attributing the error to complacency and failure to verify the runway.

synopsis: B737-400 flight crew detects smoke during climbout and isolates it to the First Officer's left yoke hand grip which is hot. All instrument lighting is turned off and the yoke begins to cool. Crew elects to divert to a suitable airport.
summary: During climb, pilots detected smoke and a burning smell from a failed light assembly on the First Officer's yoke thumb wheel. They turned off instrument lighting, discontinued the checklist as fumes dissipated, and diverted to ZZZ1 for an uneventful landing.

synopsis: B737-900 Captain reported wake turbulence from a B747 on approach to SEA on a parallel runway that resulted in a 45 degree bank.
summary: The pilot hand-flew a clean aircraft on visual approach to Runway 16R at 4,200 feet when wake turbulence from a preceding B747 caused an abrupt 45-degree bank. The pilot recovered by adding power and unloading, intercepting the glideslope for a stable, uneventful landing.

synopsis: Large wide bodied flight crew becomes confused during taxi to gate 218 at LAX due to construction on Taxiway E and uses the lead out line from Gate 209 as a shortcut to Gate 218. The Tower has the crew hold position while an airport vehicle is dispatched to check for FOD. A note on the Airport Diagram prohibits this maneuver.
summary: The flight crew at LAX mistakenly entered a poorly marked lead-in line for Gate 209 while taxiing to Gate 218 due to construction closures and confusing ramp diagrams. Tower instructed them to hold for a FOD check before Ground cleared them to proceed, with no safety compromise reported.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew descending early from minimums for landing on Runway 13L at JFK using the VOR or GPS RWY 13L/R approach with a ceiling of 1,000 feet. The Captain recognizes the error at the same time the Tower issues a low altitude alert. Flight continues to a normal landing.
summary: During a VOR/GPS 13L approach to JFK in low ceilings, the crew initiated a 700 fpm descent at DMYHL, which proved too steep for the remaining distance. The pilot leveled off above 500 feet after a Tower altitude warning and completed a normal landing on Runway 13L.

synopsis: An A300 number 1 engine anti-ice valve faulted during descent through overcast at FL240 so the crew asked for deviation clear of clouds, only penetrating a non-freezing layer before landing.
summary: During descent through clouds at FL240, an engine anti-ice valve faulted on Engine 1. The crew turned left with ATC clearance to avoid clouds but descended through a lower overcast layer due to fuel constraints, with no icing encountered and the event logged for maintenance.

synopsis: ATC issued a B777 clearance from FL200 to FL210 with opposite direction traffic and the TCAS RA alerted as the aircraft leveled with VNAV engaged, quieting the alert.
summary: Pilots climbing a light aircraft from FL200 to FL210 in VNAV received a TCAS RA to level off at FL207 due to a high climb rate of 2500 FPM. The crew acknowledged that using VERT Speed after the TA might have prevented the RA, though the conflicting traffic passed safely above and behind.

synopsis: B757 Captain experiences a failure of the left hydraulic system ten minutes into flight and returns to the departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced a left hydraulic system leak and total fluid loss about 10 minutes into flight, causing system failure. They declared an emergency, returned for an uneventful landing using alternate flap and gear extension without nose wheel steering, but the leak's cause remains unknown.

aircraft: McDonnell Douglas Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: MCD widebody cargo flight crew experiences a frozen number two thrust lever when commencing descent from FL350. After holding at 4000 feet for 25 minutes in hopes of a thaw, the engine is shut down and a two engine approach and landing ensues. Ice from water deposited by a thunderstorm during loading is thought to be the cause.
summary: During descent from FL350, the crew found #2 throttle frozen at 83% N1, suspected due to frozen water from thunderstorms. They held at 4000 feet, declared an emergency, shut down the engine per QRH, and completed an uneventful autoland.

synopsis: At FL260, an MD11 EICAS alerted GEN 1 OFF followed by GEN 3, TR 3 and BAT DISCHARGE alerts. An emergency was declared, the QRH procedures were completed and the flight diverted to the nearest aairport.
summary: The crew diverted an aircraft during climb after multiple electrical generator and battery alerts, likely caused by water ingress during heavy rain. They landed safely at a nearby VFR airport following ATC vectors and QRH procedures, with the pilot recommending mandatory pre-flight electrical compartment inspections in wet conditions.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 pushed back and started engines on an ice and snow covered ramp. When the 14Th Stage ISOL Valve Check light illuminated, the Captain momentarily advanced the thrust lever causing the aircraft skidded forward onto the tow bar, even with the brakes set.
summary: The Captain of a CRJ-200 inadvertently cracked thrust levers during a contaminated ramp pushback, causing the aircraft to slide three feet and rest on the tow bar. The incident resulted from unreported slush, worn tires, and the Captain's failure to follow abnormal operations procedures while rushing to recover a delay.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Captain noted the lack of visibility of the SYR gate lead in line lines and his inability to determine his aircraft's position relative to the gate.
summary: The Captain and First Officer stopped the aircraft during taxi-in at Syracuse (SYR) Gate X due to poorly painted, nearly invisible yellow taxi lines. Ground personnel and the Gate Agent confirmed the poor visibility of the markings, raising safety concerns for future operations in adverse weather or at night.

synopsis: B737-900 flight attendants report difficulty using the Medlink headset for a passenger emergency due inappropriate conversation by the flight crew that blocks the Medlink conversation. The attending physician believes the stethoscope from the EMK is of poor quality and jeopardizes passenger care.
summary: During a medical emergency involving a passenger with rapid heartbeat, flight attendants were distracted by the flight deck's loud, inappropriate conversation over the Medlink headset. The reporter attributed the communication difficulty and lack of professional support to the pilots' behavior and noted that the stethoscope was also inadequate.

synopsis: PA-28 instructor in the pattern for Runway 31 with a new student reports a C150 entering the pattern for Runway 21 causing several conflicts before departing the pattern. The wind slightly favored Runway 21, but Runway 31 was in use when the instructor arrived and saw no reason to switch, which seemed to annoy the C150 pilot.
summary: An instructor and student flying a pattern for Runway 31 executed a go-around when a Cessna 150 on Runway 21 approached the intersection, followed by a non-standard downwind to avoid the Cessna's low pass. The reporter attributed the conflict to the Cessna pilot's unprofessional radio conduct and lack of standard pattern procedures.

synopsis: A Glider Tow Pilot taking off on the runway reported his tow released at about 50 FT, then both aircraft took evasive action because of an impending near miss with a aircraft which depart the runway and failed to make or acknowledge CTAF pre-takeoff and takeoff calls from the Tow Pilot.
summary: A tow plane and glider experienced a near mid-air collision with a single-engine Diamond aircraft during takeoff from crossing runways at an uncontrolled airport. The conflict occurred because the Diamond pilot failed to make radio calls or take evasive action, forcing the tow pilot to release the glider and execute a steep turn to avoid impact.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Pilot reports of confusion due to a non-towered airport using a frequency to issue IFR Clearances, while pilots thought this was an actual Tower and not using the airport CTAF for position reports.
summary: Pilots departing Anniston (ANB) under IFR after a NASCAR race faced confusion due to conflicting instructions between the NTAP and FBO papers regarding contact procedures. The FBO's use of the call sign "Anniston Tower" at a non-towered airport led pilots to incorrectly request taxi clearances instead of using CTAF.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: MSN Controller drops IFR tag not realizing it and later has conflict with other IFR aircraft causing a loss of separation.
summary: An air traffic controller inadvertently dropped the data block for Aircraft Y while managing Aircraft X's descent, mistaking the remaining altitude splat for a VFR target. This error caused a loss of separation where Aircraft Y passed 300 feet vertically and 2 miles behind Aircraft X before the controller realized the mistake.

synopsis: Two ZSU controllers report of on going problem where they could not reach another facility via land line to advise the Controller of a medical emergency.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that landline outages at San Juan CERAP delayed coordination with Santo Domingo (MDSD) for Aircraft X, which was diverting due to weather after a passenger died of a heart attack. The controller eventually established contact only when the aircraft was 10 miles from MDSD airspace, describing the situation as dangerous and service-compromising.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Reporters describe situation where the radar fails at a Center and the problems associated with keeping traffic moving.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller training a Developmental experienced a total ERAM failure causing loss of track control and blue flight plans on EDST. The incident forced a switch to manual strip marking and temporary ATC Zero, resulting in holding patterns and denied airspace entry until systems were restored.

synopsis: B757 flight crew experiences a RT ENG OIL FILTER EICAS at FL360. QRH procedures for this anomaly are complied without correcting the problem. The engine is shut down in accordance with the QRH and the flight diverts to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The Captain and First Officer of a Boeing 757 at FL360 diverted and landed safely after an 'R ENG OIL FILTER' EICAS message required right engine shutdown per checklist. The crew declared an emergency, coordinated with ATC and Dispatch, and secured the engine before completing a normal visual approach.

synopsis: B777 Captain reports confusion attempting to fly the CDO 1 route to Runway 24R at RJBB. The altitude restrictions and the fixes listed for the CDO 1 are interpreted as the route instead of flying the CDO 1 route (SUC Y53 to BECKY) then the BECKY DELTA arrival. Fatigue and a developing cold were cited as factors.
summary: The flight crew, suffering from fatigue, experienced confusion during the CDO-1 arrival to Runway 24R due to the procedure being split between chart notes and the BECKY arrival plate. This led to incorrect routing instructions from ATC, prompting the crew to recommend consolidating the procedure into a single FMC database entry.

synopsis: PC-12 Captain experiences a flap asymmetry as the flaps near the up position after takeoff. QRH procedures do not correct the problem and the flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: The pilot flying selected Flaps 0 during climb, triggering a Flap Asymmetry and Pusher Safe warning. The crew returned to land safely with flaps in the affected position, executing a 0-flap landing without further incident.

synopsis: Four Line Aircraft Maintenance Technicians (AMTs) including a Lead Technician, report about their involvement with an Embraer-145 aircraft that flew four legs with the Right-Hand (R/H) Static Port covered with Speed tape.
summary: Mechanics X and Y left speed tape on the right-hand static port of an Embraer-145 during night line maintenance due to poor communication and lack of a red flag. A pilot discovered the obstruction on a subsequent walk-around, but the aircraft suffered no damage, delay, or emergency after flying four legs.

synopsis: During roll out after a normal landing, a BE-55 left main landing gear collapsed causing the aircraft to skid off the runway damaging the propeller, flap and wing tip but not injuring the pilot who evacuated the aircraft after securing it.
summary: The pilot landed a single-engine aircraft on Runway 19 in gusty winds, but the aircraft became uncontrollable and veered left during rollout. The left main gear folded, causing the propeller, flap, and wingtip to impact the terrain before the pilot safely exited and reported the incident.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: After completing a thorough preflight and NOTAM review, a pilot entered the San Francisco Bay Area from the Central Valley for a tour with NCT flight following. He was surprised to hear ATC announce an AT&T TFR was in effect just as he departed the three NM protected area. He was not a sports fan and no had idea about the TFR because it was not in any briefing.
summary: A pilot flying a pleasure flight near San Francisco briefly entered the 3 NM radius of AT&T Park but exited 10 seconds before the blanket TFR for a baseball game became active. The pilot attributed the near-miss to unfamiliarity with stadium capacity rules and event schedules, recommending the FAA explicitly publish such TFRs.

aircraft: Mooney Aircraft Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An older model M20 developed a fuel leak in the fuel pressure sense line behind the copilot side instrument panel, so the pilot declared an emergency returned to the airport he had just departed.
summary: The pilot reported a fuel leak from a hole in the pressurized line to the fuel pressure gauge while climbing through 2,000 feet. An emergency was declared, and the aircraft returned to the departure airport for an uneventful landing and shutdown.

synopsis: An experimental aircraft's landing gear collapsed while taxiing after landing with the gear handle down and three green lights illuminated. Possible gear screw jack failure.
summary: During taxi back to the hangar, the landing gear collapsed despite the handle being down and the green light illuminated. The pilot attributed the incident to a possible mechanical problem and is replacing the landing gear screw jacks.

synopsis: A B737-300 climbing to FL360 developed an un-speed condition with A symbol in the SPD window and pitched over causing an airspeed increase to near MMO. Pitch control with the autopilot failed so it was disconnected to finish the climb after three osculations. An airspeed issue as suspected by the crew.
summary: The crew experienced an erroneous under speed indication at FL355 during climb, causing the autopilot to pitch down and oscillate between FL354 and FL356. They manually overrode the autopilot to level off at FL360, noting the malfunction likely stemmed from a sensor error rather than actual airspeed issues.

synopsis: Pilot reports of going above newly assigned altitude because the Controller was late in assigning the new altitude. For safety reasons the pilot didn't want to give the passengers or attendants a G force ride attempting to manually over-ride the aircraft.
summary: The flight crew overshot a 16,000-foot level-off clearance to 16,500 feet after ATC issued a late instruction following an expedited climb. The pilot attributed the altitude deviation to controller operational error and avoided manual intervention to prevent injury to cabin crew serving passengers.

synopsis: An EMB-145 crew was notified that tape was discovered over the First Officer side ADC port by the receiving crew during a crew change they had flown numerous legs that morning.
summary: The Captain reported that aluminum speed tape was found covering the First Officer's ADC ports after four legs of flight. No inflight abnormalities occurred, but the cause remains unknown, with possibilities ranging from a missed preflight check to malicious intent or maintenance error.

synopsis: A G-200 APU Access Door was closed and locked by key before the outer door latches were closed which could allow the door to open in flight.
summary: During preflight of an aircraft returning from a dual engine change, mechanics found the APU access door latches were locked before the door was closed. The door was properly secured, the flight proceeded normally, and the reporter recommended verifying latch positioning by opening the door during future inspections.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports that protective boots currently installed over the R-134A Air Conditioning Unit Relay 'Positive' and 'Ground' terminal end studs are not adequate to protect technicians and tools from exposure to electrical power. The Air Conditioning Unit is mounted on the forward side of the aft equipment area of Cessna-560 aircraft.
summary: A mechanic working on an aircraft's aft equipment area caused arcing when a socket slipped and contacted the R-134A air conditioning unit's power relay while loosening mount bolts. The incident revealed torn and improperly installed terminal boots, highlighting a design risk where exposed terminals could be struck by tools during powered maintenance.

synopsis: A widebody freight aircraft departed on RJFR SWE2R SID and because it was exceptionally light climbed very quickly above the 500 feet right turn constraint and so the confused FMS with VNAV engaged, turned the aircraft left before the crew could respond.
summary: A light aircraft crew executing the SWE2R departure from RJFR RWY 36 experienced an FMS deviation where the aircraft turned left instead of the required right turn at 500 feet due to high climb performance. The crew requested and received a direct clearance to DGC VOR, attributing the error to the procedure being unsuitable for high-performance aircraft.

synopsis: ATL Tower Controller reports of high speed aircraft coming too close to another arrival and having to send first aircraft around.
summary: Local controller observed Aircraft Y on base for RWY 28 at 250 knots and same altitude as Aircraft X on visual approach for RWY 27L, causing a near collision. The controller canceled Aircraft X's clearance, climbed it to 40, and instructed Aircraft Y to go around due to the unsafe speed and altitude.

synopsis: Controller and pilot report of event where Controller was thinking the aircraft was going to go to one runway while the pilot thought they were going to the other.
summary: An ATC controller and a pilot conducting instrument training at OKB experienced a potential separation issue when the pilot deviated from a VOR-A approach to Runway 6 to circle for Runway 24. Although no separation was lost, the controller issued a Brasher Warning for the pilot's deviation from the published missed approach procedure.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: D10 Controller reports of a NMAC due to VFR aircraft climbing into IFR traffic.
summary: A Dallas Feeder East controller managed Aircraft X while a VFR Aircraft Y climbed into the sector without coordination from Dallas North. The lack of handoff or point-out caused a loss of separation and a CA alarm, which the controller resolved by issuing a heading change to Aircraft X.

synopsis: Controller reports of complacent Controller at the next sector who isn't pointing out aircraft or following facility SOP, which leads reporter to become frustrated about the other controllers work ethics.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that an adjacent controller failed to coordinate a flight breakup for Aircraft X and Y, resulting in airspace violations and unsafe traffic conflicts. The adjacent controller neglected to pass critical information, left Aircraft Y on a heading without control, and subsequently maneuvered it into the reporter's airspace while denying responsibility.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reports sighting a UAV in close proximity during a visual approach.
summary: During a visual approach, the Captain observed a camouflage UAV on the right base while the First Officer flew. The crew notified ATC and landed safely with no damage, attributing the incident to poor planning and communication between the tower and the military operator.

synopsis: Severe internal static developed in an EMB-145 communications system overwhelming all communications so the crew squawked 7600 and ultimately were able to communicate on speaker only while continuing to the filed destination.
summary: Pilots experienced intense interphone static after takeoff that prevented headset and oxygen mask use, forcing a switch to hand mic and speaker. Although maintenance cleared the aircraft without repairs, the crew identified an unresolved mechanical issue that compromised emergency communication capabilities.

synopsis: MD-82 Captain experiences a pressurization flow light at FL270 and declares an emergency requesting 10,000 feet as descent is initiated. The initial clearance is to FL240 and ATC is reminded of the emergency status. Manual control of the pressurization system is regained at 15,000 feet and flight continues to destination.
summary: The flight crew declared an emergency at FL270 due to pressurization system failures causing rapid cabin climb. They executed an emergency descent to 10,000 feet, manually regained cabin control, and resumed normal operations after ATC coordination.

synopsis: A300 flight crew experiences an 'air pack fault' passing FL260 during climb. The QRH is not successful at correcting the problem and a descent is initiated and oxygen masks are donned. During descent the packs come back on and it is noticed that the APU is on and supplying the bleed source for both packs. An uneventful landing ensues.
summary: During climbout past FL260, the crew experienced a dual air pack fault caused by the First Officer failing to turn off the APU master and bleed switches due to poor cockpit lighting. This error led to a cabin altitude rise, an emergency declaration at 10,000 feet, and an uneventful return to base.

synopsis: A300 Captain reports a left inner fuel tank pump failure during climb that results in a fuel imbalance without any indications of pump failure. Attempts to transfer fuel are not successful but flight is able to continue to destination.
summary: The flight crew landed an aircraft with a fuel imbalance caused by a silent left inner tank pump failure that provided no ECAM warnings or fault lights. Although the crossfeed checklist was ineffective, the crew calculated sufficient fuel to land safely with 3,000 lbs trapped, reporting the subtle failure to maintenance.

synopsis: B757 Captain believes that the ACARS takeoff data is not complete without mentioning actions for an engine failure off Runway 28 after a turn to the north is commenced. The guidance is only for failures prior to commencing the turn.
summary: A pilot reported that SFO Runway 28 ACARS takeoff data lacks the full engine failure procedure for departures requiring a right turn after the turn begins. The reporter stated this conflict with the FOM creates an unsafe and illegal situation where crews might incorrectly attempt to reacquire the 294-degree radial.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Two flight crews and two flight attendants describe a collision during taxi, with the left wingtip of a medium size twin engine jet contacting the right horizontal stabilizer of a stationary aircraft of same make and model.
summary: A flight attendant reported that while holding short for takeoff, their aircraft was struck on the right elevator by another aircraft's left winglet. The impact caused cabin movement and a seat belt burn injury, leading to a return to the gate for deplaning.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew encounters heavy weather during approach to Runway 23 at FNLU and breaks of the approach to the north, advising ATC. Two other aircraft are similarly affected and ATC manages to get all three aircraft turned around and on to the VOR approach to Runway 5, in a non Radar environment, without significant delay.
summary: Pilots flying a VOR DME approach in a non-radar environment diverted due to severe weather and were vectored to Runway 05. Confusion arose when the controller instructed them to remain on frequency until landing, though the crew successfully landed after initially being told to go around.

synopsis: B767 flight crew experiences a stall warning at FL370 after being dispatched with an inoperative autothrust system. Recovery is initiated and a descent to FL350 is requested.
summary: During cruise at FL370 with inoperative autothrottles and EECs, the crew experienced a stick shaker after airspeed bled off due to complacency. The Relief Pilot and First Officer executed a stall recovery maneuver and descended to FL350, allowing the flight to continue safely to destination.

synopsis: B777 flight crew experiences a TCAS RA at 1,800 FT on departure and complies with the RA to descend, causing a flap overspeed. At 1,200 FT the RA stops and is replaced by a GPWS 'Don't Sink' warning. ATC advises that there is no traffic in the area. The crew learns that the aircraft has a history of similar false warnings and the flight continues to destination.
summary: Pilots on a B777 received a false TCAS RA at 1,800 FT during night departure, causing a descent that triggered a GPWS warning and a flap 15 overspeed to 247 KTS. ATC confirmed no traffic, and logbook review revealed two prior identical system failures, though the crew continued the flight after notifying maintenance.

synopsis: When a failed radar made continued ETOPS operations problematic due to designation weather the flight crew of a B767 was unable to obtain satisfactory and timely assistance from their Dispatcher to conduct a diversion to an airport near their destination and opted, instead, to return to their departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a weather radar failure during climb after VFR departure and diverted from SFO to LAX due to adverse weather and lack of parts. They criticized Dispatch for delayed fuel analysis and critical point calculations while managing fuel conservation and ETOPS requirements during the diversion.

synopsis: B757 crew while beginning an Oceanic leg receive LAV SMOKE EICAS at top of climb. Immediate offset and return to departure airfield is initiated. While in the descent on the return the smoke begins to dissipate meanwhile their right engine oil pressure begins to drop.
summary: The Captain and First Officer diverted to ZZZ after a lavatory smoke advisory and burning smell at FL340, descending to 10,000 feet and turning off the right pack to clear the smoke. They landed safely after monitoring rising right engine oil temperature and pressure, shutting down the engine on the runway while fire crews observed steam.

synopsis: A320 flight crew departing Runway 9 at IAH with instructions to turn right to heading 340 after takeoff which results in a TCAS RA and a NMAC with an aircraft turning left off one of the south runways.
summary: The flight crew experienced a TCAS Resolution Advisory to reduce climb at 1,500 feet during departure from Runway 09 due to conflicting traffic. The aircraft descended to zero vertical speed while the traffic passed within approximately 500 feet, after which ATC issued revised heading and altitude instructions.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports a possible NMAC with a helicopter during takeoff from runway 28R at SFO. The helicopter was north of Runway 28R hovering, and apparently drifting south.
summary: The flight crew on a departing aircraft from SFO RWY 28R observed an unannounced helicopter hovering near the runway intersection. The crew estimated a separation of 500 feet laterally and 200 feet vertically, attributing the near mid-air incident to the helicopter drifting south without Tower notification.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reports loss of directional control during takeoff, followed by a rejected takeoff and return to the gate for an aircraft swap. Maintenance found faults with the right hand steering actuator.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff due to uncontrolled left yaw despite normal engine indications and a right crosswind. Maintenance later grounded the aircraft after finding a leaking right steering actuator and frozen link rod bearings.

synopsis: This B737 crew experienced an open First Officer cockpit window during takeoff above 80 knots. The Captain elected to continue the takeoff, and First Officer attempts to close the window were unsuccessful. Despite the difficulties with crew and ATC communications because of the loud wind noise a safe and uneventful return and landing were accomplished.
summary: The pilot flying and First Officer experienced a loud noise and an open, dislodged First Officer's side window during takeoff roll past 80 knots on Runway XX. They continued the takeoff, communicated via hand signals, and landed uneventfully on Runway XY, requiring a maintenance part replacement.

synopsis: SA-226 Captain experiences two flat tires on the left main gear after landing, during taxi off the runway. The left brakes had apparently locked up during rollout flat spotting both tires and causing the flats.
summary: The pilot reported that after landing and exiting the runway, the aircraft vibrated and slowed due to flat left main tires and leaking brake fluid. The pilot attributed the tire failure to locked brakes, though they noted using reverse thrust to avoid excessive braking stress.

synopsis: A pilot of a BE-23, departing Runway 22 at ASN (utilizing a temporary control tower facility provided during a major car race at a track immediately adjacent to the airport) was placed in a conundrum when the tower cleared him via a right turn on course to the north which would have placed him over the crowded race track and thousands of spectators. A modest conflict with a helicopter in the vicinity resulted.
summary: The pilot departed Runway 22 in a Learjet, climbing at Vx to avoid the Talladega Super Speedway due to self-imposed pressure from a trailing King Air. This resulted in a close call with a helicopter at 300 feet separation, which the pilot attributed to poor decision-making rather than ATC or traffic instructions.

synopsis: C182 pilot experiences loss of heading information in the G1000 PFD shortly after takeoff in IMC. The magnetic compass is used to navigate back to the departure airport and the PFD heading begins functioning normally prior to landing.
summary: During departure in IMC at 600 FT MSL, the pilot lost heading information on the G1000 PFD due to an inoperative heading indicator. The pilot navigated using the magnetic compass to execute a localizer approach after the instrument recovered, resulting in no injuries or damage.

synopsis: General Aviation pilot reports landing at Winsted Airport after noting some engine roughness. Upon reaching the apron he is approached by a vehicle and the driver informs that the airport is closed. Aircraft were in the pattern both before and after the incident with no mention of the airport being closed on the CTAF. NOTAM's for Winsted were not checked prior to flight due to no intention to land there.
summary: A pilot experiencing engine roughness landed at Winsted (10D) after a CTAF contact with another pilot confirmed the runway was open. The pilot later learned the runway was closed but unmarked, noting that four other aircraft also used it before the engine issue resolved.

synopsis: An EMB-145 First Officer was notified that silver colored speed tape was discovered covering the First Officer static ports of an aircraft he had preflighted and flown on a series of flights after it was released that morning following overnight maintenance.
summary: The pilot discovered metallic tape covering the right pitot static port during a preflight inspection after four flight segments. No inflight abnormalities occurred, but the reporter noted the tape was difficult to see and questioned whether Maintenance or a malicious actor applied it.

synopsis: Flight instructor reports departing on a Flight Review (BFR) in a tailwheel aircraft that the pilot being checked had built. Immediately after takeoff the cylinder head temperature shot into the red and a quick turn to land on an intersecting runway is made successfully. On landing the tailwheel steering fails and a runway excursion occurs.
summary: During a flight review in an experimental aircraft, the instructor and student experienced an engine overheat and a rough landing caused by a missing tailwheel steering bolt. The aircraft veered off the runway due to lost directional control, resulting in minor damage, while the pilot noted the aircraft was actually overdue for its required inspection.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 150 experienced a partial power loss during climb and successfully returned to the departure airport. A cracked engine cylinder was later discovered to be the cause of the malfunction.
summary: The pilot experienced a power drop from 2,500 to 2,000 RPM at 300 feet AGL during initial climbout, prompting a return to land safely on Runway XX. The cause remains uncertain, though a previously stuck cylinder valve in 2013 is suspected as the source of the partial power loss.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reports of being left out to dry by ATC when pilot did not have the NOTAM in reference to a Decision Height change.
summary: The pilot, cleared for the ILS 24 approach into HQM, was denied the clearance and held at 4,000 feet at ULESS after admitting a lack of NOTAMs. Although Seattle Radio reported no NOTAMs, the controller eventually issued an FDC NOTAM raising the decision height by one foot, which the pilot attributed to their own preflight oversight and the controller's unprofessional handling.

synopsis: BE20 Captain requests direct DALSY for the RNAV approach to BUY. ATC issues a right turn direct but the Captain sees the fix as to the left of the aircraft. ATC disagrees and the Captain requests the ILS to Runway 6 and circle to 24, which is accomplished without issue.
summary: The crew requested a visual approach to Runway 24 at BUY but switched to an ILS approach after GSO TRACON issued conflicting vectors for the DALSY waypoint. The controller insisted DALSY was on the right despite three GPS sources showing it on the left, leading the crew to suspect the controller's radar display was 180 degrees out of phase.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Flight crew reports of confusion between lack of NOTAM for temporary Tower, and the problem with instructions from temporary Tower versus what controlling facility (Center) wanted the aircraft to do.
summary: Pilots on a visual approach to VDZ were instructed by a temporary tower to circle for a disabled aircraft, but another pilot relayed a Center command to climb to 16,000 feet. The confusion resulted from a lack of NOTAMs clarifying that the temporary facility provided advisories only and lacked IFR control authority.

synopsis: ZLC Controller reports of a restricted area not being displayed HOT on his EDST, while having an aircraft in the restricted area that is not authorized to be there.
summary: An air traffic controller working R40 discovered a discrepancy where flow control had released the Utah Testing and Training Range airspace 20 minutes early without updating EDST or weather messages. This oversight occurred while managing fighter jets and a VFR aircraft near Salt Lake, requiring supervisor intervention to address potential safety issues.

synopsis: Reporter describes confusing taxiway markings that may lead to a runway incursion.
summary: Aircraft X mistakenly turned onto taxiway A5 instead of the preferred taxiway V while taxiing to RWY 28R. The pilot attributed this recurring error to confusing taxiway signs and markings, which increased the risk of conflicting with aircraft exiting the runway.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew describes the circumstances leading up to an unstabilized approach and landing at ATL.
summary: The Captain and First Officer on an ILS approach to Atlanta Runway 28 delayed configuration and missed a go-around due to confusion over conflicting tower wind reports. Although they landed safely after configuring below 1,000 feet, the crew acknowledged that the wind dispute caused a loss of situational awareness and violated stabilized approach procedures.

synopsis: An A320 flight crew descended below the recommended crossing altitude during a published visual approach, and as they noticed the error they were additionally warned of the low altitude by the Tower.
summary: The flight crew descended below the recommended 1,500 feet at SLIMR during the Stadium Visual approach to EWR RWY 29 due to an incorrect 900-foot FMGC altitude constraint. They leveled off at approximately 700 feet after Tower inquiry and completed a normal landing once visual references were established.

synopsis: A Captain reports he's had five instances where the CTR R FUEL PUMP EICAS message failed to appear on B757 aircraft after the Fueling Bay Door was closed.
summary: A B757 Captain reported five instances during preflight where the Center Right Fuel Pump EICAS message failed to appear despite center tank fuel and a closed fueling bay door. This recurring issue, affecting only the right pump, forced fuel deferrals that increased zero fuel weight and required removing passengers, mail, or cargo.

synopsis: During a turnaround preflight, an EMB-145 crew discovered silver colored speed tape covering the First Officer static ports after the aircraft had flown a series of flights since being released following overnight maintenance.
summary: The flight crew discovered silver tape covering the First Officer's static ports during preflight at an out station. Maintenance likely forgot to remove the tape after a CATII system check, but the crew safely removed it and departed after confirming no damage with Maintenance Control.

synopsis: A320 First Officer is informed by the Mechanic involved that that the aircraft is being fueled manually due to the high fuel load. The First Officer informs the Captain when he arrives who switches to auto. A short time later a large fuel spill occurs out of the left wing.
summary: The First Officer and Captain discovered a fuel spill caused by the First Officer's failure to reset center tank pumps to auto after a mechanic manually balanced an abnormally high fuel load. This procedural deviation resulted in significant fuel discharge from the left wing, requiring passenger deplaning and emergency cleanup.

synopsis: G IV Captain experiences moderate turbulence at FL450 on a transcontinental flight due to a long line of thunderstorms perpendicular to his route. He believes he may have been able to choose a better route had he been able to view a Nexrad radar image via on board WiFi which is prohibited by his company.
summary: The flight crew encountered heavy turbulence at 45,000 feet while en route to PHL, causing speed and altitude variations. The pilot attributed the lack of a smoother route to company policy prohibiting in-flight internet access for real-time weather radar, which limited situational awareness beyond the onboard radar's limited view.

synopsis: DC-10 Captain experiences a near collision with a twin turboprop aircraft during taxi on the ramp. The other pilot stopped then continued on to the wrong spot.
summary: The pilot executed an emergency stop while taxiing to Spot 13 to avoid a collision with a Fokker cleared for Spot 14 but taxiing toward Spot 13. The near-miss occurred because the other pilot ignored right-of-way protocols and failed to communicate on the congested frequency, resulting in a separation of less than 20 feet.

synopsis: General Aviation pilot reports inadvertent landing at CAE Runway 29 while attempting to land at CUB Runway 31 during night visual conditions. The error is discovered on short final but a green light is received from the CAE Tower, so landing is deemed the best option.
summary: The PIC landed at CAE instead of CUB due to darkness, weak beacon lights, and cockpit distractions while using an interstate for ground reference. The pilot safely departed CAE to land at CUB, attributing the error to poor situational awareness and HSI similarity between the two airports.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Business jet First Officer as NFP, reports nearly landing at HWO after being cleared for the visual approach to OPF on a short flight from MIA.
summary: The SIC and PIC of an IFR ferry flight mistakenly landed at the wrong airport after a visual approach clearance due to high workload and rushing. Tower controllers identified the error, directing the crew to climb and vector back to OPF for a safe landing.

synopsis: Following the pilot's failure to do a hands on security check prior to departure the canopy of a Pitts S-2B separated and blew clear of the aircraft early in the takeoff roll. No other part of the aircraft was damaged and no one was injured.
summary: The pilot reported that the aircraft canopy departed during the first 100 feet of the takeoff roll, contacting the runway without damaging the airframe. The pilot attributed the incident to failing to manually verify the canopy lock knob, likely due to distraction from being the first aerobatic flight of the season.

synopsis: C182 pilot reports turning crosswind early and catching up to the slower C172 that had departed ahead into the VFR traffic pattern. The C172 traffic is not sighted after takeoff until quite close resulting in an airborne conflict.
summary: The pilot of a departing aircraft drifted east on takeoff, overtook a C172 ahead, and intercepted it in the pattern due to a nose-high attitude and poor situational awareness. This resulted in a close call, prompting the pilot to commit to better pattern control and awareness of slower aircraft.

synopsis: AA5 pilot reports an airborne conflict with a glider at 4,000 feet inside the Gamecock I MOA while on an IFR flight plan. The glider was not talking to ATC, had no transponder and was not visible on Radar.
summary: A pilot on an IFR flight at 4,000 feet MSL encountered a glider within 500 feet in the GAMECOCK I MOA. The pilot reported that the glider was not on radar, lacked transponder equipment, and was difficult to see, prompting a request for a safety review.

synopsis: Aircraft Marshall reports a B767-400 returning to the gate for maintenance but with insufficient manpower the Captain is instructed to wait. The Captain elects to self park, missing the stop point by 30 feet with no other ill effects.
summary: A B767-400 crew spooled engines and pulled into the gate without green Accu-Park lights or hand signals due to a missing wing walker. The aircraft overshot the stop mark by over 30 feet, bringing the wing and engine within 10–15 feet of the jet bridge before being pushed back.

synopsis: A pilot questions whether Operational Control Procedures are in place in their company's Maintenance Department to ensure that proper maintenance standards are upheld. He had noticed during a Logbook preflight their CE-560XL aircraft had flown 20 flights before the left and right Main Landing Gear (MLG) tires had been replaced for having previously excessive low pressures.
summary: The Cessna-560XL crew discovered during preflight that main tires with critically low pressure were serviced instead of replaced a week prior, allowing the aircraft to fly 20 flights. The reporter attributes this to a lack of operational control procedures ensuring proper maintenance standards during the maintenance checklist.

synopsis: CE560 Captain reports a severe turbulence encounter at FL400 while navigating around a long line of thunderstorms. One passenger who was not wearing his seatbelt was injured. Flight continues to destination.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence while crossing storm tops at 40,000 feet, causing autopilot disengagement and a passenger injury. The pilot attributed the event to misjudging the storm line's extent, as airborne radar showed no severe returns despite the encounter.

synopsis: BD700 First Officer reports missing the routing note on the SHEAD 8 RNAV departure from LAS, resulting in a climb above FL190 before receiving clearance to do so.
summary: The PIC and co-pilot missed a routing note on the SHEAD 8 RNAV departure, causing an initial climb to FL210 before ATC instructed a descent to FL190 and subsequent climb to FL230. Oakland Center later contacted the crew to discuss the error, prompting a request for clearer ceiling altitude notes in the Jeppesen charts.

synopsis: B747 flight crew reports an altitude deviation descending into ZSPD due to not converting meters to feet before entering the number into the MCP. Other difficulties operating in the Shanghai FIR and into the ZSPD airport are also discussed.
summary: During descent into Shanghai, the Pilot Flying inadvertently set the MCP to 6,000 feet instead of the assigned 6,000 meters due to task saturation and unit conversion errors. The crew recognized the deviation, manually climbed to the correct altitude, and completed the flight without loss of separation.

synopsis: Pilot reports of jet blast coming from a heavy aircraft holding between runways that affects departing aircraft.
summary: Aircraft X experienced an abrupt right yaw at V1 during takeoff on SFO Runway 01L due to jet blast from Aircraft Y holding short on Taxiway F. The crew maintained control, continued the climbout, and reported no injuries, recommending that heavy aircraft not be positioned between runways with active departures.

synopsis: After taking a three hour delay for a start valve replacement on the right engine, a B767-300 Captain notes the right engine oil quantity is zero upon leveling at FL320. Oil pressure begins to fluctuate and the crew declares an emergency and returns to the departure airport. The engine is shut down during descent.
summary: The crew experienced a right engine oil loss on a jet at FL320 following a maintenance delay. They declared a Mayday, executed the engine failure checklist, and landed safely at the departure airport after shutting down the engine when oil pressure reached the amber band.

synopsis: B757 flight crew believes that they may have landed with spoilers extended after having used them to slow late in the approach. No abnormalities were noted during the approach and landing.
summary: The flight crew landed an aircraft at MTPP after a visual approach complicated by gusty winds, rain, and traffic. They discovered the speedbrakes were fully extended post-landing but could not determine if they deployed automatically or remained extended throughout the approach due to high workload.

synopsis: CRJ-700 flight crew experiences AHRS heading anomalies departing DFW resulting in a track deviation on an RNAV departure. ATC issues headings and the system is returned to normal operation a few minutes later.
summary: The flight crew experienced an AHRS failure causing incorrect heading indications and autopilot deviations during the climb on the DARTZ 1 departure from an airport with known magnetic anomalies. After reverting to standby compass and following QRH procedures, they restored normal navigation and landed safely, logging the discrepancy for maintenance.

synopsis: Flight attendants lament being dispatched in a wide body aircraft with an inoperative PA system. Some chimes do not function and megaphones are required to communicate with the passengers enmass.
summary: Flight attendants and the captain operated a widebody aircraft with an inoperative PA system deferred under MEL, using ineffective megaphones for safety briefings and announcements. The crew reported unsafe conditions, including inability to monitor seatbelts or medical needs, and concluded the aircraft should not have been dispatched.

synopsis: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) describes his efforts to determine the meaning of a message flag with 'DCU' inside a white box on the First Officer's (F/O) lower right Display. The B757-200 aircraft's Center Data Concentrator Unit (DCU) had faulted, but was incorrectly deferred as the 'Right' DCU with the concurrence of the flight crew, Maintenance Controller, and Technician.
summary: A B757 dispatcher and flight crew delayed departure 19 minutes due to an unfamiliar DCU message flag on the First Officer's display. The delay resulted from initial confusion over the white box indication and inconsistent maintenance knowledge, which was later clarified as a Center DCU fault requiring specific MEL procedures.

synopsis: C172 pilot reports making several touch and go landings before landing and discovering the left tire is flat. Directional control problems are reported but the aircraft is kept on the runway and stopped.
summary: The pilot experienced a left main gear tire blowout and loss of directional control during a circle-to-land approach in a light aircraft. The incident, occurring after a touch-and-go, was attributed to either foreign object damage or tire wear, requiring a tug to tow the aircraft to the ramp.

synopsis: A Lear 45 flight crew, lacking sophisticated autoflight VNAV and autothrottle availability, failed to make the crossing restrictions at VNNOM on the EAGUL RNAV STAR to PHX. The reporter cited the excessive complications of this and other complex RNAV STARs, which require excessive flight crew workload to reconfigure and program their FMS to meet those demands.
summary: The pilot reported that the arrival procedure between HOMRR and VNNOM intersections required an unsafe 5,000 FPM descent rate due to the short 4.1 nm distance. The pilot attributed this hazard to an overly complex design with multiple crossing restrictions and block altitudes that exceed FMS capabilities.

synopsis: C172 instructor reports difficulty canceling flight following with NY TRACON during descent due to a weak radio or lack of VHF coverage. Climbing to regain VHF contact results in a NMAC. Flight following is canceled on the ground.
summary: During a training flight descent between 3,800 and 3,500 feet, the pilot lost radio contact with NY TRACON on 120.15 due to weak coverage. After hearing a traffic warning, the pilot rapidly descended to 2,500 feet to avoid conflict and later reported that poor radio volume prevented cancelling radar services in the air.

synopsis: TBM pilot reports inadvertently selecting vertical speed on his G600 while attempting to set QNH during descent, resulting in an undetected climb. ATC notices however and the error is corrected.
summary: The pilot descended from FL250 to FL190 before receiving a clearance to 15,000 feet. While adjusting the altimeter on the Garmin G600, the pilot inadvertently changed the vertical speed from -1,200 to +400 FPM, causing an unintended climb to FL200 due to the unit's button-and-knob interface.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Controller reports of NMAC due to aircraft that was supposed to make a full stop elects to make a touch and go coming into close proximity of another aircraft in the pattern.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a near mid-air collision between Aircraft X and Aircraft Y at MRI when Aircraft X performed an unauthorized touch-and-go instead of a full stop. The controller attributed the incident to pilot deviations from clearances and a lack of pilot education regarding standard procedures.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Local Controller describes situation where a new pilot causes problems flying into the airport and then taxiing to the ramp.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managed a potential conflict between departing Aircraft Y and an unprepared VFR pilot (Aircraft X) who entered controlled airspace without clearance and exhibited poor radio procedures. The controller issued corrective instructions to separate the aircraft and directed Aircraft X to land, noting the pilot subsequently taxied without clearance across a closed runway.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Controller reports situation where the pilot turns aircraft off of RNAV departure by mistake into the flight path of aircraft departing off its right.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X departed Runway 18L on an RNAV route and turned right toward departing Aircraft Y from Runway 18C, prompting the Departure Controller to issue an immediate southeast turn to avoid collision. The controller attributed the incident to their own distraction, complex display workload, and conflicting noise abatement procedures.

synopsis: Reporter describes situation where electrical maintenance is being done at facility and center does not do a hand off to the facility causing panic to clear the runway with an aircraft on a 3 mile final.
summary: During facility electrical maintenance, the tower lost radar and communications while A90 also experienced power issues. An inbound aircraft arrived on final without prior notification from A90 or ZBW, forcing the tower to scramble vehicles to clear the runway for landing.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Reporter describes an aircraft departing the airport and can't understand the aircraft, assumes what the pilot wants, then has to react as the aircraft almost violates the LAX Class Bravo.
summary: Air Traffic Control intervened when a pilot with a heavy accent and no Class B experience departed Runway 21, flew the wrong direction, and entered restricted airspace. The controller issued immediate turns, assisted with a pattern entry after the pilot flew opposite traffic, and contacted the FBO regarding the new owner's lack of proficiency.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew experiences a GPWS 'Caution Obstacle' annunciation during a night visual approach and executes a go-around.
summary: The Captain and First Officer received a visual approach clearance in VMC conditions but triggered a "Caution Obstacle" warning due to a minor sink rate deviation near buildings. The crew executed a go-around, received vectors for a second visual approach, and landed successfully.

synopsis: After picking up a B737-300 aircraft to ferry, numerous FMS and navigational difficulties are encountered resulting in a track deviation during departure. Some of the problems cleared up but the crew believed that the aircraft thought it was still on the ground.
summary: The ferry crew experienced FMC position errors, autopilot disconnections, and TCAS failures during climb after departing a cargo ramp, causing a departure overshoot. The pilot attributed these issues to the aircraft failing to recognize it was airborne, resulting in a maintenance handover upon arrival.

synopsis: A320 Captain experiences a blue hydraulic pump overheat during initial climb and elects to return to the departure airport for an overweight landing.
summary: During initial cruise climb, the blue hydraulic pump overheated and faulted, prompting the crew to declare an emergency and return for an overweight landing. Maintenance later identified the fault as a likely precursor to pump failure, leading to an aircraft swap after a normal post-landing inspection.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reports dense white smoke billowing out of the floor vents shortly after takeoff and an immediate return for landing is requested, with only the smoke memory items accomplished prior to landing. The landing checklist is not completed until 500 FT AGL.
summary: During the RNAV departure at 1,200 feet AGL, the crew encountered thick smoke and a burning odor, prompting an emergency return and landing. Firefighters inspected the aircraft, determined an evacuation unnecessary, and allowed a safe taxi to the gate with no injuries reported.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 crew found the STAB CH 1 would not engage during preflight, so agreed to a ferry flight for maintenance. But with the appropriate circuit breaker pulled the MACH TRIM became inoperative so the crew refused to fly because the aircraft's condition was ambiguous.
summary: The pilot and Maintenance Control encountered a STAB Channel 1 failure during preflight, where pulling CB 2F5 per ferry procedures unexpectedly disabled MACH Trim.
