The pilot deemed the aircraft unsafe to ferry due to contradicting manual guidance and Maintenance's inability to document why MACH Trim failed with one STAB channel operative.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain describes an unstabilized approach flown by the First Officer who is new to the 900. The Captain laments his late involvement in coaching the First Officer who is initially high and fast then low during the approach, resulting in a low altitude alert from the Tower.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring and First Officer flew a Boeing 700/900 ILS approach in IMC with a tailwind, becoming unstable due to high speed and excessive descent. The crew corrected the low altitude alert without executing a missed approach, landing safely despite the Pilot Monitoring admitting poor judgment in not taking control or diverting earlier.

synopsis: A C-750 hydraulic line burst after takeoff with EICAS alerts HYD VOLUME LOW A and HYD PTU FAIL. Both red and green gear lights illuminated with the handle UP, so an emergency was declared, the flight diverted to a nearby airport for an uneventful landing, and then was towed off the runway.
summary: The flight crew experienced a hydraulic line burst during gear retraction after takeoff, causing zero A-side hydraulic pressure and gear disagreement. They declared an emergency, diverted to a nearby airport, and executed a safe landing using emergency braking and backup steering.

synopsis: MD83 First Officer experiences autopilot and autothrottle failures during climb along with most DFGS functions. The crew elects to divert to a suitable airport due to weather at the departure airport. The landing gear fails to extend normally when selected down and a go-around ensues. Emergency gear extension procedures are successful followed by a normal landing.
summary: During climb, autopilot and autothrottle failures caused yaw oscillations, prompting a diversion to ZZZ. Landing gear initially failed to extend, requiring an emergency extension and go-around before a safe landing and tow to the gate.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports Technicians are being pressured by their Maintenance supervisors to ignore the 'Cautions and 'Instruction' requirements in their Job Cards for Serviceability of all parts removed and retained during Elevator Servo-control Unit replacements on A320 aircraft. Lack of adequate information to ensure Serviceability and strict requirements of Airworthiness Directive AD 2011-19-04 for Elevator Servo-control rod ends were also raised.
summary: Maintenance mechanics reported that supervisors pressured them to ignore Job Instruction Card cautions regarding elevator servo-control rod end serviceability during replacement. The reporter attributed the issue to a lack of Home Shop resources and recommended eliminating mechanic determinations in favor of Non-Destructive Testing inspector verification.

synopsis: Two Aircraft Maintenance Technicians (AMTs) report they did not follow procedures in their Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM), had listened to the wrong instructions from their Lead Mechanic and did not have the correct tools to accomplish a re-torque of the Left Main Landing Gear (MLG) Side Brace Downlock Link Assembly on a company MD-11 aircraft.
summary: A mechanic and Lead Mechanic X worked on an MD-11's main landing gear side brace in a hangar but lacked the required special tool. The Lead Mechanic ordered the use of Vise-Grip pliers to tighten a bolt instead of following the Aircraft Maintenance Manual, which the reporter identified as an unsafe deviation from proper procedures.

synopsis: A CE-560 crew declared an emergency for an AP MISTRIM annunciation with a jammed trim wheel. After a safe landing the Captain discovered his iPad lodged under and jammed in the trim wheel.
summary: During descent between 4,000 and 10,000 feet, an iPad lodged under the elevator trim wheel, jamming controls and causing an AP Mistrim annunciation. The crew declared an emergency, followed checklists, and landed safely after discovering the loose device was the cause.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Controller reports of incident where the trailing aircraft doesn't slow and overtakes preceding aircraft which are separated by 1,000 feet. Reporter states that Conflict Alert goes off but not in a timely manner which may be due to use of fusion radar and a software problem.
summary: An air traffic controller stopped Aircraft X at 11,000 feet to prevent a collision with slower Aircraft Y during an RNAV arrival, triggering a late Conflict Alert. The controller attributed the near-miss to inconsistent pilot speeds on the arrival and recommended adding specific speed and altitude constraints to the procedure.

synopsis: Reporters write about loss of separation due to improper use of Vacated Altitude separation rule, leading to a loss of separation.
summary: A trainee air traffic controller and instructor in Sector 40/60 issued conflicting descent clearances to Aircraft X and Y due to a transposed altitude reading. The trainee mistakenly cleared Aircraft Y to FL260 while Aircraft X was still at FL256, triggering a conflict alert that was initially disregarded as a vacated altitude.

synopsis: ZJX Controller describes weather scenario which causes aircraft to deviate through a Warning Area in which he did not have control of.
summary: An air traffic controller in the St. Augustine Sector reported that six of seven aircraft deviated into military Warning Area W158A due to heavy weather. The controller stated that a failure to implement CAR40 procedures within 30 minutes prevented ensuring separation from potential Navy aircraft, creating a mid-air collision risk.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: SCT Controller reports of NMAC with GA aircraft and Fire Fighting aircraft that departed Fire TFR.
summary: An air traffic controller handling Aircraft X on an IFR ILS approach to CRQ reported a near mid-air collision with a firefighting aircraft. The controller attributed the incident to a lack of communication with firefighting operations regarding ingress and egress routes near the TFR.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Controller reports aircraft on final asks if a vehicle is on runway they are cleared to land on. Controller realizes he doesn't own runway currently and sends aircraft around.
summary: Local Control, including an instructor and a trainee, cleared Aircraft X for an option landing on Runway 27 without obtaining runway ownership from Ground Control. An airport vehicle was on the runway, causing the pilot to request a go-around after the controllers missed the vehicle during their scan.

synopsis: First Officer and Captain reported departing a runway that ATIS showed as closed but controllers asked if they wanted to depart on. Pilots accepted runway and later found out through company that it was closed.
summary: The flight crew at OKC accepted a Ground Control offer to depart Runway 31 despite an ATIS report listing it closed, relying on subsequent clearances from Ground and Tower. Headquarters later notified the crew they had used a closed runway, prompting the pilots to acknowledge they should have verified the runway status with ATC.

synopsis: During the last portion of a flight to ZBAA B777 flight crew notices that the aircraft has come out of LNAV and is in heading select although still on the magenta line. LNAV is reengaged but 80 NM later it is noted in heading select again and again LNAV is reselected and seems to operate normally for the remainder of the descent and approach.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced two uncommanded reverts from LNAV to Heading Select mode during descent to ZBAA. They suspected a faulty Heading Select switch or FMC programming error and reported the issue to maintenance after a normal landing.

synopsis: A CE-560XL alerted CABIN DOOR and DOOR SEAL at around 1,000 feet after takeoff so an emergency was declared and as the flight returned to land the door opened and contacted the runway after landing.
summary: During an RNAV departure shortly after takeoff, the cabin door opened on the base leg, prompting an emergency return and landing. The door contacted the ground during rollout but caused no control issues, resulting in a safe shutdown and passenger deplaning.

synopsis: A CE-560XL Captain pulled the chocks while the First Officer briefed the passengers and had to hurriedly call the First Officer to set the brakes as the aircraft rolled slowly forward.
summary: A ground handler removed nose wheel chocks while the First Officer was briefing passengers, causing the aircraft to roll forward. The handler rushed due to early passenger departure requests and admitted to violating SOPs by not confirming the First Officer was seated before removing the chocks.

synopsis: CE560 First Officer, while in the cabin briefing the passengers, hears the Captain yell 'brakes' from outside the aircraft. Moving to the cockpit, the aircraft is noted to be moving and the parking brake is set.
summary: A cabin crew member noticed the aircraft moving forward while passengers were seated and the door was open. The crew member entered the cockpit to set the parking brakes, stopping the aircraft, and attributed the incident to brakes not being set before chocks were removed.

synopsis: B747 First Officer reports receiving an ACARS message from Dispatch that the destination airport is closed by NOTAM and they will need to slow down to meet the opening time. The Captain does not recall such a NOTAM but a recheck finds a NOTAM indicating 'AD closed'.
summary: The crew en-route to ZZZZ received an ACARS message to slow down due to a NOTAM stating "AD Closed," which they initially missed before identifying "AD" as non-standard terminology for "Aerodrome." They adjusted speed, refused direct routing, and arrived after the airport reopened, recommending training updates for this ambiguous phrasing.

synopsis: A MD-83 Digital Flight Guidance System (DFGS) circuit breaker opened after takeoff, IMC near convective weather. With all DFGS system indications frozen and contending with uncommanded yaw oscillations, the crew declared an emergency and diverted to a nearby VMC airport where an emergency landing was completed after a go-around for unsafe gear.
summary: During climb in IMC, the flight crew experienced autopilot disconnect, yaw oscillations, and flight guidance system failures caused by a popped circuit breaker. They diverted to an alternate airport, managed gear indication issues, and landed safely, though cabin crew reported significant stress due to a lack of cockpit communication updates.

synopsis: B757 Captain and two Check Airmen on an initial Captain upgrade flight, experience an engine failure at 500 FT accompanied by high vibration and fire viewed by the Tower. The Captains combine efforts to accomplish checklists and return to the departure airport for a single engine landing.
summary: During an initial captain upgrade flight, the pilot flying experienced a right engine compressor stall at 500 feet AGL, causing vibration and high EGT. The crew shut down the engine, climbed to 4,000 feet, and landed safely at maximum gross weight to await fire personnel assessment.

synopsis: C152 pilot reported encountering wake turbulence at 400 FT AGL from a B787 departing on a parallel runway.
summary: A new private pilot flying a personal scenic flight to BFI encountered wake turbulence from a departing B787 due to inexperience and pressure to expedite the landing. The pilot experienced a 30-degree roll at 400 feet AGL, executed a go-around, and landed safely, attributing the incident to poor decision-making and inadequate training on assertiveness with ATC.

synopsis: C208 pilot reports an airborne conflict at 10,000 feet on A555 while out of radio contact with ZMA. The frequency copied and readback by the reporter was not correct but not caught by the Controller. Since contact was not expected on the new frequency for some time, the error was not quickly discovered and 121.5 was not being monitored.
summary: A C208 pilot on an IFR flight along A555 experienced a near midair collision with an opposing aircraft at 10,000 feet due to a frequency miscommunication that left the crew out of contact with ATC. The pilot noted that TCAS alerted them to the traffic, but visual contact was delayed, and the incident highlighted the need to monitor guard frequency during long communication gaps.

aircraft: Cessna Single Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A C-162 passenger side door opened during flight damaging the window and springing the hinges. Before takeoff the door was positively checked closed and latched by the instructor in the right seat.
summary: During a flight test in a Cessna 162, the right passenger door flew open despite preflight latch checks, damaging the window and springing the door. The pilot returned to the home airport and landed safely, though the cause of the door opening remains unknown.

synopsis: ONT Local Controller departs IFR traffic and a previous helicopter the Tower handed off to the TRACON is traffic for the departure.
summary: Local Control cleared Aircraft Y for takeoff from Runway 26L while Aircraft X maneuvered in the departure corridor after being handed off to SoCal. The controller issued a traffic alert as Aircraft Y climbed, noting SoCal failed to restrict Aircraft X from the corridor or assign a safe altitude.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: N90 Controller describes airport configuration change that he feels is unsafe.
summary: An LGA supervisor delegated Belmont airspace to JFK while five LGA aircraft were vectored for ILS 13 in IFR conditions with windshear. The reporter cleared the final arrival without go-around protection after the supervisor ignored safety warnings, noting that a go-around would have entered the delegated airspace.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: P31 Controller describes head on situation where controllers talking to the two aircraft do nothing to stop the operational error or fix the situation.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller and a Developmental Controller faced a potential nose-to-nose conflict between two aircraft at 8,000 and 9,000 feet due to the trainees' inaction and lack of communication. The reporter attributes this critical safety situation to an overwhelmed facility with inexperienced trainers and insufficient staffing.

synopsis: F11 Controller reports of a loss of separation with faster aircraft overtaking slower aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a potential loss of separation between Aircraft X and Aircraft Y during a missed approach at MLB airport. The controller attributed the incident to delayed recognition of Aircraft X's position and insufficient performance-based separation when clearing the high-performance Aircraft Y on the same heading.

synopsis: ZSU Center Controller reports of problems with adjacent foreign center and coordination or lack of coordination issues.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller at ZSU reported that MDSD and SVMI frequently send aircraft into their airspace without coordination due to labor issues and poor communications. The controller stated this uncoordinated entry is dangerous, could cause loss of life, and remains unaddressed despite multiple reports to the FAA.

synopsis: CIC from LVK Tower reports of NMAC that occurred while training was going on and the communication loss of radios with one of the involved aircraft. Pilot reports of close call between his aircraft and another while attempting to land.
summary: A trainee controller and instructor managed a near-midair collision between Aircraft X and Aircraft Y during approach due to Aircraft Y's radio failure and non-compliance with instructions. Aircraft X avoided a collision by executing a sharp left bank after the instructor issued a traffic alert when Aircraft Y failed to respond to separation commands.

synopsis: B767 Captain experiences a TCAS RA for traffic 200 feet below during ILS approach to HNL. No evasive action is required and the validity of the target is never confirmed.
summary: A pilot flying an ILS approach to runway 8L at HNL on autopilot received a TCAS RA at 1,400 feet for a target 200 feet below. The "Monitor vertical speed" alert quickly resolved to "Clear of conflict" without the crew visually identifying the target.

synopsis: B717 Captain experiences a turn in the wrong direction by the autopilot when capturing the LOC 22 at LGA. The autopilot is quickly disengaged and a right turn initiated back to the localizer. ATC notes the deviation and issues instructions.
summary: Pilots flying an aircraft at 2,000 feet MSL reported the autopilot turned left instead of right to intercept the LGA Runway 22 localizer. The crew immediately disengaged the autopilot and manually corrected the turn, suspecting a reverse sensing error caused the deviation.

synopsis: EMB-170 Captain experiences a stick shaker during takeoff, after V1 prior to Vr and the takeoff is continued. Once airborne EICAS messages for Stall Prot Fail, AOA Limit Fail, Windshear Fail and AT Fail are annunciated. After referencing the QRH the flight continues to destination.
summary: During takeoff roll near Vr, the pilot experienced a brief stick shaker and continued the takeoff, deeming the stall indication erroneous. Post-rotation, multiple EICAS failures occurred, but the crew followed QRH procedures and completed an uneventful flight after notifying maintenance.

synopsis: A319 Captain experiences a TCAS RA caused by military aircraft that have him in sight during descent into LAS. Evasive action is not required, but the Controller seemed surprised that the A319 crew would be required to comply with the RA even though the F22's had them insight.
summary: During the Sunset 3 arrival descent, a commercial crew received a TCAS Resolution Advisory while two Air Force F-22 jets accelerated behind them at similar altitudes. The conflict caused the crew to miss the Approach Checklist, which was completed later after a flight attendant reminder.

synopsis: An HS125 crew began flying the DAL JEN.JEN 9 arrival, Runway 13L assigned. When ATC assigned Runway 13R two miles prior to FUZ, the FMS was reprogrammed and in doing so the autopilot transitioned to ROLL, the FMS re-inserted the arrival at JEN 50 miles behind the aircraft and a track deviation resulted.
summary: During the Glen Rose 9 arrival to DAL at 7,000 feet, a last-minute runway change from 13L to 13R caused the FMS to reset the arrival and default to ROLL mode, resulting in a missed turn at FUZ. The crew followed ATC instructions to correct the heading, noting that late runway assignments increase workload and risk FMS errors.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew experiences a windshear alert during approach and goes around resulting in a momentary flap overspeed. With extensive vectoring before and after the approach and deteriorating weather, the crew elects to divert to their planned alternate after declaring minimum fuel.
summary: The pilot flying encountered windshear on approach to MIA, executed an escape maneuver, and diverted to RSW declaring minimum fuel due to weather and vectors. Upon landing at RSW with 3.2 tons remaining, the crew rejected a landing clearance cancellation to avoid a go-around, citing their critical fuel state.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew discovers during cruise at FL370 that the Captain's yoke can be moved several inches in both pitch and roll without disconnecting the autopilot and without affecting the flight path of the aircraft. After discussions the crew elects to autoland on a long runway, and does so without difficulty.
summary: The crew at FL370 discovered the yoke moved freely in pitch and roll without disengaging the autopilot or altering flight path. They declared an emergency, diverted, and executed a successful autoland after consulting maintenance and dispatch.

synopsis: Pilot flying in to ORD reports of a bad signal on the ILS due to B747 traffic taxiing in front of the signal.
summary: During a visual approach to ORD, a B747 cleared for takeoff blocked the localizer while taxiing, causing multiple full-scale deflections for the reporting crew. The crew maintained a stable approach and completed a normal landing.

synopsis: A319 Captain laments the closure of Runway 16/34 at RIC for construction, requiring the use of 6,600 foot Runway 20/2 under all circumstances.
summary: The flight crew executed a legal Nav approach to Runway 20 at Richmond in heavy rain and gusty winds. The pilot reported the operation was high-risk due to the short runway length and adverse weather, recommending VMC-only operations until the long runway reopens.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports being cleared for the VOR/DME 07 circle 25 CYRUS visual APP RWY 25 at MROC. The CYRUS visual is not part of the database and must be manually entered. When Runway 25 is selected the VOR approach is dumped.
summary: The pilot reported that selecting Runway 25 in the FMS during a VOR/DME 07 approach in mountainous IMC dumped the loaded approach, removing vertical guidance. This caused sink rate alerts while descending into rising terrain during a 180-degree turn, though the crew stabilized and landed safely.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reports not complying with the NOTAM change to the SMO Radial and altitude for the ILS 5R at MMMX due to workload and weather distractions.
summary: The flight crew flew the incorrect radial and altitude for the ILS 5R approach at MMMX due to failing to properly brief a confusing NOTAM amidst high workload and weather deviations. ATC queried the deviation, issued vectors, and the crew landed without incident after acknowledging the briefing error.

synopsis: Aircraft Dispatcher describes a rejected takeoff caused by an ACARS message voiding the weight and balance closeout and received as the thrust levers are being advanced for takeoff.
summary: The flight crew aborted takeoff after receiving an ACARS message regarding a payload change and weight and balance update 13 minutes after blocking out. The reporter attributes the event to the distraction caused by critical phase messaging and requests restrictions on such transmissions.

synopsis: CRJ200 First Officer discovers at the top of descent that the number one engine thrust cannot be reduced by pulling back on the thrust lever. The engine is shut down and a single engine landing ensues.
summary: During cruise descent, the First Officer discovered the left engine N1 did not respond to thrust lever movement, indicating a stuck lever. The crew executed the QRH to shut down the left engine and completed a single-engine visual approach and landing, attributing the issue to a thrust lever linkage failure.

synopsis: B717 Captain approaching RSW Runway 6, experiences an airborne conflict with a general aviation aircraft departing FMY near DOLPN.
summary: A pilot on a visual approach to RSW Runway 06 received a TCAS climb resolution advisory due to a close VFR aircraft from Page. The pilot manually climbed to avoid the traffic, landed safely, and reported that the tower issued no traffic call, suggesting VFR aircraft should follow the shoreline.

synopsis: C402 Captain reports loss of GPS signal over BVY airport during vectors for approach to BOS. The signal loss is short lived and does not interfere with the approach.
summary: The pilot experienced a brief GPS signal loss over Beverly Airport while receiving vectors for the BOS approach. The crew continued using basic ILS systems, reported the issue to ATC, and landed safely with no disruption.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain experiences loss of GPS signal on three separate occasions during approach to MMMX between SMO and the turn to intercept the Runway 5R localizer.
summary: Pilots reported FMS DR mode failures during the ILS DME Runway 5R approach at MMMX using the SMO transition. The undetected navigation failure caused heading hold and map shifts, requiring immediate left turns to avoid overshooting the localizer into high terrain.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier was cleared for the JFK GPS 13L but selected RNAV 13 because the crew did not see the FMS database index single approach chart labeled VOR OR GPS 13L. The IAF is common to all three approaches but the RNAV FAF and Missed Approach Procedures are different.
summary: The flight crew selected the RNAV 13L approach instead of the intended VOR 13L at JFK after hearing "GPS" in the clearance and seeing a shared initial fix. The error occurred because the FMC and charts listed the GPS and VOR approaches under the same title, leading to confusion despite an uneventful landing.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports being distracted by the new stadium display during a night visual approach to Runway 30L at SJC.
summary: Pilots on a night visual approach to SJC Runway 30L reported extreme distraction from bright stadium lights. Tower acknowledged the issue, noting potential flicker vertigo risks during future IMC instrument approaches.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air Carrier Captain laments the requirement to divert when the visibility is missing from the ASOS report for their destination airport and no approved weather observer is available.
summary: The flight crew diverted to PGV because faulty ASOS equipment at EWN reported missing visibility, preventing a Part 121 landing despite adequate inflight visibility. The reporter attributes the issue to the sensor's location near Bryce's Creek and the lack of an approved ground observer to correct the erroneous data.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reports continuing an approach after passing through a microburst resulting in large power adjustments and a momentary stick shaker. The approach is not stable at 500 feet but is continued to landing. Several go-arounds occur after this landing.
summary: The First Officer flew a stabilized approach into Denver in gusty winds, encountering a strong downdraft followed by a rapid updraft that triggered a stick shaker. Despite the shaker and unstable parameters at 500 feet, the crew continued the landing, attributing the event to wind conditions and acknowledging their overconfidence in managing the turbulence.

synopsis: CRJ200 reports getting very low during a visual approach with the Captain flying due to lack of attention by both pilots.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway 16L, the Captain misinterpreted an FCP capture indication, causing the aircraft to descend to 1,000 feet AGL instead of leveling at 7,000 feet. The crew recovered after the Pilot Not Flying, distracted by traffic scanning, noticed the low altitude on the PAPI and RA.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Flight Attendant reports that the new lift up style bins installed on her aircraft are prone to popping open on landing. In this instance she stood up to close it just after the aircraft touched down. Passengers closed a second bin that had popped open.
summary: A flight attendant reported that two new lift-up bins popped open during landing, requiring crew to leave jumpseats and manually close them while the aircraft was braking at high speed. The reporter attributed the danger to the bins' excessive weight, lack of assist levers, and the risk of injury to both crew and passengers.

synopsis: Aeronca and BE-95 pilots describe the events leading up to the BE-95 pilot landing behind the Aeronca without seeing him. The runway is long and the BE-95 pilot had planned a stop and go but rejects when the Aeronca is sighted at the end of the runway.
summary: A pilot in a non-radio 1932 Aeronca C-3 landed long at an uncontrolled airport while a Beechcraft Travelair training crew aborted a takeoff upon seeing the Aeronca ahead. The Beechcraft crew reported they did not see the NORDO aircraft until late, while the Aeronca pilot criticized the other crew's reliance on radio over visual scanning.

synopsis: A B727 Second Officer alerted the Captain about the Pressurization AUTO Controller failure on final approach, but the Captain dismissed him and he later learned the failure was not entered in the Maintenance Log.
summary: During final descent, the Second Officer reported a complete loss of auto pressurization, which the Captain initially dismissed before the crew manually controlled the outflow valve. Post-flight, the Captain failed to log the pressurization failure or an oil temperature gauge issue, prompting the Second Officer to contact Flight Operations and the on-call Captain to ensure the defects were recorded.

synopsis: A DA-20 engine suddenly quit on short final and landed short of the runway but rolled onto it. The pilot then started the engine and while developing low power, was able to taxi to the ramp.
summary: A student pilot experienced a sudden total engine failure at 300 feet on final approach to Runway XXL, resulting in a forced landing short of the runway threshold. The pilot attributed the failure to prior engine sputtering during idle checks and low cylinder temperatures observed during cruise.

synopsis: A DA-20 pilot reported a bird strike at 3,500 feet at night and then during landing the engine quit because the mixture and boost pump were not configured for landing. Following a hard landing he was able to start the engine and taxi to ramp where he found no damage.
summary: The pilot struck a bird, increasing workload and causing missed descent checklists that left the mixture and boost pump in cruise settings. The engine quit 100 feet above an unlit, uncontrolled runway, resulting in a hard but safe landing with only cosmetic damage.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: An instructor pilot took control of the aircraft at 1,000 feet on final to CTAF JKA after a banner tow aircraft passed directly below without any communications.
summary: Pilots approaching JKA Runway 27 via a 45-degree entry encountered a banner tow aircraft passing 100 feet below them perpendicularly without hearing traffic calls. The pilot climbed to increase separation, noting insufficient distance between the active runway traffic flow and continuous banner tow operations 3 NM south.

synopsis: A GLASAIR Pilot discovered twelve years after purchasing the aircraft that the builder had not completed Phase II Operating Limitation Certification and so ceased flying the aircraft until it was properly licensed.
summary: The pilot of an experimental amateur-built aircraft discovered an expired airworthiness certificate and missing Phase II limitations after purchasing the plane. The aircraft remains grounded until a Designated Airworthiness Representative issues new documents, as previous A&P-IA mechanics failed to identify the regulatory violation during annual inspections.

synopsis: PA44 instructor pilot is informed by a C172 pilot that a NMAC occurred while both aircraft were practicing an ILS with the PA44 overtaking from above. The reporter never saw the other aircraft and states that his CTAF communications may have been lacking.
summary: During a multi-engine stage check, the instructor and student overtook another aircraft on the ILS while approximately 200 feet above it. The near mid-air collision occurred due to insufficient radio coordination on CTAF and poor situational awareness, prompting the crew to execute a missed approach.

synopsis: The pilot/passenger not flying reports engine failure at cruise altitude. An emergency was declared. During the descent the engine restarted and a successful landing was accomplished.
summary: During cruise, the pilot declared an emergency after an engine stoppage attributed to temperatures below -30°C, gliding to a field before the engine restarted. Experts confirmed cold-weather issues, and adding isopropyl alcohol allowed continued flight without incident at temperatures below -35°C.

synopsis: A pilot and instructor experienced a nose landing gear retraction during a touch and go when the pilot receiving recurrent training moved the landing gear handle rather than the flap handle.
summary: During a touch-and-go practice in a Cessna 172RG, the student pilot accidentally retracted the nose gear instead of raising flaps, causing the nose to strike the ground and damage the propeller. The reporter attributes the error to the pilot's lack of recent experience and suggests starting in a non-complex aircraft for future transitions.

synopsis: PA28 instructor pilot reports sighting a radio controlled aircraft above his altitude and in close proximity during a visual approach to SIG. The sighting was reported to the Tower.
summary: A VFR flight approaching Isla Grande Airport encountered a radio-controlled airplane performing acrobatic maneuvers at 1,000 to 1,100 feet MSL near the Levittown water tank. The pilot avoided a collision by 500 feet and reported the hazard, which originated from a nearby R/C strip, to the Local Controller.

synopsis: The reporter, while transiting the airspace of a busy airport, describes a near miss within 200 feet of another aircraft in the landing pattern.
summary: The pilot reported a near miss with another aircraft while overflying ZZZ airport at 1,800 feet, where the second aircraft passed 200 feet above with only 20 feet of horizontal separation. The reporter attributed the incident to the other pilot failing to communicate position and intentions on the frequency until two miles north of the field.

synopsis: A PA-18 pilot transiting near 33S heard a warning about an aircraft in the area and without knowing the warning's purpose, realized it was his aircraft. Then he heard 'jumpers away' and deviated but the jumpers were still within 2,500 feet.
summary: A pilot flying northeast over 33S airport encountered skydivers without adequate warning, resulting in a close call approximately 2,500 feet away. The pilot attributed the incident to failing to check NOTAMs and the jump operator's insufficient communication and timing.

synopsis: The landing gear of a Mooney M20F collapsed/retracted during a normal landing. The reporter states that all checklists were followed and there appeared to be nothing out of the ordinary before touchdown.
summary: The pilot landed a Mooney on a crosswind runway after the landing gear failed to lock due to a worn downlock mechanism and a popped circuit breaker. The aircraft skidded with collapsed gear and a bent propeller, but the pilot exited unhurt and the plane was later towed for repairs.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A light twin pilot failed to reset his transponder code to 1200 after landing then canceling IFR so when he became airborne and at 12,500 FT still squawking IFR, he received a TCAS alert and saw an air carrier pass 600 FT overhead.
summary: A pilot departing VFR after a previous IFR flight encountered an air carrier 500 feet above while climbing over PVD. The pilot attributed the near-miss to failing to reset the transponder from the IFR code to 1200, which may have confused the situation despite a 60-second TCAS warning.

synopsis: AUS Controller describes an operational error involving a no radio aircraft and an aircraft that had just dropped parachuter's.
summary: An air traffic controller experienced a loss of separation between a parachute jump aircraft and a non-responsive aircraft due to poor radar coverage and a missed frequency handoff. The controller allowed the jump aircraft to switch to advisory frequency prematurely, resulting in a 200-foot vertical separation before both pilots maneuvered away.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reports an altitude and track deviation during the WAATS 3 arrival to SLC. Approaching QUIPA the crew is issued a descent to 11,000 FT and a runway change at the same time military jamming of GPS commences. This results in a route discontinuity and a track deviation, along with a descent to 10,000 FT instead of 11,000 FT.
summary: Pilots descending into SLC on the WAATS 3 Arrival overshot the QUIPA fix due to a GPS discontinuity caused by jamming at the Utah Test and Training Range. This distraction led to an altitude error where they initially targeted 10,000 feet instead of the assigned 11,000 feet, though no loss of separation occurred.

synopsis: A B737NG flight crew flying the ENDEE RNAV STAR to MDW was unable to program the transition between MIING waypoint on the STAR and the RNAV approach to Runway 22L. They took manual control of the aircraft and completed the approach and landing.
summary: The flight crew encountered a route discontinuity while attempting to load the MINNG RNAV (RNP) Y 22L approach transition during the ENDEE arrival. They disconnected the autopilot to fly the approach manually and received a visual approach clearance from Approach Control.

synopsis: A B737-300 encountered severe turbulence. Unable to maintain altitude, the aircraft descended 600 FT before the pilots regained control and returned to FL320 for on coming traffic.
summary: The crew encountered unreported severe turbulence at FL320, causing a 600-foot altitude deviation and temporary loss of control. They descended to FL314 to regain control before climbing back to FL320 after ATC denied a descent request due to traffic.

synopsis: A B737 Captain reported his Company's on time performance pressure on pilots, flight attendants, and agents sets the stage for numerous types of errors including unauthorized pilots in the cockpit because of faulty paperwork.
summary: Pilots identified incorrect jumpseater paperwork caused by Ticket Agent errors, which Operations agents missed due to a rushed culture prioritizing minimum turnaround times. The reporter attributes these recurring safety risks to understaffing, operational pressure, and a punitive environment that shifts full responsibility to pilots without granting authority.

synopsis: A B737-800 crew reported changing the FMS to the MOLTN TWO RNAV and the approach from the ILS 34R to the RNAV RNPZ 34R and while on a vector the crew and ATC was uncertain if they were cleared for the approach.
summary: The flight crew flying a MOLTN TWO arrival into Denver faced confusion when ATC assigned a heading change near HIMOM while they were transitioning from an expected ILS to an RNAV RNPZ approach. The pilot reported that late clarification on the specific approach clearance caused uncertainty regarding their position and potential for an unstable approach.

synopsis: A B767-300 crew reported they were unable to descend on a profile descent and cross at the altitude constraints. The efficient winglets reportedly would not allow a steep enough descent.
summary: Pilots reported that during arrival in LNAV/VNAV, the aircraft failed to meet STAR altitude restrictions due to insufficient descent performance following winglet installation. The crew manually managed the descent using FL change and speed brakes after VNAV could not achieve required crossing altitudes, resulting in a safe landing without ATC intervention.

synopsis: CE680 Flight Crew at FL410 experiences multiple failures possibly associated with MAU 1 and 2 failure. Pressurization is lost and flight diverts to a suitable airport. All failures cleared before landing and post flight checks revealed a history of MAU failures.
summary: Pilots experienced multiple Modular Avionics Unit failures and pressurization spikes at FL410, causing instrument loss and a cabin altitude warning. They declared an emergency, descended to 9,000 feet with oxygen masks, and landed uneventfully after systems recovered at low altitude.

synopsis: CE750 flight crew describes a near collision with an air taxiing helicopter during taxi out of the FBO ramp under the direction of a Marshall. The helicopter had come around a hanger from behind the CE750 and had thought the CE750's Marshall was directing them.
summary: Pilots taxiing an empty aircraft at CYUL's uncontrolled General Aviation ramp nearly collided with a helicopter that approached from a blind spot. The helicopter pilot admitted fault for a bad approach and fixating on the wrong marshaller, but no contact or damage occurred.

synopsis: C402 Captain experiences a loss of GPS signal 12 NM north of BOS for less than a minute. No disruption to the flight was reported.
summary: A pilot flying 12 miles north of BOS while receiving vectors to Runway 33R experienced a temporary GPS signal loss that resolved two miles later. The pilot notified ATC, and the incident caused no disruption to the flight.

synopsis: A B737-NG on the BSR 2 with a tailwind and an inexperienced First Officer, failed to make the BOLDR speed restriction and then NORCAL changed the approach from the RNAV 28L visual to the TIP TOE 28R causing complicated, distracted and hurried crew actions.
summary: The Captain and First Officer were task-saturated during a late visual approach to SFO, failing to meet the 250 KTS/10,000 FT restriction at BOLDR. The First Officer attributed the high and fast arrival to last-minute runway assignments, unfamiliarity with FMS setup, and leaving the MCP in LVL CHG.

synopsis: A Maintenance Technician missed a step in the MEL deactivation procedure and neglected to open and collar the Auto Speedbrake Circuit Breaker. He sighted time pressure and distractions as contributing factors.
summary: A mechanic deferred a #2 Stall Warning System fault at the gate but missed collaring the Flight Controls Auto Speed Brake Circuit Breaker due to pressure, time constraints, and distractions. The reporter attributed the error to confusing MEL instructions and suggested a consolidated circuit breaker list to prevent recurrence.

synopsis: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports he may have over-tightened the clamp or damaged the threads on a 'T' bar strap that secures the crew oxygen bottle on a B737-700 aircraft. Lack of available correct replacement hardware and pressure to avoid maintenance delays were also noted by Technician.
summary: A mechanic replacing a crew oxygen bottle on a B737-700 used a non-standard locking nut due to stock shortages, potentially over-tightening the clamp or damaging threads. Pressure to avoid delays contributed to the error, but the aircraft was later corrected after the mechanic notified Maintenance Control.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Inspector, a Parts Receiving Inspector, and an Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) report about a Structural Repair Doubler that was inadvertently fabricated and installed from a mislabeled sheet of 2024-0 aluminum instead of the harder 2024-T3 ALCLAD aluminum material. Doublers are being installed over the Horizontal Stab skin cracks found on many B737-700 aircraft.
summary: During a B737-700 heavy check, mechanics installed a horizontal stabilizer doubler using 2024-O aluminum mislabeled as 2024-T3 based on incorrect vendor certifications. The error was discovered when a mechanic noticed the metal dimpled during installation and later found the mislabeled sheet, resulting in the aircraft being grounded.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) questions how a jacking procedure could have been accomplished on one of their MD-80 aircraft without any Load Meters available for their aircraft Lift Jacks and without also addressing the aircraft ballast requirements to prevent an oil-can effect at the Aft Pressure Bulkhead lower web.
summary: Mechanics raised concerns about jacking an MD-80 in a hangar due to missing load meters, required ballast, and cooling jumper procedures outlined in the AMM. Management reportedly dismissed these requirements, causing work delays and leaving the reporter uncertain if the aircraft was eventually jacked safely.

synopsis: SR22 pilot experiences severe turbulence at 8,000 FT, resulting in autopilot disengagement and loss of heading reference for the MFD. The autopilot would not engage and recovery from a descending turn is initiated by hand.
summary: A pilot flying direct to FFT encountered unforecast severe turbulence that disengaged the autopilot and disrupted MFD alignment, causing a disorienting descent while rime ice formed. The pilot manually recovered the aircraft, regained the requested course and altitude, and was cleared to continue to the destination without further incident.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: LEX Local Controller reports of an operational error due to lack of runway distance between an arrival and a departure.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared a departing Aircraft Y for takeoff while an arriving Aircraft X was 3.5 miles out, resulting in only 5,000 feet of separation due to Y's delayed roll and X's high speed. The controller allowed X to land safely rather than issuing a go-around, citing that two departing aircraft in close proximity would be less safe.

synopsis: ZLA Controller describes scenario where a spill out happens close to a busy airport's departure path.
summary: An air traffic controller halted Aircraft Y's climb at FL210 after a Mode C intruder from the Shoshone MOA spilled into airspace near LAS departures. The controller attributed the incident to a lack of proactive notification from the controlling agency regarding the intruder's movement.

synopsis: B757 Captain reports being assigned the Stadium Visual for Runway 29 at EWR and selecting the RNAV (RNP) Y 29 in the FMC, thinking it was the same thing. ATC notes the difference.
summary: The flight crew at EWR inadvertently deviated from their ATC clearance during the short final phase of an RNAV (RNP) Y 29 approach. This occurred because the crew mistakenly believed the RNAV (RNP) procedure was identical to the assigned Stadium Visual, leading to a misunderstanding with Tower.

synopsis: Non-flying pilot follows aircraft but crosses a closed runway without permission.
summary: The pilot was taxiing to 22R when Ground instructed them to follow an air carrier across closed runway 22L. Ground subsequently reprimanded the crew for crossing without clearance, despite the pilot's belief that a closed runway does not require such clearance.

synopsis: ERJ-170 First Officer reported 'severe' wake vortex encounter on approach to SEA that rolled the aircraft beyond 30 degrees of bank and resulted in injury to the Flight Attendant.
summary: During arrival in Seattle at 10,000 feet, the crew encountered severe wake turbulence that caused a 30-degree bank and 200-foot altitude deviation. The Captain recovered the aircraft, but an aft flight attendant was injured hitting the door and floor, requiring medical aid before deplaning.

synopsis: B737-800 First Officer reports the left wing coming into contact with airstairs during a right turn, night time, self parking maneuver.
summary: The flight crew taxied to an FBO for overnight parking and struck parked airstair trucks with the left wingtip while turning right. The reporter attributed the incident to a perception error, lack of ground support for wing clearance monitoring, and difficulty turning the empty aircraft with only the number 2 engine running.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) describes how their troubleshooting efforts identified the cause of a Fuel Distribution System problem on a Dassault Falcon 2000 aircraft. A previous motor actuator replacement installation at the Right Crossfeed Valve Assembly by a Contract Maintenance Vendor was found to be 180-degrees out of position.
summary: A mechanic and the reporter discovered a right-hand fuel crossfeed valve actuator installed 180 degrees out of position on a Dassault Falcon 2000 during troubleshooting at an FBO hangar. Subsequent investigation revealed the left-hand actuator had been removed and reinstalled without documentation, leading to a report for undocumented maintenance.

synopsis: A BE-9L 'Power 90' engine was shutdown and the flight returned to land after the throttle 'snapped' backward during takeoff. Maintenance discovered an incorrect part of BE-9L right engine throttle linkage was lubricated.
summary: The pilot of a BE-9L experienced an uncommanded right throttle snap-back due to over-lubricated linkage during initial climb, causing rapid yaw and power loss. The pilot correctly executed single-engine procedures and landed safely, though the engine feathering was unnecessary as the throttle movement, not an engine failure, caused the thrust loss.

synopsis: C150 pilot experiences substantial shaking and the aircraft pulling to the left on touch down, resulting in a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot reported that shortly after landing, the aircraft shook and pulled left, causing a runway excursion onto grass before re-entering a taxiway. The pilot attributed the loss of control to potential brake imbalance or delayed rudder input, possibly exacerbated by distraction from a student passenger.

synopsis: C172 instructor reports a near collision with a C414 taking off in the opposite direction. The reporter rejects and the C414 pilot continues his takeoff. The radio was found set to the wrong CTAF setting by one click, but was thought to have been mis-set just prior to takeoff. No calls were ever heard from the C414 pilot.
summary: During a training cross-country takeoff, the instructor aborted after spotting a departing twin on the opposite runway. The incident resulted from the crew using an incorrect CTAF frequency (122.75 instead of 122.725) and the other aircraft failing to report its position.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A single engine pilot attempted to fly over the Northern Sierra Nevada Mountains VFR. Enroute he picked up an IFR clearance in IMC but because of wing icing declared an emergency, began descending and diverted to a nearby airport below the initial approach altitude.
summary: The pilot encountered unexpected icing and performance degradation while flying VFR over the Sierra foothills, forcing an emergency declaration and diversion to a high desert airport. After circling to shed ice, the pilot landed safely, noting that initial weather assumptions and delayed descent planning contributed to the incident.

synopsis: PA-34 instructor with ATP student in the left seat reports a nose gear collapse during a touch and go resulting damage to the aircraft.
summary: During an ATP training flight, a student pilot landed the aircraft and attempted a takeoff roll when the nose gear collapsed at 70 knots. The incident occurred after the gear was exercised twice during maneuvers, resulting in the aircraft sliding to a stop and the crew egressing safely.

aircraft: Piper Single Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: PA27 pilot experiences a right main gear collapse during takeoff resulting in aircraft damage.
summary: The pilot reported a right main gear collapse at 45 knots during takeoff, causing the aircraft to slide off the runway and bend the right propeller. Despite a thorough preflight and green gear lights, the pilot could not determine the cause of the failure.

synopsis: During a day VFR flight this non-current instrument rated private pilot encountered IFR conditions, declared an emergency, and flew an IFR approach to his destination airport.
summary: A pilot flying a personal VFR cross-country trip entered IMC while descending through deteriorating weather and declared an emergency for a pop-up IFR clearance. The pilot, who was instrument rated but not current, landed safely after ATC provided vectors, attributing the incident to softened VFR minimums and failure to turn back earlier.

synopsis: CE750 First Officer reports being cleared down to 2,000 feet during approach to MMU resulting in a terrain warning and a low altitude alert from ATC. A climb to 3,000 feet is initiated and the approach is continued.
summary: The flight crew received a terrain advisory while descending to 2,000 feet on arrival into MMU after New York Approach cleared them from 4,000 feet. The crew stopped the descent, climbed to 3,000 feet, and attributed the event to a premature clearance likely caused by a controller change.

synopsis: Pilot reports of busy and confusing airspace while landing at KLDJ.
summary: A pilot reported that transitioning from IFR to VFR too late while flying into KLDJ made it difficult to avoid Class B airspace and identify active runways. The lack of Unicom assistance and inability to contact KEWR Tower or Approach created a hazardous situation where departures were delayed until the pilot canceled IFR.

synopsis: Approach Controller reports of similar sounding call signs problem along with a stitching issue related to fusion radar.
summary: An air traffic controller issued conflicting instructions to three aircraft due to similar call signs and fused radar stitching errors, causing Air Carrier Y to deviate west toward Air Carrier Z. The controller resolved the conflict by assigning visual separation after Air Carrier Y activated TCAS, prompting recommendations to address call sign confusion and radar stitching issues.

synopsis: Controllers at ZHU complain about the responsibility of having to know and provide NOTAM information to pilots after an aircraft is cleared for an instrument approach to a closed runway.
summary: A Radar Controller cleared Aircraft X for an instrument approach to CZT but initially misread a valid runway closure NOTAM as expired. The pilot discovered workers on the runway, canceled IFR, and diverted VFR to COT after the controller corrected the error.

synopsis: DAB Ground Controller notes an aircraft on Taxiway P that he is not talking to. Local 2 informs Ground that the aircraft is his and was supposed to have landed on Runway 7R, but instead landed on P.
summary: Ground Control detected an aircraft landing on Taxiway Papa without communication, later identified as a solo pilot who had not realized the error. The pilot was instructed to stop, issued a warning, and requested an escort back to the ramp after admitting he was not ready for solo flight.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Recip Eng
synopsis: E10 Controller reports of a situation where he is trying to get a VFR aircraft that is having icing problems and visibility problems to its destination. Aircraft enters a higher MVA than the aircraft is cleared to.
summary: An air traffic controller in the Owens Sector cleared Aircraft X to maintain 16,500 feet MSL while transitioning through an active MOA in icing conditions. The controller inadvertently allowed the aircraft to fly below the 16,700-foot MVA due to distraction monitoring military traffic, later realizing the error after handing off to ZOA.

synopsis: ZMP Controller reports of a government agency UAS that did not follow ATC instructions in controlled airspace.
summary: An air traffic controller attempted to issue a 180-degree heading clearance to a UAS delaying in M4S, M5S, and M6S areas. The UAS pilot claimed the flight was preprogrammed and did not respond to a verification query, forcing the controller to move other aircraft instead.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Two reports of an aircraft that should have done a restricted low approach over a closed runway with men and equipment on it.
summary: A Local Controller cleared Aircraft X for a low approach over a closed, occupied runway without issuing a restricted clearance, despite prior verbal briefings. The reporter attributes the error to improper phraseology and notes that the operation was believed to be authorized by higher authorities.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Reporter describes scenario of a CTAF that was used to give control instructions to aircraft.
summary: A pilot of Aircraft X on a visual approach to uncontrolled airport ZZZ received unauthorized landing instructions from a retired controller on the CTAF. The reporter identified this as an inappropriate use of the frequency during an air show where proper NOTAMs and approvals were likely not issued.

synopsis: ZKC Controller reports of a session with weather and high traffic volume where the radar system keyboard locks up, and then they lose the radar. Controller doesn't know if he has a loss of separation between two aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller in Cowes sector faced severe weather, high traffic volume, and equipment failure involving locked keyboards and lost radar. These conditions caused a conflict alert between two aircraft at FL340, leading the controller to expedite separation while questioning management's failure to mitigate the predicted overload.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reports confusion after exiting Runway 29 at EWR on Taxiway W2 and being told to taxi via Y, ending up on the Terminal C east ramp. Lack of signage and taxiway markings is cited.
summary: The flight crew exited Runway 29 at EWR and mistakenly entered another carrier's ramp while attempting to follow a clearance to taxiway Y. The error occurred due to poor signage and markings, but ground control coordinated with ramp personnel to allow the aircraft to continue uneventfully to the gate.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot reports of many changes to the approach and runway they had planned for landing at DEN.
summary: A flight crew reported that multiple approach and runway changes by DEN TRACON during arrival forced the non-flying pilot to work below 10,000 feet MSL, preventing full briefings. The pilot attributed this unsafe task saturation to frequent procedure switches, increasing the risk of frequency errors near converging parallel traffic.

synopsis: On the first flight for aircraft after maintenance was performed, a B737-700 First Officer experiences a cabin altitude warning horn passing through 10,000 FT. The aircraft is leveled and the pressurization control switch is found in the manual position. After restoring pressurization and switching to auto, the flight continues to destination.
summary: On the first flight after maintenance, the crew received a cabin pressurization warning at 10,000 feet caused by the outflow valve switch being in manual. The crew donned oxygen masks, manually closed the outflow valve, and switched to auto to restore normal pressurization before continuing to cruise.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports a severe turbulence encounter at FL320 resulting in a 600 foot altitude loss.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence at FL320 east of BETHL, causing a violent roll and 600-foot altitude loss. Control was regained after disconnecting the autopilot, resulting in no injuries and a continued flight to landing.

synopsis: A B737-NG was removed from the ZZZ RNAV for vectors to the RNAV (RNP) Y XXL ZZZZZ1 waypoint but when the RNAV was deleted the ZZZZZ and ZZZZZ2 waypoints on the RNAV (RNP) Y XXL were also erroneously deleted which caused a track deviation prior to radar vectors to ZZZZZ1.
summary: The flight crew experienced confusion during the arrival phase when ATC issued radar vectors to ZZZZZ1 instead of the charted RNAV RNP (Y) XXL approach from ZZZZZ. This led to a route discontinuity after the crew deleted the initial approach without reloading subsequent fixes, a known issue ATC and the airline are addressing.

synopsis: B737 flight crew report a NMAC with a glider over SWEET intersection at 7,000 feet.
summary: The pilot reported a near-miss with a glider while crossing SWEET at 7,000 feet during descent. The glider, located 100 to 200 feet above and 300 to 400 feet left, was spotted visually after the aircraft ahead had previously reported its position.

synopsis: C402 Captain experiences restricted control column movement during attempt to rotate and rejects the takeoff. Inspection reveals the number two VOR control head to be loose in its mount and protruding enough to block the aft motion of the yoke.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff when a loose #2 VOR head blocked full aft yoke movement at rotation speed. The obstruction was discovered after the aircraft returned to the ramp, preventing the pilot from rotating the aircraft.

synopsis: An air carrier on a vector to intercept the SKBO Runway 31 LOC descended toward 10,000 FT before the BOG VOR but climbed after recieving an EGPWS terrain warning concurrent with an ATC request for current flight conditions.
summary: The flight crew descended below the assigned 12,000 FT while intercepting the LOC at SKBO, triggering a GPWS terrain warning. The pilot attributed the incident to crew error and ATC communication gaps regarding the mandatory altitude hold until over the BOG VOR.

synopsis: An Air Carrier Flight Attendant reported her crew and some passengers became ill from an unknown substance during flight so the Captain diverted where medical treatment was administered at a local hospital.
summary: During a transatlantic flight, flight attendants and a passenger experienced burning eyes, throat irritation, and dizziness, leading the captain to divert to the nearest airport. The crew reported symptoms worsened near the galley and 2R door, and while medical personnel treated the most affected attendant, no specific cause was identified before the crew was released from the hospital.

synopsis: A C182 private pilot departing VGT at night becomes concerned about terrain to the west when the aircraft does not perform as expected and the requested route of flight directly over LAS is not granted.
summary: A VFR pilot departing North Las Vegas at night encountered mountain wave turbulence and poor climb performance while flying a ROCKS departure. The pilot experienced spatial disorientation and drift due to strong winds, leading to a reprimand from the controller for failing to maintain the assigned heading.

synopsis: Reporters describe loss of separation between two aircraft due to a head on situation the Controller had previously denied, with a third aircraft.
summary: A New York Center controller and trainee in Sector R55 rejected a late handoff of Aircraft X at FL190 from Sector 25 due to head-on traffic. Aircraft X entered the sector without approval, causing loss of separation with Aircraft Y and Z, prompting the controller to recommend adjacent sectors adhere to 7110.65 regulations.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Reporter describes situation where a Local Controller does not use the prescribed separation between two aircraft and has an operational error.
summary: IAD Local Control 1 cleared Aircraft X to pass behind Aircraft Y on final to Runway 1R without issuing visual separation instructions. This resulted in a loss of separation, with Aircraft X passing only 900 feet below and 0.49 miles behind, attributed to the controller's lack of radar and RTF training.

synopsis: A300 Captain experiences an ADC failure at FL330 with the First Officer on a bathroom break. The autopilot pitches over, attempting to maintain Mach number which is decaying on the Captain's instruments. The First Officer returns to find the airspeed 20 knots into the barber pole on his side. The airspeed is stabilized at 280, an emergency is declared and the flight diverts to a suitable airport.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced an airspeed and ADC disagreement at FL330, causing autopilot disconnection and conflicting speed indications. They declared an emergency, diverted to ZZZ, and landed safely after managing stall buffet and instrument failures.

synopsis: CRJ-700 Captain describes an IMC airborne conflict with an unknown, unseen aircraft on approach to LGA. The reporter believes the 72 hours CAT B repair allowance is too long without an operable TCAS.
summary: A pilot reported concerns regarding the TCAS MEL status while operating an aircraft with inoperative TCAS during final approach at LGA and a ground stop before departure. The pilot argued that the current 72-hour CAT B deferral period is unsafe, citing scenarios where lack of TCAS, ATC, or radar in IMC conditions could lead to collisions.

synopsis: An A320 ECAM alerted F/CTRL - AIL SERVO FAULT, so the crew completed the ECAM, the QRH. Then they notified Dispatch and Maintenance as they proceeded to their destination.
summary: During cruise climb through FL310 with Auto Pilot #2 engaged, the flight crew experienced a slight left roll and an AIL SERVO FAULT ECAM indicating a right aileron computer failure. The crew followed QRH procedures, advised Dispatch and Maintenance, and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 developed a STAB TRIM runaway condition and the new hire First Officer completed the immediate action and QRH procedures. The flight diverted to the nearest airport where an emergency was declared.
summary: A Captain and new First Officer experienced a runaway STAB TRIM enroute, diverting to a major airport due to thunderstorms and landing without trim. The pilot attributed the event to a recurring motor short circuit, noting six prior unresolved maintenance write-ups and criticizing repeated cost-effective resets.

synopsis: MGGT ATC vectored an aircraft for the ILS Runway 02 Z but when the EGPWS alerted TERRAIN at 8,000 FT within five miles of mountainous terrain, the escape maneuver was accomplished followed by a climb to 9,000 FT and the full approach.
summary: During descent to MGGT, the crew received radar vectors that triggered a GPWS alert, forcing a climb from 8,000 to 9,000 feet to avoid terrain. The pilot attributed the incident to ATC altitude errors and language limitations, recommending adherence to charted STARs and full approaches in mountainous areas.

synopsis: An A319 crew was surprised by the aircraft transitioning to Managed Speed and accelerating to overspeed the flaps while on approach at 3,000 FT in the HDG and SPD SEL modes, APP not activated, so the crew executed a go-around, but returned for a normal landing.
summary: During a visual approach in an A319, the crew experienced an inadvertent activation of managed speed mode below 7,200 feet, causing rapid acceleration in gusty winds. The pilots executed a go-around after the First Officer pitched up to prevent overspeeding, resulting in a missed landing.

synopsis: A310 First Officer describes a night ILS approach with the tower closed that is unstable from the beginning. The crew is distracted by CTAF procedures, terrain considerations, and a C172 making approaches to an intersecting runway. The approach is continued to landing as the C172 crosses down field on a low approach.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced an unstable ILS approach due to a double slat failure and distraction from a C172 on an intersecting runway. The crew landed fast and low, while the C172 crossed the runway centerline shortly after, attributed to the First Officer's inexperience with uncontrolled fields and failure to manage the Captain's task saturation.

synopsis: BE-95 instructor disregarded fuel quantity gauges and accepted student pilot's assurance that tanks were full. After approximately one hour of flight the right engine lost power. Power was restored by switching to the auxiliary tank. Upon return to home field, left engine quit on the ramp due to fuel exhaustion.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot experienced a right engine failure during an RNAV approach in a Twin Beech 95 due to empty main tanks, despite the student's incorrect report of full fuel. The left engine subsequently failed on the ground after landing, revealing the tanks were actually empty because the previous flight had not refueled.

synopsis: C560XL flight crew on a visual approach lined up for the wrong airport until noticing that they were paralleling the Final Approach Course on the FMS. Crew re-established course to destination and landed without further incident.
summary: The flight crew misidentified the airport during a visual approach to Runway XX after being cleared by Center and switched to Tower. They corrected the error upon noticing the aircraft paralleled the FMS final approach course, turned to the correct destination, and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: A PA-28 instructor pilot took the aircraft from his student and executed a climbing, turning avoidance maneuver from traffic which ATC pointed out late as it turned toward them.
summary: A pilot and student on an IFR flight at 3,000 feet executed an emergency left turn and climb to avoid a low-wing Piper that turned directly toward them. The pilot attributed the conflict to the controller's delayed traffic advisory and the Piper's maneuver causing a momentary loss of sight.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: The pilot of a general aviation aircraft, cleared to taxi to Runway 5 at MYF but, believing he was holding short of Runway 10R, crossed Runway 5, mistakenly, without a clearance when he heard another aircraft cleared to Runway 5. Sighted faded runway signage as contributing factor.
summary: A pilot at MYF crossed active Runway 5 without clearance while taxiing to the non-standard departure runway, mistaking faded signage for Runway 10. The incident resulted from poor visibility of runway markings, a lack of situational awareness tools, and ambiguous communication with Ground Control.

synopsis: This ATP pilot, flying a small single engine G/A airplane in the traffic pattern at an uncontrolled airport and conforming to expected radio protocol, reports a near miss with another aircraft apparently not communicating.
summary: Two pilots operating in day VFR conditions experienced a 150-foot separation conflict while entering the left downwind leg of the traffic pattern. The incident occurred because the second pilot failed to see the first aircraft and incorrectly executed a turn across its path, leading to a heated ground exchange regarding right-of-way rules.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: CRQ Local Controller describes situation where fire fighting aircraft exit the TFR and become a conflict for an arrival.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported a near-midair conflict at CRQ between an ILS-approaching aircraft and a firefighting aircraft climbing opposite direction on final. The incident resulted from delayed Temporary Flight Restrictions and a lack of proactive ATC coordination with uncommunicating firefighting operations.

aircraft: Medium Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: ZSU Controller reports of two instances where he receives aircraft from a foreign facility not at the coordinated altitude.
summary: The Radar Associate reported that Aircraft Y and Aircraft X crossed the MELLA boundary at incorrect altitudes (FL360 and FL350) despite prior coordination for FL350 and FL370. The reporter attributes these deviations to mis-coordination by the Santo Domingo ACC controller, potentially exacerbated by local labor disputes.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZAN Controller reports of an aircraft descending into a lower MVA and having radio problems trying to reach this aircraft to tell it to climb.
summary: Edmonton ACC and Whitehorse Sector controllers managed Aircraft X, which descended below its assigned FL240 due to a pilot error while holding near JAGIT. Controllers relayed a low altitude alert via another aircraft after losing direct contact, prompting the pilot to climb back to FL240.

synopsis: DTW Ground Controller describes scenario where an aircraft crosses an active runway with a departure rolling down the runway. Pilot describes situation differently, where no aircraft deviation was required. Another Air Carrier over flew the taxiing aircraft.
summary: A Ground Controller issued taxi instructions to Aircraft X, which crossed Runway 4R while an Air Carrier was on departure roll, causing the departing aircraft to fly over Aircraft X. The controller attributed the incursion to confusion over a standard clearance to cross the closed Runway 9L, though no aircraft deviation was required.

synopsis: RSW Controller reports that an air carrier had a NMAC with an aircraft that the Controller did not see on the radar.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X descended to 4,000 feet on the SHFTY arrival to RSW and came within 300 feet of Aircraft Y. The controller attributed the near miss to high workload, frequent false primary targets causing mental filtering, and Aircraft Y's transponder failing to display on radar or TCAS.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: A ZLC Controller reports of a protected airspace that has two centers and the Controller does not know which is the correct one. Aircraft are flying through one of the areas because they do not know where the exact point is.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that conflicting rocket launch area coordinates, defined by both latitude/longitude and fixed radial distance, created two separate five-mile protected zones five miles apart. This discrepancy caused uncounted aircraft to be vectored into one protected airspace while attempting to avoid the other.

synopsis: IAD Specialist reports of a go-around caused by the Local Controller expediting traffic when not necessary.
summary: Local Control cleared Aircraft X to land on Runway 1R while simultaneously launching Aircraft Y for takeoff in a tight squeeze. Aircraft X initiated an unannounced go-around after crossing the threshold, which the controller attributed to unnecessary traffic pressure and a lack of required training.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: DFW Local Assist reports of problem associated with departure procedures, separation of aircraft, and aircraft that drift off departure path.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller observed Aircraft X drifting east of Runway 18L toward Aircraft Y on Runway 17R, suspecting a loss of separation violating DFW departure waivers. The controller attributed the risk to inadequate procedures for independent parallel departures and noted a dismissive response from the Supervisor.

synopsis: When cleared, first, to descend on the CENTERPOINT STAR and subsequently to fly the RNAV (RNP) Z Rwy 22 at SAT the flight crew of a B737NG was uncertain as to compliance with altitude restrictions at waypoint MEDIN which is a fix on the STAR and an IAF for the RNAV approach.
summary: The pilot reported confusion regarding an RNAV (RNP) RWY 22 approach clearance after crossing BENEY at 10,000'. The incident involved uncertainty over whether the initial clearance permitted descending below 10,000' before reaching the MEDIN waypoint to comply with approach altitudes.

synopsis: After Maintenance clearance an A300, crew ferried the aircraft which had diverted for an overspeed. During cruise, with the autopilot on 2, an ADC/IAS ECAM was displayed as the Captain's instruments and autothrottle indicated a trend toward overspeed until ADC 2 was selected.
summary: The crew experienced an ADC/IAS discrepancy and autopilot instability at FL280 following a previous overspeed event. They resolved the issue by disconnecting autothrottles, switching the ADC, and manually managing thrust, attributing the cause to unreliable indications rather than aircraft damage.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A pilot on the CLT IVANE THREE RNAV noted that a clearance to descend VIA could lead one to cross IVANE at 10,000 FT only to climb for the GIZMO 11,000 FT constraint. A chart note should be added indicating the IVANE 10,000 FT is only for Runway 23.
summary: The pilot reported a potential chart error on the IVANE THREE RNAV arrival into CLT where IVANE is listed at 16,000–10,000 feet while the next fix, GIZMO, requires 13,000–11,000 feet. This conflicting data could cause an altitude bust by requiring an unnecessary climb, and the pilot believes a misprint needs correction.

synopsis: In VMC conditions, a B777 Captain on approach to LHR Runway 27R disengaged the autopilot after the LOC activated then attempted a turned to a 360 heading instead of 271 to track the localizer. With autopilot OFF and while hand flying, the same anomaly occurred. After landing a FMC message RW ILS ERROR was displayed.
summary: The pilot reported an ILS malfunction on approach to EGLL 27R where the autopilot captured a 360-degree course instead of 271. After landing, an FMC "RW ILS ERROR" message confirmed the incorrect course, prompting the crew to report the issue to maintenance.

synopsis: Widebody First Officer reported encountering wake turbulence in trail of an Airbus at 200 FT AGL on approach to MEM.
summary: The crew experienced a wing rock at 200 AGL on final approach to Runway 36L behind an Airbus, likely due to wake turbulence from close ATC spacing and speed differences. They elected to go around.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew departing OGG reports not complying with ATC clearance to climb via the SWEEP 1, fly heading 020. ATC intended that the crew maintain heading 020 and ignore the SWEEP 1.
summary: The flight crew departed Runway 02 at OGG, flying the SWEEP 1 SID after omitting "climb via SID" during readback, despite a clearance to fly heading 020. HCF queried the deviation, instructing the crew to maintain present heading, attributing the confusion to ambiguous phraseology regarding the SID versus the assigned departure heading.

synopsis: A confusing NOTAM, unclear ATIS, and a flight planning reference from the company incorrectly advising the current chart reflected the change in the NOTAM caused a short track deviation by the flight crew of an air carrier flight inbound to MMMX.
summary: Pilots on an ILS 05R arrival into MMMX initially followed the charted 160-degree outbound course from SMO despite a NOTAM for VFR changes. ATC subsequently instructed an intercept of the 168 radial, a confusion attributed to the digital ATIS outage and unclear audio.

synopsis: EMB-170 Captain reports being cleared to FL350 from FL290, setting the new altitude in the FGCP, selecting vertical speed and spinning the vertical speed wheel, but in the wrong direction, resulting in a descent.
summary: The pilot inadvertently selected a descent instead of a climb after receiving clearance to FL350 while at 29,000 feet. The aircraft descended briefly before the pilot corrected the vertical speed input, and the flight subsequently climbed to FL350 without further incident.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 3 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Captain refused to allow Customer Service Agents to close the main cabin door because passengers were not seated nor baggage stowed in the open overheads, but insistent agents cited a Company memo directing their behavior.
summary: A pilot at LAX stopped two Customer Service Managers from closing the aircraft door at the gate because overhead bins were open and passengers held bags. The managers threatened the pilot to prioritize on-time departure over safety, pressuring the lead flight attendant to close the door prematurely in violation of regulations.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain experiences a NMAC with a light aircraft at 8,000 feet near GILRO. TCAS issued a descend RA and the Captain believes that the intruder was also descending. Both aircraft maneuvered to fly reciprocal courses.
summary: A flight crew on an HYP 5 STAR arrival to SJC received a TCAS RA at 8,000 feet after ATC issued conflicting traffic avoidance instructions. The crew executed a descent while the conflicting aircraft passed overhead 400 feet above, prompting a recommendation for improved pilot education in the NorCal area.
