synopsis: B737-700 flight crew departing Runway 34L at RNO reports a runway incursion by a Cessna taxiing at high speed on Runway 25 through the intersection.
summary: Pilots at RNO observed a Cessna rapidly crossing Runway 34L shortly after the 80 KT callout while cleared for takeoff. Tower later explained the Cessna was on Ground frequency and had been instructed to hold short, though the pilots completed an uneventful takeoff.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Large Transport flight crew on takeoff roll, approaching V1, detects a small passenger jet incurring ahead and a simultaneous command from the Tower to abort the takeoff. The Captain elects to continue at this point and clears the CRJ by less than 100 feet.
summary: A Detroit crew on Runway 04R continued takeoff after Tower ordered an abort due to an unauthorized small jet crossing the runway. The pilots judged aborting unsafe at high speed, flying over the incursion by 75–100 feet, and later learned the crossing aircraft lacked clearance.

synopsis: A B737-NG crew flying the SMF WRAPS 5 changed the arrival to a south landing on Runway 16R and after executing the FMS change, all route data except the runway dropped out.
summary: During the WRAPS 5 arrival into SMF, the First Officer and Captain experienced a navigation route drop-out after switching to south flow. ATC provided vectors to Runway 16R, and the flight concluded uneventfully, though the exact cause of the system failure remained unknown.

synopsis: A319 Captain reports discovering enroute to ABQ that night visual approaches to Runway 26 are no longer authorized by his company and that the change is not obvious when scanning the Briefing Page.
summary: The flight crew en route to Albuquerque discovered Runway 26 was unauthorized at night only after reviewing a poorly formatted Briefing Page with small print. Consequently, they diverted to the shorter Runway 30, criticizing the lack of prominent warnings or revision bars for this operational change.

synopsis: On takeoff B757 flight crew smells smoke and moments later a call from the cabin indicates there may be a fire. Crew elects to return immediately and does so. An overheated pack is suspected and turned off after landing.
summary: Pilots detected a smoke odor and received a cabin fire report shortly after takeoff, prompting an emergency declaration and immediate landing. After rescue crews found no fire and the left pack temperature spiked, the crew turned off the pack and taxied back to the gate without evacuating.

synopsis: CRJ200 First Officer reports being dispatched with both FMS's on MEL due to expired databases. The destination airport glideslope is out of service but upon arrival it is found the entire ILS is out of service and only a visual approach is possible a 1,000 foot ceiling. Two attempts are required and on the second attempt the landing gear is forgotten until reminded by the GPWS.
summary: The crew dispatched an aircraft with expired FMS databases to Syracuse, where ambiguous NOTAMS and a visual approach briefing error caused a gear horn warning at 1,000 feet AGL. The flight landed safely, but the incident highlighted risks from outdated equipment, unclear airport status, and insufficient visual approach planning.

synopsis: A DHC-8-100 gear warning horn sounded at gear extension so an emergency was declared, a go-around executed, and the gear retracted because the warning horn volume interfered with checklist performance. The gear lowered normally the second time, but after a delayed alert again the emergency extension checklist was completed followed by a normal landing.
summary: The flight crew experienced an excessively loud, unsilenceable landing gear warning horn on final approach that prevented communication, prompting a go-around and gear retraction. After successfully extending the gear again and performing an alternate extension due to a recurring unsafe nose gear light, the aircraft landed safely and was ferried for maintenance.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A small aircraft pilot reported a near miss with a military transport near FAY as he attempted to establish flight following with an intermittent transponder.
summary: A VFR pilot flying at 2,500 feet in Class C airspace experienced a 400-foot vertical separation with a climbing military transport. The incident occurred because the controller initially could not see the pilot on radar due to a suspected transponder issue, which was later resolved after recycling the code.

synopsis: A flight crew misunderstood the revised PDC clearance and so entered the route incorrect before takeoff. In flight ATC detected the track deviation and stated 'hundreds of crew' makes the same mistake.
summary: The flight crew entered an amended ATC clearance into the FMS during cruise, omitting waypoint FLM due to confusion between the new route and the original flight plan. This resulted in an off-course deviation, which ATC attributed to a recurring issue with the clearance format that misled hundreds of crews.

synopsis: Instrument qualified C182 pilot experienced track and altitude deviations on two attempted RNAV approaches in IMC due to lack of familiarity with the model of GPS installed. Pilot landed safely after vectors to an airport in VMC.
summary: A pilot flying a Cessna 182 in IMC unintentionally descended 1,000 feet and banked 30–40 degrees while attempting to program a Garmin GTN650 GPS for an RNAV approach. The incident was caused by the pilot's unfamiliarity with the new GPS interface and its interaction with the autopilot, leading to a missed approach and diversion to another airport.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reports of while under flight following the Approach Control issues traffic of two heavy aircraft, one above and one below his aircraft. Pilot is concerned about wake turbulence and later wishes they had been vectored around traffic.
summary: A low-time pilot and passenger experienced a traffic conflict while returning from SUS at 4,500 feet MSL. Whiteman Approach issued alerts for two heavy aircraft at 5,000 and 4,000 feet that passed directly over and under the small aircraft, creating a dangerous wake turbulence situation the reporter attributed to poor vectoring.

synopsis: After takeoff on a night training flight, a fatigued PA-34 commercial student turned the left magneto OFF instead of turning the landing light OFF. The instructor, not knowing the engine failure cause, assumed control but failed to feather the engine and, unable to climb or accelerate, had great difficulty controlling the aircraft. The left flap and wing tip were damaged during landing which was followed by a brief runway excursion.
summary: A Piper Seneca instructor and student experienced a left engine failure during a night training flight's final pattern, likely caused by the student inadvertently turning off the left magneto. The instructor declared an emergency, struggled with dim instruments and low airspeed, and executed a firm landing that resulted in a runway excursion and undetected wing damage.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A medium transport First Officer reported that on approach to UUWW the crew requested a QNH approach but when ATC, with poor English skills did not respond, they assume QNH clearance but determined later they were not cleared and had descended too low.
summary: An experienced pilot flying into Vnukouvo descended to 600 meters QFE instead of the required 2,660 feet QNH due to a lack of controller response and poor English proficiency. The pilot attributed the unsafe low altitude to this communication failure and noted the situation was only safe because of clear daytime weather.

synopsis: An instructor and student departed OKV and while climbing through 1,500 FT took evasive action from a UAS approximately 1.5 miles south of the airport.
summary: A student pilot and instructor in a helicopter encountered a small red UAV at 1,500 MSL near OKV airport while climbing. The crew descended and turned left to avoid the drone, which the reporter states was operating too high and close to the airport without proper regulation.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: An instructor pilot with student on a visual approach to GYI Runway 17L reported taking evasive action during a near miss from an aircraft on a practice to the same runway but flying opposite direction.
summary: A flight instructor and student on final approach to Runway 17L at GYI executed an emergency right turn to avoid a head-on conflict with a practice approach aircraft. The near-miss, caused by high traffic density, lack of radar service, and inadequate situational awareness, resulted in less than 500 feet of horizontal separation.

aircraft: Sikorsky Helicopter Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Helicopter pilot experiences a NMAC with a seaplane over the East River exclusion in NYC while turning to land at the East 34th Street Heliport.
summary: A helicopter pilot holding at 1,000 feet AGL over the East River lost visual contact with a seaplane, which then appeared in the left window while the helicopter was cleared to land. The pilot aborted the descent to avoid a collision, noting the seaplane flew below holding traffic without communication or TCAS warnings.

synopsis: C337 pilot reports failure of the landing gear to retract after takeoff with green indications. The gear handle is placed down with the green indications remaining steady. After landing during taxi off the runway the nose gear collapses.
summary: During a training flight, the pilot experienced a nose gear retraction failure after landing, causing a propeller strike while taxiing. The aircraft was safely stopped with no fuel leaks or runway damage, and ARFF was notified to assist.

synopsis: C172 pilot reports a NMAC with another C172 at a visual reporting point requesting clearance into HNL Class B airspace.
summary: A Cessna 172 with transponder issues turned north away from HNL while the reporter, already cleared into HNL Bravo, pushed the yoke down to separate from the aircraft above and to the right. The reporter continued the approach and noted the need for more proactive radio communication and aggressive visual scanning to prevent collisions.

synopsis: C195 pilot experiences a sudden crosswind gust during landing roll and departs the runway causing damage to the aircraft.
summary: The pilot reported that an unexpected 90-degree crosswind at midfield during the landing rollout caused the aircraft to veer off the right runway shoulder, damaging the left wingtip and gear. The pilot attributed the loss of control to the unreported wind condition and suggested AWOS should include midfield crosswind warnings.

synopsis: Two pilots involved in a midair collision during a low altitude formation flight describe the circumstances that caused the event.
summary: During an airshow low-altitude pass over a jet truck, the slot pilot overtook the lead aircraft in a four-ship formation, causing a propeller strike on the lead's tail spring. The incident resulted in lost propeller blades and a missing tail spring, though both aircraft landed safely after the formation discontinued the act.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: ZLC Controller reports of airborne conflict because pilot turned in opposite direction as instructed and readback.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a left turn to Aircraft X to avoid Aircraft Y during climb near Rock Springs, but Aircraft X turned right instead. The resulting 4-mile, 800-foot proximity was caused by a pilot error where one crew member read back correctly while the other turned the wrong direction.

synopsis: Numerous reports of a go-around caused by the departure of an aircraft that didn't roll as fast as the Local Controller anticipated.
summary: Aircraft X went around while Aircraft Y departed Runway 15 at ANC due to Aircraft Y failing to execute a no-delay takeoff. The controller reported maintaining visual separation on diverging courses, while the pilot attributed the unsafe proximity to the controller's negligence and lack of coordination.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: NCT Controller reports of airborne conflict due to another Controller not complying with prior coordination.
summary: Air Traffic Controllers in Sectors 29, 44, and Paradise (NCT) managed Aircraft X and Y near a sector boundary. A potential conflict occurred when Aircraft Y climbed to FL190 instead of stopping at FL170, likely due to Paradise sector's workload and coordination errors, prompting a recommendation to raise NCT airspace to FL230.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot reports of porpoising on final and then having to execute a missed approach, while off his left an air carrier departing is turning towards him. Controllers report of pilot not advising the Tower that the aircraft was going around.
summary: The controller vectored Aircraft X for a VFR landing at SFO while clearing Aircraft Y for takeoff on the adjacent runway. Aircraft X executed an unannounced go-around after a porpoising landing, creating a potential collision risk with Aircraft Y before the pilot finally declared intentions to divert to San Carlos.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew experiences loss of airspeed indication and erroneous altitude indication during cruise a FL330. EEC had switched to soft alternate. The Captain's instruments are determined to be correct and descent out of RVSM is initiated.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced conflicting altitude and airspeed indications at FL330, causing an unintended descent before the Captain regained control. The crew descended below RVSM airspace after EECs reverted to alternate mode, and the aircraft was grounded for pitot/static system checks.

synopsis: B737-300 Fist Officer reports a last minute change from runway 24R to 25L then to 25R at LAX which causes confusion and possible altitude and track deviations. The Captain reports the field in sight and is cleared for the visual.
summary: A -300 crew inbound to LAX experienced degraded situational awareness after a last-minute clearance change from ILS 25L to a direct TAANK for ILS 25R. The resulting delay in reprogramming the flight management system caused the aircraft to drift right and go slightly low before the crew recovered and completed a visual approach.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports confusion during a busy arrival, believing that a clearance direct BAMBU on ILS 26R is instead a clearance to BAMMM on the DIRTY 2 arrival. A track deviation is quickly corrected by ATC.
summary: The crew flying into ATL flew to the wrong fix due to confusion between similar names and missed ATC instructions caused by cabin announcements. The First Officer failed to respond, leading the Pilot Flying to mishear the clearance and vector toward the incorrect fix before ATC corrected the heading.

synopsis: After selecting ALT INTV to initiate a descent to the MDW PANGG1 RNAV SAILZ waypoint, a B737-800 leveled at 3,300 FT with the FMA indicating ALT HLD but 3,000 FT set in both the MCP and FMC. ATC alerted the crew about the error.
summary: Two Boeing 787 crews cleared direct SAILZ to descend to 3,000 feet inadvertently leveled off at 3,300 feet despite correct FMS settings. The pilots suspect a software issue common to the aircraft type after both flights reported the same altitude deviation.

synopsis: After departure, the flight crew momentarily detected a burning rubber odor. The odor was stronger in the cabin which caused the flight attendants to be persistent so the Captain returned to the departure airport for a cautionary landing.
summary: The flight crew and two flight attendants detected chemical and burning rubber odors at 500 feet after departure, prompting a return to the departure airport. The aircraft executed an overweight landing at 420,120 lbs with a 200 FPM sink rate as advised by dispatch.

synopsis: A321 Captain experiences a jolt during passenger boarding caused by a tug running into the tow bar. A bag handler reported to the Captain that 'the tug slipped into gear'.
summary: During boarding, an unattended tug struck the tow-bar, causing the aircraft to roll back two feet and damage the nose gear shear pin. A bag handler reported the tug slipped into gear, though no injuries occurred among the few people on board.

synopsis: EMB135 flight crew experiences stiff rudder pedals during the initial takeoff roll and rejects the takeoff. The yaw damper was annunciated upon slowing and flight returned to the gate for a ground stop.
summary: The Captain and First Officer aborted takeoff at 30 KIAS due to stiff rudder pedals and a new YD MSG annunciator. They returned to the gate for a ground stop, attributing the issue to a spurious glitch after completing standard operating procedures.

synopsis: B747 Captain laments late and poorly planned flights by station representatives and dispatchers. The Captain believes that ice crystal forecasts should be part of the package handed to crews during preflight.
summary: The Captain reported that a Station Representative and Dispatcher caused delays by failing to deliver timely flight planning paperwork and PROG charts. The Dispatcher filed a route through severe weather at FL370 without proper charts, forcing the crew to deviate 100 NM and add 8,000 KG of fuel to safely navigate the storm.

synopsis: EMB-120 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence after takeoff from SFO in trail of a B737.
summary: The pilot reported that Tower cleared multiple aircraft to hold short of Runway 28R with insufficient space, causing jet wash and wake turbulence issues during departure. The pilot attributed the incident to Tower prioritizing departure volume over safe spacing and their own failure to question the clearance.

synopsis: During taxi for takeoff, the forward and aft flight attendants detected a strong burning electrical odor with a light white cabin haze so as the aircraft returned to the gate. The Aft Flight Attendant opened the door to prevent herself from passing out. Headaches, light headedness and breathing difficulties were reported with elevated blood pressure and two flight attendants CO level readings of 5.8 and 1.7.
summary: Cabin crew detected a burning electrical odor and haze during taxi, causing breathing difficulties and headaches. The aircraft returned to the gate where doors were opened for ventilation, clearing the fumes, while the crew attributed communication delays to interphone limitations.

synopsis: Lancair pilot at FL190 experiences a sudden power loss combined with loss of cabin pressurization. An emergency is declared and flight descends to 12,000 feet where available engine power is sufficient and flight continues to destination. A turbocharger malfunction was thought to be the culprit although the aircraft had just come out of annual inspection.
summary: The pilot experienced an abrupt loss of manifold pressure and cabin pressurization at FL190, likely due to a turbo-boost failure or wastegate issue. After leaning the mixture to restore power, the pilot descended to 12,000 feet and continued safely to the destination for maintenance.

synopsis: A CL605 Captain and a BE36 pilot approaching HPN, describe an airborne conflict that develops while both aircraft are being controlled by ATC. The CL605 Captain takes evasive action for a TCAS RA with the BE36 and the BE36 pilot is issued a 360 by ATC to rejoin final for Runway 34. A third aircraft on approach to Runway 29 is issued a go-around.
summary: The pilot on final for Runway 34 at HPN executed a TCAS RA and visual maneuver to avoid an aircraft inbound for Runway 29, passing within 150 feet. The reporter attributed the conflict to ATC runway changes and lack of specific downwind instructions, which caused poor spacing and a subsequent go-around for the other aircraft.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: DAB Controller reports of an computer issue related to STARS. When changing aircraft type, the STARS changes aircraft from VFR to IFR.
summary: An Air Defense controller amended Aircraft X's type in the FDIO, causing its status to change from VFR to IFR in STARS but not in the NAS. The reporter attributes this recurring issue to a system flaw and requests a STARS build patch to prevent type changes from altering flight status.

synopsis: ZOA Controller describes situation in which he has taken a handoff and then observes the flight in an other direction. He calls the other sector and they have issued a route change with out advising the receiving Controller.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Sector 29 changed Aircraft X's altitude and route during a handoff without coordination, causing the aircraft to deviate north of its filed path. The controller attributed this unsafe situation to misinterpretation of 7110.65 paragraph 5-4-5(b) regarding handoff coordination requirements.

synopsis: B737 flight crew encounters scattered clouds during a visual approach requiring ILS information which had not been tuned in on the Captain's side. An overshoot and descent below glidepath both occur while the ILS is tuned in, resulting in an unstabilized approach.
summary: The crew missed the ILS localizer capture on approach to HOU Runway 04 because the #1 VHF NAV was not tuned, causing a descent below the glideslope. Although they corrected the flight path and landed safely in VMC, the reporter noted a go-around would have been more prudent given the configuration and navigation error.

synopsis: CRJ200 Captain laments the increasingly complex RNAV arrivals and departures with their associated descend via or climb via clearances with altitude modifications.
summary: A pilot approaching Denver on the WAHUU arrival received a confusing "descend via" clearance with a 11,000-foot restriction, requiring supervisor intervention to clarify step-down requirements. The reporter attributes the confusion to complex RNAV procedures and inconsistent ATC phraseology, recommending standardized language to reduce cockpit workload.

synopsis: C172 instrument instructor experiences an altitude deviation by his CFII student during a GPS approach. ATC also takes note of the deviation.
summary: A flight instructor and CFI-Instrument candidate flying an IFR RNAV (GPS) approach descended below the 2,000 MSL intermediate minimum due to the candidate's failure to maintain an effective cross-check. The instructor corrected the descent, but Approach issued a low altitude warning, prompting scheduled simulator training to reinforce instrument scan and cockpit management.

synopsis: A C120 pilot reported losing control during rollout resulting in a runway excursion and the aircraft flipping onto its back.
summary: A C120 pilot reported that during landing rollout, a right crosswind caused the aircraft to veer right, pitch forward, and strike the propeller on the runway. The aircraft subsequently flipped inverted on the grass, but occupants were not injured.

synopsis: C172 student pilot experiences loss of throttle control when power is reduced abeam the numbers in the traffic pattern with the engine at 900 RPM. A successful idling approach and landing is accomplished. During taxi back to the FBO engine RPM increases uncontrollably and the aircraft is shut down short of the ramp and Maintenance is called.
summary: The pilot experienced an uncommanded RPM drop to 900 during a touch-and-go approach, followed by an uncontrollable RPM increase to 1900 while taxiing. Despite checking controls and contacting the tower, the pilot landed safely and shut down the aircraft after the engine failed to respond to throttle or mixture adjustments.

synopsis: AA5 pilot with instructor reports momentary loss of control at 50 feet AGL caused by rotor wash from a helicopter landing on the parallel taxiway. The helicopter and a building are narrowly avoided as control is regained and a go-around is initiated.
summary: The pilot and CFI in a fixed-wing aircraft experienced severe rotor wash while less than 50 feet AGL during a touch-and-go, caused by ATC clearing a helicopter to land on a nearby taxiway. The incident resulted in a hard 45-degree bank requiring full throttle and nose-down input to avoid ground, building, and helicopter strikes before executing a go-around.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: OGG Controller reports of a problem with assigning a heading and a Climb via SID together on departure.
summary: An air traffic controller issued Aircraft X a clearance to LAX via the SWEEP1 SID with an initial heading of 020, but the pilot flew the SID's 024 heading instead. The controller attributed this deviation to confusion over conflicting LOA requirements and "Climb via SID" phraseology, noting the pilot did not question the clearance.

synopsis: LIT Approach Controller reports of loss of separation while working a busy session at night with weather.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller working Radar West during a rare Runway 7 operation with weather and multiple military arrivals experienced a loss of separation between Aircraft X and Aircraft Y. The controller attributed the incident to the failure to split off the Radar North position despite requests, which would have provided necessary support for the complex traffic configuration.

synopsis: ZLA Controller reports of a communication problem which involved an airspace violation.
summary: An air traffic controller at Sector 07 intercepted Aircraft X, which entered their airspace without coordination or approved routing while conflicting with a LAS arrival. The controller issued a heading change to resolve the conflict after discovering the aircraft had previously violated the protected area during an uncoordinated turn.

synopsis: CRJ700 First Officer reports receiving two SID changes from ATC after receiving clearance to taxi to Runway 13 at LGA. Initially LGA 4 Coney climb, then NTHNS 3, then back to LGA 4 with the Whitestone climb. On departure ATC is expecting the crew to be on the NTHNS 3 and issues a new heading.
summary: Pilots at LGA received three departure changes during taxi, executing the final LGA 4/Whitestone climb correctly. ATC later questioned if they were on the NTHNS 3 departure, but the crew confirmed their correct heading and received new instructions without further conflict.

synopsis: EMB170 Captain laments last minute changes to clearances, whether it is taxiing out or on arrival. Communication and FMC programing errors are more likely to occur when done in haste.
summary: The flight crew departed LAX on Runway 25R after a late runway assignment required in-taxi FMS and briefing changes. The pilot reported that late runway clearances and complex SID nomenclature increase the risk of pilot error, runway incursions, and non-compliance with departure procedures.

synopsis: C402C Pilot reported encountering wake turbulence that resulted in a 90 degree bank on approach to STT in trail of a B757.
summary: The pilot of a VFR aircraft inbound to STT RWY 10 encountered severe wake turbulence from a preceding B757 while vectored below and downwind by ATC. The pilot experienced a sharp snap roll, regained control, and landed safely, accepting full responsibility for not deviating to avoid the wake.

synopsis: Small Transport aircraft Captain reports departing without checking the fuel, causing both engines to quit enroute. A successful dead stick landing on a 2,500 foot runway is accomplished with only the main gear tires the worse for wear.
summary: The pilot conducted an inadequate preflight check, missing the fuel amount, which caused fuel starvation and dual engine failure over the airport. The pilot landed on a 2,500-foot runway with maximum braking, resulting in two blown main tires.

synopsis: A C-177RG pilot misinterpreted his taxi clearance to Runway 09 at AHN and, instead, crossed the hold short line at the approach end of Runway 27.
summary: The pilot inadvertently crossed the Runway 09/27 hold line on Taxiway B while taxiing from the maintenance area, likely due to misreading signage and assuming a route via B3 instead of the correct path via A3. The pilot attributed the incident to insufficient pre-taxi diagram review and plans to seek ground training and clarify routes when in doubt.

synopsis: A C208 pilot reported that following exposure to dusty conditions when the TKS System was activated during icing conditions in flight the fluid flow on both wings was uneven or absent providing no protection.
summary: The pilot of a C208 Caravan encountered unforecast trace ice enroute IFR while the TKS system was in high mode. Dusty air clogged the wing nozzles, preventing fluid flow over most of the wings and rendering the ice protection system inoperable.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A light twin's ILS glideslope failed on the ASH ILS14 so the pilot continued on a Localizer Approach and ATC issued a LOW ALTITUDE ALERT PULL UP but the reporter believed he was above minimums when he became VMC.
summary: The pilot flying an ILS 14 approach at ASH reported a glideslope failure and converted to a localizer approach. While in visual conditions, the Tower issued an urgent altitude alert suggesting the pilot was below the MDA, likely due to a misunderstanding that the pilot remained on the ILS.

synopsis: An HS-125-800 APR (Auto Performance Reserve) system was in inadvertently activated and at about 1,500 FT the First Officer turned the System OFF which caused a surprise power reduction similar to a dual engine failure. The Captain initiated a return to land but when he realized what had happened continued the departure.
summary: During departure from Runway 15, the crew experienced an apparent dual engine power loss caused by inadvertent APR activation on both engines. After deactivating the system at 2,800 feet, the aircraft returned to the assigned heading and altitude without conflict.

synopsis: JNU Tower Controller reports of opening Tower, observing an aircraft on the movement area and tries to contact it.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller working combined Tower and Ground positions issued taxi instructions to Aircraft X, which departed without acknowledging the Tower frequency. The controller later contacted the pilot via landline and issued a warning, attributing the incident to an honest mistake early in the morning.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZLA Controller reports of possible company problem with a particular airline not answering calls in a timely manner.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X's pilots failed to acknowledge multiple vectors, code changes, and altitude clearances on the first call, requiring repeated instructions. The controller attributed this to poor listening habits and suspected that cockpit speaker systems contributed to the missed communications, increasing workload.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZAU describes situation where he did not hear the initial call up with altitude and assumed the aircraft was doing what he thought it should be doing, when it wasn't.
summary: An air traffic controller missed a pilot's initial report of being level at FL320 due to a faulty Mode C transponder showing FL375. The controller assumed a climb to FL380 and inadvertently violated the COTON sector, though no conflict occurred because no other aircraft were nearby.

synopsis: A11 Controller questions the procedure of ANC departing a slower aircraft before a faster aircraft and what type of separation they were using.
summary: A North Radar Controller expressed concern that lateral separation between departing Aircraft X and Y at ANC was insufficient due to speed compression and a 10-degree divergence angle. The incident highlighted confusion between Tower and Approach regarding fan headings and DVA procedures, though no actual loss of separation occurred.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew encounters turbulence and windshear during approach resulting in a flap overspeed but no windshear warning. The Captain calls for the flaps to be raised to 15 initially and when clear of the virga flaps 30 are called for again (below 1,000 FT) and the approach continues to landing.
summary: The flight crew encountered turbulence and airspeed fluctuations on final approach to DEN 16L, resulting in a flap overspeed. The Captain retracted flaps below 1,000 feet without initiating a go-around, creating an unstable approach that was subsequently reconfigured and landed safely.

synopsis: A B737 departed on the ORD8 and leveled at 4,000 FT instead of 5,000 FT because the neither pilot realized 4,000 FT was set as the initial level off altitude when it really was a crossing restriction.
summary: The flight crew incorrectly set 4,000 feet instead of the cleared 5,000 feet for departure. After leveling off at 4,000 feet for less than 30 seconds, they admitted the error to the Departure Controller, who then cleared them to climb to 5,000 feet.

synopsis: A G-200 EICAS alerted R ENG OIL PRES HI so the QRH was completed and eventually the oil pressure returned to normal but the flight diverted as a precaution with idle thrust.
summary: During cruise at FL220, the crew encountered a high right engine oil pressure warning and declared an emergency. They reduced power per the QRH, allowing pressure to normalize, then elected to land short of the destination as a precaution with the engine running at idle.

synopsis: A MD-11 encountered moderate to severe turbulence in light cirrus clouds and with a low speed stall warning descended 700 feet then returned to their cleared altitude. ATC was notified.
summary: The crew encountered severe turbulence and an inadvertent thunderstorm while deviating right of course in IMC, causing uncontrollable airspeed and a stick shaker activation. After disconnecting the autopilot and lowering the nose, they lost 700 feet before recovering, with ATC confirming no loss of separation.

synopsis: CRJ700 flight crew is advised by ATC of GPS jamming ahead. When the jamming is encountered not only does the GPS fail but so does the FMC and VHF. Lost communication results in a late descent clearance for landing.
summary: Pilots lost two-way radio contact with ATC during descent at FL370 while experiencing GPS jamming and a subsequent FMS failure. The crew eventually re-established contact via 121.5 and the original frequency after 60 NM, attributing the communication loss to potential equipment failure or interference.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier Captain departed on the ORD8 with a 4,000 FT MCP constraint. After the 8 DME at 4,000 FT, ATC cleared him to 5,000 FT and asked another flight and he why they had leveled at 4,000 FT verses the 5,000 FT assigned on the SID. Many aircraft were making the same error.
summary: The flight crew departed on the ORD8 SID and incorrectly set 4,000 FT in the MCP window instead of the required 5,000 FT final altitude. ATC instructed the crew to climb to 5,000 FT after they leveled off at 4,000 FT, revealing a misinterpretation of the chart caused by crossing restrictions and residual missed approach settings.

synopsis: A321 Captain describes the effects of military GPS jamming on his aircraft over White Sands late one night.
summary: The crew experienced a 30-degree bank and navigation error near White Sands, NM, due to military GPS jamming causing FMGC signal loss. The pilot manually corrected the heading, confirmed position via VOR, and noted that ATC was unaware of the jamming exercise.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain believes the dirty sock smell prevalent in his aircraft type should be addressed and corrected. Just adding more oil when it becomes low is not satisfactory.
summary: Pilots reported excessive oil on Engine 1 and a "dirty wet sock" smell on an Embraer with over 35,000 hours, causing a return to landing after oil quantity dropped. The reporter attributes the issue to chronic oil problems and a failure to disseminate manufacturer technical notices regarding these odors to the flight crew.

synopsis: EMB145 flight crew detects smoke climbing out of 5,000 feet which is also reported by the Flight Attendant. An overweight landing ensues and the passengers are evacuated. No smoke source is found.
summary: The flight crew detected smoke and a burning smell at 5,000 feet during climbout, declared an emergency, and performed an overweight landing. Firefighters found no fire, and the reporter attributed the event to aging aircraft and inadequate maintenance responses to chronic headset and oil discrepancies.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Pilot at LFT airport reports of bad communication procedures at the airport that they thought almost caused them to be part of a runway incursion.
summary: Aircraft X crew crossed the hold short line for Runway 22R after the Tower Controller issued a crossing clearance without an initial call sign. The crew stopped upon hearing an incorrect call sign appended to the instruction, confirmed the clearance was intended for them, and then completed the crossing.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A small jet received an EGPWS TERRAIN, PULL UP alert at 5,000 feet on base leg to HND after ATC requested they remain within 3 miles of the airport.
summary: The pilot flying and SIC conducted a visual approach to Henderson Runway 17R, triggering a brief EGPWS warning after a terrain-avoidance climb. The crew attributed the event to conflicting ATC instructions regarding traffic separation and terrain, noting a need for clearer visual approach procedures.

synopsis: A Captain questions if the miniscule amount of TKS deicing fluid weeping from the middle one-third of the outer left and right wing panels, compared to the other leading edge deicing panels, is sufficient to give adequate icing protection on the Hawker Beech HS-125 aircraft.
summary: A pilot reported inadequate TKS fluid flow on the middle third of Outer Panel #7 on a Hawker HS-125 during ground checks. A mechanic deemed the faint, non-visible flow acceptable per the maintenance manual, though the pilot observed no aft fluid spread on the wings after an in-flight test.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: MD80 First Officer experiences a momentary terrain warning during a day visual approach to Runway 26 at ABQ. On final a windshear alert is annunciated and a go-around is initiated by the First Officer. During the second visual approach to Runway 26 another terrain warning is annunciated but the approach is continued to landing.
summary: The flight crew received GPWS terrain warnings and a windshear alert while visually approaching Runway 26 at ABQ, prompting an uneventful go-around. They attributed the delayed escape maneuver to distraction from a nearby C-130 and terrain, eventually landing safely after a second terrain warning.

synopsis: MD83 flight crew reports responding to a TCAS RA during climb to 13,000 FT caused by military aircraft, in loose formation, below 13,500 FT.
summary: The First Officer flying a climb to 13,000 feet received TCAS Resolution Advisories for two military aircraft in loose formation, causing abrupt descents of 1,800 and 1,500 feet per minute. The crew followed the commands to avoid conflict, notified ATC, and resumed the climb once clear.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reports landing with flaps 25 instead of the planed flaps 30 due to aircraft not fully configured at 1,000 feet AGL. At 500 feet a 'too low flaps' GPWS warning is issued and the First Officer suggests a go-around but the Captain elects to land.
summary: The First Officer reported that the Captain elected to land with flaps 25 instead of 30, triggering a "too low flaps" warning at 500 feet AGL. Despite the First Officer suggesting a go-around, the distracted Pilot Flying continued the approach, resulting in an uneventful landing on Runway 22.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: During takeoff from DEN, Tower issued an Abort command to which an incorrect aircraft also responded because of similar sounding call signs.
summary: Flight crew aborted takeoff at 40 knots on Runway 17R at Denver after mishearing an ATC abort call intended for another aircraft due to similar call signs. The controller was simultaneously managing Ground and Tower duties, leading to the confusion, but the crew safely taxied off and later departed normally.

synopsis: A B777 left engine EGT alerted overtemp during the takeoff roll at about 100 KTS so the Captain rejected and after clearing the runway, because of a language difficulty, could get neither ATC nor Airfield Rescue and Fire Fighters assistance. They parked on a taxiway, used their SAT Phone and Dispatch called for assistance as all tire fuses melted.
summary: The flight crew rejected takeoff on Runway 01 at 110 KTS due to high left engine EGT, causing brake overheating and blown fuse plugs that flattened all 12 tires. Communication delays with ATC and Operations delayed fire truck arrival, but maintenance confirmed no fire or injuries before passengers were deplaned.

synopsis: Pilot report of possibly violating a TFR due to handheld equipment or applications, that didn't display the NOTAM correctly.
summary: A lead pilot conducting a local orientation flight with two other pilots may have violated a 24-hour TFR near Sedona, AZ, after incorrectly assuming it was inactive at night. The potential violation resulted from relying on outdated GPS data and a misinterpreted NOTAM regarding the TFR's time of effect and shape.

synopsis: After takeoff a CRJ-200 Master Caution alerted INBD ANTI-SKID and PARKING BRAKE SOV, so as the crew began QRH procedures they realized the landing gear had not retracted. They request a return to land, but on the first approach executed a go-around because they were not stabilized. After the go-around the gear retraction operated normally.
summary: The flight crew experienced a landing gear failure to retract and hydraulic pressure issues during initial climbout, prompting an emergency declaration. They executed a go-around after an unstabilized approach caused by FMS configuration errors, subsequently landing safely once the gear retracted and warnings cleared.

synopsis: A B737 flight attendant crew was told the flight was 50 minutes and so did a full service. When the Final Descent Chime for a 37 minute flight alerted, a Flight Attendant prepared to land but had not secure her galley cart, so she got up from her jumpseat and landed on the galley floor.
summary: Cabin crew on a 37-minute flight rushed to secure the galley after a shortened descent, causing one crew member to fall on the floor while attempting to close kits. The incident resulted from a miscommunication regarding flight duration and poor time prioritization.

synopsis: B737-800 Purser reports Gate Agent closing the main cabin door before the doors on the overhead bins have been closed, in order to have an on time departure.
summary: A flight attendant reported that a ground agent closed the 1L door prematurely with overhead bins open due to management pressure for on-time performance. The flight attendant subsequently opened the door with the Captain's permission to alert the agent of the unsafe condition.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot practicing proficiency maneuvers at 5,000 FT prior to a VFR approach to PYM has a near miss with an aircraft which he assumed was IFR because it was not on PYM CTAF.
summary: A pilot and passenger in a single-engine aircraft performing practice maneuvers at 5,000 feet MSL near PYM experienced a near mid-air collision with a light twin flying 300 feet below. The pilot executed an immediate evasive turn after spotting the fast-moving aircraft in a blind spot, noting that ADS-B would have improved situational awareness.

aircraft: Challenger Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A CL60 departed on the TEB Runway 24 RUUDY 4 SID but because an incorrect FMS Mode as selected the aircraft did not level at 1,500 FT nor turn to the 260 heading. The pilot flying was correcting as ATC called with a track and descent clearance.
summary: The flight crew departed TEB Runway 24 on the RUUDY4 departure but overshot 1,500 feet because the FMS navigation mode was not selected, preventing the autopilot from turning. The pilot manually corrected the deviation after ATC instructed a descent to 1,500 feet and a heading of 280.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A First Officer with low time in his aircraft type reported difficulty flying an IMC RND RNAV approach and experiencing both altitude and track deviations about which ATC issued advisories.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced multiple low altitude alerts and course deviations while manually flying a non-precision RNAV approach into San Antonio. The reporter attributed the instability to tight ATC vectors requiring non-standard turns, though the GPS indicated the aircraft remained on course.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A pilot departed FTG at night and immediately after takeoff had a near miss with an aircraft which apparently had neither navigation nor landing lights on and also not making CTAF radio announcements.
summary: A pilot departing Runway 8 at Front Range Airport during a closed tower period encountered a head-on conflict with an unlit helicopter. The pilot executed an evasive maneuver to avoid a collision at 100–200 feet, attributing the incident to the helicopter's lack of lights and radio communication in Class D airspace.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Confused as to his position on the ramp at BLI, the pilot of a small, low wing aircraft cleared to taxi to Runway 34, taxied into a non aircraft movement area he believed provided access to Taxiway A. While attempting to access Taxiway A from the CFR access road the right wingtip struck a sign.
summary: The pilot taxied from a maintenance hangar via a fire station ramp to enter Taxiway Alpha, striking a STOP sign that protruded above the wing. The aircraft was subsequently shut down and towed, with the pilot attributing the incident to unclear markings and inaccurate airport diagrams.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot on initial approach to TOA Runway 29R had a near miss at 1,100 FT after a helicopter pilot deviated from his 800 FT altitude constraint because of intimidation by city personnel about neighborhood noise complaints.
summary: A fixed-wing pilot on final approach to Runway 29R experienced a near-midair collision with a northbound helicopter restricted below 800 FT. The pilot attributes the conflict to city noise abatement personnel intimidating helicopter pilots into flying higher, violating FAR 91.11 and eliminating safe altitude separation.

synopsis: LSA pilot experiences a jammed throttle linkage while attempting to level off resulting in higher than desired airspeed and engine RPM. The reporter is vectored to a suitable diversion airport with the engine being shut down and restarted several times to maintain altitude and then to taxi clear of the runway.
summary: The pilot of a RANS S-19 experienced a throttle cable snagged on a bolt at 4,500 feet, preventing full closure and causing high RPM. After diverting to ZZZ with ATC assistance, the pilot landed safely on Runway X using intermittent engine power and was towed to the ramp.

synopsis: N90 Controller describes situation where a go-around and a departure have a loss of separation. Lack of good communication in a timely manner helped cause this situation.
summary: A Radar Coordinator reported a loss of separation at LGA between a go-around (Aircraft X) and a departing aircraft (Aircraft Y) on Runway 4 due to conflicting turn instructions and premature frequency transfer. The incident occurred because the go-around turned left to 340 while the departure turned right to 090, causing the aircraft to cross paths before visual contact was established.

synopsis: After ATC revised a B737-700 RNAV STAR from the JAGGR to the PURRL, then to the JAGGR and finally back the PURRL the flight was unable to meet the descent crossing restrictions. ATC then vectored the flight, slowed it and issued a descent clearance. ATC does not understand the consequences of such clearances.
summary: The pilot flying a JAGGR arrival into Denver experienced multiple conflicting arrival clearances and a VNAV disconnect due to rapid ATC changes between JAGGR and PURRL procedures. The crew managed the descent using vertical speed and speedbrakes, landing uneventfully, though the pilot questioned a potential altitude deviation at TWNSN and cited ATC clearance instability as a safety risk.

synopsis: B737 Captain experiences a TCAS RA while being vectored for a visual approach. ATC called the traffic but claimed no altitude information was available. TCAS saw the traffic with altitude and provided the correct escape maneuver.
summary: The pilot reported a near mid-air collision with VFR traffic while vectoring for a visual approach to Runway 4. A conflict occurred during a descent and turn when the traffic climbed to co-altitude, triggering a 1,500-foot vertical speed deviation Resolution Advisory despite the pilot believing the traffic was IFR.

synopsis: B777 flight crew reports sighting a drone in IAD Class B airspace during approach.
summary: Pilots on a visual approach to IAD Runway 19L spotted a gold, saucer-shaped drone approximately 100 feet below and to the right of the aircraft while descending through 1,800 feet MSL. The Captain reported the sighting to the Tower, and the approach continued without incident.

synopsis: B747-400 reports that not all approaches are line selectable at RJAA in the B747 FMC. The result is that an arrival may be assigned that connects to a specific approach (Y or Z) that cannot be selected due to database limitations.
summary: The flight crew requested the ILS 16R (Z) approach at RJAA due to complex missed approach routing but was denied by ATC, forcing them to use the ILS 16R (Y). The crew reported that ATC inflexibility and delayed ATIS reception increased operational complexity and the potential for aircrew error.

synopsis: B757 Captain reports being dispatched with an inoperative engine driven generator and the APU generator providing the second source of electrical power. After level off the APU shuts down due to oil loss and the flight diverts to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The crew operated an aircraft with a MEL'd right generator using the APU, which failed shortly after level-off due to a cracked, oil-leaking generator. They declared an emergency, diverted to the nearest airport for a safe overweight landing, and cancelled the flight after maintenance confirmed the APU fault.

synopsis: A320 Captain describes Airbus FMGC idiosyncrasies crossing BEDLM on the HKORY 1 arrival to IAH. The autopilot will attempt to violate the crossing restriction at BEDLM unless the crew intervenes.
summary: Pilots reported a design flaw in the HKORY 1 RNAV arrival into IAH where the FMGC managed descent profile conflicted with the 280 KTS speed restriction at BEDLM, requiring manual intervention to avoid a violation. Additionally, a lack of communication regarding runway direction changes left crews on an incorrect westerly arrival while ATC assigned the same procedure for easterly landings.

synopsis: A321 Captain experiences a failure of the landing gear to extend when needed for drag on a steep RNAV approach. After repeated attempts without success a go-around is initiated. The A321 QRH does not have a procedure and no faults were indicated. Another attempt at extending the gear is successful and a normal landing ensues. The steep descent required on the approach was also brought into question. Post flight revealed that the first extension attempt had been blocked by automatic systems due speed above 260 KTS and subsequent attempts were blocked by a two minute time delay from the initial attempt in the same system.
summary: During an RNAV GPS Z approach in an A321, the landing gear failed to extend due to a speed limiter activation triggered by a sudden pitch-down maneuver. After declaring an emergency and performing a go-around, the crew successfully extended the gear on a fourth attempt following a system reset, allowing for a safe landing.

synopsis: After a dusk landing, an Air Carrier flight crew, unfamiliar with SFO, exited Runway 28R at Tango and were cleared to hold short of Runway 28L, a common clearance due to the proximity of the two runways. When neither pilot observed the closely spaced 28L/R hold short lines they continued to taxi beyond the line and only held short when the First Officer saw the left runway and alerted the Captain. The reporters cited the lack of lighting on the hold short lines, the fact the runway lights for 28L were not illuminated and the lack of depiction of hold short lines on airport charts as contributing factors.
summary: Pilots taxiing a jet on Taxiway T at SFO at dusk overran the hold short line for Runway 28L due to unlit markings and glare from bright centerline lights. The crew stopped with two-thirds of the aircraft past the line, resulting in a runway incursion caused by inadequate lighting and missing airport chart data.

synopsis: EMB145 Captain believes that the KIDDZ 1 arrival HOU is too demanding for pilots of older technology aircraft such as his.
summary: The flight crew reported excessive workload during the KIDDZ 1 arrival due to frequent step-downs and speed changes, exacerbated by controller enforcement of STAR compliance. Although no safety violations occurred, the pilots requested FAA revisions to reduce pilot workload and enhance safety.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reports deviating slightly below the segment altitude of 1,700 FT during an RNAV (RNP) Y Runway 24 at TTN with the autopilot engaged in LNAV/VNAV and a clearance for a visual approach. The autopilot is allowed to correct the 80 FT deviation and the approach is continued to landing.
summary: During a night RNAV (RNP) visual approach to Runway 24 at TTN, the Captain reported the aircraft briefly descended to 1,620 FT while attempting to level at 1,700 FT. The crew attributed the deviation to a 20-knot tailwind on the arc, noting automation self-corrected within 15 seconds without requiring manual intervention.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain experiences unreliable airspeed and altimeter indications at FL380. Both EEC's were noted to have tripped to alternate. The Captain's airspeed and the First Officer's altimeter are determined to be in error and the flight is descended to FL340 where all systems return to normal.
summary: During cruise at FL380 in IMC, the crew encountered conflicting airspeed and altitude indications that triggered autothrottle advances and EEC trips to ALTN. After manually reducing thrust and descending to FL340, instruments normalized, allowing an uneventful landing attributed to an unknown aircraft malfunction.

synopsis: Pilot reports of unfamiliarity with a couple of fixes and having problems loading them into the FMS.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring entered a re-route clearance into the FMS during climb from Long Beach but inadvertently skipped the IKAYE waypoint, causing the aircraft to cross FIXIT before turning. The crew immediately notified ATC of the deviation while manually turning toward the missed fix.

synopsis: Although they consulted an on-line weather briefing service, a flight instructor and his student failed to determine their destination airport was closed for an air show at the time of their arrival. Upon landing they were met by an FAA Inspector who advised of the violation, gathered appropriate documentation and restricted them from departing until after the TFR expired.
summary: A CFI and student landed at SFQ during an active air show TFR after relying on online weather instead of an FSS briefing. An FAA inspector intercepted them on the ramp, citing the violation caused by the pilot's failure to obtain an oral briefing and recognize the airport closure.

synopsis: C310 pilot is informed after landing that he may have been involved in a NMAC with a glider. The glider pilot believes that the reporters aircraft passed 100 FT beneath him although he only heard the aircraft pass.
summary: A pilot reported a potential near miss with a glider approximately 100 feet below while landing at BDU, though the pilot did not visually see the untransponder-equipped glider. The pilot attributed the difficulty to terrain and glider characteristics, suggesting FAA encouragement for gliders to carry transponders to improve traffic alerting.

synopsis: Experimental aircraft pilot reports failure of the left main landing gear to extend due to interference between the tire and the wheel well. The manual pump is unable to overcome the interference.
summary: The left main landing gear failed to extend due to an obstruction between the tire and wheel well. The manual pump-down backup system also failed to overcome the obstruction and extend the gear.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: MYF Tower Local Control reports of a near mid air that was reported by a pilot after it left the MYF Class D.
summary: Local Control issued traffic advisories to Aircraft X departing VFR, but the pilot reported a near miss with a westbound aircraft 10 miles east of MYF. The controller stated the conflicting traffic was outside their radar scope, making it impossible to detect or advise the pilot.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZLA Controller describes ongoing problem related to the number 2 and the word two. A SID with the number 2 in it can also be described as the word to when in a clearance.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X veered west into hot airspace W289E after misinterpreting an automated clearance for the FIXIT2 departure as a direct route to CEBAD. The controller recovered the situation by requesting and receiving transit approval, attributing the error to confusion between the SID name "FIXIT2" and the phrase "FIXIT TO."

synopsis: Four reports of a restricted area that was hot up to an unusual altitude on a day with weather that hindered the routes available for controllers to use. All reports discuss violation of a restricted area.
summary: An air traffic controller in ZDC vectored Aircraft Y too close to active military airspace R6611, resulting in a single radar hit inside the restricted area. The incident occurred during complex traffic management when the Command Center denied a requested flow restriction despite active military airspace limiting vectoring options.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: S56 controller reports of a situation where he has an aircraft that has two RA's with the same aircraft.
summary: An ATC controller managed Aircraft X's IFR departure climb while Aircraft Y held VFR nearby without Approach contact. Aircraft Y's erratic altitude changes and turns toward Aircraft X caused two TCAS Resolution Advisories for Aircraft X, prompting the controller to issue traffic alerts and a left turn.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZBW describes situation where he is distracted by one aircraft while two others lose required separation.
summary: An air traffic controller managing busy JFK arrivals in the Clipper Sector issued turns to separate two descending airliners from a climbing skydiving aircraft. The controller later corrected a speed conflict between the airliners after realizing one was overtaking the other, attributing the increased sector complexity to the jump aircraft's operations.

synopsis: Pilots report of busting an altitude and flying slightly off course due to auto pilot not engaging, and doing other duties in the cockpit.
summary: During the Pomona departure from ONT, the Captain and First Officer missed the POM 114 radial and climbed 400 feet above the 7,000-foot restriction due to distraction, failure to monitor the FMA, and a mistaken belief that the autopilot was engaged. ATC queried their track, prompting a descent back to 7,000 feet after they corrected their course.

synopsis: Pilots report of taxiing to a runway but crossing a closed runway in the process at LAX.
summary: Pilots departing LAX taxied across closed Runway 24L to reach Runway 24R after Ground Control issued incomplete instructions during irregular operations. The crew realized they lacked specific clearance to cross the construction zone only after Tower advised them they needed permission, attributing the incident to ambiguous ATC guidance.

synopsis: CRJ700 First Officer reports the loss of a cabin window seal at FL270 causing a loud pop but no loss of pressurization. An emergency descent is initiated as a precaution and the flight continues to destination. Post flight reveals damage to the right engine.
summary: During cruise at FL270, a loud pop and engine vibration occurred after a deadheading captain reported a flapping window seal, prompting an emergency descent to 10,000 feet. Post-flight inspection revealed the shattered window and five damaged blades on the right engine, though the aircraft maintained pressurization during the descent.

synopsis: EMB135 flight crew experiences the loss of a main wheel tire tread during takeoff, which they are informed of after reaching cruise altitude. An emergency is declared for landing at the destination airport which is normal in all respects. Post flight reveals that the right inboard tire has shed its tread causing damage to the flaps and the fuselage under the tail.
summary: The crew discovered a tire tread separation after ATC reported a rubber piece on the runway, prompting an emergency declaration and a low approach to verify gear integrity. The aircraft landed safely with a right inboard tire missing all tread but remaining inflated, allowing it to taxi to the gate under its own power.

synopsis: CRJ200 flight crew describes a visual approach by a new First Officer who has not flown in the last three weeks. Configuration changes are not called for but supplied by the Captain and the snowflake' is used exclusively, without regard for the PAPI, resulting in a long landing.
summary: The Pilot Flying intervened during a visual approach by a new First Officer who over-relied on the snowflake display, resulting in a landing past the touchdown zone. The reporter attributes the outcome to the First Officer's lack of recent flight time and his own failure to execute a go-around earlier.

synopsis: When an APU starter contactor welded and resulted in fire and smoke at the gate the flight crew ran appropriate checklists and called for CFR assistance. The APU was deferred inoperative but the flight ultimately cancelled due to weather.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced an APU fire warning and heavy smoke during APU start attempts following a GPU failure. A mechanic identified a welded APU starter contactor as the cause, leading to the APU being MEL'd and the flight later cancelled due to weather.

synopsis: Pilot reports of problems while flying into SAT with controller who pilot thought was overwhelmed.
summary: Pilots reported that a Houston Center Sector Controller, overwhelmed by task saturation, issued confusing clearances and speed restrictions during the arrival into SAT. The crew followed instructions but noted the controller's poor performance and lack of situational awareness, though no traffic separation issues were observed.

synopsis: When a CRJ-900 flight crew received a complete reroute during taxi-out, including the assignment of the SOLDO RNAV SID, the flight crew misinterpreted the 'at or above 5,000 FT' crossing at TREXX as a 'maintain'. The reporter advised a contributing factor was the inconsistent placement of the altitude to which cleared via the SID on the commercially provided aero charts.
summary: During taxi at DFW, the crew misinterpreted a 5,000-foot crossing restriction at TREXX as a climb and maintain altitude of 10,000 feet due to confusing chart formatting. The error resulted from rushing to avoid weather delays and inconsistent placement of altitude instructions on the SID chart.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reports forgetting to turn on the seatbelt sign prior to landing at IAD due to the extremely busy arrival and approach phase. Vectors to avoid VFR traffic and the GIBBZ arrival were cited as the major distractors.
summary: The flight crew experienced multiple distractions during the busy GIBBZ arrival into IAD, including VFR traffic conflicts and unexpected vectors to Runway 19R. These interruptions caused them to skip the In-Range Checklist, resulting in the aircraft landing with the seat belt sign off.

synopsis: C206 jump pilot reports engine failure at 4,000 FT after a sustained forward slip from 12,000 FT. The engine does not restart and an off airport landing ensues, with no damage reported.
summary: The pilot lost engine power at 4,000 FT after skydivers exited, forcing an off-field landing 8 NM from the intended airport. The pilot attributed the fuel starvation to forward slipping from 12,000 FT and failing to activate the boost pump when switching tanks.

synopsis: BE35 pilot experiences engine failure on short final due to fuel starvation. Too low to switch tanks, the approach is continued to a landing short of the runway with roll out on the runway. No damage or injuries are reported.
summary: The pilot flew a Class B approach, ran a fuel tank dry on final, and lost engine power due to high workload preventing a tank switch. The aircraft touched down short of the runway, causing a 5–10 minute closure, but sustained no damage.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot of an unidentified small aircraft departed HWD VFR and, after receiving vectors out of OAK Class C, felt that it was unsafe to turn further toward the south due to low airspeed and climbed through the overcast to avoid terrain. Pilot attributed the errors and confusion to not being given a discreet transponder code for the departure.
summary: A VFR pilot departing Hayward Airport received conflicting instructions from Clearance Delivery and Tower, leading to an unauthorized entry into Oakland Class C airspace and a terrain conflict. The pilot subsequently executed an unauthorized climb through fog to avoid mountains, likely violating Class B airspace due to a lack of a transponder code and failure to assert PIC authority.

synopsis: Pilot complains about re-route with fixes they are not familiar with and having to enter them to the FMS, while flying close to the first intersection.
summary: During climb from LGB, the flight crew deviated from an LA Center re-route to FIXIT-IKAYE-RZS by proceeding directly to RZS after crossing FIXIT. The error resulted from high workload and unfamiliarity with the fixes, which prevented proper FMS loading and cross-checking before reaching the waypoints.

synopsis: Controller reports of unmanned weather balloons that have a tracking system with altitude reply that is incorrect. This causes problems with aircraft in the NAS by not knowing exactly where the balloons are.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored Aircraft X away from an unmanned weather balloon after the balloon's Mode C altitude data was missing and its website tracking showed an incorrect 70,000 feet. The controller noted that without the vector, a near mid-air collision could have occurred due to the unreliable tracking information.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Two reports of the same incident, Developmental doesn't ensure minimum separation between successive departures.
summary: A trainee air traffic controller at IAH cleared two aircraft too closely on RNAV departures from Runway 15L, resulting in reduced separation of 2.5 miles and 600 feet. The incident was caused by premature clearance, incorrect vectoring without altitude restrictions, and confusion over new RNAV procedures and training deficiencies.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported landing with flaps 25 after encountering wake turbulence on approach to TPA in trail of an A320.
summary: During a night visual approach to Runway 19R, the crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding A320 and subsequently landed with flaps set to 25 instead of 30. The error resulted from dim cockpit lighting and distraction during the wake incident, though no performance issues occurred.

synopsis: A Captain reported ten minutes prior to entering Tehran Airspace they attempted to contact on a set of EA1/ME1 Chart frequencies in a black box with black text which turned out to be unmanned Air Defense Radar radios. Later, they found green text in a green box containing the correct frequencies.
summary: Pilots operating through geopolitically challenging regions encountered a chart printing error in the Eurasia/Middle East EA2/ME1 that obscured essential radio frequencies. This caused an inability to acquire the correct Tehran air traffic control frequency, forcing a scramble for charts that incorrectly listed Air Defense Radar frequencies instead.

synopsis: B777 Captain is informed after the fact that the Purser attempted to use the IFE system for passenger briefing after being advised that it was inoperative on MEL and not to be used.
summary: The Captain instructed the Purser not to use the MEL-placarded IFE system on an MD-11, but the Purser used it for the safety demo after mechanics allegedly claimed it was functional. The Captain later reasserted authority, confirmed the system was inoperative, and emphasized the need for clearer placarding guidance.

synopsis: A Captain and First Officer (F/O) decide to depart after observing that both Left and Right Flap fairings had a section of flap sticking out of the fairings on a CRJ-200 aircraft. Maintenance noted the flap fairings had been installed in opposite positions.
summary: The crew discovered flap fairings installed on the wrong wings during a post-flight inspection at ZZZ1. Maintenance confirmed a mechanic had swapped the parts, corrected the error in 30 minutes, and cleared the aircraft for continued operations.

synopsis: A CRJ-900 flight crew experienced AHRS heading anomalies after taking off from Runway 13 at LGA following a period of LUAW. While assessing the heading issue, the aircraft leveled at their initial cleared altitude of 5,000 FT and the airspeed increased to approximately 285 KTS before they recommenced their climb to 12,000 FT as previously cleared by Departure. The approach end of Runway 13 northwest of the intersection with 04-22 is charted as susceptible to magnetic anomalies and was likely the progenitor of the event.
summary: Pilots of a light aircraft departing La Guardia Runway 13 encountered conflicting compass readings due to magnetic anomalies and AHRS issues. Distracted by troubleshooting, they failed to notice the autopilot leveling at 5,000 feet instead of climbing to 12,000 feet, causing an airspeed exceedance to 285 knots.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A small, low wing aircraft instructor pilot experiences temporary blindness after viewing solar arrays 35 NM southwest of LAS.
summary: A CFII safety pilot on an IFR flight near Las Vegas experienced temporary blindness and distraction while scanning for traffic due to glare from three bright solar towers. The pilot could not scan a 90-degree sector for up to 10 minutes, though flying directly over the towers on a return leg partially mitigated the glare by blocking the view with the aircraft nose.

synopsis: A King Air flight crew suffered an NMAC with another King Air climbing through 15,000 FT.
summary: Pilots climbing through 15,300 feet for FL210 received a TCAS alert for traffic 100 feet above and two miles away. They performed evasive maneuvers to avoid a King Air 200 or 300 that crossed 100–300 feet below, preventing a collision near JAMIE Intersection.

synopsis: A PA-32 pilot lost control of his aircraft in the flare after a wind gust moved the aircraft and, unable to regain control, the aircraft departed the runway stopping in a mud flat without damage or injury. The pilot had not flown for six months and his previous review was in a C-172.
summary: The pilot of a Cherokee Six experienced a runway excursion during landing in gusty crosswinds, losing control during the flare and veering off the right side into mud. The pilot attributed the incident to a lack of recent experience and solo flight without prior instructor supervision, resulting in no injuries or significant damage.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A fatigued First Officer flying the TEB RUUDY4 exceeded the 1,500 FT altitude constraint by 150 FT when ATC questioned his low climb rate and after thirteen hours awake with a three hour gate weather hold.
summary: The pilot flying inadvertently climbed 150 feet above the cleared 1,500-foot level at WENTZ Intersection during departure from TEB, attributing the error to misinterpreting the controller's altitude instruction as a climb rate challenge and to fatigue from a 13-hour duty day. The pilot immediately manually descended to correct the deviation.

synopsis: Newly certified ZOA Controller describes situation using the vacated altitude rule, where the Controller decides he will never use this rule again.
summary: An air traffic controller managing two aircraft descending to SFO issued a descent clearance to Aircraft X while Aircraft Y was still vacating the altitude, causing a brief vertical overlap. The controller attributed the event to issuing the clearance before the first aircraft completely vacated the level and plans to wait for full vacating in the future.

synopsis: Two reports of an aircraft that was doing what it was told to do. The error was the departing aircraft was assigned the wrong altitude and came close to traffic that was level on an arrival.
summary: An air traffic controller issued an incorrect 13,000-foot clearance to Aircraft X during a vector for spacing, intending 9,000 feet, due to a briefing error and missing the pilot's readback while Tower interrupted. This caused Aircraft X to climb through 10,000 feet, creating a potential loss of separation with descending Aircraft Y.

synopsis: Two different reports with confusion of similar sounding intersections (BLUZZ and BLEWS) in the same airspace causing pilots to turn towards the other one.
summary: Air Traffic Controllers reported that Aircraft X and Aircraft Y confused similar-sounding fixes BLEWS and BLUZZ while approaching Memphis for Runway 18R. Aircraft X turned toward the wrong fix, and Aircraft Y required clarification, prompting a recommendation to rename one fix to prevent future unsafe situations.

synopsis: TUL Controllers' report of a situation with an emergency aircraft inbound with other traffic in the pattern. The Local had problems with the sequence while other pilots tried to advise local that they were minimum fuel.
summary: A Local Controller and CIC managed an emergency landing for Aircraft A with a stalled engine while coordinating arrivals for Aircraft X, Y, Z, and B. Confusion over clearances, poor inter-controller communication, and the controller's lack of tower proficiency caused traffic conflicts, though all aircraft landed safely after the CIC intervened to exchange traffic.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reports that the 110 volt outlets being installed in his aircraft for iPad charging do not accept a standard spad type plug.
summary: A pilot reported that a new Boeing 110V cockpit power plug physically prevents charging iPads with standard straight-spade chargers, contradicting Flight Operations Manual policies. This incompatibility risks leaving crews without flight plans on long flights if they rely solely on uncharged tablets, potentially causing FAA violations.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A crew cleared to DESCEND VIA the MMMX AVSAR TWO ALPHA crossed SLM at 13,000 FT then began a descent to 12,000 FT, which they believed that to be the SMO crossing altitude, but ATC told them to return to 13,000 FT for traffic. The crew was informed 12,000 FT was the MEA, not segment altitude.
summary: Pilots descending via AVSAR 2A into MMMX descended from 13,000 to 12,000 feet after SLM, believing the chart minimum was 12,000. ATC instructed a climb back to 13,000 feet due to traffic, leading the crew to conclude they should have set 13,000 feet in the altitude window.

synopsis: A ground crew had no headset before a CRJ-900 engine start, but indicated something wrong with a tire. Unable to confirm an anomaly after the First Officer's normal preflight, the flight crew assumed no anomaly, but were notified after takeoff a tire had failed. An emergency was declared at the arrival station followed by an uneventful landing.
summary: The flight crew and ramp agents experienced a communication breakdown during pushback due to a faulty headset, leading to the departure of an aircraft with a compromised tire. The tire subsequently failed on takeoff, causing loud noises and vibrations, which resulted in an emergency landing and confirmed tire debris on the runway.

synopsis: An EMB-145 First Officer refused to fly an aircraft after he saw a mouse disappear under the First Officer's instrument panel. The aircraft flew a round trip with another pilot and then was removed from service.
summary: A First Officer refused to fly an aircraft after discovering a mouse in the cockpit while waiting for maintenance to repair COMM 1. Although the Chief Pilot pressured the crew to fly, the aircraft was eventually removed from service for extermination after further inspection confirmed a continued mouse presence.

synopsis: A MD-80 Captain reported that after the landing gear extension the left main gear had no indication so the First Officer tested the bulbs to discover them inoperative so they were changed. There was no authorization to change any bulb.
summary: During a visual approach, the crew encountered a left main gear down light failure caused by two burnt bulbs. The First Officer replaced a bulb from the unsafe light cartridge to restore indication, allowing a normal landing, though the pilot noted this action lacked specific QRH authorization.

synopsis: B777 First Officer experiences a TCAS RA to descend at 1,500 FT on departure with the Captain as pilot flying. A descent is initiated until a terrain warning is issued at 800 FT and ATC indicates that there is no traffic in the area. After discussions with Maintenance the crew elects to return to the departure airport for an overweight landing.
summary: The flight crew experienced false TCAS RAs and TAs shortly after takeoff, leading to a GPWS warning and an emergency return. After maintenance initially reported no faults, an avionics technician grounded the aircraft following the crew's detailed debrief of the system anomalies.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Corporate Jet flight crew reported the disparity between graphic and textual crossing restriction on the MUGGS One IAH RNAV Departure.
