The reporter cited the low ceiling and distance to assigned seats as unsafe conditions that forced this compromise, urging a re-evaluation of jumpseat placement.

synopsis: A Mechanic tasked with a 1.5 hour C208 deadhead flight felt ill, developed an intoxicated feeling, a sore throat, burning sinus and headache following prolonged TKS fluid exposure during the flight.
summary: A First Officer on a Caravan reported TKS deicing system vapor exposure during a 1.7-hour flight to an outstation. The crew member experienced nausea, fatigue, and respiratory irritation, attributing these health issues to the fumes and warning of future safety risks.

synopsis: Balloon pilot reports contact between the baskets scuff and a residential chimney, during landing approach, at very low ground speed. A short burn allows the basket to clear the chimney and a normal landing ensues.
summary: During the landing phase of a hot air balloon at a festival, the pilot contacted a house chimney due to insufficient clearance. The incident resulted from target fixation and dense traffic preventing aggressive ascent, but caused no damage or injuries.

synopsis: DA40 pilot reports being cleared direct to SHINY, descend and maintain 3,600 FT, Cleared for the RNAV-D into Rangely. Descent is initiated before noticing that the minimum altitude at SHINY is 6,000 FT. Very shortly terrain advisories begin to sound and the Controller issues a climb to 6,300 FT.
summary: A VFR pilot en route to Rangely received an incorrect approach clearance to descend to 3,600 feet instead of the required 6,000 feet over SHINY. Terrain advisories prompted the pilot to level off and climb to 6,300 feet after a broken controller transmission, allowing a safe landing.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot reports of violating a Presidential TFR in an area where he is not that familiar.
summary: A pilot departing DYB for a flight around Charleston Class C airspace violated a presidential TFR over an unpopulated island. The pilot attributed the violation to failing to contact FSS for TFR updates and noted that AWOS/ATIS broadcasts did not provide adequate notification.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot departing DIJ airport reports of a balloon in conflict with his aircraft as he climbs out. Pilot turns and avoids balloon.
summary: A pilot departing DIJ VFR encountered a balloon while climbing at maximum rate due to terrain, which restricted visibility. The pilot executed a 45-degree right turn to avoid the balloon, passing it approximately 2,000 feet below and one mile away.

synopsis: BJC Tower Controller reports of an aircraft that was inbound to BJC and had two low altitude alerts while on final.
summary: An air traffic controller issued multiple low altitude alerts to Aircraft X during an ILS approach to 29R in IMC after the pilot flew south of course and below glide slope. The pilot corrected the flight path, landed high and far down the runway, and later discussed the unstable approach with the Approach Supervisor.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ARTCC Controller reports of an aircraft that needs to descend due to lack of oxygen. Aircraft descends through another Controller's airspace. Aircraft Mode C shows XXX [not known altitude, usually when climbing or descending rapidly] and its path is in conflict with an arrival aircraft. Loss of separation occurs because aircraft in rapid descent Mode C works again and indicates 1,000 FT lower than conflicting traffic.
summary: The controller managed Aircraft X's emergency descent due to oxygen depletion, but delayed coordination with Approach caused a loss of separation from Aircraft Y at 11,000 feet. The incident resulted in a possible airspace violation and pilot deviation, attributed to poor communication and lack of prior sector coordination regarding the emergency's severity.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew experiences the Number Two Engine surging passing through 10,000 FT. The engine is shut down and the flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: During climb through 10,000 feet, the Number 2 engine surged with N1 fluctuating and spiking to 102%, causing an ENG FAIL indication. The crew declared an emergency, shut down the engine, and executed a single-engine landing with flaps 15, returning safely to the departure gate.

synopsis: EMB-140 flight crew is informed of lavatory smoke shortly after takeoff by the Flight Attendant. A lav smoke EICAS message is annunciated after the Flight Attendant call and the flight returns to the departure airport. Passengers and crew evacuate through the main cabin door.
summary: The flight crew and flight attendant experienced lavatory smoke shortly after takeoff, triggering an EICAS warning. The crew returned for a visual approach, landed with flaps 45, and executed a ground evacuation after stopping on the runway.

synopsis: C172 pilot taking off reports a Mooney approaching from the opposite direction and 300 ft. AGL without communicating. A second C172 taking off has an even closer call.
summary: A Mooney crossed midfield at 300 feet AGL without using CTAF, passing less than 100 feet vertically above a Skyhawk on takeoff. The reporter warned the Skyhawk pilot to level off to avoid the Mooney, which never made radio contact.

synopsis: Small Aircraft pilot describes flight where they are cleared for one approach then the Controller asks them what approach they are on. Controller then clarifies in his mind the approach and ships the aircraft to another Approach Control. Pilot questions why they were switched from one Approach Control to another after being cleared for the approach.
summary: A pilot on an IFR flight to UWL reported that Columbus Approach mistakenly believed they were flying the VOR 6 at RID instead of the cleared VOR 27 at New Castle. This confusion resulted in an unexpected handoff to Indianapolis Approach while the aircraft was in clouds at the MEA.

synopsis: Pilot was flying out of an airport and as approaching the destination was questioned if he knew about the VIP TFR. The pilot responded he did and made a 180 turn. He then contacted Approach Control and asked if there was a way around the TFR to his destination. There was not and pilot was given a number to call for pilot deviation.
summary: A pilot departing Corona Airport encountered a Presidential TFR near the water treatment plant while climbing to 1,700 feet. After turning back, ATC denied a deviation, prompting the pilot to check TFRs proactively to avoid future violations.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported wake turbulence encounter on approach to RDU from a B737 landing on the parallel runway which resulted in an uncommanded 50-degree bank.
summary: A pilot on a visual approach to RDU Runway 5R encountered severe turbulence and an uncommanded 50-degree right bank at 1,000 feet AGL, likely caused by wake turbulence from a parallel runway landing. The pilot recovered the aircraft and landed safely, recommending future glideslope adjustments and controller wake turbulence warnings for parallel operations.

synopsis: BE-55 pilot reports a left engine failure at 100 FT after takeoff. The engine is feathered and the flight returns to the departure airport. Post flight inspection reveals that a bolt that holds the mixture control to the rear of the engine had come loose causing the mixture to go to idle cut off. Maintenance had recently been performed on this component.
summary: The pilot experienced a complete loss of power on engine #1 shortly after takeoff due to a loose bolt on the mixture cable pulling the mixture to idle cut-off. The aircraft landed safely after the pilot feathered the propeller, and the cause was traced to improper tightening during a recent annual inspection.

synopsis: ZMP Controller describes route of a flight that has a transition that has two segments which causes confusion because the transitions go in different directions.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft X direct OBSTR.WYNDE5.ORD after the pilot deviated 20-30 miles left by flying SSM.PAITN2.KORD instead of the filed TVC transition. The controller attributed the error to a confusing arrival design with two segments starting at the same point but diverging in direction.

synopsis: ZBW Controller reports of an aircraft going to an airport that was uncontrolled and questioned the pilot about NOTAMS and weather. The flight was sent over to UNICOM and the aircraft was observed by the Controller descending, then what appears the aircraft moved to a different runway. The Controller then received a phone call from the airport operations stating the aircraft tried to land on a closed runway.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft X for a visual approach to Runway 23 at uncontrolled PVD, but the pilot later turned away and leveled at 2,600 feet. Confusion arose regarding runway closures, as airport operations reported a NOTAM for Runway 16/34 while the controller believed Runway 5/23 was closed, leading the pilot to cancel the approach.

synopsis: Two ONT Tower Controllers report of a possible lack of separation due to departing the aircraft too soon.
summary: A local assist observer reported two instances where a Local Controller cleared smaller jets for takeoff immediately after Heavy aircraft began turns, allegedly violating wake turbulence separation. The observer disputed the Supervisor's interpretation of separation rules regarding diverging departure courses and requested clarification on calculating wake turbulence for Heavy aircraft.

synopsis: Distracted by an inappropriate ATC communication as they touched down and a circuitous routing to the nearby gate due to construction, the flight crew of a B737-500 failed to shut down the right engine during the taxi-in as planned and then failed to note it was still running after gate arrival until advised by ramp personnel.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a distraction from an unusual Tower call during landing and taxi, leading the Captain to incorrectly believe both engines were shut down. Ramp personnel prevented an incident by refusing to enter the safety zone while Engine 2 remained running, prompting the Captain to admit failure in verifying start lever positions during the shutdown checklist.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reports being dispatched to a Gulf state (Persian) via a route that overflies Iran and close to a current war Zone. The flight is canceled for mechanical reasons prior to any decision being made on whether to fly this route.
summary: Dispatch planned a flight over Iran adjacent to two active military operation areas with gunfire, but the trip was canceled due to a mechanical issue. The pilot noted a NOTAM warning that Iranian forces have fired at civilian aircraft near these zones.

synopsis: When advised to tow the airplane forward one full gate for inbound traffic after pushing it back, the tug driver failed to advise the wing walkers who had to sprint to avoid the aircraft's unexpected course reversal.
summary: The pushback driver moved the aircraft forward an extra gate without notifying the wingwalkers, nearly causing injury during the ground operation. Both wingwalkers had to run to avoid being run over, and the reporter subsequently voiced concerns to all involved parties.

synopsis: An MD11 crew dispatched to a forecast VMC European airport for which all approaches were OTS had to to divert to a nearby military field when low ceilings emerged and the promised radar directed approach proved to be fictitious.
summary: The crew diverted to a military field after the Dispatcher incorrectly advised an ASR approach was available despite a NOTAM stating it was out of service. This error caused confusion with Spanish controllers, disrupted service, and coincided with a SATCOM failure upon arrival.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilots report of similar sounding VOR's which caused confusion when the entered the flight plan in the FMS. This caused the aircraft to deviate from its flight plan.
summary: Pilots departing ZZZ for HPN entered the wrong Pontiac identifier (PSI instead of PNT) during climbout due to two fixes sharing the same name and the cleared fix being absent from the filed flight plan. ATC detected the deviation at FL270, clarified the correct identifier, and the crew corrected the route.

synopsis: A Captain and First Officer report about an AutoFeather 'ARM' light that illuminated on approach and later again required a Rejected Takeoff (RTO). Both pilots noted the AutoFeather System on their DHC-8-100 was selected 'OFF' during each event. The RTO was applied due to the 'ARM' light had illuminated, even though the AutoFeather System had been de-activated.
summary: Pilots rejected a ferry flight takeoff after the autofeather ARM light illuminated unexpectedly despite the system being deactivated by pulling relays. Maintenance Control confirmed the light could still activate but the system could not feather, allowing the flight to complete safely.

synopsis: After noting that neither light bulb in the Right Main Gear green light had illuminated, fatigue and the conviction that the lack of additional expected alerts caused the flight crew of a B767-300ER to land uneventfully without completing the Gear Disagree non-normal checklist.
summary: The crew of a Boeing 767 experienced a right main gear down light failure on short final, leading to a go-around and a second safe landing. Fatigue and inadequate rest facilities caused the crew to incorrectly skip the Gear Unsafe checklist and fail to complete the Gear Disagree procedure, resulting in a maintenance log discrepancy.

synopsis: After arrival, a company HAZMAT Specialist and a B737-700 Captain were informed that two of the nine articles of unserviceable fuel components that were shipped in the Aft Cargo pit had leaked through their shipping containers. Aircraft was removed from service.
summary: A HAZMAT Specialist loaded nine fuel-contaminated parts onto a B737-700 at ZZZ1, but two boxes leaked into the aft cargo bin during flight to ZZZ. The spill caused the aircraft to be pulled from service due to missed Maintenance Procedures Manual steps for draining fuel from unserviceable components.

synopsis: Two Aircraft Maintenance Technicians (AMTs) recommend adding 'Caution' notes and updating a job card for attachment of Engine Hoist Equipment PW-4000 Engines used on their B777 aircraft. Aircraft engine had been dropped due to improper connection of hoist equipment.
summary: A mechanic dropped an engine during disassembly due to improper hoist connection caused by confusing job card descriptions and communication issues. The reporter recommends updating job cards with clearer instructions and caution alerts to prevent recurrence.

synopsis: An Aircraft Machinist describes his involvement with an on-wing tack welding of new studs installed at the aft flange of a G.E. CF-6 Engine Turbine Rear Frame (TRF) Assembly for a DC-10 aircraft. Aircraft was released without a required Fluorescent Dye Penetrant Inspection (FPI) being accomplished on the new tack welds and signed-off in the logbook.
summary: Aircraft mechanics and Quality Control performed stud repairs on a DC-10's Number 3 engine using an Engine Manual procedure that initially lacked required Engineering Authorization. Confusion over manual applicability and conflicting reports regarding the completion of the mandatory Fluorescent Dye Penetrant Inspection highlighted a need for clearer guidelines on when specific maintenance manuals may be used.

synopsis: BE36 pilot reports encountering icing conditions at 16,000 FT that seem to overwhelm his TKS deice system. Loss of airspeed indication is also reported resulting in an uncontrolled descent to 12,000 FT. At this time it is discovered that the pitot heat system is not on. With pitot heat on airspeed indication returns to normal and the flight continues to destination.
summary: The pilot of a Bonanza encountered severe icing and freezing rain at 16,000 feet, causing an uncontrolled dive and instrument failures. The airspeed loss resulted from forgetting to activate pitot heat, while engine performance degraded due to a frozen air intake, though the flight was completed safely after declaring an emergency.

synopsis: BE36 pilot reports the engine cowling coming open in flight and a diversion to a suitable airport. The distraction caused by the flapping cowl results in the landing gear being forgotten and a gear up landing.
summary: A pilot experienced an engine cowling opening during VFR cruise, causing a distraction that led to a gear-up landing. The pilot attributed the error to the cowling distraction combined with a lack of recent experience in retractable gear aircraft.

synopsis: When asked by the FAA Designee to perform an engine out but unfeatherable landing at a busy controlled field during a recurrent checkride the pilot of a Beech King Air was forced to abandon the maneuver due to limited maneuverability and traffic avoidance demands. An NMAC with a Cessna single provided the incentive for doing so.
summary: During a recurrent checkride ILS approach with a simulated single-engine failure, the pilot executed a go-around due to turn radius limitations and ATC traffic constraints. The aircraft subsequently passed beneath an unannounced Cessna, creating a near-miss caused by compounding operational demands and lack of traffic advisories.

synopsis: A Raytheon Beechjet 400 Captain reports about a Low Hydraulic annunciation followed by a Left and Right LH-RH PMP Press LO annunciations during initial extension of flaps to 20-degrees. Hydraulic pressure dropped from Green to Yellow indication. Emergency declared. Maintenance found Right Hydraulic Filter housing torqued too tight, O-ring cut and drop-down ring deformed causing leak.
summary: The flight crew experienced a hydraulic system failure during descent into ZZZ1, causing partial flap and gear extension issues. The cause was a Right Hydraulic Filter housing torqued too tight during maintenance, which damaged seals and caused a leak, though the aircraft landed safely with no injuries.

synopsis: A C182 pilot took evasive action from an unsighted aircraft to which he was alerted by a Skywatch CAS which does not provide Resolution Advisories.
summary: During the initial approach to PDK, a pilot received a Skywatch collision warning for traffic not previously advised by TRACON. The pilot executed an unauthorized climb and left turn for self-protection, later receiving a conflict alert from TRACON before resuming the approach.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Landing pilot advises departing aircraft to abort their takeoff because the arriving aircraft had not passed the intersecting runway.
summary: The flight crew landing on Runway 17R aborted after the controller cleared a Metroliner on intersecting Runway 14 for takeoff before the crew had cleared the intersection. The crew stopped prior to the intersection and challenged the controller for issuing the conflicting clearance.

synopsis: ZMP Controller reports of a Restricted Area not being posted Hot. This caused many aircraft to possibly deviate into the airspace.
summary: Air traffic controllers in Area 1 failed to activate R4202 restricted airspace on radar due to being short-staffed and busy during a nearby aviation event. Numerous aircraft transited the active restricted area undetected until a second controller arrived, highlighting the need for proper staffing and scheduler oversight.

synopsis: TMC reports of an incident where the facility was busy with weather and re-routes. A Controller in an other area released airspace to the military causing an unsafe situation.
summary: ZJX TMU staff managed weather deviations but issued late playbook reroutes due to staffing gaps, causing fuel concerns and increased controller workload. The military mission coordinator was unavailable, leading to uncoordinated airspace releases and a shift from tactical to regional management.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZMP Controller reports of land line equipment failure, causing an adjacent sector to spin aircraft until communications were established.
summary: An air traffic controller experienced VSCS equipment failure while attempting to contact Toronto Mitchell (CZYZ) for a handoff of an approaching aircraft. The malfunction prevented communication and froze the system, but the controller eventually established contact via a different line, and no separation loss or airspace violation occurred.

synopsis: TMB Tower Controller reports of a NMAC with a student pilot and an aircraft on final for a parallel runway. Language barrier was also stated to be a factor.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller instructed a student pilot in Aircraft X to turn base and land Runway 9L, but the pilot failed to avoid traffic on Runway 9R finals, causing a near mid-air collision. The controller attributed the incident to the pilot's lack of ATC procedure knowledge, language barriers, and insufficient flight school accountability.

synopsis: LIT Approach Controller reports of an aircraft that takes off into the path of an aircraft that he had just told the Local Controller to wait for. Pilot report of same incident reports of an aircraft very close to them as they climbed out of LIT.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller and a departing pilot experienced a loss of separation when Local Control cleared Aircraft Y for takeoff while Aircraft X was descending nearby. The incident resulted in a TCAS climb resolution advisory due to the controller's failure to coordinate the point-out and issue a conflicting heading.

synopsis: ZFW Controller reports of automation problem between ZFW and SPS Approach.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft X from Westover MOA to SPS but failed to verify a failed automated handoff due to high workload. The controller subsequently manually refiled the flight plan to complete the transfer, citing inconsistent automation between facilities as the cause of the initial missed handoff.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZDV Controller reports of a conflict at altitude between two aircraft causing a loss of separation.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a near-midair conflict between research Aircraft X and departing Aircraft Y near Denver, caused by Aircraft X's unpredictable deviation from its flight plan and a failure by Sector 61 to issue a required point-out. The controller issued emergency descent and turn instructions after a conflict alert activated, resolving the situation despite delayed compliance and frequency congestion.

synopsis: ZFW Controller reports of a pilot that thought they could descend on the STAR whenever they needed to.
summary: Aircraft X departed FL390 for FL240 without ATC clearance during the DRLLR STAR arrival, prompting a controller to issue a descent to FL370. The pilot incorrectly believed new STARS allowed uncoordinated descents, creating a potential unsafe situation that required procedural briefing.

synopsis: A80 Controller describes the consequences of refusing a vector through weather by a B757 Captain departing ATL, although PIREP's stated only light rain and chop on the vector.
summary: The CI-Departure coordinator and DR-N controller managed a B757 departure from Atlanta during weather avoidance when the pilot refused a 6,000 FT descent and right turn. The controller vectored the aircraft to 9,000 FT and a diverging route, which the coordinator supported as necessary to prevent delays for other departures.

synopsis: Five reports of a runway incursion at LAX where a taxiing aircraft entered the runway environment on the way to a runway, causing a departure to have to be aborted.
summary: A trainee Ground Controller issued incorrect taxi instructions to Aircraft X, causing it to enter Runway 25R while another aircraft was departing. The instructor intervened to stop the aircraft, which halted short of the runway, resulting in a 30-minute brake cooling delay for the departing flight.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports missing the 280 knot speed restriction on the HAWKZ 3 Arrival to SEA which is detected by ATC.
summary: The flight crew missed a 280-knot speed restriction box on the HAWKZ3 RNAV arrival into SEA while descending at 300 knots. ATC corrected the deviation at FL230 after the crew, unfamiliar with the chart's formatting, failed to notice the note during their briefing.

synopsis: A B767-300 appeared to have suffered the loss of the left FMS during the takeoff roll when the autothrottles failed to engage and the Captain lost his command bars. Control was passed to the First Officer who was pilot flying until alternate power was provided to the Captain's flight instruments. After consultation with Dispatch and Maintenance Control they continued the flight to destination.
summary: The crew experienced autothrottle, VNAV, and center autopilot failures during takeoff and climb, with only a 'NO AUTOLAND' light indicating the issue. They manually managed thrust and flight modes, switched instrument sources, and completed the flight uneventfully after consulting maintenance.

synopsis: An important and illuminating report that addresses the effect of inappropriate and/or improper modifications programmed into the autoflight system by a fatigued flight crew cleared to fly a visual approach on a clear night. They ultimately received an EGPWS 'Terrain' warning for descent below that prescribed by the RNAV approach they had programmed specifically to act as a backup/support mechanism to mitigate the effects of their fatigue.
summary: Pilots conducting a visual approach with RNAV backup at a busy airport triggered an EGPWS terrain alert due to FMS data entry errors and excessive automation reliance. The crew executed a CFIT maneuver, recovered to a stable glidepath, and landed uneventfully after identifying the cause as incorrect altitude constraints and failure to monitor the flight path.

synopsis: The Captain of a small corporate jet reports communication problems and ATC confusion when a stuck mic on frequency renders communications unavailable for about 10 minutes. Similar company call signs contribute to ATC's confusion.
summary: During cruise, a stuck mic from another aircraft overloaded the controller, who mistakenly believed he had issued a frequency change to our flight. The controller later accused us of causing communication problems, though we had responded to his query and switched frequencies only after receiving explicit instructions.

synopsis: BE400 First Officer experiences a NMAC with a light aircraft on final approach at PPO and goes around. The light aircraft was not communicating on the CTAF nor did it have a transponder.
summary: The pilot on a visual approach to PPO executed an abrupt maneuver and go-around to avoid a non-transponder aircraft converging less than 300 feet away and 30 feet above. The other aircraft made no radio calls and triggered no TCAS warnings, but the pilot subsequently completed a normal landing.

synopsis: Both B777's engine driven generators dropped off the line during climb, then were reset but both DRIVE lights illuminated again so an emergency was declared, the QRH completed and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: Cabin crew and flight deck personnel experienced a dual generator failure during cruise, indicated by DRIVE lights on both switches. The crew declared an emergency, jettisoned fuel, and returned to the departure airport for a safe landing after maintenance coordination.

synopsis: A B737 First Officer questions the legitimacy of Center clearing flights to 'descend via' the DRLLR (and MSCOT) RNAV STARS to IAH without also providing a bottom altitude to which cleared, the reason being that there are three runway transitions beyond DOMNO, the last common fix, which include two different bottom altitudes.
summary: The flight crew operating an RNAV arrival into IAH questioned the legality of a "descend via" clearance without a prescribed bottom altitude due to pending runway assignments. No incident occurred, but the pilot highlighted a potential threat in the new procedure regarding MCP altitude selection.

synopsis: B737 Captain describes a ground conflict with an EMB145 at Taxiway Alpha during taxi out for takeoff at ORD.
summary: The pilot of a B737 taxiing at ORD at night nearly collided with an EMB 145 on Taxiway Alpha after the EMB failed to yield despite the B737's taxi light being on. The pilot stopped hard and radioed "Stop!" to avoid impact, forcing Ground Control to issue new instructions to resolve the conflict.

synopsis: A B777 Captain instructed the IRO's about data link clearance procedures then left the cockpit only to discover during taxi that the Clearance PDC had not been obtained because no transponder code was available.
summary: The flight crew and two Reserve IROs departed without receiving a data link clearance, discovering the missing document only after takeoff. Despite initially squawking 0000, they verified the code with ATC and confirmed their flight plan was active, resulting in no incident.

synopsis: A319 Captain experiences an EGPWS warning at 1,000 FT AGL during night visual approach to Runway 16R at DEN. A go-around is initiated and the flight returns for another approach with the EGPWS deactivated. An altimeter setting error is discovered during the next approach causing the aircraft to be higher than actual, but the impact of this error on the EGPWS is not clear.
summary: The flight crew experienced an EGPWS terrain warning and abnormal displays at 1,000 feet during a visual approach to Denver, triggering a go-around. The crew suspects the cause was an incorrect altimeter setting from a wrong ATIS printout, though a system fault remains possible.

synopsis: An A320 flight crew, crossing STAAV at 12,000 MSL on the STAAV RNAV SID from LAS was reminded by ATC that the fix was required to have been crossed at 13,000 and asking if they intended to cross the next fix, TRALR, at 17,000. TRALR has no crossing restriction published on the chart.
summary: During departure from LAS, the flight crew and ATC disputed an altitude restriction at TRALR due to conflicting information and insufficient automation monitoring. The crew attributed the potential deviation to high gross weight, a new procedure, and inadequate monitoring of climb restrictions and MCDU warnings.

synopsis: CRJ200 Captain reported departing the gate with the correct fuel load according to the flight release. Enroute it becomes apparent that insufficient fuel was boarded for the flight and a diversion is initiated. Once on the ground it is discovered that there is a second release in the system that the crew never received, requiring more fuel.
summary: The flight crew departed with 9,010 pounds of fuel based on incorrect paperwork, but encountered double the forecast headwinds. They diverted to BNA as a precaution after discovering the system actually listed 10,100 pounds of fuel and an alternate.

synopsis: Following the loss of the First Officer's flight instruments and the autoflight systems the flight crew of a CRJ-900 later experienced uncommanded full or near full rudder deflections to both the left and right. They descended and landed without further incident at their destination.
summary: During climb to FL330, the First Officer's instruments failed and uncommanded rudder deflections occurred, prompting the Captain to hand-fly in raw data and declare an emergency. The crew descended below RSVM altitudes, completed the flight safely, and filed maintenance reports suspecting an IRS failure.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier crew reported a significant localizer signal deviation on final to RIC Runway 16 which was reported to ATC but did not disrupt their stabilized approach.
summary: The crew experienced significant localizer signal deviations on final approach to Runway 16, an issue also reported by a subsequent MD-80. Despite notifying ATC via radio and phone, the crew completed an uneventful stabilized approach and landing.

synopsis: B767 Relief Pilot reported being dispatched as part of a four man crew in an aircraft with only one curtained crew rest seat. With no rest obtained during his break he is overcome with fatigue and falls asleep while on duty in the cockpit.
summary: A relief pilot on a four-person crew flight to Europe fell asleep while flying at 2 am due to exhaustion. The incident occurred because the aircraft lacked sufficient crew rest facilities, forcing the pilot to rest in a lit cabin during meal service instead of the single curtained seat.

synopsis: An Air Carrier pilot reported taking evasive action to a TCAS RA flight of two targets at TEDDY Intersection on the ORD JANESVILLE 6 Arrival without an ATC traffic point out.
summary: The pilot reported a TCAS RA at 11,000 feet while approaching TEDDY intersection due to two unseen targets at the same altitude. The crew manually executed a right turn and descent to avoid a likely collision, attributing the close call to sun glare and rapid target approach.

synopsis: A pilot reports about logbook discrepancies that were incorrectly identified and improperly deferred by Maintenance using Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM) and General Maintenance Manual (GMM) references not applicable for the discrepancies written-up on their A319 aircraft. MEL and Configuration Deviation List (CDL) limitations were also noted as contributors.
summary: A pilot reported that maintenance personnel incorrectly deferred a broken right-hand nose landing gear bonding wire and a damaged static discharge wick using invalid General Maintenance Manual categories. The pilot argued these airworthiness issues required immediate repair rather than long-term deferral, citing conflicts with Airbus and FAA regulations.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: A BHT-430 SUMP PUMP chip light illuminated about six minutes after takeoff. The pilot decided to return to the departure airport because he forgot until near landing that this was a LAND ASAP emergency.
summary: During a repositioning cruise at 2,500 feet, the pilot observed a transmission chip light and returned to the departure airport instead of landing immediately. The pilot admitted failing to consult emergency procedures early enough, resulting in a delayed "land as soon as possible" response.

synopsis: MIA TRACON turned an Air Carrier to a MIA Runway 9 visual final about 4NM from the runway. The Captain set 1,000 feet in the MCP and descended too low but returned to the glideslope following an EGPWS Glideslope warning.
summary: During a visual approach at MIA, the First Officer noticed the VASI was red and received a below glideslope warning while the Captain descended below 1,000 feet. The Captain corrected the descent to regain the glideslope and landed normally, though the First Officer questioned the decision not to file a report.

synopsis: A PA28-181 engine began running roughly at about 10 feet after takeoff, so the instructor took command of the aircraft from his student, landed on the runway and taxied to the ramp.
summary: An instructor and student experienced engine roughness at 10–20 feet during takeoff in a training flight. The instructor took control, aborted the takeoff, and landed safely on the remaining runway with no injuries.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant reports how a mandated company policy change that increases the temperature in the Forward Cargo Compartment has affected flight crew rest periods on some of their B777-200 aircraft. The bunk room floor and walls were hot when touched, caused by heat radiating from the cargo area, even with the thermostat at full cold.
summary: Flight attendants on a Boeing 777 with a Lower Lobe Crew Rest reported extreme heat radiating from the cargo area, preventing rest during the third break. The reporter attributes this to a post-merger procedural change mandating high cargo heat settings, which affects aircraft with lower crew rest locations.

synopsis: Air Carrier Flight Attendant believes that a lavatory spill on an aircraft she was assigned to was not properly cleaned and disinfected prior to departure.
summary: Cabin crew reported soiled waste from an aft lavatory on a Denver-bound jet, but the pilot refused to delay departure despite contamination of safety equipment and floors. The reporter cited a breakdown in crew resource management and inadequate decontamination, resulting in fluid spillage during landing and exposure to potential infectious waste.

synopsis: On a visual approach to Runway 19 at MSY the recently qualified First Officer of a CRJ-700 descended early and too aggressively triggering a low altitude alert from ATC.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway 19 at MSY, the Captain intervened when the First Officer descended too steeply, causing a low altitude alert at 1,400 feet MSL. The crew leveled off after the Captain manually adjusted the vertical speed, attributing the incident to insufficient monitoring of the descent.

synopsis: RV7 pilot experiences an alternator failure on an IFR flight plan in VMC and elects to cancel IFR and return to the departure airport.
summary: A pilot en route to OAK at 10,000 feet experienced an alternator failure causing electrical loss and radio silence. After troubleshooting and contacting Oakland Center via cell phone, the pilot navigated back using analog gauges and landed safely after restoring limited radio reception near the destination.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Light aircraft pilot reports loosing power at 500 feet shortly after takeoff. All efforts at restoring full power are unsuccessful and the reporter is able limp into an airport along his route of flight. Contaminates in the fuel are found to be clogging the fuel strainer.
summary: The pilot experienced repeated engine power loss and surging shortly after departure, forcing an emergency off-airport approach and landing without tower contact. Post-flight inspection revealed carburetor contamination, despite the engine being rebuilt in 2004 and stored for ten years prior to installation.

synopsis: C172 pilot experiences engine failure on short final after a low power descent from 3,500 feet. The aircraft lands short but rolls onto the runway without hitting any obstacles. The engine restarts on the second try and the aircraft is taxied clear of the runway.
summary: A pilot flying a C172 at night experienced a complete engine failure during final approach to a towered airport while at 200 feet AGL. The pilot attributed the stoppage to fuel starvation, executed a forced landing short of the runway threshold to avoid approach lights, and successfully restarted the engine with no injuries or damage.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot reports while landing and before his aircraft had passed an intersecting runway, Tower Controller clears an aircraft for takeoff. Landing pilot slams on brakes and stops before intersection. Pilot advised Tower while stopping and departing aircraft rejected takeoff.
summary: During landing at LRD on Runway 17R, the crew stopped before crossing Runway 14 after Tower cleared a holding aircraft for takeoff. The crew alerted Tower to their position, causing the departing aircraft to abort, and both planes stopped safely before the intersection.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot experiences a bird strike shortly after lifting off with passengers. After a moment of disorientation the pilot is able to return to the departure heliport.
summary: A helicopter pilot struck a bird during a climbing left turn into Class Bravo airspace, penetrating the pilot-side window and causing facial injury and temporary disorientation. The pilot stabilized the aircraft, returned to the departure point, and landed safely with unharmed passengers before repositioning to base for inspection.

synopsis: BE33 pilot taking off to the north reports a NMAC with a helicopter departing from behind hangars on the northeast quadrant of the airport and flying to the runway centerline. The hangar apparently blocked VHF communication between the two aircraft.
summary: A Bonanza pilot taking off VFR from Runway 36 at ASW encountered a helicopter that departed from behind a hangar east of the runway and entered the flight path below 200 feet AGL. The pilot avoided a collision by turning right, attributing the conflict to the helicopter's unobserved departure and radio blockage caused by the hangar.

synopsis: Bellanca pilot reports a take off conflict with an Aeronca back taxiing from the opposite end of the runway. Neither pilot was using their radio and the Aeronca taxiied off the runway to avoid a collision.
summary: The pilot of a Bellanca narrowly missed an Aeronca Champ taxiing back on the same runway at an uncontrolled airport. The near-miss occurred because the pilot could not hear the passenger's warning due to low intercom volume, and neither pilot made radio announcements or visually detected the other aircraft.

synopsis: When the flight crew of a B737NG received a 'too low gear' EGPWS warning at 500 they pushed in the gear handle and immediately got three (six total) green lights and proceeded with an uneventful landing. Some disagreement surfaced in the reports as to the decision to continue vice go-around.
summary: During a visual approach in a Boeing 700, a brief gear warning and subsequent GPWS "Too Low Gear" alert occurred due to the gear handle not being fully pushed down. The Captain wiggled the handle to extinguish red lights, allowing the crew to land safely despite the First Officer's initial intent to go around.

synopsis: On climbout through approximately FL180 the crew of a Boeing 737 was notified by a Flight Attendant of a faint odor of smoke in the cabin. When a definitive determination of the nature and seriousness of the event could not be made, the Captain returned to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew returned to the departure airport after flight attendants reported a faint smoke odor during climb, which dissipated as the gasper fan was inadvertently left on above 10,000 feet. The aircraft landed safely with emergency services standing by, was removed from service, and the crew identified the need for better pressurization panel scanning and immediate diversion protocols.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reports forgetting to shut down the right engine after arriving at the gate and not noticing the omission during the parking checklist. A ramp person came up to inform the Captain that the engine was still running.
summary: The First Officer and Captain landed and parked the aircraft but failed to shut down the number two engine during the parking checklist. A ramp worker discovered the running engine, prompting the Captain to shut it down and rerun the checklist after the First Officer had already left the aircraft.

synopsis: A ramp employee describes his efforts to address an unsafe condition that occurs while towing CRJ-700 aircraft using Super Tugs that have an automated electric-hydraulic nose gear cradle system. CRJ-700 nose gears have shifted sideways inside the cradle during turning motions causing nose tires to be cut after striking the cradle hydraulic unit. Other times the nose gear will slam forward into the hydraulic unit.
summary: Ground crew towing a CRJ-700 observed the aircraft's front main gear shifting right in the cradle while crossing a taxiway hump. The reporter fears this recurring issue, previously linked to tire damage, could cause the aircraft to disconnect from the Super Tug, resulting in injury or death.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer is informed after the fact that he operated a flight with QRH's specific to an aircraft with a different engine type.
summary: The IRO reported that Quick Reference Handbooks (QRH) for the wrong engine type were on board, though the flight remained safe due to available Aircraft Operating Manuals. The incident was attributed to potential crew complacency in checking publications, prompting recommendations for color-coded covers and procedural reviews.

synopsis: CRJ200 First Officer reports a last minute runway change and to an ILS instead of a visual, resulting in an unstabilized approach with stick shaker activation due to the spoilers being fully extended and forgotten. The spoilers are retracted and the approach is continued to a landing.
summary: Pilots flying a jet experienced a rushed approach after ATC changed the runway and approach type from visual to ILS 9R. High workload led to a stick shaker activation caused by extended spoilers during a glideslope correction, though the crew recovered and landed safely.

synopsis: When the First Officer of an A320 returned to the flight deck after a break the Flight Attendant was unable to open the door to allow him to return. During the extended time required to find a way for the pilot to gain admittance the Captain failed to comply with a descent clearance due to distractions directing potential solution suggestions to the Flight Attendant.
summary: During descent, a First Officer was locked out of the cockpit due to a jammed door caused by missing screws in the frame. The crew resolved the issue by using the escape panel, but the distraction caused a missed crossing restriction at FL330, requiring the aircraft to maintain FL370.

synopsis: CRJ-900 First Officer reported they experienced an unstabilized approach. Reporter stated the Captain was demonstrating how a real visual approach should be accomplished. During the approach numerous aural warnings, including bank angle, glide slope, pull up and descent rate were heard.
summary: The Captain executed an unsafe visual approach with steep descents and turns, triggering multiple aural warnings and exceeding flap extension speeds at 210 KTS. The aircraft landed with flight spoilers deployed on the Captain's side, which he later corrected after the First Officer reported the issue.

synopsis: B737-700 flight attendants reported a burning plastic, chemical odor in the cabin causing headaches, burning eyes and throat. After arrival the aircraft was removed from service, but the crew continued, then reported ill at the next destination and sought medical attention. Hydraulic fluid was reported in the air conditioning system.
summary: Flight attendants and pilots reported a burning chemical smell and physical symptoms during cruise, attributed to maintenance or leaking hydraulic fluid in the ventilation system. The crew continued to the destination, were hospitalized for chemical inhalation, and the aircraft was grounded for an unknown issue.

synopsis: A B737 Flight Attendant reported noxious fumes after engine start, so the aircraft was returned to the gate where mechanics started the engines and confirmed TCP contamination. The reporter sought medical attention.
summary: Cabin crew experienced noxious fumes, coughing, and nausea after engine start during pushback, requiring a return to the gate. Maintenance identified the cause as TCP ingestion of phosphate ester, leading to the reporter's emergency room treatment and concerns about future neurotoxic effects.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot reported a problem at LAX where initial clearance was given to Runway 25L. Pilot was then instructed to taxi across Runway 25L and turn right, then taxi full length to Runway 25R. Pilot's problem was they were expecting a departure from Runway 25L and had to program aircraft now for departure off of Runway 25R.
summary: The flight crew reported confusing taxi instructions from LAX Ground while taxiing from the FBO ramp, as the initial clearance mentioned Runway 25L despite a later departure assignment to Runway 25R. The pilot stated this caused unnecessary FMS reprogramming and potential hazard by failing to specify the actual departure runway in the initial instructions.

synopsis: Two pilots report of near midair collision on final at ORL Airport.
summary: A student pilot and instructor in Aircraft X experienced a near midair collision with Aircraft Y on final approach to Runway 25 after Y accelerated from behind and banked right to avoid them. The reporter attributes the incident to Y's short approach, poor visibility, and the controller's failure to ensure adequate separation before the aircraft were within 15 feet.

synopsis: A Lancair pilot performed an emergency gear extension with the aircraft on jacks but failed to put the gear handle down, so on the next takeoff the gear retracted at too a low an airspeed as the ground/air switch closed.
summary: A pilot reported that after an emergency gear extension left the switch up, the gear retracted at 50 knots during takeoff when the air/ground switch closed the circuit. The pilot attributed the event to a missing checklist item and recommended adding a gear position check and calibrating the airspeed switch to activate above rotation speed.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot orbiting CTAF N51 after checking NOTAMs and TFRs was told that he was violating the airspace, but did not leave until he was harassed by another aircraft that created a near miss situation.
summary: A pilot circling Solberg Airport (N51) at 1,600 feet MSL was confronted by another pilot who claimed an airspace violation despite Flight Service confirming no restrictions. The second pilot aggressively maneuvered within 250 feet, cutting off the reporter's pattern and forcing a departure from the area.

synopsis: Oceanic Controller reports of an aircraft that is not at the correct altitude and continues its descent. Emergency is declared and aircraft is directed to airport.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managed an emergency for Aircraft X at FL410 after an engine shutdown caused an uncommanded descent. Poor HF radio quality initially delayed communication until the pilot switched frequencies, declared a MAYDAY, and was cleared to descend to FL260.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier crew's initial LAX VTU5 Departure filed route was changed on the PDC to the FIXIT 2 Departure but the crew failed to see the change. After takeoff ATC advised about active military airspace so after landing Dispatch confirmed the missed revised PDC routing.
summary: The flight crew departed LAX on the VENTURA 5 departure but was vectored by ATC to avoid military airspace after failing to notice a PDC amendment changing the route to FIXIT 2. The pilot attributed the oversight to confusing PDC formatting that displayed both the original and amended routes with unclear minus signs.

synopsis: A B737-700 inbound to SFO, descending on the MODESTO 5 STAR to FL200 received and responded to TA and RA warnings with respect to opposite direction climbing traffic. While doing so they refused contradictory flight path corrections provided by ATC.
summary: During descent through FL210 to FL200 on the MODESTO 5 arrival into SFO, the crew received a TCAS climb RA while ATC issued conflicting descent instructions and a turn toward the conflicting traffic. The crew prioritized the RA, climbing to FL220 to resolve the conflict before resuming descent per ATC.

synopsis: An air carrier automation fully active on an ORD VEECK 1 did not appear to honor the selected modes when it failed to maintain a SPD Select during level off and then failed to capture an armed APP LOC.
summary: During arrival to ORD, the crew experienced unexplained speed changes and an autopilot failure to capture the ILS 10R localizer while in LNAV/VNAV and Approach modes. The controller attributed the speed discrepancies to a clearance error for another aircraft, while the cause of the missed localizer capture remained unknown despite verified automation settings.

synopsis: An Airbus crew departed toward weather and while working with ATC for weather avoidance failed to raise the landing gear but did not recognize the vibration's source until an emergency had been declared for a diversion to a nearby airport.
summary: The flight crew of an Airbus jet failed to retract the landing gear after takeoff due to distraction by weather avoidance and traffic, causing airframe vibration. They diverted and landed safely after realizing the gear was down, attributing the error to skipping the after-takeoff checklist.

synopsis: A pilot landed at Angeles City, (Clark) Philippines in what was described at the most intense rain he had ever seen just ten minutes after the Tower reported light rain with no more recent verbal updates.
summary: The pilot reported landing at Clark Airport on a VOR approach in severe, unreported heavy rain that obscured PAPIs and the runway centerline below 200 feet. The reporter attributed this unsafe condition to the tower's failure to provide current field condition updates despite the intensity of the precipitation.

synopsis: An ERJ-170 developed a dirty socks odor during takeoff and again during descent. Engine 1 Bleed OFF seemed to help control but not eliminate the chemical contaminate (TCP) responsible for the odor from entering the left PACK.
summary: The flight crew experienced a strong, sickening odor from PACK 1 during takeoff and descent, which they attributed to toxic organophosphate contamination from a suspected CF34 engine seal failure. Although maintenance deferred the APU, the crew was not informed of the potential toxicity and requested engine repairs and crew education to prevent poisoning.

synopsis: While departing LAX on the FIXIT 2 RNAV, SOCAL Departure cleared a CRJ900 to contact ZLA and comply with restrictions, which included 290 KTS. Switching to ZLA, they were asked their speed and told to slow to 250 KTS, a previous restriction.
summary: A pilot climbing from LAX on the FIXIT 2 RNAV Departure maintained 290 KTS to comply with SID restrictions. ZLA incorrectly requested 250 KTS, but the pilot clarified SOCAL's instructions, and the flight continued without incident.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported encountering a rolling motion at 50 FT AGL on approach to BOS Runway 4L they felt was caused by jet blast from a heavy Airbus departing on Runway 9.
summary: A captain flying a visual approach to Runway 04L at BOS encountered significant rolling motion at 50 feet AGL caused by jet blast from a heavy Airbus departing Runway 09. The pilot corrected the roll and completed an uneventful landing, suggesting that simultaneous operations on perpendicular runways should be prohibited.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A pilot reported taking evasive action during a light twin near miss on final to Fond du Lac Runway 36 during a nearby event. The temporary Tower Controller issued an avoidance clearance to him with an incorrect call sign so he was slow to respond.
summary: The pilot, cleared to land Runway 36, mistakenly believed a Tower instruction for a right turn to 090 was for them after seeing a twin-engine aircraft on final. The pilot complied, performed a 360-degree turn back to final, and landed uneventfully behind the other aircraft.

synopsis: Pilot reports of an issue they had with a Controller who issued a clearance the crew could not accept due to fuel. Controller then gave them a new clearance which the Controller stated, they would accept. Flight crew accepted the second clearance because they had the right amount of fuel for the flight.
summary: A pilot en route from ZZZ to HYA rejected a clearance over ENE due to insufficient fuel, prompting the Center Controller to demand an emergency declaration. The controller later issued an acceptable alternative route from PSB to KHYA, which the crew accepted, followed by a post-incident call from the POI.

synopsis: DA40 pilot reports being confused when cleared for the ILS and to maintain 2,000 FT until established in VMC and starts descending before glideslope intercept.
summary: The pilot descended below 2,000 feet during an ILS approach after misinterpreting the clearance to maintain altitude until established on the localizer as permitting descent without glideslope interception. This error caused a rapid correction, a glideslope overshoot, and a low altitude warning before the aircraft was handed over to Tower.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: ZLA Controller reports of issue with GCN Tower and having an aircraft request an opposite direction arrival and making the aircraft cancel IFR.
summary: A radar controller cleared Aircraft X for an ILS Runway 3 approach despite the local controller stating IFR service required cancellation. The controller later realized the initial vector was too sharp and corrected it, while a subsequent dispute arose over conflicting instructions regarding IFR versus visual approach procedures.

synopsis: AMA Tower Controller reports of a period of time when all positions except FLM were combined at Local Control.
summary: A Local Controller relieved a trainee managing combined frequencies with four aircraft and four vehicles, including three on an active runway. The controller requested a Ground Controller, but the Flight Line Manager arrived late and left early, creating an unsafe single-controller situation due to chronic understaffing.

synopsis: An Air Carrier Captain taxiing to Runway 13R at night reported unlighted taxiway signage on Papa and Lima made transitions between taxiways difficult without taxi and landing light illumination.
summary: Outbound crews at DAL reported difficulty following taxi instructions to Runway 13R at night due to distracting white floodlights and unlighted signage on Taxiway Papa. The reporter recommends installing lighted taxiway signage to improve visibility of pavement markings in low-light conditions.

synopsis: B777 Captain experiences an ENG BLEED OFF light during taxi out, associated with two MEL's on the left engine. After consulting with Maintenance Control the flight departs. During descent for landing the APU is started as usual and ten minutes later the left pack is lost and fifteen minutes later the pack comes back on its own.
summary: The crew experienced an ENG BLEED OFF light and a temporary left pack loss on an aircraft with multiple MELs, causing a return to the blocks and a delayed departure. The reporter attributed these issues to inadequate MEL placard information and a lack of maintenance support, noting that procedures failed to resolve the pack failure.

synopsis: A First Officer and Captain report that one third of a nosewheel rim had broken away on the inboard side of the right nose tire on a B757-200 aircraft during takeoff, causing wheel shaking and vibrations. Aircraft landed in emergency conditions at destination. Tire was still inflated, but severely out of round. Captain noted that Mechanic had lied about condition of tire and moved aircraft without discussing with Captain, Dispatch or Maintenance Control.
summary: The flight crew experienced severe nosewheel shimmy during takeoff and landing due to a fractured wheel rim on a damaged tire. An outsourced mechanic lied about the damage to avoid alarming the female captain, then towed the aircraft with passengers on board despite the risk of tire failure or debris ingestion.

synopsis: At altitude the crew of a DHC 8-400 responded to a smoke filled cabin and smoke invading the cockpit by advising ATC, initiating an emergency descent, and landing.
summary: The flight crew encountered smoke filling the cockpit and cabin, triggering a warning light and an emergency descent. ATC cleared the aircraft to the airport, where the crew landed with gear extended at 226 KTS due to the suspected in-flight fire.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain is informed his First Officer after post flight inspection, that a tool is stuck to the top of the right wing at the wing to fuselage fairing.
summary: The First Officer discovered an 8-inch metallic tool left on the right wing after maintenance and missed during preflight. The tool remained attached throughout the flight at FL360 but posed potential risks of FOD, engine ingestion, or ground injury.

synopsis: EMB-170 Captain reports taking evasive action shortly after takeoff to avoid a flock of seagulls. No bird strikes occur and the flight continues to destination.
summary: The Captain and First Officer encountered a flock of large seagulls at 500-800 feet AGL during climb. The Captain executed an aggressive right bank, triggering a 'Bank Angle' warning, to avoid the birds before returning to a standard climb profile.

synopsis: When the flight crew of a CE-750 smelled electrical odors emanating from the passenger accessible microwave they shut off power to it, advised ATC, and diverted to the nearest suitable airport where they evacuated the aircraft following an uneventful landing.
summary: The flight crew experienced an apparent electrical fire originating from an in-use microwave while cruising at FL450. After turning off the microwave and Interior Master, the Captain declared an emergency, diverted to a nearby airport, and evacuated the aircraft on the runway where emergency services confirmed the fire was out.

synopsis: A Captain reports about a Release Collar under the Flap Handle knob of an A320 aircraft that broke while on approach. The spring loaded Release Collar was flopping around and would not lift out of the flap detent to allow the flap lever to be moved. Flaps were stuck at Position-2 (14-degrees Flaps). Go-around initiated and aircraft landed in emergency condition.
summary: An Airline Transport Pilot on approach to Runway XX at ZZZ experienced a flap handle failure that stuck at Position-2. The crew initiated a go-around, requested fire trucks, and completed a normal landing at Flaps-2 without excessive brake temperatures.

synopsis: A320 Captain used an abnormal amount of aft stick to get the aircraft to rotate during takeoff. Once airborne it is determined that the aircraft has auto trimmed to a substantially different setting from the takeoff setting. A message is received from the company indicating that 40 bags were loaded in the forward bin but not accounted for in the weight and balance.
summary: The flight crew experienced extreme rotation forces and excessive trim changes on takeoff due to a Weight and Balance error of 40 bags in the front bin. Operations notified the crew 25 minutes after pushback, causing the aircraft to consume an extra 1,000 feet of runway.

synopsis: A B757-200 Captain utilized the occasion of finding an open and banded Circuit Breaker (CB) during preflight to address what he believes to be diametrically opposed understanding of undirected CB operation between flight crew and cabin staff. He further addressed what he believes to inappropriate direct flight attendant/maintenance interface without prior consultation with the Captain.
summary: The Captain reported multiple open circuit breakers for galley and water systems, which a mechanic reset without clear documentation, while flight attendants improperly reset breakers without notifying the Captain. The reporter attributed these events to flight attendants misunderstanding their responsibility to report discrepancies and recommended immediate system-wide training on circuit breaker policies.

synopsis: Dispatched with a deferred inoperative aft fuel boost pump the flight crew of a large commercial fixed wing jet were concerned when the autofuel management system turned off the forward pump as well but did not open a crossfeed to provide positive fuel pressure to the engine. To maintain pressure they went to manual but, approaching top of descent, received a CAS warning of trapped\unavailable fuel which caused them to declare an emergency.
summary: The crew managed a fuel system malfunction during cruise and descent involving an MEL for Tank 1 Aft pumps, which caused an ENG 1 SUCT FEED alert and rapid imbalance between Tanks 1 and 3. They declared an emergency, switched to manual pump operation, and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: CRJ900 Captain experiences an 'R REV INOP' caution message at 20 knots during takeoff and continues. After takeoff an 'EDP 2A' caution message appeared but before QRH procedures can be applied a 'HYD SYS 2 LO PRESS' message appears. From the hydraulic synoptic page the root cause of all the messages is determined to be loss of fluid in the number two system. An emergency is declared and the flight returns for landing at the maximum allowable landing weight.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a hydraulic system 2 failure on a Boeing 900 shortly after takeoff, causing empty reservoirs and lost brake pressure. They declared an emergency, burned fuel to meet weight limits, and landed safely on the longest runway with hot brakes.

synopsis: When a flight attendant aboard a B737-700 observed a passenger utilizing a military style 'flameless ration heater' they confiscated and secured it. After landing they failed to deliver it to operations due to conflicting duties.
summary: The 'C' Flight Attendant secured a passenger's flameless military ration heater in the wheelchair compartment during the flight. The Purser forgot to hand the item to operations upon arrival while managing an unaccompanied minor and crew change.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: After landing at SAC, a pilot taxied to parking on Taxiway H without referencing an airport diagram and taxied into the closed apron area where his propeller struck a taxi light. The taxiway centerline was clearly visible deceiving the pilot into believing the area was open.
summary: The pilot struck a plastic taxi light with the propeller while taxiing on a closed apron area marked with yellow lines. The incident occurred due to a pavement dip obscuring the lights and the pilot's reliance on familiar markings without consulting the updated airport diagram.

synopsis: Stearman pilot reports a NMAC with a drone at 800 FT approaching FBL. No evasive action is taken as the drone passes 300 FT off the right wing co-altitude.
summary: A pilot flying a Stearman at 1,800 MSL near FBL encountered a drone with attachments passing 300 feet off the right wingtip. The pilot avoided a collision but noted the drone was operating above the 400-foot maximum altitude limit.

synopsis: ZAN Controller reports of a conflict that they tried to resolve but the confliction was in another Center's airspace.
summary: The controller reported a loss of separation in CZEG airspace involving Aircraft X and an unknown aircraft at FL350 after CZEG requested traffic stops that conflicted with prior coordination. The incident occurred during a NEG RVSM transfer, highlighting the risk of rerouting aircraft after acceptance.

synopsis: SAV Controller reports of a airborne conflict caused by SVN Tower vectoring aircraft in his airspace.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller in South Radar sector reported a collision alert when an Army-controlled Aircraft Y, vectored by SVN Tower into FAA airspace, tracked directly toward Aircraft X on an ILS28 base leg. The pilot of Aircraft X executed evasive action to avoid a mid-air collision, which the controller attributed to the SVN Controller's non-compliance with airspace procedures.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ZLA Controller describes situation where Yuma Approach Controller violates his airspace with three different aircraft. This is considered an airspace deviation and leads to an increased workload for the receiving Controller.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Yuma Range initiated three unauthorized handoffs of IFR aircraft into their airspace without proper coordination or flight plan data. The controller rejected the transfers due to insufficient separation, but the aircraft entered anyway, requiring supervisor assistance to establish radar tracks.

synopsis: The pilots of an A319 were alerted by flight attendants of aft galley fault warning lights and a serious overheat problem that could not be quickly rectified by the usual processes. The Captain determined that a diversion to the nearest airport was warranted, they advised ATC, and expeditiously landed the aircraft.
summary: The flight crew diverted due to an overheated circuit breaker panel and coffee machine border in the aft galley. After pulling relevant circuit breakers failed to cool the surfaces, the captain landed at the nearest airport where emergency crews confirmed no fire or smoke.

synopsis: An A319 Captain refused a reassignment at the end of his four day trip due to fatigue. Contributing factors included a greatly extended and delayed inbound flight, a post midnight arrival, and unprofessional behavior on the part of his First Officer on short final.
summary: The Captain took control of the aircraft during final approach to ORD after the First Officer failed to respond to gear and speed instructions, citing a disagreement over fuel management and energy control. Following the landing, the Captain refused a reassignment to a fifth day due to fatigue and received a fatigue call instead.

synopsis: A B757 flight crew experience significant landing gear vibration during the takeoff and requested emergency equipment standing by on landing. One nose gear tire was found to be substantially missing. Communications problems with the company enroute were a significant contributing factor to the flight's uneasiness.
summary: The Captain experienced severe nose wheel shimmy during takeoff and subsequent communication failures with Dispatch and Maintenance Control. After declaring an emergency and landing with gear down, inspection revealed significant damage to the right nose wheel, which a mechanic had initially concealed.

synopsis: A B777's oven caught fire in flight, so a Flight Attendant extinguished the fire leaving a great deal of smoke. The Captain diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: A cabin crew member reported smoke and flames from an aft galley oven, which a Flight Attendant extinguished using three halon bottles. The Captain diverted to the nearest suitable airport, where the aircraft landed uneventfully after the crew completed applicable checklists.

synopsis: Pilot reports of landing with a tailwind and is not happy with the circumstances. Aircraft is turned in inside the outer marker and pilot is questioned if they have traffic they are following in sight.
summary: The pilot reported landing Runway 17L with a 15-knot tailwind due to activity at Ft. Knox. ATC provided tight vectors from 4,000 feet, requesting in-sight traffic following, which the crew declined, noting that tailwind operations require more runway time and should not rely on crew separation.

synopsis: After arriving in the gate an A330 Captain, holding brakes manually to preserve extra block to block minutes prior to 'setting the parking brake'--thus triggering the flight crew's block in time--was surprised when he misinterpreted the meaning of a self-park lighted advisory acronym to mean the nose gear had been chocked. He then released the brakes. He was quickly alerted by his First Officer that the aircraft was now rolling backward on the sloped ramp and then re-stopped the airplane and set the brakes properly.
summary: The pilot reported that an Airbus A330 rolled backwards on a steep ramp at the gate after misinterpreting an "INBLK" display as confirmation of chocks and releasing brakes before setting the parking brake. The pilot attributed the incident to this error and pressure to minimize block times, while recommending improved ground guidance and immediate chocking.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported encountering wake turbulence after takeoff in trail of an A320 that resulted in a momentary stick shaker.
summary: The crew experienced wake turbulence from a preceding A320 during climb, approximately 3.5 miles in trail. The encounter caused brief aircraft bumping and activated the stick shaker, but no further issues occurred.

synopsis: An air carrier dispatched to ASE during an active thunderstorm period broke off the approach while still VMC and while climbing to 17,000 feet to hold took evasive action from a TCAS RA. Aspen is not equipped to assist pilots during summer weather.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe weather and conflicting ATC clearances while approaching Aspen with a FL250 restriction due to an MEL. They aborted the approach, avoided traffic and storms by holding at AJAXX, and later landed safely, citing dispatch and ATC weather limitations as safety concerns.

synopsis: When approach cleared a B737NG to cross 6 DME from the runway at 2,000 FT, cleared to land Runway 28R at PDX the Captain refused the clearance reminding the Controller that the ILS DME is transmitted from the far end of the runway by the localizer transmitter and, as a result, 6 DME was just 4.3 NM from the approach end of the runway and an approach from that altitude at that distance would, by definition, exceed stabilized approach criteria.
summary: The pilot rejected an Approach Controller's visual approach clearance to cross 6 DME at 2,000 feet, explaining that the DME originates from the runway's far end. Correcting the clearance prevented an unstable approach that would have occurred 4.3 miles from the runway threshold.

synopsis: A C-208 pilot reported burning eyes, nose and throat along with a foul taste and headache following TKS usage during in-flight icing.
summary: The pilot reported using the TKS anti-icing system during flight and subsequently experienced a cockpit odor, burning eyes, nose, and throat, a bad taste, and a headache. The narrative attributes these symptoms to the use of the TKS system but does not specify a confirmed cause or outcome.

synopsis: A passenger reported the passenger seated in the aisle seat next to him/her was of such size as to make it impossible to remain in the center seat unless the arm rest between seats A and B was up in which case the reporter intruded on the space of the window seat passenger. In addition, it would have been impossible to take a brace position should it have become necessary.
summary: A deadheading crew member reported a safety concern on a passenger flight where an oversized passenger occupied half of seat 12B, preventing the crew member from assuming a brace position. Although an agent threatened to require a second seat, the issue remained unresolved, leaving the crew member unable to sit safely for takeoff and landing.

synopsis: An A319 passenger was smoking a cigarette in the lavatory but the smoke detector failed to alert. A Flight Attendant detected the odor, confronted the passenger and found a smoldering cigarette in a beer can which she extinguished.
summary: A male passenger smoked a cigarette in the lavatory and hid the lit end in a Budweiser can, which was discovered by a flight attendant who extinguished it with water. Although the smoke detector failed to activate, the crew reported the incident to the FAA and the Captain.

synopsis: B737-900 Flight Attendant, jump seating to work, notices the 2L door is not armed during taxi out and arms it.
summary: A commuter pilot discovered the L2 door was unarmed while taxiing out and immediately armed it. The pilot reported the incident to the cabin crew, noting the door had been left unsecured despite a prior galley check.

synopsis: M20 pilot reports the glare from a Solar Power Plant requires the pilot seat to be lowered so the glareshield blocks the mirrors, but also eliminates the view forward.
summary: A pilot reported that glare from the Ivanpah Solar Power Plant illuminated the cockpit while approaching BOACH Intersection on V21. This glare blocked traffic scanning over 40 degrees of the horizon, forcing the pilot to lower their viewpoint to avoid eye discomfort.

synopsis: A small aircraft pilot forgot to level at 1,300 FT departing Runway 27 at OSH during a local aviation event and offers suggestions.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna departing Runway 27 at OSH forgot to level at 1,300 feet as required by a NOTAM for a local aviation event. The pilot attributed the error to memory reliance and distractions during taxi and takeoff, though no traffic conflict occurred.

synopsis: M20 pilot reports the glare from a Solar Power Plant requires the pilot seat to be lowered so the glareshield blocks the mirrors, but also eliminates the view forward.
summary: A pilot approaching WHIGG Intersection on V21 reported that glare from the Ivanpah Solar Power Plant illuminated the cockpit and blocked traffic scanning over 40 degrees of the horizon. To avoid eye discomfort, the pilot lowered their viewpoint to place the mirrors below the glareshield.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZLC Developmental describes a situation where and aircraft is given a void time to depart the airport and departs after the void time. This causes an operational error with an arrival that is vectored too late to avoid the error.
summary: The D-Side controller issued a void-time clearance to Aircraft X departing COD while Aircraft Y arrived from FL230. When Aircraft X departed late and climbed through 8,200 feet, the R-Side controller vectored Aircraft Y, resulting in a loss of separation within 4 miles due to reliance on radar and void times.

synopsis: ZOA Oceanic Controller describes situation where he knows there should be an aircraft, attempts to track down the aircraft through another Center. The other Center knows nothing about the aircraft. The Oceanic Supervisor finds the aircraft, and the controller does not advise the other Center of the aircrafts position.
summary: An air traffic controller handling Aircraft X en route from SCEL to KRIV encountered a missing flight plan and CPDLC log-on failure while the aircraft flew through uncontrolled airspace. The controller took no further action after a supervisor located the flight plan, though the report recommends contacting commercial radio or ZLA to confirm the route and block airspace.

synopsis: PHL Tower and TRACON Controllers' report of a procedure where if FOD is reported on a runway the other crossing runway is closed until the FOD is removed. In this instance two aircraft were cleared to land on converging runways and sent around causing a NMAC.
summary: A bird strike on Runway 35 triggered a procedure closing intersecting Runway 27R, causing a double go-around and a 0.18 nm, 900-foot proximity between two aircraft. Later, miscommunication regarding Aircraft Z's handoff during re-sequencing created another near-miss with Aircraft A at 3,000 feet.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ZOB Controller reports of an incident involving a skydiving aircraft that isn't pointed out to him and he has to find out what the aircraft is going to do.
summary: A Detroit Area controller observed a parachute aircraft (code XZXY) climbing from 11,500 feet dangerously close to a holding stack at MIZAR, violating LOA procedures. The local controller failed to protect the holding airspace, dismissed the conflict by citing VFR status, and did not coordinate an official point-out.

synopsis: ZTL Controller reports of mid shift traffic that was delayed due to weather and the heavy workload the controllers were under. Positions were combined to normal mid shift configuration but the planes were deviating due to the weather and not talking to the controllers.
