summary: An air traffic controller in the Atlanta sector experienced a loss of separation when vectoring a departing aircraft at FL260 while another descended to 240, caused by communication failures due to VSCS maintenance and absent supervisors. The controller corrected the conflict after realizing the descending aircraft was 1,000 feet below, amidst widespread delays and diversions.

synopsis: AUS Ground Controller observes the Local Controller telling an aircraft to LUAW, while another aircraft is on short final to the same runway.
summary: A Ground Control controller reported that Local Control instructed an aircraft to line up and wait on Runway 35R while Aircraft X was on short final approximately 100 feet AGL. The reporter believes the controller knowingly used anticipated separation, violating facility safety logic regarding preceding aircraft clearance.

synopsis: B777 flight crew is informed by the Purser of an oven fire in the aft galley. A great deal of smoke is generated and two halon fire bottles are used to extinguish the flames. Flight diverts to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: During cruise at FL370, a galley oven fire caused by a plastic lid required diversion, resulting in smoke inhalation for one passenger and two crew. The crew used halon and PBAs to extinguish the fire, exceeded 250 KTS below 10,000 feet with ATC approval, and landed 5,800 lbs overweight without evacuation.

synopsis: An A320 flight crew descending on the FLUNK Arrival to SMF suffered a TA\RA conflict with a VFR Cessna Conquest in the process of requesting flight following from ATC during its climbout.
summary: A pilot descending to 10,000 feet on the Flunk Three Arrival into SMF experienced a TCAS RA conflict with a climbing VFR Cessna Conquest. The pilot manually executed an escape maneuver after receiving conflicting ATC vectors and minimal separation warning from NORCAL.

synopsis: A300 flight crew reports descending below the glideslope inadvertently during a visual approach, then correcting and landing normally.
summary: The First Officer and Captain conducted a training vertical speed visual approach on an ILS backup. After increasing descent rate to 1,000 FPM to correct a high altitude, they briefly went below the glidepath triggering an alert, but corrected and landed safely in the touchdown zone.

synopsis: EMB145 Captain reports being issued holding instructions during approach and contacting Dispatch with the news. Dispatch responds the minimum fuel required for diversion to the alternate and the Captain notes they are already below that amount. The diversion is otherwise uneventful.
summary: The flight crew held at 6,000 feet after an ATC diversion and discovered they were below bingo fuel due to weather deviations. They proceeded to the alternate airport and landed uneventfully, requesting additional fuel for future weather deviations.

synopsis: An EMB-145 crew reacted physically during and after a flight in which they were exposed to a dirty socks odor. All crew members were treated at an emergency facility.
summary: The flight crew and a flight attendant experienced chemical inhalation symptoms and a musty odor during cruise-to-descent, prompting a precautionary landing. After shutting down engine bleeds and packs, all crew members were hospitalized for evaluation and diagnosed with chemical inhalation.

synopsis: An Air Carrier Captain described his experience with ERI ground agents repeatedly pushing for quick turn arounds which interfere with and disregard the requirement to complete preflight procedures and checklists.
summary: A pilot reported that at ERI, ramp agents and station management repeatedly interrupted preflight duties and checklists to rush boarding, causing the crew to restart procedures multiple times. The pilot stated this pressure to achieve quick turns increases the risk of missed items and safety errors, noting that on-time performance priorities are compromising flight safety.

synopsis: Helicopter Check Airman discovered the empty weight moment data on the aircraft weighing sheet appeared to be incorrect. The error was transferred to a computer program producing weight and balance errors on all aircraft using the program for 18 months.
summary: Pilots discovered incorrect empty weight moment data on a BH-222 weighing sheet caused by Excel rounding errors and magnified by added equipment. They corrected the documentation, logged the issue, briefed the next crew, and recommended company-wide reviews of weight and balance sheets.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reports difficulties during pushback due to poor comprehension of english by the tug driver at SCEL.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a pushback error at SCEL due to a language barrier with a new tug driver, causing the aircraft to move onto the wrong taxiway and block traffic. The First Officer alerted the Captain to unintended brake release, and a new driver eventually stopped the push after the crew intervened.

synopsis: B757 flight crew experiences a green REV indication on the right engine at 80 KTS during takeoff and rejects. Crew returns to the gate and Maintenance takes the aircraft out of service.
summary: The pilot not flying rejected the takeoff below 80 KTS after the right engine reverse deployed, indicated by a green REV annunciation on the upper EICAS. The aircraft was taxied clear of the runway, returned to the gate, and placed out of service by maintenance.

synopsis: B767 flight crew experiences an engine rollback climbing out of 5,000 FT that result in a large yaw angle and a momentary stick shaker. The thrust lever for the affected engine is brought to idle and attempts to increase thrust are not successful. An emergency is declared, some fuel is dumped and the flight returns to the departure airport. While being vectored for approach the thrust lever is advanced again and the engine responds normally.
summary: The pilot flying encountered a right engine compressor stall and stick shaker warning during a turn in IMC while climbing to 6,000 feet. The crew declared an emergency, returned for an overweight landing, and later restored normal engine operation after troubleshooting.

synopsis: MD83 flight crew is informed by Ground Personnel that the outboard tire on the right side is missing some tread after gate arrival. Damage to the right engine and flap is noted and it is suspected the damage occurred during takeoff, but was not detected by the crew.
summary: The pilot reported a right outboard main gear tire tread cap separation during takeoff, likely exacerbated by a CDL flap hinge fairing requiring higher speeds. The debris caused damage to the flaps and engine, but the flight remained normal with no in-flight indications.

synopsis: A320 First Officer reports that when the HHOOD 2 RNAV arrival to PDX landing Runways 28L and R is entered in the FMGC, the MEA of 7200 feet between HHOOD and BLRUN is not honored. Manual entries to the FMGC are required to keep the aircraft above 7200 feet until after BLRUN.
summary: The pilot reported that the Airbus FMGC would have descended the aircraft below the 7200-foot MEA between HHOOD and BLRUN during the HHOOD 2 RNAV arrival into PDX. This potential violation resulted from the FMGC programming a 280-knot descent to anticipate a 'TOO STEEP PATH' alert, a continuing issue requiring fleet and FAA attention.

synopsis: Five minutes after gate arrival and receiving the chocks in signal, the Captain was about to leave the cockpit when he detects the aircraft is moving and quickly sets the brake. After repositioning the jetway the Captain learns that only nose wheel chocks were in place and were apparently not adequate for the slope.
summary: The Captain reported that the aircraft rolled back two feet after receiving the 'chocks in' signal because the ramp crew only chocked the nose wheel. The Captain immediately set the parking brake, preventing injuries or damage, and noted the main wheels were chocked later than expected.

synopsis: An air carrier crew on approach to LAS Runway 19R was cleared to cross LEMNZ Intersection at or above 3,500 FT but consider 1,400 FT AGL at 2.6 NM from the airport an unstabilized approach setup.
summary: The flight crew received a clearance to cross LEMNZ at 3,500 feet for a visual approach to Runway 19R at LAS, which placed them 1,400 feet AGL only 2.6 NM from the runway. Although the crew managed energy to complete the approach, they reported the clearance created an unstable approach threat.

synopsis: A320 Captain reports being cleared for the visual approach to Runway 19L via the GRNPA 1 to LEMNZ which is less than 3 NM from the runway end. STAR shows a 6100 foot MEA to LEMNZ, resulting in an unexpected close in turn to final with potential for an unstabilized approach.
summary: A pilot reported that the GRNPA 1 STAR groundtrack to RNAV 19L was unsafe due to a 4000-foot descent requirement over three miles, exceeding the 5200-foot MVA. Despite requests for direct routing, ATC denied the request, resulting in a third potentially unstable visual approach.

synopsis: B757 Captain experiences iPad waypoint entry errors when cutting and pasting the route from the flight plan as taught by ground school instructors. The flight plan format of 40N50W produces erroneous waypoints in the Jeppesen Flight Pro on the iPad.
summary: Crews reported that following Saber instructor guidance to copy-paste routing into Jeppesen Flight Pro caused erroneous positions during the Gander to New York FIR transition. The error occurred because the app requires manual entry of latitude/longitude points rather than pasted flight plan data.

synopsis: EMB145 First Officer arriving EWR is informed by ATC of opposite direction traffic 500 FT below. A TA is annunciated stating 'monitor vertical speed' with red indicated on the VSI for any descent. The First Officer maintains level flight but the Captain takes control and initiates a descent, which the First Officer quickly countermands. The Captain begins climbing and levels off at 6,000 FT.
summary: During an ILS approach to Newark, the Captain initiated an unauthorized descent due to confusion over traffic location, contradicting a TCAS "Monitor Vertical Speed" alert. The First Officer corrected the error by commanding a climb, and the crew leveled at 6,000 feet before resuming the approach.

synopsis: A Captain and First Officer return to a departure airport after noticing the Number 2 Hydraulic Quantity was down to one quart on their DHC-8-100 aircraft and no caution lights had illuminated. After Normal Gear Extension the Number 2 Hydraulic Quantity went to .7, Caution lights illuminated. Maintenance noticed a hydraulic flex line had failed in the Nose wheel well, even though the line was still within duty cycle limitations.
summary: The crew experienced a Number 2 hydraulic leak in the nose wheel well after gear retraction, causing low quantity and open gear doors. They returned to the airport, landed on Runway 34 with degraded systems, and cancelled the flight after maintenance attributed the leak to a flex line within cycle limits.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: DHC8 First Officer reports his aircraft rolling forward as the Captain brings the condition levers out of feather after engine start. Normal braking is attempted to no avail and the emergency brake is used, stopping the aircraft abruptly and injuring the Flight Attendant.
summary: A Flight Attendant was injured when the aircraft rolled forward during engine start after the Captain moved condition levers out of feather, despite the parking brake being set at 2,600 PSI. The Captain stopped the aircraft using the emergency brake, shut down the engines, and requested medical assistance for the injured crew member.

synopsis: A G-IV flight crew suffered two consecutive conflicts with aircraft in the vicinity of their airport of intended landing. They followed a TCAS RA to avoid the first then came nose to nose with the second from which they took undirected evasive measures.
summary: During an IFR descent into MVY, the crew received a TCAS RA while following ATC instructions to avoid traffic, but a second aircraft appeared immediately after leveling off. The pilot executed evasive maneuvers to avoid a collision with the twin-engine aircraft at approximately 500 feet separation before landing.

synopsis: Hawker 900 flight crew experiences a loss of cabin pressurization at FL410 and declares an emergency before descending to 12,000 FT. The crew elects to divert to a suitable alternate.
summary: Two pilots on a ferry flight at FL410 experienced rapid cabin altitude rise and depressurization warnings, prompting an emergency descent to 12,000 feet. They landed safely at ZZZ after a post-flight inspection found no cause for the depressurization, though fuel vapors were detected in the cabin.

synopsis: B777 Captain experiences loss of reliable airspeed, loss of vertical guidance, loss of autothrottles and loss of autopilot while in heavy turbulence and at times extreme rain. Possible overspeed occurs and the crew elects to divert to a suitable airport. A few minutes after exiting the rain all systems gradually return to normal.
summary: The crew experienced multiple system failures, including unreliable airspeed and autopilot loss, during climbout through heavy rain and turbulence. The reporter attributed the incident to potential water ingress during loading, noting that systems recovered after exiting the rain, allowing a safe emergency diversion and landing.

synopsis: The flight crew of a commercial transport aircraft was given a revised runway and RNAV SID with their taxi clearance at VIDP. During the hurried attempt to reprogram the changes while taxiing for takeoff they failed to re-consult the separate departure chart detailing 'INITIAL CLIMB PROCEDURES DURING MIXED MODE OPERATION' which specifies: a different first turn altitude, a different heading to which to turn, a different altitude to which to climb following the turn, and the directive to expect '...further with radar.' They also advised they failed to comply with a directive to limit rate of climb to 1,500 FPM.
summary: The flight crew at VIDP flew the UXABA RNAV departure from Runway 11 with an initial climb to 2,600 feet, missing the ATIS "Mixed Mode" requirement to climb to 1,500 feet first. The crew attributed this error to high workload from a last-minute clearance change, information overload, and ambiguous chart procedures.

synopsis: B757 Captain discovers after landing that the nosewheel steering has failed. The aircraft is towed to the ramp, where maintenance discovers a bolt missing from the steering linkage.
summary: After landing and exiting a high-speed taxiway, the crew found nose wheel steering inoperative with both the tiller and rudder pedals. Maintenance identified a missing bolt on the summing link as the cause, requiring the aircraft to be towed back to the ramp.

synopsis: B767 Captain reports that after pushback and tow to the top of the alley with both engines running, the tug driver dismounts and attempts to disconnect the tow bar without telling the Captain to set the parking brake. Eventually the set brake signal is received from the wing walker and the towbar is successfully disconnected.
summary: During a night pushback with two ground crew, the tug driver lost communication while attempting to release the pin with both engines running. The pilot set brakes after flashing lights and receiving a hand signal from the wing walker, citing a need for retraining and recommending a three-person crew or mechanic oversight.

synopsis: Air Carrier Dispatcher reports a flight crew accepting an ATC reroute through weather he had flight planned to avoid and doing so against his specific advice.
summary: A dispatcher warned the flight crew that an ATC-assigned re-route would take the aircraft into severe thunderstorms, but the crew accepted the clearance and departed without communicating their decision. The dispatcher reported that the crew ignored safety warnings and subsequent contact attempts, highlighting a lack of communication and unauthorized route acceptance.

synopsis: An EMB-145 crew cruising at FL220 detected the cabin altitude climbing through 8,800 FT with no EICAS messages so they declared an emergency, completed the memory items and descended to 10,000 FT. The right pack was MEL'ed inoperative after landing.
summary: During cruise at FL220, the flight crew observed a rapid cabin altitude climb to 10,400 FT without an EICAS message. They executed an emergency descent to 10,000 FT, landed safely, and deferred Pack 2 to the MEL due to inoperative status.

synopsis: A B737 pilot comments that after takeoff SLC Departure frequently issues altitude and/or airspeed alterations to already complex WEVIC 3 and EDETH 3 RNAV departures which removes one pilot from monitoring traffic and aircraft systems.
summary: A pilot reported that published WEVIC 3 and EDETH 2 RNAV departures from SLC are routinely modified by ATC shortly after takeoff. These frequent changes to airspeed and altitude restrictions create high workload for the monitoring pilot.

synopsis: An A319 parked un-chocked at the gate because of lightning during the arrival, rolled backward and lodged the door on the jetway after the parking brake pressure depleted.
summary: During cockpit setup of a cold/secured aircraft, the un-chocked plane rolled back and snagged the jet bridge door. The pilot attributed the movement to a lack of chocks due to a prior lightning-induced ramp closure, noting that the new crew was unaware of this condition.

synopsis: A319 First Officer reports the Captain releasing the parking brake at the gate due to high brake temperatures. The aircraft slowly rolls into the jetway due to no chocks.
summary: The Captain released the parking brake due to high temperatures while the First Officer was conducting preflight, causing the aircraft to roll back and strike the jet bridge. The reporter attributes the incident to the failure to chock the airplane.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilots report of a flight into LAX in which the Controller assigned one speed then told the pilots they were going too slow. Pilots had to scramble to keep aircraft fast into the airport.
summary: Pilots flying a winglet aircraft on the SEAVU2 arrival into LAX encountered conflicting speed clearances from SoCal Approach, including demands to maintain 250 knots versus 210 knots at GAATE. The controller's unrealistic instructions and aggressive communication forced the crew to disconnect the autopilot and manually decelerate using speed brakes to achieve a stabilized ILS approach.

synopsis: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) describes a hostile work environment where an aggressive and irate Line Maintenance Supervisor attempted to intimidate him into working around FAA Rules and Regulations. Technician had found a damaged 'Wing to Body' panel during an overnight maintenance visit on a B737-800 aircraft.
summary: A mechanic found potential wing panel damage on a B737-800 during a walkaround and requested a Line Engineering Order to defer the repair. The Maintenance Supervisor became aggressive and attempted to intimidate the mechanic into releasing the aircraft without the order, creating a hostile environment and reducing safety standards.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot and an examiner began the LMO Runway 29 GPS Approach straight in and made the appropriate CTAF calls with no response. During the touch and go, traffic was seen on the runway which created a near miss as they took off over the aircraft then discovered their radio malfunctioned.
summary: A pilot conducting an IFR checkride in a single-engine aircraft on a GPS approach to Runway 29 at a non-controlled airport nearly collided with a jump plane on the runway due to radio communication failures. The pilot avoided the aircraft by lifting off just before impact and exiting the pattern, attributing the incident to the radios not being live during initial calls.

synopsis: DA20 Flight Instructor reports a nose gear failure upon landing with no injuries.
summary: A student pilot and CFI experienced a nose gear failure upon landing. Neither occupant was injured.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A single engine pilot flying the MRY 10R ILS set 278 FT in the altitude alerter and descended below the 480 FT DH before realizing his error, then executing a missed approach.
summary: The pilot inadvertently set the altitude alert to 278 feet instead of the 480-foot decision height during an ILS approach to Runway 10R at MRY in IMC. The pilot descended below the decision height without visual contact and immediately initiated a missed approach.

synopsis: A glider pilot near N85 saw parachutist 1 mile ahead and circled to gain altitude but was then approach very closely by the jump aircraft twice before exiting the area.
summary: A sailplane pilot encountered a single-engine jump plane while soaring near N85. The jump plane made two uncomfortably close passes across the sailplane's nose, presumably to warn of parachutists, though the pilot considered the second pass unnecessary and potentially indicative of air rage.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: While making a practice short field landing at F72 the pilot of a small low wing aircraft landed 'three inches' short of the asphalt runway surface and later determined he had struck a 1.5 to two inch 'berm' of untapered material causing damage to the 'upper part' of the landing gear area.
summary: The pilot reported landing short on Runway 27 at Franklin Field, where the main gear struck a non-standard 1.5 to 2-inch high berm at the asphalt threshold. This impact caused damage to the upper landing gear area, which the pilot attributes to the berm's presence and lack of tapering.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A pilot flying from HIO to the coast reported a near miss with an unidentified aircraft which both his grandson and wife saw momentarily, but he did not.
summary: A pilot flying a single-engine aircraft at 4,500 feet MSL reported a near-midair collision with a blue single-engine aircraft that descended from above and passed just left of the wing. The pilot did not see or feel the event, though passengers observed the other aircraft or a flash while the pilot monitored 122.9.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot taxied and departed Runway 1 using proper CTAF communications procedures but on the incorrect frequency and had a near miss with an aircraft landing on Runway 19.
summary: The pilot, departing Runway 01, discovered an aircraft beginning a takeoff run on Runway 19 at 400 feet AGL. The pilot attributed the missed communication to selecting the incorrect UNICOM frequency (XXX.025 instead of XXX.05) and resolved to avoid repeating the error.

synopsis: PA18 pilot reports losing control during landing, resulting in a runway excursion and the aircraft flipping on its back. Minor injuries and damage are reported.
summary: The pilot reported that during landing, the aircraft pulled left and flipped onto its back before they could correct. The incident resulted in minor damage and a leg scrape for the pilot, with no other injuries.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reports departing for a short flight in less than VFR conditions to find the destination airport weather deteriorating even further. The decision is made to continue with a visual approach at very low altitude resulting in contact with pine trees and damage to the aircraft.
summary: A pilot conducting VFR training encountered deteriorating weather and low ceilings, leading to a decision to land at an alternate airport. During a low-altitude turn to final, the left wing struck pine tree tops, causing skin and aileron damage, which the pilot attributed to flying before VFR conditions were confirmed.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot reports of a runway incursion that was caused by possible miscommunication and a frequency that was not issued.
summary: The First Officer reported that while taxiing to Runway 17L, the crew followed preceding traffic on an incorrect Tower frequency (132.35) due to ATC instructions. After switching to the correct frequency (133.3) before takeoff, ATC provided a contact number for a possible deviation regarding the frequency error.

synopsis: Anticipating substantial delay after taxi out due to weather the Captain of a B737-300 opted to taxi on one engine and, to protect against lateral fuel imbalance, opened the fuel crossfeed. When the delay proved minimal they started the second engine and departed only to discover during cruise they had not closed the crossfeed and were now faced with a 4,000 LB lateral imbalance.
summary: The pilot opened the fuel crossfeed valve during a one-engine taxi for weather delays but failed to close it before takeoff, causing a 4,000 LBS imbalance noticed in cruise. Vectors were requested on arrival to balance the fuel, resulting in a normal landing with a 700 LBS difference.

synopsis: A B777 Captain reported that the navigation database in his company's aircraft included commands to cross the first two fixes (PRAWN AND RUMSY) on the PECAN 1B RNAV SID from VHHH at or below 5,000 but the fixes on the Jeppesen SID graphic shows no such restriction.
summary: Pilots at VHHH discovered erroneous "at or below 5,000" altitude restrictions in the FMC for the PECAN 1B SID that did not match Jeppesen charts. This database error could cause aircraft to unintentionally level off at 5,000 feet during VNAV departures if pilots are distracted, despite higher ATC clearances.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reports receiving a low altitude alert from the Tower while on a visual approach to Runway 10C at ORD. The crew was above the glideslope intercepting final inside RAYYY when the alert was issued and continued to a normal landing.
summary: The flight crew received a low altitude alert from ORD Tower while intercepting the final approach course for Runway 10C on a visual approach. The crew verified they were slightly above the glideslope profile and continued to an uneventful landing.

synopsis: An Airbus Captain flying a morning, daylight VMC approach below an overcast, reported the LAX Runway 25L PAPI dimly lit while the 25R PAPI was very bright. Tower was unable to adjust either PAPI's illumination level.
summary: Pilots reported that the PAPI for Runway 25L was dimly lit while the PAPI for Runway 25R was excessively bright during approach, despite Tower's failed attempts to adjust brightness. The crew noted this could cause crews to land on the incorrect runway in low ceilings and questioned why the takeoff-only Runway 25R PAPI was active.

synopsis: B757 Captain describes and arrival and landing at MPTO that he believes was unsafe due to the Controller's instructions to keep speed up, the strong Spanish accents and the use of Spanish for most ATC instructions.
summary: Pilots of a B757 reported unsafe ATC operations at MPTO during approach and taxi in rain, citing language barriers and excessive speed restrictions that compromised a stabilized approach. The crew also noted a Ground Controller's unsafe instruction to expedite clearance while a B777 blocked ramp access, concluding that current ATC practices are hazardous.

synopsis: Dispatcher reports assigning a weather avoidance route to one of his flights then having send a new release when an aircraft swap is required. The new release defaults to the standard company route but the weather avoidance route remains on file with ATC. The crew is cleared as filed which is not the route on the current release.
summary: A dispatcher reported that regenerating a flight plan after an aircraft swap replaced the original FAA-filed route with a company default, causing a mismatch between crew paperwork and ATC clearance. The error resulted from insufficient system proficiency, high workload, and a lack of procedures to refile strips or request full clearances during tail swaps.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew experiences an engine failure passing FL220 during climb. The engine is secured and the flight returns to the departure airport for an overweight landing.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced a Number 1 engine failure at FL220 due to a disintegrated hot section, resulting in an overweight emergency landing. The crew returned to the departure airport, where ARFF confirmed no fire and maintenance found metal fragments from the aft turbine section.

synopsis: MD83 flight crew experiences a tail compartment temp high during climbout and returns to the departure airport.
summary: During climbout, the crew experienced a tail compartment temperature warning followed by a left pack failure. They declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport, and deplaned passengers after requesting ARFF observation.

synopsis: SR22 pilot experiences a dramatic loss of power at 3,000 FT and is able to land safely on an available grass strip.
summary: The pilot experienced a dramatic power loss during flight, declared an emergency, and landed uneventfully on a grass strip at ZZZ. Large oil quantities were found on the belly, but the exact cause of the leak remains unknown.

synopsis: CE340 Pilot reports ignoring an EGPWS warning during a right base visual approach to Runway 19 at TEB, caused by a 694 foot radio tower a half mile right of final and 1.6 miles from the runway end. Even though daylight VMC prevailed the tower was not detected visually until it passed by the left wingtip 50 feet below. A late advisory was issued by the Tower.
summary: A pilot flying a visual approach to Runway 19 at Teterboro Airport passed within 50 feet of a 600-foot radio antenna after disregarding GPWS warnings. The pilot attributed the near-miss to failing to identify the obstacle during the approach briefing and ignoring the terrain advisories.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZAB Controller reports of discussion with MMZT Controller about deviations for weather and what he could approve in his airspace. The aircraft came in on non approved routings and violated ATCAA airspace.
summary: An air traffic controller managed deviations for two aircraft near VYLLA due to weather and active military airspace. Both aircraft initially violated the SELLS ATCAA boundary, prompting an emergency declaration for the first and a forced 360-degree turn for the second, attributed to insufficient planning time.

synopsis: ZDC Controller reports of two airspace violations due to forgetting that the airspace was active.
summary: An air traffic controller failed to provide a point out to Giant Killer for two aircraft transitioning through active Warning Area W-122 while routing them on a shortcut to comply with a TMU restriction. The controller realized the error 10-15 miles inside the airspace, obtained approval, and attributed the incident to forgetting the requirement due to the routing change.

synopsis: When the reporter/Approach Controller cleared the B737 (descending to 11,000 FT while established on the FISSK RNAV STAR to MDW) to proceed '...direct to HALIE, fly the Runway 4R transition' the 737 crew continued their descent and suffered a loss of separation with an IFR M-20 at 10,000 FT. The flight crew advised they were descending on the arrival.
summary: A B737 pilot on the FISSK3 arrival to MDW descended into an IFR M-20P while following a "descend via" clearance. The reporter attributes this loss of separation to ambiguous ATC phraseology that allows pilots to misinterpret instructions and descend without specific clearance.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports that the work to install EMAS for Runways 1L and 1r also included taxiway changes. The work was completed one month early and the airport diagram does not reflect these taxiway changes.
summary: Pilots reported confusion while taxiing to Runway 1L at SFO via Taxiway A1, which was rerouted north due to EMAS installation. The new taxiway configuration was not yet reflected on the SFO 10-9 chart, causing a discrepancy between the clearance and the published diagram.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reports being distracted by the Runway Entrance Lights (RELs) illuminating at IAD during landing on Runway 19C.
summary: A pilot reported that Runway Entrance Lights at IAD were distracting during a dusk landing, appearing like a vehicle from 400 feet AGL to rollout. The pilot suspects the lights remained on bright daylight settings, causing unnecessary distraction and raising concerns about future runway incursion recognition.

synopsis: An A319 Captain reported the flight attendants and pilots detected an unusual odor in flight in foreign airspace and the flight diverted to a domestic airport for an emergency landing. The crew went to the hospital with headaches and other symptoms.
summary: The flight crew diverted from FL360 due to a cabin odor and crew symptoms, suspecting a fume event. After a precautionary overweight landing, paramedics treated the crew, and a subsequent AIR BLEED message showed high right pack temperatures, though the odor's cause remained unconfirmed.

synopsis: A321 Captain experiences three red UNLK indications accompanied with an ECAM msg of L/G GEAR NOT DOWN LOCKED when the landing gear is selected down during approach. After consulting with Maintenance the landing gear is extended using the gravity extension method and a normal landing ensues.
summary: The crew experienced a landing gear failure on approach at 2,000 FT MSL, indicated by three red UNLK lights and an ECAM message. After executing the Gravity Extension Checklist, they successfully extended the gear, landed normally, and attributed the issue to a Landing Gear Control failure.

synopsis: Captain reports an EICAS Pack-1 VLV CLSD message appeared during climb thru FL240 on an EMB-145 aircraft. Performed EMERG/ABNORM procedure and message went away. While reviewing logbook for previous occurrences, pilot notes a maintenance write-up for a 'Ram Air Duct blown out' had not been cleared. Documented discrepancy not corrected.
summary: The flight crew encountered a PACK 1 VLV CLSD message while climbing through FL240 and executed the EMERG/ABNORM procedure. The reporter identified an uncorrected ram air duct discrepancy from a previous maintenance write-up, noting incomplete logbook documentation and unresolved discrepancies.

synopsis: A First Officer describes a Captain's encounter with a visibly angry Maintenance Supervisor after the Captain questioned serviceability of three portable Halon fire extinguishers on their EMB-145 aircraft. Placards on the three fire bottles displayed conflicting information, giving rise to Airworthiness issues.
summary: During a pre-flight safety inspection, the Captain reported conflicting placards and damaged labels on flight deck Halon fire extinguishers, but a hostile Maintenance Supervisor signed them airworthy without verifying serial numbers or expiration requirements. The Captain noted the Supervisor failed to provide a required ID number and reinstalled a unit with illegible operating instructions despite the damage.

synopsis: BD700 Captain experiences multiple TCAS RA's departing CCR while the flying First Officer takes evasive action. The Captain questions why he was instructed to takeoff with so much traffic in the area.
summary: The pilot reported three TCAS RAs within two minutes of an IFR departure from CCR due to conflicting traffic, including a downwind aircraft and an unreported intruder. The crew executed multiple altitude changes between 3,000 and 4,000 feet, attributing the event to a breakdown in ATC separation and questioning the initial takeoff clearance.

synopsis: Pilot reports of an RA caused by an aircraft going Mach 1 that went through its assigned altitude.
summary: During descent into OAKB, the crew received a climb RA due to a Mach 1 aircraft that ballooned above its cleared altitude, resulting in 700 feet of vertical separation. The conflict was resolved by FL250, though the crew could not see the traffic or hear the controller on the assigned frequency.

synopsis: MD-11 Captain reports rejecting a takeoff above 140 knots when the Captain's airspeed indicator fails. Brake overheats occur and eventually at least one fuse plug blew after returning to the gate..
summary: During takeoff roll, the Captain's airspeed indicator stagnated at 120 KTS while the First Officer's increased normally, triggering an IAS comparator alert. The Captain rejected the takeoff, executed a 180-degree turn, and taxied back, resulting in brake overheats and a blown fuse plug.

synopsis: A B757-200 Captain rejected the takeoff at 120 KTS when the nose tire vibration became excessive due to flat spots developed because the aircraft sat fully loaded with fuel over a weekend.
summary: A Check Airman pilot flying a student First Officer rejected takeoff at 120 KTS due to extreme nose gear vibration caused by severe tire flat spots from prolonged parking with full fuel. Maintenance replaced both nose tires, confirming the flat spots as the cause, and the aircraft returned to the gate safely.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: While an instructor and student were waiting for assistance on CTAF SIG Runway 9 edge following an engine failure on final, a light twin pilot, who did not hear their transmissions, took off and passed nearly directly over their disabled aircraft.
summary: A flight instructor and student experienced engine power loss on short final at SIG, resulting in a hard landing. While attempting to clear the runway, they narrowly avoided a collision with a multi-engine aircraft taking off from Runway 9 after the instructor pulled their plane onto the grass.

synopsis: A B757 crew flying the SFO FMS BRIDGE VISUAL 28R was asked to slow for traffic and while distracted configuring, slowing and monitoring traffic apparently selected FLCH which permitted the aircraft to descend below the MCP 1,500 FT SAMUL constraint.
summary: The flight crew executing a visual approach to SFO Runway 28R slowed from 210 to 160 KIAS to avoid traffic on parallel Runway 28L. This maneuver caused the aircraft to level off at 1,200 feet below the 1,500-foot restriction at SAMUL due to sun glare and workload preventing confirmation of VNAV re-engagement.

synopsis: Pilot reports that a communication tower (1052126) three miles south of LVJ has been unlighted or partially lighted for years and needs to be repaired instead of just issuing Notam's.
summary: A pilot reported a 1200-foot unlit broadcast tower near Pearland Regional Airport (LVJ) within 1.5 miles of the Runway 32 approach, noting repeated NOTAMs failed to ensure safety. The FCC stated no rule violation existed because the owner maintained NOTAMs while purchasing equipment to replace the failed lighting system.

synopsis: A C-210 engine failed at 4,500 FT but the pilot was unable to glide to a divert airport as the passenger pumped only the main gear down. A safe off airport landing was completed with the nose gear retracted.
summary: During a westbound familiarization flight, the pilot experienced engine roughness leading to total failure and a non-windmilling propeller. The pilot executed a forced landing on a paved road with extended flaps but only partial landing gear extension, resulting in a 400-foot rollout on the main gear and nose.

synopsis: A Lead Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) was informed he had not tighten one of the bolts that secure the Tail Rotor Control tube on a Bell-206L helicopter after replacing the Aft Evaporator Blower motor. Technician noted that pressure from supervisors to get the job done and the use of pilots to look over major maintenance work accomplished by mechanics were contributors.
summary: A mechanic and a pilot missed an untightened bolt on a helicopter's tail rotor control tube during a maintenance inspection. The mechanic attributed the error to operational pressure to return the aircraft to service and noted that pilots lack adequate training to inspect major flight control maintenance.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot reports filing an SFRA flight plan for departure from MTN with entry at the WOOLY gate and a planned altitude of 4,300 FT. After takeoff from Runway 31 he is chastised for entering Class B airspace without a clearance to do so.
summary: The pilot departed MTN and entered Class B airspace without specific authorization while climbing to 4,300 feet, believing radar contact with Potomac Approach granted entry. This resulted in an immediate descent to 2,000 feet after a commercial carrier passed within 300 feet, caused by the pilot's misunderstanding that Approach could authorize Class B entry.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZLA Controller reports of pilot telling him about a RA that he had while talking to the underlying Approach Control. Controller alluded to this happening all the time.
summary: An air traffic controller in Sector 21 reported that Aircraft X experienced a Resolution Advisory while climbing from SoCal TRACON into ZLA airspace. The controller attributed the conflict to SoCal TRACON failing to monitor VFR traffic during climbs, suggesting a change to the Letter of Agreement or airspace boundaries.

aircraft: Heavy Transport; Low Wing; 4 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZNY Controller reports of an aircraft that was not at the altitude it was supposed to be at.
summary: Aircraft X entered New York airspace at FL380 while cleared for FL360, a discrepancy detected via ADS/CPDLC despite the pilot reporting FL360 via HF. The event was attributed to a pilot deviation for climbing without clearance, as neither Piarco nor Dakar Centers issued the climb instruction.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier was holding short of LGA Runway 13 when the preceding aircraft used excessive break away thrust causing instrument disturbances which delayed their takeoff and required an aggressive taxi on Runway 13 to clear for landing traffic.
summary: While taxiing at LGA, jet blast from a preceding ERJ135 triggered persistent EICAS messages, requiring maintenance assistance. The Captain deviated from rapid ATC instructions to avoid aggressive maneuvers that could have caused a go-around for an aircraft on final, citing intense congestion as the cause.

synopsis: An A319 flight in descent with SOCAL Approach responded to a TCAS RA generated by another aircraft who failed to comply with its clearance to maintain a higher altitude.
summary: The flight crew received a TCAS RA during descent to 5,000 feet after ATC cleared them below a skydiving Cessna descending through their altitude. The crew executed the RA and turned left to avoid the conflict, which ATC attributed to the other aircraft being instructed to maintain altitude above them.

synopsis: An Airbus First Officer comments that flight crews at his air carrier, who have flown domestic trips only, are now transitioning to the Airbus and flying into very mountainous Latin American airports unaware of lax ATC procedures and potential CFIT situations.
summary: A First Officer reported that multiple Captains flying Airbus aircraft to and from Bogotá lacked mountainous terrain training, leading to unsafe maneuvers like bypassing SIDs and descending below Grid MORAs. The reporter warned that this complacency and reliance on ATC for terrain clearance in Latin America could result in a Controlled Flight Into Terrain event.

synopsis: A widebody crew on the OMDB RNAV Runway 12L became rushed attempting to slow and descend behind traffic. The Captain selected APP while descending to the 2,000 FT FAF crossing constraint and the busy First Officer detected the aircraft descending at 1,200 FT prior to the FAF and alerted the Captain who climbed to 2,000 FT.
summary: During an RNAV 12L approach into Dubai, the Captain selected APP mode instead of VNAV while rushing to descend, causing an unintentional descent to 1,200 feet below the protected 2,000-foot minimum. The First Officer called out the low altitude, prompting the Captain to disconnect the autopilot and climb back to 2,000 feet before crossing the FAF.

synopsis: A PA-44 instructor and student shutdown an engine for training but were unable to unfeather it. Multiple unfeather attempts drained the battery, caused communications difficulties, required manually lowering the landing gear and landing in an emergency condition.
summary: During a multi-engine training flight, a student and instructor experienced an engine restart failure that caused intercom and instrument loss, leading to an emergency landing with gear extended via emergency procedures. The reporter attributed the electrical issues to excessive load during restart attempts and recommended improved maintenance and checklist updates.

synopsis: An A320 engine generator faulted after start and was MEL'ed. At cruise the APU faulted and would not restart so crew diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: The crew diverted an aircraft with an in-flight APU generator failure at FL320, leaving only one generator operational. They performed an overweight landing at 151,800 lbs after unsuccessful restart attempts and fuel burn, with no issues reported.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Inspector reports their Inspection Manager, who is also their Chief Inspector, had been overriding non-routine write-ups made by inspectors during C-Checks for excessive wear on B717 aircraft pulley and slat track bearings, and then signing them off as serviceable bearings.
summary: A Maintenance Inspector reported that an Inspection Manager approved worn B717 pulley and slat track bearings during a C-Check, contradicting Boeing SOPM requirements. The reporter attributed this unsafe decision to unrealistic schedule pressures and the manager's lack of aircraft knowledge, warning of potential slat jamming.

synopsis: Pilot reports an Eclipse-500 aircraft pulled to the left upon landing during application of the aircraft's brake pedals. Further application indicated a right brake failure. Directional control was maintained, but aircraft ran out of runway with minor damage to left wing and flap. Aircraft was recently upgraded with an anti-skid system.
summary: The pilot reported that upon landing an Eclipse, the aircraft pulled left due to a suspected right brake failure following a recent anti-lock-skid system upgrade. Despite disabling the system, the pilot lost braking capability, overran the runway, and struck a light that punctured the left wing skin and flap.

synopsis: An ultralight aircraft was upset by a wind gust during approach at about 10 -20 FT and landed on its side with pilot apparently uninjured, still in it.
summary: A solo pilot flying a Part 103 ultralight experienced a sudden roll during the final 10–20 feet of landing on Runway 13 due to strong turbulence. The aircraft landed on its side, but the pilot was unharmed and local pilots assisted in securing the scene.

synopsis: A PA-18 instructor reported that he believes his student inadvertently locked the brakes on landing causing the aircraft to pitch over onto its back.
summary: A student pilot in the front seat instinctively applied brakes during rollout after landing, causing the aircraft to lock up and flip onto its back. The reporter attributes the accident to the student panicking despite having ample runway remaining.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZDV Instructor and Developmental report of a pilot who asks if they need to comply with the restrictions for speed on a STAR and the Developmental advises the pilot after a certain point they need to comply. The pilot later on gets written up for violating the speeds on the STAR.
summary: A Radar Developmental Controller and Aircraft X were involved during the northwest arrival into DEN. The pilot claimed to be cleared for fast speeds until RAMMS, contradicting the controller's instruction to comply with MOLTN2 arrival speeds, resulting in a filed pilot deviation.

synopsis: Center Controller reports of three helicopters that encountered icing while working them and two were declared emergencies to be able to descend.
summary: An air traffic controller managed three aircraft deviating for weather and icing, resulting in lost radar contact, multiple unauthorized descents, and emergency declarations. The controller attributed the safety issues to poor radio and radar coverage, inadequate pilot training, and similar call signs.

synopsis: A PHL area Approach Controller reported the controlled fixed altitude relationship of one IFR and two VFR aircraft with required 500 FT separation turned chaotic when the Air Carrier in the middle of the altitude sandwich responded to a TCAS RA. His suggested resolutions included giving flight crew discretion as to whether to respond to RA's in congested airspace.
summary: Air Carrier Z, a VFR helicopter, and a VFR aircraft were in PHL Bravo airspace when the carrier's TCAS RA caused an unnecessary climb toward the VFR aircraft. The controller restored separation, but the reporter attributed the dangerous situation to the TCAS sensitivity and the crew's response to the advisory.

synopsis: A B737-700 flight crew submitted a report echoing a number of others addressing the failure of ATC to provide the necessary information to conduct a descend via clearance when the necessary 'bottom altitude' for doing so exists only on the routing to the runway subsequent to the last 'common point' of the STAR itself.
summary: Pilots reported that Houston Center issued a Descend Via clearance for the KIDDZ 1 Arrival without a runway transition, leaving them unable to program the FMS correctly. The controller admitted lacking transition information, creating an unsafe situation where altitude constraints conflicted with the incomplete clearance.

synopsis: An air carrier First Officer advised of flaws in the programming of the GLEN ROSE STAR to DAL in his aircraft's FMC database.
summary: The pilot reported a potential FMS route error on XXXDAL01 during the GLEN ROSE Arrival to DFW, where changing runways could delete the ISABL 11,000 restriction. Although no violation occurred on this flight due to pilot awareness, the issue poses a risk of altitude restriction loss and separation violations.

synopsis: Dispatched with the right center tank fuel pump inoperative the flight crew of a B737 opted to divert for maintenance when the left pump failed enroute leaving them with inadequate reserves to continue to destination.
summary: The crew diverted to a nearby airport after both center fuel pumps failed while en route with an existing MEL on the right pump, leaving 5,000 LBS of unusable fuel. Maintenance reset the pumps, allowing the flight to continue to the destination with 4,000 LBS of usable fuel remaining.

synopsis: A319 Captain reports that the airport diagram does not reflect the current taxiway configuration at the south end of Runways 1L and 1R after recent construction.
summary: The pilot reported that taxi charts and iPad applications were outdated due to recent SFO construction, causing concern about Runway 1R length during taxi and cruise. Although the dispatcher did not reply to an ACARS query, the takeoff was normal, and the pilot requested an immediate NOTAM with updated charts.

synopsis: A319 Captain is informed of a fuel leak from the left wingtip vent during refueling. Passengers are deplaned and eventually the left wingtip tank Fuel High Level Shutoff System is MELed and the flight departs. Lost comm in Kingston FIR results in a weather deviation without clearance.
summary: The flight crew experienced a significant fuel leak from the left wingtip vent tank during pre-flight fueling, causing a two-hour delay and requiring an MEL deviation. Later, due to inoperative ground radio and ATC communication failures, the crew exercised PIC authority to deviate 40-50 miles east of track to avoid thunderstorms.

synopsis: An air carrier Captain reports lining up on Runway 11 at ISN to discover a Citation jet preparing to takeoff on Runway 29. The Citation crew had not made any CTAF calls and elects to taxi clear of the runway.
summary: The pilot reported a runway incursion at uncontrolled ISN where a Citation Jet entered Runway 29 while the crew was lining up on Runway 11. The incident occurred due to limited visibility from hold short bars, missed radio calls by the Citation, and the assumption that other pilots would follow standard CTAF procedures.

synopsis: CE750 Captain experiences a yaw damper failure while holding short for takeoff. An unsuccessful circuit breaker reset is attempted at the Maintenance Controllers suggestion, and the crew returns to the ramp for maintenance.
summary: Pilots holding for takeoff received a 'YD UPPER B FAIL' message and were pressured by a Maintenance Controller to reset the circuit breaker to continue. Although the checklist stated 'Do Not Dispatch,' the crew returned to the ramp to log the non-MEL'd malfunction after the message reappeared.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reports forgetting to enter RNGRR in the FMC after CRI to fly the Breezy Point transition of the Kennedy 1 Departure, proceeding direct to RBN after CRI. ATC issues a heading to correct, then direct RBN.
summary: The crew departed JFK Runway 31L on the Kennedy 1 departure but failed to manually load the RNGRR intersection in the FMC due to distraction. ATC detected the deviation from the Breezy Point climb transition and issued a heading correction to return the aircraft to the proper route.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reports copying and IFR clearance from SQL with complicated initial departure instructions, that is successfully read back with one omission that is corrected by SQL Ground. Eighteen minutes later after takeoff, the notes cannot be deciphered and a turn in the wrong direction is initiated then corrected by Norcal.
summary: A pilot flying a Cherokee on an IFR departure from San Carlos Runway 30 became confused by complex instructions and flew an incorrect heading, creating a traffic conflict with an aircraft on final approach. The pilot attributed the error to insufficient note-taking of the clearance and failing to clarify ambiguities before takeoff.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A corporate jet pilot holding short of TEB Runway 24 was cleared to line up and wait but held just beyond the hold short line after he saw an single engine aircraft on short final landing Runway 24.
summary: A corporate jet holding short of Runway 24 crossed the hold short line after being instructed to line up and wait, then stopped abruptly upon seeing a single-engine aircraft on short final. The single-engine aircraft landed safely in front of the jet, preventing a close call that would have occurred had the jet not stopped.

synopsis: An SQ2000 pilot conducting a very short EFIS airspeed test flight took off then immediately landed where, upon nose gear touchdown, it collapsed.
summary: The pilot and a crew member conducted a high-speed taxi and brief flight in an experimental aircraft during the 40-hour test period. Upon landing, the nose gear collapsed due to a component failure, resulting in limited airframe damage but no injuries.

synopsis: Falcon 10 Captain reports smoke coming from the pedestal near the FMS unit passing through FL220. The flight diverts to the nearest suitable airport and the passengers are evacuated through the main entryway.
summary: A pilot reported electrical smoke from the central pedestal near the FMS unit while climbing through FL220 with six passengers. The crew performed an emergency descent, diverted to the nearest airport for a slats-only landing, and evacuated all occupants safely.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: CIC reports of not being informed of a mission and the time period it took to receive the information.
summary: The CIC reported that a controller lacked information on an aircraft entering AW006, requiring a visit to TMU to obtain a mission depiction. The reporter concluded that orbit depictions and mission descriptions should be available before the aircraft arrives.

synopsis: ZAN Controller describes heading and altitude control difficulties detected while attempting to vector a PA24 pilot to the LDA X at JNU. Poor ATC communication capability north of JNU is also cited as an ongoing problem.
summary: An ATC controller vectored a disoriented PA24 pilot inbound to JNU who could not locate the LYNNS intersection or receive navigation signals. The controller issued headings and altitude changes to avoid Minimum Safe Altitudes while the pilot experienced spatial disorientation, eventually diverting for a visual approach to GST.

synopsis: ZNY Oceanic Developmental reports of conflict between two aircraft that he observed prior to a loss of separation. Computer malfunction in not showing a conflict led to the problem.
summary: An air traffic controller in Sector 21 identified a potential loss of separation between Aircraft X and Aircraft Y at FL350 near fix SLATN after the Ocean21 conflict probe failed to detect the conflict. The controller issued a descent clearance to Aircraft X to FL340 to mitigate the risk, noting that the system also failed to probe Aircraft X against Aircraft Z.

synopsis: SBN relieving Local Controller reports of an operation in which the FLM had vehicles approved to be on and or near the closed main runway. The FLM had removed all of the magnets which signified the vehicles call signs. The relieving Controller had to obtain information from each vehicle to find out its clearance. The relieving Controller was briefed about one aircraft and there were a total of eight.
summary: A relieving tower controller discovered a supervisor had omitted details about eight vehicles on a closed runway during the position brief. The supervisor had disregarded vehicle clearance magnets, leading the reliever to manually verify clearances and recommend restoring standard procedures for airport vehicle management.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: DEN Tower Controller reports of numerous runway incursions that have happened at the airport due to poor runway signs. This causes go-arounds if there is an aircraft on final.
summary: A pilot of Aircraft Y blew past a hold short line for Runway 17R approach while taxiing to 17L, causing a go-around on short final. The controller attributes this to confusing signage and markings at DEN Tower that mislead pilots on the correct hold short location.

synopsis: DEN Tower Controller reports of a problem with aircraft not holding short of an approach area to a runway causing aircraft on short final to go-around.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a pilot holding short of Runway 17R approach at Denver International Airport crossed the line despite correct readback, forcing a go-around on short final. The controller attributed this recurring issue to confusing signage with multiple hold-short lines on taxiways L and M, causing pilot deviation.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ARR Tower Controller reports of a FLM that is having aircraft line up and wait [LUAW] while working Local Control combined. This is against FAA policy.
summary: A Flight Line Manager (FLM) improperly signed onto both Local Control and CIC while using LUAW procedures, violating regulations requiring the position to stand alone. Low staffing left only a trainee present, prompting refresher training to prevent the acceptance of this unsafe practice.

synopsis: GEG Approach Controller describes poor altitude control and incorrect heading read back of a PA46 pilot being vectored to the ILS 22R at SFF.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored a PA46 for an ILS approach to SFF, but the pilot repeatedly misread headings and altitudes, causing deviations and a low altitude alert near final. The controller attributed the errors to pilot confusion or disorientation, advised Tower to monitor the flight, and later learned the pilot incorrectly flew a departure with another controller.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: OMA Local Controller reports of a student pilot landing and then exiting the runway prior to an intersection, because the pilot used too much left rudder. The Controller then let the aircraft taxi to the FBO at his own discretion.
summary: A student pilot on a solo VFR touch-and-go at OMA veered off Runway 14R into grass and struck a light due to mistaken full left rudder input. The pilot subsequently taxied across closed runways and taxiways to the ramp, sustaining minor damage to the left strut.

synopsis: ZLC Controller reports of a previous Controller allowing Flight Following of an aircraft that is below radar and radio coverage.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a VFR aircraft was given Flight Following below radar and radio coverage without altitude information. The controller lost all contact and radar contact, creating a dangerous situation where the pilot likely believed radar services were being provided.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Center Controller reports of an aircraft that has engine trouble, changes its destination and then lands at a Fire TFR closed airport safely.
summary: An air traffic controller assisted Aircraft X, which experienced engine trouble while descending near a Fire TFR, by vectoring it toward ZZZ. After discovering ZZZ was closed for firefighting, the pilot declared an emergency and landed safely with ground coordination arranged by the controller's supervisor.

synopsis: ZLC Controller reports of an altitude change that he is not able to modify on the radar screen because another ATC Center has control of the aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a descent clearance to Aircraft X at FL350 but failed to hand off the aircraft to ZLA33 due to ZLA32's refusal to update data blocks. The reporter attributes this unsafe coordination failure to ZLA's inefficient procedures and calls for a directive clarifying hand-off responsibilities.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: BFI Ground Controller reports of an aircraft taxiing across a runway that the aircraft was never cleared to cross. The Ground Controller looked for the aircraft, didn't see it, and issued instructions.
summary: A Ground Control controller inadvertently allowed Aircraft X to cross Runway 13L while another aircraft was on short final, causing a go-around. The controller failed to verify the aircraft's position or issue a hold-short clearance, resulting in an unauthorized runway incursion.

synopsis: An A320 Captain executed an IMC go-around in response to an EGPWS TERRAIN warning after he developed a high sink rate to capture the ILS glideslope from above.
summary: The flight crew descended to recapture the glide slope but experienced a high sink rate triggering a terrain warning. They executed a go-around and received vectors for an alternate approach to land.

synopsis: A B737 First Officer reported taking evasive action to a TCAS TRAFFIC advisory from a departing jet at 7,000 FT near SMO on the LAX SADDE STAR.
summary: During the SADDE arrival, the crew received a TCAS RA while passing a de-conflicted RJ ahead. The pilot manually pitched up in response to the brief climb command before the advisory cleared, allowing the aircraft to resume descent to 7,000 feet.

synopsis: A B737 pilot refused taxi clearance at CLE between Spots 2 and 5 because the Airport diagram restricts aircraft with wingspans 118 FT and greater from the Inner J Taxiway between the two spots.
summary: A pilot reported that Ramp Tower at CLE repeatedly issued prohibited taxi clearances for a Boeing 737 from Spot 2 to Spot 5 along Inner J Taxiway, violating the 10-9 restriction for aircraft with 118-foot wingspans. The pilot refused the clearance and took an alternate route, noting that other aircraft illegally accepted these instructions.

synopsis: Two flights in the same vicinity with the same SelCal id were confusing to ATC.
summary: A pilot reported that two aircraft in the same area shared the same SelCal ID, causing confusion with Air Traffic Control. The narrative does not specify the aircraft type, flight phase, or the outcome of the incident.

synopsis: A First Officer reports about the lack of any 'guidance' or 'reference notes' in their QRH or MEL Manual procedures informing flight crews, Maintenance, and Dispatch that a special procedure exists in their Aircraft Operations Manual (AOM) for Dual (Left-Right) Yaw Damper Inop lights illuminating after engine starts on certain B757s.
summary: Flight crew of a Boeing 757 experienced illuminated yaw damper inoperative lights after engine start. Although specific AOM procedures allowed departure, maintenance control insisted on a logbook write-up, forcing the crew to return to the gate due to a communication breakdown regarding the new procedure.

synopsis: An A319 seat belt sign OFF and ON switch positions are reversed between Airbus aircraft. The seat belt sign was ON during cruise and OFF for landing.
summary: Pilots and cabin crew on an aircraft with reversed seat belt switches failed to notice the sign was off during descent and landing due to the non-standard configuration and degraded cross-checks. An FAA Inspector identified the error upon landing, attributing the oversight to the reversed switch positions and potential fatigue after a ten-hour duty day.

synopsis: A Q400 VNAV and LNAV coupling disengaged on an RNAV approach inside the IF and while troubleshooting, the Captain lost situational awareness and descended more than one dot below the glidepath and fortunately became VMC for landing.
summary: During an RNAV approach, the pilot flying lost VNAV and LNAV coupling and descended below the glidepath due to distraction and degraded alertness from sleep deprivation. The pilot not flying failed to monitor or call deviations, but the crew received a visual approach clearance and landed safely.

synopsis: An EMB-145 Flight Attendant notified the flight crew at 300 FT after takeoff about smoke apparently from a light so ATC was advised, the QRH completed and the flight returned to the departure airport. The Flight Attendant later said the smoke was present during taxi but she was afraid to interfere with pilot pre-takeoff duties.
summary: During initial climb at 300 feet, a flight attendant reported smoke near row seven from photo-luminescent lights, prompting the flight crew to return to the departure airport. The aircraft landed safely overweight after the smoke ceased, though the crew noted the smoke was actually observed during taxi and takeoff but not reported until after liftoff.

synopsis: A B737-NG center tank fuel quantity totalizer was inoperative which required a special MEL procedure completion before the FMC PERF-INIT weight was correct. Maintenance failed to fully comply with complex procedure so the required fuel was 2,400 LBS low.
summary: Pilots and maintenance personnel encountered a fuel discrepancy on an aircraft with a center tank fuel indicating system MEL, where incorrect ME-10 form data led to a 350-gallon under-fuel. The crew arrived with low reserves, prompting station maintenance to disable the totalizer and implement a revised fueling procedure to ensure accurate loads for subsequent flights.

synopsis: The Captain of an A320 expressed concern about the latest in a string of apparent miscommunications between DEN Center and DEN TRACON with respect to landing direction and the inappropriate STAR by which they had been cleared to descend by Center which then came as a big surprise to TRACON.
summary: The flight crew descended via the BOSSS RNAV STAR to DEN but was incorrectly told by Approach they were too low at QUAIL 17,000 FT. The controller later admitted the STAR was inconsistent with north landings due to poor coordination with Center, though the crew completed a safe visual approach to Runway 35L.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew reports being questioned by an FAA Inspector after gate arrival about an opaque area on the right side window, which the Captain does not think is significant and makes no logbook entry. The inspector makes no comment but the Captain contacts maintenance later, and the aircraft is taken out of service at a down line station.
summary: A pilot reported a side window delamination noticed by an FAA inspector after shutdown, which the pilot initially deemed within tolerances. Maintenance Control later confirmed the defect was out of limits, resulting in the aircraft being ferried back to base for window replacement.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain describes an altitude deviation caused by a misunderstood arrival clearance. The clearance was via the TELLR arrival and to maintain 280 KTS or greater and descend and maintain FL270. This is interpreted by the First Officer as a descend via clearance.
summary: The Captain and First Officer descended to FL190 during the TELLR arrival into Denver, mistakenly believing they had a "descend via" clearance. ATC later confirmed no such clearance was issued, attributing the error to crew distraction and failure to verify the altitude selection.

synopsis: Airbus Captain is informed by his First Officer of a ramp worker down next to the tug with other workers gathering around. The Captain uses his authority to get a Flight Attendant to the ramp with an AED then an EMT trained passenger.
summary: The Captain and a Flight Attendant assisted an unconscious ramp worker during preflight boarding after the Purser initially refused to allow a passenger EMT or crew to leave the aircraft. The Captain directed the Flight Attendant to use the AED and oxygen, later escorting the EMT to the scene until paramedics arrived, prioritizing life-saving care over full cabin crew staffing.

synopsis: A flight crew misunderstood a clearance to climb via an RNAV SID and maintain 15,000 FT. The clearance is interpreted to mean climb unrestricted to 15,000 FT which is not correct.
summary: A pilot flying an IOE leg misinterpreted a "climb via... except maintain 15,000" clearance, deleting an intermediate altitude restriction and climbing to 7,000 feet instead of maintaining 6,000. The deviation resulted from confusing similar phraseology regarding altitude restrictions, leading to a controller-reported pilot deviation.

synopsis: B777 First Officer laments the Captain's decision to use a nonstandard break schedule on a 12 hour flight resulting in insufficient rest for the two relief pilots.
summary: The Captain implemented an unjustified 4-6-2 break schedule for himself and a relief pilot, causing the relief pilot to fall asleep in the seat during the six-hour duty period. The Captain dismissed fatigue concerns, prioritizing his ego over safety and leaving half the crew asleep while operating.

synopsis: B767 First Officer reported hearing a couple of loud popping noises shortly after rotation. After flap retraction there was an audible noise in the cabin accompanied by vibration and the stall buffet feathers on the First Officer's ADI remained displayed despite the flaps showing fully retracted. When the flaps are extended the vibration dissipates and the crew elects to dump fuel and return to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced loud popping noises, cabin vibration, and persistent stall buffet warnings during flap retraction shortly after rotation. They declared an emergency, dumped fuel, and returned for a smooth overweight landing after maintenance could not resolve the issue.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew experiences a loss of cabin pressure passing FL240 during climb and declares an emergency. Descent to 10,000 FT does not silence the cabin altitude warning and the descent is continued to 8,000 FT. The flight continues to destination where post flight inspection reveals a galley service door seal has failed.
summary: During climb to FL320, the flight crew experienced rapid depressurization caused by a blown galley service door seal. After declaring an emergency, they descended to 8,000 feet, stabilized cabin altitude, and landed safely with no injuries.

synopsis: Pilot reports of a slam dunk approach into LAX, closer than the normal slam dunk approach he is used to getting at this airport.
summary: The pilot reported an unstable approach to LAX runway 24R caused by Approach Control vectoring the aircraft inside the final approach fix, resulting in a high and fast descent. The pilot noted that aggressive, unnecessary vectors at LAX frequently create unstable approaches requiring creative recovery, though a go-around was not executed in this instance.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reports being high and fast after a downwind entry to a visual approach. With the approach unstabilized and the traffic ahead not clearing the runway, ATC issues a go-around that the crew was about to announce on their own.
summary: The crew arrived at SMF high on downwind, accepted a clearance for Runway 16R, and executed a go-around due to an unstable approach and a preceding aircraft not clearing the runway. The pilot not flying attributed the instability to delayed descent and noted intercom limitations during radio communication.

synopsis: Business jet Captain laments new SOP's that have been implemented without any formal training and only a written guide describing how the new procedures should be accomplished.
summary: A pilot reported that untrained crews implementing new SOPs became distracted, causing uncertainty about takeoff clearances and radio frequency errors due to awkward equipment configuration. The reporter attributed these safety hazards to insufficient training, conflicting interpretations, and poorly conceived procedural changes.

synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported rejecting a takeoff on KSEA Runway 16L when Tower was heard clearing another aircraft to cross the same runway. Tower did not advise that the crossing aircraft was behind the aircraft taking off.
summary: A pilot reported two rejected takeoffs on Runway 16L at SEA after hearing ATC clear another aircraft to cross the runway while the pilot was starting the takeoff roll. The pilot attributed the confusion to the clearance omitting "on Taxiway C" and the high workload during takeoff, warning that this practice desensitizes crews to potential runway incursions.

synopsis: B737-900 flight crew reported they were unable to make a charted crossing restriction on the LAS SHEAD8 RNAV departure when they were distracted by wake vortex encounter from the preceding B737.
summary: The flight crew departed behind a B737 on the SHEAD 8 RNAV departure and deviated from the path to avoid wake turbulence. This distraction caused a late climb from 7,000 feet due to an incorrect MCP altitude setting, resulting in a missed restriction at MDDOG.

synopsis: A B737 Captain reported extreme fatigue during the second duty period in twenty-four hours beginning with an AM transcontinental flight, attempting mid PM rest and finally flying an all night period.
summary: A pilot and First Officer experienced extreme fatigue and nodding off during a red-eye flight following a double-duty period and insufficient rest. The pilot attributed the incident to the airline's scheduling practices and expressed concern that this could lead to an accident.

synopsis: B757 flight crew describes an approach into MROC with thunderstorms and with a last minute change from the ILS 07 to the VOR 07 circle to land Runway 25. A mistake is made modifying the VOR approach in the FMC and the approach is flown in raw data until an EGPWS Terrain caution is announced approaching MONTE at 4,900 FT. The escape maneuver is flown with a turn to the north then to the west as an EGPWS Terrain warning sounds. The crew climbs to 18,000 FT and diverts.
summary: The pilot flying and captain encountered heavy thunderstorms while executing a VOR 07 circle-to-land approach at San Jose. An incorrect FMC setup and weather avoidance led to EGPWS terrain warnings, forcing an escape maneuver, climb to 18,000 feet, and diversion.

synopsis: A Captain reports experiencing uncommanded yawing oscillations and rudder pedal movement in a CRJ-200 aircraft during climb to final cruise altitude. When the CRJ entered a 'Dutch Roll', the pilot disconnected the autopilot and flight director to correct the aircraft attitude. Flight diverted. During descent, oscillations continued to be felt in pedals with yaw in both directions.
summary: A CRJ-200 crew experienced uncommanded yawing and Dutch Roll while climbing to FL280, likely due to rudder pedal oscillations. The Captain manually controlled the aircraft, followed the QRH emergency procedure, and diverted for a safe landing.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant reports being so rushed during preflight that she forgets to brief the overwing exit row passengers prior to takeoff.
summary: A flight attendant reported failing to brief exit row passengers before takeoff due to being rushed by operations agents who began boarding immediately upon crew arrival. The reporter attributed this safety lapse to operational pressure preventing the completion of required pre-boarding duties and security checks.

synopsis: Four B757-200 flight attendants report illness during and after a flight on which a dirty socks odor was detected and reported to Captain. The flight continued and no medical attention was requested at the destination.
summary: During climbout, flight attendants on an aircraft reported a "stinky feet" odor and symptoms like nausea and dizziness caused by a seal leak introducing toxic fumes into the aft cabin. The Captain attempted to recycle air and rotate crew but allegedly failed to report the illnesses or divert, leaving the odor unresolved until landing.

synopsis: Two Aircraft Maintenance Technicians (AMTs) report about an MEL disconnect procedure they had performed on the right engine, right outboard anti-ice valve on an MD-83 aircraft. The valve was later found to be connected and not in compliance with the MEL dispatch requirements they had signed for. Technician notes that undocumented maintenance had occurred.
summary: Maintenance personnel placarded an inoperative right engine anti-ice valve on an MD-83 per MEL after troubleshooting an inbound discrepancy. The aircraft flew six days without fault until Maintenance Control found it out of compliance due to undocumented maintenance and a missing electrical jumper.

synopsis: Pilot reports the left brake completely locked on his Van's RV-8 aircraft during landing rollout, followed by the right brake locking when he applied right rudder and brakes. The aircraft nosed over and came to rest on the spinner. Parking Brake Valve had actuated, caused by the sheath of the Parking Brake Actuator cable slipping in a clamp, allowing the valve to actuate on its own.
summary: The pilot of an RV-8 experienced a nose-over on Runway XX at ZZZ airport after both brakes locked due to a slipping parking brake cable sheath. The incident destroyed the propeller and spinner, damaged wheel pants, and caused minor structural deformation to the left gear tower.

synopsis: A C172 pilot took evasive action at 5,500 FT to avoid a small metallic object.
