summary: A pilot practicing maneuvers south of Lafayette, Indiana, at 5,500 feet MSL spotted a basketball-sized metal object approaching the nose. The pilot executed an immediate turn to avoid collision and returned to Lafayette.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier crew cleared from SWB to MUURY had erroneously entered MURRY in the FMS during preflight, so after passing SWB the aircraft turned northeast toward MURRY verses southeast. The distance from SWB to MUURY is 133 NM, to MURRY is 482 NM. The MUURY to MURRY distance is 381 NM northeast. Two other MURRY waypoints exist, one in Australia, another in the Hong Kong FIR.
summary: During cruise at FL370, the crew deviated from the MUURY route due to a pilot FMS waypoint misspelling (MURRY) coupled to the autopilot. Corrective action involved disconnecting the autopilot, resulting in a 100-foot altitude loss and an ATC query before the aircraft returned to the planned route.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A single engine pilot performing touch and go landings at PAE lost control during takeoff after a Boeing heavy jet exited Runway 16R and parked perpendicular to the runway with power apparently above idle.
summary: A pilot executing a touch-and-go on ILS 16R experienced significant buffeting and temporary loss of control immediately after takeoff due to jet blast from a large Boeing jet conducting a taxi test on an adjacent taxiway. The pilot recovered the aircraft and noted that no jet blast warning was issued by the tower despite the large aircraft's proximity to the runway.

synopsis: A J3 Cub lost power at about 800 FT just off the coast, so the pilot attempted a beach landing. Upon touchdown power was restored, (happened twice) so he maneuver vigorously to clear a fuel line, then flew to nearby airport where water and debris were discovered in the fuel tank.
summary: A pilot experienced intermittent engine power loss during a coastal transit, attributed to a fuel strainer partially plugged with water, trash, and flaky debris. After two precautionary beach landings and in-flight power fluctuations, the aircraft landed safely at a nearby airport where the contaminated fuel system was cleaned.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot at 5R4 reported near misses with two aircraft who initially entered the very busy pattern without employing the recommended CTAF communications protocol.
summary: The pilot reported two near misses at 5R4 while on downwind, caused by a straight-tail aircraft with vision problems that failed to make radio calls and an experimental aircraft passing within 300 feet. The pilot executed an evasive nose-down maneuver to avoid collision, while other traffic performed go-arounds to maintain separation.

synopsis: The Captain of a Super King Air departing SNA, taxiing northbound on C and just short of J, was buzzed by a single engine Cessna taking off from Runway 19L making a premature left turn out passing just feet above the King Air.
summary: A pilot taxiing on Taxiway Charlie at SNA reported a near-miss with a departing Cessna from Runway 19L that passed 10 feet overhead after turning before the runway end. The reporter attributed the loss of separation to the Cessna pilot's early turn and criticized ATC for failing to intervene or enforce proper departure procedures.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) with Inspection Authority (I/A) reports about a ground loop incident involving a Stinson L-5 aircraft with a modified Tailwheel Assembly.
summary: During a trainee's three-point landing in a Stinson L-5C, tailwheel compression springs reached full travel and broke, causing a ground loop and right wing damage. The incident occurred because the firm landing exceeded the spring's limited travel, resulting in a loss of tailwheel steering and rudder control.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Recip Eng
synopsis: ALB Controller reports an aircraft was cleared for takeoff on a closed runway.
summary: A Tower controller cleared an aircraft for takeoff from a closed runway due to a missed briefing detail and lack of physical runway closure markings. The incident was attributed to severe understaffing, extended duty hours, and the absence of X's on the closed runway despite ATIS advisories.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: AUS Tower CIC reports of an ongoing issue related to pilots calling for pushback clearance in a non-movement area. Signs at each gate advise pilots to call ground prior to pushback.
summary: A Tower Controller reported that a Ground Control Trainer instructed a trainee to authorize pushbacks in a non-movement area obscured by the terminal, violating the LOA and AFD. The controller stated this willful disregard of rules creates a liability risk for controllers and the FAA if an aircraft strikes an obstacle.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ZMP Center FLM reports a pilot lands at an airport then advises the Controller the airport is closed. No NOTAMS are in effect at the time for the runway closure.
summary: A pilot landed at 14Y and reported the runway was closed despite receiving NOTAMS. The Airport Manager later issued a vague NOTAM stating a runway was closed without specifying the number or section, which the pilot attributed to inadequate training of city workers managing the airport.

synopsis: A B737-300 crew used the Landing Gear Manual Solenoid Release to raise a non-responsive landing gear and while completing the QRH determined that was an unauthorized procedure. After landing, Maintenance discovered a tripped landing gear circuit breaker caused the problem.
summary: During departure in an older aircraft, pilots used the manual solenoid release to raise the gear after the handle failed due to a tripped circuit breaker, which they later learned violated QRH procedures. Maintenance identified the tripped breaker, likely caused by rapid seatbelt retraction, and the flight landed uneventfully.

synopsis: When the landing gear failed to retract and the handle refused to pass through the 'off' detent after takeoff the flight crew of a B737 pulled the override trigger and retracted the gear, then proceeded to conduct their departure clearance from a major airport. When then conducting the QRH procedure they learned their initial actions were contrary to the procedure.
summary: The crew experienced a landing gear handle jam during climb due to a tripped solenoid circuit breaker caused by the First Officer's seatbelt. They used the override to retract the gear, continued to the destination, and landed normally after maintenance confirmed the fault.

synopsis: An Airbus A320 series flight crew flying the ILS DME Runway 07 at MZBZ found the GFMS programmed procedure turn returned them inbound on the localizer above the glideslope. Judicious energy management allowed them to capture the glideslope from above prior to the FAF.
summary: The pilot reported that while flying the ILS DME 07 approach, the NAV procedure turn only extended to 7 DME, leaving the aircraft 400 feet high at 2,500 feet. The pilot attributed this to incorrect approach coding and recommended using the ILS DME VOR 07 until the procedure is recoded to 8 DME.

synopsis: Pilot reports of issue where DME that is OTS is still being used for clearances he is receiving out of IND airport.
summary: The pilot reported that Indianapolis ATC issued MAREO2 departure clearances for Runway 23L despite the required IFVJ DME being NOTAMed out of service. The pilot noted that controllers often issue headings predicated on inoperative equipment or request early turns, creating confusion regarding departure compliance.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reports a shattered Captain's side front windshield at FL260 and starts descending. ATC is advised and an emergency is declared before diverting to a suitable airport.
summary: Pilots at FL260 experienced a shattered Captain's side windshield with no obvious cause, prompting an immediate descent to FL100 before receiving clearance. They later declared an emergency to mitigate risks of pressure loss and visibility restrictions while maintaining communication with ATC.

synopsis: EMB-170 First Officer describes an FMS anomaly during approach to LAX that will not allow the approach to be changed from Runway 25L to Runway 24R as assigned by ATC. Runway 24R is entered twice and each time reverts back to 25L. A hand flown approach to Runway 24R is accomplished.
summary: During the approach to LAX, the flight crew experienced an FMS malfunction that repeatedly reverted the selected runway from 24R to 25L despite manual corrections. The pilots manually flew the aircraft using raw data to align with Runway 24R after the automation failed to maintain the correct approach setup.

synopsis: While donning his oxygen mask in preparation for First Officer's break, a B737-800 Captain's oxygen mask inflatable harness burst. An observer's mask replaced the Captain's for the flight's duration.
summary: During cruise at FL360, the Captain's oxygen mask harness burst while being donned. The Captain exercised emergency authority to replace the failed unit with the First Observer's spare mask, verified its operation, and resumed normal flight.

synopsis: A medical helicopter flight to transfer a patient was diverted due to weather. The patient was transferred to a ground ambulance.
summary: The pilot and med crew encountered sudden showers and reduced visibility during a patient transport flight, forcing a return to a nearby hospital for patient transfer. The pilot attributed the event to undetected weather in hilly terrain and noted limitations of the aircraft's older GPS system.

synopsis: A C208 pilot reported burning eyes, nose and throat with the taste of TKS fluid about 20 minutes into the 80 minute flight. The symptoms disappeared about 20-30 minutes after landing.
summary: The pilot reported burning sensations in the eyes, nose, throat, and lips, along with tasting TKS fluid, approximately 20 minutes into the flight. The pilot landed after 1 hour and 20 minutes, and symptoms resolved within 20 to 30 minutes post-flight.

synopsis: Air carrier pilot flying the LDA X Runway 8 at JNU reports descending below the 5,600 foot MEA on the SSR 007 degree radial after setting 5,600 in the MCP and initiating a vertical speed descent. No chime was heard and the deviation was not noted until 4,900 feet and corrected.
summary: During a second LDA Z approach to Juneau, the crew descended below the assigned 5,600 feet because the altitude alerter failed to chime while in vertical speed mode. The pilots recovered the aircraft to 5,600 feet after noticing the deviation at 4,900 feet, remaining in visual meteorological conditions throughout the event.

synopsis: An A320 pilot reported the aircraft's strobe light system is poorly designed and located and constitutes a safety hazard by compromising flight crew vision.
summary: The pilot reported that on an Airbus, cockpit strobes flash internally at night, blinding the crew during traffic scans and destroying night vision. This forces the pilot to turn off the lights, reducing aircraft visibility and causing potential vertigo, which the pilot attributes to Airbus's refusal to fix the design.

synopsis: When, after V1, debris from a failed main gear tire was ingested by the left engine on the takeoff roll a significant power loss and compressor stalling resulted. The engine was shut down in flight and the aircraft returned to the departure airport.
summary: The pilot reported left engine vibration, power loss, and compressor stalls after V1 at ZZZ, leading to an emergency shutdown and landing. Post-landing, a flight attendant reported a medical emergency in the aft cabin, requiring paramedics to treat and remove the passenger before disembarkation.

synopsis: MD-82 Captain reported wake vortex encounter at FL310 five miles in trail of an A319 resulting in a 25 degree roll in both directions. Reporter was surprised at the intensity of the encounter given the relatively small aircraft he was following.
summary: A pilot reported encountering wake turbulence from an Airbus A319 while cruising at FL310, causing a 25-degree roll despite having seven miles of separation. The crew disconnected the autopilot to recover and descended to FL250, noting the unexpected severity of the wake from the smaller aircraft.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A fuel spill near a parked MD-82 admitted fuel fumes into the cabin which made a Flight Attendant nauseas but she worked the flight because she could not afford the pay loss or a sick day on her record.
summary: A cabin crew member reported nausea and dizziness from a jet fuel spill odor in the cabin while the aircraft was at the gate and during pushback. The Captain advised removal from the trip, but the crew member remained due to financial concerns and sick call implications, enduring 45 minutes of exposure while the air conditioning circulated fumes.

synopsis: M20 pilot experiences an engine failure at 1,500 AGL after takeoff. The engine cannot be restarted and landing in a field is deemed the best option which is accomplished without damage.
summary: The pilot and co-pilot experienced a sudden engine failure at 1,500 feet AGL after takeoff, forcing an emergency landing in an alfalfa field. A mechanic later found a missing screw in the fuel injection system, though the exact cause of the failure remains unknown.

synopsis: A C90 skydiving jump pilot at 14,500 feet attempted to avoid dropping his jumpers on a cloud at about 6,000 feet but was told after landing the divers had penetrated the cloud.
summary: The pilot and skydivers encountered a cloud over the airport during a jump run climb. Five jumpers penetrated the cloud despite the pilot's warning and subsequent course adjustment, leading to a ground announcement enforcing cloud clearance requirements.

synopsis: When the forecast weather proved invalid, the pilot of a C-172 found himself and his passenger intermittently VFR in IMC and/or on top. The dilemma was further compromised by the failure of all VHF communications, both VORs and--a potentially valuable asset--his tablet computer dead due to a dead battery. Clever thinking and the eventual ability of his passenger's smart phone to display satellite map images permitted him to navigate and arrive safely at his destination.
summary: A pilot and passenger encountered deteriorating weather and IMC conditions during a VFR return flight, resulting in dual NAV and radio failures. The pilot navigated using DME and visual references to execute a descent and land safely at the departure airport after becoming disoriented.

aircraft: Cessna Single Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: This light aircraft pilot reported that because of terrain on the downwind side of the left hand traffic pattern it is difficult to acquire and maintain visual contact with other aircraft in the traffic pattern. It is additionally stated that the hills possibly block or hinder radio transmissions.
summary: A pilot on a visual approach to a left-hand pattern failed to see or hear another aircraft due to hills blocking line of sight and radio propagation. The pilot in the pattern extended their downwind leg to maintain separation, and the reporter recommends a right-hand pattern to improve safety.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot experiences a power loss during initial climb and elects to land in a parking lot. The engine anomaly appears to clear up during descent but the approach is continued to landing as a precaution. Visual inspection on the ground reveals no anomalies and the helicopter is flown back to base.
summary: During a training flight's top of climb, a helicopter pilot experienced engine roughness and vibration caused by a stuck valve. The crew executed a precautionary landing in a mall parking lot, inspected the engine, and returned to base uneventfully after the issue cleared.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot at CTAF MLE taking Runway 12 for takeoff with 3 knots of wind exited the runway after another pilot reported landing Runway 30 when the preferred Runway with wind less than 5 knots is 12.
summary: The pilot at MLE lined up on Runway 12 for departure but heard an experimental aircraft rolling out on Runway 30. The pilot exited Runway 12 to allow the other aircraft to clear, then taxied to Runway 30 to depart.

synopsis: ZAB Controller describes a shift where weather is causing aircraft to deviate and that the controllers are trying to recall restricted airspace to allow flights better deviations.
summary: Air traffic controllers and Aircraft X faced extreme weather while military restricted areas R5103B/C remained active below FL500. The pilot declared an emergency to deviate left into the restricted airspace after standard routings were insufficient, prompting controllers to coordinate with White Sands Missile Range for clearance.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: SBN Controller reports of an audio jack that is out of service. Maintenance works on the jack and while doing so a loud squeal emits from the frequency into the Controller's ear.
summary: An air traffic controller in the South High sector experienced a deafening squelch tone through their headset and TRACON speakers while a technician tested a faulty headphone jack on an adjacent scope. The technician admitted she did not know the frequency was keyed up, causing hearing damage and operational disruption.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reports that his aircraft failed to turn at DOMNO on the DRLLR 2 to IAH. The Chief Pilot informs the Captain that there is a database error that creates a duplicate waypoint when a runway change is initiated.
summary: Pilots flying a DRLLR arrival into IAH deviated from course after an FMS runway change created a duplicate waypoint due to a known database error. The crew failed to detect the duplicate during verification, resulting in a loss of lateral navigation that required an immediate rejoin of the arrival.

synopsis: CRJ-700 Captain is informed of a fuel spill during fueling at the gate with fuel coming out of the wing tip vent. The problem is traced to the fuel high level sensor which is MEL'd. The Captain has many questions about how the system works and whether the MEL is adequate to prevent overflow in flight.
summary: During preflight fueling, a spill occurred while the APU was running, likely caused by a faulty high-level sensor and manual mode limitations. The crew and ARFF contained the spill, and maintenance applied an MEL after verifying engine operation, though the reporter noted gaps in procedures and MEL clarity.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reports forgetting to turn on the pitot heat switches after engine start and responding without checking at the checklist prompt. As takeoff thrust is set a Master Caution Light illuminates due to the omission, and the takeoff is rejected.
summary: The Captain missed turning on Pitot Probe Heat switches during the After Start checklist while monitoring push back, causing a low-speed rejected takeoff. The reporter attributed the error to distraction by ground crew, poor workload distribution, and lack of cross-verification.

synopsis: An air carrier took evasive action from a TCAS RA which transited perpendicular across the TCAS screen. The crew believed a phantom target was the source because no clear of conflict was issued.
summary: During an ILS approach to IAD, the crew executed a TCAS RA climb from 2,500 to 3,000 feet due to a suspected phantom target that disappeared without a clear of conflict. After leveling briefly, they were cleared to 2,000 feet and completed the approach and landing without incident.

synopsis: Two back to back flight crews reported a spoiler deferral on their common MD-82 had been managed incorrectly and all spoiler functions were inoperative as opposed to only auto-spoilers as advised in the AML.
summary: The flight crew operated an aircraft with a deferred auto-spoiler MEL item that was improperly performed by maintenance. During descent and landing, the flight spoilers failed to deploy as air-brakes because the handle was locked out, a condition undetectable until needed.

synopsis: A300 flight crew describes being vectored for the ILS 22L at EWR and kept high and fast, resulting in an unstabilized approach. The Captain elects to continue the approach rather than go-around due to traffic departing on the right runway.
summary: The flight crew vectored for ILS 22L at EWR accepted a clearance leaving them high and fast, resulting in an unstabilized approach 15 knots above Vappr at 500 feet. They elected to land rather than go around due to busy airspace, attributing the event to accepting restrictive altitude and speed instructions too close to the airport.

synopsis: B737 Flight Attendant reports helping the CSA close the main cabin door before the rest of the cabin crew has announced their readiness for door closure. The door is left ajar and not armed until the ready announcement is made.
summary: A D Flight Attendant nearly closed the L1 door before the aft cabin was secure due to pressure for on-time departure and miscommunication with a CSA agent. The door was left ajar until the A Flight Attendant confirmed the cabin was ready, highlighting that safety must take priority over schedule.

synopsis: A Line Maintenance Supervisor discovers the actuating plunger on the Pneumatic Assembly for Door-2 Right Emergency Assist on an ERJ-170 aircraft was still locked-out from previous Maintenance servicing. The lock-out condition prevented door assist during door slide activation. Supervisor recommends any servicing of Door Assist include a Required Inspection Item (RII) prior to aircraft release.
summary: A Maintenance Supervisor discovered at the gate that the Door 2-Right emergency assist plunger was left locked out after servicing, preventing proper slide activation. The technician was unaware the lockout needed resetting to 'Normal', prompting a recommendation to make this a Required Inspection Item.

synopsis: The pilot of a CE650XL failed to note that Runway 16L at his destination was NOTAM'd closed. When advised on short final he opted to land on the parallel runway which he later realized was shorter than the Part 135 required length which was applicable to his operation.
summary: The pilot failed to see a NOTAM regarding the closure of runway 16L at HEF until 10 miles out, forcing a switch to 16R. Although the landing was safe, the FAR 135 required distance exceeded the runway length due to rushed preflight planning and late ATC notification.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports an altitude deviation departing ATL on the THRSR 7 due to not noticing the 10,000 foot limit in the routing box. The First Officer was using NOS plates which he was not familiar with.
summary: During a post-maintenance check flight from Atlanta, the crew incorrectly entered 14,000 feet into the FMS while missing a 10,000-foot restriction on the NOS departure plate. This pilot deviation caused a potential conflict with traffic, prompting ATC to order a descent and report the incident.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Following a normal three point landing the pilot of a Waco biplane was unable to arrest a ground loop, perhaps the result of some failure of the right landing gear structure, and significant damage to the gear was the result.
summary: The pilot of a Waco biplane experienced a right wing drop and left drift during rollout that full rudder and brake could not stop. The aircraft ground looped after the wheel rim dug into the asphalt, resulting in a collapsed right shock strut and folded support strut.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot and controllers report of a scenario while running tripps to a set of runways, an aircraft is bounced off curse by winds and because of close proximity to other traffic is pulled out and resequenced. Controllers advise that tripps should not be run in bad weather just for this reason.
summary: A pilot flying Aircraft X on a PRM approach to ATL encountered wind shear and turbulence, triggering CWS mode and a right turn into the NTZ. The controller instructed an immediate climb to 4,000 feet to avoid a conflict with Aircraft Y, attributing the incident to severe weather and triple arrivals.

synopsis: ZAB FLM reports of radio problems in various sectors that appears to be going on daily.
summary: An INW RCAG site glitch caused constant static on R67 receivers while the controller managed 10-13 aircraft, complicating instruction verification. The recurring issue, occurring daily on multiple frequencies, required temporary frequency shifts and site resets, prompting a request for immediate BUEC repairs and a full site inspection.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: EWR Controller reports of a situation where he forgets about an aircraft that is departing while he tells a landing aircraft to cross the departures runway while another aircraft is on final. Controller aborts the departure, sends the arrival around, because crossing traffic has passed the hold short bars.
summary: An air traffic controller missed Aircraft Z's takeoff on Runway 22R due to a visual scan obstruction, causing a stop-short and go-around. A pilot on Runway 22L crossed 22R after a conflicting clearance change, stopping just clear of the runway while other aircraft aborted or went around.

synopsis: B737-300 First Officer experiences an MCP failure at FL350, losing both autopilots, the flight directors and the altitude alerting system and descends out of RVSM airspace. The first reset attempt by the Captain is not successful but the second attempt by the First Officer is. Dispatch is contacted and replies with diversion instructions as the MCP fails again. The MCP is reset again and functions to landing.
summary: During cruise at FL350, the crew experienced a Mode Control Panel (MCP) lockup causing autopilot and flight director loss. The First Officer successfully reset the MCP twice to allow for a safe descent and landing at ZZZ, after which the aircraft was swapped.

synopsis: Passenger on a B737-700 observed a screw on the wing not fully secured. Maintenance addressed the problem.
summary: Maintenance informed the flight crew that a passenger on a previous flight noticed an unsecured screw on the wing. The passenger did not report this finding to the flight crew at the time.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew experiences an Anti-Skid Inop light at lift off. Soon after a Flight Attendant informs that a passenger saw a tire throw its tread. After discussions with Dispatch and Hydraulic System A fluid loss the crew elects to return to the departure airport.
summary: During departure, a blown right inboard tire triggered an Anti-Skid Inop light and subsequent A and B hydraulic system leaks. The crew declared an emergency, returned for a landing with directional drag, and safely stopped after confirming debris on the runway.

synopsis: First Officer voices objection to the intent of two senior Captains to takeoff with a reported windshear alert. The takeoff is delayed.
summary: The First Officer reported two instances where senior Captains initially intended to depart despite active Tower windshear alerts while taxiing or holding for takeoff. The First Officer intervened to delay both departures, emphasizing that avoidance is required during active alerts rather than relying on precautionary takeoff profiles.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports diverting for a possible fuel leak and a fuel imbalance.
summary: Pilots diverted an aircraft at FL380 after a right fuel imbalance indicated a suspected leak, landing safely at ZZZ. Maintenance later confirmed a malfunctioning cross-feed valve was transferring fuel despite being closed, grounding the aircraft.

synopsis: A B-777 flight crew found their workload during a weather diversion to have been significantly increased due to the difficulty of accessing required information, data and diversion planning resources utilizing the iPad tablet devices recently instituted by their company to replace previous paper based documents.
summary: During a weather divert, pilots struggled to access required documents because paper backups were removed and iPads froze below 10,000 feet. Inadequate training on the new electronic menu and device failures compromised safety margins while briefing an RNAV approach for the active runway.

synopsis: An A320 flight crew requested assistance and landed straight in at their destination when they determined the left engine was losing oil quantity.
summary: During descent, the crew observed decreasing left engine oil quantity and smoke trailing from the engine at idle. They executed a visual approach, shut down the engine after landing, and taxied to the gate after confirming it was secure.

synopsis: An A330 in heavy St Elmo's fire with engine anti-ice on developed a strong electrical odor which crew and passengers reacted to, so the flight returned to the departure airport. Maintenance discovered no anomalies and suspected a weather related phenomenon.
summary: During climb to FL370, the flight crew and cabin crew detected an electrical smell with no visible smoke, likely linked to engine anti-ice and St. Elmo's fire. The crew diverted to the departure airport, declared an emergency due to recurring odor, and landed normally, resulting in medical checks for three flight attendants and two passengers.

synopsis: The Captain of an air carrier aircraft touching down on Runway 25 at PHF was alarmed and initiated max braking after hearing Tower clear a Citation for takeoff on Runway 20 which intersects with 25 at the rollout end. There had been no notification of authorized LAHSO being in effect. Tower advised they had cleared the other aircraft based on 'reasonable expectation of separation' criteria.
summary: The pilot landing on Runway 25 at PHF applied maximum braking after a Citation was cleared for takeoff on intersecting Runway 20. The pilot stopped short of the intersection but was instructed to keep rolling based on the Tower's claim of "reasonable expectation of separation," which the pilot deemed unsafe due to limited visibility and potential collision risks.

synopsis: Although their cleared descent altitude of FL280 was both set and confirmed in the altitude alert window the pilot flying a G-IV noted the aircraft descending through FL278, stopped the descent and returned to FL280. He noted that the altitude alert window had changed to 27,500. He attributed the change excessive sensitivity of the set knob.
summary: The pilot flying inadvertently descended through FL280 to FL277 in a GIV aircraft after the sensitive altitude selector knob likely moved to FL275 when his finger was removed. The crew manually recovered to FL280, and although ATC requested confirmation, no further action was taken regarding the deviation.

synopsis: Required to back taxi down Runway 15 to depart Runway 33 at INT due to taxiway closures the flight crew of a CE-560 found themselves nose to nose with an aircraft which had just landed on 33 without a clearance.
summary: The pilot back-taxied onto Runway 33 and stopped when an aircraft appeared on the centerline without landing clearance or Tower contact. The other pilot, confused after an Approach handoff, landed illegally but avoided collision by taxiing slowly while the reporting pilot stayed to the right.

synopsis: MD83 flight crew is informed after the flight that Vmo was exceeded by 19 KIAS during descent. The event is described by the Captain as a new hire First Officer attempting to learn the auto flight system on the line, since the company will not do this training in the simulator.
summary: The Captain reported that a First Officer, two weeks out of training, caused an airspeed exceedance of 19 KIAS above Vmo during descent after incorrectly engaging VNAV and failing to manage the IAS/Mach changeover. The incident was attributed to inadequate initial training on autopilot modes and aircraft systems, requiring the Captain to disconnect the autopilot and manually control the aircraft.

synopsis: A B737NG Check Airman witnessed as the flight crew, following the company procedure, turned off the left center fuel tank pump shortly after takeoff when the its low pressure light illuminated but did not concurrently open the crossfeed valve...which is NOT directed by the procedure. A short time later the fuel imbalance light illuminated and the reporter advised the crew of the cause, the left engine now burning from the left main tank and the right from the center tank via the right center tank boost pump.
summary: A line check observer noted that after takeoff with 1,400 pounds in the center tank, a left center pump low pressure light illuminated, leading to a fuel imbalance when the crew followed procedures that omitted opening the crossfeed. The observer attributed the issue to the current fuel management procedure and suggested operational changes for low center tank fuel loads.

synopsis: MD-11 First Officer describes an unstabilized approach, due to a late start down and late configuration by the flying Captain, that may have met stabilized criteria at 500 feet.
summary: The Captain flew an unstable approach due to late descent and configuration, resulting in a long landing while high on the glideslope. The First Officer attributed the event to poor crew communication, distraction, and the Captain's fatigue, noting they failed to call for landing clearance.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reports discovering smoke coming from an oven in the aft galley. The smoking oven is opened and sprayed with two Halon fire extinguishers while using a PBE. A great deal of smoke is generated and the flight diverts to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: During initial beverage service, a flight attendant discovered smoke and flames in an aft galley oven. The crew extinguished the fire using two Halon extinguishers and a PBE, but heavy smoke and gas required the attendant to use oxygen before the aircraft landed at ZZZZ.

synopsis: Experimental aircraft pilot experiences a left main gear failure upon landing. As the aircraft departs the runway the right gear fails.
summary: The pilot reported that the left main gear failed upon landing, causing the aircraft to skid off the runway and break the right gear in the grass. No prior indication of gear problems existed, and the cause of the initial failure remains unclear.

synopsis: Glider pilot reports a conflict with an A320 at 3,000 feet SSW of SBJ. Evasive action is taken by the reporter to avoid a collision.
summary: A solo glider pilot without a transponder experienced a near-miss with a descending Airbus 320 while ascending through 3,000 feet MSL in the NY Class B airspace. The pilot attributed the incident to the lack of a transponder, no prior ATC notification, and failure to monitor the approach frequency, noting the airliner crew likely did not see the glider.

synopsis: Pilot at INT was issued back taxi instructions when taxiing an opposite direction arrival appears on the runway. Tower Controller never issued a landing clearance or knew abut the landing aircraft.
summary: While holding short for a back-taxi departure on Runway 33, the crew observed Aircraft Y landing without clearance due to the other crew's task saturation. Both aircraft held position, allowing Aircraft Y to taxi clear before the crew completed their back-taxi and departure without further incident.

synopsis: Controllers report of bad weather and aircraft deviations causing an airspace violation.
summary: Air Traffic Controllers in Sector 42 released military airspace despite heavy weather, causing a formation flight deviating north to clip the Baghdad MOA. The violation occurred because the flight could not turn left due to weather and could not climb due to other traffic, highlighting unsafe airspace release decisions.

synopsis: ANC Controller describes a release system with red and green lights that doesn't indicate with some type of aural alarm as to what color the light has changed to. By having the alarm the controller would know of the change.
summary: An air traffic controller at LHD Class D cleared an SVFR departure under 4-mile visibility without noticing a red light indicating traffic on Elmendorf final. The controller subsequently instructed the aircraft to perform a 360-degree turn after spotting the conflicting traffic, highlighting a need for improved coordination regarding light status changes.

synopsis: ZLA Controller describes a climb clearance given to an aircraft and the aircraft's climb rate changes the last 500 feet causing another aircraft to have an RA and the Controller to have a loss of separation.
summary: An air traffic controller issued climb clearances to Aircraft X and Aircraft Y converging on BLD VOR, resulting in a TCAS event for Aircraft X. The controller attributed the conflict to Aircraft Y's non-standard climb rate after leveling at FL355, prompting traffic advisories and visual contact.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports being cleared direct RANJR after initially holding for landing DCA. A weather deviation is requested and approved (15 left) then a frequency change. The next sector asks where they are going and issues a 90 degree heading change.
summary: The flight crew and ATC experienced task saturation while diverting to DCA with weather deviations. A supervisor issued an immediate 90-degree turn after the crew was directed toward other traffic, resulting in an uneventful remainder of the flight.

synopsis: When the B737-700 crew, flying direct to cross RANJR at FL280, was cleared to deviate off the TRUPS RNAV STAR for weather;'...direct USAAY when able, descend and maintain FL210;' they did so. After a frequency change an urgent response from ATC advised they were descending into traffic and to stop their descent at FL230 and fly heading 150 for traffic.
summary: The flight crew deviated left for weather while descending to FL210 on the TRUPS STAR to DCA. A supervisor intervened after the crew appeared to conflict with traffic, issuing a climb to FL230 and a heading change before clearing them to rejoin the arrival.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported they lined up to land at RNT instead of their intended BFI destination. The flight crew executed a go-around after ATC pointed out the error. Reporter stated non-compliance with SOPs contributed to the event.
summary: During a ferry flight to BFI, the Captain deviated from SOPs by descending early and turning base without checklists, causing the crew to line up for the wrong airport (Renton). ATC instructed a go-around, and the reporter attributed the error to non-standard procedures, poor communication, and unfamiliarity with the local airports.

synopsis: Confusion reigned when the flight crew of an EMB Phenom was cleared for the RNAV visual to Runway 19R at LAS but discovered it was not in their FMS database. The fractional operator had failed to inform ATC, or the Phenom flight crews, that the company's Phenom fleet was not yet equipped to conduct that approach although they had earlier advised that all of their fleets were configured to do so.
summary: The Phenom crew received a clearance for a "visual RNAV to 19R" at LAS, which their FMS database did not support. The controller subsequently canceled the approach and issued a visual clearance after realizing the aircraft lacked the required database capability.

synopsis: EMB505 First Officer is issued a clearance to fly the RNAV 19R Visual Approach to LAS. Not finding this approach in the Garmin, he assumes he is to intercept the RNAV Runway 19R final approach course and fly visually to the runway. This is not correct and the Controller issues vectors.
summary: The Phenom 300 crew received a clearance for the RNAV 19R Visual Approach but lacked the procedure in their Garmin avionics, causing confusion. The Approach Controller corrected the error by issuing vectors after the crew attempted to fly the non-existent procedure.

synopsis: CE560XL flight crew reported being cleared to depart DWH via the STYCK 1 except maintain 2,000 FT which is set in the altitude alerter. During taxi the departure is briefed and the SID altitude of 4,000 FT is set in the alerter by the pilot not flying Captain and not challenged by the First Officer who copied the clearance.
summary: Two pilots departed in a right turn, climbing to 4,000 FT instead of the cleared 2,000 FT due to a briefing error and reliance on the SID plate rather than the written clearance. The controller later corrected the altitude to 5,000 FT after the crew reported the discrepancy.

synopsis: A B777 approached a severe weather line on an Oceanic NAT Track westbound and unable to obtain a requested track deviation clearance, climbed 300 FT and deviated off track before receiving the clearance. ATC was surly about the unauthorized deviation.
summary: The flight crew deviated 70 NM left of Track Delta to avoid hazardous weather, climbing to FL363 per NAT procedures after initial clearance delays. While the flight landed safely, the pilot reported that Gander Radio's hostile and unprofessional communications created a significant distraction during this critical phase.

synopsis: A B737-800 First Officer related the loss of situational awareness that occurred when his Captain, the pilot not flying, advised Tower the field was in sight when he the pilot flying (PF) did not. A subsequent runway change with the field still not in sight by the PF resulted in a go-around.
summary: The First Officer, pilot flying, executed a go-around after the Captain reported the field in sight for a visual approach to MIA 8L while the First Officer could not see the airport due to sun and haze. The crew mistakenly identified a taxiway as runway 9 before correcting the error and landing uneventfully.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew experiences two runway changes during approach to WSSS. After the second change the ILS frequency is not tuned in a timely manner resulting in an overshoot. A normal landing ensues.
summary: During approach to Changi, a runway change from 20R to 20C caused the Pilot Monitoring to fail hard-tuning the localizer while activating the secondary flight plan. This error, attributed to incorrect prioritization and lack of verification, resulted in overshooting final and requiring a right turn to re-intercept the localizer.

synopsis: Two B737-800 Flight Attendants report a Captain, apparently new to the left seat, lost control of the aircraft in the flare and made a very hard landing which resulted in two bounces before coming to stop.
summary: Flight attendants reported two hard landings in a Boeing 737 during final approach, involving high sink rates, runway bounces, and wingtip proximity. The crew attributed the incidents to a captain new to the left seat, improper flap 40 usage, and a failed go-around decision, noting a lack of post-incident communication from the flight deck.

synopsis: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports about the inadequate locking design of One-Quarter turn oil plugs used on GE CF34-8C Engine Starters that have resulted in oil starvation and starter failures. The engine and starters are used on CRJ-700 and -900 aircraft.
summary: A mechanic serviced the right engine starter with Turbo 2380 oil, but the starter failed due to suspected oil starvation from an open port. The failure prevented engine start, requiring a starter replacement and causing a late departure.

synopsis: Observers reported to an Aeronca pilot that his aircraft's landing gear failed after takeoff. Upon returning to land on a grassy airport area, the right gear separated from the aircraft.
summary: During a local flight, ground observers reported the landing gear collapsed to the centerline. The pilot landed in a grassy area parallel to the runway, where the gear collapsed further and the right gear separated, damaging the aircraft but leaving the pilot uninjured.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Two instructor pilots in the MER traffic pattern report a near miss as both aircraft on base turns for Runway 13 approached each other. One aircraft turned a 360, the other continued.
summary: A pilot conducting a touch-and-go at a non-radar airport expedited a turn to avoid conflicting traffic on the right 45, which had initiated a left 360. The pilot later reported a physical threat from the other pilot and recommended installing radar at the airport.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A passenger/pilot reported passing 30 feet overhead an aircraft which entered S12 Runway 16 without CTAF communications during his takeoff from Runway 34 into an interfering sun.
summary: During a pre-purchase test flight departure from Runway 34, the pilot and buyer missed another aircraft vacating Runway 16 by 30 feet vertically. The near-miss resulted from distraction during extended run-up checks, poor visibility due to sun angle, and failure to hear CTAF calls from the other aircraft.

synopsis: A C182 engine caught fire during engine start forcing the pilot and four sky divers to evacuate. Hand fire extinguishers quelled the fire before fire fighters arrived but the ignited fuel's source is unknown.
summary: The pilot and four occupants evacuated a Cessna during engine start when smoke appeared, followed by a fire below the engine. The pilot suspects a carburetor fuel leak or fuel selector failure caused the fire, which damaged the engine and instrument panel but resulted in no injuries.

synopsis: NCT Controller reports of false alarms on non conflicting traffic possibly due to fusion radar.
summary: An air traffic controller reported an erroneous conflict alert when Aircraft Y passed one mile behind Aircraft X while both were separated and diverging. The controller attributed the false alarm to issues with fusion radar processing at NCT, which distracted from actual traffic management.

synopsis: ZMP FLM and Controller report of a non-standard flight being overtaken by speed of a trailing aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft Y, deviating for thunderstorms, nearly collided with a six-aircraft formation (Aircraft X) due to non-standard spacing and a trailing aircraft lacking Mode C. The controller attributed the loss of separation to the speed differential and the inability to verify the trailing aircraft's altitude, requiring visual separation to prevent a conflict.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: NCT Controller reports of aircraft being separated and then after they passed about a mile apart the conflict alert went off.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a false conflict alert between Aircraft X at 4,000 feet and Aircraft Y at 3,500 feet after they passed on opposite courses. The controller attributed the erroneous alarm to Fusion radar processing at NCT, which distracted from actual traffic and requires system review.

synopsis: An Air Carrier Captain reports a severe Flight Attendant injury due to a liquor cart tipping over in flight. He believes the carts are poorly designed and loaded in a top heavy condition. This condition can easily lead to carts tipping over.
summary: A flight attendant was severely injured when a top-heavy liquor cart tipped over in the back galley due to irregular flooring, worn wheels, and aircraft pitch. The reporter attributes the accident to the cart's inherent instability, which allowed it to be pushed over with minimal effort.

synopsis: With a loud pop, a B737-800 Captain's windshield cracked at FL350 followed by spider web glass cracking, so an emergency was declared, the QRH completed and the flight diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: During level flight at FL350, the captain's side windshield cracked after a loud pop and electrical glow. The crew declared an emergency, diverted, and landed overweight without incident before transferring to another aircraft.

synopsis: OMDB ATC attempted to vector an aircraft to OMDW vice nearby OMDB because somewhere the incorrect destination was entered in the ATC system although the flight plan was correct.
summary: ATC vectored the crew for an ILS approach to Runway 30 at OMDW, though the flight plan listed OMDB. The pilots identified the error when the final approach course was behind them, preventing an arrival at the wrong airport caused by an incorrect destination entry in the ATC system.

synopsis: An EMB-145 crew reported detecting smoke in the cockpit, and diverting to a nearby airport. A recirculation fan bearing had failed.
summary: The crew detected smoke in the cockpit, prompting ATC to re-clear the aircraft to its destination. An emergency evacuation was subsequently accomplished.

synopsis: After departure a B737-900ER crew received and entered a revised zero fuel weight of 113.8 in the FMS. At FL390 the weight and balance was reexamined because of sluggish performance and the correct weight of 133.8 entered which required a descent to FL370.
summary: During climb, the pilot not flying incorrectly entered a zero fuel weight of 113.8 instead of 133.8 into the FMS due to a lack of verbal verification. This error caused the aircraft to struggle at FL390, prompting a descent to FL370 after the crew corrected the weight entry.

synopsis: An A319 Captain realized that the recently revised Sabre flight planning software fuel release was based on time, FAR, and taxi but no additional fuel. Dispatch was surprised by the automation oversight and provided additional destination fuel remaining.
summary: The Captain discovered a software error in the Sabre system caused a flight plan to show insufficient remaining fuel (3,441 lbs) for an Airbus 319. Operations increased the fuel load to 6,000 lbs to prevent a mandatory diversion triggered by low-level fuel warnings, resulting in a 15-minute departure delay.

synopsis: While in line for takeoff, an air carrier flight crew received an urgent message to return to gate. They were informed that a Mechanic was concerned he had not fully completed rebuild work approximately a week and a half earlier on their A320 Main Landing Gear (MLG). Captain very concerned about the number of flights flown and length of time before the maintenance error was addressed.
summary: The flight crew was cleared to return to the gate after a mechanic expressed concern that a Main Landing Gear rebuild completed 1.5 weeks prior might be incomplete. Although mechanics verified all parts were in place and signed off the aircraft, Ramp Operations had already swapped the A320 for an A319 and deplaned passengers before the crew could depart.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A pilot taxiing to SFO Runway 1R on Taxiway A1 subsequent to an A1 Taxiway configuration change, was confused because his EFB and paper Airport diagrams had not been updated to reflect the taxiway reconfiguration following Runways 1L and 1R EMAS installation.
summary: The pilot reported that an air carrier flight ahead experienced a ground incursion at SFO while taxiing to Runway 1R due to airport diagrams conflicting with actual signage and taxiway geometry. The reporting crew avoided the error by following verbal instructions after observing the preceding aircraft's confusion.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: After landing Runway 36 at SKRG a flight exited at Taxiway C and while holding was approached head on by another aircraft which was not directed by Ground Control to stop. The U.S. crew flashed lights alerting the other aircraft but ATC acted casually and jovially to the ground conflict.
summary: The pilot reported a near-collision at SKRG while holding on Taxiway C after Ground Control issued a conflicting clearance in Spanish to another aircraft. The crew prevented a collision by flashing lights and rerouting, attributing the incident to the controller's lack of situational awareness, casual attitude, and use of Spanish instead of English.

synopsis: B777 Captain reports refusing a 1,400 pound shipment of Lithium Batteries listed as Class 9 dangerous goods. After the batteries have been removed an ACARS message is received from the Dispatcher indicating that certain Lithium Ion batteries can be carried as long as they meet certain requirements (i.e. watt hour rating limit and packaging), but the batteries are left behind.
summary: The flight crew at WSSS rejected a 1,482-pound Class 9 Lithium Ion battery shipment because the Shipper's Declaration listed them as forbidden on passenger aircraft. Although Dispatch later claimed company approval existed, the crew refused to reload due to verification concerns and potential safety risks.

synopsis: EMB145 Captain reports encountering severe icing conditions at FL370 while avoiding a thunderstorm that results in loss of airspeed indication. A descent is initiated with power up due to confusing indications, until wind noise and aileron shake indicated an overspeed was occurring. Pitch and power is used to reduce to a safe flying speed and the descent is continued until airspeed returns to normal.
summary: The Captain and First Officer encountered severe icing between FL300 and FL370 during night IMC, causing airspeed and altimeter failures. They declared an emergency, descended to FL250 to unfreeze instruments, and landed safely at an alternate airport due to outdated dispatch weather data.

synopsis: B767-300 flight crew detects a rumbling vibration from the right engine shortly takeoff. With N1 low, N2 near the limit, fuel flow high and LPT vibration at 5.0 the decision is made to return to the departure airport. Maintenance discovers a turbine failure.
summary: The pilot reported right engine vibration and high fuel flow during takeoff in rain, suspecting a cargo container shift. An emergency was declared for an overweight landing, which was uneventful with no cabin reports of smoke or debris.

synopsis: B777 Flight Attendant reports discovering incorrect demo life vests aboard an aircraft he is preflighting. The fleet uses two types of life vest and it is necessary that only the correct demo vests be placed aboard.
summary: A flight attendant discovered two dual chamber demo life vests and old safety cards stowed in the forward closet of an aircraft equipped with single chamber vests. The crew member removed the incorrect equipment, citing a recurring issue where outdated demo gear risks being used during safety demonstrations due to unclear fleet configuration processes.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant was injured when the aircraft encountered turbulence.
summary: A cabin crew member performing pre-landing safety duties was thrown into the aft galley and struck their mid-back when the aircraft suddenly and abruptly ascended.

synopsis: B737 Flight Attendant is informed by an FAA Inspector that a FAOM revision dated in the future must be installed during the flight, in order to be compliant with FAR's. The Inspector also does not comply with the reporters request to remain clear of the forward galley while the Captain is out of the cockpit and sits on a jumpseat.
summary: A First Officer spent 45 minutes inserting a manual revision during flight after an FAA inspector demanded immediate compliance. The inspector later entered the flight deck while the Captain was away and sat on the forward jumpseat, claiming her prior flight attendant experience justified the action.

synopsis: A Maintenance Controller was informed by a Captain about a grinding, vibration type sound coming from the Nose Landing Gear (NLG) area of a Dassault Falcon 2000 aircraft after landing. Captain had stopped his taxi, examined nosewheel, began taxiing again and was informed by Tower that smoke was coming from the NLG. Outer wheel bearing missing from left nose tire wheel half.
summary: The Dassault Falcon 2000 crew reported a grinding sound and smoke from the nose landing gear while taxiing after landing, leading to an evacuation and tow. Inspection revealed a missing outer wheel bearing on the left-hand nose gear assembly, which had been replaced three days prior, causing the aircraft to be taken out of service.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: An pilot departed HWO on the unpublished VFR SHERIDAN/SHORELINE Departure but his G1000 database did not contain it or the following IFR Miami Two Departure segment, so he entered the DRUMM waypoint, instead of DRUUM, and turned toward it. ATC detected the incorrect turn and cleared him on the departure direct HEDLY.
summary: The pilot departing HWO Runway 10R under IFR received conflicting downwind instructions and failed to load the Miami 2 SID due to a database omission. After entering an incorrect waypoint, the pilot deviated from the procedure until Miami ATC issued a direct clearance to HEDLY.

synopsis: C-150 pilot discovers after performing some basic flight maneuvers, that the engine will only produce partial power. A landing on an available dirt road is chosen as the least risky option and accomplished successfully.
summary: During an introductory flight in a C-150B, the engine produced only partial power during stall recovery despite carb heat and mixture adjustments. The pilot executed a precautionary landing on a dirt road with no injuries or damage to the aircraft.

synopsis: SR22 pilot reports being vectored behind a C210 for the ILS approach to Runway 33 at FNL, then switched to a visual when the field is reported in sight. After a 360 degree turn the right the SR22 pilot is also cleared for the visual approach. During roll out after landing the SR22 pilot reports coming nose to nose with the C210 which had landed in the opposite direction. The C210 pilot was using the wrong CTAF.
summary: The pilot and a C210 pilot encountered a runway incursion at FNL after the C210 landed on the wrong frequency (122.8 instead of 122.7). The C210 entered the runway opposite the reporting aircraft, causing a near collision that was avoided by both pilots moving to opposite sides of the runway.

synopsis: When the PA-28's throttle cable separated with the engine at full power after recovery from a training stall the instructor pilot assumed control, declared an emergency and, using excellent spur of the moment energy management techniques, landed uneventfully at a nearby airport.
summary: During a practice stall recovery, a throttle cable broke, causing the engine to run at full power. The instructor declared an emergency, diverted to a longer runway, and executed a safe engine-off landing by using the mixture for power bursts while the student assisted.

synopsis: Balloon pilot reports injury, caused by the burner, to a crew member during a hot inflation.
summary: During hot balloon inflation, a crew member tangled his foot in ropes and exposed his arm to flames while trying to free himself, resulting in a second-degree burn. The pilot stopped the inflation, and subsequent procedural changes were implemented to prevent foot entanglement and improve crew positioning.

synopsis: When a homeowner near the airport found an aircraft shimmy dampener from a PA-28 had fallen through the roof of his home he was able to track down the aircraft via the part type and investigation of such equipped aircraft at the airport. The reports were submitted by the pilot undergoing a BFR and his check airman who had flown the offending aircraft during the time period in question.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot reported a missing nose wheel shimmy dampener from a flight school aircraft, which reportedly fell through a nearby house roof. The part's loss occurred during an unknown flight segment, and the crew noted no in-flight vibrations or preflight anomalies despite a thorough gear inspection.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: JFK tow driver describes a situation where he is using a slow tug to move an aircraft across a runway. JFK Controller tells tug driver a new instruction, driver crosses runway and then later is issued a 'ticket' and his ID is pulled.
summary: A pilot towing Aircraft X with a super tug received conflicting ATC instructions to cross Runway 13L while still approaching Uniform-Alpha. The pilot crossed the runway based on the urgent clearance, resulting in a runway incursion, a Board of Review citation, and ID suspension due to ambiguous taxiway instructions.

synopsis: A small experimental biplane pilot was told after the fact that another aircraft took evasive action on short final to avoid a midair with his aircraft. The biplane pilot did not see the other aircraft.
summary: A pilot reported that after a normal landing, a witness stated another aircraft on short final had to execute a steep bank to avoid a collision. The pilot, who had no visual contact, suspects a nonstandard procedure caused the near-miss.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ADS Tower Controller reports of missing data blocks that are being removed against his wishes.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that personnel at D10 Approach Control removed their data blocks without approval on at least six occasions. The controller warned this unauthorized action creates a safety risk for traffic calls and urged immediate intervention to prevent a future incident.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: ELM Approach Controller cannot identify an aircraft but sees an intermittent target and assists the aircraft into a landing at ELM airport.
summary: An air traffic controller managed an aircraft declaring an emergency due to attitude indicator failure and intermittent radar coverage while approaching Elmira. The controller used an Emergency Obstruction Video Map to guide the pilot to a safe landing despite poor weather and radar issues.

synopsis: ZDV Controller reports of a loss of separation due to a slow descent rate of the lower aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller managed conflicting southwest arrivals and south departures routed via PUB due to weather. The controller lost lateral separation between Aircraft X and Aircraft Y while descending, attributing the issue to Aircraft X's insufficient descent rate and a premature turn to BRK.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: ZJX Controller describes a situation with tow aircraft that are at the same altitude and he needs to ship one to the next facility. He issues a 15 degree turn to the left and then ships the aircraft. Controller states the turn did help because the other aircraft descended to the turned aircraft's altitude.
summary: An Atlanta Approach controller turned Aircraft X 15 degrees left to avoid a collision with a descending VFR target after the receiving controller refused to provide separation. The reporter attributed the conflict to the receiving controller's indifferent attitude toward separating IFR and VFR aircraft.

synopsis: ZME Controller describes a refueling flight that is non-RVSM capable due to the two aircraft that are refueling are not capable.
summary: An air traffic controller corrected Aircraft X's flight plan after its RVSM status was incorrectly downgraded due to refueling with non-RVSM Aircraft Y and Z. The controller updated the equipment modifier, notified the next sector, and instructed the pilot to confirm RVSM capability upon formation breakup.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew experiences a Right Wing-Body Overheat light during initial climb. QRH procedures are complied with and the crew elects to return to the departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced a Right Wing-Body Overheat light at 11,000 feet during departure, prompting an emergency return and visual approach. Fire crews inspected the aircraft on the ground and found no visible damage or fire, allowing the flight to proceed to the gate.

synopsis: When their B737-700 was climbing out of FL380 for FL390 the flight crew discovered they were in Vertical Speed mode instead of NVAV and the airspeed was rapidly declining into the yellow arc. The PF took over manual control to re-accelerate which resulted in the loss of approximately 1,000 feet. They then continued climb to their cleared altitude.
summary: The flight crew lost 1,000 feet while climbing from FL380 to FL390 because the aircraft was inadvertently in Vertical Speed mode instead of VNAV. The Pilot Flying disconnected the autopilot to recover, attributing the error to excessive trust in automation and fatigue during the final leg of a night flight.

synopsis: Following abnormal vibration during landing gear retraction and a report of rubber on their departure runway the flight crew of a B737-700 returned to their departure airport, did a tower fly by and landed with two damaged left main gear tires and a broken and leaking hydraulic 'A' system line on the gear strut.
summary: The crew experienced a vibration during takeoff rotation, returned for a visual approach after Tower observed damaged tires, and landed safely. Post-landing inspection revealed ruptured Number 1 and 2 tires and a severed hydraulic line caused by runway debris, requiring maintenance repairs before towing to the gate.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew experiences an LE Flap Transit light at FL370 and complies with QRH procedures to extinguish the light. During approach, at low altitude, the light comes on again and stick shaker activated. The First Officer calls for a go-around, but the Captain elects to add power and land.
summary: The crew experienced a left slat 4 position switch fault causing intermittent LE flap alerts and a stick shaker activation on final approach due to increased minimum speed. Despite the First Officer calling for a go-around, the Pilot Flying elected to land the aircraft, citing controllability and the extinguished light as justification.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer describes fatigue accumulated over a month of flying due to insufficient time allocated for sleep. The First Officer did not remove himself from the trip although he believed he was not fit for duty.
summary: A fatigued First Officer on day five of a trip reported difficulty focusing due to averaging five hours of sleep nightly. The Captain determined the crew member was unfit for duty, yet they completed the flight without errors or threats.

synopsis: An EMB-145 Captain advised his company's revised vertical navigation SOP to provide greater climb angles to comply with altitude restrictions on RNAV SIDs from DEN exceed the aircraft's performance capability and resulted in a stall.
summary: The pilot reported that while following a new company steeper climb profile on a DEN RNAV departure, the stick pusher activated and the aircraft stalled shortly after selecting VS/1000 fpm. The reporter attributes the incident to the combination of the company procedure and summer thermals, noting the Pitch Limit Indicator was visible.

synopsis: A B777 Flight Attendant noted a burning rubber odor around Rows 30-36 which the flight crew identified as air conditioning pack oil and so secured the pack which stopped the odor but several flight attendants reported headaches, congestion and muscle pain following the long flight.
summary: During cruise, a burning rubber odor from a leaking air conditioning pack seal affected the crew for three hours until the pack was turned off. Upon landing, a mechanic refused to assist with the required paperwork, violating SOP, while several crew members reported headaches and muscle pain.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant reports being injured in flight when a cart she is attempting to stow tips over on her leg.
summary: A cabin crew member in the Y galley fractured their left first metatarsal and suffered a laceration when a heavy liquor cart tipped over during meal service. Medical professionals on board treated the wound, and the crew member was hospitalized upon arrival for the injury.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician was informed that a broken Emergency Brake System line he had removed and capped off was not replaced on their Cessna CE-560E aircraft. The brake line was discovered missing during a Post Maintenance Check.
summary: A technician and Lead Mechanic were inspecting a Cessna CE560E when an emergency brake line (P/N 6527365-16) broke during removal. The broken line was not ordered or documented due to a communication failure and was later discovered during a post-maintenance checklist.

synopsis: Captain reports the Nose Landing Gear (NLG) on a Mitsubishi MU-26B-40 (MU-2P) aircraft failed (collapsed) five to seven seconds into the landing rollout. A rod end for one of the two NLG Drag braces had broken at a crossbar that co-ordinates extension and retraction.
summary: The pilot reported a nose landing gear failure five to seven seconds after landing on Runway 09 at ZZZZ during a straight-in visual approach. Despite observing three green gear lights and a warning sound, the gear collapsed on rollout, though the aircraft was successfully moved off the runway and towed to the ramp.

synopsis: When the C-172 pilot on an IFR flight plan in scattered cloud conditions, lost essentially all electrical he was able to contact an FSS by cell phone, cancelled his flight plan and arranged a cell contact with the tower upon arrival at his destination.
summary: A Cessna 172M pilot lost all electrical systems at 8,000 feet while on an IFR flight plan south of PRN. The pilot descended VFR to 3,000 feet, used a cell phone to coordinate with FSS and Pensacola TRACON, and executed a no-flap landing at PNS after re-establishing radio contact with the tower.

synopsis: PA32 pilot on an IFR flight plan experiences smoke in the cockpit and diverts to a suitable airport with the aid of ATC. Post flight inspection revealed that the transponder had failed internally.
summary: A pilot experienced smoke and an electrical smell during an IFR climb when a Garmin GTX 330 transponder failed internally, causing charring without tripping the fuse. The pilot descended to a nearby airport for a safe landing, and post-flight inspection confirmed the transponder failure.

synopsis: CL300 Captain reports being issued a sidestep to Runway 22R after the Tower puts a B737 in position on Runway 22L at MDW. The runway length does not meet the runway length required by company SOP but is accepted by the Captain rather than go-around or land in the wake turbulence of the B737.
summary: The flight crew landed on Runway 22R at Chicago Midway after ATC issued a late sidestep clearance while a Boeing 737 occupied Runway 22L. The crew accepted the marginal 4,629-foot wet runway despite SOPs requiring 5,000 feet, suspecting the controller deliberately pressured them to prioritize flow over safety.

synopsis: Upon touchdown in a moderate left crosswind the pilot of a C-172 lost control of the aircraft which exited the runway onto a grassy area and came to a stop close to a crossing taxiway. No damage or injuries were reported and the undamaged aircraft was taxied back onto the hard surface and to parking.
summary: The pilot reported that during a 10-knot crosswind landing, the aircraft veered sharply left immediately after touchdown and exited the runway onto grass between the runway and Juliet Taxiway. Despite applying right rudder and brakes, the plane stopped adjacent to Juliet with no structural damage before the pilot taxied back to the East Ramp.

synopsis: Captain of a non FMC LR35 reports missing the crossing restriction at LTOWN, while on the WLDER8 STAR, landing south with the First Officer flying, after making the restriction at SPKER, due to an excessive amount of altitude to lose by LTOWN.
summary: The First Officer reported that while flying a descent via the WLDER 8 STAR, the published restriction to cross SPKER at FL230 and 280 knots made it physically impossible to meet the subsequent LTOWN restriction of 10,000 feet and 230 knots due to the short 19-nautical-mile distance. The pilot concluded the STAR design is flawed and recommended deleting the FL230 restriction at SPKER to allow for a safe, continuous descent profile.

synopsis: At the end of its landing roll on an unprepared surface, a PA-18 crossed a slight depression then hit a small Alder thicket at a very low speed which nosed the aircraft low causing a prop strike.
summary: The pilot landed on an unimproved glacier area where an angular depression caused the aircraft to swerve into an Alder thicket. The aircraft stopped nose-low with minor propeller contact, but no airframe damage occurred due to the low speed.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: EWR Tower Controller complains about a VFR aircraft that is getting close to a MLB TFR. His complaint is there is no security or an intercept aircraft to discover or track the violating aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller at the LGA CBA position detected an aircraft violating a sports TFR near the Hudson River at 1,400 feet. The controller attempted contact and handed off the target to another sector, but no law enforcement interception occurred, raising concerns about unpatrolled security zones.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilots report after landing at MSP they observe an aircraft crossing the runway. Pilot was never advised to hold short (LAHSO), but aircraft landing behind them was.
summary: The Pilot Flying on a visual approach to Runway 30L at MSP observed an aircraft crossing the runway during the flare while unaware of a LAHSO clearance issued to a following aircraft. The reporter noted no conflict occurred but expressed concern that excluding their non-LASHO company from the clearance created a disconcerting situation with potential safety risks.

synopsis: B757 Captain laments the use of 'jargon' by ground crewmen, Ramp Control and Ground Control to describe various aircraft types when issueing instructions. Even gate markings do not match standard FAA designations.
summary: Pilots, ramp controllers, and maintenance personnel at ORD used nonstandard slang like "57" instead of FAA designations, causing mismatched taxi instructions and readbacks. The reporter warns this lack of standardized phraseology creates dangerous assumptions and urges immediate alignment with FAA terminology.

synopsis: During pushback at a foreign airport, an A330 Captain employed a new Pushback Crew disconnect command at which time he expected the Guideman to disconnect. After a long start process, the Captain released the parking brake and found the Guideman still connected.
summary: During pushback, the flight crew released the parking brake briefly while the tug remained attached due to a long disconnect delay and loss of interphone communication. The aircraft did not move because manual brakes were engaged, but the incident highlighted a procedural gap where ground crew disconnects before confirming towbar removal.

synopsis: A B757-200 pilot executed a go-around at 2,600 FT because of weather and overshot 3,000 FT after employing full power and pitching up.
summary: During an ILS approach in thunderstorms, the crew executed a go-around at 2,700 feet due to low RVR and windshear. The First Officer manually disconnected the autopilot, causing an altitude excursion to 3,500 feet, which the reporter attributed to a lack of specific training for manual go-arounds from a coupled approach.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant reports the new galley oven hot plate racks on their B737-900 and B767-300 aircraft are very flimsy, do not stay in place and do not lock when pulling meals out. Previous oven racks had safety stops. Concerns also raised about the potential for getting burned or severely hurt.
summary: Cabin crew reported that galley oven racks failed to lock or stay in place during flight, creating a burn hazard when retrieving meals. The reporter questioned if this unsecured equipment violates FARs and asked what safety steps the carrier is taking.

synopsis: A B767-300 Flight Attendant attempted to move a beverage cart with the brake locked and turned it over in the aft galley injuring another flight attendant. While cleaning the galley and uprighting the cart she was further injured.
summary: Two flight attendants were involved in the galley during beverage service when a beverage cart tipped over while being repositioned, spilling liquids and striking one attendant's leg and foot. The incident caused potential strains to the reporter's back, neck, shoulder, and finger, though the flight was completed after cleanup.

synopsis: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports an escape slide at passenger Door 2-Left on an ERJ-170 aircraft had deployed with the door slide lever in the up and 'Disarm' position. Technician had been troubleshooting a flight crew squawk that the 'arming levers get stuck when arming door.'
summary: A mechanic inspected a reported stuck arming lever on the L-2 door and found rough operation during disarming. While lifting the handle to open the door, the escape slide deployed completely, likely caused by misrigging or wear preventing proper mechanism disengagement.

synopsis: A PA-28 owner without a medical asked an instructor to fly with him to add hours to his newly overhauled engine. The engine quit for unknown reasons but a safe off airport landing followed. The PIC instructor did not know that the annual had not been completed until the FAA inspected the aircraft.
summary: A pilot and an owner flew a Piper Arrow IV with a recently overhauled engine when it lost power during descent to 7,000 feet, forcing a successful highway landing. The cause remains unknown, though the aircraft was later found to be out of annual inspection due to an administrative oversight.

synopsis: A commercial and instrument rated pilot flying a single engine aircraft describes his near fatal loss of situational awarness when intentionally descending below minimums on an instrument approach.
summary: A fatigued single-pilot operator flying an ILS approach to 250 FT DA in fog failed to execute a missed approach upon reaching decision altitude. The pilot inadvertently descended below minimums and turned left before recovering at low altitude to land safely, attributing the incident to flawed judgment and a lack of commitment to go-around procedures.

synopsis: SR22 pilot reports encountering a UAV at 7,800 FT near PVD. The UAV was of a single or coaxial rotor design.
summary: The pilot reported a close encounter with a grey, drum-shaped UAV while descending through clouds at 7,800 feet on V146 near PVD. The pilot executed an immediate right turn to avoid the UAV, noting that IMC conditions and lack of detection equipment made visual avoidance impossible.

aircraft: Piper Twin Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A PA-39 engine with 250 hours on the heads suffered a catastrophic cylinder failure when one separated from the crankcase in flight. An emergency was declared, the engine shutdown and a safe landing followed at a nearby airport.
summary: The pilot experienced a catastrophic left engine cylinder head failure during cruise, causing severe vibration and cowling damage. After shutting down the engine and receiving ATC assistance, the pilot executed a controlled single-engine landing with no injuries, though a right tire was found flat upon taxi.
