Manually selecting Flaps 25 provided 1,640 feet margin, revealing a discrepancy between the computer's "Optimum Flap" logic and Dispatch calculations.

synopsis: A B737-800 crew became distracted during pushback and engine start by ATC changing the runway and departure. While recalculating performance data the First Officer failed to lower flaps which the crew discovered when the Taxi Checklist was reviewed during taxi.
summary: The Captain and First Officer inadvertently skipped the Before Taxi checklist during pushback and taxi due to simultaneous clearance changes and performance programming. The First Officer corrected the flap setting to five while moving, and the crew subsequently re-ran the checklist to confirm configuration.

synopsis: A B737-700 crew became distracted during pushback by a runway and ATIS change. During single engine taxi they realized the performance computer and FMC distractions caused them to miss lowering the flaps.
summary: The flight crew planned a single-engine taxi after engine start but failed to call the Before Taxi checklist. Consequently, they discovered the flaps were not set for takeoff only after switching from Ramp to Ground Control.

synopsis: A B737 Captain noted that while flying a programmed RNAV Arrival, he changed the landing runway, selected EXEC and the FMC reprogrammed itself to a waypoint behind the aircraft. After reestablishing on the RNAV Arrival he verified his actions with the same result.
summary: Pilots failed to close a route discontinuity in the FMC during an RNAV arrival, causing the aircraft to turn backward when the landing runway was changed. The crew disconnected LNAV, received a direct vector from Approach, and landed safely after erasing the erroneous discontinuity.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier pilot reported they were given taxi clearance via Taxiways A, P1, U to Runway 28, but because of night conditions, construction barrier lights and poor signage transitioned to U at P. ATC alerted about the error.
summary: The flight crew incorrectly entered Taxiway U while taxiing for departure on Runway 28 at night due to poor signage, construction barriers, and another aircraft. After acknowledging the error to Ground, the flight continued uneventfully, with the crew recommending improved signage and verified routing instructions.

synopsis: A B737-300 developed asymmetrical trailing edge flaps, one at 15 the other 18. The crew executed a go-around, completed the Flap/Asymmetrical TE Checklist and had an uneventful landing.
summary: The crew encountered a trailing edge flap asymmetry with the left at 15 degrees and right at 18 degrees during approach. They executed a go-around, followed the checklist, and landed uneventfully on Runway 25 Right using flaps 15.

synopsis: A heavy jet Captain taxiing on IAD Taxiway J was alerted by the off duty First Officer to stop because of an impending collision with an aircraft pushing back.
summary: During pushback, the aircraft's wing projected over Taxiway J while the First Officer retrieved ATIS, nearly colliding with a marshaller's aircraft. The Captain stopped abruptly to avoid a major impact, though Ramp personnel later denied any issue existed.

synopsis: B747 Captain believes his IRS navigation database (magnetic variation) is out of date as the compass heading being flown between two waypoints in northern Canada does not match the Sabre Flight Plan or the course drawn on a chart.
summary: A 747 pilot reported that the Inertial Reference System (IRS) steered 12 degrees off the published magnetic course between waypoints N63W130 and FANES due to outdated magnetic variation software. The pilot noted this deviation exceeds regulatory standards and requested FAA guidance clarifying crew responsibility for the uncorrected navigation database.

synopsis: A B737 at 2,000 FT on an ILS approach took evasive action after a TCAS RA from a FAA Flight Check aircraft while both were under ATC control. The other aircraft reported the B737 insight but took no evasive action.
summary: The crew on a visual approach received a TCAS Resolution Advisory when an FAA Flight Check aircraft crossed the localizer perpendicular to their path at nearly the same altitude. The First Officer manually executed the RA, climbing to miss the traffic by 300 feet before re-establishing a stabilized approach and landing safely.

synopsis: CRJ700 First Officer reports seeing an object, possibly a UAV or a balloon, pass below her aircraft at 1,900 FT during approach to Runway 4 at LGA.
summary: Pilots on approach to Runway 4 at La Guardia reported seeing a silver object, possibly a drone or balloon, below and east of the flight path at approximately 1,700 to 1,900 feet. The crew reported the sighting to the Tower, which confirmed other reports, but no course or altitude deviation was required to avoid the object.

synopsis: Pilot reports of an airborne conflict that was pointed out by ATC. ATC turns the aircraft and the aircraft then receives an RA and climbs. ATC questions the pilot why they were using TCAS in a terminal environment and why they climbed.
summary: A flight crew approaching Scottsdale received a heading from Luke AFB Approach toward traffic at 5500 feet, triggering a TCAS climb Resolution Advisory. The controller became upset when the crew complied with the RA, questioning their use of TCAS in the terminal area despite the aircraft climbing within 300 feet.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier crew enroute to PHX was allowed a deviation left of course near BTY for weather and then ATC issued an immediate right turn more than 90 degrees to avoid entering a restricted area.
summary: Pilots departing ZZZ to PHX requested a left weather deviation, which ATC approved, but were later urgently instructed to turn right to avoid a Restricted Area. The crew executed a 90-100 degree turn to the south, noting that their instruments do not display special use airspace boundaries.

synopsis: Learjet 35 flight crew reports receiving an IFR clearance via phone for an early AM departure, prior to engine start, and departing. ATC questions the crew about their clearance status, stating that they must be VFR because they are not IFR.
summary: The crew departed IFR after receiving a phone clearance without a void time, but ATC later stated no IFR departure clearance was received. The flight continued as planned, though the report notes the need to verify clearances on the ground when no void time is issued.

synopsis: A B737-800 left engine was slow to spool which caused a yaw and the nose wheel to turn, so the takeoff was rejected. Crew was later notified the reject speed was 103 knots.
summary: During takeoff on a single runway, the crew aborted after hearing "departure roll, nose gear" warnings while correcting for left engine spool issues. The captain initiated the stop at 103 knots, believing the speed was lower, and the aircraft taxied to the gate without incident.

synopsis: A Technician reported a CE-750 pilot called while inflight about a Navigation System malfunction, which should have been handled by his Chief Pilot.
summary: A Citation X PIC called Maintenance in flight regarding a #2 IRS 'ON BATT' light and a non-functional #1 heading bug without disclosing the aircraft's status. The reporter resolved the IRS issue remotely but noted the PIC violated FOM procedures by seeking deferrals while airborne, creating a dangerous situation.

synopsis: Pilot is cleared for an approach to CVN that is NOTAMed Not Authorized.
summary: The pilot requested the VOR 22 approach at KCVN, was initially denied, then cleared by a second controller. After landing, the pilot discovered the approach was unauthorized and noted Cannon Approach never advised of the procedure's status.

synopsis: When the instructor/check out pilot exited the aircraft at the run-up area to inspect the condition of the Citabria's tailwheel due to directonal control issues on taxi out, Ground Control remonstrated the reporter/pilot being checked as to the need to coordinate any such egress in a movement area with ATC.
summary: During a taxi to the run-up area in a Citabria 7GCBC, the pilot-in-command lost directional control, and the instructor exited the aircraft without notifying ground control to inspect a flat tail wheel. The incident resulted in a controller warning and a tow back, with the pilot attributing the error to deferring authority to the instructor instead of maintaining control.

synopsis: A PA32 pilot shooting practice instrument approaches into a high altitude airport in IMC suffered erratic altitude and heading readings which were likely the result of pitot static blockage.
summary: A pilot conducting IFR practice approaches encountered altitude and heading control issues caused by a blocked pitot tube and subsequent rime ice accumulation in an overcast layer. After clearing the blockage with pitot heat, the pilot cancelled the IFR plan and descended below the clouds to complete a visual approach due to icing and controller altitude restrictions.

synopsis: C150 pilot reports striking a power line during a low approach to a private strip.
summary: The pilot departed a private strip and struck a power line on the east end of the runway while circling for a low approach. The pilot continued to the home strip and later returned to the accident site by automobile.

synopsis: Citabria pilot experiences the loss of the cabin door in flight over an unpopulated area. Pilot diverts to a suitable airport.
summary: A Citabria pilot reported losing a door in flight about 4 miles northeast of the airport over an unpopulated area. The pilot diverted to the nearest practical airport and executed a successful normal landing.

synopsis: HCF Controller describes situation where an a conflict arises due to a bad clearance issued by Clearance Delivery at the Tower of departure.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a 3-mile separation between Aircraft X and Aircraft Y at 7,000 feet after Aircraft X deviated from its filed IFR route to fly low-level VFR sightseeing. The controller attributed the incident to Aircraft X's unauthorized routing and the tower's failure to identify the required oceanic clearance for the filed refueling route.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZDC Controller reports of a airspace deviation that is caused by flight deviations and traffic workload in the sector.
summary: An air traffic controller missed a northbound aircraft at FL390 while managing complex traffic and a departure push, triggering a conflict alert. The controller turned the conflicting aircraft right to maintain separation but could not obtain official permission from the adjacent sector due to unanswered calls.

synopsis: LAX Tower Controller describes an operational error caused by a technique employed at LAX. A faster aircraft is told to maintain visual separation from a slower aircraft and passes the slower aircraft causing the loss of separation.
summary: LC controllers applied a "Last to the beach visual" technique for Aircraft Y and Aircraft X departures, assuming equal performance. Aircraft X out-climbed Aircraft Y, causing a Conflict Alert with less than two miles lateral separation due to the technique's failure to guarantee positive separation between dissimilar aircraft.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZAB Controller describes a situation where the aircraft suffix is different then what it actually is. This error may have led to a loss of separation throughout the flight of the aircraft. The aircraft suffix was actually a G but filed as a L, which allowed the aircraft to be in RVSM airspace.
summary: An air traffic controller climbed Aircraft X from FL270 to FL350 after the pilot claimed Non-RVSM capability, though the aircraft was actually a test flight requiring 2000 feet separation. The controller failed to coordinate this separation and noted the pilot filed an incorrect equipment suffix, admitting both parties needed better communication.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported being vectored off the MNZNO 2 RNAV after YUGLU for terrain when the aircraft does not immediately start climbing out of 9,000 FT.
summary: The pilot and first officer of a Boeing 737-300 departing ABQ on the MNZNO TWO RNAV departure received an early ATC heading clearance for terrain avoidance while climbing to FL200. No GPWS warnings occurred, and the flight continued safely despite the crew's surprise at the timing of the instruction.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported becoming confused as to the lowest altitude to maintain during the EAGUL 5 arrival to PHX landing east. The crew descended below 7,000 feet after HINEY before asking ATC for guidance.
summary: The crew descended past 7000 feet on the EAGUL 5 arrival to PHX due to confusion over the 4000-foot limit at HINEY. The Pilot Not Flying corrected the error at 6000 feet, and Approach subsequently cleared them to 4000 feet without detecting the initial mistake.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reports being cleared for the ILS to maintain 3,000 feet until established, but the First Officer elects to set the FAF altitude of 2,000 feet in the MCP window. His action resulted in a descent below 3,000 feet prior to glideslope intercept and received a query from ATC.
summary: The pilot and First Officer descended to 2000 feet instead of the cleared 5000 feet on an ILS approach to IAH Runway 8R due to an unverified altitude change and lack of verbalization. ATC queried the deviation, but the crew intercepted the glideslope at MATON and landed safely.

synopsis: Pilot reports of a ATC facility forgetting about the aircraft they were flying and then flying an extra 60 miles to be able to land.
summary: The pilot reported that while on the Jiims Arrival at 4,000 feet, Philadelphia Approach lost track of the aircraft, causing it to fly 60 miles out of airspace before being turned around over McGuire. The pilot attributed this unsafe situation to communication problems and recommended retaining two separate approach frequencies.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain describes the confusion that ensues when a company aircraft comes on the Approach Control frequency with a nearly identical call sign.
summary: During descent into CLT, the crew experienced confusion with flight ABA due to similar call signs, leading to a TCAS traffic advisory and a nose-to-nose conflict. The reporter attributes the incident and subsequent reslotting to ATC and crew miscommunication caused by the company assigning indistinguishable flight numbers.

synopsis: EMB145 Captain reports a NMAC with an EMB135 during a visual approach. The EMB145 crew complied with a TCAS RA to climb and avoided the nearly head on EMB135 which apparently did not comply with an ATC clearance to 'keep it in tight'.
summary: The EMB145 crew received a TCAS red warning during final approach to Runway 22 when an EMB135, cleared for a visual approach, strayed outside its assigned area and passed 200 feet below them. The reporter attributes the near-miss to the EMB135 pilot's failure to maintain a proper lookout and disregard for ATC clearances.

synopsis: An ERJ-175 declared an emergency, shut down the right engine and diverted to the nearest suitable airport after determining they had a significant fuel leak in the number two tank.
summary: The flight crew detected a suspected fuel leak during climb-out, declared an emergency, and diverted to ZZZ. They performed a precautionary engine shutdown and landed safely after dismissing an erroneous low-level warning, though cabin crew could not visually confirm a leak.

synopsis: When their ERJ-170 struck turbulence on descent a flight attendant suffered a severe leg injury. An emergency was declared and their arrival to their destination was expedited by ATC.
summary: During the arrival descent, the flight crew encountered moderate turbulence that caused a flight attendant to suffer a broken leg while performing service. The crew declared a medical emergency, received priority handling from ATC, and landed to allow paramedics to treat the injured crew member.

synopsis: EMB145 flight crew detects smoke in the cockpit and the Flight Attendant detects it in the cabin. The flight diverts to the nearest suitable airport where maintenance determines that the left pack is likely the culprit and is MEL'd. The passengers are reboarded and the flight departs. The odor is again detected causing another diversion.
summary: The flight crew and cabin crew detected a burning odor at FL350 linked to Pack #1, prompting an emergency descent and overweight landing at ZZZ. After the odor recurred during a subsequent climb to FL190, the crew declared an emergency and returned to the departure airport for aircraft replacement.

synopsis: A BAE-125-850XP departed a CTAF airport and during initial climb red HDG flags appeared on the Captain's and First Officer PFDs and MFD with all heading sources lost, so ATC declared an emergency and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: During initial climb, the crew experienced total heading and flight director failures on all displays, forcing a magnetic compass-only diversion back to the departure airport. The aircraft performed an overweight landing 150 pounds above maximum weight after ATC declared an emergency, though the descent rate remained low and passengers were unaffected.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier flying North in Colombian airspace changed routes for weather avoidance and on UG444 discovered the mountain near Waypoint PETER is close to a 19,000 foot mountain. An emergency drift down with a course reversal in that area would be into raising terrain.
summary: The pilot reported a hazardous high-terrain decision point at "PETER plus 14 NM" on Airway UG444 in Colombia, where a required course reversal would lead into rising mountains near Pico Cristobal Colon. Dispatch subsequently locked out the route for analysis after the flight arrived safely in VMC conditions.

synopsis: A DHC-8-200 First Officer reported his Captain refused to divert without first attempting an approach at an airport with the weather below minimums because he feared Company accusations.
summary: The First Officer reported that the Captain, despite repeated concerns about RVR being below minimums, elected to attempt an approach in 1/2 SM visibility and 800 RVR due to pressure to perform. The crew executed a missed approach at minimums with no runway in sight and diverted to the alternate airport.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Flight Attendant describes an incident with a passenger becoming suctioned to the toilet after flushing while seated with the seat up.
summary: Cabin crew assisted a passenger who became suctioned to the lavatory bowl after flushing while seated, causing her to become faint and bleed. The crew broke the seal with the Captain's help, landed with the passenger in the lavatory, and transferred her to EMTs at the gate.

synopsis: An instructor pilot reported GUS was unable to provide radar coverage within ten miles of the BVT VOR possibly because of ground interference. The pilot feels because of the training traffic density, a LAF airspace upgrade may be needed to provide the needed safety margin.
summary: A flight instructor and student pilot experienced repeated radar contact loss while requesting IFR clearance near the BVT VOR, which the instructor attributes to wind turbine interference. The crew canceled IFR to continue VFR, concerned that invisible VFR traffic could conflict with IFR arrivals due to poor radar coverage.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A pilot departed SQL West bound, climbed to 3,700 feet and there took evasive action from GTN 750/650 TIS alerted traffic 400 feet below. During the climb he momentarily entered SFO Class B.
summary: The pilot climbing from San Carlos Airport at 3,700 feet received a traffic conflict alert on Garmin avionics from a fast-moving aircraft below. To avoid a probable mid-air collision, the pilot climbed to 4,100 feet, briefly entering SFO Class B airspace, before descending back to 3,700 feet.

synopsis: A PA-18 pilot ground looped his aircraft and scraped a wing. The pilot admitted that his control inputs were not timely and conducted when the aircraft's airspeed was too low for airflow.
summary: The pilot experienced a ground loop to the left with right wingtip damage during a practice tailwheel landing. The incident was caused by delayed and ineffective rudder inputs due to low airspeed and lack of airflow over the rudder.

synopsis: Pilot reports of possibly violating Restricted airspace while under flight following.
summary: The pilot of an MDX 20 en route to TRM was advised by Los Angeles Center to turn left after approaching restricted airspace R-2502A, which the pilot believed was avoided based on GPS and sectional charts. The pilot attributed the incident to potential GPS software faults or chart oversight, while the ATC supervisor acknowledged radar inaccuracies and insufficient assistance.

synopsis: Pilot reports of receiving flight following and the Controller asking him if he is talking to CLL Tower for permission to go through the Class D airspace.
summary: A VFR pilot flying from SEALY to Waco via CLL VOR entered Class D airspace without contacting the tower while receiving traffic advisories from Houston Approach. The pilot attributed the oversight to map clutter and a lapse in situational awareness, though no near miss occurred.

synopsis: NCT Controller reports of an aircraft under flight following and isn't sure of the routing the aircraft is flying. Aircraft enters PAO's Class Delta but isn't pointed out to the Tower.
summary: An air traffic controller lost track of Aircraft X during a VFR flight following request to SFO after the pilot deviated south of the expected route. The controller transferred the aircraft to Woodside, but it inadvertently entered PAO airspace without coordination before proceeding to SFO without incident.

synopsis: N90 controller describes a runway change that affects numerous airports. The change is made but communication between ATC is not good and a loss of separation occurs.
summary: An air traffic controller at the Mugzy position experienced a loss of separation between two aircraft at 3,000 feet during a runway change at TEB and MMU. The incident occurred because MMU Tower unexpectedly diverted an arrival to a different runway without coordinating the maneuver, causing a conflict with another aircraft on downwind.

synopsis: A B737-700 engine made a loud bang with vibrations after takeoff. Suspecting an engine stall the crew completed the QRH and returned to the departure airport where after landing the Number 2 Engine Fail light alerted.
summary: The flight crew experienced a loud bang and vibration in engine #2 shortly after takeoff, prompting an emergency return. Although initial indications were normal, the engine #2 fail light illuminated after landing, leading the crew to manually shut down the engine while taxiing.

synopsis: Signage on the Alpha and Bravo bridges at ORD is in one direction only for aircraft to 'not stop on the bridge.' Bridges are occasionally used in a nonstandard direction and no signage is available.
summary: A pilot reported that "Do Not Stop on the Bridge" signage at ORD's Alpha and Bravo bridges is visible only in one direction. The reporter questioned if signage should be bidirectional to cover non-standard taxi scenarios, such as snow plowing, where aircraft might taxi opposite to normal assignments.

synopsis: A Q400 ROLL SPLR INBD HYD and #1 HYD ISO VLV caution lights illuminated intermittently so the QRH was partially completed prior to landing. After landing with no brakes or nose wheel steering, the crew realized they had not completed the checklists which would have alerted a hydraulic system leak.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway 7, the pilot and First Officer experienced intermittent hydraulic caution lights but completed only one checklist due to task saturation. They landed with no normal braking caused by a #1 hydraulic leak, though they stopped safely using props and parking brake.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A flight crew filed J11 to DRK then transition to the PHX MAIER 5, but ATC assumed the crew transitioned at CORKR because that waypoint is designated CORKR.MAIER with waypoints common to both J11 and the MAIER beyond CORKR.
summary: A Part 91K crew en route to PHX experienced a routing misunderstanding with ATC due to shared intersection names between airway J11 and the MAIER 5 arrival. The controller assumed the crew joined the arrival at CORKR, while the crew continued on the airway to DRK, requiring a clearance direct to BRUSR to resolve the deviation.

synopsis: The Captain of a night time commercial departure from JNU reported a conflict with an inbound Piper 'Cub.' A new airport procedure specifying coordination of opposite direction, concurrent arrivals and departures at night was cited as a contributing factor.
summary: A departing crew and a Piper Cub experienced a near-miss at night due to rigid runway procedures that prevented the Cub from landing while the crew taxied. The Cub held in poor visibility, then flew 200 feet below the departing aircraft, which the reporter attributes to poor procedures restricting ATC discretion.

synopsis: When an MD82 Captain's seat failed to latch into position, a Flight Attendant was called to the cockpit to hold the seat in position while the Captain landed the aircraft. Uneventful landing.
summary: The Captain reported that his seat failed to latch during descent, requiring a flight attendant to hold it steady for a safe landing. He attributed the issue to a known seat defect and chose to fly the aircraft himself rather than allow the inexperienced First Officer to land.

synopsis: B757 First Officer experiences a L HYD ENG PUMP EICAS message during descent, followed by a L HYD QTY EICAS message when Flaps 1 is selected. The approach is continued and when flaps 30 is selected, a TE FLAP ASYM EICAS and a RUDDER RATIO EICAS message appear. After landing the nosewheel steering is discovered to be inoperative and the aircraft is towed to the gate.
summary: The Captain and crew managed a left hydraulic system failure caused by a split line during approach, resulting in asymmetric flaps, rudder ratio issues, and inoperative nose wheel steering. The aircraft landed safely but required a tow to the gate after the Captain manually stopped it on the runway.

synopsis: CRJ200 flight crew reported hearing a thud passing 13,000 FT. As the aircraft rolled slightly to the left the Captain corrected with aileron. An emergency is declared and the flight returns to the departure airport, where post flight inspection reveals a large section of the thrust reverser has been ripped off
summary: During climb at 13,000 feet and 310 knots, the crew heard a thud and experienced a left roll, prompting an emergency return due to suspected structural damage. Post-flight inspection revealed the bottom half of the left engine thrust reverser had ripped off, though the aircraft landed normally after handling improved at lower speeds.

synopsis: BE33 instructor and two students report a NMAC with a small low wing aircraft about 6 NM south of CHD at 2,500 FT. The other aircraft was detected too late to take evasive action and passed within 200 FT. The other aircraft did not have an operating transponder.
summary: A student pilot and check pilot experienced a near mid-air collision with a Piper Warrior while descending to 2500–3000 feet for Chandler Airport. The other aircraft, which had an inoperable transponder and was undetected by TCAS or radar, passed within 150–200 feet laterally.

synopsis: A Lead Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) was informed of a possible non-compliance with Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM) procedures involving Static grounding of aircraft to earth during maintenance. Lead Technician also notes the lack of approved, tested, certified and identifiable earth grounds at two Terminal fingers for B737 aircraft, may have contributed to the possible non-compliance issue.
summary: A maintenance technician reported potential non-compliance with B737 grounding procedures at ZZZ Terminal X and Y, citing unverified earth grounds and reliance on tire conductivity. The reporter concluded that approved grounding points were unavailable, creating a safety risk for maintenance tasks requiring static grounding per the Aircraft Maintenance Manual.

synopsis: When a Citation flight crew was cleared to cross runways 28R and L at OAK on B they mistakenly turned on A. The flight crew and the Ground Controller agreed that poor signage was the major contributing factor, the Controller stating they see similar events 'a thousand times a year.'
summary: A Cessna crew at OAK mistakenly crossed Runway 28R hold short lines on Taxiway A due to unclear signage while a twin Cessna was on final approach. The ground controller ordered the landing aircraft to go around after the crew corrected their position report.

synopsis: PA-28 commercial rated pilot reported forgetting to extend the landing gear during approach after being asked by the Tower to extend the downwind for traffic on an intersecting runway. The Tower Controller detected that the gear is up at a low altitude and issued a go around. Poor and inadequate instruction was cited as a factor in the incident.
summary: A solo pilot practicing touch-and-gos forgot to lower the landing gear during a short field approach, prompting a tower go-around before descending below 50 feet. The pilot attributed the error to poor instruction and a lack of consistent checklists, resolving to verify gear position at every pattern leg.

synopsis: MSY Controller describes a situation where he climbed an A319 aircraft through the wake of a B757 and didn't use the residual wake turbulence rules for proper separation.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managed a near-miss between Aircraft X on downwind and departing Aircraft Y, climbing Y to FL150 after their paths crossed. The controller attributed the wake turbulence risk to failing to have Y wait or maintain visual separation from the Heavy aircraft.

synopsis: A319 First Officer reports a near collision with a B747 during taxi into an alley gate. The B747 was under tow into a gate on the opposite side of the alley and may have been pushed back slightly. Ramp Control did not mention that the B747 was under tow.
summary: The flight crew was cleared by ramp control to taxi to a gate while a B747 was being towed backwards nearby. The pilot stopped the aircraft to avoid a collision with the B747's winglet, which occurred because the controller failed to inform them of the ongoing tow operation.

synopsis: EMB505 Captain discovers damage to the main cabin door on post flight, and makes a logbook entry for maintenance. Maintenance attempts to defer the airstair door as a 'panel;' stating that the EMB505 MEL/NEF provided relief to defer ANY 'panel' in the aircraft. The crew does not agree.
summary: The flight crew reported damage to the EMB505 main cabin airstair door after landing, but maintenance attempted to defer the repair by classifying it as a deferrable panel under MEL 25-00-00. The crew refused this relief, citing that the door is not a panel and noting a pattern of maintenance pressure to fly the aircraft despite the damage.

synopsis: CE560 Captain reported discovering that a passenger will not remain upright with the seat unoccupied and that three other seats will not remain upright when occupied. A logbook entry is made and a local mechanic is dispatched to effect repairs. After the repairs have been completed and the logbook signed, the Captain finds that nothing has changed.
summary: A flight crew member reported that an onsite mechanic, pressured by Maintenance Control, signed off unrepaired passenger seats on an XL aircraft despite failed operational checks. The crew discovered the next morning that the seats remained inoperative, highlighting a systemic issue where maintenance was closed without resolution to reduce downtime.

synopsis: Arriving at destination at a traffic peak the flight crew of a B737NG failed to receive a timely turn to intercept the localizer for their approach. Immediately after passing through the final approach course, ATC called advising them to intercept, and asked them why they had failed to do as cleared. During a post flight interview it was determined that another flight had responded to their clearance and the error went undetected by both ATC and the reporters.
summary: The pilot flying and first officer could not request a turn to intercept the ILS for runway 22R due to extreme radio congestion, causing them to overshoot the localizer. The controller supervisor later confirmed the crew was not at fault because a previous turn instruction was mistakenly acknowledged by another aircraft.

synopsis: An A300 flight crew conducted appropriate checklists and landed safely following a left hydraulic system failure.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced left hydraulic pump failure and low quantity during descent, leading to asymmetric flaps and loss of nose wheel steering. They landed safely but required a tow to the gate after failing to activate the flap override switch and losing steering capability.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew changes the FMC database six hours early and finds that there are differences between the FMC OAK ILS 30 and the Jepp ILS 30 with the same effective date. A Visual Approach and landing is accomplished.
summary: The Captain prematurely updated the MD-11 FMS database before the correct Zulu time, causing corrupted ILS 30 OAK data. This error revealed significant altitude discrepancies and a missing fix between the FMS and Jeppesen databases, forcing a visual approach instead.

synopsis: EYW Tower FLM reports of a drone that violated Class Delta airspace.
summary: A drone operated within Class Delta airspace without communicating with the controlling ATC facility. The report identifies this lack of communication as the safety issue.

synopsis: An SF340 flight descending into MYNN, cleared to descend to 8,000 feet, narrowly avoided an NMAC with an opposite direction Cessna Caravan. Approach advised they were not talking to them.
summary: The pilot and first officer flying to MYNN stopped a descent from 11,000 to 2,000 feet after visually spotting an uncontrolled Cessna Caravan 500 feet below. Nassau Approach had issued the descent clearance without traffic advisories, forcing the crew to deviate to avoid a collision at a closure rate near 400 knots.

synopsis: When the PC-12 suffered abnormal propeller RPM response the flight was continued to destination where, upon landing, the prop failed to shift to Beta mode and the aircraft accelerated and demanding immediate and extreme braking to stop on the runway. Both main gear tires were flatted and deflated as a result. No injuries or other damage to the aircraft.
summary: The pilot of a PC-12 experienced low propeller RPM en-route and a forward surge upon selecting beta after landing. Heavy braking applied to stop the accelerating aircraft caused both main tires to flat spot and deflate, though no further damage occurred.

synopsis: PA-28 tow pilot experiences a NMAC with a sailplane flying in the opposite direction. Both pilots take evasive action and the glider under tow releases.
summary: A Piper PA-28 tow pilot and a glider with instructor and student experienced a near miss at 1800 AGL while both were operating near a gliderport. The pilot attributed the conflict to a momentary scan breakdown and potential glider structure obstruction, resulting in evasive maneuvers and a closest approach of approximately 300 feet.

synopsis: SJC Controller working CD/FD issues the wrong altitude to an aircraft via PDC. NCT Controller expects aircraft to climb to 5,000, but aircraft is climbing to 12,000 and deviates into another controller's airspace.
summary: An air traffic controller accidentally issued Aircraft X a clearance to maintain 12,000 feet instead of 5,000 feet due to a PDC input error. The pilot climbed to 12,000 feet, deviating into another sector's airspace because the receiving controller failed to notice the discrepancy.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: BUR Tower Controller describes a situation where an aircraft goes missed approach due to its speed on final. The Controller describes an unsafe situation where the aircraft has to be told to remain in the traffic pattern which is too small to handle this type of aircraft. The close proximity of VNY airport and other IFR arrivals to BUR add to the complex situation.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported that Aircraft X executed a go-around on a visual approach to Runway 8 at BUR due to excessive airspeed. The controller cited unsafe procedures forcing the aircraft into a right downwind pattern, creating potential conflicts with nearby Class D airports and other traffic.

synopsis: ZKC Controller describes a situation with another facility that doesn't have the capability to change flight plans. After conversing with the other controller the aircraft checks on climbing to an uncoordinated altitude. A few moments later the ZKC Controller also observes the aircraft off route and queries the pilot as to where he is going.
summary: An air traffic controller in Sector 06 reported a handoff error from Vance AFB involving Aircraft X, where the pilot climbed to FL290 and deviated from the route without proper approval. The reporter attributed the incident to inadequate training and equipment at Vance, which led to flight plan discrepancies and unauthorized altitude changes.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported being unable to adequately brief the flight attendants due to the Agent boarding before the crew was ready. The company is pushing the agents and the agents are pushing the flight attendants to board early.
summary: The Captain reported that an agent began boarding before the crew was ready, preventing an adequate safety briefing with the distracted Flight Attendant. The reporter attributes this safety issue to management policies pressuring agents to board early, arguing that the Captain must control boarding readiness to ensure safety.

synopsis: A B737 Captain assessed what he believes to be excessive pressure on operational personnel to achieve on-time departures, often at the expense of required aircraft security and crew coordination duties.
summary: The pilot reported that ground agents frequently began boarding before the security checklist was complete and before the flight deck could brief the cabin crew. This pressure to meet unrealistic on-time timelines caused distractions and rushed safety inspections, compromising pre-flight readiness.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reports being given taxi instructions that include crossing Runway 31R. Approaching the runway it appears that a Gulfstream jet is about to touch down and the Captain holds short. As the Gulfstream rolls out Ground is queried and indicates that he was not aware the runway was active.
summary: While taxiing to cross Runway 31R, the Captain stopped the aircraft after spotting a Gulfstream landing, preventing a runway incursion. The Ground controller admitted he was unaware the runway was active, though the pilot noted the controller was in the Tower.

synopsis: After updating destination weather which unexpectedly decreased to CAT III, the B737-800 crew requested an alternate but the ACARS with the release was not received until after landing at the filed destination.
summary: The crew and dispatcher experienced a communication failure regarding an amended release for alternate ZZZ2 during descent for a CAT III approach. The dispatcher claimed to have sent the message, but the crew did not receive it, resulting in a landing with 5.4 hours of fuel remaining.

synopsis: B737 Captain perceives safety threats from agents and ground personnel who are constantly badgering flight crews to release the brakes for an on time departure, before they have completed cockpit set up and briefing.
summary: The flight crew at Boston Logan was repeatedly pressured by ground agents and pushback crew to release brakes before completing complex flight plan changes. The captain refused the requests to maintain safety during a complex departure, resulting in a one-minute delay attributed to the crew's refusal to release brakes prematurely.

synopsis: An EMB-145 EICAS intermittently alerted FUEL 1 LOW LEVEL during descent, so the crew, uncertain about the actual fuel state advised ATC and after landing dipped the tank which revealed a faulty totalizer.
summary: The flight crew experienced intermittent FUEL 1 LOW LEVEL EICAS warnings during descent into ZZZ while operating with an ACARS INOP MEL. They diverted briefly but continued to land safely after determining the cause was a faulty system component rather than actual low fuel.

synopsis: An EMB-145 Captain described the safety hazards, distractions and increased flight crew workload because of the Company requirement to ACARS non flight related anomalies even when the causes are well known.
summary: Pilots reported that mandatory ACARS prompts for delay reporting caused distraction and increased workload during a challenging flight involving weather deviations and RNAV changes. The reporter attributes this safety hazard to the company's requirement to input non-flight data while managing complex operational conditions.

synopsis: A CE-560 First Officer reported the right brake failed briefly during taxi, veered left but the crew stopped the aircraft. This is the fifth maintenance write up for the same issue.
summary: The pilot reported a right brake failure during taxi to the departure runway, causing the aircraft to veer left before stopping. This recurring issue, logged five times in 13 days, prompted the crew to demand immediate repairs to prevent further incidents.

synopsis: An A321 FMGC dumped the primary and secondary routes when the Captain selected an RNAV Visual 13R in the Secondary Flight Plan while the First Officer was flying the VOR 13L in the Primary Flight Plan. They were able to partially recover before landing.
summary: During a visual approach to Rwy XXL, an FMGC database dump occurred when the FO attempted to load the approach, causing navigation loss and subsequent APP mode failure. This led to manual thrust control, a brief destabilization below 500 feet with a GPWS sink warning, and an uneventful landing.

synopsis: A flight crew changed the FMC NAV DATABASE on XA00Z SEP to the next month which changed the PHX arrival to EAGUL 6 but the Company had filed the PHX EAGUL 5 arrival with the previous calendar day's date. ATC caught the error over GEENO because of a crossing restricting difference.
summary: The flight crew departed Phoenix with an FMC programmed for the EAGUL6 arrival instead of the filed EAGUL5 due to a JeppTC mid-cycle database update. This caused an altitude restriction mismatch at the GEENO waypoint, requiring ATC to issue lateral separation and vectors to final approach.

synopsis: An A300 Captain spilled coffee on the center pedestal and caused a loss of all communication.
summary: Crew spilled coffee on the ADF and VHF #2 panels during cruise, causing VHF #2 failure and subsequent VHF #1 deterioration during descent. The flight crew used transponder code 7600, ACARS, and a cell phone to coordinate a visual approach and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: A CRJ-200's flaps auto extended to near flaps 8 at FL260 which caused a pitch up and an altitude gain. Maintenance found no overspeed damage but the crew refused the aircraft for their next flight.
summary: During cruise at FL260, the flight crew experienced uncommanded flap extension and gear indications, causing a 400-foot altitude deviation requiring manual control. Maintenance found no immediate cause, leading to an aircraft swap and cancellation of the day's flying due to unresolved safety concerns regarding the deployment.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported wake turbulence encounter in trail of an MD80 on approach to DTW that resulted in a 25-degree roll and a 'sudden downward push'.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe wake turbulence from an MD-80 while on final approach to DTW Runway 22R, causing a sudden downward push and 25-degree bank. The crew initiated a go-around, attributing the event to ATC's close spacing and a light tailwind.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports being zapped by a green laser at 8,000 feet while on vectors to the ILS 36 at SEQU. After landing, a turn off on to the wrong taxiway is initiated due to poor signage lighting and effects from the laser on vision.
summary: A pilot on an ILS 36 approach experienced a 30-second green laser event causing partial visual impairment. This vision loss, combined with poor signage lighting, led to an inadvertent turn onto taxiway J instead of H after landing.

synopsis: B737 flight crew experiences a TCAS RA at FL350, 16 NM north of DUSLO Intersection on UB753. A climb is initiated in compliance with the RA and the event reported to Merida Center.
summary: The crew of a flight at FL350 north of DUSLO received a TCAS climb resolution advisory due to converging traffic climbing into their altitude without prior ATC notice. They executed a climb to 35,520 feet to clear the conflict, then returned to FL350 after ATC acknowledged the situation without explanation.

synopsis: B777 First Officer is informed during preflight by the relief pilot that charts for primary destinations are missing from the shipset. A call to the Duty Manager reveals that the paper charts have been removed and iPads will be the primary method of storing and displaying charts.
summary: During preflight, a relief pilot discovered missing destination charts in his ship set due to a company bulletin removing them. The reporter argues this modification marginalizes the relief pilot's critical safety role during ground operations below 10,000 feet where iPads are restricted.

synopsis: A320 Captain describes a track deviation that ensues when ATC clears the flight direct to SEEVR and changes the arrival from the BRDJE 1 RNAV to the SEEVR 1 RNAV approaching DFW. Without being aware of the SEEVR 1 the crew believes that the BRDJE 1 is correct since SEEVR is part of it.
summary: The flight crew, distracted by an in-flight medical emergency, inadvertently flew the SEEVR.BRDJE1 arrival instead of the correct SEEVR.SEEVR1 at DFW due to missing a flow-direction note on the chart. Air Traffic Control vectored them back to the correct path, attributing the error to fatigue and confusing arrival naming conventions.

synopsis: A319 Captain reports refusing an aircraft after the previous crew reported the number one engine exceeding 610 degrees during climb with the EGT gauge pulsing amber and the fuel flow 500 pounds per hour higher than the number two engine.
summary: The outbound Captain refused the aircraft for a flight to ZZZ1 due to inbound reports of #1 engine EGT exceeding 610 degrees, high fuel flow, and maximum oil pressure. Line maintenance noted the #1 engine had 20,308 hours, leading the crew to reject the flight due to discomfort with the engine's condition.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 departed JFK and was level at 5,000 feet on a vector when a Controller alerted about VFR traffic at 5,500 feet. The VFR traffic descends unexpectedly causing a TCAS RA and a near miss.
summary: The First Officer reported a TCAS conflict during the JFK departure phase while climbing at 5,000 feet. A VFR Piper Cherokee descended from 5,500 feet to within 200–300 feet vertically, forcing the crew to manually descend to 4,300 feet to avoid collision.

synopsis: Air Cargo First Officer describes an attempt to taxi out of the parking spot, forgetting that the Mechanic is still below the aircraft on the headset, waiting for the 'cleared to disconnect' command. The aircraft is quickly stopped and no injuries occur.
summary: The flight crew initiated a power-out taxi at SGF before the mechanic was clear, rolling a foot or two due to inattention to the non-standard procedure. The captain stopped immediately upon the mechanic's warning, apologized, and the aircraft departed uneventfully after the marshaller guided it out.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reports the aircraft not tracking the desired course to the next waypoint on NAT E and heading is adjusted manually. While visible on the ND the next waypoint is not on the legs page and is not reported as the next waypoint to Shanwick via CPDLC. The missing waypoint is reentered and the crossing continued without further difficulties.
summary: Pilots flying an aircraft in LNAV through RESNO into NAT E found the 20 West waypoint missing from the legs page and the CPDLC report incorrect. They manually re-installed the waypoint and selected heading to maintain track, noting the error occurred despite correct pre-entry checks.

synopsis: B757 First Officer reports being unable to use the ACARS during preflight to initialize the FMC and obtain the flight plan and winds. Maintenance defers the ACARS and the flight departs. Approaching Moncton airspace CPDLC would not log on and when trying to get the Oceanic clearance it returned the message AIRCRAFT REGISTRATION ERROR. It is discovered that the N number on the flight plan does not match the number of the aircraft they are in.
summary: The pilot reported that an ACARS defect and a flight plan containing a different aircraft registration caused CPDLC and oceanic clearance failures during cruise. Dispatch corrected the registration error, allowing the flight to continue normally, though the pilot attributed the oversight to similar N-numbers and manual workarounds.

synopsis: Pilot reports of a close call with another aircraft. The other aircraft is not displayed on the TCAS, and possibly not on the Controller's radar system, because the Controller never issued traffic.
summary: The pilot monitoring spotted a climbing Aircraft Y while receiving a heading 200 clearance from an approach controller at 4,000 feet. The controller aggressively ordered the turn despite the conflict, but Aircraft Y executed a hard descending turn to avoid a collision, allowing the flight to safely join the ILS 18L.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reports damage to the left winglet during attempt to taxi out of a gate after the push back fails due to a bent tow bar. The flight is cancelled.
summary: The pilot attempted a nonstandard taxi-out due to a bent towbar and missing ground crew, striking the jet bridge with the left winglet during a tight turn. The collision occurred because the wingwalker was out of sight and the marshaller lacked wands, resulting in flight cancellation and damage.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports a go-around during landing due wake turbulence from a heavy jet departing the adjacent runway. During the second approach there is miscommunication and confusion about the assigned runway for landing and the Tower issues a side step to 28R at the last minute.
summary: During a training flight at SFO, the crew encountered wake turbulence and executed a go-around, followed by a runway clearance confusion between 28L and 28R caused by a missing data block entry from Approach. The crew ultimately sidestepped to land safely on 28R after the Tower Supervisor confirmed the communication error.

synopsis: PA32 pilot inbound to Chena Marina reports a NMAC with a Helio Courier departing FAI Runway 2R at 1500 FT. The PA32 pilot was Radar identified and talking to FAI Tower but neither pilot received a traffic advisory until evasive action had been taken by the PA32 pilot.
summary: A pilot flying a Cherokee repositioning to Chena Marina encountered a converging Helio Courier departing Fairbanks International at 1,500 feet due to delayed Approach-to-Tower handoff and lack of traffic advisories. The pilot executed a left turn to avoid a collision, attributing the near-miss to limited visibility and late controller coordination.

synopsis: PA24 pilot experiences engine failure at 400 feet AGL and lands on the runway remaining, resulting in a runway excursion and damage to the wing and left landing gear. Fuel exhaustion was thought to be the cause as the left main tank was dry.
summary: The pilot and passenger experienced a total power loss at 400 feet AGL during takeoff, likely caused by running the left main fuel tank dry. They executed a hard landing straight ahead, departing the runway into soft soil with left main gear damage but no injuries.

synopsis: When the C-172's taxi lights failed during runup the pilot requested progressive taxi back to the FBO. While enroute the propeller struck an unlit pylon while on a taxiway as directed by the Controller. The aircraft was towed back to the FBO.
summary: The pilot taxiing to holding line 36 struck an unlit restricted pylon while following Ground Control directions, causing substantial propeller damage. The flight was cancelled, and the aircraft was towed back to the FBO.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reported encountering wake turbulence in trail of a B757 departing ATL that resulted in a ten-degree roll.
summary: The pilot flying encountered wake turbulence from a preceding B757 at 1,000 feet AGL during the RNAV DAWGS departure from Runway 27R. The aircraft rolled 10 degrees, which the pilot corrected with opposite aileron input, and the flight continued without notifying ATC.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Pilot under flight following is advised he has violated a Tower's airspace. Pilot is confused and thought ATC would take care of the issue of the point out.
summary: A pilot on flight following to PAO was advised by ATC to contact LVK Tower after entering their airspace, though the tower preferred initial contact before transit. The pilot realized the need to communicate with the controlling facility for the specific airspace and plans to route around or climb over Class D airspace in the future to reduce workload.

synopsis: C172 instructor describes an incident with his student departing on his first solo cross country flight YIP. After taxiing via Taxiway C the student is cleared for takeoff on Runway 5L from Taxiway C but turns right and takes off on Runway 23R.
summary: A student pilot on a solo cross-country flight at Willow Run Airport mistakenly took off on Runway 23R instead of the cleared Runway 5L after turning the wrong direction. The tower controller immediately cleared the student for Runway 23R, and the instructor noted the error resulted from failing to verify runway direction with a compass or heading indicator.

synopsis: CE550 Captain is informed of smoke in the cabin by passengers and the right seat pilot at FL210. Difficulty is encountered donning and communicating with oxygen masks on but eventually ATC is informed and a descent is requested. The Checklist for Environmental Smoke is accomplished and the recirculation fan is turned off which seems to be the culprit. Flight diverts to a suitable airport for an overweight landing.
summary: During cruise at FL210, the flight crew detected a strong smoke smell and requested an immediate descent after experiencing communication difficulties with oxygen masks. They diverted to ZZZ for an uneventful overweight landing, with maintenance inspecting the aircraft for the smoke source.

synopsis: C172 Flight Instructor with student on V94 at 6,500 FT, reports a NMAC with skydivers over E60 airport. The reporter had been monitoring the CTAF for E60 and heard no calls for jumpers away.
summary: A flight instructor and student practicing on V94 at 6,500 feet spotted two jumpers with patrons off the wing after receiving no jump advisories on E60 CTAF. The pilot took immediate evasive action, citing major parachute operations in the student practice area as a rising safety issue.

synopsis: C182 pilot on a visual approach, experiences an NMAC with another Cessna at about 100 FT AGL as the second Cessna overtook and passed beneath the reporters aircraft then went around. The reporter also went around.
summary: A pilot executing a VFR landing at ZZZ experienced a near mid-air collision with a Cessna performing an ILS missed approach at 80–120 feet AGL. The reporter attributes the incident to the other pilot failing to see the traffic while under the hood and violating right-of-way rules by overtaking in the pattern.

synopsis: SFO Local Controller reports of two aircraft that were a loss of separation in NCT's airspace. Controller gave more than minimum distance between the aircraft and more then 1,000 FT of separation. NCT Controller reports of a loss of separation on departure between two aircraft that should have been 7 miles apart opposed to 3 miles for same fix separation.
summary: SFO Tower cleared Aircraft X and Y for takeoff, resulting in a loss of separation that Norcal TRACON observed while managing the departures. The reporter attributes the incident to SFO's failure to account for aircraft performance and LOA spacing requirements, recommending improved training and visual spacing tools.

synopsis: ZNY Oceanic Controller is advised that a flight needs to deviate for weather. Controller sends information that deviation is approved at FL370 or FL390. Aircraft is at FL380 and deviates prior to receiving message and is a conflict for another aircraft at FL380.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft X to deviate west for weather at FL370 or FL390, but the pilot began the maneuver without clearance. The controller subsequently issued an immediate descent to FL370 after ATOP failed to generate an alert despite diminishing separation with another flight.

synopsis: D10 controller describes a flight that he descends and ships to another sector. The aircraft clips the corner of a non pointed-out airspace. The Controller has pre-arraigned coordinated use of that airspace, but did not realize the aircraft was going to enter said airspace during the arrival.
summary: A Dallas East controller reported that an aircraft on the new TRYST1 RNAV arrival clipped DR1 airspace because the controller did not execute required pre-arranged coordination steps. The controller attributed the incident to the arrival design, which forces airspace violations unless the aircraft is vectored off the procedure.

synopsis: ZLA controller describes a situation that is ongoing where VFR aircraft worked by another facility are going through arrival aircraft flight path.
summary: The controller descended Aircraft X and Y under LOA with L30 but halted traffic after Nellis identified VFR Aircraft Z and W ignoring commands near FYTTR. This forced the controller to request a LOA violation for their arrivals due to military aircraft cutting through the arrival stream.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ZHU Controller describes a situation where he thought an undirected handoff was incorrect. The Controller took the handoff back and directed it to what he/she thought was the correct area. Controller later finds out other facilities airspace had changed, which resulted in an airspace deviation.
summary: An air traffic controller inadvertently allowed a westbound aircraft at flight level 060 to enter the I90 DAS sector without a handoff due to an undirected flash caused by a recent airspace floor reduction. The controller attributed the error to failing to review the updated sector map before the transfer.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew describes an unstabilized approach that results from a late runway change from Runway 25L to Runway 19R at LAS. The go-around is commenced above 4,000 FT but insufficient thrust is added and the stick shaker is activated. With more thrust and lowering the nose, the stick shaker is silenced and the next visual approach is successful.
summary: Pilots flying a jet into LAS experienced a stick shaker warning during a visual approach to Runway 19R after late runway changes and high-altitude maneuvers. The event occurred when autothrottles failed to maintain airspeed during a flap extension, causing a pitch-up and speed decay that required manual intervention to recover.

synopsis: Noting weather west of MCO, B737 flight crew requests an alternate from their Dispatcher and additional fuel. The Dispatcher states the weather is stationary and the forecast is good, so no additional fuel. Upon arrival there are thunderstorms in all quadrants and the Captain elects to land with a tailwind greater than 10 knots rather than go-around with minimum fuel.
summary: Pilots departed MCO without an alternate or extra fuel after Dispatch assured them weather would not impact the area. Upon arrival, they encountered storms and fluctuating tailwinds, forcing a landing with low fuel to avoid a critical situation while the airport switched runways.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew experiences a rapid change in visibility to below Cat I minimums during taxi out for takeoff. The requirements for the low visibility takeoff are discussed but the crew forgets to request a takeoff alternate from Dispatch.
summary: The Captain and First Officer departed an aircraft in reduced visibility (RVR 800) without a required takeoff alternate. The omission occurred because the crew overlooked the regulatory requirement triggered by the rapid weather change during taxi and departure.

synopsis: Dispatcher reports missing a NOTAM establishing restricted airspace over the Pacific Ocean east of Guam and plans a flight through the area. Ninety minutes into the flight the Dispatcher is contacted by the crew, reporting that ATC has issued a reroute around the area. This area was not active in the Sabre flight planning software.
summary: A dispatcher missed a NOTAM regarding Valiant Shield 14 airspace restrictions and filed a flight plan through the closed area. The crew received an ATC reroute approximately 90 minutes into the flight, and the flight was redispatched to avoid the restricted airspace.

synopsis: When the flight crew of an A320 misinterpreted ATC's 'climb via except maintain 16,000 FT' clearance they had already exceeded 5,000 FT prior to passing DWSUN which must be crossed at or below 5,000 FT.
summary: Pilots on an IAH departure misinterpreted a clearance to climb via the SID except maintain 16,000 FT, removing the DWSUN 5,000 FT restriction from the FMS and crossing the intersection high. The crew attributed the error to high task loading and noted they should have queried ATC before entering the change.

synopsis: An aircraft departed EDDP filed on the NAMUB 2S but ATC stated they should have been flying the ODLUN 2S and so issue that change to them.
summary: Pilots at EDDP received conflicting departure clearances, flying the ODLUN2S instead of the filed NAMUB2S due to a language barrier and radio congestion. The crew flew 75 NM off-route before the controller corrected the error, prompting the pilot to insist on phonetic readbacks for future clearances.

synopsis: A MD-80 Captain checked the Takeoff Configuration Warning with no response during taxi out but at about 110 KTS the SLAT DISAGREE and Takeoff Configuration Warning alerted so the Captain rejected the takeoff then returned to the gate for maintenance and brake cooling.
summary: The pilot rejected takeoff at 110 kts due to a late takeoff configuration warning and slat disagree light. The reporter concluded the warning was likely false, suggesting continuing the takeoff would have been the better choice per company procedures.

synopsis: CRJ200 First Officer reports lining up with the wrong runway while attempting a visual approach to Runway 9 at SWF. The NDB at the FAF and the Runway 9 localizer were being used as aids and the localizer does not indicate correct alignment. A go-around is initiated.
summary: The crew initiated a go-around during a visual approach to Runway 9 at SWF after noticing the localizer was not centered and the runway appeared incorrect. The reporter attributed the confusion to the ADF coincidentally pointing to the Final Approach Fix of the wrong runway.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot reports of confusion of which arrival to fly into their destination because controllers changed it a few times.
summary: Pilots reported confusion during handoffs while en route to Houston on the RIICE SEVEN arrival, where multiple controllers issued vectors to fixes not on the assigned procedure. The crew had to repeatedly clarify their arrival, resulting in a delayed descent clearance until they were finally vectored for the approach.

synopsis: A newly minted Private Pilot on a cross country to HSV lined up on closed Runway 36R vice Runway 36L for landing. The Tower intervened and appropriate advisories and course adjustments prevented an incident.
summary: The pilot, while on final approach to runway 36R, was alerted by Tower that the runway was closed and they were actually cleared for 36L. The incident resulted from the pilot's failure to draw the parallel closed runway on their flight log, leading to incorrect runway identification and a subsequent go-around to land on 36L.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A VFR pilot with flight following was handed off from PDX TRACON to HIO Tower but was unable to establish communications and, thinking he had clearance entered HIO airspace, but was later advised he had violated Class D.
summary: A VFR pilot penetrating Hillsboro Class D airspace reported being ignored by Tower after a Portland Approach handoff. The pilot realized the transfer was not a formal handoff, resulting in an unauthorized airspace entry and a subsequent deviation report.

synopsis: While lined up and waiting on Runway 7L at LAS Tower cleared an EMB-135 to taxi forward to A-8. As they approached Runway 1R the First Officer noted traffic on short final and shouted a warning to the Captain who managed to stop in a timely fashion.
summary: Pilots at LAS reported confusion after ATC issued nonstandard instructions to taxi on Runway 7L while another aircraft took off from an intersection. The crew stopped upon spotting an unannounced aircraft on short final for Runway 1R before receiving clearance for immediate takeoff from their present position.

aircraft: Bellanca Aircraft Corp Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An unusual short term vibration from the tailwheel of high wing LSA during landing practice an another airport was a harbinger of the eventual failure of directional control upon landing, concluding with a ground loop back at the home airport.
summary: The pilot experienced a tailwheel vibration during practice landings, followed by a ground loop and severe left-turning tendency on the home airport runway due to a non-steerable tailwheel. The aircraft was recovered with FBO assistance and taxied to the hangar using brake control, with no damage or injuries reported.

synopsis: The instructor and student pilots aboard a C172 IFR training flight in IMC encountered apparent icing induced loss of airspeed indication along with inexplicable low fuel quantity warnings while enroute. Airspeed indications returned to normal after leaving IMC and post flight maintenance determined both tanks contained significant amounts of fuel, totaling nearly 20 gallons.
summary: During night cross-country training in IMC, the pilot and student experienced a false low fuel warning and a pitot tube blockage causing zero airspeed indication. The pilot activated pitot heat, landed safely, and post-flight inspections confirmed adequate fuel and no defects, attributing the airspeed loss to stray ice.

synopsis: Reporter encountered a deer during landing rollout, causing minor damage to his aircraft. He has become concerned over the wildlife program at this airport since he continues to see deer in the area.
summary: The pilot reported striking a deer with the right wing during the landing roll at Taunton Airport (TAN) at night, causing skin damage. The pilot attributes the incident to inadequate fencing and frequent deer presence on the airfield, deeming the airport unsafe.

synopsis: Pilot gets notification by a ground observer who reports the flight to the FAA that their flight went over a nuclear power point. No restrictions were to be found not allowing the pilot to do so.
summary: A helicopter pilot overflew the Mcquire nuclear power plant while climbing to 1600 feet MSL to avoid Charlotte Class B airspace. An FAA inspector contacted the pilot to report the incident but confirmed no charted restrictions exist for operations near the facility.

synopsis: TBM850 instructor and student plan and request a practice emergency descent from ATC, starting from FL280. Oxygen mask noise prevents proper communication with ATC and the descent is initiated without approval.
summary: During TBM 850 recurrent training, a student and instructor initiated a simulated emergency descent from FL280 after the instructor's oxygen mask microphone failed to transmit their request to ATC. ATC questioned the unauthorized descent, forcing the crew to level off, clarify the equipment failure, and obtain proper clearance before completing the maneuver.

synopsis: While departing on a maintenance test flight the flight crew of a LJ-35 experienced the loss of the right avionics cowling which was held against the windshield by the airflow until after landing when the aircraft slowed and it fell off and was run over by the left main wheels. The emergency airbrakes had been serviced via the missing cowling and the Mechanic had failed to secure the retention screws. Fatigue due to continuous shift duties by the Mechanic was cited as a contributing factor.
summary: A mechanic servicing emergency air forgot to tighten right avionics cowl fasteners, causing the cover to dislodge during takeoff. The crew executed an emergency landing with flaps 8 and gear down, but the cowl was run over by the left main gear upon stopping.

synopsis: News helicopter pilot reports being illuminated by an individual in in a high school football stadium. The Sheriff is notified and with the help of the news crew, the perpetrators are identified and apprehended, however no laser pointer is found on their persons.
summary: A news helicopter pilot covering a football game was illuminated by a green laser from the stadium for over two hours. ATC coordinated with the Sheriff's Office, which used a captured laser image to identify and detain suspects, though they were released without the laser found.

synopsis: BE90 instructor pilot experiences a NMAC with a black helicopter hovering over a freshly paved runway. The helicopter did not respond to CTAF calls and was invisible until the BE90 was in the flare. The instructor takes control and pulls up and turns, narrowly missing the helicopter.
summary: A King Air 90 instructor and student conducting a practice ILS approach encountered a stationary, dark-painted Robinson helicopter on the runway threshold at 50 feet AGL. The helicopter pilot failed to communicate or acknowledge CTAF calls, forcing the instructor to execute an emergency go-around to avoid a collision.

synopsis: C172 pilot reports narrowly avoiding an FBO fuel truck that enters the runway while the reporter is taking off. The takeoff is rejected. The driver stated he had forgotten his handheld VHF and did not see the departing C172 until too late to stop.
summary: A pilot aborted a takeoff from runway 29 after an airport fuel truck crossed the hold short line without hearing CTAF calls due to a forgotten radio. The pilot stopped safely 100 feet from the intersection, and the truck driver later admitted he did not see the aircraft until entering the runway.

aircraft: Cessna Aircraft Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A small aircraft flight crew flew at 9,500 FT near the Solar Generating Station and experienced a light similar to a welder's arc, which reflected from the tower itself was blinding 360 degrees for twenty miles.
summary: The pilot and crew reported that blinding glare from a Solar Generating Station south of Las Vegas, NV, caused eye pain similar to snow blindness despite wearing sunglasses. The crew agreed with NOTAMs that the facility's 360-degree bright lights pose a hazard to aviation.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: CLT Local Controller reports of a runway conflict and runway incursion with a vehicle and a departing aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft X for takeoff on Runway 36R while a vehicle entered the runway for inspection, triggering an ASD-X warning. The controller did not cancel the takeoff as the aircraft was rotating and the vehicle was clearing the runway, prompting a recommendation to install Runway Status Lights.

synopsis: A B737NG pilot reported difficulty complying with crossing restrictions on the WHINY RNAV STAR to DFW.
summary: Pilots flying a Whiny 1 RNAV arrival into DFW reported the aircraft accelerated despite full speed brakes while on LNAV/VNAV between VANCO and BERMS. The crew attributed the issue to a tight crossing constraint of 250 knots at 2,000 feet and requested a redesign of the intersection for greater flexibility.

synopsis: A pilot reported that DFW chart 61-19 dated 12 Sept 2014 does not depict GPM and situational awareness about the Class D airspace would be enhanced if airport were depicted.
summary: The crew descended to 2,300 feet for a visual approach to Runway 36L and landed without traffic or low altitude alerts. They noted Grand Prairie Airport was not depicted on the Runway 36L approach chart, though it appears on the Runway 35R chart.

synopsis: CRJ200 flight crew reports smoke filling the cabin and cockpit after the second engine is started, with the APU bleed supplying the packs. The packs are switched to the engines as the APU EGT is pegged in the red and CFR is called. With little improvement the Captain orders an evacuation, possibly after the passengers have self initiated.
summary: During taxi out after the second engine start, an APU overheat caused heavy smoke and a fire report in the cabin, prompting the crew to evacuate the aircraft. Passengers exited via stairs and overwing exits with assistance from additional crew, resulting in no injuries.

synopsis: A flight attendant, unaware her normal jumpseat was deferred and not usable, used it for an initial flight and was only briefed as to its status prior to a subsequent departure.
summary: A flight attendant failed to identify an inoperative aft center jumpseat during preflight due to an obscured sticker and lack of briefing. Consequently, the attendant occupied the ACM jumpseat while a non-revenue passenger incorrectly sat in the ACM seat instead of the aft center position.

synopsis: A C172 pilot was confused approaching DAL when the landing direction was not as expected. Runway 13R was requested and clearance granted when the pilot actually intended and lined up for 13L. Tower revised clearance to land on Runway 13L on short final.
summary: The pilot landed on runway 13L at DAL after a miscommunication with approach and tower controllers regarding the requested runway. The pilot attributed the error to disorientation caused by unexpected vectoring and anticipating a landing on runway 31R based on wind conditions.

synopsis: A Twin Comanche pilot became task saturated during an IMC arrival to DAL and was directed to go-around by ATC when he failed to capture the 13L localizer as cleared. Heavy radio traffic, a fast talking controller and difficulty accessing the correct approach page from his electronic tablet were cited as contributing factors.
summary: A pilot on left downwind in IMC at 3000' missed the localizer while searching for the ILS 13L chart on an iPad during rapid instructions from a fast-talking controller. The pilot broke off the approach, but a second attempt with a slower-speaking controller and the correct chart resulted in a successful landing.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Recip Eng
synopsis: Pilot asked for, and received a clearance to cross another Tower's airport mid-field, prior to departure. As the pilot tries to get a frequency change, the controller is busy and pilot switches to new frequency by himself. New Tower Controller holds aircraft out of airspace for a few minutes, then clears pilot through, as requested earlier.
summary: A pilot departing Montgomery (KMYF) on a coordinated transition to Mid-Field Miramar (KNKX) received a "hold position" command from Miramar Tower while at 2900 MSL. To avoid entering Class B airspace, the pilot executed a steep right turn and held a westerly heading until clearance was granted, questioning why the coordinated transition was not properly managed.

synopsis: A PA-28 pilot reported a near miss at 3,000 FT with an unmanned vehicle while descending to his destination in Class B airspace. The FAA was notified and recorded the event.
summary: A pilot flying VFR with one passenger encountered a red and silver unmanned aerial vehicle at 3,000 feet, passing 50-100 feet off the left wing tip during descent. The pilot reported the incident to Approach Control and subsequently filed an FAA near-miss report.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reports inadvertently entering a stadium TFR which had apparently been extended and did not show up on Sky Vector.
summary: The pilot flew a Cessna with two passengers near Stanford Stadium at 2,400 feet, believing a TFR had ended. The pilot deviated from the restricted area because the game was extended into overtime, a status not reflected in pre-flight TFR checks.

synopsis: BE400 Flight Crew reports not noting the altitude limit of 10000 feet on the BLECO 6 RNAV departure from DFW, which is located in the routing box at the bottom of the chart. The crew levels at YAMEL at 5000 feet and is admonished by ATC.
summary: The flight crew incorrectly leveled at 5,000 feet during the BLECO 6 RNAV SID departure from DFW due to relying on a prior flight's clearance and missing the textual 10,000-foot top altitude on the chart. Departure control corrected the error, prompting a continued climb with no traffic conflicts.

synopsis: An MD-80 Captain strongly asserts that arrivals (RNAV STARs) in DFW are '...out of control' and provides examples of ATC alterations to them that have made his tasks more difficult rather than safer and more efficient. He further advises. 'You gotta be a lawyer to understand the whole 'via' thing.' Less than state of the art autoflight tools on his aircraft were cited as a contributing factor.
summary: A pilot reported unsafe arrival procedures at DFW involving conflicting altitude and speed clearances, runway changes, and excessive vectors. The reporter attributed the risk to antiquated aircraft equipment and unrealistic STAR designs created by personnel not operating in real-world conditions.

synopsis: An Approach Controller addressed his concern that the tracks of non-FMS equipped aircraft utilizing the YEAGR (Non RNAV) STAR (via a 310 heading from YEAGR) are insufficiently precise to avoid traffic conflicts with other controller's airspace as they approach the airport.
