summary: An instructor and student held short of Runway 25 at Merrill Field but entered the runway after the student dialed the wrong frequency, 126.8 instead of 126.0. This caused an aircraft on final to go around, which the reporter attributes to the frequency error and poor aircraft positioning.

synopsis: M20 pilot experiences three go-arounds due to his inability to get the aircraft to slow to landing speed. On the fourth attempt the mixture is pulled on short final and a normal landing ensues. The throttle cable was found disconnected from the fuel control lever.
summary: The pilot executed four go-arounds due to an inability to slow the aircraft, caused by a disconnected throttle cable Heim bearing. The missing fastening bolt and hardware rendered the throttle ineffective, forcing the pilot to use the mixture control to land and taxi.

synopsis: SDF Approach Controller has a loss of separation when an aircraft on final over takes another.
summary: An air traffic controller at SDF lost separation between two jets during a busy night arrival sequence due to fatigue from working consecutive midnight shifts. The controller failed to monitor the trailing aircraft's position after reassigning it to a different sector, resulting in the loss of required spacing.

synopsis: Tower describes a situation where he is talking to a helicopter and in lands off the airport in an emergency situation.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared a helicopter into ZZZ Class B airspace near ZZZ1 airport before the pilot declared a mayday and reported going down. The pilot later confirmed a safe landing with no injuries, stating maintenance would be contacted, though the controller filed the event as a potential accident due to unknown aircraft condition.

synopsis: LHD and MRI Controller's report of an aircraft at MRI airport on the ground, talking to LHD Controller's asking for takeoff clearance. LHD Controller clears aircraft for takeoff and at MRI the Controller sends an aircraft around because the aircraft was close to the runway.
summary: A student pilot in Aircraft X confused LHD and MRI tower frequencies, causing a takeoff clearance error and a runway incursion where Aircraft Z had to go around. The pilot later departed without clearance while communicating with the wrong tower, forcing other traffic to maneuver to avoid a conflict.

synopsis: ZHU Controller describes problems with various aircraft inbound to IAH that are not clear with a NOTAM that has speed restrictions on it that relate to a STAR for IAH.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a turbojet pilot on the Tejas2 RNAV arrival into IAH maintained 300 knots instead of the NOTAM-mandated 280 knots, claiming the restriction applied only after transitioning to IAS. The controller noted this dispute caused unnecessary frequency congestion and recommended moving the speed restriction from the NOTAM to the published STAR.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reported wake encounter departing ATL in trail of an MD-80 that resulted in two low altitude 20-degree rolls.
summary: The crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding MD-80 shortly after takeoff on 26L, causing two uncommanded 20-degree bank rolls between 300 and 2,000 feet AGL. The Captain corrected the aircraft, and the First Officer reported the incident to Atlanta Tower, noting concerns regarding low-altitude wake turbulence under new re-categorization standards.

synopsis: A320 Captain reports not noting the fact that the JAGUAR4 Departure from MCO has a second page containing the initial climb and routing information.
summary: The pilot and first officer misinterpreted the JAGUAR 4 SID by missing a small print note indicating a second page, leading them to incorrectly conclude the altitude was 18,000 feet. The reporter suggests consolidating the chart pages or enlarging the text to prevent future errors.

synopsis: While preparing for the before start checklist, a B737 Captain reports only turning on one center tank fuel pump. This is not detected by either pilot during the checklist and the flight departs in that condition. An impending fuel imbalance is detected during climb and several minutes pass before the cause is detected and corrected.
summary: The Captain missed turning on the right center tank fuel pump during the before engine start checklist due to visual confusion with a nearby switch. This caused a fuel imbalance during climb, prompting an emergency declaration and return to Airport ZZZ until the pump was activated and fuel feed normalized.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports landing with a flap setting of 25 due to strong gusty winds which is contrary to the company's authorized landing flap settings. Low time for both pilots in the aircraft, ATC issues and weather were cited as factors in the incident.
summary: A new Captain and First Officer in a B-737 landed with Flaps 25 due to the Captain applying outdated procedures from previous aircraft types during gusty crosswinds. The crew failed to recognize that Flaps 25 is not an authorized landing configuration for the 737, resulting in a hot landing and a missed opportunity for a go-around.

synopsis: A321 flight crew reported three wake encounters on climbout in trail of a B777-200 that induced roll and prompted the crew to deviate from the assigned course.
summary: An A321 climbing above 10,000 feet on the HOLTZ 9 departure encountered four wake turbulence events while trailing a B777-200, causing large roll variations. The pilot deviated from the assigned track and required alternate ATC headings, noting the A321 cannot outclimb heavy jets on the same route.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Cessna pilot reports a NMAC in the traffic pattern at APA requiring evasive action. The traffic landing ahead of the reporter does not clear the runway after landing requiring a go-around. The traffic on the runway, the traffic for the parallel runway and the traffic for the crossing runway were all cited as conflicts during the go-around.
summary: A pilot inbound to Centennial Airport experienced a near mid-air collision with a high-wing tail dragger on a conflicting touch-and-go pattern and a runway incursion caused by a preceding aircraft stopping and reversing. The pilot attributed these events to poor tower traffic management and inappropriate clearance of cross-runway operations.

synopsis: C182 pilot, on takeoff roll, sights a PC12 entering the runway down field and rejects the takeoff. No reports had been heard on the CTAF from the PC12 pilot, but he did apologize after the incident.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff on Runway XY after a Pilatus entered the runway without CTAF communication or lights, forcing a stop 1,500 feet from the intruder. The incident caused a Piper to abort its landing, but no damage occurred, and the crew eventually departed normally after the Pilatus exited.

synopsis: After being issued a descend via the ENDEE 3 except maintain 11,000, a CE560 Captain is issued a Runway 31C transition via GAGGA by Approach. Without the altitude being mentioned or modified the Captain levels at 11,000 FT and is queried by ATC as to why.
summary: A pilot flying an ENDEE THREE arrival into MDW reported confusion after Approach Control modified a Descend Via clearance without explicitly canceling a previous "maintain 11000" restriction. The pilot noted that omitting the restriction from the new clearance caused ambiguity regarding crossing altitudes, suggesting clearer phraseology is needed to prevent communication errors.

synopsis: A small aircraft pilot failed to contact PHX Tower before transitioning through their Class B airspace while on a VFR flight plan. The pilot did not have the PHX frequency available after their GPS unit failed and the sectional fell in an unreachable location.
summary: A pilot en route from SDL to CHD experienced a GPS failure and lost access to sectional charts due to turbulence. Unable to contact PHX Tower regarding an airspace deviation, the pilot continued on the last known heading and altitude, later admitting they should have requested the FFZ frequency and diverted east.

synopsis: ZDV Controller reports of confusion from a briefing he received on whether an aircraft is VFR or IFR. He treated the aircraft as VFR while the aircraft was actually IFR.
summary: An air traffic controller in sectors 31/32 was not briefed that a VFR aircraft intended to pick up an IFR flight plan after exiting an MOA. The ZMP controller failed to coordinate this change or confirm the clearance, causing a data block discrepancy until the pilot informed Sector 19 of his IFR status.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: ZSE controller reports of an aircraft that is cleared for an approach but descends below the MEA.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a Low Altitude Alert to Aircraft X after it descended below the MEA of 120 while on the V120 airway following a "cleared for approach" clearance. The pilot eventually climbed back to 120, an incident the controller attributed to pilot complacency regarding descent rules and potential GPS fixation.

synopsis: HCF TMU Controller reports failing to note the active status of W-188 until queried by another Controller about a target at FL350 in the Warning Area. PMRF is contacted and the target is identified as a UAV. Multiple faxes from PMRF changing the active times resulted in the oversight.
summary: An air traffic controller failed to update the SIA board regarding active W-188/RAINBOW airspace, causing a C17 inbound to HNL to transit the area without proper coordination. The controller corrected the oversight after discovering a missed schedule fax and obtained a point-out from PMRF for the UAV.

synopsis: ERJ170 flight crew, distracted by a concern for clearing the gate for an incoming aircraft, failed to contact Ground Control prior to commencing taxi.
summary: The flight crew taxied onto the runway without clearance after mistakenly believing they had contacted ATC while running a checklist to avoid delaying another aircraft. This error resulted from complacency and misinterpreting a tower frequency call as taxi instructions, though the crew stopped safely after crossing the non-movement area line.

synopsis: A321 First Officer experiences the failure of the Blue hydraulic pump during climb passing FL240. After consultation with the company the crew elects to divert to a suitable airport.
summary: During climb at 24,000 feet, a blue hydraulic electric pump overheat message appeared, leading to zero pressure and degraded flight controls despite troubleshooting. The crew declared an emergency and diverted due to unrecoverable system redundancy, landing safely before maintenance identified a seized pump.

synopsis: 'Descending via' the KLNDR RNAV STAR to DFW without benefit of autoflight NVAV capability the flight crew of an E145 descended through the required 11,000 FT prior to DIETZ and received a TCAS TA and an alert from ATC to return to 11,000 FT. The lack of autoflight VNAV capability, and the non-user-friendly location of the single FMS control head were cited as contributing factors.
summary: The Captain and First Officer descended below 11,000 feet on the KLNDR1 RNAV arrival into DFW due to an incorrect FMS altitude constraint and poor crew cross-checking. This deviation caused a Traffic Advisory and required an immediate climb to 11,000 feet after the Captain manually arrested the descent.

synopsis: E145 Captain describes a test of wills between the gate agent and himself when the gate agent is instructed not to board until a new flight attendant arrives at the aircraft. The aircraft is boarded without the cockpit crew present and with no power on the aircraft.
summary: The Captain reported that a flight attendant's aggressive behavior during cruise prompted passenger complaints, leading to the attendant's removal. Subsequent delays occurred when a gate agent ignored the crew's hold instructions and a supervisor obstructed the Captain's communication with operations while passengers boarded an unpowered aircraft.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports a near ground collision with van that fails to yield during taxi out from the gate.
summary: During taxi at 5 mph, a cargo van cut across the aircraft's path, forcing the flight deck crew to brake aggressively to avoid a collision. The sudden stop injured a standing flight attendant, prompting the reporter to recommend better ground worker training and moving strobe lights.

synopsis: CRJ700 flight crew reports being asked by ATC for their best rate to FL350, then being distracted by minor tasks that allow the aircraft to slow to 180 knots and sticker activation. A text book recovery is performed.
summary: During a climb to FL350, the Captain and First Officer lost situational awareness due to a spilled meal and a printer jam, causing an airspeed decay and autopilot disconnect at FL348. The crew recovered by descending 4,000 feet to FL310 after ATC clearance, attributing the incident to distractions during a vulnerable flight phase.

synopsis: A private pilot and multi-engine instructor in a PA-44 experienced a landing gear structural failure during takeoff roll.
summary: A flight instructor and student in a Piper PA-44 Seminole aborted a short-field takeoff at Airport ZZZ when the left main landing gear collapsed during the ground roll. The collapse caused the left wing and propeller to strike the runway, resulting in significant damage, though both occupants remained uninjured.

synopsis: C210 pilot experiences flashing runway edge and centerline lights during a night visual approach to Runway 26R at ATL. When propeller RPM is varied the strobe effect is varied and it is decided that the effect is caused by propeller interaction with the LED lights which are apparently flashing at a high rate.
summary: Two pilots on a nighttime visual approach to ATL Runway 26R observed flashing runway and centerline lights on both parallel runways. They determined the cause was a propeller strobe effect interacting with LED lighting, which they confirmed by varying engine RPM.

synopsis: Instructor pilot reports electing to enter clouds without a clearance due to unexpectedly low ceilings while on a VFR flight. A clearance is quickly obtained from Approach Control and the instructor and student continue to destination.
summary: An instructor and student flying a P80 entered IMC while descending VFR near Lacamas Lake due to poor communication regarding flight controls and an exit plan. They subsequently requested and received an IFR clearance to BTG for an ILS approach after climbing out of the clouds.

synopsis: A student pilot had difficulty understanding ATC instructions and mis-identified the aircraft he was to follow. His early turn led to a traffic conflict that was separated by ATC. The current and former flight instructors provided similar accounts and suggestions.
summary: A student pilot on a solo cross-country flight misidentified a Cessna on the runway as the lead aircraft while cleared to land runway 15. The student reported the traffic in sight, prompting the tower to order an immediate go-around and left turn due to the student's lack of situational awareness.

synopsis: Stearman pilot lost control of his aircraft when he encountered a tailwind gust during landing, resulting in a ground loop and slight wing tip damage.
summary: The pilot landed a Stearman on Runway 28R in a crosswind, weather-vaned left, and ground-looped off the runway due to delaying a go-around despite a tailwind gust. The aircraft sustained minor wingtip fabric damage but was deemed safe to taxi back to the hangar after ATC coordination.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: SFB Tower Controller reports of an incident where he advises an aircraft to turn onto an active runway with an arrival on short final to that runway. Traffic exits runway before aircraft on final crosses the threshold.
summary: Local 1 and Local 2 controllers were involved during a landing phase when Local 1 forgot to transfer Runway 18/36 status to Ground Control. This caused Aircraft X to turn onto Runway 36 just 15–20 seconds before Aircraft Y crossed the threshold, creating a runway incursion risk.

synopsis: JAX Controllers report of a runway incursion by an airport vehicle with an aircraft on final that goes around due to the vehicle's position.
summary: An OPS vehicle crossed Runway 26 without permission while Aircraft X was on short final, causing the aircraft to go around and be re-sequenced. The incident occurred because the operator failed to request a runway crossing despite intending to sweep glass across the runway.

synopsis: HIO Controller reports of an aircraft in the VFR pattern that reported multiple laser illuminations while on final.
summary: A flight instructor in Aircraft X reported two unauthorized green laser illuminations at 1NM final and 800 MSL during touch-and-go training on Runway 31. The crew subsequently diverted to Runway 20 for a safe landing with no injuries, prompting the Controller In Charge to notify law enforcement and file a Mandatory Occurrence Report.

synopsis: B737 Captain discovers that while the Bridge Visual Runway 29 at EWR has no missed approach procedure, it does have a balked landing procedure hidden away in note 2.
summary: Pilots reported that the EWR 19-4 approach plate places the rejected landing procedure in small print at Note #2. This non-intuitive location is often overlooked during briefings or when executing a go-around.

synopsis: An A320 flight crew had a close encounter with a UAV they identified as a red, white and blue model aircraft operating above 10,000 FT, within the confines of and at or above the MCO Class B.
summary: The pilot reported a near-miss with an unregistered remote-controlled aircraft while climbing through 10,200 feet northwest of MCO. The pilot reduced speed to 250 knots, passing the drone by 100–200 feet, and attributed the conflict to the drone operating without transponder or registration in controlled airspace.

synopsis: B737-400 Captain detects very sluggish takeoff performance and suspects that the takeoff data they received did not reflect the actual aircraft load.
summary: The crew experienced low acceleration and climb performance during takeoff due to suspected incorrect FMC N1 settings caused by an ACARS data transfer failure. They manually increased power to 92% N1 at 1,000 feet AGL, resolving the issue, while speculating that old flight data may have populated the system.

synopsis: Hawker 850 flight crew describes a rejected takeoff that results after the Captain begins having directional control issues at 60 knots. Post flight revealed that the right nose tire had come off its bead.
summary: During takeoff roll, the pilot flying lost directional control due to a right nose wheel tire coming off its bead, prompting an abort. The aircraft was stopped on a taxiway using aerodynamic braking and reverse thrust, with no injuries reported and the plane subsequently towed by maintenance.

synopsis: B737-900 flight crew reported slower than normal acceleration on takeoff roll, possibly resulting from autothrottle malfunction or error in weight and balance calculations. Captain added power at rotation to assure obstacle clearance.
summary: The flight crew of a Boeing 737-900 experienced slow acceleration during takeoff on Runway 28R due to auto-thrust failing to reach the planned reduced thrust setting. The Pilot Monitoring manually advanced throttles to full power, allowing the aircraft to clear approach lights safely, and maintenance was notified to investigate the auto-thrust anomaly.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Flight crew reported receiving a low altitude alert from the tower on a night visual approach to TUS runway 11L.
summary: During a night visual approach to TUS 11L, the Pilot Flying and Captain lost visual contact with the runway due to low light settings and configuration tasks, triggering a low altitude alert. They executed a go-around, received vectors for a new approach, and landed safely.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Captain reports two similar sounding fix names used by PCT with the HYPER 5 arrival resulted in a track deviation. The reported fixes are CEEVE and SIGBE.
summary: A pilot flying the Hyper 5 arrival to Manassas confused the fixes CEVEE and SIGBE due to similar names, leading to an incorrect initial clearance readback. The controller corrected the route after the pilot queried the fix, prompting a recommendation to rename one intersection to prevent future confusion.

synopsis: A glider pilot inadvertently entered restricted airspace and experienced a near-mid-air-collision with a high performance military aircraft. The lack of a transponder may not have allowed ATC to recognize that the pilot was off the expected route.
summary: A glider pilot flying near Inyokern entered restricted airspace R2505 and nearly collided with a fighter jet passing 150 feet below. The pilot attributed the incident to misinterpreting moving map displays due to sun glare and failing to monitor China Lake CT for high-speed traffic.

synopsis: The pilot of a small aircraft landing at a non-towered airport, observed the aircraft ahead land on the grass alongside the runway, then taxi across the runway unannounced. The landing aircraft was forced to take evasive action to avoid a ground collision.
summary: The pilot of a landing aircraft at a non-towered airport avoided a collision with a Super Cub that crossed Runway 19 without radio communication or visual clearance. The incident occurred because the Cub pilot failed to see the approaching aircraft or hear radio calls indicating traffic behind him.

synopsis: The pilot of a V35 Bonanza experienced engine power problems and diverted to a nearby airport. A loose fuel line was identified as the problem.
summary: During climbout on a VFR flight, a BE35 Bonanza experienced rough running, fuel spray, and fumes due to a loose fuel line. The pilot declared an emergency, received vectors from Approach, and executed a successful landing after the engine quit during rollout.

synopsis: The pilot of a multi-engine aircraft became aware of another aircraft in close proximity, and took evasive action. ATC was unaware of any traffic in the area, and was unable to identify any on radar.
summary: During cruise at 17,000 feet, the pilot and passenger observed an unlit aircraft with only white wingtip lights passing approximately 200 feet above. The pilot executed an immediate descent to avoid a collision, but ATC reported no radar contact with the other aircraft.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew experiences a TCAS TA and EGPWS cautions and warnings while on a night visual approach. The First Officer makes adjustments to the glide path to silence the warnings although no actual deviations below the glidepath are detected and the approach is continued to landing. The aircraft had been written-up for lightning strikes recently.
summary: The crew of an -800 received multiple GPWS cautions and one warning during a visual approach backed by a Localizer, likely due to recent lightning strikes. Despite being above the glide path, they continued and landed, later acknowledging they should have executed a go-around per company policy upon the first caution.

synopsis: After being issued a speed restriction by ATC along with the advice, 'Expect short approach;' B737-700 flight crew slowed below assigned speed due to their high, in close position. ATC advised of a possible violation.
summary: The flight crew on a jet descending for Runway XXL slowed and extended flaps based on Approach's repeated "expect a short approach" advisories. ATC later issued a possible pilot deviation notice after vectoring the aircraft right to increase spacing from a trailing flight, though the crew believed their actions aligned with the controller's intent.

synopsis: B767 First Officers describe a CAT III approach during which LAND III does not appear in the Autoland Status Annunciator (ASA) descending below 1,500 feet and is not detected. Below 400 feet Flare and Roll out does not appear in the ASA and is not detected. Approaching minimums the Captain detects the lack of a Land III indication and disconnects the autopilot to land manually.
summary: Three pilots on an augmented flight missed the 'Land 3' annunciation during a Cat III autoland in 500-meter RVR fog. The Captain hand-flew the landing after disconnecting the autopilot at 50 feet, resulting in a float and a safe touchdown despite the crew's failure to initiate a missed approach earlier.

synopsis: B757 First Officer discovers during takeoff that auto thrust is inoperative during the takeoff. The takeoff is continued and in cruise it is discovered that maintenance pulled the wrong circuit breaker while attempting to comply with an MEL procedure for the left autopilot.
summary: The crew continued takeoff after auto throttles failed due to maintenance pulling incorrect circuit breakers, disabling the TMC servo instead of the autopilot. Dispatch was unresponsive to phone requests, forcing the crew to contact Maintenance Control via ACARS before completing the flight.

synopsis: A Dispatcher lost contact with a long range flight on a polar route, missing real time position reports at three fixes (later received) and was unable to communicate the re-dispatch message as required.
summary: An aircraft flying a polar route lost communication and passed the BADRO re-dispatch fix without a release. Attempts to contact via three satcom lines and SFO ARINC failed, while position reports for DEKMO, DEVID, and BADRO were delayed until communication was restored.

synopsis: DHC8-100 Captain experiences a lightning strike in cruise resulting in the loss of both DC generators and both VOR's. The generators are successfully reset but the VOR's are not and the flight diverts to a VFR airport.
summary: The crew experienced a lightning strike near CTF that disabled both DC generators and VORs during IFR flight. They diverted to ZZZ for a VFR landing due to unreliable ILS data, landed safely, and found no aircraft damage on the post-flight inspection.

synopsis: Flight Dispatcher reports being unable to contact a crew to inform them that their next flight is canceled. ATC is contacted and the filed flight plan is canceled. The crew manages to get around this obstacle and depart on time.
summary: A dispatcher failed to reach the crew of aircraft XXX to cancel a flight, and ATC re-filed the flight plan after the captain clarified the flight number. The aircraft departed and became airborne despite the dispatcher's attempt to cancel the flight plan due to communication failures.

synopsis: A Captain was informed he had flown a CRJ-200 aircraft with the Right nose wheel tire improperly installed. The chine (tire ring) was found facing inward instead of outward. Pilot noted certain factors may have contributed to the missed chine position that included the aircraft was already delayed, time pressure to get back on schedule and the aircraft tug was already connected to the nose gear.
summary: A CRJ-200 departed with a right nose wheel tire installed incorrectly, with chines facing inward instead of outward. The reporter attributes this oversight error to time pressure and the tug being hooked up, noting no change in ground handling was observed.

synopsis: Upon takeoff the Captain of an EMB-175 found it necessary to maintain full down elevator deflection to prevent over rotation. The condition continued until flight attendants were able to move passengers forward. The Captain recalled noting the trim set at 4.8 units ANU during preflight and the First Officer noted 10.1 ANU during the struggle to maintain a safe attitude.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced an uncommanded pitch-up shortly after takeoff due to a suspected aft CG caused by incorrect passenger weights and a potential trim runaway. They regained control by moving passengers forward and trimming the stabilizer, resulting in a safe return and landing.

synopsis: A319 First Officer reported encountering wake on arrival to DFW in 10-mile trail of an A380 that resulted in a 25-degree bank.
summary: The flight crew of BOOVE1 encountered wake turbulence from an Airbus A380 during arrival at DFW, causing a 25-degree roll and throwing a flight attendant into a passenger. The crew attributed the event to crossing the A380's vertical profile despite maintaining 10 miles spacing, resulting in no injuries.

synopsis: CRJ-700 flight crew reports entering an incorrect holding pattern at SKARF due to misunderstanding the clearance and the way the arrival chart is laid out.
summary: During descent on the FRNCH 3 Arrival into Denver, the crew held left at SKARF after misidentifying the TOMSN fix due to task saturation. The First Officer later realized the error, but the aircraft exited the hold and landed without ATC correction or incident.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Private pilot reports inadvertently entering IMC at 2500 feet. ATC is contacted and provides assistance resulting in a safe landing.
summary: A private pilot entered IMC near Winchester while flying VFR after failing to contact Flight Watch or FSS for weather updates. The pilot climbed to avoid obstacles, received assistance from Potomac TRACON, and landed safely at MRB after descending below the ceiling.

synopsis: ZOA Controller describes a situation where a smaller CL60 is following a B767 and encounters severe turbulence. The B767 is 10 miles in front of the Challenger.
summary: A CL60 pilot reported severe turbulence and a 30-degree roll at FL340 while descending 10 miles behind a clean, level B767. The pilot attributed the event to the B767's wake, noting a lack of awareness regarding wake hazards at that distance and altitude.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZJX controller describes a loss of separation while using ERAM and a distraction from an ERAM SME while working traffic.
summary: An air traffic controller at Sector 73 lost separation between Aircraft X descending to FL110 and Aircraft Y climbing to FL230 due to a distracting ERAM technician interrupting operations. The controller issued a corrective heading to restore separation, attributing the incident to the technician's unnecessary interference during a busy session.

synopsis: Without informing ATC, B737-700 flight crew slowed below last assigned speed in order to descend fully configured in a stabilized approach.
summary: During the ZZZ Arrival, the crew reduced speed to 145 knots to correct a high and fast approach but failed to coordinate this deviation with Tower. The controller subsequently cited the crew for non-compliance with the 180-knot restriction after they reported their actual speed.

synopsis: When the flight crew of a B737-NG negotiated a more neighborly RNAV SID for departure from DAL with Clearance Delivery their Departure Controller was apparently not informed and asked the crew which of DAL's 22 SIDs they were on after giving them a 'direct to' clearance on course. When advised they were on the KRUMM the Controller verbally shook his head stating '...I just can't keep track of them all.'
summary: The flight crew and controllers at Dallas-Fort Worth operated a delayed departure on the KRUMM 4 RNAV SID after requesting runway 13R for noise abatement. The pilot reported a potential loss of separation risk due to confusion between the original SWTSR (7,000 ft) and assigned KRUMM (5,000 ft) climb limits in complex airspace.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain describes FMC anomalies that occur when changing from the RNAV X RWY 22L to the RNAV Y RWY 22L approaching MIING on the ENDEE3 arrival to MDW. This change results in the entire ENDEE3 arrival being entered into the FMC and creates a route discontinuity after MIING.
summary: The flight crew experienced an LNAV disconnect and lateral deviation while executing the ENDEE3 22L RNAV Y arrival due to a discontinuity after re-selecting the STERE transition. The pilot attributed the event to ATC failing to issue a specific transition, forcing a last-minute re-brief in congested airspace.

synopsis: A Contract Mechanic was directed by Maintenance Control to pressurize the cabin of an EMB-145 aircraft to below sea level in the manual mode. Flight crew and Flight Attendant were not made aware after being requested to start engines with the main cabin door closed. Uncomfortable ear pressure was experienced. Crew departed in the morning, but pressurization and flight at altitude may not have been advisable due to scuba dive effect.
summary: Flight and cabin crew on an EMB-145 were exposed to a cabin altitude below sea level during an unbriefed maintenance leak check at 3.0 psi. The contract mechanic, directed by Maintenance Control without a checklist or warning, caused ear pressure issues, resulting in the removal of a flight attendant with hearing aids for medical evaluation.

synopsis: A B737-NG First Officer reported sighting a UAV within 400 FT of their flight path as they climbed through 4,000-4,500 MSL south and west of DFW on the HRPER1 SID.
summary: During the departure of HRPER1 from runway 18L, a pilot observed a remote-controlled drone approximately 300 to 500 feet below the aircraft at 4,000 to 4,500 feet MSL. The pilot reported the unauthorized drone, which was flying well above the 400-foot limit, noting the significant collision risk posed by such unregistered recreational aircraft.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reports inadvertently fueling with the main cabin door closed. After engine start, a PA28 is heard on the CTAF to be taxiing for takeoff. Upon reaching the parallel taxiway the PA28 is seen to be accelerating down the taxiway, and lifts off very close to the CRJ.
summary: The captain reported two incidents: unnecessary fueling occurred due to misreading the dispatch release, and a Piper Cherokee took off from a taxiway at an uncontrolled field, passing within 25 feet of the aircraft. The captain attributed these events to communication errors and the inherent risks of uncontrolled airports.

synopsis: Pilot reports entering Los Angeles class bravo airspace without clearance, while under flight following.
summary: A VFR pilot descending from 15,500 feet inadvertently entered Class B airspace while distracted by obtaining a revised ATIS and relying on ATC for airspace protection. The pilot attributed the incursion to prioritizing ATIS over requesting a clearance and assuming controllers would prevent the violation.

synopsis: PA28 instructor, with student flying a GPS approach under simulated partial panel conditions, reports allowing his student to drift off course into the approach path of the parallel runway, consequently causing a NMAC with a Bonanza. The Bonanza pilot asks the Tower what the PA28 is doing, alerting the instructor to the deviation.
summary: During a practice GPS approach to Runway 4R, the instructor and student drifted toward parallel Runway 4L, resulting in a near midair collision with a Bonanza at 200 feet separation. The incident was caused by the instructor's insufficient single-pilot resource management while focusing on student instruction rather than traffic monitoring.

synopsis: B737 First Officer describes an arrival during which a new Captain, also new to the B737, experiments with the FMC and MCP much to the chagrin of the First Officer, resulting in track deviations that are detected by ATC and vector headings are issued.
summary: A new Captain on a Boeing 767 arrival into SLC ignored descent clearances due to FMC misconceptions, leading to a deviation from the arrival track and steep banks. The First Officer took control to correct the heading and altitude, resulting in a safe landing after the Captain admitted to disregarding crew input.

synopsis: C310 pilot discovers that his aircraft has lost all electrical power when the gear will not retract after takeoff. Unicom is contacted via cell phone and the first approach results in a go-around when the flaps cannot be extended. The second approach is planned with no flaps and ends successfully.
summary: The pilot experienced an electrical failure during the climb and traffic pattern, causing avionics brownouts and loss of gear indication lights. The aircraft landed safely without flaps after confirming gear down via ground observation, with preliminary analysis citing weak batteries and tripped voltage regulators.

synopsis: C210 pilot experiences icing conditions at 9,000 feet with no ability to descend due to a MVA of 8,500 feet. With the icing becoming excessive, pilot stresses urgency to ATC and a descent to 8,000 feet results in VMC and temperatures above freezing.
summary: A pilot encountered rapid, severe rime icing at 9,000 feet during an IFR flight, exceeding planned escape options. After declaring an emergency, ATC authorized a descent to 7,300 feet, allowing the aircraft to exit clouds and melt ice before a safe visual landing.

synopsis: AGS FLM reports of an ALTRV that no one was briefed on. The controllers were unfamiliar with an ALTRV and apparently have never worked one before.
summary: Air traffic controllers at Ft. Gordon range control handled an ALTRA event without prior management briefing or experience. The lack of preparation forced controllers to consult the 7110.65 manual in real-time to manage the unusual situation.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Arrival Controllers describe situation of a configuration change that didn't go smoothly resulting in a loss of separation with an opposite direction arrival.
summary: A Departure 1 controller and Arrival 3 controller at ZZZ airport experienced loss of separation between departing aircraft and an inbound arrival due to TMU miscommunication regarding flow changes. Additionally, a low-fuel aircraft lost separation with a departure because Tower continued launches on Runway XXR despite instructions to hold for a north flow transition.

synopsis: ZLA Controller reports a Hawker 125 reported severe turbulence, the aircraft was following a heavy B767-300 on the same route 10 to 12 miles ahead. The Controller gave a further descent clearance to the aircraft to a suitable altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller descended Aircraft X to FL300 after the pilot reported severe wake turbulence from Aircraft Y, which was 10–12 miles ahead. The controller assigned a slower speed to increase separation while coordinating with SLC sector 46 during the descent into LAS.

synopsis: Arriving into IAH off the HKORY1, B737 flight crew is issued a runway change from Runway 9 to Runway 8R. The crew makes an incorrect assumption that this runway requires a north transition over DOMNO. The routing note describing the route for each runway is missed when the iPad is zoomed in.
summary: The flight crew flying the HKORY ONE RNAV arrival into IAH for runway 8R incorrectly selected the DOMNO transition instead of HOWLN due to a missed note on their zoomed-in iPad charts. ATC intercepted the deviation at PRAYS intersection and vectored the aircraft to the correct heading, resulting in no conflict with other traffic.

synopsis: An EMB-170 flight crew inbound to DFW filed for, set up and briefed to descend via the JOVEM RNAV STAR, IBAKE transition was given two STAR changes during their descent, first to descend via the DEBBB then, as they approached FAWNT Intersection, via the SHAAM STAR. Upon programming they noted there was no 'bottom' altitude to set, in fact no bottom altitude anywhere on the arrival or the six transitions thereof. ATC then asked if they were going to make their 9,000 restriction at GREGS for which the only charted restriction is 'At 250 KT.'
summary: Pilots flying a flight near DFW were reassigned to the SHAAM STAR shortly before the TOD, but the chart lacked a depicted bottom altitude for the descent. The crew crossed GREGS at 9,000 feet without violation, though the reporter attributed the confusion to a flawed chart and late STAR changes.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reports forgetting to set the flaps to takeoff prior to taking the runway, due to a long taxi in low visibility and fatigue. Autothrust will not engage on the runway and when thrust is pushed up to taxi clear the takeoff warning sounds.
summary: The crew rejected takeoff due to a perceived autothrottle failure, but the actual cause was forgetting to configure the aircraft and complete the first half of the Before Takeoff checklist. Fatigue and high workload from low visibility and delays contributed to the error, which was corrected after clearing the runway.

synopsis: First Officer notes a number of alerts being displayed on the EAD that did not make sense during preflight. Going below it is discovered that the tether used to keep the nose wheel from lifting off the ground during loading is too long. The tether is quickly shortened by ground personnel.
summary: The RFO observed a nose gear lift during loading caused by ground crew installing an incorrect, longer 777 tether on the aircraft. The nose wheel rose 1.5 feet before settling, resulting in no damage, attributed to the wrong tether and parking in a 777 stand.

synopsis: While troubleshooting a flight crew report of Rudder-Aileron Trim wheel binding on a CE-560XL, an Aircraft Maintenance Inspector finds the Autopilot Control wire bundle tangled in the Rudder-Aileron Trim Assembly vertical shafts, inside the aft end of the cockpit Center pedestal. Inspector questions if a Task Card for inspecting the routing and security of wire bundles and tie-wraps had been accomplished.
summary: During pre-flight on a Cessna 560XL, the rudder trim bound left and contacted the aileron trim wheel due to a tangled autopilot wire bundle. Mechanics untangled the wires and reinstalled the trim assembly per the maintenance manual, restoring normal operation.

synopsis: Captain of a Learjet-31A aircraft reports he felt a slight 'catch' in the aileron controls during departure lift-off. Concerns for possible flight controls binding, pilot decides to do a precautionary return to field.
summary: The pilot reported an aileron control catch during departure from ZZZ. A precautionary landing was executed on runway 16 without incident after advising the tower.

synopsis: Pitts pilot reports a weather divert to BWG and landing without announcing on the CTAF. Pilot neglects to make announcement due fear of looking down to tune at low altitude and the poor forward visibility of his aircraft. During roll out, a business jet is observed going around overhead.
summary: A VFR pilot diverted to Bowling Green due to low ceilings and visibility, then landed on Runway 21 while a business jet executed a missed approach overhead. The pilot attributed the conflict to poor forward visibility preventing radio tuning and noted a subsequent discussion with the other pilot regarding decision-making.

synopsis: VNY Ground Controller describes a loss of separation with a faster aircraft over taking a slower aircraft on departure.
summary: A ground controller reported that a trainee and supervisor allowed two IFR propeller aircraft to depart parallel runways without adequate spacing, causing the faster Aircraft Y to overtake Aircraft X near the VNY 2.2 DME fix. The controllers incorrectly relied on visual separation despite the performance mismatch, creating an unsafe situation that required removing one aircraft from the SID to prevent a collision.

synopsis: ZID Controller describes a flight break up that wasn't the usual type of break up resulting in an airspace violation.
summary: An air traffic controller and trainee managed a military formation breakup where Aircraft Y contacted ATC directly instead of the flight leader, causing confusion during a busy session. The controller resolved a conflict with traffic at FL290 by issuing a heading and altitude clearance after creating a missing flight plan.

synopsis: PCT Controller and pilots of the aircraft describe an airspace violation.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring and Pilot Flying departed DCA on the NATIONAL 3 SID in IMC, deviating from the cleared 328-degree course while hand-flying in VOR/LOC mode. The deviation caused a potential airspace violation requiring ATC intervention, leading to an investigation and the crew's decision to cease flying duties.

synopsis: When their flaps refused to extend beyond five degrees on approach the flight crew of a B737 opted to go around to troubleshoot the problem. When fuel remaining became an issue they [advised ATC] and, during the subsequent approach, the flaps this time extended normally.
summary: The crew experienced a flap indicator disagreement during approach, triggering a go-around at 2,000 feet MSL and a Mayday declaration due to low fuel. After troubleshooting the confusing QRH checklist, they successfully extended flaps and landed uneventfully with 4.0 fuel remaining.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports leveling at 13,000 feet crossing RIOOS on the TRALR5 with the intention of climbing to FL190 after passing TRALR, as stated in the routing box. ATC is not happy with this interpretation of the verbiage and the crew is told to continue climb to FL190.
summary: The flight crew departed LAS on the TRALR5 SID and leveled at 13,000 feet due to ambiguous chart wording regarding the FL190 climb instruction. After an agitated controller ordered a continued climb to FL190, the crew complied, attributing the confusion to unclear chart formatting and missing top altitude data on PDC.

synopsis: B767 flight crew detects electrical fumes in the cockpit at FL350 and elects to divert to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: During cruise at FL350, the flight crew detected electrical fumes in the cockpit and executed the Smoke, Fire, or Fumes QRH, declaring a Mayday to divert to ZZZZ. The aircraft landed safely after a high-speed descent, with the crew managing the emergency and passenger communications effectively.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports the First Officer (F/O) cleared his O2 mask and noted the O2 pressure dropped to zero in flight. Seconds later the pressure returned to 950 PSI. Arrival station Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) found O2 bottle handle only one-quarter turn opened. Captain had made logbook write-up at previous station suspecting bottle was 'closed', but was assured the O2 handle was 'open'.
summary: The crew suspected a closed oxygen valve during preflight, but maintenance confirmed it open. In flight, pressure dropped to zero then recovered; the mechanic later found the bottle closed and opened only a quarter turn, causing the system malfunction.

synopsis: An international B757 flight received their PDC clearance via CPDLC and noted it contained no 'revised segment' annotation although there was a 'LOAD' prompt on one of the CDU displayed pages and opted to leave their filed route programmed in the FMS. After takeoff ATC cleared them to a fix that was not in their filed route at which time they learned the route had been revised and was available to them had they activated the 'LOAD' prompt.
summary: The flight crew departed with the filed route instead of a significant CPDLC reroute because they missed the load prompt and the aircraft could not print the message. This caused initial confusion with ATC, but no altitude or separation issues occurred after the crew manually loaded the correct route.

synopsis: B747 First Officer describes routine runway and arrival changes that are issued by ATC during arrival to ZBAA. In addition, the arrival designations printed on Jeppesen charts and used by ATC do not match the designations used by the Honeywell FMC.
summary: A B747 crew approaching ZBAA via KM was issued last-minute STAR changes to KM 01A and KM 07B, which were missing from the FMC database. The pilot manually entered waypoints to comply with ATC clearances, highlighting a discrepancy between Jeppesen charts and Honeywell database data that risks route deviations.

synopsis: B757 Captain experiences a near ground collision with a vehicle that cuts in front of the aircraft while being marshalled into the gate.
summary: The pilot stopped the aircraft hard during a slow tow-in approach to avoid a ground vehicle that sped across the clear zone on a collision course. The incident occurred because the marshaller and wing walker failed to stop the vehicle or signal the crew, but no injuries were reported.

synopsis: B777 Captain reports being unable to turn off the runway after landing due to the tiller being jammed on the First Officer's side by the unused iPad mount.
summary: The Captain attempted to exit the runway but found the nosewheel steering tiller jammed by the First Officer's iPad mount. The obstruction prevented the aircraft from turning off the runway as intended.

synopsis: A B747-400 flight crew received an EICAS STAB GREENBAND warning during pushback, conducted the associated QRH procedure and returned to the gate for assistance. A subsequent dispatch was successful.
summary: The flight crew and load supervisor encountered a persistent >STAB GREENBAND EICAS message due to a suspected center of gravity issue at 29% MAC. After verifying all cargo positions twice and receiving maintenance dispatch, the aircraft completed two uneventful flights from ZZZ to ZZZ2.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 flight crew declared an emergency, executed a controlled emergency descent, and diverted to a suitable airport when the Captain's windshield arced and then shattered at FL350.
summary: During cruise at FL 350, the left windshield arced and shattered, prompting the flight deck crew to declare an emergency and descend. The crew followed emergency procedures, managed cabin oxygen deployment, and completed the flight with modified descent rates to ensure safety.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain experiences a jet bridge collision with the aircraft while the agents are attempting to remove it after boarding. A different agent is able to get the jetbridge clear and the aircraft is carefully inspected, with no damage found. During taxi the aircraft pulls to the right and the Captain elects to return to the gate.
summary: The pilot reported that a malfunctioning jetbridge impacted the aircraft fuselage during pre-pushback, causing the nose gear to rock. Although initial inspections found no damage, the aircraft subsequently pulled right during taxi, leading the pilot to cancel the flight and switch to another aircraft due to suspected gear damage.

synopsis: HS-125-800XP Captain reported wake vortex encounter in 10-mile trail of a B767 on arrival to LAS.
summary: The crew encountered severe wake turbulence from a trailing 767 at FL320 while enroute to LAS with an inoperative TCAS. They disconnected the autopilot to recover, descended to FL300, and increased separation, noting that functional TCAS might have prevented the encounter.

synopsis: When inappropriate electrical anomalies resulted from the removal of ground power after engine start the Captain of a DHC-8 asked that ground power be restored. When ramp personnel alerted the flight deck to smoke and sparks emanating from the left engine the engines were shut down, the passengers evacuated and both fire bottles were emptied into the left engine as a precaution.
summary: The flight crew experienced a DC bus failure and #1 engine smoke while shutting down at the gate, prompting an evacuation via right-side exits. The captain discharged both fire bottles and coordinated with ramp personnel, resulting in a safe evacuation with no injuries, though the crew noted that reconnecting ground power may have exacerbated the issue.

synopsis: McDonnell Douglas Heavy Captain experiences difficulty moving the speedbrake handle in flight and applies more pressure. The result is a roll to the left which is first detected by the First Officer and corrected. During approach the spoilers are armed and function normally on landing.
summary: The pilot forced a binding speed brake handle during descent to meet a late crossing restriction, causing an asymmetric spoiler deployment and a 35-degree left roll. The First Officer disengaged the autopilot to recover the aircraft, which the pilot attributed to water accumulation in flight control bays causing binding.

synopsis: A ramp member was injured when opening a cabin door of an A310 while the cabin was pressurized due to a regulator failure.
summary: A #1 cabin pressure auto control system regulator failed closed, causing the aircraft to pressurize on the deck. When a ramp worker opened the main cabin door, it opened violently and struck the worker in the face.

synopsis: Pilot reports of violating Class Delta airspace while under flight following.
summary: A pilot conducting VFR flight following and instrument training received conflicting altitude instructions from VRB Tower and Miami Center while transitioning to FPR. The reporter suspects VRB Tower requested the climb to 2600 feet to keep the aircraft out of their airspace, noting a lack of coordinated frequency handoffs.

synopsis: Flight Attendant finds an elderly woman seated in the exit row, who boarded early and used a wheelchair. When queried as to her ability to assist in an emergency she responds in the affirmative and is allowed to stay in her seat. A Supervisor contacted after the flight indicates that if exit row passengers are queried and respond in the affirmative that is all that is required by the FAR.
summary: A flight attendant identified an elderly passenger with mobility issues seated in an exit row and requested she move, but the purser and supervisors allowed her to remain based on her verbal claim of capability. The reporter believes this outcome violated FAR 121.585, as the passenger's physical limitations rendered her unable to assist in an emergency.

synopsis: A Maintenance Technician narrowly avoided serious injury while darting in front of a running engine to retrieve tools during a maintenance procedure. Loose items from his pockets were ingested by the engine.
summary: A maintenance technician nearly entered a running Engine #1 intake while retrieving tools during a complex cross-bleed start procedure at the gate. The incident, caused by the technician forgetting the engines were running, resulted in his ID and pens being sucked into the engine, forcing an immediate shutdown and passenger deplaning.

synopsis: Pilot reports of being under flight following and violating another Tower's airspace.
summary: A pilot flying a photography mission was instructed by MLB to follow the coast but was not handed off to COF Tower. Upon contacting COF, the controller stated the aircraft was already in their airspace, which the pilot described as a hazardous situation caused by adjacent airspaces lacking automatic handoffs.

synopsis: Pilot reports of possibly violating LAX Class Bravo.
summary: A VFR pilot departing CNO reported that the EMT tower controller spoke too fast and failed to provide a handoff clearance upon exiting Class D airspace. The pilot descended from 2,500 to 2,300 feet to avoid LAX Class Bravo airspace while the controller eventually provided the next frequency.

synopsis: A Federal Agent reported a suspicious sighting of a UAV flying near the window of an office building.
summary: A pilot observed a UAV with red and white lights near a 17th-floor office window at dusk. An operator was seen on a nearby building roof attempting to land the drone, though the operator's identity could not be determined due to darkness and distance.

synopsis: A King Air 90 pilot reports a confusing clearance to taxi via Lima and Kilo while holding short of Runway 27C on Lima at SFB. The clearance is interpreted as Lima and Kilo 1 which is not correct and the reporter is admonished by the Ground Controller for a runway incursion.
summary: The pilot taxied onto an active runway without clearance after receiving confusing instructions from a busy ground controller with a difficult accent. The deviation occurred due to unclear taxi routing via Taxiway Lima and Kilo, though no conflict with other aircraft resulted.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: SRQ Tower Controller reports of a runway incursion due to a missed readback.
summary: An air traffic controller issued taxi instructions to Aircraft X, who failed to read back the hold short of Runway 04 and crossed the line while Aircraft Y was landing. Aircraft Y braked to avoid a collision, resulting in no damage or injuries, prompting the controller to emphasize the need for confirmed read backs.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: CCR Tower Controller reports of a reported NMAC by an aircraft that did not report a 2 mile left base.
summary: Air Traffic Controller and Aircraft X experienced a reported 30-foot NMAC with Aircraft Y while X was on a short approach to runway 32L. The controller attributed the incident to hazy weather, high workload on runway 32R, and failing to verify X's 2-mile base report, resulting in a go-around.

synopsis: ZTL Controller reports while trying to separate two aircraft another Center violates airspace which distracts the ZTL Controller.
summary: The controller in Sector 29 resolved a potential head-on conflict between Aircraft X and Y descending to FL240 by issuing divergent turns and expedited descents. Additionally, a W32 violation caused a conflict with Sector 33 traffic, requiring a climb to FL260 to maintain separation.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: EWR Tower Controller describes a go-around that then becomes a conflict with an aircraft inbound to another close proximity airport..
summary: An air traffic controller issued a go-around to Aircraft X on Runway 4L due to a departing aircraft, potentially losing IFR separation with a southbound LGA arrival (Aircraft Y). The controller attributed the risk to the lack of a published missed approach procedure that avoids conflicts with adjacent airport arrivals.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: ZLA Controller describes a situation where an aircraft is auto handedoff to him but is already in his airspace. He doesn't observe the target and coordinates with another sector who is handing off the aircraft to him.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X automatically handed off into their airspace near HII airport while descending from 090 to 060, despite the area's Minimum Vectoring Altitude being 061. The controller attributed the premature handoff and temporary radar loss to known radar coverage issues, though no loss of separation occurred.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ZFW TMC reports of a dialog with the ATCSCC and D10 reference arrival and departure rates that he wants to implement reference the weather.
summary: A TMU controller managing DFW arrivals coordinated with the command center regarding weather, RVR outages, and wind shear causing go-arounds and diversions. Although the controller requested a ground stop, the command center declined, resulting in over 70 aircraft diversions and a report that ZFW controllers need more trust in their decisions.

synopsis: MEM Tower Local Control describes a situation where they had to take an aircraft out for resequence due to its speed on final.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller on Local 3 managed a CRDA arrival to Runway 27 that went around after a supervisor ordered an S-turn instead of sending a Runway 18L arrival around. The controller subsequently issued conflicting headings before resolving the situation by climbing the aircraft above traffic and returning it to approach.

synopsis: A PA-44 is issued a go-around when a green shuttle van is sighted crossing the active runway without communicating with the Tower. When no way out is found the van recrosses the runway and exits via the FBO parking lot.
summary: A PA44 in VFR traffic was instructed to go around after a green shuttle van crossed Runway 31. The van ignored ground control and red light signals, crossed Runway 02, and exited the airport, prompting a recommendation to review security procedures for new hangars.

synopsis: When the flight crew of a B737NG reprogrammed their FMS to comply with a takeoff runway change they failed to note that an enroute fix was not included. ATC advised and they corrected.
summary: The crew reprogrammed the FMC after a runway change at SMF, inadvertently dropping waypoint FRA from the departure route. ATC later identified the missing waypoint, noting the same error occurred with a preceding company aircraft.

synopsis: Pilot reports of speed changes assigned by ATC not in compliance with what is on the arrival. Also the pilot describes in the scenario late runway changes.
summary: Pilots approaching Denver (DEN) reported excessive workload due to multiple late ATC changes to speed, runway, and arrival procedures. These changes prevented proper briefing and FMC setup for the RNAV 35L approach, creating an unsafe condition that was only mitigated by visual conditions.

synopsis: B737 Captain laments the lack of a Cuban overflight permit number while avoiding thunderstorms adjacent to Cuban airspace. He also believes that iPad displayed enroute charts cannot take the place of paper charts due to the lack notes and the difficulty bring what notes are available using the touchscreen in turbulence.
summary: The flight crew deviated west of track for weather near the Cuban FIR border but avoided entering Cuban airspace due to a missing overflight permit in the Sabre briefing. The pilot reported that the current electronic briefing system and Jeppesen EFB charts are inadequate for managing unexpected deviations and displaying critical FIR data.

synopsis: The flight crew of an EMB-145 declared an emergency and returned to their departure airport after smelling a foul odor also detected in the cabin by passengers.
summary: The Captain and First Officer detected an intensifying burning smell during the departure turn and declared an emergency to return for an immediate landing on Runway XXR. After a successful landing with emergency vehicles following, the crew noted the odor originated near the front cabin and recommended training to identify foul odors associated with potential fires.

synopsis: MD-83 flight crew experiences a landing gear indication failure during approach, with two green indications and the right main with no indication. The light test switch indicated the bulbs were burned out and a go-around is initiated to troubleshoot. Bulb assemblies are swapped to the inoperative position but due not indicate green and will not test. Upon returning the bulb assemblies to their original positions they no longer function. After a flyby a normal landing ensues.
summary: The flight crew experienced a right main gear indicator malfunction during approach, causing a missed approach and low pass for visual confirmation. After confirming the gear was down but possibly unlocked, they declared an emergency, landed gently, and pinned the gear on the runway before taxiing to the gate.

synopsis: MD-11 Captain reported that during cockpit setup crew noticed the TAT indication was well above normal and the FMS would not calculate V speeds or EPR. Crew then realized ground personnel were using a tether from a larger aircraft that allowed the nose to rise enough that the flight/ground switch was activated.
summary: During preflight, the FMS failed to calculate V speeds because the nose strut extended, falsely triggering an airborne signal. This occurred because a longer tether from a larger aircraft allowed the nose wheel to lift, a hazard the crew did not anticipate.

synopsis: An MD-11 flight crew diverted to the nearest suitable airport upon receipt of Level three CRG Fire Aft warnings.
summary: The crew at FL 370 experienced multiple Level 3 aft lower cargo fire warnings. They declared an emergency, followed the QRH, and diverted to the nearest airport.

synopsis: A transoceanic B777 flight crew, after leveling at cruise altitude, was advised by the purser of smoke/fumes and a smoke detector alarm sounding in the upper crew rest area and passenger reports of light grey haze/smoke in the cabin. Prompt decisions were made to divert to an airport ahead of them and to dump fuel while doing so to expedite a landing. Problems with ATC and flight deck communications while wearing 02 masks, access to approach plates for their diversion airport--including a frustrating failure by both first officers to obtain them via their tablet EFB--and finding appropriate checklists increased flight crew workload to significant levels. Approach chart/airport information was ultimately obtained from ATC and via the navigation database.
summary: The flight crew declared an emergency at FL 360 due to smoke and fumes in the upper crew rest, descending to ZZZZ with fuel dumping. After initial confusion over runway lengths and chart availability, they diverted to a longer runway, landed safely, and cancelled the flight pending maintenance inspection.

synopsis: A B757 Captain reported sighting a large model airplane or helicopter about 100 FT below and 500 FT laterally away from them as they were on base leg for Runway 22L at JFK.
summary: Pilots on a visual approach to JFK 22L at 2,000 feet AGL observed a large model aircraft or helicopter approximately 100 feet below and 500 feet laterally. They reported the proximity to Tower and lost sight of the object upon turning final.

synopsis: Pilot reports of a go-around due to not being able to see if the departing heavy aircraft was actually airborne.
summary: Pilots on approach to CLT 36R encountered wake turbulence from a departing Heavy aircraft and executed a go-around due to inadequate spacing. The reporter attributed the event to the Heavy's slow taxi and takeoff roll, which prevented it from becoming airborne before the arriving aircraft would have touched down.

synopsis: B767 flight crew experiences a right wing slide caution message during initial climb on a ferry flight after an A check by Maintenance. The QRH is consulted and the right wing is examined visually with no deployment noted. During approach, as the flaps are extended from 20 to 30, a noise is heard and vibration is felt. The Tower reports something trailing from the aircraft and possible smoke coming from the lower rear fuselage. A normal landing ensues.
summary: Following a heavy check, the crew received a right wing slide EICAS message but continued flight until ground observers reported a hanging hose and smoke during flap extension. The incident resulted from a partially open slide door and loose hose caused by improper reinstallation after maintenance.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported encountering jet blast and resulting turbulence from an aircraft taking off shortly before landing at SNA. Reporter stated this tight spacing is common practice in SNA and he is not comfortable with it.
summary: Pilots on final approach experienced significant jet blast from a departing aircraft cleared for takeoff while the landing crew was below 1,200 feet and 3 miles out. The disturbance caused an unstable flare, though a safe landing was achieved, highlighting a need for stricter ATC separation limits on this short runway.

synopsis: A B777-300 flight crew, nearing the end of a 14 hour flight, discussed the difficulties and distractions of reprogramming and complying with ATC alterations to RNAV STAR 'descend via' clearances.
summary: The flight crew flying a long-haul arrival into DFW on the DEBBB 1 RNAV procedure experienced high workload due to multiple ATC speed and altitude modifications. These changes required manual FMC reprogramming, causing VNAV to drop off path and preventing the aircraft from maintaining assigned speeds while descending.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reports of landing at a military airport and seeing arresting gear on the runway.
summary: The crew of Aircraft X landed at NYL on a GPS approach and held short of an un-noticed arresting cable on Runway 3L while taxiing. The cable was not published due to a NOTAM system outage, but the crew safely back-taxied to an alternate route with no damage or injuries.

synopsis: While deadheading in the cabin and sitting in the last row of an EMB-145 aircraft, a Captain notices a section of the left wing trailing edge skin cavitating, collapsing at cruise altitude. Skin distortion appeared to go back to normal below 10,000 feet and remained smooth with flaps extended for landing.
summary: A deadheading pilot observed wing skin cavitation on an EMB-145 at cruise altitude, which normalized below 10,000 feet. The pilot reported the incident to the PIC and supervisors, suspecting a fleet-wide fatigue issue requiring an Airworthiness Directive for high-altitude inspections.

synopsis: Flight crew opted to divert to the nearest suitable airport after the First Officer's side window shattered with a loud bang at FL360.
summary: The crew diverted to ZZZ after the FO's side window shattered at F360, likely due to heating element scoring and arcing concerns. They declared an emergency, landed safely, but reported an accusatory and offensive response from the maintenance controller regarding their decision.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported the aircraft moved about nine feet after setting the brakes at the gate. Crew reported brake pressure was in the green when the brakes were set.
summary: The captain reported that an A320 rolled forward approximately 9 feet at the gate while the parking brake was set and indicated active, likely due to a temporary pressure loss during single-engine taxi. The crew stopped the movement with manual brakes, logged the incident, and recommended updating the FOM to require brake pressure verification after parking.

synopsis: Pilot reports of an NMAC caused by the Tower Controller sequencing traffic and not issuing traffic.
summary: Pilots conducting touch-and-goes at PVU experienced a loss of vertical separation when an experimental aircraft passed 200 feet above them on base leg. The pilot attributed the incident to the controller's instruction to perform a right 360 for spacing, which placed the aircraft directly under the traffic.

synopsis: When cleared by Clearance Delivery to 'climb via' the PHX SNOBL RNAV departure off the east runway complex the flight crew of a Falcon 50 climbed so as to cross GOALY at or below 9,000 FT as depicted on the graphic and described in the INITIAL CLIMB text box. As they climbed through 8,000 FT ATC advised they were required to maintain 8,000 FT as stated in the ROUTING text box.
summary: The flight crew climbed to 9,000 feet following the "Initial Climb" instructions on the SID chart, but TRACON advised they should have stopped at 8,000 feet as specified in the "Routing" section. The controller noted this chart confusion is common, and the crew attributed the error to poor chart design rather than operational failure.

synopsis: A320 First Officer reported encountering wake vortex in 6 miles trail of a B757 on approach to LAX that rolled the aircraft up to 60 degrees. Reporter cited wind conditions as probably contributory.
summary: The pilot flying an A320 on final approach to LAX RWY 25L encountered wake turbulence from a preceding B757 at 6 nm separation and 3,500 ft AGL, causing a 45-60 degree roll. The pilot recovered manually and attributed the encounter to 12-15 mph headwinds transporting the wake further than standard guidelines predict.

synopsis: Following the loss of both packs due to right and left engine bleed air failures the flight crew of a B757 diverted to a nearby airport and landed safely.
summary: During climb to cruise, simultaneous Right and Left Bleed EICAS messages caused loss of both PACKS and a CABIN ALT warning. The crew descended to 10,000 feet while performing QRH procedures and landed safely.

synopsis: The instructor and IFR training pilots aboard a PA28R suffered a partial power loss, advised ATC, and landed at the airport where they had been shooting practice ILS approaches.
summary: During a dual IFR training flight in VMC, the crew experienced a partial power loss with RPM dropping from 2700 to 1300 at 500 AGL after a missed approach. The emergency checklist failed to restore power, but the aircraft landed safely on an alternate runway after ATC cleared them to land on any available runway.

synopsis: B757 First Officer reported losing cabin pressure when both pneumatic bleeds failed at FL350.
summary: During climb to cruise, the crew received Right and Left Bleed EICAS messages causing loss of both PACKS and a CABIN ALT warning. The crew initiated a descent to 10,000 feet while performing QRH procedures.

synopsis: A student pilot with his flight instructor overheard their position announced to an aircraft transitioning the airport area, but they were not provided position information in regard to the traffic. They were surprised to find themselves in a near-mid-air-collision situation and took evasive action.
summary: Pilots on a flight to ZZZ encountered a conflicting aircraft while entering a right base for XX, prompting evasive action due to a lack of timely traffic advisories. Post-landing, the crew's compromised situational awareness caused an inadvertent entry onto RWY XY/XZ before receiving taxi instructions.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: A C525B flight crew on a vector to intercept the localizer suffered an NMAC with an unidentified aircraft. Their decision to stop the turn to intercept, causing them to fly through the localizer, may have been a contributing factor.
summary: The crew received traffic alerts while intercepting the LOC for VNY, causing them to cross the course to visually spot the target. They subsequently climbed after a second alert indicated an aircraft within 100 feet, eventually completing a visual approach.

synopsis: Pilot reports of being questioned about violating Class C airspace, while being under flight following from the overlying TRACON.
summary: A pilot flying a VFR Medevac flight transited San Jose Class C airspace without a frequency change, assuming coordination between NorCal Approach and San Jose Tower. The tower supervisor initiated a pilot deviation investigation for the unauthorized transit, though no traffic conflicts occurred.

synopsis: Pilot reports of advising ATC while under flight following that he was descending to avoid clouds. While doing so he entered a Class D airspace.
summary: A VFR pilot cruising at 3500 MSL descended to 2500 MSL and inadvertently entered FOK Class D airspace while reversing course. The New York Approach controller instructed the pilot to climb above 2600 MSL to exit the airspace, prompting the pilot to clarify future communication regarding Class D transits.

synopsis: Three pilots report extremely dangerous behavior by the pilot of a biplane operating in the traffic pattern of a non-towered airport.
summary: A pilot conducting closed traffic at ZZZ observed a biplane departing runway XX without radio calls and performing erratic, low-altitude maneuvers that cut off other aircraft in the pattern. The reporter and another pilot discontinued their flights due to the biplane's disregard for traffic rules, which created a risk of mid-air collision.

synopsis: BE-95 pilot experiences a gear failure during landing resulting in damage to the aircraft and a runway excursion. Upon being lifted the main gear are found to be partially extended and the nose gear is retracted.
summary: The pilot landed a single-engine aircraft with landing gear partially extended, causing a runway excursion onto the grass. Although gear indicators appeared normal, the nose gear remained retracted and main gears were only partially down, resulting in loss of control and a skid.

synopsis: BJC Controller reports of another controller prompting a pilot to cancel IFR to remain in the pattern at the airport.
summary: A Local Controller instructed an IFR aircraft to cancel IFR to re-enter the pattern after a go-around due to high winds. The reporter states this violated 7110.65, leaving the aircraft in a VFR status with low visibility and creating an unsafe situation.

synopsis: B737-300 flight crew experiences an autopilot disconnect horn after the TO/GA button is pushed during takeoff. The takeoff is rejected and troubleshooting indicates that the autopilot must have been engaged at some time during preflight and not detected until the TO/GA button was pushed. A child visitor to the cockpit may have pushed the button during preflight.
summary: The crew experienced repeated autopilot disconnect horns during takeoff roll, assuming a child had inadvertently engaged the autopilot on the ground. They rejected two takeoffs, consulted maintenance with no discrepancy found, and departed uneventfully after logging the event.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Flight crew experiences a stuck mic during initial climb and attribute the problem to the combination of a new ACP and a Bose headset. When the headset is unplugged the stuck mic goes away.
summary: The flight crew experienced a stuck microphone on the new Audio Control Panel while climbing to 12,000 feet, preventing communication with Departure Control. The issue was resolved when the Captain unplugged his headset, clearing the stuck MIC and restoring radio contact.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports not writing up a Standby Power Check failure due to being admonished by the Chief Pilot on a previous occasion. The Standby power Check is no longer a flight crew function and is checked only by Maintenance.
summary: A Captain reported a failed standby power check during preflight but chose not to log the defect after an Assistant Chief Pilot instructed him to stop performing the check to avoid delays. The Captain noted this directive contradicted company policies requiring flight crew to document all observed mechanical defects.

synopsis: After landing with nearly full fuel tanks in just above freezing conditions the flight crew of a B737NG planned--but failed--to check the tops of the wings for cold soaked fuel frost prior to their subsequent takeoff. A lengthy layover permitting intervening distractions may have been a contributing factor.
summary: The Captain reported a potential Cold Soaked Fuel Frost (CSFF) event during a DEN arrival with tankered fuel. Due to a long turn, the Captain forgot to re-check the wings before departure and realized the omission after takeoff, leaving the presence of frost uncertain.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain experiences an EGPWS terrain caution at 6,600 feet during a night visual approach to Runway 16R at RNO and goes around.
summary: The flight crew flying a KENNO RNAV arrival to Reno (RNO) received a 'CAUTION TERRAIN' alert at 6,600 feet while descending below the recommended 7,100 feet minimum. The captain initiated a go-around, attributing the event to failing to use conservative altitude values during the visual approach despite thorough pre-flight briefings.

synopsis: B757 flight crew experiences a Right Bleed EICAS Message followed by a Left Bleed EICAS message, resulting in loss of both PACKS which results in a CABIN ALT warning. Flight diverts to a suitable airport.
