synopsis: BE55 pilot reports hitting trees during a night visual approach to Runway 29 at HPN. Runway has a 1300 foot displaced threshold and no PAPI or REIL lights.
summary: The pilot struck tree tops one-eighth mile short of the displaced Runway 29 threshold during final approach. The incident caused minor damage to the right wing and landing light due to the absence of VASI or glide slope guidance.

synopsis: Maule pilot departing HTH experiences an airborne conflict with a Cessna landing opposite direction after a straight in approach and not making position reports.
summary: The Maule pilot departed Hawthorne on Runway 10 and offset right after liftoff to avoid a head-on collision with a Cessna landing without radio communication. The reporter attributed the near-midair collision to the Cessna pilot's failure to use a radio, fly a standard pattern, or acknowledge the departing aircraft.

synopsis: Instrument instructor reports being assigned a foreign student for refresher training in preparation for a 709 ride. The student does not complete the training and the instructor is later informed that the student was not a US citizen, did not have a TSA clearance to undergo flight training and did not have a current BFR.
summary: A flight instructor provided training to a student for an FAA 709 re-examination, unaware the student lacked TSA clearance and a current flight review. The instructor later learned the student likely violated regulations by acting as PIC, prompting the report to emphasize verifying student documentation before training.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: After a variety of issues that cause a lengthy delay, an MD80 Captain reports being cleared to line up and wait but proceeds to line up and go. The mistake is realized at low speed and the takeoff is rejected.
summary: The Captain rejected a takeoff on an MD80 after mistakenly accelerating on a "line up and wait" clearance while a Cessna was departing. The low-speed abort was caused by the Captain forgetting the clearance status, though the crew confirmed sufficient fuel to continue after consulting Dispatch.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Medium Transport flight crew rejected takeoff below 80 knots when directed to 'stop' by the Tower due to another aircraft on the runway.
summary: Local Control and a departing Air Carrier Jet on Runway 10L were involved when a Twin Turbo-Prop incursion at A4 intersection prompted an immediate "Stop" command. The pilot rejected the takeoff before 80 knots, successfully stopping the aircraft to avoid a collision with the intruding plane.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: MLI Tower Controller describes a situation where he almost forgets about a vehicle on the runway while an aircraft is on short final to the runway.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller cleared Aircraft X to land Runway 13 while Vehicle Y remained on the runway because the controller forgot to issue an exit instruction. The controller attributed the near-miss to distraction from recent radar training notes and a lack of full focus on the Local control position.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: C90 Controller describes situation where they are trying to vector aircraft for the visual approach but are having trouble with getting aircraft in resulting in separation losses.
summary: An air traffic controller at C90, hindered by low staffing and poor visibility, failed to instruct Aircraft X to join the localizer, causing a potential conflict with Aircraft Y on 27L. The controller also misidentified Aircraft A as Aircraft B and allowed Aircraft Z and another aircraft to descend below 3 miles separation.

synopsis: A319 First Officer experiences an EGPWS terrain warning during a night visual approach to Runway 16R at RNO. Evasive action is taken initially then the approach is continued to landing.
summary: During a visual approach to Reno 16R, the crew received a terrain warning while turning to join the localizer near 7000 feet. The pilot attributes the alert to a high descent rate combined with a nearby hill, initiated an escape maneuver, and subsequently landed uneventfully.

synopsis: CE680 flight crew reports a track deviation during a flight to PSP via V208 TRM PSP. When the non-flying Captain in the right seat enters the VOR approach into the FMC a direct PSP is inadvertently selected, turning the aircraft toward high terrain.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring reported that after loading a backup approach, the FMS routed the aircraft directly from WARNE to PSP instead of continuing to TRM, causing a terrain alert. ATC intervened with climb and turn instructions to rejoin V208, resulting in a safe landing after the crew identified the programming error.

synopsis: B737-NG flight crew experiences a runway change during arrival to SEA on the HAWKZ 4 approaching COFAY. The ATIS had said to expect the ILS 16R and the runway and approach were changed to RNAV RNP Z Rwy 16C. During the change to this new procedure, a discontinuity is introduced and a track deviation occurs.
summary: The flight crew deviated laterally from the RNAV arrival while reprogramming the FMC for an unexpected RNAV (RNP) Z to Runway 16C clearance issued below 10,000 feet. The deviation resulted from a high workload causing a LEGS page discontinuity that disconnected LNAV, forcing the aircraft into CWS mode before the crew corrected the course.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported an uncommanded yaw motion during level flight at 17,000 feet with the First Officer flying and the autopilot engaged. The Captain assumed control and performed the uncommanded yaw motion memory items and called for the QRH. During this time it was determined that the rudder was trimmed full nose right and was adjusted back to center. No further rudder anomalies occurred and the flight continued to destination.
summary: During level flight at 17,000 feet, the crew experienced a violent right yaw caused by a suspected rudder trim runaway while the autopilot was engaged. The pilots manually controlled the aircraft, disconnected the yaw damper and autopilot, and completed a normal landing with no injuries.

synopsis: A321 Captain reports experiencing a terrain warning during a night visual approach to Runway 25L at LAS. Evasive action is taken then a left 360 is requested to lose altitude. During this maneuver the flying Captain switches of the automation off, becomes task saturated, and passes control of the aircraft to the First Officer.
summary: A fatigued crew flying a night visual approach to LAS encountered terrain alerts after deviating from the arrival path to cut a corner. The pilot manually climbed, requested a 360-degree turn to lose altitude, and transferred control to the first officer due to task saturation and loss of situational awareness.

synopsis: B737 Captain experiences a near collision with a ground vehicle during taxi at DEN. A turn by the Captain and hard braking by the vehicle driver averted the collision.
summary: The pilot and left seat crew member avoided a collision with a speeding ramp vehicle during taxi by executing an evasive turn. The vehicle passed under the right wing without impact after the driver braked, leading to a visual inspection, an ongoing investigation, and the pilot being placed on a fatigue list.

synopsis: Captain describes a failure of the main cabin door balancing mechanism as the door was opened from the exterior on an EMB505/Phenom 300. The cable apparently snapped throwing shards of metal from the cable into the cabin.
summary: A Phenom pilot reported a main cabin door balancing mechanism failure on the Phenom fleet when the door was opened from the exterior. The support cable snapped, ejecting metal shards and damaging the interior, creating a high risk of serious injury to crew or passengers.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) was informed the fuel nozzles that he and two other Technicians had installed on Number 2 Engine were not only incorrect Part Numbers (P/Ns), but the nozzles were scheduled to be installed on Number 1 Engine. Technician noted the paperwork for their B737-800 aircraft was confusing and not clear about which engine required work.
summary: Three mechanics replaced fuel nozzles on the wrong engine (#2 instead of #1) of a B737-800 because they failed to verify part numbers or work orders. The error was discovered the next day, prompting a recommendation for clearer paperwork and mandatory cross-checks against the IPC.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports there seems to be confusion about when a Bill of Work (BOW) and an Out of Service (OTS) Work-package should be generated for aircraft that are disabled, cannot be assigned a trip and do not have a scheduled Check. AMT references several of their Air Carrier Procedural Manual (PM) Chapters that support the BOW/ OTS Work-package requirement and the Non-compliance that resulted from not being issued.
summary: A B767-300 at ZZZ was Out of Service for a hydraulic leak without a required Work Package due to conflicting Procedures Manual interpretations. The reporter states this ambiguity caused non-compliance and confusion among mechanics regarding when such documentation is mandatory.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot departs HND airport and assumes he is cleared into the LAS Class Bravo because he is under flight following. Pilot violates LAS Class Bravo and is told to descend below it by LAS Approach Controller.
summary: A single-pilot aircraft departed HND and entered Class B airspace without clearance while climbing to 17,500 feet after a handoff to LAS Departure. The pilot descended immediately due to rising terrain and controller instruction, attributing the error to a misunderstanding that the handoff granted airspace entry.

synopsis: C207 Captain reports installing seats after a freight run but forgets to install the seatbelts that are stored in the seat back pocket. The standard passenger briefing is given and no passenger asks for help with their seatbelts. On the next passenger leg a passenger does ask and the lack of seatbelts is discovered.
summary: A pilot operating a freighter with reinstalled seats failed to install seatbelts on a passenger flight due to fatigue and distraction from a child's health issues. The pilot discovered the missing belts during loading, installed them, and reported the incident to management.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Pilot reports of receiving an amended clearance and having difficulties with other ATC facilities reference the clearance.
summary: Pilots flying to IAD experienced conflicting descent instructions after ATC changed their arrival from GIBBZ2 to DOCCS2 due to poor inter-facility communication. The crew clarified the correct procedure with controllers, executed a descent to 6000 feet, and maintained visual separation from another aircraft without TCAS alerts.

synopsis: C172 Instructor experiences a NMAC with an overtaking aircraft that had departed the same airport just after he had.
summary: A student pilot and instructor in a training aircraft departing LVJ Runway 14 experienced a close call when an experimental airplane climbed rapidly behind them and appeared 100–200 feet above. The reporter attributes the incident to the experimental pilot's failure to see the slower climbing aircraft and their own passive reliance on see-and-avoid rather than proactive separation.

synopsis: Aerial survey pilot, operating at 600-700 feet AGL due to weather, is informed after the fact that he may have flown too close to a drone operating in the same area.
summary: A pilot conducting an aerial photography mission in low ceilings and turbulence descended to approximately 600–700 feet AGL, prompting a complaint from a drone operator in the same vicinity. The pilot attributed the incident to potential conflicts between low-flying aircraft and drones in the boundary layer and plans to monitor altitude and drone activity more carefully.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZFW Controller thinks he issued a lower altitude to an aircraft and put that altitude in the data block. Controller ships aircraft to next sector and observes aircraft climbing above altitude that he thought he was assigned.
summary: An air traffic controller mistakenly cleared Aircraft X to climb to FL330 while intending FL310 due to a conflict, causing the aircraft to climb to FL322. The controller admitted the error after the pilot acknowledged a subsequent instruction to maintain FL320.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain describes the circumstances leading up to an unstabilized approach after nearly three months off flight status.
summary: The Captain, returning from medical leave, flew a Boeing 787-800 into Chicago where four rapid approach changes caused distraction. This led to a late configuration and unstabilized ILS 13C approach, resulting in a firm landing with abrupt deceleration.

synopsis: A B747-400 Captain advised the Jeppesen STAR identifiers for arrivals into ZBAA are not the same as the line selectable STARs in their FMS database.
summary: Flight crews at ZBAA struggled to select the correct STAR in the FMC when approach control made last-minute changes. The issue occurred because Jeppesen STAR names do not match FMC names, and the Jeppesen binder lacks a key page to correlate the two.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain laments a continuing problem he sees with Customer Service Representatives not properly noting Persons Carrying Firearms (PCFA) on the Passenger Count Form and not briefing multiple PCFA's of the presence and location of the others.
summary: The pilot reported that Customer Service Representatives failed to list an armed FBI agent in the correct section of the Passenger Count Form and neglected to inform other armed passengers of each other's presence. The reporter attributed these recurring procedural failures to a lack of CSR training.

synopsis: A B777 Captain reported extreme difficulty in taxiing to the gate following a low minima autoland on Runway 19L at IAD. Inoperative taxiway lights and inadequate taxiway markings were cited as contributing factors.
summary: After an autoland to Rwy 19L at Dulles, the crew reported difficulty taxiing due to visibility below the reported 800 FT RVR, missing edge lights, and faded markings. The pilot attributed this to poor lighting and paint conditions, recommending RVR restrictions or follow-me vehicles until repairs are made.

synopsis: Captain experiences a L COWL A/I warning message during descent for landing and elects to divert to a suitable airport without icing in the forecast. The aircraft had a history of six previous similar writeups and Dispatch was not helpful in finding an alternate.
summary: The crew diverted the aircraft due to a L COWL A/I warning caused by a large hole in a duct. They selected an alternate destination after Flight Ops suggested options requiring descent through ice, forcing the pilots to independently research weather conditions.

synopsis: A reporter advises he has resorted to devices such as a personal O2 supply and mask to combat debilitating ENT [Ear-Nose-Throat] effects of TKS fluids ingested in the AC systems of his company's C208 fleet. He also utilizes a spray painting vapor mask to combat the fluids vapors during walk-arounds.
summary: A pilot flying a TKS-equipped Caravan enroute reported inhaling alcohol fumes from the TKS system when operating cabin heat, causing throat irritation and light-headedness. The pilot attributes the fumes to residual fluid drain-down entering the bleed air system and warns of ongoing health hazards from repeated exposure.

synopsis: B777 Captain reports discovering enroute that ZSPD weather, which was forecast to be VFR, was now IFR with low ceiling and visibility. With questionable diversion airports available the Captain elects to wait out the assigned holding and lands safely.
summary: The Captain and First Officer, with a Line Check Airman, diverted to ZSPD due to unforecast IFR weather and holding delays that depleted fuel below alternate requirements. After dispatch failed to provide a viable alternate, the crew declared an emergency and successfully executed a CAT III autoland on the first attempt.

synopsis: Four days after servicing crew oxygen on a CRJ-200 aircraft, a Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) realizes the green bottle he used was actually a nitrogen bottle. Aircraft was grounded shortly after.
summary: A line truck mechanic servicing a CRJ-200 at the gate mistakenly used a nitrogen bottle, assuming it was oxygen due to similar green coloring and lack of warning signs. The mechanic serviced the aircraft with 120 psi of gas before discovering the error and notifying management.

synopsis: A track deviation occurred when the flight crew of a C560XL turned right toward SLI as they approached MUSEL, having misinterpreted the plan view depiction of the MUSEL SID off SNA and failing to have briefed the textual description which requires flights to maintain a 177 degree heading for vectors to MUSEL.
summary: The flight crew departed SNA on the MUSEL7 procedure, executing a right turn before the MUSEL intersection due to a Jeppesen chart depiction that conflicted with the text description. The crew later identified the chart error, which incorrectly suggested a direct route to MUSEL instead of a heading for vectors, though no traffic conflict occurred.

synopsis: Lear 25 flight crew experiences a rapid decompression at FL410 and initiates an immediate emergency descent but does not declare an emergency, even when queried by ATC. The bleed valves are successfully reset at FL270 and the crew returns to FL410 using supplemental oxygen for the remainder of the flight.
summary: Pilots experienced rapid decompression at FL410, descending to FL265 due to autopilot altitude capture failure and porpoising caused by excessive nose-down attitude. After resetting bleed valves to fix pressurization, they climbed back to FL410 where the autopilot porpoised for 30 minutes before stabilizing, prompting a post-flight report regarding a possible pilot deviation.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: General aviation pilot reports landing at the wrong airport after a high EGT reading causes him to turn back to T41. The GPS is misprogrammed for EFD instead of T41 and between troubleshooting and maneuvering the reporter ends up landing on Runway 22 at EFD instead of Runway 23 at T41. The high EGT indication was found to be a false indication due to a loose EGT probe.
summary: A pilot flying a VFR flight from LaPorte (T41) landed at the wrong airport, Ellington Field (EFD), due to tunnel vision caused by a high EGT reading and a GPS waypoint error. The pilot subsequently returned to T41 after discovering the loose EGT probe and the incorrect landing.

synopsis: Lear 31 Captain experiences difficulty locating PDK Runway 21L during a night visual approach. The RNAV Y to Runway 21L had been loaded in the FMC for situational awareness but the 15 degree offset was not noticed, causing confusion.
summary: The flight crew conducting a night visual approach to runway 21L at PDK initially misaligned due to overlooking a 15-degree RNAV offset on the approach plate. After verifying their position with the tower controller, they corrected their alignment and landed uneventfully without traffic conflicts.

synopsis: BE33 pilot under instruction reports rejecting a takeoff at low speed due to the control column becoming stuck in the full aft position.
summary: During a third stop-and-go practice of a power-off 180 landing, the flight control column failed and stuck in the full aft position before takeoff. The pilot aborted the takeoff prior to applying full power and taxied the aircraft back to parking with no injuries.

synopsis: Commercial pilot on a flight review was instructed by ATC to hold 2,500 feet. While setting up for an airspace transition, the pilot inadvertently descended to 2,200 feet.
summary: During a bi-annual flight review at Goodyear Airport, the pilot descended below the tower-instructed 2,500 feet to approximately 2,200 feet while transitioning to Glendale Airport. The pilot attributed the altitude deviation to distraction and intimidation by the instructor, noting a failure to maintain the assigned altitude before exiting Class D airspace.

synopsis: Cessna 340 pilot is instructed by Approach Control to call CHD Tower, however, the CHD Controller re-directs the pilot to call IWA for permission to cross IWA airspace. Pilot entered IWA airspace before contacting the tower.
summary: A pilot descending for landing at CHD reported that PHX Approach terminated radar coverage without handing off to IWA Tower, despite the pilot already being in IWA airspace. The pilot noted no traffic advisories were given and questioned why the handoff was not performed.

synopsis: ZJX Controller reports of automation that does not work well and causes confusion with controllers if aircraft are or are not direct certain fixes.
summary: An air traffic controller lost separation between Aircraft X and Aircraft Y while descending to 11,000 feet near CLT due to unclear relief briefing details and system limitations preventing flight plan amendments. The controller issued speed and vector corrections to restore separation after realizing both aircraft were not proceeding to the intended BOOZE intersection.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZAB Controller uses altitude leaving rule and has a loss of separation.
summary: An air traffic controller managing two landing aircraft (SDL and IWA) issued conflicting descent clearances while applying the "observed leaving an altitude" rule. The controller reported a loss of vertical separation and recommended workforce education on the proper application of this rule to prevent similar incidents.

synopsis: ZAU Controller describes situation where he is trying to display a TFR on the radar scope, and has to go back to the TMU multiple times to find the correct radius.
summary: An air traffic controller conducting OJT struggled to display active TFRs due to missing radii, incorrect coordinate formats, and conflicting information from the CIC and TMU. This caused significant delays in depicting areas A, B, C, and D on the ERAM system while managing high traffic volume.

synopsis: B737-300 Captain reports attempting to climb to FL360 with the FMC indicating the optimum altitude is FL358. For unknown reasons the aircraft will not climb above FL355 with the autopilot engaged and begins accelerating. The crew requests FL340 and is cleared to descend. Post flight investigation indicates that an alpha floor event was triggered.
summary: Pilots climbing from FL340 to FL360 encountered an uncommanded descent when the MCP reverted to Level Change mode and airspeed exceeded .76. The crew attributed the Alpha Floor Excursion to being heavier than expected and light turbulence, noting that training on disengaging the autopilot was insufficient.

synopsis: When cleared to descend via a STAR, the flight crew of an A320 failed to cross an intersection at or above FL240 as charted. Both pilots advised the restriction was not in the aircraft's NAV database.
summary: The flight crew missed a ZZZZZ intersection altitude constraint during descent due to an FMC database error, compounded by fatigue and turbulence from a pre-flight injury. ATC queried the crew at 19,000 feet, and the pilot attributed the oversight to the missing database data and physical distraction.

synopsis: PC12 Captain experiences severe turbulence and heavy rain while attempting to fly through a cold front with thunderstorms. Neither NexRad nor onboard radar displayed the severity of the weather encountered. Once clear the flight diverts to a suitable airport.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence, icing, and a stall warning while maneuvering around a cold front in IMC conditions, despite ATC claiming no exits existed. The pilots recovered the aircraft, descended to warmer altitudes, and landed safely at Airport ZZZ with no visible damage.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Zenair pilot reports pilot entry door opening just after rotation. On downwind during return to the airport the leg door departs the aircraft. A normal landing ensues.
summary: Pilots reported that the entry door opened just after rotation despite pre-flight verification, leading to a cleared return to the runway. The door subsequently detached on the downwind leg and was lost in a nearby swamp, but the aircraft landed without incident.

synopsis: While conducting the RNAV (GPS) Runway 15 approach to PGD the pilot of a BE35 misread the FAF crossing of 1,600 FT MSL as 1,000 FT MSL. A low altitude alert from ATC prompted a correction.
summary: A pilot on an RNAV 15 approach to Punta Gorda (KPGD) misread the FAF altitude as 1000 feet instead of 1600 feet. Tower queried the low altitude after receiving a report from Fort Meyer Approach, revealing obstacles in the area and highlighting the need for thorough approach briefings.

synopsis: C150 Private Pilot experiences power loss at 7,500 feet. An emergency is declared and the reporter descends through IMC to land at a suitable airport. The power loss is attributed to carburetor ice.
summary: The pilot experienced carburetor ice while flying over a valley, forcing an emergency descent through IMC due to engine power loss. Visible water drained from the air cleaner after landing, and the engine operated normally once the skies cleared two hours later.

synopsis: P80 controller describes possible loss of separation and advises FUSION radar as not giving adequate updates as it should.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a potential loss of separation between two aircraft near OZIER due to understaffing, complex traffic, and poor FUSION system updates. The controller believes the aircraft were within 3 miles and attributes the situation to budget-driven staffing shortages and inadequate radar display capabilities.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZID Developmental uses the altitude leaving rule and ends up having a loss of separation.
summary: An air traffic controller descended Aircraft X from FL350 and Aircraft Y from FL360 to FL350 while landing at LEX, triggering a conflict alert and RA on Aircraft Y. The controller attributed the event to Aircraft X's slower-than-normal descent rate, noting that separation rules were applied correctly.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZID instructor reports of his developmental descending aircraft using the vacated altitude rule, which led to a loss of separation.
summary: A developmental controller cleared two converging aircraft to descend, resulting in a TCAS resolution advisory for Aircraft Y due to Aircraft X's slow 500 fpm descent rate. The reporter attributes the event to the pilot's uncoordinated choice of descent speed rather than a standard rate.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: FAY Approach controller describes seeing an aircraft lower than what they thought they assigned, at an altitude right at the MVA. Controller listened to tapes and pilot read back incorrect altitude, but controller did not catch it.
summary: A trainee controller assigned 2,300 feet for an ILS approach, but the pilot read back and descended to 2,000 feet. The controller assumed the pilot was at 2,300 feet until the pilot confirmed the lower altitude, highlighting a failure to verify readbacks.

synopsis: During arrival into TPA, a B737-800 First Officer reports requesting a weather deviation along with numerous pilots. The frequency becomes completely congested and the Controller becomes unresponsive. The crews involved deviate around the weather at will without any input from ATC. Eventually a frequency change is issued and the crew continues to a normal landing.
summary: Pilots descending into TPA on the FOOXX4 STAR initiated an 80-degree deviation to avoid severe weather after ATC frequency congestion prevented controller response. The crew self-vectoring around the weather until receiving a handoff, attributing the situation to the controller losing the picture and failing to manage traffic.

synopsis: When there was a delay in shutting down the left engine of the B-737 at the gate due to being unable to power the aircraft with the GPU, a wing walker walked in front of the engine and was nearly sucked into it.
summary: The pilot shut down the #1 engine after concluding the GPU was inoperative while waiting at the gate. The outbound Captain later reported that a left wing walker nearly entered the running engine, causing a near-fatal incident.

synopsis: EMB505 Flight crew experiences an airborne conflict during a visual approach to Runway 35 at TRM. The crew made position reports during pattern entry, downwind and base. As they are about to turn final a Cessna announces entering Runway 17 for departure and does not respond to requests from the EMB505 crew to allow them to land first. A go-around is initiated and a TCAS RA is complied with.
summary: Two pilots flying a passenger aircraft to TRM executed a missed approach and received a TCAS climb resolution advisory after a Cessna departed Runway 17 without proper CTAF communication. The Cessna passed 500 feet below the passenger aircraft, prompting the pilots to land safely on Runway 17 after the other pilot failed to respond to radio queries.

synopsis: A C208 pilot is asked by Maintenance to use the TKS anti icing system in flight to see if the cockpit sealing procedures were effective. They were not and the reporter develops the typical TKS exposure symptoms, headache, general fatigue, slight nausea, throat irritation, breathing restriction and lightheadedness.
summary: A pilot experienced TKS fume symptoms, including headache and breathing restriction, while checking cockpit sealing procedures in the aircraft. The exposure caused temporary incapacitation requiring a medical visit, leading the pilot to recommend always wearing an oxygen mask during TKS system tests.

synopsis: Captain of a B737-800 accidentally turns off the Hydraulic 'B' pumps vice the Engine anti-ice which he was reaching for. Shortly after, the Yaw damper light turns on and the crew notices the aircraft not slowing as expected. Noticing something isn't right they announce a go-around to work the problem and realize the Captain's mistake. Switches are corrected and warning lights turn off and flaps are retracted on schedule. Landing follows shortly after.
summary: The pilot flying a Boeing 737 inadvertently turned off the B system hydraulic pumps while attempting to deactivate engine anti-ice, causing flap disagreement and speed control issues during descent. After executing a go-around and restoring the pumps, the crew completed an uneventful landing.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew experiences numerous electrical faults, including two generator faults, during initial climb with the Captain flying. The APU is started and the electrical system is stabilized, although several faults remain. During descent the process starts over and an emergency is declared for landing at destination. Maintenance finds water in several compartments housing avionics and electrical equipment.
summary: The MD-11 crew experienced multiple electrical failures and display losses during climb-out and descent, suspecting water intrusion into avionics compartments. Maintenance confirmed excess water in belly compartments, leading to an emergency declaration and a visual approach to the destination.

synopsis: When both runway 4 ILS's at EWR were out of service the flight crew of a B767 debated with Dispatch about their legality to fly the published RNAV procedures.
summary: The flight crew held over SLT while approaching EWR because ILS approaches were unavailable and they were unqualified for the required RNAV approach. Dispatch incorrectly advised them to proceed based on a misinterpretation of the FOM, but the crew refused until the ILS was restored.

synopsis: EMB190 Captain experiences severe turbulence caused by windshear during descent. Momentary loss of control occurs with airspeed varying from 220 knots to well above the barber pole while attempting to maintain 250 knots. The flight plan weather packet did not accurately portray the severity of the turbulence.
summary: During descent from 11,000 to 5,000 feet, the crew encountered severe turbulence caused by vertical shear and strong horizontal winds, resulting in uncommanded bank angles and airspeed excursions exceeding redline. Although loose items were thrown and passengers struck cabin surfaces, no injuries were reported despite inadequate pre-flight turbulence information from dispatch.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew experienced a 'left and right wing anti-ice fail' EICAS message on approach in icing conditions, descended below icing and landed without incident. After system checked OK on the ground by Contract Maintenance, despite company pressure to continue, flight crew elected to delay departure until the following day due to forecast icing conditions enroute to final destination.
summary: The flight crew encountered icing and anti-ice system failures during descent, landing safely but refusing to depart the next day due to forecast severe icing and management pressure. They cited prudent risk management and FAA guidelines for cancelling the flight despite the aircraft being legally signed off.

aircraft: McDonnell Douglas Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Mcdonnell Douglas Widebody Captain reported encountering wake vortex in trail of a B747 on approach to ORD. Speed assignment from ATC was cited as a factor.
summary: A pilot on the WATSN 2 arrival into Chicago Center slowed from an assigned 300 knots to 250 due to decreasing separation, despite initial controller confusion. The pilot subsequently encountered wake turbulence from a preceding 747 on short final, attributing the safe outcome to the speed reduction and poor two-way communication.

synopsis: An instructor and his student suffered a close encounter with a tandem parachute drop shortly after takeoff.
summary: The instructor and student avoided a collision during takeoff when a tandem skydiving canopy dropped in front of the aircraft. The instructor executed a radical 90-degree bank and nose-down maneuver at 60 feet to evade the canopy and safely completed the climb.

synopsis: BE33 pilot reports descending the below the prescribed altitude during a practice RNAV approach to LOU in VMC. Both the aircraft GPS and the Tower give low altitude alerts.
summary: A pilot descended below the prescribed altitude during a practice RNAV approach, triggering attitude alerts from the tower and GPS. The pilot climbed back to the correct altitude and completed the approach, attributing the incident to a lack of vigilance in altitude control.

synopsis: A small aircraft instructor reports that despite many years of futile advocacy from users, the TUS airport has failed to improve the West Ramp area commensurately with the rest of the airport. The user's primary complaints are lack of area illumination and surface edge/taxiway lighting appropriate to the ongoing use of the area for night time operations.
summary: Pilots reported a long-standing lack of taxi lighting on the West Ramp at Tucson International Airport, citing airport management's repeated delays in the Master Plan as the cause. The reporter concluded that safety on the ramp has been neglected due to this pattern of procrastination.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ZJX Controller describes situation related to severe weather that has six aircraft declaring emergency because of the weather.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that six aircraft in the ZJX sector experienced engine power loss, pressurization failure, and icing during a stalled front. The controller attributed these emergencies to an unreported 30-degree temperature change at FL360-FL430, noting a lack of SIGMETs or other hazard warnings for pilots.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Controller reports of an aircraft that loses an engine, declares an emergency, and then lands at a new destination. Controller was concerned because he didn't give the aircraft a clearance to the new destination.
summary: An air traffic controller managed an emergency for Aircraft X at 9,000 feet after the pilot reported an engine failure and instrument loss. The controller issued a descent to 2,000 feet and landing clearance for a safe arrival, though they later realized they never formally amended the pilot's clearance to the destination.

synopsis: EMT Local Control Instructor reports while training, he let his Developmental get two aircraft get too close together, causing an NMAC report by one of the pilots.
summary: An air traffic controller trainee on the Local position caused a near mid-air collision between two aircraft in the VFR pattern by issuing conflicting instructions and failing to provide traffic advisories. The trainee turned one aircraft into another, resulting in a 50-foot separation, due to losing track of traffic while managing multiple arrivals and departures.

synopsis: S56 TMU controller reports of two aircraft departing SLC on the NSIGN departure that may have been issued lower than normal altitudes on the climb out, causing them to possibly enter a MVA that they weren't at yet.
summary: An air traffic controller in the SLC departure sector observed Aircraft X level off at 9,000 feet while climbing via a clearance to FL230, causing it to enter an 110 MVA at 10,600 feet. The controller attributed the incident to the "climb via" procedure, which the pilot likely misinterpreted as a restriction to maintain 9,000 feet.

synopsis: DAB TRACON Controller reports of an aircraft that requests a surveillance approach to DAB. Controller advises FLM then is ordered to combine his position to another Controller and then run the surveillance approach.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a supervisor forced them to close the S-AR scope to conduct a surveillance approach for an aircraft at DAB, doubling traffic on the N-AR scope. The controller stated this action compromised safety by overloading the remaining position during high traffic volume.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZMP Controller reports of confusion of two STARS that go to one airport with similar fixes. Controllers do not know what STAR the pilots are actually flying until reporting in or questioned.
summary: An air traffic controller re-routed Aircraft X, but the pilot flew the ERNNY2 arrival instead of the expected MADII1 because the flight plan did not require reading back the arrival name. The controller reported this is unsafe due to overlapping STARs and potential FMS programming errors, recommending a single STAR with different transitions.

synopsis: VNY Local Instructor reports of a VFR airspace violator that enters VNY airspace and causes havoc while attempting to land in IFR conditions. Two aircraft are sent around and three departures are delayed.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managing VNY airspace during IFR weather directed a VFR violator (Aircraft X) to land while issuing missed approaches to two IFR arrivals (Aircraft Y and Z) to avoid conflicts. The controller attributed the confusion to unnecessary sector splits and a dangerous missed approach procedure that directed aircraft into another airport's arrival stream.

synopsis: B747 Captain reports a near collision with a regional jet during initial taxi out from the ramp at ORD. The RJ was on inbound Ground and taxiing very fast.
summary: The pilot reported a near collision at ORD while taxiing outbound on Alpha taxiway when an inbound RJ aircraft passed under their nose. The incident occurred because the larger RJ did not yield despite the pilot stopping after crossing the hold line, prompting a report to ground control.

synopsis: When all three landing gear failed to retract after takeoff the flight crew of a Q400 aircraft conducted a flawed checklist, got three green lights nonetheless, declared an emergency and returned uneventfully to their departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced a landing gear retraction failure after takeoff and initially misinterpreted the checklist, responding "YES" to a verification item instead of following the correct arrow. This error led to an unnecessary gear extension command, but the gear eventually extended normally, allowing for a safe landing.

synopsis: Pilot reports of being questioned by Controller as to why they aren't climbing. Pilot responds they were climbing via and leveling to make restrictions on the departure. Controller advises pilot to climb. Debate ensues between pilot, Controller and Front Line Manager (FLM). Pilot is not sure of what to do when climbing out.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X departing KIAH on the MMUGS1 SID leveled at 4,000 feet to honor a published constraint but was told by Houston Departure to climb to 16,000 feet without "unrestricted" wording. The controller mocked the pilot's request for clarification, leading to a heated exchange and a report questioning whether local norms override standard altitude constraints.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: MD-80 Captain described limitations of his aircraft FMS that makes flying complex DFW RNAV arrivals difficult.
summary: A pilot reported that an MD-80's FMS failed to compute ETAs or provide VNAV guidance during the BOOVE 1 RNAV arrival into DFW. The crew manually managed the descent using airspeed and vertical speed modes, complying with all constraints while the system recovered after the arrival.

synopsis: CRJ700 Captain laments inaccurate runway surface condition report by JAC Tower. Tower reports a wet runway when in fact dry, resulting in removal of passengers and cargo.
summary: The pilot reported that ATC inaccurately broadcast wet runway conditions at XA45Z, XB45Z, and XC45Z, despite the runway being dry by FAA definition. This error forced dispatch to reduce contingency fuel, passengers, and cargo, compromising operational efficiency and safety margins.

synopsis: B737-300 flight crew reports discovering that the First Officer's airspeed indicator is inoperative above 80 knots when the he calls it out. The Captain takes time to analyze the situation and initiates a reject at 120 knots.
summary: The First Officer reported no airspeed indication during takeoff roll due to an intermittent instrument failure, prompting the Captain to reject the takeoff at approximately 120 knots. The aircraft stopped safely on the remaining runway, and the crew completed a 30-minute brake cooling hold before returning to the gate.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew after landing on Rwy 14 at LNK and exiting at the end of the runway was confused by the conflicts between the Jeppesen 10-9 display of the exit area and the actual layout of the hard surface in that area. Cited as contributing factors were a night arrival and the ability of his iPad tablet to expand the chart for greater detail...in this case inaccurate detail. Of significant importance is the fact that the hard surface area in that location does not connect to Runway 17/35 as shown on the chart.
summary: The flight crew experienced confusion while taxiing at night at LNK due to inaccuracies on the Jeppesen 10-9 chart regarding the area beyond Runway 14. The chart incorrectly depicted the runway end position and taxiway connections, leading the crew to request a chart update to prevent future confusion.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported being targeted by a laser on a visual approach to SFO that later resulted in a trip to the emergency room and degraded visual acuity.
summary: The pilot reported being illuminated by a green laser for approximately 20 seconds during a visual approach to SFO at 2500 feet, originating from west-northwest of San Carlos. The exposure caused temporary vision degradation in the pilot's left eye, requiring an emergency room visit, though the landing remained normal.

synopsis: After initiating descent on a visual approach with glideslope out of service, an A319 Flight Crew initiated a go-around when flight director caused airspeed increase and climb to intercept altitude set for ILS to previously assigned runway.
summary: The First Officer became task-saturated while reprogramming the FMGC after a clearance change from visual to ILS 22L, causing the aircraft to exceed max flap speed while descending. The Captain initiated a go-around to correct the exceedance after the First Officer realized the error just in time.

synopsis: B737 flight crew experiences stiff flight controls as the takeoff roll is initiated and the takeoff is rejected at low speed. Upon performing a second flight control check the autopilot disconnect horn sounds and the crew returns to the gate for maintenance.
summary: Pilots rejected takeoff on a delayed flight after experiencing stiff controls and an unexpected autopilot disconnect warning during the roll. Maintenance identified an "autonomous fail" code, concluding the autopilot engaged unintentionally between preflight checks and departure despite no crew input.

synopsis: Ground personnel reports discovering ice on the back side of the fan blades during his walk around inspection and reporting it to his manager. The manager takes a look and does not believe it is significant and the aircraft is allowed to depart.
summary: A mechanic with 17 years of deicing experience found icing on fan blades during a walk-around and advised the push driver and manager to clear the contamination. The manager authorized the aircraft to proceed despite the ice, reportedly due to pressure from multiple planes waiting for gates.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reports slowing down to avoid hitting a speeding catering truck, while approaching his gate in PHL.
summary: The captain reported that while taxiing an aircraft at PHL, a catering truck accelerated to approximately 60 mph on the outer roadway to beat the aircraft to the gate. The pilot slowed to avoid a collision, noting the driver failed to yield at stop points despite the aircraft having the right-of-way.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew describes the events leading up to a taxiway excursion while attempting to taxi away from the gate with new snow covering all surfaces. The aircraft is eventually towed back to the gate for a maintenance inspection.
summary: The flight crew of an aircraft at CYWG taxied off the concrete apron onto snow-covered grass during a left turn after pushback due to poor visibility and a misaligned pushback angle. The aircraft was recovered without damage after passengers were deplaned, with the pilot attributing the incident to lost situational awareness and lack of communication with ramp agents.

synopsis: A Captain describes two situations involving their Hawker HS-125-800XPC aircraft with Honeywell TFE 731 engines. Pilot noticed the #-1 engine oil temperature would not come up to the minimum 'green' arc during taxi-out that was found to be an internally cracked fuel/oil heater dumping fuel into the oil system. He also explains the history and confusion for pilots between the company's Aircraft Operations Manual (AOM) versus the Manufacturer's Aircraft Flight Manual (AFM) regarding when to taxi with engine oil temperatures not yet in the 'green' arc.
summary: The pilot of a Hawker HS-125-800XPC experienced low Engine #1 oil temperature due to a cracked oil/fuel heater allowing fuel contamination. The pilot also realized they incorrectly taxied with Engine #1 oil temperature below the green arc, violating the operator's AOM limitation which prohibits taxiing until temperatures are normal.

synopsis: EMB-175 First Officer hand flying on departure climb, became confused by the disparity between the Flight Director and the Path Vector on the PFD, lost airspeed, nosed over when the stick shaker activated then pulled up after an overspeed and reactivated the stick shaker. Captain talked the First Officer through the recovery process.
summary: The pilot flying experienced a stick shaker activation during climb after becoming confused by conflicting Flight Director and Path Vector indications while turning ahead of the heading bug. The pilot attributed the incident to inexperience with the display and overconfidence, but recovered airspeed following the Captain's calm instructions to lower the nose.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew experiences a possible brake application during takeoff with the First Officer flying, who denies touching the brakes. When a second more vigorus application is felt the Captain rejects the takeoff.
summary: During takeoff roll near 80 knots, the First Officer and Captain felt uncommanded braking jolts without aural warnings, prompting a rejected takeoff. Maintenance suspected a faulty brake control valve as the cause, though no obvious damage was found, and passengers deplaned normally.

synopsis: A Mechanic removed a component from the aircraft to perform a repair. In the process, the Mechanic notified the Flight Attendant to advise the Flight Crew to write it up. When the Mechanic returned to the gate, the aircraft had departed without the component.
summary: Mechanics repaired logbook items and removed an ELT with a loose release tape for repair, instructing the flight attendant to log the discrepancy. The aircraft departed early without the ELT because the flight attendant likely forgot to inform the crew, leaving the unit in the mechanics' possession.

synopsis: King air pilot descending in the traffic pattern experiences a NMAC with a PA28 at 1500 feet overflying the airport. The King air pilot was descending at a high rate and making position reports while the PA28 pilot was apparently not on the the CTAF. Visual contact occurred too late to evade.
summary: A skydive pilot descending on downwind at 1500 feet AGL for Runway 30 encountered a Piper Cherokee flying level through the pattern without CTAF communication. The pilot passed behind and below the Cherokee due to the other aircraft's failure to report position and reduced visibility from haze and sun glare.

synopsis: C182 pilot learns how long his aircraft will fly starting with full tanks and one fuel cap not installed (two hours). A successful engine off landing is accomplished at the nearest airport and the problem is diagnosed.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine failure at 4,000 feet due to fuel exhaustion caused by an unsecured right fuel cap, which also resulted in erroneous fuel gauge readings. The pilot executed an uneventful power-off landing at a nearby grass strip after realizing the missing cap post-incident.

synopsis: When both engines failed simultaneously on the UC-1 'Twin Seabee' the two pilots aboard collaborated to land safely in an open field where one wheel became mired but no damage or injuries resulted. No mention or speculation as to the cause of the dual failures was provided.
summary: Two occupants experienced an engine power failure at 1,300 feet AGL during descent, likely caused by the pilot flying's dead foot on the throttle. They executed a precautionary landing in a farmer's field with no injuries or aircraft damage, though the right wheel sank into the turf.

synopsis: Business jet Captain reports descending to the final approach fix altitude at RST using the wrong altimeter setting, resulting in being 1,000 feet low. ATC is queried and the correct altimeter setting is provided along with a low altitude alert.
summary: During an ILS approach to runway 31 at RST, the first officer entered an incorrect altimeter setting of 30.21 instead of 29.21, placing the aircraft 1,000 feet below assigned altitude. The pilot initiated a climb after a low altitude alert, and the crew landed safely following a CRM failure where the first officer did not report difficulty understanding the weather broadcast.

synopsis: A conflict resulted when a King Air C90 departing Runway 12 and an arriving sailplane on Runway 30 failed to co-ordinate their operations. The sailplane altered its arrival runway to facilitate separation.
summary: A skydive pilot departing RWY 12 at a non-towered airport nearly conflicted with a glider turning base for RWY 30, which switched to RWY 23 to avoid the aircraft. The pilot attributed the near miss to high traffic volume and communication timing, noting the glider should have announced position earlier and not turned base after the departure call.

synopsis: CE560 flight crew reports being queried by PHX Departure Control about their compliance with the BXK3 Departure. The crew was flying a 070 degree heading past the point at which they should have turned to a 100 degree heading.
summary: Departure control mistakenly believed the tower had assigned a runway heading of 100 degrees to a crew flying the BXK3 departure from Phoenix. The controller issued a new heading after confusion arose regarding the SID procedures, though no aircraft conflict occurred.

synopsis: The pilot of a C-182, after experiencing difficulty starting and utilizing a jump start to begin his days round trip, experienced multiple electrical and nav system malfunctions and failures during his night return to departure airport. Anxiety about going around with increasing failures triggered a decision to land on a taxiway.
summary: A pilot returning VFR to ZZZ experienced repeated avionics failures and low voltage warnings, forcing a go-around and an emergency landing on Taxiway Quebec. The incident resulted from prior jump-start issues and the pilot's initial failure to report system difficulties to the tower.

synopsis: PA31 pilot reports departing RMN VFR to pick up an IFR flight plan airborne. An IFR clearance is issued then a few minutes later it is canceled and the reporter is told to turn 20 degrees right, descend to a VFR altitude and contact PCT on a different frequency. The new Controller points out traffic and the reporter deduces the IFR clearance cancellation was due to this traffic.
summary: A pilot reported that after departing RMN on an IFR flight, the initial controller terminated the clearance to avoid a King Air conflict without coordinating with the next sector. This caused confusion and resulted in less than 500 feet vertical separation with the military aircraft before IFR status was resumed.

synopsis: A BE-36 pilot suffered a nose gear collapse after the landing gear failed to extend during traffic pattern practice and the alternate gear extension procedure was utilized but failed to illuminate the gear down indications.
summary: A solo pilot flying a pattern proficiency flight experienced a nose gear collapse after manual extension due to a lack of gear down indications. The pilot landed safely with no injuries, though the nose gear collapsed at 50 kts, and admitted to forgetting their license and medical certificate.

synopsis: BJC CIC describes a low altitude alert issued to a PA42 on the ILS to Runway 30R. Several calls are required to get the pilot to respond and climb to a more appropriate altitude.
summary: A CIC controller issued Low Altitude Alerts to a PA42 inbound for Runway 30R after the aircraft deviated low and south of the ILS course. The pilot acknowledged and corrected, landing safely, though the cause remained uncertain between a localizer malfunction or autopilot issue.

synopsis: PHL Controller and pilots report of a runway incursion caused by possibly bad lighting on the taxiways and runway.
summary: A pilot and controller at PHL experienced a runway incursion when the pilot mistakenly turned left onto Echo 4 instead of right onto Echo, crossing Runway 35. The controller attributed the error to the confusing intersection layout and subsequently issued complex re-routing instructions to resolve the conflict.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: I90 Approach Controller describes a feed from a trainee that causes him to work harder then he should because the trainee is not following the SOP.
summary: The Final South controller reported that a training feeder's non-SOP vectors increased workload, leading to a descent clearance issue with Aircraft X. Although the controller failed to ensure descent to 2000 feet and speed compliance behind Aircraft Y, the pilot executed a go-around, causing delays and fuel burn without loss of separation.

synopsis: EVV FLM reports of a situation when maintenance is returning RADAR equipment back into service and the ARTS equipment doesn't work correctly.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller turned the CENRAP switch to OFF, causing a complete ARTS data loss and blank radar scope. The outage resulted from recent equipment room changes for STARS eLITE installation that altered the switch's function, which maintenance personnel failed to anticipate.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: HIO Local Controller describes a NMAC where an aircraft is told to follow an aircraft type on final, while there are two of the same type of aircraft on final. Downwind traffic turns in to follow wrong aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft A to follow a Cessna on final, but poor visibility and ambiguous instructions caused Aircraft A to misidentify the lead aircraft. Aircraft A executed an evasive climb to avoid a collision with Aircraft Z, which was also on final, before landing safely.

synopsis: Two B737-800 flight crews describe strange electrical problems that occur during gate arrival for the first crew and departure for the second crew. The aircraft would not accept ground power, then would not accept aircraft generator power without first turning the battery power off then on. The aircraft is grounded and turned over to Maintenance.
summary: The crew experienced a total electrical failure when connecting ground power at the gate with the APU inoperative and one engine running. Power was restored only after recycling the battery switch, a non-procedural action, though the previous crew had passed this unlogged anomaly to the incoming flight.

synopsis: B737 flight crew experiences a loss of cabin pressurization passing FL330 in the climb. The cabin altitude cannot be controlled and an emergency descent is initiated and a return to the departure airport is accomplished. The crew reported problems in the cabin with both passenger and Flight Attendant oxygen systems.
summary: Flight crew experienced rapid cabin pressurization loss climbing through FL330, peaking at 20,000 ft, likely due to a faulty controller. They executed an emergency descent to ZZZ, landing overweight and exceeding MMO/VMO, while reporting failed oxygen deployment and erratic valve behavior.

synopsis: Q400 First Officer reports descending below the JAKSN crossing altitude on the GLASR9 Arrival to SEA, after being vectored off the arrival and told to descend to 16000 feet then told to go direct JAKSN and descend via the arrival. The MCP altitude is reset to 12000 feet prior to capturing 16000 and the aircraft continues descending to 14800 before it is noticed.
summary: The flight crew descended below the assigned 16,000 ft while attempting to engage VNAV and reset the altitude alerter during the GLASR9 arrival into Seattle. The deviation occurred due to task saturation and premature automation changes, requiring a manual climb to 15,000 ft after an amended clearance was obtained.

synopsis: EMB135 flight crew departing RIC on Runway 20 experiences a conflict with an aircraft that had previously been cleared to land Runway 20. The crew detects the landing aircraft on short final and stops short of the runway and Tower sends the landing aircraft around.
summary: The flight crew at RIC held short of Runway 20 before crossing to Runway 16 for takeoff. They stopped just before entering Runway 16 after the captain spotted an aircraft on short final, which was simultaneously instructed to go around by tower due to limited visibility of the approach path from their holding position.

synopsis: CE560 Captain experiences a NMAC on short final during a day visual approach. An aircraft symbol was detected on TCAS in close proximity with no aural alert and a shallow climb is initiated. At 900 feet a TCAS RA is generated with any descent depicted as red and a go-around is initiated. A VFR aircraft that was told to report four miles, did not and was forgotten by the Tower.
summary: Pilots on final approach to runway 36 at 700 feet MSL detected a nearby target on TCAS without an initial advisory, prompting a shallow climb until a "monitor vertical speed" alert occurred at 900 feet. The crew attributed the delayed recognition to cumulative fatigue and recommended TCAS aural warnings extend to the ground.

synopsis: B737-900 Captain describes the FMC's reaction to a runway change entered during an RNAV arrival. A route discontinuity is created and the autopilot reverts to heading hold.
summary: During descent on the HAWKZ 4 arrival, a runway change to 16C caused an FMS disconnect and LNAV disengagement near PIKEZ. The pilot manually turned the aircraft while the first officer corrected the FMC software issue, which the reporter attributes to duplicate fixes appearing during mid-arrival runway changes.

synopsis: During climbout, a Captain and First Officer respond to a master warning light illumination and a right engine thrust reverser 'Arm' and 'Unlock' light on a Beech Jet BE-400XP. The right engine reverser did not indicate Re-lock after the Captain pushed the Right Emergency-Stow button on the glare shield. Crew declared an emergency and returned to departure airport.
summary: During climb out at 2000 ft MSL, the flight crew encountered a right engine thrust reverser unlock warning and illuminated emergency stow light. The captain pushed the emergency stow button, declared an emergency, and returned to ZZZ for an uneventful landing on runway 10L.

synopsis: Pilot reports of being advised of helicopter traffic while departing. Pilot sees traffic then rejects takeoff due to close proximity of traffic.
summary: A pilot rejected a takeoff on RWY 20R at SNA after a helicopter descended perpendicular to the departure path despite ATC stating it would remain east. The helicopter narrowly avoided collision by banking steeply at 100 feet left and 200 feet above the runway, prompting the pilot to criticize ATC's traffic information and clearance management.

synopsis: An R44 instructor pilot and his student suffered an NMAC with another aircraft as they were approaching their non-towered destination at night.
summary: During a night instrument training flight near ZZZ, the instructor and student flew 100–300 feet above another aircraft while the student was under the hood. The near mid-air conflict occurred due to traffic congestion near airspace boundaries and the instructor's fixation on previously reported traffic.

synopsis: C210 pilot experiences a loss of engine power during descent for landing after a five hour flight. When it is determined that the airport cannot be reached a highway is chosen for landing. The gear is extended late and the main gear do not extend fully before landing on the road.
summary: The pilot experienced a propeller control failure during descent, resulting in an engine power loss that forced a belly landing on a highway. The aircraft struck a road sign, rupturing the fuel tank and causing it to roll into a ditch, though the pilot evacuated safely.

synopsis: CL601 Captain reported climbing through an altitude restriction on departure from LAS. Wake turbulence distraction and a newly qualified First Officer were factors in the event.
summary: During departure from LAS, the pilot not flying misread a Jeppesen chart and set an incorrect altitude, causing an altitude limit violation. Contributing factors included the crew's inexperience with the specific avionics and charts, wake turbulence requiring manual flight, and pre-flight distractions that prevented a complete procedure review.

synopsis: BE58 pilot experiences pitot heat failure descending through icing conditions at 8000 feet. Within moments the AHRS begins to malfunction along with other components of the glass panel display. Backup instruments and GPS ground speed are used perform an ILS approach to landing. The reporter is informed by his avionics shop that loss of pitot input can cause loss of AHRS function. He believes that the system should be designed to operate normally with loss of pitot input.
summary: The pilot experienced a pitot heat failure during descent below 8,000 ft, causing airspeed loss and subsequent AHRS malfunctions that blanked the glass panel. The pilot completed the ILS approach using backup instruments, attributing the cascading failures to poor engineering design where pitot loss disables all AHRS functions.

synopsis: C180 pilot reports an engine failure on short final and a landing short of the field without damage or injury.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine failure on short final and landed in a field just short of the airport. The reporter stated there was no damage to the airplane or property.

synopsis: PCT Controller reports of confusion of routes when VIP flights depart the DCA airport.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a VIP departure from ADW to P56B during peak traffic and strong winds caused arrival delays and routing conflicts when the aircraft unexpectedly turned toward RFK Stadium. The controller attributed these issues to a lack of set procedures, undisclosed routes, and political barriers preventing operational improvements.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: CCR FLM describes a problem with the Radar system that shows duplicate beacon codes at times. Aircraft that are not removed from the system correctly tag up later in the day on another aircraft.
summary: A CCR controller observed a conflicting data block for Aircraft Y while monitoring Aircraft X on a VFR practice approach. The error occurred because the Northern California TRACON failed to clear an inactive data block, causing the ARTCC to reassign it to a new flight while the old call sign remained visible on local radar.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ABE TRACON and tower controllers describe a situation where two aircraft became a conflict resulting in traffic breaking themselves out to re-sequence.
summary: An arrival controller and local controller lost separation between Aircraft X and Aircraft Y during a visual approach to RWY 24. The local controller uncoordinated a turn for Aircraft X, creating a head-to-head conflict with Aircraft Y, which the arrival controller attributed to a procedural ban on monitoring arrival frequencies.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew believes that Runway 33L at BWI is unsafe while construction is in progress.
summary: A Boeing 737-800 pilot reported a visual approach to shortened Runway 33L at BWI where construction personnel and equipment were located directly under the glide path. The pilot cited increased accident risk due to conflicting glide slope guidance, missing touchdown markings, ungrooved surface conditions, and a lack of EMAS beyond the runway end.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reports having to brake to avoid a catering truck during initial taxi off the gate.
summary: During initial taxi after pushback, a catering truck approached the aircraft at high speed, forcing an abrupt stop to avoid a potential right wing conflict. The pilot reported the driver showed no regard for the aircraft's position and notified operations and the Chief to address the safety concern.

synopsis: A B737 Captain questions the legality of forecasted arrival weather. He is met with confrontation and attitude upon contacting the Dispatcher to receive an updated forecast and discuss the paperwork.
summary: The pilot reported that initial weather forecasts indicated an illegal landing due to wind limits on a wet runway. A confrontational Dispatcher only updated the forecast after being asked, changing the crosswind by one knot to make the flight legal while questioning the pilot's judgment regarding safety concerns.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports misunderstanding an MEL procedure and departing with the right pack off and the right bleed off for a right wing anti-ice valve fixed open. When the bleed valve is turned on, the pack valve is left off. The flight continued in single pack operation without difficulty. The pack should not have been turned off.
summary: The crew deferred a right wing valve per MEL and incorrectly turned the right Pack off for takeoff due to misinterpreting proviso (I). Although cabin pressure remained normal, the crew realized the MEL does not require the Pack to be off, attributing the error to ambiguous guidance rather than oversight.

synopsis: B757 flight crew encounters black ice during taxi out after a fuel stop. Braking action and steering are nil and the aircraft slides to the edge of the taxiway and is shut down.
summary: The flight crew lost braking and steering on black ice while taxiing a Boeing 757 on Taxiway A at ZZZZ, requiring reverse thrust to stop. Although the aircraft remained on pavement, the incident caused a 16-hour delay, crew timeout, and a subsequent deadhead return after passengers were denied disembarkation.

synopsis: A B-737 Captain was distressed when, after a night gate arrival, both cargo doors were opened although the left engine was still running while awaiting ground power availability. A station policy directing that APUs not be utilized on arrival aircraft was cited as a contributing factor, as the running engine was required to power aircraft systems including lighting for deplaning passengers.
summary: Ramp crew opened cargo doors and used a belt loader while engine number 1 ran and the beacon was on during gate arrival. The pilot reported this violated safe approach procedures, noting the ramp lead failed to intervene despite acknowledging the rule.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reports being cleared to taxi via U and Z to Runway 22R cross Runway 11-29. Approaching Runway 11-29 an aircraft is detected taking off on Runway 29 and the reporting Captain stops before the hold line as a Gulfstream rotates abeam Taxiway U.
summary: The flight crew, taxiing a heavy aircraft at Newark at night, stopped short of Runway 29 after spotting a departing Gulfstream despite holding a clearance to cross Runway 11. The near collision occurred because the controller was aware of the conflict but had not amended the taxi instructions before the other aircraft departed.

synopsis: An EMB-135 flight crew initially cleared by the GARDNER STAR but switched to descend on the QUABN RNAV STAR to BOS with a substantial tailwind--was unable to comply with an ATC directed crossing altitudes at UROWT. Multiple runway changes combined with imprecise altitude expectations created a flight crew workload environment that forced them to reply 'unable' to the last runway change.
summary: During descent into BOS on the QUABN 3 arrival, the crew failed to meet the UROWT crossing restriction due to late altitude clearances, strong tailwinds, and multiple runway changes. The aircraft crossed UROWT 1,100 feet high and 28 knots fast, with the pilot attributing the error to delayed clearances and increased workload from conflicting runway assignments.

synopsis: CE560 flight crew believes they may have violated company dispatch rules in a very complex dispatch situation. The first Dispatcher did not take the mountainous terrain and steep glideslope into consideration. The new Dispatcher and the crew did not catch a NOTAM requiring a local altimeter setting (which was missing) to fly the approach.
summary: The crew identified that Dispatch released a 91K flight violating night landing slope and tailwind limits, prompting a runway change and alternate addition. Although the crew departed after winds diminished, they noted the original release was invalid due to Dispatch errors stemming from staff reductions.

synopsis: A C-208 pilot reported suffering symptoms of TKS exposure consistent with those noted on the TKS 406B MSDS (Material Safety Data Sheet).
summary: A pilot on an IFR night flight at 11,000 feet in IMC activated the TKS anti-ice system and immediately smelled a cooked odor. The pilot subsequently experienced breathing difficulties, chest tightness, and throat irritation consistent with TKS chemical exposure symptoms.

synopsis: Distracted by ATC modifications to the constraints of a complex arrival and a late runway change the flight crew of a CRJ-700 failed to program and confirm the appropriate cabin altitude for the landing airport elevation and the cabin climbed rapidly to ambient upon touchdown.
summary: The flight crew missed setting the field elevation during a busy arrival with multiple ATC changes, causing rapid cabin depressurization on touchdown. The pilot attributed the error to being hyper-focused on meeting crossing restrictions and failing to cross-check the other pilot.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A Flight Attendant reports that photo-luminescent emergency floor path lighting strips on their Airbus aircraft were almost unnoticeable after a gate pushback and extended hold delay by ATC. Should an evacuation have been necessary during taxi-out or after an aborted takeoff, there would have been no floor path lighting available to direct passengers during an emergency egress.
summary: During a 45-minute ground delay caused by ATC computer malfunctions, cabin crew left photo-luminescent floor path lights uncharged despite the reporter's recommendation. Consequently, the lights were ineffective at takeoff, creating a potential safety hazard for evacuation due to a lack of manual guidance on recharging during delays.

synopsis: C414 pilot experiences a runaway elevator trim with the autopilot engaged and takes over manually. The elevator is retrimed and the autopilot re-engaged. During this time a frequency change is issued and contact with the next Controller is never established.
summary: The pilot experienced repeated autopilot disengagements and pitch-downs at FL230, requiring manual flight and trim adjustments. The reporter attributed the incident to a possible missed frequency change interruption and distraction caused by the autopilot malfunction.

synopsis: Despite multiple routine CTAF position reports while inbound the pilot of a DA-40 suffered an NMAC with a C-310 departing opposite direction from the airport's single runway. Post event alleged CTAF transmissions by the other pilot were not heard by the reporter or others monitoring the CTAF frequency.
summary: The reporter, landing on Runway 23 at E38, executed a missed approach after seeing Aircraft 2 taking off in the opposite direction without making Unicom announcements. The near miss was caused by Aircraft 2's failure to communicate and its use of the wrong runway orientation, despite high density altitude.

synopsis: After departing YIP a flight instructor and his instrument student were cleared direct to SVM, 'cleared for the VOR A approach;' as requested. After departing SVM, the IAF/FAF, on course for the VOR A approach to 1D2, Canton-Plymouth-Mettetal airport ATC advised of a track deviation. Further inquiry determined the clearance had been for the VOR-A approach at YIP, not the VOR-A to 1D2. SVM is the IAF for both procedures. The reporter did not recall if the airport name had been appended to either the clearance or his readback.
summary: During an instrument training flight, a pilot and student were inadvertently cleared for a VOR-A approach to YIP instead of the requested 1D2 due to ambiguous ATC instructions regarding the destination airport. The confusion was resolved without traffic conflict, prompting the pilot to adopt a practice of explicitly reading back the airport name in future approach clearances.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reports departing on an IFR flight plan in IMC. Climbing to 7,000 feet power becomes insufficient to continue climbing. Carb heat is tried along with fuel pump and switching tanks without success. ATC is advised and a diversion planned but the aircraft runs out of altitude before reaching the airport and lands in a muddy field.
summary: The pilot of a four-occupant aircraft experienced a loss of climb power near 5,000 feet during an IFR flight in rain, suspecting carburetor ice despite troubleshooting attempts. After ATC vectored the crew to an alternate, the pilot executed a forced landing in a muddy field at 400 feet AGL with no injuries or damage.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: BJC Local Controller describes a conflict with two arrival aircraft that he resolves by keeping one of the aircraft on an extended downwind.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a conflict between VFR Aircraft X and high, fast IFR Aircraft Y, which was switched late from approach control. The controller held Aircraft X on downwind, instructed Aircraft Y to climb and execute a missed approach for resequencing, and resolved the situation safely after Aircraft Y landed.

synopsis: ZAN Controller reports of an aircraft entering his airspace that takes a wrong turn. CPC queries pilot and determines route is different than what the controller had.
summary: An air traffic controller observed Aircraft X deviate from its filed route while crossing AMOTT at 12,000 feet, creating a potential loss of separation with slower traffic. The controller attributed the error to a discrepancy between the pilot's displayed routing and the flight plan, likely originating from an incorrect clearance or data entry prior to entering the sector.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports being unable to maintain the descent path on the JFRYE1 RNAV arrival to DAL with a 40 knot tailwind. ATC provides relief without being prompted.
summary: Pilots flying a Boeing 737 on the JFRYE 1 RNAV arrival into DAL encountered excessive altitude deviations and VNAV SPD reversion after JTROE due to steep descent gradients and tailwinds. Regional Approach issued a descent clearance to 5,000 feet, resolving the conflict, though the crew reported the arrival is un-flyable under these conditions.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reports departing with light freezing rain falling, without being anti-iced with type IV fluid. A study of the de ice sheet indicates they should have deiced with type I and anti-iced with type IV.
summary: The flight crew departed without re-deicing despite new freezing rain reports and a warning from another aircraft, later admitting they erred in judgment by failing to perform a required two-step deice. The Captain and First Officer agreed they should have taxied to the deice pad for Type 1 and Type IV fluid application before takeoff.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports landing in LAX with 3600 pounds of fuel due to a variety of factors, after expecting to land with 6600 pounds.
summary: The Captain reported arriving at LAX with only 3,600 lbs of fuel after ATC descent and speed restrictions increased burn, while FMC guidance initially suggested adequate reserves. The pilot attributed the low fuel state to a lack of communication with Dispatch regarding the full tanks and non-optimal landing fuel, noting no opportunity to divert to PHX or LAS.
