summary: During arrival, the crew descended to 6500 feet instead of maintaining 7000 feet because both pilots were distracted by programming a complex hold into the FMS. The altitude alerter was not reset, and the Captain failed to monitor the flight path while assisting with the confusing clearance.

synopsis: When the instructor pilot aboard a C172 misjudged the spacing between a landing Cessna and a following banner tow plane entering the pattern on a left base to drop the banner he told his student to takeoff immediately. During their initial climbout from the non-towered airport the pilot of the banner two advised on CTAF that they were climbing immediately below him.
summary: A pilot and student in a departing aircraft misjudged the speed of a banner tow aircraft on a high left base at an uncontrolled Class G airport. This resulted in a loss of separation as the banner tow descended 200 feet above the departing aircraft, caused by the tow's non-standard pattern entry and the pilot's poor judgment.

synopsis: AFW instructor reports of a loss of separation due to not sending an aircraft around after Developmental clears a jet for takeoff.
summary: A trainee controller cleared Aircraft Y for takeoff on Runway 34R while Aircraft X was on short final, incorrectly believing X would land before Y's departure roll. Aircraft X passed the displaced threshold as Y began its roll, forcing X to execute a touch-and-go to avoid a simultaneous operation conflict.

synopsis: HCF Controller describes a situation where an aircraft departs an airport under their control but does not follow the standard departure. Aircraft turns incorrectly and is in an area with a low MVA. Controller issues a vector towards a lower MVA and flight resumes safely.
summary: An air traffic controller in Sector R intercepted Aircraft X departing HHI after it climbed toward mountains on an unexpected radar vector instead of a SID. The controller attributed the error to an inexperienced colleague issuing a vector clearance due to a navaid outage and recommended TRACON controllers issue all HHI departures.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Recip Eng
synopsis: ZLA Controller describes a situation with a SCT Controller who doesn't take a call from ZLA and then tries to handoff the aircraft. ZLA needed the aircraft to make a restriction and the SCT Controller yelled they were busy. ZLA Controller didn't know if the SCT Controller gave the aircraft the restriction.
summary: A PSP controller reported a potential head-on conflict between an overflight on V386 and a PSP departure due to icing and restricted airspace. The incident occurred because a SoCal controller refused to answer calls or issue a required altitude restriction, forcing the reporter to maneuver the aircraft and delay the handoff.

synopsis: I90 Controller describes a loss of separation he finds out by the tool TARP advising the wake turbulence remnant. Controller wonders if this tool (TARP) can tell them that there was a loss of separation why can't it provide the controller information to prevent the loss.
summary: An air traffic controller managed Aircraft Y (heavy) and Aircraft X (large) on downwind legs for runways 26L and 27, instructing visual separation after Aircraft Y turned base. The controller disputes a TARP finding of wake turbulence violation, asserting that lateral separation exceeded minimums and available tools were used to maintain safety.

synopsis: An air carrier on the SFO 28R localizer took evasive action and executed a go around after another air carrier on the 28L localizer drifted 400 feet over them with no ATC intervention.
summary: During an ILS approach to Runway 28R, a parallel RJ aircraft descended over the reporting crew at 400 feet separation, triggering a descent RA. The crew executed a go-around after breaking off the approach to avoid the RJ, which had incorrectly flown the 28R localizer before correcting to Runway 28L.

synopsis: Confusion between two different flight level/meter conversion tables and a small error in the altitude reporting of the transponder resulted in a small altitude deviation and a corrective clearance from ATC for the flight crew of a B747.
summary: During departure from Beijing, the crew climbed to FL292 using an FOM conversion chart instead of the enroute chart, while a faulty right transponder reported an additional 100 feet high. ATC issued an immediate descent and turn to avoid traffic after detecting the aircraft was 200 feet above the assigned 8,900 meters.

synopsis: A B757 developed an unfamiliar odor during the first takeoff and climb on a ferry flight following heavy maintenance. The distracted crew had a track deviation and determined after the flight that new brakes were the odor's source.
summary: The flight crew experienced vibration and a hot rubber odor during takeoff and climb, suspecting a tire failure but later identifying new brake pads as the cause. Distraction from the fumes led to an unintentional deviation from the LNAV departure routing, which was corrected after ATC intervention, resulting in an uneventful landing.

synopsis: An ERJ-175 rudder trim indication was MELed, but the crew discovered after flying two legs that substantial left trim was needed for coordinated flight. Maintenance removed the aircraft from service.
summary: Pilots operated an aircraft with an inoperative Yaw Trim Indicator MEL, experiencing excessive rudder trim requirements and taxi pull due to vague MEL procedures and maintenance errors. The aircraft was grounded after maintenance agreed the MEL was incorrect, citing potential control issues during an engine failure.

synopsis: A commercial pilot reports the current Jeppesen airport page for BRO does not reflect the current identification of the airport runways.
summary: The pilot reported that Jeppesen 10-9 charts for BRO remained incorrect regarding runway numbering changes, causing cockpit confusion when cleared to cross a runway not depicted on the chart. The reporter attributed this to Jeppesen's failure to proactively publish updated plates despite the runway changes occurring over a month prior.

synopsis: A Maintenance Controller reports about the sheer volume of work that contributed to a B777 aircraft being dispatched with a known damaged flaperon installed. Major contributors were failure of their Work (Job) Card Management System to issue job cards and multiple aircraft out of service.
summary: A maintenance controller oversaw swapping a good fairing from Aircraft X to Aircraft Y, then ferrying Aircraft X with a temporary repair to ZZZZ1. The controller attributed the error to high workload and system failures preventing proper decision-making time.

synopsis: Several B767-300 flight attendants describe a cabin fume event during climbout and the problems associated with preparing the cabin for an emergency return to land with Utility Power removed.
summary: The purser and flight attendants reported an intermittent acrid smell from cabin vents shortly after takeoff, prompting the captain to return to the departure airport. The captain announced an emergency due to smoke and strong winds, though crew clarified there was no visible smoke, and the aircraft was later found to have an entertainment system fault.

synopsis: EMB175 Flight Attendant notes a slushy snow/ice mixture on the aircraft wings as the flight is about to takeoff and informs the Captain. The Captain returns to the gate for a second deicing but the flight is canceled for lack of a crew at the destination airport.
summary: A flight attendant reported significant snow and ice accumulation on the wings and windows after a 20-minute taxi following de-icing, causing the aircraft to return to the gate. The flight was subsequently canceled due to crew fatigue, though the reporter attributed the contamination to potential failures in de-icing procedures, chemical mixture, or excessive taxi time.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports how misinterpretation of an A320 aircraft Job Card reference contributed to the right-hand Main Landing Gear (MLG) side stay bushing retaining nut having a final torque twelve times greater than specified. Issue involves Airbus abbreviations for Pounds Force Inches (lbf) (in.) versus more common reference of lb. in. for Foot Pounds inches.
summary: A maintenance team over-torqued a right main landing gear side stay bushing on an aircraft while performing Task Card XXX002. The error occurred because the crew misread the required 500 pound-inches as 500 foot-pounds due to confusing unit notation on the paperwork.

synopsis: SA227 Captain experiences static system anomalies after the aircraft is left out overnight in extreme cold conditions and deiced just prior to departure. In flight ATC questions the reporters' altitude and the Captain discovers his altimeter reads 500 feet lower than actual. Switching to the alternate static source corrects the altimeter error but both VSI's are in error.
summary: The pilot experienced conflicting altimeter and VSI readings during level flight at 11,000 feet, likely caused by ice blockage or de-icing fluid in the static ports. After switching to the alternate static source and parking the aircraft in a heated hangar, subsequent flights showed no irregularities.

synopsis: DFW Controller loads the runway while an aircraft is on final to same runway. Controller gets distracted by discussion with Local Assist. Pilot of landing aircraft asks Local if this is going to work and is sent around. Controller blames the assist for the distraction and complains that Local Assist should not have been open.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft X to land and instructed Aircraft Y to line up on runway 36L but forgot about them while conversing with an assist controller. The controller subsequently sent Aircraft X around, attributing the distraction to an unnecessary assist position requirement at DFW.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: SCT Controller describes a loss of separation between a HHR arrival and a LGB departure.
summary: An air traffic controller in the Downey sector lost separation between Aircraft X and Aircraft Y while sequencing arrivals to HHR. The controller attributed the conflict to Aircraft Y entering airspace without transponder contact or communication, requiring immediate heading changes to avoid collision.

synopsis: S46 Controller switches a heavy jet to a different runway. The jet loses FMC data because of the switch and requests a vector to restart the approach.
summary: A pilot flying Aircraft X on the MARNR4 arrival lost FMS lateral and vertical guidance after ATC issued Runway 16R instead of the programmed Runway 16L. The pilot requested a heading off the arrival, highlighting a recurring system issue affecting all aircraft types on these procedures.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZLC Controller reports of switching an aircraft over to Tower, then at 300 feet the aircraft reports to the Center Controller that he just broke out and can see the runway. Pilot did not switch to Tower frequency and landed on a runway with a snowplow on it.
summary: A radar controller cleared Aircraft X for an RNAV Z approach to Jackson Hole and terminated radar, but the pilot failed to contact tower and landed within 15 feet of a snowplow. The controller noted the pilot likely forgot to switch frequencies or tower missed the call, highlighting a need for better coordination regarding runway snowplows.

synopsis: ZWY Controller describes a situation where two aircraft that he was responsible for were on a course to collide. Controller separated traffic.
summary: An air traffic controller at ZWY Area E detected Aircraft X deviating from L452 to M325 while parallel to Aircraft Y at FL370, creating a potential collision risk near ONGOT. The controller vectored Aircraft Y to avoid conflict after discovering a flight plan discrepancy caused by the tower activating the wrong route, which ATOP failed to flag due to system limitations.

synopsis: P50 Controller reports of ZAB feed to P50 as being excessive. P50 Controller reports that the Time Based Flow Management (TBFM) is not set up correctly and that the facility needs to configure it correctly.
summary: ZAB controllers dumped Aircraft Y to 11,000 feet in front of Aircraft X without an APREQ, causing improper sequencing. This resulted in ZAB over-delivering 42 arrivals in 30 minutes instead of the agreed 18 due to incorrect TBFM setup and a refusal to push data to the glass.

synopsis: ZLC Controller reports of another less experienced Controller issuing a clearance to an aircraft below a useable altitude. The ZLC Controller then took over the position and rectified the situation.
summary: An inexperienced controller issued a 120-foot clearance below the 140-foot MIA, prompting the relieving controller to verify terrain clearance with the pilot. After the pilot rejected 140 feet, the controller directed a VFR westward route to avoid obstacles before issuing a valid IFR clearance.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZLC Controller describes a flight into an airport and is concerned about the Minimum IFR Altitudes (MIA) and altitude to assign the aircraft. Controller should have climbed the aircraft a thousand feet higher.
summary: An air traffic controller in Sector 3 cleared Aircraft X for landing on runway 36U but misinterpreted Minimum Instrument Altitude lines, believing 13,000 feet was safe despite rising terrain. The En-Route Minimum Safe Altitude Warning did not trigger, leading the controller to suggest revising alert procedures for hard altitude entries near airports.

synopsis: TPA Controller describes a loss of separation due to data tag overlap and amount of traffic during the session.
summary: An air traffic controller managing 19 aircraft during a busy VFR departure phase missed a Conflict Alert due to distraction and lack of timely handoff. This resulted in Aircraft X and Aircraft Y passing within approximately 500 feet laterally at the same altitude, attributed to supervisor oversight in staffing.

synopsis: U90 Approach Controller describes a confusing reply from his trainee to a pilot. Pilot requested a block altitude, Controller answered 'On request.' Pilot later climbs on his own and separation was lost.
summary: A trainee air traffic controller managing Aircraft X and Y during departure from Tucson allowed Aircraft X to climb above its 10,000-foot restriction due to frequency congestion and an ambiguous response to a block altitude request. The pilot climbed without approval, resulting in a loss of separation with Aircraft Y, which the controller attributed to pilot deviation and frequency management issues.

synopsis: During climbout, a B737 flight attendant crew detected a metallic or electrical odor so ATC was advised, the QRH completed and flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: During climb through 13,000 feet, pilots and flight attendants reported a metallic or electrical smoke smell in the cabin, prompting an immediate return to the departure airport. Fire crews found no visible source, passengers were deplaned, and the crew deadheaded to ZZZ after the captain determined the aircraft should not operate the next leg.

synopsis: A fatigued B747 Captain reported crossing the runway threshold low during a night approach in moderated rain and winds.
summary: The pilot reported a Boeing 747 night approach in moderate rain where fatigue likely caused a low glidepath profile. The aircraft descended through 50 feet before the threshold and crossed at an estimated 40 feet, triggering a GPWS 'Too Low' warning but resulting in a normal landing.

synopsis: B737 First Officer does not believe the Runway 32 landing length available is correctly calculated on the JEPP 10-9 A chart and does not agree with ACARS data sent by the company.
summary: A pilot reported a discrepancy during the approach to SRQ on Runway 32 where ACARS landing data showed 7460 feet available, conflicting with Jeppesen charts indicating 6460 feet from the glide slope due to an 840-foot unavailable section. The pilot noted the ACARS and Jeppesen data did not match the published bullet 7 restriction.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier pilot reports confusion after being cleared to taxi via A4 left on A in very low visibility conditions. The intersection of A with A5 is the cause of the confusion with the reporter being unsure which way to turn.
summary: Pilots taxiing in heavy fog and freezing temperatures received conflicting ground instructions at an intersection lacking signage. The crew nearly entered a cargo ramp due to the absence of signs indicating the required 45-degree turns, highlighting a need for better signage in low visibility.

synopsis: A B757 Captain discovered after a new ACARS software installation that when an ACARS screen marked '>7500' is left up for more than two minutes, 7500 code is automatically sent to alert Dispatch of an unwanted situation.
summary: During preflight, a pilot accidentally triggered an ACARS hijack alert (squawk 7500) while reviewing new software, likely by leaving the screen active for two minutes or pressing the adjacent DNES button. Dispatch contacted the crew to verify the false alarm, prompting the pilot to recommend manual confirmation for such messages to prevent future unintentional transmissions.

synopsis: During the takeoff roll an EMB-145 First Officer call for a reject after scanning his instruments and interpreting the 0 altimeter indication as an airspeed indicator failure.
summary: The First Officer mistakenly aborted takeoff after fixating on the altimeter and confusing it for the airspeed indicator. The crew identified the error as a visual fixation, confirmed no aircraft malfunction, and completed the flight safely.

synopsis: B777 flight crew describes an un-stabilized approach caused in part by fatigue and very low time in the seat by the First Officer and the Captain allowing the First Officer to get a little too far behind before taking over.
summary: The First Officer failed to arm Approach mode on a Boeing 777 during an ILS 36R approach, causing the aircraft to remain above the glide slope until the Captain intervened at 1,500 feet AGL. The Captain manually descended to intercept the glide slope in visual conditions, resulting in a low altitude alert but a safe landing.

synopsis: ATC called an Airbus crew with a low altitude alert while the aircraft was on the LDA DME RWY 25 to EGE descending at slightly higher than normal rate but on profile with the terrain in sight.
summary: The flight crew flying an Airbus on the LDA DME 25 approach to EGE received a low altitude warning from ATC while descending from 13,800 to 12,900 feet. The crew attributed the alert to a slightly high descent rate, though they crossed the AQULA fix at the correct altitude with no terrain issues in VFR conditions.

synopsis: Captain states that while the EDGAR1B arrival to MMUN shows crossing EDGAR between FL390 and FL340 at 280 knots, the FMC showed the crossing as 280/FL320BFL340A which is not possible.
summary: The flight crew identified a conflicting altitude constraint error at the EDGAR fix on the EDGAR 1B arrival into MMUN while using the Pegasus FMC. They manually corrected the FMC data to resolve the impossible "below FL320" and "above FL340" conflict before continuing the approach.

synopsis: The flight crew of an air carrier twin jet departing MKE on the ACCRA RNAV SID failed to note the restriction to maintain 250 knots until advised by ATC. They cited the format of the chart as a contributing factor.
summary: Pilots on a MKE ACCRA SID exceeded the 250-knot restriction by flying 300 knots after 10,000 feet because the limit was not visible on their chart. The crew attributed the error to the restriction being difficult to notice despite pre-flight review.

synopsis: The flight crew of a commercial fixed wing aircraft failed to note the small 'Note 4' in the heading of the Jeppesen 10-3B UECKR ONE RNAV SID out of MKE advising departures to 'maintain 250K until advised.' After receiving the clearance to 'resume normal speed' for the second time the reporter inquired and was advised of the small font note.
summary: The pilot and first officer missed a 250-knot climb restriction on the UECKR1 departure plate from MKE, incorrectly resuming normal speed at 11,000 feet after ATC clearance. The error occurred because the restriction was a small note on the EFB that both crew members overlooked for two consecutive days.

synopsis: When the B737 Captain noted the left engine vibration indicator was blank during taxi out, he contacted maintenance who had him cycle the associated CB which returned the indicator to service. The Captain then insisted it was necessary to return to the gate and have the log book properly documented and signed off by licensed maintenance personnel.
summary: During taxi, the crew observed a blank number 1 engine vibration indicator and cycled a circuit breaker per Maintenance Control's advice. The Captain refused to depart with an unsigned logbook entry, returned to the gate, and forced Maintenance to examine and defer the issue in compliance with regulations.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports a pushback with no wing walkers and a wave off by the tug driver, not using proper signals.
summary: The pilot reported that after pushback without wing walkers, a Ramp Supervisor provided incorrect taxi signals without wands in the dark. Despite repeated complaints to Ops, the pilot decided to taxi and depart after the supervisor failed to provide a proper release.

synopsis: CRJ 200 Flight Crew experiences an engine failure during descent that is initially not detected but is felt as turbulence. The ITT is then noticed to be rising above limits and the engine is shut down. After shutdown all indications are normal and the Captain believes a restart should be attempted. The First Officer agrees and a restart is attempted, followed by another ITT exceedance and shutdown. A single engine landing ensues.
summary: During descent at 20,000 feet, the crew experienced a left engine failure indicated by rising ITT and low oil pressure, likely caused by a flameout or compressor stall. After an unsuccessful restart attempt that caused another ITT spike, the crew declared an emergency and performed a safe single-engine landing.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A DHC-8 flight crew, cleared to descend to 3000 feet got distracted and failed to note the aircraft hadn't leveled but instead descended to ~2300 feet at which point they intervened and climbed back to 3000 feet.
summary: The flight crew descended below the cleared 3,000 feet altitude to 2,400 feet during the approach to runway 4R due to an unannounced autopilot capture. The pilot manually disengaged the autopilot to climb back, and ATC subsequently cleared the aircraft for a visual approach to 2,000 feet.

synopsis: After de-icing of the gate, a CRJ700 Captain reports returning to the gate to board passengers. During boarding significant ice is noticed still adhering to the fuselage and a second de-icing is accomplished prior to takeoff.
summary: The flight crew and de-ice crew discovered residual ice on the fuselage and vertical stabilizer after a gate return for heating and deicing in extreme cold. Although the wings were clean, the reporter attributed the missed contamination to difficult night conditions and noted that verbal verification of such ice is now required.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reports landing with Mu readings of 26, 24, 23 and finding the braking action to be nil. The Tower had just opened and the readings were old.
summary: The pilot landed a large aircraft on a short, sanded runway at night with reported Mu values of 26, 24, and 23, but encountered nil braking action causing an uncontrolled skid near the runway edge. The aircraft was stopped at the very end of the runway after the pilot corrected a 30-degree yaw, attributing the incident to outdated Mu data and a lack of recent PIREPs.

aircraft: McDonnell Douglas Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Flight crew reported executing a go-around after encountering wake turbulence in trail of a B777 on approach to MEM. Reporter stated ATC should be more aware of wind issues when deciding which approaches and runways should be used.
summary: Pilots on a visual approach to runway 36L behind a B777 encountered strong wake turbulence and a wind shift to 23 knots at 300 feet AGL, causing wing rock and glide path deviation. The crew elected to go around to maintain safety before stability was compromised.

synopsis: B757 flight crew describes a night visual approach to Runway 28L and the conflict that develops with traffic landing runway 28R. The distraction results in the Tower not being contacted until in the flare.
summary: A First Officer flying a visual approach to SFO Runway 28L reported a TCAS alert caused by parallel traffic on Runway 28R deviating into their path. The crew also nearly landed without clearance because the approach controller failed to transfer them to Tower frequency.

synopsis: A flight crew flying the ILS Runway 28R approach to the bridge then a change to Runway 28L, with four miles visibility and still outside of 6 DME, was unable to get visual on Runway 28L. They then begin to go missed when the runway comes into view. Captain elects to continue the landing.
summary: The flight crew experienced four runway changes during an ILS approach to SFO in IMC conditions, causing the Pilot Monitoring to lose situational awareness. The crew attempted a late side-step to Runway 28L without visual acquisition, resulting in an unstable approach that was continued to landing after the runway was spotted.

synopsis: After suffering the loss of the A321 First Officer's Nav display an error conducting the QRH to restore instead resulted in the loss of the Captain's as well. Already established in their descent prior to the loss, their request for special handling and raw data procedures was facilitated by ATC and a safe arrival at their destination resulted. A significant contributing factor to their inability to resolve the anomaly in a timely fashion was the failure of the dispatchers to connect them to their Maintenance Control department.
summary: During descent, the First Officer misread a QRH procedure and pulled the wrong circuit breaker, causing a dual FMGC failure. This led to high workload, confusion with ATC regarding navigation clearances, and a raw data approach, though the aircraft landed safely.

synopsis: CRJ200 Captain experiences a CAS message for GLD unsafe during vectors for the ILS, at the same time precipitation changes to FZRA. With the Ground Lift Dump failure, spoilers began deploying inflight uncommanded and the Captain elects to divert to a nearby alternate.
summary: The crew received a GLD UNSAFE caution while vectored for an ILS approach in freezing rain, prompting a diversion to an alternate airport. They declared an emergency, landed safely with the first officer flying manually below 2500 FT, and reported the issue to maintenance.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew describes a night VMC ILS flown by the First Officer with his Flight Director inoperative. The First Officer has difficulty maintaining a proper glideslope using raw data and the PAPI. On short final a glideslope warning is heard and 1.5 dots low is noted by the Captain. A thrust adjustment is made to land in the first 500-700 feet of the runway.
summary: During a night ILS approach, the First Officer's flight director failed, causing him to struggle with raw data and deviate below the glideslope due to visual illusions over dark water. The Captain monitored but delayed intervention until aural warnings, resulting in a late correction and a landing 500–700 feet down the runway.

synopsis: A319 First Officer reports being confused by the QRH FCU reset procedure after receiving an ECAM for AUTO FLT FCU 2 FAULT in cruise.
summary: The pilots encountered an 'AUTO FLT FCU 2 FAULT' while approaching FL350. Unclear QRH steps led them to incorrectly complete the procedure, causing an 'AUTO FLT 1+2 FAULT' with loss of autopilot and auto thrust.

synopsis: B737 Captain is informed of an odd smell in the cabin by a Flight Attendant. Odor cannot be identified nor its source located. The crew elects to divert to a suitable airport after declaring an emergency.
summary: During cruise at FL340, flight attendants reported a strong hot linen odor in the cabin, prompting the crew to declare an emergency and divert. The aircraft performed an uneventful overweight landing after fire services inspected the exterior and found no fire or smoke.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain is informed by the gate agent that the spoilers are partly deployed and may be contacting the rubber bumper on the jet bridge. The spoiler lever in the cockpit is found to be not correctly positioned.
summary: The Captain observed partial spoiler deployment and potential bridge contact while parked, likely caused by the speedbrake handle not being fully stowed after takeoff. Maintenance inspection found no damage, though ground personnel admitted failing to stop the aircraft or verify spoiler status before bridge activation.

synopsis: A First Officer reports he noticed the Engine Fire Panel (P-8) had been installed upside-down in the center pedestal of a B777. The Right Engine Fire Handle was positioned where the Left Engine Fire Handle should have been. Concerns were raised about the possibility of the fire handle cannon plugs being cross-connected and just how long the aircraft had been operating in that condition. Two other FOs also add their perspectives.
summary: The flying First Officer discovered the engine fire panel installed upside down during preflight, causing the engine indicators to be reversed. Maintenance corrected the installation, though they were puzzled by how the wiring allowed the error, and the flight continued uneventfully.

synopsis: An A320 Captain, after suffering the loss of yellow system hydraulic quantity, opted to return to their departure airport but found himself unable to communicate reliably with either Dispatch or Maintenance. The reporter expressed in strong terms his conviction that the company was not providing the communications capabilities required by their flight crews and required by regulation.
summary: During cruise at FL380, a Pilot Monitoring reported a HYD Y RSVR LO LVL ECAM warning, prompting a return to the departure airport. Although the crew managed the aircraft, they experienced significant delays and failures in receiving responses from Dispatch and Maintenance via ACARS, hindering ground coordination.

synopsis: An A319 Captain reported serial breaches of company SOP by recently contracted ground personnel. He fears his airline is expanding the use of safety task related contracted personnel around without providing effective training in the carrier's carefully developed SOPs.
summary: The pilot reported that outsourced ground agents at the departure station closed the cabin door early and attempted pushback using hand signals due to a missing headset. The agents lacked knowledge of company procedures and failed to communicate, creating a dangerous situation caused by inadequate training.

synopsis: B777 First Officer, on a 15 hour flight to VHHH, reports running out of potable water again due to the company's policy of only filling two of the potable water tanks to save weight.
summary: The flight crew reported that potable water was exhausted 12 hours into a 777 flight to VHHH, leaving 275 people without water for three hours. The captain continued to Hong Kong despite pressure from operations managers, attributing the shortage to company directives disabling a water tank and reducing load limits.

synopsis: A cargo loading reporter advised a flight had been dispatched with an improper pallet loading leaving 16 to 20 inches of unrestrained movement of unlocked pallets.
summary: A load plan adjustment moved a PMC pallet to positions without locks, creating a 16 to 20-inch gap behind eight LD3s. Without container stops available, the LD3s were free to move this distance, a condition reported to supervisors after dispatch.

synopsis: B747 flight crew reports being cleared to descend to 1900 feet during vectors to ILS 27 at VABB. The Controller questions their altitude stating they should be at 2900 feet at about the time a GPWS terrain warning is annunciated. The ridge causing the warning is visible and the approach is continued to landing.
summary: The flight crew descended to 1900 feet MSL on an ILS approach to Mumbai, triggering a GPWS warning due to terrain conflict caused by ATC instructions and heavy frequency congestion. The pilot manually climbed to clear the mountain ridge, landed safely, and attributed the incident to poor briefing and challenging visibility.

synopsis: First Officer describes a failed LOC/DME BC RWY 22 to HOM, caused partly by his inexperience and setting the RMI needles to ADF when at least one needed to be on VOR to define the lead in radial. The localizer is overshot toward high terrain causing ATC to issue a MSAW. The second attempt is successful with the RMI still improperly set.
summary: During a LOC/DME back course approach at Homer, the First Officer misconfigured the RMI to ADF, causing a missed approach and GPWS alert. After correcting the setup and receiving a new clearance, the crew successfully completed the approach and landed.

synopsis: An A330 crew detected a dirty socks odor in flight which dissipated allowing the flight to continue. On approach the odor returned causing some flight attendants to become ill.
summary: During climb out and approach, an electrical odor caused headaches, dizziness, and nausea in most cabin crew, requiring oxygen use and paramedic checks. Although maintenance cleared the aircraft after a two-hour delay, a slight odor was reported again on the subsequent takeoff.

synopsis: Flight crew reported deviating from an altitude restriction on the TECKY1 departure from SJC. Chart design and wake turbulence were cited as contributing factors.
summary: Pilots departing SJC on the TECKY1 RNAV departure misinterpreted the SPTNS waypoint restriction as "at or above" instead of "cross at," causing an altitude deviation. The error resulted from assuming Class B speed limits, IMC conditions, and a new procedure, leading ATC to order a climb stop at 7,000 feet.

synopsis: A319 First Officer reports not noticing the speed limit of 250 knots until advised, on the ACCRA1 departing MKE, until notified by ATC.
summary: The pilot flying and captain departed MKE on the ACCRA 1 SID, exceeding the 250 KIAS restriction by flying 300 KIAS to make up time. The controller corrected the speed after the crew failed to locate the limit in the chart's Notes section, prompting a recommendation for more prominent placement of such restrictions.

synopsis: Bell 206 pilot departing LUK using CTAF procedures, reports being overtaken by a corporate jet one minute after lift off without any announcements on the frequency.
summary: A pilot reported that approximately one minute after takeoff, a jet overtook their aircraft from below and behind, leaving no time for evasive maneuvering. The pilot noted that neither crew heard any transmissions on frequency 118.7 prior to the incident.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: CE525 Captain is informed by ATC that night instrument approaches are no longer authorized at TRK. The reporter accepts an approach clearance believing that it is not officially night time and breaks out 3,000 FT above airport elevation and cancels IFR before landing uneventfully.
summary: The pilot accepted an IFR approach clearance to TRK at night despite a new, unpublicized limitation prohibiting night approaches. The pilot landed safely but noted that the confusing chart footnote and lack of NOTAM or ATC guidance created a potential safety issue.

synopsis: A PA-32 pilot reported distress when, on final approach cleared and configured to land on Runway 33 at ISM, he was directed to turn left to 270 degrees apparently to accommodate a faster Gulfstream closing behind him that had performed a 360 to slow and lose altitude. While on the heading he was alerted of towers ahead by his ground proximity warning system.
summary: The pilot, on short final for RWY 33, was instructed by tower to turn heading 270 below 500 feet AGL to accommodate a Gulfstream, forcing a climb to avoid terrain obstructions over a residential area. The pilot attributed the unsafe maneuver to poor spacing and the Gulfstream's excessive speed, while admitting an unauthorized taxiway entry caused by frustration.

synopsis: PA28 pilot noticed that the Alt Amp meter read zero and the JPI digital engine monitor was flashing 'BATT' indicating a discharging battery, and returns to the departure airport. The aircraft owner and his Mechanic are contacted and they state this indication is normal. After the next takeoff the same indications are noted and 30 minutes after entering IMC all power is lost. A Handheld VHF is used to communicate with ATC and the ceiling is sufficiently high to allow a contact approach at destination.
summary: The pilot of a Piper Arrow experienced an electrical failure in IMC after ignoring initial alternator warnings and continuing the flight. The failure caused radio and navigation loss, forcing an emergency contact approach using a handheld transceiver, though the alternator recovered during the low-power approach.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports using his Captain's emergency authority to avoid turbulence associated with a thunderstorm, beyond what the Controller would authorize due to Radar coverage.
summary: The pilot deviated east of AR24 to avoid moderate turbulence and strong winds while approaching OHLAA, refusing an ATC instruction to turn early due to visible weather and other aircraft reporting severe conditions. The pilot exercised emergency authority to maintain the deviation until clear, after which the aircraft resumed course to URSUS.

synopsis: C210 pilot reports taking off into IMC with a heavily loaded aircraft with an aft CG. The normal trim setting led to a very nose high attitude and a left turning tendency, which was noticed by the Tower. At this time the aircraft broke out into the clear and full control was regained.
summary: A pilot flying a Piper P210 with an aft center of gravity experienced excessive nose-up pitch and left-turning tendency during a foggy takeoff, causing a deviation from the required right turn. The pilot corrected the attitude using rudder trim and broke out of the clouds after tower notification, attributing the incident to unfamiliarity with the aircraft's aft CG handling characteristics.

synopsis: Reports from both pilots of an NMAC event at non-towered E16 provide classic narratives of the same event seen from different points of view...and cockpits.
summary: Two pilots in high-wing Cessnas experienced a near mid-air collision on final approach to Runway 32 at South County Airport (E16). The reporter attributed the incident to the other pilot failing to see the aircraft due to blind spots and not hearing radio position reports, despite the reporter announcing all legs.

synopsis: King Air pilot experiences two green lights and a blank indicator when the gear is extended for landing. A go-around is initiated and while troubleshooting freezing rain is encountered requiring an IFR clearance and vectors for an approach. The gear indicator bulbs are changed and a normal landing ensues.
summary: The single pilot of a King Air went around at ZZZ due to a missing landing gear light caused by burned-out bulbs. Freezing rain then caused severe icing that disabled VFR flight, forcing an instrument approach after the pilot replaced the bulbs and completed the landing.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: A pilot did not comply with taxi instructions at SJC. He interpreted 'Victor, Delta, Charley, and Bravo to 30L', as meaning 'pass delta to charley the way we always used to go.' Ground control called and asked why he did not follow his directions.
summary: The pilot deviated from a taxi clearance at San Jose by skipping Delta to avoid crossing the abandoned Runway 29, believing the clearance intended a direct path to Bravo. Ground control intervened to correct the deviation, causing a delay but no traffic conflict.

synopsis: A Private pilot on a night cross country lost communications, navigation and GPS capability and then followed a highway toward a major airport where he made a landing without a clearance and, after turning off the runway, ran out of fuel. After taxiing to the FBO for gas on the dregs of fuel in the other tank...where the engine quit again. After fueling he got the radios working again, took off, and then suffered two additional instances of lost communications on the way to his destination. Upon landing he 'voluntarily' grounded the aircraft for maintenance.
summary: A pilot flying a personal aircraft at night experienced total radio, NAV, and GPS failure over swamplands, leading to a fuel-starved emergency landing. An avionics technician later attributed the recurring failures to broken wires, antenna interference, and proximity to ground-based antennas, resulting in the aircraft being grounded.

synopsis: A single engine aircraft experienced engine failure two times. The pilot was unable to restart after the second loss and landed in a polo field. He stated that there was no damage to the aircraft.
summary: A pilot flying a Rotax 503-powered aircraft at 2,500 feet MSL experienced two engine failures, forcing a precautionary landing in a polo field 8 nautical miles from ZZZ. Inspection revealed cylinder scoring and piston damage, resulting in no injuries or aircraft damage.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: P50 Controller describes two incidents involving the same aircraft. First issue was the relationship to a jump area that ZAB did not point out to the appropriate sectors. Second issue was the aircraft was not on an assigned heading that the TRACON Controller knew about. Coordination was not complete.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that ZAB46 handed off a Non-RNAV aircraft without coordinating a parachute jump or assigning a specific heading as required by the Letter of Agreement and JO N7110.65. The aircraft entered the controller's airspace on a radial without proper coordination, creating a potential conflict that management has failed to resolve.

synopsis: A B737-700 First Officer set an incorrect altitude in the altitude window causing the crew to fly through an intermediate level off altitude while on the TECKY1 SID. The Captain also missed the mistake.
summary: The First Officer, acting as Pilot Flying on a Boeing departure from SJC, failed to program a mandatory 5,000-foot altitude constraint into the MCP during the briefing. This error caused the aircraft to climb through the restriction before the Captain manually leveled off at 6,000 feet, though ATC subsequently cleared a continued climb to FL 190.

synopsis: Two B777 First Officers describe the protocol that is involved when a passenger becomes ill in flight and had previously had contact with Ebola patients.
summary: During cruise, a passenger with fever and vomiting history of travel to an Ebola area was isolated by flight attendants and treated with an anti-nausea tablet. Upon landing, CDC and customs boarded to evaluate the passenger and collect contact information before releasing the crew and passengers.

synopsis: The flight crew of a B767 that encountered a significant windshear event on arrival to BDL provided testimonials to the performance of the installed predictive windshear system.
summary: The crew of a 767 executed a missed approach at BDL due to windshear, aided by predictive windshear equipment. While maintaining 3000 feet, radar attenuation prevented rain cell detection, causing turbulence that briefly accelerated the aircraft to 275 knots below 10,000 feet.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reports discovering in flight that one of the Flight Attendants working the flight is inebriated. The flight continues to destination and the Flight Attendant is removed from the trip.
summary: During cruise on leg 4, the Captain observed a flight attendant exhibiting incoherent, slurred speech and insubordinate behavior, indicating impairment. The crew diverted to the nearest airport where management met the aircraft to evaluate the flight attendant, who was confirmed impaired and unable to walk unassisted.

synopsis: B747-400 flight crew reports being cleared direct to the second fix on an SAS 12I arrival to ZSPD before being cleared for the arrival. When the arrival clearance is issued the crew does not clean up the legs page in the FMC to reflect direct to the second waypoint and a minor track deviation occurs.
summary: The relief crew and operating pilots experienced an FMC navigation error while approaching ZSPD after delayed ATC approach clearances. The aircraft turned 30 degrees left because the Initial Approach Fix was not cycled, causing the active waypoint to be behind the aircraft, a situation attributed to late clearances, FMC complexity, and crew fatigue.

synopsis: A B757 Captain, hand flying a practice RNAV (GPS) approach for proficiency development noted drift and bank conditions he attributed to an aileron or other roll control anomaly, advising roll control never felt 'quite as it should be.'
summary: The pilot reported unusual flight control resistance and a right drift during a radar-vectored visual approach while practicing an RNAV (GPS) RWY 05R approach. After manually correcting the drift with aileron trim, the aircraft landed safely, and the pilot logged the issue for maintenance without notifying ATC.

synopsis: A PC-12 flight crew flying the RNAV (GPS) Runway 1 IAP at RUT received a TAWS alert shortly after beginning their descent from the FAF, WIRAX, to the MDA of 3,100 MSL. They executed a go-around and requested and safely completed the Runway 19 RNAV approach.
summary: Pilots flying an RNAV (GPS) runway 1 approach at RUT received a TAWS "terrain too low" warning between 3,800 and 3,600 feet MSL despite following published step-downs. They executed a go-around and switched to runway 19, later concluding the alert was unexplained as they were flying the approach correctly.

synopsis: Two Line Aircraft Maintenance Technicians (AMTs) explain why different procedures must be used to access the correct MEL illustration for deferring a High Pressure Shut-Off Valve (HPSOV) on a B777-200 engine when using a desktop computer or maintenance tablet. They had locked out a Pressure Regulating Shut-Off Valve (PRSOV) on the right engine instead of the HPSOV.
summary: Two mechanics on a B777-200 deferred a right engine Bleed HPSOV fault using MEL 36-3a but locked out the wrong valve due to a confusing illustration on the maintenance tablet. This error caused the pilot to report the bleed system off on the ground but on at cruise power.

synopsis: A PA-20 pilot landed gear up. He is uncertain whether he reacted to the initial gear up landing by trying to place the gear lever down after (he) had touched down, but he reports having performed a landing checklist and not hearing a gear warning horn prior to touchdown.
summary: A solo pilot practicing short-field landings in a retractable-gear aircraft bounced on touchdown and veered right, coming to rest on the runway. The pilot suspects the landing gear was up, noting no warning horn despite performing the GUMPS checklist, though the gear lever was found down after securing the aircraft.

synopsis: After a water landing on a calm surface, the pilot of an amphibious aircraft notes the aircraft beginning to lean to the right. An attempt to fast taxi to the shore results in the aircraft sinking faster and eventually flipping 100 feet from shore.
summary: The pilot reported that after a normal water landing, the aircraft sank due to right float compartment failures caused by non-structural composite materials instead of specified carbon fiber. The crew successfully evacuated after the plane flipped while taxiing to shore.

synopsis: C172 Instructor experiences a NMAC at 2,500 feet with another aircraft overtaking from below after departure from ADS. TIS first identified the conflict but no evasive action was necessary.
summary: During departure from ADS, another aircraft overtook the reporting pilot by passing underneath instead of on the right, triggering a TIS warning. The reporter attributed the inadequate separation to the other pilot's incorrect overtaking procedure and insufficient visual scanning, though no collision occurred.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Inspector reports a Gulfstream G-V aircraft experienced Left engine compressor stalls inflight, requiring an unscheduled landing at a field other than the intended destination. A High Pressure Compressor (HPC) Stage-5 Bleed air Non-Return Valve was installed in reverse on the Rolls Royce BR710 engine. Maintenance Manual did not address the valve's air flow direction during installation.
summary: A technician incorrectly installed a non-return valve during scheduled igniter maintenance on the left engine, causing inflight compressor stalls and an unscheduled landing. The reporter attributes the error to technician complacency, insufficient follow-up inspection, and a maintenance manual lacking specific directional installation instructions.

synopsis: An AA5B pilot with little recent flight experience landed at a Class D airport below Class B without landing clearance because he selected the incorrect Tower frequency.
summary: A student pilot returning after 32 years landed without clearance at a Class B airport due to using the wrong Tower frequency. Ground control informed the pilot of the error, which resulted from failing to verify the correct frequency or use available resources under stress.

synopsis: During takeoff, a B767 Takeoff Configuration Warning alerted but as the Captain called 'Reject;' the First Officer reset the Stabilizer Trim into the Green Band silencing the Warning. The takeoff was continued.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring and Captain called for a rejected takeoff after a stabilizer configuration warning, but deferred to the check airman Pilot Flying who silenced it with nose-up trim. The crew continued the takeoff, though the Captain later realized they should have taken control to reject and reset the trim.

synopsis: TPA TRACON Controller describes a loss of separation with two aircraft. Controller identifies second aircraft and makes the aircraft IFR while in close proximity of another IFR.
summary: During a skill check, a developmental controller issued an IFR clearance to Aircraft Y while it converged with climbing Aircraft X, creating a separation loss. The OJTI and supervisor failed to immediately use override capability to stop the clearance, though separation was eventually restored after delayed heading instructions.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZME Controller reports of a STAR that goes to three runways. ATIS stated a specific runway in use, pilot sets up aircraft to land on that runway. Unknown to ATC pilot is going to a different runway than cleared and there is a 4,000 foot difference of altitudes between runway Controller wanted and the runway the pilot was descending for.
summary: A pilot flying Aircraft X into Memphis entered Runway 27 into the FMS despite a North transition clearance, causing an early descent due to conflicting STAR profiles. The aircraft descended below altitude but recovered before entering approach airspace, a situation the reporter attributes to confusing chart design rather than pilot error.

synopsis: Pilot reports of Controller descending them to an altitude, then telling pilot to maintain an altitude they are at and going through. Pilot advises ATC and climbs up to specified altitude. Traffic is below their aircraft 1,000 feet. Controller forgot about the other aircraft orbiting.
summary: During descent on the HUSTN 2 Arrival into CLT, JAX Center issued conflicting level-off and climb clearances due to forgetting an orbiting aircraft. The crew hand-flew to FL330 to avoid a conflict, resulting in another aircraft passing immediately below at FL320.

synopsis: When the flight crew and the lead flight attendant all noted strange behavior, loud talking and slurring by the second flight attendant they elected to have the flight met and have the flight attendant evaluated. No results of that evaluation were included.
summary: During cruise, flight crew observed a flight attendant exhibiting loud, slurred speech and strange behavior. The crew coordinated with dispatch to arrange medical assistance at the destination, deciding to continue the flight as safety was not jeopardized.

synopsis: After having been vectored off the BRDJE RNAV STAR to DFW and descend to FL240 an A320 flight crew was cleared direct to intercept the STAR at SEEVR, and cleared to descend via the arrival. Believing they had assured the arrival was properly programmed both pilots undertook other required preparations for the arrival. Shortly, they noticed that they had descended well beyond the minimum SEEVR crossing of FL200 although they had not yet reached that fix. They advised ATC who re-cleared them and the balance of the flight was uneventful. Both airmen expressed skepticism about the ability of their aircraft to successfully navigate the complex procedures, especially when any ATC alteration to the line selectable procedure is required by ATC.
summary: Two pilots reported unintentional altitude deviations while descending on the BRDJE ONE arrival into DFW after ATC issued modified speed and altitude clearances. The aircraft descended to 17,000 feet before reaching the SEEVR fix due to automation issues, prompting the crew to level off and contact ATC, though no traffic conflict occurred.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 Captain was advised by a passenger on his aircraft that significant ice had built up on his right wing. He learned of this after the flight and wondered whether the manufacturer would consider this to be an expected situation.
summary: The Captain observed significant ice accumulation on the right wing behind the heated leading edge during approach in moderate mixed icing conditions, despite active anti-ice systems and green indications. The crew reported the icing to approach and contacted maintenance to inspect the system for potential roll-back issues.

synopsis: A Maintenance Supervisor describes a pushback incident where several factors contributed to a Mechanic with a headset on and still connected to the Crew Interphone System, had to run away from a company B767-300 as the aircraft suddenly began rolling forward. Procedures to establish visual contact with ground crew and steering pin removal confirmation were not followed.
summary: A B767-300 rolled forward during pushback, nearly striking a mechanic behind the nose gear after the crew moved without confirming visual contact or steering pin removal. The incident, attributed to complacency and reliance on aural communication, led to new procedures requiring constant visual contact and delayed pin removal.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A Flight Instructor reports that his student experienced an engine failure on short final as the student is told to go around. When the throttle is pushed in the engine fails resulting in a landing short of the runway.
summary: A student pilot executing a go-around at 300 feet AGL experienced an engine failure upon advancing the throttle. Unsuccessful restart attempts resulted in the aircraft landing short of the runway.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports being cleared to taxi via the ramp taxiway to Runway 33 at BUR for a night departure. The Runway 33/15 hold bars on the ramp taxiway are inadvertently crossed causing an aircraft landing Runway 33 to go-around.
summary: A flight crew taxiing at night to Runway 33 at Burbank crossed an unlit hold short line due to unclear ATC instructions and difficult visibility, causing an approaching aircraft to execute a go-around. The crew attributed the incident to the unmarked line, unfamiliar airport layout, and lack of specific safety alerts on their charts.

synopsis: A Widebody Transport crew inserted the approach for a runway other than the one cleared for. Simultaneously, when they broke out, they called for go-around. They then entered the correct approach and landed. Insufficiently charged IPads were an important and distracting factor.
summary: During a CAT I approach to PHL RWY 9R, the Pilot Flying inadvertently selected the ILS RWY 9L in the FMC while the Pilot Monitoring avoided changing iPad pages due to low battery. The crew executed a go-around after ATC queried their position and they identified the incorrect approach, subsequently completing the correct ILS Z 9R without incident.

synopsis: The flight crew of a G-IV failed to note the initial level off at 5,000 feet on their assigned SID from SJC. Fatigue was cited as a contributing factor.
summary: The Captain and First Officer missed a 5,000 ft crossing restriction on a new SID during departure due to fatigue from an abrupt time zone change and lack of advisory notes. ATC queried the violation and immediately issued a climb clearance to 13,000 ft.

aircraft: Embraer Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Embraer Jet flight crew describes a conflict with a helicopter doing hover practice over the grass at an uncontrolled airport. The helicopter is facing away from the Embraer Jet and slowly drifting backwards toward the taxiway. The helicopter crew finally pivots to the right and sees the Embraer Jet and continues across the taxiway to the fuel ramp.
summary: The pilot reported a near-midair collision while taxiing at an uncontrolled airport after a helicopter practicing hover operations drifted within 50 feet of their aircraft. The helicopter crossed the taxiway without communication or evasive action, prompting the pilot to stop urgently to avoid contact.

synopsis: A B737 had a track deviation when a rushed crew entered waypoint METRO instead of MERTO. ATC commented the error had occurred before.
summary: The crew incorrectly entered "METRO" instead of "MERTO" in the FMC during preflight, causing the aircraft to turn west after HYLND. ATC clarified the error and cleared the flight direct to MERTO, resulting in a late arrival.

synopsis: A300 flight crew experiences failure of both automatic pressurization controllers during climbout resulting in a cabin altitude warning. The aircraft is brought back down to 10,000 feet while the pressurization system is examined. The First Officer is able to gain control of the outflow valve manually and the flight continues to destination.
summary: During takeoff at 12,000 feet, both cabin pressure regulators failed, causing the cabin to climb with the aircraft and triggering an emergency descent to 10,000 feet. After momentarily exceeding the speed limit, the crew manually controlled the outflow valves, cancelled the emergency, and continued to the destination.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier crew landed on ABQ Runway 8. They mistakenly exited the runway at closed Taxiway E5 due to poor signage indicating closure and lack of signage indicating the location of E6.
summary: The flight crew exited Runway 8 onto closed taxiway E5, mistaking it for E6 due to poor signage and markings that resembled active taxiways. The controller prevented a runway incursion, and the crew corrected the error after realizing their location, citing inadequate closed taxiway markings as the root cause.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: During climb a C525 left engine oil indicated low pressure. After running the checklist and troubleshooting with no effect, the engine was shut down and returned to the departure airport.
summary: During climb through 15,000 feet, the crew observed low left engine oil pressure after activating engine anti-ice. After troubleshooting failed to resolve the indication, they performed a precautionary shutdown and executed a normal single-engine landing at the departure airport.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot reports of being handed off what they consider late to ZAB reference the close proximity of the airport they want to land at. Pilot requests direct a fix, but Controller cannot give it to them. The Controller tells the pilot to hold when aircraft is 1 mile past initial hold fix. Pilot makes educated guess and turns aircraft around, then is cleared for approach.
summary: The pilot and First Officer requested a direct routing to KEREY for an RNAV approach to CNM but were handed off from ZFW to ZAB too close to the fix. Due to the late handoff and high controller workload, the crew was forced to hold behind the fix before receiving approach clearance.

synopsis: TBM pilot notices a cabin decompression light passing 15,000 feet and descends to 10,000 feet to complete the flight. The next day the aircraft is taken up to FL230 without any issues.
summary: The pilot of a TBM climbing from 15,000 feet to FL230 reported a false cabin decompression light and descended to 10,000 feet after coordinating with ATC. The pilot suspects a bad sensor signal caused the false reading and plans to have the aircraft inspected at a shop.

synopsis: BUR Tower Controller describes an operation where a departure was slow to get airborne causing an aircraft on short final for a crossing runway to go-around. Now, the conflict is worsened by having no missed approach procedures to separate the aircraft.
summary: A Local Control/Ground controller at BUR cleared a departing aircraft from Runway 15 while an arriving aircraft was on final for Runway 8, causing the arrival to execute a go-around due to the tight separation. The controller attributed the conflict to staffing shortages suspending Line Up and Wait operations and restrictive missed approach procedures that prevented safe vectoring of the go-around aircraft.

synopsis: BUR Tower Controller reports of a go-around and aircraft following it that need to be sequenced due to the go-around. BUR does not have a DVA so aircraft are turned over to Approach Control for sequencing to the airport. This causes airspace violations and losses of separation.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X executed a go-around on a visual approach to Runway 33 at BUR due to 55-knot windshear. The lack of a Diverse Vectors Area forced the aircraft into a left traffic pattern, violating Class D airspace and requiring TRACON to re-sequence two following aircraft to avoid a collision.

synopsis: Two ZDC controllers describe a recurring problem they are having with Airbus aircraft not meeting the crossing restriction at MAYOS on the IVANE5 arrival to CLT.
summary: An A319 descended prematurely below FL240 while executing a "descend via" clearance for the IVANE5 arrival into CLT due to a known Airbus FMS issue. The aircraft entered a lower sector at FL232 before climbing back to FL240, prompting the controller to recommend suspending "descend via" clearances for this arrival until the FMS is fixed.

synopsis: BUR Tower Controller reports of lack of procedures for go-around aircraft which often leads to airspace violations and possible losses of separation.
summary: Air Traffic Controllers reported that Aircraft X executed a go-around due to wind shear on short final at BUR. The lack of a Diverse Vector Area forced the aircraft to violate Class D airspace at WHP and VNY, creating a loss of separation with VFR traffic.

synopsis: ZID Controller reports of an aircraft popping up in his airspace. He tracks down who is suppose to be working the aircraft and then later finds another flight plan on the same aircraft. Controller reports of lack of concern from ZDC controllers who were working the aircraft.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller in Sector 24 reported that Aircraft X entered their airspace without coordination or handoff from ZDC Sector W01, who mistakenly believed the flight was in Charleston Approach airspace. The controller was forced to manually identify the aircraft and attributed the error to ZDC's lack of training and nonchalant culture regarding airspace boundaries.

synopsis: B737 flight crew was cleared for a visual approach to Runway 23R when the Tower also clears another aircraft for takeoff on the same runway. As the reporter's aircraft was descended through 700 feet, a go-around is initiated, and vectors received for a visual approach to Runway 23L.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway 23R at IND, the crew executed a go-around at 600 feet after a B757 entered the runway for takeoff. The reporter attributed the incident to the Tower clearing the departure before ensuring final was clear and the B757 crew failing to verify the runway was clear.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ATC cleared on aircraft onto DAL Runway 31R. That aircraft interfered with the ILS glideslope and caused an aircraft on final to pitch down and receive an EGPWS alert. The crew executed a missed approach.
summary: The crew executed a go-around during an ILS approach to Runway 31R at Dallas Love due to an errant glideslope signal and GPWS obstacle alert caused by an aircraft penetrating the critical area. A second approach was uneventful, resulting in a four-minute late landing.

synopsis: A319 Captain describes an altitude deviation caused by the First Officer pulling the baro set knob to set QNH and forgetting to push it back in for QNE. This results in a 350 foot overshoot while descending to FL310.
summary: The First Officer failed to reset the altimeter to standard after entering field pressure, causing the aircraft to undershoot FL310 by 350 feet. The crew advised ATC of the error and received clearance for a descent via.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports being illuminated by a green laser light at 1,400 feet during approach to Runway 4 at LGA. The reporters are not harmed and a normal landing ensues.
summary: During final approach to runway 4 at LGA at 1,400 feet AGL, the flight crew experienced two green laser illuminations while hand-flying. The Captain avoided looking at the light, reported the incident to ATC, and completed an uneventful landing.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported NMAC on approach to SFO Runway 28L when another aircraft overshot the parallel approach course.
summary: During a localizer 28L approach, the crew received a TCAS Resolution Advisory to descend due to an aircraft on parallel 28R overshooting from above and behind. The crew descended to 900 feet AGL, accelerated to gain separation, and selected TA mode to avoid terrain and the intruder, which was later ordered back onto its approach by Tower.

synopsis: After receiving a Dispatch briefing indicating their aircraft had no deferrals, a Captain was informed by the lead Flight Attendant that all coffee makers on their B767-300 had Circuit Breakers (C/Bs) pulled and collared with Inoperative (Inop.) stickers on them. Lavatory water heaters were also inoperative and the MEL Card was 10-pages long. Maintenance had signed-off work as being completed.
summary: The flight crew discovered inoperative coffee makers and lav water heaters on a ZZZ/ZZZZ flight despite dispatch paperwork showing no deferrals. A maintenance delay occurred because a mechanic had falsely signed off on incomplete repairs, requiring his return to finish the work.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported the flight crew could not release the autobrakes after a normal landing until after coming to a full stop and cycling the parking brake several times.
summary: The Captain reported that autobrakes remained engaged after landing, requiring parking brake cycling to release, while an FAA controller unilaterally declared an emergency without crew consent. The incident resolved with normal brake function, though the controller's unauthorized actions and incorrect information caused unnecessary emergency response and confusion.

synopsis: Pilot reports of a RA that happened on departure with an aircraft also departing.
summary: The pilot reported a TCAS "Monitor Vertical Speed" RA during initial climb on the SSTIK1 RNAV departure from SFO runway 1L while ahead of Aircraft Y on runway 1R. The pilot attributed the brief conflict to the departure procedure design and the other aircraft's climb profile, noting the event resolved in under five seconds.

synopsis: Pilot of a medical mission helicopter reported an NMAC with another aircraft in the vicinity of LEX. Reporter commented the TCAS seemed to be malfunctioning.
summary: The crew departed LEX in an aircraft with non-functional TCAS, which they mistakenly believed was normal, while company operations failed to alert them of an inbound aircraft. This resulted in a 400-foot separation after the crew coordinated a climb to 2200 feet to avoid the other aircraft descending to 1800 feet.

synopsis: CRJ-900 First Officer describes difficulty controlling the aircraft in a hand-flown missed approach.
summary: The pilot flying a ZZZ to CLT approach executed a go-around after TWR issued the instruction due to a slow-departing aircraft on the runway. During the subsequent turn, the pilot lost control awareness, prompting the other pilot to take over, climb to 4,000 feet, and complete a second successful approach.

synopsis: MD11 flight crew receives a Level 1 alert AIR SYS 2 OFF followed by a Level 3 alert AIR MANF 2 FAIL shortly after level off in cruise. An emergency is declared, fuel is dumped and the flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: The pilot declared an emergency due to an air manifold failure caused by a broken jet pump hose, requiring a return and 27,000-pound fuel dump. Post-flight distractions prevented the pilot from logging the fuel dump, necessitating a later correction to maintenance records.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported that on takeoff roll following ground de-icing they experienced near-zero visibility in the cockpit due to smoke and/or fumes introduced through the air vents, presumably related to the ground de-icing.
summary: The flight crew experienced heavy smoke and near-zero visibility in the cockpit during takeoff from BOS in snow and fog after a Bleeds Off departure following de-icing. Suspecting de-ice fluid entered the APU bleed system, they continued the takeoff as aborting was unsafe, with the smoke clearing by 1,500 feet AGL for an uneventful flight.

synopsis: A late change in the A319's takeoff runway and the flight crew's failure to program the associated flex thrust temperature prior to start of the roll, resulted in a EWD warning and the use of TOGA thrust for takeoff. Workload, time pressure and the resultant breakdown in CRM were cited as contributing factors.
summary: During taxi at Miami, a runway change from 8R to 12 caused the First Officer to fail to enter the FLEX temperature in the FMGC. This omission triggered an "ENG-thrust not set" ECAM message during takeoff, requiring the Captain to select TOGA thrust to continue the departure.

synopsis: The flight crew of a CRJ200 taxiing for takeoff mistook a line up and wait clearance intended for another flight coming from the opposite side of the runway as being for them and entered the runway without a clearance. A prior query from ATC asking if they would be 'ready at the end' was cited as a contributing factor to their assumption of the clearance.
summary: The flight crew reported confusion during final taxi and runway entry when ATC issued a "line-up and wait" clearance. The crew suspected they may have assumed the instruction applied to them without hearing their call sign, highlighting a need for greater vigilance in verifying ATC instructions.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier Captain reported ATL ATC was upset because the crew delayed their takeoff for spacing behind a B757 because they were not aware the RECAT program was in effect at ATL.
summary: A pilot reported a conflict with an ATC controller during takeoff at Atlanta after following a 757, as the crew was unaware of the local RECAT program classifying the 757 as non-heavy. The controller became irritable when the crew requested extra spacing, later explaining that 6,000 feet separation was sufficient under the new rules.

synopsis: An A320 flight crew descending for a planned CATIII autoland at BOS incorrectly set their altimeters to 29.96 when the actual pressure was 29.28. A low altitude alert was received from ATC as they descended to 2000 MSL (or 1320 MSL with the correct pressure setting) at which point their altimeters were corrected, they climbed back to 2000 and completed a visual approach consistent with the now improved weather.
summary: During a night descent to BOS, the crew set altimeters to 29.96 instead of 29.28, causing an inadvertent descent to 1600 feet while cleared for 2000. ATC issued a low altitude alert, prompting an immediate climb; the crew attributed the error to fatigue after a long duty day and missed checks.

synopsis: During takeoff a B777 left engine compressor stalled so the Captain rejected the takeoff. The engine had developed a high EGT and the EICAS alerted ENGINE FAIL L so the ENGINE FAIL and SURGE STALL Checklists were accomplished with a returned to the gate.
summary: The flight crew aborted takeoff before 100 knots after a loud bang, vibration, and high EGT indicated a left engine failure. They taxied back to the gate with the left engine at idle to avoid exceeding temperature limits, completing relevant checklists and debriefing with Dispatch.

synopsis: An A321 First Officer's FMGC and MCDU locked up in flight causing multiple NAV failures. The flight diverted to the filed alternate because of poor destination airport weather.
summary: During cruise at FL340, the First Officer's navigation displays failed and the MCDU locked, causing GPS loss and speed reference failure. The crew diverted to an alternate, hand-flew a visual approach, and cancelled the flight due to unresolved conflicting navigation system failures.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 EICAS alerted STAB TRIM during takeoff but the crew continued. In flight, the Stabilizer Trim was found failed and would not reset so the flight returned to the departure airport for maintenance.
summary: The flight crew continued takeoff after a 'STAB TRIM' caution appeared above 80 KTS but could not reset the system despite QRH procedures. They returned to the departure airport for a safe landing, with maintenance later suspecting a short in the trim panel caused by debris entering the center console.

synopsis: An EMB145 flight crew rejected their takeoff at ~100KIAS upon receipt of an EICAS baggage door open message. The reporter cited snow covered runways, braking action fair reports, reduced visibility and being well above 80KIAS as factors making the go/no go decision difficult.
summary: The flight crew rejected a takeoff on Runway 22 during snowy winter operations after an EICAS baggage door open warning appeared at 100 knots. The Captain initiated the abort, and the aircraft safely returned to the gate for maintenance coordination.

synopsis: An EMB-145 First Officer reported while flying the IAH DRLLR4 Arrival and after multiple runway changes, the aircraft did not make the turn to final so the crew overrode it to prevent an overshoot. The error may be in the FMS design after multiple changes.
summary: During the DRLLR4 arrival, the crew managed late runway and altitude changes that caused the FMS to fail turn anticipation at the DOMNO intersection. The First Officer overrode the autopilot to correct the flight path, preventing a significant overshoot and attributing the error to FMS shortcomings in handling frequent late arrival modifications.

synopsis: A pilot new to the CE-560 was distracted by an ATC bird alert during takeoff rotation and overshot the first altitude. Once he realized, it was too late and the autopilot would not capture it.
summary: An IOE pilot flying a takeoff received a bird advisory just before V1, leading to an autopilot altitude overshoot and heading confusion due to inexperience and headset malfunction. The Captain took control to correct the flight path, while the pilot attributed the incident to distraction during a critical phase and recommended delaying such advisories.

synopsis: A CE-560 STAB MIS COMP alerted after takeoff followed by a HYD PRESS light so the abnormal checklists were completed and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a Stab Miscompare and hydraulic pressure warning shortly after takeoff, followed by a loud thump when disconnecting the hydraulic circuit breaker. They returned for a precautionary landing, which was completed normally after the warnings extinguished upon extending flaps and gear.

synopsis: After gate arrival, Maintenance notified the crew that the left wing inboard slat movable edge cover bound on the fixed slat cover and partially tore the fixed slat cover plate off.
summary: The flight crew discovered damage to the right inboard slat after blocking in, noting torn rivets and a bent edge with no in-flight alerts or performance issues. Maintenance determined the slat edge cover likely bound on the fixed cover during retraction, though the exact timing remains unknown.

synopsis: An A320 Flight Attendant reported even though the aircraft smelled strongly with a fuel odor, it was boarded and departed. Adherence to Company safety standards were questioned.
summary: Cabin crew reported strong toxic fumes in an unserviced aircraft during pre-flight boarding, noting the odor persisted for 35 minutes despite high air flow. Although the crew identified a health hazard, the airline agent instructed them to proceed with boarding, forcing the crew to work despite the risk to their health.

synopsis: A Maintenance Controller explains why he believes an A320 'Land Verify Test' was not required for an FMGC-1 that had been MEL'd under Chapter 22-83-00, but later reversed prior to dispatch, when another Circuit Breaker (C/B) cycle attempt was successful.
summary: Maintenance personnel on an A320 at Airport ZZZ successfully reset an inoperative FMGC-1 by cycling a circuit breaker after a failed dispatch attempt. The reporter concluded that a CAT II/III ground recertification was not required because the aircraft never reached the point of dispatch or takeoff.

synopsis: A Maintenance Controller informs a flight crew that if they did not accept a Non-Essential Equipment and Furnishings (NEF) type deferral of their EICAS Fuel Synoptic Display missing the green flow bars to the engines on a B777, than their aircraft would be taken out of service, because a standard MEL 28-19 would have expired. The NEF had been issued 133 days prior.
summary: A mechanic and B777 flight crew disputed using an expired NEF deferral instead of the MEL for missing fuel flow bars. Management grounded affected aircraft after the crew elected to fly, citing an incorrect deferral reference.
