synopsis: A Citation CJ3 aircraft overran the departure end of a Runway in snowy conditions. Actual runway condition was likely misreported. Additionally the anti-skid system may have hurt rather than helped the Captain to bring the aircraft to a stop on the runway.
summary: A Citation CJ3 crew overran Runway XY in snowy conditions after being advised by the airport manager that the runway was sanded, though fresh wet snow had fallen since. The aircraft stopped in a grass clearway due to poor braking, potentially caused by undetected ice or anti-skid system limitations, resulting in minor damage but no injuries.

synopsis: Believing the flight was a non-revenue operation the pilots of two BH-212 helicopters departed as a flight of two and flew in formation for a period of time for photos. They were later advised the flight was actually planned as a revenue flight thus making the formation flight a violation of FAR Part 135 restrictions.
summary: Two BH-212 crews conducted a formation flight within three rotor diameters believing it was a non-revenue positioning flight. The operator manager failed to brief them that it was actually a Part 135 revenue flight, resulting in a violation of formation flight restrictions while carrying passengers.

synopsis: A C182 pilot filed an IFR flight plan to just below the forecast freezing level and when rime ice started accumulated was initially unable to get cleared to an altitude below the freezing level. Fortunately, a climb got him between layers until the undercast allowed a descent free of moisture.
summary: The pilot encountered light rime icing at 9000 feet while flying IFR in IMC despite filing below the forecast freezing level. After ATC cleared the aircraft to 11000 feet due to terrain, ice accumulation ceased, and the ice melted after descending to 7000 feet.

synopsis: Two ZDC Controllers report another instance of an Airbus flight crew missing the crossing restriction at MAYOS on the IVANE5 arrival to CLT.
summary: An A320 cleared to descend via IVANE 5 into CLT crossed the MAYOS intersection at FL220 instead of the required FL240–FL260 window. The controller stopped the descent, and the reporter attributed the error to the aircraft's computer, recommending pilot training to manually override it.

synopsis: CRP Controller reports of the lack of a data link between his facility and NGP. Both facilities use STARS but the system does not communicate and the controller has to make manual hand offs on all inbound traffic. Controller reports this is a safety risk.
summary: Air traffic controllers at a STARS facility reported that incompatible radar systems with a Navy base force manual handoff calls, diverting attention from the scope. This equipment gap compounds read-back errors with new pilots, creating a significant safety risk that the reporter attributes to unresolved funding issues.

synopsis: B737 flight crew experiences a cabin altitude warning horn passing 13,000 feet during climb with the pressurization control panel displaying false indications of cabin altitude and differential pressure and actual cabin altitude oscillating up and down. Pressurization is controllable in manual but the crew elects to return to the departure airport due to passenger ear problems.
summary: A Boeing 737 crew experienced a pressurization malfunction with fluctuating cabin altitude and differential pressure gauges during climb out, triggering an emergency descent to 10,000 feet. The crew returned to the departure airport, landed uneventfully, and had EMS meet the aircraft due to passenger discomfort caused by the erratic cabin pressure.

synopsis: A B-737 First Officer was unable to adjust to the demands of his schedule which required him to sleep during the day before departing for flights during the night. He reported fatigue resulting from the unworkable rest periods making mistakes on ATC communications. He was also nodding off.
summary: The pilot reported severe fatigue during the descent and approach to ZZZ2 on a night segment, causing communication errors with ATC. This impairment resulted from unworkable rest periods and insufficient sleep prior to the flight, exacerbated by challenging landing conditions including wind and special procedures.

synopsis: A Dispatcher reported an aircraft departed NTD with incorrect ZFW numbers from CLP. The aircraft was 19,700 lbs. heavier than what CLP was told by 'ride along.' The air crew were given incorrect numbers prior to takeoff.
summary: The crew departed NTD with incorrect Zero Fuel Weight data provided by CLP due to a communication error with the ride-along. The aircraft was 19,700 lbs heavier than reported, resulting in incorrect takeoff numbers and highlighting a flawed weight system.

synopsis: An MD-11 air crew received two level one fuel alerts. Approximately five minutes later, the Number 2 start valve open light illuminated. They then smelled acrid fumes. They declared an emergency and began divert procedures while running the SMOKE/FIRE/FUMES checklist and then the START VALVE LIGHT ILLUMINATED INFLIGHT checklist. They landed, were inspected, and proceeded to taxi in and shut down.
summary: The flight crew experienced fuel alerts and acrid fumes at FL380 en route to ZZZ, likely caused by a #2 start valve failure affecting the pneumatic system. They declared an emergency, isolated the system, and landed safely at ZZZ for a normal post-flight inspection.

synopsis: An MD-11F air crew descended below the published altitude for an intermediate fix on final approach and received the 'TOO LOW GEAR' warning. They climbed back to the appropriate altitude, continued the approach and landed.
summary: The Captain, while descending to 2,000 feet in V/S mode during an RNAV 30R approach, failed to engage Prof mode before setting a 461-foot minimum altitude. This caused the aircraft to descend below the required crossing altitude, triggering a 'TOO LOW GEAR' EGPWS warning before the crew climbed back to 2,000 feet and landed safely.

synopsis: A320 Captain reports being dispatched with an inoperative generator (IDG low oil) with the APU generator operating. During descent the remaining engine driven generator Indicated Drive Director (IDG) indicates low oil and is disconnected. A normal landing ensues at destination.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a second IDG low oil pressure failure on a flight already operating with one generator on MEL. They declared an emergency, received priority handling, and landed uneventfully, suspecting improper servicing caused the identical failure on the next flight.

synopsis: An EMB-140 First Officer, while parked at the gate, observed a '...ramper drove the tug into the right wing tearing gash in the leading edge of the right wing, and damaging the outer tip of the wing as well.'
summary: While the aircraft was parked at the gate with passengers boarding, a ramper driving a tug struck the right wing, causing a leading edge gash, tip damage, and fuel leakage. The reporter attributed the incident to the tug driver's excessive speed and lack of attention to surroundings.

synopsis: B737 Captain is in formed during approach by the Flight Attendants that both lavatory smoke alarms are going off but no smoke was seen. The approach is continued and just before landing the Equipment exhaust cooling light and the Auto Fail light came on. the aircraft continues to the gate with ARFF following but no smoke is ever seen.
summary: During an RNAV arrival, the crew encountered simultaneous aft and forward lavatory smoke alarms, an equipment cooling exhaust light, and an auto fail light with no visible smoke or fire. The pilots declared an emergency, landed, and taxied to the gate for a controlled evacuation, where maintenance and fire crews found no faults.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported he was within one mile of touchdown on SFO Runway 28L when Tower cleared an aircraft to cross the runway. Tower then directed a go-around to resolve the conflict.
summary: The flight crew on a visual approach to SFO Runway 28L executed a go-around at 100 feet AGL after Tower cleared another aircraft to cross the runway while they were 0.5 nm from the threshold. The pilot attributed the incident to the controller's loss of situational awareness regarding their proximity to the runway.

synopsis: A B737-800 air crew upon receipt of a descent clearance, pressed the 'ALT INTV' button. In doing so the first altitude constraint was deleted and they crossed it 1,000 feet low.
summary: The pilot monitoring reported that pressing the 'ALT INTV' button during a descent via Arrival into ZZZ cancelled the FL240 constraint at Fix ZZZZZ, causing the aircraft to cross the fix 1,000 feet low. The flight landed safely with no controller intervention, and the pilot attributed the error to insufficient monitoring of altitude constraints.

synopsis: A B737-800 Captain upon receiving a descent clearance pushed the alt intervene button which deleted the first crossing restriction and caused the aircraft to cross that fix 1,000 feet low.
summary: The pilot descended via the arrival to ZZZ but inadvertently deleted the FL240 crossing restriction at Fix ZZZZZ by pressing 'alt intervention' twice while in Alt Hold. This resulted in crossing the fix at FL230, 1,000 feet below the required altitude, due to complacency and mode confusion.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An MD-80 flight crew experienced an engine failure during climbout at about 12,000 feet and elected to return to the departure airport. The return was uneventful, and the passengers were deplaned at the gate.
summary: The pilot monitoring experienced a right engine shutdown at 12,000 feet due to an oil strainer clog, high pressure, and rapid oil loss. After declaring an emergency and securing the engine, the crew landed safely at ZZZ with no fire, though oil was found on the cowling.

synopsis: A B-737 flight crew was reported by company as having had a hard landing. The Captain under instruction reported being distracted by the HUD display.
summary: The Captain on an Initial Operating Experience flight performed a practice CAT III approach in gusty crosswinds with flaps 40. Distraction by the HUD display and delayed flare initiation caused a firm touchdown and rapid nose-down rotation, which the company classified as a hard landing.

synopsis: PA28 Instructor pilot experiences low power during a stop and go takeoff and rejects.
summary: A student pilot, instructor, and observer aborted a takeoff during a stop-and-go maneuver due to abnormal engine sound, low RPM of 2,100, and insufficient airspeed acceleration. The crew exited the aircraft, taxied back to the ramp, and shut down the engine.

synopsis: While making a go-around at a small uncontrolled airport with a student a flight instructor pilot was surprised to see a pickup truck parked on the runway and a motorcycle speeding down the runway itself. He was further surprised when, after a subsequent landing, he confronted the individuals involved and ultimately learned that one of them was the Airport Manager.
summary: During a go-around and landing at ZZZ Municipal Airport, a pilot observed an airport manager driving a motorcycle and truck on the active runway. The pilot reported a runway incursion caused by the manager's failure to use radio communication or recognize runway markings despite claiming city authorization.

synopsis: Flight attendants do not believe that their current ground school training philosophy is in compliance with the flight attendant manual procedures.
summary: A flight attendant reported that training videos and drills contained incorrect procedures, unsafe goggle usage, and contradictory evacuation commands that conflict with the FAOM. The reporter stated these errors place passengers and crew at risk by teaching unrealistic actions and failing to align with established safety protocols.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) was informed the # 1 Engine Intake Bypass Door Actuator head end was found not connected to the lower cowl support clips on a Q-400 aircraft. The attach bolt he had installed had gone through the bearing support plate but missed the end hole on the actuator head. This unsecured condition had existed for approximately nine months.
summary: A mechanic reported that a previous installer likely missed the actuator end hole on the #1 engine intake bypass door due to limited access and visual confirmation via mirror. The bolt was found misaligned during a replacement task, requiring rework to correct the installation.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) was inform by his Quality Assurance department that he may have incorrectly routed the # 2 Fire Extinguisher bottle discharge lines on an MD-83 aircraft. Technician noted that other maintenance had occurred on the same fire bottle discharge lines he had previously connected prior to their Base Maintenance technicians discovering the cross-connected lines.
summary: A mechanic reported potentially incorrectly routing fire extinguisher deployment lines while replacing a low-pressure Number-Two bottle. The mechanic stated they followed the diagram and believed the lines were aligned correctly, though they acknowledged the serious consequences of improper routing.

synopsis: CE680 Captain reports descending to 860 feet during a non precision approach to RNT and receiving a caution obstacle from the GPWS and at the same time a low altitude caution from Renton Tower is issued. A go-around is initiated and the flight diverts to BFI for an ILS. Maintenance finds water in the pitot static system.
summary: The crew received conflicting altitude warnings during final approach due to an altimetry error caused by water in the static system. After executing a missed approach and landing, maintenance purged the lines and returned the aircraft to service.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: The single pilot of a Cessna Citation destined for a fueling stop at a small Texas airport found the weather reported by AWOS and TRACON to be inaccurate and made a missed approach when he broke out at minimum but already over the end of the runway. While conducting a hand flown MAP he inadvertently exceeded his cleared altitude.
summary: The pilot missed a GPS approach at BGD due to lower-than-expected ceilings and fuel concerns. During the missed approach, the pilot failed to contact Approach due to a radio error, then climbed above a 7,000-foot clearance to AMA while preoccupied with navigation and fuel management.

synopsis: M20F pilot experiences failure of the landing gear to extend during approach. Multiple attempts at electrical extensions are unsuccessful. Attempts at manual extension are also unsuccessful and results in the manual extension handle being broken. A gear up landing ensues with no injuries.
summary: The pilot experienced a landing gear extension failure during landing preparation, causing the gear to collapse on touchdown after multiple electrical and manual extension attempts failed. The aircraft slid 50–75 feet before stopping, but both occupants exited safely with no injuries.

synopsis: A four plane formation of T-6 Texan II's was maneuvering in their assigned training area when a TCAS traffic advisory alerted flight lead to a possible bogey at their altitude and closing fast. Shortly thereafter, reporter saw another T-6 in a hard left hand turn to avoid. He was heading south at 4,500 feet MSL, and reporter's aircraft was heading north. They passed within 300 feet of each other. Had other aircraft not aggressively maneuvered, it would have flown directly through reporter's formation.
summary: A division lead of a three-aircraft student formation at 4,500 feet MSL experienced a near midair collision with Aircraft X while performing turns. The other pilot aggressively turned left to avoid the formation, passing within 300 feet, despite the lead believing they were within approved de-confliction procedures.

synopsis: A C-172 pilot on downwind had to take evasive action after an aircraft that had taken off after them began to turn crosswind in front of them.
summary: The pilot reported that while flying an extended upwind, crosswind, and downwind as advised by the tower, another aircraft that had taken off after them made an uninstructed crosswind turn. This required the pilot to take evasive action to avoid a collision.

synopsis: CRP Controller reports of the discontinuity of the STARS at his facility and the STARS at NGP. The interface between the two systems does not allow handoffs, which must be made manually.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that the lack of data link between FAA and Navy STARS systems forces manual landline handoffs during approaches to a Navy base. This diverts controller attention from the radar scope and compounds read-back errors with new pilots, creating a significant safety risk.

synopsis: ZOA Controller describes a read back hear back issue resulting in an aircraft descending lower than the Controller wanted. Controller complains about the noise level in the control room as a distraction. Descending aircraft was traffic for another aircraft 1000 feet below what controllers thought was the altitude assigned, resulting in a loss of separation.
summary: An air traffic controller in a noisy sector issued Aircraft X a descent to FL330 but missed the pilot's readback of FL230 due to high workload and fatigue. This resulted in a conflict alert with Aircraft Y at FL320, which was resolved when the next sector vectored Aircraft X away.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: ZBW Controller discovers an untagged aircraft in his airspace. Controller tries to identify aircraft and checks on frequency for the aircraft. Controller calls possible previous sector and Controller transfers communication to the investigating Controller. Controller asks pilot what happened and pilot advised a Controller possibly forgot about them.
summary: An air traffic controller encountered an aircraft with an unassigned code and altitude that failed to auto-acquire on the new system. The aircraft was later identified as lost due to a manual handoff error between sectors, prompting a recommendation for automatic data block acquisition to prevent future safety risks.

synopsis: ABI TRACON Controller describes a situation where an aircraft under their control does not auto handoff and violates another Controller's sector, resulting in an airspace deviation.
summary: An air traffic controller handling a VFR departure from T23 became distracted by other traffic and failed to hand off Aircraft X to the ZFW Possum sector. The aircraft entered ZFW Ednas airspace before the controller manually initiated the handoff, an error attributed to inefficient scanning and a lack of expected autoflash reminders.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported difficulty finding their assigned standard taxi route after landing at ATL, citing unintuitive indexing practices used in their EFB as contributing.
summary: The flight crew encountered difficulty locating the correct Standard Taxi Route (STR) for Green 7 on their EFBs after landing at ATL due to poor indexing. They followed the preceding aircraft and switched frequencies after Tower contact, noting the EFB's single-chart display and incomplete color code listings caused operational stress.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported difficulty accurately trouble shooting a malfunctioning fuel gauge.
summary: The flight crew experienced a fuel imbalance on departure from DEN caused by a malfunctioning number one fuel gauge, leading to incorrect cross-feeding and an overweight landing. Maintenance confirmed the gauge error at the gate, and the crew safely landed after burning excess fuel and adhering to QRH procedures.

synopsis: B737-700 First Officer reported an unstabilized approach to PHX airport that resulted in a GPWS alert and a go-around.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway 26, the Pilot Flying programmed the FMC while heads down, delaying descent and causing the aircraft to overshoot the glide path. This resulted in a GPWS "PULL UP" alert and a go-around at 1,200 feet AGL due to excessive descent rate.

synopsis: A B737 air crew landed on Runway 10R after being cleared to Runway 10L. The approach was initially obscured by scattered clouds and when they broke out the lighting on 10R was very bright and visually overpowered the 10L lighting.
summary: The crew of Flight X to ZZZ landed on runway 10R instead of the cleared 10L due to confusion over the clearance and bright 10R lighting overpowering 10L. Tower controllers confirmed the error post-landing and advised the pilots not to worry.

synopsis: A B737 air crew got low on the glide slope on final approach. There seem to have been inputs made to the mode control panel, which were unverified. This led the Pilot Flying to think the aircraft was in VNAV when, in fact, it was in level change, resulting in flight below the glide path.
summary: During a VNAV descent for ILS 16L at ZZZ, the crew descended 900 feet below the crossing altitude because the MCP altitude was incorrectly set to the touchdown zone instead of 1,900 feet. The Pilot Flying disconnected the autopilot and added power to intercept the glide path after realizing the error.

synopsis: A B757 First Officer called in fatigued and unable to complete his pairing. This happened after a number of schedule modifications, a lengthy diversion, and three early morning show times and minimal downtime between legs.
summary: A pilot reported fatigue concerns after a medical diversion and ground delay caused by uncertified maintenance personnel refilling oxygen. The resulting schedule changes led to a third pre-dawn start and extended duty time, leaving the pilot unfit to safely fly the final leg.

synopsis: B777 Captain on an international overwater flight reported he experienced an engine failure on taxi in at destination. Reporter commented that maintenance was watching the engine with some concern, but the only cockpit indication of a problem was slightly elevated engine vibration indication.
summary: A 777 captain reported elevated #1 engine vibration during cruise, which maintenance noted but the crew ignored until a loud rubbing sound occurred during taxi-in. The mechanic subsequently declared the engine broken and requiring replacement, noting the flight crew lacked sufficient knowledge of the engine's deteriorating condition.

synopsis: After descending to FL240 due to turbulence the flight crew of an A320 was cleared to descend via the IVANE RNAV STAR to CLT. Although they had set FL240 as a firm crossing on their preplanned programming of the arrival they failed to realize that so doing satisfied the crossing restriction at MAYOS (Between FL260 & FL240) and, thus, the restriction was removed from consideration by the FMGC. When they selected a VNAV/Managed Descent the FMGC factored the next crossing at KIYEN (At or above FL220) and began a descent...thus triggering the deviation. The Primary reporter cited reliance on automation as a contributing factor.
summary: The flight crew missed a hard FL240 restriction at MAYOS while descending on the IVANE5 STAR due to the FMS automatically deleting the constraint. High workload from turbulence and over-reliance on automation prevented timely intervention before Atlanta Center cleared the aircraft to FL220.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 air crew after being 'cleared for the approach' felt the airplane pitch up sharply. The Captain disconnected the autopilot and continued the approach while hand flying and landed without further incident. The crew was told that the autopilot had attempted to climb up to and capture a false Glideslope.
summary: During the ILS 17 approach at ZZZ, the autopilot caused an uncommanded climb to 4,200 feet while attempting to capture a false glideslope instead of holding the assigned 3,000 feet. The Captain disconnected the autopilot, hand-flew the aircraft, and landed safely.

aircraft: Light Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: A Captain, preparing for an Advanced Qualification Program (AQP) oral, reports on the many shortcomings of the IPad as a replacement for traditional aircraft flight manuals.
summary: A pilot reported that the iPad used during an Advanced Qualification Program oral exam lacks a complete table of contents and functional search, making it difficult to locate specific airport performance data. The reporter attributed this issue to the device's nested tab structure and poor search algorithm, which hinders efficient information retrieval.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reported noting an E2 REV DISAGREE light on takeoff roll at about 95 kts that resulted in a rejected takeoff.
summary: The Captain aborted takeoff at 95 knots due to an E2 REV DISAGREE EICAS message, likely caused by gusty winds affecting thrust reverser stowage. The crew returned to the gate, where maintenance MEL'd the reverser, allowing the flight to continue to its destination.

synopsis: C208B pilot reported contacting the approach light system on an instrument approach. Pilot elected to continue landing, and lost control of the aircraft after touch down.
summary: The pilot conducting an ILS 16L approach in low visibility initiated a go-around after realizing the aircraft was still over the approach light system, resulting in contact with the lights. The aircraft subsequently landed, veered off the runway onto the grass median, and stopped at the edge of Taxiway B due to a hard left turn on nose wheel touchdown.

synopsis: An A319 Captain reports the lack of a loadmaster at a down line station. That station wanted him to sign the weight and balance worksheet. He refused to do so since he was not a 'Loadmaster'. He called Central Load Planning and had them generate a computer generated weight and balance. He signed one copy of that weight and balance and left that copy with the station.
summary: The captain reported that a station without a Loadmaster requested he sign the weight and balance worksheet, which he refused due to unclear policy and lack of loading supervision. He instead used ACARS and Central Load Planning to generate a legal weight and balance, expressing concern that outsourcing station operations without proper oversight compromises safety.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported his aircraft was deiced early in the morning prior to his arrival without following his airline's procedures for doing so.
summary: The crew found an unauthorized individual sleeping in the cockpit and discovered the aircraft was improperly deiced at the gate while ground air and packs ran simultaneously, violating FOM procedures. The pilot attributed these safety failures to a lack of accountability and supervision among contract personnel and station staff.

synopsis: CRJ-700 Fist Officer reported confusion on altitude assignment on arrival to CYYC, citing differences in U.S. and Canadian ATC terminology with respect to 'descend via' clearances.
summary: Pilots on an arrival to runway 35L received conflicting altitude clearances from Edmonton Center and Canadian controllers regarding the IGVEP3 arrival. The reporter attributes the confusion to differing terminology between U.S. and Canadian ATC procedures, recommending pilot education on these distinctions.

synopsis: A B757 flight attendant crew arrived late for their flight because of weather delays and found that the gate agents had begun boarding their flight without them having had the opportunity to do their pre-flight checks. The aircraft was not ready for boarding.
summary: Flight attendants boarded a Boeing 757 at Gate XX after a late arrival, discovering passengers and a non-working pilot already on board. Ground agents had initiated boarding without verifying the crew's presence, forcing the cabin crew to manage safety checks and passenger handling before they could stow luggage or inspect equipment.

synopsis: BE20 pilot reported confusion and an unsafe situation when ATC issued a new route clearance just two minutes after departure.
summary: The pilot reported that shortly after takeoff from ONT, SoCal Approach issued a direct POM VOR clearance not in the flight plan, causing the autopilot to turn toward an incorrect waypoint. The pilot attributed the deviation to the controller's failure to coordinate with Tower and the unsafe timing of the re-route requiring immediate GPS programming.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Flight instructor reported loss of directional control and a runway excursion after landing at BTL in snowy and icy conditions.
summary: A flight instructor and student on a training flight at BTL veered off runway 23L during a go-around due to a suspected locked brake and icy conditions. The aircraft sustained no damage and there were no injuries.

synopsis: G450 First Officer experiences a taxiway excursion at DVT during a turn from Taxiway A to A13. The right main gear departs the paved surface during the turn.
summary: The flight crew reported that the right main wheel went off the taxiway while turning from Taxiway A to A13. The pilot attributed the incident to the narrow taxiway, lack of hard surface margins, and a non-smooth turn arc at the intersection.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Light twin pilot receiving instruction reported an NMAC with a helicopter in the pattern at LGU.
summary: During a multi-engine check ride with a simulated left engine failure, the pilot and examiner missed a helicopter on left downwind at 4,800 feet while circling for Runway 35. The near miss occurred because high radio traffic and the engine-out distraction prevented the crew from identifying the helicopter's position until they had passed it.

synopsis: A flight crew discovered that their FMS had kept the wrong transition points for their arrival runway. The arrival STAR was not loaded in the FMS. A confusing note over an expected transition point added to the confusion.
summary: The crew misread a chart note while on the RODIO2 arrival into KSAT, initially selecting the wrong FMS transition for Runway 4. The error was caused by a flight plan filed without a specific runway, which loaded incorrect waypoints until the STAR was manually selected.

synopsis: IAH Tower Controller describes a departure turning the wrong direction, into the arrival path of a smaller jet causing a wake turbulence problem.
summary: Air Traffic Control cleared Aircraft X for takeoff with a right turn, but the pilot incorrectly turned left, creating a wake turbulence conflict with arriving Aircraft Y. Controllers instructed Aircraft X to expedite its climb and advised Aircraft Y to continue descending below the wake to avoid turbulence.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZOB Controller instructing describes a situation where the developmental is working a combined sector. The developmental is certified on one of the combined sectors where all the problems occur. The developmental has aircraft head-on at the same altitude, then refuses to use positive control. The instructor fixes the problems so there were no losses of separation.
summary: An OJTI and a certified trainee controller at YQG/DRE experienced unsafe conditions where the trainee repeatedly created head-on conflicts and refused positive control. The instructor intervened multiple times to prevent imminent traffic situations, noting the trainee's poor execution could have caused NMACs or TCAS events.

synopsis: An A319 flight crew, level at FL220 near MSTRD and cleared via the IVANE RNAV STAR to CLT, was cleared to 'descend via' the arrival and the flight crew selected managed descent after confirming that each had reviewed the procedure, its restrictions and had determined and set the 'bottom altitude' for the procedure as 6,000 MSL. The aircraft then began a descent to cross ROYOS between FL230 and FL190 as charted, but failed to meet the requirement to cross the active waypoint, KIYEN, at or above FL220 as restricted.
summary: An A319 crew descended early via the IVANE5 arrival before reaching the KIYEN restriction due to engaging NAV descent mode prematurely. The controller stopped the descent at FL200, attributing the error to Airbus software behavior and insufficient pilot training on the procedure's specific crossing restrictions.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: PHL TRACON Controller described a situation where the receiving sector is using a different radar feed which the PHL Controller is not aware of. Airspace is violated by the receiving controller and when he calls the other sector, he finds out about the radar use. Controller implements plan for future handoffs and requests Miles In-Trail [MIT], which are denied by management.
summary: A PHL North High controller managed Aircraft X and Y on the JAIKE3 arrival when N90 Metro could not see the traffic due to radar limitations, forcing manual entry into N90 airspace. The incident highlighted a lack of late handoff procedures and a denied request for 20 miles-in-trail, which the reporter states increases the risk of operational error.

synopsis: ZID Controller reported another controller didn't know that an aircraft was Non-RVSM due to another aircraft in the flight while refueling.
summary: An air traffic controller relieving the 84D sector discovered Aircraft X was negative RVSM while refueling Aircraft Y, a status unknown to sector 86. The controller notified the supervisor and sector 86 to ensure proper separation until the aircraft separated.

synopsis: SCT Controller describes a situation where an aircraft is issued the published missed approach at BUR and starts the turn early causing a conflict with another aircraft along with an airspace violation.
summary: Aircraft X, an ILS approach to BUR, executed two go-arounds due to TCAS RAs with VNY traffic. On the second go-around, the pilot deviated from the published missed approach by turning early, causing a loss of separation with departing Aircraft Y due to conflicting procedures and lack of DVA tools.

synopsis: A320 flight crew experiences turbulence and strong gusty winds during approach to Runway 16R, resulting in a decision to go-around. During the go-around, flap overspeed occurs, and again while configuring for the subsequent approach.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence, low-level wind shear, and shifting winds on approach to Reno Runway 16R, necessitating a missed approach. Rapid airspeed gains during the go-around caused two flap overspeed events in configurations 3 and 1, which were reported to maintenance after a successful second landing.

synopsis: B737 Captain believes that the RAM mount suction cup fastened to the L3 window is causing overheats and delaminations.
summary: The pilot discovered L3 window delamination caused by a RAM mount suction cup on a heated window. The pilot suspects the mount absorbs and reflects heat, potentially causing serious safety issues and unnecessary maintenance costs.

synopsis: While level at FL240 prior to MAYOS on the IVANE RNAV STAR to CLT the flight crew of an A319 opted to initiate their previously received 'descend via' clearance, set their 6000 MSL bottom altitude in the altitude alert and selected managed descent. As directed, the Flight Management Guidance Computer (FMGC) initiated the descent despite not yet having complied with the minimum FL240 altitude at MAYOS.
summary: The crew of an Airbus descending via the IVANE RNAV STAR at FL240 inadvertently descended below the Mayos crossing restriction because the FMS failed to enforce the limit. They intervened at 23,800 feet after ATC clarified the requirement, attributing the error to FMS software limitations.

synopsis: An Air Carrier flight crew on approach to Runway 27L at ORD is issued a 'contact Tower at the TAFFS intersection' clearance. The Captain switches to Tower immediately after and is told by ORD Tower to go back to Approach Controller. C90 Controller reminds them of the importance of not switching frequencies too soon.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway 27L, the captain switched to tower frequency immediately upon clearance, causing the crew to miss a speed reduction instruction from approach control. The incident resulted from expectation bias regarding local phraseology and the pilot flying's failure to monitor radio selection.

synopsis: EMB-145 flight crew discovers during approach that the flaps were never fully retracted during the prior departure due to and ATC distraction during the departure.
summary: The flight crew flew an entire flight with flaps set to 9 after an ATC turn clearance at 1,500 feet interrupted the after-takeoff flow, causing them to fail to retract the flaps. Maintenance inspected the aircraft post-landing and signed it off, while the crew attributed the error to the interruption and complacency during the checklist.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reports arriving at EYW to find the only available approach is an ASR to Runway 27 which is not authorized at night, according to the approach plate. After consulting with the Dispatcher it is decided that the ASR is legal with ATC approval. VMC are encountered at 1,300 feet and the flight lands visually.
summary: Dispatchers and a pilot faced confusion over night ASR approach minimums at Key West (EYW) due to an "N/A" notation on the chart. Despite ATC confirmation, the Director of Operations later ruled the approach invalid, but the flight had already landed before the dispatcher could intervene.

synopsis: C402 Captain experiences moderate to severe turbulence at 4,500 feet resulting in a 200 foot altitude loss.
summary: The pilot and copilot encountered sustained moderate and isolated severe turbulence at 4,500 MSL, 75 miles northeast of BIL. This caused momentary loss of control, a 200-foot altitude loss, and head injuries to both crew members while no passengers were on board.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain as PF is issued a runway change at six miles which the First Officer accepts but the Captain rejects. The First Officer attempts to inform ATC of their desire to remain with the original runway but frequency congestion prevents the exchange. A normal landing ensues on the new runway. Days later the Captain is informed that a flap overspeed occurred during the approach.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a late runway change from 4R to 4L at BOS, causing distractions that led to an unnoticed flap overspeed. The Captain attributed the event to the close-in clearance change and advised the crew to verify future runway assignments.

synopsis: B757 flight crew experiences multiple arrival changes during arrival to MROC resulting in the crew getting behind and the aircraft attempting to level and slow prematurely. Stick shaker is encountered and quickly corrected. The approach continues to landing.
summary: Conflicting ATC clearances during arrival in San Jose, Costa Rica, caused the crew to be high on path. The pilot selected Vertical Speed without lowering the MCP altitude, causing the aircraft to level off, slow below maneuver speed, and trigger a brief stick shaker before the crew corrected the error and landed safely.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reports leveling off at 3,000 feet on departure using the HUD, as he has been flying aircraft without the HUD for several months. VNAV is selected but it is not acknowledged in the HUD and not detected by the reporter. As a result, autothrust maintained climb power at level off and exceeded 250 knots.
summary: The pilot flying experienced an airspeed excursion to 278 KIAS during departure after task saturation from simultaneous clearances and HUD use prevented monitoring of Flight Mode Annunciators. The autothrust system remained in EPR mode instead of engaging VNAV, requiring manual power reduction and pitch correction to restore speed limits.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reports setting QNE too early departing EGLL resulting in a level off at FL060 which is 500 feet above the assigned altitude of 6,000 feet. ATC does not comment.
summary: During initial climb from EGLL on SID Southampton 3J, the relief pilot and flight crew inadvertently reset altimeters to 29.92 at 6000 feet instead of waiting for clearance above transition altitude. This caused a 500-foot altitude deviation due to the 1037 local setting, though no traffic conflict occurred and ATC issued a higher climb clearance shortly after.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reports being cleared by NCT to descend and maintain 2,100 feet approaching BERKS during an ILS 19L at SFO. This is below the approach segment altitude of 2,800 feet but was clear and unambiguous and the readback was not challenged. This altitude is not correct and NCT issues a climb to 2,900 feet.
summary: Pilots vectored for ILS 19L descended to 2100 feet per ATC clearance, despite it being below the published 2800-foot minimum. After confirming altitude, ATC instructed a climb to 2900 feet to cancel the approach, then recleared the crew for ILS 19L, resulting in an uneventful landing.

synopsis: A321 Captain experiences aileron control difficulties upon disengaging the autopilot at 400 feet on the approach and a go-around is initiated. The First Officer finds no control difficulties and the second approach is uneventful. Post flight reveals that an external battery pack is hindering full left side stick movement.
summary: The Pilot Flying experienced degraded aileron control at 400 feet AGL on final due to an external battery pack lodged between the sidestick and nose wheel steering handle. A go-around was performed, control transferred to the First Officer, and an uneventful landing was accomplished.

synopsis: An A321 flight crew inbound to CLT on the IVANE RNAV STAR in managed descent mode received multiple improper FMGC commands regarding the need for drag and improper warnings with respect to prognosticated compliance with future crossing restrictions. The flight crew overrode the automation and complied manually with the restrictions.
summary: The Captain and First Officer of an A321 descended below the MAYOS altitude constraint on the IVANE5 arrival into CLT due to distraction and failure to monitor. The crew manually leveled the aircraft and complied with subsequent constraints, noting the FMS incorrectly indicated compliance despite the deviation.

synopsis: Phenom 300 Captain reports receiving a VENTRAL RUD FAIL - CAS message after engine start and shuts down to contact Maintenance Control. Maintenance Control wants to do a circuit breaker reset which the Captain refuses to accomplish, believing it should be written up in the Logbook and corrected by a licensed Maintenance Technician.
summary: A Phenom 300 pilot refused a Maintenance Control directive to reset a circuit breaker for a ventral rudder failure using a non-FAA-approved POH procedure. The pilot declined to perform the undocumented maintenance, citing the PIC's ultimate authority over airworthiness and the requirement to follow only approved AFM and AOM procedures.

synopsis: B767 First Officer reports being dispatched with the left pack inoperative then having the right pack trip for an over temp at FL350. Masks are donned and the QRH is complied with, resulting in the pack being reset in STBY N.
summary: The crew encountered a right pack over-temperature shutdown at FL350 while the left pack was already inoperative. After donning oxygen masks and following the QRH, they restored the right pack using STBY N and continued to the destination without incident.

synopsis: B777 flight crew reports descending below charted altitude on the LIMKO1 arrival to LLBG which is detected by one of the IRO's and ATC but too late to prevent the deviation.
summary: During the LDA 30 approach at TLV, the Pilot Not Flying set 4,500 ft in the altitude window, and the Pilot Flying pressed the altitude selector, causing an early descent below the 5,000 ft LIMKO restriction. ATC acknowledged the deviation and cleared the aircraft to continue the approach at 4,500 ft with no further incident.

synopsis: EMB190 Captain reports several errors by his First Officer under training? during a night visual approach to Runway 12L at MSP. The First Officer inadvertently turned off the autopilot then selected an MCP altitude below field elevation then selected FLC. This resulted in decaying airspeed and flight below the glideslope before the Captain takes over.
summary: During a visual approach to MSP runway 12L, the First Officer inadvertently set a 700-foot altitude constraint and disconnected the autopilot, causing auto-throttles to idle and the aircraft to decay below glide path. The Captain intervened to manually increase thrust and pitch, recovering the approach for a safe landing.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: An instructor reported the student pilot taxied onto FDK Runway 30 at Taxiway A because he missed the signage at the Taxiway A and B intersections which is a hot spot with poor signage and lighting for night operations.
summary: A flight instructor and student entered an active runway during a night cross-country training flight after the student missed a taxiway turn while the instructor was distracted adjusting G1000 brightness. The instructor immediately directed the student to exit the poorly lit, unsigned hot spot, and no collision occurred.

synopsis: EMB145 First Officer reports missing the KLNDR crossing restriction during the KLNDR1 arrival to DFW and describes how difficult it is to comply with an RNAV STAR in an aircraft without VNAV or autothrottle capability.
summary: The flight crew descended 800 feet above the published altitude while flying the KLNDR1 arrival into DFW. The reporter attributed this error to distractions and high workload from complex restrictions, noting the aircraft lacked vertical navigation and autothrottles.

synopsis: PA-46 Captain reports a NMAC departing VIS with a C208 entering the the downwind from an overhead entry. A traffic alert system aboard the PA-46 allowed the reporter to spot the conflicting traffic and take evasive action.
summary: A departing pilot and a Cessna Caravan pilot experienced a near mid-air collision two miles from Visalia between 1,300 and 1,600 feet MSL. The conflict occurred because the Caravan, released by Fresno Approach at Kingsburg, entered the pattern on a converging course, forcing the pilot to execute an evasive climbing left turn.

synopsis: PA-28 Instructor pilot describes an airborne conflict during traffic pattern entry at LAF with a Cirrus already in the Runway 23 pattern and a B737 on a visual approach to Runway 28. LAF Tower does not have Radar and the reporter believes it would have been very useful this day, although the Controller did an admirable job of separating the traffic without it.
summary: A student pilot and instructor in a Piper Archer inbound to Lafayette received a last-minute right turn instruction from a developmental controller to avoid a Cirrus on an extended downwind. The reporter attributed the conflict to the non-radar environment and noted that neither aircraft received wake turbulence advisories despite both passing behind a Boeing 737.

synopsis: Helicopter Instructor experiences a Low Boost light climbing through 8,000 feet followed by an engine failure at 10,000 feet. An autorotation is performed to the nearest airport, where the fuel cap is found to be loose and then tightened. The aircraft starts normally and is flown to a nearby airport for fuel then back to base.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine failure at 10,000 MSL after a 'Low Boost' light illuminated at 8,000 MSL, forcing a safe auto-rotation. The cause was identified as a loose left fuel tank cap, which allowed the engine to restart normally once tightened.

synopsis: LR60 First Officer reports being cleared to 2,400 feet by Approach Control but realizes during the descent by looking at the terrain on the ILS approach chart that the Controller must have said 3,400 feet. A low altitude alert is issued by ATC as the reporter is starting to climb.
summary: The pilot climbing on vectors for the ILS 13 approach to HIO realized a nearby DME arc required 3,700 feet while at 2,900 feet. The pilot initiated a climb, and the controller issued a low altitude alert, instructing the crew to maintain 3,400 feet.

synopsis: C208 Captain reports encountering unforecast freezing rain approaching his destination, with similar conditions throughout a widespread area. The reporter elects to continue to destination with the help of ATC to achieve a rapid descent and approach.
summary: The pilot encountered unforecast moderate to severe freezing rain while approaching STL with an empty aircraft. Despite rapid deterioration, the crew maintained control and landed safely, though the pilot noted that TKS anti-ice systems would have reduced the risk compared to the installed boots.

synopsis: A pilot reported that because MCX and OXI are in close proximity and share a common CTAF frequency, sometimes an aircraft's location is confused. Reporter stated some pilots do not clearly speak the respective airport names adding to the confusion.
summary: Pilots at White County (MCX) and Starke County (OXI) airports experience radio confusion on their shared CTAF/UNICOM frequency due to similar names, unclear pronunciation, and inconsistent use of city names. The reporter recommends the FAA assign separate frequencies to prevent these communication errors.

synopsis: PA-28 Instructor Pilot experiences a NMAC with another PA-28 joining the final approach course in a non-standard fashion after not making understandable position reports on the CTAF.
summary: The reporter and a student in a Piper Archer encountered a Piper Warrior on a diagonal final to Runway 18 at White County (MCX) after the Warrior pilot entered traffic with poor radio communication. The reporter executed a right 360 to avoid the cut-off, while the Warrior pilot continued making unclear calls before departing.

synopsis: C208 Captain reports a near ground collision with an airport vehicle that is supervising the snow plows but apparently not looking ahead. The C208 had stopped and was about to shut down the engine when the truck driver noticed the aircraft and stopped quickly.
summary: During taxiing in poor visibility at ORD, an airport maintenance truck nearly struck the aircraft's propeller while the pilot prepared for an emergency shutdown. The incident occurred because the truck driver failed to monitor their path while supporting deicing operations, stopping only five feet from the aircraft.

synopsis: Light Sport Aircraft (LSA) pilot reports being overtaken on the base leg of the VFR traffic pattern by a PA-28 that had reported entering on the crosswind but apparently never understood the location or the speed of the LSA.
summary: A light sport aircraft pilot and a Piper Cherokee pilot experienced a near mid-air collision while operating in the traffic pattern at Cambridge-Dorchester County Airport. The Cherokee passed 100 feet above the light sport aircraft due to the Cherokee's failure to monitor CTAF and scan visually, and the reporter's failure to confirm the Cherokee had visual contact.

synopsis: A pilot within two miles of HMT at 2,520 FT had a near miss with a radio controlled model aircraft which passed very nearby while climbing above his altitude.
summary: A pilot descending to 2,550 feet for a left downwind at HMT encountered two RC aircraft climbing vertically near 2,500 feet, leaving no time for evasive action. The reporter attributed the incident to a modeler operating above the 1,000-foot limit despite a NOTAM restricting unmanned aircraft to 2,512 feet.

synopsis: R-22 Instructor pilot experiences an engine failure shortly after takeoff and is able to auto rotate to an unused taxiway at the departure airport.
summary: During a routine training flight departure, the pilot experienced a loss of engine power. The aircraft executed a right turn below 100 feet AGL and performed an emergency landing on an adjacent unused taxiway.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: CE525 flight crew experiences a loud squeal on ZLA frequency 135.2 making communication nearly impossible. After switching to a new frequency comm returns to normal. During the next day's departure the 135.2 frequency is again assigned with the same results.
summary: The flight crew experienced loud radio interference on 135.2 MHz while descending on the LYNXX 8 STAR and contacting Los Angeles Center. This noise caused confusion regarding altitude restrictions at HEC, leading to a deviation from the published expected clearance, though no traffic risk occurred.

synopsis: G1159 flight crew reports a tire failure at 80 knots during takeoff resulting in a rejected takeoff. As the aircraft is brought to a stop a second tire on the same side burst.
summary: During the take-off roll at 80 KTS, the Captain aborted after the right main tire burst, causing a second right main tire to burst while stopping. The event resulted in no injuries or significant aircraft damage.

synopsis: PA32 pilot experiences a power loss shortly after takeoff and determines insufficient runway remains to land straight ahead and elects to land on an adjacent highway without damage or injury.
summary: During takeoff, the pilot lost engine power while accelerating in ground effect and executed an emergency landing on an empty highway. The aircraft was subsequently taxied off the road and towed back to the airport by emergency responders.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZJX Controller describes a situation where aircraft were in or in close proximity to a warning area and the lack of coordination leading up to the airspace becoming active.
summary: A Missions Specialist Controller activated W155A airspace early without notifying the West Area supervisor or sector controllers, disregarding instructions to wait. This caused significant distraction and increased workload for Nepta and Brewton controllers, who struggled to coordinate reroutes and pointouts for affected aircraft.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: LAF Controller describes a situation where the facility is short staffed and the Controller departs two aircraft in sequence, thinking the second is VFR. The second aircraft is IFR and the Controller has a loss of separation.
summary: A controller managing combined positions during a staffing shortage cleared an IFR aircraft for takeoff assuming it was VFR, causing a procedural deviation. The reporter attributed the error to excessive workload, inadequate staffing, and the Air Traffic Manager's failure to assume a position to assist.

synopsis: Two Air Carrier pilots and the Approach Controller involved describe being vectored for the ILS 23 at CRW while Runway 5 is the active runway and ILS. The autopilot captures a false signal initially, that quickly becomes erratic and a go- around is initiated and the mistake is discovered.
summary: Pilots and controllers were involved during an ILS approach to Runway 23 when the autopilot captured false signals from the active Runway 5 antennas. The controller admitted forgetting the runway change, causing erratic instrument indications that forced a missed approach before a successful landing on Runway 5.

synopsis: ASE TRACON Controllers report of a loss of separation given to them by ASE Tower. Controllers report on the situation and describe how it could have been fixed by the Tower.
summary: Local Control trainees launched a high-performance Aircraft X behind a slow Aircraft Y on the LINDZ8 departure, causing an unsafe overtake due to insufficient separation and restricted MVA turns. The Terminal Control instructor resolved the conflict by expediting climbs and issuing turns, though the Local Control OJT instructor failed to intervene earlier.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: ZDC Controller describes an aircraft given a descent clearance, the aircraft descending, and then climbs back to old assigned altitude. Controller thought this a company problem, but this aircraft was the same type, but a different company.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller issued a descent clearance to an Airbus at FL210 west of MOL, but the aircraft initially descended slowly before climbing back to FL210. The controller attributes this altitude deviation to a suspected Airbus-specific issue and urges the manufacturer and FAA to investigate to prevent future accidents.

synopsis: B737 flight crew experiences a leading edge flap transit light during approach to RNO. QRH procedures are examined but the requirement for a flaps 15 landing is overlooked. During this time the First Officer gets high and slow requiring the Captain to offer assistance. A normal landing ensues.
summary: The Captain, acting as pilot flying, missed the QRH requirement to land with flaps 15 during a Leading Edge Flap Transit malfunction on approach to RNO. This oversight caused a low airspeed warning and unstable approach, though the First Officer corrected the flight path and landed safely.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reports his aircraft beginning to slow automatically during an RNAV approach while level at 3000 feet, with 2400 feet set in the altitude window for the next step down altitude. ATC asks for 210 knots to be maintained and speed intervention is selected on the MCP which results in an early descent that is quickly corrected.
summary: During an RNAV approach, the pilot used Speed Intervention to maintain 210 knots at 3000 feet but failed to notice the aircraft drifted down to 2600 feet. The pilot attributed the altitude deviation to an automation error and admitted personal fault for not understanding the system.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported receiving a momentary forward cargo fire warning on taxi-in that was later traced to a motorized wheelchair that still had the battery connected.
summary: The Captain experienced a false forward cargo fire warning while taxiing to the gate, caused by a motorized wheelchair battery overheating and rubbing against an object. The crew shut down the engines, and maintenance confirmed burnt rubber from the wheelchair triggered the detection system.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain experiences a standby attitude indicator failure in cruise without displaying any failure flags.
summary: Pilots on a B-737-700 cruise flight observed the standby attitude gyro precessing without displaying the orange Gyro Failure flag. Maintenance replaced the unit, but the report highlights a safety risk where pilots could not distinguish valid attitude references if primary displays also failed.

synopsis: B757 First Officer states that an aircraft he was assigned to fly has a back course button and three control wheel steering buttons on the Mode Control Panel that do not belong there.
summary: The pilot reported that their aircraft had unlisted, untrained, and unlabeled buttons on the Mode Control Panel, unlike other fleet aircraft. Maintenance Control deemed the configuration acceptable, but the pilot considered it unsafe due to the lack of training and documentation.

synopsis: B737 flight crew describes mistakes that occurred during an ILS PRM 28R approach into SFO and indicates the following contributing factors: fatigue and ATC stepping the flight down 1,000 feet at a time.
summary: Pilots flying an ILS 28R PRM approach at SFO experienced a low airspeed warning after disconnecting autopilot to recapture the glideslope, caused by late descent clearances, a rushed briefing, and incorrect altitude settings. Despite the warning and discussion of a go-around, the crew stabilized the aircraft and completed a normal landing.

synopsis: B747 flight crew experiences failure of the DC Distribution bus 1 in cruise. After contacting Maintenance Control it is discovered that a circuit breaker had tripped and was likely caused by the iPad ram mount, on the floor, hitting it. The circuit breaker is reset.
summary: During cruise, an iPad RAM mount resting against the circuit breaker panel likely popped DC distribution bus 1 breaker no.1, causing autopilot and navigation losses. The Captain reset the breaker after consulting maintenance, restoring most systems except the number 1 EEC, which remained in alternate mode for the remainder of the flight.

synopsis: While performing a post departure FOD inspection at his assigned gate the Lead Marshaler was alarmed by the sound of engines spooking up behind him and only then noted that an aircraft was taxiing into the gate despite his presence in its path and the lack of a Marshaler. He recovered quickly, got the flight crew's attention with a wands crossed 'STOP' signal and then marshaled the balance of their arrival.
summary: A ramp marshal performing a FOD walk was startled when an aircraft rolled down the lead-in line about 10 feet behind him without marshaling. The marshal immediately displayed a stop signal, then marshaled the aircraft to the stop mark after discarding the debris.

synopsis: A320 First Officer experiences confusion after Approach Control gave him direct to MAVEK and cleared for the RNAV ILS 05R at MMMX. The plain ILS 05R is selected from the FMGC database but no transition from SMO is available and is created manually. Heading and altitude deviations occur and ATC eventually takes over with vectors and altitude assignments.
summary: The crew incorrectly programmed the FMS for the ILS 05R approach at MMMX, causing a deviation at MAVEK and an altitude error to 9,200 feet instead of 9,700. ATC provided vectors to rejoin the localizer, and the aircraft landed safely after the crew corrected the flight path and altitude.

synopsis: A Captain reports their A320 MEL and Flight Manuals are not specific enough to determine if an MEL 29-30-03F of an ECAM Hydraulics Page Indications, System Pressure is appropriate for the system failure being addressed. First Officer (FO) had noticed on the ECAM HYD Page that a line extending up from the blue pump was green instead of amber as it should be with no Blue System pressure.
summary: During preflight, the first officer questioned the applicability of MEL 29-30-03F for a green line indication on the HYD ECAM page, citing ambiguous documentation. The crew departed after the indication turned amber, but the pilot concluded that unclear MEL and flight manual definitions caused the safety concern.

synopsis: On short final for Runway 20R at SNA the flight crew of a Challenger was surprised by a RAAS announcement of 'approaching 19R.' The runway number had been altered and, apparently, the RAAS database had not yet been updated.
summary: The flight crew executed a visual approach to runway 20R at SNA when the Runway Awareness Advisory System incorrectly announced runway 19R. The crew attributed the error to an outdated or uninstalled RAAS database following a 2014 runway renumbering, which caused a distraction during the critical approach phase.

synopsis: A B737 Captain reported improper and unsafe ground handling by ramp personnel.
summary: During taxi after pushback, the flight crew stopped the aircraft to avoid a collision with a ramp tug returning to check an access panel. The pilot attributed the incident to the ramp crew rushing and the crew's failure to monitor company frequency due to non-tower radio settings.

synopsis: When their MD-83's normal stab trim failed to function after takeoff the flight crew returned to their departure airport. After maneuvering for approach employing the alternate stab trim and autopilot the normal system returned to operation when the autopilot was disconnected for final approach and landing.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a total horizontal stabilizer trim failure shortly after takeoff, which resolved after resetting the main stab trim cutoff switch and using alternate trim switches. The crew returned to the airport and landed normally, albeit overweight at 135,000 lbs, after all trim systems functioned correctly on downwind.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Pilot determines that they can depart a specific runway with a tail wind of 10 knots or more with company. Aircraft departs and pilot thinks they are cleared on course due to transmission earlier given by ATC. ATC is expecting them to fly the SID. Course deviation happens amidst the confusion.
summary: The pilot departed Heber City (36U) Runway 22 in VMC but received a conflicting COOLI 4 departure clearance intended for Runway 4. Although ATC verbally authorized a direct route after radar contact, the mismatch between the filed procedure and actual runway usage required an incident report due to the clearance error.

synopsis: Pilot reports of confusion after receiving his clearance from VNY ATCT. He is given a SID and also told to comply with the Obstacle Departure Procedure. Pilot departs and controller directs his flight to another direction away from the Burbank final.
summary: A pilot departing VNY under IFR clearance confused the ADAMM ONE SID with the ODP, turning left toward the BUR final approach course. The Burbank controller issued a right turn to heading 180 to avoid a separation error, which the pilot attributed to failing to clarify conflicting procedures on the ground.

synopsis: A GLFIV flight crew rejected their first takeoff attempt from runway 25 at ZZZ due to an unexplained master caution and aural warning. When no cause for the warning was evident they attempted another takeoff. They then received and disregarded the same warning, and when back pressure was applied at Vr there was no pitch response. A second rejected takeoff was initiated at very high speed. The aircraft was brought to a near stop and exited at the far end of the runway.
summary: The PIC and SIC rejected takeoff twice on Runway 25 due to a master caution and suspected LP bleed exceedance, followed by a total loss of flight control pressure during the second attempt. The aircraft stopped on Taxiway A with hot brakes and a right main gear fire, requiring an immediate evacuation of all passengers and crew.

synopsis: PA28 pilot entering the traffic pattern for Runway 15 at FLY experiences a NMAC with a Bonanza departing Runway 15 and turning east. A head on situation develops with the PA28 pilot diving under the Bonanza to avoid collision.
summary: A pilot on a 45-degree entry to Runway 15 at FLY descended 200–300 feet to avoid a head-on conflict with a departing Bonanza that climbed over them, missing by 100 feet. The reporter attributes the near miss to the Bonanza switching to Springs Approach immediately after departure, leaving the pilot unaware of its position on CTAF.

synopsis: BFI controllers described a runway incursion involving a departing cleared for takeoff small aircraft and a vehicle that was already approved to be on the runway. The Controller did not use the RID (Runway Incursion Device) when he allowed the vehicle onto the runway. Pilot advised Tower of traffic on runway, Controller removed the vehicle off the runway and the aircraft departed.
summary: Local West controller cleared Aircraft X for takeoff from Runway 13R while a city vehicle was inspecting the runway, failing to activate the Runway Incursion Device or see the vehicle due to a blind spot. The controller immediately ordered the vehicle to exit, re-cleared the aircraft after the runway was vacated, and the departure proceeded without incident.

synopsis: B737 flight crew describes a terrain warning caused by attempting to fly over the tall buildings of Houston during a visual approach to Runway 31L. The First Officer was flying and the Captain takes control for the go-around when the First Officer's response is too slow.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced obstacle alerts during visual approaches to Dallas (DAL) Runway 31L after deviating left of course toward downtown buildings. The Captain executed go-arounds in both instances, attributing the events to inadequate briefing of known terrain threats and failure to monitor the approach path.

synopsis: Both pilots of a B737 were a little surprised to see a Flight Manager Computer (FMC) unit without an Automatic Communications Addressing and Reporting System (ACARS) access function. No abnormal log data or Configuration Deviation List (CDL) was found so it was assumed the older aircraft simply wasn't so equipped. They subsequently learned the lack was unintentional and should have been entered in the Aircraft Maintenance Log (AML) and investigated.
summary: The First Officer and Captain operated a ZZZ aircraft without ACARS capability because the MCDU lacked a MENU button, a discrepancy not noted in the logbook. They proceeded with the flight using COMM 2 for clearances, later discovering the aircraft was incorrectly configured without its standard MCDU.

synopsis: Pilot reports that from start to finish of flight including taxi out, ATC complained of a stuck MIC. A new MIC switch was installed incorrectly on the First Officer's yoke the night prior, which led to a hot MIC connection without any activation of the switch on their B737 aircraft.
summary: The crew experienced a stuck microphone throughout all flight phases caused by an incorrectly installed First Officer yoke switch that hardwired the mic hot. After troubleshooting and switching to alternate mode, the aircraft landed uneventfully, prompting a recommendation to re-evaluate maintenance evaluation procedures.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reports receiving a TCAS RA while descending to 7,000 feet with the engines at flight idle. After selecting Takeoff/Go-Around (TOGA) mode to evade, a 4-5 second delay is experienced before TOGA thrust is achieved.
summary: During a visual approach, the crew received a TCAS climb resolution advisory but experienced a 4-to-5-second thrust lag when advancing to TOGA. The captain executed a lateral turn to evade the traffic, and the aircraft was later grounded for thrust system testing.

synopsis: B737 flight crew experiences confusion when cleared for the RNAV Visual RWY 19R at LAS off the GRNPA1 arrival. The crew assumes the Controller means the RNAV (GPS) RWY 19R, which is not correct and results in an upset Controller and a go-around.
summary: Pilots descending on GRNPA1 into LAS were cleared for RNAV Visual RWY 19R but failed to locate the procedure in their FMC due to its unusual chart placement. This caused them to become high and fast, resulting in a cancelled approach and a subsequent visual landing on RWY 25L.

synopsis: A B737 Captain reported the recent preflight checklist response changes contained some system setting and selection responses which were not completed or were inaccurate. This situation lead him to feel the policy was promoting a normalization of deviance.
summary: A 737 pilot reported that the preflight checklist forces Captains to falsely confirm items checked by the First Officer or not yet set, such as the Mode Control Panel V2 speed. The reporter argues this design promotes "Normalization of Deviance" by requiring Captains to lie about checks they did not personally perform or witness.

synopsis: A baggage handler and safety representative at ORD describes a near collision between two golf carts and a baggage tug that was narrowly averted. He believes the primary problem is driving too fast and not obeying traffic rules for airport vehicles.
summary: A baggage handler operating an electric tractor at ORD avoided a collision with two golf carts that failed to stop at a ramp stop sign. The reporter attributes this recurring near miss to excessive speeds, wrong-way driving, and a general disregard for safety rules by ramp personnel.

synopsis: A CRJ700 flight crew and the Dispatcher involved describe a diversion due to fumes in the cabin. Prior to departure Maintenance had made repairs to air conditioning duct work using 'some kind of super glue', which may have been the source of the fumes.
summary: The flight crew diverted to Airport ZZZ due to cabin fumes and crew shortness of breath caused by disconnected ducting repaired with tape and glue. A dispatcher failed to amend the release in time due to limited cockpit communication during the emergency, though the aircraft landed safely and one passenger required hospitalization.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer reports diverting to an alternate airport due to thunderstorms over and in the vicinity of their destination airport, against the wishes of their Dispatcher.
summary: The flight crew diverted to MCO due to severe weather and turbulence while approaching PBI, rejecting dispatch instructions to penetrate storms that would have critically depleted fuel reserves. The reporter attributed the incident to inadequate preflight fuel planning, poor dispatch communication, and a company culture that prioritized avoiding diversions over safety.

synopsis: Dispatcher reports being assigned a desk that is being 'watched over' by another Dispatcher that has not received a proper turnover, due to the originally assigned Dispatcher being sent home early to be legal for his next shift. Upon signing in it is noticed that the desk is monitoring over 80 flights, both in the air and on the ground. Operational control was reestablished.
summary: An overnight dispatcher was sent home early for rest, leaving a relief dispatcher without a proper pass-down before the scheduled dispatcher arrived to find 83 flights allocated, including 24 in the air. Operational control was reestablished after the dispatcher signed in, though the report attributes the issue to unrealistic workload and inadequate handover procedures.

synopsis: After touchdown the pilot of a C-402 was unable to arrest the aircraft's skid toward the left side of the runway where it exited the hard surface and the left landing gear collapsed. All aboard evacuated without injury.
summary: The pilot reported that after landing on runway 9, the aircraft skidded left and exited the runway, causing the left main gear to collapse while skidding through grass. The pilot shut down the aircraft and evacuated passengers with no injuries.

synopsis: Multiple factors combined to result in a seriously un-stabilized approach during which multiple calls for a go-around by the two first officers went without response. A late and barely adequate addition of power and flattening of descent saved the ultimate arrival.
summary: The flight crew experienced confusion and task saturation during an RNAV-to-ILS arrival at SBGR due to conflicting ATC clearances and fatigue from a delay. Despite First Officer go-around calls for excessive descent rate and low airspeed, the captain elected to continue, resulting in a late touchdown 1,500 feet down the runway.

aircraft: Heavy Transport; Low Wing; 4 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Cargo Captain discovers that the new paperless automatic weight and balance system is not aware of MEL restrictions on loading and requires human intervention, but the humans responsible are not aware of this requirement.
summary: The crew reported that despite Dispatch notifying the ramp agent of MEL-voided positions, the ramp agent transposed small cans into those voided spots because the paperless Auto WB system does not recognize MELs. This error was discovered post-landing after Dispatch alerted the flight crew to the potential transposition.

synopsis: A Maintenance Technician reported an oil leak and significant oil consumption without apparent notice by other Maintenance or Company Personnel. He noted that the oil tracking program is not identifying the elevated consumption.
summary: The pilot discovered a significant oil leak from the left Rolls Royce RB211 engine's IDG drive shaft caused by a damaged O-ring after block-in. The reporter attributed the failure to stop the ETOPS flight to crew oversight and a broken Oil Monitoring Program that failed to flag the high consumption rate.

aircraft: Medium Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: A turboprop Captain, performing an engine run-up test procedure in a non-movement area of the airport noted the aircraft was sliding on the snow and ice encrusted runway. Before he was able to disengage the power lever trigger to allow throttle movement the aircraft had slid onto an active taxiway.
summary: The crew initiated an engine run-up on a snow-patched non-movement taxiway, causing the aircraft to lose traction and slide onto an active taxiway. The slide occurred because inadvertent power lever trigger actuation locked the levers, delaying power reduction and reverse thrust application.

synopsis: While in a practice holding pattern at 4,500 feet, a C172 Instructor experiences a NMAC with a Bonanza. ATC indicated the Bonanza was IFR at 4,000 feet and never left that altitude.
summary: A flight instructor and student in a VFR training aircraft at 4,500 MSL observed a Bonanza climbing into their path while holding over the Electric City VOR. The instructor executed a turn to avoid the conflict, but the controller dismissed the report of the Bonanza exceeding 4,000 MSL, citing transponder data and approving a frequency change.

synopsis: After landing safely at their destination, the flight crew of an LJ-60 found the taxiways covered in black ice and were unable to prevent the jet from sliding off the taxiway. They came to a stop with no damage or injury to the pilots, the sole occupants. Chemical dispersants are used on the runways, but not permitted on the taxiways due to environmental reasons.
summary: A ferry flight crew experienced a steering failure and skid on black ice while taxiing on an untreated taxiway at a 121 airport. The aircraft slid off the pavement and rotated 180 degrees onto the grass without damage, attributed to sand-only treatment and strong tailwinds.

synopsis: B737 Captain at FL380 reports being blinded by the solar array southwest of LAS.
summary: A pilot reported that blinding reflection from a solar facility made it uncomfortable to look in that direction, even with sunglasses. Consequently, the pilot could not scan for traffic from that direction.

synopsis: When traffic compression required the Center Controller to vector and manually descend traffic on the ROBUC RNAV STAR to runway 4R at BOS, he cleared a B737, currently on a vector, direct to JOODY (a waypoint with no crossing restrictions) at which point the jet began a descent so as to cross the next fix, SOFFE, at or above 9,000 feet as restricted. While doing so the flight entered airspace given via LOA (Letter Of Agreement) to Providence Approach when BOS is landing on 4R. The reporter cited the 'cumbersome and unwieldy' nature of 'descend via' clearances when addressing returns to the STAR after interruptions.
summary: An air traffic controller managing Boston arrivals issued a "Descend Via" clearance to a B737, causing it to descend into Providence airspace instead of remaining in the delegated sector. The controller attributed the error to unfamiliarity with the new procedure during vectoring and acknowledged a failure to issue a specific altitude restriction.

synopsis: A C-172 failed to stop prior to crossing the hold short line abnormally distant from Runway 28 on the parallel south taxiway.
