summary: During an RNAV arrival into IAH, the flight crew experienced an FMS database error that duplicated waypoints, causing the aircraft to stop descending at 13,000 feet and cross GLAMM 1,000 feet high. The crew manually descended and corrected the flight path, attributing the issue to the FMS loading crossing restrictions twice.

synopsis: After entering the correct runway and departure an Airbus flight crew followed the incorrect left turn indicated by the flight director on the NITE1 RNAV departure out of SFO. ATC issued a vector for a right turn back on course.
summary: The pilot flying followed an erroneous left turn command from the Flight Director shortly after takeoff from SFO on the NITE1 departure, deviating from the required right turn. Air Traffic Control intervened to correct the heading to 020 degrees, preventing a conflict with Runway 01L, while the crew attributed the error to blindly trusting the Flight Director.

synopsis: A B767 EICAS alerted REC FAN so the crew accomplished the QRH. The flight attendants then reported cabin smoke and haze so the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced a right recirc fan trip and cabin fumes 80 miles west of departure, prompting a return. After an overweight landing, fire services inspected the aircraft, which was then returned to the gate.

synopsis: After takeoff, a PC-12 engine was running hotter than normal so the crew returned to the departure airport where the cowl inlet plug was found still installed.
summary: The pilot and First Officer experienced abnormal engine temperatures after takeoff due to a missing engine inlet cover. The crew returned safely to the departure airport after the pilot admitted failing to verify the First Officer's preflight inspection.

synopsis: A C-150 electrical system failed during a practice instrument approach to a Class D airport. Without radios the pilot navigated through and around Class B and D airspaces to return to the home airport.
summary: The pilot experienced electrical failures affecting Nav/Comm radios and transponder altitude reporting while vectored for a practice approach. After losing radio contact and mistakenly setting transponder code 7500 instead of 7600, the pilot avoided Class D airspace and executed a no-flap landing due to inoperative electric flaps.

synopsis: A DA2000 descending to FL330 with head-on traffic at FL320 took evasive action from a TCAS RA, climbing to clear the conflict. ATC had advised about the traffic.
summary: During descent from FL410 to FL330 in intermittent IMC, the crew received a TCAS Resolution Advisory to pitch up due to traffic at FL320, causing a climb to FL350. The crew complied with the RA, reported it to ATC, and continued to a successful landing after the conflict cleared.

synopsis: A C182 pilot cancelled IFR with ATC prior to landing, but he did not close out his flight plan after landing. ATC requested that local police contact the pilot to verify his well-being.
summary: The pilot conducted an IFR flight to an airport with closed tower and approach services, requesting IFR cancellation from Center during final approach. Although the landing was normal, police later searched for the missing aircraft because the flight plan closure was not properly confirmed by Center.

aircraft: Light Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: PCT Controller reports of an aircraft that entered his sector with a late point out from ZDC, which later crosses onto another sector. Reporter realizes he should have pointed this aircraft out to the other sector in PCT's airspace.
summary: A ZDC controller failed to coordinate a point out for Aircraft X descending through ENO airspace, causing a coordination gap with GRACO. The ENO controller attributed the error to assuming ZDC would handle intra-facility coordination under the LOA, a mistake resulting from not reviewing the full agreement.

synopsis: STL Local Controller reports of an aircraft taking off without a clearance. Aircraft was told to line up and wait, but Controller didn't tell him it was for spacing on previous departure.
summary: An air traffic controller on Local Control observed Aircraft X begin an unauthorized takeoff roll on runway 12L while Aircraft Y approached runway 12R in rainy weather. The controller attributed the incident to the pilot's habit of turning left and a lack of explicit instruction regarding the hold short clearance, though no collision occurred.

synopsis: A B737NG Captain's sliding window which was closed but not locked, opened during the takeoff roll. Unable to close and lock it, the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The Pilot Flying reported a side window slid open at 80 knots during takeoff and later detached from its frame when closure was attempted at 500 feet. The crew returned to the departure airport for an overweight landing of 139,000 pounds, attributing the failure to potential incomplete latching or window design.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Airline flight crew reports misunderstanding a taxi clearance to the ramp after landing on runway 31L at DAL.
summary: The flight crew missed a turn onto Taxiway B5 after landing at Dallas due to a confusing Ground clearance omitting Taxiway C5 and misleading airport diagrams. This distraction caused them to enter an uncontrolled area, though they were advised to continue to the gate without incident.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports missing a descent crossing restriction with the First Officer flying due to a new cruise altitude being programed into the FMC.
summary: The Captain and First Officer descended early from FL400 to meet a crossing restriction but arrived 1,500 feet high because the FO had unknowingly changed the FMC cruise altitude to FL310. This input error delayed Top of Descent calculations and vertical guidance, though ATC accepted the deviation.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew report encountering wake turbulence in trail of an A380 at FL390 that resulted in a 35 degree roll that could not be countered by ailerons.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe wake turbulence from an overtaking A380 while climbing to FL390, causing a 30-40 degree bank and 400-foot altitude loss with ineffective ailerons. The pilots descended to FL370 and turned right to escape the turbulence, attributing the incident to insufficient spacing behind the larger aircraft.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier crew was cleared to cross a point at FL240 and after programming the FMC became distracted in conversation. Consequently, they failed to set the MCP altitude and crossed the fix high.
summary: The pilot flying failed to set FL240 in the MCP window after programming the FMC, causing a distraction that delayed the descent. The crew subsequently initiated a steep vertical speed descent with speedbrakes to meet the crossing restriction at FL240, leveling off slightly south of the required point.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports being cleared to line up and wait on Runway 5L at MMMX. After crossing the hold line, a small commuter turboprop is noted on short final and the Captain stops the aircraft well short of the actual runway, at the same time the Tower issues hold instructions and the turboprop lands.
summary: The flight crew stopped their aircraft 20 feet beyond the Runway 05L hold-short line after observing a landing turboprop on short final. The incident resulted from the tower clearing the landing aircraft to sidestep to 05L without a landing clearance while simultaneously clearing the departure crew to line up.

synopsis: B777 Captain reports misunderstanding or not hearing a taxi clearance after landing Runway 26L at IAH.
summary: The Captain and First Officer missed a ground clearance to turn left on the first parallel while taxiing at Houston in heavy rain. The Captain attributed the missed instruction to the loud 3000-foot audio call, high-speed wipers, and visual distractions, leading to a ground controller questioning their position.

synopsis: A crew on approach to ORD Runway 28R executed a go-around when they realized at the outer marker that ATIS reported the runway closed. The FMS had been programmed during preflight hours earlier, but the fatigued crew forgot to change the arrival data.
summary: The First Officer, fatigued after 17 hours awake, failed to update the FMC from ILS 28R to 28C at Chicago O'Hare. The crew executed a missed approach upon realizing the error and subsequently completed an uneventful autoland on 28C.

synopsis: B757 flight crew discovers apparent damage to the right engine cowl, which appears to be an old repair that has failed. The damage is written up but Maintenance indicates that it has been previously documented and signs it off.
summary: Pilots discovered a failed repair on the right engine inlet cowl during pre-flight, which was undocumented in the logbook or flight plan. Maintenance Control claimed the damage was previously deferred and within limits, but the crew re-wrote the discrepancy to ensure proper airworthiness documentation before departing.

synopsis: DEN airline ramp employee reported leads have to deal with in-transit animals, including a wild wolf that was the subject of this report. Reporter stated they had no training in how to deal with animals.
summary: A ramp lead in Denver released a wild wolf from its kennel to clean it, violating the ramp service manual which prohibits removing animals. The incident occurred because local management lacks a vendor and provides no animal handling training, creating an unsafe situation the reporter fears will cause a tragedy.

synopsis: A B767 crew reported that during an oceanic crossing, the aircraft's EICAS alerted UNABLE RNP FMC with loss of the GPS signal. No loss of navigation accuracy was discovered, and later normal GPS functions returned.
summary: During an oceanic crossing, the crew experienced an UNABLE RNP message due to lost GPS reception, causing the FMC to revert to IRS and DME/DME updates. The Captain manually adjusted RNP to 12.0, and GPS resumed over land with no post-flight discrepancies found.

synopsis: An A320 pilot had been unable to update his IPad at several different locations. An FAA inspector, during the course of a line check, showed him how to use the airport Wi-Fi to update his IPad.
summary: A pilot reported being unable to update their Jeppro app due to poor Wi-Fi bandwidth at the ZZZ lounge and hotel. A federal inspector assisted during preflight by using a mobile hotspot to complete the update, prompting the pilot to adopt this method for future compliance.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A321 Captain reports being given holding instructions at FL180 with a low altimeter setting making FL180 unusable. The distraction of attempting to clarify with ATC results in low airspeed and the flaps being extended above 20,000 feet.
summary: The flight crew descended into ATL and entered a hold at FL180 despite a low altimeter setting, causing confusion with an agitated controller. While transitioning to the approach, the crew extended flaps believing they were below 20,000 feet, attributing the situation to ATC unawareness of altitude limitations and high traffic workload.

synopsis: ERJ-175 Captain reported a failed thrust reverser was not properly deferred at a contract maintenance station.
summary: The flight crew reported an ENG 2 REV FAIL message on landing at ZZZ1 after a contract mechanic at ZZZ improperly deferred the #2 reverser without securing it. This caused a second delay at ZZZ1 while two mechanics completed the required 15-step deferral process, leading the crew to lose trust in ZZZ maintenance reliability.

synopsis: A First Officer (FO) describes the procedural steps that he and the Captain followed that led them to believe their A320 aircraft had lost all cargo smoke detection capability after receiving two ECAM messages for SMOKE FWD CRG DET FAULT and SMOKE AFT CRG DET FAULT in-flight. The ECAM Status page also displayed, under INOP SYS: 'FWD CRG DET' and 'AFT CRG DET.' After engine shut-down, ECAM Status displayed INOP SYS 'CIDS' and Class II maintenance status messages 'CIDS 2' and 'SMOKE.'
summary: During cruise, the flight crew received simultaneous forward and aft cargo smoke detection fault messages, suspecting a CIDS issue rather than actual smoke. They coordinated an ARFF escort to the gate as a precaution, where ground checks confirmed no fire, and maintenance later resolved the fault.

synopsis: CRJ900 First Officer reports getting his foot caught on the metal skid plate under the rudder pedals during takeoff, causing a momentary loss of directional control. The plate was attached to the carpet but the carpet was not attached to the floor and foreword end of the plate was bent up allowing it to catch on the reporters' heel.
summary: The pilot-flying experienced momentary loss of directional control during takeoff roll when their heel jammed on an unsecured, bent metal kick plate beneath the left rudder pedal. The pilot recovered control before rotation, but transferred flight duties to the captain for landing to avoid recurrence.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew reported deviating from charted approach procedure altitudes on a night IMC approach to PIA, resulting in an unstabilized approach and a CFTT event.
summary: During a night ILS 13 approach in IMC, the Captain failed to arm approach mode due to distraction from new checklist procedures, causing an excessive descent rate below 1,000 feet AGL. Although the Pilot Monitoring requested a go-around, the crew continued and stabilized the approach after capturing the glideslope at 750 feet, resulting in a safe landing.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reported encountering wake turbulence in trail of a B737-700 on arrival into ATL.
summary: The Captain and First Officer encountered wake turbulence from a preceding 737-700 while descending on the WARRR1 arrival into ATL. The turbulence caused significant bank angles and autopilot disconnection, which the crew attributed to the preceding aircraft's potential high altitude and strong tailwinds.

synopsis: EMB145 First Officer experiences a loss of the programed arrival while attempting to enter a runway change into the FMC. A new and unfamiliar FMS was cited as a contributing factor.
summary: The flight crew, operating a new FMS during descent into DFW, lost the flight plan while reprogramming for a runway change. This distraction caused the aircraft to cross the HOWDY fix 1,300 feet high, which the pilot attributed to unfamiliarity with the new system and poor CRM.

aircraft: Cessna Citation Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A Citation pilot, after starting the APU, set the parking brake per the checklist. He noticed a 'Rudder Limiter Failure' CAS message, rebooted the aircraft and noted that the parking brake was still set. He then pulled the remaining chocks from the aircraft and went in to the terminal. The other pilot texted him that the aircraft had rolled forward by 25 to 50 feet.
summary: The pilot removed nose wheel chocks without confirming the parking brake was set, causing the aircraft to roll 25 to 50 feet onto taxiway H while the copilot was inside. The incident occurred during pre-departure at LAS after a rudder limiter failure reboot, resulting in the nose crossing into the movement area before passengers boarded.

synopsis: A320 Captain reports being asked by a new Flight Attendant to monitor her actions while she disarms and opens an aft galley door. The door is already disarmed but is rearmed and opened before the reporter can react, blowing the slide.
summary: A Flight Attendant and a supervisor opened door 2R while cleaners were working, causing the slide to deploy after the door was armed. The incident resulted from rushing, distraction, and pressure from cleaners, leading the new employee to operate on muscle memory.

synopsis: An A319 air crew, while taxiing for departure, was alerted by their cockpit jumpseater of an imminent collision hazard with a single engine prop aircraft. The aircraft had been instructed to give way to the A319 and was taxiing at a very high rate of speed. Hard braking by the A319 crew prevented a probable collision.
summary: While taxiing an Airbus A319, the crew avoided a collision with a single-engine propeller aircraft taxiing at over 30 knots after a jumpseater alerted the pilot. The other pilot, who had been instructed to yield by ATC, failed to see the A319 or deviate, resulting in a near-miss that the reporter attributes to excessive speed and lack of situational awareness.

synopsis: B757-200 flight crew on an ETOPS overwater flight reported they were tasked with testing the APU with an inflight start, and the APU would not restart. Reporter recommended they do these kind of tests on domestic flights.
summary: The crew operated an ETOPS flight with a new APU, keeping it running until two hours before top of descent to meet a cool-down requirement. Subsequent restart attempts at FL390 and below FL350 failed with an APU fault, leading the pilot to recommend avoiding such procedures during ETOPS operations.

synopsis: A Captain and First Officer report that during aircraft loading operations, the Main Cargo Door on their MD-11 aircraft remained opened, allowing rain to enter the aircraft. Shipping containers (cans) were also loaded with tops covered with water that ran down into the Center Accessory Compartments (CAC) onto Cannon plugs causing random alerts of AOA, Slat Disagree, Slat EXT, GPWS and Radar Altimeter. Aircraft removed from service.
summary: During loading in rain, an open cargo door allowed water to enter the Center Accessory Compartment, causing electrical faults and cockpit alerts. Maintenance grounded the aircraft for a transload, and the captain subsequently declined the flight due to fatigue.

synopsis: DC-9 Captain experiences a Master Caution light during climbout due to ENG/Airfoil Ice selected by the flying First Officer with the OAT well above 10 C and thrust not reduced to accommodate the ice selection. After this problem is corrected the attitude indicator malfunctions require a diversion to a VMC airport.
summary: During climb, the First Officer activated anti-ice systems above temperature limits without notifying the Pilot Monitoring, causing a Master Caution and loss of heading due to erroneous artificial horizon indications. The crew diverted due to instrument failures and poor weather, landing safely after troubleshooting and receiving ATC guidance.

synopsis: CRJ900 Captain experiences a brake overheat warning at rotation. The aircraft is leveled at 5,000 feet and the gear is extended to cool the brake, before continuing the climb to FL390. At FL390 the same brake indicates an overheat and the crew elects to descend to extend the landing gear then divert to a suitable airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a Left Hand Outer Brake overheat warning at rotation and again at 39,000 ft, requiring gear extension to reset the BTMS. Due to persistent indications and fuel concerns, they diverted and landed, where the warning reappeared with an amber dashed line.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot reports of flight following being terminated due to SFRA and then he is advised later that he violated Class C on the other side of the SFRA.
summary: A pilot departing LAX northbound through a special flight rule corridor experienced a flight following drop and subsequent squawk change, leading to an inadvertent incursion into Burbank Class C airspace. The controller reported no traffic conflict, but the pilot suggested that a direct handover instead of dropping flight following might prevent such deviations.

synopsis: SA227 Captain experiences loss of both hydraulic systems during descent for landing. An emergency condition is encountered and the gear is extended via the QRH, resulting in three green indications. An ILS approach and landing ensues.
summary: The pilot reported intermittent hydraulic pressure warnings on arrival that became solid with zero pressure. After declaring an emergency to Approach, the pilot vectored for an ILS, manually extended the gear per the Quick Reference Handbook, and landed safely.

synopsis: HCF Controller reports of problems associated with flying from a radar environment into a non-radar environment and not being able to display routes to look for issues.
summary: Air Traffic Controllers reported that Aircraft X and Aircraft Y lacked lateral separation when transitioning from radar to oceanic airspace because Aircraft Y filed a latitude/longitude coordinate instead of a required named boundary fix. This non-compliance prevented controllers from verifying separation without manual plotting, creating a safety risk at the HCF airspace boundary.

synopsis: CVG Local Controller reports of a pilot missing his turn-out off the runway. Controller instructs pilot to taxi on parallel runway where sweepers were working. Before Controller could advise the vehicles, a Sweeper calls the Tower to alert him of an aircraft on the runway.
summary: An air traffic controller directed Aircraft X to cross Runway 27 after the pilot missed a taxi turn, while three sweeping vehicles were present. One vehicle entered the grass to avoid the aircraft, which was taxiing at approximately 50 mph, prompting a recommendation to simplify vehicle call signs during runway operations.

synopsis: F11 Controller reports of an automation problem with aircraft tagging up on the wrong scopes, even after clearance delivery modified both aircraft to the correct tab list.
summary: Air traffic controllers at MCO reported that two low-level aircraft incorrectly tagged up on the high sector 'E' scope instead of the low sector 'D' scope. Despite manual corrections by clearance delivery, the automation failure persisted, which the reporter identifies as a long-standing issue requiring a system fix.

synopsis: ATL Local Controller has a clearance problem with a foreign carrier and when the aircraft departs it drifts off the RNAV course into another Local's airspace.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller issued an RNAV takeoff clearance to Aircraft X, which subsequently drifted off course due to wind and language barriers. The controller corrected the deviation with an immediate left turn and a 230-degree heading, concluding that issuing headings instead of RNAV procedures is safer for foreign pilots.

synopsis: ZLA Controller reports of high altitude balloons in which the sectors didn't have any information on. Traffic Management Unit said they knew about them the night before and should have paperwork in the area.
summary: An air traffic controller discovered three unidentified high-altitude codes (FL520-590) later confirmed as balloons, despite missing paperwork and lack of prior notification from the area. The controller alerted adjacent sectors ZDV and ZLC, highlighting the collision risk with high-altitude Global Hawks in the shared airspace.

synopsis: B777 flight crew on visual approach to Runway 28L at SFO experiences a TCAS RA with a B757 on approach to Runway 28R. The B757 had drifted slightly left of course and was slightly high and initiated a go around at the same time the B777 crew received their RA.
summary: Two flight crews on a Boeing 757 and another aircraft vectored for visual approaches to SFO Runways 28L and 28R experienced a lateral closure as the B757 slowed and drifted left. The B757 initiated a go-around, triggering a TCAS descent RA for the reporting crew, who complied and landed safely without further avoidance maneuvers.

synopsis: A Dispatcher reports an A319 under his control encountering severe turbulence descending out of FL320 near IRW.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence and downdrafts at FL250 near IRW while descending from FL320 to escape moderate turbulence. This triggered a TCAS RA requiring further descent, but the aircraft landed safely with no injuries.

synopsis: An EMB-145 flight crew and one of the C90 Controllers involved describe a misunderstanding between the crew and C90 resulting in vectors for a second approach. After initially being cleared for the visual to Runway 27R the EMB145 crew accepts a clearance meant for another aircraft to land Runway 27L and moves over.
summary: The flight crew misunderstood an ATC offer for runway 27L, intended for another aircraft, and initiated a sidestep without using their call sign. The controller vectored them away from the wrong runway and back to 27R, resulting in a safe landing despite the communication error.

synopsis: An EMB190 flight crew and the Flight Attendant involved, describe the circumstances surrounding an unintentional slide deployment.
summary: Flight attendants and the captain attempted to open the L1 door after arrival, encountering resistance and conflicting indications before Maintenance Control directed a second opening that deployed the slide. The crew attributed the issue to unclear girt bar indications in low light and a malfunctioning door assist mechanism.

synopsis: CE680 Captain reports starting engines with the left fuel boost pump on and the crossfeed open to alleviate a fuel imbalance. This results in an amber CAS messages showing low fuel pressure (R) and Fuel Boost pump ON (R) and the messages cannot be cleared. Maintenance determines that nothing is wrong and that the crew was using an inappropriate procedure.
summary: Pilots reported abnormal fuel pressure CAS messages during engine start on a Cessna 680 while cross-feeding fuel to correct an imbalance. Maintenance and Cessna dismissed the indications as normal and attributed them to an unapproved procedure, despite the crew's concern that this response lacked proper investigation.

synopsis: An ERJ-175 First Officer was concerned after the fact that he and Captain, both as low time pilots, had been paired together.
summary: A pilot reported a potential green-on-green situation involving two inexperienced crew members during daily flight operations. The pilot requested increased company oversight for green crew, noting the issue was not immediately apparent while focused on safe flight execution.

synopsis: EMB-120 First Officer experiences a runway excursion during taxi due to icy conditions. The slide is eventually stopped by the snow berm at the edge of the runway.
summary: During a slow taxi out on a snow-covered taxiway, the flight crew lost directional control while turning toward the departure runway. Despite applying reverse thrust, the aircraft slid into an adjacent runway's snowbank and stopped at a 45-degree angle with the left main gear contacting the bank.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: GSO Controller reports of a loss of separation with an arrival and a departure aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a potential loss of separation between a visual approach and an IFR departure at INT, resulting in an estimated 2-mile and 600-foot proximity. The controller attributed the incident to INT Tower applying visual separation without notifying the departure controller, despite issuing traffic advisories.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Miami Center (ZMA) Controller reports of having to spin an aircraft because the Jacksonville Center (ZJX) Controller would not take the handoff. When the aircraft was in its turn, the ZJX Controller took the handoff. The ZMA Controller reports this type of thing happens often.
summary: A pilot reported that while Aircraft X was level at FL410 approaching the Jacksonville Center Knemo sector boundary, the controller failed to answer three handoff calls. The pilot initiated a turn to heading 120 to avoid an airspace violation before the controller finally accepted the handoff, citing a dangerous pattern of delayed responses.

synopsis: A Northern California TRACON (NCT) Controller reports of an aircraft on a new Optimization of Airspace & Procedures (OAPM) route that is supposed to descend to 11,000 feet, but the aircraft ends up descending lower than that. The Controller also reports about confusion of the names on the arrivals in which the east is on the west and the west is on the east.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managed Aircraft X on the Bodega One Arrival to SFO, which descended below its assigned 11,000 feet to 9,400 feet. The controller issued a descent to 8,000 feet to stop further descent, attributing the error to confusion over new OAPM routes and procedures.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: RVS Tower controller reports of an aircraft that just departed having to return to the airport. The Front Line Manager answers the phone line and coordinates with departure control and coordinates things that aren't common. The controller then gets confused as what to do with his next departure and the returning aircraft.
summary: During a staffing shortage, the FLM approved Aircraft Y's return and directed Aircraft X to a 300 heading, contradicting the 270 release. This caused confusion and a traffic conflict, which the reporter attributes to the FLM approving non-routine actions without full situational awareness.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: VNY local controller working three locals combined describes a situation where he isn't sure what to do and asks for help but doesn't receive a timely answer. Aircraft in the pattern flies underneath a VIP aircraft which leads the TRACON call to complain about the operation.
summary: An overwhelmed Air Traffic Controller working combined positions at VNY allowed a Bonanza or Baron to pass under Aircraft Y at 2,300 feet MSL while descending to 3,700 feet MSL. The controller attributed the conflict to excessive workload from frequency overlap and lack of staffing, recommending the recombination of Ground Control and Helicopter positions.

synopsis: GGG Tower Controller reports of having a procedural error due to an opposite direction arrival being less than 10 miles from the airport, [9.5] while another aircraft was approaching the other runway. Aircraft were never closer than 12 miles from each other according to the reporter.
summary: Pilots reported that Aircraft X on ILS 13 and Aircraft Y on RNAV 31 missed the ODO cutoff point by 0.5 miles while remaining 12 miles apart. The reporter recommends moving ODO cutoff points closer to the airport to address this separation issue.

synopsis: A B-737 Flight Crew and a Check Airman describe a TCAS TA event during which the crew took evasive action. ATC had pointed out the climbing traffic, but had not indicated there would be any conflict.
summary: During a line check descent into SAN, the crew received non-standard vectors and a late descent clearance, leading to a conflict with climbing traffic. The crew stopped descent and climbed to FL240 after a TCAS TA and ATC traffic call, resolving the incident without further issues.

synopsis: B-737 flight crew reports a late turn at TERPZ during the TERPZ4 departure after being instructed by ATC to expedite climb through FL180. The First Officer surmised that the heading mode was inadvertently selected while making inputs on the MCP to comply with the ATC clearance.
summary: During climbout on the TERPZ departure, the crew missed the turn at TERPZ after the Pilot Flying inadvertently selected HDG mode while complying with an expedite climb instruction. The aircraft drifted 1.5 to 2 NM west of course until Air Traffic Control issued a heading correction, after which the crew re-engaged LNAV and continued uneventfully.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reports a track deviation flying the new TERPZ4 departure from Runway 15R at BWI. The TERPZ3 had required runway heading after takeoff while the TERPZ4 requires a turn direct PIRCH. ATC issues a reminder.
summary: Pilots of a -300 aircraft deviated from the new TERPZ4 departure by continuing on runway heading instead of turning to PIRCH at 667 feet MSL. Tower controllers reminded the crew at 1,200 feet AGL, prompting a corrective turn; the error resulted from assuming the procedure remained a heading-based departure.

synopsis: B737-300 First Officer performed a slow speed Rejected Takeoff (RTO) after the Takeoff Configuration Warning Horn sounded. After the Captain 'jiggled' the flap handle and speedbrake lever, Configuration Warning did not sound on the second takeoff.
summary: During a rolling takeoff attempt, the pilot advanced thrust levers, triggering an erroneous Takeoff Warning horn twice. After the Captain jiggled the flap and speedbrake handles to clear the fault, the warning check passed, and a normal takeoff was completed.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A flight crew flying a less automated aircraft than they were accustomed to and somewhat overloaded, took another aircraft's clearance which resulted in a TCAS alert along with a call to ATC.
summary: Pilots of an older aircraft received a TCAS alert after mistakenly accepting a climb clearance and frequency change intended for another aircraft during departure. The error occurred because the Departure Controller issued both instructions in a single transmission, violating standard procedures.

synopsis: B777 flight crew receives an EICAS status message during push back indicating the C2 Demand Hyd-pump had failed, and returns to the gate. The pump is deferred using the wrong MEL, which the crew detects, requiring a great deal of extra time and effort on the part of maintenance and eventually resulting in flight cancellation due to crew fatigue.
summary: The flight crew refused to accept a Boeing 777 for a 10-hour flight due to repeated incorrect MEL applications for a hydraulic pump failure and pressure to extend duty time. The aircraft was eventually grounded because the crew was too fatigued to safely operate the plane after extensive troubleshooting delays and conflicting maintenance information.

synopsis: B737 flight crew and ATC clearance confusion associated with the West transition versus the WESLA fix on the East transition of the SFO SERFR1 STAR.
summary: The flight crew descended via the SERFR1 STAR after ATC confirmed the WESLA transition, but a subsequent controller cleared them direct MENLO for Runway 28L. The crew realized ATC intended a west landing approach, not the WESLA transition.

synopsis: B-737 flight crew and ATC confusion regarding 'West' and 'WESLA' transition terminology on the SFO SERFR1 STAR results in a heading deviation.
summary: The flight crew, cleared for the SERFR 1 STAR 'West' transition, mistakenly selected the 'Wesla' transition after ATC confirmed a previous aircraft's routing. The crew corrected the error by returning to the 'West' transition for an uneventful ILS approach to Runway 28L.

synopsis: B-747 flight crew reports accepting an aircraft just out of heavy maintenance for a revenue flight. Many cockpit switches are found out of position during preflight, but the flight is uneventful until landing. During rollout at approximately 80 knots multiple EICAS messages appeared as well as aural warnings. The crew is able to taxi in, but the engines do not shut down normally and Maintenance Control indicates there are 50 plus status messages that the crew never saw.
summary: The flight crew experienced multiple EICAS messages and abnormal engine shutdowns upon landing after an otherwise normal flight. Maintenance attributed the issue to over 50 pre-existing status messages and incorrect switch positions left after heavy maintenance, which were not communicated to the crew.

synopsis: A-321 flight crew is informed by an FAA examiner that their iPad electronic table of contents is out of date and must be updated prior to gate departure. This is accomplished using iPhone personnel hotspots at the examiners direction.
summary: An FAA examiner found the pilot's iPad Table of Contents out of date during a line check. The pilot used a personal cell phone hotspot to update the iPad in the cockpit, and the flight departed on schedule.

aircraft: Medium Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Twin turboprop Captain reports arriving over VASHN expecting a clearance for the RNAV Z to 16R at SEA, but instead receives vectors to the final approach course. A 130 heading to intercept is issued and the RNAV glideslope appears below the aircraft so the descent is continued until breaking out at 3,000 Feet about four miles from FINKA. The descent is arrested at the same time ATC issues a low altitude alert and the EGPWS alerts with a 'Caution, Obstacle.' The approach is continued to a normal landing.
summary: Pilots flying into Seattle loaded the RNAV Z approach via VASHN but descended below the glide path due to an erroneous indication caused by missing final approach waypoints. This resulted in an altitude alert and obstacle caution before the glide path corrected and the crew completed a visual approach.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot reports of a VIP passenger who refuses to sit in a seat and remains lying in the bed. Captain and assistant discuss matter. Pilot reluctantly decides to let passenger remain laying down to avoid a company problem.
summary: During the descent below 9,000 feet, a high-profile passenger refused to leave his berth for landing despite crew instructions regarding turbulence and safety regulations. The flight crew decided to land without forcing compliance due to the sterile cockpit environment, the passenger's volatile history, and company concerns about confronting the owner.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Corporate Captain reported taking evasive action from a VFR Small Transport, High Wing, 2 Turboprop Engine near 15,500 Feet while descending on the QUABN3 arrival to BOS at night after ATC allowed the aircraft to remain in the arrival corridor.
summary: During an IFR descent on the QUABN3 arrival, a VFR research aircraft at 15,500 feet turned toward the crew's aircraft at 17,000 feet, triggering a TCAS climb resolution advisory. The crew climbed to FL180 to avoid a 300-foot vertical separation conflict, resulting in a missed altitude restriction before landing uneventfully.

synopsis: B747-400 First Officer reported they departed with incorrect cargo weight information, resulting in a much heavier gross weight than planned for. They returned to departure airport.
summary: The crew returned to the origin airport after the air carrier discovered an incorrect cargo weight calculation by their operator. To comply with landing weight limits, the crew dumped fuel to 60,000 lbs, resulting in a safe landing and taxi.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reports of being cleared for takeoff, then having it cancelled by ATC who tells him that they weren't cleared for takeoff.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff on Runway 24 after Tower instructed "Hold on," despite having received a takeoff clearance. The controller later claimed no clearance was given, attributing the confusion to four aircraft staged in the run-up area.

synopsis: C550 flight crew describes an ILS approach to minimums, then landing apparently with the autopilot/yaw damper engaged. During the flare an abrupt right turn occurs which the pilot flying corrects back to the center line. Post flight reveals a hole in the left flap behind the landing gear.
summary: During an ILS approach to CID in deteriorating weather, the aircraft made an abrupt right turn at flare because the autopilot and yaw damper remained engaged despite the pilot's disconnect attempt. The pilot recovered control, but the extended flaps struck a runway light, causing a hole in the flap trailing edge.

synopsis: A C172 Instructor Pilot experiences a loss of throttle control with the engine at 1,800 RPM. An emergency landing is successfully planned and executed.
summary: The pilot reported a throttle cable detachment due to a missing cotter pin, causing engine RPM to stick at 1800. An emergency landing was safely executed at a private airport after troubleshooting failed, with no injuries and the aircraft later repaired.

synopsis: A C150 pilot reports completing a currency check with his flight club after 6 months away from flying. After the instructor is dropped off, the flight continues with several more touch and goes. The pilot then makes a flight to BFI. During the visual approach the reporter is distracted by traffic for the parallel runway and the aircraft is allowed to get very close to terrain.
summary: A pilot returning after six months of inactivity descended too steeply while fixated on parallel traffic during a base leg at a valley airport. The pilot flew close to trees and houses before recovering above the glideslope, attributing the incident to degraded scanning skills and premature descent.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: An LAX Tower Controller reports of a stuck microphone on the Ground Control frequency and not having the ability to use a direction finder to track down the stuck microphone.
summary: Air traffic controllers reported a stuck microphone on Ground Control 1 (121.75) for 1.5 hours at LAX, causing multiple close calls and one go-around. The incident occurred because no personnel or equipment were available to locate the fault, highlighting a need for assigned responsibility.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A Dallas Fort Worth (D10) Controller reports of an aircraft being cleared for an approach that they later find out was out of service. The facility was not aware that the approach was not working correctly.
summary: Air traffic controllers cleared Aircraft X for an ILS runway 31 approach at RBD during training, unaware the approach was out of service. The controller reported that the outage was missing from their IDS5 display and briefings, prompting a call for improved management vigilance regarding NOTAMs and equipment outages.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: A Seattle Center (ZSE) Controller reports of confusion about the procedure for a missed approach off of RDM airport with an aircraft arriving on the opposite direction arrival.
summary: An approach controller and RDM tower managed Aircraft X and Y during a runway change and missed approach, resulting in a Conflict Alert. The reporter attributed the alert to vectors below Minimum IFR Altitude caused by the tower failing to issue the required SID for the visual approach.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A Montgomery (MGM) Approach Controller describes advising an aircraft that the runway direction is changing, and an arresting cable needs to be lowered. The pilot elects to land over the cable after being given a few options by the Controller. The aircraft is switched to Tower and lands impacting the cable and damaging the aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller advised a pilot on a GPS approach to Runway 10 about a raised cable and offered options including landing over it. The pilot landed over the cable, cracking wheel covers, though the report concludes the aircraft should have been resequenced to hold until the cable was removed.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Northern California TRACON (NCT) Controller working the mid shift reports that he didn't catch errors that he normally would have. The Controller reports he didn't catch a bad read back from a pilot and didn't remember that a runway was closed. The Controller reports that he was tired and having difficulty focusing.
summary: An Area E controller, fatigued during a mid-shift handoff, issued a direct routing to Aircraft X for an ILS 28R approach while missing a runway closure in the ATIS. The controller attributed the error to exhaustion, habit-based decision-making, and overlooking small red text in the outage box.

synopsis: A Miami Center (ZMA) Controller reports of a loss of separation with two aircraft after he handed them off and transferred communications to another sector. Someone had removed the assigned speeds from the data block indicating normal speed had been given, resulting in a loss and an aircraft was climbed through the others altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller in sector R64 reported a loss of separation between two departing aircraft after their assigned speeds were removed from the system data block. The controller attributed the incident to understaffing, which prevented adequate sector coverage and traffic flow management during high-volume operations with active military airspace.

synopsis: A Phoenix TRACON (P50) Controller reports the information that they have for reference aircraft flying in and out of the airspace for a car race is useless because it tells them nothing. No altitudes, no route of flight, times, etc., were given.
summary: Air traffic controllers reported that special race aircraft privileges were issued via faxes lacking specific altitudes, routes, durations, or aircraft types. This absence of original requests and approvals prevents proper coordination, unlike previous practices where details were posted on ADATS.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Fort Myers (RSW) Approach Controller reports of an aircraft going to land at one airport, but instead lands at another airport. This happens under the Approach Controller's jurisdiction.
summary: A radar approach controller cleared Aircraft X for a visual approach to FMY after the pilot reported the airport in sight. The pilot subsequently landed on RSW runway 24 without clearance, an error the controller attributed to the pilot's incorrect airport identification.

synopsis: MHT FLM reports of receiving a clearance on an aircraft and while not busy, he full routes it. He didn't notice before he did the full route, that in the remarks section is did say FRC. FRC was hidden by the pilots' phone number. FLM is concerned that an inexperienced controller would have missed the FRC.
summary: A tower controller working alone discovered that an FRC remark for Aircraft X was truncated and hidden by a phone number in block 9 of the departure strip. The controller identified the full route clearance only after manually printing the route, noting that less experienced staff might miss such critical information.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: A Southern California TRACON (SCT) BUR area Front Line Manager (FLM) reports of a conflict and states that it has to do with distractions in the area. Controllers are not paying attention to what is going on in the area and by chance the FLM heard an odd heading, checked it out, and prevented a loss of separation between the two aircraft.
summary: A Front Line Manager observed a VNY jet cleared on an unusual heading 160 intersecting a BUR departure on heading 210, requiring a climbing right turn to avoid collision. The controller admitted to turning away from the scope due to distractions and failing to use flight strips for the converging traffic.

synopsis: D10 arrival and departure Controllers plus pilot of Aircraft X report on a loss of separation due to the clearance delivery person issuing the incorrect altitude for initial climbout.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a near-miss between departing Aircraft X and arriving Aircraft Y and Z at DFW caused by a tower clearance for 16,000 feet instead of the required 10,000. The controller issued a traffic alert after Aircraft X climbed rapidly, resulting in a 300-foot vertical separation from Aircraft Y and a resolution advisory for Aircraft Z.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain describes a test of wills with the Gate Agent and the deice crew to get his aircraft properly deiced at the gate.
summary: The Captain and First Officer could not verify the aircraft was clean of frost after initial gate deicing at PHL, despite repeated requests for re-inspection. The aircraft was eventually towed to the deice pad where the crew confirmed frost remained and performed a second deicing.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Medium passenger jet flight crew, with the First Officer on IOE, reports an unstabilized visual approach that results in a go-around. On the second visual approach the aircraft is configured early and allowed to get low resulting in a low altitude alert from the Tower. The approach is continued to a normal landing.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring and First Officer (IOE) flying a visual approach to DAL 31L executed a go-around due to being high and fast, then received a low altitude alert at 1,400 feet MSL on the second attempt. The crew attributed the instability to a 13-knot tailwind and the Pilot Monitoring's distraction, but corrected the path and landed safely.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A flight crew flying the MDW RNAV (RNP) RWY 13C were previously cleared to 3,000 feet on the FISSK 3 RNAV Arrival which put them below the mandatory 4,000 feet at OOPLA on the approach.
summary: The crew arrived at Chicago Midway via FISSK 3 and was vectored below the 4,000-foot mandatory altitude at OOPLA. ATC later questioned the clearance, but the crew declined to climb in VMC and completed an uneventful landing.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain is dispatched on a transpacific flight with the APU deferred, which it had been for four days. Upon arrival at the gate, ground power is connected and the engines are shut down. Ground power quickly fails and cannot be reestablished leaving the aircraft on battery power alone. After five minutes the battery is turned off leaving the aircraft in darkness.
summary: The crew flew an Aircraft X transoceanic flight with an inoperative APU, relying on MEL allowances. Upon arrival, external power failed, forcing the crew to shut down all battery power to prevent dangerous discharge while passengers disembarked.

synopsis: A300 flight crew departing ATL on the CADIT9 Departure and approaching RONII, is admonished by ATC for an early shallow banked turn to BEDRK. Vectors are issued and the crew explains that the FMC was following its programing, although the early turns normally occur only at higher altitudes and airspeeds.
summary: During departure from Atlanta on the CADIT9 RNAV procedure, pilots deleted a 250-knot speed restriction at RBEKA, causing the FMC to initiate an early turn to BEDRK. The controller vectored the aircraft and cleared it direct to CADIT, attributing the deviation to the FMC anticipating acceleration despite the aircraft maintaining 250 knots.

synopsis: A B757-200 EICAS alerted FWD WINDOW with two cracks, then shortly a loud noise accompanying a shattered Captain's window. The QRH was completed, the flight diverted to a nearby airport and landed in emergency condition.
summary: During cruise at FL370, the Captain's forward windshield cracked and shattered, prompting a QRH-directed overweight landing at the nearest suitable airport. The First Officer executed a normal landing, and the emergency was terminated after taxiing to the gate, though communication with local operations was difficult.

synopsis: CRJ200 Captain reports a near collision with a high speed pickup truck while attempting to park at the gate using the DGS. A quick by the Captain avoids the collision.
summary: During gate lining using the DGS, a white pickup truck accelerated rapidly from the aircraft's right, forcing the flight crew to slam brakes to avoid a collision. Passengers were alarmed, but the aircraft parked safely after the crew reported the unsafe driving to Ramp Control and the Chief Pilot.

aircraft: Embraer Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An Embraer Captain experiences a strange vibration climbing out of 9,000 feet and levels at 10,000 feet. Previous experience indicates that the lavatory service port cap may be loose. The Captain elects to return to the departure airport where the suspicion is proved correct.
summary: The flight crew diverted after a harmonic vibration during climb, caused by a loose lavatory service port cap that popped due to pressure differential. The cap was found dangling post-landing with no aircraft damage, prompting a recommendation for design changes and better pilot awareness.

synopsis: CL300 flight crew reports an altitude deviation over ARCHI during the Quiet Bridge Visual approach into SFO. The MCP was properly programed but the autopilot captured late and was quickly corrected by the pilot flying.
summary: During a Challenger 300 descent into SFO for a Quiet Bridge Visual approach, the autopilot failed to capture the cleared 8,000-foot crossing altitude at ARCHI. The pilot promptly disconnected the autopilot and pitched up, limiting the deviation to 7,800 feet for less than 10 seconds.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier crew departed and struck a bird flock between 5,000 feet and 6,000 feet. Because of engine and airframe vibration the crew returned to departure airport where damage was found to the radome, #2 engine fan blades, the right wing and winglet.
summary: The crew experienced multiple bird strikes on the right side during departure between 5,000 and 6,000 feet, causing vibration but normal engine parameters. They returned for an overweight landing; maintenance later found a radome hole, fan blade damage, and wing impacts, with #2 engine vibration noted during taxi.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reports attempting to extend flaps to 1 at 22,000 feet to maintain 200 knots per ATC request. An ECAM warning is immediately annunciated and the flap handle is pushed forward before any flap movement occurs.
summary: During descent into EGE, the crew attempted to extend flaps at FL220 to mitigate speed restrictions, triggering a brief ECAM warning due to exceeding the flap extension altitude limit. Maintenance confirmed no inspection was required as the handle was reset before actual flap movement occurred.

synopsis: An MD-11 alerted TNK3 FUEL QTY LO level 1 which resulted in a trapped fuel alert. Following manual fuel transfers in the descent for landing, the system returned to normal with all fuel usable.
summary: During cruise, the flight crew managed a 'TANK3 FUEL QTY LO' alert by manually transferring fuel, which triggered a 'TNK3 TIP TRAPPED' alert leaving 5100 pounds trapped. The trapped fuel unstuck at 13,000 feet, allowing an uneventful landing with CFR vehicles following to the gate.

synopsis: An A320 Captain noted that as station operations are outsourced, adherence to ramp SOP is lacking. At this Station, the pushback verbiage and hand signal were not employed.
summary: During pushback, ground personnel failed to follow SOPs, omitting the required 45-degree hand signal and using an incorrect gesture instead. The pilot could not reach Operations via radio to request a qualified marshaller, citing a safety risk due to inadequate training at the outsourced station.

synopsis: After the fact, a B757 First Officer was made aware that he and Captain taxied with a ground crewmen head set still attached to the aircraft. Neither pilot saw the person.
summary: The flight crew taxied the aircraft after visually clearing the area and receiving ground control clearance, unaware that ground personnel had not disconnected the tow bar. This communication breakdown resulted in an unsafe situation where the aircraft moved with the ground crew still attached, though no injuries occurred.

synopsis: Just prior to departure, SFO changed the departure Runway to 28R so the crew reloaded the new FMS data and GNNRR 1 RNAV routing except for STINS. During climb, ZOA detected the error.
summary: The flight crew departed SFO on runway 28R after a last-minute change from 28L, inadvertently deleting the STINS waypoint from the FMC due to a rushed discontinuity closure. ATC subsequently vectored the aircraft direct to REDWD after questioning the crew's position on the GNNRR1 departure.

synopsis: A Captain reports about a CRJ-700 aircraft with a history of discrepancies involving Anti-Skid System faults and the aircraft veering to the right during braking on landing roll that were misdiagnosed until the Asymmetry/Loss of Braking Immediate Action/QRH items were addressed in a Logbook write-up. Maintenance then found the left MLG inboard Anti-Skid Transducer had been binding resulting in a false-locked wheel signal to the Anti-Skid Control Unit (ASCU).
summary: A CRJ-700 pilot reported that a binding left inboard anti-skid transducer caused false locked wheel signals, disabling that brake and creating asymmetric braking during landing. This resulted in the aircraft veering right, a condition the pilot attributes to misdiagnosed logbook entries and inadequate maintenance procedures.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot and co-pilot report of confusion on departure of flying the RNAV departure or flying to a fix. ATC corrects them and advises that they aren't the first ones to do that.
summary: The crew misunderstood a Miami clearance for the Hedly 1 departure, flying the RNAV route to Senoy instead of radar vectors. ATC corrected the error after takeoff, noting this is a known issue with how the departure is verbalized.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 GEN 2 Master Caution alerted so the Captain, with the QRH, began the Reset procedure but turned GEN 1 OFF. GEN 1 was quickly re-establish now with the ADG deployed. Both generators were eventually re-established.
summary: During arrival at IAD, the Pilot Monitoring accidentally switched off Generator 1 while troubleshooting a Generator 2 fault, causing the ADG to deploy. Power was restored after the error was recognized, and the crew recommended QRH checklist improvements to include explicit confirmation steps for guarded switches.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Recip Eng
synopsis: A light twin commercial carrier pilot approaching SJU reported a near miss at about 2,000 feet after descending in response to an ATC alert about approaching an approaching aircraft.
summary: A pilot flying to San Juan at 2,000 feet received two ATC advisories for traffic at 2,100 feet and descended 50–100 feet. An Aero Commander subsequently passed 100 feet directly above the aircraft in the opposite direction.

synopsis: G150 Captain reports having to brake hard to avoid a high speed fire truck that cuts in front of his aircraft without warning. The fire truck, with lights flashing makes a 360 in front of the G150 then departs and was apparently not responding to an emergency.
summary: A Part 91 pilot landing at IAH after dark braked hard to avoid a lone fire truck that cut across the taxiway without ATC warning. The truck performed a 360-degree turn and departed, marking the pilot's second such incident involving high-speed, uncoordinated fire trucks at the airport.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reports forgetting to configure their aircraft prior to attempting takeoff, due to distractions and fatigue. The takeoff warning horn sounds and the takeoff is rejected.
summary: Fatigued flight crew on the 13th night leg at LAS aborted a takeoff from Runway 01R after auto-throttles failed to advance due to an unconfigured aircraft. The error resulted from routine disruption caused by a runway change and fatigue, leading to a missed configuration call despite completing the below-the-line checklist.

synopsis: A CRJ-900 air crew, after starting one engine and shutting down the APU observed an APU SOV OPEN status message. The message remained on after starting the second engine but they elected to continue and flew one flight. At their destination the Captain troubleshot the aircraft and was convinced that the APU PWR/Fuel switch was inoperative. Maintenance disagreed. The crew swapped into another aircraft for the flight.
summary: The Captain reported that on a CRJ900, the APU PWR/fuel switch failed to de-energize the APU, causing a persistent "APU SOV OPEN" message despite the valve functioning. After maintenance control insisted the MEL was correct and refused to dispatch mechanics, the Captain deferred the aircraft and swapped to another for the flight.

synopsis: Pilot is cleared for takeoff and is approaching V1 when he hears Tower clear another aircraft for takeoff on the same runway. Pilot wonders what would happen if his aircraft had to abort, and also wonders what type of separation is required by ATC to have two aircraft on the same runway.
summary: The pilot reported that while still on the runway below V1 during a night takeoff from ORD runway 28R, the tower controller cleared the following aircraft to takeoff. The pilot considered this clearance too soon, noting that a required abort could have resulted in a runway collision or debris ingestion by the second aircraft.

synopsis: A321 Captain climbing through 10,000 feet, experiences a TCAS TA and queries ATC about traffic at 11,500 feet. ATC replies that there is traffic at 11,500 feet as the TCAS changes to a descending RA.
summary: The Captain flying a CLT departure received a TCAS Resolution Advisory for VFR traffic at 11,500 feet while climbing to 23,000 feet. The pilot descended to avoid the conflict after ATC failed to provide separation from the VFR aircraft communicating with Charlotte Approach.

synopsis: A320 flight crew describes the problems departing TNCM due to late paperwork, procedure changes and no ACARS. The flight departs over an hour late and does not use the runway planned by Dispatch and shown on the weight and balance.
summary: The flight crew at TNCM experienced significant delays due to ACARS failure and late paperwork, leading to a departure on Runway 10 using performance data calculated for Runway 28. Dispatch later confirmed the aircraft was overweight for the actual runway, though the crew was never instructed to return to the ramp.

synopsis: Pilot reports of flying below the Class Bravo while in a descent into SFO on the SERFR1 STAR. Pilot advises there may be something wrong with the arrival that takes the aircraft out of the Class Bravo which is built to protect the aircraft.
summary: The flight crew descended below SFO Class B airspace while flying the SERFR 1 RNAV arrival in VNAV mode. The pilot attributed the breach to a flawed procedure design that allows descent below Class B while complying with restrictions and recommended discontinuing the arrival until adjusted.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain believes that the RAAS is a hazard to safe flying.
summary: During landing rollout at BUR on runway 08, pilots could not hear Tower exit instructions because the RAAS announcement masked the clearance. The crew attributed this critical communication loss to the RAAS, which they described as a pointless safety hazard.

synopsis: CE-750 flight crew experiences many heading assignments and speed changes arrival into ASE. Eventually, with the field in sight, the crew is 'cleared direct the field for the visual approach'. The words 'cleared for the approach' were not issued but the crew assumed they were and begins descent. The error is pointed out and the visual approach clearance is issued.
summary: Pilots descended below 16,000 feet into ASE after misinterpreting "cleared direct to the field" as a visual approach clearance due to high ATC traffic volume. The crew acknowledged the pilot deviation resulted from failing to verify the instruction amidst rapid speed and heading changes.

synopsis: A small aircraft pilot towing a banner had a near miss with a parasail. His evasive actions prevented a collision. He suggests that parasail operators need more training and that parasail operations should be regulated.
summary: A banner towing pilot flying southbound along the Santa Monica shoreline turned left and climbed over the pier to avoid a parasail approaching from offshore. The pilot attributed the conflict to the parasail boat driver heading directly for the aircraft and called for better training and regulation.

synopsis: A C-414 air crew shortly after takeoff experienced aerodynamic forces on the tail of the aircraft favoring a nose low attitude. Electric and manual trim exacerbated the condition. The pilot then ran the trim in the direction of nose down resulting in a positive rate of climb. 'The trim System was installed backwards'.
summary: The PIC and safety pilot experienced severe nose-down control forces during takeoff of Aircraft X due to a trim system installed backwards. After struggling to maintain pitch with limited elevator authority, the pilot stabilized the flight path by applying opposite trim and landed safely without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper Pawnee experienced an engine problem while towing a banner, resulting in an off-field landing in the water.
summary: A pilot conducting a banner tow circuit experienced an unexplained engine failure at 1,000 feet while attempting to maintain 1,300 feet in gusty winds. The pilot released the banner, declared an emergency, and executed a forced landing in water after losing power despite using carburetor heat and adjusting the mixture.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot is told to fly to a fix that is not on his route and flies towards the IAF. On a second approach the controller tells the pilot to go to another fix which according to the pilot does not exist. After landing the pilot's boss calls approach control and finds out they are still using expired charts.
summary: A pilot and student flying an IFR flight to HNZ encountered confusion when Raleigh Approach controllers issued vectors to non-existent fixes due to expired charts. The pilot deviated from instructions to fly to valid waypoints, completed the approaches, and later confirmed the controllers' charting error via telephone.

synopsis: PA-28 Instructor pilot on short final is surprised by a M-20 overtaking from the left and landing ahead of him. A go around is initiated. After landing it was learned that the M20 pilot had attempted to land downwind on Runway 15 then went around, performing a 90/270 to come into conflict with the reporter. The wrong CTAF was also being used by the M20 pilot.
summary: During a VFR training flight on final approach to Runway 33, a Mooney pilot entered a collision course after using the wrong CTAF frequency and ignoring the published right traffic pattern. The instructor executed a go-around and evasive turn to avoid a mid-air collision caused by the Mooney pilot's lack of pre-flight planning and situational awareness.

synopsis: SF340 flight crew experiences loss of oil pressure and the engine is shut down. The flight diverts to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The SIC reported a loss of left propeller oil pressure and a visible oil leak in cruise, prompting a QRH-guided engine shutdown to prevent catastrophic damage. The crew deviated to ZZZZ airport for a safe landing, where passengers were rebooked and the aircraft was repaired and returned to service the same day.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA32 made an off-field landing following loss of engine power. It was later determined that the fuel system was feeding from an empty fuel tank.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine failure at 2,200 MSL during cruise due to fuel starvation caused by misidentifying the fuel selector position. This resulted in a forced landing on a golf course with nose gear damage and a propeller strike, but no injuries.

synopsis: A flight instructor and his student encountered a UAV/Drone while practicing training maneuvers. They announced its presence on a local CTAF and, along with other aircraft in the practice area, departed as a precaution.
summary: A flight instructor and student encountered a red quadcopter drone at 3,500 feet while practicing maneuvers near Buckhorn Lake. The instructor reported the fast-moving drone on Unicom, prompting area aircraft to evacuate, and later filed a formal report with Raleigh Approach.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: CE-525 pilot reported making an error programming a hold in his FMS, highlighting several 'gotcha' areas that can trip up the unwary or undertrained.
summary: The pilot, flying an aircraft equipped with a Honeywell GNS/XLS FMS, inadvertently created a present position hold instead of programming a hold at the CUKBO fix while descending from 8,000 feet. This FMS input error caused the aircraft to turn 360 degrees and descend to 6,200 feet before the pilot corrected the route to the intended fix.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-28 lost control of the aircraft during landing rollout, resulting in a runway excursion and contact with a taxiway sign.
summary: The pilot reported a runway excursion during landing rollout on runway 19 where the aircraft swerved right and struck a taxiway sign. The pilot attributed the incident to unequal braking, likely caused by locked right brakes and reduced left brake leverage while holding left rudder, resulting in flap and sign damage.

synopsis: R22 student pilot inadvertently closed the throttle when raising the collective for takeoff. Instructor pilot took control and leveled the aircraft, but was unable to restore throttle. A hard landing resulted.
summary: During helicopter training, an elderly student pilot inadvertently cut throttle while raising collective, causing a low hover and hard landing. The instructor recovered the aircraft to prevent a rollover, attributing the incident to the student's repeated throttle errors and a rubberized glove hindering control override.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An MD80 Captain reported multiple flight crews requested that the ATL Runway 9L runway lights be dimmed for evening takeoffs in low ceilings and fog. The Local Controller advised they were unable to do so per the FAA. On their subsequent takeoff the reporter found the intense reflected light made it difficult to read the flight instruments.
summary: A pilot reported that during a low-visibility takeoff from Atlanta on runway 9L, new LED runway lights were so bright they hindered instrument readability. The pilot attributed this safety issue to FAA rules preventing the tower controller from dimming the lights despite repeated crew requests.

synopsis: The pilot of a Rockwell Commander experienced a nose landing gear collapse during landing rollout. The aircraft had just had the landing gear serviced.
summary: The pilot of an AC11, recently serviced on landing gear oleo struts, landed normally but experienced a nose collapse upon braking. The nose gear failed to support the aircraft, causing the propeller to strike the ground and the aircraft to slide.

synopsis: An AA5B private pilot, after landing on and exiting Runway 28R at SFO, continued beyond the hold short line of 28L. He believes the existing markings could be improved to prevent future incursions.
summary: The pilot crossed the hold short line of runway 28L while taxiing from runway 28R after landing. The reporter attributed the incident to inadequate markings, suggesting 28R should have the same color hold short marks as 28L.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cirrus SR-22 received an altitude alert for an unknown reason, which led to a missed approach. On the subsequent approach, ATC issued a second altitude alert due to the pilot's inadvertent premature descent.
summary: The pilot received two low altitude alerts during practice GPS approaches due to starting altitude step-downs one waypoint too soon and descending below circling minimums. The pilot executed missed approaches and corrections, landed safely, and scheduled refresher training with a CFII.

synopsis: A pilot performing practice instrument approach with a view limiting device was advised by his safety pilot that another aircraft was turning towards their position. The pilot removed the view limiting device and performed an evasive maneuver. It was reported that ATC had turned the aircraft towards them.
summary: During a practice ILS final approach, the pilot and safety pilot encountered a high-wing Cessna turned west by ATC directly into their path. The controller failed to inform the pilot that the previously identified traffic was being vectored against the final approach, forcing the pilot to take evasive action.

synopsis: Aviat Husky pilot reported ground looping the aircraft resulting in slight damage.
summary: The pilot ground looped a Husky with large bush wheels on tarmac, damaging the tailwheel and right wing tip due to lost directional control. The pilot attributed the incident to lack of recent experience, unfamiliar wheel handling, and a potential tailwheel failure.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Corporate flight crew became distracted when SFO issued a new SID and departure runway while taxiing at night. Thinking that Taxiway L was Runway 1R, the takeoff was begun. The Captain detected the error and rejected the takeoff.
summary: The flight crew misaligned on Taxiway L instead of Runway 1R at SFO after receiving a late reroute clearance while lining up. The pilot aborted the takeoff roll below 40 knots, attributed to the simultaneous clearance and reroute causing loss of orientation.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot and instructor were confused by the updated clearance provided by ATC that appeared to direct them towards rising terrain. Before the crew could question the clearance, ATC provided an low altitude alert along with notice of a possible pilot deviation.
summary: Pilots climbing via the North Town Three Departure received an ambiguous "fly straight out" clearance from Las Vegas Departure at 3,800 feet, causing them to continue westerly toward terrain. This confusion triggered a low altitude alert, prompting ATC to issue a right turn and initiate a deviation report.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cirrus SR22 on final approach was surprised to hear ATC clear another aircraft for takeoff. When questioned, ATC requested that the aircraft on approach go-around or perform a 360 degree turn.
summary: A pilot on short final was cleared for takeoff by the tower while another aircraft began its roll, forcing the pilot to execute a 360-degree turn at 200–300 feet AGL with full flaps. The maneuver resulted in a near-stall situation just above tree tops, with no apology received from the controller.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: General Aviation pilot reports being confused by the description of an aerobatic box adjacent to the SEF airport and believes that it does not come close to describing the actual location and size of the box. During the confusion the pattern direction specifically prohibited by the AWOS message is used for approach and landing. No conflict develops.
summary: A pilot inbound to Sebring Regional Airport entered a left downwind for Runway 14 due to confusion over an ambiguous AWOS description of the aerobatic practice area. Although no conflict occurred, the pilot attributed the error to unclear verbal instructions and recommended FAA-approved announcement scripts to prevent future misunderstandings.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: RSW controller reports of an aircraft that is having alternator problems, but didn't want to declare an emergency. ATC tried to hand off the aircraft to ZMA but they didn't want the aircraft because they were too busy. Controller complains that ZMA should have taken the aircraft. Aircraft continued on its way.
summary: Aircraft X reported an alternator problem to EST radar but refused a handoff to ZMA LAL HI, claiming controllers were too busy. The pilot declined advice to land, continued north, and exited radar coverage without declaring an emergency.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: ZLC Controller reports of an aircraft under ATC control that is not at the required altitude and the Controller advises and issues altimeter. Aircraft cannot hold altitude and is off and on radar contact. Pilot reports of icing and Controller gets the aircraft turned toward airport for a visual, but pilot reports the might not be able to maintain the airport insight. Controller then clears aircraft for a VOR approach.
summary: An air traffic controller observed a general aviation pilot on V611 to LWT flying below assigned altitude due to icing and lack of DME. Despite multiple altitude corrections and approach clearances, the underpowered aircraft maintained 6,000 feet before landing safely.

synopsis: DAL Tower controller reports of an airspace violation by a D10 controller. The D10 controller then has his aircraft become a conflict for the DAL controller's aircraft. The D10 controller wanted his aircraft to be able to do a downtown tour, but due to the runway configuration at DAL it was not approved.
summary: A D10 Approach controller ignored Local Control's refusal to accept Aircraft X for a downtown tour, causing a conflict with Aircraft Y at 1,500 feet. The D10 controller eventually maneuvered Aircraft X to avoid the conflict after disregarding multiple coordination requests and violating airspace procedures.

synopsis: A B737-700 flight crew reported they took off with flaps set incorrectly after a late change to departure runway.
summary: The Captain and a new First Officer took off with flaps set to position 1 instead of the required position 5 due to rushing after last-minute changes and failing to rerun the Before Taxi Checklist. The error was discovered during the takeoff roll call, though the speed difference was minimal and the stopping margin reduced by only 100 feet.

synopsis: A B737-700 flight crew reported they had difficulty contacting ATL Approach on a STAR arrival, citing frequency congestion and controller workload as contributing.
summary: During descent on the KOLTT 2 to ATL, the crew received a climb RA after failing to contact Approach due to blocked transmissions. The crew complied with the RA, switched radios, and eventually established contact, landing uneventfully despite the controller's claim of prior attempts.

synopsis: B767 First Officer reported he was unable to update his company iPad and suggested a change in the software involved.
summary: A pilot reported that the company iPad software failed to download or open the OM Volume I for the 757/767, displaying a gray screen even after multiple attempts and on a personal device. The pilot attributed the issue to buggy software and warned that this prevents access to critical manuals during flight.

synopsis: An A319 Captain reported he failed to properly brief applicable approach restrictions due to ships in the harbor on an approach to BOS runway 4R.
summary: The pilot executed a Category 1 ILS approach to Boston Runway 4R in deteriorating weather, disregarding tower advisories about a 148-foot ship. Post-flight review revealed the pilot failed to brief approach restrictions regarding harbor vessels exceeding 144 feet, mistakenly assuming the displaced threshold accounted for them.

synopsis: A330 Captain reported ground personnel at destination advised forward and aft cargo containers were not properly locked down.
summary: A baggage handler reported to the cockpit upon arrival that no cargo locking mechanisms were engaged, causing all pallets and containers to shift. The reporter attributed this incident to baggage handlers failing to perform their duties.

aircraft: Dash 8 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
