summary: The flight crew descended from FL340 to FL320 without initial ATC clearance due to garbled radios and a 40-knot airspeed loss caused by possible mountain wave activity. They regained communication at FL330 and received clearance to continue the descent after the aircraft neared stall speed despite maximum power.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain rejected takeoff at approximately 110 knots when the FO inquired if he wanted to place his hand (which was on the glareshield) back on the throttles 'for the reject.'
summary: The Captain initiated a rejected takeoff at 110 knots after mishearing the First Officer's query about hand placement as a command to reject. The crew subsequently performed maintenance checks and completed a normal takeoff.

synopsis: C560 Captain (pilot flying) reports a track deviation during the DSERT2 arrival to SDL when the pilot not flying (PNF) elects to enter the landing runway in the FMC. This creates a route discontinuity as BUSTD is about to be crossed which the PNF attempts to repair but is initially unsuccessful, resulting in a track deviation. Flying multiple aircraft/FMC types was cited as a factor in this incident.
summary: The PIC and copilot in a Citation V deviated from the DSERT2 arrival while descending to Scottsdale after the copilot entered the runway, causing the FMS to deactivate legs and turn the aircraft incorrectly. The PIC eventually hand-flew the aircraft back to the correct course using visual landmarks and received a visual approach clearance.

synopsis: CE560 flight crew reports losing NAV capability shortly after returning to the IVANE5 RNAV from deviations around weather. ATC is not advised in a timely manner and Radar vectors to a different runway are issued. The crew is asked to call Approach Control at their convenience.
summary: Pilots flying a Universal UNS1Esp-equipped aircraft on the IVANE5 arrival to CLT experienced an FMS data dump after weather deviations, causing a loss of route guidance and altitude restrictions. The crew manually navigated but delayed notifying ATC, resulting in a reported airspace violation and a "possible pilot deviation" notice before being vectored for a safe landing.

aircraft: Light Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Cargo aircraft First Officer reported descending below cleared altitude in mountainous Alaska terrain, when he fell asleep, following a very fatiguing series of flight assignments.
summary: A fatigued pilot and first officer on an IFR flight to OME descended below their cleared 7,000 ft altitude after the pilot fell asleep. The crew initiated an immediate climb to avoid a mountain ridge, attributing the incident to crew fatigue caused by long commutes, consecutive duty days, and interrupted rest.

synopsis: BE55 pilot reported nearly landing with gear up and damaging the props in the process. He pulled up a few feet, extended the gear, and landed long.
summary: The pilot, flying a Cessna 172 on visual approach to Airport ZZZ, executed two go-arounds due to traffic and a KX155 radio failure. During the second go-around, the pilot forgot to lower the landing gear, resulting in a propeller strike that curled the blade tips after a long landing on Runway 32.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: TMB Local Controller puts an aircraft into position on an active runway in between an aircraft rolling out and one on final. The Controller then notices another unknown aircraft approaching opposite direction, he tells the aircraft that is in position to exit the runway and then the arriving aircraft lands on a parallel runway. Controller did not know anything about the opposite direction arrival.
summary: An air traffic controller working local south ordered Aircraft X to exit runway 9R after noticing Aircraft Y approaching from the opposite direction. The controller attributed the incident to a lack of timely communication and coordination regarding Aircraft Y's turn toward the runway.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: BJC Controller reports of an Opposite Direction Operation that Local Controller is unaware of its close proximity and violates the facilities ODO Policy.
summary: A new Controller in Charge observed Aircraft Z enter the airspace for Runway 30R without confirmed opposite direction operation coordination while Local Control managed heavy traffic. The situation resulted in Aircraft Z circling to the ramp after a pilot alert, caused by controller overload and incomplete coordination during complex traffic conditions.

synopsis: BWI Controller and airline pilot report of a NMAC. Controller thought climb rate would be better for the air carrier based on previous departures. Once the pilot acquired the aircraft visually, a turned was made to avoid it.
summary: An ATC controller and a B737 pilot reported a near-miss between the departing jet and a VFR helicopter near BWI. The pilot turned north to avoid the helicopter, triggering a Resolution Advisory, and passed behind it at 500–1000 feet separation.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: M98 controller describes a day that the normal radar was out and they had to use another site that gave 12 second updates instead of the usual 1 second updates. According to the reporter the procedures in place did not work. There were many deviations and they had to separate traffic on various STARs. Controller requested a procedure which he felt would have made the traffic manageable, but was not approved by management and Traffic Management Coordinator.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that degraded radar updates and unavailable RNAV overlays during arrivals caused coordination failures and airspace violations. Management's refusal to implement "knock it off" procedures resulted in overwhelmed controllers, late frequency changes, and potential loss of separation.

synopsis: ORD Local instructor reports the Developmental crosses traffic downfield, then clears an aircraft for takeoff. Departing pilot questions clearance and Local Control cancels takeoff until crossing is complete. Reporter does not recall using the memory jogger for crossing aircraft.
summary: A developmental controller cleared Aircraft X for takeoff while Aircraft Y was still crossing the intersecting runway, causing the pilot to question the clearance. The supervisor immediately cancelled the takeoff, attributing the error to the failure to flip the departure strip as a memory jogger during the crossing.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported both his and the FO's iPad were in need of a charge, but the charging cords supplied by the company were inoperative. Reporter stated the iPads are the primary source of charts and that the charging cords are not tracked as maintenance equipment.
summary: Pilots on the third leg of a multi-leg flight found company-provided iPad charging cords inoperative despite a handwritten warning note. They used personal chargers to power their electronic charts, while reporting that the lack of a formal maintenance tracking system for this equipment creates a safety risk.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported noting in flight that the APU shutoff switch was not working. Maintenance recommended they continue on another leg, which they did, but the Captain stated he should have written it up and not continued.
summary: The pilot reported that the APU switch failed to turn off the unit before takeoff, yet Maintenance Control advised continuing the flight with the APU running. Upon arrival, the overhead switch remained ineffective despite no fault codes, leading the pilot to conclude the aircraft should have been grounded for repairs.

synopsis: CRJ200 flight crew reports being cleared to Runway 21R at DTW via Runway 9L and M Taxiway. The Captain taxies past Taxiway M and the next intersection is Runway 21R where an incursion occurs, causing a rejected takeoff.
summary: The flight crew mistakenly taxied past taxiway M onto runway 9L while heading for a 21R departure at DTW, nearly crossing the 21R hold short line. The aircraft stopped just before the line after the first officer alerted the captain, though ASDE data indicated a hold short line crossing occurred.

synopsis: A B737-900 Captain reported a Dispatch alert not to deplane passengers at the destination until advised because of a potential 'tipping aircraft.' No one seemed to have details about the issue.
summary: The flight crew of a 900ER kept the seat belt sign on at Airport ZZZ due to a potential tipping issue, but a gate agent opened the front door after knocking, prompting the pilots to intervene before deplaning. The reporter attributed the incident to crew conditioning to rush and a lack of situational awareness regarding safety protocols.

synopsis: An air carrier Captain at 4,000 feet near LEE reported numerous hang gliders at or near his altitude which posed a collision hazard. ATC had no information about the glider activity.
summary: The pilot reported encountering twelve hang gliders near 4,000 MSL while on radar vectors southwest of LEE, with three initially within 200 meters. Although JAX Approach had no radar contact, the crew maintained a high alert scan and required no flight deviation, though the density posed a clear danger.

synopsis: A Dispatcher reported computer maintenance required dispatch center's computers to be restarted for a memory issue. The interruption lasted 3 hours with no method of controlling aircraft.
summary: A dispatcher reported that an IT system failure caused a three-hour outage of dispatch tools and weather data while five flights were airborne. The reporter attributed the incident to server memory issues and criticized management's response, citing a serious safety risk due to the inability to manage reroutes or flight plans.

synopsis: A fatigued B777 Captain flying an ICAO SID procedure had his First Officer SPEED INTERVENE to 220 KTS at 1,000 feet and began a descent which oversped the flaps. All three non-flying pilots verbalized the descent before the EGPWS 'DON'T SINK' alerted.
summary: The Captain of a Boeing 777 reduced climb rate during initial departure with Flaps 15, causing an overspeed to 260 knots and a 'Don't Sink' warning at 1040 FT MSL. The crew reestablished a normal climbout after verbal warnings, attributing the event to distraction and fatigue.

synopsis: CL604 Captain experiences severe turbulence over ALS at FL390 resulting in a 1,000 FPM climb at idle thrust and partial spoilers. Flight eventually descends to FL350 with ATC's approval, but the Captain cannot read the altimeter during the initial descent due to the turbulence. The crew elects to divert to inspect the aircraft for damage before continuing to destination.
summary: Pilots encountered severe turbulence and mountain waves near ALS during an empty reposition leg, causing uncommanded climbs and accelerations. After descending to FL350 with ATC assistance, they made a precautionary landing for inspection, found no damage, and continued the flight.

synopsis: A Captain questioned the EGSS FL055 ATIS transition level while descending to 6,000 feet and was told it should have been FL070. A transition at FL055 would have resulted in a 600 foot altitude error.
summary: Pilots inbound to EGSS identified a discrepancy between the ATIS Transition Level of FL055 and London Approach's QNH clearance to 6,000 feet. The crew verified the correct altimeter setting with ATC, avoiding a potential 600-foot altitude deviation caused by conflicting Transition Level information.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reports landing prior to the displaced threshold for Runway 34 at CIU, due to poor runway markings, blowing snow and a poor depiction on the Jeppesen airport diagram.
summary: Flight crew on an RNAV GPS approach to Runway 34 at CIU landed 50 feet short of the displaced threshold due to blowing snow, poor markings, and an inaccurate Jeppesen chart. The crew mistook the full paved surface for the landing area because the relocated threshold chevrons were not visible.

synopsis: A321 flight crew experiences an engine failure at 3,000 feet during approach and elects to go-around to perform ECAM actions and QRH procedures. The Captain takes control of the aircraft for the single engine approach and landing. ECAM had annunciated 'ENG 2 FUEL CTL FAULT', just before the engine rolled back.
summary: During an ILS approach at 3,000 feet, the First Officer flew while the Captain managed ECAM and QRH procedures after Engine 2 failed due to a fuel control fault. The crew aborted the approach, discharged fire bottle 1, and the Captain took control for a single-engine landing.

synopsis: An EMB-145 EICAS alerted SPOILER FAIL while at cruise, so the UNCOMMANDED SPOILER DEPLOYMENT IN FLIGHT QRH was completed and the flight diverted to a nearby airport. The aircraft control felt normal but after landing the crew determined this was a repeat anomaly.
summary: The pilot monitoring reported an uncommanded spoiler deployment indication at 37,000 feet, attributed to a floating spoiler. The crew followed the QRH, diverted to a nearby airport, and landed safely without incident after burning fuel to reduce landing weight.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A jet crew on a left downwind visual approach to APC Runway 18R was given an extended downwind and because of raising terrain received several ATC low altitude alerts, as well as an EGPWS CAUTION TERRAIN.
summary: Pilots flying a jet to APC airport received multiple low altitude alerts from Napa Tower while executing a left downwind visual approach to runway 18R. The crew climbed to 3,000 feet to clear rising terrain and landed safely, noting the tower's pattern instructions conflicted with stabilized approach requirements.

synopsis: B777 flight crew arriving ZSPD is informed they are off course by ATC, but no deviation can be detected in the cockpit. An EICAS message 'NAV unable RNP' is then displayed and the crew requests vectors to the ILS, which are eventually provided. Once on the ground the left GPS returns to normal operation.
summary: During descent on the SAS 11E STAR into Shanghai, the crew received an ATC alert for being two miles off course despite the ND showing on-course. A GPS failure caused a 20-mile position discrepancy and an UNABLE RNP message, requiring radar vectors for a safe ILS approach.

synopsis: On final a B737-800 crew realized the trailing edge flaps were apparently not extending below 25, so they increased approach speed and landed without incident.
summary: During a visual approach to Runway XY, the crew attempted to extend flaps to 30 degrees at 180 KIAS, exceeding the 175 KIAS limit, causing the flaps to stop at 25 degrees. The pilots continued the landing with flaps 25, landing uneventfully and logging the flap malfunction in the maintenance logbook.

synopsis: A Q400 Captain apparently left the nose wheel steering powered during pushback which resulted in the ground crew's inability to disconnect the tow bar. The aircraft returned to gate for maintenance.
summary: The Captain reported that inadvertent nose-wheel steering activation during pushback caused the wheel to lock, breaking two tow-bar sheer-pins during subsequent towing attempts. Passengers were deplaned and bussed to the terminal before the aircraft was successfully towed to the gate with only the crew onboard.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain and Check Pilot seated in the jump seat reported they were confused as to track and altitudes on the SJC BMRNG1 SID and ATC was not much help.
summary: A flight crew departing San Jose on the Boomerang SID encountered conflicting altitude instructions and routing confusion from ATC, including a right turn command that conflicted with the FMS default left turn. The crew manually overrode the FMS to comply, attributing the incident to poor SID design, unclear ATC guidance, and the First Officer's lack of FMS training for long-way-around turns.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: During a night approach to SPS Runway 15C, the pilot sidestepped to Runway 15R because the pilot controlled lighting is installed only on 15R. Both the Pilot and Dispatcher missed the Jeppesen and AFD notes regarding the location of the lights installed.
summary: The captain flew an ILS approach to Runway 15C at SPS, but pilot-controlled lighting only illuminated Runway 15R due to an erroneous approach plate. The pilot executed a safe VFR sidestep to 15R, though the report notes a potential go-around would have been required if weather had been below minimums.

synopsis: A flight attendant reported feeling ill while at cruise on an out and back flight. Then she was reminded that her company had pilots use pressurization low flow to save fuel. She felt better after asking for increased air flow.
summary: A flight attendant reported feeling airsick and fatigued on flights to and from Airport ZZZ due to reduced cabin airflow from company cost-saving measures. After notifying the cockpit, airflow was increased within 5 to 10 minutes, resolving symptoms the crew member attributed to hypoxia.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant used the aircraft's 120VAC system to charge a passenger's two Portable Oxygen Concentrator batteries inflight. She was uncertain about her company's electrical use policy.
summary: A passenger's portable oxygen concentrator had a low battery, requiring two portable oxygen bottles for the flight duration. The reporter requested an exception to charge the device using the onboard 120V outlet.

synopsis: A Maintenance Manager reports finding Circuit Breaker (C/B) A-4 for the RAT AUTO/MAN CTRL deactivated at the P-49 Panel with a lock out tag device installed during a Remove/Replacement (R/R) of the APU battery in the Aft Cargo pit. The B777-200 aircraft was in for a Maintenance Phase Check.
summary: During a P-45 check, a maintenance technician found an irrelevant lockout tag deactivating the RAT AUTO/MAN CTRL circuit breaker while replacing the APU battery. After verifying no other tags or system faults, the aircraft was returned to service following a successful RAT operational check.

synopsis: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) was informed he had installed a cannibalized Generator Input/Output module-2 card (GEN I/O-2) upside down into the Modular Avionics Unit-2 (MAU2) on an outbound ERJ-170 aircraft. Technician noted that even though both cards were removed and reinstalled with the arrows facing up, instead of down, they still passed the AMM Operational Checks.
summary: A mechanic cannibalized a GEN I/O 2 card from an ERJ-170 to repair another ERJ-170 at the gate, installing the module upside down on both aircraft by ignoring the AMM's arrow-down requirement. Although operational checks initially passed, the error was discovered days later when the incorrect orientation caused a system fault.

synopsis: A Premier 1 (RA390) tire failed during takeoff. Due to the high speed reject, the pilot was unable to stop on the runway. The aircraft sustained little to no damage in the grass after the pilot successfully protected the nose gear.
summary: The pilot aborted an IFR takeoff on Runway 9R after a right main tire failure caused a rough bump and rumbling noise. The aircraft overran the runway end onto grass at 30-40 knots but stopped safely with no injuries, engine damage, or FOD found.

synopsis: An A320 was hit by lightning prior to landing at the previous station but the Captain failed to have an inspection. On arrival at the next airport, the Lead Flight Attendant informed the oncoming Captain about the strike and no inspection. The previous Captain returned and had words.
summary: The reporting pilot refused to accept an aircraft after the previous captain allegedly ignored two lightning strikes and declined a required maintenance inspection to avoid delays. The pilot reported the incident to the assistant chief pilot, who supported the decision to ground the aircraft for a proper inspection despite visible damage on the radome.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A corporate crew was cleared to taxi B2 to Runway 8 at JNU, but incurred the Runway at B2 since they forgot Taxiway A was being used as Runway 8.
summary: The Captain and First Officer inadvertently crossed the hold short line onto a closed runway while taxiing at JNU due to a briefing error and overlooked NOTAMS. The crew stopped upon noticing runway markings, attributing the incident to distraction by departure procedures and reduced visibility from rain obscuring taxiway lines.

synopsis: PA28 Flight Instructor is informed after landing that a second PA28 was over flown on final during a practice engine out approach. CTAF procedures were in effect and both aircraft had radios.
summary: During a training flight in the traffic pattern, a student pilot executed a simulated engine-out maneuver without visually confirming or hearing radio calls from another aircraft on final approach. The student's aircraft passed over the other plane, forcing it to go around, prompting the crew to agree on verifying final approach status via radio before future maneuvers.

synopsis: BE60 pilot experiences a NMAC after descending through a broken layer under ZMA control. The traffic is not reported by ZMA nor sighted by the reporter but is detected by the onboard Traffic Advisory System.
summary: A pilot on an IFR flight to FPR received a Traffic Advisory for an aircraft 300 feet below while descending through clouds after being cleared to 2,000 feet by Miami ATC. The pilot arrested the descent to avoid a near miss, attributing the conflict to a lack of traffic advisories while being vectored into the situation.

synopsis: ZJX controller reports of weather deviations and advises Front Line Manager that the sector was going to become unmanageable if something wasn't done to spread out the traffic. Reporter told of aircraft deviations and possible losses of separation due to deviations. Controller requested fifty miles in trail.
summary: An air traffic controller in the Greencove D-side sector reported that high workload, weather deviations, and frequency congestion led to a loss of standard separation between two aircraft and airspace violations of three sectors. The controller attributed the safety event to insufficient traffic management actions despite prior warnings to the supervisor.

aircraft: Cessna Twin Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: BGM Tower is informed of a UAV in the traffic pattern by a C303 pilot. Unfortunately the OCIC failed to log the incident or file an MOR.
summary: A C303 pilot in the VFR traffic pattern at 3,000 feet reported a UAV 500–1,000 feet below to the tower, which notified the OCIC. The OCIC failed to log the incident or file a MOR, highlighting a need for training on drone reporting procedures.

synopsis: Ground controller reports of a runway incursion due to emergency equipment entering the runway for the wrong aircraft.
summary: Ground Control managed an emergency Cessna 172 landing on Runway X while coordinating multiple emergency vehicles using four separate call signs. A fire truck entered the runway without authority to follow a non-emergency aircraft, requiring controller intervention to clear the path for the emergency landing.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reports being cleared for the FMS Visual Runway 28R at SFO. Later, a second clearance for the visual approach is received and the captain misunderstands it to mean a standard visual. A waypoint is deleted and descent is initiated while the First Officer is occupied, which is quickly detected by NCT.
summary: The Pilot Flying descended below the 6,000 FT restriction at TRDOW while flying the BRIDGE Visual to SFO Runway 28R after misunderstanding a runway-in-sight query as a normal visual clearance. The controller intervened to level the aircraft at 5,500 FT, cancelling the approach due to the altitude violation, though the flight subsequently landed uneventfully.

synopsis: B737 First Officer arriving MDW on the PANGG2 believes that note 1 should be revised to the RNAV (RNP) Y RWY 22L, since the RNAV (GPS) Z RWY 22L has been removed.
summary: The crew identified an invalid note on the PANGG RNAV arrival referencing a removed RNAV (GPS) Z RWY 22L approach. The procedure incorrectly directs pilots to this non-existent route instead of the current RNAV (RNP) Y or X RWY 22L approaches.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: The anatomy of a NMAC from the perspective of both flight crews and the N90 Controller involved.
summary: The Captain and First Officer of an aircraft at 6000 FT received TCAS Resolution Advisories while being vectored by NY Approach, causing a near miss with Aircraft Y. The Captain descended and turned right to avoid the conflict after visually acquiring the opposing aircraft, which also maneuvered, resulting in a safe separation.

synopsis: Assigned to descend via the SERFR ONE Arrival and to expect the TIPP TOE Visual to RWY 28L at SFO, B737 First Officer noted a 1,000 FT variance in the altitudes at MENLO for the two procedures.
summary: Pilots descending into SFO on the SERFR ONE Arrival experienced minor confusion due to conflicting altitude instructions for the MENLO fix and a temporary exit from Class Bravo airspace. Despite the discrepancies, the aircraft remained on VNAV PATH, and the approach to runway 28L proceeded without incident or deviation.

synopsis: A300 flight crew experiences a bird strike on takeoff that seems to be in the nose gear area. Holding is initiated to contact Maintenance and ATC informs that another crew saw fire from the left engine at rotation. The crew elects to return to the departure airport where three bent fan blades are discovered by Maintenance.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a bird strike with a Red-tailed Hawk just after V1 during takeoff, causing a suspected left engine compressor stall. After learning of a reported engine fire from another aircraft, they declared an emergency, returned to the departure airport, and landed safely with minor engine damage.

synopsis: An EMB-145 engine oil pressure initially dropped, stabilized, then dropped into the RED band. The QRH was referenced, the engine shutdown, and the flight diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: The crew diverted a cruise flight after Engine 1 oil pressure dropped from amber to red, triggering a precautionary shutdown per the QRH. They completed a single-engine approach to the ramp, discovering oil on the nacelle, which the reporter attributed to a maintenance issue.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot reports discovering that the weight and balance charts for his company helicopter, are using an incorrect moment arm for the search light mounted on tail of the helicopter.
summary: A mechanic discovered an incorrect weight and balance arm entry for the SX-5 nightsun, causing erroneous center of gravity calculations for the aircraft since its arrival. The reporter attributed this undetected error to a failure of Quality Assurance to properly execute their duties.

synopsis: EMB-175 First Officer reports confusing the TO-1 setting [a thrust setting] with the flaps 1 setting. This results in a takeoff warning when autothrust is engaged and the takeoff is rejected.
summary: The pilot incorrectly set flaps to position 1 instead of the required TO-1 setting during runway entry. This error triggered a "no takeoff flaps" master caution after auto-throttle engagement, resulting in a rejected takeoff.

synopsis: CRJ900 Captain experiences a TCAS RA shortly after leveling off at 3,000 feet on the NATIONAL5 departing DCA on Runway 19. ATC issues heading changes resulting in a TCAS TA. ATC questions the aircraft's climb capability, indicating that 3,000 feet may not have been the expected level off altitude.
summary: A pilot departing DCA on Runway 19 received a TCAS RA and TA while climbing to 3,000 feet under Departure Control. The pilot attributed the conflict to a Turbo Commander crossing the departure path and rapid evasive heading changes, suggesting improved procedures to prevent such encounters.

synopsis: A Maintenance Controller was informed by a CE-560 flight crew that the Battery Disconnect switch would not disconnect the aircraft battery. Controller also noted the flight crew would not reply to technical questions to assist in troubleshooting. Concerns raised that the relay that energizes open, to disconnect power from the system was stuck.
summary: Flight crew on a CE-560 reported a battery disconnect switch failure, prompting Maintenance Controllers and pilots to investigate. The switch likely has a stuck relay, leading to a flight cancellation and a recommendation against unauthorized crew testing.

synopsis: Eclipse 500 pilot reported deviating from assigned heading on arrival into BWI when he experienced wake turbulence in trail of a B737.
summary: A pilot flying a RIPKN1 arrival to BWI encountered wake turbulence from a preceding B-737 at 9,000 and 4,000 feet MSL, causing a 30-degree roll and delayed turn initiation. The pilot attributed the resulting diminished situational awareness to distraction from the turbulence, acknowledging personal responsibility for maintaining awareness during the arrival.

synopsis: PA28 pilot experiences low oil pressure and notes oil on the cowl at 5,000 feet. The destination airport is within range should the engine fail, but required flight through restricted airspace without a clearance. No oil remaining and a cracked oil cooler were discovered on post flight.
summary: The pilot flying to ZZZ experienced dropping oil pressure and visible leakage from a cracked oil cooler while descending from 5,000 feet. The pilot entered nearby restricted airspace to execute a straight-in landing on runway 32, arriving with no oil remaining.

synopsis: T-45C instructor on an IFR flight plan, experiences a NMAC with a BE-35 at 8,500 feet during the HI-TACAN Runway 23R approach to TYS. ATC advises the reporter of the conflict after the BE-35 had passed.
summary: During a HI-TACAN approach to Knoxville (TYS), an IFR flight experienced a near mid-air collision with a co-altitude Beechcraft Bonanza while descending from 8,500 to 6,000 feet. The reporter attributed the avoidance of collision to pure chance, noting the VFR aircraft passed within 500 feet despite the IFR clearance.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: MD80 flight crew reports copying incorrect Weight and Balance information during a phone call. The center of gravity (CG) is copied as 3.59 instead of 30.59, resulting in an incorrect stab setting. During takeoff roll the nose begins to lift at 70 knots and the takeoff is rejected.
summary: The First Officer and Captain aborted an MD80 takeoff at 90 knots due to uncontrollable nose rise caused by an incorrect Center of Gravity of 3 instead of 30. This error resulted from miscommunication with the weight and balance operator regarding an empty aircraft load, leading to improper stabilizer trim settings.

synopsis: C172 pilot reports picking up his IFR clearance airborne and receiving a different route than filed. Attempting to program the GPS while climbing, both track and altitude deviations occur and are noted by ATC.
summary: The pilot departed Robbinsville without a clearance, climbed to 5,000 feet, and deviated to 5,500 feet while programming the Garmin 430, causing an altitude hold failure. McGuire Approach issued alerts due to traffic conflicts, prompting the pilot to return to 5,000 feet and resume the cleared route.

synopsis: BE35 pilot experiences confusion after landing full length Runway 35L at DWH with a destination on the west side of the field. A back taxi is required to taxiway E with instructions to stop upon exiting and contact ground, which are not heard. The Tower Controller is upset.
summary: The pilot landed at DWH after receiving weather from ATC due to ATIS failure, then taxied past Taxiway E before being instructed to stop and contact Ground. A subsequent pilot deviation report was filed, though the pilot disputed the accuracy of the recorded instructions and noted the tower was implementing new, unverified exit procedures.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Front Line Manager reports of a loss of separation due to an aircraft descending through another aircraft's altitude. The D-Side was unaware of the loss of separation, due to the R-Side's dimly lit map and targets. The reporter also suggests the Monitor Alert Parameters MAP be lowered when military airspace is given away.
summary: A supervisor observed a loss of standard separation between Aircraft X descending from FL400 to FL340 and Aircraft Y at FL370 in a restricted sector. The incident was attributed to delayed descent clearance, high traffic volume, and the Radar Associate's inability to read small data blocks due to dim scope settings.

synopsis: D01 controller describes an Opposite Direction Operation [ODO], which he wasn't sure if it was legal to do or not. Later that day he does another ODO like operation, then after review is told to cease ODO's. Controller asks for clarification on what he can and can't do reference ODO's.
summary: An approach controller attempted to facilitate Opposite Direction Operations (ODO) for Aircraft X on ILS 35R, initially coordinating with the tower before realizing the clearance violated procedures. Although no separation loss occurred, management ordered a cessation of ODO assistance due to unclear definitions and inconsistent interpretations of the rules.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Traffic Management Coordinator reports of issues related to flow control and the fact that when asked for an extension the Air Traffic Control Command Center (ATCSCC) denies the request. The reporter then goes on to report that the ATCSCC cannot see the traffic and should not deny the controllers what they need for flow.
summary: ZDC controllers reported that ATCSCC denied requests to reroute RDU arrivals around convective weather, preventing separation from deviating departures. The reporter attributed this unsafe situation to ATCSCC lacking equipment to view local sectors and aircraft deviations.

synopsis: A B737-700 flight crew reported they flew the wrong departure out of LAX when they failed to catch a routing change in the PDC.
summary: Both pilots missed a SID change to VTU5 in the PDC during pre-departure, believing they were cleared for the CASTA 4 Departure. SoCal re-cleared them via runway heading with radar vectors to the PXN3 Arrival, resulting in no conflicts due to light traffic.

synopsis: An A319 Captain reported a loss of cabin pressure at FL310. The flight executed an emergency descent to a safe altitude and continued to the destination.
summary: During descent from FL310, the crew encountered a pressurization failure where the outflow valve stuck open, causing cabin altitude to climb to 11,400 feet. The pilots executed an emergency descent to 7,000 feet with oxygen masks donned, resulting in a normal landing despite the failed pressure controllers.

synopsis: A B777 Captain does not believe that the Company Terrain Critical Depressurization Procedures apply to flight along UR640 and may not apply to the model B777 being flown. After discussions with the Dispatcher and the Fleet Technical Manager the flight departs with unstated alterations to the route of flight.
summary: The captain of a Boeing 777-200 questioned the applicability of Terrain Critical Depressurization Procedures for airway UR640 due to a manual exclusion note. After consulting dispatch and technical managers, the crew agreed to use the existing chart, allowing the flight to depart safely without rerouting.

synopsis: A B737 Captain expressed concern about ramp safety following his air carrier's change in a procedure that would keep an engine running at the gate.
summary: The Captain at SFO rejected the airline's "Don't-Start-the-APU" arrival SOP, citing risks to ramp personnel from running engines. He continues to keep the APU running until ground power is confirmed to ensure safety, arguing the mandated procedure violates FARs by operating carelessly.

synopsis: An EMB-175 Captain reported a number of system failures annunciated on EICAS following a hail encounter departing MMMY.
summary: The crew of an air carrier aircraft departing MMMY encountered hail and IMC at 5,000 feet, triggering multiple flight control EICAS failures. After completing QRH procedures and consulting Dispatch via ACARS, they safely completed the flight, though ground checks revealed persistent FLT CTRL NO DISPATCH and ADS probe failures.

synopsis: CE560XLS Captain reports deviating west of the of the DCA 328 degree Radial on the NATNL5 departure due to entering IMC and turning to the west prior to the DCA VOR.
summary: Pilots departing Runway 1 on the NATNL5 SID entered clouds at 400 feet and overshot the 328-degree radial due to low weight and temperature while turning west without visual reference. The reporter attributed the deviation to the SID lacking a defined initial heading to an RNAV fix.

synopsis: An SR22 pilot reported an NMAC in the pattern at SNA.
summary: A Cirrus pilot executing a base turn at John Wayne Airport at 700 feet MSL encountered a Cessna 172 flying an inside pattern on a collision course. The pilot dove to avoid the Cessna, which passed immediately behind the tail, before landing safely on Runway 20L.

synopsis: A Captain taxiing into the International Terminal at SFO became confused by the lack of signage on Taxiway A when Ramp Taxiways H1, H and M do not align with corresponding outer taxiways of the designation.
summary: The pilot misidentified Taxiway H as M while taxiing to the gate, causing an incorrect route of H, A, H instead of H, A, M. The error resulted from confusing the continuous H/H1 alignment and a lack of ground markings or signboards at the intersection of Taxiways A and H.

synopsis: A qualified observer reported a damaged and unattended blimp parked at the Tijuana International Airport. If untethered while unmanned, the airship poses an air travel danger.
summary: A pilot reported an un-airworthy White blimp parked at Tijuana International Airport as a hazard to commercial aviation. The airship, damaged by inexperienced personnel and lacking required maintenance or supervision, poses a threat to landing and departing aircraft if it breaks from its mooring mast.

synopsis: A BE350 Captain reports that his G1000 with a current chart subscription does not indicate that there is more than one page to the BOWIE3 arrival to DFW. Only on the third page is it noted that the procedure is slightly different for turboprops, requiring a different heading from a different fix. The BOWIE3 for turboprops cannot be line selected in the GPS and a track deviation occurs when the aircraft passes the turn point.
summary: Pilots of a King Air 350 overflew the HIKAY waypoint during the Bowie Three Arrival into DFW because the G1000 FMS defaulted to a turbojet route containing the SILER fix instead of the required propeller route. The incident resulted from automation dependency, incomplete chart display, and confusion over a buried note specifying a 160-degree heading for propeller aircraft.

synopsis: BD70 (GLEX) flight crew reported overshooting charted altitude during RNAV approach. Crew reported they thought they were in VNAV but were actually in VS mode.
summary: The pilot flying descended 600 feet below the cleared 3000 feet during the RNAV GPS 35 approach because the aircraft was in Vertical Speed mode instead of VNAV. ATC alerted the crew at 2600 feet, prompting an immediate climb back to 3000 feet caused by unconfirmed flight modes and inadequate monitoring.

aircraft: Fairchild Swearingen Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: PT19 pilot reports landing in a strong crosswind normally then losing control when the tail wheel contacts the runway. This results in the aircraft departing the runway before stopping on the parallel taxiway. After taxi to the ramp it is determined that the tailwheel steering linkage was broken.
summary: The pilot landed a tailwheel aircraft in crosswinds, but a broken tailwheel steering linkage caused a rapid right turn and runway excursion onto a taxiway. The pilot taxied to parking using right turns only, while the tower failed to return the pilot's post-incident calls.

synopsis: A Los Angeles Center (ZLA) Controller describes a situation where an aircraft is circling on a mission and is in constant conflict due to altitude and position.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that orbiting government aircraft at 14,500 and 15,000 feet near EMT conflicted with LOOP departures from KLAX due to a lack of pre-departure coordination with ZLA. The controller attributed the safety risk to missing information flow and recommended a meeting between ATC and the operating agency to improve separation and efficiency.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Atlanta TRACON (A80) Controller reports of having to use two different radar systems at one position to monitor traffic safely. The reporter states that it is stressful on all of the controllers involved.
summary: Air Traffic Controllers managing triple simultaneous approaches faced unsafe conditions when severe weather caused multiple go-arounds, forcing them to simultaneously use PRM and RACD displays. This distraction, combined with a 10-15 second radar track loss for one aircraft, compromised controller ability to safely vector departing traffic.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain on the GIBBZ2 arrival to IAD, reports confusing their clearance direct MOSBY as direct MOSLE, and believes they are too similar to be in the same airspace.
summary: The flight crew misheard a clearance to proceed direct MOSBY while on the GIBBZ 2 Arrival near KIKKR and flew to MOSLE instead. The controller corrected the error, noting the similar names of MOSLE and MOSBY caused the confusion.

synopsis: An air carrier Captain notes that his company provided preflight weather package does not include several Sigmets that are available from other weather services. He believes that the weather service always understates significant weather elements provided to the crews by the company.
summary: The flight crew discovered that dispatch omitted severe turbulence and volcano SIGMETs from flight planning paperwork for a flight near Japan. The crew independently verified the hazards and deviated from the dispatch route to fly below the forecast severe turbulence, while dispatch incorrectly claimed the original plan avoided these areas.

synopsis: The crew of a B767-300 reports inadvertently taking off with a thrust setting much lower than required for the actual aircraft weight. The First Officer had set D2 in the Thrust Management Computer (TMC) and the Captain decided he preferred the assumed temperature method of de-rating thrust, but the D2 was never removed from the TMC.
summary: The First Officer and Captain took off in D2 mode with an assumed temperature reduction instead of the intended reduced takeoff from Max, resulting in 40,000 lbs less thrust. The crew attributed the error to the First Officer pre-selecting D2 without Captain approval and both failing to verify the Thrust Management Computer setting before departure.

synopsis: A B757 Flight crew experiences an EGPWS terrain warning at 2,300 feet during a night visual approach to Runway 17 at MHT. The crew was NNW of the field at the time and took evasive action.
summary: During a visual approach to runway 17 at MHT, the crew received an EGPWS "Terrain Pull Up" warning while descending. The pilot flying disengaged the autopilot and climbed, clearing the terrain before completing a normal landing.

synopsis: DA2000 flight crew reports diverting for a door warning light at FL430 in an aircraft that had a history of apparently false door warnings. The crew does not believe that MEL 52-1-0, used to defer an inoperative warning light, is applicable.
summary: The flight crew diverted a Dassault Falcon 2000 after a red doors warning light illuminated at FL430, extinguishing at FL290 during descent. The crew refused to defer the functioning system under MEL 52-1-0, citing company pressure to fly with a known maintenance issue and an improperly worded MEL.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew report discovering in cruise that their control column can be moved freely about eight inches fore and aft, without disturbing the autopilot or producing elevator movement. The flight continued to destination with the autopilot engaged. During a turn at 11,000 feet the autopilot becomes disengaged and cannot be reengaged. Although the elevator felt soft the Captain is able to manually land the aircraft.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a loose control column with 8 inches of travel during descent on a Boeing aircraft. They maintained autopilot, descended slowly to restore elevator authority, and landed safely with flaps 30 after flight director modes failed below 11,000 feet.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: After engine starting issues at the hangar the gust locks are re installed during trouble shooting by the pilot of a small aircraft. The second start attempt is successful but the gust locks are forgotten about until 40 knots in the takeoff roll and the takeoff is rejected. With limited elevator control porpoising commences and cannot be controlled. The nose gear separates and the propeller contacts the runway.
summary: The pilot aborted a takeoff in gusty winds after discovering gust locks were still installed, causing the aircraft to porpoise and break the nose gear. The pilot attributed the accident to distraction from earlier engine start issues and failing to complete the pre-departure brief.

synopsis: ZAU Front Line Manager (FLM) reports of an aircraft that had a radio failure but weren't sure if the aircraft was still IFR. The FLM inquires to see who knows what and finds out that no one is sure of the aircraft's intentions. The FLM questions the CIC in another area for not letting others know what was going on with this aircraft.
summary: ZAU FLMs and controllers managed Aircraft X, an IFR flight at 7000 FT with electrical issues, after it lost radio contact and squawked 1200 then 7600. Uncertainty regarding VFR/IFR status and delayed DEN reporting occurred because adjacent FLMs were unavailable and CICs lacked clear guidance on notification procedures.

synopsis: A commuting pilot reports overhearing a Flight Attendant discussing company security procedures with a passenger.
summary: A Flight Attendant disclosed detailed flight deck security procedures to a passenger after the aircraft arrived at the gate. This occurred in front of a full cabin of listening passengers following a comment about the flight deck door.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports being unable to upload weight and balance information into the FMC until an erase prompt is noticed on the route page and pressed. Once airborne it is determined that the erase prompt has removed all the route changes made at the gate. The SID is quickly reentered.
summary: During preflight, the crew experienced FMC weight upload failures and subsequent loss of SID and STAR data despite prior verification. The issue resolved after erasing a prompt, but the missing route data created a potential navigation deviation risk, highlighting manual guidance gaps and FMC quirks.

synopsis: B777 First Officer describes a Visual Approach to SFO by a Captain not entirely familiar with the airport or the aircraft, resulting in a slightly unstabilized approach and a low altitude alert from the Tower.
summary: The Captain, unfamiliar with the Boeing 777 and SFO arrival, deviated below the glide path during final approach due to improper flap sequencing and speed brake management. The crew corrected the descent after a tower altitude alert and landed safely, though the First Officer noted a missed approach would have been safer.

synopsis: CRJ900 First Officer experiences a BRAKE OVHT Red Warning Message on EICAS Display 1 at FL340. The crew elects to descend to a lower altitude and extend the gear in compliance with QRH procedures. The warning is extinguished but returns when the gear is retracted. The gear is extended a second time but the warning remains displayed and the crew elects to divert to a suitable airport. Maintenance determines that the Brake Temperature Monitoring System (BTMS) 1 is at fault and MELd.
summary: Pilots encountered a false BRAKE OVHT warning at FL340 caused by a BTMS computer communication link failure. They diverted to ZZZ1 with gear down for a visual inspection, which confirmed no damage before mechanics repaired the system.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: After landing on Runway 36R at CLT, a Regional Jet flight crew experiences a very convoluted taxi lasting over one hour due to VIP movement. Entering the ramp at C10 the crew is unable to get clearance in, resulting in a landing aircraft on 36R not being able to clear and another aircraft going-around. New ramp control frequencies may have confused the crew.
summary: The flight crew experienced a one-hour taxi delay due to VIP movement and received conflicting ramp instructions while instructed to "hustle." Poor communication and unclear frequency assignments caused the crew to block a taxiway, forcing an arriving aircraft to go around.

synopsis: ERJ170 Captain experiences a pressurization anomaly passing FL210 and stops at FL220 to perform QRH procedures. With Presn Auto Fail, manual is selected but also fails. The flight descends to 10,000 feet for the remainder of the flight to destination airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced dual pressure control failures during climb, forcing a descent to 10,000 feet with one pack off. They continued to destination with stable cabin altitude but faced fuel concerns due to ATC vectors, landing uneventfully while attributing the failure to inadequate maintenance procedures.

synopsis: Early in the flight a hum and vibration were detected, which the A320 crew suspected to be a pack malfunction. Later when fumes developed the crew began to divert to a suitable airport. Once the COM QRH procedure was commenced, a VENT BLOWER OVRD ECAM confirmed a VENT Fan failure.
summary: The flight crew experienced a loud hum, vibration, and burning oil fumes during cruise, suspecting a PACK fault before executing an emergency descent. The issue was resolved by turning off PACK 1, which triggered a VENT BLOWER OVRD command, revealing the cause was a failing blower fan that disintegrated.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier crew was cleared at departure to DFW with filed BRDJE One Arrival (RNAV). Entering the terminal airspace, they were cleared for the arrival but were not told the SEEVR One Arrival (RNAV) was active. As a result, the flight crew did not meet the crossing restrictions.
summary: The flight crew and ATC controller experienced a descent clearance misunderstanding during the DFW arrival phase due to conflicting arrival procedures and off-course vectors. The controller failed to communicate concerns about crossing restrictions, leading to confusion until the crew requested clarification and reprogrammed the FMGC.

synopsis: A319 First Officer reports being assigned direct to a fix on a new arrival and a descent clearance as the Captain is leaving the cockpit for a lavatory break. A request for a confirmation of the altitude assignment and a heading to the new fix is made. During the confusion, the altitude knob on the FCU may have been turned instead of the heading knob resulting in track and altitude deviations. ATC issues a new altitude assignment and back to the previous arrival as the Captain is returning to the cockpit.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced confusion during descent when ATC issued a new arrival and altitude clearance while the Captain was returning from the lavatory. The FO likely misdialed the altitude selector due to distraction, though the aircraft eventually descended to FL220 and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: During preflight CE-560XL crew discovered excessive horizontal stabilizer play because of excessive attach bolts and bushings wear.
summary: During preflight, the pilot and first officer discovered excessive free play in the horizontal stabilizer caused by worn attach point bolts and bushings. A mechanic verified the defect, leading to the aircraft being grounded for immediate inspection and a recommendation for fleetwide checks.

synopsis: During the departure climb a B757-200 left engine fuel control malfunctioned and commanded takeoff thrust. While near VMO at 5,000 FT, the engine was shut down, the QRH completed and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The Captain and First Officer of a Boeing 757 experienced a left engine runaway with thrust levers at idle shortly after takeoff, causing airspeed to exceed VMO. They returned to the departure airport, secured the engine using the fuel lever, and executed a safe overweight single-engine landing.

synopsis: A Helicopter Pilot reports of being issued a clearance for departure and not being given a frequency change or told to contact Tower. When the pilot departed and was airborne they were chastised for not talking to Local Control before departing.
summary: A helicopter pilot departed east from a ramp after Ground issued a downwind clearance without transferring to Tower, causing a deviation. The pilot attributed the error to Ground issuing flight instructions and failing to provide a frequency change, though Tower noted a potential conflict with an Archer on final.

synopsis: A Pilot reports of an airspace issue relayed to him by approach control. The aircraft departed OSU airport and climbed to 3,400 feet, made a right turn to a 240 degree heading. Approach stated that the aircraft entered into the Class C airspace of CMH and they had to restrict a carrier above this aircraft.
summary: Two pilots departing OSU on Runway 9 climbed to 3,400 feet within Class D airspace before contacting Approach, believing they had not entered the overlying Class C airspace. An ATC supervisor later determined they had penetrated Class C at 2,500 feet, requiring a report despite no traffic alerts or near misses occurring.

synopsis: A C177 landed in a crosswind and weathervaned toward the runway edge. The pilot then executed a go-around but struck a runway sign causing a small skin puncture below the passenger door.
summary: The pilot weathervaned off runway 34 during landing, initiated a go-around, and clipped a breakaway exit sign. A subsequent low pass and ground inspection revealed a non-structural ¼-inch skin puncture, with no undercarriage damage reported.

synopsis: A C182 pilot is informed after landing at destination that an NMAC had occurred during his previous departure. The weather was clear but the other aircraft was never detected.
summary: The pilot reported a close proximity incident at M78 after landing involving an unknown aircraft conducting a simulated instrument approach with a safety pilot. The pilot did not see the other aircraft or hear radio transmissions on CTAF, having switched to company frequency in the area during CAVU conditions.

synopsis: MH60 student pilot at 1,000 feet on a Night Vision Goggles training exercise reports an NMAC with another helicopter at 900 feet.
summary: Two NVG-equipped pilots in a helicopter returning to base encountered another helicopter 10 NM NW of ZZZ at 1000 FT MSL. Cultural lighting delayed traffic detection, resulting in a left turn avoidance maneuver with approximately 200 FT lateral and 100 FT vertical separation.

synopsis: Minneapolis Center (ZMP) Controllers report of an airspace violation and a loss of separation when a military jet is cleared into airspace that another Controller owned. The other Controller had traffic in the way leading to the loss of separation.
summary: During a Functional Check Flight, a D23 trainee and trainer lost separation with Aircraft Z in Sector 19 due to a bad beacon code, delayed handoff, and the Sector 19 controller's lack of LOA awareness. Controllers resolved the conflict by issuing heading changes to Aircraft X and Z, though communication delays complicated the maneuver.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A Boston TRACON (A90) Controller reports of having difficulty with an aircraft transponder. The Controller stated the data tag would go into a coast mode and he had to tag up the aircraft often.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X, an IFR training flight departing CON, experienced intermittent radar contact and data tag coasting due to STARS system settings. The controller noted that the 30-second coast timeout was insufficient during a position relief briefing, causing the tag to drop to the suspend list in mountainous terrain.

synopsis: Southern California TRACON (SCT) and MYF Controllers report of a loss of separation between two aircraft, in which the SCT Controller should have issued traffic. An assumption that another SCT controller was watching the reporting Controller's traffic was wrong. The Tower Controller had other priorities and didn't notice the loss until it had occurred.
summary: An SDER controller accepted a visual approach for Aircraft Y while Aircraft X was on ILS 28R, but failed to coordinate with the SDNR sector. This lack of coordination and traffic exchange caused a loss of IFR separation, forcing the controller to restrict Aircraft Y's descent and resequence traffic.

synopsis: A Local Controller at TEB reports a loss of separation given to him at Local, he then tries to use visual separation but cannot. Finally sees both aircraft and lets the second aircraft land instead of sending it around.
summary: Approach controller MUGZY/N90 sequenced a Phenom 300 and a G-V less than 3 miles apart on the ILS for Runway 19 at TEB, causing a loss of separation. The local controller cleared both to land after the second aircraft reported visual contact, noting that Approach must improve sequencing under new wake turbulence rules.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A Chicago Center (ZAU) Controller reports that he issued a visual approach clearance to an aircraft and the pilot canceling IFR a few minutes later. The pilot then returned to the frequency and asked the Controller if he knew of any NOTAMS for the airport. The Controller read him two NOTAMS, both of which were for the two closed runways at the airport. The pilot then left the frequency before the Controller could ask his intentions.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft X for a visual approach to CMY Runway 29 after the pilot reported the airport in sight. The pilot later contacted the controller to ask about runway closures, which the controller confirmed were active, though the pilot had previously acknowledged receiving all NOTAMs.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: An Anchorage Center (ZAN) Controller reports of receiving information on an IFR aircraft that, because of its altitude, will be below the Minimum IFR Altitudes (MIA). The Controller coordinates with another facility to get the aircraft a higher altitude. When the pilot checks on the Controller issues a low altitude alert and tells the pilot to climb. The pilot says he wants VFR on top and the Controller lets the aircraft remain VFR on top. Controller is concerned about correct procedures for this type of operation.
summary: An IFR flight to ANC at FL160 faced potential terrain conflict with high Minimum IFR Altitudes in uncontrolled airspace lacking radar coverage. The controller issued an immediate climb to FL220 after the pilot declined a prior FL200 offer, though the pilot later requested VFR On Top citing visual terrain clearance.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Potomac TRACON (PCT) Controller reports of a tethered balloon [Joint Land Attack Cruise Missile Defense Elevated Netted Sensor System] that is above the altitude is should be at as reported by an aircraft in the vicinity. Balloon does not have a transponder on it to show altitude.
summary: Aircraft X shortcut over active restricted area R4001C at 11,000 feet, passing less than 500 feet above a JLENS Aerostat that Aircraft Y observed at its own altitude. The reporter attributes this to the military operating the Aerostat above the restricted area limits without transponder activation or coordination.

synopsis: ZLA Controller explains that an aircraft reported an aircraft 500 feet below them. The area and altitude of the aircraft was in SCT airspace and also an area of known parachuting. The aircraft was on a discreet code indicating its involvement. The ZLA Controller advised that SCT should have issued traffic to the aircraft or kept the aircraft until the conflict was no longer a factor.
summary: Aircraft X experienced a near mid-air collision with a parachute operation aircraft while climbing out of 8,000 feet in SOCAL Approach airspace. The reporter attributes the incident to the transferring controller switching frequencies before resolving conflicts and notes that no TCAS or collision alarms activated.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An MSN Ground Controller and pilot of an aircraft report of a NMAC at MSN. The conflicting aircraft was off course in the traffic pattern and Local had to tell the pilot four times to make right traffic. Local Control departed the reporting pilot's aircraft and did not issue traffic to pilots.
summary: A Ground Control/Flight Data/Controller In Charge observer and a departing Captain reported a near-miss at MSN between Aircraft X on takeoff from Runway 36 and Aircraft Y on left downwind. The event resulted from conflicting instructions, poor readback, and excessive radar pointouts, leaving the aircraft in close proximity below 1,500 feet with inhibited TCAS.

synopsis: A B737 was dispatched to LAS and arrived to find gusty winds and dust. The crew executed a go-around on the first approach but with fuel considerations landed on the second approach by flying beneath the gusts near the surface.
summary: The crew encountered severe windshear and turbulence during two ILS 1L approaches at LAS, causing a go-around and a long landing with emergency thrust. The pilot attributed the fuel stress to reactive dispatch planning and early descent, recommending proactive alternate policies for gusty conditions.

synopsis: An IND aircraft marshaller reported the lead-in lines and stop marks at Gates A17, A21, A23 and A24 have faded to non-detectability resulting in aircraft being stopped at incorrect locations and then being pushed to accessible locations.
summary: Ground personnel at Indianapolis reported worn lead-in lines and missing stop marks on gates A24 through A17, particularly at night. This caused multiple incidents where aircraft parked incorrectly and required towing to the correct position.

synopsis: An EMB-145 developed a violent shake with a thumping sound during climb at FL260, so the flight diverted to a nearby airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced violent control shaking and increased drag at 26,000 feet, prompting a diversion to the nearest airport. They executed a precautionary landing roughly 700 lbs overweight with a smooth touchdown after ATC vectored them to the final approach.

synopsis: An EMB145 Captain experiences failure of the nose gear doors to close after gear retraction on takeoff. The gear is cycled and the doors close. After landing Maintenance is queried about a write up and it is suggested that none is required and none is made. After two more legs are flown without incident the doors remain open on the fourth leg and are closed by cycling the gear. Again no logbook entry is made.
summary: The flight crew experienced recurring wind noise and open nose gear doors on two climb-outs, resolving both by cycling the gear. The pilot later admitted to not reporting the issue due to maintenance advice and schedule pressure, acknowledging this judgment error prevented building a maintenance history.

synopsis: A C208 pilot reports being assigned the ILS 5R at GSO initially then switched to ILS 5L due to an aircraft on the runway. The late change to 5L results in an overshoot of the localizer and an early descent due to mistaking the Vertical Speed Indicator (VSI) bug, at -450 FPM for the glideslope indicator. Tower then issues a low altitude alert at 1,800 feet and descent is stopped until the glideslope is captured from below.
summary: The pilot, arriving at GSO for ILS 5R, was vectored to ILS 5L due to a preceding aircraft delay. Rushing to reconfigure, the pilot misinterpreted the VSI bug as the glide slope, descended below the glide path to 1,780 feet, and triggered a low altitude alert before correcting and landing.

synopsis: A B767-300 flight attendants reported a cabin odor along with an activated mid cabin lavatory smoke alarm. The odor was either electrical or petroleum in nature, but no smoke was seen.
summary: The flight crew diverted at FL380 after cabin crew reported a mid-galley alarm and an electrical or oil odor, triggering a lavatory smoke detector. The aircraft landed normally with utility buses off, and fire personnel inspected the suspect lavatory where no smoke or heat source was found.

synopsis: At cruise, a B777 engine shutdown in flight after the FUEL SHUTOFF VALVE closed so the crew diverted to a distant airport for a safe landing.
summary: The crew experienced an unexplained left engine failure at FL370 caused by a closed fuel shutoff valve. They diverted to a suitable airport, executed a single-engine landing in heavy rain, and landed safely with minor radome paint damage.

synopsis: A pilot reported confusion about a conflict which IAH ATC alleged during a triple simultaneous ILS approach where no special procedures are specified different from standard ILS approaches.
summary: The pilot reported a disputed loss of separation during a triple simultaneous ILS approach at IAH, where both aircraft tracked assigned localizers, altitudes, and speeds. The pilot attributed the incident to unclear ATC procedures and lack of pilot information, noting the controller admitted partial responsibility and suggesting the operation be suspended.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence in trail of a B777 on approach to ATL that resulted in rapid left and right rolls.
summary: A pilot reported encountering wake turbulence at 5,000 feet on downwind while following two heavy 777s, causing rapid 30-degree rolls. The aircraft recovered without incident, and the reporter suggested reviewing separation policies despite no errors by crew or ATC.

synopsis: A Captain reports the Pre-Catch Lever for the forward entry door had been incorrectly re-installed preventing actuation of the lever on a Cessna CE-680 aircraft. The aircraft had been released from a maintenance station two days earlier.
summary: Cabin crew discovered the pre-catch lever was blocked by the stair frame during post-maintenance cleaning at ZZZ1. Improper reassembly after painting and stair replacement by Contract Maintenance Aviation prevented lever actuation, causing the flight to be canceled.

synopsis: A B737 flight crew reports arriving at their destination with low fuel and then having the Tower clear an aircraft for takeoff in front of them with tight spacing which results in a go-around. A tight visual pattern is flown and the aircraft arrives at the gate with 4,000 pounds of fuel.
summary: The crew reported a runway incursion where a Dash 8 took off while they were on final, compounded by a premature tower clearance and the departing pilot's failure to look out. This forced a go-around and minimum fuel declaration, resulting in a safe landing with low fuel after an oxygen mask deployment earlier restricted the flight to FL250.

synopsis: An A320 crew, relying on incorrect V speeds and weights, rotated and did not take off. The Captain maintained the takeoff attitude and let the aircraft fly itself off the runway. Once established in cruise, the crew compared the performance printouts and discovered the last performance numbers received from Sabre, were for 138.3 and not the final weight of 156.2.
summary: The crew departed from an intersection on runway 15L using incorrect ACARS performance data for a lower weight, causing sluggish rotation and V2 dropping below VLS. The pilot aborted the rotation but allowed the aircraft to fly off the runway, later discovering the MCDU contained outdated weight figures instead of the actual takeoff weight.

synopsis: A B767 Captain reported dangerous goods loaded in the bulk cargo hold which was not tied down as per company procedures. This issue is on going for his international flights.
summary: A flight crew member discovered unsecured caustic liquids in the bulk cargo hold during pre-flight inspection and requested ramp personnel to secure them. The reporter attributes this recurring issue to rapid ramp staff turnover, inadequate training, and a lack of necessary equipment like cargo nets.

synopsis: A321 Captain experiences a bad over night due to a very noisy hotel. During approach at the end of the next day, the First Officer calls for the missed approach altitude to be set and the Captain inadvertently initiates a climb. Autothrust and autopilot are disconnected and the approach is continued manually.
summary: A fatigued pilot on a six-day reserve schedule inadvertently engaged climb mode during final approach after poor sleep at a noisy Las Vegas hotel. The copilot disengaged automation to hand-fly the approach, and the pilot attributed the error to cumulative fatigue and inadequate rest facilities.

synopsis: A B777 flight crew reports entering the holding course instead of the holding Radial as cleared by ATC, for a holding pattern at BNN. The Captain detects the error prior to BNN and corrects it but the FMC does not initially update and the pattern is entered in the wrong quadrant. As ATC issues vectors, the pattern on the map display flips to the correct quadrant.
summary: The flight crew entered a holding pattern at BNN, but the Navigation Display initially showed the pattern in the opposite quadrant due to a software lag after correcting FMS inputs. ATC vectored the aircraft while the display updated 90 seconds later, revealing a potential FMS software issue with late holding entries.

synopsis: EMB175 Flight Attendant reports the emergency call lights flashing in the galley, but no answer from the flight crew when the phone is picked up. Attempted communication from the forward station is also unsuccessful. Notes are eventually passed between the flight attendants and the pilots and it is determined that the interphone system malfunctioned.
summary: Flight attendants encountered repeated emergency chimes and lights during service but received no response from the flight deck. They established communication via notes after discovering the emergency button was not pressed, continuing the flight and landing with the alarms active.

synopsis: During the flight an ERJ-175 Cabin Emergency Light and alert tones sounded because of a computer fault. The flight attendants could not communicate with the flight crew because they did not select the Cabin to Cockpit alert. Confusing communications and a cockpit lock down resulted.
summary: Cabin crew encountered a flight deck door access malfunction during service when emergency alerts activated without a call button press. Communication was established via notes after denied access, and maintenance identified a computer problem as the cause of the false emergency signals.

synopsis: A B737-800 Flight Attendant reported a three year old child injured when a passenger seat arm rest forcefully fell and struck the child behind her right earlobe causing a large bruise and swollen earlobe.
summary: A flight attendant reported that a 3-year-old passenger was injured when a faulty armrest snapped down and struck her behind the ear. The armrest failed to stay up, causing a bruise and swelling, prompting the crew to provide an ice pack and request EMTs upon arrival.

synopsis: A Lead Technician with multiple years of experience as an Aircraft Maintenance, Engine Start, Run-up, and Taxi Instructor, reports about the recent policy changes to the training and re-qualification requirements in their Procedures Manual. They believe the changes are flawed and will increase 'at risk' behaviors due to the lack of not accomplishing fleet specific proficiency Check rides on each type of fleet aircraft as previously required.
summary: A Lead Technician reported that revised Procedures Manual requirements allow one proficiency checkout to requalify an Aircraft Maintenance Technician on all fleets, rather than requiring fleet-specific checks. The reporter argues this policy flaw increases accident risk by failing to identify at-risk behaviors specific to different aircraft types.

synopsis: A G200 flight crew reports picking up an aircraft out of maintenance and performing a very thorough preflight. Once airborne the Captain's airspeed fails and is followed shortly by the First Officer's airspeed failing. The crew returns to the departure airport using pitch and power with ATC providing ground speed and altitude reports. The post flight reveals that both of the pitot heat circuit breakers are tripped.
summary: The crew of a post-maintenance flight experienced dual pitot heat failures and total airspeed loss after tripped circuit breakers were missed during split preflight duties. They landed safely using radar vectors and pitch/power settings, concluding that joint preflights and deliberate circuit breaker checks are necessary for future maintenance flights.

synopsis: A SA227 Captain experiences an engine failure climbing through 10,000 feet, followed quickly by an engine fire warning. The engine is shut down and the flight diverts to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: A cargo pilot reported an engine fire, power loss, and yawing at 10,000 feet MSL shortly after departure due to adverse weather delays. Following the inflight engine fire checklist, the crew diverted and landed safely on ILS runway 11 without further incident.

synopsis: A C-172 Instructor reported the aircraft began veering right while taxiing while the student was under control of the airplane. The instructor took the controls and tried to turn to the taxiway but was unable and shutdown the engine as the aircraft exited the taxiway.
summary: A pilot and student exited the taxiway onto grass during a left turn while taxiing for takeoff due to unresponsive rudder and left brake controls. The aircraft was shut down and towed to maintenance with no damage reported.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air taxi jet crew leveled at FL240 on the BACHR1 RNAV to DAL and when cleared VIA before ANGST, the lowest STAR MCP altitude was selected. The aircraft began a descent before the crew realized the error but they recovered to FL240.
summary: The flight crew descended below the assigned FL240 restriction at the ANGST fix while executing the BACHR1 STAR to Dallas Love Field. The premature descent occurred after the pilot activated VNAV and was briefly distracted, requiring manual intervention to stop the descent before any traffic conflicts arose.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air carrier Captain is informed of GPS jamming in ZLC airspace and issued a revised route of direct SLOWN direct BAM. When the jamming takes effect, the crew forgets they were cleared direct SLOWN and uses the VOR to proceed direct BAM, which ZLC questions.
summary: The crew flying a flight over the Rockies lost GPS navigation due to reported jamming and inadvertently flew direct to BAM instead of the superseded SLOWN clearance. ATC detected the deviation and vectored the aircraft back to course, prompting the crew to recommend improved situational awareness during GPS outages.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A GA pilot attempted to land at his home airport in gusty conditions, but after a bounced landing attempted a go-around then struck a runway sign as the aircraft struggled out of ground effect. A flap was damaged on the go-around.
summary: The pilot experienced severe wind shear during landing, causing multiple bounces and a go-around where the left flap struck a runway sign due to a hard crosswind gust. The incident resulted in flap damage and a minor tail strike, but the aircraft landed safely with no injuries.

synopsis: PA28 pilot experiences a possible TFR entry near Dodger stadium due to not being advised of the TFR by the briefer at 800-WX-Brief. The briefer explained after the fact that since it was a published NOTAM they were not required to brief it.
summary: A VFR pilot conducting a pleasure flight near Dodgers Stadium suspected entering an active TFR despite a pre-flight briefing stating none existed. The briefer later explained that published NOTAMs are not required to be briefed, leading the pilot to conclude that relying solely on Flight Service for TFR checks is inadequate.

synopsis: C172 pilot, landing in a direct crosswind on a grass runway, experiences a runway excursion. The berm is soft and the aircraft noses over ending up on its back.
summary: A pilot reported that strong crosswinds pushed the aircraft off a grass runway after touchdown, causing the right main gear to stick in a soft berm. The wind subsequently rolled the aircraft onto its back, resulting in no injuries but requiring damage assessment.

synopsis: NCT Controller, while instructing, observes the Developmental turn an aircraft into the flight path of another aircraft at the same altitude. The instructor fixes the problem by turning the aircraft back to previous heading. Minutes later the Developmental issues the same turn to the same aircraft. Instructor thought he might have missed an altitude climb or descent, but did not. Due to frequency congestion the instructor could not save the loss of separation.
summary: An instructor correcting a student during OJT at OAK found the student repeatedly issued unsafe turns causing Aircraft X and Y to converge while climbing to 5,000 feet. Despite frequency congestion from a VFR aircraft, the instructor eventually restored separation, though it was reduced to 2.8 miles and 500 feet.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: SDL Local Controller reports of a attempted handoff late from P50. SDL Controller advises he's unable handoff due to other traffic. Minutes later the aircraft is on his frequency cleared for a visual approach. SDL Controller had to send an aircraft around due to the overtake from the un-handed off aircraft. A new LOA went into place 3 days prior.
summary: The SDL Tower controller reported that P50 Biltmore Sector initiated a late data transfer for Aircraft X, which the tower rejected due to pattern traffic. P50 subsequently switched the aircraft to the tower frequency against the controller's decision, forcing Aircraft X to go around and creating a safety conflict with Aircraft Z.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
