synopsis: An A320 engine failed at cruise prior to descent, so the QRH was completed and the flight diverted to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced an uncommanded yaw and Engine 1 failure at 33,000 feet during cruise, triggering ECAM alerts. They diverted to the nearest airport, completed a single-engine ILS approach to Runway 5R, and landed safely with no injuries or damage.

synopsis: A Pilot reported the new FAR 117 Regulations permit companies to schedule pilots in such a way as create more fatigue than previous regulations.
summary: A pilot reported severe fatigue and mental fog after accumulating 78 flight hours in 18 days under FAR Part 117 regulations. The crew member refused a scheduled five-day Europe trip assignment, attributing the incapacitating exhaustion to aggressive scheduling and circadian rhythm disruption from frequent international time zone changes.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew report of being pushed back between pier DX and C reports being cleared to taxi via Taxiway Tango to Runway 10 but turns early onto Taxiway A instead. ATC issues new taxi instructions. Taxiway construction and airport Diagram clutter were cited a contributing factors.
summary: The flight crew incorrectly turned onto Taxiway Alpha while taxiing to Runway 15R at BWI due to confusing signage and construction. Ground Control intercepted the error, scolded the crew, and issued new instructions to reach the runway via Taxiways T, E, and P.

synopsis: A320 flight crew experiences GPS jamming in ZLC airspace resulting in a momentary track deviation. The jamming was NOTAMed but the aircraft's reaction to the jamming was unexpected.
summary: During cruise with autopilot 2 engaged, the aircraft made an unexpected left turn due to a 4-mile FMGC 1/2 position disagreement caused by GPS jamming. Salt Lake Center queried the deviation, but the FMGCs synchronized within one minute, correcting the course and resolving the navigation uncertainty.

synopsis: B-777 crew performed a max effort stop while taxiing in order to avoid a catering truck.
summary: During taxi to Runway 10L, a catering truck encroached onto active Taxiway Bravo past its stop point. The flight crew executed a maximum effort stop to prevent the aircraft's number 2 engine from striking the truck's cab.

synopsis: B-767 Captain points out conflicting/out-of-date depressurization escape routes in the South America section of the flight manual.
summary: An instructor pilot reported that the South America section of the flight manual contains outdated depressurization escape route pages with inconsistent formatting. The reporter noted that combining text and maps onto single pages and copying them into SKBO Jeppesen charts would improve accessibility and safety during emergencies.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported concern about an MEL on the fleet that allows aircraft to be dispatched with the cockpit access keypad inoperative, since that would preclude any emergency access to the cockpit.
summary: The pilot reported that after a keypad replacement, the cockpit door chime failed, prompting a technician to apply an MEL that removed keypad power and inhibited emergency access on the Airbus. The pilot stated they would have refused the aircraft had the chime not been repaired, as the MEL sealed the flight deck without an emergency entry option.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reports being cleared via N7, L to Runway 25C at EDDF, but not detecting that N7 jogs left at N and taking N8. EDDF Ground detects the error and states that it is common.
summary: The flight crew, including the First Officer and International Relief Officer, mistakenly taxied onto N8 instead of N7 at Frankfurt while using Jeppesen 10-9 charts. The ground controller attributed the error to the taxiway's appearance as a former parking area and unclear chart markings, requesting a report to address the recurring issue.

synopsis: B767 Captain reported his South America operations manual contained a number of out-of-date pages that in some cases contained fixes that no longer exist.
summary: A pilot reported that the South America chapter of the operations manual is two years outdated, containing obsolete fixes. This discrepancy makes planning and loading escape routes into the Flight Management Computer challenging or impossible.

synopsis: B757 First Officer is assigned a deadhead and a ferry flight that eventually exceeds the 16 hour reserve duty day. The company asks to extend the duty day by two hours and the crew agrees. Later the First Officer learns that a reserve duty day cannot be extended.
summary: A B757 crew encountered a navigational fault during taxi, causing a delay that triggered a dispute over Flight Duty Period limits. Although the Duty Manager authorized an 18-hour extension, the pilot later determined this violated the FOM, which caps duty at 16 hours.

synopsis: An airline Safety Observer reports that a new company procedure for chocking arrival aircraft could lead to injury of ramp personnel.
summary: A safety observer reported that the new mainline chocking procedure creates a fatality risk by requiring ground crew to walk past running engines to retrieve chocks staged in front of the aircraft. The observer attributes this hazard to the crew's focus shifting to the chocks immediately after wing walking, recommending a return to the previous procedure.

synopsis: MD-11F flight crew reported encountering wake turbulence at approximately 200 feet AGL after takeoff from RKSI in trail of a B777.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe wake turbulence from a preceding B777 at 2,000 feet AGL during climb from RKSI runway 33L, causing rapid rolls exceeding 30 degrees. The Captain took control to neutralize the aircraft, and the flight continued safely after the encounter.

synopsis: ERJ-190 flight crew reported rejecting the takeoff between 80 and 100 kts because they failed to arm the autothrottles.
summary: The Captain and First Officer rejected takeoff on Runway 9 due to an 'ENG TLA NOT TOGA' message caused by un-armed autothrottles from task saturation. The high-speed reject required a gate return and maintenance inspection, though the crew later confirmed the takeoff could have continued.

synopsis: A B757 air crew performed a rejected takeoff after multiple bird strikes at around 100 knots. They returned to the gate. After maintenance inspected the aircraft they once again departed for their destination uneventfully.
summary: The Pilot Flying aborted takeoff on Runway 18 after striking a flock of pigeons at 60–80 knots, causing damage to the nose, slats, and engine nacelles. The crew coasted to a stop without using brakes, leading to a runway closure for inspection and a subsequent uneventful departure three hours later.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 First Officer reported the flight crew was distracted by a company communication while awaiting an ATC clearance and holding short of the runway.
summary: While holding short for departure, a SELCAL alert triggered by a non-critical Crew Support message distracted the pilots during a sterile cockpit. The First Officer attributed this safety risk to the practice of sending administrative requests via ACARS during critical flight phases.

synopsis: While flying in the vicinity of thunderstorms, CRJ-700 crew encountered severe turbulence and windshear resulting in altitude deviations and stall warning activation.
summary: The First Officer and Captain encountered severe turbulence and windshear while navigating between thunderstorm cells, causing rapid airspeed loss and a stall shaker activation. After executing a stall recovery and descending 1,000 feet, they received clearance to FL350 and resumed flight with moderate turbulence.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 Captain delayed the engine start during taxi, and while starting it near the Runway's end, the First Officer seated the flight attendants. ATC then cleared the aircraft to line up and wait but as the Captain taxied onto the runway the First Officer, who did not hear line up, began the Takeoff Checklist. The Captain began the takeoff was told to reject around 100kts.
summary: The First Officer and Captain mistakenly believed they received a takeoff clearance while the First Officer was making a passenger announcement and the Captain's headset volume was low. They initiated a rejected takeoff at 115–120 knots after Tower clarified no clearance was issued, resulting in an 87-minute delay for maintenance checks and refueling.

synopsis: Flying at FL370, B-757-200 crew experienced vibration and power loss in the left engine. Crew executed an uneventful landing back at the departure airport.
summary: Cockpit crew encountered left engine vibration at FL370, requiring power reduction and a return to the departure airport after ice cycling failed. The aircraft executed an uneventful overweight landing.

synopsis: At the destination airport, an SR22 Pilot encountered construction equipment on the runway and, due to severe weather in the area, landed without incident on an adjacent taxiway.
summary: The pilot diverted 50–75 miles for thunderstorms and experienced severe turbulence while unable to contact ZZZ. Upon discovering construction equipment on Runway 17 during final approach, the pilot landed safely on the adjacent clear taxiway.

synopsis: C172 pilot reports losing directional control and departing the runway after landing.
summary: The pilot lost directional control after touchdown, coming to rest 200+ feet left of the runway at a 70-degree angle. The reporter attributed the incident to a lack of early go-around for an unstable approach and insufficient power reduction, rudder, and brake inputs after landing.

synopsis: C172 Flight Instructor experiences a pitch up and airspeed loss when the autopilot is engaged at 1,000 feet during climb. The autopilot is switched off but does not seem to disengage, making manual control difficult in IMC. ATC is advised and eventually it is determined that autopilot induced nose up trim is causing the problem and that the autopilot is indeed off.
summary: A Cessna 172 pilot experienced a rapid pitch-up and airspeed decay after engaging the autopilot during an IFR climb. The pilot initially suspected an autopilot failure but later realized the aircraft had trimmed up, requiring manual re-trimming to regain control before breaking out into VFR at 3,000 feet.

synopsis: LongEZ pilot reported an unresponsive throttle in flight, fortunately on short final to an airport.
summary: During a straight-in approach to Runway 22R, the pilot encountered an unresponsive throttle caused by a bent accelerator cable. Unable to add power for a go-around, the pilot diverted to land on Runway 22L ahead of a taxiing aircraft and taxied to the hangar for repairs.

synopsis: After touchdown, a tail-wheel aircraft departed the right side of the runway. Pilot recovered back to the runway and cleared on a taxiway. Tower closed the airport for FOD inspection. No FOD or aircraft damage found.
summary: A pilot flying a tailwheel aircraft experienced a right swing after a three-point landing, departing the runway at 25 MPH. The pilot recovered onto the runway, and after a brief airfield closure for FOD and damage checks, the aircraft taxied to parking with no issues found.

synopsis: C152 pilot reports a conflict in the pattern at DTO and stated they felt improper ATC procedures were a factor.
summary: A pilot in a C152 on downwind for Runway 36 encountered confusion when a second aircraft joined base, causing the Tower Controller to lose separation. The controller issued an improper "fly eastbound" instruction instead of a specific go-around, leaving the pilot unsure of the required action.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports about a forward trim cable that had a catastrophic failure inflight at the trim servo motor on a Piper PA28-161 Warrior aircraft. The trim servo solenoid was not disengaging the motor in the manual trim mode, causing significant tension on the trim cable when the trim wheel is operated manually.
summary: The pilot of a high-use PA28-161 experienced a catastrophic forward trim cable failure at the servo, likely caused by a solenoid not disengaging the motor in manual mode. The pilot safely returned to the airport with no injuries or additional mechanical damage.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: While taxiing on STL Taxiway Foxtrot, a flight crew was cleared for takeoff on Runway 12L at Taxiway Sierra but missed the turn onto Sierra and entered Runway 24.
summary: The crew cleared for takeoff on Runway 12L missed the turn at Sierra, crossing hold short lines for inactive Runway 24. Tower corrected the error, and the Captain returned for takeoff, citing poor runway markings and an unclear Jeppesen diagram as causes.

synopsis: A Tower Controller describes a low altitude alert issued by a newly certified Local Controller to a B737 on short final. The altitude did not seem far off and the reporter wondered if the equipment may have been faulty, but the crew acknowledged the deviation.
summary: A recently certified controller working a complex shoreline configuration issued a low altitude alert to a B737 during parallel approaches below 1,400 feet. The pilot corrected immediately, but the reporter remains unsure if the aircraft was actually low or if the alert resulted from faulty equipment.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported being instructed to clear Runway 19R on Taxiway Y at LAS, but Y does not connect to Runway 19R. Taxiway W is chosen instead, but W is closed.
summary: Pilots exiting Runway 19R were confused by conflicting ATC instructions, incorrect chart labels, and ambiguous ATIS wording regarding closed Taxiway Whiskey. They exited onto Whiskey instead of the requested Victor, leading to a controller dispute after the aircraft had already cleared the runway.

synopsis: A319 crew experienced an overheating engine warning and were able to resolve the issue before landing. Overheat warning reoccurred during taxi, resulting in cancellation of the next flight after the crew encountered communication difficulties with Dispatch and Maintenance Control.
summary: The flight crew experienced an Engine 2 EPR mode ECAM and subsequent left engine overheating during cruise, descending to FL290 before landing uneventfully. The engine overheated again at the gate, forcing a shutdown and flight cancellation due to unresolved mechanical issues and poor ground communication.

synopsis: An A319 Captain reported abnormal engine indications after a bird strike shortly following takeoff. The flight crew elected to return to the departure airport.
summary: The pilot reported a bird strike on the left side during climb-out from ZZZ at 10,500 feet, causing an ENG 2 STALL ECAM. The engine stabilized after leveling at 13,000 feet, allowing a normal landing and taxi to the gate following a precautionary drive-around inspection.

synopsis: CRJ200 Captain reports sighting a UAV (model aircraft) at 5,000 feet while on left downwind for Runway 36L at CLT.
summary: The First Officer spotted a small drone passing 5–10 feet above the aircraft at 5,000 feet while on left downwind for 36L at CLT. The encounter lasted 1–2 seconds at 190 knots, preventing evasive action, though ATC was notified and alerted other traffic.

synopsis: A B737-800 Captain reported he felt inappropriate pressure from a Chief Pilot to accept an aircraft he was not comfortable operating with an inoperative forward lavatory.
summary: The Captain and First Officer refused to operate a flight to ORD with an inoperative forward lavatory, citing MEL requirements for first-class service. Despite the Chief Pilot's inappropriate pressure at the gate, Dispatch provided a replacement aircraft, resulting in a 72-minute departure delay.

synopsis: B737 flight crew executes a go around at low altitude as an A330 under tow crosses the runway in front of them. The Captain does not initially detect the incursion as he is watching to insure that the aircraft landing ahead has cleared the runway.
summary: A pilot and First Officer executed a go-around at 300 feet AGL on approach to JFK Runway 13L after an A330 was towed across the active runway. The incident occurred because the towing aircraft crossed without Tower authorization, creating a conflict with landing traffic.

synopsis: After takeoff a G-200 crew received 'R HYD PUMP PRESS LOW', 'HYD LEVEL LOW' and 'AUX HYD PUMP ON' warnings. The crew accomplished the appropriate checklists and as a precaution diverted to an airport with a long runway for an uneventful landing.
summary: The pilot reported a right hydraulic system failure shortly after takeoff from ZZZ1, characterized by low pressure and fluid level warnings. The crew diverted to ZZZ2, dumped fuel to reach maximum landing weight, and landed safely after pressure stabilized upon gear extension.

synopsis: A C182 pilot reported running out of fuel in flight resulting in a forced landing with no damage or injuries.
summary: The pilot and a student pilot ran out of fuel in a Cessna 182 during cruise due to relying on a visual check and faulty gauges instead of verifying filler caps. They executed an uneventful off-airport landing on a gravel bar, refueled with 20 gallons, and continued with no damage.

synopsis: HS-125 Captain reported encountering severe turbulence and windshear on approach to BDL that resulted in a GPWS warning.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence and windshear approximately 5 miles from Bradley Airport during final approach. This caused a major airspeed increase, downdraft, and triggered a ground proximity warning.

synopsis: Two controllers and three pilots report of a loss of separation due to a Controller not issuing traffic on or before departure.
summary: A pilot departing Burbank Runway 15 and a VFR helicopter deviating from the Ventura freeway caused a loss of separation, triggering a TCAS descent resolution advisory. The pilot descended under the helicopter to avoid collision, resulting in a GPWS warning and a conflict with terrain before ATC resolved the situation.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported they misunderstood the Controller's clearance and a track deviation resulted.
summary: Pilots misinterpreted a Washington Center clearance for STEVY as GBEES due to static, executing a route change to the wrong waypoint. The controller later corrected the error, clarifying the original intent and issuing a new clearance direct to HNN VOR.

synopsis: B777 First Officer (FO) reported one of the other crewmembers fell asleep on the international flight.
summary: On a Boeing 777 cruise over the Pacific, a First Officer observed another First Officer and an FAA inspector appearing asleep while the crew was on SELCAL watch. The inspector later woke the sleeping First Officer, but no formal debrief occurred after the flight landed uneventfully.

synopsis: During approach, a cockpit observer suggested to the flight crew that a Go-Around was warranted during to an unstable approach condition. Flight crew executed a Go-Around.
summary: An Airbus crew flying to RNO executed a go-around at 700 feet RA after an unstable approach caused by excessive speed and improper configuration. The observer attributed the incident to the Captain's failure to adhere to speed limits, delayed gear extension, and disregard for stabilized approach criteria.

synopsis: A B777 flight crew encounters turbulence at FL390 approaching a thunderstorm over South America. A sudden temperature increase and wind shift make FL390 untenable and a descent is requested. At FL370 the crew is able to maintain airspeed and altitude.
summary: The Captain and First Officer declared a Mayday and descended from 39,000 to 37,000 feet after a sudden temperature increase near a thunderstorm caused a coffin corner situation and altitude loss. The crew attributed the event to rapid atmospheric changes despite maintaining a 20-mile clearance and criticized dispatch for lacking real-time weather tools.

synopsis: B737 Flight Attendant reported emergency equipment in this fleet is shrink wrapped and is difficult to access.
summary: Cabin crew reported that all emergency equipment on a Boeing 737 was shrink-wrapped, making it difficult to access. The Emergency Medical Kit was specifically tamper-resistant, requiring a sharp object to open.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant (FA) noticed an ill passenger during the boarding process. An investigation revealed that the passenger had recently travelled to Africa. The Passenger was observed to be sweating and vomiting. The FA notified the Lead FA and Captain of the situation. A Complaint Resolution Official (CRO) was called and the passenger was removed from the flight. The reporter was concerned that no precautions were taken for the crew and that the aircraft was not sufficiently cleaned and disinfected upon arrival at the destination.
summary: A flight attendant reported that a severely ill passenger with potential Ebola exposure boarded without screening, vomited in the galley, and was later hospitalized. The crew alleged the airline failed to follow CDC/OSHA guidelines, neglected proper disinfection, and ignored follow-up procedures despite the biohazard risk.

synopsis: PA28R pilot reported an airborne conflict with a B737 on approach to ISP, citing weather and ATC technique as contributing.
summary: A Cherokee pilot on final to Runway 33 at ISP executed a go-around after a 737 on an intersecting approach to Runway 24 also climbed, creating a collision course. The pilot attributed the conflict to the 737's late configuration, misinterpretation of ATC instructions, and controller inaction regarding wind conditions and separation.

synopsis: DA20 Instructor with student experience a NMAC with a crop duster at low altitude on final approach. Evasive action is taken by the crop duster and the DA20 crew goes around and returns to their home field.
summary: A pilot and student in a training aircraft encountered two crop dusters during pattern work at a non-towered airport. The first crop duster crossed the runway without radio contact, while the second descended behind them on final, forcing a go-around to avoid a collision caused by the crop dusters' unsafe operations.

synopsis: ZFW controller reports of an aircraft that doesn't climb because of a false target being displayed on their TCAS. Controller had climbed aircraft to requested altitude and then became traffic for another aircraft because it didn't climb to requested altitude. Pilot told controller this problem happened with the aircraft before. Event lead to a loss of separation.
summary: An air traffic controller and the pilot of Aircraft X experienced a near-midair collision with Aircraft Y at FL355 due to a ghost target on Aircraft X's equipment. The controller issued immediate avoidance clearances after Aircraft X descended without response, preventing loss of separation while the pilot attributed the event to faulty sensors.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: AMA controller and pilot of one of the aircraft involved report of a near miss due to the aircraft on downwind coming in close proximity of the trainer jet on a straight in final. Pilot was told to make 360's on downwind, but flew close to the final.
summary: An air traffic controller instructed a student pilot in a training aircraft to perform multiple left 360-degree turns on downwind for Runway 22 while radar was inoperative. The aircraft crossed the final approach path of a faster jet, resulting in a close proximity incident attributed to communication errors, difficult speed judgment without radar, and the student's limited visibility.

synopsis: B-777 First Officer fell asleep due to fatigue.
summary: The First Officer on a Boeing 777 inadvertently dozed off during the enroute phase while an FAA Observer and International Relief Officer were present. The pilot attributed the event to poor pre-flight rest, short scheduled breaks, and uncomfortable rest facilities on this specific aircraft model.

synopsis: A320 First Officer reported receiving a TCAS warning for what was apparently a phantom target.
summary: During departure climb from KMSY, the crew encountered phantom TCAS targets at FL360 due to a known system malfunction. After a communication failure caused by a disconnected hand mic, ATC issued a right turn and descent for another aircraft, while the crew manually held FL355 before resuming the climb to FL360.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot reports of a problem with a helicopter that would be in conflict with them as it crossed midfield and they were on short final. The crossing aircraft looked closer to the pilot then midfield and he was concerned how close they would be if they had to make a missed approach.
summary: During a visual approach to runway 33L in Baltimore, the pilot reported a helicopter crossing mid-field at 1,000 feet MSL created a potential collision risk if a go-around was initiated. The pilot estimated a collision could occur within 5-7 seconds, though the landing was completed without incident.

synopsis: An EMB-145 First Officer describes a flight in convective weather with several lightning strikes. At FL360 the crew begins to see airspeed flags and eventually lose both pilot airspeed indications. The crew elects to divert with the Captain flying pitch and power and the First Officer providing targets from the QRH. During approach, at 4,000 feet, the Captain's airspeed indication returns to normal.
summary: The crew of an ERJ encountered severe weather and lightning strikes during climb, causing dual airspeed failures and communication issues. After diverting to SAT due to deteriorating conditions and an initial QRH procedural error, they executed an overweight landing following intermittent air data recovery.

synopsis: EMB-175 crew declined to fly an aircraft with a single operative pressurization system that had experienced two separate malfunctions the previous day. Crew was replaced on the flight.
summary: The Captain and First Officer refused to fly an aircraft with one bleed system on MEL and a recent transitory failure on the other, citing safety concerns for a 3-hour flight at FL310. The Chief Pilot deemed the flight legal but removed both crew members from the schedule without pay.

synopsis: B757-200 flight crew reported they were targeted by a laser on approach to LAX, resulting in 'blind spot and halo effect' in the First Officers (FO)s right eye.
summary: A pilot flying a visual approach to LAX runway 24R at 3,000 feet encountered a green laser from the 2 o'clock position. The beam caused minor blind spots and halo effects in the right eye, which were reported to ATC and Dispatch.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported they diverted because of weather at destination and realized later it was not an authorized airport for his fleet.
summary: The Captain diverted an A319 from ZZZ1 to ZZZ due to thunderstorms and turbulence preventing a direct approach, despite Dispatch initially authorizing ZZZ2. The crew landed safely with 4,400 LBS of fuel after resolving conflicting authorization messages, though the Captain noted a failure to declare an emergency and difficulties locating authorized airport data on the iPad.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain laments the experience level of new First Officers that the company is hiring and believes that they are trained to be overly reliant on automation.
summary: The Captain intervened during climb windshear and a near-overshoot on approach caused by the First Officer's automation reliance and hesitation. The Captain took control at 5 feet to prevent a wing strike, attributing the events to the FO's inexperience, fatigue from extended duty, and over-reliance on automation.

synopsis: Pilot doesn't understand how SoCAL [SCT] doesn't know if he is on the GORMAN4 or CASTA4 departure. Aircraft turns northbound and controller vectors it back to a 250 heading.
summary: The flight crew, cleared for the CASTA4 departure from LAX, was misidentified by SoCal ATC as being on the GORMAN4 after a runway change. This error caused a conflicting altitude clearance and a near-separation incident with inbound traffic, requiring an immediate heading correction.

synopsis: C208 pilot reported he was on approach to Runway 2 at MGY when an aircraft taxied onto the runway triggering a go-around decision.
summary: While on final to Runway 2 at KMGY, the pilot executed a go-around after a Piper Cherokee taxied onto the active runway without radio contact and departed. The reporter noted the Cherokee had already committed a runway incursion by performing its run-up beyond the hold short line.

synopsis: BE20 pilot reported losing multiple flight instruments on approach to OKC.
summary: The pilot experienced multiple pilot-side instrument failures and conflicting data while descending for an ILS Rwy 17L approach at KOKC in IMC. Flying using copilot instruments with high workload, the pilot executed a stabilized but slightly long landing after maintaining higher-than-normal altitude and speed to ensure safety.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: LBB Developmental/Front Line Manager (FLM) reports of a loss of separation due to compression on final. The Developmental/FLM asked his instructor if they were capable of running 2.5 miles on final and the instructor replied he didn't think so. After the two aircraft landed the Developmental found out that they needed three miles instead of 2.5.
summary: A trainee controller and trainer allowed Aircraft X to compress to 2.5 miles behind Aircraft Y on ILS approach to runway 26 in a dust storm. The separation was insufficient because the facility does not qualify for reduced separation, requiring 3 miles, leading to a post-event determination that the trailing aircraft should have been sent around.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: A Jacksonville Center (ZJX) radar associate Controller reports of confusion around restricted areas being hot or not and how high the altitudes were if they are hot or not. The Controller tried many times to get the correct answer from the Front Line Manager (FLM) and Traffic Management Coordinators (TMC). The Controller reports of, 'The entire scenario was one of mass confusion, unnecessary movement of aircraft and potential loss of separation.'
summary: A Radar Assist controller at Brewton reported confusion over conflicting Special Use Airspace altitude data from the Jacksonville TMU, causing unnecessary aircraft vectors and potential separation loss. The incident resulted from inaccurate ATWS entries, poor coordination, and TMU distractions, including a party, which prevented correct military airspace status updates.

synopsis: Denver Center (ZDV) Controllers report of a loss of separation due to NON RVSM aircraft going through the airspace refueling with a tanker.
summary: A trainee controller in Denver airspace managed a non-RVSM military formation deviating for weather, but lacked initial equipment data. This communication breakdown resulted in three commercial arrivals descending within 2,000 feet of the formation, violating non-RVSM separation standards.

aircraft: M-20 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: ZLC Controller reports of a change to an altitude in the scratch pad area of a data tag that was changed but never coordinated. Controller reports that the BOI Approach airspace is a failure due to things not being coordinated and BOI Approach not having respect for the 7100.65.
summary: A pilot reported that BOI Approach flashed Aircraft X to R30 with an uncoordinated altitude change from 12,000 to 10,000 feet. The pilot intervened to prevent a deviation, citing a systemic failure in coordination and disregard for 7110.65 procedures during the airspace test.

synopsis: ZLC Controller reports of a failure from BOI Approach to follow the LOA reference handoff altitudes into ZLC airspace.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X was handed off from BOI Approach climbing to FL120 while requesting FL350, violating the LOA limit of 160 or the requested altitude. The controller attributed this to a failed BOI airspace test, expressing concern that repeated failures could lead to a fatal accident.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZTL Controller reports of the Traffic Management Controller (TMC) calling and telling to slow an aircraft to its slowest practical speed. The ZTL Controller claimed it was unsafe and the TMC should have given some other type of restriction like miles in trail.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that the Traffic Management Unit (TMU) issued unsafe speed restrictions to Aircraft X during its enroute phase from ATL to IAH. The controller stated this practice is hazardous, causes indefinite delays, and risks near collisions by bypassing controller judgment.

synopsis: CID Tower Controller reports a small aircraft pilot performing a touch and go on Taxiway E thinking it is Runway 13 which he had been cleared for. This is a new, wide taxiway with fresh, bright concrete and white splotches that look similar to touchdown zone markers.
summary: An air traffic controller observed a pilot on his first pattern flight mistakenly execute a touch-and-go on parallel Taxiway E instead of Runway 13. The controller attributed the error to confusing fresh concrete markings on the taxiway with runway touchdown zone markers.

synopsis: A Captain was informed by a passenger departing their B737-700 aircraft that rivets appeared to be loose on the upper wing skin leading edge area, just inboard of the left engine pylon. Maintenance determined passenger's observations were correct and the attach fasteners were loose. Maintenance Control approved a 100-hour MEL deferral with Repetitive Inspections.
summary: A departing passenger pilot reported loose rivets on the left wing top near the engine pylon, which maintenance confirmed were not holding, grounding the aircraft. The reporter noted the damage was undetectable during normal preflight duties without a ladder and requires more frequent maintenance inspections.

synopsis: An A320 Flight Attendant reported smoke from the ceiling near the forward galley during descent to their destination so ATC expedited the arrival. At the gate, the aircraft was deplaned normally because the smoke had dissipated.
summary: During descent at FL200, the flight crew of an A320 reported white smoke and an electrical smell near the forward galley. The crew donned oxygen masks, vectored for a visual approach, and landed uneventfully; ARFF inspection found no fire, so the aircraft taxied to the gate for a normal deplane.

synopsis: An International Relief Officer reported extending his duty day beyond 19 hours as allowed by FAR 117 for a four pilot crew, then prior to landing recognizing his extreme fatigue.
summary: A relief pilot reported being impaired by fatigue after a 21-hour duty day, which exceeded the 19-hour FAR 117 limit due to a 5-hour maintenance delay and a pack failure. The pilot considered the operation unsafe at landing and concluded that extending duty days prevents accurate forecasting of future fatigue levels.

synopsis: A Captain was informed by a Lead Flight Attendant that passengers complained their seat belts were too short on a B757-200 aircraft. After landing, company Technician noted that not only was the hardware the seat belts attach to incorrectly installed, but the seatbelts were also incorrectly positioned at the seats. Captain also raises concerns their maintenance inspection process, at some point, failed to identify and correct the discrepancies.
summary: The Captain reported that after passenger complaints, inspection revealed eight first-class seat belts incorrectly installed with hardware facing aft, shortening them by four inches and invalidating their safety function. The Captain suspects a maintenance contractor failed to follow instructions during a recent C-Check, prompting a recommendation to inspect all belts on the aircraft and fleet.

synopsis: ERJ-170 First Officer continued approach and landing after complying with a momentary 'climb' TCAS RA and subsequently found that company SOP requires a go-around if the aircraft was configured for landing.
summary: The pilot flying received a climb RA during a visual approach while fully configured, but the conflict cleared immediately upon initiating the climb. Although the crew landed safely, they later realized SOPs required a go-around after receiving an RA in landing configuration.

synopsis: CE560XLS First Officer reported encountering a likely frozen pitch trim anomaly on descent. Pitch trim returned to normal operation when they descended to warmer temperatures.
summary: The flight crew experienced a frozen pitch trim malfunction while descending from FL400 to FL340. After executing the jammed trim checklist, the system unfroze at 4,000 feet, allowing for a safe landing with ATC assistance.

synopsis: CRJ900 flight crew is issue direct TORNN on the GUSHR3 arrival to IAH then issued a hold as published at TORNN. The pattern does not look correct, but is correctly entered. ATC agrees and issues vectors to reenter the holding pattern at TORNN. It is discovered that the charted out bound course of 243 degrees is off by 100 degrees at CHMPZ and TORNN. It should be 343 degrees.
summary: The flight crew holding at TORNN on the GUSHR3 arrival to IAH at FL280 entered the pattern west instead of north due to a Jeppesen chart misprint showing an outbound heading of 243 instead of 343. ATC vectored the aircraft back to the arrival after identifying the error, which the crew attributed to the incorrect chart data and delayed clarification.

synopsis: CRJ700 Captain experiences SELCAL chimes during takeoff that nearly lead to a rejected takeoff, due to the high volume and inappropriate timing.
summary: During the initial takeoff roll, pilots received a loud, erroneous SELCAL audio notification indicating the aircraft was out of service, nearly causing an aborted takeoff. The reporter attributes this dangerous disruption to a flawed avionics design that broadcasts excessively loud alerts during critical flight phases.

synopsis: A PA28-181 Instructor reported a violent, very loud slapping noise during descent with the engine instruments indicating normally so he diverted to a nearby airport for a safe landing.
summary: During descent, the pilot experienced violent engine shaking and loud knocking at power settings above 1300 RPM, prompting a diversion to a nearby airport. Although instruments remained normal, the pilot noted a slight oil loss and no external damage after landing.

synopsis: PA44 Instructor with student experiences a possible lightning strike or discharge in the visual traffic pattern causing total electrical failure. The power returns of its own accord during final approach but the gear is extended manually due to tripped circuit breakers. Aircraft is taxied to the ramp for maintenance.
summary: A student pilot and CFI in a training aircraft experienced total electrical failure and landing gear malfunction at 700-800 feet on upwind, attributed to a nearby lightning strike. The crew manually extended the gear after a popped hydraulic pump circuit breaker and landed safely on runway 25L with no injuries.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reported encountering wake turbulence at FL330 from an aircraft at FL340 that resulted in minor injuries to three flight attendants.
summary: During a cruise climb at FL330 near HACKS, the crew encountered sudden moderate turbulence suspected to be wake turbulence from unseen traffic at FL340. Three flight attendants sustained minor injuries while serving in the aisle but declined medical assistance and continued the flight.

synopsis: During descent a B777 TCAS generated an apparent false traffic target and issued a descend command followed by a climb command. ATC reported no traffic in the area so this is an assumed null bus fault.
summary: During descent through FL210, the flight crew received conflicting TCAS RAs showing a target at their own position and altitude. ATC reported no traffic, leading the crew to conclude the TCAS malfunctioned by detecting the aircraft itself, prompting a maintenance write-up.

synopsis: A300 flight crew reported green hydraulic system anomalies and stated the QRH procedure is complex and confusing.
summary: During cruise and approach, the crew experienced sequential Green hydraulic pump failures on an aircraft at FL350 and 11,000 feet. The pilot flying missed a QRH step requiring gravity gear extension because the system remained pressurized by electric pumps, leading to a normal landing despite ambiguous checklist wording.

synopsis: After departing the terminal, a Flight Attendant saw a passenger from the previous flight dump her purse contents on the sidewalk. When asked why, the passenger responded her electronic cigarette's safety was off and it melted some purse contents as she exited the aircraft earlier.
summary: A flight attendant observed a passenger outside the terminal with a smoldering purse caused by an electronic cigarette with its safety switch off. The passenger had dumped the contents after noticing smoke while exiting the aircraft, preventing a potential onboard fire.

synopsis: While reviewing a GE CF-34 Engine Change Job Card and Parts paperwork for an ERJ-175 aircraft at the end of his Nightshift, an Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) realizes he did not have any paperwork for the forward bushings and most likely had not installed them over the forward mount bolts as required. AMT believed not having the bushings in hand and being in a hurry to finish the job 'on time' contributed to his oversight.
summary: A mechanic performing an engine change on an ERJ-175 failed to install forward mount bushings due to missing parts and time pressure. The error was discovered during a self-inspection before logbook sign-off, and Dayshift corrected the issue prior to the aircraft returning to service.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Lead pilot of a warbird formation flight in Washington DC reported he deviated from assigned altitude because of concerns for wake turbulence and bird encounters.
summary: A lead pilot flying a four-ship formation through the Washington DC SFRA descended below briefed altitude and adjusted speed to avoid wake turbulence, birds, and photo ships. The pilot prioritized formation integrity and engine safety over strict adherence to TRACON vectors, citing the aircraft's lack of speed brakes and the risks of rapid power changes.

synopsis: A Pilot on final to APA was asked to slow for departing aircraft, but could not because his aircraft was at approach speed so ATC issued a runway change on very short final creating a perceived unsafe situation for the pilot.
summary: A pilot on final approach was forced to switch runways by a controller to accommodate a VFR single-engine departure, despite already being at approach speed. The pilot reported this unnecessary action created safety risks due to last-minute speed and runway changes, noting the controller appeared dismissive of these concerns.

synopsis: An aircraft on downwind vectors for MEM Runway 18C took evasive action to a TCAS near miss at 3,000 feet.
summary: The crew received a TCAS climb resolution advisory while being vectored to base for Runway 18C at MEM after ATC reported traffic at 1,100 feet without altitude context. The aircraft climbed to avoid the conflict, passing the traffic at a 200-foot separation, and resumed the approach with no further ATC comment.

synopsis: A PA-28 Instructor took the aircraft at 600 feet and returned to land after the engine began running rough and lost power.
summary: The pilot reported that shortly after passing the end of Runway 20 at approximately 600 feet, the engine ran rough, backfired, and lost power. The pilot executed a 180-degree turn to return to Runway 2 and landed safely.

synopsis: A DA-40 Pilot was cleared to taxi to Runway 18L for a midfield takeoff. When cleared for takeoff the Pilot turned left on Runway 36 and as he began his takeoff, Tower said 'Stop' do a 180° and cleared for takeoff. The Pilot had not referenced his compass.
summary: A newly licensed pilot conducting a solo midfield takeoff on runway 18L at ZZZ mistakenly turned left instead of right due to a lack of visual references and failure to verify heading with a compass. The pilot stopped immediately after Tower intervention, turned 180 degrees, and completed a normal takeoff.

synopsis: A PA-31 left engine after lost power and when troubleshooting did not recover it the pilot feathered the engine while level at 1,000 feet preparing to land.
summary: The pilot reported a left engine running rough that lost power during descent, causing a drop in EGT and manifold pressure at 1,000 feet AGL. After troubleshooting failed, the pilot feathered the engine to prevent further altitude loss while approaching the shoreline.

synopsis: After being cleared direct to MLB, a C421 pilot discovers that the autopilot has not maintained the direct course as selected on the Garmin 530 and turns to intercept course. ATC takes note and states that an airliner had been off course in the opposite direction moments before.
summary: The pilot flying a Garmin 530-equipped aircraft deviated right of course while in NAV mode after being cleared direct to MLB. ATC attributed the deviation to a suspected GPS system abnormality affecting multiple aircraft, though the pilot successfully resumed NAV tracking shortly after.

synopsis: A C-402 Pilot forgot to turn the alternators ON after engine start because of a procedural change to leave them off until after engine start and when nearing his destination lost all electrical power with dead batteries. He discovered his error after landing and establish communications with ATC.
summary: The pilot experienced a total electrical failure and radio loss during a visual approach to runway 19 after failing to turn on both alternators post-startup. The pilot completed an uneventful landing using light signals and later restored power via the emergency circuit.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot reported a near miss in VMC with another aircraft in Class E, but not communicating with TRACON.
summary: A pilot and passenger in a VFR flight climbing to 7,500 feet MSL encountered a converging single-engine aircraft at approximately 4,500 feet MSL with a closest distance of 300 feet. The pilot attributed the near-miss to congested airspace, lack of ATC communication, and the other aircraft's poor visibility, though no evasive action was required.

synopsis: A Mooney 20E student pilot under instruction landed gear up. Both the instructor and the student report that they followed checklists and that the green gear down indicator lights were illuminated. Additionally, the student reported that he checked the floor indication that the gear was down and that there were no alarms sounding. ATC had instructed a go around just before the propeller struck the runway.
summary: A student pilot and instructor attempted a normal landing with gear indicators showing down, but the gear failed to extend, causing propeller contact on touchdown. The pilot initiated a go-around after ATC instruction, but the aircraft settled, resulting in an uneventful evacuation with no injuries.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot in the busy, hazy RNT VFR traffic pattern became distracted while concentrating on following traffic and descended to about 200 feet AGL turning base.
summary: The pilot descended too low to approximately 200 feet AGL while turning base in hazy conditions due to a fixation on following traffic and flying a tight pattern. The pilot recovered by adding power to regain altitude and completed a normal landing, citing loss of situational awareness as the primary cause.

synopsis: A Quality Assurance Inspector reports a company helicopter departed with a Supplemental Type Certificate (STC) not complied with, resulting in a Return to Service (RTS) of their AS350 Eurocopter without proper maintenance documentation or project completion and Part 135 Operations Manual and Repair Station procedures not being followed. Management had insisted the aircraft depart even with an incomplete STC and FAA Form 337.
summary: A mechanic installed incomplete broadcasting equipment on a helicopter under management pressure, departing without a completed FAA Form 337. The pilot ignored the mechanic's warning, resulting in an unauthorized return to service that violated repair station procedures and Part 135 operations manuals.

synopsis: F11 Approach Controller reports of the Tower waiting to change the runway of an arrival that was catching the preceding arrival. The second aircraft was changed to a parallel runway and landed safely.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored Aircraft Y to follow Aircraft X on a visual approach to Runway 18R but delayed issuing a runway change until Aircraft Y was below 1,100 feet and two miles out. The reporter claims the tower controller intentionally created an unsafe, unstable approach by failing to offer the available Runway 18L sooner.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier descending into ABQ was given a descent clearance to 5,000 ft, but when the Captain asked ATC if 5,000 ft was correct they were assigned 8,500 ft. ABQ field elevation is 5,315 ft.
summary: During a high-workload descent into ABQ with weather deviations, the crew queried ATC after receiving a 5000-foot clearance below field elevation. The controller immediately amended the clearance to 8500 feet, allowing the crew to complete the approach and land uneventfully.

synopsis: A B737-700 crew on the SILCN 1 arrival was high approaching KLIDE event though the FMC indicated the aircraft was on the VNAV path. NCT stated they have seen the same result with other aircraft.
summary: Pilots flying the SJC SILCN 1 Arrival to Runway 30L found the aircraft approximately 3,000 feet high on the glidepath at waypoint SSEBB due to a lack of hard altitude constraints. The crew received a vector from ATC to assist descent and landed without incident, recommending a hard 4,000-foot altitude at KLIDE to fix the profile.

synopsis: During takeoff above 100 knots a B737-700 encountered a windshear with 30-40kt airspeed fluctuation. Maximum thrust was maintained and aircraft turned away from mountains and out of maintain wave area.
summary: During takeoff roll above 100 knots, erratic airspeed indicators and wind shear caused the crew to delay rotation and turn away from mountains. The pilot applied full power, advised ATC of the maneuver, and maintained takeoff configuration until clear of the shear with no complications.

synopsis: A Dispatcher reported major weather disruptions in the New York and Washington DC areas caused his flights arriving into those areas to overload him making it impossible to release some of his flight.
summary: A dispatcher relieving a colleague during scattered convection affecting NY/DC arrivals struggled to manage 16 airborne flights and 193 ATC advisories. Due to the volume of reroutes and weather, the dispatcher diverted within 90 minutes and could not release flights even after three were removed from their desk.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Ramp service was able to stop in order to avoid a collision with an aircraft which taxied around a corner during push back from ORD C Concourse.
summary: Ramp Service Employees pushing an aircraft from the C Concourse nearly collided with another aircraft that appeared around a corner. The employees stopped the pushback in time to avoid a collision.

synopsis: A Ramp Service Employee reported new procedures require chock prepositioning on the ramp in front of the engines which is an ingestion safety hazard for both personnel and chocks when the engines may be left running for minutes after gate arrival.
summary: Ramp personnel reported that current procedures require placing chocks in front of arriving aircraft engines, creating an ingestion hazard while engines run and visibility is blocked. The previous procedure placed chocks outside the safety zone near wingtips and aft of the engines.

synopsis: A heavy jet Captain on the PHL JIMMS 2 RNAV Arrival took evasive action to a momentarily TCAS RA DESCEND command followed by a CLIMB command. The climb from the other IFR traffic was to about 6400 ft before returning to 6000 ft.
summary: The pilot reported a TCAS RA conflict at 6000 ft on the JIIMS2 arrival while under ATC control. The pilot executed a climb to 6400 ft per SOPs after the other aircraft reduced separation, noting ATC provided no communication regarding the event.

synopsis: An A319 Captain reported taking evasive action to an EGPWS alert level at 5,000 feet preparing for an approach to MDPC/PUJ Runway 9. The NAVIGATIONAL TERRAIN Display did not activate.
summary: Pilots experienced a GPWS "Terrain Pull up" warning while descending toward MDPC with the TERR button active but no terrain displayed. They executed a 1.5 G climb to 5,000 feet and completed a normal landing.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An aircraft departed JNU Runway 26 after helicopter traffic but at a 3,500-4,000 FPM climb rate was only able to take modified evasive action from the TCAS RA 'DESCEND NOW' command. The First Officer reports the traffic 3,000 ft abeam.
summary: During a Part 121 takeoff from Runway 26 at Juneau, a high climb rate caused a closure with a helicopter north of the Runway 8 localizer, triggering a "Descend now" RA. The crew manually reduced pitch and banked left to comply, noting that current clearances allow unsafe proximity between merging flight paths.

synopsis: A MD-83 CADC DATA 1, CADC DATA 2 and MACH TRIM COMPENSATOR Fail lights alerted at the same time the autothrottles disconnected and the ENGINE ANTI-ICE VALVE alerted. The radar was not painting weather but ice was accumulating on the window. After entering VMC conditions all systems returned to normal indicating a potentially overwhelmed pitot anti-ice system.
summary: The First Officer hand-flew the aircraft at FL330 in IMC and turbulence when CADC data failures caused autopilot disconnect and unreliable airspeed indications, leading to an uncommanded descent. Suspecting an icing event, the crew descended to FL310, executed memory items, and continued to destination once all systems returned to normal.

synopsis: DA40 Instructor pilot reports a NMAC with a drone at 6,500 feet beneath PHX Class B airspace.
summary: A pilot on a training cruise flight at 6,500 feet west of Rio Verde reported a quad-copter drone passing 50 feet to the left. The pilot notified PHX approach of the encounter.

synopsis: C182 pilot experiences loss of GPS NAV capability while flying south bound beneath the SEA Class B airspace and believes he may have entered a MOA while attempting to navigate using paper charts.
summary: A VFR pilot flying to OLM south of SEA-TAC experienced a GPS freeze and switched to paper charts. The pilot skirted around MOAs southeast of SEA and east of TCM, noting a possible inadvertent entry into one.

synopsis: An RV4 still in the flight hour testing program before certification took off on its third flight and the engine quit at 10 feet above the runway. The pilot landed safely, was able to restart the engine, and taxi to Maintenance.
summary: The pilot of an experimental aircraft experienced an engine failure at 10 feet AGL during the third takeoff. The pilot landed safely, restarted the engine on the taxiway, and taxied to the ramp for maintenance after a post-event run-up showed no anomalies.

synopsis: A B737-400 landing gear extended uncommanded during descent through 9,000 ft as the aircraft was slowing to 210 kts. Safe indications resulted with the QRH execution.
summary: The pilot monitoring reported an uncommanded gear extension while descending through 9000 ft to 6000 ft with the handle in the OFF position. After completing the QRH procedure, the gear lights turned green when the handle was moved to DOWN, and the flight landed safely.

synopsis: Decathlon instructor pilot reports being issued two 360 degree turns on the downwind for spacing for an inbound T38. During the maneuvers the student allows his aircraft to drift into the final approach course and a NMAC results.
summary: An instructor and student in a Super Decathlon experienced a close call with a T38 during touch-and-goes at an airport with nonfunctional primary radar. The incident occurred after the controller issued conflicting downwind instructions, causing the aircraft to drift near the runway centerline while a T38 passed uncomfortably close below.

synopsis: ZOA Controller states that many controllers at his facility are lax in their knowledge of NOTAMs that pertain to the sectors that they are controlling, especially when it comes to GPS jamming NOTAMs.
summary: An air traffic controller discovered GPS jamming NOTAMs affecting RNAV approaches after a certification check supervisor dismissed the hazard. The reporter attributed the oversight to controllers failing to read NOTAMs or update the SIA board, urging management to enforce these safety procedures.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: An AZO Tower Controller tells an aircraft to maintain VFR on the go-around due to a gear problem. The Controller is confused after the aircraft lands in that he told the aircraft to maintain VFR and cancelled his IFR clearance.
summary: An air traffic controller managed Aircraft X's go-around and holding pattern due to a landing gear issue on a visual approach to RWY 35. The controller later realized instructing the IFR flight to maintain VFR was a procedural error, though the aircraft landed safely with emergency services standing by.

synopsis: ZNY Controller describes a situation where an aircraft shows up on his frequency without his knowledge. The aircraft wasn't handed off or coordinated with N90. Controller had to figure out where aircraft was going and attempt to get it there. Another data tag of the same call sign added to the problem.
summary: Aircraft X departed JFK climbing to FL120 without a manual handoff from N90 under a new procedure, resulting in conflicting flight plans and unclear track control. The situation remained unresolved despite supervisor assistance and manual coordination with R86, which the controller attributed to procedural regression and a culture prioritizing speed over data accuracy.

synopsis: A80 Departure Control in Charge (CIC) requests a single flow off of ATL airport due to weather. He coordinates with the Tower and reports that after the coordination the departures are still coming off the airport as normal operations dictate.
summary: The CIC Departure requested single headings for south and north departures to merge traffic and avoid weather, but the Tower supervisor refused. This refusal caused aircraft to continue on RNAV departures despite safety concerns, which the reporter states detrimentally impacted the operation.

synopsis: A Large Transport Aircraft was high on the SILCN 1 arrival profile because the ILS 30 transition point is GILRO which occurs after the common SILCN 1 to ILS 30 transition point KLIDE. Therefore the FMC will fly from KLIDE to GILRO to KLIDE which requires the additional altitude.
summary: The flight crew flying the SILCN 1 arrival into SJC encountered a steep descent profile after ATC cleared them to maintain FL200 instead of the fix's FL200A restriction. The crew manually adjusted speed and removed altitude constraints to regain profile, recommending a procedure update to prevent future deviations.

synopsis: An A320 Captain noted that departing DEN Runway 08 at night, only 2,000 to 3,000 feet of centerline lights preceding the aircraft are visible. The runway end alternating red and white lights are not visible until approaching them.
summary: A pilot departing Denver Runway 08 at night reported that runway centerline lights were only visible for 2,000 to 3,000 feet, obscuring the alternating red and white lights at the runway end. This limited visibility could hinder directional control during an engine-out situation, a condition other pilots have also observed at Denver.

synopsis: An A320 Captain noted that when his flight release is revised, his air carrier's revised SABRE flight plan briefing packages do not always include the alternate's weather and NOTAM information.
summary: A pilot reported that after swapping an A320 during preflight, the Sabre Briefing Package for Flight XXX contained the old aircraft's log and DIL while missing weather and NOTAMs for a new alternate. The pilot attributed this recurring error to the Sabre Flight Planning Program failing to update documentation following aircraft changes.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reports becoming distracted during taxi out at ORD due to an estimated departure clearance time and a departure runway change. Takeoff data for Runway 9L is inadvertently requested and used for takeoff from Runway 9R. Both crew members detect the error during the takeoff roll and elect to continue due to 9R being longer than 9L.
summary: The Captain and First Officer departed ORD on Runway 9R but loaded FMC data for Runway 9L due to distractions, time pressure, and unfamiliarity with new runway names. They continued the takeoff after realizing the error at 100 knots, determining a high-speed abort was unsafe given the correct flap setting and conservative performance data.

synopsis: EMB-170 flight crew describes the scenario leading up to a runway incursion at DCA.
summary: The flight crew at DCA mistakenly crossed Runway 1 while configuring for Runway 33, believing they had a clearance to cross Runway 1 instead of Runway 4. This runway incursion occurred due to a misheard ATC instruction, causing a CRJ to reject its takeoff before the crew was stopped and directed to the correct runway.

synopsis: Passing FL180 in the climb, an EMB145 First Officer notices that his altimeter STD/local reset button is missing from the Primary Flight Display (PFD) control panel, along with the slip indicator. The First Officer's PFD bezel had recently been removed and replaced by Maintenance.
summary: The First Officer and Captain discovered a missing slip indicator and STD button on the #2 PFD while climbing through 18,000 feet, caused by an incorrect bezel replacement. The omission was attributed to the indicator's location behind the control column, pre-flight distractions, and failure to check the maintenance log.

synopsis: Captain reports the right elevator was moving an abnormal amount with the gust lock engaged on a DHC-8-100 aircraft. Maintenance Control placed the malfunctioning gust lock under a Non-Essential Function (NEF) MEL 26-6 deferral stating the mechanical problem was not a safety of flight issue. Pilot refuses aircraft. Maintenance later finds elevator gust lock spring lock plunger binding, sticking.
summary: The Captain reported abnormal flight control movement with the gust lock engaged after landing, but Maintenance Control and mechanics initially dismissed the issue and deferred it under an inappropriate MEL. The flight was canceled after the Chief Pilot confirmed the defect did not affect airworthiness, though the Captain attributed the mishandling to company performance pressures.

synopsis: During climb through FL360, M.74 a Falcon 2000 slats extended uncommanded with no abnormal handling characteristics. During descent to a divert airport, the slats retracted at about FL250. An uneventful landing was accomplished.
summary: During climb, both slats extended without command, and flaps retracted automatically through FL250. The crew followed the checklist, diverted to a nearby airport with long runways, and completed an uneventful approach and landing.

synopsis: A B767 flight crew failed to complete the Before Takeoff checklist due to distractions and discovered that the flaps were not set for takeoff when the Takeoff Warning horn sounded.
summary: Fatigued pilots experienced distractions from taxi instructions, construction, and a last-minute runway change, causing them to advance thrust with flaps not set for takeoff. The crew rejected the takeoff, corrected the flap setting, and successfully departed after clearing the runway for landing traffic.

synopsis: A321 flight crew describes a transcontinental flight that is circuitous due to weather and then is assigned holding during the arrival. The flight crew plans a diversion and informs ATC of minimum fuel, at the same time the flight attendants inform of an ill passenger. Clearance to the original destination is then received without delay. The close in ninety degree intercept of the localizer results in an unstabilized approach that is continued to landing.
summary: A new Airbus crew faced fuel concerns and a medical emergency after ATC delays and holding, leading to an unstable ILS approach where the glide slope was not captured by 1,000 feet. The Captain knowingly violated stable approach SOPs to avoid a go-around due to low fuel and fatigue, but the aircraft stabilized at 800 feet for a safe landing.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An aircraft with SNA as its destination was being vectored to an LGB final when the crew finally questioned the Controller who had become confused about the flight's destination. The flight was climbed and returned to SNA.
summary: The flight crew and approach controller were involved during descent to SNA when the controller mistakenly vectored the aircraft toward LGB. The crew delayed questioning the conflicting clearance until a wrong turn was issued, resulting in a climb to 3,000 feet and a corrected approach after the controller apologized.

synopsis: A reporter states that a VFR aircraft, after being terminated for flight following, enters a restricted area. A call in the blind is answered by the VFR pilot and is told that they entered the restricted area. The pilot disagrees and says the altitude that is not is higher than they are. The Controller disagrees and advises the pilot. The pilot finds out that the depiction on his GPS system is incorrect.
summary: Aircraft X entered R-5314J while descending to 3,500 feet, causing a near-midair conflict with Aircraft Y. The pilot mistakenly believed the airspace started at 6,000 feet based on a GPS display that omitted the lower R-5314J boundaries.

synopsis: A DA2000 flight crew reports inadvertently selecting the ILS for Runway 27L when cleared for the ILS 27R. The flight is issued a go-around for spacing issues before the error becomes apparent. On the next approach the error becomes apparent to ATC and the crew eventually corrects the ILS 27R.
summary: The flight crew inadvertently selected the ILS 27L frequency instead of 27R after a go-around, causing them to fly south of course. The error resulted from failing to re-brief the approach and relying on the FMS without verifying the frequency, though they corrected it and landed safely.

synopsis: SF34 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence on arrival to MIA in trail of a B757 which resulted in altitude and track deviations.
summary: Pilots on a visual approach to MIA runway 8L encountered severe wake turbulence from a preceding B757 at 11 miles out. The turbulence caused an unintended 1000 ft climb, a 10 kt airspeed increase, and a 7-second loss of heading control before the aircraft stabilized and landed normally.

synopsis: PA28 instructor pilot reports taking evasive action at 800 feet AGL while turning downwind, to avoid a Bellanca entering the pattern on the crosswind. The Bellanca pilot had made one radio transmission enquiring about the active runway without stating his position.
summary: An instructor pilot on an instructional flight at FHB avoided a near mid-air collision with a student pilot by taking controls and descending after the student entered the pattern without stating position. The incident was caused by the student's poor radio communication and lack of situational awareness regarding the active runway.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot experiences a NMAC on short final for Runway 30 at EUL with an aircraft departing Runway 12. No CTAF report was made by the aircraft departing Runway 12 and the pattern was full of aircraft landing Runway 30. The reporter side steps to the right then goes around.
summary: The pilot reported a near-midair conflict at uncontrolled EUL while on final for Runway 30 with a high-wing aircraft departing Runway 12. The pilot aborted the landing due to the other aircraft's lack of radio transmissions, lights, and avoidance maneuvers in a congested environment with mixed helicopter and fixed-wing traffic.

synopsis: ZNY Controller reports of an airspace that is going to become hot. He coordinates with the airspace authority to have one last aircraft go through this airspace, which is approved. Minutes later the Controller sees targets entering the area going towards his pointed out aircraft. Coordination ensues, and his aircraft is still approved into the airspace. His aircraft is stopped above the other targets and the pilot reports a RA due to the fast moving targets.
summary: A radar controller and Giant Killer managed Aircraft X near W-107 airspace when military targets unexpectedly headed toward the aircraft instead of eastbound. The controller stopped Aircraft X's descent after an RA alert triggered a climb to FL220, attributing the incident to poor communication between Giant Killer and the military pilots.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ORL Tower Controllers report of a NMAC involving a VFR departure clear of the Class Delta but in the Class Bravo and an IFR arrival inbound. TRACON did not issue traffic to the arrival, and called to alert the Tower. Tower was unable to call traffic before the inbound aircraft responded to a RA.
summary: Aircraft Y (VFR) and Aircraft X (visual approach) experienced a near-miss at ORL due to a missed traffic advisory before a frequency change. Aircraft X executed a TCAS RA climb, but both aircraft landed or continued without incident.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: An S46 Controller reports of working an aircraft and then getting busy with other traffic. The aircraft enters Class Delta Airspace and the Controller fails to notice this. The Controller was working combined airspace and this aircraft was inside another Controller's airspace and not handed off to him.
summary: An air traffic controller managing multiple arrival positions at SeaTac failed to notice Aircraft X penetrating McChord Air Force Base Class D airspace due to high workload and lack of route information. The controller eventually coordinated a handoff to the North position and McChord Tower after being alerted by the CIC.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reached the end of the EMZOH RNAV Arrival having just received further clearance for an instrument approach. Crew was programming the FMC for the cleared approach procedure as the aircraft arrived at the end of the RNAV approach. Erroneous programming by the crew resulted in a turn not cleared by ATC.
summary: The crew executing an EMZOH 1 RNAV arrival into OAK deviated from course after a late ILS 30 clearance caused an LNAV disconnect and incorrect FMC entry. The Captain corrected the turn following ATC vectors, resulting in an uneventful landing with no loss of separation.

synopsis: A B737 Captain is queried by ATC about not descending quickly enough to make the instrument approach into SJC and a vector is accepted. The SILCN1 STAR had been connected to the ILS 30L approach at KLIDE without removing the GILRO fix producing extra mileage and a late descent.
summary: The Pilot Flying and First Officer on an RNAV (Z) 30L approach to SJC experienced a 3,000-foot altitude deviation after the FO inadvertently selected a non-existent GILRO transition. The crew accepted an ATC vector to correct the path, and the First Officer later admitted he failed to immediately correct the FMC error during the descent.

synopsis: A Captain and First Officer report of a loud noise and vibration felt just after takeoff on a B777 aircraft. The noise continued and became so loud the crew had to yell at other flight deck crewmembers. Fuel was dumped and aircraft returned to departure airport. Maintenance found a connecting rod for the Nose Landing Gear (NLG) right door had disconnected from the NLG.
summary: The flight crew experienced loud noise and vibration after takeoff caused by a disconnected nose gear door rod. They returned to ZZZ for an overweight landing after dumping fuel, with maintenance confirming the rod had unscrewed from the nose wheel door bolt.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer experiences a NMAC with a helicopter at 700 feet AGL on final approach. The traffic was not called out by the Tower, but the helicopter had been instructed to pass behind the reporters' aircraft.
summary: Pilots on a visual approach to runway 23 received a TCAS traffic advisory at 700 feet AGL for a helicopter passing above and in front of them. The tower failed to provide traffic information, later claiming the helicopter was supposed to pass behind the aircraft.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reports getting low during a night visual approach from the downwind position. ATC is the first to detect that the crew has descended out of 3,000 feet prematurely.
summary: The pilot misread the Final Approach Fix altitude during a night visual approach to MCI at 3,000 feet, causing an early descent. After ATC noted the aircraft was low, the pilot climbed to re-establish the profile, intercepted the glide slope, and landed normally.

synopsis: ERJ-170 crew inadvertently took off overweight when the ground crew failed to communicate the correct number and location of all gate-checked bags.
summary: The flight crew and ramp agent misinterpreted a confusing load report, resulting in approximately 20 unlisted gate-checked bags being loaded in the aft cargo bin. This error likely caused the aircraft to exceed maximum takeoff weight and balance limits, forcing the crew to burn fuel before departure to comply with weight restrictions.

synopsis: A Captain expresses his concerns about the 'quickness' that Maintenance had performed on a Bird Strike Inspection on # 2 Engine for an A320 aircraft, without any reference procedure noted in the Logbook sign-off. Adding to his concerns, was his Air Carrier's removal of a previous requirement that an Airworthiness Release also be issued after a Bird Strike Inspection.
summary: The First Officer reported bird strike damage on the #2 engine during pre-flight, but Maintenance signed the aircraft "ok for flight" after a brief inspection. The pilot suspects the inspection was inadequate and notes questionable logbook entries regarding landing gear safety devices, fearing potential future engine failure.

synopsis: Gulfstream IV Captain experiences a 'STAB/FLAP Fail' ECIAS message at FL430. The crew elects to divert to the nearest suitable airport and execute a no flap landing to avoid disturbing the stabilizer through the flap inter connect. Passing FL200 the indication disappears and an uneventful no flap landing ensues.
summary: During climb to FL430, the crew experienced a flickering 'STAB/FLAP Fail' ECIAS message and a non-zero stabilizer indication, prompting a diversion for a precautionary zero-flap landing. The warning extinguished below FL200, and the crew completed an uneventful ILS approach with 160 KIAS minimum speed, though the cause remained undetermined.

synopsis: After commencing takeoff roll, CRJ-200 crew noticed an aircraft about to enter the runway and rejected the takeoff.
summary: The flight crew aborted takeoff from Runway 1 below 80 kts after another aircraft attempted to cross due to a mistaken clearance readback for a different flight. The intruding aircraft stopped before entering the runway, and the incident was resolved without injury or damage.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew and a dispatcher describe a flight to MDPC that is rerouted over the WATRS area by ATC. The crew accepts the clearance before realizing a HF radio is required to fly this route. Significant time is required to get the flight routed back into VHF range.
summary: A dispatcher and flight crew involved a flight to MDPC that entered the WATRS without required HF radio due to dispatcher task saturation and unclear FOM language. The crew eventually coordinated with ATC to reroute the aircraft back toward the coast and into radar coverage.

synopsis: A B747 First Officer experiences pressurization anomalies from right after liftoff and throughout the seven hour flight. The pressurization system will only operate in manual mode and then with occasional erratic climbs and descents of the cabin altitude. The problem had been written up numerous times and never properly repaired.
summary: During departure and cruise, the relief First Officer and Pilot Monitoring manually controlled pressurization after the left outflow valve failed and automatic systems became unresponsive. The mechanic confirmed multiple system failures, attributing the loss of automatic control to a history of uncorrected maintenance issues on this aircraft.

synopsis: Upon reaching cruise altitude, flight crew smelled fumes and received call from Flight Attendant alerting them to smoke in the cabin. Crew performed Smoke and Fumes Checklist and returned to departure airport.
summary: The flight crew detected smoke from a business class seat shortly after reaching initial cruise altitude. They returned to the departure airport, exceeded 250 KIAS below 10,000 feet, and performed an uneventful landing after running emergency checklists.

synopsis: B757 flight crew reports a loud impact on the left radome, from a large bird at 7,000 feet. Initially no anomalies are detected but then the flight attendants report a strange sound and a strong vibration coming from the left engine. The crew also feels the vibration and elects to return to the departure airport.
summary: During climb out at 7,000 feet, the flight crew suspected a bird strike after hearing an impact and seeing a white object. Subsequent left engine vibration and N3 indicator spikes prompted a return for an overweight landing, where ARFF inspected the engine and gear before the aircraft proceeded to the gate.

synopsis: A CE560 Captain landing at ZZZ experiences a conflict with an Air Tractor taking off in the opposite direction. The flying First Officer breaks right and goes around and the Air Tractor continues its takeoff. The Air Tractor pilot apparently had no radio and was taking off downwind.
summary: A Part 91 Citation crew conducting an IFR approach to Runway 20 at ZZZ executed a go-around after a Part 137 Air Tractor took off downwind from Runway 20. The reporter attributes the near mid-air collision to the agricultural operator's failure to monitor CTAF and violation of right-of-way rules.

synopsis: C172 pilot reports landing at EFT at night and discovering that the runway is closed. After taxi back and assessing the runway condition, takeoff is initiated. The closure had a NOTAM, but not noticed by the reporter.
