The indications of closure were unlighted cones on the connecting taxiways and an unlighted yellow X outside of the touch down zone, none of which were detected prior to landing.
summary: A pilot flying a Cessna 172 unknowingly landed on closed Runway 2 at EFT during a cross-country flight to DPA. The incident resulted from failing to review current NOTAMs and was compounded by unlit cones, an off-threshold closure X, and no AWOS remark indicating the runway closure.

synopsis: Citation flight crew experiences moderate to severe turbulence at FL180 for 15 seconds that apparently causes both Garmins to shut down. This eliminates both Navigation and Communication and will not reset. The crew elects to remain VFR, squawk 7600, and divert to a suitable airport. When the aircraft is powered back up for trouble-shooting the Garmins work normally.
summary: During an IFR flight to HYI, the crew encountered severe turbulence while deviating around storms, causing both Garmin 530 and 430 units to blank due to an internal 5G switch activation. The pilots squawked 7600, descended to VMC, and landed at a nearby airport before recovering avionics power and continuing VFR.

synopsis: SR20 instructor pilot experiences an NMAC with an IFR aircraft that had been pointed out by ATC immediately prior to flight following being canceled. On board, Skywatch re-alerted the reporter to the proximity of the intruder and allowed for visual acquisition and avoidance.
summary: An instructor pilot conducting a VMC instructional flight to BTL experienced a near collision after canceling flight following and becoming distracted by ATIS issues. The pilot avoided the northeast-bound traffic only after an onboard Skywatch alert, attributing the incident to lost visual scanning and timing of the flight following cancellation.

synopsis: Shorts 360 Captain experiences an engine failure at 12000 feet and diverts to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced an unannounced #1 engine failure at 12,000 feet during a routine reposition flight. They diverted to ZZZ, landed safely single-engine, and found excessive oil at the rear of the engine nacelle upon inspection.

synopsis: ZMP Controllers describe the radar being released to Maintenance for a specific time, then realized that they shouldn't be operating drones in the airspace if they don't have radar. Controllers then advise they get the radar back in service. Controllers state it is a big push to get drones integrated into the NAS, yet very little thought is being given to provide the controllers specific procedures.
summary: An air traffic controller in Sector 24 could not clear Aircraft X into restricted airspace R5402 due to a Finley Radar outage preventing drone monitoring. The incident highlighted a lack of approved non-radar routes for drone integration, raising safety concerns about operating without radar surveillance.

synopsis: A B767-300 flight crew experienced a 'too low gear' GPWS warning at 200 feet AGL and went around. The gear indicators showed the gear to be down and three green. The next approach was uneventful.
summary: The crew received a false "TOO LOW, GEAR" warning at 200 feet AGL during an ILS approach with gear down and locked. They executed a go-around, found no system discrepancies, and completed a second uneventful landing.

synopsis: A330-300 First Officer reported airspeed fluctuation on approach probably due to wake vortex encounter caused by a heavy aircraft ahead.
summary: During approach at 1200 feet, an A-330 crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding heavy aircraft, triggering a false reactive windshear warning and momentary airspeed drop. The pilots did not execute a go-around, suspecting the warning resulted from turbulence-induced speed fluctuation rather than actual windshear.

synopsis: Q400 Captain is advised by the tug driver that he is cleared to start number two engine and the starter is engaged. Within a few seconds the tug driver announces that the engine is not clear and to shut it down. The engine never lit off and the propeller never turned. After arriving at the destination, the Captain has a cell phone message from the Duty Manager indicating that the reporter 'started an engine without clearance and a ramper had to run for his life.'
summary: The pilot and First Officer attempted to start engine 2 after the ramper initially cleared them, but aborted when the ramper immediately retracted clearance due to a perceived propeller obstruction. The crew completed the abort checklist with no fuel flow or engine ignition, resulting in no injuries or damage despite a subsequent safety report alleging the ramper had to run for his life.

synopsis: A pilot reported that the North Atlantic Plotting Chart date March 2014 did not include EGGX airspace entry waypoints RESNO and NETKI. The waypoints were in the FMC and on the flight plan.
summary: The pilot reported that NATS exit points RESNO and NETKI were missing from current plotting charts, though they appeared on older charts, the flight plan, and the current FMC NAV database. No operational incident occurred, but the chart discrepancy was noted.

synopsis: An Air Carrier Captain experiences a Runway Awareness and Advisory System (RAAS) warning 'ON TAXIWAY ON TAXIWAY' while attempting to takeoff on Runway 23L at RCTP from the S10 taxiway. The warning is ignored as the runway has a displaced threshold for landing that does not apply to aircraft taking off.
summary: The flight crew experienced a false Runway Awareness and Advisory System (RAAS) "ON TAXIWAY" alert during takeoff from Runway 23L due to a displaced threshold. The reporter attributes the nuisance alert to incorrect RAAS/EGPWS database programming and recommends a system fix or crew notification.

synopsis: A BE36 pilot reports encountering snow and turbulence at 9,000 feet causing an autopilot disconnect that is not noticed. ATC does notice and a climb back to 9,000 is initiated before very low airspeed is detected. A rapid descent to 4,000 feet is initiated and ATC is advised. Lack of pitot heat was the likely cause of the low airspeed indication and the flight is able to continue to destination.
summary: The pilot, flying in IMC at 9,000 feet, lost autopilot due to turbulence and experienced a rapid airspeed drop caused by an unheated, ice-plugged pitot tube. Fearing a stall, the pilot descended to 4,000 feet to regain visual contact and control before continuing to the destination.

synopsis: After a steep and fast approach, a C210 pilot reports initiating a go around and retracting the gear. Shortly after, the engine quits. With insufficient time to extend the gear, a belly landing ensues on the remaining runway.
summary: The pilot executed a go-around during approach, retracted the gear, and suffered an engine failure, forcing a gear-up landing. The pilot attributed the engine failure to an overdue annual inspection and recommended delaying gear retraction after power application to mitigate future risks.

synopsis: PA32 pilot reports encountering severe rain and turbulence during an RNAV 20 approach to MKL. Control of the aircraft is momentarily lost along with 1800 feet of altitude. At 1200 feet the reporter is able to regain control, climb to 2000 feet and complete the approach. Communication with ATC is lost when the mic cord becomes unplugged during the turbulence.
summary: A pilot flying an IFR GPS approach to MKL encountered severe turbulence and downdrafts, causing an unusual attitude and altitude loss to 1200 feet. The pilot also lost radio contact due to a disconnected mic plug but recovered and completed the approach after re-establishing communication.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: C525 is informed by ATC prior to descent into SLC that GPS jamming is occurring and a non RNAV arrival is assigned. After landing the NOTAMs are checked and none can be found for the jamming event.
summary: The flight crew experienced GPS signal jamming and lost both GPS systems while descending for a non-RNAV arrival at Salt Lake City. They completed an uneventful landing using DME/DME and VORs, noting the lack of NOTAMs regarding the GPS outage.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A Front Line Manager (FLM) describes a situation where a VFR pilot is stuck above the clouds and cannot find a hole to get VFR through. The FLM queries all sectors to see if any of them are VFR. The FLM then searches the control room and finds a controller who is a pilot, and familiar with this type of aircraft. The controller gets the aircraft though the clouds into VFR conditions and the plane lands safely.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller assisted a pilot of Aircraft X who was lost in clouds above 14,000 AGL without oxygen. A certified instructor controller guided the pilot to descend to 5,000 AGL, allowing the aircraft to break out of clouds and land VFR.

synopsis: CNO Controller reports of an airspace violation and an airborne conflict caused by the overlying TRACON not giving them a point out or remaining clear of the Tower's airspace.
summary: SCT controllers failed to alert CNO controllers about Aircraft X, which passed within 100 feet vertically and half a mile horizontally of Aircraft Y on final approach to Runway 26R. The reporter attributes this near-miss to SCT's daily airspace violations and lack of traffic advisories for inbound RAL traffic.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A LEX Tower Controller reports of an airborne conflict that traffic has been issued to. One of the two aircraft sees the other. The other aircraft gets an RA and descends. Legal separation was continued but the Controller is reporting that this type of conflict happens all the time in the Class C environment. The Controller is concerned about the 'boy yelling wolf' scenario that pilots might lose faith in the RA System.
summary: Aircraft X and Y operated in Class C airspace near LEX while maintaining 500 feet vertical separation. Aircraft X received a TCAS Resolution Advisory and descended despite no loss of separation, causing the pilot confusion over the unwarranted alert.

synopsis: A New York Center (ZNY) Controller reports of a SOP violation caused by another sector not descending an aircraft to the appropriate altitude which, in turn, caused multiple conflictions for the receiving Controller.
summary: R86 controller Aircraft X through R66 airspace without altitude restrictions to maintain in-trail spacing, ignoring SOPs and coordination requirements. This created a dangerous conflict requiring R66 to vector Aircraft Z away from Aircraft X to ensure separation.

synopsis: LGB Tower Controller reports of a session where the other Local Controller did not follow the SOP and/or the 7110.65 for the safe separation of traffic. The other local had a loss of separation with an aircraft on the runway and one over the landing threshold, and advised the landing aircraft to hold short of a runway. This was against the LAHSO rules and the SOP.
summary: Local Control 1 cleared Aircraft Z for takeoff on Runway 25R with insufficient separation from Aircraft A on final, then directed Aircraft A to land on Runway 30 despite a crosswind and LAHSO ineligibility. The reporting controller cancelled Aircraft X's takeoff to avoid conflict, citing a need for recurrent training on separation and coordination.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A New York Center (ZNY) Controller reports of an aircraft altitude being displayed on his scope. The Controller finds out who is working the aircraft and then accepts a point out on it. The Controller reports that the aircraft's route was on its fourth amendment and on a Tower En-route Clearance (TEC) due to the Traffic Management Unit (TMU) dropping the altitude to 6,000 feet due to heavy restrictions caused by weather.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller in Sector 39 identified a Traffic Management Coordinator data block for an aircraft on a fourth-amended TEC routing due to weather restrictions. The report attributes the issue to late frequency changes during training and a lack of coordination regarding altitude reductions between the Traffic Management Unit and feeding sectors.

synopsis: An LGB Controller reports of an airborne conflict caused by his lackadaisical scan. He departed a jet off of runway 30 then departed a helicopter moments later. The helicopter's path crossed the departing jet's causing the conflict. The jet had to maneuver away from the helicopter. The pilots' report of the same scenario.
summary: Local Control cleared a helicopter from a helipad intersecting Runway 30 while Aircraft X was taking off, causing Aircraft X to turn right to avoid the helicopter. The controller attributed the conflict to a lackadaisical scan and failure to check the runway before issuing the helicopter clearance.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Southern California TRACON (SCT) Controller reports of read back that was a caused an operational error. The pilot did not read back key words and because of this the Controller is charged with a loss of separation.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a visual approach clearance with wake turbulence caution to Aircraft X approaching Runway 25L behind a heavy Airbus. The pilot failed to read back the clearance correctly, prompting the controller to criticize degraded frequency discipline and the risk of invalidating separation standards, though Aircraft X landed without incident.

synopsis: A319 Captain and First Officer both experience password issues and are unable to access their iPads in flight.
summary: The Captain and First Officer were locked out of their iPads due to password issues during a flight involving a hydraulic problem. This prevented access to the Flight Manual and Bulletins, leaving the crew feeling unsafe while managing the hydraulic emergency.

synopsis: MD82 flight crew experiences a right reverser unlock light at 85 knots and rejects the takeoff.
summary: The crew aborted takeoff at 90 knots on a 140,000 lb aircraft after the right engine reverser unlock light illuminated. The aircraft stopped safely, and fire services inspected the brakes, which reached 300 degrees, before the crew taxied to the gate.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: The reporter stated a ground employee's hat was sucked into a pack inlet during ground operations.
summary: A ground employee kneeling under the fuselage to unhook an AC air hose had their hat sucked into the operating left air pack unit intake. Tech Ops opened the unit to retrieve the hat, resulting in no injuries or aircraft damage.

synopsis: A CRJ Captain reports a fuel truck driver not yielding as they were turning into the ramp. The aircraft is stopped and as the truck passes by the driver appears to be fully engrossed in his cell phone.
summary: The Captain and First Officer were taxiing a Boeing 737 southbound at Philadelphia after landing when a fuel truck approached while the driver appeared to be using a cell phone. The Captain stopped the aircraft to avoid a collision, noting the truck driver was not paying attention, though the First Officer's vigilance prevented an incident.

synopsis: A319 crew took off without the required operating HF radio for the planned route. Crew obtained a modified clearance from ATC with routing that precluded the HF radio requirement.
summary: The flight crew encountered a routing issue after departure when ATC required HF radio, which the aircraft lacked, forcing a 340-mile delay to obtain a new clearance via relay. The pilot attributed the event to a lack of pre-flight confirmation regarding oceanic route requirements and HF equipment availability.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A B787 crew made an intersection takeoff after weight & balance calculations had been based on a full-length takeoff.
summary: The flight crew departed runway 21 from the taxiway intersection instead of the displaced threshold, losing 1,300 feet of planned runway. This error occurred due to missing runway edge lighting and misleading airport diagrams that obscured the threshold location and taxiway end.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reports missing an assigned crossing restriction of FL220 at MAYOS on the IVANE5 RNAV. The original altitude window of FL260-FL240 is changed to FL220, but the aircraft does not honor the new altitude and the deviation is detected too late to catch up.
summary: Two pilots on an aircraft executing the Ivane5 arrival into CLT crossed the MAYOS waypoint 800 feet high of the cleared FL220 restriction. The crew attributed the deviation to automation unexpectedly leaving the vertical profile while they were distracted by arrival duties, noting no separation issues occurred.

synopsis: A B737 Captain reported being distracted by a Runway Awareness and Advisory System (RAAS) warning on rollout in OGG that had the potential to lead to a runway or taxiway incursion.
summary: During rollout on Runway 02 at OGG, the pilot reported that a loud Runway Awareness and Advisory System (RAAS) alert masked Tower instructions to turn right on Runway 05. The pilot attributed the hazardous event to the RAAS noise making it difficult to hear the critical taxi clearance.

synopsis: A B737 flight crew reports being vectored off course before actually beginning the HHOOD2 RNAV arrival. They are then cleared direct to HHOOD but do not comply with the RNAV speed restriction of 280 knots since they are not on the STAR until HHOOD. ATC is not happy with this interpretation of the speed restriction.
summary: The pilot flying a jet to PDX exceeded the 280 KIAS arrival restriction after being vectored off the HHOOD2 procedure and re-cleared direct HHOOD. The pilot attributed the speed violation to confusion over when the restriction applied while managing the flight alone as the other crew member was unavailable.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A pilot flying the BWI RAVNN 3 in a non VNAV capable aircraft commented on the high workload safety aspect when flying an RNAV arrival with hard altitude crossing constraints.
summary: A pilot flying an aircraft without VNAV capability reported that the RAVNN 3 RNAV arrival into BWI requires excessive monitoring of hard altitude constraints. This workload prevented timely approach briefing and was identified as a safety hazard due to the diversion of pilot attention from other duties.

synopsis: A B737 Captain reported a ground conflict on IAH at the intersection of WW and WB after another air carrier aircraft crossed in front of them at a high speed. A flight attendant was injured during the stop.
summary: The pilot stopped the aircraft on taxiway WB to avoid a high-speed intruding air carrier at the WW intersection. A flight attendant fell during the emergency braking, sustaining a potential injury that required medical attention.

synopsis: A B737 Captain is concerned about first officers selecting FLIGHT DISPLAY SOURCE ALL ON 2 without consulting the other pilot because TERRAIN ON or altimeter settings my be changed or deselected without the other pilot's knowledge.
summary: A First Officer nonverbally switched flight displays to the Captain's side using the overhead panel, resetting the altimeter and removing terrain warnings. The reporter states this dangerous practice eliminates individual crosschecks and causes loss of critical display settings.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier crew on vectors for GRK ILS Runway 15 was given a descent to 3,000 feet but read back and descended to 2,000 feet. The crew felt low and when asking about the cleared altitude received an EGPWS 'TOO LOW GEAR' aural warning.
summary: The flight crew received a clearance to descend to 2,000 feet for ILS 15 vectors, triggering a "too low gear" warning. The controller subsequently instructed a climb to 3,000 feet, and the crew completed the approach after verifying the low altitude was likely a communication error.

synopsis: An aircraft on approach to CEF was unable to land because the airport was closed and neither ATC nor the company Dispatch were aware the closure. On short final with no ILS, PAPI or Runway lighting the crew was told to go around and hold until the airport opened.
summary: The flight crew received a visual approach clearance from Bradley Approach to CEF, unaware the airport was closed and not CTAF operational. They executed a go-around at 200 feet after airfield operations contacted them on a secondary frequency, then held until the airport opened for a successful landing.

synopsis: A CRJ-700 passenger with long legs refused to remove them from the aisle for flight attendant passage and after the service cart bumped his feet in passing where he then threw a wine bottle at her. Witnesses corroborated her story and police met the passenger at gate arrival.
summary: A First Class passenger obstructed the aisle with his legs, causing a Flight Attendant to be grabbed and a wine bottle to be thrown at a second Flight Attendant, damaging a service door. The Captain contacted police, who met the flight upon arrival to investigate the aggressive behavior and property damage.

synopsis: A B737 Purser reported the gate agent refused to tell her where the Law Enforcement Officer (LEO) and Federal Air Marshal (FAM) were seated on their aircraft because to do so would be a security breach.
summary: The Purser reported that a Law Enforcement Officer and a Federal Air Marshal boarded without prior notification from the Customer Service agent during check-in. The agent later claimed that disclosing armed passengers in advance would compromise security, despite the information being available on the final paperwork.

synopsis: After ground looping a C170B, the pilot discovered the tailwheel tension springs were the incorrect part and not properly installed. The previous owner's errors were corrected.
summary: The pilot reported a ground loop to the right at touchdown on Runway 31 caused by uneven tail wheel tension springs. Inspection revealed the springs were the wrong size and improperly installed, so the pilot replaced the hardware with correct parts.

synopsis: At 1,500 feet after departure, a King Air 200 pilot did a precautionary engine shutdown while dealing with nearby traffic and ATC communications.
summary: The pilot shut down an engine after takeoff due to a precautionary need, advising ATC to standby while securing the aircraft. Once the engine was secure and traffic was identified, the pilot completed a normal single-engine landing.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: An instructor with student completed an introductory SFO Bay tour and when returning to the airport did not receive a NCT to OAK handoff until abeam the Oakland Coliseum. OAK Tower wanted information about the late communications handoff.
summary: A pilot conducting a student discovery flight over the San Francisco Bay reported a delayed hand-off from Norcal Approach to Oakland Tower due to frequency congestion. The pilot maintained two-way communication throughout but was instructed by Oakland to establish contact prior to entry, despite already being in contact with Norcal.

synopsis: A helicopter near the LA Coliseum reported a near miss with another helicopter at 700 feet after that helicopter violated the Dodger TFR then proceeded to land at a nearby airport.
summary: A pilot flying a helicopter at 700–800 feet MSL near the LA Coliseum received a TCAS alert for an aircraft approaching from the North within the Dodger Stadium TFR. The other aircraft passed 100–200 feet below the pilot, and its tail number was later obtained after another helicopter intercepted it.

synopsis: A pilot departed a towered airport using CTAF procedures on 121.5 while the Tower was open because he had referenced [website] data which indicated the Tower closed at XD:00 local when in fact it closed at XE:00. The aircraft's Communications system confusion was a contributing factor.
summary: The Pilot in Command failed to establish two-way communication with the Tower before taxi and takeoff because the transmitter selector was set to COM2 on 121.5 Guard. The error was discovered after takeoff when the Approach controller advised the pilot was broadcasting on Guard, prompting an immediate switch to COM1.

synopsis: Pilot of C-172 experienced a NMAC with C-152 while on visual approach to a parallel runway.
summary: A pilot landing at LVK on 25R experienced a near-miss with a C152 crossing directly underneath at 50 feet lower after the controller diverted the C152 to 25L. The reporter attributes the incident to a lack of traffic information from the tower and confusion regarding the C152's position.

synopsis: A flight crew terminated a visual approach after detecting another aircraft at the same altitude at approximately 1/2 mile distance on approach to the same airport.
summary: HNL Approach cleared a small transport for a visual approach to JRF Runway 04L without coordinating with JRF Tower regarding a conflicting B767-300. The pilot executed an evasive turn to avoid the B767 at co-altitude, while the controller admitted misapplying visual separation rules and failing to ensure adequate spacing.

synopsis: Piper Seminole took evasive action after experiencing NMAC.
summary: The pilot, under the hood during VFR vectoring for ILS 24 PNE, had the safety pilot take control to perform evasive action after being advised of a potential conflict. The other single-engine aircraft continued on course.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reports sighting a drone near PHL at 3,000 feet.
summary: A drone was observed approximately 100 feet from the aircraft's right wing. The narrative does not specify the flight phase, crew involved, or the outcome of the encounter.

synopsis: Pilot of R-22 momentarily lost control while attempting to retrieve an airport diagram, resulting in some aircraft damage.
summary: A student pilot flying a Robinson R-22 Beta II solo experienced an uncommanded roll and nose drop after improperly holding the collective crossbar to retrieve a dropped diagram. Subsequent inspection revealed broken teetering droop stops, indicating the pilot had narrowly avoided catastrophic mast bumping and tail boom strike.

synopsis: A passenger reported being initially startled by a Flight Attendant PA banter on landing until he realized the theatrics were not aircraft related noise.
summary: A pilot reported that cabin crew used the PA system to imitate horse noises immediately after touchdown. The pilot was momentarily frightened, mistaking the sounds for a flight deck crew member with a stuck microphone expressing fear during a critical phase.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot lifted off CTAF airport PGV Runway 26 VFR and had near miss with an IFR aircraft departing Runway 2 which did not use the AIM suggested CTAF position reports. Runway 2 and 26 thresholds are not visible from each others' ends.
summary: The pilot departing Runway 26 at PGV aborted takeoff after a transient IFR aircraft departed Runway 2, passing overhead with only 20-30 feet vertical separation. The near-miss occurred because the other pilot made no radio calls and the runway thresholds were obscured by a blind spot.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: A pilot departing ACK reports the Tower Controller told him to turn left to 010 heading. In doing so, the co-pilot then gets control of the aircraft and attempts to turn the aircraft to the runway heading because of the Obstacle Departure Procedure (ODP) 800 foot restriction. The pilot regains control of aircraft and turns to a heading of 010 and at that time the aircraft is at 800 feet. The pilot is not sure if the 010 heading should have been followed until he was at 800 feet, like the co-pilot was trying to do.
summary: The pilot and first officer disagreed during climb out from Nantucket Runway 06 regarding a tower-issued left turn to 010 versus Obstacle Departure Procedure requirements. The pilot delayed the turn until 800 feet MSL to ensure obstacle clearance, later filing a report due to uncertainty about whether the tower instruction overrode the ODP.

synopsis: B737-700 First Officer reported deviating from departure track out of EWR when they encountered wake turbulence in trail of a B767.
summary: The pilot monitoring reported that the crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding 767 during takeoff from Runway 22R at EWR. The resulting delay in turning to the intended heading of 220 was attributed to the pilot's lack of vigilance and assertiveness in directing the proper course.

synopsis: A pilot reports of being high and above the glideslope while flying into OAK airport on the ILS to runway 30. He is kept high by NorCal approach.
summary: Pilots reported that NorCal Final Approach vectors for the OAK ILS30 approach placed aircraft too high, causing intense workload and preventing FAF verification. The reporter attributes this destabilization to tight, high vectors and frequency congestion that limited requests for lower altitudes prior to intercept.

synopsis: A B737-700 flight crew failed to complete the Before Taxi Checklist due to distractions and discovered the flaps were not set for takeoff when the Takeoff Warning Horn sounded.
summary: The Captain and First Officer omitted the Before Taxi Checklist due to ground controller interruptions during engine start, resulting in a Takeoff Warning Horn activation caused by flaps remaining up. They stopped, completed the missed checklists, set flaps to 5, and departed safely.

synopsis: A B737-700 pilot engaged the APP Mode on the SFO 28R ILS when tracking the Localizer in LNAV about 14NM out at which time the aircraft made a hard right 30 degree turn for no apparent reason. The APP Mode was reselected outside AXMUL without incident. An airport equipment anomaly is suspected.
summary: The Pilot Flying reported that selecting Approach mode during an ILS 28R approach to SFO caused an uncommanded 30-degree right bank, requiring manual override and a missed approach. The pilot attributed the event to rough localizer signals rather than aircraft equipment malfunction, noting similar issues with other ILS systems nationwide.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported deviating from ATC vectors on departure from EWR after being distracted by wake turbulence.
summary: The pilot reported that residual wake buffeting from a preceding 767 during takeoff distracted them from following SID vectors of heading 190 then 220 out of 2.3 DME. This distraction caused the pilot to initiate the first turn slowly and fail to execute the proper procedure in due course.

synopsis: A B737 flight crew returned to the departure airport due to a Cabin Altitude/Pressurization warning passing through FL260. During the descent it was discovered that the wrong altitude had been set in the Pressurization Control Panel.
summary: During climb through FL260, the pilot set the pressurization panel to 12,660 feet instead of 1,226 feet due to a checklist verification error. This caused a cabin altitude warning, forcing a return to the departure airport for maintenance and refueling.

synopsis: A B737 Captain attempted to stop passenger boarding to protect a Mechanic working near hazardous equipment but a company zone person refused his request, overriding the Captain's authority as described in the FOM.
summary: The flight crew reported that Zone operations ignored their request to halt boarding, forcing a mechanic working on an exposed high-power TV panel into an unsafe position. The captain questioned Zone's authority to override flight deck safety decisions, citing the FOM's statement that the captain holds absolute authority during all flight-related operations.

synopsis: A Ramp Agent reported a portable baggage scanner left on the belt loader after unloading bags. The scanner fell from the belt loader as the tug was driven away and caught fire after it was caught under a cart tire near the aircraft.
summary: A ramp agent and an on-line runner failed to secure a scanner left on a belt loader during unloading. The scanner was caught under a tug tire, scraped the ground, and caught fire near the aircraft.

synopsis: A IAH Ramp Agent reported that his company is slow to clear ramp personnel to safety with lightning in the vicinity even when it is close, over head and within the airport area.
summary: An IAH ground employee reported dissatisfaction with delayed ramp closures during a major thunderstorm despite visible lightning. The reporter attributed heated radio conversations to untimely decisions and called for improved communication and alert methodologies to prioritize safety over operations.

synopsis: After departure an A319 ECAM alerted HYD G ENG 1 LO PR. The crew completed the ECAM procedure then called both local Maintenance and Maintenance Control for guidance. Both said to continue because it was an indication problem but the Captain believed it was actual but continued.
summary: During climb, the crew received a HYD G Eng 1 Lo PR ECAM and followed procedures while consulting dispatch and maintenance. The pilot reported that maintenance intentionally provided false information claiming an indication problem to influence the decision to continue, disregarding safety.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported a hard landing following a B757's takeoff from the same runway. Captain believes jet blast could have been a factor.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a bounced landing on a Boeing 757 at MSP while landing behind a departing 757. The reporter attributed the firm bounce to jet blast and turbulence from the departing aircraft, which caused a sink during the flare despite maintaining increased approach speed.

synopsis: A crew flying the ORD WATSN 2 RNAV VOLGR transition to ILS Runway 27L failed to selected the 281° heading at WATSN to intercept the localizer because the RNAV procedure did not indicate the transition. The transition was only on the ILS 27L chart.
summary: The pilot flying a WATSN2 arrival into Chicago O'Hare misinterpreted the VOGLR transition for Runway 27L due to chart ambiguity and an unfamiliar clearance. This caused the aircraft to overshoot the localizer, requiring a re-intercept from the north after the controller noted the error.

synopsis: A Captain reported the gate agent retracted the jetway before taking the closeout paperwork and closing the main cabin door. No jetway presence exposed the flight attendant to a potentially hurtful fall while closing the heavy door.
summary: The Captain and a flight attendant discovered the jetway was retracted 25 feet away while the main cabin door remained open during pre-flight. Although the Captain warned the gate agent that crew could fall to the pavement, the agent retrieved paperwork and began retracting the jetway again before the door was closed.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: While flying the RNAV GPS 18 Approach to F70 a medium sized turbo jet crew reported an EGPWS 'TERRAIN, PULL-UP' on profile at about 2,400 feet, past DISEY, with an 800 feet overcast. Terrain reference was obtained as the terrain avoidance maneuver was initiated so the flight continued to land.
summary: Pilots flying an RNAV Runway 18 approach in IMC received a GPWS terrain warning at 1,000 feet AGL due to high terrain and lack of ATC radar below 3,000 feet. They executed terrain avoidance, broke out to VMC, and landed safely, recommending mandatory GPWS for this approach.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier crew on approach to IAH received an EGPWS WINDSHEAR alert with a 15-20kt speed increase and a flap overspeed. The approach was continued, even though unstabilized, because severe weather was visible at the other end of runway.
summary: The pilot encountered windshear and overspeed warnings below 1,000 feet AGL during final approach in visual conditions. Despite a GPWS pull-up alert, the crew continued the landing to avoid severe weather and potential microbursts during a go-around, successfully reaching the runway.

synopsis: A US carrier aircraft operating internationally with ADS-B installed did not have the ADS-B Operations Specification on file indicating its aircraft were authorized flight above FL290.
summary: Pilots reported that the Operations Department filed flight plans for flights above FL290 in Vietnam, China, and Hong Kong without valid ADS-B Operations Specifications. Although the aircraft had operational ADS-B equipment, the crew discovered the company lacked the required approval to operate in this airspace.

synopsis: Flight crew received a new clearance enroute to avoid weather. During vectors to final approach they realized that the vectors were for the wrong airport. Destination airport was apparently changed by ATC when the new routing was issued.
summary: A flight crew and Columbus Approach miscommunicated during a weather reroute, causing the crew to be vectored toward Columbus Intl (CMH) instead of their intended destination, Rickenbacker (LCK). The crew corrected the error by clarifying their destination, receiving vectors for LCK Runway 23R, and landing safely.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Approaching the aircraft for preflight, crew noticed extensive aircraft damage from an apparent lightning strike of the ramp adjacent to the aircraft.
summary: While parked and triple chocked at KSGR, the aircraft was struck by lightning during a thunderstorm while the crew was off duty. The strike entered near the left rear static wick and exited through the tires, causing concrete explosions, tire burn marks, and minor skin damage, resulting in the aircraft being grounded for inspection.

synopsis: Upon breaking out at the completion of an instrument approach, crew of PC-12 noticed that the runway was closed with a large yellow X on the runway threshold. The entire airport had been closed for construction, but no NOTAM was issued. Crew diverted to an alternate airport.
summary: The pilot operating an owner flight to A08 executed a go-around after discovering the runway closed with construction vehicles present, despite no closure NOTAMs being issued. The airport manager admitted forgetting to file the closure NOTAM, prompting a diversion to another airport.

synopsis: Upon completion of QRH procedure for a cracked windshield, crew of CRJ-900 remembered a company memo with clarifying info.
summary: The captain reported a windshield shatter at 33,000 feet, prompting a descent to 25,000 feet and cabin pressure adjustment to 6.2 psi. The crew noted the emergency checklist lacked specific descent guidance, relying instead on a separate memo recalled by the first officer.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Two Aircraft Maintenance Technicians (AMTs) report how a 'Doghouse' access panel temporarily re-installed on the Vertical Stab of an MD-80 aircraft was damaged during Maintenance trouble shooting for an inflight runaway Nose-Down condition. Aircraft would not hold a Nose-up configuration when the Horizontal Stab's Primary Trim Motor 'pickle' switches on the Aileron Control wheel were released. Pilots used thrust and spoilers to augment lift.
summary: Mechanics troubleshooting a runaway horizontal stabilizer on an MD-80 installed a trim motor with a missing gasket and temporarily secured the access panel with only four fasteners. While cycling the stabilizer to inspect the jackscrew, wind dislodged the panel, causing the right elevator fairing to crush it and rip the screws, resulting in structural damage.

synopsis: IAD support specialist reports of a flight inbound and outbound to/from IAD that is using the same call sign at the same time. He reports this has been happening for over 7 months and nothing has been done about it.
summary: A Tower Front Line Manager reported two Aircraft X flights with identical call signs, one arrival and one departure, airborne simultaneously at IAD. The incident was caused by the airline's failure to change the outbound call sign, though controllers managed the situation without stopping departures.

synopsis: ZDC controller reports of something he hadn't ever seen before. PCT has the ability to change altitudes of data tags on his center scope. Controller reports that a sector at PCT did this and it caused confusion and an airspace deviation by them doing so.
summary: Air Traffic Controllers in Sector 38 and Sector 11 experienced confusion regarding a point-out for Aircraft X descending to FL130. The incident involved a mistaken FL070 altitude entry by TAPPA and a failure to verbally confirm the point-out before the aircraft entered Sector 11's airspace.

synopsis: On a night, visual base leg following a go-around due to an unstable initial approach, crew of B-737 experienced EGPWS Caution Terrain alert.
summary: The flight crew experienced a Terrain Caution at 7,700 feet during a night visual approach to Runway 26 at ABQ after a last-minute runway change caused time compression. The pilots climbed to silence the alert and landed, later realizing they should have gone around due to the rushed setup and lack of a backup approach.

synopsis: After a flights departure time, Dispatcher noticed that the modified fuel on board had not been acknowledged by the crew.
summary: A dispatcher reported that the Captain of Flight ZZZ-DEN unilaterally departed with less fuel than permitted by the actual zero fuel weight, ignoring a release remark to load maximum fuel due to weather. The Captain attributed the error to distraction, though the dispatcher identified a systemic issue regarding crew compliance with fuel instructions and regulatory misunderstandings.

synopsis: During cruise, B-737 crew noticed that the crew oxygen system was indicating zero. Crew obtained two portable oxygen bottles from the cabin and after conferring with Dispatch diverted to a closer airport. Cause of the loss of crew oxygen not reported.
summary: The flight crew diverted to ZZZZ during cruise after the crew oxygen pressure dropped to zero, confirmed by failed mask tests. They executed an overweight landing to avoid burning fuel over Mexican airspace without oxygen, then continued to the destination after maintenance replaced the bottle.

synopsis: Dispatcher reports inadequate aircraft systems training.
summary: A dispatcher reported that training covered aircraft numbers and systems but omitted actual fleet dispatch routines, QRH, and irregularity information. Consequently, the dispatcher feels uncomfortable advising or assisting other dispatchers with this fleet despite self-study.

synopsis: On taxi out, A321 crew received 'RIGHT WING OVERFLOW' ECAM message. After completing the QRH procedure and visually confirming the venting fuel, crew shut down both engines to stop the fuel venting and the aircraft was towed to the gate. Cause of fuel venting was not reported. MEL for fuel pump or valve had been cleared before the flight.
summary: The flight crew experienced a right wing fuel overflow during taxi after recent maintenance on a fuel pump or valve. Despite shutting down engines and fuel pumps, the leak persisted, forcing a passenger deplaning and tow attempt that failed due to continued fuel spillage.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: During pushback, a tug crew failed to push the aircraft to the proper location and disconnected the tow bar before obtaining clearance from the flight crew. The aircraft momentarily began to roll before the flight crew applied brakes.
summary: During pushback, the flight crew and ground crew experienced a premature tow bar disconnect after the crew set toe brakes but before issuing a disconnect clearance. The aircraft began rolling because the ground crew assumed the push was complete at an incorrect location, highlighting a need for explicit disconnect instructions and spot verification.

synopsis: A pilot reported his BAe 125 Series 800 rudder pedals became very difficult to displace during climbout as if the Rudder Bias system had self-engaged, so the crew returned to the departure airport where the rudder pedals released with the thrust levers at idle.
summary: The pilot reported excessive rudder pedal resistance during a climb at 200 KTS after the SIC engaged the YD, suspecting the Rudder Bias system engaged on both sides. The aircraft returned and landed safely, with pedal resistance recurring only when thrust was advanced.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A crew had difficulty contacting ATC for a clearance while on the ground at COE and finally received clearance through Lockheed Martin Flight Service. After departure they were unable to contact GEG Departure on the 133.5, the assigned frequency. They finally used GEG charted frequency, 133.35.
summary: The crew experienced communication failures with Spokane Departure on assigned frequencies 132.1 and 133.5 during taxi and climb-out at COE. They eventually established contact on 133.35 found on the airport chart, attributing the issue to outdated frequency information.

synopsis: An EC-135 pilot reported when using Night Vision Goggles (NVG) and flying an aircraft which requires the instrument panel night vision external light shielding, the chin bubble mat blocks all downward vision thus obstructing obstacles during steep landing descents. The glareshield curtain permits downward vision but also filters the light from the instrument panels.
summary: An EC135 pilot reported that chin bubble floor mats required by certain NVG STCs restrict the viewing field during landing operations. The pilot considers this unsafe and recommends standardizing glare shield curtains, which mechanics plan to install during upcoming maintenance.

synopsis: During approach to South American airport, crew initiated descent earlier than the DME/altitude restriction for the airport's arrivals.
summary: A fatigued crew on a South American arrival descended to 5,000 feet per ATC clearance but violated a step-down restriction requiring 7,000 feet until 25 DME. The controller subsequently ordered an immediate climb to 8,000 feet after the aircraft descended too early due to pilot complacency.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: After engine start following pushback, crew of an Airbus experienced the loss of all three hydraulic systems. The crew started the APU, shut down both engines, and had the aircraft towed back into the gate. Maintenance personnel discovered that all three maintenance hydraulic system switches had been left in the OFF position.
summary: The flight crew experienced total flight control and hydraulic loss warnings immediately after engine start at LAX, forcing an engine shutdown and tow back. Maintenance discovered three hydraulic maintenance switches had been left off by an unknown person, leading the captain to refuse the flight due to unresolved safety concerns.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported an FMS issue when trying to load the ILS 02 Zulu approach to MGGT.
summary: The flight crew encountered an FMS navigation coding error on the ILS 02 Zulu approach at Guatemala City, which displayed an erroneously extended outbound teardrop path beyond the 7-mile limit. The pilot disengaged the autopilot at 6 DME to manually intercept the ILS course and landed safely in VMC conditions.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported he is unable to reach the interphone from his assigned seat in particular B767 aircraft.
summary: A flight attendant reported that their assigned jump seat (2 CTR L) on a Boeing 767 lacked interphone access, preventing communication with the flight deck during emergencies. Consequently, the crew member relocated to jump seat 2 CTR R for landing to ensure safe communication capabilities.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) describes his work environment where the lack of adequate Ground Power Units (GPUs) to supply electrical power to all their ERJ-170 aircraft requires the running of APU's all night in their hangar. As a result, due to the excessive noise levels, mechanics have chosen not to wear ear protection in order to communicate even though they face long term hearing loss.
summary: Mechanics at ZZZ Hangar servicing ERJ-170s face hazardous noise from running APUs due to a single Ground Power Unit shortage. Management delays in procuring additional GPUs force workers to choose between hearing loss from noise or heat exposure from closed hangar doors.

aircraft: Medium Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Twin engine, high wing turboprop First Officer reported losing an engine shortly after takeoff. Flight diverted to a nearby airfield where a safe landing was made.
summary: The First Officer and Captain of Aircraft X experienced a left engine failure at 200 feet during takeoff from an unimproved strip, likely due to a Flight Control Unit failure. After diverting to a short runway with poor braking, a right brake fire occurred from hydraulic leaks and heavy braking, though all personnel evacuated safely without injury.

synopsis: Cessna T188 pilot reported unexplained loss of directional control on landing roll that resulted in a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot reported an unexplained right swerve during rollout that could not be corrected with full control deflection, causing the aircraft to depart the runway.

synopsis: C208 Amphibian flight crew reported landing in FLL with the gear up, following a go-around that was directed by ATC. During the go-around, the flight crew encountered wake turbulence from a departing A320.
summary: The Captain and SIC of a C208 amphibian landed gear up at Fort Lauderdale International after the SIC misinterpreted a blue water-landing indicator as a flat tire. No damage occurred, and the crew mechanically lowered the gear before towing the aircraft for inspection.

synopsis: During a training maneuver, a C-152 elevator became locked forward of neutral so the flight returned to the airport. The instrument cooling fan had become lodged in the elevator control mechanism behind the glareshield.
summary: A student and instructor experienced limited elevator travel during maneuvers in the practice area. The instructor took control, returned to the home airport, and executed a safe landing using elevator trim for the flare with no injuries or damage.

synopsis: A LA4-200 engine quit because of fuel starvation because the bladder cell had detached from its rear hanger and collapsed preventing the pilot from filling it completely during preflight.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine failure three hours into a VFR flight due to a collapsed fuel bladder that prevented the tank from filling to capacity despite topping off the filler neck. The pilot successfully executed an off-airport landing on a road with gear down and flaps up, sustaining no injuries.

synopsis: A SFO Front Line Manager (FLM) reports of an airborne conflict he observes that local is having a problem with. Coordination with Northern California TRACON (NCT) is attempted but the resolution is denied by NCT. In order to save 1,000 feet between the aircraft the FLM instructs local to have the aircraft maintain a specific altitude below the higher aircraft. The altitude to maintain was below the MVA which had recently changed by 100 feet higher, causing an airspace deviation.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller issued an incorrect 2,500-foot altitude restriction to a departing aircraft due to recalling an outdated Minimum Vectoring Altitude. This error resulted in a loss of separation from another departure, though the required 1,000-foot vertical separation was ultimately maintained.

synopsis: A Jacksonville Center (ZJX) Controller questions why a restricted area that goes hot every day was removed from the Information Display System (IDS) in the area. Traffic Management Unit (TMU) removed the information and questioned the Controller as to why they needed it on the information page. The Controller was concerned that the area was going to go hot without any flow control for it.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported that the Traffic Management Unit removed a restriction preventing traffic south of J2 from entering active Restricted Areas R2914/15/17/18/19. The Controller stated this created an unsafe situation where weather could force aircraft into the restricted airspace with insufficient time to reroute.

synopsis: SCT Controller reports of a loss of separation he attributes to the pilot descending early next to another aircraft and the radios associated to his position. The Controller has noticed a degradation of radio clearness and the experience of upgraded pilots in that area using the radios.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a 3,300-foot altitude clearance to Aircraft X for the ILS 25L approach, but poor radio quality caused a readback confusion that led the aircraft to descend to 3,100 feet. The controller transferred Aircraft X to Tower control after observing it descend behind Aircraft Y, attributing the incident to deteriorating radio communications in the LA area.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported loss of aircraft control, for approximately 15 seconds, when they encountered severe wake turbulence 10 miles in trail of a B777 on approach to LAX. A Flight Attendant was reportedly slightly injured in the event.
summary: While descending through 11,000 feet into LAX behind a 777, the crew encountered severe wake turbulence causing uncontrollable rolling. The Captain disconnected the autopilot and climbed to recover, resulting in a Flight Attendant sustaining a neck injury.

synopsis: Pilot reports of a confusing transmission and instruction to climb to a different altitude then assigned and then descend back to the previously assigned altitude.
summary: The pilot reported a potential deviation while climbing from Denver on the SPAZZ departure after an ATC controller initially queried a climb to 11,000 ft before correcting to 10,000 ft. The pilot attributed the resulting confusion and altitude excursion to the controller's erroneous instruction, though ATC later acknowledged the error and noted no conflict occurred.

synopsis: Captain was informed that the B757 aircraft he had just flown was taken out of service due to rubber seals at Left and Right ailerons were installed backwards and curling laterally. Conditions of the seals were noted by himself and Maintenance at the previous departure station, but were not considered to be a safety of flight issue.
summary: The crew and mechanics inspected curled rubber seals on both ailerons, attributing the issue to excess paint and deeming the aircraft safe for flight to ZZZ1. The aircraft was later grounded because the seals were installed backwards, though the crew reported normal handling and no flight issues.

synopsis: Flight crew reported that a passenger in business class on their B777 aircraft noticed damage, dents and delamination of the right wing upper surface behind the inboard slat, after slat retraction. Aircraft returned to departure airport when Maintenance could not guarantee the damaged area would not continue to tear or peel back.
summary: A business class passenger reported wing damage, including delamination and dents behind the inboard slat, along with inoperative Satcom voice. Maintenance could not guarantee the damage would not worsen, leaving the aircraft's airworthiness uncertain.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew diverted to an alternate upon reaching bingo fuel because the destination airport visibility was reported below minimums. The crew experienced communication difficulties and eventually climbed into Class A airspace without ATC clearance for fuel conservation purposes.
summary: The pilot diverted to ZZZ2 due to visibility below minimums and bingo fuel, climbing into Class A airspace without clearance to conserve fuel. Although the weather observer later reported improved visibility, the pilot proceeded to the alternate, resulting in a pilot deviation report that was subsequently withdrawn.

synopsis: A military charter departing a foreign station with a ride along agent to report aircraft status, repeatedly relayed incorrect weight and balance cargo loads. After departing the gate the aircraft returned to move pallets because the station agent reported the correct numbers which put the aircraft out of CG limits.
summary: The loadmaster reported conflicting cargo and passenger weight data from agents caused a nose-heavy imbalance on a military charter before pushback. The flight returned to the gate because the Captain refused to move passengers and cargo to achieve the required balance.

synopsis: Pilot reports being instructed by Ground Control to taxi to a specific runway and in doing so was given crossing instructions for two runways. Pilot was told to hold short of the last runway while non-flying pilot checked with Tower due to seeing traffic on the runway. Pilot then gets on locals frequency and is told they weren't given crossing instructions. Aircraft was over the hold short line by 3 feet while departing 1R traffic passed and became airborne.
summary: The flight crew received a taxi clearance from Ground to cross runways 1L and 1R but was stopped by Tower while crossing due to an active departure. The reporter attributes the incident to a Ground controller issuing unauthorized clearance, likely due to a coordination error, though strict adherence to SOPs prevented a serious event.

aircraft: Embraer Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Upon aircraft power up at the start of preflight, crew experienced TAWS fail warnings. Maintenance Control and Dispatch provided the crew with a manufacturer bulletin that cleared the problem.
summary: The flight crew experienced a TAWS failure warning during preflight in ZZZ. Maintenance Control and the Chief Pilot attributed it to a known Garmin database error and authorized three aircraft resets to clear the nuisance message, allowing the flight to continue.

synopsis: A First Officer questions whether a logbook corrective action entry by Maintenance was appropriate or just ridiculous. He found the emergency brake and landing gear pneumatic vent lines dripping hydraulic fluid during a post flight walk around of their Cessna Citation X aircraft. Maintenance had disconnected, vacuumed, cleaned with alcohol, and re-secured the lines.
summary: A pilot reported that an aircraft was grounded at ZZZ airport due to hydraulic leaks in emergency brake and gear vent lines. After technicians cleaned and re-secured the lines, the leak recurred the next day, leading the pilot to criticize the inadequate corrective action and a negative maintenance culture.

synopsis: A B737-800 Captain reported that during landing roll a first class passenger's iPad flew from her hands during braking with Autobrakes 3 and max reverse, landed on the floor, and slid under the cockpit door stopping in the flight station.
summary: Pilots reported an unknown iPad with a keyboard slid under the flight deck door after a First Class passenger lost it during landing on a short runway. The device illuminated the cockpit, raising concerns about unsecured items during deceleration and the security risk of objects entering the flight deck without opening the door.

synopsis: SF340 First Officer reports departing for TPA with a clear forecast and no alternate required. Enroute developing thunderstorms are reported and an alternate is requested from Dispatch. During the approach, a 20+ knot speed increase is noted and heavy rain is encountered. Aircraft ahead and behind the SF340 break off their approaches and this crew soon follows and diverts to their alternate.
summary: Aircraft X crew encountered severe windshear and heavy rain during an ILS 1L approach to TPA, despite ATC assurances that thunderstorms were dissipating. The crew executed a go-around and diverted to MCO, attributing the incident to unreliable weather data, inadequate dispatch monitoring, and conflicting ATC instructions.

synopsis: Captain describes the routine communication difficulties encountered when in communication with Yangon Control, this time resulting in a possible altitude assignment misunderstanding. The problem is due to both poor communications equipment and poor English speaking ability.
summary: The flight crew experienced poor radio quality with Yangon ATC while climbing from FL270 to FL370. A revised clearance to FL290 issued after passing FL300 caused a minor overshoot to FL305, which the pilot attributed to communication difficulties rather than an altitude deviation.

synopsis: Pilot reports of encountering icing conditions and not being able to get a response from ATC. Pilot descends out of assigned altitude for 1,000 feet lower to get out of icing conditions, attempts to call ATC but is difficult in doing so, eventually contacts ATC and advises them they are in an emergency descent to get out of the icing conditions.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe weather and icing while en-route at FL390 after INDY Center ignored deviation requests. The aircraft slowed near minimum maneuvering speed, forcing the Captain to exercise emergency authority to descend to FL380 without clearance to recover airspeed.

synopsis: Pilot reports of confusion caused by similar sounding waypoint names while on the FOOXX4 Arrival into TPA. The pilot hears, reads back, and proceeds to the wrong waypoint after being cleared by Approach Control.
summary: The pilot misheard an approach controller's clearance to COSME as GUSNE during the FOOXX4 arrival into Tampa, causing the aircraft to track to the wrong point. The error occurred because the waypoint names sound similar, and neither the controller nor the captain caught the incorrect readback until the controller noticed the deviation.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Taylorcraft pilot reported severe wake turbulence and loss of aircraft control in 6-mile trail of an A319 at CID.
summary: A Taylorcraft pilot encountered severe wake turbulence from an A319 while on final approach, causing the engine to quit and the propeller to flail before restarting. The pilot landed safely at CID and attributed the incident to misidentifying the preceding aircraft's size and insufficient separation in calm wind conditions.

synopsis: FA-18 Instructor reports his student wingman losing sight of lead in IMC and falling well back and below, in Class A airspace, without advising lead, ATC or squawking altitude.
summary: A student wingman lost visual contact with his instructor during an IMC climb from FL200 to FL300, drifting 24 miles and 5,000 feet below due to poor air work and failure to squawk. The pair rejoined VFR at 16,500 feet after the student notified the lead of the deviation, with no ATC errors reported.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: P31 Controller reports of taking a handoff on an aircraft then the data tag mysteriously disappears a minute after taking the handoff. Aircraft flies through airspace for 30 miles without a data tag. Controller wonders who or what dropped the data tag.
summary: An air traffic controller lost radar contact with Aircraft X after its tag was prematurely terminated by an unknown party or automation error shortly after handoff. The aircraft flew 30 miles without a tag in the controller's airspace, preventing a proper handoff to the ZJX controller.

synopsis: ZNY ARTCC Front Line Manager reports of a skydiving operation that is not signatory to a LOA with the FAA. The operation has skydivers dropping through an LGA arrival route.
summary: A skydiving company operating at 13,500 feet over the LGA arrival stream has failed to secure a Letter of Agreement with ZNY. The reporter recommends relocating the jump site five miles north or south to increase safety margins and establish clear operational responsibilities.

synopsis: PVD Controller reports of an aircraft not talking to approach or Tower lands opposite direction with a carrier on final to the landing runway. Carrier was sent around and controllers attempted to talk to landing aircraft but there was no answer. Aircraft taxied to parking and was met by airport operations. ASDE-X did not alarm.
summary: During a TFR at PVD, an uncommunicative Aircraft X landed opposite direction on Runway 5 while an air carrier was cleared to land. The Local/Ground controller spotted the incursion, canceled the carrier's clearance, and diverted it; Aircraft X taxied to the ramp without ASDE-X alerts or loss of separation.

synopsis: PVD Controller reports that while he was giving instruction on Local Control he and the Developmental did not observe an aircraft that landed opposite direction. Controller reported he and Developmental were both discussing a previous loss of separation and did not scan correctly.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller and a trainee missed a VFR aircraft landing on Runway 5 at PVD while managing moderate traffic. The controller attributed the missed target to distraction from a prior separation loss, while the trainee cited excessive focus on other traffic.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: ZID controller reports of releasing and aircraft with a void time, then moving to the D-side. Controller never observed the aircraft tag up, and after void time called Tower to see what was up. Tower advised they should be talking to aircraft. Aircraft was still on Tower's frequency, 30 miles West of airport at assigned altitude.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X departed PKB without an observed transponder or communication until reaching 9,000 feet. The aircraft was later located 30 miles east in ZOB airspace, attributed to the pilot failing to activate the transponder before takeoff.

synopsis: TOL TRACON Controller reports of being told about a practice hung ordinance requested procedure. Controller later finds out it was not a practice, but the aircraft had actual hung ordinance and had possibly flown over populated areas.
summary: An air traffic controller received incorrect information from a supervisor regarding a military aircraft's hung ordinance situation, mistaking a real emergency for a practice procedure. This error forced the controller to scramble traffic away from populated areas, creating an unsafe situation that could have been avoided with accurate communication.

synopsis: An SNA Controller reports of working a combined position with a helicopter that requested landing at a specific FBO. The position gets split and the Controller keeps the aircraft that is now in another controller's area. The Controller clears aircraft to go where they requested and has what he describes as a NMAC with a departure that the other Local was working.
summary: An air traffic controller managing heavy traffic on combined positions instructed a helicopter to approach the ramp from the west to avoid the pattern. The pilot became confused, turned left across the runway end, and nearly collided with a departing aircraft, an incident the controller attributed to fatigue and potential miscommunication.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: IND TRACON Controller and Front Line Manager (FLM) report of a pilot that was not IFR rated had to descend in IFR conditions due to weather. ATC got the aircraft down to decision height where the pilot could see the runway and landed without incident.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a VFR-only aircraft with low fuel stuck in overcast by vectoring it for an ILS 32 approach at IND. The co-pilot used basic instrument training to land safely after seeing the runway at 1,900 feet, aided by additional staffing and traffic separation.

synopsis: A B737 Captain experiences difficulties contacting Medical Services on the listed Commercial Radio frequencies over the Atlantic Ocean east of MLB. Eventually a usable frequency is found to discuss the condition of an ill passenger.
summary: During cruise at FL390, pilots attempted to contact Medical Services using Dispatch Release frequencies 130.70 and 131.17 but encountered no response or severe distortion. They established usable communications via JAX Operations on 131.70 after a 12-minute delay, highlighting a need for improved radio capability to prevent critical decision-making delays.

synopsis: A320 flight crew experiences a track deviation when a revised segment on their PDC is overlooked, believing that no change actually exists. Complicating matters the Dispatch computer did not generate a release number two with the new routing and the PDC only contained one fix on the new routing.
summary: The flight crew navigated to HANKK past GONZZ, but ATC advised this was not their filed route due to a Dispatch re-route that Sabre failed to re-release. The crew accepted a new routing to HOCKE after discovering they had overlooked a revised PDC segment directing them to SYR.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Airbus flight crew reports being offered and accepting a runway change to accommodate departing traffic. The First Officer becomes distracted with MCDU work and the Captain does not call for the gear until just prior to the 1,000 foot point. This results in a gear warning until the gear indicates green and the approach is continued to landing.
summary: During a visual approach to runway 25R at PHX, the First Officer's distraction configuring the MCDU caused a delayed gear extension and a configure warning at 900 feet AGL. The crew stabilized the aircraft and completed a normal landing, attributing the event to rushing the runway change and poor crew resource management.

synopsis: A CE680 Captain reports writing up an aircraft for rusty aft cockpit window trim retaining screws. Maintenance wants the Captain to change the write up to 'screws missing paint' since the corrosion write up is grounding. The Captain does not agree to the change.
summary: The SIC discovered corrosion on fasteners during preflight, grounding the aircraft, but a maintenance controller pressured the crew to mislabel the issue as missing paint to allow a deferral and maintain schedule. The crew refused to alter the write-up, citing safety concerns, while the controller hung up, creating an intimidating environment that discourages reporting legitimate airworthiness discrepancies.

synopsis: B767 flight crew experiences a TCAS RA caused by Learjet that is cleared to level off 1000 feet below but continues to slowly climb.
summary: Pilots on a HILEY5 arrival at FL260 executed an evasive right turn and climb after TCAS indicated a climbing Learjet at FL250 was on a collision course. The conflict resolved quickly, though the reporter suspected the Learjet may have used a local altimeter setting or experienced a cockpit distraction.

synopsis: First Officer reports being cleared to FL070 by SLVR ATC with no crossing restrictions or arrival procedure mentioned. ATC indicates to the crew that they are too low during the descent and levels off. After landing an arrivals page, which the crew believed to be an area chart, is discovered in the Chart manual but no arrivals exist in the FMC.
summary: The crew descended below the required altitude for the area while en route on UA304 due to a missing arrival in the FMC and an unidentified generic chart. ATC advised them to climb after reporting they were too low, prompting the crew to level off and delay the descent.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: On an ILS final approach, the crew of a MD-80 crew experienced an intermittent localizer signal. The crew landed safely after the help of ATC headings.
summary: The crew experienced intermittent Localizer signal failures while intercepting Runway 35C in instrument weather, causing weaving on final approach. A RAPCON supervisor attributed the issue to sporadic antenna problems at DFW, though the crew stabilized and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: During arrival procedure, B-737 crew overshot published minimum altitude. Crew had received numerous altitude and airspeed changes from ATC and neglected to engage VNAV.
summary: Pilots flying a JOVEM arrival received eight rapid airspeed and five altitude changes from ATC, exceeding FMC programming capabilities. This caused an inadvertent descent below 12,000 feet, requiring a manual climb back to 12,000 before proceeding uneventfully to a visual approach.

synopsis: B757 Captain is informed by the First Officer that he cannot arm the R1 door. Maintenance is called and indicates that the slide may have been improperly installed and will have to be deferred.
summary: The First Officer and Captain could not arm the R1 door due to an activation line wrapped around the girt bar, which was discovered after finding cords and a carabiner in the track. A mechanic inspected the issue, MEL'd the slide, and the flight continued to destination.

synopsis: A-320 captain points out potential fatigue issues with certain flight pairings.
summary: A pilot reported that a company schedule requiring duty 42 hours after an early start, including a cross-country flight and a 0200 report time, violates fatigue risk management principles. The pilot stated that while they managed naps to feel fine at departure, alertness during the critical descent and landing phases is uncertain and compromised.

synopsis: A Dispatcher is informed by one of his flights that they have been assigned FL380/M85 on North Atlantic (NAT) A instead of FL350. The computer software will not accept this altitude and a flight plan with accurate times and fuel burns cannot be generated.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that computer software failed to display the crew's requested FL380/M85 on NAT A, showing only lower altitudes instead. This prevented the controller from providing accurate fuel burn and critical fuel scenario data for the North Atlantic crossing.

synopsis: EMB-145 crew diverted to alternate airport due to low fuel state caused by multiple vectors, icing and lower assigned altitude.
summary: The flight crew of an EMB-145 diverted to ZZZ1 due to fuel concerns after ATC delays and a temporary Pitot 2 blockage caused by ice at FL370. Although the blockage resolved itself, the crew noted they should have reported the incident for maintenance tracking.

aircraft: Cessna Citation Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A flight crew discovered corroded cockpit window screw heads during pre-flight. They reported the discrepancy to maintenance who subsequently tried to pressure them to change their report to say the screw heads were 'missing paint'. They refused to comply.
summary: Pilots reported rust and corrosion on cockpit window screws, but maintenance pressured them to alter the log entry to "missing paint" and threatened an investigation. The crew refused to change the report, noting that the aircraft delay resulted from the unairworthy condition and poor maintenance procedures, not pilot actions.

synopsis: A B737 Captain reported bright reflections from three solar fields southwest of their departure airport caused temporary blindness during climbout.
summary: A departing LAS crew reported temporary blindness caused by bright glare from three solar reflectors southwest of the airport while passing the BOACH fix at dawn. The reflection was intense enough to cause visual spots for several minutes after looking away.

synopsis: Pilots report of rejecting a takeoff due to ATC cancelling takeoff clearance.
summary: The crew aborted a takeoff on Runway 1R at SFO after ATC cancelled clearance due to an A380 on final. The aircraft stopped at low speed near Taxiway M and subsequently departed from that position once the arrival landed.

synopsis: After takeoff with the TKS system set to high, a C208 pilot detects fumes and develops a headache. Oxygen is used for the reminder of the 50 minute flight. On the return leg the TKS system is set to normal for the first 15 minutes then high and no odor is detected nor does a headache develop.
summary: The pilot reported TKS fumes and a headache during a 4500-foot flight after activating the TKS system to HIGH on the ground while flying into the sun. Symptoms resolved with oxygen and fresh air, and did not recur on the return leg when the system was initially set to NORM.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier flight crew was issued an RA climb command while in cruise at FL320 that would have climbed them into their traffic which was 300 feet above them. They began to comply but then descended instead to remain clear of traffic.
summary: The pilot and First Officer received a climb RA while at FL320, but the pilot immediately descended to FL317 after realizing the conflicting traffic was at FL323. The RA resolved, and both aircraft reported their responses before the pilot returned to FL320.

synopsis: B767 Flight Attendant laments the reconfigured galley design of some of her company's aircraft and believes that FARs are being violated in order to work efficiently.
summary: Flight attendants on a reconfigured B767 reported that galley design forces FAR violations, including unrestrained carts and open trash bins, to complete service within 4-5 hours. These unsafe conditions block jumpseats, delay securing carts during turbulence, and require standing on carrier boxes due to missing stepstools.

synopsis: EMB175 Flight Attendant describes an ill passenger incident and the diversion that follows to get medical attention.
summary: A flight attendant assisted a passenger who fainted and lost her pulse after being slapped by her husband. An onboard RN administered aid using an AED and oxygen, allowing the passenger to regain consciousness before EMTs removed her upon landing.

synopsis: C172 instructor pilot was reported overdue when he failed to add time for touch and goes in his flight planning.
summary: A new flight instructor filed a VFR flight plan with an incorrect enroute time, omitting pattern work for touch-and-goes. This inattention caused the pilot to be declared overdue upon landing, attributed to a lack of experience with flight plan filing and estimating.

synopsis: Single engine Cessna pilot experiences a GPS failure on a flight to SFZ. After circling for a few minutes the GPS begins to function again and the flight is continued with a second failure occurring closer to SFZ. PVD airport is mistaken for SFZ and a landing ensues without contacting the Tower.
summary: A Cessna 152 pilot experienced repeated GPS failures en route to SFZ, leading to an inadvertent landing at Class C airport PVD while believing they had reached the destination. The pilot attributed the incident to poor decision-making and a lack of flight watch contact during the navigation equipment malfunction.

synopsis: On final visual approach, C-172 crew on a CFI training flight experienced a NMAC with a crop duster also on final approach. Crew executed a go-around, re-entered the traffic pattern and landed.
summary: During a CFI training flight on final approach at 800 ft MSL, a crop duster cut in front of the aircraft, causing wake turbulence that forced a go-around.
