The pilots attributed the near-miss to the crop duster's failure to communicate and the challenging visual environment, though they acknowledged their own potential fault in not spotting the lower aircraft.

synopsis: Citation crew read back incorrect descent clearance resulting in an airborne conflict with other traffic.
summary: The First Officer and Captain descended to 11,000 feet after misreading a clearance for 17,000 feet, triggering a TCAS RA due to conflicting traffic. Post-flight tape review confirmed the Captain's incorrect readback and the controller's failure to correct it, leading the airline and ATC to attribute the incident to controller error.

synopsis: SR22 pilot experiences lost communications in the vicinity of UNV at 8000 feet, an area where he had experienced lost communications previously. Communication is regained on a different frequency and the radio appears to operate normally.
summary: A pilot on an IFR flight experienced a loss of communication with New York Center due to fuzzy transmissions and no response. The pilot re-established contact via University Park Tower and Cleveland Center, suspecting missed handoffs where controllers failed to attempt a second contact.

synopsis: Pilot reports of DCA controllers 'climbing into my cockpit' and how they are telling the pilots various things that he feels they shouldn't be doing.
summary: A Captain reported that DCA Tower controllers aggressively managed traffic during landing by issuing "minimum time on runway" instructions and directing departing aircraft to "power up" immediately. The pilot attributed this dangerous environment to controllers pushing aircraft to clear exits and manage complex military helicopter traffic.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A General Aviation pilot is informed by PAO Tower during approach that a law enforcement TFR is in effect along his approach path, 2,000 feet and below. The reporter had been unaware until this point and thought that the information should be part of the PAO ATIS.
summary: A pilot descending into KGO reported that PAO Tower failed to notify them of a sudden police-declared TFR until the aircraft was near Class Bravo airspace. The controller then instructed the pilot to maintain 2,500 feet, potentially directing them into the restricted area without prior warning from ATIS or other controllers.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Taxi Captain, while taxiing to the FBO after landing, had a ground vehicle rush in front of him on the taxiway. He applied brakes rapidly and was told by Ground Control that the ground vehicle had been told to give way to him.
summary: After landing on Runway 12R, the flight crew of Aircraft X was cleared to cross Runway 12L when a pickup truck rushed into their path. The captain applied brakes to stop the aircraft, and Ground Control confirmed the vehicle was instructed to yield before taxiing resumed.

aircraft: Boeing Company Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Pilot reports of being under tow and crossing a runway. Aircraft on final is not sent around, but overflies the aircraft under tow and lands down further on the runway.
summary: A pilot reported that while being towed and turned on Runway 19 at FRG, a landing aircraft passed overhead at approximately 100 feet while the tow vehicle remained on the runway side of the hold short line. The pilot attributed the lack of a go-around to the controller's distance and busy conditions, noting no imminent danger occurred.

synopsis: PA-28 pilot reported an NMAC in the pattern at RHV.
summary: The pilot reported an imminent collision with departure traffic while on the downwind leg at 1,500 feet MSL. After ATC advised maintaining altitude, the pilot executed an evasive dive and turn to avoid the aircraft, which was slightly above.

synopsis: BE90 pilot, on a ferry flight to HNL from the west coast, reports a complete loss of GPS signal about two hours out of HNL. At about the time a VOR signal comes in range the GPS begins to function normally. Interference from a GPS antenna failure is thought to be the cause.
summary: A pilot on a ferry flight to Honolulu experienced a 1.5-hour simultaneous GPS signal loss on dual Garmin units, an iPad, and a satellite tracker approximately 350 NM from the destination. Garmin support attributed the total outage to a faulty antenna on one unit causing interference, a design flaw that left the aircraft without satellite navigation until VOR signals were acquired near Hawaii.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot reports of flying VFR to WHP under flight following with SCT. SCT Controller advises pilot that Controller will help him all the way to WHP, then vectors the aircraft around VNY due to traffic. Pilot continues descent and then Controller advises pilot that aircraft entered the VNY class D airspace. Pilot was under the assumption that he had approval to descend into Class D as long as he told ATC about it and AATC would take care of the point out to VNY Tower.
summary: A pilot flying from Avalon to Whiteman entered Van Nuys Class D airspace while being vectored by Southern California Approach. The controller released the pilot to contact Van Nuys Tower, highlighting the need to obtain explicit clearance before descending into airport airspace.

synopsis: CE-560XL First Officer reported difficulty dealing with a descend via clearance, in part because of crew errors, but also in part because of multiple ATC clearance changes.
summary: During descent into Richmond, the flight crew deviated 1,000 feet above a crossing restriction after ATC repeatedly changed clearances from "descend via" to "descend and maintain." The reporter attributed the error to the First Officer's inexperience with RNAV arrivals and the complexity added by conflicting ATC instructions.

synopsis: FA10 flight crew reported descending to 800 feet AGL on a visual approach to FTW when the pilot flying followed a false glideslope.
summary: The pilot on a visual approach to runway 34 inappropriately armed the approach mode, causing a descent to 800 feet AGL five miles from the runway due to a false glide slope capture. The crew climbed to 1,500 feet after the copilot and tower intervened, attributing the error to complacency in visual conditions.

synopsis: LA25 pilot reported flying into IMC under a VFR flight plan because of lack of communication with ATC and making incorrect assumptions.
summary: A VFR pilot flying from ALN to SUS was vectored by STL Approach into IMC at 3,500 feet while on a VFR flight plan, mistakenly believing an IFR plan was filed. After confirming IFR qualifications, ATC converted the flight to IFR, vectored the aircraft to the SUS ILS 8R, and the pilot landed without incident.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot reports of flying into SDM and not being familiar with the jump zones that are close to the airport. Controller vectors aircraft for a visual approach, leaves the aircraft high, and then ships the aircraft to the Tower. Aircraft turns away from airport to continue its descent and Tower Controller advises pilot he is going into a jump zone. Pilot finally lands at SDM. Pilot reports that this is an unsafe operation and offers suggestions to make flying into SDM better.
summary: A Part 91 pilot reported that Socal Approach vectored their aircraft into an active skydiving drop zone while clearing a visual approach to Brown Field Runway 26R. The pilot had to maneuver to avoid the zone, and Tower subsequently vectored them for a safe landing, citing dangerous proximity of drop zones to the approach and an overworked controller.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) was directed by an I/A Inspector to remove an upper wing skin access panel on a Piper PA46-310 Malibu for an Annual Inspection (A/I). During removal, AMT realizes the panel was part of the right wing fuel tank. Inspector and Technician believe the Piper Aircraft Maintenance Manual (AMM) is not very informative or detailed for the Malibu aircraft.
summary: A mechanic in ZZZ accidentally peeled back a fuel tank while removing a right wing panel, resealing it before the aircraft flew to ZZZ1 with half tanks. A small leak was later discovered, attributed to the mechanic's lack of experience and haste, requiring panel repairs at the home airport.

synopsis: C182RG pilot detects electrical fumes about 20 minutes after takeoff and elects to return to the departure airport. Visible smoke is detected and the decision is made to land at the nearest suitable airport. The gear would not extend normally due to a tripped landing gear circuit breaker and is pumped down. With the circuit breaker tripped the fumes clear and the reporter elects to fly back to his home airport with the gear extended.
summary: The PIC diverted an enroute aircraft to MMU after smelling burning and seeing smoke from a popped landing gear breaker. After pumping the gear down for a safe landing, the pilot flew the aircraft home with gear locked for repairs.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZBW Controller describes an almost loss of separation between two aircraft he was working that he catches and saves at the last minute. Controller was working a combined sector and aircraft were deviating because of weather. When the sector get splits he forgets to tell the relieving Controller about a TFR, and later that Controller violates the TFR.
summary: An air traffic controller in the Bosox and Providence sectors issued a conflicting descent clearance to Aircraft X toward Aircraft Y's path due to momentary memory loss, though the error was corrected seconds later. The controller also failed to brief a TFR over OQU to a relieving controller, resulting in holding instructions issued into restricted airspace.

synopsis: A B737 flight crew reported a pressurization problem that forced an early descent. The issue was complicated by the First Officer's Oxygen Mask Microphone exhibiting a shorting cable.
summary: The flight crew experienced an uncontrolled cabin altitude rise to nearly 14,000 feet at 36,000 feet, triggering an emergency descent to 10,000 feet despite normal air conditioning indications. Communication was briefly hindered by a shorted First Officer microphone wire, which was manually fixed to restore contact.

synopsis: CRJ-700 Captain reported encountering 'fairly severe' wake turbulence nine miles in trail of a heavy jet on the WYNDE6 arrival into ORD.
summary: The pilot reported severe wake turbulence while descending on the WYNDE6 arrival to ORD behind a heavy aircraft at 11,000 MSL. The crew climbed back to 11,000 MSL to escape the turbulence, citing inadequate separation due to winds and atmospheric conditions as the cause.

synopsis: An ERJ-175 flight crew accepted a descent clearance to 1500 feet from ATC that they thought might be too low. They questioned the clearance but ATC affirmed the altitude. Later while ATC was issuing vectors for the approach, the Controller told them to maintain 2500 feet. The flight crew then climbed to 2500 feet, flew the approach and landed safely.
summary: The flight crew received an erroneous ATC clearance to descend to 1,500 feet while approaching BDL, which conflicted with the 1,800-foot minimum at the final approach fix. After the controller corrected the clearance to 2,500 feet, the crew climbed immediately, resulting in a safe landing with no danger to the aircraft or passengers.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Captain and First Officer report their Air Carrier has been using a Guidance letter from the aircraft's Manufacturer not yet approved by the FAA, to dispatch their aircraft with water/moisture condensation at LED lights and associated power sources in the sealed Navigation, Strobe, Beacon, and Emergency light positions. Letter had not been included in their Aircraft's Flight Manual (AFM) to allow proper dispatch.
summary: Pilots grounded an aircraft due to condensation in five navigation and strobe lights, citing no MEL allowance for water near electrical components. Maintenance authorized flight under an unapproved Manufacturer's Guidance Letter, prompting the crew to report the lack of FAA oversight and improper maintenance procedures.

synopsis: A flight crew reported an NMAC with a light single on departure from SUU.
summary: During climb out from runway 21R, the crew executed an evasive nose-down maneuver to avoid a high-wing single-engine tailwheel airplane flying 500 feet above. The near miss occurred because the other pilot took no evasive action, prompting the crew to descend 300 feet below the intruder to prevent a collision.

synopsis: PA-44 instructor pilot reported an NMAC on final at DVT.
summary: A student pilot practicing an RNAV 7R approach into DVT inside I-17 reported a BE300 accelerating underneath without warning before sidestepping to 7L with landing clearance. The reporter noted that TIS is unreliable in the DVT area.

synopsis: A helicopter pilot was beginning a tour of the Hoover Dam when he caught sight of another Helicopter about 500 feet away. Aircraft Y pilot asked Aircraft X pilot if he saw him but the Aircraft X pilot stated that he was surprised and did not respond. Aircraft X did a 360-turn to allow Aircraft Y to precede him and reported that he incorrectly did not get back to him on the CTAF.
summary: A pilot conducting a Hoover Dam tour at 3,000 ft encountered a helicopter 500 ft away while entering the standard S-turn. The pilot executed a tight 360-degree turn to yield space but failed to respond to the helicopter's radio call, causing the other pilot to become upset.

synopsis: A PA28R pilot reported an NMAC after departing Runway 14 at 7B2, a non-Towered airport.
summary: The pilot departed Runway 14 at 7B2 after hearing another aircraft declare intentions for that runway. During climb, the pilot observed an unseen aircraft landing on Runway 32, attributing the near miss to the aircraft's green color blending with a mountain and a lack of radio communication.

synopsis: A Bellanca BL17 pilot reported loss of directional control after landing that led to a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot reported that the aircraft pulled sharply left upon runway contact, and subsequent rudder corrections caused increasing oscillations. The plane departed the runway into grass, rolled 250 feet, and stopped with no damage.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ZHU controller describes a session where he had to hold aircraft in his airspace due to weather effecting the arrivals into IAH. Controller describes that he feels the amount of traffic he was holding was unacceptable and extremely dangerous. Controller wonders how the session got that way.
summary: An air traffic controller in sector R70 reported that rapid weather buildup and excessive handoffs from surrounding sectors caused traffic volume to exceed acceptable levels. The controller deemed the resulting workload, which required an additional tracker and holding stacks, to be extremely dangerous.

synopsis: An Oakland Center (ZOA) Controller reports of confusion from pilots on the transition names of the STARs. The Controller would like a different arrival name for every transition.
summary: An air traffic controller trainee reported that a pilot flying Aircraft X on the OAKES1 west transition repeatedly questioned the clearance and chart details. The controller attributed the excessive queries to potential automation issues or pilot caution, warning that this behavior could lead to errors and recommending unique arrival names for each transition.

synopsis: A Northern California TRACON (NCT) Controller reports of being told that he had a wake turbulence loss of separation according to the Traffic Analysis and Review Program (TARP).
summary: An air traffic controller separated Aircraft X and Y at 7,000 and 8,000 feet, respectively, before climbing Aircraft X on diverging courses. The controller reported a TARP wake turbulence remnant of 4.9 miles and 900 feet, noting that scope display limitations forced a delayed climb.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported dealing with a low fuel situation when weather affected operations at their destination.
summary: The flight crew diverted from EWR to PHL due to weather and fuel concerns, then returned to EWR before executing a go-around due to a microburst. After declaring minimum fuel and diverting to LGA, the crew landed on Runway 31 with 45 minutes of fuel remaining following a missed approach caused by being high on final.

synopsis: A B737 First Officer reported being targeted in flight for nearly two minutes by a laser.
summary: During cruise at 16,000 feet, the First Officer experienced direct laser illumination for nearly two minutes while shielding the source with a tablet. The Captain observed indirect flashing, and ATC was notified post-landing to identify the source near Springfield, MA.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer, planning on departing Runway 4L reports receiving V speeds for Runway 4L at the arrival airport. The Captain caught the error during the takeoff briefing and the crew contacted their Dispatcher, who could not explain the error but sent new data.
summary: The flight crew identified erroneous takeoff data for the destination runway 4L instead of the departure runway 4L during pre-pushback checks. They resolved the software anomaly by manually loading correct performance data from the dispatcher, preventing a potential departure with incorrect FMC inputs.

synopsis: A321 flight crew were issued go around instructions just prior to glideslope capture. The fatigued First Officer incorrectly performed the go around maneuver causing the Captain to take over and return for another approach. The highly experienced First Officer also attributes his poor performance to a lack of Mode Awareness.
summary: During an ILS 09R approach, the First Officer failed to execute a proper go-around after ATC issued a climb instruction, causing an 800-foot altitude loss and overspeed due to incorrect autopilot mode selection and fatigue. The Captain eventually took control to level the aircraft at 3,000 feet, attributing the error to the First Officer's hesitation and failure to select TOGA thrust.

synopsis: A320 Captain experiences severe turbulence during descent, upon entering scattered white puffy clouds with tops at 13,500 feet, at a speed of 340 to 280 knots. Two passengers and a Flight Attendant are tossed into the overhead, with the Flight Attendant requiring medical attention.
summary: The captain reported encountering severe turbulence at 13,500 feet during descent, injuring an aft flight attendant and damaging cabin equipment. Two unbelted passengers also struck overhead panels, leading to a short base turn, landing, and hospital transport for the crew member.

synopsis: EMB145 Captain experiences a NMAC with a helicopter at 500 feet during approach to Runway 10L at ORD. The Tower had alerted the crew to the helicopter's presence, then advised that it was no factor. The helicopter had no transponder and there was insufficient time for evasive action.
summary: During an autopilot landing on runway 10L at ORD, the crew encountered a non-transponder-equipped helicopter at 500ft despite Tower advisories. The pilot continued the landing to avoid the risk of a go-around, noting that an operational transponder would have provided necessary traffic awareness.

synopsis: Dash 8-300 Captain experiences a momentary nose landing gear unsafe indication during approach after the gear had already been verified down and safe. A go-around is initiated and the gear is extended utilizing the alternate gear extension procedure.
summary: During approach at 2000 feet MSL, the crew experienced landing gear warning horn activation and erratic nose gear lights, prompting a go-around and alternate gear extension. The aircraft landed safely without declaring an emergency, with the crew attributing the event to a presumed mechanical anomaly in the gear operating or monitoring systems.

synopsis: CE750 Captain reports having his umbrella sucked up against the APU air intake during a night post flight inspection in the rain. The inlet screen is damaged.
summary: A mechanic performing a night postflight inspection on an aircraft with the APU running had a golf umbrella sucked into the APU intake screen. The suction force dislocated the forward, bottom, and half of the rear sections of the protective screen, requiring maintenance notification and log entry.

synopsis: C208 pilot describes the effects of exposure to a carbon dioxide rich environment when his aircraft is loaded and left closed up for over an hour with 67kgs of dry ice on board. The vents and side window are opened and the symptoms disappear.
summary: The pilot experienced breathing difficulties during a pre-departure delay after the aircraft was locked for an hour with 67kg of dry ice loaded floor-to-ceiling, blocking cockpit ventilation. The pilot resolved the issue by opening vents and windows, attributing the symptoms to reduced oxygen levels caused by the sealed cabin and cargo configuration.

synopsis: A310 flight crew reported that autopilot and autothrottles appeared to re-engage at touchdown after being disconnected, slowing selection of reverse thrust and affecting directional control.
summary: The crew reported that the autopilot and autothrottles re-engaged at touchdown, causing throttles to advance and preventing reverse thrust. The Captain manually retarded throttles and applied brakes to stop the aircraft from exiting Runway 23, attributing the event to stiff controls and suggesting improved maintenance training.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: A medevac Captain describes the events surrounding the transport of a seriously ill passenger that results in a diversion when the patient goes into cardiac arrest.
summary: The pilot and First Officer diverted a medical transport aircraft during descent after the patient suffered cardiac arrest, landing on a taxiway for emergency services. The crew noted that while ATC provided priority handling, they did not declare an emergency, and communication gaps delayed body removal and caused confusion regarding the flight's medevac status.

synopsis: Air carrier flight attendants reported they feel they were coerced to work beyond the FAA mandated 20 hour duty day maximum.
summary: Cabin crew were pressured by Crew Scheduling to exceed the 20-hour FAR duty maximum after a 7-hour 13-minute gate delay. Despite being awake for 23 hours, they continued the flight to avoid losing premium pay and facing reassignment penalties.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A pilot departing FFZ reported a near miss with a UAV at 3,700 feet.
summary: During departure from FFZ Tower, a pilot and student encountered an RC helicopter 2 NM south of RC Park at 3,700 feet MSL. The unmanned aircraft, described as 3 feet wide with green/red lights, was observed approximately 300 feet below the airplane.

synopsis: A Honolulu Control Facility (HCF) Controller reports of losing a data tag with an aircraft on a 9 mile final. The Controller coordinates with tower, but doesn't know why the data tag went missing. The Controller assumes someone dropped the data tag because of a different flight with the same call sign.
summary: An air traffic controller lost the data tag for Aircraft X during an ILS Runway 2 approach into OGG at 9 DME. The controller suspects the tag was removed because another aircraft filed with the same call sign, prompting a recommendation to prohibit duplicate call signs and establish specific procedures.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Chicago Center (ZAU) Controllers reported a situation where a military airspace is supposed to be going hot in a few minutes. Another sector had an aircraft going into the airspace and the Controllers questioned the other Controller. The other Controller advised them that they have extended the cold time for 10 minutes to allow this aircraft to go through it. A few minutes later another aircraft was handed off to them which will go through the airspace. Controller dialogue ensued. The other sector thought it was ok to delay the airspace for traffic, but the reporting Controller had military aircraft that needed to use the airspace.
summary: An LNR trainee and CPC reported a conflict with ZMP AUWLO regarding military airspace VE, where AUWLO incorrectly delayed activation to route Aircraft Z through while LNR vectored Aircraft X around. The incident caused a safety risk due to AUWLO's unauthorized airspace delay and lack of coordination with LNR and the military.

synopsis: B737-800 First Officer reported encountering wake turbulence in 5 mile trail of another B737-800 on approach to BWI.
summary: The crew encountered moderate wake turbulence from a preceding 737-800 while on the TERPZ arrival at BWI, causing 10-degree rolls and airspeed fluctuations. ATC provided vectors to final approach, and the autopilot remained engaged throughout the event.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported receiving a new flight release over the ACARS printer just prior to scheduled push back, showing landing with 2000 pounds less fuel. Dispatch was contacted for an explanation and the Captain was informed that the cargo weight has increased. The fuel load was increased to make up the difference.
summary: A pilot at ZZZZ discovered an unauthorized 2,000 lb landing fuel reduction on a hard-to-read ACARS printout caused by a payload increase. The pilot questioned Dispatch and load planning, preventing a potential fuel shortage that would have occurred had the change gone unnoticed during pre-flight duties.

synopsis: EMB-145 First Officer reported being targeted by a laser on approach to Runway 4 in MLU.
summary: During final approach to Runway 4 in Monroe, the left cockpit window was struck by a green laser four times. The crew reported the incident to Tower, experienced no night vision impairment, and landed without incident.

synopsis: EMB-145LR Captain reported being pressured by ATC to accept a clearance through severe weather at his destination.
summary: Pilots encountered severe thunderstorms and minimum fuel while approaching ZZZ, facing pressure from ATC to fly into the storm despite radar evidence of hail and lightning. The crew refused the clearance, diverted around the weather, and landed safely with slightly less fuel than required for a full diversion.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier flight crew while in cruise smelled the faint smell of cigarette smoke. The 'A' Flight Attendant confirmed that a passenger had lit a cigarette in the forward lavatory. They followed QRH procedures and elected to divert. Law enforcement removed the passenger from the aircraft.
summary: During cruise, the flight crew detected cigarette smoke from a passenger in the forward lavatory, though no EICAS message appeared. The crew followed QRH procedures, consulted Dispatch, and diverted to a nearby airport where law enforcement removed the passenger.

synopsis: Three Aircraft Maintenance Technicians (AMTs), one who was in training, describe their involvement with a B767-300 ETOPs aircraft returning to departure airport with a nose landing gear (NLG) pin not removed. One Technician noted that the AMT in training was not clear on the NLG towing bypass pin and NLG downlock pin locations. Also, the streamer flag for the NLG downlock pin is hidden by the gear strut and fixed gear doors, flag needs to be longer.
summary: Mechanic Z, a trainee, accidentally removed the nose gear towing bypass pin instead of the downlock pin during a B767-300 ETOPS turnaround, causing a gear retraction failure. The error resulted from inexperience, poor flag visibility, and a lack of independent verification before departure.

synopsis: Cirrus SR20 pilot reported encountering icing conditions that forced a return to departure airport.
summary: A VFR pilot departing FAT encountered limited visibility and moderate icing while climbing on an IFR clearance to V165. After the controller initially refused a lower altitude due to the pilot being in IMC, the pilot turned back and eventually broke out of clouds to return to FAT.

synopsis: Small aircraft pilot reported TAN airport runway lights are out of service but no NOTAM to alert pilots of the outage.
summary: A pilot landing at Taunton found runway lights inoperative despite a NOTAM only citing a beacon outage. After failing to activate lights via PCL, the pilot landed on the taxiway, noting the unreported light failure created a safety hazard for unfamiliar crews.

synopsis: PA32 pilot reports departing on a short IFR flight then losing electrical power. The reporter elects to descend to VMC conditions below 1000 feet AGL and return to the departure airport. The landing gear is pumped down manually and the nose gear collapses on touch down.
summary: A pilot experienced a total electrical failure at 3,000 feet while on a base leg vector for a GPS approach, losing all navigation and communications except the transponder. After returning to the departure airport under VFR conditions, the nose gear collapsed upon touchdown following an unsuccessful attempt to confirm gear extension due to the power failure.

synopsis: Turboprop flight crew with an IFR clearance accepts taxi and takeoff instructions for a company VFR flight with a very similar call sign. The First Officer read back his call sign each time thinking the Controller was making an error and the controller ignored it each time thinking the pilot was making an error.
summary: ATC issued VFR instructions to an IFR flight due to a call sign mix-up with another aircraft, despite the crew correcting the call sign multiple times. The crew departed without questioning the conflicting clearances but followed their filed IFR procedure, resulting in no loss of separation.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: A CRP Controller, while instructing, has an aircraft that is supposed to fly heading 350 and join V13. The developmental sees the aircraft not tracking correctly and instructs the aircraft to fly heading 350. The aircraft later enters a MOA because it didn't join V13. The Controller didn't realize at the time that the developmental should have reiterated the heading and also to join the airway.
summary: A trainee controller at Low East radar issued a clearance to Aircraft X to join VICTOR 13 but later clarified the heading, causing the pilot to misinterpret the instruction as a new clearance. The pilot subsequently flew past the airway and entered an active MOA without clearance due to this miscommunication and the supervisor's lack of attentiveness.

synopsis: A PNE Controller reports of three different issues he had while working all the Tower combined.
summary: An air traffic controller reported three incidents involving Aircraft X, Z, U, and V during arrival and departure phases at Runway 6, caused by controller overload, fatigue, and a NORDO aircraft violating Class D airspace. The controller attributed the errors to compressed work schedules and lack of ground controller support, resulting in a go-around, a cancelled takeoff, and a Mandatory Occurrence Report.

synopsis: A B737 Captain reported a ramp employee walked too close to their running engine during taxi-in. The Captain feels a new company policy of delaying APU start until just prior to gate was a factor.
summary: The First Officer attempted to start the APU prior to gate arrival, but it failed twice, requiring Engine 1 to run until ground power connected. The reporter states this new procedure creates a ramp hazard, as a ramp worker nearly walked into the running engine, highlighting the risk of unexpected engine operation at the gate.

synopsis: A B737 flight reported rejecting the takeoff when they noticed smoke coming from air conditioning vents. The smoke was later traced to an engine wash that was done the previous night.
summary: The crew rejected takeoff at ZZZ below 80 knots after smoke and an oil smell emerged from the First Officer's gasper vent following thrust application. Maintenance attributed the incident to a recent engine wash, noting similar past occurrences, and found no damage or system malfunctions during subsequent ground checks.

synopsis: An Air Carrier Dispatcher discovers that one of the flights that was originally dispatched without an alternate required one at the time of departure. The Sabre flight planning software apparently detected the need for an alternate and automatically issued 1;1;3 exemption without the Dispatcher being aware.
summary: A pilot discovered that the Sabre system automatically added a 1-1-3 alternate exemption to a flight release after a new TAF required an alternate, without dispatcher knowledge. The crew accepted the release believing it was legal, raising concerns that the system may have applied exemptions to other flights inappropriately.

synopsis: ERJ-190 flight crew reported encountering strong wake turbulence at FL360 in trail of a B747 on arrival to IAH, which caused a 55-degree bank.
summary: Pilots on a flight at FL360 on the DOOBI2 arrival into IAH encountered wake turbulence from a descending B747, causing a 55-degree right bank and autopilot disengagement. The crew recovered the aircraft, requested a heading change to avoid further wake, and terminated the flight without incident.

synopsis: A CE-560 flight crew reported an airspace violation when they had the wrong airport in sight during a visual approach to a non-towered airport.
summary: The crew visually fixated on closed airport KHLR while approaching uncontrolled KILE, causing an overshoot and brief entry into Gray AAF airspace. The error resulted from MFD distance inaccuracies and failure to identify the correct airport, though the crew corrected the approach and landed safely.

synopsis: During preflight, a Citation crew noticed a puddle of oil beneath the APU drain. Maintenance diagnosed over-servicing as the problem and cleaned up the excess oil. The aircraft was re-released and the crew flew two subsequent flights using the APU during ground ops. After landing on a third flight, the crew started the APU and shut down the engines at the gate. The cabin began to fill with smoke and the aircraft was shut down and the passengers evacuated. Maintenance MELd the APU. A Subsequent crew refused the fly the aircraft. Maintenance then discovered an internal oil leak in the APU.
summary: Pilots reported an APU oil leak and subsequent cabin smoke event, which maintenance initially attributed to over-servicing before later confirming an internal leak. The aircraft was grounded twice after crews refused to fly due to unresolved safety concerns and the lack of a thorough post-smoke inspection procedure.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier turboprop First Officer (FO) reported landing at an alternate in a low fuel situation following multiple unsuccessful instrument approaches at intended destination. FO stated the Captain's planning and decision making were weak.
summary: A First Officer reported that a Captain's poor planning, instrument skills, and CRM led to four failed approaches and a critical fuel deviation to a distant alternate. The crew landed with less than 25 minutes of fuel remaining after the Captain refused to declare an emergency or properly manage fuel reserves.

synopsis: BE-65 pilot reported shutting down right engine when smoke was spotted coming from the nacelle. He was unable to fully extend the landing gear and the gear collapsed on landing.
summary: A single-pilot King Air A90 experienced smoke from the right engine nacelle during climbout, leading to an engine shutdown and subsequent landing gear failure. The pilot successfully evacuated skydivers, executed a gear-up landing with buckled gear, and evacuated uninjured after exhausting all recovery options.

synopsis: L30 Controller reports of an aircraft he wants to turn base but the aircraft reports its too high and needs to extend its downwind. The aircraft then violated another areas airspace because the controller wouldn't accept a point out.
summary: An air traffic controller managing a BE58 and three other aircraft inbound to runway 19 at L30 reported that the BE58 pilot extended the downwind leg due to being too high and fast. This resulted in an airspace deviation into Nellis sector, which the controller attributed to a lack of precise procedures and traffic management between nearby airports.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: MDW Tower Controller reports of IFR conditions at the airport with 70 to 80 knot overtakes on final. Controller reported that C90 continually ran this operation and should be providing or thinking the Tower will be able to provide visual separation to save the overtakes.
summary: C90 TRACON controllers managed a C90 aircraft on an ILS Runway 4R approach, ignoring SIA IFR 500 ceiling data and visual separation restrictions. The controller forced a go-around due to excessive speed and insufficient spacing, citing ongoing non-compliance with separation protocols.

synopsis: VNY Tower Controller reports of releasing an IFR aircraft off the airport when he was instructed by the overlying TRACON to hold for release.
summary: The pilot departed without a release after mishearing SCT's "hold for release" instruction as "release." The pilot attributed the error to confusing phraseology and recommended changing the instruction to simply "hold" to prevent future misunderstandings.

synopsis: DWH Tower controller becomes confused when he doesn't follow facility procedure of telling landing aircraft to turn left and stop. Front Line Manager (FLM) yells at controller and distracts him from remembering if he told the aircraft to stop. Aircraft passes a hold short line becoming a conflict with an arrival to another runway.
summary: An air traffic controller managed conflicting traffic involving Aircraft X, a Sea Ray, and a P28A while Aircraft Y requested landing. The controller failed to obtain a readback for Aircraft X's exit instruction due to supervisor distraction and staffing pressures, causing Aircraft X to encroach on the active runway and forcing Aircraft Y to execute a long landing.

synopsis: ORD Tower Controller reports of miscommunication between him and another Tower Controller that lead to confusion and a go around. Other controller wasn't specific in what was going on which lead the reporter to give the TRACON an unsafe situation.
summary: The tower controller managed departures of Aircraft X and Y while a North Satellite light was active, then diverted arrival Aircraft Z due to an uncoordinated aircraft on Taxiway Tango. The controller reported potential separation loss and confusion caused by unclear tower communications regarding the taxiway conflict and uncoordinated heading changes.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZLA controllers report of asking a pilot if he could make a new altitude restriction. The pilot advised that he could and then Controller issued the instruction. Controller was concerned that the aircraft was 'losing steam' as it approached it assigned altitude. Controller vectored traffic away from climbing aircraft and has a loss of separation due to climbing aircraft not getting level as they said they could.
summary: An ATC trainee and supervisor managed a LAS departure (Aircraft X) and crossing traffic (Aircraft Y) when X unexpectedly lost 1,700 feet while climbing to FL330. The controller issued emergency turns and descents, suspecting a TCAS resolution advisory or flight control issue, though the pilot never confirmed the cause.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: A11 Controller reports of a loss of separation between two IFR aircraft. Controller was distracted working with a VFR aircraft when one of the IFR aircraft descended into the altitude of traffic restricted below it.
summary: An air traffic controller lost lateral separation between IFR Aircraft X and Aircraft Y while distracted by a VFR pilot's request to remain at 1000 ft over Campbell Lake. The controller attributed the loss of separation to frustration with the VFR pilot and a facility culture that discourages denying unnecessary requests during busy operations.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Medium transport flight crew, distracted by weather conditions and lightning on final approach, missed the setting of flaps 30 until reminded by a too low flaps warning. Crew selected flaps 30 and landed.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced an ACARS failure and navigated thunderstorms while approaching BWI, resulting in a "too low flaps" warning at 300 feet due to distraction and checklist omission. Despite the First Officer calling for a go-around, the Captain continued the approach, selected flaps 30, and landed safely in heavy rain and lightning.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Pilot questioned the procedure of automatically cancelling system annunciator lights from known causes (such as the 'ELEC' and 'HYD' lights resulting from single engine taxi) without confirmation. Pilot suggests that such a procedure can foster a bad habit pattern.
summary: The pilot reported that Captains and First Officers often reflexively cancel 'ELEC' or 'HYD' annunciator lights during single-engine taxi without positive identification. This practice hinders error detection and suggests adding a crew confirmation step before taxi to address potential anomalies more effectively.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence, while in a 5-mile trail of an A300 on approach to SDF.
summary: A pilot reported encountering wake turbulence from a preceding heavy A300 while on a right base to 35L at 4000 FT, causing autopilot disconnect and a 200-300 FT altitude loss. The crew executed a go-around due to insufficient separation, attributing the event to the lead aircraft's early speed reduction and calm winds prolonging wake dissipation.

synopsis: During preflight, Embraer crew discovered a weight discrepancy on the Hazmat cargo form. Discussions with Dispatch and Ramp Supervisor resolved the confusion.
summary: The pilot and First Officer identified a weight and balance discrepancy during pre-departure where ground crew omitted 107 lbs of cargo weight from the report due to a language barrier and lack of Hazmat training. The crew corrected the Cargo Load Report after verifying the actual package weight, causing a minor delay but ensuring regulatory compliance.

aircraft: Medium Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Twin turboprop Captain reports receiving a clearance for Radial to Radial navigation to their destination. The First Officer sets up the FMC and the Captain attempts VOR raw data. Neither is successful. Fatigue was cited as a factor.
summary: The Captain and First Officer, both fatigued from recent overtime, incorrectly entered and tuned a radial during the en-route phase after a ground reroute. This resulted in simultaneous navigation errors on two separate systems, placing the aircraft on the wrong radial.

synopsis: An A319 flight crew after landing discovered a pair of vice grip/pliers wedged in the landing gear during the aircraft walk around. Local Maintenance stated that they had not yet touched the aircraft. The Captain concluded that the pliers had been left by the departure station Maintenance.
summary: The First Officer discovered vise grips wedged in the landing gear and open panels during a preflight walkaround at ZZZ1 after a weekly inspection. The crew suspects ZZZ Maintenance left the tools and failed to close panels before signing off the logbook, though they had not touched the aircraft since its arrival ten minutes prior.

synopsis: A DHC-8 flight crew experienced aircraft pressurization indications that they thought to be erroneous. They ran the checklists, descended, and continued to their destination. On landing their ECUs failed requiring Maintenance to reset the ECU circuit breakers. They then taxied to the gate.
summary: The pilot reported erratic pressurization indicators at 16,000 feet, prompting a precautionary descent to 10,000 feet and a minimum fuel declaration. Upon landing, dual engine manual cautions required a circuit breaker reset, resulting in an inability to restart engine #1, forcing a single-engine taxi to the gate.

synopsis: An A319 air carrier pilot reported becoming extremely fatigued as a result of maintenance delays which were followed by long all night flights. The reporter commented the assignment was legal but not safe.
summary: A pilot reported that a severe maintenance delay forced the crew to wait 4.5 hours at the airport instead of resting, resulting in two consecutive red-eye flights and significant fatigue. The pilot attributed this unsafe condition to poor company scheduling decisions that prioritized technical legality over meaningful crew rest.

synopsis: A B-747 flight crew attempted to do a 180-degree turn on a runway due to taxiway closures. The Captain began the turn with about seven knots but was unable to complete the turn with that initial ground speed. The nose tire partially departed the runway and cables were used to get the Aircraft back on to the Runway. The aircraft was found to have no damage and cleared for flight.
summary: The flight crew attempted a 180-degree turn on Runway 08 for Aircraft X, but the nose gear skidded and partially left the pavement due to the runway being 5 feet narrower than required. The aircraft was stopped, pulled back with cables, and cleared for flight after inspection revealed no damage.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Captain reports an uncommanded Right Rudder hard over of approximately 15 degrees and roll had occurred on their MD-80 while climbing thru FL275. Descended to FL240, slowed to 280 knots. Followed QRH and turned Yaw Damper to 'Override'. Descended to FL240. Everything normal. Returned Yaw Damper to 'Normal' position. Landing normal. Maintenance found fault in the restricted rudder portion of the Rudder PCU and Rudder Limiter switch.
summary: During climb through FL275, the crew experienced an un-commanded rudder input while the First Officer hand-flew. The Captain engaged the Yaw Damper Override to resolve the issue, and maintenance later identified a fault in the Restricted Rudder portion of the rudder package.

synopsis: An MD-11 flight crew performed a high speed rejected takeoff just before V1 when the First Officer noted a loss of airspeed and called 'Reject'.
summary: The crew rejected a takeoff at 133 knots on a 455,000 lb aircraft due to a First Officer's call citing loss of airspeed and flickering displays. The stop resulted in hot brakes and tire fuse plug deflation, requiring fire department monitoring and tire replacement before returning to the blocks.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew reported rejecting their takeoff at about 110 kts when the First Officer airspeed indicator became unreliable.
summary: During takeoff, the First Officer reported an airspeed discrepancy on an MD-11, prompting the Captain to reject the takeoff. The crew executed rejected takeoff procedures, managed overheating brakes by taxiing to cool them, and parked for maintenance write-ups regarding the airspeed and brake issues.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A flight crew on final to DAL Runway 13L were advised of a drone on final at 1,000 feet and sidestepped to 13R. They detected the helicopter investigating the drone, but did not see the drone.
summary: The flight crew operating a revenue flight to Dallas was vectored for a visual approach to runway 13L when ATC reported a drone and a law enforcement helicopter on final. The crew accepted a sidestep clearance to runway 13R and landed without incident, observing the helicopter but not the drone.

synopsis: A B777 First Officer reported, due to distractions, that their flight took off without completing the Before Takeoff checklist.
summary: The crew departed without completing the Before Takeoff checklist due to distraction from a complex taxi route and the First Officer changing his display to NAV. The reporter noted that leaving the checklist visible on the screen would have prevented this omission.

synopsis: A B737 flight crew reported experiencing multiple system anomalies that prompted their return to departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced an auto slat failure before takeoff and subsequent flight director and airspeed indicator malfunctions during climb, causing intermittent stick shaker warnings. They returned to the departure airport for a normal landing after the First Officer flew the approach once the stall warnings ceased at a lower altitude.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported they failed to run the landing checklist and were below 800 ft AGL with the gear still up. They executed a go-around and returned for a normal approach and landing.
summary: The flight crew missed the landing gear call during the SFO approach to runway 28R while slowing to 160 knots. A gear warning at 750 feet prompted a go-around, as the crew realized they had failed to complete the landing checklist.

synopsis: A B747 Captain reported his aircraft's navigation system is unable to comply with navigation standards.
summary: The pilot reported significant magnetic variation discrepancies between flight plans and IRS steering at EPLED and BITTE intersections, causing 19 and 16-degree navigation display errors. The reporter concluded the compass error exceeded design limits, preventing compliance with standard aviation navigation auditing requirements.

synopsis: A ramp employee reported a bag of lithium batteries on the ramp near an aircraft smoked for thirty minutes then caught fire. The batteries produced large amounts of toxic smoke.
summary: A bag containing mixed batteries, including lithium, caught fire on the ramp after smoking for thirty minutes. The incident required three fire extinguishers, caused a flight delay and gate change, and posed potential toxic smoke hazards due to unknown contents.

synopsis: An EMB-175 flight crew reported overshooting their cleared altitude during a go-around that was executed because of an unstable approach flown by the new-hire First Officer.
summary: During a New Hire First Officer IOE visual approach at DFW, the student failed to react to an unstable approach call, forcing the Pilot Monitoring to execute a go-around. Task saturation led to a temporary altitude deviation to 3,300 feet before the crew corrected to the assigned 3,000 feet.

synopsis: Dash-8 201 flight crew reported a persistent fire caused by arcing at the First Officer window terminals.
summary: During descent, a First Officer reported arcing and fire at the window heat terminals, which reignited despite two extinguisher discharges. The crew increased airspeed to Vmo, landed safely, and executed an emergency evacuation with no injuries, attributing the incident to window heat failure.

synopsis: BAE-125-850XP Captain reported encountering wake turbulence in 6-mile trail of a B737 on approach to IAD.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe wingtip vortices from a B737 six miles ahead while on the GIBBZ2 arrival into IAD at 4,000 feet. The pilot manually regained control after the autopilot disengaged, climbed to 5,000 feet to escape the turbulence, and completed the approach with no injuries.

synopsis: A B767 flight crew noted an unusual vibration upon gear retraction. They continued to their destination and when they selected gear down the nose gear seemed to immediately fall into place. They did a Tower fly-by and both ATC and another pilot observing said the gear appeared to be extended abnormally. They continued to land without incident.
summary: The crew experienced nose gear vibration on liftoff and abnormal extension indications during a flyby at ZZZ1, prompting a go-around. After maintenance inspection and pin installation on the taxiway, the aircraft landed uneventfully with no damage reported.

synopsis: A B737-800 crew on approach to Runway 07R at PHX in VMC was cleared to continue on 7L, but when selected the 7L appeared out of service. The Captain flying the HUD was a little fast and high during the approach. Later, a GPWS 'PULL UP' alert was received to which the Captain corrects and lands uneventfully.
summary: The crew accepted a visual approach clearance to runway 07L while flying with the HUD and no glideslope. A GPWS 'pull up' alert occurred due to being fast and high, but the Captain corrected the flight path and landed uneventfully.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A First Officer reports that he was off frequency when the Captain received a clearance to level at FL200 to avoid traffic at FL190. The crew then received a TCAS RA and complied with the procedure, but descended 300 feet below FL200.
summary: During descent into CHO, the First Officer misinterpreted ATC vectors and traffic information, causing the aircraft to descend toward a conflicting flight. This resulted in a TCAS RA, a climb that took the aircraft 300 feet below FL200, and the reporter attributed the incident to poor ATC communication and his own misunderstanding of the traffic situation.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 Captain reported being put into an uncomfortable situation on approach to MKE when he had two aircraft in conflict that gave him limited options.
summary: During a visual approach to MKE Runway 1L, the crew received TCAS RAs due to two VFR aircraft crossing their path while ATC failed to establish contact. The pilot attributed the conflict to poor spacing, communication breakdown, and VFR airmanship, noting they should have initiated an earlier go-around.

synopsis: After landing a CRJ crew copied a taxi clearance intended for another aircraft and subsequently entered the approach area for an active runway, which necessitated a go-around by an aircraft on final approach.
summary: Pilots taxiing a jet after landing on runway 9L mistakenly entered the 9R approach area, causing an aircraft to go around. The reporter attributes the incursion to a miscommunication where a clearance intended for another aircraft with a similar call sign was issued and read back without correction by ground control.

synopsis: A Citation crew encountered severe turbulence on departure and diverted for required inspection and maintenance.
summary: Pilots departing on an RNAV SID were vectored to avoid weather but encountered severe turbulence and IMC despite no radar returns. The event disabled the autopilot and caused a momentary control upset, leading to a diversion for inspection before resuming flight.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Air Carrier on the SFO SERFR ONE RNAV was cleared to 6,000 FT approximately 35NM from SFO which is below the SFO Class B 8,000 FT shelf. The Captain delayed to the descent at 7,700 FT to remain near the Class B before descending to 6,000 FT at the 240KT mandated speed.
summary: The pilot descended below the Class B airspace floor while executing the SERFR 1 RNAV arrival into SFO after receiving a clearance to 7000 feet. The incident resulted from the pilot's situational awareness error in starting the descent too early, compounded by the procedure design and ATC clearance.

synopsis: An A320 Flight Attendant reported the Captain executed a rejected takeoff because of a windshear alert. Following the rejected takeoff at least some of the main gear tires deflated.
summary: The Captain aborted takeoff due to a wind shear alert, causing an abrupt stop and tire deflation. The cabin crew assessed the situation, confirmed no immediate danger, and safely deplaned all passengers via stairs and buses with no incidents.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A pilot neglected to switch to the Advisory Frequency for his intended airfield and landed the wrong way on the active runway.
summary: The pilot and a passenger pilot landed on the wrong runway at BTF after cancelling IFR below 7,500 feet and failing to monitor Advisory frequency 122.8. The error occurred due to reliance on the passenger's familiarity, distraction from the passenger's aircraft evaluation, and light variable winds, forcing a Piper Archer to exit Runway 16 to avoid a collision.

synopsis: Cessna 150 pilot experienced a complete engine failure and landed the aircraft in a field.
summary: A pilot flying a Cessna 150J experienced sudden severe engine vibration and power loss at 3,500 feet MSL during cruise, forcing a forced landing in a field. The aircraft flipped onto its back upon touchdown due to the nose wheel digging into the soil, but both occupants escaped uninjured.

synopsis: A Searey LSA pilot detected cockpit smoke while taxiing. The aircraft was secured and evacuated. Reporter discovered an eroded battery case strap which allowed the battery to dislodge and come to rest on an aluminum support, eventually exposing cell posts and shorting. Reportedly, wet rags were used to quench the smoldering material.
summary: The pilot reported smoke from a loose battery after landing and taxiing. An investigation found the dislodged battery abraded its case against an aluminum strap, exposing gel cell posts and causing the smoke.

synopsis: Pilot reports a low fuel pressure alert appeared on his MFD/EFIS display while flying his Zenith CH701 Amateur Build Experimental aircraft with a Rotax 912 Engine Type. A newer designed engine fuel pump that was previously installed to comply with Service Bulletin (S/B) SB-912-063UL had failed. Pilot landed on a Model Airplane strip.
summary: The pilot experienced a Rotax ULS fuel pump failure causing low fuel pressure and engine surge seven miles south of ZZZ. After declaring a Mayday, the pilot landed safely at a nearby RC model strip with no injuries or damage, and the pump was replaced in the field.

synopsis: Gulfstream IV flight crew reported flying through cleared altitude when the pilot flying misunderstood the descent clearance.
summary: The Captain and First Officer descended 750 feet below their assigned FL430 clearance on the MOD5 arrival due to mishearing the altitude and failing to verify the altitude pre-select. The reporter attributed the deviation to procedural failures and fatigue from an early morning departure and maintenance issues.

synopsis: Skylane 182 Instructor and BFR pilot reported a close conflict with another light aircraft at 3,000 FT in the vicinity of HIO.
summary: During an FAA flight review in mountainous Class E airspace, a pilot and CFI nearly collided with another aircraft while both were focused on navigation charts. The CFI initiated a climb after spotting the traffic, causing the other pilot to dive and turn away, though the reporter noted neither aircraft had traffic alert equipment.

synopsis: CE560 Captain reports not noticing the altitude assignment in the routing section of the XEROX3 departure from ROC. Departing Runway 4, 1,200 feet is used as the level off altitude until ATC points out that they should be climbing to 10,000 feet.
summary: The flight crew at KROC misinterpreted the XEROX3 SID top altitude as 1,200 feet due to non-bold text formatting, prompting an immediate climb to 10,000 feet after ATC clarification. The pilots attributed the error to poor chart design and noted they should have resolved their concerns before takeoff.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported taking off slightly over ATOG when the departure was rushed.
summary: The flight crew departed a weight-restricted Boeing 737-800 with 169 passengers after the agent corrected a load sheet error. Dispatch later sent a message to add ten bags, but the crew ignored it as the aircraft was already airborne and the change would have required a new load sheet.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Airline flight crew reports sighting a drone at 1,000 feet during approach to DAL Runway 13L.
summary: During final approach to Dallas Love Field 13L at 1000 feet AGL, the flight crew and jumpseat observer spotted a stationary quadcopter 40 to 50 yards to the right. The aircraft passed the drone without maneuvering, and the crew reported the sighting to Tower before landing without incident.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported engine fire indications during pushback shortly after they started the engine. The crew fired both bottles and returned to the gate after fire was verified out.
summary: During pushback, the flight crew experienced a rapid Engine #1 fire warning while starting the engine. They executed the fire checklist, discharged both bottles, and received clearance from ground personnel and fire crews before taxiing to the gate on Engine #2.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence in climb at FL378, causing a 'very abrupt' roll that resulted in minor injuries to some of the flight attendants working the flight.
summary: During climb to FL380, the crew encountered an abrupt 15-20 degree left roll at FL378, likely caused by wake turbulence from an aircraft five miles away. While no passengers were injured, some flight attendants reported neck and shoulder pain but declined medical assistance and remained fit for duty.

synopsis: B737-700 First Officer reported deviating from the RIIVR2 arrival to LAX when they had difficulty programming the FMS and the aircraft dropped out of LNAV.
summary: Two pilots returning from leave experienced FMC programming errors and automation disengagements during descent into LAX due to an arrival chart anomaly and lack of monitoring. This resulted in being high and off course, requiring ATC vectors and a manual descent, though no altitude restrictions were violated.

synopsis: An Air Carrier Ramp Lead expresses his safety concerns and also describes his work environment where company ramp personnel are being assigned to work a Regional Operator's CRJ-700 aircraft that they are not qualified or trained on. Company Management have been unresponsive to his concerns for safe operations.
summary: Unqualified Air Carrier X ramp personnel in ZZZ serviced Regional Operator X's CRJ aircraft despite lacking training, leading to a towbar error that caused potential damage. Supervisors dismissed safety concerns, while a separate incident on a qualified ERJ-175 resulted in cargo compartment damage and delays.

synopsis: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports a flight crew had noticed a binding, bump feel in both yoke controls when pulling the yoke rearward during their preflight on a Cessna CE-750 aircraft. Troubleshooting later revealed an incorrect cable retaining bolt had been installed on the elevator aft sector that would contact the elevator feel pushrod when the elevator yoke was moved to a nose-up position.
summary: The flight crew and a mechanic found binding in the co-pilot's elevator controls on a CE-750 caused by an oversized cable retaining bolt damaging the feel pushrod. The incorrect hardware and damaged pushrod were replaced, though the reporter noted the issue should have been detected during the recent inspection.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reports sighting a drone in the FFZ traffic pattern and reporting it to the Tower.
summary: A pilot reported a drone hovering near the right base turn for runway 22R, approximately 1 NM northeast of FFZ. Tower dispatched a police helicopter to investigate, which found no drone but located a suspicious vehicle in the area.

synopsis: DA-20 pilot reported flying formation with an aircraft that was unaware of his intentions.
summary: A pilot mistakenly joined formation with an identical Citabria aircraft, believing it to be his friend's plane. The error occurred because the wrong aircraft shared the exact same model, paint scheme, and tail markings, while the intended friend was not flying that day.

synopsis: Pilot of C-182 experienced an engine failure enroute. Application of carb heat enabled the engine to restart. Proceeding to the nearest airport, the engine failed again and the pilot landed on a highway. After inspecting all power plant and fuel systems, and suspecting carb icing as the original problem, the pilot restarted the aircraft and flew to destination after obtaining additional fuel and arranging ground transportation for the passengers.
summary: A pilot carrying two passengers experienced an engine failure at 8,500 feet due to suspected carburetor ice, forcing an emergency landing on an interstate highway. After refueling and confirming no mechanical anomalies, the pilot successfully completed a solo flight to the original destination the following day.

synopsis: LR-40 flight crew reported running off the end of the runway when they experienced failure of brakes, thrust reversers, and autospoilers after touchdown.
summary: The pilot reported a loss of brakes and thrust reversers during landing at Airport ZZZ, causing the aircraft to overrun runway X into the dirt without damage or injury. The pilot attributed the incident to focusing on troubleshooting the systems instead of immediately using the emergency braking handle.

synopsis: A balloon pilot reported that after landing the upper envelope of his balloon was contacted by another balloon whose pilot then took evasive action.
summary: The reporter landed a hot air balloon near a target when another balloon's basket struck their envelope. The reporter attributes the collision to the other pilot prioritizing scoring over maintaining safe altitude and distance, contrary to right-of-way rules.

synopsis: Pilot of a Velocity reported an NMAC with another light aircraft on approach to X26.
summary: A VFR pilot approaching Runway 10 at X26 to avoid jumpers experienced a near miss when a Cherokee passed 200 feet below on a left base for Runway 5. The pilot evaded by climbing, attributing the incident to the Cherokee's lack of communication and misjudgment of distance.

synopsis: A glider crew experienced a rear canopy malfunction resulting in a partially open rear canopy. Front-seat pilot landed the glider.
summary: During a winch launch of a glider, the rear canopy opened in flight due to a broken limit cord eyebolt, causing sudden pressure changes and instructor injury. The student pilot took control, stabilized the aircraft, and landed safely with a cracked canopy.

synopsis: ZMA Front Line Manager (FLM) reports of flow control through a sector that TMU had in place, but the surrounding Towers were not complying with the Call For Release (CFR) that was in place. By not complying, one sector had to hold traffic to attain 10 minutes in trail separation. While working on this problem the FLM noticed a possible loss of separation.
summary: An Area Supervisor reported that satellite towers disregarded TMU release calls for Havana's 10-minute trail requirement, causing excessive vectors and holding. This congestion, compounded by military airspace and weather, led to a conflict alert at R40 where standard separation may have been lost.

synopsis: B777 FO reported they lost all power to the aircraft, indicating a problem with backup systems, during a test flight when they turned off all four generators.
summary: During a standby power check at 15,000 feet, turning off the fourth generator caused a total power loss except for the ISFD and clocks. A contract engineer restored the Captain's systems by striking the P310 panel with a water bottle, allowing the crew to complete a normal hand-flown landing.

synopsis: Ramp employee reported having some difficulty releasing the new tow bar from the aircraft after pushback, causing a 'rough disconnect.'
summary: A wing walker reported a tight tow bar disconnect during pushback on a new aircraft, prompting a mechanic inspection and a return tow to the gate. Mechanics attributed the tightness to a new tow bar and confirmed the aircraft was safe.

synopsis: EMB-145LR flight crew reported pitot tube 2 iced up and showed incorrect information. Indications returned to normal when the flight descended into warmer temperatures.
summary: The crew encountered undetected high-altitude icing while circumnavigating thunderstorms near Chicago, causing Pitot 2 to freeze and display erroneous airspeed at FL350. They followed QRH procedures, descended out of RVSM using Captain and standby instruments, and the system recovered below FL280 as temperatures increased.

synopsis: EMB-145LR First Officer reported encountering wake turbulence on arrival into IAH in trail of a B767-300.
summary: A crew on a LINNK1 arrival to IAH encountered severe wake turbulence from a preceding B767-300 at 3,000 MSL, causing autopilot disengagement. The captain regained manual control, and the reporter attributed the event to following a heavy aircraft despite having more than standard separation.

synopsis: G-200 flight crew reported noticing heading miscompare warning after takeoff. Reporter stated the aircraft 'has a long history of these problems.'
summary: The flight crew experienced a heading miscompare and frozen RMI during climb-out in a G200, caused by magnetic flux anomalies. They informed ATC, aligned instruments to the standby compass, and grounded the aircraft for flux detector inspection after the system temporarily self-corrected.

synopsis: A CE-680 air crew, while enroute, were cleared to fix 'SINDE'. The Captain mistakenly typed the fix as 'CINDE'. The crew began to turn to the wrong fix when they were queried by ATC who also respelled the fix name. The crew entered the correct fix and proceeded as cleared. CINDE is 150 NM northwest of SINDE.
summary: During cruise, the flight crew incorrectly entered "CINDE" instead of the cleared "SINDE" fix due to expectation bias and similar-sounding names, causing a 30-degree heading error. Air Traffic Control detected the deviation and queried the crew, allowing for immediate correction before the aircraft strayed significantly off course.

synopsis: B737 Flight Attendant informed Captain that a contract ramp employee attempted to open a cabin door while an orange band was still across the window.
summary: A flight attendant reported that a contract ramp agent opened an aft door while the slide armed indicator was visible, though the slide was already disarmed. The reporter attributed this safety hazard to inadequate training for the new ramp personnel.

synopsis: B767-200 flight crew reported the autothrottles were deferred INOP and that they got a stall warning in a turn when the speed dropped.
summary: The pilot experienced a stick shaker activation while holding at 14,000 feet with inoperative autothrottles after manually turning past the outbound leg. The event was caused by airspeed decay due to a steepened bank angle and distraction, which was recovered by advancing throttles.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier aircraft departed on the DFW HRPER2 Departure (RNAV) mid-morning and at 9,000 feet the First Officer saw an object believed to be a drone pass by at a close range. The flying Captain did not take evasive action.
summary: During the DFW HRPER departure at 9,000 feet, the First Officer reported a close-range object that might have been a drone, while the Captain did not see it. The First Officer notified ATC, and the flight continued uneventfully.

synopsis: A300-600 Captain reported they diverted to a nearby airport after receiving a Green Hydraulic System Overheat ECAM.
summary: The flight crew diverted to ZZZ1 after a Green Hydraulic system overheat warning persisted during climb and cruise. Upon landing at ZZZ1, a tire deflated due to fuse plug meltdown caused by heavy weight and high density altitude braking.

synopsis: ERJ-175 Flight Attendant reported broken ankle related to turbulence encounter.
summary: A flight attendant was injured during descent into [destination] when unexpected violent turbulence threw her around the cabin, breaking her right ankle. She was treated by paramedics after landing, and she recommends flight attendants remain seated when such weather is anticipated.

synopsis: A Maintenance Manager reports that a pilot for their customer's Cessna Citation Excel aircraft had informed a Ramp Supervisor that wrapping a tow strap around the chrome section of the nose landing gear was incorrect. The Supervisor had noted to the Manager their Lektro tug tow training never said to tow the aircraft that way.
summary: A line service supervisor towing a Citation Excel was instructed by the pilot to move the tow strap from the nose landing gear chrome to the gear casing. The supervisor noted this contradicted his Lektro training and recommended updating FBO procedures to match the Aircraft Maintenance Manual.

synopsis: A Line Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) states that aileron flight control cables had frozen on an ERJ-175 aircraft after he had deferred a Forward Galley coffee maker for lack of water. Technician noted the lack of any information in the MEL about deferring coffee makers and the possibility of flight controls freezing needs to be addressed.
summary: A mechanic deferred inoperative forward coffee makers using the MEL without inspecting for water leaks, unaware that such leaks could freeze and stiffen flight control cables. The reporter noted that completing the Fault Isolation Manual might have discovered the leak and prevented the subsequent inflight emergency on Aircraft X.

synopsis: A B55 Baron pilot reported an NMAC when he overtook a light single in the pattern at DVT.
summary: A pilot flying a Baron into Deer Valley Airport overtook a Cessna on short final for Runway 7L after following tower instructions to trail the slower aircraft. The pilot attributed the close proximity to a possible missed go-around directive, controller workload, and insufficient separation for differing aircraft speeds.

synopsis: SR22 Instructor pilot reported encroaching (or nearly encroaching) on Class B airspace while in the pattern at FTG.
summary: A flight instructor and student flying a private aircraft to FTG for touch-and-gos entered the right base for Runway 8 and inadvertently flew near Class B airspace due to the instructor's outdated memory of the boundary. The instructor realized the error after querying the tower, which confirmed the airspace began at Imboden Road, and subsequently tightened subsequent base turns to maintain clearance.

synopsis: A Helicopter pilot on an instrument approach descended below approach minimum until alerted by Approach Control. The situation was corrected and a safe landing was made.
summary: The pilot hand-flying an aircraft in IMC on final approach descended below the 1,020 feet MSL minimum due to an improper instrument scan. Approach Control alerted the pilot to a low altitude warning, prompting a correction that allowed the approach to be completed without incident.

synopsis: Pilot on a VFR flight changed planned destination enroute inadvertently penetrating a TFR, resulting in an airspace security breach.
summary: The pilot of a Stearman diverted to Airport ZZZ due to passenger medical concerns, inadvertently entering a TFR centered on Wilmington. The pilot attributed the violation to failing to research the new route for TFRs after changing destination in flight, resulting in a Secret Service interview and aircraft search.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Pilot reports that there is a need for safety overruns at the Cortland Country Airport.
summary: A pilot reported that two aircraft accidents occurred at Cortland County Airport (N03) over the past two years, which could have been prevented with safety over-runs. The reporter requested funding for these enhancements to improve safety for the specific aircraft types operating at the facility.

synopsis: Cessna pilots were conducting a simulated engine failure under simulated instrument conditions and failed to make the recommended airport traffic pattern radio calls.
summary: During an Instrument Proficiency Check, a pilot and instructor entered a non-standard pattern for a simulated engine-out landing without monitoring CTAF, causing a conflict with an ultralight. The reporter attributed the near miss to the instructor's decision to withhold airport information, which prevented radio calls and limited traffic scanning to one pair of eyes.

synopsis: A HOM FSS Controller reports of hearing a pilot report to another pilot that they had a NMAC.
summary: An AFIS controller reported a near midair collision between Aircraft X and Aircraft Y on final for Runway 22, caused by Aircraft X failing to contact Homer Radio for traffic advisories. The controller filed a Mandatory Occurrence Report but faced management dispute over not entering the data into CEDAR before their shift ended.

synopsis: ZTL Controller reports of a handoff issues with ZDC. They couldn't handoff a specific aircraft because there was another aircraft with the same call sign that ZDC was attempting to handoff to ZTL.
summary: An air traffic controller at R28 reported that Aircraft X to BWI and Aircraft Y from BWI passed 8 miles apart near GSO due to a failed automated handoff and a missing flight plan at ZDC. The controller attributed the error to high traffic volume and the complexity of the EDST system.

synopsis: A80 controller reports of two aircraft with the same call sign in the airspace, one an arrival and the other was a departure. Controller added a letter to the end of one of the calls signs.
summary: An air traffic controller on Departure Radar North encountered two aircraft from the same airline sharing a call sign, causing confusion and increased workload. The controller resolved the issue by assigning a new call sign to the departing aircraft and updating the ERAM system.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ATC Controller reports of issuing a release to a tower for a departure and issues traffic they are working in close proximity. Tower departs the aircraft and gets visual on the pointed out aircraft. Tower then calls TRACON Controller and says that was close. TRACON Controller does not like that the Tower departed the aircraft so close to the point out.
summary: A tower controller released an IFR departure (Aircraft X) southbound while a VFR aircraft (Aircraft Y) was making passes at 1,000 feet, triggering a Collision Alert. The reporter attributes the conflict to the tower launching the departure directly at the VFR traffic without switching Aircraft Y to tower control.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: ZKC Developmental Controller releases an aircraft from a Tower controlled airport and instructs the Tower to use visual separation. Aircraft comes onto ZKC Controller's radio and Controller is confused on how the Tower provided the use of visual separation.
summary: An OJTI and trainee radar controller lost separation between a departing Aircraft X and an inbound Aircraft Y at GCK after the trainee incorrectly assumed the tower's visual separation responsibility extended beyond departure. The trainee released Aircraft X without issuing a heading, causing it to climb within two miles of Aircraft Y before the OJTI intervened.
