summary: The crew descended below the 8000ft minimum at DOMNO fix while configuring the MCDU for a new arrival clearance, resulting in an open descent mode. They leveled off and climbed back to 8000ft after realizing they were 400 feet low, though ATC did not mention the deviation.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports being unable to comply with ATC instructions to avoid restricted airspace while deviating around thunderstorms and tells ATC to inform the restricted airspace controlling authority of his presence.
summary: The Captain and First Officer encountered turbulence while climbing from LAS and requested a west deviation to avoid thunderstorms. After ATC instructed a turn toward weather and cited a restricted area, the Captain refused the clearance and asserted authority to avoid the hazard.

synopsis: CRJ-700 flight crew reported smelling smoke on short final which was observed and confirmed by the Flight Attendant. They evacuated the aircraft after landing.
summary: During short final, the crew detected a fireworks-like smell and visible smoke in the cabin, prompting the flight attendant to recommend evacuation. The captain coordinated with ATC, executed the evacuation checklist, and evacuated the aircraft, resulting in no injuries.

synopsis: The ERJ170 crew received a takeoff configuration warning because of an incorrect entry into the FMS. The captain decided to continue the takeoff as he determined that the aircraft was properly configured and there was another aircraft on short final.
summary: The Captain incorrectly entered flaps 4 in the FMS weight and balance page instead of the performance page, triggering a false takeoff configuration warning. Despite verifying physical flap settings, the Captain felt pressured by an aircraft on final and continued the takeoff instead of rejecting it.

synopsis: A Captain reported having difficulty activating his new iPad as an EFB for a trip. Company procedures and policies complicated the effort.
summary: A pilot refused a flight assignment due to an inability to activate a second Electronic Flight Bag (EFB) iPad caused by a discontinued bracket and absent technical support staff. The Regional Chief Pilot eventually activated the app shortly before departure, resolving the issue after the pilot cited safety risks regarding single-IFR operations and manual compliance.

synopsis: On visual approach to a foreign airport with the First Officer flying, the aircraft was vectored in high and close such that the stabilized approach criteria was not met at 500 FT AGL. The Captain took the aircraft and elected to land.
summary: ATC vectored the aircraft too close to the final approach fix, causing an unstable ILS approach where the First Officer initiated a go-around at 500 feet. The Captain took control, rejected the go-around, and landed the aircraft safely despite high sink rates and full-scale glideslope deviation.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: The crew was cleared to descend via the ALDAN1 ILS 23R RDU but was high at BUTTS. The reporter misread the crossing restriction due to workload and referencing the Electronic Flight Bag (EFB).
summary: Pilots descending via the ALDAN1 arrival to RDU crossed waypoint BUTTS at 8,000 feet instead of 8,000 feet, prompting ATC concern about the upcoming ILS turn. The crew attributed the high altitude and setup difficulty to the single-page display limitation of their Electronic Flight Bag during high workload.

synopsis: B757 Captain reports having to penetrate heavy rain and turbulence while conducting a localizer only approach. Due to gusty wind conditions the final flap selection was delayed until the indicated airspeed permitted, resulting in the final configuration not being achieved prior to 1000 feet AGL. The captain evaluated landing versus going around in increasingly hazardous weather conditions and elected to land.
summary: The flight crew encountered heavy rain, turbulence, and windshear while executing a LOC RWY 9 arrival at MIA in thunderstorms. Despite exceeding flap speed limits and completing the checklist below 1000 feet, they continued to a normal landing, attributing the difficulty to the inactive ILS and steep LOC glidepath.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported that they received an alert indicating loss of Hydraulic System 1. A safe landing was made at their destination.
summary: The crew experienced a Hydraulic System 1 leak at cruise, triggering an alert and pump shutdown. They landed uneventfully on the longest runway, where fire crews confirmed fluid leakage from the port side and a slow leak in Brake System 1 accumulator.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported declining an all-nighter flight due to fatigue from an emergency on the previous leg which involved a lengthy procedure and delay.
summary: The flight crew experienced a flap retraction failure after takeoff, requiring a 75-minute fuel burn and non-standard landing. Concerned that fatigue from the irregular event and overnight delay would compromise safety, the pilots refused to continue the next segment without an intervening rest period.

synopsis: A B737 crew was not able to retract the flaps from the flaps 5 position after takeoff so they circled to burn down to landing weight and landed uneventfully. Communication with the company was difficult.
summary: During climbout at 3,000 feet AGL, flaps stopped responding at the 5 position, forcing a return to the departure airport after burning fuel below maximum landing weight. The crew calculated their own Flaps 15 landing data after Dispatch could not provide it, and communication difficulties with Dispatch were resolved by switching to ACARS.

synopsis: Hawker 800XP Captain reported an inflight shut down following a high oil pressure problem. Reporter stated the issue had been written up nine times over the last three months.
summary: During the climb phase, the flight crew encountered high oil pressure on engine 1, requiring thrust reductions and an eventual inflight shutdown. The crew noted this anomaly had been documented in nine work records over three months prior to this event.

synopsis: HS 125-800 experienced an engine rollback during takeoff resulting in a high speed rejected takeoff. This was caused by an engine computer failure.
summary: During takeoff roll on runway 16 at Airport ZZZ, the crew aborted after the right engine rolled back at approximately 95 KIAS, activating rudder bias. Post-abort inspection revealed a number 2 engine computer failure, leading to a safe taxi to the FBO and flight cancellation.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reports the Captain took the controls at 500 feet AGL and landed even though they were not fully stabilized.
summary: The pilot flying and captain were hand-flying an ILS 12L approach at Airport ZZZZ when inadequate ATC vectors prevented glide slope capture. Despite the pilot initiating a go-around at 500 feet due to an unstable approach, the captain took control and landed the aircraft.

synopsis: CRJ-700 First Officer reported they failed to continue the climb beyond the first restriction because of lack of clarity within the cockpit of the meaning of a 'climb via' clearance.
summary: The flight crew leveled off at 10,000 feet during the SPAZZ3 departure after misinterpreting a "climb via SID" clearance due to the absence of a new altitude assignment. This misunderstanding stemmed from the crew's expectation of a specific altitude instruction, leading to a query from ATC before a corrected clearance was issued.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported detecting smoke in the cabin coming from a sidewall vent. The flight diverted to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: Flight attendants detected smoke and an electrical burning smell from a sidewall vent near row 30 during cruise, prompting the Captain to divert and land safely. The crew secured the cabin and turned off in-seat power, though the specific fire source remained unconfirmed.

synopsis: Small aircraft pilot reports approaching his destination and noting it is between weather cells on his XM and ADSB NexRad weather displays. While on vectors for the ILS, 1,000 feet is lost due to downdrafts. After regaining the lost altitude the reporter diverts to his alternate to wait out the weather.
summary: The pilot encountered severe downdrafts and windshear while approaching MQS for an ILS 29 landing, causing a rapid 1,000-foot altitude loss and control difficulties. After climbing back to 2,500 feet, the pilot diverted to the alternate airport, LNS, and landed safely, attributing the incident to weather conditions worse than depicted on radar.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported a UAS in the vicinity of his aircraft and reported the encounter to ATC.
summary: A passenger on a flight observed a red and silver drone-like object at the one o'clock low position for 3 to 5 seconds. The crew queried ATC, which reported no traffic in the vicinity, and subsequently advised the controller of the encounter.

synopsis: The pilot of a tailwheel aircraft equipped with heel brakes was unable to prevent a runway excursion. The sudden wind and the brake system design were contributing factors.
summary: A pilot with over 2000 tailwheel hours lost directional control on Runway XXL during landing due to a 4-6 knot crosswind, despite full right rudder. The pilot intentionally exited onto the grass to avoid a ground loop, stopped using heel brakes, and returned to the runway, attributing the event to the lack of toe brakes.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper Super Cub experienced an engine problem on climb out. When unable to determine a solution, the pilot elected to perform an off field landing in an irrigated pasture.
summary: During climb out from Runway 35, the engine sputtered and quit, preventing the pilot from maintaining altitude or returning to the runway. The pilot executed a straight-ahead off-field landing in a muddy, irrigated pasture with no injuries reported.

synopsis: PA28 Instructor reports using the tow bar to position his aircraft at the fuel pump then forgetting to remove it before attempting to taxi. The propeller strikes the tow bar during taxi and the aircraft is shut down.
summary: An instructor and two students in a training aircraft taxied away from a fuel pump with a tow bar still attached to the nose gear. The tow bar struck the propeller during taxi, causing damage, which the pilot attributed to fatigue, poor decision-making, and failing to perform a walk-around inspection.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: An instructor pilot reports departing BRD VFR and discovering airborne that the field is IFR. The tablet software showed VFR while the weather in the avionics (G-1000) showed IFR when zoomed out. The ASOS was not transmitting at departure time but later reported 2.5 miles visibility.
summary: Two pilots in a G-1000 equipped aircraft departed BRD VFR after observing conflicting weather reports between ForeFlight, G-1000, and ASOS. The crew relied on visual observations of 4+ miles visibility to continue VFR, noting that system delays and data conflicts prevented immediate IFR filing.

synopsis: Intending to file an enroute IFR flight plan, the pilot of a Cessna 182 misunderstood instructions from ATC to do so with Flight Service Station as an order to change frequencies. With only a single radio, this caused a loss of communication with ATC Center.
summary: A pilot on a VFR training flight requested an IFR clearance from Center due to forecast mountain obscuration but was directed to contact FSS to file the plan. The pilot experienced communication confusion and a handoff delay because the single-radio aircraft required leaving the frequency, leading to a late IFR filing point.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A corporate jet flight crew reported confusion at PSP regarding the hold short line for the temporary Runway 13R.
summary: The flight crew inadvertently crossed the hold short line for Runway 13R at PSP while taxiing, caused by confusion over a non-standard line location due to recent construction and outdated charts. Ground control instructed them to contact the tower, where they were subsequently cleared for takeoff.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: A pilot reported that RSW METAR at times was inaccurate with outdated conditions or conditions which have not occurred.
summary: Pilots, dispatchers, and meteorologists at RSW reported inaccurate METAR/SPECI and ATIS weather data caused by improper ATC augmentation of the ASOS. This resulted in poor decision-making and flight planning errors, including false reports of thunderstorms and funnel clouds.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper Arrow inadvertently rotated the fuel selector valve beyond the intended position which resulted in fuel starvation. The pilot was able to reposition the valve and resupply fuel to the engine.
summary: During an IFR climb to 4,000 ft, the pilot inadvertently selected the fuel selector to OFF instead of the left tank, causing engine failure. The pilot executed an emergency checklist, restarted the engine, and landed safely, attributing the incident to a faulty selector stop and confirming a need for repair.

synopsis: MU-2 Captain experiences very cold conditioned air at FL180. Initial attempts to warm the air are unsuccessful until manual is selected, then the air becomes too hot producing smoke. Attempts to cool the air using manual control are unsuccessful initially, so the bleeds are turned off and the aircraft is descended to 11,000 feet. Flight continues to destination at 11,000 feet.
summary: During cruise at FL180, a pilot experienced sudden cabin overheating and smoke after manual temperature adjustments, prompting a descent to 11,000 feet. The crew isolated the issue by turning off bleed air switches, and mechanics later identified the auto temperature control box for the Air Cycle Machine as the probable cause.

synopsis: Gulfstream II flight crew reported confusion with the approach clearance issued by a MMTJ ATC controller.
summary: The pilot reported confusion during an IFR approach to TIJ after receiving a clearance for the VOR2 approach without specific vectors. The crew had to make short-notice changes to intercept a radial, which the pilot described as potentially unsafe and incompatible with FMS procedure turn capabilities.

synopsis: BE36 pilot reported a NMAC with another aircraft on a visual approach to UMP when he became disoriented and flew a track to the wrong runway.
summary: The pilot, flying a visual approach to UMP, confused runway 15 with 33 due to a thought error and approach's speed instruction. This resulted in landing on the reciprocal runway while a departing aircraft passed overhead, a situation attributed to poor pattern discipline and lack of a formal briefing.

synopsis: Cessna 172 pilot reported losing directional control after landing and hitting a taxiway sign.
summary: The pilot in command of an aircraft at FXE experienced a hard landing and high-speed taxi due to crosswind and excessive rudder input. The aircraft skidded off the runway and struck a taxiway sign, an outcome the pilot attributed to failing to execute a timely go-around.

synopsis: Pilot reported departing 1H0 northbound using a Garmin 530W to show the Class B airspace above. During the climb, the reporter became confused as to the floor of the Class B ring in his immediate vicinity and quickly dived to 1100 feet, exceeded 250 knots, and descended below 1,000 feet AGL over a populated area.
summary: The pilot entered St. Louis Class B airspace without authorization while climbing from 1,600 to 3,000 ft MSL. Confusion over Garmin 530W altitude data caused an unauthorized descent to 1,100 ft MSL at excessive speed over a populated area before exiting the airspace.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: A New York Center (ZNY) Controller reports of an aircraft that drops sky divers while conflicting traffic for it is inbound to an airport in close proximity. The Controller thinks this operation is not safe. The pilot was not on frequency all of the time and was off coordinating on UNICOM.
summary: An ATC controller reported that Aircraft X released jumpers despite traffic advisories for Aircraft Y, then descended rapidly without responding to calls while coordinating with UNICOM. This resulted in a potential target merge and an exceptional vertical rate alert, highlighting ongoing safety concerns with the operator lacking a Letter of Agreement.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew report being cleared to taxi via Taxiways B, F1 and A to the gate, but were not sure that they used taxiway F1 to transition to A. Signage is reportedly lacking and the depicted boxed inset on the 10-9 page is not representative of what is visible from the taxiways.
summary: The Captain and First Officer taxied at SFO after landing on Runway 28R but struggled to identify Taxiway F1 due to poor ground markings and confusing signage. They inadvertently cut from Taxiway B to F1 prematurely but successfully joined Taxiway A without incident, attributing the difficulty to inadequate visual aids compared to the departure area.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew experiences a main gear tire failure just prior to rotation and continues the takeoff. The gear is left down and the A hydraulic system fails shortly thereafter. The flight returns to the departure airport.
summary: The crew continued takeoff after a #2 tire blowout at 150 KIAS, lost 'A' system hydraulics, and landed with gear down. The aircraft was shut down on the runway, and passengers were deplaned via air stairs while cargo remained onboard.

synopsis: B737 First Officer describes a difficult arrival to DEN due to weather, holding, and fuel considerations.
summary: The Pilot Flying reported that fatigue, poor weather warnings, and saturated ATC caused fuel concerns and duty time risks during a Denver arrival. The crew proactively diverted to Cheyenne as an alternate after being vectored away from the destination, eventually landing safely at Denver.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier captain reported noncompliance with a published speed restriction on the PDX TMBRS2 STAR due to a low cost index profile programmed in the FMC computer with automation engaged.
summary: The pilot flying the TMBRS2 Arrival exceeded the 280-knot speed restriction by maintaining 285 knots while using Cost 40 index. The violation occurred because the pilot failed to notice the restriction box on the chart during the arrival briefing, prompting an ATC inquiry.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported he was not satisfied with maintenance releasing his aircraft for service after a hydraulic leak was found. Maintenance ultimately agreed with the reporter.
summary: A pilot reported a hydraulic fluid leak on the ramp after parking, which Contract Maintenance initially dismissed as normal venting. After the pilot provided photographic evidence of the leak source, Maintenance reversed their decision and grounded the aircraft.

synopsis: B737 flight crew described the extra workload and opportunities for errors when they received multiple departure runway assignment changes on taxi out at DEN.
summary: The flight crew experienced multiple runway assignment changes between Runway 8 and 17R during pre-taxi and taxi phases at Denver. These frequent changes by Ground Control forced repeated reprogramming and re-briefing, which the pilot identified as a major source of potential errors and operational delays.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported taking off with a 15 knot tailwind because they were never told about the current conditions.
summary: The pilot reported that while taxiing for takeoff on runway 25R, a preceding aircraft went around due to a 15-knot tailwind not reflected in the ATIS. The crew continued their takeoff after passing 80 knots, noting they could have queried the controller about the go-around to obtain current wind information.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reports being admonished by his Captain and a Maintenance Technician for reporting an eroded silicone seal on the engine cowl strake resulting in a delay.
summary: A pilot reported recurring erosion of the cowling strake moisture seal on Boeing 737-700/800 aircraft during preflight, causing delays due to a lack of company MEL procedures. The situation escalated into a verbal confrontation with the captain and led the pilot to terminate the trip, citing the need for a standardized maintenance fix.

synopsis: Pilot reports of marginal weather inbound to LAX and being asked if they could maintain visual with another aircraft. Pilot responded that they could, but would lose the aircraft when it went into the cloud deck. Controller told them to maintain an altitude, then cleared them for the ILS. Pilot wondered why controller would issue the visual when they were aware of the clouds and why did the Controller not issue a clearance cancellation.
summary: The flight crew, while on an ILS 25L approach in IMC, was instructed to maintain visual separation and climb to 3800 FT despite holding an instrument approach clearance. This resulted in a high and fast arrival at the FAF, which the crew attributed to poor ATC controlling and confusing verbiage.

synopsis: B767-300 Captain believes that under certain wind conditions, takeoffs and landings at SEQM can be very dangerous. While departing on the Condorcocha departure from Runway 18, two instances of stick shaker occur during the turn to the north. Landings are also problematic during these wind events.
summary: The pilot reported an unstable approach and multiple stick shaker activations during departure from Quito (UIO) due to severe mountain wake turbulence and variable winds. The pilot attributed the hazardous conditions to unpredictable wind shear near the Andes, noting that standard procedures were insufficient to maintain safe flight parameters.

synopsis: EMB175 Flight Crew reports being cleared direct to CAYKO on the ROYAL6 departure but selects and confirms direct KEOKK. ATC detects the error and gives the crew a phonetic spelling of the fix name.
summary: During initial climb from MCI, the crew inadvertently loaded fix KEOKK instead of the cleared CAYKO due to high workload and insufficient verification. Departure Control identified the error when the crew confirmed the wrong heading, prompting a corrective heading of 310 before being cleared direct to KEOKK.

synopsis: The crew experienced three hard rolls to the right and vibrations. They disconnected the autopilot and returned to the departure airport.
summary: The First Officer experienced three uncommanded hard right rolls with vibrations while the autopilot was engaged, suspecting a spoiler deployment. The Captain took control, hand-flew the approach to ZZZ, and landed safely; the aircraft was subsequently grounded for maintenance with no EICAS messages recorded.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: After receiving a direct clearance to PEVEE while flying the LAX HOLTZ9 SID, a slight track deviation resulted as the waypoint was inadvertently deleted while intending to execute direct PEVEE.
summary: During the HOLTZ9 RNAV departure, the Pilot Flying and Pilot Monitoring reported that the PEVEE waypoint was unexpectedly deleted from the FMS after activation. The crew re-entered the fix and executed an immediate turn to resume the SID after deviating slightly northwest of the waypoint.

synopsis: B767-300 First Officer describes a maintenance test flight that results in false master warnings that cannot be silenced by any QRH procedures. A Maintenance technician is aboard and appropriate circuit breakers are pulled. The reporter believes that all QRH's should have procedures to silence false master warnings which are very distracting.
summary: During a 767 maintenance test flight, pilots experienced repeated false Master Warning horns for 'CONFIG' and 'FLAPS' after takeoff due to unsuccessful repairs. The crew silenced the distracting aural alerts by pulling Circuit Breakers B-16 and H-35, allowing them to land uneventfully despite the lack of a QRH procedure for false warnings.

synopsis: Upon advancing throttles for takeoff, a 777 pilot reported receiving an EICAS takeoff configuration warning due to Main Landing Gear not locked for takeoff. A low speed rejected takeoff was performed.
summary: The crew rejected takeoff on the captain's leg after a master warning and configure gear steering alert appeared on the EICAS upon advancing thrust. The pilot attributed the warning to insufficient rollout distance before gear lock and subsequently departed uneventfully.

synopsis: MD11 Captain departing VHHH reports being cleared to FL140 by ATC. Upon leveling at FL140, he is advised that the clearance was to FL120. Both pilots believe they heard and read back FL140.
summary: During departure, the crew and ATC experienced a clearance discrepancy where the crew read back FL140 while ATC intended FL120. The reporter notes that the situation could have been corrected if ATC had recognized the incorrect readback of the intended altitude.

synopsis: MD11 flight crew reports being cleared for the SEAVU2 Arrival to the ILS 25L at LAX and the FMC is programed accordingly. Crossing SEAVU it suddenly became apparent that the active waypoint was not appropriate for the ILS 25L approach appearing to be the ILS 24L instead. The crew quickly corrects the FMC just as SCT takes notice of the track deviation. The Captain may have accidentally switched the secondary flight plan in the FMC.
summary: The Captain accidentally swapped the active and secondary flight plans in the FMS while preparing for the ILS 25L approach into LAX, causing the aircraft to deviate 1.1 nm right of course at the SEAVU waypoint. The crew corrected the FMS input and returned to the proper approach path, landing without incident.

synopsis: During preflight at SFO a flight crew discovered the ACARS printer was out of paper and so read the PDC, but incorrectly. After takeoff ATC issued sequential vectors until the filed route was acquired.
summary: The flight crew programmed the incorrect TRUKN2 departure instead of the cleared NIITE2 into the FMS due to reading the screen without a printed PDC comparison while distracted by ACARS paper and release issues. ATC vectored the aircraft to the correct route after the first fix, and the flight continued without further incident.

synopsis: CRJ700 Captain experiences a takeoff warning due to takeoff configuration and rejects the takeoff. The First Officer selected flaps 8 for the reject and believes they were up when the takeoff roll was initiated.
summary: The Captain and First Officer rejected take-off after a 'Takeoff Config' warning appeared due to suspected incorrect flap settings. The Captain attributed the error to inattention during checklists, specifically failing to visually verify the flap indication on ED1 or the 'Takeoff Config OK' message.

synopsis: A CRJ taking off on one runway had a potential near-miss/conflict with a CRJ landing on an intersecting runway. The landing aircraft was instructed by the Tower to go-around.
summary: ATC cleared a departing aircraft on Runway 27L and an arriving aircraft on intersecting Runway 36 simultaneously, causing a loss of separation at approximately 200 feet AGL. The arriving aircraft executed a go-around to avoid the departing flight, which the crew attributed to ATC error and inadequate spacing.

synopsis: A flight instructor with 2 students became distracted and started the engine with the tow bar still attached to the nose landing gear of a Piper Cherokee, causing damage to the propeller.
summary: The pilot and two students experienced a propeller strike while taxiing at Airport ZZZ after the nose gear tow bar was left attached. The incident resulted in damage to the propeller and tow bar, caused by the pilot's failure to remove the bar and complete a walk-around inspection before engine start.

synopsis: An EMB175 Flight Attendant describes an unexpected encounter with severe turbulence that causes them an injury.
summary: Two flight attendants serving beverages encountered unexpected severe clear air turbulence, causing one to strike her head and neck on overhead bins while securing a galley cart. The pilots had no prior warning, but the crew protected passengers and the injured attendant continued working the remainder of the trip.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: General Aviation pilot reports there is a depression about one inch deep that presents a danger when taxiing at SQL. The depression is near the wash rack.
summary: A pilot reported a one-inch deep depression on the taxiway from C Hangars to Piombo near the wash rack, posing a risk of aircraft damage or collision. Airport management stated repairs are delayed for years due to funding issues, despite the hazard existing for months.

aircraft: M-20 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: During the takeoff following alternator maintenance, a M-20 pilot experienced what he believed was a complete power loss. He landed long and rolled of the runway end. Later, Maintenance found number four piston top and both its spark plugs damaged.
summary: The pilot declined an intersection departure for a full-length takeoff post-maintenance, then experienced a complete loss of engine power at 150 feet AGL. The aircraft overshot the runway into a grass field, and subsequent examination revealed spark plug and piston damage in cylinder #4 following alternator maintenance that involved removing fuel servo air ducting.

synopsis: LAX Local Assist reports of two Super aircraft east of Taxiway Whiskey which is not allowed if an aircraft is on the ILS to Runway 24L. Controller did not advise local which was a developmental to ask the pilot if they could accept a visual approach instead of the ILS. This would have solved the problem.
summary: Local Control 2 and Local Assist 2 at LAX allowed two Super aircraft east of Taxiway Whiskey during an ILS approach to Runway 24L, violating a new rule. The controller attributed the violation to training inexperience and the first aircraft's unpreparedness for departure.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: HCF Controller reports of a new procedure that he needs to coordinate with a FLM. The controller cannot find a FLM and then States Article 65. The controller does not know why the FLMs are not being able to be found when this is part of the procedure.
summary: An R7 controller at HCF could not complete a required IAFDOF procedure for Aircraft X at FL390 because no supervisor responded to calls. The controller reported that this new procedure distracts from traffic monitoring, creating a safety risk and potential for mid-air collision.

synopsis: B767-300 Flight Crew reports being cleared to pass abeam CCC at 12000 feet and 250 knots and cross ROBER at 9000 feet. The ZBW Controller involved believes the clearance was to expect ROBER at 9000 feet and sends the crew back up to 12000 feet.
summary: The pilot flying descended below the assigned 12,000 feet while approaching ROBER, believing they were cleared to cross at 9,000 feet instead of the expected altitude. ATC queried the deviation and instructed a climb back to 12,000 feet, attributing the error to confusion between "cross" and "expect" restrictions on the STAR.

synopsis: SPI Tower Controller departed a slow aircraft and minutes later departed a faster aircraft. The controller forgot to advise the departure controller not to turn the slower aircraft until they were turning the faster aircraft. The controller then went to work on putting in a new flight plan on the faster departure because somehow it was removed. The controller does not know if there was a loss of separation.
summary: The Tower Controller managed departures for Aircraft X and Y but failed to coordinate a turn restriction for Aircraft X while resolving a flight plan error for Aircraft Y. This distraction by ground duties caused a potential loss of radar separation as Aircraft X turned toward Aircraft Y's path.

synopsis: ZLA Controller hands off an aircraft to another sector. The handoff, because of a Temporary Altitude in the scratch pad area, goes to another sector. The handoff should have went to the sector that the aircraft was 'temped' at, not one that is possibly a future scope.
summary: An air traffic controller stopped Aircraft X at FL330 due to descending traffic but the auto handoff incorrectly transferred it to ZAB65 instead of ZAB91. The controller attributed this safety risk to a system flaw and a sector combination driven by training needs rather than staffing requirements.

synopsis: A80 controllers report of using fusion radar on the final sectors. Controller turns an aircraft into a hole, the aircraft did not turn as the controller thought it would, then jumped showing it on a different then assigned heading., The controller had visual separation so all was good separation wise, but didn't like the way the aircraft jumped. Controller exclaimed and another controller also saw what happened. Controller thought the jumping of radar targets on final is unacceptable.
summary: Final controllers at ATL experienced significant radar target jumping and false returns on the Fusion display due to the LZU ASR operating in IBI mode. The team temporarily switched to single-sensor mode to ensure accurate traffic presentation until Tech Ops resolved the feed issue.

synopsis: B737-700 First Officer (FO) reported encountering icing conditions at FL390 that could have been a factor in the later failure of both bleed valves that resulted in loss of cabin pressure.
summary: Pilots enroute at FL390 encountered unusual high-altitude icing and subsequent dual bleed air trips, causing a rapid cabin altitude rise and emergency descent. The bleed systems reset automatically at FL220, restoring normal pressurization, though the crew suspects the icing may have caused the valve failures.

synopsis: Dispatcher experiences a loss of ACARS communication with one of his flights while inbound to MMMX during a weather event. Attempts at voice communication through Commercial Radio are also unsuccessful. The communication outage lasts for over one hour, until the aircraft lands safely in MMMX.
summary: A flight to MMMX lost ACARS and voice contact with dispatch for over an hour while holding in adverse weather due to system failure. The dispatcher could not locate the aircraft until ground verification, prompting a recommendation to equip flights with SELCAL or SATCOM for direct contact.

synopsis: B777 flight crew experiences the loss of the Center Hydraulic System on final approach with the aircraft fully configured for landing. The crew elects to continue the approach to landing and is then towed to a hard stand due to the loss of nosewheel steering.
summary: The flight crew landed an aircraft on ILS 7L at VHHH after a center hydraulic system failure caused a burst line and steering loss. They elected to continue the approach due to terrain constraints, successfully exiting the runway using rudder pedals before being towed to a hardstand.

synopsis: B777 flight crew experiences an APU fire indication and automatic shut down just prior to push back. Difficulties communicating with ground personnel and company representatives are reported.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced an APU fire indication and fire bottle discharge on the ground with engines shutdown, causing a total loss of electrical power and blank screens. The crew contacted ATC for fire services, confirmed no actual fire, and deplaned passengers after the Fire Chief verified the situation, though ground power and air conditioning were never restored.

synopsis: A321 flight crew experiences a TCAS RA at 4,500 feet over FFZ during a visual approach to Runway 26 at PHX. The RA commands a climb that leads to a go-around. The intruding aircraft is never sighted by the crew.
summary: The pilot flying received a TCAS RA to climb at 4,100 feet during the EAGUL6 arrival into PHX due to an uncontacted aircraft that intermittently appeared on radar. The crew aborted the approach, landed safely, and later learned the target was likely a white crop duster or drone flying erratically near the approach path.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported receiving TCAS 'descend' commands on a parallel approach to DFW that took them down to 1500 FT and prompted a low altitude alert from Tower.
summary: A 737 crew inbound to DFW on an ILS approach to 17L received TCAS 'descend' RAs due to a parallel descending aircraft on 17C. The crew complied, descending below 3000 FT and receiving a low altitude alert before resolving the conflict at 1500 FT AGL and landing safely.

synopsis: M20K pilot experiences a lengthy ground delay during which time the mixture is ground leaned. Once cleared for takeoff the mixture is not returned to full rich, resulting in low power and rising temperatures. During the return the lean mixture setting is detected and corrected prior to landing.
summary: The pilot of a Mooney 231 experienced low fuel flow and high engine temperatures shortly after takeoff due to the mixture being left in the ground lean position. The pilot attributed this error to distractions from a complex clearance and taxi delay, corrected the mixture mid-flight, and landed safely.

synopsis: R22 instructor pilot experiences a NMAC with a powered glider in the BDN traffic pattern. The glider was apparently thermaling with no intent to land and was not using radios.
summary: During initial approach to Bend Airport, a helicopter and an electric-powered glider experienced a near-midair conflict while both were in the downwind for Runway 34. The glider, which had no radio, turned toward the helicopter at the same altitude, forcing the helicopter pilot to take control and alter course to avoid collision.

synopsis: CE550 Captain requests weather deviation on the ADDEL1 arrival to HND and a speed of 225 knots for turbulence from ZLA, which is approved before switching to LAS Approach. The speed information is apparently not passed to Approach by ZLA and the Approach Controller is not happy.
summary: The Citation Bravo pilot deviated south of the ADDEL1 arrival into Las Vegas for weather and turbulence. While LA Center approved the deviation, Las Vegas Approach expected 250 knots; the pilot maintained a safer 225 knots but admitted they should have explicitly informed Approach of the reduced speed.

synopsis: L39 pilot reported ATC questioned his speed in the DC SFRA and appeared confused about the difference between IAS and ground speed.
summary: A pilot conducting a VFR training flight at 13,500 feet within 60 NM of DCA was advised by Potomac TRACON of a speed violation due to 310 knots ground speed. The pilot maintained 230 knots indicated airspeed as required, attributing the high ground speed to altitude and tailwinds, and suggested clarifying SFRA rules to distinguish between indicated and ground speed.

synopsis: PA28 pilot experiences an engine failure after takeoff and lands in a field.
summary: The pilot reported an engine failure shortly after takeoff, necessitating an off-field landing. No specific aircraft type, altitude, or further cause was detailed in the narrative.

synopsis: ZOB Controller reports of a Controller coming to work and attempting to find out from medical if they can take some medicine and work. Time passes and there is no answer from medical. Controller complains about not being able to find out if a Controller can work while taking a specific type of medicine.
summary: An air traffic controller reported an inability to obtain immediate medical clearance for medication due to the lack of a 24/7 on-call doctor. The controller stated this six-month gap in coverage prevents timely fitness-for-duty determinations, creating an unacceptable risk to 24/7 operations.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports not noticing the 280 knot speed restriction on the FWA6 Departure due to chart positioning on his iPad.
summary: The flight crew missed a 280-knot speed restriction at the top of the FORT WAYNE 6 Departure chart while climbing to cruise. The error occurred because the iPad chart was zoomed in, obscuring the restriction, prompting a request for better highlighting or FMC programming.

synopsis: B737 flight crew experience a VNAV disconnect during the HYDRR1 RNAV Arrival into PHX approaching CHAVO. CHAVO may have been crossed 200 feet low and the speed was allowed to increase above the CHAVO limit of 210 knots.
summary: During a B737 HYDRR1 RNAV arrival into PHX, the crew experienced a VNAV disconnect near CHAVO due to turbulence and shifting tailwinds, potentially causing a 200-foot altitude deviation. The pilots managed the speed increase with speedbrakes and vertical speed mode to comply with the LEMOE restriction, completing the arrival without further incident.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew experience a main gear tire failure at rotation. The takeoff is continued, the gear is left down and the loss of System A hydraulics is noted. The crew returns to the departure airport for an overweight landing where it is discovered that the left brakes are inoperative. A runway excursion occurs at low speed with no further damage to the aircraft and no evacuation is necessary.
summary: The flight crew experienced a left main gear tire blowout at rotation, causing hydraulic loss and disabled brakes. Despite an overweight landing, the aircraft departed the runway due to lost directional control, stopping off the surface with no injuries.

synopsis: B757 Captain reports arriving at 30 west on Track C two minutes past the ETA and noting the actual wind is different from the FMC stored wind. New winds are requested and entered in the FMC. Crossing 40 west the time is three minutes different from the ETA.
summary: The Pilot Flying observed a wind variance and requested an uplink, which delayed significantly before updating. Subsequently, a three-minute arrival time variance at waypoint 40 west was recorded, attributed to wind changes occurring between the update and the waypoint.

synopsis: A319 Captain reports receiving an ECAM message 'ENG 1 Compressor Vane' at 50 knots and rejects the takeoff. Previous write ups for the same anomaly had been noted in the Logbook.
summary: The Pilot in Command rejected the takeoff at 50 KTS after an ECAM warning indicated a #1 Engine Compressor Vane fault. The aircraft returned to the gate following standard procedures, with the pilot noting a history of related maintenance issues in the logbook.

synopsis: A319 Captain reports receiving an ECAM message 'ENG 1 Compressor Vane' at 70 knots and rejects the takeoff. A previous write up for the same anomaly had occurred earlier in the day and the aircraft is taken out of service.
summary: The Captain rejected takeoff at 70 knots due to an ENG 1 Compressor Vane ECAM message, exiting the runway without incident. The crew switched aircraft after noting a previous identical fault earlier that morning, though the specific cause and maintenance action remained unknown.

synopsis: CRJ700 flight crew is informed of a track deviation after crossing SAV on the HUSTN2 Arrival to CLT. The First Officer had not entered the SAV transition when entering the HUSTN2 into the FMC and had merely closed the route discontinuity.
summary: The First Officer incorrectly entered the HUSTN2 arrival into the FMS without selecting the SAV transition, causing the aircraft to fly direct to HUSTN instead of NAVEE during cruise. The Pilot Monitoring identified the deviation, corrected the FMS, and returned the aircraft to the proper arrival path.

synopsis: CL605 flight crew experiences damage to the left winglet during taxi out from the FBO ramp. The damage is not detected at the time but reported by ground personnel at the arrival airport.
summary: The flight crew taxied between two parked aircraft on the ramp after being redirected from Z1 to Z2, misjudging wing clearance. They struck the left winglet of a parked airplane, causing damage that was discovered only after landing.

synopsis: EMB175 Captain reports receiving an inaccurate load close out from a Ramp Agent, even when the Agent is directly questioned about an extra box in the forward cargo compartment. The box is described as gate checked baggage and not included in the weight and balance. It was actually 85 pounds of cargo.
summary: The Captain discovered an unaccounted 85-pound cargo box and dry ice discrepancies during boarding at ORD after ramp agents provided conflicting load reports. Despite repeated attempts to clarify the total weight, the agents failed to provide a correct load report before departure.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reports receiving a new departure procedure during taxi out and enters it into his Universal FMS but the First Officer does not (new to the company and the Universal FMS). The First Officer is the flying pilot and a track deviation results.
summary: The Captain and First Officer departed on the wrong JPOOL7 transition instead of the cleared NELYN5 due to failing to verify both FMS units after a clearance change. The crew corrected the deviation by taking control, reloading the correct flight plan, and receiving a direct clearance to NELYN.

synopsis: An international air carrier flight crew reported they deviated from assigned altitude when they responded to a clearance intended for another air carrier with the same flight number. The Controller's accent was mentioned as contributing.
summary: The crew of a flight departing ZBAA mistakenly climbed to FL350 after receiving a clearance intended for another aircraft with a similar callsign due to poor radio quality and a controller's accent. ATC later clarified the error and instructed the crew to remain at FL350 for the remainder of the flight.

synopsis: B777 Captain reports departing on a five hour flight with live animals and 90 KGs of dry ice in the same compartment. Load planning is queried and the crew is told that this was allowed by the cargo loading manual. After the flight, the Captain is informed that an error in interpretation was made.
summary: The Captain and First Officer discovered 90kg of dry ice loaded with live dogs in the same aft cargo compartment, conflicting with company policy. Despite initial concerns and a delay to verify regulations, the crew continued the flight, which concluded safely with healthy animals, though the Captain admitted the decision was wrong.

synopsis: B757-200 International Relief Officer reported an airborne conflict on arrival into LFPG that was apparently due to a Controller error. Reporter cited Controller's accent as contributing.
summary: During the LUKIP7E arrival into CDG, a flight crew received a TCAS alert while descending from FL280 to FL230 and executed evasive action after ATC issued a turn. The reporter attributed the conflict to an ATC handling error and noted that language accents and non-English communications may have reduced situational awareness.

synopsis: A Captain reported an NMAC with a glider on departure from HIO airport. ATC reported no targets in the vicinity.
summary: During a climb through 5,000 feet on the BERNI2 RNAV departure from HIO, the crew passed within 300-400 feet of a glider near HETAT. The pilot reported the near miss to ATC, who observed no targets, and recommended extending airspace and requiring glider transponders.

synopsis: A Captain reports about his efforts to convince Maintenance and Dispatch that the Right-Hand Outboard Brake (RHOB) on a CRJ-900 aircraft had not been operating and the Brake Temperature Monitoring System (BTMS) deferral was not the problem.
summary: The pilot reported a suspected Right-Hand Outboard Brake failure on an aircraft with a history of Brake Temperature Monitoring System issues. Despite mechanics in ZZZ1 declaring the brakes airworthy, the pilot found the wheel cold after landing in ZZZ2 and wrote up the aircraft again, believing it was not airworthy.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported evacuating their aircraft when smoke began to fill the cabin shortly after pushback.
summary: After pushback, a flight attendant reported smoke and fire at the 1A bulkhead, prompting the crew to initiate an evacuation via overwing exits. The pilot recalled passengers due to rain after inspecting the area, and Fire Rescue confirmed the threat was eliminated with no injuries reported.

synopsis: A330 Flight Attendant reported strong fumes in the cabin on taxi in.
summary: During taxi-in, the Captain shut down the engine and immediately started the APU without the required 30-second wait, causing fumes to overwhelm the cabin. Flight attendants and passengers experienced burning eyes, noses, and throats, forcing crew to leave their jumpseats for clean air.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reports finding the landing gear control cables in the forward cargo pit ceiling wrapped around each other at approximately frame station 300 on a B767-300 aircraft. Pilots had made several previous write-ups for a stiff gear handle with a 'grinding noise and feel.' A floor beam repair had recently been accomplished that removed the cables. 'Clearance to Close' panels also an issue.
summary: A mechanic found landing gear control cables wrapped together during a post-FCF inspection, causing a grinding noise and stiff handle. The issue stemmed from improper cable routing after a recent floor beam repair, which was resolved by rerigging the cables per the AMM.

synopsis: R44 helicopter pilot reported he was 'frightened' by the close, and apparently deliberate, pass of three F-16s.
summary: A pilot flying a R44 at 2,500 feet southwest of 35A encountered three F-16s that matched their descent to 250 feet AGL on a collision path. The military aircraft avoided impact by executing an aggressive high-speed turn at 500 to 700 feet distance, leaving the pilot shaken.

synopsis: Cessna 172 instructor pilot reported engine failure on final approach. A safe landing was made just short of the runway.
summary: A student pilot and instructor experienced an engine failure during final approach at 500 feet when the throttle failed to respond to power requests. The instructor took control, executed a forced landing short of the runway, and the aircraft stopped 100 feet before the 1,000-foot markings.

synopsis: AA5B pilot reported a hard landing that resulted in a prop strike and runway excursion.
summary: The pilot of an AA5B stalled during a high flare on the third landing attempt, causing a bounce and prop strike. The pilot attributed the incident to insufficient landing training and the aircraft's lack of forgiveness compared to a previous Piper Cherokee, resulting in an overrun of 50 feet.

synopsis: Two instructors working together reported an NMAC on approach to DAB. Reporters were critical of ATC handling.
summary: During a CFII training low approach to Runway 7L, a high-wing aircraft received a TCAS warning and evaded a converging low-wing aircraft at 500 feet MSL due to a blind spot and congested tower frequency. The crew executed evasive maneuvers, including a dive and turns between runways, to avoid collision before climbing to 1200 feet and exiting Class C airspace.

synopsis: A PA-30 pilot reported his battery was drained when both alternators dropped off line. He reset the alternators and returned to the departure airport, flying long enough to charge the battery for landing gear extension.
summary: The pilot experienced a dual alternator failure and battery drain during enroute flight, causing electrical system loss and gear malfunction. After returning to base to recharge the battery, the pilot successfully extended the gear and completed a normal landing.

synopsis: Prior to takeoff, seaplane crew noticed a small airborne helicopter. Crew waited until helicopter had completed a water landing before taking off. Crew later learned that the craft was part of an FAA test drone program and that the local seaplane operator had not been notified.
summary: A seaplane pilot conducted a water landing and takeoff near a river event after confirming no published restrictions, despite an unannounced FAA drone program nearby. The pilot maintained altitudes above 500 feet, avoiding the 200-foot drone limit, and reported no conflicts with the restricted airspace.

synopsis: Tower Controller is advised by the Controller he is relieving that a runway incursion is about to occur. As a result, a Cub on short final is sent around. The incurring C172 was confused by the Ground Controller into thinking that a clearance to cross Runway 21L was being issued when it was not.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller prevented a runway incursion on RWY 21L by instructing a Cessna Cub on final to go around after a C172 encroached into the safety area at Taxiway Delta 3. The incident resulted from the Ground Controller's last-minute route change and poor pre-planning, requiring enhanced training for the individual.

synopsis: After holding for a closed runway and with foreign ATC confusion about available approaches (assigned VOR approach not available in crew's EFB), crew diverted to an alternate airport.
summary: Flight X crew diverted to ZZZZ2 due to fuel concerns after ATC confusion over a closed runway and an unavailable VOR DME XXL approach. The crew returned to ZZZZ with 4.7 fuel on board, attributing the delay to missing approach plates and communication barriers.

synopsis: Deadheading pilot reported notifying the flight crew during taxi out of cold soaked fuel frost on the wing surfaces that had presumably gone undetected during preflight.
summary: A deadheading passenger on a Boeing 737 observed cold soaked fuel frost on the left wing during taxi and notified the flight crew. The Captain stopped the aircraft, and the frost melted during a subsequent 30-minute ground delay, though the Captain appeared annoyed by the report.

synopsis: A B-777 flight crew lost an engine while enroute. They ran appropriate checklists, dumped fuel, and returned to their departure airport and landed.
summary: A deadheading First Officer and flight crew experienced a left engine compressor stall and severe damage at FL380, causing N1 collapse and EGT spikes. The crew diverted to ZZZ, jettisoned fuel, and landed safely with fire trucks standing by, later confirming destroyed turbine sections.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reports sighting a drone pass 100-200 feet off the left wing during the approach to CLT at 1,250 feet AGL.
summary: The Captain and First Officer sighted a maroon and silver drone 100–200 feet horizontally from the aircraft at 1,250 feet AGL while on a visual approach to Charlotte runway 23. They reported the incident to the tower and were instructed to provide further details after landing.

synopsis: Two EMB145 Check Airmen, one in the right seat and one on the jump seat, report a missed crossing restriction on the DRLLR4 arrival by the Captain flying. The flying Captain did not recognize the FL240 crossing restriction at OILLL and did not follow the Vertical Path Indicator (VPI) as briefed.
summary: During a line check on the DRLLR FOUR arrival, the crew descended below the FL240 crossing restriction at OILLL after receiving a "descend via" clearance. The Captain lost situational awareness while the Check Airman failed to monitor the descent, resulting in an altitude deviation of nearly 1,000 feet before leveling off.

synopsis: C750 flight crew arriving to SFO on the BDEGA1 and expecting Runway 28R is told to expect Runway 28L. However, the runway is not changed in the FMC and the aircraft turns on to the 28R transition. NCT detects the error and issues vectors. The crew eventually lands on Runway 28R.
summary: Pilots flying a BDEGA ONE RNAV arrival to SFO mistakenly programmed the FMS for Runway 28R instead of the assigned 28L due to task saturation. ATC detected the error, issued vectors, and later reassigned Runway 28R, resulting in a safe landing without further incident.

synopsis: CE680 Captain describes roll control problems at lift off after accepting an aircraft from Maintenance that had had work done on the speed brake/spoiler system. Half of the maximum possible aileron trim is required to trim for wings level flight. Flight diverts to a nearby airport.
summary: The pilot reported that immediately after rotation on a post-maintenance flight, the aircraft rolled hard left due to aileron and rudder trim settings outside normal parameters. The pilot corrected the flight path manually, landed safely, and requested a test pilot check before further line operations.

synopsis: A BK-117 CAD alerted ACTUATOR with an audio indication along with minor uncommanded yaw and rudder pedal feedback during takeoff. The pilot landed without incident. This aircraft and other similar aircraft have displayed the same behavior.
summary: The flight crew experienced minor uncommanded yaw inputs and a CAD 'Actuator' warning shortly after takeoff. The pilot landed safely, and the issue was identified as a recurring maintenance concern requiring trend analysis and manufacturer guidance.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew report being assigned the OAK7 Departure from OAK with the added waypoint of DEDHD via PDC. The waypoint is never entered into the FMC and when ATC issues a clearance direct the crew requests vectors.
summary: The pilot and co-pilot failed to fully enter a PDC route change adding the OAK7 SID and DEDHD fix into the FMS during departure. This oversight caused initial navigation errors and required ATC radar vectors, which the pilot attributed to inadequate briefing and verification of the route change.

synopsis: Air carrier crew report misspelling a waypoint during FMC set up which is not detected until the FMC indicates landing with zero fuel. On the Kennedy One Departure CANARSIE climb it is not noticed that the route discontinuity after CRI is missing resulting in a turn toward the first flight plan waypoint. The Captain detects the wrong turn direction and requests ATC assistance.
summary: During climb out of JFK on the Kennedy One Departure, a First Officer misspelled waypoint BENEE as BENNE and omitted a discontinuity, causing the flight director to command an incorrect right turn toward LGA. The Captain corrected the heading, contacted ATC for a new heading, and re-entered the route to resolve the FMS error.

synopsis: A B737-800 Flight Attendant detected a metallic taste and developed a headache lightheadedness. Later a heart rate increase was noted along with heart palpitations. The after effects continue and the flight attendant is off work more than a month later with continued cognitive issues.
summary: A flight attendant investigating a leaky seal on L2 experienced symptoms of bleed air contamination, including respiratory distress and cognitive issues, while passengers also reported breathing difficulties. A mechanic suspected engine oil or hydraulic fluid contaminated the unfiltered cabin air, leading to the crew's illness and the attendant's ongoing medical leave.

synopsis: A C560XL Captain reported pitch trim problems that caused an upset at FL280. The flight diverted to a suitable alternate.
summary: During climb through FL200, the crew encountered a pitch trim warning and abnormal resistance, causing momentary pitch instability at FL280. They diverted to land without flaps due to control concerns, but maintenance found no cause after inspection.

synopsis: BE90 Captain reports not converting UTC time to local time when determining the time of a runway closure at HQG. There were no yellow X's on the runway but reexamination of the NOTAM revealed that the runway was closed.
summary: The pilot landed on closed Runway 20 at HQG, mistaking workers for farmers and an adjacent aerial applicor landing for normal operations. The incident resulted from misinterpreting the NOTAM closure time as local 24-hour clock instead of Zulu time.

synopsis: PA28R student pilot reported an airborne conflict with another aircraft at TTA, a non-Tower airport.
summary: A student pilot and instructor conducting commercial maneuvers at a non-towered airport encountered a near midair collision while turning base to final. The conflict occurred when another aircraft made an unannounced straight-in approach to Runway 21, forcing the student to execute an immediate climbing right turn to avoid impact.

synopsis: PA-28 pilot reports departing DTL from a runway intersection, with only Parachute Jumping Exercise (PJE) as an airport NOTAM. Upon return to the airport, yellow Xs are noted over the runway numbers.
summary: The pilot departed from a runway intersection at DTL, unaware of yellow 'Xs' marking the runway closed due to an obscured view. The pilot attributed the missed closure markings to the intersection takeoff and assumed they related to a nearby parachute jumping exercise noted in NOTAMs.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Corporate jet flight crew report landing without clearance and remaining on the runway until Ground Control can be contacted for taxi instructions. During this time an Air Carrier goes around.
summary: The flight crew landed on Runway 1L at MKE while remaining on the approach frequency, missing tower instructions to exit. This caused a 30-second runway hold that forced a following aircraft to go around, followed by a taxiway error due to communication confusion.

synopsis: C414 pilot reports commencing CTAF procedures 20 NM out for landing at GUC with no response from other aircraft. After touchdown, another aircraft is noted taking off in the opposite direction. Each moves to the right and pass on the runway. The other aircraft's crew later reports they had a bad radio.
summary: A VFR pilot landing at GUC encountered a commercial fixed-wing aircraft on the takeoff roll. The collision was avoided by both crews moving right, caused by the commercial crew's radio failure which prevented them from hearing the pilot's landing intentions.

synopsis: Maule M5 220C pilot reported damaging his tailwheel during takeoff from a river bank. He lost directional control on the ensuing landing when the tailwheel came off and the right main gear collapsed.
summary: The pilot landed a tailwheel aircraft for a picnic, felt a thump on takeoff, and returned to a nearby airstrip. Upon landing, the tailwheel and spring detached and the right main gear collapsed, causing a ground loop; the pilot attributed the failure to striking a rock during takeoff.

synopsis: Falcon 50 First Officer reports a track deviation while flying the HYPER5 Arrival into IAD. The flying Captain's FMS was not properly programed to make the turn at MULRR to SIGBE resulting in vectors from PCT.
summary: During the HYPER5 arrival to IAD, the pilot flying failed to program the post-MULRR segment, causing a deviation from the RNAV arrival. The crew attributed the incident to high workload and insufficient procedure review, requiring ATC to issue corrective headings and altitudes.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 172 landed long on a relatively short runway, which led to a runway excursion and contact with a fence.
summary: The pilot landed a light aircraft on Runway 32 at ZZZ after observing a helicopter departure due to unavailable wind information. A sudden headwind gust caused the aircraft to float, resulting in a runway overrun that bent a propeller blade and damaged the end fence.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Instructor pilot reports crossing the hold line for Runway 4R at SFF (a complex intersection and HS1), while changing frequency to the Tower at Ground Control's request.
summary: The pilot crossed the hold line for Runway 04R at SFF without clearance while changing to tower frequency. The incident was caused by distraction during the radio change, but the pilot stopped immediately with no other traffic present.

synopsis: A Seattle Center (ZSE) Controller reports of becoming busy and while vectoring an aircraft to final, the aircraft drifted close to a lower Minimum IFR Altitude (MIA).
summary: An air traffic controller vectored Aircraft X to intercept the LMT314 radial while managing weather deviations and fighter jet priority requests. The controller believes the aircraft may have drifted near the 100 MIA due to high sector pressure, cluttered displays, and difficulty distinguishing MSAW alerts.

synopsis: A Cleveland Center (ZOB) Controller reports of a loss of separation attributed to Severe Weather Avoidance Plan SWAP0 and aircraft not being pointed out correctly.
summary: An air traffic controller in sector R-47 intercepted Aircraft X climbing to FL330 on an inconsistent SWAP route that conflicted with westbound Aircraft Y at FL320. The controller stopped the climb and turned Aircraft X left to restore separation, attributing the conflict to uncoordinated route usage.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Northern California TRACON (NCT) Controller reports of a problem associated with the BDEGA1 arrival when an aircraft flies the wrong heading and enters another controller's airspace. The Controller describes this is an ongoing issue and states that management has not provided guidance or proper training on how the routes should be issued.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a pilot flying Aircraft X on the BDEGA1 arrival incorrectly followed the runway 28R route instead of the assigned runway 28L route, entering SUTRO airspace and conflicting with departures. The controller attributed this unsafe situation to a poorly designed STAR, lack of standardization, and insufficient management training.

synopsis: A Yankee TRACON (Y90) controller describes an airborne conflict due to VFR aircraft being in the vicinity of the airport and the final approach course. Controller recommends changing the airspace from a Class Charlie to a Class Bravo to offer better protection from the VFR traffic.
summary: An air traffic controller vectored Aircraft X for an ILS runway 6 approach at BDL while Aircraft Y conducted VFR survey work. A conflict occurred when an unknown VFR climb forced a turn that conflicted with Aircraft Y, requiring expedited descents and climbs to maintain separation due to unpredictable uncontrolled traffic and poor approach selection.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: A CVG Controller reports of losing a total loss of electrical power. The Controller attempts to use the backup radio but it does not work. The Controller plugs the backup radio into a different outlet and it then works. The Controller reports that he/she is appalled at the lack of maintaining the equipment at the airport.
summary: An air traffic controller at HTS lost all power during a combined Local and Ground shift when a truck hit a utility pole, causing both backup generators to fail. The controller eventually restored radio contact with an inbound aircraft by plugging a transceiver into an airport outlet, though the facility suffers from chronic equipment disrepair.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Oakland Center (ZOA) Controller reports of a loss of separation due to an aircraft taking a different heading then they were supposed to. A Pilot reports of entering information into the FMS and then aircraft turned to continue on the routing assigned.
summary: An ATC controller and pilots of Aircraft X and Y experienced a loss of separation to 4.97 miles during Aircraft X's descent into RNO after a destination change to SMF. The controller attributed the conflict to the pilot's delayed turn and garbled readback of the direct MOEGL clearance, while the pilot cited fatigue and confusion over the fix name.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: TRACON Controller reports of a loss of separation between two aircraft. Controller was training a Developmental that he was unfamiliar with and let the situation go too far. Instructor took over but aircraft did not respond timely.
summary: An air traffic controller training an inexperienced developmental allowed Aircraft X and a VFR skydiving Aircraft Y to converge to 2 NM separation due to poor supervision and fatigue. The controller attributed the incident to inadequate staffing, improper training assignments, and the presence of parachute operations in the departure area.

synopsis: B737 flight crew departing EWR reports a runway incursion during taxi to Runway 22R. ATIS had stated that Runway 22R at W was the departure runway and the crew planned accordingly. However, during taxi out the crew is told to contact clearance for a revised route. The First Officer is fully occupied as the Captain continues to taxi to Runway 22R. The initial clearance was to Runway 22R at W, which was forgotten during the complicated taxi and reroute, and Runway 11/29 is crossed without clearance.
summary: The flight crew at Newark became task-saturated while rushing to input a reroute, causing them to miss a taxiway turn and cross Runway 11-29 instead of departing from the ATIS-specified intersection. They stopped to re-brief and checklists before receiving a full-length takeoff clearance for Runway 22R.

synopsis: A B737 flight crew reports receiving delay vectors before being finally cleared for a visual approach to Runway 26R at ONT. A descend RA is received inside the FAF and is complied with. A heavy jet for Runway 26L receives a climb RA and goes around.
summary: The pilot reported that Approach and Tower controllers vectored their aircraft through the final approach course at Ontario, resulting in a close proximity with a faster heavy aircraft. This led to a descent Resolution Advisory for the pilot and a go-around for the other carrier, which the pilot attributed to poor ATC separation and communication.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports being cleared via the YOKES4 DEHLI transition, departing Runway 8 at DEN. After YOKES the aircraft proceeds direct to ONL, since the DEHLI transition had been eliminated from the FMC. ATC takes notice and states that this has been occurring for about a year.
summary: The flight crew departed Runway 08 and received a direct YOKES clearance, but the FMC unexpectedly dropped the DEHLI fix and inserted two others before ONL. Denver Center noted this FMC anomaly has reportedly occurred for a year, prompting the crew to request an investigation into the cause.

synopsis: A B737 flight crew were notified while enroute of two ill passengers, one of whom was thought by medical professionals on board, to be very close to death. They diverted and landed in an emergency condition. EMTs were waiting at the gate and successfully treated both passengers.
summary: The flight crew diverted to COS at FL340 after two passengers became unconscious, one from a suspected drug overdose and the other from dehydration. Despite difficult MedLink communications and thunderstorms, the crew landed safely, allowing EMTs to treat the passengers, with one walking off and the other reboarding.

synopsis: B747 flight crew describe a track deviation during the GNNRR2 RNAV Departure from SFO. The Captain had entered the procedure in the FMC but had not selected the AMAKR transition and just closed the route discontinuity, eliminating STINS.
summary: The flight crew departed SFO on the GNNRR2 RNAV SID but incorrectly programmed the FMC to fly direct from GNNRR to AMAKR, omitting the required STINS fix. NORCAL queried the routing, revealing the error caused by misinterpreting the PDC clearance, though no traffic conflict occurred and the crew continued direct to AMAKR.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports receiving a runway change from 23L to 23R approaching EKEKE on the KOLTS1 RNAV Arrival to IND. When the runway change is executed in the FMC, EKEKE disappears along with its crossing restriction and an altitude deviation occurs.
summary: The crew descended via the KOLTS1 arrival into IND and changed the FMC runway from 23L to 23R, inadvertently inserting a discontinuity that disengaged V-NAV. While the First Officer manually flew, the aircraft descended below the 10,000-foot restriction at EKEKE to approximately 9,400 feet before the error was corrected.

synopsis: An air carrier reserve Captain reports receiving a missed call from scheduling after going into a FAR 117.21 mandated ten hour rest period. The company disagrees with the pilot union on how this FAR should be interpreted.
summary: A reserve captain received a disciplinary mark for missing a short-call assignment notification during a legally mandated rest period. The company enforced the penalty despite the pilot's compliance with FAR 117, creating an unsafe environment where pilots face termination for following regulations or flying while fatigued.

synopsis: A Q400 Captain reports requesting flaps to 35 from the flaps 10 position during a visual approach. The normal call is flaps 15 from flaps 10 and this is what the First Officer selects. The error is not detected until the EGPWS alerts at 500 feet, 'too low flaps' and a go-around is initiated.
summary: The crew performed a go-around below 500 feet due to a "TOO LOW CONFIG FLAPS" warning caused by setting flaps to 15 instead of 35. The reporter attributed the error to expectation bias, lack of cross-checking, and fatigue from a long duty day.

synopsis: A319 flight crew note a revised PDC to include the TERPZ5 RAMAY transition. The TERPZ5 is loaded in the FMGC but the RAMAY transition is not selected, resulting in LITME being omitted. ATC takes notice then issues direct to RAMAY.
summary: The flight crew missed the LITME waypoint in the FMGC flight plan during preflight due to rushing and failing to cross-check the printed TERPZ5 departure against the FMS. ATC detected the error when the aircraft bypassed LITME by four miles, but issued a direct clearance to RAMAY with no further incident.

synopsis: EMB145 First Officer reports descending below a step-down fix when transitioning from the DOOBI2 arrival to the ILS26L Approach into IAH. The Vertical Path Indicator was being used to comply with crossing restrictions but it dropped out crossing BOZZZ but the descent was continued until it reappeared and showed below profile. ATC took notice.
summary: During an RNAV arrival to IAH, the First Officer descended below the charted 7000 feet at MKAYE after relying solely on the Vertical Path Indicator, which dropped out during the transition to the ILS 26L approach. The deviation occurred due to task saturation and a lack of cross-checking raw data, requiring a shallow climb after ATC advised the altitude restriction.

synopsis: An EMB175 Captain experiences a RH and LH BRK FAULT message on a reposition flight after Maintenance had attempted to correct the same fault from the previous flight. The reporter states that this is the eighth or ninth time this aircraft has been written up for the same fault and the aircraft is almost new.
summary: Pilots reported recurring RH and LH BRK FAULT messages on a new aircraft shortly after maintenance replaced wiring and valves. Despite planning for 50 percent braking loss, the crew landed safely but observed reduced brake power and uneven temperatures, recommending a maintenance flight before further revenue service.

aircraft: Medium Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain is told that since the computers were down that they would use the old weight manifest and that all hazmat had been bumped. Upon arrival, a HazMat package is noticed in Zone 1. The package is not arrows up, not secured and the net is not closed.
summary: The pilot discovered an unsecured dry ice package in Zone 1 despite the manifest showing no hazmat or freight due to computer failures. The pilot requested the ramp manager take possession of the package, citing a need for better hazmat training for ramp agents.

synopsis: B777 Captain reports being cleared to descend via the SEEVR2 Arrival and delete the speeds until BRDJE. The speeds are deleted in the FMC legs page, but the crossing restriction for THEMM is inadvertently placed on SEEVR.
summary: The pilot monitoring and first officer inadvertently entered an incorrect altitude restriction on the FMC during the SEEVR2 arrival, causing the aircraft to be too high at the SEEVR waypoint. Fort Worth Approach instructed them to expedite descent to 6,000 feet, allowing for a normal approach to runway 17C.

synopsis: A B757-200 Captain rejected the takeoff at about 70 KTS when the First Officer called 95kts. Maintenance had worked avionics issues to resolve an autothrottle system and takeoff speed display anomalies.
summary: The Captain rejected takeoff between 65 and 75 KIAS after the First Officer incorrectly called "95 Knots" during an acceleration phase following avionics issues. The crew attributed the call to an airspeed discrepancy, exited the runway safely, and taxied back to parking after verifying brake energy limits.

synopsis: A B737 Captain reports discrepancies between the amount of fuel pumped by the fuel truck and the amount shown on the aircraft totalizer. He believes that the Flight Operations Manual procedures are unclear in this situation and requests guidance.
summary: The pilot reported fuel discrepancies on the same aircraft where the totalizer indicated over-fueling while the truck pumped less than calculated. Unclear Flight Operations Manual procedures and conflicting tank stick measurements prevented resolving the 45-gallon difference between the totalizer and truck amounts.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier aircraft holding short of EWR Runway 4L entered the runway following a garbled transmission which they misinterpreted was their takeoff clearance after ATC did not respond to their confirming takeoff clearance.
summary: A crew at EWR mistakenly entered Runway 04L after misinterpreting a garbled ATC transmission as a takeoff clearance. The controller attributed the error to a stepped-on readback, subsequently issued the correct clearance, and the flight departed without further incident.

synopsis: An EMB-145 crew ferried an aircraft with the First Officer's PFD MEL'ed and failed to intercept a Victor airway after deleting the wrong waypoint.
summary: During a ferry flight climb, the First Officer's PFD and MFD failed, causing high workload. While manually flying heading 040, the crew incorrectly sequenced the FMS, resulting in a lateral deviation by missing the Victor Airway intercept.

synopsis: An EMB-145 flight crew incurred a runway while rushing for a time constrained takeoff with complex taxi instructions because of a closed taxiway.
summary: A pilot and a trainee air traffic controller were involved when an aircraft crossed active Runway XY without clearance while taxiing to Runway XX. The incursion resulted from rushing to meet a wheels-up time, confusing taxiway barricades, and a left turn at intersection D instead of the cleared right turn.

synopsis: EMB-145LR First Officer reported failing to make a crossing restriction on the BLUZZ1 Arrival into MEM when they were distracted by a wake turbulence encounter in trail of an MD-11.
