summary: A flight attendant on 24-hour reserve reported being called for a redeye turn involving nearly 10 hours of night flying without crew rest. The crew member stated this lack of rest compromises safety during potential emergencies and makes the subsequent drive home dangerously fatigued.

synopsis: RV8 pilot departing OSH reported an NMAC with an aircraft arriving on the FISK arrival.
summary: A departing IFR aircraft encountered two VFR aircraft on the FISK arrival at 1,800 feet while climbing to 3,000 feet. The pilot executed a left maneuver to maintain 300 feet separation, noting the VFR aircraft had transponders off and made no avoidance corrections.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot took evasive action to avoid a UAV and the chase airplane behind it at 8,500 FT near a local airport.
summary: A pilot flying westbound at 8,500 feet MSL near P03 encountered a grey UAV and chase Aircraft Z crossing their path. The pilot executed collision avoidance by climbing and turning southwest after receiving no response on CTAF 122.8.

synopsis: A distracted small aircraft pilot preparing for takeoff at SUA airport intended to utilize the full runway length and taxied beyond the runway end because he did not clearly see end markings. He made his 180° turn in the adjacent EMAS which appeared as a runway overrun.
summary: The pilot inadvertently contacted EMAS blocks while turning on Runway 12 to capture full length during a pre-takeoff taxi. No aircraft damage occurred, and the pilot attributed the incident to performing the before-takeoff checklist while maneuvering.

synopsis: PA32 pilot reported landing at FPR after total electrical failure with no radio contact and no light signals from the Tower.
summary: The pilot experienced a total electrical failure while approaching FPR, squawked 7600, and landed on runway 28R after receiving no tower light signals. Believing the aircraft was trapped in a fenced area with a dead battery, the pilot took off again and landed on runway 10R to reach Customs safely.

synopsis: An Instructor reported his student took evasive action at 1,000 FT from a radio controlled (RC) aircraft, which was apparently being flown with intent toward and around their maneuvering aircraft. They were near an RC park northwest of Utah Lake.
summary: A student pilot and instructor in a training aircraft at 5,500 feet MSL over Lehi/Saratoga Springs executed an immediate right turn to avoid a radio-controlled airplane diving through their flight path. The reporter suspected the RC operator intentionally targeted them and moved the aircraft to a different area to continue maneuvers.

synopsis: C172 student pilot reported loss of directional control on short final that led to a hard landing and a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot reported a hard landing and runway excursion at JYO caused by a sudden crosswind gust and disrupted pattern flow due to a helicopter's erratic operations and a required runway inspection. The aircraft ran off into the grass but was re-entered within 20 seconds with no damage to the plane or occupants.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A general aviation pilot reports that, while maneuvering in the traffic pattern and communicating his intentions on the CTAF frequency, he was cut off by another aircraft which was not radio equipped. This conflict resulted in a go-around.
summary: The pilot on short final executed a go-around and hard right turn to avoid a taildragger cutting off the approach during a downwind-to-base transition. The conflict occurred because the other pilot had no radio to communicate intentions on CTAF, despite multiple aircraft in the pattern.

synopsis: An instructor with his flying student was entering a 45 degree left downwind for PAO Runway 31 at 1,000 FT when he detected a UAV about 2-3 FT wide, approximately 100 FT beneath his aircraft.
summary: A CFI and student flying a training aircraft encountered a hovering drone while entering the left downwind for Runway 31 at PAO. The drone was spotted at pattern altitude approximately 100 feet away, with no prior ATC advisories, though no evasive action was required.

synopsis: PA38 pilot reported an airborne conflict with a high wing Cessna in the vicinity of ORK.
summary: A pilot monitoring CTAF 10 nm from ORK observed a high-wing Cessna passing below and ahead during a descent. The pilot executed a right evasive maneuver due to hazy conditions and the visibility difference between the low-wing and high-wing aircraft.

synopsis: C172 pilot reports departing on a flight to a nearby airport. Upon return, when the ATIS is tuned AWOS is heard, indicating that the Tower may be closed. The CTAF/Tower frequency is used for position reports with no response from anyone. During landing, vehicles with flashing lights are noted, but none are on the runway. After parking the reporter is informed by an airport administrator that he has landed at a closed airport.
summary: A pilot flying a rented C172S VFR landed at ZZZ on Runway 31 after monitoring CTAF 120.5, but the airport administrator later claimed the airport was closed due to a prior accident and that the pilot was not cleared. The administrator cited incorrect frequencies and alleged light gun signals and a runway vehicle, which the pilot did not observe.

synopsis: Lancair pilot, climbing through 11000 feet experiences a sudden loss of power and advises ATC. Clearance is granted direct to the departure airport and with the engine producing partial power is easily achieved. Post flight reveals that the right turbocharger had seized.
summary: The pilot experienced a partial engine power loss at 11,000 feet during an IFR climb due to a seized right turbocharger. After following emergency checklists, the pilot returned to the departure airport for a safe landing and subsequently replaced the failed component.

synopsis: HS 125 Series 700 Captain reported an altitude excursion probably caused by a wake vortex encounter.
summary: During a ferry flight's initial climb to 10,000 feet, the autopilot lurched up and disengaged altitude hold, causing a rapid 300–400 foot climb. The crew manually corrected the deviation after ATC instructed them to stop climbing, noting a jet passed 5,000 feet above shortly after leveling off.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot departed CTAF Runway 14 after making the required communications and had an encounter with a light twin which departed crossing Runway 7. Both pilots stated the required communications were made.
summary: The pilot of a departing aircraft on runway 14 at a non-towered airport encountered another aircraft climbing from runway 7, passing behind and below it with at least 500 feet separation. The reporter attributes the near miss to simultaneous radio transmissions blocking each other and potential communication impairment caused by obstacles between the runway departure ends.

aircraft: Cessna Citation Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: CE500 Flight Crew on an IFR flight to ODO, late at night, reports canceling IFR and accepting a visual approach. After landing they discover they have landed at MAF.
summary: The pilot and passengers landed a 3.5-hour flight at MAF instead of ODO after accepting a visual approach at night. The pilot attributed the error to fatigue and unfamiliarity, noting similar runway alignments, but reported no injuries or airspace violations.

synopsis: A helicopter pilot preparing to depart a Charleston area hospital helipad attempted clearance into CRW Class C, but could not hear ATC and so hovered at 100 feet until cleared. ATC was upset that he took off, but communications from area hospital helipads is poor.
summary: A helicopter pilot at a Charleston hospital helipad could not contact Tower on 125.7 until lifting to 100 feet, causing a misunderstanding about departure status. The pilot later received an aggressive call from Tower regarding communication issues, attributing the initial silence to poor radio reception at the helipad.

synopsis: A G550 Captain reports being cleared to maintain 210 knots to the FAF for the ILS to 19 at TEB. He asks to slow prior to the 1,500 foot FAF to allow for a stabilized approach and is ignored.
summary: Pilots arriving at TEB for Runway 19 were instructed by Approach to maintain 210 knots to the FAF, exceeding the 200-knot limit for Class B/D airspace. The crew ignored the clearance to slow for a stabilized approach, citing that high speeds at the FAF create a risk of runway excursions.

synopsis: The wingman in a flight of two light aircraft reports being cleared to enter a left downwind and cleared to land. After the lead aircraft turns left base the Tower issues instructions for both aircraft to extend the downwind for jet traffic, but the wingman does not hear the instructions and lands. The jet is issued a go-around.
summary: A flight of two aircraft was cleared to land on 28R but was instructed to extend downwind for jet traffic. The second aircraft became NORDO due to a radio problem and continued to land, forcing the tower to instruct the jet traffic to execute a missed approach.

synopsis: Jetstar First Officer experienced an unnoticed autopilot disconnect at FL360 with the Captain in the lavatory. The aircraft is recovered from a 45 degree bank at FL330 and ATC is advised. The autopilot is reengaged and functions normally for the remainder of the flight.
summary: While the Captain was away from the flight deck, the autopilot disconnected at FL360, causing the aircraft to enter a 45-degree left bank and lose 3,000 feet. The First Officer recovered the unusual attitude after being distracted by FMS programming, and the flight continued hand-flown with no further issues.

synopsis: ZNY Developmental Controller issued a heading of 360 degrees to Aircraft X. Controller meant to climb Aircraft X to FL 360. The 360 degree heading put Aircraft X into conflict with Aircraft Y. Aircraft Y was deviating for weather on a different controller's frequency.
summary: An air traffic controller in Sector 39 issued a heading 360 instruction instead of a climb clearance to FL 360 for Aircraft X, causing a loss of separation with Aircraft Y. The controller attributed the error to fatigue and stress from working consecutive days for both the FAA and the military.

synopsis: ZAN Controller described problems associated with non-radar and radar aircraft, and separation requirements. Controller was unsure of what standard applied to the aircraft involved.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller relieved a supervisor in Sector 68 to resolve a MEARTS data tag error and identify a non-radar aircraft entering from Oakland Oceanic. The reporter noted a potential procedural separation issue with a westbound flight but concluded radar identification was established before minimums were breached, recommending ATOP expansion to prevent recurrence.

synopsis: An air carrier aircraft diverted to SDF because the filed destination was closed. During the extensive ground delay the Captain attempted to access the terminal and was told only one person could open the jetway. The Captain questioned the safety implications of no passenger access in the event of an aircraft emergency.
summary: The pilot attempted to deplane passengers at SDF after a diversion caused by a power outage but could not open the jetway door without a special badge. A 20-minute delay occurred while waiting for the only authorized staff member, leading the pilot to identify this access restriction as a safety hazard for potential emergency evacuations.

synopsis: B737 flight crew experienced an unstabilized approach during the Visual to Runway 31 at LGA and goes around. The crew levels at 1,000 feet on runway heading and is then instructed to climb to 3,000 feet and head 340 degrees. The climb and turn are initiated, but heading select is never engaged resulting in a turn to 095 degrees before ATC questioned the heading.
summary: During a go-around at LGA, the crew overshot a 340-degree heading clearance because they assumed Heading Select was active while the aircraft was actually in Control Wheel Steering. The pilots attributed the mode confusion to rushing after a challenging approach and failing to strictly verify lateral control modes.

synopsis: During push-back, B737 crew experienced a hung/hot start while attempting to start engine number two. Crew was reassigned a different aircraft.
summary: During pushback, the First Officer aborted a hung start on engine two after EGT reached 811 and N1 rose to 36%, while the Captain was clearing ground crew. The aircraft was taken out of service, and the Captain attributed the event to the First Officer missing the EGT rise due to a slow N2 increase and the Captain's focus on external duties.

synopsis: During descent a B737 Leading Edge Flap Transit light illuminated. The rushed crew failed to complete a new iPad Boeing QRH procedure requiring they inhibit the GPWS and Flap Inhibit. The GPWS Warning sounded on final.
summary: The flight crew encountered a Leading Edge Flap Transit light during approach in mountainous terrain. Unfamiliarity with the new Boeing QRH on the iPad caused them to miss steps to inhibit GPWS, resulting in a warning due to misinterpreting checklist completion instructions.

synopsis: A B737 prepared for a maintenance ferry flight with a permit, was ready for an incoming crew to depart on arrival. During the preflight walk around a 1.5 by .75 inch tear was discovered in a trailing edge flap. The aircraft was not accepted by the fatigued crew.
summary: The flight crew encountered a 1.5-inch hole in the right inboard flap panel during a preflight for a ferry flight following a previous flap overspeed event. Citing fatigue and concerns over missed maintenance inspections, the crew declared themselves fatigued and were deadheaded back to the origin airport.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A flight crew was cleared from BOS via HYLND4 HYLND MERTO YSO but entered HYLND4 HYLND METRO YSO which caused a track deviation after HYLND. The error was very difficult to detect on the FMC even though Company SOP verification was completed during preflight.
summary: The crew departed BOS with a First Officer who inadvertently entered METRO instead of MERTO into the FMC, causing an unauthorized left turn. ATC corrected the deviation, but the crew required three attempts to recognize the transposition error despite following standard verification procedures.

synopsis: B757 First Officer reported detecting smoke after leveling off at FL360. The crew elected to divert to a suitable alternate. The fumes greatly diminished after the smoke and fumes checklist was accomplished.
summary: The flight crew and cabin crew detected burning fumes at FL360 with no EICAS warnings, prompting a diversion to ZZZ. After executing smoke removal checklists and a temporary passenger lighting failure, the aircraft landed safely with no further fumes.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported encountering severe turbulence at FL350 while deviating around thunderstorms.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence while deviating around thunderstorms, causing a 25-degree roll, 200-foot altitude loss, and autopilot disconnection. One passenger sustained a hot water burn, prompting paramedic arrangements and a maintenance log entry.

synopsis: An A319 ECAM displayed 'L/G Shock Absorber Fault, AUTO FLT A/THR Fault, CAB PR LDG ELEV Fault, ANTI ICE STBY Fault, AUTO FLT AP Fault, and VENT BLOWER Fault' after the landing gear was lowered for landing. A go-around was executed followed by a normal landing.
summary: During a VFR approach, the First Officer flew a manual landing after multiple system faults, including landing gear shock absorber and autopilot failures, caused data to dump from the FMGC. Maintenance had replaced the faulty switches three days prior for the same landing gear issues.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier First Officer reported a UAV near miss at 7,000 FT while flying the PHX BRUSR1 Arrival near the KUCOO intersection.
summary: The First Officer on a flight inbound to PHX at 7,000 feet observed a small drone passing 100 feet below the nose while on the BRUSR1 arrival. The crew notified ATC and landed safely, though the pilot warned that a descending aircraft could have struck the drone.

synopsis: EMB170 flight crew is instructed to cross 70 NM east of RINTE on the SNKPT1 Arrival to IND at FL300 which is entered into the FMC. This crossing restriction is already behind the aircraft as ATC had meant to say 30 NM east at FL300. The crew is not aware of the problem until ATC questions the crew about the crossing restriction.
summary: The flight crew at FL350 entered an ATC-issued crossing restriction of 70 miles east of RINTE at FL300 into the FMS, but realized they were already inside the point. ATC later admitted the restriction was a mistake and should have been 30 miles, while the crew attributed the oversight to fatigue and complacency regarding FMS acceptance.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported their push back crew deviated from proper procedures in apparent haste to get the flight out on time.
summary: The pilot and push crew at DFW attempted a pushback while an inbound aircraft was behind them, causing the crew to push tail east instead of the cleared tail west direction. The pilot attributed the error to the crew prioritizing on-time performance over safety and following incorrect instructions.

synopsis: An EMB-145 Captain placed a passenger's cat and crate in the cockpit before takeoff, ignoring the First Officer's objections to blocking the exit. This violated company policy and ignored the First Officer's objections because of his cat allergy.
summary: The First Officer reported that the Captain brought an uncrated cat into the flight deck, blocking an emergency exit and exposing the allergic First Officer to the animal. The Captain ignored safety concerns and forced the First Officer to remove themselves from the trip after blocking the aircraft out.

synopsis: A Captain qualified EMB-145 First Officer reported the Captain's behavior as distracted, nonstandard, and lacking in CRM.
summary: A First Officer reported that a Captain reset an aircraft to clear a Short dispatch message, skipped checklists, and taxied onto a runway without clearance, causing a runway incursion near a landing aircraft. The First Officer stopped the aircraft, and the Captain later apologized for the incident.

synopsis: An A320 pilot reported the sharklet equipped aircraft strobe lights are positioned such that in flight at night and in clouds they are blinding in the cockpit and cause vertigo. The reporter turned the strobes off.
summary: The pilot reported that aircraft strobes flash brightly into the cockpit, causing vertigo. Consequently, the pilot must turn off the strobes for the entire flight, increasing potential collision risk.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Captain reported maximum brake application while taxiing at DFW in order to avoid a fuel truck which appeared would not give way. The truck did stop but flight attendants were injured during the hard braking.
summary: During taxi at DFW, the Captain applied maximum braking to avoid a rapidly approaching fuel truck that passed 20 feet from the right wing. Although flight attendants initially reported no injuries, all three later revealed injuries and were removed from duty after the flight.

synopsis: A MD-80 First Officer discovered towels wrapped around cables in the wheel well which maintenance was able to remove with some difficulty. It was discovered the towels were paper, but the aircraft remained grounded for an inspection.
summary: During preflight, a pilot discovered paper towels wrapped around flight control cables in the left main gear wheel well. Maintenance removed the towels, but the Captain grounded the aircraft, resulting in a replacement and delay.

synopsis: BE99 Captain reports using standard CTAF procedures arriving Runway 35 at PPA to find himself nose to nose with an Ag aircraft landing on Runway 35. The reporter goes around and lands on Runway 35.
summary: The pilot reported that while on final for Runway 17 at PPA, an AG aircraft turned low final for Runway 35 without radio communication. This lack of monitoring caused reduced situational awareness, forcing a go-around and re-entry into right traffic for a normal landing.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant describes a high wind event while deplaning passengers at the gate. With most of the passengers off, the tail of the aircraft is violently buffeted by the wind but the Customer Service agent would not allow the remaining passengers off due to the gap that had developed between the aircraft and the jet bridge.
summary: During deplaning, 70 mph winds and hail knocked the aircraft off its blocks into the jetway, violently lifting the tail where passengers and flight attendants were trapped. A customer service agent initially blocked evacuation due to a 5-inch gap, while slides were deemed unusable in the severe weather.

synopsis: A C182 Pilot reported landing off airport after the engine stopped and would not restart.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine stoppage while en route to the airport. After an unsuccessful restart attempt, the pilot established best glide and prepared for an off-airport landing in a field.

synopsis: A M-20J pilot noticed his oil pressure drop rapidly at cruise, so diverted to a nearby airport. There he discovered the Oil Quick Drain Valve broken off but the threads still in the oil pan.
summary: A pilot experienced rapid oil pressure loss at 10,000 feet due to a broken oil quick drain valve. After receiving vectors and a descent clearance to 3,000 feet, the pilot managed the emergency and landed safely, though the cause of the valve failure remains unknown.

synopsis: A pilot not thoroughly familiar with the Fairbanks area unintentionally landed at FAI VFR intending to land at FBK. Visibility was somewhat restricted in rain.
summary: A pilot approaching Fairbanks International (FAI) cancelled IFR and switched to the Ladd Army Airfield advisory frequency, mistakenly landing at FAI instead of Ladd due to rain-reduced visibility and confusion over tower handoff instructions. The pilot attributed the error to cancelling IFR prematurely, unfamiliarity with the area, and ambiguous controller instructions regarding the correct tower frequency.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot requested a low pass over OTH Runway 22, but after the maneuver ATC was upset because the 500 FT altitude was understood to be a transit request through Class D, not a low pass over traffic.
summary: A pilot descending for a flyby at 500 feet miscommunicated with OTH Tower, resulting in an unauthorized overflight of Runway 22 near pattern altitude while a helicopter was cleared for takeoff. The pilot attributed the incident to ambiguous terminology and delayed radio contact, prompting a corrective turn to exit Class D airspace.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A pilot approached the San Francisco Bay Area from the South intending to land at PAO. They were vectored to the airport by NCT, but once nearing the PAO pattern he had difficulty seeing the airport, entering the pattern, maintaining altitude. Turning final for Runway 31 they had a NMAC.
summary: A private pilot flying a single-engine aircraft into PAO descended below pattern altitude while complying with NORCAL Approach and Tower instructions to join the left downwind for Runway 31. The pilot executed a 360-degree turn and an immediate climb to avoid a Cessna passing 300 feet below before landing uneventfully.

synopsis: A Hawker 700 landed with a simulated engine out and did not respond to normal braking. The aircraft did respond to emergency brakes, but ran off the runway's end where the aircraft was shut down and exited.
summary: During a single-engine training approach in a Hawker, the crew selected full flaps to reduce speed, causing the aircraft to float and overrun the runway. Severe nose wheel shimmy and ineffective braking led to an emergency stop 200 feet off the runway end in the grass with no injuries.

synopsis: BE33 pilot climbing out of U64 experiences a NMAC with a Cessna at 8200 feet flying in the opposite direction. The Cessna was not detected in time to take any evasive action.
summary: A pilot climbing to 10,500 feet MSL between BDG and U64 encountered a white Cessna passing less than 75 feet below while monitoring 122.8. The reporter attributed the near-miss to the other aircraft's failure to communicate on 122.8 for traffic advisories in the mountainous area.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ZDV Controller reported of traffic overload and weather deviations at the end of the shift. Mid person came in and Front Line Manager left. Controller asked mid person for help and it was given. Reporter stated this happens too often and something needs to be done to help with traffic at the end of this shift.
summary: An air traffic controller in ZDV Sector 37 faced severe workload and a 5-mile conflict due to high traffic volume, weather, and understaffing of three instead of five controllers. The supervisor left without assistance, forcing the controller to work overtime until a mid-shift controller provided Radar Assistant support.

synopsis: ZBW Controller reports of deviations due to weather and precipitation with traffic inbound to BOS. Controller let aircraft descend early and assumed BOS had the airspace, but ended up violating airspace belonging to Providence Approach.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a descend via clearance to Aircraft X after weather deviations and holding, but the pilot descended below the required altitude at the JOODY fix. This caused an airspace violation with PVD approach because the clearance lacked a crossing altitude restriction, highlighting confusion with the descend via procedure during deviations.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier on approach to MDW encountered severe turbulence with momentary losses of control. Unable to completely avoid the weather and with windshear warnings at MDW, the flight diverted to its alternate.
summary: The crew diverted to an alternate after encountering severe turbulence and windshear near Chicago while approaching MDW, causing loss of control and inability to maintain clearance. The pilot attributed the incident to outdated weather forecasts and criticized following aircraft for ignoring their report and entering the same hazardous conditions.

synopsis: B737 flight crew experienced a GPWS terrain warning during a night visual approach to Runway 28R at PIT and goes around. On the second approach more care was taken to remain on profile and a second GPWS warning was annunciated while showing three white over one red on the PAPI. The approach was continued to landing.
summary: The flight crew executed a night visual approach with the glideslope out of service and received a "Too Low Terrain" caution, prompting a go-around. They attributed the warning to terrain on final and recommended strict step-down procedures instead of visual approaches at night.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported wake turbulence encounter 20 miles in trail of a B747 at FL340, which resulted in a minor injury to a flight attendant.
summary: The crew encountered wake turbulence from a preceding 747 while at FL340 on track D, causing a 25-second disturbance that required a 3L offset. Although no immediate injuries occurred, a flight attendant later reported a possible calf muscle strain sustained during the event.

synopsis: B-777 Captain reports an 'echoing' problem on an ATC frequency. No corrective action is reported.
summary: Pilots reported severe echoing on the frequency when the air traffic controller transmitted, a problem the controller acknowledged. Other aircraft also complained, creating a potential for miscommunication.

synopsis: During the takeoff roll the First Officer's airspeed lagged behind the Captain's so the flight returned to the departure airport. The aircraft had been washed, the pitot system inspected by the IRO, but yellow tape was found inside the First Officer's pitot tube upon inspection after landing.
summary: The First Officer's airspeed indicator lagged by up to 30 knots during takeoff, triggering an Airspeed Disagree EICAS message. The crew executed the Airspeed Unreliable checklist, returned to ZZZ, and performed an uneventful overweight landing with brake cooling required.

synopsis: Pilot reported the Standby Attitude Indicator (SAI) in an A320 making a grinding noise and becoming very hot, unstable/shaky on climbout. Pilot pulled the Overhead panel Circuit Breaker (CB) labeled NAV Stby Horizon at location F12, but that action DID NOT remove electrical power from SAI. Reporter stated another CB in E/E compartment labeled STBT INST/BATT controls a relay that latches the SAI to the Hot Batt bus when the normal power source is removed.
summary: During climbout, the pilot and First Officer experienced a loud, unstable Standby Attitude Indicator that distracted them. Pulling the NAV Stby Horizon circuit breaker failed to cut power until touchdown, likely due to a latching relay on the Hot Batt Bus.

synopsis: A320 First Officer reports entering the BNDTO4 in the MCDU departing IAH, then receiving a revised PDC for the PITZZ3, which is entered. During taxi a runway change is issued and entered but the route is not checked prior to takeoff. Once airborne ATC questions the crew about their departure and they find they are flying the BNDTO4.
summary: The flight crew departed with the BNDTO FOUR procedure loaded in the MCDU despite holding a PITZZ THREE clearance, failing to verify the route after a runway change. Departure control identified the discrepancy, and the crew corrected the flight path by manually selecting the correct fixes to join the cleared departure.

synopsis: EMB145 First Officer reported entering the expected arrival and runway into the FMC prior to departure then not changing it when the airport switched from landing south to landing north. This resulted in a track deviation on the HYPER5 into IAD.
summary: The flight crew descended at IAD on the HYPER 5 arrival without updating the FMS after a runway change, causing a lateral deviation past MULRR toward COUVR instead of SIGBE. ATC instructed a direct route to HUSEL to rejoin the arrival, preventing potential proximity to other aircraft due to the unverified FMS data.

synopsis: At some point during preflight and passenger boarding, a G200 flight crew reports the rudder trim becoming adjusted far to the right. This is not detected prior to takeoff resulting in difficult handling for the pilot flying. Once level at 3,000 feet the cause is detected and corrected.
summary: During takeoff, the aircraft turned right due to rudder trim set off-center, a result of preflight interruptions by ground crew. The pilots identified the trim error at a safe altitude, centered it to restore control, and continued the flight after receiving amended ATC instructions.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: MD80 pilot departing SJC on the LOUPE3 departure was advised by NCT that the speed limit beneath Class B Airspace (SFO) is 200 knots. The reporter suggested that the Class B veil should be depicted on all SIDs and STARs.
summary: The flight crew exceeded the 200-knot Class B speed limit while climbing above 3,000 feet AGL on the LOUPE3 departure from SJC. The controller advised maintaining current speed, noting the restriction was not published on the SID due to overlapping SFO airspace.

synopsis: A MD-82 TAIL COMPARTMENT TEMP HI annunciator alerted at about 13,500 FT in the climb so the QRH was completed and the flight returned to the departure airport for an uneventful landing. Thermal imaging on the ground detected no unusual heat.
summary: During climb-out at 13,500 feet, a tail compartment overheat warning prompted the crew to return to the departure airport. After an overweight landing, a thermal scan confirmed no critical temperature, allowing the aircraft to taxi to the gate with ARFF escort.

synopsis: B757 Captain reports becoming distracted by fuel considerations for the next leg and forgets to call for the before takeoff checklist. The flaps are never set and the takeoff warning sounds at 45 knots, resulting in a rejected takeoff.
summary: The Captain and First Officer missed setting flaps during the before takeoff checklist due to distraction from fuel and delay discussions. They executed a rejected takeoff at 60 KIAS after a configuration alert, cleared the runway, and departed uneventfully after completing required procedures.

synopsis: MD11 Dispatcher and the flight crew report a flight departure with an incorrect fuel load on the weight and balance. The aircraft had been dispatched with the number one fuel tank gauge inoperative, rendering the totalizer and FMC fuel indications inoperative. The correct fuel load (85K) was on board but the weight and balance showed 67K.
summary: Dispatch and the flight crew discovered a 17,000 lb fuel discrepancy on the preliminary weight and balance caused by a ramp agent error and an inoperative fuel indicator MEL. The crew rotated 3 knots early due to incorrect V-speeds calculated from the erroneous weight, though no controllability issues occurred.

synopsis: Pilot of a single engine retractable aircraft experiences an engine failure shortly after takeoff and lands in an open area off the end of the runway. The nose gear collapses during the landing roll.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine power loss and sputtering at 50 feet after takeoff, forcing an off-runway landing. The aircraft's nose gear collapsed upon touchdown after the nose dug into the ground, though the pilot safely shut down systems and exited.

synopsis: Captain reported a very loud grinding sound with considerable vibration and no throttle movement in the Throttle Quadrant of an MD-83 aircraft at cruise altitude. After Auto-Throttles were disconnected, a hot rubber smell dissipated with # 1 Engine rollback. Vibrations continued emanating from Number-1 Engine even after QRH shutdown had been accomplished. Flight diverted.
summary: The Captain and First Officer of an MD-83 diverted to ZZZ2 during cruise at FL 330 after throttle quadrant grinding and vibration caused a Number-1 Engine rollback. They executed an emergency landing with Fire Rescue present due to continued engine vibration, though the aircraft taxied to the gate under its own power.

synopsis: An instructor reported a close encounter with a drone (UAV) at an altitude of 5,000 feet, requiring an evasive maneuver.
summary: A pilot reported a 2-foot silver cylindrical drone at 5000 MSL on PXR 030 at 23 DME. Evasive action was taken to avoid the object.

synopsis: SR22 instructor pilot experiences a loss of control by his student on his seventh landing. The instructor takes control but is unable to prevent the aircraft from departing the runway. No damage to aircraft or airport equipment is reported.
summary: During a student-led landing, the aircraft veered left of the centerline despite the instructor's full right rudder input, causing it to depart the runway into grass. The crew shut down the aircraft with no damage to the plane or airport property.

synopsis: ZTL Controller reported a situation while using TBFM [Time Based Flow Management] into Atlanta when he observed a shift in times that made his job more difficult. Controller wants TBFM stopped until everyone at ZTL understands how it supposedly works.
summary: An air traffic controller at ZTL reported that Time Based Flow Management (TBFM) anomalies caused unexplained delay time shifts and sequencing errors during visual approaches to ATL. The controller attributed these safety risks to system malfunctions, lack of visibility for adjacent sectors, and insufficient staff training, recommending a suspension of TBFM until resolved.

synopsis: Pilot and Controller report of a situation where the pilot had an RA and the Controller had issues trying to hand off the aircraft. Two aircraft came close to each other and the pilot reported receiving an RA and descending to clear the aircraft. Controller reported making an aircraft IFR, having problems handing it off to the correct sector, and then having a loss of separation.
summary: Aircraft X, climbing on an IFR flight plan near Pueblo, received a TCAS descent advisory and ATC instruction to descend to 14,000 feet, passing 500 feet below Aircraft Y. The pilot attributed the near-miss to a coordination failure between Springs Approach and Denver Center regarding the handoff and clearance.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Sector was notified of a radar outage affecting separation standards 11 minutes late. The Controller worked four aircraft during this period none of which had separation which was less than required.
summary: An air traffic controller managing combined sectors 34 and 47 experienced a COV radar outage that increased the HALO from 3 to 5 NM, causing three BOS arrivals to pass 1,000 feet above Aircraft X. The controller attributed the near-miss risk to a communication breakdown where the Operations Manager failed to verbally relay the equipment failure before a delayed written notice arrived.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Local Controller reported the same call sign being used for an aircraft on final as well as another aircraft taxiing for takeoff. Reporter states this is an ongoing problem at this facility and causes confusion for the controllers and pilots. Furthermore, the departure aircraft data tag will not acquire on the departure controllers radar display when this occurs. This is distracting and causes confusion for ATC. Contributing to the situation is dispatchers using the same call sign for an outbound aircraft when the aircraft that is supposed to fly that outbound leg is delayed while inbound.
summary: A Front Line Manager reported that two aircraft with identical call signs operated simultaneously in IAD terminal airspace, causing a controller to issue conflicting clearances for landing and line-up-and-wait. The incident resulted from regional carriers dispatching outbound flights with the same call sign as delayed inbound arrivals, creating unsafe conditions and radar data tag failures.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Local Controller reported clearing an aircraft for takeoff with another aircraft on short final in the opposite direction on the same runway.
summary: Local Control cleared Aircraft X for takeoff on Runway 33 while Aircraft Y was landing on Runway 15 due to a missed scan and distraction from training. The controller cancelled the takeoff, instructed Aircraft X to exit at B8, and allowed both aircraft to clear the runways safely without a go-around.

synopsis: ZMP Controller reported of ZDV giving him a situation where three aircraft will be a conflict within thirty miles of entering his airspace. Controller tried to get Denver to fix the problem, but instead was given control of the three aircraft to fix it himself.
summary: An air traffic controller received three conflicting eastbound aircraft from Denver Center at the same altitude within 30 miles of their airspace. The controller issued vectors and route changes to maintain separation, noting that Denver Center frequently hands over aircraft destined to lose separation and reacts belligerently when confronted.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain experienced a track deviation as a result of miss programing the FMC with METRO instead of MERTO. The two waypoints are several hundred miles apart and not in line.
summary: The Captain programmed the FMC with the wrong intersection (METRO instead of MERTO) due to a spelling transposition during preflight for a BOS departure. At FL230, the error was identified by ATC, who cleared the crew direct to the correct intersection, resulting in minimal navigational deviation and no traffic disruption.

synopsis: B737 Captain experienced a MCP failure at FL380 causing the autopilot to disconnect. Maintenance is contacted and a circuit breaker reset restores the MCP to normal operation.
summary: During cruise at FL380, the autopilot tripped off and the MCP panel blanked and flickered. The crew used emergency authority to cycle circuit breakers under maintenance guidance, restoring the systems.

synopsis: B-757 Captain described an unsatisfactory working relationship with the Purser and the galley person during an oceanic crossing.
summary: The Captain reported a safety issue during cruise when the Purser and galley crew refused to serve pilot meals, citing that customers take priority over pilots. This refusal created a deliberate distraction and unsafe environment, leading the Captain to reassign crew members and confront supervisors who confirmed the passenger-first policy.

synopsis: EMB145 First Officer discovered a damaged #1 main tire during post flight and it is changed prior to the next departure. After takeoff, burnt rubber is smelled in the cockpit and the #3 brake temperature gauge is inoperative, leading the crew to believe a tire has failed. The departure airport Tower confirms rubber on the runway and the crew prepares for landing with a failed tire. The landing is uneventful and post flight reveals it is the #2 tire that has failed.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a tire blowout shortly after rotation, causing burnt rubber smells and debris on the runway. They landed safely, deplaned passengers due to tire and flap damage, and taxied to the gate on one engine after maintenance confirmed the aircraft was safe.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported he refused an attempt by ramp personnel to fix an overweight concern by moving carry-on bags from cargo compartment to the cabin.
summary: The pilot refused a company directive to move carry-on bags from cargo to the cabin to bypass weight limits, citing a lack of supporting procedures in the FOM and FSM. Consequently, four passengers deplaned to reduce weight, causing a 35-minute departure delay and highlighting a serious compliance and training gap.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported leaving the cockpit after parking the aircraft and realizing later one engine was left running.
summary: The Captain reported that after a ground stop at DTW, an unidentified individual alerted the crew that the number two engine was running near idle while the First Officer was away. The Captain immediately shut down the engine, which had been left running despite the aircraft being parked with only the Check Airman and Flight Attendant on board.

synopsis: A300 flight crew reported that shortly after touchdown the aircraft lifted off again, possibly from a wake encounter or a wind gust.
summary: The crew experienced an unexpected lift-off approximately 5 feet after touchdown on Runway 25L at LAX, likely caused by wake turbulence from a preceding 777 or a wind gust. They executed a go-around, received vectors to 2,000 feet, and completed an uneventful second landing.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reported an NMAC with a glider under tow during departure from HIO.
summary: A pilot reported a near mid-air collision with a glider under tow while climbing on the CHISM3 departure from HIO at 2,500 feet. The glider, which lacked a transponder and was not on TCAS, passed 200–300 feet laterally as the crew executed a left turn without evasive maneuvers from either aircraft.

synopsis: A T-45 Instructor with a flight of four became distracted after departure and overshot his assigned altitude of 4000 feet while trying to join formation and remain VMC. ATC requested descent to assigned altitude.
summary: An instructor pilot leading a four-ship T-45C division exceeded the assigned 4,000-foot clearance while attempting to maintain VMC during departure. The pilot acknowledged the deviation was caused by assuming a higher altitude would be granted and immediately corrected the flight after Approach control advised the error.

synopsis: Beechjet 400 Captain reported spotting unannounced traffic on short final lining up to land from the opposite direction on the runway which they had just started their takeoff roll. Takeoff was aborted.
summary: A Beechjet 400A pilot aborted takeoff on Runway 10 at Statesville Regional Airport after spotting an aircraft on short final for Runway 28. The reporter attributed the runway incursion to the other pilot using an obsolete CTAF frequency and failing to see the Beechjet.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Aircraft Y, a VFR parachute aircraft, was descending out of 11,500 feet. Aircraft X, an air carrier, was below Aircraft Y while climbing on a converging heading. Aircraft X received a TCAS/RA on Aircraft Y and responded accordingly. Aircraft Y released parachutists in the immediate vicinity of the Aircraft X's departure route.
summary: Approach controllers routed Aircraft X near parachute Aircraft Y, which was descending from 14,500 feet after releasing jumpers. Aircraft X descended to 10,500 feet due to a TCAS resolution, but the reporter warns that repeated close proximity by the facility creates a fatality risk for jumpers and aircraft occupants.

synopsis: Tower Controller pointed out a small aircraft satellite airport departure to TRACON Controller. TRACON Controller approved point out referencing their heavy jet traffic on approach which passes over the satellite airport. Tower Controller allowed the small aircraft to pass behind heavy jet with less than required wake turbulence separation. TRACON Controller stated this type of scenario happens on a regular basis and that Tower Controllers do not comply with the wake turbulence separation criteria.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that ZZZ2 ATCT improperly point-out a Part 135 aircraft departing ZZZ1 while a heavy jet was on final approach to Runway XXR. The controller stated the tower failed to provide required Class C services or visual separation, creating a potential wake turbulence conflict as the small aircraft climbed through the heavy jet's path.

synopsis: A TRACON Controller clears a locally departing IFR aircraft and a transitioning VFR aircraft to the same 3000 foot altitude. The Controller issued instructions to expedite separation yet the IFR departure still receives a TCAS RA.
summary: An air traffic controller issued conflicting altitude clearances to a departing aircraft and a VFR aircraft, both at 3,000 feet, due to distraction and memory error. The aircraft passed closely, triggering a resolution advisory on the departing flight, prompting immediate corrective climb and descent instructions.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: OGG Controller reports of an overtake on final that if not resolved may have resulted in a NMAC. Controller described that this type of situation is a recurring event where HCF TRACON does not provide adequate spacing on final due to speed issues.
summary: Local Control reported that Aircraft X failed to slow for Aircraft Y on final approach to RWY 2, causing a near-miss due to inadequate spacing from HCF. The controller intervened to clear Aircraft X to land only after Aircraft Y exited the runway, attributing the event to HCF's failure to enforce speed restrictions.

synopsis: A B737 on the SJC SILCN1 RNAV appeared high on profile to NCT but the crew explained late ATC clearance to 'join the 30L Localizer' prevents the FMS from calculating distances correctly. The FMC calculates the altitude to KLIDE, back to GILRO and the return to KLIDE and causes a high approach. Crew managed the error manually.
summary: The flight crew descended on the SILCN1 RNAV Arrival into SJC but was reported high by ATC due to an un-closed FMC discontinuity adding 20 miles to the path. The crew accepted a vector to lose altitude and landed uneventfully, noting the issue stemmed from ATC not issuing an early "join localizer" clearance.

synopsis: A B737-700 Captain intending to crossbleed start #2 engine from #1 bleed air, instead shut down #1 engine. With the APU inoperative, the aircraft was towed back to the gate for a second start.
summary: The pilot inadvertently shut down the number one engine while taxiing for a crossbleed start due to muscle memory triggered by a brake shimmy. The aircraft was towed back to the gate on battery power, and the flight departed uneventfully after the engine was restarted correctly.

synopsis: A tug driver reports stopping a pushback abruptly (grabby brakes) when a truck drives behind the aircraft and the wing walker signals stop. The abrupt stop caused the shear pin on the towbar to break and maintenance is called.
summary: During pushback, a van appeared behind the left wing, prompting an abrupt stop that sheared the towbar pin. Maintenance later found a broken taxi light, and despite the reporter's denial of contact, management classified the event as a near miss and held the pushback operator responsible.

synopsis: A ramp person reports being struck by an LD3 container that is blown over by a B777 being taxied by a maintenance crew from the adjacent gate.
summary: A B777 taxi crew overpowered engines during pushback, causing an empty LD3 container to lift off its carrier and roll onto a ramp worker. The impact pinned the worker to a stationary cart, resulting in injuries to the head, shoulder, and hip that required emergency room treatment.

synopsis: A pilot began taxiing at SEA on the new BLUE line closest to the terminal. An ORANGE line aircraft's ground crew, slightly behind and outboard of the BLUE line, headed to the terminal and ran in front of the lead taxiing aircraft.
summary: The pilot reported a near-miss during taxi clearance when ground crew from a company aircraft running to the far taxi line crossed the path of the reporting aircraft. The incident highlighted a safety gap in dual taxi line procedures where push crews lack a safe route to return to the gate.

synopsis: A B737 Captain experiences a very strong thunderstorm while in the terminal between flights. After arriving at the aircraft it is discovered that a baggage cart, belonging to another carrier, has been blown across the ramp causing damage to the aircraft fuselage.
summary: A violent storm with high winds caused an unsecured baggage cart to blow into the fuselage of a parked aircraft, bending it near the left wing root. The Captain, First Officer, and flight attendants were involved, and ramp management accepted responsibility for the damage.

synopsis: B747 First Officer experiences an Aft Cargo fire EICAS message along with the master warning and fire bell at 1500 AGL during approach. The approach is continued and the Relief Pilot handles the QRH procedures. The fire agent is discharged just before landing and the fire warning blanks. During the roll out the fire warning starts again and Airport Rescue and Fire Fighting (ARFF) is summoned, but no indication of fire is found.
summary: During approach, the crew discharged cargo fire bottles after a FIRE CARGO AFT warning, which briefly cleared before reappearing on rollout. The aircraft stopped on a taxiway for an emergency inspection, received an all-clear, and taxied to parking, though the reporter noted the shutdown checklist lacked CVR circuit breaker location details.

synopsis: B737-800 First Officer reports being vectored off the CONLE1 Departure for traffic then cleared direct Dixon (DIW). The next Controller questions the heading and discovers the crew was actually cleared direct DIXXE on the CONLE SID.
summary: Pilots on a CONLE1 departure were cleared to fix DIXXE but believed they were cleared to DIW (Dixon) due to similar names. The confusion arose from the phonetic similarity between the two fixes, leading the crew to misunderstand the clearance while avoiding weather.

synopsis: B767-300 flight crew reports being vectored into a thunderstorm during approach after requesting that the storm be avoided. Previous aircraft had reported severe turbulence and this crew reported stick shaker and flap overspeed along with bank angles to 40 degrees before exiting.
summary: Pilots on downwind at 7000 ft were vectored into severe thunderstorms by ATC, encountering wind shear that caused airspeed fluctuations from stick shaker to overspeed with flaps 20. The crew attributed the incident to ATC extending the downwind into weather despite prior crew warnings, resulting in an overspeed report.

synopsis: Flight Attendant laments the arming and disarming of entry doors by flight attendants that are not part of the working crew, in order to be helpful. He believes this practice may have been encouraged by the other merger partner.
summary: A flight attendant reported that jumpseaters, who are not active crew, improperly armed and disarmed aircraft doors. The reporter attributed this to cultural training differences and warned that such actions could compromise door safety and lead to fatal outcomes.

synopsis: In the process of trying to correct to the proper flight path on an approach, the flight crew was issued a low altitude alert by air traffic control. After taking corrective action and stabilizing the approach, a safe landing was accomplished.
summary: The flight crew experienced VNAV and LNAV engagement failures during an unfamiliar arrival transition, causing a high profile and autopilot disconnect. ATC issued a low altitude alert, but the crew stabilized above 1,000 feet MSL and landed safely, attributing the event to late clearance timing and FMC selection pressure.

synopsis: ZMA controllers report of one controller using incorrect phraseology and this lead to an airspace violation. Controller used term, 'Not radar contact.' Controller heard radar contact and transferred communications to adjacent sector.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported that improper phraseology by Sector R2, who said "Not radar contact" instead of "Unable," caused Sector R64 to misinterpret the status and request a handoff for Aircraft X. This communication breakdown occurred while Atlantic routes were closed, leading to confusion over whether to accept the handoff or reroute the aircraft.

synopsis: A PHL Tower Controller reports of having a runway incursion because he forgot about traffic crossing and cleared an aircraft for takeoff.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft X for takeoff while forgetting a previously approved crossing clearance for Aircraft Y at taxiway Tango. The controller admitted the error occurred due to high traffic volume and flipping the departure strip back over before Aircraft Y had entered the runway.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A D01 TRACON Controller reports of ZDV ARTCC transferring communication of aircraft while still on a C tag to Denver Approach control. Similar call signs did not help the situation. Weather was a factor which lead to traffic being a complex scenario. The Controller stated ZDV does this often during this scenario.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a near-midair conflict between Aircraft X and Aircraft Y caused by a missed call sign readback and improper handoffs from Denver Center. The controller resolved the situation by issuing immediate vectors and altitude changes, noting that Center failed to respect "unable" responses and delivered aircraft out of position.

synopsis: Two instances of military aircraft exiting the confines of the MOA without clearance. In one case an aircraft came into conflict with an air carrier. In a separate instance an aircraft exited below the base of the MOA and returned to its base without clearance or contacting the ATC Facility.
summary: An air traffic controller lost separation between a military aircraft spilling out of an MOA at 13,000 feet and civilian traffic at 13,500 feet due to a wrong call sign and duplicate transponder codes. The controller issued a traffic alert, the civilian pilot saw the military aircraft, and no resolution advisories occurred.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: Tower Supervisor/Traffic Management Coordinator advised TRACON to change arrival runway to a different parallel runway due to Tower workload. Tower was issuing weather reroutes and had taxiway closures affecting their normal operation. The TRACON Supervisor refused to comply with the Tower Supervisors' instructions.
summary: The Tower FLM and Traffic Manager requested TRACON to route arrivals to Runway XYL to balance workload during taxiway closures and reroutes. TRACON refused, continuing arrivals to Runway XXR despite safety concerns, which the reporter attributed to a culture of non-compliance and arrogance.

synopsis: Three Tower Controllers report that a Front Line Manager (FLM) had an aircraft land on a closed runway. The FLM also reported that he did land the aircraft on what the Controllers thought was a closed runway, but it was closed due to noise abatement and this aircraft did not have a noise abatement issue, so landing on this runway according to the FLM was not an issue. Controllers thought otherwise and tried to stop the FLM from landing on the runway he chose.
summary: A supervisor working Local Control intentionally landed an aircraft on closed Runway 25L despite repeated warnings from other controllers that the runway was unavailable for noise abatement. The supervisor refused to divert the aircraft to the open Runway ZZ, creating an unsafe situation with potential ground personnel and equipment hazards.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZAB Controller reported of traffic coming off SAF airport that do not know where they should be heading and enter a lower MIA [Minimum IFR Altitude]. Controller states this has happened more than a few times and is concerned that the terrain is higher on the route they are flying as opposed to what they file.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X, released to 130 with SYD discretion, flew runway heading toward mountainous terrain instead of its filed route to ZZZ. The controller attributed the incident to the pilot's failure to respect terrain and lack of situational awareness, noting high sector workload prevented issuing a weather route.

synopsis: This flight crew reported that, due to an early turn toward the airport, the approach exceeded the parameters for a stable approach. However, due to a potential conflict with a departing aircraft on the same runway, both pilots determined that continuing the approach and landing was a better course of action than a go-around.
summary: The First Officer and Captain flew a visual approach to LAX Runway 24L but failed to meet stabilized approach criteria due to high energy and late configuration. Although a go-around was considered at 500 feet, they continued to land to avoid conflicting with an aircraft cleared for takeoff on the same runway.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported encountering unforecast severe weather on his flight from SEQM to the United States, and stated he did not get much help from Dispatch, either in the planning stage or enroute.
summary: Pilots on two flights from SEQM encountered severe storms not shown on missing SIG Charts due to an IT propagation failure. They deviated up to 80 nm to avoid the weather, while Dispatch remained unaware of the conditions despite the pilots' reports.

synopsis: B777 flight crew reported they exceeded maximum lateral deviation on an oceanic track in an attempt to minimize wake turbulence from the preceding A380.
summary: The LCA captain and first officer exceeded the 2 NM SLOP limit by deviating 3 NM right to avoid Super 380 wake turbulence. After ATC advised the maximum limit, the crew corrected to 2 NM and returned to course.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported difficulty getting the flight attendants to bring up crew meals in a timely fashion.
summary: The non-flying pilot reported that flight attendants delayed crew meals for 90 minutes due to galley constraints and passenger service priorities, refusing to interrupt service. The pilot cited this delay as a safety issue distracting from flying duties and expressed concern over the crew's unprofessional conduct and potential failure to follow cockpit direction in an emergency.

synopsis: A300 flight crew experienced confusion when being dispatched in the 'payload' mode and could not determine if fueling the center tank was allowed. The center tank was fueled, but not permitted by FOM supplemental procedures.
summary: The flight crew and dispatcher mistakenly operated a flight in Payload mode with fuel in the center tank due to misleading Systems Manual wording. Although the flight proceeded safely within weight limits, the crew identified the error and recommended manual updates to prevent future confusion regarding Payload mode fuel requirements.

synopsis: A Controller cleared an air carrier crew to 4,000 feet on SAN LYNDI THREE RNAV arrival and then issued a terrain alert with a clearance back to 5,000 feet. The crew suspected a SCT Controller error.
summary: Pilots arriving at SAN on the LYNDI3 RNAV arrival were vectored off the procedure and cleared to descend to 4,000 feet direct VYDDA. The controller subsequently issued an urgent climb to 5,000 feet due to a low altitude alert, which the pilots attributed to a controller error caused by heavy workload.

synopsis: A330 Captain reported extreme passenger and crew discomfort related to high temperatures in the aircraft on the ground at a European airport. APU was on MEL and improper aux air conditioning was provided.
summary: The flight crew and 295 passengers experienced extreme cabin heat on an ETOPS aircraft at a hard stand due to an inoperative APU and lack of auxiliary air conditioning. Improper maintenance planning and delayed ground assistance caused a 35-minute wait, nearly forcing emergency procedures to cool the cabin before pushback.

synopsis: Upon reaching cruise altitude, the flight crew noted a fuel imbalance. Appropriate troubleshooting procedures were unsuccessful in correcting the problem, so an immediate diversion to the nearest suitable airport was accomplished.
summary: The crew experienced a rapid fuel imbalance at FL320, with the left tank decreasing while the right remained constant, prompting a diversion. Maintenance later confirmed the left tank was 1,500 pounds lower than the right, and all procedures were followed per company guidelines.

synopsis: MD80 Captain reported being dispatched with an inoperative APU and a Note that required the aircraft to be routed through maintenance bases due to engine driven generator problems a week prior. This note is not compatible with the APU MEL and the Captain asks that it be removed since a week has passed since the generator was repaired. This required a great many phone calls and a long delay to be accomplished.
summary: The Captain refused an MD80 with an inoperative APU and a logbook note regarding generator reliability after Maintenance Control initially refused to remove the note. Following a 45-minute delay involving multiple calls and passenger discomfort, Maintenance Control authorized the note's removal, allowing the flight to depart.

synopsis: A300 Flight Crew is dispatched with MEL 29-24-01 for an inoperative Yellow electric pump. The MEL does not allow the Captain to check the Yellow system/accumulator pressure prior to engine start nor does the MEL require maintenance to perform the check. The reporters believe that both the MEL and the push back procedures need to be modified to accommodate this MEL.
summary: The flight crew operated Leg 2 with MEL 29-24-01 (Yellow system electric pump inop) and could not verify alternate brake accumulator pressure due to inadequate MEL procedures. Although maintenance confirmed the accumulator was good and the flight was uneventful, the crew noted a lack of guidance for preflight checks and alternate pushback procedures.

synopsis: CRJ-200 FO reported the Captain continued to a landing after receiving a red windshear warning at 500 feet on the approach.
summary: During approach to Runway 19, the crew received a red windshear warning at 500 feet. The First Officer advanced throttles, but the Captain reduced them to land, resulting in a safe touchdown despite the reporter citing a misinterpretation of the warning.

synopsis: C99 pilot reported a right engine fire on approach that led to an inflight shutdown.
summary: During an ILS approach, the pilot detected a right engine fire, discharged the extinguisher, and feathered the engine at 200 feet AGL. The aircraft completed an uneventful single-engine landing, taxied clear, and was towed to the hangar by maintenance.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported a taxiway incursion when the Captain's iPad went dark at a critical time.
summary: The flight crew deviated from the assigned taxi route to Runway 28R by turning onto Taxiway Bravo instead of Tango after the pilot's iPad went blank. Ground control identified the error, and the aircraft was instructed to backtrack to the correct taxiway.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported returning to departure airport after #1 engine compressor stalled and then over temped.
summary: The crew experienced a compressor stall and over-temperature on the #1 engine during takeoff, prompting a return for landing. They executed a soft landing with the aircraft overweight, followed by emergency equipment response and logbook entries.

synopsis: EMB-145LR Captain reported rejecting the takeoff just prior to V1 when he experienced blown tire or tires.
summary: The Captain rejected takeoff just prior to V1 due to vibration, unusual noise, and loss of directional control caused by blown tires. The aircraft was stopped safely on the runway with no injuries, fire, or brake overheating, and passengers deplaned with Fire Department assistance.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: A pilot reported encountering wake turbulence on approach to BOS in trail of a B737. Reporter stated he would have been happier with 'descend at pilot's discretion' clearance.
summary: The pilot encountered wake turbulence buffet and a strong left roll while descending to 2,500 feet behind a 737 on approach to runway 4R. The pilot recovered using opposite aileron and attributed the incident to ATC instructions placing the aircraft directly in the preceding arrival's wake.

synopsis: B767-300ER flight crew reported precautionary shutdown of left engine that was exhibiting stall conditions.
summary: The flying pilot experienced a left engine failure to respond to throttle inputs while on an ILS approach. The crew shut down the engine to prevent damage, then completed an uneventful landing and taxi in VFR conditions.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported getting an altitude alert from ATC on a visual approach to LGA Runway 22.
summary: The flight crew, vectored for a visual approach to Runway 22 at LGA, received an altitude alert from Tower while maneuvering for spacing. They acknowledged the alert and landed uneventfully, noting a need for better spacing and diligence in maintaining parameters during visual approaches.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported deviating from cleared track in RJJJ airspace to avoid weather even though ATC refused to clear the deviation.
summary: The Captain of an inbound aircraft at FL350 exercised emergency authority to deviate 10 NM right of track N to avoid severe weather after ATC denied offset requests due to airspace restrictions. The crew successfully bypassed the showers and moderate turbulence before returning to centerline, though Dispatch did not respond to the post-event notification.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported noticing anomalies in the allowable operating weights generated by his performance computer.
summary: The pilot encountered conflicting takeoff performance data between Operations and ACARS systems regarding climb limit weights at varying temperatures. Departure was delayed until the outside air temperature dropped to 34°C, allowing a legal takeoff based on the more conservative performance figures.

synopsis: Flight crew is informed of UAV at 2,700 feet on final to ORD Runway 27L. The flight crew becomes distracted while on final to Runway 28C, as they looked for the conflict.
summary: Pilots on final approach to RWY 28C were informed by approach of a UAV at 2700 feet near RWY 27L. The crew described the situation as dangerous and distracting, as they were forced to scan for the unpredictable drone during a critical flight phase.

synopsis: An EMB-145 Captain intercepting the DTW Runway 22R localizer noted the aircraft overshot the runway centerline because the localizer signal did not center coincidental with the runway centerline. The interference may be a runway specific issue.
summary: The pilot reported losing the localizer signal while intercepting DTW RWY 22R, causing the aircraft to drift near RWY 22L. The pilot visually maneuvered back to the centerline in VMC, attributing the event to a recurring localizer issue on the aircraft.

synopsis: CL600 FO reported taking off with a data error of 10,000 LBS entered into the FMS. FMS multiple character input issue was a factor in the incident.
summary: Pilots at ATL entered incorrect fuel data into the ACARS due to an FMS key-stroke anomaly, resulting in takeoff speeds calculated for a weight 10,000 pounds too low. The error was discovered when landing data showed negative fuel, though no low-speed indications occurred because actual N1 settings exceeded the erroneous TDM requirements.

synopsis: Dash 8 flight crew reported they shut down the #1 engine in flight because of low oil pressure. Flight diverted to a suitable nearby alternate.
summary: The flight crew experienced fluctuating #1 engine oil pressure at 12,000 feet, triggering warnings and necessitating a diversion to ZZZ. They feathered and secured the engine due to low oil levels, landing safely with no observed damage or leaks.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew reported right engine failure about ten minutes after departure. The flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: During initial climb, the right engine suffered a loud bang and flameout, causing a yaw and triggering fire warnings. The crew executed emergency checklists, performed an overweight landing, and maintenance later found visible damage at the engine's exhaust end.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported customer service boarded 70 passengers on their 69-seat aircraft and no one caught the error.
summary: Cabin crew discovered an unaccounted lap child and a 70th passenger on a 69-seat aircraft during pre-takeoff checks. They attributed the error to a gate agent failing to scan a boarding pass and the child being concealed by the mother's clothing.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported being injured in a severe turbulence incident on arrival.
summary: A flight attendant was injured by severe turbulence while securing the aft galley during the arrival phase at ZZZ. The sudden jolt caused the crew member to strike their head on an emergency exit sign, requiring EMT assistance after landing, despite pilots reporting no instrument alerts or turbulence from the preceding aircraft.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported being dispatched with the oxygen panel inoperative at an occupied seat row. After arrival, Maintenance said this was an error.
summary: A flight attendant reported that seats 29DEF with a duct-taped oxygen latch were not blocked despite maintenance approval, leading to latch failure and dangling masks below 25,000 feet. A mechanic later confirmed the seats were miscoded and should have been inoperable, though no injuries occurred.

synopsis: AA5B pilot reported encountering a large number of balloons in flight that had been released in the vicinity of his destination, PYM.
summary: A pilot approaching PYM at 1,200 feet MSL encountered approximately fifty helium balloons launched for a bicycle race with no time for evasive action. No balloons struck the aircraft, but the pilot noted the absence of a NOTAM for the event near the airport.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported Los Angeles Center frequencies were jammed, making traffic management and awareness difficult.
summary: Pilots at 17,000 feet reported a near-midair collision with an aircraft descending 600 feet above while climbing to FL230. A TCAS descent advisory resolved the conflict, though frequency congestion delayed the controller's ability to repeat instructions.

synopsis: AA5 pilot reported some communication difficulties during operations at VPC, a non-tower airport.
summary: Two pilots taking off from Runway 19 at Cartersville GA/Bartow County airport (VPC) did not hear a Mooney pilot's CTAF transmissions regarding a conflicting departure from Runway 01. The Mooney pilot proceeded to take off anyway, resulting in a near-midair conflict that the reporting pilots only discovered after becoming airborne.

synopsis: CTLSi pilot reported having the wrong frequency set during his arrival into LPR, a non-Tower airport. After a go-around to avoid a conflict with an aircraft on the ground, the pilot set the proper frequency.
summary: A pilot approaching LPR on final for Runway 25 missed traffic on Runway 07 due to tuning the radio to the wrong Unicom frequency, 121.7 instead of 122.7. The pilot executed a go-around to avoid a collision with the stopped aircraft, corrected the frequency, and successfully landed on Runway 07.

synopsis: SR22 instructor pilot reported a ground conflict at JWN when an aircraft landed behind him, apparently unaware of the back taxi procedures in effect while construction is in progress.
summary: The reporter and a Piper PA28 pilot encountered a nose-to-nose conflict while back-taxiing at JWN due to construction. The incident occurred because the Piper pilot ignored NOTAMs and AWOS warnings regarding the mandatory back-taxi procedure, leading the reporter to recommend a temporary tower controller or airport closure.

synopsis: C172 Instructor Pilot reported observing a Citation taking off against the flow of traffic at MGY, a non-Tower airport. Reporter stated he has noticed an increase in this kind of activity from private jets.
summary: A flight instructor and student on a training aircraft at uncontrolled airport MGY aborted a departure from Runway 2 after a Citation 10 entered the runway from a perpendicular taxiway. The instructor attributed the incident to the jet ignoring traffic flow and wind conditions to expedite its departure.

synopsis: Schleicher glider pilot reported an NMAC with a light single and did not get an alert from his PowerFlarm unit.
summary: A glider pilot cruising at 2,600–2,700 feet encountered a descending power plane 50–100 feet above while returning to the gliderport. The pilot reported no PowerFlarm alert despite the close call, suspecting the other aircraft lacked an active transponder or the system had a connection issue.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: C525 First Officer reported another aircraft executed a go-around when they taxied onto Runway 30 at CYBL, a non-Tower airport.
summary: Pilots at uncontrolled CYBL crossed the hold line at taxiway A while another aircraft executed a high go-around, which the crew missed due to inadequate diagram review and visual checks. The crew back-taxied after the other pilot confirmed the go-around, with Campbell Radio later advising the correct taxiway C route.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Two captains flying together, each with their 'own operational nuances regarding technology;' created confusion for each other on the KEFFR3 STAR to SNA Runway 20R.
summary: Two captains flying a descent into KSNA experienced a loss of situational awareness when the PNF altered the PF's FMS routing without briefing, causing an unexpected turn and VNAV disengagement. The reporter attributes the subsequent confusion and delayed arrival to the PF abrogating course management duties, which created role confusion and disrupted standard operating procedures.

synopsis: C172 instructor pilot reported executing a go around on approach to BEC Runway 1 when he noticed another aircraft on approach to Runway 19 who was not on CTAF frequency.
summary: Two aircraft on final approach to Runway 1 at BEC executed simultaneous go-arounds at 100 feet AGL after failing to see each other due to the other pilot using the incorrect CTAF frequency. The incident was attributed to light variable winds, the other crew's checkride pressure, and missed visual contact until short final.

synopsis: B747 Captain reported lining up at night for a closed runway at MIA because the runway lights were brighter on that runway than on the parallel open runway.
summary: A 747 crew on a visual approach to MIA Runway 26L mistakenly aligned with closed Runway 26R due to its brighter lights and PAPIs, which were on maintenance test settings. The crew executed a go-around after Tower intervention and landed safely on 26L without incident.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported unintentionally flying into IMC conditions.
summary: A VFR pilot unintentionally entered IMC conditions while cruising at 4,500 MSL due to indistinguishable gray clouds and fog. The pilot immediately requested a descent to 3,000 feet from Tampa Approach, maintained visual ground contact, and safely exited the clouds.

synopsis: C152 instructor pilot reported his student landed at a non-tower airport when the runway was occupied by a small jet that was back taxiing. Reporter stated they never heard any communications from the small jet.
summary: A flight instructor and student conducting touch-and-goes in a training aircraft landed on Runway 17 while an Eclipse Jet was taxiing on the same runway. The instructor attributed the near-miss to the Jet's transmitter not being selected to the CTAF frequency, noting they never heard the Jet's communications.

synopsis: PA-25 glider tow pilot reported getting too close to another aircraft at an uncontrolled airport and stated he did not hear any calls from the other aircraft.
summary: The tow pilot returned to an uncontrolled airport after a glider release and encountered another aircraft on final without hearing a radio call. Although no course changes were required, the proximity was uncomfortable, and the pilot attributed the situation to the other aircraft's failure to announce its position.

synopsis: ZDV Controller reports of opening up a position and not having the correct information displayed on ERAM (Enroute Automation Modernization). No one entered information into the computer that a certain airspace was going to be hot. An Aircraft was in the hot airspace. Controller thought it was the Front Line Managers duty to enter this information.
summary: An air traffic controller and a D-side controller encountered a display failure for restricted airspace R2601 during morning sector opening because it was not activated in ERAM. This prevented URET alerts and scope display until the other controller manually enabled the airspace, revealing Aircraft X was inside the restricted zone.
