synopsis: GSO Controller reports of a busy session working a combined position due to a training class. Controller had a loss of separation with two aircraft and attributes it to not being a strong controller and being unable to work busy sessions with non-combined positions. Controller indicates it was the lack of staffing that led to combined positions, being overloaded, and having a loss of separation.
summary: An air traffic controller managing combined West and Final sectors reported a loss of separation between Aircraft Y and Aircraft X due to high traffic volume and insufficient staffing preventing the opening of the Final Radar sector. The controller attributed the 2.61-mile, 800-foot conflict to management's refusal to authorize overtime, creating dangerous conditions at the facility.

synopsis: Controller and pilots report of being cleared for takeoff and an aircraft that was cleared to cross the runway did in a slow manner. Controller thought aircraft had already crossed and then cleared the carrier. Carrier started takeoff roll and observed red lights down field and aborted takeoff.
summary: A controller cleared Aircraft Y for takeoff while Aircraft X was still crossing the runway, causing Y to abort after seeing red advisory lights. The pilot attributed the incident to the controller failing to verify Aircraft X had cleared the runway before issuing the takeoff clearance.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZAB Controller reported of SAF ATCT personnel who removed the SID for an aircraft. Reporter stated this is a violation of FAA Order 7110.65 paragraph 2-2-11.c. By removing the SID, the minimum initial release altitude goes up 4,000 feet higher due to terrain.
summary: SAF ATCT removed the TAFOY2 SID for Aircraft X at proposed departure time without verbal coordination. This action changed the minimum initial release altitude from 100 to 140 due to terrain, creating an invalid release altitude for Sector 16.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported they failed to make a crossing restriction when they missed a step in FMS setup.
summary: Pilots descending on the MILTON 4 Arrival to Keating (ETG) crossed the waypoint 500 feet high after failing to enter FL330 in the altitude window before selecting VNAV. The reporter attributed the error to divided attention during simultaneous tasks and noted that ATC-altered FMC arrivals introduce systemic error potential.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported uncommanded 45 degree roll from preceding aircraft wake on approach to Runway 9R at ATL.
summary: The crew encountered a 45-degree roll from wake turbulence on approach to ATL RWY 9R, causing Control Wheel Roll to disengage LNAV. The deviation was corrected by the crew and ATC, and the remainder of the approach and landing was normal.

synopsis: B737 flight crew departed SJC after tower had closed without ATC clearance, thinking the PDC they received before tower closure was sufficient.
summary: The flight crew departed uncontrolled SJC after tower closure, incorrectly assuming a pre-departure clearance (PDC) constituted an IFR clearance. NORCAL Departure advised they should have contacted FSS or Departure Control first, an error attributed to fatigue from a long, eventful duty day.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported he has seen multiple instances of the B737 autoflight system deviating from the HYDRR1 RNAV arrival into PHX.
summary: The Captain and First Officer manually intervened during a B737-700 descent on the HYDRR 1 arrival into PHX when the autopilot failed to maintain 9000 ft at CHAVO. The aircraft pitched down with increasing speed, requiring manual leveling to prevent an altitude deviation below the constraint.

synopsis: With the Cockpit to Cabin Interphone locked up, a First Officer and Captain describe the initial difficulty their Flight Attendant Purser had trying to communicate with them, as sparks and smoke emanated between two First Class seats on a B777 aircraft. Captain also noted the professionalism and command by the Purser of the Flight Attendant crew actions.
summary: During climb, a locked interphone delayed the crew's response to sparks and smoke from Seat 1K caused by a loose power cable entangled in an electric footrest gear. The flight diverted to ZZZZ, dumped fuel, and landed safely after Maintenance Control instructed power cutoff to the affected seats.

synopsis: Captain reports about a rushed APU deferral that resulted in the maintenance release of an A320 aircraft without the actual MEL maintenance deferral items being accomplished. MEL had required cockpit Circuit Breakers L41 and L42 to be 'Pulled and Safetied.' APU had an extensive auto-shutdown history.
summary: The Captain and maintenance personnel were involved when a rushed APU deferral was issued without accomplishing required MEL breaker safeties. The aircraft departed with the Maintenance Release falsely stating compliance, a discrepancy the crew only detected during flight.

synopsis: A ramp crew member reports his concerns about a safety hazard caused by the 100 percent Oversteer Warning System siren sounding off inside the cab of their supertugs during aircraft towing operations. The loud, shrieking siren sound overwhelms the Ground Controller, Ramp Controller and Tug Operator's efforts to communicate with each other, especially when crossing active runways and taxiways. The siren cannot be turned off unless the aircraft is disconnected from the Supertug.
summary: A ground handler reported that a supertug's 100 percent Over Steer siren activated during a turn on taxiway bravo, creating a life-and-death hazard. The loud alarm prevented concentration and radio communication with the FAA and Ramp Towers while crossing active runways.

synopsis: Pilot reported of an arrogant Controller that he has complained to the Tower manager about. Reporter then stated he will not put up with his attitude, anger problem anymore.
summary: A pilot reported that an SDF approach controller used an aggressive, yelling tone when issuing instructions and confirming altitude. The pilot described the controller's unprofessional behavior as a major distraction and a safety risk, requesting his removal from operations.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported the flying First Officer descended below cleared altitude on approach to MMSD after misunderstanding an ATC clearance.
summary: The Captain and First Officer descended below minimum vectoring altitude while en route to Cabo due to the Captain's distraction assisting another flight. The crew accepted a visual approach clearance while not established on the approach segment, resulting in an unauthorized descent.

synopsis: Regional jet flight crew reported receiving a terrain warning on approach to AVP Runway 22.
summary: The flight crew received a terrain warning while descending to 2700 ft on a right downwind for Runway 22 at AVP, likely due to task saturation during approach preparation. They executed an immediate climb to 3700 ft, the sector's minimum vectoring altitude, and subsequently completed a stable ILS landing without further incident.

synopsis: ERJ-175 flight crew reported they had a possible altitude deviation on approach to CLT when they were distracted by the Captain's iPad mount coming loose and falling onto his arm.
summary: The pilot reported that an iPad mount falling on their arm caused distraction during the descent via IVANE 5 arrival, leading to an unmonitored descent profile. The crew passed through 9,000 feet while the controller questioned their altitude, prompting the pilot to recommend hard mounts to prevent future disruptions.

synopsis: EMB-145LR First Officer reported flap failure resulting in a successful zero flap approach and landing.
summary: During arrival, the crew experienced a flap failure with no position indication after EICAS warnings. They executed a QRH procedure, calculated landing distance for a zero-degree flap landing, and safely landed the aircraft with no further issues.

aircraft: Medium Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: While maneuvering for an approach, the flight crew received a 'terrain, pull up' warning from the EGPWS on the aircraft. After making an altitude correction, a successful approach and landing was competed.
summary: The flight crew on approach to ZZZ received an EGPWS warning after misunderstanding a clearance to descend to 2000 feet instead of the correct 2400 feet. Tower subsequently cleared them for a visual approach, allowing the crew to complete the landing safely.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Business jet Captain reported an encounter with an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), at approximately 2,600 feet, during initial approach to LAX Runway 24L. No evasive action was required.
summary: The First Officer on a flight to LAX runway 24L observed a drone at 3,000 feet AGL while at 2,600 feet AGL on right downwind. The drone posed no risk, required no evasive action, and the flight landed safely after the First Officer notified ATC.

synopsis: A Hawker BE-400XP Captain and First Officer report about the Right and Left Engine Starter/Generators dropping offline during descent. No annunciators, no engine instrument indication or radio available. Emergency (Standby) Battery power not available when selected. Maintenance found Left Generator had self-destructed and the Generator Control Unit had failed.
summary: During initial descent, both generators tripped offline, and emergency power failed to activate. The crew restored the right generator using main battery power and continued to the destination, landing safely with the aircraft operating on battery and the right generator.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence on approach to ORD, possibly from a preceding heavy jet.
summary: The crew descending on left downwind for RWY 27L at ORD encountered severe rolling moments and turbulence, likely from wake turbulence generated by a preceding heavy jet on approach to RWY 28C. The First Officer disconnected the autopilot to manually control the aircraft, reporting altitude difficulties to ATC before stabilizing the flight.

synopsis: Air carrier Dispatcher reported a known incorrect MEL that would allow dispatch with TCAS inoperative into countries that do not in fact allow that condition.
summary: The flight crew refused to dispatch the aircraft with an inoperative TCAS system, citing that the MEL incorrectly permits deferral in countries like India and China where it is prohibited. Maintenance insisted on the MEL text despite acknowledging the operational reality, creating a safety conflict over the aircraft's ability to avoid traffic.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported injuries to herself and others when the aircraft came to an abrupt stop.
summary: The Captain slammed the brakes while flight attendants were in demo positions, causing them to be thrown violently. The reporter suffered a concussion, brain bleeding, and neck injury, while two other crew members and one passenger were also injured.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported sustaining an injury when a large cart rolled in turbulence because it did not have any brake pedals on one side.
summary: A flight attendant in the aft galley was injured when a large service cart without brake pedals on one side rolled during moderate turbulence, pinning her left forearm. The reporter attributed the accident to catering placing the defective cart on the aircraft.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported attempting to land at BIH after he listened to the ASOS. Pilot observed an 'X' on the runway and wondered why the runway closure was not on the ASOS. Pilot had not checked NOTAMs before departing for the destination.
summary: A VFR pilot flying to BIH missed a runway closure NOTAM and encountered maintenance trucks on Runway 12, forcing a go-around and landing on Runway 34. The pilot attributed the incident to complacency and the inability of the airport operator to update the NOAA-owned ASOS with local runway status.

synopsis: C172 instructor pilot reported his student applied excessive pitch on a practice soft field takeoff and lost directional control, hitting a runway light and damaging a brake in the process. The subsequent landing proved difficult to control with the brake damage and the aircraft departed the runway.
summary: A CFI and student in a Cessna 172 experienced a runway excursion during soft field training when the student's abrupt pitch-up caused the left main gear to strike a runway light, damaging the brake. The subsequent brake failure and ineffective rudder on the narrow runway caused the aircraft to skid off into a bush, resulting in no injuries or significant damage.

synopsis: Shortly after takeoff, at 80 knots and commencing a left turn, H269C helicopter instructor pilot encountered lateral oscillations, high frequency vibrations, and subsequent Low Rotor RPM warning and Main Rotor Transmission Temp/Press light. Pilot executed a successful forced landing in a gravel parking lot.
summary: The pilot and student experienced low rotor RPM and vibration during a traffic avoidance turn shortly after departing ZZZ, causing a forced landing in a gravel lot. An excessive flare to avoid trucks resulted in tail stinger contact, but the helicopter stopped safely with no injuries.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: A light twin Flight Instructor experienced a gear up landing while instructing. Preparations for a no flap landing and an ATC assigned runway change may have gotten in the way of completing the landing check.
summary: An instructor and student in a twin-engine aircraft impacted the runway on a full-stop landing with gear up after the instructor failed to verify gear extension. The instructor attributed the error to distraction by approach speed management and confusing the gear warning horn with the stall warning, resulting in no injuries or substantial damage.

synopsis: SandShark UAS landing gear departed the aircraft after touchdown.
summary: Shortly after touchdown, the right main landing gear departed the aircraft, but directional control was maintained as it skidded to a stop. Following documentation and mission commander clearance, the aircraft was removed for repair with no major damage reported.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Flight crew reported a lack of company guidance regarding a new return to gate fueling policy and how to comply with the requirement for two forms of egress.
summary: The Captain coordinated a return to gate with passengers onboard, where the Fire Chief mandated door arming for fueling due to a new airport policy requiring two egress forms. The crew complied by arming an aft door under Fire Chief direction, though the Captain noted a need for company guidance on this procedure.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: The pilot was confused by the ambiguity of an amended clearance which deleted the intersection at the junction of two airways.
summary: A pilot flying an IFR flight from Monterey to Redlands paused at the DARTS intersection after ATC amended the clearance to delete it, waiting for explicit instructions to join the next airway. The controller subsequently directed the pilot to continue on the flight plan, resolving the ambiguity without airspace penetration or conflicts.

synopsis: C177RG pilot reported inadvertently entering IMC conditions while enroute to an airport that was forecast for better weather.
summary: A VFR pilot flying to airport ZZZ for maintenance encountered rapidly lowering ceilings and entered clouds despite reported 1,400-foot conditions. The pilot attributed the incident to complacency from area familiarity and reliance on outdated forecasts, but safely landed after receiving vectors from ZZZ1 Tower.

synopsis: A small aircraft pilot reported communication problems with ATC that led to an airborne conflict with a transport aircraft.
summary: The pilot experienced intermittent radio transmission issues at Camarillo but took off and later lost contact with Mugu Tower. While maneuvering to avoid airspace conflicts, the pilot inadvertently crossed the runway centerline, creating a potential conflict with an overflying jet before landing safely at the destination with restored communications.

synopsis: AS350B3 helicopter pilot reported two NMACs with crop dusters during flight.
summary: An EMS helicopter pilot flying at 500 feet AGL with a patient encountered two crop dusting aircraft flying perpendicular below without visual contact. The lack of a common frequency prevented communication, though climbing to 1000 feet AGL increased separation to 700 feet for the second encounter.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: DEN Tower Controller reported clearing an aircraft to land then joining a discussion. Controller used a memory aid to remind him of the landing traffic. Controller then did a few other things and removed the memory aid and joined the conversation again. Controller then scanned the runway seeing no traffic on it and cleared the next aircraft for takeoff. Traffic was on landing roll and the pilot advised Tower they were still on the runway. Controller told departing aircraft to line up and wait. Controller is aware of distractions and stated that he should have been more attentive to the position.
summary: A distracted Local controller inadvertently removed the runway 17R memory aid while conversing, leading to a takeoff clearance for Aircraft Y while Aircraft X was landing. The controller halted Aircraft Y after realizing the conflict, attributing the incident to inattention and improper conversation timing.

synopsis: CLT controllers reported of an aircraft departing on a RNAV departure that turned towards another aircraft. Aircraft was supposed to turn right but turned left into other departing traffic. Controller called the aircraft but they had switched to departure control.
summary: Local control cleared Aircraft X and Y for simultaneous takeoffs from Runway 18C and 18L, but Aircraft X deviated left instead of right on the SID, creating a conflict. The controller lost contact with Aircraft X while instructing Aircraft Y to turn away, resulting in a 1.5-mile, 500-foot separation due to the noise waiver delaying vectoring.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported they received final weights with a 900 pound increase in cruise flight.
summary: The flight crew received a revised Take Off Weight message from Dispatch while in cruise, revealing they had departed with incorrect data. The pilot noted that while no incident occurred, the error could have compromised an engine failure or abort scenario near V1.

synopsis: The flight crew reported that there were inadequate resources and supplies to clean up after an airsick passenger.
summary: Flight attendants and a pilot reported that a passenger vomited in the forward galley during a flight from ZZZ to ZZZ1. Inadequate cleaning equipment at both stations resulted in improper cleanup, leaving the aircraft unsanitary and forcing crews and passengers to endure the mess on subsequent legs.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A flight crew reported that, while in flight, a smoke detector alarm in one of the lavatories activated. After consulting the appropriate checklists, confirming that there was no indication of smoke, fumes, or odors, and securing the lavatory, the decision was made to continue to the destination airport.
summary: Flight crew and cabin crew experienced a false aft lav smoke detector alarm during flight with no smoke or fumes present. Pilots followed the QRH to pull circuit breakers, closed the lavatory, and landed safely without declaring an emergency before logging the issue for maintenance.

synopsis: B737 Flight Crew experiences a NMAC with a glider at 10000 feet 25 NM south of LAS during arrival. ATC was aware of the gliders in the area but did not inform the crew. A TCAS TA was the first indication of traffic with no altitude indication.
summary: Pilots on a KEPEC descent to 8,000 ft south of Las Vegas encountered a glider 200–300 ft above after a TCAS alert. Approach Control stated they could not warn of the gliders because they were operating outside Class B airspace, despite multiple reports of activity.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports having to make an abrupt stop approaching his gate due to a catering truck approaching rapidly from the right.
summary: The pilot reported a near-miss while taxiing when a catering truck approached at high speed from the right and failed to stop. The pilot applied heavy braking to avoid a collision, attributing the incident to the driver's reckless operation and failure to respect aircraft right of way.

synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported FOD at BOI airport. Infield grass and areas between the runways and taxiways has been replaced with sand/gravel mix which blew into the jet engines.
summary: The flight crew and maintenance personnel found sand and gravel debris in both engines after a dust storm at Boise, caused by new airport surface material. The aircraft was grounded for a borescope inspection after debris was expelled during an idle motor test, raising concerns of potential dual engine failure.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported encountering wake turbulence at FL340 when a Widebody Transport aircraft crossed their path 20 miles ahead of them that resulted in an uncommanded 45 degree bank.
summary: A crew at FL340 encountered sudden moderate turbulence and a 45-degree roll near the Atlantic City-Baltimore coast, causing autopilot disengagement. The controller attributed the event to a widebody transport crossing 20 miles ahead, which was deemed too distant to report.

synopsis: B737 flight crew experiences a lavatory smoke alarm in flight. A flight attendant immediately called the cockpit to inform that a passenger had been discovered smoking an electronic cigarette in the lavatory.
summary: A passenger smoking an electronic cigarette in the right aft lavatory triggered a smoke alarm during flight. The crew confirmed no fire, completed the false activation checklist, and landed uneventfully while ground security met the aircraft to address the passenger.

synopsis: EMB135 Captain reports diverting to an alternate airport after extensive vectoring during arrival and ATC being unable to provide an expected landing time.
summary: Pilots diverted to ZZZ after ATC issued indefinite vectors and fuel concerns during a congested arrival. The reporter attributed the event to ATC-induced delays and inadequate dispatch support, which caused an unnecessarily long ground stay.

synopsis: Air carrier pilot reported that he was close to declaring minimum fuel because of inadequate reserves and unrealistic flight planning combined with arrival vectoring.
summary: The pilot reported that ATC vectoring for spacing and altitude deviations caused excessive fuel burn, reducing reserves to under five minutes. The crew declared minimum fuel to the dispatcher but landed safely on runway 11 after requesting a direct approach.

synopsis: Departing out of ERI, the pilot inadvertently entered YAARK instead of YARRK into the flight plan, resulting in a heading deviation after takeoff.
summary: The pilot entered the wrong initial fix, YAARK instead of YARRK, during flight plan loading at ERI. After turning east toward the incorrect fix during climb-out, ATC queried the position, prompting the crew to correct the heading and continue safely.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: After dispatching with one pack inoperative, the aircraft had the other bleed trip which resulted in no pressurization, a very hot cabin, and a return to the departure airport at DFW.
summary: The crew departed DFW with an inoperative left pack and encountered a right bleed fault at 4,000 ft. They restored the right pack per QRH, returned for an overweight landing, and the post-flight inspection reported nothing unusual.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilots report of being told to cross and having a short delay in doing so. The Tower Controller then clears a departure for takeoff while aircraft is slowly crossing downfield. The departing aircraft aborts takeoff and Tower has crossing traffic call for a possible deviation.
summary: The crew of an arriving aircraft experienced a brake delay while crossing runway 16L, and the tower controller cleared Aircraft Y for takeoff before verifying the crossing aircraft was clear. Aircraft Y aborted its takeoff due to the runway incursion caused by the controller's failure to confirm the runway was clear.

synopsis: The crew misread the charted DME on the LGA5 departure procedure and started their turn two miles late.
summary: The First Officer misread the LGA5 Whitestone departure chart, turning left to heading 040 at 4.5 DME instead of the required 2.5 DME. Air Traffic Control queried the aircraft's position, prompting the crew to highlight the DME on the chart to prevent future errors.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: A Flight Attendant reported that ramp personnel were not accepting oversized bags during boarding. When confronted with policy and FAR violations, the lack of ramp management oversight and lack of ramp employee concern for their actions' consequences was cause for concern.
summary: During boarding at FLL, a flight attendant intervened when ground crew refused to gate-check oversized bags or apply required green tags, citing staffing issues. The crew eventually tagged and loaded the bags after the attendant insisted on security and weight-and-balance compliance, preventing a potential safety violation.

synopsis: Flight Attendant reported inadequate time for their preflight responsibilities.
summary: Flight attendants reported that passengers boarded at departure minus 55 minutes while the crew was conducting their safety briefing, preventing them from checking emergency equipment or manning exits. The crew attributed this to a mismatch between gate agent boarding times and crew report requirements, requesting a schedule adjustment to allow adequate preflight time.

aircraft: Cessna Citation Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: The flight crew reported illumination of a 'door not locked' warning light, followed by inability to control cabin pressurization. They diverted to the nearest suitable airfield, corrected the problem, and continued uneventfully to their destination.
summary: The crew experienced false door and cabin altitude warnings at 9,500 feet due to imperfectly aligned main door indicator flags, causing an immediate descent and diversion. After realigning the flags and re-filing, the flight continued to the destination without further incident.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: On approach to HEF in IMC, there was a breakdown in communication about an assigned altitude between the pilot and the Controller.
summary: The pilot and two passengers descended below the minimum vectoring altitude to 2,000 feet MSL while in IMC after receiving conflicting instructions from Potomac Approach. The crew immediately climbed back to 2,600 feet MSL upon realizing the error, and the flight concluded uneventfully after being cleared for the ILS 16L approach.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: After takeoff, a rough engine caused the pilot to return to ORL.
summary: The pilot departed ORL with a clogged fuel injector and engine roughness while two banner tows were also departing. To avoid a midair collision with unseen traffic, the pilot climbed above the cleared 1,500 feet, potentially piercing the Class B floor, to safely return to the airport.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported encountering what he considers to be substandard ATC handling by SCT TRACON while flying into VNY.
summary: Two experienced pilots flying VFR near Van Nuys were vectored by SoCal Approach toward terrain at 3,300 feet MSL to separate from faster jet traffic. The pilots deviated from the controller's heading instruction to avoid a 6,000-foot mountain, citing the controller's dismissive response and a pattern of prioritizing jets over general aviation.

synopsis: A M201J gear actuator circuit breaker tripped when the gear was selected down. A gear up landing was completed with minimal damage.
summary: The pilot experienced a landing gear actuator circuit breaker trip and jammed emergency extension cable during final approach, forcing a missed approach and return to the departure airport. The aircraft completed a gear-up landing with minimal damage to the gear doors, propeller, and cowling, resulting in no injuries or fluid leaks.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A local pilot did not check for NOTAMs and assumed that other aircraft were not using the CTAF frequency. He later discovered that a temporary tower had been opened due to heavy fire fighting activity in the area.
summary: A pilot flying into McClellan Field (KMCC) unknowingly used the CTAF instead of the activated tower frequency, resulting in no radio contact during arrival and departure. The pilot attributed the error to not checking for weather updates and relying on charts that listed only the CTAF frequency.

synopsis: Just after takeoff from MDW, the pilot was distracted by a miscommunication which resulted in an altitude and airspeed exceedance.
summary: During a Runway 4R departure from MDW, the pilot exceeded 3,000 feet and 250 knots after the tower controller aggressively corrected the copilot's incorrect readback of a left turn heading. The pilot attributed the altitude and airspeed excursions to diverted attention caused by the controller's alarmist reaction to the readback error.

synopsis: During an ATP AMEL checkride in a PA-34-200T, the pilot experienced an actual engine malfunction, so he feathered the engine and landed successfully.
summary: During a Piper Seneca II ATP checkride, the applicant and examiner experienced a left engine failure with unresponsive RPM and propeller governor issues while circling to land. They feathered the left propeller, announced the situation on CTAF, and landed single-engine without incident.

synopsis: A glider instructor was informed some time after his instruction flight that he may have been involved in a near miss with a jet near 1OR4. The glider crew did not see the aircraft.
summary: A glider instructor and student flying from 1OR4 were identified by a nearby tower as the probable cause of a jet's reported close encounter at 2,800 feet. The crew did not see or hear the jet, though their glider was the only one in the vicinity at that time.

synopsis: Local Controller allowed the Ground Controller to approve a tug towing an aircraft to cross the active runway. The Local Controller forgot about the tug crossing the runway and cleared an aircraft for takeoff. The tug towing the aircraft had not cleared the runway when the departing aircraft took off.
summary: An understaffed Ground controller and Local controller lost surface separation when Local cleared Aircraft X for takeoff while a tug was crossing the runway. The incident resulted from the Ground controller's oversight while managing multiple positions and the Local controller's failure to verify the active crossing.

synopsis: Controller was being handed off two aircraft on converging headings at the same altitude. In the controller's opinion it was an imminent situation. The controller called the adjacent sector and instructed them to issue a heading to one of the aircraft to ensure lateral separation in the receiving controller's airspace. The reporter states this is a common situation between these two sectors.
summary: An ARTCC controller handed two aircraft at flight level 410 on conflicting courses to the reporting controller, who instructed a 30-degree left turn to prevent a loss of separation. The reporter attributes the recurring safety issue to the ARTCC sector's failure to manage traffic, noting that wind assistance helped achieve the necessary separation.

synopsis: An air carrier flight crew and SCT Controller reported an airborne conflict between the flight crew's aircraft and another air carrier flight. Contributing factors included a misread PDC by the flight crew and improper altitude reporting during initial contact with SCT. Frequency congestion likely contributed.
summary: Pilots of Aircraft Y departed LAX, mistakenly climbing past their 5,000 ft clearance to 11,000 ft due to misreading the PDC. This caused a loss of separation and a Resolution Advisory with Aircraft X, which was climbing through 7,500 ft on the LOOP departure.

synopsis: The 737 crew violated FAR 117 due to a divertion followed by a taxi/takeoff delay.
summary: Pilots reported that Dispatch and Crew Scheduling reduced the ZZZ1-ZZZ block time to 59 minutes despite weather and holding, causing a 9-hour 6-minute daily block time violation. Ground delays and a 13-minute wheels-up time, contrary to the 12-minute limit provided, resulted in the flight exceeding FAR 117 limits due to flawed operational coordination.

synopsis: A pilot reported his B737-700 had 11 complex MELs with a 27 page print of MEL procedures needing to be checked or procedures needing to be completed prior to flight.
summary: The First Officer reported receiving a confusing 27-page MEL printout for a flight with 11 deferred items, complicating the pre-flight review of restrictions and circuit breaker status. The Captain's casual comment that the aircraft had been flying for days raised concerns about compliance and maintenance standards, though the flight departed safely due to a delay.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A First Officer reported requesting Dispatch make a new release available because they could not print from Operations. After discovering the TCAS inoperative with an international destination, Dispatch still refused to issue new release up until the flight was delayed without it.
summary: The First Officer and Captain faced a departure delay when flight planning documents were unavailable in SABRE and the TCAS was placarded inoperative. Although a new release was eventually issued, the crew later received conflicting advice from management regarding the legality of operating with TCAS inoperative for international flights.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An aircraft was dispatched to a foreign destination with the TCAS inoperative but the crew did not realize it until later that the Ops SPEC and MEL prevent dispatch to a foreign destination with the TCAS inoperative.
summary: The flight crew failed to thoroughly study the Minimum Equipment List (MEL) Spec Notes for a deferred TCAS during pre-flight. This oversight meant they did not realize the aircraft was prohibited from operating to non-US destinations.

synopsis: The flight crew reported that, during a critical phase of their approach, the ILS glideslope signal was disturbed by an aircraft taxiing down the runway. The autopilot was quickly disengaged, however the aircraft momentarily descended below the glidescope, generating a terrain proximity warning from the control Tower. A timely correction was made and the approach and landing were completed successfully.
summary: During an ILS approach to CLT 36R, the tower's decision to taxi another aircraft across the runway disturbed the glideslope signal, causing the AFCS to pitch up and upset the flight. The crew disengaged the AFCS to recover, resulting in a low altitude warning before continuing a stable visual approach.

synopsis: An ERJ flight crew reported that, due to cloud conditions, they were unable to maintain visual reference from preceding traffic. After advising ATC of the situation they were told to level off immediately, resulting in a momentary speed excursion to 280 knots below 10,000 feet. A correction was accomplished and the flight continued uneventfully.
summary: During climb out from ZZZ, the crew lost visual separation with a preceding aircraft entering IMC. An ambiguous ATC instruction to "level off" while in FLCH mode caused an airspeed increase to 280 KIAS, which the pilot corrected by reducing power to maintain 250 KIAS below 10,000 feet.

synopsis: BE-400XP flight crew received an abnormal landing gear indication on approach, so they diverted to a VFR, Tower-controlled airport. With assistance from company Maintenance and with a visual inspection by the Tower. They followed an unusual procedure, received normal gear indications, and landed uneventfully.
summary: The flight crew diverted to ZZZ1 after a red gear handle warning light illuminated despite three green lights on approach. Pulling the emergency gear door retraction handle extinguished the warning light, allowing a normal landing with emergency personnel on standby.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier pilot questioned the SJC BMRNG2 RNAV Departure wording clarity about 'CLIMB TO 3,000 feet'. Should the climb continue while expecting vectors or should the statement be 'CLIMB TO AND MAINTAIN 3,000 feet EXPECT VECTORS'?
summary: A pilot reported that the BMRNG TWO RNAV departure from SJC is unclear regarding whether to maintain 3,000 feet or continue climbing while expecting vectors. The pilot stated this ambiguity could cause future altitude deviations and recommended changing the wording to "Climb and Maintain" or "While Climbing Expect."

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier Captain noted while flying the SFO SERFR ONE Arrival ATC issues a 'Descend VIA except maintain 10,000 feet' so while flying the SFO BDEGA ONE after a runway change from 28L to 28R he automatically selected 10,000 feet as the CORKK crossing restriction. Consistent final crossing altitudes would help.
summary: The pilot descended via the BDEGA ONE arrival to 10,000 feet instead of the required 11,000 feet due to preconceived notions from previous SERFR ONE arrivals. The crew corrected the altitude after the PM questioned the level-off, attributing the error to complacency and reliance on non-SOP tribal knowledge.

synopsis: BD700 Flight Crew reported not detecting a 280 knot speed restriction on the TMBRS2 RNAV to PDX. Once pointed out they believed it did not apply since they were proceeding direct to a fix on the arrival but not actually on the arrival. The crossing restriction at PORTL was missed due to descending in V/S instead of VNAV and misinterpreting the chart.
summary: The crew descended below the 11,000-foot minimum at PORTL and VANTZ fixes while executing the TMBRS 2 arrival into PDX due to autopilot mode selection errors and missed chart restrictions. They recovered by climbing back to 11,000 feet, and ATC issued no comments or requests for follow-up.

synopsis: A student pilot lost control of his PA-28 after touchdown and departed the runway with no damage.
summary: A student pilot lost directional control on the runway after a solo landing, veering into the grass and damaging runway lights. The instructor attributed the incident to the student panicking, overusing brakes, and failing to steer with rudders instead of hands.

synopsis: A possible CFTT event departing RDM was avoided by the crew through good situational awareness and an expeditious climb.
summary: Fatigued pilots at RDM accepted an unusually low 4,000-foot clearance limit due to rushing for a wheels-up time, nearly causing a CFIT event near mountains exceeding that altitude. The First Officer promptly requested a higher clearance, allowing a safe climb to 14,000 feet before terrain impact could occur.

synopsis: Pilot was queried by Controller why he was turning his EMB-600 Legacy aircraft at 14,900 instead of 15,000 as directed. Pilot noted all three altimeters did read 15,000. They rebooted the system onboard and the altimeter read correctly. The next day the same aircraft had the same condition. They rebooted the system and no further issues arose.
summary: During climb out of ZZZ, the pilot turned direct to ZZZ1 at 15,000 feet based on altimeter readings, but ATC reported the aircraft was actually at 14,900 feet. The discrepancy was caused by a faulty system that displayed incorrect altitude until the pilot rebooted the avionics, an issue that recurred the next day.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: MD-80 crew discovered after takeoff a large GPS position error, which caused a track deviation but were given ATC vectors on course where VOR airway tracking continued. Later in the flight GPS accuracy was attained and therefore used to the destination.
summary: The First Officer and Captain of an MD-80 experienced a severe FMS/GPS navigation error during climb, causing a 310 NM longitude discrepancy. They reverted to VOR navigation, amended their flight plan, and continued to the destination after verifying fuel sufficiency and VOR coverage.

synopsis: BE200 pilot reported filing a VFR flight plan to MMTJ from further south in Mexico. When MMTJ Tower was contacted for landing, the instructions were to enter a left base for Runway 26R. MMTJ only has Runway 9/27 and after several queries the reporter was switched to SDM Tower and cleared to land Runway 26R. No EAPIS had been filed for landing in the USA.
summary: The pilot, flying VFR to MMTJ, was cleared by Tijuana Tower for Runway 26R at Brown Field despite the pilot's repeated concerns that Runway 27 was intended. The pilot landed on Runway 26R to avoid TCAS traffic conflicts, noting they had not filed an EAPIS.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: D01 TRACON had to evacuate their facility and declared 'ATC Zero' due to an emergency situation. There are procedures in place in which the ARTCC takes over the airspace of the TRACON. The ARTCC personnel did not know how to implement the procedure for this situation.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that during an emergency evacuation, TRACON personnel exited the control room, leaving airspace management unclear and IFR services suspended. The controller attributed the confusion to a lack of required contingency training and recommended annual drills for such scenarios.

synopsis: An Air Carrier crew was cleared on the PHX SNOBL 3 Departure during a full route clearance but read back SILOW 4. A total of three clearances, include to Departure, were read back and acknowledged as SILOW 4. The crew was East Coast based not tuned to West Coast verbal sounds.
summary: Two pilots misheard the SNOBL 3 departure clearance as SILOW 4 at Phoenix due to similar phonetics, leading to an incorrect route assignment. The error was discovered at 7,000 feet when ATC issued a turn to QUAKY, which was not part of the intended departure.

synopsis: B737-700 First Officer reported a track deviation following a wake turbulence encounter on approach to ATL.
summary: During approach to Atlanta Runway 9R, wake turbulence from a preceding aircraft caused a roll change, disengaging LNAV and activating Control Wheel Steering. The crew corrected the deviation after a late turn, and ATC issued a new heading to intercept the localizer for a normal landing.

synopsis: An aircraft on a visual to ATL was requested to maintain 180 kts to the marker behind a heavier aircraft, but slowed in order to maintain 3 miles spacing behind the heavy. ATC objected and stated 2.5 miles is the new separation standard.
summary: The pilot reported that while following a B757 on a visual approach, they had to slow below the assigned 180 knots to maintain wake turbulence separation. Although the landing was safe, the pilot criticized the controller's initial refusal to acknowledge the speed deviation and the subsequent dispute over required separation distances.

synopsis: The pilot reported that it is often difficult to achieve a stabilized approach profile at DCA as approach control is 'slam dunking' arrivals, clearing them for the approach while high and fast and close to the FAF.
summary: The pilot reported that DCA ATC cleared their aircraft for an LDA Z approach to Runway 19 while 1,500 feet high and two miles outside the final fix. This aggressive clearance in marginal weather caused an unstable approach requiring aggressive descent control to capture the profile near 1,200 feet.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported being cleared for the IVANE5 RNAV then vectored off and given a speed restriction. They were then given a descent, direct to MAJIC, and to resume IVANE5 speeds at MAJIC. Managed descent was selected, but the aircraft was below the path and continued descending in vertical speed. ATC detected the error.
summary: The flight crew received a direct clearance to MAJIC while descending on the IVANE5 arrival but failed to ensure the flight management system processed the new route. Consequently, the aircraft defaulted to vertical speed mode, causing the crew to descend below the 10,000-foot crossing restriction at AMOBE.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: EMB-170 flight crew reports becoming confused attempting to program the FMC to cross 30 NM west of the airport at 11,000 feet. The PBD fix was entered as 10 NM instead of 30 and not detected until prompted by ATC and the crossing restriction was missed.
summary: The Pilot Flying entered an incorrect 10-mile point distance instead of 30 miles in the FMS while descending into SYR, causing a discrepancy with ATC regarding the 11,000-foot crossing restriction. The crew corrected the error by increasing descent rate to meet the restriction 25 miles from the airport, attributing the mistake to high workload and MCDU interruptions.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier pilot at 7,000 FT on the FLL JINGL 4 RNAV Arrival received a TCAS RA descend advisory caused by VFR traffic westbound at 7,000 FT. During the evasion, MIA TRACON issued a descent to 6,000 FT. The reporter saw a light twin pass above to their left.
summary: During the JINGL 4 arrival between JAREM and BEPAC at 7,000 feet, the crew received a TCAS RA and executed a turning descent to avoid a head-on conflict with a VFR twin-engine aircraft. The reporter attributes the near-collision to the other pilot flying an odd altitude in Class E airspace without ATC contact, noting that TCAS and the intruder's transponder prevented a crash.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: On a night visual approach to Runway 3 at GEG, the crew was confused by the erratic localizer and glideslope indications which was attributed to the 'switching around' of the localizer.
summary: The crew experienced autopilot deviations during two visual approaches to runway 3 at GEG due to capturing the wrong localizer signal. The cause was identified as a ground switch of the localizer, which shares the same frequency but different identifier with the runway 21 approach.

synopsis: EMB-175 flight crew reported returning to their departure airport because of oil pressure and vibration problems with Engine 2.
summary: The flight crew experienced erratic engine oil pressure and vibration on Engine 2 during climb, prompting a return to the departure airport. They landed overweight after consulting the QRH and maintenance, deciding it was safest to return rather than continue the flight.

synopsis: Citation crew initially flew the wrong SID. ATC noticed the error and issued a new heading.
summary: The First Officer misread the handwritten clearance and briefed the wrong SID, causing the crew to execute an incorrect turn after departure from OKC. The error was corrected by ATC instructions, and the reporter attributed the incident to misreading handwriting, heat fatigue, and SOP deviations.

synopsis: CRJ200 Captain reports being given shortcuts on the JIIMS2 RNAV from over BRIGS then given a heading and queried if he is on the arrival. The arrival is designed to avoid a skydiving area. Another company flight with a similar flight number was also on the arrival.
summary: The flight crew and a female air traffic controller were involved during the RNAV arrival to Runway 26 at PHL. Conflicting clearances directing the aircraft over the Cross Keys Jump Zone caused confusion, which the crew attributed to potential controller error or similar call signs, though no traffic conflict occurred.

synopsis: A fatigued B747-400 crew was advised their departure time was being moved up and in the process several weight and balance reductions were received. The First Officer incorrectly entered the cargo weight in the FMS Aero Data zero fuel weight field causing V Speed errors near 30 KTS low. After landing a tail strike was discovered.
summary: An augmented crew of three on a departure from runway 27 experienced a tail strike after the First Officer entered cargo weight instead of Zero Fuel Weight into the Aero Data system. This input error generated incorrect takeoff speeds, resulting in a sluggish roll and high rotation force despite the crew's subsequent verification of the data.

synopsis: B757 Captain experienced a wind shift during approach, necessitating a go-around. The Tower wanted the crew to remain in the pattern at 2500 feet but a TOGA had already been initiated and the altitude was exceeded before thrust could be reduced.
summary: Pilots descending in a jet encountered a 17-knot tailwind and initiated a go-around, but conflicting ATC instructions and simultaneous MCP inputs caused a 500-foot altitude overshoot. The crew subsequently accepted a rushed approach with unadjusted speeds, resulting in a barely stable landing at 500 feet due to expectation bias and poor coordination.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: The non-flying pilot reported a near-miss while receiving traffic advisories from IND Approach.
summary: During an aerial survey at 4,700 feet MSL, a pilot reported a near midair collision with an opposing aircraft after Indianapolis Approach lost the pilot's beacon code due to a system fault. This technical failure, combined with controller lack of situational awareness, prevented traffic advisories and allowed the aircraft to pass within 100–200 feet.

synopsis: A pilot flying near Windham High Peak in Greene County New York, at 3,500 feet was approached by an elaborate UAV with a brilliant surface on top of an inverted bowl shaped container with long rectangular antennas protruding downward. The UAV approached, tracked, and flew around the reporter before speeding off toward the west with two other like shaped UAVs.
summary: A glider pilot and passenger encountered a fast-moving, radiant UAV approximately 25 yards away at 3,500 feet near Windham High Peak. The pilot aborted the flight and returned to the airport after the object maneuvered aggressively and two additional UAVs appeared from the clouds.

synopsis: C172 instructor pilot reported that after takeoff from the non-towered DKX airport he experienced an NMAC with an inbound aircraft.
summary: The pilot departed DKX runway 08 under IFR release and encountered an aircraft on localizer 26 at approximately 1800 MSL. The other pilot failed to announce position or report seeing the departing aircraft until it passed 200–300 feet below, prompting a traffic advisory from Knoxville Departure.

synopsis: GA pilot reported loss of power after takeoff so he returned to departure airport. After landing, power loss was reportedly traced to vapor lock.
summary: A pilot experienced engine sputtering and fuel pressure loss at 2,500 feet MSL shortly after departure due to a failed electric fuel pump switch and vapor lock from high temperatures. The pilot returned to the departure airport, was cleared to land on runway 15, and the issue was resolved after repairs.

synopsis: C210 pilot reported his engine quit on final from fuel starvation.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine failure on final approach due to fuel exhaustion caused by erroneous gauges and unmonitored fueling at the previous departure. The aircraft coasted off the runway, was pushed to the ramp, and later taxied under its own power for autopilot repairs.

synopsis: A Thatcher CX4 pilot diverted because of a strong fuel smell and determined the auxiliary tank was vented into the cockpit. After refueling, he ran off the runway in gusty conditions and damaged the aircraft.
summary: The pilot experienced fuel venting into the cockpit during climb and returned to land. On a subsequent takeoff attempt in gusty conditions, the aircraft ground looped off the runway into brush, damaging the right wheel, propeller, and cowling.

synopsis: TRACON could not perform an automated handoff of a departing aircraft to the ARTCC. The reason was a flight plan with the same call sign as the departure was an active flight already in the ARTCC system. Unbeknownst to the ARTCC Controller the ARTCC active flight plan was an arrival to the same airport as the departure which would not handoff. The TRACON Controller mistakenly told the ARTCC Controller the ARTCC active flight plan had already landed. The ARTCC Controller then removed the flight plan from the ARTCC system. This caused the ARTCC sector working the active arrival to lose data on this aircraft.
summary: A ZKC ARTCC controller and a TRACON controller experienced an automation handoff failure for Aircraft X due to a duplicate flight plan in the system. The TRACON controller incorrectly assumed the arrival had landed, but removing the plan while the departure was airborne caused an ARTCC disruption.

synopsis: TRACON Controller assigned a closed Runway for landing to a VFR aircraft. Tower Controller corrected the instructions and coordinated with the TRACON.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared a VFR inbound aircraft into Class B airspace for a closed Runway XX, forgetting the closure despite ACE-IDS alerts and shift briefings. The controller failed to complete a manual point-out to the arrival controller, who later redirected the aircraft to Runway YY after the pilot reported the airport in sight.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: VFR aircraft requested an altitude to drop parachute jumpers. Controller restricted the aircraft 1,000 feet below its requested altitude and advises there will be a delay for approval for jumpers due to traffic. VFR aircraft releases parachute jumpers anyway and advises Controller to move traffic away from the jump area.
summary: Aircraft X, conducting parachute jumps, ignored ATC instructions to wait for traffic clearance and proceeded to drop at 12,500 feet. The pilot blocked the frequency and engaged in a verbal exchange with the controller, resulting in an order to maintain radio silence.

synopsis: ATC assigned parallel runways to VFR arrivals. The aircraft assigned the Left runway mistakenly lined up to land on the Right runway. There was another aircraft on final approach to the right runway which took evasive action.
summary: A Local controller and two pilots were involved during the approach phase when Aircraft X landed on Runway XX Right instead of the cleared Runway XX Left, causing a 30-50 foot separation with Aircraft Y. The controller attributed the incident to the pilot proceeding on the wrong runway despite a correct readback and the controller's delayed visual scan.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Controllers reported a situation where aircraft could not land at their destination due to the unavailability of parking space. Contributing to the problem was poor communication signal.
summary: Air traffic controllers managed Aircraft X and Y at [airport] during solar flare-induced HF communication failures and a full parking situation. Aircraft Y held without clearance due to lack of space until controllers coordinated Aircraft X's departure to allow Y to land safely.

synopsis: B767-300 flight crew reported the Dispatcher may have overlooked an important planning factor when they were dispatched with an MEL for C Hyd Sys inoperative.
summary: The crew managed a Center Hydraulic system pressure loss caused by an MEL item, resulting in inoperative gear and flap extension. They continued to the destination with an amended release after advising dispatch that a potential diversion would require higher fuel reserves due to the inability to retract the landing gear.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Air Carrier pilot reports that a red light atop the windsock for Runway 23L at GSO aligns precisely with the left most VASI light for the same runway. This means that an on glide path indication is red (pink), white, red, red from the FAF to about 500 feet AGL, causing confusion.
summary: A pilot reported that a bright red light on a windsock near Runway 23L at GSO visually aligned with the VASI during the ILS approach from BRANT OM to 500 feet AGL. This caused the leftmost white VASI light to appear red, distorting the glide path indication, prompting a recommendation to relocate the windsock.

synopsis: EMB-175 flight crew got themselves into a low fuel situation due to un-forecasted weather and weight and balance issues on the ground.
summary: The flight crew experienced multiple weight and balance issues at a hot, high-altitude airport, leading to a minimum fuel situation caused by dispatch errors, inexperience, and ATC holding the aircraft high. The crew declared minimum fuel, executed a go-around due to an unstabilized approach, and landed safely with 2,100 pounds of fuel remaining.

synopsis: A DA-2000 climbing through FL220 developed a burning smell and ejecting smoke from a gasper which was then closed. Oxygen masks were donned, a diversion began and the checklists were completed. After landing no hot spots were seen by emergency personnel.
summary: Pilots and a flight attendant experienced smoke and a burning smell at 22,000 feet, likely originating from the cabin, forcing an emergency landing. The crew managed the descent with oxygen masks despite difficult communications, landed safely, and determined the aircraft was secure after fire department inspection.

synopsis: B737-800 First Officer experiences a late night ground conflict during taxi to the gate via Taxiways W and U on Tower frequency. A departing aircraft had been cleared to taxi via U and W on ground frequency and the two aircraft met at the intersection with the inbound crew yielding.
summary: The flight crew stopped short on taxiway W at night to avoid a potential conflict with another aircraft taxiing in the opposite direction. The reporter attributed the near-miss to the controller managing multiple frequencies and the use of a bi-directional taxiway, which prevented the crew from hearing the other aircraft's instructions.

synopsis: A B737-900 Crew reported four flight attendants were nauseous and dizzy at cruise. Sometime later all were well but during descent a passenger developed the symptoms then departed unassisted. Paramedics examined the flight attendants: one was removed, deadheaded home and admitted to a hospital for carbon monoxide poisoning.
summary: During cruise at FL350, flight attendants and a passenger in seat 12F experienced dizziness and nausea between rows 19 and 22 without detecting an odor. The flight continued to destination where the lead flight attendant was hospitalized with carbon monoxide poisoning, indicating an air quality issue.

synopsis: An A321 Flight Crew, holding short of Uniform on Bravo at the ILS critical hold bars, east bound, experiences a near collision with a B777 northbound on Uniform. Flashing lights by the A321 crew get the B777 stopped in time to avoid a collision.
summary: A pilot holding short of Taxiway Uniform at LAX observed a B777 crossing Runway 25R with insufficient wingtip clearance. The pilot used radio calls and flashing lights to stop the B777, preventing a potential collision, and recommended moving the hold line or designating the intersection as a hotspot.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Pilot on a night visual to SDF was issued a low altitude alert by Tower after descending rapidly from a high turning, descending base but intercepted the final at 900 feet AGL.
summary: The pilot flying a night visual approach to SDF accepted a tight base turn and remained high on the glideslope, triggering a low altitude alert. Despite the alert, the crew continued the approach and landed safely, though the pilot noted the situation should have resulted in a go-around.

synopsis: B747 pilot reported deviating from assigned track on his overwater flight under control of Tokyo Center when he encountered weather and Tokyo was slow to respond with a clearance to deviate.
summary: The flight crew at FL350 deviated left to avoid thunderstorms after CPDLC requests to Tokyo Center went unanswered. The crew attributed the delay in receiving deviation approvals to the system being too slow to meet urgent safety needs.

synopsis: An A319 flight crew reported deviating from cleared arrival into CLE when the FMS failed to load all the required waypoints.
summary: During descent into CLE on the CXR arrival, the flight crew deviated from the cleared route due to an FMS error omitting the LEBRN fix. ATC reassigned the clearance, and the crew manually programmed the missing fix to proceed safely, prompting a recommendation to update the FMS database and reinforce verification procedures.

synopsis: A DA2000 Maintenance Test pilot reports accepting an aircraft out of heavy maintenance and performing an extensive preflight before starting and taxiing out. After taxiing out and more checks, takeoff clearance is requested from the Tower. The Tower advises that the airspace is closed by the Center due to weather and the crew taxies back to the ramp. On post flight a yellow plastic ribbon is found hanging down and taped to the inside of the clamshell thrust reverser.
summary: A maintenance pilot conducting a Falcon 2000 maintenance flight discovered a 2-foot yellow plastic ribbon left inside the left thrust reverser by maintenance technicians after a ground run-up. The flight was grounded by Washington Center before departure, preventing the ribbon from trailing behind the engine during flight.

synopsis: A BE-400XP First Officer reported rejecting the takeoff when the right engine failed to produce calculated takeoff thrust.
summary: The pilot aborted takeoff when the right engine failed to reach 98.5% N1, rolling back to 97.9% during the roll. After notifying ATC and following checklists, the crew taxied back to parking and reported the issue to maintenance.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported the ground push back crew deviated from proper procedures and terminology during the push back maneuver.
summary: During pushback, the pilot reported a safety hazard caused by a ramp agent's insufficient training and refusal to use working headsets for communication. The tug driver disconnected the tow bar using unconfirmed hand signals while the parking brake was off, leading to a verbal dispute over proper phraseology and safety procedures.

synopsis: The flight crew of a B737 experienced a loss of oil quantity indication during takeoff. While preparing for a return to the field, they received a turn away from a TFR that may have been delayed due to their running of the checklist.
summary: During takeoff, the crew observed a rapid drop in left engine oil quantity to zero, prompting a return to the field. Task saturation while assessing the malfunction caused a delayed turn to avoid a TFR, but the aircraft landed safely with both engines running before shutting down the left engine on the ground.

synopsis: An A320 First Officer reports being cleared for a night visual approach to Runway 12L at STL with the Captain flying. The Captain begins descending below the FAF altitude well outside of it and is queried by the First Officer. The descent is continued until the Tower asks the flight to check their altitude and a GPWS warning is annunciated. The crew climbs to 3,000 feet and is still outside the FAF so a second visual approach is attempted with the same results. This time the missed approach is completed and vectors are received to the ILS.
summary: During a night visual approach, the pilot flying descended below safe altitude after misidentifying the airport, triggering a GPWS terrain warning and two go-arounds. The crew eventually landed normally after re-engaging the autopilot and following the ILS, attributing the incident to the pilot's disorientation and failure to execute a full go-around initially.

synopsis: An A319 Captain returned to the departure airport after a significant vibration developed which seemed to emanate from the tail area. The aircraft had a history of these vibrations.
summary: During climb through 12,000 feet, the crew experienced a growing tail vibration unrelated to engines, which intensified despite speed and load changes. Maintenance advised returning to PHX due to the aircraft's history, resulting in a precautionary landing.

synopsis: B777 First Officer experienced compressor stalls climbing through FL230 that resulted in high EGT and vibration, along with smoke in the cockpit. The reporter was most concerned with the difficulty encountered donning the separate oxygen mask and smoke goggles. The engine was shut down and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: During climb through FL230, the crew experienced left engine compressor stalls and smoke, requiring oxygen masks and goggles. The reporter states the separate mask and goggle setup was awkward and time-consuming, creating a significant distraction from the emergency that a one-piece system would have avoided.

synopsis: A CE680 at FL410 begins a shallow descent which then causes the auto pilot to disengage. The descent steepens and the crew is initially unable to arrest the descent. Control is regained at FL390 after completing memory items and QRH procedures. Secondary trim is selected and the diversion is flown without further difficulty.
summary: While cruising at FL410, the crew experienced an autopilot failure causing an uncommanded descent to 40,600 feet. After completing memory items and QRH procedures, they regained control, leveled at FL390, and diverted to ZZZ for an uneventful remainder of the flight.

synopsis: Air cargo crew executed two go-arounds at IAH due to windshear system activation with an approaching thunderstorm and then diverted.
summary: The crew encountered windshear twice during ILS approaches at IAH, forcing escape maneuvers that required turning left toward an RJ to avoid severe weather and hail. Despite controller instructions to fly runway heading, the crew maintained visual separation, and later overshot a 3,000-foot clearance to 3,900 feet before descending.

synopsis: A First Officer reported a runway incursion at PSP due in part to an incomplete understanding of the applicable construction NOTAM.
summary: Pilots taxiing for departure at PSP crossed non-standard hold short lines near a closed runway while looking for tower frequency. Ground control allowed them to proceed from that position due to no arriving traffic, though the crew noted the lines were not repainted despite other runway markings being updated.

synopsis: The pilot reported that the marshaller had to panic stop the pushback because of a baggage cart tug driving directly behind the aircraft.
summary: During pushback, a marshaller stopped the aircraft after a baggage cart tug entered the taxiway behind it, causing passengers to be thrown. The pilot reports frequent close calls in the concourse alleyway where tug drivers appear to rely on aircrew to stop for them.

synopsis: CRJ-200 reports missing a crossing restriction at WDBRY on the MUSCL2 arrival to MSP.
summary: During the MUSCL2 RNAV arrival to MSP, the First Officer descended below the 10,000-foot restriction at WDBRY and the aircraft entered an incorrect lateral mode, causing a deviation. The reporter attributed these errors to low familiarity with "descend via" procedures, distraction from a traffic hold, and initiating an early shallow descent.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) reported their aircraft ended up off the center line and in a ditch during an aircraft taxi after complying with a request from Ground Control to expedite a runway crossing.
summary: Two technicians taxied an aircraft from a gate to a hangar when the pilot in the right seat lost situational awareness while monitoring an inbound aircraft. The aircraft veered off the centerline into a ditch, requiring the crew to exit via the R-1 door after notifying Ground Control.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician recommended his Air Carrier fix the malfunctions with their IPAD/Digital communication software program that cleared a 'System-2 Regulator' fault discrepancy instead of deferring the Logbook item.
summary: A maintenance technician deferred a 'Sys 2 Reg' fault on an aircraft using an iPad, but the MEL was inadvertently cleared four days later due to a suspected digital communication software malfunction. The technician reported the error to management and recommended fixing the iPad software to prevent recurrence.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: General aviation pilot reports contacting a power pole guy wire with his right wingtip while attempting to taxi around a tractor trailer rig parked on the ramp. The pole is just off Aviation Way at an access road to the ramp. The coordinates are 39 24' 56' N 77 22' 49.37' W.
summary: While taxiing to the avionics shop at Frederick, the pilot's right wing tip struck a power line stabilization cable while maneuvering around a parked tractor trailer. The pilot attributed the incident to fixation on the vehicle and noted the cable had been hit previously, suggesting its relocation.

synopsis: The pilot of an amphibian experimental aircraft identified a potential landing gear issue prior to landing. During the landing rollout, one main landing gear collapsed.
summary: The pilot landed a hull-type amphibian with the left gear leg unsecured, which collapsed during taxi due to a failed bracket unable to support the aircraft's weight. The runway was closed for 10 minutes while the pilot and spectators jacked the hull to manually lock the gear, allowing the aircraft to taxi off.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Stinson pilot reports being cut off on short final by a C208 jump plane. Both pilots were communicating on the CTAF. The Stinson pilot went around.
summary: The pilot reported a near-midair conflict with a Cessna Caravan during the traffic pattern at an uncontrolled airport. The Caravan pilot ignored right-of-way procedures by cutting in front on short final, forcing the reporter to execute a go-around.

synopsis: Pilots of a Beechcraft King Air experience an oil pressure and temperature issue, resulting in an inflight shutdown.
summary: The crew experienced low right engine oil pressure and high temperature while climbing to 4,000 feet. They reduced power, executed an emergency shutdown, and landed safely before evacuating the aircraft with fire and rescue assistance.

synopsis: C310 pilot experienced loss of power in the right engine after climbing through rain showers. Power returned to normal during descent and was subsequently attributed to water contamination of the fuel due to faulty tank gaskets.
summary: The pilot experienced a right engine power loss on a JPI-760 powered aircraft while climbing to 10,500 feet in rain. A mechanic later determined water infiltration into the fuel tanks caused the issue, recommending gasket replacement.

synopsis: DC-3 flight crew experienced right engine vibration shortly after the chip detector light had illuminated. Crew secured the engine and diverted without further incident.
summary: The pilot reported a right engine chip detector light and abnormal vibration three miles past the coast, leading to an engine caged and feathered return. The aircraft landed without flaps on short final, was towed to the ramp, and met by a fire truck.

synopsis: The pilot of a PC12 experience a runaway rudder trim condition on climb out.
summary: The pilot experienced a flight control issue during climb out, notified ATC, and returned to the departure airport. The aircraft landed without further incidence.

aircraft: M-20 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: M20 pilot reported an upset from a building storm that resulted in a 50 degree bank and 1,500 FPM rate of descent. Aircraft control was recovered after a loss of 1,000 feet.
summary: The crew encountered an unforecast downdraft while cruising at 6,000 feet in IMC, causing a 1,500 FPM dive and 50-degree bank that disengaged the autopilot. They recovered nearly 1,000 feet below altitude, advised ATC of the deviation, and filed a PIREP.

synopsis: Private pilot observing from the ground, reports a NMAC between an R44 helicopter and a drone during a visual approach to Runway 13 or 14 at STP. The drone was hovering near the base leg of the VFR traffic pattern and 100 feet above the helicopter.
summary: A pilot on the ground near Battle Creek Park observed a drone hovering on the VFR base leg approach to Runways 13 and 14 at STP. The drone was at the same altitude as an operating R44 helicopter, creating a potential collision hazard during the approach.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reports checking in with MMU Tower 8 NM out, according to his GPS, then told to ident. The Tower indicates that he is 5 NM south and the reporter believes that there may be a bad GPS signal in this area.
summary: A VFR pilot approaching Morristown Municipal reported a GPS discrepancy showing 8 miles out at 1,500 feet, while ATC placed the aircraft 5 miles south, outside the Class D airspace. The pilot attributed the error to a potentially misleading GPS signal and requested documentation to warn other pilots.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported an NMAC in the pattern at FRG when he apparently misidentified the aircraft he was expected to follow.
summary: The pilot on right downwind for Runway 19 turned to right base while descending, discovering a conflicting aircraft 500 feet ahead. The tower instructed an immediate left turn and a 180-degree maneuver to rejoin the correct landing sequence behind the intended traffic.

synopsis: Mooney M20 pilot reported the landing gear would not extend electrically or manually, and the aircraft was landed gear up.
summary: The sole pilot experienced electrical landing gear failure and a jammed manual crank during landing. After a chase ship confirmed the gear was up, the pilot shut down the engine at 300 feet AGL and landed gear-up with no injuries or damage.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Descending on the BDEGA ONE STAR into KSFO, corporate jet flight crew received clearance to Runway 28L which had not been programmed in the FMS. After aircraft turned toward routing for Runway 28R, ATC issued vectors and crew reprogrammed the FMS. Ongoing problems associated with changes to expected routing on KSFO STARS were noted by the reporter.
summary: The flight crew descended via the BDEGA ONE STAR to 11,000 feet at KSFO but failed to update the FMS for the cleared Runway 28L, causing the aircraft to track toward the previously loaded Runway 28R. Norcal Approach issued a heading correction after querying the crew, who then updated the FMS and landed safely.

synopsis: Piper Warrior pilot reported returning to departure airport after the engine began running rough. The runway was wet and the aircraft slid off the end, striking a REIL.
summary: During initial climb, a pilot experienced engine power loss due to cracked spark plugs, necessitating a return landing on a wet runway. The aircraft slid off the departure end, striking a REIL and sustaining minor damage before stopping in a field.

synopsis: SA227 Captain reported shutting down right engine in flight when he experienced high EGT indications.
summary: The Captain and First Officer managed a No.2 engine failure at FL190 and a subsequent nose gear indicator light failure during approach to ZZZ. They executed a single-engine go-around, verified gear status via warning horn and tower confirmation, and landed safely with no aircraft damage.

synopsis: PA-34 Instructor Pilot reported his student experienced loss of directional control and even with the Instructor's efforts the aircraft left the taxiway and struck an airport sign. Instructor stated he felt the issue was with a mechanical failure rather than pilot technique.
summary: During taxi after landing, a student pilot and instructor lost directional control due to a suspected braking and steering hydraulic failure. The aircraft struck a taxiway sign, damaging the left propeller and wing fuel tank, causing a minor fuel leak with no injuries.

synopsis: General Aviation pilot reported an NMAC with another light aircraft in the pattern.
summary: The pilot of a Grumman AA5A with engine issues entered the traffic pattern and was instructed by Tower to maintain visual separation from a Cessna. Although the Cessna initially reported visual contact, it later stated the Grumman flew off its nose, leading Ground Control to cite the pilot for a deviation by overflying the Cessna.

synopsis: Aircraft was deviating for weather from facility A airspace into another Facility B airspace. Facility B controllers delegated some of their airspace to Facility A to accommodate weather deviations. This caused Facility A to work airplanes 40 to 60 miles in Facility B airspace. Facility B Supervisor overrode their controllers and required Facility A to make individual Point Outs. Facility B declines to take handoffs and work these aircraft. This increases facility A's workload greatly. These facilities are in different countries further complicating a possible solution.
summary: Air traffic controllers reported that an adjacent facility's refusal to accept handoffs for aircraft deviating 40 to 60 miles into their airspace due to weather created a coordination nightmare. The reporter attributes the resulting workload and separation risks to the lack of defined weather airways and the adjacent facility's unwillingness to manage aircraft within their own sector.

synopsis: Aircraft landed with left main gear retracted. This was a known malfunction.
summary: The sole pilot of Aircraft X reported a gear malfunction shortly after VFR take-off, with the pilot-side gear retracted and co-pilot gear down. The aircraft performed a low approach, circled for fire brigade arrival, and landed disabled at the runway intersection with no injuries.

synopsis: A320 Captain reported noticing slight vibration after takeoff, and later in the flight received the ECAM message L/G SYS DISAGREE. Approach and landing were normal.
summary: Pilots reported a loud noise and rumbling after departure, suspecting an open access panel, and lost VHF/ACARS communications en route. Near destination, they observed four amber crosses on the nose gear wheel page, landed with normal gear extension, and received an L/G SYS DISAGREE message at shutdown.

synopsis: Test button activated the upper cargo deck Halon fire suppression system during preflight for a Combi modified aircraft, Crew evacuated the aircraft.
