summary: During preflight on a Combi aircraft, the upper deck cargo fire suppression system discharged two 125lb Halon bottles, filling the forward vestibule with vapor. The reporter and forward crew evacuated to avoid Halon exposure while passengers remained on board, though no passengers were affected.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported airspeed indicator malfunction on approach. A go around was executed, and flaps failed to retract. Flight diverted to a nearby airport with a longer runway.
summary: During approach to Runway XY, the crew encountered an airspeed anomaly with conflicting barberpole and Alpha warning indications, prompting a go-around. Flaps subsequently stalled at 9 degrees, leading to a diversion and uneventful landing at an alternate airport after the airspeed indications normalized.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew experienced low oil pressure on the number one engine during climb to FL350. Once level the light extinguished and returned an hour later. After discussions with Dispatch the engine was shut down and the flight diverted to a suitable airport. Maintenance found the oil tank cap unsecured.
summary: The flight crew experienced intermittent amber oil pressure warnings and a 3-quart oil loss on Engine 1 while climbing to FL350, prompting a shutdown and diversion to ZZZ. Maintenance determined the cause was an unsecured oil cap, highlighting the need for greater mindfulness during maintenance tasks.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant identified during boarding that young children were incorrectly issued exit row seats. After requesting that they were reseated, Flight Attendant was informed that Customer Service was too busy to confirm seat positions during the boarding process.
summary: A flight deck crew member requested a customer service agent to reseat a mother and three children from an emergency exit row due to a FAR 121.585 violation. The agent admitted the boarding pass reader beeped but claimed insufficient time to address the seating violation.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Maintenance Technician lost control of an aircraft following an expedited taxi across a runway with approaching landing traffic.
summary: The pilot lost control of the aircraft while attempting to expedite a runway crossing after receiving clearance from the tower to avoid an approaching landing aircraft. The aircraft failed to respond to right turn inputs and ended up on a grassed area due to the urgent need to clear the runway.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot on base observed another aircraft turn in front of him before the Tower personnel noticed the conflict. The pilot is concerned about the attitude of the Contract Tower personnel.
summary: A pilot on a right base leg observed another aircraft turn left base inside their position without tower clearance, nearly causing a mid-air collision. The tower only intervened after the intruder was on final, prompting the pilot to criticize the private contract tower's professionalism and oversight.

synopsis: BE350 Captain reports getting 60 feet low prior to the FAF at HRL with the autopilot flying, which results in a low altitude alert from the Tower. The autopilot corrects back to 1,400 feet and the approach is continued to landing.
summary: During an ILS 17R approach into HRL, the autopilot in VNAV mode descended slightly below the 1,400-foot restriction to approximately 1,340 feet, triggering a low-level alert. The system automatically corrected the altitude, and the crew completed a visual approach to Runway 17L without further incident.

synopsis: The pilot of an Ercoupe 415 experienced a loss of engine power after takeoff. He was able to perform a landing on a closed runway with intermittent engine power available.
summary: The pilot experienced intermittent engine power loss between 300 and 400 feet AGL during takeoff on runway 13R, likely due to carburetor icing. After declaring an emergency and maneuvering to maintain control, the pilot successfully executed a forced landing on runway 31R and taxied to the hangar.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: MD80 flight crew experiences a failure of the Captain's PFD and heading failure. The crew elects to divert to a suitable airport.
summary: During cruise, the Captain's PFD and AI failed, causing autopilot disconnect and total navigation loss on that side. The First Officer took control, used the whiskey compass to restore heading, and diverted to a safe landing due to an unavoidable mechanical failure.

synopsis: During a VOR Approach to Runway 14 at RAP, a small jet flight crew mistakes RCA for RAP and lands there on Runway 13.
summary: The flight crew mistakenly landed at RCA Air Force Base instead of RAP Airport after mistaking Runway 13 for Runway 14 during a visual approach. The error resulted from confirmation bias, a late descent, and the similar alignment of the two runways in improving weather conditions.

synopsis: Air Carrier First Officer laments the inability of his aircraft's cooling system to function on very hot days and the lack of properly functioning ground equipment that will take its place. On this day, two different aircraft experience Tail Temp High annunciations requiring the APU to be shut down and ground equipment that cannot handle the task on the ground.
summary: A fatigued crew experienced repeated Tail Temp High annunciations and ground power failures at an outstation lacking cooling equipment, causing extreme cabin heat and a passenger heat stroke. The crew returned to LAS after a second failure and declined further duty, attributing the events to equipment deficiencies and maintenance issues.

synopsis: A Quad City Challenger Rotax Engine wooden propeller departed the aircraft inflight. The aircraft landed safely on a nearby road. The wooden propeller has not been re-torqued after being flown several months earlier from a high humidity area to a dry climate.
summary: During a pleasure flight, the pilot reported that propeller bolts failed, causing the propeller to depart the aircraft. The pilot subsequently landed on a private road with no damage to the airplane or ground property.

synopsis: An aircraft on a VFR Flight Plan cancelled flight following and advised Center they were turning around for weather to land. The ARTCC controllers amended the flight plan to route the aircraft flight plan back to its departure airport. The destination Tower did not notice the revision or the software did not process the revision to the destination Tower. They correctly assumed the aircraft was overdue. An ALNOT was issued and search procedures for the aircraft were initiated. ARTCC Supervisors and controllers who worked the aircraft at the ARTCC researched sector recordings and radar display replays. They discovered the aircraft had cancelled on the ARTCC frequency and returned to an airport other than its original departure airport.
summary: A VFR pilot flying Aircraft X at 6,500 feet canceled flight following due to low weather and returned to the departure airport, but an automation failure prevented the flight plan from being removed downstream. This caused a three-hour overdue alert and search effort until the original controller confirmed the cancellation via radar replay and the aircraft was located safely on the ground.

synopsis: A80 Departure Controller reported that two aircraft came off on different departures that were a conflict of each other. One was on a RNAV departure and the other was assigned a heading, but inside of the RNAV departure. Reporter wants some type of standardization to let the Departure Controller know if the aircraft is on a RNAV departure or a heading.
summary: Departure controllers and two pilots experienced a potential conflict when Aircraft Y was vectored inside Aircraft X's RNAV path due to unclear transition phraseology. The controller assumed Aircraft Y remained on the SID, resulting in a 2-mile separation at 8,000 feet before corrective turns were issued.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain experiences a math error by his First Officer during approach speed calculations. The weight used is 20,000 pounds too light and the slow approach speed that results is detected by the feel of the aircraft.
summary: The First Officer entered an incorrect, manually calculated weight into the FMC of a Boeing 737-800 prior to descent, resulting in erroneous flap speeds. The Captain detected the error on final approach, flew faster to compensate, and executed a normal landing.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports being cleared to line up and wait on Runway 25L at LAS, then cleared for takeoff with the previous departure in sight. The previous aircraft appears to rotate into the setting sun and the reporter begins his takeoff. The previous aircraft rejects and the Tower calls for the reporter to reject, which is accomplished at low speed.
summary: The flight crew rejected takeoff on runway 25L at 70 KIAS after Tower cleared them while a preceding aircraft was still rolling, causing a high-speed rejection ahead. Low sun angle obscured the preceding aircraft's rotation, leading to the clearance error and a required 25-minute brake cooling delay.

synopsis: An air carrier crew manually loaded the FMS with a company non-standard route. Enroute ATC notified them about a track deviation because KM360 was not in the database. The crew did not verify the route against the clearance.
summary: The crew of an aircraft departing MEM discovered waypoint KM360 was missing from the FMC because it was not in the database and required manual entry. The error occurred because pilots failed to verify the route page against the filed clearance after activation, though ATC issued a direct to VXV.

synopsis: A B767 returned to the departure airport after the business class flight attendants became light headed. Coach flight attendants were unaffected. Forty four pounds of dry ice were in the forward cargo hold.
summary: Flight attendants in the forward galley experienced dizziness and breathing difficulties, likely caused by dry ice in the forward cargo compartment. The crew descended to FL240 and used portable oxygen, allowing symptoms to resolve so the flight could continue to the destination.

synopsis: A Captain discovered during preflight that his company issued iPad's Pilot Mobile APP had signed his flight's release before he had examined the flight plan. Upon further examination, the flight plan and release for his flight that day was for that flight two days prior with his information.
summary: The Captain discovered the Pilot Mobile App automatically signed off a flight plan for a future date without input from the crew or dispatch. The error was identified before departure, the correct plan was manually signed in Sabre, and the flight departed without incident.

synopsis: A B737NG with LNAV/VNAV anomalies was cleared for an ILS following a storm but the ILS was inoperative. The crew continued on the LOC but executed a go-around because of nearby terrain in night IMC. The aircraft autoflight returned to normal so a RNAV was flown to the opposite runway.
summary: The flight crew experienced VNAV and LNAV failures during descent, leading to an unbriefed localizer clearance to runway 6L. They executed a missed approach due to discomfort with the procedure and system issues, then successfully landed on an RNAV approach after recovering from an unintended TOGA mode.

synopsis: During climb a B757 forward galley oven over heated and caught fire. Food from a previous flight caused the fire which subsequently damaged the oven and required a Halon fire extinguisher to contain.
summary: During climb through 28,000 feet, a galley fire in the forward oven caused smoke and burning smells, prompting the crew to return to airport ZZZ for an overweight precautionary landing. The fire was extinguished by a flight attendant, and the cause was attributed to old food in the oven or a possible electrical short.

aircraft: Medium Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: An aircraft on a visual approach circling to land ASE Runway 33 in gusty conditions and high on approach developed an excessive rate of descent which triggered the EGPWS TERRAIN PULL UP alert. A go-around was executed followed by a second successful visual circle to land Runway 33.
summary: The pilot descended for a visual approach to runway 33 at Aspen and triggered a terrain GPWS warning near the RAFTR fix due to a high descent rate. The crew executed a missed approach, climbed away from the terrain, and successfully completed a second approach and landing.

synopsis: After being cleared to 11000 feet, an EMB145 First Officer is instructed to level at 7,000 feet for traffic passing 6500 feet. As the aircraft leveled at 7,000 feet on autopilot the TCAS called for a descent. The autopilot was disengaged and a descent initiated. The intruder was sighted and passed 500 feet overhead as the reporter's aircraft descended through 6,500 feet.
summary: During an IMC climb out of EWR, the crew received a TCAS Resolution Advisory to descend after ATC restricted their climb to 7000 ft for traffic. The pilots manually overrode the autopilot to execute the descent, avoiding a single-engine aircraft that overflew them by approximately 500 ft with no lateral separation.

synopsis: CRJ900 flight crew reported heading syncing with current heading when the autopilot heading knob is turned initially. The crew disengaged the autopilot to hand fly and airspeed is allowed to decrease to stick shaker.
summary: During a descent through clouds, the Captain manually maneuvered after the heading bug synced to the current heading, causing a momentary stick shaker activation at 150 KTS due to speed bleed-off. The aircraft recovered immediately with power application, and the recurring heading sync issue was subsequently MEL'd.

synopsis: The crew reported that the 9G net was not properly secured before block out on this MD-11 freighter.
summary: The pilot reported that the load team failed to secure the 9G cargo net before sealing the smoke curtain during pre-flight. This oversight, compounded by an inaccessible Directional Gyro and time pressure, created potential for aircraft damage or injury, though no incident occurred.

aircraft: Gulfstream Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A flight crew reported that their aircraft was struck by an eagle during the takeoff roll. The takeoff was successfully rejected and the aircraft returned to the hangar for damage assessment.
summary: The flight crew aborted takeoff on runway 14 at KSTP after a bald eagle struck the nose gear, left wing root, and engine cowl at 90 knots. The aircraft was safely stopped and cleared the runway, allowing maintenance to remove bird remains before the crew departed on a replacement aircraft.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: MD80 Captain reports rejecting a takeoff at 120 knots when the aircraft begins to rotate on its own. The yoke was full forward with the pitch rate increasing when the Captain assumed control and initiated the reject. Left elevator was found jammed in the full up position by Maintenance.
summary: During takeoff roll, the First Officer experienced uncommanded nose-up pitch unresponsive to forward yoke pressure, prompting an aborted takeoff. Mechanics later confirmed the left elevator was stuck in the up position, requiring a tow to the gate.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cirrus SR22 failed to reinstall both fuel caps after self-serve fueling.
summary: A single-engine IFR pilot forgot to replace fuel caps after self-service refueling at ZZZ, departing with both caps missing. Air Traffic Control advised an immediate return to ZZZ1 after discovering a cap on the ground; the pilot landed safely with 49.6 gallons remaining, having lost approximately 3 gallons during the flight.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cirrus SR20 experienced an engine power loss during go-around for unknown reasons.
summary: The pilot experienced a power failure and oil light warning after an approved go-around on Runway XX. This forced an immediate landing on Runway XY following notification to the tower.

synopsis: CE500 Captain reported arriving at CRG to find the only instrument runway NOTAMed closed. Fortunately, a visual approach was possible and accomplished. The NOTAM for runway light repairs had been issued after the flight had departed for CRG.
summary: A Medevac crew carrying a surgical team and organ requested an RNAV approach to CRG but found runway 14/32 closed due to light maintenance. They successfully executed a visual approach to runway 5 after spotting the airport through a cloud hole, noting that delayed NOTAM dissemination nearly forced an unplanned diversion.

synopsis: After loss of forward display panel and then all communications, pilot used hand-held phone to communicate with ATC/Tower and diverts his Piper PA32-301R. With no indicator lights, no Mode C, landed after performing fly-by to confirm landing gears down. Battery terminals found to be significantly corroded and not secured correctly. Previous Annual Inspection found to be deficient.
summary: The pilot experienced avionics and comms failure during IFR flight due to corroded battery terminals and improper alternator grounding. A mechanic later found the alternator was incorrectly installed with non-OEM wiring and the #1 cylinder used connecting rod nuts during the prior annual inspection.

synopsis: A pilot driving between Garber, OK and Enid, OK at night noticed a turbine windfarm with numerous unlit turbines in excess of 200 FT.
summary: A pilot driving near WDG observed over 20 unlit 400-foot windmills at night. Flight Safety stated only the owner could report the failure, and no NOTAM was issued despite the lights reportedly never working.

synopsis: The pilot of a Mooney M20 misconfigured the aircraft's audio panel and was not transmitting location information while entering a CTAF traffic pattern being utilized by firefighting aircraft.
summary: A pilot on a visual approach with fire tankers failed to switch transmitters on the audio panel, resulting in a close pass with a tanker. The pilot realized the error after the tanker radioed that the Mooney was silent and resolved to confirm radio switching more diligently.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 185 utilized accumulated time flown on several legs over a 30 day period to track available fuel, only to run out of fuel approximately 18 minutes short of his destination.
summary: The pilot ran out of fuel 52 minutes into a return flight and landed on a highway without injury or damage. The incident resulted from poor judgment and failure to account for increased fuel consumption during numerous short takeoffs over the preceding 30 days.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: The pilot of a small aircraft radioed immediate assistance on behalf of another pilot whose airplane was experiencing engine problems. The airplane was able to land safely.
summary: The pilot led a Cessna 150 on a 200 NM flight at 5,500 feet MSL when the follower experienced a total power loss, suspected to be a carburetor issue. The leader declared an emergency, obtained radar coverage, and the Cessna 150 executed a safe dead-stick landing at a nearby airport.

synopsis: The pilot of a Piper PA-32 experienced loss of braking system on landing rollout, resulting in a runway excursion and contact with a fence.
summary: The pilot reported that upon landing, the right brake pedal went to the floor while the left remained firm, causing the aircraft to swerve off the runway and strike a barbwire fence. The incident resulted in dents to both wing leading edges, though the pilot noted the brakes had functioned normally on previous flights.

synopsis: A pilot with sophisticated navigational equipment was surprised to be advised of a Temporary Flight Restriction (TFR) by ATC. For unknown reasons, it was not depicted on his primary GPS/Multifunction display.
summary: A pilot flying VFR at 8,500 feet reported that specific Temporary Flight Restrictions appeared on their iPad FlyQ software but were missing from the Garmin GTN750, despite the system indicating a recent data update. The pilot navigated around the TFRs using the iPad, and the local FSDO could not explain the discrepancy.

synopsis: S46 and ZSE Controllers reported confusion with similar call signs that led to a loss of separation.
summary: An air traffic controller issued incorrect vectors to Aircraft Y due to similar-sounding call signs with Aircraft X, causing a 2.8-mile separation loss in Seattle approach airspace. The controller realized the error when Aircraft Y did not follow instructions, corrected the situation, and attributed the incident to call sign confusion and missed readbacks.

synopsis: ZDC Controller reported of an aircraft that transited in RVSM airspace, but was not qualified to be in that airspace. Controller reported that there was a loss of separation due to the aircraft not being RVSM equipped. Controller thought someone upstream should have verified if the aircraft was RVSM qualified.
summary: An air traffic controller in the TYI sector accepted a handoff for Aircraft X, which was incorrectly assumed to be RVSM capable despite being a co-related primary target. The aircraft transited Class A airspace without conflict, but the controller later learned it was ineligible for RVSM operations due to equipment limitations.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reports a drone at 800 feet AGL during approach to Runway 4R at BOS. The drone was 200 to 400 feet below and to the right of the B737 and no evasive action was necessary.
summary: A First Officer on a visual approach to BOS Runway 04R at 800 feet spotted a DJI Phantom drone 200-400 feet below. Although no avoidance maneuver was required, the sighting distracted the crew during a critical flight phase, prompting an alert to Tower and subsequent reporting to the Supervisor.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported becoming confused by similar sounding call signs during approach to ATL and mistakenly accepted a descent clearance meant for another aircraft.
summary: Pilots on a STAR arrival to Atlanta descended from 12,000 ft to 3,000 ft after receiving a clearance intended for another aircraft with a similar call sign. The descent was halted at 5,000 ft after ATC queried the aircraft, attributing the error to frequency congestion and the lack of a similar-sounding call sign warning.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports retrieving ATIS indicating landing Runway 22L at EWR. Upon check in with N90 the ILS 22L is assigned. Checking in with EWR Tower the runway assignment is 22R and the controller indicates that N90 should have assigned Runway 22R as Runway 22L is closed. The ATIS is rechecked after landing and is stating 22R is the landing runway.
summary: The crew briefed for Runway 22L at EWR based on an outdated ATIS, but the Tower cleared them for a side-step to 22R after discovering 22L was closed. The aircraft landed safely on 22R, and the crew later confirmed the ATIS had listed 22L as closed during their vectoring.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported receiving three messages for inaccurate weights with the push back crew standing by for push. After the weights were entered into the FMC, the Captain stated to the tug driver 'Brakes are released, cleared to push'. No response was received, but the aircraft started to move. Further attempts at communication were unsuccessful then the aircraft stopped. A wing walker came on the intercom and informed the flight crew that no one was in the tug when the aircraft started to move.
summary: The flight crew halted a pushback after receiving no verbal response from the push crew, despite releasing brakes and confirming clearance. A wing walker later reported via headset that the tug was unoccupied, causing the aircraft to stop.

synopsis: Air carrier ground employee reported a dangerous condition existed with a cargo door propped open with a broom handle because of an inoperative door counter-balance mechanism.
summary: A mechanic reported that a cargo door counter-balance was inoperative and deferred, requiring a makeshift wooden rod (a broken broom handle) to support the door. This created a risk of the door dropping and injuring an employee during operations.

synopsis: A319 First Officer reported trailing edge flaps jammed and locked out at Flaps 1 position.
summary: During approach, the pilot requested flaps 2, but they jammed and locked at flaps 1. The pilot discontinued the approach, climbed to 10,000 feet, held at the VOR, completed the QRH procedure, and landed without incident.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported declaring minimum fuel when weather and reroutes increased his fuel burn. Reporter also cited increased workload from yaw damper failure that required hand flying the aircraft.
summary: The flight crew experienced a yaw damper malfunction requiring manual flight and multiple weather reroutes that depleted fuel to 1,600 lbs. A lost localizer signal during final approach triggered a go-around and min fuel declaration, but the crew landed safely after a visual approach.

synopsis: B767-300ER Captain reported he was notified by oversight authorities at his European destination that an electric wheelchair loaded in the bulk pit was not properly secured and the power was still connected and on.
summary: Ground personnel loaded an unsecured, powered electric wheelchair with connected batteries into the aircraft's bulk pit before departure. The Federal Aviation Office notified the crew upon arrival, prompting a recommendation for employee verification to prevent potential onboard fires.

synopsis: Captain describes his efforts to explain to a Maintenance Controller and the Assistant Chief Pilot why their EMB-505 (Phenom 300) aircraft was not airworthy after he discovered the Emergency Brake accumulator had bled down to zero overnight. ACP continued to pressure pilot to accept aircraft as is, even after being informed the MEL language indicates a 'No Dispatch condition'. Pilot refused. Aircraft does not have Thrust Reversers.
summary: A pilot discovered zero Emergency Brake accumulator pressure on an EMB-505 Phenom 300 during preflight, conflicting with MEL "NO DISPATCH" guidance. Despite maintenance and management pressure to fly, the pilot filed an Aircraft On Ground squawk due to the unexplained pressure loss and lack of documented tolerance.

synopsis: B747 Captain reported receiving a second oceanic crossing clearance from CZQX via CPDLC after already accepting a first clearance and entering NAT Z. Gander indicated there had been ACARS difficulties and they had no idea where the second clearance came from. The second clearance had a lower clearance number but the same route at a higher altitude.
summary: The flight crew received a conflicting ACARS clearance for FL360 from Gander ATC while en route oceanic, despite a prior denial of a climb request due to traffic. The crew rejected the erroneous clearance, verified the situation via SATCOM, and maintained FL350 after ATC confirmed the second message was a system glitch.

synopsis: During taxi in, after the completion of a test flight, the right engine is shut down using the fire switch. At the gate the First Officer is instructed to shut down the left engine using its fire switch, which was accomplished. A Maintenance Technician that was on the ground during the shutdown stated that the shutdown sounded abnormal. It was then noted that the left engine EGT had latched an overtemp.
summary: During post-test flight taxi and shutdown, the First Officer pulled the left engine fire switch, resulting in an EGT overtemp latch. The Captain suspects the cause was the First Officer resetting the fire switch before turning off the fuel switch, a deviation from the checklist.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reports using an infrared thermometer to measure food temperatures brought on board by catering. All of the food is in the high seventies or low eighties and the aircraft is not equipped with chillers.
summary: Cabin crew measured food and cart temperatures on an aircraft lacking refrigeration, finding readings between 77.6°F and 83.3°F within the FDA danger zone. A supervisor subsequently purchased replacement meals for first class and removed the unsafe food to prevent serving items stored over two hours at unsafe temperatures.

synopsis: After APU start during preflight, the flight attendants and passengers detected a strong musky, wet sock odor making them nauseous. The Captain attributed the odor to dirty air filters and so ignored them. Historically, APU oil reservoir over service has been a known cause.
summary: Crew and passengers experienced strong odors and nausea after APU start, which the captain attributed to filters or potential hydraulic fluid. Maintenance was not called due to on-time pressure, despite crew concerns that the issue required inspection.

synopsis: EMB175 Flight Attendant reported being informed by the Customer Service Representative as the main cabin door is closed, that a passenger they boarded is intoxicated but shouldn't pose a problem. He did not, but the passenger seated next to the possibly intoxicated passenger informed the Flight Attendant during deplaning that the possible intoxicated passenger urinated in his seat during landing.
summary: A flight attendant reported that a gate agent warned of a potentially intoxicated passenger just before closing the main cabin door, delaying crew awareness. Although the passenger caused no issues during flight, he urinated on a seat upon landing, requiring hazmat cleanup and highlighting the agent's failure to provide timely information.

synopsis: A pilot of a vintage single engine aircraft reported striking a deer during landing rollout. No injuries were reported to either the pilot or his passenger, however the aircraft did sustain visible damage to exterior components.
summary: The pilot struck a deer crossing from the left immediately after touchdown on Runway 32 at Jefferson County Airpark (2G2) while using wheel landing mode with two notches of flaps. The strike damaged the propeller, gear fairings, belly panels, venturi, and transponder antenna, but the pilot maintained control with no injuries.

synopsis: The Captain of a corporate Falcon jet reported a loss of cabin pressurization while cruising at flight level 430. An emergency descent was accomplished and the aircraft was successfully diverted to a suitable enroute airport. The highest cabin altitude noted was 15,000 and one passenger reported some ear discomfort.
summary: Pilots and cabin crew experienced a rapid cabin pressure increase at FL430, triggering an emergency descent to 7000 feet due to a pressure computer failure. The aircraft landed uneventfully after completing checklists, with one passenger reporting ear discomfort.

aircraft: Challenger Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: The Captain of a Bombardier Challenger aircraft reported being tightly sequenced behind a heavy Boeing 747 while in the traffic pattern at LAX. He felt this placed the corporate jet in jeopardy of encountering serious wake turbulence. The situation was further exacerbated by the Tower clearing a Super Airbus 380 for takeoff while the Challenger was still on final approach.
summary: The pilot reported that while approaching LAX runway 24L behind a 747, ATC issued a heading that reduced wake separation and then cleared an A380 for takeoff with zero wake separation. The pilot attributed this unsafe situation to ATC prioritizing traffic flow over safety standards regarding vortex generation and thrust wake.

synopsis: A pilot of a light aircraft, performing pipeline patrol duty, reported inadvertently penetrating a wildfire TFR due to the rapidly changing restricted airspace environment.
summary: A pilot conducting a pipeline patrol in a single-engine aircraft likely penetrated a Temporary Flight Restriction (TFR) due to wildfire while managing high workload and complex airspace. The incident resulted from misidentifying a new fire location as a previously tracked one, compounded by heavy traffic and reduced visibility from smoke.

synopsis: LGB Tower Controller reported that there was approval for two aircraft to cross the runway. After one crossed the Controller reported that they cleared an aircraft for takeoff. Ground Control advised Local Control of the second aircraft that was cleared to cross. Local cancelled the takeoff clearance before the crossing aircraft crossed the hold short bars.
summary: The tower controller cleared Aircraft X for takeoff while a second aircraft was still crossing Runway 25L, forgetting the crossing due to marginal staffing preventing Line Up and Wait usage. The controller cancelled the clearance after Ground Control alerted them, allowing Aircraft X to exit and the crossing aircraft to complete its maneuver safely.

synopsis: EUG Tower Controller reported that he was questioned by Airport Operations if he had spoken to a particular aircraft. The Controller did not recall talking to the aircraft. Aircraft was found to be at the north ramp. Pilot stated he had ATC clearance to land. It was found out later that the pilot never talked to ATC.
summary: An unknown pilot landed Aircraft X on the east runway without ATC authorization or communication, entering Class Delta airspace while dark. Airport Ops found three occupants, including two deaf-mute individuals, and the pilot claimed he had received clearance, though no such contact occurred.

synopsis: B737 Captain reports holding at POOGY at 17,000 feet on the ENDEE3 arrival to MDW, then told to proceed direct to POOGY and descend via the ENDEE3. The next Controller chastises the crew for not descending via the ENDEE3 (still at 17,000 feet) but not required to descend until NANEE at or below 15,000 feet. The reporter is perplexed.
summary: A pilot flying the ENDEE 3 Arrival into Chicago reported a conflict with Chicago Center ATC while holding at POOGY at 17,000 feet. After confirming altitude compliance, the controller aggressively questioned the crew's understanding of the "descend via" clearance and diverted the aircraft, which the pilot attributed to controller stress and potential staffing shortages.

synopsis: Captain reported their Disabled Checklist for loss of Center (C) Hydraulic System quantity and pressure directed the pilot to select an Air Driven (Demand) Pump (ADP) on B777 aircraft. The Electronic Checklist logic stopped the continuation of the Disabled checklist due to a momentary spike in the 'C' System pressure. As a result, the Center System hyd pumps were left on even with the Center Hyd quantity and pressure at zero.
summary: The flight crew landed with a lost Center hydraulic system after gear and flap extension on final approach. Although pumps showed faults, the electronic checklist disabled pump securing actions due to a momentary pressure reading, causing pumps to run dry for over 40 minutes.

synopsis: B737 flight crew notes flaps at 25 degrees during the landing check with the flap handle set to 30. The First Officer moves the flap handle to 25 then back to 30 with no change, then 40 and back to 30 with no change. The Captain elects to land in the current configuration.
summary: During approach, the Captain and First Officer encountered a stuck trailing edge flap indicator showing 25 despite the handle being at 30. They continued a stabilized landing with the "too low flap" warning deactivated, later discovering the indicator functioned normally once the handle was moved post-landing.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: While executing a standard instrument departure, the flight crew failed to level of at an assigned intermediate altitude. After being advised of their error by air traffic control, the climb was resumed uneventfully.
summary: The Captain and First Officer misinterpreted a "climb via SID except maintain 16,000 ft" clearance during departure, deleting the 5,000 ft restriction and climbing too high. The controller corrected the error at 5,800 ft, and the crew descended to 5,000 ft before receiving clearance to climb to 16,000 ft.

synopsis: The Boeing 767 crew diverted to a nearby airport after noticing low oil pressure and quantity.
summary: During cruise at FL360, the crew observed zero right engine oil quantity and low pressure, prompting thrust reduction and a diversion to ZZZ. The aircraft landed safely, and the right engine was shut down on the ramp after maintenance was notified.

synopsis: The Captain of an Airbus A300 freighter reported experiencing multiple system failures after takeoff which precluded entering into icing conditions or RVSM airspace. A collaborative decision was made to abort the flight and return to the originating airport where an uneventful landing was accomplished.
summary: The crew returned to ZZZ after takeoff due to multiple failures including inoperative gear, transponder, probe heat, and flight director. They held in VMC to burn fuel and avoid icing before landing safely.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An aircraft ACARS printer was inoperative so Dispatch emailed the performance data to the crew. During takeoff the nose heavy aircraft extended the takeoff roll. In flight the crew determined the V speeds were too low for the installed engine type.
summary: Pilots and a dispatcher experienced a heavy rotation on takeoff due to incorrect V-speeds caused by a Performance Data Report error for the wrong engine model. The aircraft departed safely without incident, though the specific data error could not be reproduced.

synopsis: PC-12 Captain reported he and the First Officer had noticed an anomaly during the before-takeoff flight control check, involving a 'catch' in the elevator movement.
summary: During a pre-takeoff control check on the ground, the First Officer and Captain experienced the elevator yoke catching and sticking during forward movement. They attributed the issue to a potential loose component or obstruction that could cause catastrophic failure if it stuck in flight, prompting them to cancel the flight for maintenance.

synopsis: CRJ-700 Captain reported receiving a L BLEED DUCT warning followed by a R ENG BLEED caution. Captain decided to divert to nearest suitable airport.
summary: During cruise at FL340, the crew encountered a L BLEED DUCT warning causing both bleed valves to close and cabin pressurization loss. They executed an emergency descent and landed overweight, resulting in an expedited deplaning due to cabin fumes and a passenger injury from a falling oxygen mask panel.

synopsis: BED Tower Front Line Manager reported of a Local Controller who, while distracted by a Developmental, led to a runway separation event. FLM reported Controller's speed of actions was not up to the tempo of traffic. FLM reported Controller should have done something different to avoid the loss of separation.
summary: A local controller holding a C172 on Runway 11 while a jet landed on the same runway caused a runway incursion risk due to inexperience with crossing traffic and distraction from a developmental controller. The controller failed to anticipate the jet's speed and misunderstood the situation's severity while blaming the pilots.

synopsis: Columbia 400 pilot reported deviating from published procedure on departure from BFI.
summary: A pilot departing VFR south on RWY 13 Right Blake Island failed to turn downwind as required by the procedure while maintaining 800 ft. The deviation occurred as the pilot focused on visual separation from SeaTac landing traffic while flying directly toward the Fauntleroy ferry dock.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reports sighting a UAV or model aircraft shortly after takeoff from SKBO. The UAV was at about 700 feet AGL and below their aircraft and flying in the same direction.
summary: The First Officer reported spotting a fixed-wing drone approximately 300–400 feet below and 200 meters right of the aircraft during climb-out from SKBO Runway 13L. Although the crew did not take evasive action, the tower incorrectly identified the object as a helicopter and failed to acknowledge the drone threat.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: NCT Controller described how procedures into SFO are allegedly not correct. Aircraft are going to the wrong runway, leaving the Bravo airspace, and are violating speed restrictions below the Bravo. Pilot of aircraft described how they set up for one runway and then were assigned another, which led to confusion in the cockpit.
summary: The flight crew on Aircraft X flying the BODGA1 arrival into SFO entered the depart sector at 11,000 feet without coordination after confusing STAR procedures caused a routing error. The pilot attributed the incident to poorly designed arrival routes and FMS setup errors, noting that management has failed to address these recurring safety issues.

synopsis: TRACON Controller reported of two aircraft that traffic was called to on one another. One aircraft climbed into the others proximity and the Controller questioned the pilot as to why they climbed. Pilot responded they thought the other aircraft was descending. Controller reported that one aircraft's air carrier is not required to have water safety gear on board and is confused as to why they do not have it, but others are required to. This puts more strain on the Controller by having to keep the aircraft within gliding distance to land.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a conflict between inbound Aircraft Y at FL100 and outbound Aircraft X at FL090 when X climbed into Y's path. The pilot stated he climbed because he mistakenly believed Y was descending, triggering a conflict alert.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: HCF Controller described a situation where the KOA Tower Controller vectored an aircraft to avoid another. KOA controllers are not allowed to provide vectors and this led to a loss of separation with an inbound aircraft.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a contract tower controller at KOA improperly vectored Aircraft X eastbound, reducing separation to under 5 miles with trailing Aircraft Y. The tower controller claimed visual contact with a late VFR aircraft, but lacked the radar authority to vector IFR traffic, creating a loss of separation.

synopsis: ZTL Controller described a situation where it is observed that an aircraft is at the wrong altitude for direction of flight. Nothing is observed in the fourth line of the data block where information should be.
summary: An air traffic controller identified Aircraft X as inappropriate for direction of flight at FL390 due to a missing deviation clearance in the fourth line from ZJX Sector 34. The controller reported the coordination failure and a subsequent incident where the ZJX controller used profanity in the fourth line for Aircraft Y, citing a risk of separation loss.

aircraft: Light Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: PDX Tower Controller reported a large aircraft's wing went over a smaller aircraft, claimed by the smaller aircraft. Smaller aircraft was delayed going into the alley way and larger aircraft continued taxiing. Another aircraft said there was plenty of room.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a near-midair collision risk on the taxiway between Aircraft X, delayed waiting for a marshaller, and Aircraft Y taxiing to Runway 28L. The controller allowed Aircraft Y to pass without stopping to avoid braking risks, noting the pilots later agreed there was sufficient clearance.

synopsis: A90 TRACON Controller reported of a loss of separation of final due to speed control. Controller observed aircraft on final and slowed the following aircraft. Following aircraft did not slow as fast as the controller anticipated. Controller attempted to save the operation by removing the following aircraft off of final, but did so too late.
summary: An air traffic controller managed two high-speed IFR arrivals on Runway 6, where Aircraft Y nearly overtook Aircraft X due to a high-speed descent profile and airspace constraints. The controller issued a speed reduction and diverted Aircraft Y, resulting in a minimum separation of 2.83 nm and 900 ft, attributing the incident to flawed arrival routing and limited sequencing options.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ZMA controller reported a confusing communications issue which needed to be corrected. Due to equipment being out of service and having to use commercial landlines for coordination, a visiting supervisor picked up a phone call and gave it to the controllers. The controllers thought they were talking to another ATC facility and issued instructions, when they were actually talking to the pilot. Controllers figured something was wrong and called the other ATC facility to check on the release. The other ATC facility sterilized the airspace and the aircraft became airborne. Controller wants the land lines fixed so this will not happen again.
summary: A ZQA trainee and trainer at D61 issued an incorrect clearance to a pilot at MYEM after a visiting supervisor transferred the call to their sector without identifying the caller. The error occurred because dedicated MEVA lines were out of service, forcing reliance on unsecured regular phone lines that allowed unauthorized access.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported multiple mechanical issues, including bleed trip and loss of cabin pressure, which led to the decision to return to departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a right bleed trip off at rotation, leading to a return where pressurization failed and the altitude warning horn sounded. They landed normally with 30-knot winds but could not engage the right engine reverse, stopping using autobrakes and the left engine.

synopsis: A300 pilot experiences a failure of the landing gear to retract after takeoff on system one position detection. On system two the gear retracts but autopilot one will not engage as the Captain's flight director is inoperative along with his pitch trim. Autopilot two is successfully engaged but other anomalies begin to appear and the crew elects to return to the departure airport after burning off enough fuel.
summary: The crew experienced multiple system failures including landing gear, autopilot, transponder, and pitot probe overheating during climb, forcing an immediate descent below 14,000 feet. They held at 11,000 feet to burn fuel before landing overweight in visual conditions due to thunderstorms.

synopsis: EMB145 flight crew experienced severe turbulence en route to Houston at FL370 while deviating around thunderstorms, which the First Officer believed were avoidable. He also believed they encountered super cooled water droplets and the airframe picked up ice on unprotected areas of the fuselage. The ice was shed during descent.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence and icing while deviating around weather near COT due to a radar tilt error and lack of shared mental model. This caused a 300-foot altitude deviation, autopilot disconnect, and anti-ice system failures, requiring QRH procedures and a flaps 22 landing.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 flight crew reported encountering wake turbulence shortly after takeoff at ATL in trail of a B737 that triggered a momentary stall warning.
summary: The pilot encountered wake turbulence from a preceding 737 shortly after takeoff at Atlanta, triggering a stall shaker. Recovery involved applying max thrust and lowering the nose, which stabilized the aircraft despite a brief right engine ITT excursion that was later deemed within limits.

synopsis: A G550 MEL 52-6-0 permitted dispatch with the Main Entry Door Acoustic Curtain/Door System immoveable in the lock/secured position preventing access to LEFT ELECTRONIC EQUIPMENT RACK and POWER DISTRIBUTION BOX circuit breaker panels. The flight crew questioned the aircraft's airworthiness because the QRH requires access to that area for certain abnormal procedures.
summary: The Captain and First Officer identified that MEL 52-6-0 secured the Main Entry Door open, blocking access to critical circuit breaker panels required for preflight and in-flight checklists. Although the Chief Pilot deemed the aircraft airworthy, the crew refused to fly, citing an inability to comply with SOPs and QRH procedures due to the blocked access.

synopsis: Flight crew reported being dispatched with loop A of the number three engine fire detection system on MEL. At cruise altitude a fire warning was annunciated on the number three engine and it was shut down. Flight diverted to a suitable airport for an uneventful landing. After landing a cabin smoke alert was activated and the crew elected to evacuate the aircraft. No evidence of fire was found on the engine or in the cabin.
summary: The crew diverted a four-engine aircraft from FL350 after an Engine 3 fire warning with one loop deferred, followed by an Engine 1 loop failure and a false Cabin Smoke alert. They evacuated the aircraft, but fire services found no fire or smoke, leaving the interrelation of the three system faults unclear.

synopsis: DA2000 Captain reports an altitude deviation during descent due to an apparent misunderstanding of what ATC said and what the First Officer read back.
summary: During a reposition flight, the Captain and First Officer descended to 6,000 feet instead of the cleared 16,000 feet due to miscommunication and the First Officer's distraction from back pain. The crew acknowledged the altitude bust to ATC and climbed back to 16,000 feet.

synopsis: An air carrier Captain reported executing a missed approach on a SFO Runway 28L visual after the second TCAS RA climb command from another aircraft which apparently erroneously lined up on 28L instead of the assigned 28R.
summary: The flight crew executing a visual approach to SFO Runway 28L offset left after observing an air carrier jet deviating toward their course. Two TCAS RAs occurred, forcing a missed approach, likely because the other jet erroneously intercepted the 28L localizer instead of 28R.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: While taxiing at HNL, an overloaded First Officer and Captain talked about the confusing nonstandard taxi instructions, their taxiway incursion and an impatient Controller.
summary: The flight crew at HNL missed a taxi turn due to an unusual clearance and distractions from controller reprimands, causing a stop on Taxiway A. They were subsequently re-routed to avoid a damaged taxiway section and delayed on Runway 8R while a heavy jet departed.

synopsis: The 777 crew were cleared to push back, released the brakes and moved back about ten feet before realizing that there was no one driving the tug.
summary: The flight crew attempted to push back after loading the FMC, but the aircraft moved ten feet without tug driver response. The pushback stopped when the crew discovered the tug was unoccupied, causing the aircraft to roll back before halting.

synopsis: The Captain was uncomfortable being assigned to fly as an ERJ 170 First Officer with minimal experience and training in that position.
summary: A Captain with over 10 years of ERJ 170 experience was moved to the right seat as First Officer due to a new Captain's lack of 100 hours PIC time. The reporter believes safety is compromised because they have never flown as First Officer in this aircraft, making it difficult to override established muscle memory.

synopsis: After landing, evidence of damage below the cargo door of the SF340 was discovered by the ground crew.
summary: The flight crew operated an aircraft with a feathered engine from departure to ZZZ, where ground crews discovered significant lower fuselage damage likely caused by ground equipment at the origin. The aircraft was flown unairworthy because the damage went unreported, requiring a ferry flight for major repairs.

synopsis: Captain lamented the training he received for new procedures instituted by his company in order to mirror the procedures of a main line carrier. He also does not believe that the CRJ200 to CRJ900 differences training is adequate.
summary: A pilot reported that their airline implemented new checklists and procedures without providing required simulator, live, or video training. The pilot attributed this unsafe practice to inadequate management oversight and a lack of effective FSDO supervision, fearing high non-compliance rates and potential accidents.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier aircraft encountered un-forecasted severe turbulence and mountain wave activity over the Andes Mountains in South Central Argentina.
summary: A crew operating an eastbound flight at FL370 near REPEV encountered sudden severe mountain wave turbulence, causing airspeed excursions and altitude changes while the autopilot remained engaged. The event displaced cabin items and spilled hot coffee on a flight attendant, but no injuries were reported.

synopsis: After landing the APU was started, but auto shutdown accompanied by a dirty socks odor and cabin haze. At the gate Maintenance determined an APU oil seal failed allowing oil in APU bleed air. The aircraft was removed from service. The First Officer was examined at an ER and released with a persistent headache.
summary: The flight crew experienced a toxic oil vapor leak from the APU after activating the bleed air system while taxiing, causing a "dirty sock" smell and cabin haze. Maintenance confirmed a blown APU seal, and the crew sought medical attention for nausea and headaches before being released.

synopsis: After several reroutes and holding, the crew declared minimum fuel but were able to land at their original destination of ORD instead of diverting.
summary: The flight crew rejected partial ATC reroutes and declared minimum fuel due to weather and fuel concerns, diverting from ORD to MKE before returning to ORD. Despite ATC requests to cancel their status, the crew maintained priority, executed a visual approach, and landed with 2,700 lbs of fuel.

synopsis: The First Officer became sick en route to DFW, the flight was expedited and landed uneventfully.
summary: During cruise over the Gulf of Mexico, a First Officer suffered food poisoning and vomiting, prompting the Captain to utilize a commuting pilot as a safety observer. The crew advised ATC, received priority clearance, and landed uneventfully on Runway 17R at DFW, where the First Officer was checked by EMTs.

synopsis: CRJ900 Flight Attendant described an unexpected encounter with severe turbulence during beverage service. The service cart hit the ceiling and landed back in the aisle without injuring anyone. No warning was received from the flight crew.
summary: A flight attendant serving row 16 encountered severe turbulence without warning from the flight deck, causing a service cart to strike the ceiling and scatter contents. The crew reported no passenger injuries but noted cart damage and criticized the pilots for failing to communicate the weather due to being occupied with storm avoidance.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician recommended a specific tool be made or listed in the Aircraft Maintenance Manual for technicians to use to avoid damage to CFM-56 Engine Fan disks when removing the N1 Fan Blade Shim/Keeper weights. Inadvertent tooling damage by Technician required unscheduled engine replacement on a B737-900 aircraft.
summary: A mechanic damaged the N1 fan disk with tool marks while removing a fan blade per the Aircraft Maintenance Manual, necessitating unscheduled engine replacement. The incident occurred because the manual lacked specific tooling for removing shim/keeper weights, making manual removal impossible.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) working as an on-call Air Carrier Technical Representative describes his excessively long, irregular work days, ever changing work hours, lack of adequate support for re-scheduling hotels and fatigue from lack of sleep.
summary: A mechanic repaired a B737 at ZZZ1 and ZZZ4 but faced repeated hotel and flight reservation cancellations because Scheduling failed to update the mechanic's itinerary during crew changes. The reporter attributes this to a lack of 24/7 support for mechanics, resulting in severe sleep deprivation and personal inconvenience.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician reported finding a third Cessna CE-560XLS aircraft in a month with Main Landing Gear Uplock Hook bushings worn during their Post Maintenance Checklist inspections. Technician believed that since they have migrated from doing Phase 1-4 Inspections to performing Phase-A and Phase-B Inspections, the Uplock Detailed Inspection Task has been overlooked.
summary: A technician discovered a worn bushing on the left main landing gear uplock hook during a post-maintenance checklist, marking the third occurrence in a month. The reporter attributes this to Task XXXX001 being overlooked in the AAIP and recommends incorporating it into scheduled maintenance.

synopsis: C206 pilot reported landing on Runway 14 at HEQ and sighting a Thrush on downwind. The reporter pulled into the turnaround at the end of Runway 14 and watched the Thrush make a low approach and appear to depart to the south. He announced a back taxi on Runway 32, but halfway down the runway his passenger reported the Thrush was landing behind them. Taxi speed was greatly increased and a collision was avoided.
summary: The pilot and a mechanic landed at HEQ on Runway 14, then taxied back on the runway to exit. A Thrush aircraft landed on Runway 32 behind them, closing to within 1,000 feet of their tail, but the pilot accelerated to avoid a collision.

synopsis: G-IV Captain reported encountering wake turbulence at FL340 from another aircraft about 10 miles ahead of them.
summary: The pilot reported experiencing heavy wake turbulence while climbing to FL400 from TEB, causing the autopilot to disengage and requiring manual control to maintain wings level. The pilot attributed the event to a heavy jet 10 to 11 miles ahead on the same airway and recommended ATC advisories for such situations.

synopsis: DV20 pilot reported an NMAC with another aircraft shortly after takeoff from PVU.
summary: The pilot, conducting right traffic after takeoff on Runway 13, observed an aircraft that had just departed Runway 18 passing directly underneath on its upwind leg. The pilot reported an estimated vertical separation of 400 to 500 feet between the two aircraft.

synopsis: BE99 Captain experienced the collapse of the right main landing gear upon landing, cause unknown.
summary: The pilot reported that shortly after touchdown at ZZZZ, the right wing dropped and the aircraft veered right due to a gear failure. The aircraft was shut down upon stopping, but the specific cause of the gear failure remains undetermined.

synopsis: During landing, an RV-9 right main gear touched the roof of a passing vehicle.
summary: During landing, the aircraft's right main wheel struck a vehicle traveling north on a road perpendicular to the runway. The aircraft landed normally with no injuries, sustaining only a minor fracture to the right main wheel pant.

synopsis: PA24 pilot experienced engine failure at 10,000 feet and quickly selects another tank and turns on the electric fuel pump, restoring normal operation. After landing the left tip tank was found to be empty, which would not have been the case had the fuel management plan been followed. The left tip tank may have inadvertently been selected when attempting to select the left main tank.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine power loss during climb due to suspected fuel starvation from incorrect tank selection. After restarting the engine and landing safely, the pilot concluded the incident was likely caused by operator error in managing the fuel selector.

synopsis: A Hatz CB-1 pilot ground looped his aircraft in a crosswind causing slight damage when the right wing impacted a fence.
summary: The pilot reported that a crosswind lifted the left wingtip during landing, causing the aircraft to ground loop and strike a fence with the right wing. The incident resulted in slight damage to the aircraft but no injuries.

synopsis: CE120 pilot attempts a VFR flight across 6 NM of water to a nearby airport without a radio or a functioning compass and enters IMC. After becoming lost he chooses to land on a taxiway at a military field.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 120 encountered IMC and lost compass reliability while lacking functional radios. Due to fuel concerns and inability to reach the intended destination, the pilot executed an emergency landing on a military airport taxiway and was subsequently apprehended by security.

synopsis: C172 pilot experiences a NMAC with a drone at 2,500 feet.
summary: During a photo reconnaissance training sortie at 2,500 feet MSL, a small orange drone passed over the left wing for two seconds. The encounter was too brief for evasive action, so the pilot provided contact details to Approach after landing.

synopsis: C208B pilot reported a ground conflict at HDH when another light aircraft taxied into his path.
summary: A pilot taxiing a large aircraft to refuel nearly collided with a small tailwheel airplane exiting the runway onto the same taxiway. The incident occurred because the small plane's pilot failed to look left due to complacency, requiring the taxiing pilot to apply brakes and enter beta to stop safely 75 feet away.

synopsis: An HS-125-800 engine shuddered and shutdown while at cruise altitude FL330. Then emergency checklists were completed and the flight landed a short time later.
summary: The crew experienced a shudder and shutdown of the Honeywell TFE-731-5R-1H engine. They secured the engine, completed emergency checklists, and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported his iPad failed to load the needed approach charts during a practice approach.
summary: During an IFR training flight at 4,500 feet, the pilot discovered ForeFlight approach plates were inaccessible on an iPad due to failed overnight map updates. The pilot resolved the issue by switching to paper charts, reducing power to manage workload, and successfully completed three approaches without notifying ATC.

synopsis: C210 pilot experienced electrical failure after having a new battery installed. The landing gear is selected down 8-10 miles from the field but the landing gear indicator lights have failed. A gear up landing ensues.
summary: A pilot flying a short trip for maintenance experienced electrical failure and radio loss in hazy conditions. Despite lowering the gear handle, the pilot landed gear up because the inoperative down light prevented visual confirmation of the gear being locked.

synopsis: A BE-60 nose gear indicated not down and locked on the previous approach but did lock after landing. A mechanic recommended gear down ferry to home base. The next landing the left main collapsed followed by the nose gear. No injuries resulted.
summary: The pilot reported that the left main and nose landing gear collapsed during landing, causing the aircraft to rest off the runway with no injuries to the five occupants. The pilot attributed the failure to a suspected gear motor issue following a previous landing where the nose gear down-and-locked indication was initially absent.

synopsis: B737 flight crew experienced high EGT during takeoff and the Captain elected to reject the takeoff just prior to V1. A Flight Attendant notified the Captain that an elderly passenger had been adversely affected by the reject and EMT's should meet the aircraft at the gate.
summary: The First Officer called a high EGT on the right engine at 138 knots, prompting the Captain to reject the takeoff before V1 due to an engine overheat light. The aircraft stopped safely, was inspected by fire crews, and returned to the gate where medical personnel removed an ill passenger before maintenance took over.

synopsis: B737 First Officer became confused during arrival when cleared for a visual approach after expecting vectors for a straight in approach. The aircraft was positioned on a 45 to the right downwind when the visual approach clearance was received and between the maneuvering required to line up and the sun angle into the cockpit, airspeed was allowed to get very low. The Captain commanded a go around and the second approach was successful.
summary: Two crews reported visual approach incidents involving sun glare, airspeed decay, and buffet leading to go-arounds. Causes included ATC positioning, delayed engine spool-up, and procedural errors during the missed approach, though both aircraft landed safely on subsequent attempts.

synopsis: An air carrier Captain discovered while climbing to cruise from ABQ that the passenger manifest count was off and the aircraft weight was off by 5,800 pounds making the actual takeoff weight heavier than what was shown on the loading schedule.
summary: The pilot failed to verify passenger counts before pushback at ABQ, resulting in a 5,800-pound Zero Fuel Weight discrepancy discovered via Dispatch ACARs during climb. The crew adjusted the weight data after takeoff, noting the error should have been caught during the Before Push Checklist.

synopsis: An MD-11 crew returned to the departure airport after experiencing an 'EMER PWR ON' event with an associated battery discharge.
summary: The relief pilot and First Officer on an MD-11 experienced a Level 1 'EMER PWR ON' alert and rapid battery discharge, prompting a return to base. The crew turned off the emergency power switch due to fire concerns and requested better AOM guidance for this scenario.

synopsis: B767 flight crew experienced a track deviation in Chinese airspace approach DONVO, possibly due to GPS jamming. ATC detects the error while it is still minor and the anomaly does not reoccur during the remainder of the flight.
summary: Pilots on a B-767 deviated approximately 1 NM from a 6 NM right offset while changing speed near DONVO, likely due to FMC turn calculation errors or GPS jamming. ATC detected the drift, prompting a manual correction and a direct clearance to ANRAT, with no further issues.

synopsis: PC-12 Captain reports sighting a drone on final approach to Runway 22 at LGA. No evasive action is necessary.
summary: A pilot sighted a drone less than 100 yards away, slightly below and left of the aircraft, while on final approach to RWY 22 at LGA. The pilot reported the incident to the tower and followed up with a phone call to the supervisor as requested.

synopsis: A G-V oven produced a large amount of smoke inflight which the Flight Attendant and Relief Pilot controlled. The flight continued and it was determined that unnoticed paper with the food tray caught fire.
summary: During a flight to Europe, a Flight Attendant and third crewmember extinguished smoke from a galley oven caused by overheating cardboard food covers mistaken for aluminum foil. The crew secured the oven, vented the cabin, and continued the flight without diversion after confirming the fire was contained.

synopsis: C182 pilot reported a near miss with an individual operating a parasail in the vicinity of PHX.
summary: During descent through 6,100 ft near Lake Pleasant, a pilot had a near miss with a parasail while distracted by a radio frequency change. A passenger alerted the crew, revealing the parasail was approximately 100 ft vertically and 300 ft laterally separated from the aircraft.

synopsis: Falcon 2000EX First Officer reported loss of cabin pressure at FL430 resulting in an emergency descent and diversion to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: Both pilots initiated an emergency descent from flight level 430 after a rapid cabin pressure increase triggered the Cabin Altitude CAS and deployed oxygen masks. The aircraft descended to 7000 feet while avoiding thunderstorms and landed uneventfully, though the crew noted the transponder emergency selection process could be improved.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A student pilot on a cross country solo became very confused about the takeoff clearance and instead of taking off and turning right, turned right on the runway. ATC corrected the error and after back taxiing, the pilot departed.
summary: A student pilot and air traffic controller were involved during a solo cross-country departure from Runway 9. The pilot misunderstood a right turn instruction as a taxi maneuver, resulting in a runway incursion and cancelled takeoff due to the pilot's lack of experience and knowledge of the airport.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A distracted pilot made a turn for a SFB Runway 9R base but took evasive action at the same time ATC called to issue a turn and climb because of traffic already on final for 9R.
summary: A pilot flying a VFR pattern at Sanford International encountered traffic on final while turning base, prompting an evasive climb and power increase. The pilot attributed the conflict to personal distraction from passenger conversation or a controller's failure to advise of the traffic.

synopsis: HCF Controller reported of a problem that happens often with aircraft on the VECKI8 STAR to KOA. Pilots descend below the Minimum IFR Altitude when cleared for the ILS in conjunction with this arrival.
summary: An air traffic controller observed Aircraft X descend below the 088 Minimum IFR Altitude while on the VECKI8 arrival, triggering an MSAW alert. The pilot halted descent after the controller advised the altitude restriction, though the reporter attributes the recurring issue to confusion with the STAR design rather than individual pilot error.

synopsis: ZME Controller reported of an aircraft that encountered severe turbulence on its route. Controller then took steps to advise others of the turbulence.
summary: An air traffic controller relayed severe turbulence reports from Aircraft X and others near the ZME/ZTL boundary at FL340 and FL370 to nearby pilots. The controller noted that while injuries were later reported, the initial lack of verbal coordination between adjacent facilities delayed the dissemination of these critical PIREPs.

synopsis: SCT Controller and Front Line Manager reported of an aircraft that went around due to traffic, then was being sequenced to same runway as another arrival. Pilot attempted to question and advise the controller but, due to congestion on frequency, was not able to get a word in. Pilot squawked emergency and turned in to final. Traffic in front and alongside aircraft had to be turned out.
summary: An A321 arrival declared a Mayday and turned final without prior fuel notification while the controller managed multiple conflicting traffic priorities. The controller subsequently separated the aircraft from traffic ahead and cleared it for a safe landing on Runway 24L.

synopsis: Pilot and Copilot reported an instance where there was confusion on who to follow. Pilots were told to follow second aircraft, which they thought they did. Controller wanted them to follow an aircraft they did not see. Pilots complained of controller's non-standard phraseology.
summary: Pilots taxiing to Runway 13 followed the only visible Carrier B aircraft after ATC instructed them to follow "the second carrier," causing confusion when Ground Control later questioned why they did not wait for a different, unseen Carrier B. The reporter attributed the incident to ATC's non-standard phraseology and failure to specify which aircraft to follow during high congestion.

synopsis: A B757 flight crew reported EICAS TRAILING EDGE FLAP ASSYM message and the FLAPS ELEC status alert. With flaps between 13-15 the flight continued to a nearby airport for maintenance.
summary: During takeoff at 1,000 feet AGL, the flight crew experienced a flap freeze and asymmetry message. They continued the departure, consulted dispatch, and landed uneventfully at the next destination with flaps set at 13–15.

synopsis: An A321 crew was forced by the company's inaction to complete a flight in violation of the FAR 117 thirteen hour flight duty period limitation.
summary: The Captain and First Officer faced repeated maintenance delays on an A321 that threatened their 13-hour FDP limit. Despite their concerns and requests to re-crew, the company insisted they fly, resulting in an illegal landing at the destination.

aircraft: Embraer Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A crew expecting the DCA Runway 19 River Visual did not hear the clearance issued so they did not program the FMS transition. When the aircraft did not turn to EYESS, PCT noted the track deviation but then chastised the crew for not asking about the clearance after the EXPECT had been issued.
summary: A fatigued captain flying a jet en route to DCA neglected to load the south transition into the FMS while anticipating a familiar visual approach to Runway 19. This caused the aircraft to miss the turn at EYESS, prompting ATC to issue vectors and an admonishment before the crew landed safely.

synopsis: An EMB-145 ferry flight with ballast fuel diverted because of poor destination weather after holding and learned ballast fuel cannot be burned as holding fuel.
summary: During a ferry flight holding at 12,000 feet, the crew diverted to an alternate due to weather and landed with 3,000 lbs of fuel, below the actual 3,300 lb reserve. Dispatch later clarified that their software failed to account for 1,500 lbs of ballast fuel, causing confusion over the true reserve requirement.

synopsis: A B737-800 landed on BOS Runway 4R and exited at Taxiway Y but incurred Runway 33R because they did not see a hold short or other markings for that Runway.
summary: The First Officer landed a Boeing 737 on Runway 4R at BOS and exited at high speed onto Taxiway Y, inadvertently crossing the hold short line for Runway 33R. The pilot attributed the incursion to a lack of signage, acute approach angle, sun glare, and unexpected aggressive braking.

synopsis: Captain described his efforts to have an MEL Maintenance Procedure properly completed by a Foreign Air Carrier's Contract Technician while his company's foreign and domestic Maintenance Controllers disagreed with each other on whether the Right Engine Anti-Ice Valve light should remain illuminated after the Maintenance Procedure. Rejected Takeoff of the B757-200 followed due to a Right Engine Anti-Ice EICAS message had appeared. Anti-Ice Valve found broken.
summary: The crew of a B757 rejected takeoff below V1 after an Engine Anti-Ice EICAS message appeared due to a broken valve and an initially incorrect MEL completion. The Captain aborted the takeoff to prevent potential engine damage from the bleed air system issue.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported of flying through the approach course, attempting to contact Approach. No response, so they changed to Tower frequency and got vectored back on to final. Approach Controller told pilots they should not have switched to Tower frequency. Controllers stated they were in a briefing.
summary: Pilots on a right base vector to Runway 36R could not contact Approach Control despite multiple attempts, causing them to fly past the airfield. They contacted Tower for a visual approach clearance, after which Approach attributed the silence to a briefing and denied any transmitter failure.

aircraft: McDonnell Douglas Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: DC-10 crew diverted to a nearby airport because of a fuel malfunction that trapped 5,800 pounds of fuel in the tip tank making it unusable.
summary: The flight crew received fuel system alerts indicating trapped fuel and pump failure just prior to descent. They diverted to the nearest airport due to an inability to manually manage the fuel imbalance without risking engine flameout, landing uneventfully.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Two aircraft on downwind to CTAF U42 had a near miss after one pilot in the pattern turned downwind early to avoid Class B and may not have made a downwind call in accordance with Advisory Circular 90.66 or the other pilot entering the pattern downwind did not hear the downwind call.
summary: Two IFR pilots on a 45-mile inbound approach and a student-instructor pair in a high-performance aircraft had a 30-foot close call at a non-controlled airport. The incident resulted from the student's wide downwind turn intercepting the inbound course, compounded by smoke, haze, and a lack of negative contact calls.

synopsis: The BE20 pilot returned to his departure airport after the left engine torque indication decreased and asymmetric thrust increased. He landed uneventfully with the engine feathered.
summary: The pilot departed on an IFR flight plan in VFR weather and experienced left engine torque loss and asymmetric thrust during initial climb. After attempting to restore power, the pilot feathered the propeller and returned for a successful no-event landing.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A solo corporate jet pilot's tablet overheated in the sunlight during vectors to EWR. He switched tablets but it too overheated. During this time he was slowing to comply with an ATC request. Finally, the initial tablet became operational and remained out of sunlight.
summary: During a busy approach to EWR, the pilot failed to comply with an assigned 180 KTS speed while both cockpit tablets overheated in direct sunlight. The distraction caused by switching devices to reference approach plates led the crew to revert to printed charts.

synopsis: LGA Tower Controller reported of a go-around due to traffic not being airborne. Controller separated traffic and was told to transfer communications to the Departure Controller. Initial altitude of 2,000 was given. Controller thought the aircraft should have been given a higher altitude due to MVA of 2700 feet.
summary: An air traffic controller at LGA issued a go-around to an arriving aircraft due to a departing aircraft on runway 22, climbing the arrival to 2000 feet. The controller noted a lack of written coordination for higher altitudes and highlighted a Minimum Vectoring Altitude discrepancy regarding the Freedom Tower.

synopsis: Pilot questions why their dispatcher(s) are not getting a copy of their Maintenance Check Flight form prior to planning a Functional Check Flight (FCF) flight plan. He also questions the practice by the Director of Operations of determining, once airborne, where the airplane will go after a pass or fail Functional Check Flight becomes known. The perceived secrecy does not allow the check flight crew to effectively plan the flight and leads to degraded ATC coordination.
summary: A pilot reported safety concerns during a Functional Check Flight where the arrival airport was changed mid-flight with Director of Operations approval, but the Dispatcher lacked the FCF form and confirmed approval. The reporter requested procedural changes to ensure Dispatchers receive the FCF form and Director of Operations approval prior to flight planning.

synopsis: An A-319 crew inadvertently struck an air conditioning cart with their number one engine while taxiing in to their gate. Both piloted report that there was no left side wing walker present.
