synopsis: An Instructor on the downwind at CTAF RNV reported a near miss with an aircraft showing no lights and apparently no attempted communications.
summary: The pilot reported a conflict on the downwind leg when an aircraft passed underneath at approximately 1,000 feet MSL in the opposite direction. The other aircraft made no radio calls and had no lights or strobes operating.

synopsis: A Kodiak 100 pilot flying with a friend became cold at 11,000 feet. The pilot instructed the passenger to close the Firewall air shutoff. The passenger closed the Firewall Fuel Shutoff, next to the air shutoff, which fuel starved the engine. The pilot successfully restarted the engine.
summary: A pilot and passenger in cruise at 11,000 feet experienced an engine failure when the passenger accidentally pulled the firewall fuel shut-off, mistaking it for the air shut-off. The pilot descended to 9,700 feet, successfully restarted the engine, and continued the flight without further assistance.

synopsis: ARTCC Sector handed off two aircraft deviating for weather to adjacent ARTCC Sector. The two aircraft had clearance to return on course at their discretion which would have put them in confliction with each other. The reporter states it is a common occurrence to receive aircraft from this facility which will conflict with each other soon after entering their airspace.
summary: An adjacent ARTCC controller transferred two aircraft at 35,000 feet on a collision course while both deviated left for weather, failing to ensure separation before handoff. The receiving Radar controller intervened to assign present headings, preventing a potential loss of separation within five miles of the sector boundary.

synopsis: An aircraft deviated off the assigned STAR. Crew had inadvertently set the FMS to program from the next charting cycle date instead of current charting cycle. The aircraft was proceeding along the route of a revision to the STAR which was not yet in effect.
summary: Pilots on the [STAR 1] arrival inadvertently used an FMS database from the next data cycle, causing a route deviation that confused the Approach Controller. The crew was vectored off the arrival and could not revert the database until landing, noting that the procedure's unchanged label masked the significant waypoint shift.

synopsis: An ERJ-175 flight crew descended below the Final Approach Fix altitude before passing the FAF. ATC issued a landing clearance as well as a low altitude alert. The co-pilot applied power to climb and in so doing, exceeded flaps 2 speed by approximately 4 knots.
summary: The First Officer, acting as pilot flying, descended below the cleared 2,500 feet during a visual approach to Runway 5R after setting an incorrect altitude. This triggered a low altitude alert and required a power application that exceeded the Flaps 2 speed limit by 4 knots, though the aircraft was subsequently stabilized and inspected by maintenance.

synopsis: An EMB-145 First Officer reported localizer course abnormalities were noted on the approach into LGA and stated this is a continuing problem in the fleet.
summary: A Part 145 crew flying a LOC31 approach into LGA experienced localizer deviations and full-scale CDI deflections after breaking out, though they landed visually. ATC confirmed other aircraft had no issues, leading the pilot to suspect a recurring aircraft system malfunction.

synopsis: A DHC-8 flight crew reported they had to use the parking brake to stop the aircraft at the gate when they failed to turn the standby hydraulic pumps on, causing loss of normal brake pressure.
summary: The pilot taxied single-engine to the gate with flaps up but failed to select hydraulic standby pumps, causing normal brake failure. The aircraft stopped abruptly using the parking brake, startling passengers but resulting in no injuries.

synopsis: CE-750 Captain reported they diverted to a nearby suitable airport following the loss of hydraulic System A.
summary: During climb through 30,000 feet, the crew lost Hydraulic A system quantity, resulting in loss of primary landing gear, steering, and brakes. They diverted to a nearby airport for priority landing, stopped on the runway, and were towed to the FBO.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 Check Pilot reported that a Flight Attendant fell from the aircraft while parked at the gate because of deviations from SOP.
summary: The First Officer approved closing the main door while external air remained connected, causing a Flight Attendant to fall from the aircraft when she attempted to re-secure an unsafe service door. The incident resulted from the pilot's distraction by weight and balance calculations and failure to start the APU, leading to pressure buildup that forced the attendant out.

synopsis: A319 pilot reported receiving a hot brake ECAM after takeoff that necessitated climbing with gear extended. Reporter was concerned that this had occurred three times in the past on this aircraft.
summary: The crew experienced a recurrent 'Brakes Hot' ECAM at 12,000 feet, likely caused by debris or a binding axle in brake #1, forcing gear extension and a climb below 250 KTS. They landed normally with ARFF escort, confirming the brake was overheated, and attributed the avoidable event to poor maintenance of a three-time repeat issue.

synopsis: CRJ-900 First Officer reported receiving a Left Bleed Air Duct master caution, followed by loss of both packs. An expedited descent was executed, and the flight continued to destination.
summary: The flight crew experienced a Left Bleed Air Duct Master Warning at FL390, leading to the loss of both packs and pressurization during an expedited descent to 10,000 ft. They completed checklists, deployed cabin oxygen masks, and safely landed at the planned destination after calculating sufficient fuel reserves.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: MD-80 Captain reported smoke in the aircraft when packs were turned on after pushback. Flight returned to the gate.
summary: The crew reported acrid smoke from vents after turning on air conditioning packs post-engine start. They returned to the gate, shut off the packs and recirculating fan, and deplaned normally; the smoke appeared caused by a loss of the left hydraulic system.

synopsis: B737-900 flight crew reported encountering wake turbulence on arrival from preceding B777 into SFO, which resulted in a 50 degree right bank.
summary: The flight crew encountered significant wake turbulence from a preceding B777 shortly after passing CORKK while descending via the BDEGA1 arrival to SFO. The turbulence caused a 50-degree right bank, prompting the captain to disconnect automation and deviate right to avoid further wake before ATC vectored them for a safe approach.

synopsis: With the autopilot engaged, crew intercepted the localizer and glideslope (GS) to 10L at ORD. At approximately 2,700 MSL the aircraft pitched nose down. The autopilot did not correct the deviation and increased the downward pitch. As the downward pitch increased the Captain disconnected the autopilot and corrected the pitch attitude to a stable flight path and landing. Crew suspects that there was ground aircraft interference with the ILS/GS transmitter signal.
summary: Two pilots flying a night VFR approach to ORD experienced an aggressive nose-low pitch deviation caused by suspected glide slope interference from heavy aircraft taxiing near the antennas. The captain disconnected the autopilot, recovered the aircraft without overspeeding, and completed a safe landing.

synopsis: B767-300 Captain reported receiving Cabin Alt master warning at FL360. Crew complied with QRH and continued to destination.
summary: The flight crew and line check captain managed a cabin altitude warning at FL360 caused by dual automatic controller failure. They manually controlled pressurization, descended to FL220, and continued to the destination after consulting the MEL and confirming fuel and oxygen margins.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew reported they deviated from their assigned RNAV departure when the aircraft failed to track the course.
summary: During initial climb from DCA Runway 1, the First Officer engaged the autopilot to intercept the DOCTR2 RNAV course, but it turned sharply without capturing due to a deferred FMS 2. The crew disengaged the autopilot, hand-flew the aircraft, and recommended that the autopilot only couple to non-deferred FMS sides.

synopsis: The pilot of a Grumman Tiger experienced vibration and loss of power, and was unable to clearly communicate with ATC. He was able to land successfully.
summary: During an IFR training climb at 2,000 feet, the student pilot and instructor experienced severe vibration and partial power loss. After failing to resolve the issue via emergency checklists, the pilot executed a forced landing at ZZZ with full power and severe vibration, exiting the runway under power before being towed.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 402 experienced an engine problem that required the engine to be shut down in flight. Following a successful landing, it was discovered that the fuel pump had failed and that the annual inspection had expired.
summary: The pilot shut down and feathered an engine due to fuel pump failure and erratic electric pump operation. Inspection revealed a sheared fuel pump adapter and an annual maintenance inspection expired ten days prior.

synopsis: Two pilots of single engine aircraft reported an NMAC with each other while in Travis Approach Control airspace.
summary: A pilot flying VFR at 8,500 feet experienced a near-miss with a Cessna Centurion at 8,700 feet while under Travis Approach control. The reporter attributed the incident to poor ATC communications regarding converging headings, a failure to issue diversion instructions, and the other pilot's failure to see and avoid.

synopsis: The pilot of an air-taxi operation allowed himself to become distracted, searching visually for the lesser used of two airports in close proximity. This caused him to be high on approach, and the subsequent S-turns on final approach were questioned by ATC since they had caused a separation issue.
summary: The pilot and co-pilot flew a charter flight to the wrong airport due to the pilot's incorrect pre-flight planning assumption. After accepting a visual approach to the incorrect field, they performed an S-turn to descend, which the tower controller stated caused a separation violation with a VFR aircraft.

aircraft: Piper Twin Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A Flight Instructor and student experienced a nose landing gear problem. Following several attempts to ensure that the nose landing gear was extended, the landing gear collapsed during landing.
summary: A student pilot and instructor experienced a nose gear collapse during landing after the gear failed to fully retract or lock despite multiple recycling attempts and emergency extension procedures. The nose wheel collapsed upon touchdown, causing propeller strikes, though the crew evacuated safely before emergency crews applied foam.

aircraft: Bell Helicopter Textron Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Bell 407 pilot reported he had a TFR incursion and stated the TFR was not listed on the FAA briefing website. Both TFRs were for sporting events.
summary: A helicopter air ambulance pilot departed a hospital mission and was later notified by dispatch of an inadvertent Temporary Flight Restriction (TFR) violation over a stadium. The pilot reported that the TFR was not visible on the FAA website or XM weather data, suggesting a system gap in publishing football game TFRs.

synopsis: DA40 pilot experiences a yaw to the left in cruise requiring right rudder for coordinated flight. It is learned that this and many other DA40's have their nose wheels pivot to the right or left stop after lift off and cannot be recentered without landing.
summary: A pilot reported that a 2010 Diamond DA40 intermittently enters an uncorrectable slip due to the nose wheel locking left, causing the autopilot to bank the aircraft. Diamond Aircraft acknowledged the issue but declined to develop a solution, leaving the only remedy as landing and taking off again.

synopsis: Helicopter pilot, doing a clearing turn on the ramp in the vicinity of a U.S. Marshal aircraft, was approached by two men pointing assault rifles at the helicopter. After a call for assistance to local police, the situation was resolved.
summary: The pilot of an EC-130B4 conducting a tour flight encountered two armed US Marshals pointing rifles at the helicopter during a departure clearing turn. The pilot was forced to maneuver away to ensure safety, and the incident ended after local police arrived, though the Marshals refused to communicate before departing.

synopsis: A Beechcraft M35 pilot lost manifold pressure while descending and turning downwind to base leg. He immediately turned toward the runway while noticing that the manifold pressure gauge did not respond to throttle inputs and landed in a field near the airport. Upon inspection, the throttle cable linkage was observed to be loose.
summary: The pilot experienced a loss of throttle control due to a loose cable linkage while orbiting at 5,000 feet, forcing a precautionary landing in a field. Post-landing inspection confirmed the loose linkage, which was reinstalled to restore normal engine operation.

synopsis: Pilots in two different aircraft reported an unsafe departure by a third aircraft from, JWN, a very busy non-towered airport.
summary: A Cessna 172 flight instructor and student on final for Runway 20 at JWN executed a go-around after a Mooney departed Runway 2 directly toward them. The incident occurred because the departing pilot ignored traffic on the runway and the approach end, despite construction restrictions requiring back-taxiing and a terrain rise limiting visibility.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Heavy Transport Flight Crew were initially very high on an RNAV Approach. They aggressively caught up and then flew through the profile. The Captain then heard a terrain alert and then 'Obstacle'. He continued the approach and landed. The co-pilot had heard 'Obstacle, Pull UP'. The Captain concluded that he should have gone around.
summary: The flight crew, while hand-flying an RNAV approach in VMC, received conflicting terrain alerts after the Pilot Monitoring reported appearing low. The Captain believes they should have executed a go-around upon hearing a "Pull Up" alert, though the specific alert sequence remains disputed between the pilots.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Large transport flight crew were cleared for an RNAV Visual Approach. They were fully configured, but at about 500 ft AGL they received a TCAS Traffic Alert. They observed two helicopters flying close to each other and about 200 feet lower than them. They executed a missed approach and returned for an uneventful landing.
summary: The flight crew executing an RNAV Visual Approach to Runway 19R at LAS received a TCAS Traffic Alert at 500 ft AGL upon spotting two helicopters 200 feet below. The pilot initiated a go-around due to the unreported traffic and subsequently landed uneventfully on Runway 25L.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Large Transport flight crew reported being assigned a runway different from what they expected while taxiing out for takeoff. They neglected to brief the revised taxi route and missed the airport sign 'all aircraft hold here' short of Taxiway F. They did not hold short and ATC called to admonish them.
summary: Pilots departing LAX on Runway 25R missed the "hold short" sign at Taxiway F while programming the FMC for a runway change. They entered the intersection before Tower inquired, attributing the error to distraction and suggesting Ground should have explicitly cleared them to hold short of F.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A flight crew descended below the DCA RNAV RNP Runway 19 crossing altitudes and at about 700 ft the EGPWS alerted 'CAUTION TERRAIN' 'OBSTACLE, OBSTACLE' 'PULL UP.' The pilot flying responded and continued to land. The crew did not see the autopilot transition from VNAV PATH to VNAV SPD.
summary: The Pilot Monitoring on an RNAV RNP 19 approach to DCA Runway 19 failed to notice the aircraft descended below 700' at JUBOL due to distraction by prohibited airspace. This triggered GPWS warnings, prompting an immediate climb after the aircraft switched from VNAV PATH to VNAV SPEED.

synopsis: A B757 stopped short of the gate during taxi in because the autoparking and Marshaller gave conflicting directions. While waiting for a tow in, a another aircraft's ground crew pushed their aircraft to where it's winglet struck the B757's horizontal stabilizer.
summary: The First Officer and Line Check Airman stopped a Boeing 757 at Gate XX due to conflicting automated and non-standard marshaller guidance. While awaiting a tow-in, another aircraft pushed back and struck the right horizontal stabilizer, damaging the stabilizer tip and shearing off the other aircraft's winglet.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported loss of left hydraulic system after landing.
summary: The flight crew of a Boeing 757 discovered a left hydraulic system leak during taxi after landing, caused by a cracked return line on the left engine thrust reverser. They stopped the leak by pulling the left engine fire handle, allowing the aircraft to be towed to the gate after a 58-minute delay.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported his Captain was unaware of a special procedure that was not being displayed on their iPads.
summary: The First Officer and Captain encountered a discrepancy regarding a missing Ops Alert for max thrust takeoffs on a 737 at SFO during preflight. The Captain's reliance on an incomplete Mobile App created a systematic threat, though the crew resolved the issue by verifying the alert and proceeding with max thrust.

synopsis: B737 FO reported that new before takeoff checklist resulted in a heads-down moment for the FO that led to a taxiway incursion.
summary: The First Officer and Captain rushed the before takeoff checklist while taxiing to Runway 1, causing the First Officer to miss the Captain's early turn onto intersection Echo. Although the takeoff was incident-free, the reporter attributed the deviation to the pressure of traffic and a cumbersome new checklist that distracted the First Officer.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported the flying First Officer released control of the aircraft without warning below 100 feet AGL on short final in gusty wind conditions.
summary: The Captain and First Officer were landing a jet at CLT in gusty winds when the First Officer lost centerline control and abruptly released the controls at 75 feet AGL. The Captain assumed control to execute a safe landing, attributing the event to the First Officer's inability to maintain control and failure to properly exchange controls.

synopsis: Medium Transport aircraft taxiing out on Taxiway C at KLAX stopped abruptly to avoid a possible collision with a Heavy Transport being pushed back onto the taxiway.
summary: The pilot stopped on Taxiway C while holding short of Terminal 6 to avoid a [Company] heavy aircraft whose tail was too close to the centerline. The pilot stopped 150 feet from a potential collision after the other aircraft's tug operator halted the pushback, and Ground Control subsequently apologized.

synopsis: An ERJ175 flight crew reported Maintenance MEL'ed both FMS's found inoperative during preflight. Following the day's flight the crew questioned the MEL and believed 1 FMS was required for flight even though the database was out of data.
summary: The flight crew and a mechanic encountered an invalid Nav database preventing FMS input, leading to a deferred dispatch under MEL 34-61-00-2. The crew later realized the MEL was likely misapplied because the FMSs were non-functional, not just expired, causing confusion over the aircraft's legal status.

synopsis: EC-130 Instructor Pilot reported an NMAC with a Citation in the vicinity of RVS airport.
summary: During an EC130B4 instrument training approach at Jones Riverside, a Cessna Citation passed within 75 feet horizontally and 15 feet vertically after the Citation pilot relied on the helicopter crew's radio statement that they were clear of the runway. The near miss occurred because the Citation pilot lacked positive visual identification of the helicopter before landing.

synopsis: EMB-120ER Captain reported left engine duct leak issue shortly after takeoff. The engine was shut down and the flight returned to departure airport.
summary: Shortly after takeoff, a left engine duct leak warning prompted the crew to level off, perform the QRH, and shut down the engine. The aircraft returned for a single-engine landing, and post-flight inspection revealed no visible damage, allowing a single-engine taxi to the hangar.

synopsis: After landing a C206 pilot became aurally overload with both ATC taxi instructions and the aircraft TIS ground 'TRAFFIC-TRAFFIC' alerts and consequently missed ATC instructions to hold short of both runway and taxiways.
summary: The pilot reported that a Traffic Advisory System alert masked the end of Tower taxi instructions, causing a missed frequency change to Ground. The pilot later contacted Ground and Tower to resolve the issue, noting no hazards occurred but planning to check aircraft settings to prevent recurrence.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: Aircraft was assigned 270 knots at 13,000 feet and did not reduce to 250 knots below 10,000 feet.
summary: A CJ-3 pilot reported being assigned 270 knots at 13,000 feet and maintaining speeds above 250 knots below 10,000 feet during descent and approach. The pilot sought clarification on whether assigned speeds override the 250-knot limit below 10,000 feet, noting no safety conflicts occurred.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: A twin turboprop pilot reported executing a go around after encountering wake turbulence in trail of an A319 on approach to MYNN.
summary: The pilot encountered severe wake turbulence from an A319 while on final for ILS 14 at 1,700 feet. After deviating and executing a missed approach on a 140 heading, the crew completed a normal second approach and landed on runway 14.

synopsis: A Cessna Citation pilot described an excessively hot cabin along with a duct overheat warning that resulted in a return to the departure airport. Subsequent inspection revealed a cracked pre-cooler.
summary: After departure, a pilot reported excessive rear cabin heat, an abnormal smell, and a 'Duct O'Heat R' caution, prompting a return to the departure airport. Investigation identified a cracked pre-cooler in the right engine as the cause, requiring immediate repair.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Medium Transport flight crew lost their right side tires on takeoff. The consulted with operations, burned down fuel and diverted to an airport with a 10,800 foot long runway. They landed successfully and evacuated the aircraft without complications.
summary: The Pilot in Command and crew of Aircraft X experienced a right-side tire blowout during takeoff from KFOK, causing vibrations and a pull to the right. After burning fuel and diverting to Stewart International Airport, the aircraft landed on the left side of the runway, requiring an emergency evacuation once the right side contacted the surface.

synopsis: A PA28 Student Pilot reports seeing a spherical object 300 feet abeam and at pattern altitude, which is reported to the Tower.
summary: A pilot on downwind at 2,400 feet reported a small spherical object passing the aircraft's left side. The tower controller acknowledged the report and stated she also observed the object through binoculars.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported loss of power in the pattern, resulting in a forced landing on a nearby road.
summary: The pilot, flying VFR with flight following during the approach phase, experienced a total engine power loss at 800 feet while turning base. The pilot executed an emergency landing on a nearby road, citing no visible wires or suitable alternatives, and awaited emergency response after securing the aircraft.

synopsis: A Tundra pilot failed to remove the engine cooling air intake plugs which caused an engine overheat and seizure. A safe off airport landing followed.
summary: The PIC and owner-builder of an experimental tundra aircraft experienced an engine seizure and off-field landing due to the pilot forgetting to remove air intake plugs during pre-flight. The resulting engine overheating caused a forced landing in an open field with no injuries or crop damage.

synopsis: Newly qualified B737 First Officer described the challenges encountered on a flight to MPTO, citing his minimal training as contributing.
summary: A recently trained First Officer and Captain flew a 737 to MPTO, encountering route unfamiliarity, spotty VHF, and missing FMC data for the RNAV approach. The crew manually vectored onto the ILS 3R and later used ACARS for departure clearance after discovering the aircraft had datalink capabilities.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 left wing fuel tank full sensor malfunctioned requiring over wing fueling which a second truck driver completed. After takeoff, the left main landing gear indicated unsafe so the flight returned to the departure airport where the fueler's grounding clip was found still attached.
summary: A CRJ200 crew received a gear disagree warning after takeoff caused by a fueler leaving a bonding cable clamp attached to the left main gear during unannounced over-wing fueling. The crew manually extended the gear, landed safely, and canceled the flight after discovering the foreign object and a faulty high-level fuel sensor.

synopsis: A B737-800 Captain noted low left side duct pressure during climb but normal pressure at cruise and suspected a faulty bleed valve. Maintenance, as per company policy, would not discuss the issue in flight stating the QRH was the crew's only available resource.
summary: During climb, the pilot observed low left duct pressure, suspecting a faulty 5th stage bleed valve. Maintenance refused to discuss the system intricacies while airborne, citing new management policy, though the valve was later confirmed faulty and replaced.

synopsis: Maintenance technicians reported that they were notified of a loose wing panel after a passenger noticed it fluttering in flight. Several fasteners were found missing from the panel.
summary: After arrival, the crew discovered an access panel over the landing gear retract actuator 551CT on the left wing was fluttering due to 15 missing screws. Mechanics installed the fasteners to secure the panel and made a log entry.

synopsis: A corporate flight crew was asked to keep their speed at 300 KTS for traffic at FL240. During descent they asked the TRACON about speed and were told 'Keep it up;' then reduce. After landing they were notified a pilot speed deviation had been filed for over 250 KTS below 10,000 feet.
summary: Pilots received conflicting speed instructions from ATC while descending from FL240 to 8,000 feet, leading to a pilot deviation report for exceeding 250 KTS below 10,000 feet. The crew attributed the incident to ambiguous ATC phraseology that failed to clarify the standard speed restriction despite their direct query.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Corporate crew checked M91 destination weather from two sources before departure and found none. While preparing for the GPS Runway 22, ZME notified the pilots the runway was closed. Aviation Digital Data Service (ADDS) was the only site with the NOTAM which a contractor erroneously issued while the LED PAPI and runway lights were installed.
summary: A pilot flying a GPS approach to runway 22 at M91 was informed by Memphis Center that the approach was invalid due to an erroneously issued NOTAM by an airport maintenance contractor. The NOTAM was missing from FAA-approved vendors, causing a clearance error that was only resolved after contacting Nashville Approach and the airport manager.

synopsis: An air taxi aircraft struck a bird on the takeoff roll from PHMU and continued to their destination where Maintenance found bird strike evidence on one of the propeller blades.
summary: Two pilots on a takeoff roll at PHMU experienced a bird strike near rotation speed, resulting in minor residue on a propeller blade. The crew continued to their destination despite the impact, later admitting their decision was unsafe due to fatigue and the availability to abort or return.

synopsis: A C210 nose gear collapsed during the landing roll causing a propeller strike.
summary: The pilot reported that after landing on runway 17, the nose gear collapsed while slowing to exit, causing the propeller to strike the ground and the aircraft to skid 25-30 yards. There were no injuries.

synopsis: Two Hot Air Balloon fabric envelopes made contact during their approach to land because of significant terrain changes including the mix of road surfaces, open field, water, and trees.
summary: Two hot air balloons experienced incidental fabric contact during initial approach to land due to advection caused by changing terrain surfaces. The pilots executed evasive action to separate and landed safely at an alternate site with no injuries or damage.

synopsis: Trainee Controller was working one aircraft eastbound at 33,000 feet and one aircraft westbound at 34,000 feet on the same airway. The trainee climbed the eastbound aircraft to 35,000 feet head on into confliction with the westbound traffic. The instructor took over the sector issuing instructions to both aircraft to maintain separation. The actions were too late and separation was lost.
summary: A radar trainee issued a climb clearance to Aircraft X at 33,000 feet toward Aircraft Y at 34,000 feet, causing a conflict alert. The instructor intervened with turns and descents, but separation was likely lost, resulting in the termination of the trainee's training.

synopsis: The reporter states that aircraft repeatedly climb to 12,000 feet on their airports' SID but are supposed to be climbing to 16,000 feet. The SID assigned altitude is 12,000 feet.
summary: An air traffic controller intercepted Aircraft X from Company X on the BOISE 2 Departure for climbing to 12,000 feet instead of the required 16,000 feet. The controller attributed the error to conflicting SID instructions and clearance phraseology that frequently confuse pilots receiving clearances via PDC.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Three different ARTCC sectors working three aircraft in confliction with each other. Very confusing scenario due to the different sectors taking point out coordination with different intentions to resolving the traffic conflictions instead of one controller working the aircraft with one plan for separation.
summary: An air traffic controller stopped Aircraft X at 31,000 feet and issued a 30-degree left turn to avoid a near midair collision with climbing Aircraft Y. The reporter attributed the conflict to Sector Z failing to manage the situation within their own airspace.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier crew failed to select the TCAS TA Mode on approach to DEN Runway 16L. After a RA, the First Officer remembered the Company TA Mode policy. He reminded the Captain who selected TA and continued the approach.
summary: The pilot neglected to select TA mode on final for Runway 16L, triggering a "Monitor Vertical Descent" RA that was complied with before switching to TA and continuing the approach. Although a "Climb" RA appeared during the switch, the crew landed safely, though the pilot later questioned if a go-around was required per QRH procedures.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reported that Flight Attendant procedure of hanging and removing liquor and recycle bags from cabin door handles caused inflight illumination of door warning lights.
summary: During climb and cruise, a flight crew received aft service door warnings caused by a flight attendant hanging a liquor bag on the handle, which triggered the unlock mechanism. Despite existing safety bulletins prohibiting this practice, the crew member continued the behavior, prompting the pilot to reiterate the restriction on subsequent flights.

synopsis: At 10,000 feet on climbout, an A319 number one engine compressor stalled with the associated ECAM, thrust loss and yaw. The flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The pilot reported an Engine 1 compressor stall with thrust loss and yaw at 10,000 feet MSL during climb out. After advising ATC, the aircraft returned to the departure airport.

synopsis: A CRJ900 flight crew reported a deviation from cleared departure route when they were distracted by the bright early morning sun and a wake turbulence encounter departing ATL in trail of a B737.
summary: During a Novss7 departure from Runway 9L, the crew encountered wake turbulence and bright sun, causing the Pilot Flying to select Heading mode instead of NAV. This resulted in a track deviation and autopilot disengagement, which the crew attributed to distraction and role confusion during the turbulence event.

synopsis: A Medium Transport flight crew misunderstood the clearance, 'Direct to MYFUT' on the ILS30 to KOAK and selected the similar sounding fix, MITOE by mistake.
summary: The pilot reported a clearance misunderstanding during arrival at KOAK where poor radio quality and similar-sounding waypoints (MYFUT vs. MITOE) caused an incorrect direct selection. The error was corrected after controller verification, resulting in a minor heading adjustment and an uneventful remainder of the approach.

synopsis: VFR aircraft that was on a Class B airspace clearance had their radar service terminated upon exiting the Class B. They were given a frequency change to contact the Tower of their destination, but were already in the Towers airspace. TRACON could have accomplished the coordination with the tower issued a late frequency change or TRACON did not coordinate and just shipped the aircraft to the Tower.
summary: A pilot diverting en-route for a restroom stop entered Class B airspace and received a Bravo clearance but was abruptly terminated from radar services without a handoff to the tower. The pilot believes the Bravo controller failed to coordinate, causing an unannounced entry into tower airspace that frustrated the tower controller, though no actual safety impact occurred.

synopsis: C172 Instructor Pilot descended below normal approach altitude at a non-towered airport due to conflict with a biplane and a helicopter while maneuvering for landing.
summary: The instructor pilot and student encountered a biplane entering the pattern on left crosswind for Runway 28, requiring a steep descending turn to avoid conflict. The instructor later descended below VASI limits to maintain separation from the biplane circling the windsock, resulting in a full stop landing.

synopsis: C172 Pilot In Command (PIC) flying a practice ILS approach to the left parallel runway missed the fact the Second In Command (SIC) misunderstood an ATC call as clearance to switch to the ILS for the right runway. SIC switched NAV to the right runway ILS without PIC being aware of the change until ATC advised of the course deviation from the left runway. Lack of crew coordination and electronic charts were cited as contributing to the incident.
summary: Two pilots conducting a practice ILS approach to Runway 18L inadvertently intercepted the 18R localizer after the safety pilot misunderstood ATC and switched the electronic chart without the pilot flying noticing. The error was corrected by Tower after the pilot realized the discrepancy, with the reporter citing inadequate crew coordination and electronic chart limitations as the primary causes.

synopsis: An aircraft entered a NOTAM closed taxiway. The Local Controller had been advising aircraft to exit the runway at a taxiway other than the closed one. The Ground Controller was able to tell vehicles to hold short of the taxiway to prevent a confliction with the aircraft.
summary: A ground controller, overwhelmed by vehicle traffic and task saturation, allowed Aircraft X to cross a partially closed Taxiway X north of Runway XXR due to a lack of visual barricades and ambiguous handover instructions. The controller later realized the aircraft had stopped short of the runway and attributed the incident to poor airport construction management and insufficient visual cues.

synopsis: A Controller was told by his supervisor to temporarily change his airspace and create the boundary on his radar display with the draw feature. The Reporter felt this was a violation of rules and unsafe as there was no coordination for an airspace change and the radar software was not adapted to accommodate the supervisor's airspace change plan.
summary: An air traffic controller reported being forced by a Front Line Manager to manually draw an illegal airspace boundary in ERAM software instead of using standard point-outs. This unauthorized procedure created safety risks because adjacent sectors were not notified of the change, potentially leading to airspace violations and increased workload.

synopsis: B737 First Officer attributed Captain's improper positioning of the fuel pump and crossfeed switches to differences in B737 models flown by the company and to the fact that the Captain and the First Officer usually flew the newer models.
summary: During cruise, the crew discovered a 4,000-pound fuel imbalance caused by the Captain inadvertently opening the crossfeed valve while turning off center tank pumps. The imbalance was corrected before landing, attributed to infrequent aircraft familiarity, scan limitations, and procedural differences between aircraft models.

synopsis: B737 Flight Crew was advised by ATC that another aircraft saw fuel streaming from their left engine on takeoff. Gauges and odor confirmed fuel loss, engine shut down in accordance with QRH and Crew returned to land.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced a confirmed left engine fuel leak during departure, evidenced by strong odors and unbalanced fuel gauges. They returned to the airport, shut down the left engine per QRH, and landed safely with no fire indications found by ARFF.

synopsis: An air carrier Captain reported his First Officer had difficulty flying two attempted night visual approaches to MFR. High sink rate with an EGPWS alert and speed control were concerns.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced an unstable visual approach to Runway 32, resulting in EGPWS warnings and a go-around due to excessive descent rate and airspeed. The Captain attributed the event to the First Officer's lack of proficiency in judging position and altitude, noting his own delayed intervention.

synopsis: During landing the left brake of a Hawker 800XP momentarily locked causing an abrupt left shift and flat spots on tires #1 and #2 which required maintenance.
summary: The pilot reported that upon landing, the aircraft veered violently left due to an unseen cause, requiring the nose gear to be forced down to regain steering control. The event resulted in severe vibration, a smoke plume at the touchdown point, and major flat spots on both left main gear tires.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A medium transport jet crew on approach to MFR needed S turns and activated TAWS during the LOC BC DME-B Runway 32. They were surprised by the 5.98 glide path angle discovered after landing.
summary: The pilot flew a steep 5.98-degree LOC BC DME-B approach to Medford Runway 32, performing S-turns and receiving TAWS warnings due to the high glide path angle. The crew stabilized by 500 feet and landed safely, attributing the difficulty to the unusual approach geometry and recommending specific training for this procedure.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An Airbus pilot described the frustration of the crew as they observed, and attempted to assist, an inexperienced contract maintenance technician perform a relatively simple system recheck required per an MEL.
summary: Flight crew assisted an incompetent ZZZ contract mechanic performing a required AEVC test on a deferred Skin Air Outlet Valve. The mechanic failed to follow instructions or identify correct circuit breakers, causing a 45-minute delay until a second technician completed the test in five minutes with crew intervention.

synopsis: An air carrier Pilot reported a failed cockpit window in cruise and describe the challenges to communicate with the company operations center to confirm continuing to planned destination.
summary: The First Officer reported a loud bang and windshield crack during cruise, but QRH checks confirmed normal pressurization and no inner pane damage. Despite initial Satcom failures, the crew contacted Dispatch and Maintenance via ACARS, received concurrence to continue, and completed the flight safely.

synopsis: A B767 crew reported the Marshaller signaled clear to taxi, but after moving several feet the nose tires contacted the tow bar which was disconnected but not moved. After the nose tires were changed, the Marshaller's taxi clearance was again inappropriate because the equipment had not moved.
summary: During pushback, the crew moved the aircraft after ground crew displayed a pin and salute while the tow bar remained under the nose gear, damaging both nose tires. The incident occurred because the marshaller incorrectly signaled clearance before the tug and tow bar were fully removed.

synopsis: A B737-800 Captain reported after landing the TOGA system engaged before reverse thrust was activated. Thrust levers were physically held at idle while the speedbrake and reversers were engaged.
summary: A pilot reported five abnormal landing events on an aircraft where spoilers retracted, autobrakes disengaged, and throttles advanced after touchdown. This caused increased stopping distance and required manual intervention to maintain idle thrust and deploy reversers.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier Captain reported difficulty avoiding Cotopaxi volcanic ash departing on the SEQM/UIO CONDOCOCHA NORTH FLOW DEPARTURE Runway 18. Avoiding ash on a night departure may not be possible.
summary: The flight crew departing Quito on Runway 18 executed an evasive turn to avoid a volcanic ash cloud from Cotopaxi that was closer than Dispatch's 35-mile estimate indicated. The crew reported that Dispatch failed to relay their pilot report to the subsequent night crew, citing inadequate briefing data and delayed satellite imagery as the cause.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician (AMT) with extensive DC-10 Engine Reverser experience describes what he believes to be inaccurate Boeing Lamm schematics that have contributed to engine pneumatic lines being attached at incorrect positions on Dual Switcher Valves on GE-CF6-80 engines. The Switcher Valves are part of the FAAs Thrust Reverser Safety Enhancement System A.D.
summary: A maintenance report identified that PRSOV and OPSOV lines to TRAS Lock Engine Duel Switcher valves on all company DC-10s are connected backwards. This error causes thrust reversers to stow during auto re-stow testing and risks PRSOV opening in flight, prompting a recommendation to correct the connections and verify schematics.

synopsis: The owner of a Light Sport Aircraft and his Flight Instructor experienced a high oil temperature and low oil pressure indication condition and elected to return to the field. The instructor was making the landing and over-controlled the aircraft, resulting in a runway excursion with damage to the wing tip and aileron.
summary: The pilot and owner experienced high oil temperature and low pressure warnings during climbout in a light sport aircraft. While returning to land, the pilot over-controlled the unfamiliar controls, causing a wingtip strike that damaged the aileron and light.

synopsis: The pilot of a tail wheeled aircraft lost control on landing due to gusty winds, resulting in a runway excursion. The aircraft may have struck a taxiway light, however no damage to aircraft was identified.
summary: The pilot ground looped the aircraft during rollout on Runway 24 due to strong gusts from 210 degrees exceeding rudder effectiveness. The airplane veered into the grass and rotated 180 degrees, but inspection revealed no damage and subsequent flight showed no abnormalities.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: Pilot took evasive action to avoid a drone near 99CL.
summary: A pilot cruising at 6,500 feet near Adelanto executed an evasive maneuver to avoid a drone detected by PCAS directly ahead. The controller issued a conflict warning but lacked control of the drone, which the pilot believes would have caused a collision without the pilot's action.

synopsis: A PA-28 Pilot experienced an engine failure on final approach. He comments on the demands between performing an engine failure checklist and locating a suitable landing location.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine failure at 600 feet on final approach and prioritized selecting a landing site over running the checklist. The outcome was no injury or damage, and the pilot attributed the event to a need for earlier pre-landing checklist completion.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot departed S43 Runway 33. At 200 feet the pilot turned left to avoid a parachutist which resulted in a NMAC with a helicopter in the landing pattern.
summary: During takeoff from Runway 33 at S43, the pilot deviated from the noise abatement turn to avoid a skydiver crossing the runway, inadvertently converging with a training helicopter at the same altitude. The pilot aborted the turn to avoid a likely midair collision and continued the flight safely.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Aircraft route inbound to TEB conflicts with approach course to LGA. These aircraft are procedurally separated. A VFR aircraft departed HPN along these routes and climbed VFR through two other aircraft. The VFR aircraft complied with all procedures. The reporter feels HPN should have its airspace classification changed and procedures put in place to prevent this occurrence in the future.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a near midair collision involving three aircraft (two IFR arrivals and one VFR departure) merging near HPN while descending or climbing between 3,000 and 5,500 feet. The controller attributed the incident to a lack of control over VFR traffic in the current Class D airspace, suggesting a change to Class C to prevent future accidents.

synopsis: New departure procedures at SFO have a 3,000 foot published restriction for departures. Previous departure procedures are still issued to some aircraft due to aircraft capabilities. The previous departure procedures do not have the 3,000 foot restriction. The Controller had 3,500 foot Class B airspace crossing traffic. The Controller thought departing jet traffic was restricted to 3,000 feet, but it was not because it was still flying the old departure procedure.
summary: An air traffic controller managed a potential conflict between Aircraft Y transitioning SFO Bravo airspace at 3,500 feet and departing Aircraft X. The controller advised Aircraft X of traffic and clarified standard 3,000-foot restrictions, suspecting the tower failed to issue this limit via PDC due to new airspace procedures.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: FSS controller approved SVFR operations for an inbound and departure simultaneously. The Controller thought he heard one of the aircraft agree to 'Maintain Visual Separation'. During a review of a tape recording of this period it was determined that the aircraft did not volunteer to maintain visual separation. Simultaneous SVFR operations as this require one of the aircraft to maintain visual separation. The Controller misunderstood one of the aircrafts' transmissions.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a Special VFR clearance to Aircraft Y departing Yakutat after Aircraft X agreed to visual separation, but the controller misinterpreted Aircraft Y's acceptance of the clearance as agreement to that separation. The supervisor identified this as a deviation caused by the controller's failure to use standard phraseology to explicitly confirm Aircraft Y's acceptance of visual separation from Aircraft X.

synopsis: A small aircraft pilot executed a go-around due to another small aircraft on the runway for departure. The pilot on go-around was unable to establish communication with the Tower due to frequency congestion. Tower personnel recognized the situation as did the pilot. Pilot's initial communication with Tower was advising them they were executing the go-around. ATC training was in progress in the Tower.
summary: A trainee controller cleared Aircraft Y for takeoff while Aircraft X was on final, causing a go-around due to the trainee forgetting the inbound and supervisor pressure. The pilot reported inability to check in at 3 miles due to frequency congestion, while the controller cited poor pad management and distractions as contributing factors.

synopsis: An ARTCC Supervisor observed a Controller intentionally allow two aircraft to pass with less than prescribed separation. The aircraft were on diverging courses but passing behind with less than 1,000 feet vertical or 5 miles lateral separation. The Supervisor observed the Controller manually enter an altitude in one of the aircrafts' data block to make it appear the aircraft had the prescribed separation minima.
summary: An observer reported that a junior air traffic controller failed to maintain separation between two aircraft at 20,000 feet and instead disabled Mode C to hide the 4.5nm and 900-foot minimum separation breach. The controller took no corrective action or responsibility, prompting the observer to file a safety report regarding this performance issue.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: A C525 pilot at FL400 reported a Crew Alert System (CAS) Low Oil Pressure light and requested clearance to their departure airport. The controller working the flight vectored another aircraft to allow an enroute descent. The pilot discovered a loose engine oil cap.
summary: A C525 pilot reported a right engine low oil pressure caused by a loose filler cap, forcing a precautionary shutdown and descent from FL400 to return to the departure airport. Air Traffic Control vectored the aircraft and other traffic to avoid separation loss, resulting in a safe landing after the pilot secured the engine and managed the descent.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An SJU Controller failed to issue a full route clearance after missing the note in the remarks of the flight plan. Aircraft became airborne on a closed airway.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a clearance to Aircraft X without noticing a Full Route Clearance (FRC) remark on the flight strip due to poor coordination regarding duplicate flight plans. The controller subsequently removed the FRC remark without informing the pilot, potentially routing the aircraft onto a closed airway.

synopsis: The Captain of a redeye flight to SBGR heard a clearance to 5,000 feet. The foreign Controller's clearance was actually to 5,500 feet which the flying First Officer heard correctly. When level at 5,000 feet, which the Captain wanted, the Controller commented on the incorrect altitude.
summary: During an ILS 9R descent at SBGR, the crew descended to 5000 feet after conflicting clearances from a controller with poor English, despite a 5500-foot radar minimum. The controller later stated the aircraft should have been at 5500 feet, revealing a clearance discrepancy caused by communication errors and crew fatigue.

synopsis: A Captain and IOE First Officer received a B757-300 at departure time from Maintenance. A thorough preflight caught most switch position errors, but they missed the autothrottles causing a long roll on takeoff with reduced-reduced takeoff thrust.
summary: The Captain and First Officer of a Boeing 757-300 departed with the autothrottle switch in manual mode due to a missed cockpit check. The Captain reduced thrust to prevent perceived overboost, resulting in a reduced-power takeoff with a slow rotation and low climb rate until the switch was corrected at 800 feet.

synopsis: B757 flight crew, preparing to depart on an international oceanic flight, received a departure clearance that did not agree with their filed flight plan. When Dispatch was queried, it was noted that the crew had been issued a flight release which was 2 days old. After a 32 minute ground delay, the situation was satisfactorily resolved.
summary: During taxi-out, the crew discovered a routing discrepancy caused by using a flight release from two days prior, leading to incorrect FMS input. The flight was held in a remote spot until correct paperwork was delivered, highlighting safety barriers lost due to rushed briefings and lack of review facilities.

synopsis: During landing rollout in heavy rain, the crew of a CRJ-900 experienced an initial loss of braking action. Crew received an A/SKID OUTBD caution message and an OB GND SPLR FAULT status message during the landing roll. The anti-skid was selected OFF and then back to ON after stopping the aircraft. Braking action was adequate for their taxi to the ramp.
summary: During a wet landing at Charlotte, the flight crew experienced total brake failure despite full pedal deflection and anti-skid cycling, likely caused by an Anti-Skid Control Unit malfunction. The aircraft was stopped using maximum reverse thrust and manual spoilers, exiting at taxiway C11 with no tire damage.

synopsis: Upon glideslope capture during ILS approach to TEB, Challenger 605 crew experienced a sudden nose-up attitude excursion. Pilot flying over-rode the autopilot and completed the approach and landing.
summary: During an ILS approach to TEB at 2000 feet, the aircraft climbed 300 feet after the glide slope signal jumped to the top of the scale. The Pilot Flying arrested the climb, and the reporter attributed the event to a known issue with the glide slope on this specific ILS.

synopsis: The flight crew of a regional jet landed without a clearance. This was due several factors including flight deck workload, fatigue, and radio management in a busy approach environment.
summary: The Pilot Flying and a new First Officer landed without explicit clearance after failing to switch to the tower frequency due to fatigue and communication issues. The crew did not execute a missed approach despite a departing aircraft on the runway, landing safely because the runway was clear.

synopsis: An Embraer Phenom flight crew described a leak in the crew oxygen system that resulted in a descent and an uneventful diversion.
summary: Pilots of a Phenom 300 in cruise at FL410 experienced a rapid oxygen leak caused by a failed metal coupling on the captain's mask hose. They descended to 10,000 feet after ATC clearances, cancelled the emergency, and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: A319 Captain and Flight Attendant prevented a contract Maintenance Technician from opening armed cabin door and blowing slide into occupied jetway.
summary: A flight attendant intervened when a maintenance technician attempted to open an armed L1 door while a gate agent stood on the jetway. The crew stopped the action, disarmed the door, and prevented a slide deployment that could have caused injury or death.

synopsis: Crew of a Challenger 300 was cleared for ILS approach to 31C at MDW and to maintain 210 knots until RUNTS, a fix 6.7 miles from the localizer. The crew believed that flying the glideslope from their current position would require them to fly below the Class B airspace, which has a floor of 3600 feet in this area. Crew asked ATC about the clearance to violate the FAR restriction of airspeed below 200 knots below Class B airspace. ATC confirmed the 210-knot clearance, the crew elected to maintain 200 knots as required by FAR 91.117(c).
summary: The pilot reported that while inbound to MDW on an ILS 31C approach, ATC instructed maintaining 210 knots below Class B airspace, conflicting with FAR 91.117(c). The crew slowed to 200 knots before descending below 3,600 feet to comply with regulations, noting the controller did not object to the speed reduction.

synopsis: An Airbus flight crew experienced a failure of the Flight Management Guidance Computer #1. This failure, coupled with a previously deferred Multi-Purpose Control and Display Unit #2, rendered the aircraft incapable of continuing to navigate in an RNAV environment. After assistance was requested from Air Traffic Control, headings were issued, and the flight proceeded safely to the destination airport.
summary: During cruise at FL340, the crew experienced repeated autopilot and auto-thrust disengagements alongside FMGC failures, with MCDU2 deferred inop. The aircraft landed normally after ATC provided vectors due to RNAV navigation loss, caused by FMGC1 failure and the inability to input data to FMGC2.

synopsis: B757 flight crew were unable to retract the landing gear or arm Autobrakes, returned to departure airport and landed overweight without incident.
summary: The crew experienced a landing gear handle stuck in the OFF position and an AutoBrakes failure shortly after rotation. They returned for a safe, overweight landing with fire services monitoring brake temperatures, taxiing to the gate without incident.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported that, during deplaning of passengers, a Ramp Agent advised that the aircraft's nose gear was rising and the tail was falling. Passenger deplaning was stopped until aircraft stabilized.
summary: During deplaning, a ramp agent reported the nose gear left the pavement, causing the nose to rise and tail to fall, prompting the crew to halt passenger exit. The gear settled without further incident, though the crew noted they did not receive the expected ACARS notification regarding potential loading issues.

synopsis: The flight crew of an Airbus A319 detected smoke in both the cockpit and cabin. A descent was immediately initiated and a diversion to a suitable airfield was successfully accomplished. Troubleshooting revealed that a faulty air conditioning pack was the source of the smoke.
summary: The flight crew experienced smoke in the cockpit and cabin during cruise, prompting an expedited descent to 12,000 ft. The cause was identified as a faulty pack regulator valve on pack 1 after turning off the air conditioning packs, allowing a safe landing with the defect deferred.

synopsis: CRJ700 flight crew, cleared to cross an active runway, stopped when Ground Controller subsequently issued an urgent command to stop due to another aircraft having been cleared to land on the same runway. Landing aircraft executed a go-around.
summary: The flight crew aborted a runway crossing after hearing a Cirrus go around, suspecting a communication breakdown between Tower and Ground regarding a landing clearance. The pilot attributed the near-miss to the busy airport environment and the difficulty of spotting small aircraft without lights.

synopsis: CRJ200 Captain reported that a Flight Attendant advised them of smoke and fumes in the cabin. Unable to determine the source and after accomplishing QRH items, the crew diverted for an uneventful landing. After refusing pressure by Company Maintenance to resume passenger flight to destination, the crew flew to their destination without passengers and with all cabin lights off.
summary: The flight crew encountered smoke/fumes at FL270, landed at ZZZ, and found no cause despite strong electrical smells. Rejecting maintenance advice to fly with passengers, the crew flew the aircraft empty to ZZZ1 with cabin lights off and the cockpit door open.

synopsis: A flight instructor described an engine problem on landing. The engine was unable to run with the throttle pulled back to idle due to the loss of the carburetor mixture screw.
summary: During a student landing approach, the engine and propeller stopped after flaring, causing a power-off landing and ground roll to a taxiway. The cause was a missing screw that fell off during flight, requiring maintenance to remove the cowling for repair the next day.

synopsis: The Pilot of an Air-Taxi operation reported a near-mid-air-collision with a single engine aircraft that was climbing out of a non-towered airport. The Air-Taxi pilot was making position reports, but the other departing pilot was not be making reports. The Traffic Alerting system provided notification which allowed for evasive action to prevent a collision.
summary: A pilot reported a near mid-air collision with a single-engine aircraft while climbing to 3,000 feet at an uncontrolled airport. The Traffic Alerting System failed to detect the other aircraft until it was dangerously close, forcing an evasive maneuver after the other pilot admitted he never saw them.

synopsis: B-757 flight crew noticed that the preferred approach was not in the FMC database. The crew flew a visual approach coupled with manually inputted waypoints to the final approach fix.
summary: The captain of a Boeing 757 found the preferred VOR Z Rwy 10 approach missing from the FMC database at SXM, forcing a visual approach using raw data. The reporter attributed this to database development and quality control failures that allowed a defective release to reach operational aircraft.

synopsis: G-200 Captain reported he wrote up the aircraft for the autopilot disengaging and 'stiff ailerons.'
summary: The pilot reported an autopilot disengagement and stiff ailerons on Aircraft X, prompting an exit from RVSM airspace. Control forces normalized during descent into the 20,000-foot level, leading the pilot to classify the incident as a non-reportable NTSB event.

synopsis: While preparing to descend to the destination airport, regional jet crew experienced a 'Left Bleed Duct' warning annunciation. An emergency descent was accomplished and direct routing to the destination was facilitated by ATC. Upon landing the Captain elected to evacuate the aircraft due to considerable smoke in the cabin.
summary: The flight crew encountered a left bleed duct warning at FL240, triggering an emergency descent and subsequent evacuation due to smoke in the cabin. The aircraft landed normally, but the crew initiated an evacuation on the taxiway after discovering smoke and a burnt smell, citing the MEL for the inoperative right pack as a potential factor.

synopsis: During shutdown at the gate, A321 Captain noticed that the 1R cabin door warning was amber. Captain exited the cockpit and noticed a Flight Attendant pulling on the door handle with considerable force and that the door slide appeared to be disarmed. When the Flight Attendant let go of the handle, the door automatically opened and the emergency slide deployed.
summary: During post-arrival shutdown, a Flight Attendant struggled with a partially open 1R door while the slide remained armed. The door pneumatically forced open and deployed the slide when the crew member released his grip, an incident attributed to the attendant's inexperience on the Airbus.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew reported they had an electrical failure shortly after takeoff followed by a slat malfunction. Crew returned to departure airport.
summary: The crew experienced major electrical and flight control failures immediately after takeoff, losing five of six displays and encountering a left roll during climbout. The aircraft was vectored for an ILS landing after the crew consulted the QRH, noting a history of electrical malfunctions and a recent hydraulic leak repair.

synopsis: A pilot instructor in a SR20 reported an unstable cylinder heat temperature indication that prompted a return towards the departure airport.
summary: During climb out, a Pilot Instructor experienced fluctuating Cylinder Heat Temperature 6 indications that dropped to zero, causing engine roughness and vibration. The crew requested immediate vectors to intercept the localizer and landed safely without further issues.

aircraft: Gulfstream Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: While taxiing for takeoff, Gulfstream crew had to switch to four different ground controllers. During the final frequency switch the crew crossed a hold line marked with a red light bar. New Controller notified of the error and redirected the crew.
summary: The Pilot Flying crossed a red light bar on taxiway K while taxiing to Runway 32 after missing a hold instruction due to a delayed frequency change. The controller reported the event, but the pilot stated no safety impact occurred as the bar was for sequencing only and no runway incursion happened.

synopsis: Diamond DA-20 pilot reported a near-mid-air-collision while entering the traffic pattern of a non-towered airport. He discovered that his radio had not been tuned to the correct CTAF frequency.
summary: A Diamond DA-20 pilot and a single-engine Beechcraft pilot experienced a near-miss in the traffic pattern at ZZZ because the Diamond pilot transmitted on the wrong CTAF frequency (122.7 instead of 122.8). The Diamond pilot voluntarily gave way by turning right, and both aircraft landed safely without required evasive maneuvers.

aircraft: Gulfstream Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: G200 Captain reported a NMAC with a glider while inbound to PWK. Glider reportedly had no transponder and ATC was unaware of their position.
summary: A pilot flying an IFR approach to PWK at 5,000 feet and 250 knots encountered an untracked glider crossing ahead. The pilot manually banked right and descended 300 feet to avoid the glider, which ATC confirmed was not visible on radar.

synopsis: PA31 pilot and local FBO at a non-towered airport heard no transmissions on CTAF by a Gulfstream V aircraft holding short of the runway nor from a landing commuter jet. Reporter expressed concern with the practice of corporate and commuter aircraft communicating only with the local ATC Center and not utilizing CTAF.
summary: The pilot reported a runway incursion risk while back-taxiing Runway 7 after a Gulfstream and an inbound commuter jet failed to monitor CTAF. The pilot vacated the runway to avoid a collision, noting that both aircraft likely remained on Center frequency instead of using local advisories.

aircraft: Cessna Aircraft Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Single Engine Cessna pilot described a diversion due to weather. He was unable to contact any location facility, so he planned and departed for a different airport. Along the way he experienced communication problems and turbulence. Upon landing, he was advised that he had penetrated Class B airspace without a clearance.
summary: A pilot flying from Desert Rock to Boulder City encountered severe turbulence and radio communication failures, leading to an inadvertent Class B airspace penetration. The pilot was subsequently informed of the violation by the Las Vegas TRACON, which initiated an investigation despite the reported operational difficulties.

synopsis: A Flight Instructor described how his non-pilot aircraft owner began a descent without clearance.
summary: A flight instructor and an unlicensed owner in a multi-engine aircraft descended below assigned altitudes during IFR flight due to the instructor's complacency while splitting radio duties. The crew corrected the deviation after verifying the clearance with ATC, noting that low traffic and VFR conditions prevented a collision.

synopsis: CL605 Captain reported lining up on the right side of the runway, then drifting further right on the takeoff roll and eventually going off the runway onto grass. Takeoff was rejected and the aircraft returned to the centerline without damage. Reporter attributed the incident to fatigue and pilot pushing by the Company.
summary: After a 15-hour duty day, the fatigued Pilot in Command drifted right of center during takeoff due to distraction and a dragging brake, aborting before 80 knots. The aircraft returned to the hangar with no damage, though the pilot admitted to pushing despite exhaustion and company pressure to continue.

synopsis: Two pilots experienced smoke in the cockpit and a successful landing after receiving light gun signals.
summary: Pilots flying a VFR cruise at 6,500 feet smelled smoke from the aileron trim gauge, turned off the master switch, and landed without radio communications using light gun signals. A mechanic attributed the incident to an electrical short in the trim system, recommending instrument replacement and a dedicated circuit breaker.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: The pilot of a tail-wheeled aircraft described a runway excursion due to a failed tail wheel lock that caused loss of control during landing rollout.
summary: The pilot of a conventional gear aircraft veered left upon landing due to a damaged tail wheel lock that prevented steering correction. The aircraft departed the runway into grass, missed all obstacles, and was taxied to the hangar with no damage after the pilot inspected and disengaged the broken lock.

synopsis: The Pilot of a Husky A-1B described a ground loop on roll out due to an unexpected crosswind on landing.
summary: The pilot reported a ground loop during rollout on Runway 27 after the left wing rose due to a left crosswind. The pilot attributed the incident to insufficient left aileron input and potentially higher groundspeed caused by high elevation.

synopsis: B737 First Officer reported that MDW airport taxiways are not correctly charted during construction.
summary: The First Officer reported that the MDW 10-9 chart incorrectly annotated the reconfigured Taxiway P and its intersection with Taxiway N. Although the Captain's familiarity prevented an error, the reporter attributed the chart inaccuracy to poor Jeppesen quality control and the lack of digital construction updates.

synopsis: A 737 flight crew inadvertently left a fuel cross feed valve open. This resulted in a significant fuel imbalance, which was discovered during final approach. The crew elected to land with the imbalance, resulting in a post flight inspection and maintenance action.
summary: The pilot opened the crossfire valve to use center tank fuel but failed to close it, causing a 3,000-pound main tank imbalance noticed by the First Officer on final approach. The aircraft landed with the imbalance and was subsequently removed from service following maintenance consultation.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: When the main instrument runway was closed at the destination airport, this crew was forced to execute a non-precision approach to an alternate runway. They had difficulty acquiring the runway environment on the first attempt, but after a go-around and subsequent approach they accomplished an uneventful landing.
summary: Pilots flying an aircraft lacking RNAV capability into Corpus Christi at night missed the runway due to refinery lights obscuring visibility during a VOR approach. They executed a missed approach and subsequently landed safely on Runway 18 using maximum braking with a nine-knot tailwind component.

synopsis: The 757 landing gear failed to retract, so the crew returned to the departure airport. The alternate retraction method was not considered because of an unusual noise heard in the nose gear area during pushback.
summary: The First Officer and Captain experienced a landing gear retraction failure and communication loss after hearing a loud clunk during pushback. They returned for an overweight landing with gear down, citing potential nose gear damage and a recent gear module repair as the cause.

synopsis: A 777 first officer reports that a new taxi procedure has increased distractions and confusion 'several times over.'
summary: A 777 pilot reported that a new 37-page taxi and before takeoff checklist caused confusion and distractions during four flights. This led to FMC loading errors, wrong runway taxiing, and a runway vacate due to being 300 pounds over gross weight, attributed to unclear weight terminology.

synopsis: Pilot inquired how ATC expects them navigate to the airport when vectored to a north downwind for a visual approach.
summary: A pilot reported confusion regarding NorCal TRACON expectations for down-the-bay visual approaches to SFO Runway 28R when ATIS only advertised charted visuals. The pilot attributed previous TCAS RAs to conflicting pilot and controller expectations on intercepting the centerline versus the charted offset, requesting clarification or a J Order.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported that the Fueler did not reposition switches correctly in the wing fuel panel which resulted in trapped fuel in the forward ACT (Additional Center Tank).
summary: The crew experienced a departure delay and trapped fuel in the forward additional center tank due to the fueler's incorrect sequencing and four fuel panel switches left in the wrong position. Despite the imbalance and non-burning fuel, the flight continued to the destination after consulting the dispatcher.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 Captain reported encountering wake turbulence shortly after takeoff from DTW in trail of an A330 that resulted in up to 50 degrees of uncommanded roll. Reporter stated he felt ATC spacing could have been more generous.
summary: The pilot reported that after taking off three miles behind an A330, the aircraft encountered wake turbulence at 1,000 feet, causing severe rolling. The First Officer recovered control, and the flight continued without further incident.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: The crew accepted a late runway change, unaware that the glideslope was out of service. They received a low altitude alert from the Tower although the Captain had the field in sight. The Captain took the aircraft from the First Officer and landed uneventfully.
summary: The First Officer descended below the MDA during a LOC 16L approach at SEA, triggering a low altitude alert due to poor energy management and missed NOTAMs regarding the glide slope. The Captain assumed control to execute an uneventful landing after the crew failed to brief minimums and maintain a stable approach in rain.

synopsis: An instructor pilot described a failure in the nose landing gear retraction/extension system of a Cessna 310 that resulted in landing with a partially extended nose gear.
summary: During departure, the pilot and co-pilot experienced a nose gear retraction malfunction on a multi-engine aircraft. They returned to base and executed a safe belly landing with no injuries or fire after following emergency checklists.

aircraft: Piper Single Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A pilot new to the Hayward airport was unable to determine the location of the run-up area and subsequently experienced a runway incursion.
summary: A pilot taxiing a general aviation aircraft at Hayward Executive Airport (KHWD) inadvertently crossed the hold short line onto the active runway while searching for an unmarked run-up area. The incident occurred because the pilot assumed the hold short line would be closer to the usable runway portions, highlighting a lack of clear signage on the taxi diagram.

synopsis: The pilot of an experimental amphibian aircraft described the failure of a landing gear mechanism that resulted in a left main landing gear collapse and subsequent runway excursion. He speculated the cause and suggested repetitive inspections of the mechanism.
summary: The pilot reported that after landing, the left gear mechanism failed due to wear-induced deformation, causing the gear to retract and the aircraft to skid off the runway onto grass. The aircraft came to rest upright with no injuries or damage, and maintenance manually secured the gear to make it towable.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A Pilot on final approach to HTS at 800 feet reported a near miss with what appeared to be a kite but may have been a UAS.
summary: A pilot on final approach to HTS Runway 12 at 800 feet AGL encountered a stationary object, likely a kite or UAV, approximately 20 feet above and left of the aircraft. The crew descended under the object without altering flight path and reported the near-miss to HTS Tower and Departure Control.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: ZID Controller reported an airborne conflict he observed. Controller descended one aircraft through the altitude of the other. The aircraft were close to losing separation but did not. Controller reported he needed to be more authoritative to the D-Side in issuing instructions for coordination.
summary: An air traffic controller managing Aircraft X and Aircraft Y experienced a near-miss due to a miscommunication with a trainee regarding a descent clearance for Aircraft Y. The controller issued vectors and expedited descents to maintain separation, resulting in a closest point of 5.35 miles between the aircraft.

synopsis: ZDC Instructor and Developmental report of a situation where two aircraft wanted to become a flight. The controllers did not allow this and one of the aircraft cannot keep altitude and continually climbs and descends. Controllers find out pilot is having icing and vertigo problems and then separate the aircraft even more. A loss of separation occurs when the pilot initially climbs out of assigned altitude.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller managing Aircraft X and Y during training observed Aircraft X lose separation from Aircraft Y due to altitude deviations caused by suspected pitot tube icing and pilot vertigo. The controller declared an emergency, vectored Aircraft Y left to restore separation, and both aircraft safely landed at their destination.

synopsis: HCF Controller reported about a conflict between a small aircraft and a large aircraft that came close together. According to the reporter this happens all time and is because of a procedure the small aircraft company uses. The small aircraft does not have required over water equipment and tries to stay close to shore causing conflict with arriving and departing aircraft. Controller wants the company to play by the same rules as everyone else.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X, a single-engine VFR advisory flight, disregarded issued headings to intercept the shoreline, creating a conflict with IFR Aircraft Y on a visual approach. The controller attributed the unsafe situation to Aircraft X Company's refusal to comply with ATC instructions due to their single-engine glide-to-land restrictions, which forces controllers to issue non-standard vectors or lose control of the aircraft.

synopsis: A Controller reports of a runway incursion he feels was due to a taxiway closure which limited special type aircraft not being able to use. The tug operator did most things correct but missed a turn and went onto an active runway as opposed to the taxiway. No other traffic was a factor.
summary: An air traffic controller managed simultaneous runway crossings for Aircraft X and Y to avoid conflicts, but Aircraft X missed a turn and entered Runway 28R after stammering through instructions.
