summary: Mechanics serviced a leaking #1 Engine Driven Pump (EDP) and deferred it after deactivation. The aircraft was later diverted due to #1 engine oil loss and shutdown, prompting a recommendation for more detailed leak check procedures in the AMM.

synopsis: After making appropriate CTAF radio announcements and entering the runway environment, a Piper pilot and passenger observed landing traffic on short final, so they quickly exited the runway. It was later determined that the landing aircraft had experienced radio problems.
summary: The pilot and passenger missed an aircraft on final approach due to obscured vision and reliance on a quiet CTAF, causing a runway incursion that was avoided by stopping and exiting. The other aircraft landed safely despite radio failure, prompting the pilot to adjust scanning techniques and never assume silence indicates no traffic.

synopsis: The crew misread the CHINS1 arrival restriction at RADDY for landing at BFI.
summary: The flight crew, descending on the CHINS1 arrival to BFI, incorrectly briefed RADDY intersection constraints for Runway 31 while intending to land south. The crew acknowledged the error was their fault for missing the runway-specific note.

synopsis: General aviation pilot reported he thought he had filed a flight plan online to Charleston, West Virginia (CRW), but received a clearance to Charleston, South Carolina (CHS).
summary: The pilot reported a flight plan error where Approach initially cleared them to Charleston, South Carolina, instead of the intended Charleston, West Virginia. After the pilot questioned the conflicting right-turn instruction and clarified the destination, Approach corrected the clearance to West Virginia with no traffic conflicts occurring.

synopsis: Ground Controller heard an aircraft that was cleared onto the active runway advise the Local Controller of traffic on final. Landing traffic was advised to land on the adjacent parallel runway.
summary: A Ground Controller reported that a C172 pilot on short final for Runway 30L correctly rejected a Local Control clearance to line up on Runway 30R, preventing a potential runway incursion with a departing CL30. The incident was likely caused by controller confusion or a readback error, but the pilot's visual scanning and refusal to accept the unsafe clearance averted a catastrophic event.

synopsis: B737 flight crew executed a go-around after forgetting to set final flaps and complete the Before Landing Checklist due to attention outside the cockpit on ATC reported traffic concerns.
summary: The crew executing a visual approach at ZZZ missed configuring flaps 30 and completing the Before Landing Checklist due to outside distractions from ATC traffic advisories. This resulted in a "Too Low Flaps" warning at 500 feet, prompting a go-around followed by an uneventful landing.

synopsis: A B737 flight crew reported a bird strike during the takeoff roll, damaging one of the engines. The takeoff was safely aborted and the aircraft returned to the gate for maintenance action.
summary: The flight crew rejected takeoff after a large hawk struck the number two engine, causing a loud pop and right yaw. The aircraft stopped safely with no brake cooling required, though visual inspection later revealed damaged fan blades and feathers.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An airline Captain reports descending early on the Stadium Visual to Runway 29 at EWR. The reporter believes that either VNAV was not selected or did not engage. The error was not detected until 200 feet low.
summary: The pilot descended below the 2,500-foot restriction during a Stadium Visual Approach to Runway 29, encountering a Teterboro departure at 2,300 feet. The pilot attributes the deviation to failing to engage VNAV, causing the Flight Director to follow the 1,500-foot Altitude Select Window instead of the FMC waypoint restriction.

synopsis: B777 First Officer, upon returning from his break, was informed by the Captain that Dispatch had called to tell them of a possible cargo loading error. The aircraft was within limits in either of the loading scenarios and the crew landed without difficulty.
summary: The First Officer and Captain received a dispatch report of a possible cargo loading error before landing at ZZZZ. Load planners confirmed the aircraft remained within performance limits for either scenario, and the flight concluded without incident, though the actual loading status was never confirmed.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported they returned to departure airport because of 'unusual' control feel in roll.
summary: During climb out, the First Officer and Captain experienced unusual roll control forces above 10 degrees of bank with flaps up, likely unrelated to existing speed brake deferrals. The crew diverted to EWR; the issue resolved upon flap extension for landing and did not recur on the ground.

synopsis: B767 Captain reported a track deviation departing HNL when the FO lost situational awareness and blindly followed the flight director that was giving incorrect track information.
summary: During an HNL departure, the First Officer (PF) followed a Flight Director that stopped turning, causing the aircraft to deviate from the assigned 140-degree heading while the Pilot Monitoring (PM) was distracted by airspeed oscillations. The PM identified the deviation and the PF manually corrected the heading after the controller issued a turn instruction.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported the landing gear was retracted at a speed above the limit when the crew failed to retract the landing gear and it was not noticed until climbing through 10,000 feet and 250 KTS.
summary: An IOE captain and First Officer oversped the landing gear after failing to retract it during climb due to the captain's distraction with flight director modes. The crew executed QRH procedures to resolve the disagree warning and continued to the destination.

synopsis: CE560 flight crew failed to arm the VNAV mode of the FMC and did not descend to meet ATC assigned crossing altitude.
summary: Two pilots missed a crossing restriction at VOR ZZZ while level at 14,000 feet because the pilot flying failed to arm VNAV and the pilot monitoring did not notice. The crew subsequently received a descent clearance to 6,000 feet after realizing the error.

synopsis: DHC8-300 Captain detected the odor of hot electrical wiring during descent for landing. The Flight Attendant was notified and advised there was no odor in the cabin and the checklist indicates to land as soon as practical, which was accomplished.
summary: During descent, the crew smelled an odor and experienced a temporary blank Captain's IVSI, prompting smoke checklist execution and passenger evacuation. The source remained unknown with no visible smoke, leading to a "land as soon as practicable" decision and safe landing.

synopsis: EMB-175 First Officer attributed a 'near miss' with a small, single engine aircraft to being 'heads down' working in the MCDU on climb out. There was no TCAS alert until after evasive action had been taken.
summary: During climb after departure, the Captain executed an evasive maneuver to avoid a small single-engine aircraft seen visually at 01:00 high while the First Officer was focused on the MCDU. The near miss occurred because the traffic was not initially displayed on TCAS, highlighting the need for continuous visual scanning.

synopsis: A B757-200 First Officer reported they returned to their departure airport because of high right engine vibration indications.
summary: The crew experienced right engine vibration after departure, prompting autothrottle disengagement and an overweight landing at an alternate airport due to terrain concerns. They executed a soft landing 2,000 lbs over maximum weight with flaps 25, delaying brake application until below 50 knots, and taxied to the gate uneventfully.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier flight crew reported encountering significant wind shear while conducting an approach. They executed a missed approach and, due to a critical fuel state, requested a traffic priority and diverted to an alternate airport.
summary: The crew encountered unforecast windshear below 500 feet on approach to RWY 23L, causing an unstable approach and go-around to 3,000 feet. With bingo fuel, they requested priority climb to divert to ZZZ1 after ATC initially denied the request due to congestion.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported a track deviation inbound to DTW when they failed to note the offset localizer in use on the ILS Y 22R.
summary: During an IOE descent, the First Officer and Captain missed a 2.5-degree offset localizer on the ILS Y 22R approach due to an incomplete brief and high workload. The crew intercepted the correct course after ATC vectors, attributing the incident to the briefing omission and the student pilot's inexperience.

synopsis: Two Q400 flight attendants report separate anomalies on one of their flights. The B Flight Attendant reports the Customer Service Representative (CSR) sending passengers down without asking or informing the crew, and with the Lead Flight Attendant off the aircraft. Upon arrival at their destination, the A Flight Attendant wan unable to open the door because the handrail pins were incorrectly installed.
summary: A single Flight Attendant on a Q400 could not open the forward door at arrival due to incorrectly installed handrail pins, likely from the previous flight. Station personnel began boarding without crew permission, allowing one passenger to board before the FA could intervene.

synopsis: The pilot of a PA31 observed smoke and a small fire during run-up. An aircraft shutdown and evacuation were executed. A fuel leak from an engine driven fuel pump is suspected.
summary: The pilot reported a fuel fire on the left engine during the run-up phase after the aircraft sat in rain. Fuel leaked from the left side, ignited by hot engines, causing flames and smoke that were extinguished by shutting down fuel and electrical systems.

synopsis: A PA28 pilot and instructor noticed a strange noise but noticed no abnormal engine indications. After a successful return to the departure airport, a broken exhaust stack was noted.
summary: During an IFR training flight in a Piper Arrow II, a loud noise occurred with normal engine gauges, prompting the instructor to cancel IFR and land safely. Post-flight inspection revealed a broken right front cylinder exhaust stack that had damaged the cowling.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Small aircraft single pilot reported striking snow stakes planted along the edges of runways and taxiways at FZY with his wingtips. The wingspan is 36 feet and the distance between posts is 42 feet.
summary: The pilot reported that while taxiing, the aircraft's wings struck newly installed 42-to-44-foot posts, causing damage from the leading edge to the ailerons on both wings. The incident occurred because the posts created a virtual gate with less than three feet of clearance for the aircraft's 41-foot wingtip height.

synopsis: An A320 Flight Attendant detected an oil odor during an early morning preflight. The flight departed but then diverted with the pilots on oxygen after the odor intensified once airborne. The reporter experienced painful headaches and dizziness days after the exposure.
summary: Cabin crew reported a strong oil odor on an A319 before departure that worsened after takeoff, causing the Captain to don oxygen and divert. The crew remained on board for over an hour and subsequently suffered headaches and dizziness, with the reporter questioning why the flight departed given the pre-flight smell.

synopsis: Reporter describes incident of a go-around at Burbank Airport. When aircraft are conducting a Visual Approach and have to go-around Burbank Tower is required to keep the aircraft in their VFR pattern as opposed to a heading and altitude and handoff to TRACON for re-sequencing. The reporter states that it is impossible to keep certain jet aircraft executing a go-around in their VFR pattern within the confines of their airspace. These aircraft routinely enter adjacent Tower's airspace.
summary: A pilot on a visual approach to Burbank Runway 33 executed a go-around due to a TCAS RA from a helicopter. The aircraft subsequently violated Whiteman and Van Nuys airspace because Burbank lacks go-around procedures, resulting in a conflict with an IFR departure from Van Nuys.

synopsis: A 737 Captain reported a rising engine temperature indication in one engine during climb out, which resulted in a return to the originating airport.
summary: The pilot reported that during climb out from ZZZ, engine number one temperature entered the caution range. The crew executed the QRH and landed uneventfully.

synopsis: A 777 flight crew was alerted by the flight attendants of unusual noises heard emanating from the cargo area. A loose pallet was suspected and a successful precautionary landing was made using minimal braking.
summary: During cruise, flight attendants reported loud bangs from the mid-galley, which dispatch attributed to a cargo pallet. Post-landing inspection revealed the pallet was neither tied down nor locked, allowing it to move freely and cause the noise.

synopsis: A B737 First Officer reported returning to departure airport when the flight crew noticed high number 1 engine EGT.
summary: During climb-out from ZZZ at FL240, the crew managed a Number 1 Engine EGT amber indication by reducing thrust and returning to land at ZZZ. After an uneventful landing complicated by a green laser and runway availability, the crew declined a Flight Duty Period extension due to fatigue concerns and went to a hotel.

synopsis: B757-200 flight crew reported diverting to a nearby alternate when they experienced violent nearly uncontrollable rolls in climb at FL270 from a malfunctioning yaw damper.
summary: During climb through FL270, the flight crew experienced violent uncommanded rolling with no EICAS messages. They isolated the issue by turning off the left yaw damper, which stopped the oscillation, allowing them to continue to the destination after maintenance deferred the unit despite no recorded data exceedences.

synopsis: A MD-11 First Officer reported the number 2 engine rolled back in cruise flight when the fuel pumps for that engine were inadvertently turned off while troubleshooting a fuel system issue.
summary: During en route flight, the Captain accidentally turned off engine 2's boost pump while manually rescheduling fuel, causing an engine flameout. The crew restored the pump, relit the engine, and completed the 'SELECT FADEC ALTN' checklist, allowing the flight to continue without further interruption.

synopsis: LR-45 Captain reported diverting to a suitable alternate when they got a CAS for low hydraulic quantity.
summary: The pilot reported a hydraulic quantity low CAS on departure, followed by flap and gear extension issues during visual approach. The crew diverted to an airport with a longer runway as a precaution for potential brake failure, landing safely with normal braking.

synopsis: EMB-145XR flight crew reported a low fuel situation resulted from a wind-shear induced go-around and diversion to an alternate.
summary: The flight crew encountered unforecasted windshear during final approach, forcing a missed approach and diversion to a nearby airport due to minimum fuel. The pilot attributed the unwanted aircraft state to low fuel planning for mountainous terrain and the resulting windshear, noting no crew errors were made.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilot reported being issued traffic and observed the traffic. Aircraft received an RA and aircraft descended to avoid traffic. After traffic passed the aircraft climbed back to assigned altitude. Pilot advised ATC of altitude deviation for traffic.
summary: The flight crew departed Newark and received a TCAS warning while climbing to 4,000 feet near traffic at 4,500 feet. They descended to 3,800 feet to avoid the conflict, attributing the event to a clearance that placed them within 500 feet of known traffic without horizontal spacing.

synopsis: EMB-145XR flight crew reported diverting to an alternate after encountering wind shear on approach to CYHZ. Landing gear and windshield wiper limits were exceeded on go-around.
summary: Pilots approaching CYHZ encountered severe windshear, causing instrument readability issues and a diversion. They exceeded gear and wiper speed limits by 10–30 KTS due to improper aircraft cleanup during the challenging event.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A flight crew reported multiple distractions due to weather and an icing equipment malfunction. These distractions resulted in several speed excursions before the flight was finally stabilized and a successful landing was accomplished.
summary: The crew encountered moderate icing and turbulence during an ILS approach in IMC, experiencing a sudden 10-15 knot airspeed loss and stall warning at 600 feet. The Pilot Flying added power to recover and continued the landing to avoid returning to icing conditions, noting the event was likely caused by unpredicted wind shear.

synopsis: The flight crew of a regional jet reported a traffic conflict resulting in an RA. The TCAS evasive maneuver was followed and the aircraft returned to the original clearance.
summary: A pilot on the BRDJE2 arrival into Dallas received a TCAS RA to climb from 11,000 to 12,000 feet due to a departing aircraft below. The pilot attributes the conflict to insufficient vertical spacing between arriving and departing traffic in this high-closure-rate area.

synopsis: A321 flight crew experiences a red ECAM- auto thrust lock, during level off at 4,000 feet. The Captain performs the ECAM actions which causes a rapid increase in thrust and an over speed of the slats.
summary: The First Officer, flying the last leg of a three-leg duty day, experienced a red ECAM auto-thrust lock and asymmetric thrust at 4,000 feet on downwind. Rapid engine acceleration during the ECAM procedure caused an 11-knot slat overspeed and a 300-foot altitude deviation, but the crew retracted slats and completed a manual ILS landing safely.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain experiences an airborne conflict with a C172 at 6,000 feet during the CATH1 departure from PSP. TCAS commanded a descent while the aircraft was climbing at a high rate of speed and 5,500 feet was reached before descent begin. The reporter has some comments on ATC handling of the incident.
summary: A commercial crew departing PSP experienced a TCAS RA with a C-172 while climbing from 5,000 to 10,000 feet due to a lack of coordination between Tower and SOCAL. The crew descended to avoid the traffic, passing within 500 feet, and attributed the incident to airspace limitations and controller communication failures.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew reports not making the crossing restriction at AANAH on the NITZR2 arrival to MSP due to a late start down. ATC is not advised and AANAH is crossed 800 feet high.
summary: During a CRJ descent via the NITZR TWO Arrival to MSP, the crew failed to cross AANAH at 10,000 feet due to a late speed reduction to 250 KTS. The aircraft crossed AANAH at 10,800 feet and 265 KTS because the CRJ could not simultaneously descend and slow down effectively.

synopsis: C99 pilot reported a landing gear issue that resulted in a right gear collapse after touchdown.
summary: The pilot experienced a right main gear malfunction during initial climb at ZZZ, causing a circuit breaker trip and failure to lock despite emergency extension attempts. After diverting to ZZZ2, the aircraft landed with the right gear collapsing upon touchdown, resulting in a runway stop with no injuries reported.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported a trailing edge flap issue which limited flap extension to 15 degrees.
summary: During final approach to ZZZ, flaps failed to extend past Position 2, prompting a go-around and holding while the crew followed QRH alternate procedures to extend them to Position 15. The aircraft subsequently completed an uneventful visual approach and landing, followed by a Fire Chief inspection before taxiing to the gate.

synopsis: EMB-190 Captain reports an injury to a Flight Attendant when moderate turbulence is encounter at 10,000 feet. The Flight Attendants had been warned by the Captain but the B Flight Attendant had been unable to secure his cart before the turbulence was encountered and it caused his injuries.
summary: During descent through clouds at 10,000 feet, moderate turbulence caused a flight attendant's cart to strike his shoulder while he was stowing it. The crew declared a medical emergency, landed safely, and the injured flight attendant was treated by EMTs with no serious injuries reported.

synopsis: EMB-175 First Officer reported multiple system issues on short final that resulted in the flight being towed to the gate after landing.
summary: The flight crew experienced multiple system failures, including display units and autothrottle loss, during final approach after accepting a visual clearance to Runway XXR. They landed safely but lost steering on the ground, requiring a tow to the gate, with the crew suspecting a link to recent heavy maintenance.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew reported they returned to their departure airport after noticing a burning smell shortly after takeoff. Fumes were suspected to be the result of an engine wash accomplished earlier.
summary: The flight crew detected a burning smell shortly after departure from ZZZ, suspected the left pack, and returned for a normal landing. Mechanics later attributed the fumes, which smelled like oven cleaner, to a recent compressor wash on the left engine.

synopsis: CE-750 flight crew reported the First Officer's windshield shattered in flight, so the flight diverted to the nearest suitable airport.
summary: During climb to FL240, the co-pilot's side window shattered due to a suspected windshield heat malfunction, causing a loud noise and shockwave without cabin depressurization. The crew donned oxygen masks, descended, and landed safely at ZZZ with three passengers, while maintenance deemed the event unrelated to a pre-existing baggage door seal issue.

synopsis: B777 flight crew reported being unable to receive a rereleased fuel required at their planned redispatch point due to the fact that the flight planning software was currently down. The crew was told to continue toward their destination and the required fuel was finally sent 16 minutes past the redispatch point.
summary: The flight crew proceeded past the IMRAD rerelease point without updated fuel calculations because the dispatcher's flight planning system was offline and no backup existed. The dispatcher authorized continuing based on extra fuel, issuing the required fuel figures 16 minutes after crossing the point, though the crew questioned the legality of this action.

synopsis: MD80 First Officer reports being cleared for a visual approach and declining due to a rain shower over the end of the runway. The flight is then cleared for the ILS, but the Captain apparently does not hear the clearance and continues on the visual. ATC issues an advisory and the Captain climbs to intercept the glideslope. At minimums, in the rain shower, the approach becomes unstable and the First Officer calls for a go around, but the Captain lands.
summary: The First Officer and Captain flew an ILS approach in heavy rain, descending 500–700 feet below clearance due to confusion over visual versus instrument instructions. The First Officer called a go-around for an unstable approach, but the Captain landed roughly with spoilers failing to deploy automatically, requiring manual activation.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Captain of an international flight reports a navigational error on a flight departing ESSA for North America. The first two waypoints of the oceanic segment would not uplink to the FMC and had to be created manually on the nav data page. The first waypoint was entered correctly but the second waypoint, which was 7310N (N7300.0W01000.0), was entered as N7310.0W01000.0 and displayed as 7310N. ATC detected the error and informed the crew.
summary: During an oceanic flight between ESSA and North America, the crew manually entered an incorrect latitude for waypoint 7310N in the FMS due to time pressure during a quick turn. This error caused a 9-10 mile deviation in RNP 12 airspace, which was detected by ATC via CPDLC and subsequently corrected by the crew.

synopsis: MD11 flight crew has their departure runway changed twice during taxi to the runway and forgets to accomplish the before takeoff checklist above the line. The takeoff warning sounds when thrust is pushed up due to flaps not being set and the takeoff is rejected at 10 knots.
summary: The flight crew aborted a takeoff on Runway 25R at LAX after advancing thrust without completing the before takeoff checklist due to multiple runway changes. The event resulted from skipping the "above the line" checklist items and failing to call "Cleared to Configure," leading to a takeoff warning horn and a subsequent safe departure after reconfiguring.

synopsis: EMB175 First Officer reports discovering on post flight that the rear cargo bin was loaded with 42 United States postal bins that were not reflected on the load manifest.
summary: The flight crew discovered 42 unlisted postal bins in the rear cargo bin after landing, as the load sheet was incorrect and preflight inspection was blocked by ground equipment. The pilot attributed the incident to poor ramp-to-flight deck communication and recommended mandatory bin inspections during unloading.

synopsis: CRJ-700 flight crew described the circumstances leading to a takeoff with one engine programed for takeoff thrust and the other set to flex thrust. The number one engine is started then shut down due to an ATC delay. When the engine is restarted the flex thrust temperature setting is not reentered.
summary: Pilots experienced asymmetric thrust during takeoff after a delayed engine start following a clearance delay. The cause was failing to re-enter the flex thrust value, resulting in one engine set to takeoff thrust and the other to flex thrust, which was corrected after liftoff.

synopsis: CRJ-700 Captain is assigned an aircraft that had been written up by the previous crew for having a very heavy control wheel feel and Maintenance Personnel had cleared the discrepancy claiming it was within tolerances. The Captain finds the pitch and roll forces to be beyond his tolerances and refuses the aircraft.
summary: The pilot reported excessive control wheel resistance on an aircraft previously cleared by maintenance, noting it required two arms to operate. Citing unsafe flight control manipulation and a lack of proper tail assembly inspection, the pilot grounded the aircraft despite maintenance claiming it passed written test procedures.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain experiences a cabin altitude warning passing through 16,000 feet while training a new First Officer. The climb is stopped and descent to 10,000 feet is initiated while ATC is contacted and vectors requested back to the departure airport.
summary: During an IOE climb to FL250, the Captain and new First Officer experienced a cabin altitude alarm exceeding 10,000 feet due to pressurization failure. They descended to 10,000 feet, diverted back to the departure airport, and landed safely after maintenance logged the discrepancy.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: B787 Captain is informed upon returning from break that the 180 minute ETP is actually one minute over 180 minutes and dispatch is contacted. Dispatch disagrees with the crews assessment but chooses an alternate within the 180 minute rule flight time.
summary: During cruise, the crew discovered a flight plan conflict where the engine-out time from the ETP exceeded the 180-minute rule by one minute. Dispatch later added an alternate to rectify the issue but claimed the original plan was legal, despite the pilot admitting they missed the error during pre-flight checks.

synopsis: An aircraft on an RNAV Arrival with published descents deviated for weather. The aircraft continued descending even though it was no longer on the published route.
summary: The flight crew descended below 24,000 feet during a weather deviation on an RNAV arrival because they failed to confirm an altitude with ATC after receiving a direct clearance. The aircraft descended to 23,600 feet before ATC issued a clearance to 13,000 feet, highlighting the need to verify altitudes during off-course vectors.

synopsis: BE1900 Captain experiences the loss of right engine oil pressure at FL230 and diverts to the nearest suitable airport. The torque on the right engine is reduced to idle and the engine is allowed to run until after landing.
summary: The pilot reported a right engine low oil pressure warning and fluctuating gauge at FL230 while deviating around thunderstorms. The crew declared an emergency, diverted to ZZZ, and secured the right engine after landing to prevent further damage, noting normal ITT and oil temperatures.

synopsis: The Falcon 2000 crew was on a maintenance check flight and was distracted by maintenance checks which resulted in the transponder being left off despite being on the taxi checklist. This led to a near miss with a Bonanza at approximately 5,000 feet, as the TCAS did not work and Approach Control had not yet established radar contact with the Falcon.
summary: Pilots and maintenance crew conducted a VFR maintenance test flight in a Falcon 2000 to check engine anti-ice and nose-wheel steering systems. A near-miss with a Bonanza occurred during climb-out because the transponder was left off and crew distractions from troubleshooting prevented traffic detection.

synopsis: Small jet First Officer describes the shoddy maintenance practices of the company he works for. An engine that had low oil pressure was 'repaired' and the crew tasked to ferry the aircraft back to base. The engine exhibits high oil pressure and erratic oil temperature in flight and is operated at reduced thrust to return to base. Mechanics removed the oil filter and oil screen revealing large amounts of metal chunks, flakes, and dust and informed the crew that they had cleaned metal from the oil system several times before.
summary: A First Officer, Captain, and fatigued mechanic flew a repaired cargo aircraft that exhibited high oil pressure and erratic temperatures due to metal debris in the engine. The crew continued the flight after the mechanic, who had worked over 24 hours, fixed a previous oil leak without a pre-flight test, despite prior knowledge of recurring metal contamination.

synopsis: SR22 pilot reports going around at NEW when Runway 36R is assigned at the last minute due to conflict with a Texan II on Runway 36L. The 75 foot width of Runway 36R and crosswind were factors in his decision. On the next landing the Texan II is told to go around when the reporter does not clear the runway in timely manner.
summary: The pilot vectored by New Orleans Approach for a visual approach to runway 36L at 2,000 feet encountered a Texan trainer at 900 feet. A late clearance to runway 36R, combined with crosswinds and close proximity, forced the pilot to go around, subsequently causing the Texan to also go around due to insufficient separation.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot took evasive action from an aircraft taxiing on a crossing runway while taking off on CTAF BWG Runway 3.
summary: A departing pilot on Runway 03-21 pulled up to avoid a collision after Aircraft Y, taxiing on non-active Runway 12-30, failed to stop and crossed the active runway just inches ahead. Multiple witnesses observed this runway incursion and near-miss incident.

synopsis: Light twin pilot experiences high Cylinder Head Temperature (CHT) and high oil pressure on departure from CO12 and enters Class B airspace inadvertently while trouble shooting. He believes the DEN Class B should be redesigned to accommodate pilots of light twins operating from CO12.
summary: During departure from CO12, the pilot experienced a number 1 engine CHT redline and rapid oil pressure increase, causing a momentary climb to 6,400 feet into Class B airspace. The pilot corrected the altitude but noted the low floor creates an uncomfortably low altitude for handling emergencies and recommended reviewing the airspace cutout alignment.

synopsis: C421 Captain questions an ATC clearance departing Runway 12 at JVW to 'turn left heading 010 for obstructions upon entering controlled airspace', but accepts the clearance. He believes that the published obstacle departure procedure would be far safer for avoiding the 1,560 foot tower to the southeast of the field.
summary: The pilot departed Runway 12 and received an ATC clearance to turn left heading 010 for obstructions instead of the published procedure. The pilot felt unsafe due to proximity to antennas during the turn and concluded that published procedures are safer than the controller's instructions.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reports taking off on Runway 8R at ATL without clearance after a short taxi. They had been cleared to line up and wait, but the tower said nothing until the flight was airborne.
summary: The Pilot Flying and Captain departed without a takeoff clearance after entering runway 8R, mistaking the "into position and hold" instruction due to compressed taxi time and checklist workload. The crew acknowledged the error after Tower queried them, though the subsequent climb via the SUMMT9 departure proceeded normally.

synopsis: BE-36 pilot reports difficulty learning to operate a new Garmin 750 and contacting the company to ask questions.
summary: The pilot and owner partner departed with a Garmin GPS 750 that incorrectly identified waypoint ZZZ1 as ZZZ, commanding a 354-degree heading instead of the correct 270 degrees. The tower controller queried the deviation, which the pilots attributed to difficult equipment training, incomplete data downloads, and poor manufacturer support.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported ingesting a large bird at 75 knots on the takeoff roll and rejecting. Upon examination by Maintenance, the left engine was found to have at least three damaged fan blades and the aircraft was taken out of service.
summary: The crew rejected takeoff at 80 knots after ingesting a large bird into the left engine, causing fan blade damage and a burning smell. The aircraft was inspected, found to have three damaged fan blades, and subsequently removed from service for maintenance.

synopsis: While flying the initial segment of the IZZZO 3 RNAV DEP out of PHX, B737 crew was given a 'delete speed restrictions' clearance by Departure Control. Due to the short spacing between the first three fixes on the SID, the crew induced a 'Route Discontinuity' in the current segment of the FMC route immediately after removing the speed restriction on the third fix. Since they were nearly on top the first fix, the crew proceeded direct to the second fix. Crew was unsure if they had followed the correct SID track exactly during the time it took to correctly reprogram the FMC. Crew recommends that ATC not issue this 'delete speed restrictions' clearance until flights are clear of these closely-spaced fixes.
summary: The crew of an older aircraft departing PHX on the IZZZO 3 departure experienced a route discontinuity after the Pilot Monitoring changed the MASVE speed restriction to 250 knots instead of deleting it. This caused late turn guidance and a course overshoot near KEENS, which the reporter attributes to incompatible speed programming and premature ATC clearance to delete restrictions.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reports departingusing maximum power and flaps 25 to a 3,000 foot level off. The auto thrust reacts aggressively to the approaching level off resulting in loss of airspeed and altitude and EGPWS warnings for 'Don't Sink' and 'Too Low Terrain'. Auto thrust is quickly disconnected and full thrust applied to recover.
summary: The flight crew experienced an autothrottle-induced power reduction and airspeed decay during a maximum power takeoff in IMC conditions at 2,400 feet MSL. The pilot manually disconnected the autothrottles and applied full power to arrest the descent and avoid terrain after GPWS warnings.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew discovers during approach that the calculated aircraft weight is dramatically off and adds 10 knots to the approach to compensate. The weight and balance computations were done using a passenger count of 22 instead of the actual count of 122. Ground personnel at the departure airport detected the error and attempted to contact the crew prior to takeoff unsuccessfully. When told that the flight was airborne they elected not to inform the crew of the roughly 18,000 pound discrepancy.
summary: The First Officer input an incorrect passenger count of 22 instead of 122 from the loading schedule into the performance computer, resulting in erroneous weight calculations for takeoff and landing. The error was discovered during taxi-in after a safe flight, attributed to a failure to verify the data and inadequate ground-to-cockpit communication protocols.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain discovers late in the taxi for takeoff that the flaps have not been set and a checklist has not been run, due to distractions at a very busy airport.
summary: The crew experienced a warning horn during a throttle burst on engine one while crossing Runway 9L, following a ramp pushback error and distractions that delayed the Before Taxi Checklist. The pilot attributed the event to rushing the checklist due to ground crew interruptions and complex taxi instructions.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reports using the zero fuel weight instead of the takeoff weight in the weight and balance computations, a 17,000 pound error, resulting in low V speeds and sluggish takeoff performance.
summary: The flight crew incorrectly entered Zero Fuel Weight instead of Takeoff Weight into the ACARS performance module due to an unfamiliar MEL procedure, resulting in calculated takeoff speeds that were too low. The aircraft rotated sluggishly but recovered safely, prompting the pilot to recommend ACARS interface changes to prevent future weight entry errors.

synopsis: A B737 flight crew departed LAS Runway 1R behind a regional jet on the same runway and were told to maintain visual separation but they were unable because the B737 performance over took the other aircraft. ATC issued a vector for separation.
summary: Pilots of an MEL'd TR aircraft executing a max thrust takeoff on Runway 1R outclimbed a preceding regional carrier, triggering a Traffic Advisory at 7000 feet. The conflict resolved after Departure assigned a south heading, though the report attributes the near-miss to RNAV departure procedures using altitude rather than ground points for turns.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reports a hard landing and a tail strike with the First Officer flying, after a nine hour flight from Europe.
summary: The First Officer hand-flew a stabilized visual approach to runway 28C at ORD, resulting in a hard landing and tail strike due to high descent rate, low main gear strut charge, and pitch attitude. The strike was confirmed by a flight attendant's report of scraping and subsequent inspection of the tailskid pad.

synopsis: A B737 Captain rebalanced fuel three times in two hours but maintenance found no fuel system anomalies to account for the behavior. The crew refused the aircraft because a fuel crossfeed valve leak could not be ruled out.
summary: The flight crew experienced a steadily increasing fuel imbalance requiring three rebalances totaling 900 pounds during an inbound flight. The pilot refused the aircraft due to concerns that maintenance failed to check the crossfeed valve for leaks, leaving the cause unisolated.

synopsis: B767 flight were experienced a GPWS terrain warning during a night visual approach to Runway 30 at OAK. The crew was on the OAKES2 Arrival, had been cleared direct MITOE, and cleared for the visual, but did not stay with the OAKES crossing restrictions. The warning was momentary and the terrain avoidance maneuver was barely started when the warning ceased.
summary: The pilot flying received a momentary GPWS terrain warning while descending direct to MITOE for a visual approach to Oakland Runway 30. The crew immediately disconnected the autopilot and arrested the descent, clearing the terrain without a full climb maneuver before landing safely.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew reported taking the clearance of another company's flight with the same flight number and descending below their assigned altitude. This resulted in a TCAS RA.
summary: During descent on the BOOVE3 arrival into DFW, the Captain mistakenly followed ATC descent instructions intended for another aircraft with the same flight number. This caused a TCAS conflict, requiring an immediate climb to 11,000 feet and resulting in a reported pilot deviation.

synopsis: A300 Captain reported encountering severe turbulence at FL240 during climb with no 'G' limits exceeded.
summary: During an IOE training flight, the crew encountered severe turbulence at FL240 after an ATC direct routing clearance diverted them south of their planned path. The pilot attributed the event to undetected weather despite preflight planning and noted that ATC threat information lacked meaningful context for the new route.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant collecting service items was bumped causing a water spill on another passenger. That passenger later threw a cup of water on the Flight Attendant and used abusive language. Police met the aircraft.
summary: A flight attendant spilled water on a passenger during service, but later the same passenger threw liquid on the attendant and an iPhone 6 during arrival while using profanity. The Captain declared a Level 2 threat, police met the aircraft, and the passenger was removed after statements were taken.

synopsis: A low time instrument rated pilot departed a CTAF airport for night landings in his PA-28 and it became IMC. He contacted the TRACON, was honest about his situation and was vectored without charts for an ILS to a nearby airport.
summary: A solo pilot flying a night currency flight lost ground reference immediately after takeoff due to rapidly developing fog. The pilot climbed to 1,600 feet, contacted Approach, and was vectored to an alternate airport for an ILS approach using an onboard GPS.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An air carrier First Officer climbing to FL280 with FL290 traffic ahead, misinterpreted his TCAS RA red/green visual cues and continued climbing with the VSI needle in the red band. The FL290 aircraft crew took evasive action to the climbing traffic RA.
summary: During enroute climb to FL280, the First Officer manually flew a TCAS RA but misinterpreted the VSI display, causing an overshoot to FL282 before correcting. Later at FL290, a second TCAS RA required a climb to FL300 to avoid traffic that ATC had not previously advised.

synopsis: A C-210's left landing gear collapsed on landing after it apparently had not fully extended without any failure indication. The hydraulic pack had been replaced recently and this was the first flight flown following an annual.
summary: The pilot landed a single-engine aircraft on Runway 22 after an annual inspection and avionics work, but the left main gear collapsed onto closed well doors despite a green indicator light. The aircraft veered off the runway into dirt without injury, likely due to an incomplete gear extension sequence following recent hydraulic pack replacement.

synopsis: A Bombardier Global Express HYD 1 LO QTY CAS alerted so the crew completed the HYD 1 LO PRESS Checklist. They then secured the #1 engine as a precaution and diverted to the nearby airport.
summary: The crew diverted to ZZZZ after a rapid Hydraulic System 1 fluid loss triggered a precautionary shutdown of Engine 1. Following total system depletion, they completed a single-engine approach and landed safely with no further issues.

synopsis: Pilot entered Montgomery airport's airspace without clearance due to a congested Tower frequency and nearby Class B airspace as well as conflicting traffic. Pilot climbed above pattern altitude and eventually received clearance from Tower.
summary: A VFR pilot exiting KSAN Tower airspace encountered a jammed KMYF frequency due to other pilots ignoring callsign-only instructions. Unable to communicate while approaching Class D airspace, the pilot climbed above the traffic pattern to avoid banner tow traffic before eventually contacting KMYF and landing safely.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Pilot reported he may have violated a Fire Fighting TFR near IZA because of differences between his DUATS briefing and his tablet display.
summary: A pilot flying from IZA to ZZZ departed without DUATS showing a TFR but later found a conflicting firefighting TFR on a tablet. The pilot observed no fire or aircraft and attributed the discrepancy to differences between official and non-official TFR sources.

synopsis: Due to severe flooding in Austin Texas the TRACON was closed and the Tower was intermittently open and closed. This situation caused confusion for the pilot/reporter who began taxiing without a clearance from the Tower. The pilot contacted FSS which told them all ATC facilities had been evacuated. The flight crew had dialed the wrong ground control frequency leading them to believe the tower was not staffed. They eventually realized their mistake and contacted Ground Control.
summary: Due to flooding in Austin, the crew lost ATC contact and used the wrong frequency (120.1 instead of 121.0) while taxiing. Conflicting information from FSS and Tower regarding airport status caused a miscommunication, though no conflicts occurred before the field became uncontrolled.

synopsis: PA28 pilot reported an engine compartment fire during engine start.
summary: The pilot experienced an engine backfire and black smoke during start-up, triggering an unsuccessful fire extinguisher attempt before smoke entered the cockpit. The pilot evacuated and later extinguished the fire using a water hose after pushing the aircraft into range.

synopsis: Control Tower observed an aircraft on radar squawking a VFR code following the path of the GPS Approach to the airport. Airport weather was IFR at the time with very limited visibility due to fog. The aircraft descended to a very low level and the Controller briefly observed the aircraft fly by through the fog. The Controller then observed the aircraft depart the area to the northeast. While monitoring this aircraft the Controller failed to include 'FG' for fog in the METAR and ATIS broadcast for the airport.
summary: An air traffic controller observed a VFR aircraft squawking 1200 fly a GPS approach profile below minimums in foggy conditions, causing the controller to omit fog from the METAR. The aircraft descended to zero indicated altitude, missed the runway, and departed northeast after a second go-around.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: An aircraft was instructed to hold short of a runway. The aircraft disregarded the instruction and entered the runway. The controller's views toward that particular direction are blocked by a radar display and support beams causing a delay in the Controller noticing the runway incursion.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft Z for takeoff on Runway 16R while Aircraft X was crossing the runway, creating a conflict due to tower blind spots. The controller cancelled the clearance and diverted Aircraft Z after it failed to stop, attributing the incident to obscured visibility and pressure to maintain departure flow.

synopsis: Aircraft on IFR arrival route responded to a TCAS/RA to avoid a VFR aircraft. TRACON had issued the traffic to the IFR arrival pilot and the pilot reported the traffic in sight. The IFR arrival aircraft was restricted to 6,000 feet to stay above the VFR target who's Mode C indicated 5,500 feet. The reporter states this is a routine occurrence in this area as the overlying Class B Airspace does not provide protection for this airport's arrival routes.
summary: An air carrier on the OAKES2 arrival to Oakland at 6,000 feet executed a TCAS RA climb to 6,300 feet due to a non-communicating VFR aircraft at 5,500 feet. The pilot attributed the conflict to inadequate SFO Class B airspace protection allowing VFR traffic into IFR descent paths.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Departures from Runways 28L and 28R at SFO have the potential for conflict and the resulting RA when a strong crosswind is blowing. One departure is an RNAV track and the other is a runway heading. The aircraft departing in heading mode does not correct for drift and may be blown close to the track of an aircraft on an RNAV departure which is corrected for wind drift.
summary: Pilots on Runway 28L received a TCAS RA at 1000 ft from an aircraft taking off 10 seconds later on Runway 28R. The reporter attributes the conflict to crosswinds pushing the right-departing aircraft into the left-departing aircraft's TCAS bubble while both followed their respective RNAV procedures.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported exceeding published speed departing DTW.
summary: The flight crew missed a 280-knot speed restriction above 10,000 feet on the PALACE EIGHT departure plate due to time pressure and briefing from the FMC instead of the chart. This caused the aircraft to exceed the limit while in VNAV, prompting a speed query from Cleveland Center.

synopsis: B737 FO reported they took off without complying with a fuel system MEL and were left with less fuel than they were planned with.
summary: The crew departed with MEL'd center tank pumps and initially miscalculated usable fuel by failing to account for 2.9 tons of unusable fuel in the center tank. Despite the First Officer's recommendation to return, the Captain declared minimum fuel and continued to the destination, landing with 4.2 tons of usable fuel.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: B787 FO reported fatigue on a trans-Pacific international route when FAR 117 dictated a rest schedule that was less than optimum for the flight crew's physiological needs.
summary: A ferry flight crew experienced fatigue and micronaps during a trans-Pacific flight due to reversed sleep schedules and a malfunctioning bunk thermostat. The Captain declared fatigue during descent, resulting in multiple errors, but the aircraft landed safely with assistance from International Relief Officers.

synopsis: B767-300 flight crew rejected the takeoff at approximately 90 knots in response to conflicting airspeed indications.
summary: The Pilot Flying rejected takeoff on runway 17R after observing a significant airspeed discrepancy between the Captain's and First Officer's indicators. The event resulted in a rejected takeoff at approximately 95 knots, followed by a one-hour brake cooling delay due to elevated brake temperatures.

synopsis: B757-200 pilot reported rejecting two successive takeoff attempts when the Captain's airspeed failed to register because of pitot blockage.
summary: The crew executed two rejected takeoffs due to no airspeed on the Captain's indicator, caused by an obstructed pitot tube that maintenance failed to thoroughly inspect. The reporter attributed the second rejection to inadequate maintenance checks and recommended installing pitot covers during ground storage.

synopsis: Q400 FO reported departing the gate overweight for the weather conditions. Flight returned to gate to offload some passengers.
summary: The crew returned to the gate after discovering icing conditions required performance data unavailable for their takeoff weight, despite load planning incorrectly claiming they were not overweight. The reporter attributed the error to unfamiliarity with icing procedures and criticized load planning for attempting to override the Captain and Dispatcher's operational control decision.

synopsis: A flight crew reported an NMAC with a non-transponder equipped aircraft on descent into FSD.
summary: During descent into Sioux Falls, the pilot monitoring observed a non-transponder cropduster passing within 500 feet without ATC advisories or TCAS alerts. The crew descended below the aircraft, reported the incident to Approach Control, and completed a normal landing.

synopsis: Dash 8-100 FO reported loss of hydraulic system 1 on approach. Crew ran the checklist and a normal landing ensued.
summary: During approach, the crew identified a total loss of hydraulic pressure and fluid in system one. They executed the emergency checklist for a zero-flap landing, advised Tower, and landed the aircraft without incident before it was towed to the gate.

synopsis: CRJ-200 First Officer reported an abrupt stop was required to avoid a collision with a fuel truck on the ramp at PHL.
summary: The flight crew taxiing to Spot 11 was cut off by a fuel truck, forcing an abrupt stop to avoid an accident. The First Officer notified the ramp controller and reported that improved communications between ramp and fuel trucks are needed.

synopsis: CE-750 Pilot reported an inflight engine shutdown and diversion to an alternate resulted from low oil quantity on right engine.
summary: The flight crew diverted and secured the right engine due to rapid oil loss, dropping from 1 to 8 quarts low, during cruise. Post-flight inspection revealed excessive oil on the cowling despite a secure cap, resulting in a safe landing with no damage.

synopsis: C-208 pilot reported donning the full face oxygen mask to reduce the fumes from the TKS anti-ice system.
summary: The pilot experienced TKS fluid odor and exposure symptoms while cruising at 11,000 ft in IMC after activating the anti-ice system. The flight was completed using a full face oxygen mask, and the reporter described the incident as a well-known standard problem with the aircraft's TKS system.

synopsis: Wide body air carrier flight crew reported an abrupt stop was necessary to avoid a collision on the ramp with another wide body aircraft.
summary: The pilot and first officer of an aircraft taxiing east on Taxiway X nearly collided with Aircraft Y, which unexpectedly turned right onto Runway XX. The incident occurred because the crew's radio was set to the guard frequency instead of Ground, causing them to miss potential instructions to yield.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier flight crew reported receiving a descent clearance to FL250 while on the SNKPT1 Arrival to IND, but the Controller meant to issue a speed of 250.
summary: During cruise at FL300, the crew descended to FL280 after misinterpreting a speed clearance of 250 knots as a descent to FL250 due to radio congestion. The controller queried the descent, clarified the instruction, and directed the aircraft to level at FL280 while slowing to 250 knots.

synopsis: A SR22T pilot reported striking the prop and left wingtip during landing.
summary: A student pilot in a Cirrus SR22T struck the propeller and left wing tip on landing at ZZZ due to an improperly timed flare. The pilot executed a go-around with full flap retraction, landed safely on runway 16, and reported damage to the propeller, pitot tube, and wing.

synopsis: CE560XL flight crew received several RA's on approach to SGR along with a descent well below charted minimums related to loss of situational awareness.
summary: During an RNAV (GPS) approach to SGR, the crew encountered two TCAS RA events while being vectored by ATC. The second RA caused a climb through the approach course, leading to a loss of situational awareness and an inadvertent descent below the assigned 2000 feet before ATC issued a low altitude alert.

synopsis: PA28 flight instructor reported departing from cleared altitude in response to a confusing clearance. Reporter cited fatigue as contributing.
summary: A pilot conducting a training IFR approach into Vero Beach descended below the assigned 3000 ft due to misinterpreting the controller's "are you ready?" query as an immediate descent clearance. The pilot corrected the altitude after ATC intervention, attributing the deviation to fatigue, urgency, and vague instructions.

synopsis: Model aircraft pilot, who is also a private pilot, discovered that he has been operating his model aircraft 4 SM from SHD airport while believing he was outside 5 SM previously.
summary: A model aircraft operator flew 4.02 miles from Shenandoah Regional Airport without notifying ATC due to a distance measurement error. The operator acknowledged a regulatory breach and etiquette violation but reported no actual safety issue, noting the need for better fly/don't fly information.

synopsis: C150 pilot reported returning to departure airport when fumes from the electrical system filled the cockpit.
summary: The pilot and passenger detected a burning smell and smoke from a hot electrical panel during takeoff, prompting a return to the airport with the master switch off. Fire crews found no active fire or blown fuses but could not confirm an electrical fire without powering the aircraft.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Pilots reported of flying an approach, but did not see a mandatory crossing altitude on the approach. The pilots briefed the approach but did not see the mandatory altitude. ATC corrected the problem.
summary: Pilots flying an ILS Runway 06 approach with a circle to land at Teterboro descended on the glide slope instead of adhering to a mandatory 1500-foot restriction at DANDY. ATC corrected the error, prompting an immediate descent to the required altitude before the aircraft completed the circle and landed safely.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Maintenance Technician reported a nose landing gear collapse when the tug was unintentionally accelerated in reverse.
summary: A ground handler pushing an aircraft to a hangar accidentally pressed the accelerator instead of the brake on the push tractor. The tractor lunged backward, pulling the nose strut out and causing the aircraft to collapse, though no injuries occurred.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: ARTCC Traffic Management Controller coordinated military special use airspace status with the military controlling facility. Due to a miscommunication, the ARTCC controller and the military facility were not aligned as to what airspace was under military control.
summary: A Traffic Management Unit controller deactivated military Special Use Airspace based on a misunderstood coordination call, leaving the airspace cold for one hour while the military facility intended it to remain active. The reporter attributes this error to excessive workload and unclear communication, noting that aircraft may have inadvertently entered the restricted area.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Tower Controller advised a landing aircraft to exit the runway 'quickly' so as to expedite departing traffic. The landing aircraft than was switched to Ground Control. Ground Control delayed the arrival's runway exit for their taxiing aircraft. The Airport Movement Area Safety System did not alert. The controllers were not sure if the arriving aircraft was completely clear of the runway prior to the departure taking off.
summary: The tower controller cleared Aircraft Y for takeoff while Aircraft X was exiting the runway, but Ground Control reported Aircraft X was not clear. Although ASDE-X showed no alarm and the controller believed Aircraft X was clear, the pilot reported remaining on the runway as Aircraft Y departed.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported departing without obtaining a PDC. Fatigue was cited as contributing.
summary: The crew departed without a PDC clearance due to an early arrival and long turn, discovering the missing route only after ATC assigned a transponder code. The pilot attributed the oversight to complacency from having excessive ground time rather than rushing, noting the flight continued normally after confirming the clearance with ATC.

synopsis: B737-700 flight crew reported encountering severe turbulence at FL400.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence at FL400, causing a Mach Max exceedance and rapid airspeed decay. They descended 4,000 feet to regain control after inadvertently flying over a small cumulus cloud not detected by their weather radar.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported confusion when cleared to 'climb via' the PHX FTHLS3 departure that may have led to an altitude excursion.
summary: The flight crew misinterpreted a "climb via except maintain FL210" clearance on the FTHLS3 departure, believing it deleted the 8,000-foot restriction at VANZZ. This likely caused a TCAS RA conflict with another aircraft, which the crew resolved by following RA guidance before continuing to FL210.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported noticing a flight planning anomaly related to ETOPS fuel calculations.
summary: A pilot reported that flight planning for a Boeing 777-200A ETOPS flight used an incorrect 256 kias diversion speed instead of the approved 290–320 kias. This error resulted in an underestimated fuel requirement, potentially leaving insufficient fuel for a critical point diversion at the correct speed.

synopsis: B777 Captain reported the company procedures at international stations needs to improve to prevent fatigue and safety issues.
summary: A pilot reported fatigue and operational confusion on a long-range international flight due to an unnecessary wake-up call and conflicting schedule updates from the company. The pilot attributed the issues to poor communication processes that bypassed local station control, resulting in incorrect wake times and transport delays.

synopsis: A B767 Captain reported one of his flight attendants was injured during a climb in turbulence and the flight returned to the departure airport.
summary: The flight crew encountered moderate turbulence shortly after departure, injuring a flight attendant. Due to the injury and failed medical consultations, the crew diverted back to the departure airport where paramedics met the aircraft.

synopsis: A B777 Captain reported an international station attempted to load 350 lbs of lithium ion batteries onto his flight.
summary: The pilot received an ACARS notification of 350 lbs of lithium ion batteries prior to pushback, but the HAZMAT specialist confirmed only "Miscellaneous HAZMAT" was listed. The pilot ordered the batteries removed, and the aircraft departed uneventfully after operations cleared the cargo.

synopsis: A319 Captain reported deviating from assigned track as a result of communication difficulties related to AUS ATCT degraded capabilities.
summary: The crew received an incorrect enroute clearance from the Austin temporary tower due to equipment failures, causing them to fly toward College Station instead of Navasota. Houston Center corrected the error, confirming no traffic conflict and attributing the mistake to ATC communication issues.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported a wake turbulence encounter at FL370 from an opposite direction B747 that was 1000 feet above them.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe wake turbulence from a B747 at 37,000 ft, causing a 25-30 degree left roll and a 500 ft altitude gain. The pilot flying manually recovered the aircraft after disengaging the autopilot, while a flight attendant sustained a back injury from falling.

synopsis: The Captain of a regional jet reported that 2 extra static wicks were installed on a recently replaced winglet. After consulting with maintenance personnel it was determined that the aircraft was airworthy and was dispatched under a Part 91 ferry permit.
summary: A CRJ 700 undergoing LH winglet repair at CKB had nine static wicks installed instead of the standard seven. After consulting maintenance and the flight department, the reporter determined the configuration was legal, allowing the aircraft to depart under Part 91 rules.

synopsis: A CRJ-200 flight crew reported diverting after the Captain's window displayed arcing and then shattered.
summary: During cruise at FL290, arcing in the Captain's windshield caused it to shatter, prompting the crew to turn off windshield heat and divert due to low weather at the destination. The aircraft landed safely after the First Officer managed radios and ATC coordination while the Captain referenced the QRH.

synopsis: An EMB-175 First Officer reported returning to the departure airport after receiving an EICAS message for dual bleed overpressure.
summary: The First Officer reported that during climb to 3,000 feet, dual bleed overpressure warnings occurred, prompting a return to the departure airport with one engine idle. The crew successfully landed using CRM, though the reporter noted that switching pilot duties mid-checklist caused slight confusion.

synopsis: A helicopter pilot near AGC reported a small UAS 200 feet away from his aircraft while cruising at 2000 feet MSL.
summary: The pilot reported encountering a small, silver drone 6 NM NW of AGC at 2000 ft MSL during departure. The object was observed for 10 seconds before disappearing, prompting the pilot to notify Approach, who subsequently alerted local law enforcement.

synopsis: Crew experienced erroneous airspeed indications on the copilot's indicator. Crew was then alerted by ATC and subsequent TCAS Resolution Advisory of deviations from assigned altitude. Crew corrected the altitude deviation with the help of ATC and diverted to a nearby VMC airport.
summary: The crew experienced copilot airspeed failure and erroneous altitude indications during climb and cruise due to a pitot-static issue. They diverted to a VMC airport, relying on ATC for altitude verification, and landed safely with the failures persisting.

synopsis: A Captain reported a recent SOP change moved the required callout from 1,000 feet above approach minimums to 1,000 feet AGL, which produces unclear procedural requirements on approaches to airports in mountainous terrain. The Captain cited three examples from recent flights and urges a return to the old procedure of requiring a callout at 1,000 feet above minimums.
summary: A pilot reported that a new SOP requiring 1,000-foot callouts based on TDZE instead of approach minimums degrades situational awareness and stabilized approach criteria during instrument approaches in mountainous terrain. The reporter argues this change disrupts operational rhythm and suggests reverting to minimums-based callouts to enhance safety.

synopsis: B757-200 Captain reported returning to departure airport after noting high vibration on the right engine.
summary: Pilots encountered high right engine vibration at cruise, reduced power per checklist, and returned to ZZZ with ATC clearance. The aircraft landed overweight but uneventfully, with the engine issue and landing weight logged for maintenance.

synopsis: A B777-200 pilot reported firing the APU fire bottles when smoke was observed near the APU after gate arrival.
summary: A ramp agent reported smoke and heat near the APU after shutdown, prompting the pilot to discharge fire bottles while ground power was connected. The incident resolved with no flight deck indications, though the pilot noted an abnormal power surge when selecting secondary external power before primary power was established.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported losing communication with ARTCC. The reporter stated they were on the appropriate frequency the entire time, but may have been in an area of limited radio coverage.
summary: During descent into ZZZ, the flight crew experienced VHF communication loss likely due to a dead zone, causing them to miss multiple Center calls. The crew later contacted a supervisor via telephone to report the issue and criticized the practice of issuing phone numbers during critical flight phases.

synopsis: A First Officer reported that the pilot flying descended to an unsafe altitude on a visual approach in to DEN. After becoming reoriented, the flight landed without making contact with the tower.
summary: During a visual approach to Denver, the Pilot Flying selected an inappropriate 6,000-foot altitude on the Flight Control Panel, causing a low altitude alert and distraction. This led to a missed tower contact at JOULE, though the crew landed safely after receiving a green light signal from the tower.

synopsis: CRJ-700 First Officer reported the flying pilot appeared disoriented during a visual approach and descended to an unsafe altitude.
summary: During a visual approach to Boise, a new captain fixated on terrain and ignored flight instruments, causing disorientation and a low-altitude obstacle warning on the second attempt. The First Officer initiated a go-around and later a safe landing, attributing the incident to the captain's poor airmanship and his own delayed intervention.

aircraft: Beechcraft / Beech Aircraft Corp Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Beech aircraft air taxi Captain reported a ground conflict with an air carrier aircraft during low visibility operations at DFW.
summary: A cargo flight crew at DFW International Airport nearly collided with another aircraft on Taxiway Charlie due to low fog visibility and a potential language barrier. The First Officer's initial position report may have been misunderstood by ground control, leading to conflicting taxi instructions that were resolved when both aircraft stopped safely.

synopsis: C172 pilot reported making an off airport landing because of fuel starvation.
summary: The pilot experienced fuel starvation at 8,500 feet due to miscalculated fuel planning, forcing an off-airport landing. After refueling with auto fuel, a rejected takeoff occurred due to a stall warning triggered by a bump, but a second attempt succeeded.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Pilot became disoriented during an instrument approach in IMC conditions. Pilot discovered the track error by noticing his previous error while programming his iPad for the approach. Pilot reprogrammed the approach and landed safely in VMC.
summary: A Part 91 pilot flying a corporate flight into night IMC conditions misprogrammed the GNS 480 GPS, causing a deviation from the RNAV approach course. The pilot corrected the error, cancelled IFR upon breaking out into visual conditions, and landed uneventfully, attributing the mistake to fatigue and complacency.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A corporate jet flight crew reported that after being cleared to cross an active runway they noticed another aircraft commencing takeoff on the same runway. The flight crew stopped prior to crossing the runway, avoiding a potential critical conflict.
summary: The flight crew of XA07L stopped at Taxiway Quebec while taxiing to Runway 24 after observing a Learjet entering Runway 19 despite holding short instructions. Ground control attributed the conflict to a misunderstanding between Ground and Tower controllers before reissuing the crossing clearance.

synopsis: A general aviation pilot reported a malfunctioning alternator while inflight. He requested assistance from ATC and received a traffic priority in order to expedite his arrival at the destination airport where an uneventful landing was accomplished.
summary: A pilot flying a Cessna to ERI experienced a partial alternator failure at 5,000 feet, leading to battery discharge and distraction from ATC delaying airliners. The pilot landed safely on runway 24 after initially misinterpreting downwind instructions due to stress and assumptions about landing direction.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: TRACON Controller reported an aircraft was cleared for an RNAV Approach and switched to Tower frequency. The aircraft broke off from the approach and turned away from the airport below the minimum vectoring altitude. The Controller did not get a clear explanation from the flight crew. The flight crew reported the airport in sight and the Controller cleared them for a visual approach.
summary: An adjacent sector controller transferred Aircraft X to the reporter's frequency while the aircraft was below Minimum Vectoring Altitude and heading south. The reporter issued a climb to 3,500 feet and a visual approach after suspecting a pilot deviation from the RNAV approach.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: ATC Center Controller reported improper coordination by an adjacent Center Controller, due to an apparent misunderstanding of standard procedures.
summary: ZZZ1 X sector controller instructed ZZZ X sector to descend two aircraft to 31,000 feet but failed to coordinate with ZZZ Y sector. The reporter states this procedural error created a safety risk for potential loss of separation, though no conflict occurred as the aircraft were in separate airspace violations.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported Denver Approach issued two changes to their cleared arrival procedure and expected landing runway. Initial clearance was for the BOSSS TWO RNAV Arrival, landing 35R. That was changed to the QUAIL SEVEN Arrival, and then changed back to the BOSSS TWO RNAV Arrival, landing runway 35L. While reprogramming their navigation computer for that latest clearance, the crew did not program the entire approach transition and as a result failed to fly the arrival/approach transition as cleared. ATC noticed the aircraft track error and issued a vector to intercept the final approach course.
summary: The pilot reported that during an arrival into Denver, fatigue and multiple ATC changes caused them to skip briefing the approach transition and fly a direct route instead. This error prompted ATC to issue a heading correction to intercept the localizer, though the flight concluded without further incident.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew reported an altitude deviation due to a misinterpretation of ATC instructions in regard to the published instrument departure.
summary: The flight crew departed Denver on the COORZ THREE RNAV departure and climbed through the 10,000-foot restriction at LINGR while transitioning to a new top altitude. The pilot attributed the altitude deviation to distraction regarding speed requirements and expectation bias from previous eastbound departures, noting the flight director failed to command a level-off.

synopsis: A regional jet pilot reported an engine fire while starting the number 2 engine. The fire was successfully extinguished and the aircraft was safely towed back to the gate.
summary: During pushback, ground personnel reported a fire in engine 2 after a start attempt, despite no cockpit indications. The crew executed memory items, confirmed the fire was extinguished, and safely deplaned passengers after towing the aircraft back to the gate.

synopsis: An employee reports he was informed by their Lead Mechanic that a Mandatory Service Bulletin inspection of Engine Front Support Pins issued by the engine manufacturer for their BK-117C1 Eurocopters also included a logbook entry requirement after the last flight of the day. The logbook entry requirement had not been included in the pilot maintenance checklist/signoff form from their company.
summary: A pilot and Lead Mechanic discovered that BK-117C1 operators were unaware of a mandatory Turbomeca engine pin inspection logbook entry due to a failure in disseminating the Engineering Order. Consequently, required daily logbook entries were not made until the oversight was identified and reported to Regional Maintenance Management.

synopsis: The flight crew of a cargo aircraft reported a significant decrement in airspeed at the top of descent. This was attributed to an inoperative auto throttle system, auto flight mismanagement, and fatigue.
summary: The First Officer reduced thrust during a descent from FL340 with auto throttles deferred, causing airspeed to drop into the yellow range and trigger an AIRSPEED LOW annunciation. The Captain added power and hand-flew the aircraft to restore speed before continuing the descent and landing uneventfully.

synopsis: A widebody air carrier Captain reported what he felt was unsafe arrival spacing by ATC at ATL.
summary: The pilot of Aircraft X reported that Air Traffic Control cleared Aircraft Y to cross Runway 08L while Aircraft Z was on a 2-mile final in low visibility. This created a potential runway incursion as Aircraft Y crossed the runway while Aircraft Z was at 300 feet AGL, which the pilot attributed to unsafe runway opening decisions and congestion.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Flight crew took off with the improper transponder code set. Upon receiving the correct code from ATC, the crew left the transponder in the Standby mode while flying the ATC-assigned heading. ATC had apparently lost track of the flight until queried by the crew.
summary: The Captain and First Officer departed KSJC but failed to set the correct transponder code, leaving it in standby due to task saturation and incomplete PDC verification. NORCAL Departure lost radar contact until the crew queried for vectors, realized the error, and reactivated the transponder.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Captain reported the weight manifest was over 6,000 LBS under actual weight because load planning relied on the shipper's weight figure.
summary: The flight crew discovered at Laredo that freight paperwork listed 6,000 pounds while the actual weight was 12,126 pounds, causing unexpected trim and power requirements. Although no structural or performance limits were exceeded, the error resulted in insufficient cargo straps and an invalid flight release due to the weight discrepancy.

synopsis: An air carrier Flight Attendant reported the flight began takeoff roll without allowing sufficient time for the flight attendants to get to their jump seats.
summary: During the takeoff roll, three cabin crew members could not reach their assigned jump seats after hearing engines revving. Two crew members secured themselves in vacant passenger seats while one flight attendant braced on the floor, as the PA call for crew to be seated was not heard.

synopsis: A Passenger Service Representative attempted to board a disabled passenger in an emergency exit row. The Flight Attendant cited the FAR prohibiting certain passengers, but the agent stated the passenger could perform the duties even if unable to exit.
summary: Flight attendants refused to board a passenger with limited mobility in an over-wing exit row, citing FAOM requirements for physical capability. The Passenger Service Representative disagreed, claiming training only required asking the passenger about their ability rather than assessing it, while also referencing FAR 121.587.

synopsis: An EMB-145 Flight Attendant reported an experience communicating with the flight crew during an inflight Hydraulic System malfunction and subsequent landing.
