The crew was forced to reposition to a different gate, delaying care and exposing the passenger to potential health risks.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A DC-9 landed on a snowy runway previously reported with 'GOOD' braking by an air carrier crew but discovered 'POOR' braking. The aircraft skidded with no side load toward the runway edge and was taxied to the gate with no apparent damage.
summary: The crew landed an aircraft on Runway 19R in snow and slush, experiencing braking action worse than the reported "Good" and sliding near the runway edge. Post-landing inspections revealed no damage, though the crew reported "Poor" braking and requested a maintenance check, which found conditions acceptable.

synopsis: An aircraft was instructed to depart a fix on a heading. The aircraft acknowledged the clearance but read back a different similar sounding fix. The Controller did not catch the read back error. The aircraft did not turn to the heading the Controller wanted due to the communication confusion.
summary: Pilots and a controller experienced a radio miscommunication during the arrival phase when the controller instructed a turn at FAWNT, which the crew misheard as PHAUP. The controller was unaware the aircraft was cleared direct to RBUKL, bypassing FAWNT, but the flight landed safely with no traffic conflict.

synopsis: B757-200 experienced right engine uncommanded shutdown at FL360, no abnormal indications prior to event, restart attempt unsuccessful. Destination was also nearest suitable landing airport, uneventful landing.
summary: During cruise at FL360, the right engine experienced an uncommanded shutdown with no prior indications. A restart attempt failed, but the aircraft remained under control and landed uneventfully at the destination airport.

synopsis: During cruise climb after takeoff the aircraft encountered severe clear air turbulence. The event incurred cabin crew injuries and the flight returned to originating airport.
summary: The flight crew encountered unforecast severe turbulence at 27,000–30,000 feet shortly after takeoff, causing significant airspeed loss and injuring two flight attendants. The aircraft returned to the departure airport for an overweight landing, after which the pilots declined further duty due to physical and mental fatigue.

synopsis: B737 crew experienced a weather radar failure enroute. Due to predicted thunderstorms at the destination, crew elected to divert and have the problem corrected.
summary: The Captain and First Officer diverted to ZZZ1 after a weather radar failure enroute to ZZZ, despite an MEL placard. They executed an overweight landing on Runway 10L with ARFF support to minimize brake heat, resulting in a safe arrival and subsequent maintenance inspection.

synopsis: B757 First Officer reported ATC not acting in a professional way during flight into a non-busy ATC environment. Pilot requested ILS approach and Controller stated several times the location of the airport and that it was in the clear. Pilot went on to describe how ATC needs to comply with pilot requests when able.
summary: The flight crew requested vectors for an ILS Runway 14 approach at SGF, but the Approach controller repeatedly questioned the request and refused to comply with company policy requiring instrument approaches for unfamiliar airports. The crew eventually completed the approach and landing without incident, though the controller's unprofessional attitude created potential FOM violations and increased risk.

synopsis: B777 Dispatcher reported one of his flights diverting back to Japan due to a fire warning in the lower aft cargo compartment. Maintenance Control became involved with choosing a divert airport for maintenance considerations, when the nearest suitable airport should have been the only consideration with a fire warning.
summary: A dispatcher and flight crew managed a diversion to ZZZZ1 after a lower aft cargo fire warning and extinguisher discharge. Maintenance Control attempted to direct the flight to ZZZZ2 but sent messages to the wrong tail number, creating unnecessary communication overlap during the emergency.

synopsis: B737-900 Flight Crew reported that load planning was routinely applying weight restrictions to 900 series aircraft destined for high altitude airports, without consideration of actual weather icing conditions at the destination. Should icing conditions exist, climb capability for single engine operations would be a consideration.
summary: The Captain and Dispatch challenged an unwarranted weight restriction imposed by Load Planning on a B737-900 flight to DEN, which had caused the removal of 15-20 passengers. After confirming no icing conditions existed, the restriction was lifted, allowing all passengers to board for an uneventful flight observed by an FAA inspector.

synopsis: B757 flight crew on an international leg reported the cabin crew successfully dealt with an overheating passenger seat power issue.
summary: During a flight from London, the crew detected smoke from seat 3A caused by the In-Flight Entertainment system. After cabin crew isolated power and used a halon extinguisher, the smoke dissipated, allowing the flight to continue and land uneventfully with the IFE switch kept off.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier Captain reports mistaking 4D0 for Runway 10R at LAN (6 NM west) until EGPWS alerts for an obstacle an a go-around is initiated.
summary: The fatigued flight crew approached the wrong runway (9) instead of cleared runway 10R due to lost situational awareness and failure to verify the FMS. They initiated a missed approach after an obstacle alert at 500 feet and subsequently landed safely on runway 28L.

synopsis: The pilot of a Regional Jet reported being concerned about the weather along the planned route of flight. The Dispatcher was reported to not share the same concern and seemed to be pushing the Captain into operating the flight. Ultimately the flight was cancelled without ever leaving the gate.
summary: The pilot at ATL faced a dispatcher who insisted on operating into a severe thunderstorm line despite tornado warnings and inflight convection risks. After the pilot consulted the Chief Pilot, who agreed to delay, the flight was eventually cancelled due to the hazardous weather conditions.

aircraft: Medium Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: A Turboprop Captain reports getting below the glideslope during a night visual approach to PHL with the First Officer flying. The First Officer indicates that something is amiss with the approach and the Captain takes control and executes a go-around at the same time the Tower issues a low altitude alert.
summary: During an ILS V 9R approach at PHL, the flight crew executed a go-around after the First Officer noticed the glideslope indicator failed and the autopilot descended the aircraft off-path. The crew attributed the event to a possible glideslope failure and successfully landed on Runway 17 after ATC vectors.

synopsis: A CE-680 flight crew reported that even though they followed all proper procedures, they found the brakes were frozen solid upon landing from slush and ice.
summary: The crew departed ZZZ in heavy slush and 32-degree temperatures, implementing precautions against brake freeze. Upon landing at MSP, the brakes locked, causing main gear damage, but the aircraft stopped safely with no injuries before being towed.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew reported returning to their departure airport after receiving an EICAS message 'SMOKE AFT LAV' and smelling fumes in the cabin.
summary: The captain and first officer experienced an EICAS SMOKE AFT LAV warning after takeoff, prompting a return to land due to strong cabin fumes reported by flight attendants. Maintenance later diagnosed the cause as improperly performed engine maintenance conducted the night prior.

aircraft: Regional Jet CL65; Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: CRJ Captain reported of landing and being issued taxi instructions with a hold short of another runway while still on the initial runway. The pilot taxied as instructed and held short. The Controller issued the crossing instruction and the pilot checked left and right and aircraft started to move. The Controller told pilot to hold short of same runway again. The Pilot saw they are across the hold short line and advised Tower. Tower sent traffic on arrival around and then crossed the reporting pilot's aircraft.
summary: The flight crew at IAH was instructed to cross Runway 26L while Aircraft Z was landing, causing them to pass the hold short line before being told to stop. The crew reported their position, prompting a go-around for Aircraft Z, and attributed the incident to the controller issuing the crossing clearance too early.

synopsis: The crew of this Boeing 777 cargo aircraft reported experiencing a 'Fire Cargo Aft' warning while at cruise altitude. They accomplished all appropriate checklists, coordinated a clearance with Air Traffic Control, and successfully diverted to a suitable airfield.
summary: A B777 crew at FL310 diverted and performed an overweight landing at ZZZZ1 after a persistent 'Fire Cargo Aft' warning required fuel jettison. The warning reappeared post-shutdown, prompting evacuation, with the crew suspecting undeclared Hazmat caused the fire.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported narrowly missing a ramp employee when taxi was begun before the signal was given.
summary: The pilot reported a near-collision with a ramp agent during taxi after misinterpreting the agent's arm signals as a clearance to move forward. The agent had retrieved chocks on the taxiway side and ran in front of the aircraft, which the pilot stopped just in time.

synopsis: A flight instructor in a SR20 reported a fluctuating oil pressure indication that resulted in a turn back towards the departure airport. The indications became more severe and the engine also was reported to be rough running, so the flight was diverted to the closest airport where a successful landing was made.
summary: The instructor and student pilot experienced fluctuating oil pressure and rough engine operation shortly after departure. They diverted to the nearest airport, ZZZ1, where they landed safely and requested emergency vehicles as a precaution.

synopsis: B757 Relief Officer sitting in the cabin noticed smoke coming from another cabin seat. Smoke subsided when power was removed from seat.
summary: An In-Flight Rest Operator detected smoke from seat 3A's IFE motor during a break and alerted the crew. After the In-Flight Supervisor cut power and the crew verified no heat remained, maintenance advised keeping the IFE switch off, allowing the flight to continue safely.

synopsis: A tractor driver stopped the pushback when a vehicle was observed crossing behind the aircraft while the driver was using a cellphone.
summary: During pushback, a pilot applied brakes to stop after a distracted vehicle driver crossed behind the aircraft while using a cell phone. No damage occurred, and the pushback resumed once the area was cleared using standard signage.

synopsis: ERJ-170 flight crew reported receiving a wind shear warning on approach to LGA but nevertheless continued to landing.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced wind shear with 15-knot speed fluctuations during an ILS 13 approach to LGA in IMC. Although a wind shear warning occurred at 500 feet and the FO called for a go-around, the Captain continued the approach and landed safely, later agreeing a go-around was required.

synopsis: A Captain reported they were not aware that ATC expected them to 'descend via' the RAZRR2 arrival into SJC.
summary: Pilots flying to SJC were cleared direct to RAZRR for the RAZRR2 arrival without altitude restrictions, causing them to cross the fix 6,000 feet below the published altitude. The resulting confusion with NorCal Approach regarding descent requirements was resolved after the crew clarified they had not received a "Descend Via" clearance and were subsequently cleared to 6,500 feet.

synopsis: A B737-800 departed with two seats too few for passengers, crew, two trainee flight attendants and a Flight Attendant jump seater. Gate agents failed to account for the trainees and jump seater having given their seats to passengers.
summary: The crew continued takeoff after a cabin chime regarding a Flight Attendant trainee lacking a seatbelt due to a boarding pass miscount. Dispatch and the duty chief pilot authorized continuing to the destination with a qualified non-revenue FA occupying the cockpit jumpseat to ensure all crew had seats.

synopsis: Aircraft engine and APU halon fire bottles received from the vendor have been found with squibs not properly protected for shipping and handling.
summary: Mechanics discovered Halon engine and APU fire bottles in stores with improperly protected squibs and missing caps. The reporter attributes this dangerous configuration, which risks injury from accidental discharge, to vendor failure in preparing the vessels for shipping.

synopsis: An Aircraft Maintenance Technician reported about the effects of a 'De Facto' policy of reprimand by his air carrier's local Management whenever a Technician is involved in a late departure due to maintenance on originator flights. Technician did not torque one of two bolts securing a spring clip that retains a main landing gear wheel to axle nut on an ERJ-170 aircraft.
summary: A mechanic performing a main landing gear wheel replacement on an aircraft in the hangar could not torque a bolt due to a stripped adapter. Pressure to avoid a late departure and management reprimands led the mechanic to falsify the work card, leaving the bolt secured only by safety wire.

synopsis: The pilot of a Cessna 210 reported that during rollout the left brake pedal felt normal and the right brake went all the to the stop and had no braking effect of the right main gear wheel, resulting in a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot experienced right brake failure during landing at ZZZ due to debris and aged O-rings in the master cylinder. Pumping the pedal dislodged the debris, restoring braking to stop the aircraft in the gravel overrun, followed by a system rebuild and new checklist item.

synopsis: CE560XL flight crew reported executing an emergency descent after loss of cabin pressure at FL410.
summary: The pilot flying and pilot monitoring experienced rapid cabin depressurization at 41,000 feet, triggering an emergency descent to 11,000 feet. The crew completed the flight to the nearest airport, attributing the incident to a pressurization failure and noting that extreme fatigue later prevented further flying.

synopsis: The pilot of a PA31 experienced deep snow during landing that resulted in a ground loop, runway excursion, and main landing gear collapse.
summary: The pilot landed on a snow-covered runway with no ground reports, estimating shallow snow based on a fly-by. Upon encountering deeper wet snow, the aircraft decelerated rapidly, ground-looped off the runway, and collapsed both main landing gears, though no injuries occurred.

synopsis: The flight crew of a LR35 descended below the ATC cleared altitude due to a communication breakdown during issuance and read back.
summary: Pilots descended to 2,000 feet after misinterpreting an ATC clearance for 6,000 feet, which controllers failed to correct during two readbacks. ATC subsequently ordered a climb to 3,000 feet, noting the altitude was lower than the standard 4,000 feet for that position.

synopsis: HS125 First Officer reported the Captain did not share his concern with wet snow sticking to the wing during taxi out at Kodiak.
summary: The First Officer and PIC of a Kodiak aircraft encountered heavy snow accumulation on the wings during taxi. Despite the First Officer reporting wet snow sticking to the leading edge, the PIC refused to delay departure, asserting authority as PIC and dismissing the contamination as not an issue.

synopsis: c152 Instructor Pilot was surprised that another aircraft was allowed to land so close behind them that it could have resulted in a ground collision had they been slower exiting the runway.
summary: A student pilot and instructor in a Cessna landed on Runway 24 while an Archer was cleared to land behind them, resulting in a near-miss as the Archer touched down while the Cessna was still on the runway. The reporter attributes the incident to the Archer's failure to go around, controller distraction during training, and the Cessna's inoperative transponder.

synopsis: The pilot of a single engine, fixed landing gear Piper experienced a failure of the left main landing gear during landing, resulting in a runway excursion.
summary: The pilot and passenger experienced a left main landing gear failure during landing, causing the aircraft to pull left and scrape the left wingtip on the runway. The pilot maintained control, diverted to the grass median to prevent fire, and stopped safely with no injuries.

synopsis: A Helicopter pilot departed SAT transiting east over RND Class E but during the return flight RND had become Class D without notification and not in accordance with the AFD stating Class E on weekends.
summary: A pilot operating a civil aircraft near Randolph AFB requested to cancel ATC services to reduce congestion, later discovering the tower was unexpectedly open on a weekend. The pilot attributed the confusion to sporadic operating hours, inaccessible ATIS, and a reliance on typical weekend closure patterns despite checking with San Antonio Approach.

synopsis: B747 pilot reported the scheduling practices used at her international airline were extremely fatiguing and unsafe.
summary: A pilot reported that gross understaffing and 17-day global pairings caused severe fatigue due to constant time zone changes and schedule disruptions. The pilot described a specific week involving multiple 20-hour overnights and a 50-hour delay, resulting in accumulated fatigue that crashed their body upon return despite existing fatigue programs.

synopsis: Piper PA31 pilot noticed in cruise that one of the engine cowls was not fully attached and elected to return to the departure airport. It was reported that the cowling had not been properly locked following maintenance activity.
summary: The pilot returned to the departure airport during cruise after discovering the left engine cowling was loose due to three of six fasteners being improperly locked. Maintenance confirmed the improper installation, highlighting a need for better preflight checks on fastener locking and post-maintenance verification.

synopsis: A C172 pilot reports sighting an object in the sky while taxiing to Runway 23 at LAF. The Tower is also able to see the object which appears to be a balloon with a metallic object swinging below. The Tower Controller was initially unaware of the object and it appeared to be in the Class D airspace.
summary: While taxiing to Runway 23, a pilot observed an unidentified white object at 2,000 feet AGL moving at 15 knots. The tower controller, initially unaware, later identified it as a balloon with a tethered metallic device, consistent with a similar sighting four months prior.

synopsis: A C441 corporate pilot was unable to extend the nose landing gear by normal or alternate means, resulting in a successful landing with nose gear not extended. It was reported that a failure to safety the nose landing gear actuator hardware following maintenance work caused the mechanical problem.
summary: The pilot of an IFR flight experienced a nose landing gear failure to extend during a visual approach, despite hydraulic pressure and multiple cycle attempts. After emergency procedures failed, the pilot landed nose-high on the main gear, resulting in propeller contact with the runway but no injuries.

synopsis: The pilot of a C172 returned to the departure airport after experiencing the loss of electrical power due to an overloaded generator. The pilot did not initially recognize the tripped generator circuit breaker.
summary: A low-hour pilot experienced an alternator circuit trip caused by overloading lights, leading to electrical failure and an initial incorrect 7700 squawk. The pilot corrected the code to 7600, relayed communications via another flight, and landed safely after resetting the tripped breaker.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: Two company aircraft with similar call signs were taxiing out and departing at the same time. As one aircraft was lifting off it was cleared for takeoff by the Tower Controller.
summary: The pilot of flight XXXX took off from runway 22R intersection Whiskey at Newark behind flight YYYY, despite confusion caused by similar callsigns. Although the tower issued a conflicting "line up and wait" instruction during the takeoff roll, no loss of separation occurred, and the pilot attributed the incident to the need for extreme caution with similar callsigns.

synopsis: C172 pilot, west bound on V186 near EMT at 4,500 feet is informed by ATC that he has drifted into Class B airspace and to turn right to return to the centerline. The reporter's indications were that he never left the centerline.
summary: A pilot flying VFR at 4,500 feet on V-186 was advised by ATC to be inside LAX Class B airspace and received northbound vectors. The pilot reported that their VOR indications showed they were directly on the V-186 centerline at the time of the advisory.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported diverting after experiencing loss of cabin pressure and noticing a burning smell.
summary: The flight crew experienced a loss of cabin pressurization at FL370, initiating an emergency descent to 10,000 feet MSL. A subsequent burning smell prompted an immediate diversion to a nearby alternate, where the aircraft landed safely with fire rescue standing by.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported returning to departure airport after a bird flock encounter in initial climb caused extensive damage to the right engine.
summary: Pilots reported a bird strike shortly after takeoff at 2,000 feet AGL, causing right engine vibration and burning smells. They returned to the field with the engine at idle, landed safely, and post-flight inspection revealed extensive damage and blood spray in the inlet.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: While enroute at night, crew was notified that the destination airport's runway edge lights were inoperative and the runway did not have centerline lighting. In consultation with Dispatch and AMA Tower, the crew determined that sufficient partial runway lighting was available to permit approach and landing. Specifically, the runway remaining makers were illuminated and the crew determined that those provided the 'minimum partial runway lighting' required by the airline's Operating Manual.
summary: The flight crew held at KAMA due to a total airport lighting outage during cruise. They landed safely using operational approach lights, PAPI, and runway remaining markers, though the report questions if these satisfy the FOM requirement for partial runway lights.

synopsis: A B737 flight crew reported being vectored to intercept the final approach course localizer while another aircraft was established on the parallel runway final approach course. The aircraft on the intercept vector received a momentary TCAS/RA for the parallel traffic which they had in sight. They did not respond as it was one warning, then it stopped and they had the traffic in sight.
summary: The flight crew received a brief climb RA while intercepting the final approach on a 310-degree heading with parallel traffic in sight. The conflict cleared before the crew could initiate the maneuver, allowing them to continue a normal visual approach and landing without ATC comment.

synopsis: Airline crew clearing runway at LAX misunderstood taxi clearance.
summary: The flight crew at LAX mistakenly turned onto Taxiway Yankee after landing on Runway 24R due to misinterpreting taxi instructions amidst radio congestion and post-landing callouts. Tower corrected the error, and the crew held on Yankee before contacting Ground to taxi to the gate.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: An air carrier crew diverted to TWF from a missed approach. After takeoff from TWF and upon landing, a non-revenue pilot notified the crew they departed with the runway lights off, also observed by passengers.
summary: The flight crew diverted to uncontrolled TWF due to low ceilings and departed after 90 minutes. Although the crew recalled seeing runway lights, a non-revenue pilot reported that customers claimed no lights were visible, potentially due to the crew failing to activate pilot-controlled lighting.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported rejecting a takeoff when the aft entry door annunciator illuminated. After clearing the runway, the Flight Attendant was asked to cycle the door handle. The warning extinguished and the flight departed. The Dispatcher was not contacted as required by the FOM.
summary: During takeoff, the pilot rejected the flight at 74 knots due to an illuminated Aft Entry Door annunciator. After cycling the door handle extinguished the light, the pilot failed to contact Dispatch as required, an omission later corrected by the Assistant Chief Pilot.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported being unable to use LNAV after takeoff from SLC. A vector was requested from ATC and once cleared direct to MUSAW the FMC and LNAV returned to normal operation.
summary: During the EDETH 3 RNAV departure from SLC, the crew lost LNAV guidance and flight director bars shortly after takeoff, causing a missed turn to SAPEE. The pilots attributed the failure to the route not being activated on the ground and received vectors from ATC before restoring navigation systems.

synopsis: An Air Carrier crew flying the SLC NORDK3 RNAV arrival had a track deviation because of confusion about the two D Ball Notes with separate instructions to either Runway 16L or Ruways 16R, 17. The SKEES3 Arrival caused the same confusion.
summary: The fatigued flight crew missed the 16L Localizer intercept during the NORDK3 arrival into SLC due to confusing, out-of-sequence chart notes and late-night bias. The crew acknowledged their failure to review the approach correctly and recommended adopting two-page chart depictions to prevent recurrence.

synopsis: The crew of a Boeing 737 reported that the aircraft rolled back while parked the gate with the parking brake set. A maintenance inspection revealed a faulty parking brake valve which resulted in the flight being cancelled.
summary: The flight crew reported that a faulty parking brake valve caused brake pressure to bleed off, allowing the aircraft to roll backward while parked with the brake set. This movement pulled the tug and jetway, creating a safety hazard before maintenance grounded the aircraft for repairs.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew on approach to HRL was cleared to 2000 ft from 4000 ft while IMC on the LOC BC Runway 35L. When level, the crew was told to return to 3000 ft because of towers in the area.
summary: The flight crew received conflicting altitude clearances from Valley Approach while descending for HRL in IMC conditions. ATC initially cleared the aircraft to 2,000 ft but later corrected the clearance to 3,000 ft, prompting an immediate climb with no EGPWS warnings.

synopsis: Captain refused aircraft due to multiple maintenance issues.
summary: A deadheading pilot inspected an aircraft rejected by the previous crew due to a non-operable FMS and failed pressurization system requiring manual control. The pilot refused the aircraft, citing that manual pressurization would effectively single-pilot the flight, making it unsafe for a busy airport despite favorable weather.

synopsis: B737-700 crew experienced a pressurization failure during takeoff, which resulted in a diversion to a nearby airport.
summary: The crew experienced repeated Right Pack Trip and Auto Fail lights during takeoff and climb, causing pressurization system failure with a stuck outflow valve. They diverted after following QRH procedures, maintaining manual cabin pressure control for the remainder of the flight without declaring an emergency.

synopsis: Flight crew reported overshooting an altitude on the arrival and missed a turn to the next fix due to difficulties operating the autopilot and flight director. ATC provided a vector to intercept the final approach course.
summary: The Captain descended below the 7,000-foot restriction at ZZZ1 intersection due to an unengaged VNAV mode, causing a speed and course deviation. After manually correcting altitude and intercepting the ILS, the crew landed uneventfully and reported the incident to ATC.

aircraft: B787 Dreamliner Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: B787 flight crew reported they missed a routing change in the PDC and were alerted by Tower during the takeoff roll.
summary: The flight crew received a conflicting RNAV departure clearance while rolling for takeoff at LAX, leading to an argument with the controller. The crew eventually reprogrammed the FMC to comply with the new departure, noting the lack of a pilot alert box caused significant distraction during the critical phase.

synopsis: B747 flight crew experienced a failure of the First Officer's PFD during approach that was accompanied by loud arcing sounds and copious amounts of smoke. Within a minute the PFD circuit breaker tripped and the smoke began to dissipate. A normal landing ensued.
summary: During a descent from 6,000 feet, smoke and sparks emanated from the First Officer's PFD and Navigation Display, causing circuit breaker trips and an acrid smell. The crew executed an immediate priority approach and landed safely without evacuation, with maintenance and fire services inspecting the aircraft at the gate.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: First Officer failed to enter the 250 kt speed restriction during preflight. During climbout at 3010 feet the aircraft accelerated to 280 kts. The error was detected at 4500 feet and the aircraft slowed.
summary: During climb out from SFO on the TRUKN2 departure, the FMC reverted to ECON mode at 3020 feet due to a missing 250-knot restriction in L2, causing airspeed to reach 280 knots. The Captain corrected the speed to 250 knots after the First Officer noticed the high speed at 4500 feet.

synopsis: B767 Captain refused aft cargo compartment loose package lithium ion batteries because they were loaded near airbag pyrotechnic initiators. Before departure the forward cargo 'lithium batteries' were thought to mislabeled and subsequently removed. Total 'battery' cargo weight removed was 10,000 pounds. Dangerous goods cargo should be suspect because of faulty labeling and documentation.
summary: The flight crew discovered improperly documented lithium batteries loaded with pyrotechnic initiators in the aft cargo compartment at XA21. This led to a two-hour delay while batteries were offloaded due to missing documentation and mislabeling by third-party handlers.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A flight crew reported a deviation from a departure clearance due to a communication issue with ATC.
summary: The crew departed CLT with a deferred APU and a transient spoiler fault, then received a conflicting takeoff clearance for runway heading instead of the required SID turn. ATC questioned the aircraft's course at 2,000 feet, attributing the deviation to the clearance wording, though the crew was subsequently vectored back on course.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A flight crew reported a deviation from a departure clearance due to a communication issue with ATC.
summary: The flight crew and ATC experienced a miscommunication during the departure phase after takeoff clearance for runway 36C. The crew followed the assigned runway heading while ATC expected an immediate turn to 330 degrees per the ESTRR1 procedure.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A flight crew reported inadvertently taxiing into an ILS critical area due to communication ambiguities with the taxi clearance issued by ATC.
summary: The First Officer reported that Ground Control instructed the crew to taxi to Runway 4 without specifying a hold short of the ILS critical area, leading the aircraft to cross it before Tower ordered a stop. The reporter attributed the incident to inconsistent controller instructions and ATIS information regarding the critical area, noting that other aircraft had crossed without issue.

synopsis: B757 flight crew was advised prior to departure their destination was going to be SAV, but the Dispatcher did not have time to make the changes prior to the scheduled departure time and a new flight plan would be sent enroute. When the flight plan was received the crew entered and executed it without advising ATC. This was a complete surprise to the controller involved whose report was included.
summary: A B757 crew deviated from their assigned route to Savannah after loading a dispatcher's ACARS message without ATC clearance, causing a 40-degree heading error in Class A airspace. The pilots corrected the deviation after realizing the dispatcher's "airborne re-file" comment did not constitute an ATC clearance, resulting in a reported pilot deviation.

synopsis: A CRJ-900 on short final to JFK airport had a near miss with a UAS similar in appearance to the Raytheon Killer Bee.
summary: Pilots on short final for runway 31L at 1500 feet encountered a fixed-wing drone that passed within 50 feet of the nose. The pilot reported the stealthy UAV was untrackable by ATC radar and attributed the close call to the operator's deliberate approach down the runway centerline.

synopsis: GII crew experienced a rapid decompression and difficulty obtaining a clearance for lower altitude from ATC.
summary: During descent, the crew experienced rapid decompression and oxygen mask deployment, forcing a descent below an FL270 restriction before contacting ATC. After receiving clearance to 17,000 feet, the pressurization issue resolved, allowing the aircraft to continue to destination without further incident.

synopsis: A controller was vectoring an aircraft for in trail spacing to the next facility. The controller issued a 020 degree heading. The controller observed the aircraft turning much farther left than the 020 heading towards other traffic. The controller descended the other traffic and attempted to vector the first aircraft back to the correct direction. During the turns and descents the deviating aircraft received a TCAS/RA alert and responded accordingly.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a loss of separation between Aircraft X and Y during descent when the pilot of Aircraft X mistakenly flew a 320-degree heading instead of the cleared 020-degree heading. This error, compounded by a subsequent RA climb, resulted in a minimum separation of 4.2 miles and 900 feet.

synopsis: A controller took handoffs on two departures off different airports on converging routes. Although both aircraft were climbing to 17,000 feet, the controller was initially only in communication with one of the aircraft. He could not make contact with the aircraft he intended to keep climbing and waited too long to issue other aircraft instructions to ensure separation.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a loss of separation between Aircraft X and Aircraft Y climbing on crossing RNAV SIDs to 17,000 feet. The conflict occurred because the adjacent sector failed to transfer Aircraft X, leading the controller to issue emergency descent and vector instructions after realizing the aircraft were converging.

synopsis: Local Controller cleared an aircraft into position after the previous landing and became distracted by an ASDEX alarm, assumed to be an operations vehicle. The aircraft in position was forgotten until the next jet arrival crew asked about it and were sent around at 200 feet.
summary: The Pilot Flying and First Officer executed a go-around on final approach to Runway XXR after discovering a stationary twin-engine general aviation aircraft on the runway. The incident occurred because Tower was unaware of the conflicting traffic despite issuing landing clearance, forcing the small plane to exit while the crew returned for a visual approach.

synopsis: Dispatcher was notified by Gate Agent that an aircraft departed without the correct weight and balance information. Also, the flight crew did not crosscheck the loading schedule.
summary: An operations agent provided incorrect fuel data to dispatch, resulting in a flawed loading schedule issued to the flight crew. The crew failed to cross-check the schedule as required by the AOM, but the flight continued and landed safely after confirming the zero fuel weight was accurate.

synopsis: B737 flight crew experienced a split trailing edge indication and leading edge flaps remaining up when flaps 1 are selected during approach. QRH procedures are complied with resulting in a flaps up landing.
summary: During an IOE flight with an FAA observer, the crew observed split flap needles and no leading edge device movement at 3000 feet while configuring for Flaps 1. The aircraft entered a holding pattern, and the Upgrading Captain executed an uneventful flaps-up landing after the auto-throttles were deferred INOP.

synopsis: B767 Captain described the conditions under which flight planning is completed at a foreign airport with no Company Operations in a small room with inadequate communications.
summary: Pilots reported that the flight planning room at ZZZZ is unsuitable due to poor phone connectivity, lack of space for charts, and difficult access requiring ramp escorts. Consequently, crews often skip dispatcher briefings and plan flights in the cockpit, which the reporter identifies as unsafe due to distractions and limited space.

synopsis: Deicing truck driver ran into the concrete bollard around the fuel island while repositioning the truck. Deicing lines ruptured and drained the tank.
summary: A guideman and driver maneuvering a dual-tank fuel truck near a fuel island caused the vehicle to strike a concrete bollard while turning. The impact ruptured Type I and Type IV fill lines, draining the full fuel tank onto the ground.

synopsis: While in cruise, the B767 crew received a number of apparently false alerts/warnings as well as failure of altimeters and one airspeed indicator. After a short period of time, most of the warnings disappeared although the First Officers altimeter remained failed. After consulting with the company, they decided to divert into an airport with good maintenance support.
summary: During cruise, the crew experienced simultaneous failures of both primary altimeters, airspeed, and multiple warning lights, likely linked to recent EGPWS maintenance. Although the anomaly resolved partially, the First Officer's altimeter remained failed, prompting a decision to divert to an alternate airport due to RVSM limitations and concerns over inadequate risk assessment for the original destination.

synopsis: B-757 crew experienced engine failure en route. Crew was unable to obtain descent clearance from ATC. Crew turned off track and began drift-down descent. Crew diverted and landed safely.
summary: The Second Officer and Captain managed an unexplained left engine failure at FL390 while en route. After coordinating with ATC to avoid traffic, they diverted to ZZZ1 and completed an uneventful single-engine landing with emergency services standing by.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported of confusion over a waypoint that was in their flight plan. ATC had another waypoint that was spelled differently. This caused confusion and being off course.
summary: The flight crew omitted the HESTN waypoint from the FMS flight plan between ODATE and IRK, likely confusing it with the similarly pronounced HSTON. Air Traffic Control identified the error when questioning the route, prompting the crew to recognize the confusion caused by the two close, similarly named waypoints.

synopsis: The crew responded to an RA after departing OKC while trying to check in with Kansas City Center.
summary: A crew departing OKC experienced a TCAS Resolution Advisory at 15,000 feet while climbing to intercept the PER 195 radial after a delayed check-in with KC Center. The Pilot Flying executed an aggressive climb and bank to avoid a conflicting twin-prop aircraft, later learning the intruder was under OKC Approach control.

aircraft: Any Unknown or Unlisted Aircraft Manufacturer
synopsis: An aircraft flew into the BJC Class D airspace without an ATC clearance. The aircraft was confused by the VFR flyway planning chart and thought they were outside of the Class D.
summary: An air traffic controller observed a VFR aircraft flying west of the established corridor due to confusing airspace boundaries. The controller took no enforcement action because the pilot appeared genuinely confused and no other traffic was present, but proposed extending Class D airspace to improve control.

synopsis: The pilot of a C172 lost directional control during landing due to nosewheel steering technique in crosswind conditions.
summary: The pilot reported that during landing, the aircraft skidded left of the runway due to premature nose wheel lowering and insufficient counter-reaction to initial swerving. No injuries or major damage occurred, but the pilot identified a need for additional crosswind control training.

aircraft: Cessna Single Piston Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: Cessna pilot attempting to use an intersecting grass runway to practice wheel landings discovers mowers on the runway and other fixed wing traffic using the paved intersecting runway. On short final with one mower still on the runway and unseen traffic departing on the intersecting runway, the reporter elected to go around resulting in a NMAC as he flies under the departing traffic.
summary: A pilot practicing wheel landings on Runway XXL executed a late go-around due to uncertain mower positions and radio congestion preventing deconfliction with a departing aircraft on intersecting Runway YY. The pilot flew beneath the departing aircraft at 20–30 feet AGL, noting the close pass resulted from poor timing and frequency overload.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: After requesting and receiving a different runway for takeoff, crew was assigned a different departure procedure. Crew failed to notice the different final altitude clearance of the new departure.
summary: An experienced flight crew departing SFO on runway 28R climbed to FL190 instead of the assigned 3,000 feet after a last-minute SID change. The error resulted from rushing the briefing and failing to notice the altitude restriction, leading to an ATC correction and a mandatory post-flight investigation.

synopsis: The seaplane pilot experienced an engine failure near NUW, landed safely in rough water, and was towed to port.
summary: A pilot flying a seaplane below Class C airspace at 800 feet MSL experienced an unannounced engine failure and performed a rough water landing. The aircraft remained afloat until a vessel assisted in towing it to a marina after initial rescue attempts were hindered by heavy swells.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: While replacing the #1 and #2 main landing gear wheel assemblies on a commercial aircraft, the technicians did not find any washer under the axle nut for either wheel assembly.
summary: Two mechanics replaced the #1 and #2 wheel assemblies on an aircraft but initially omitted required washers due to confusion over maintenance manuals and advisory notices. The missing washers were discovered days later, forcing the aircraft out of service to install the parts.

synopsis: An I90 TRACON Front Line Manager observed a Controller using visual separation with a large category aircraft behind an A380. The Manager advised the Controller visual separation rules are not permitted following an A380. The required seven miles separation was lost and the Controller broke the second aircraft out for re-sequencing.
summary: A Front Line Manager observed a controller lose separation between two aircraft during a visual approach clearance. The controller failed to maintain the required 7-mile distance despite a 20-knot overtake, resulting in a pullout and recovery incident attributed to a lack of controller education.

synopsis: FFZ Tower Controller taxied and cleared for takeoff an aircraft he believed to be on a VFR flight plan, but that was actually on an IFR flight plan.
summary: A PA46 pilot failed to advise Ground of his IFR status during taxi, causing the aircraft to be cleared for takeoff as VFR. The Local Controller circled the aircraft while the Controller in Charge coordinated with TRACON to obtain an IFR release before the flight departed.

synopsis: A Controller reported not hearing an altitude read back error because he had unplugged his headset momentarily to plug into a different headset jack.
summary: An air traffic controller missed a pilot's altitude readback while switching headphone jacks during a relief briefing. The aircraft remained level at 2,500 feet instead of climbing to 3,000 feet before being cleared for a visual approach.

synopsis: Crew began taxi before completion of the engine start sequence and post-start checklist. As a result, the aircraft was not properly configured and all hydraulic systems were not turned on. Crew faulted the urgency from Tower to move the aircraft and recommended that local procedures be changed so that flight clearances are not broadcast to crews over the busy tower frequency.
summary: The flight crew stopped the aircraft after moving two to three feet during taxi because flaps were at zero and 'A' pumps were off. The reporter attributed this error to pressure from ATC and Ramp to move quickly, which caused the crew to overlook the Before Taxi Checklist.

synopsis: A B737 First Officer reported he felt considerable pressure to rush through his duties after a reassignment to another flight.
summary: The First Officer faced pressure from Scheduling and ground agents after a four-hour inbound flight and aircraft change, causing concern about rushing pre-flight duties. The flight departed 23 minutes after blocking in without incident, though the reporter noted that better communication between departments could have prevented the perceived pressure.

synopsis: After a straight out departure in IMC from an airport surrounded by high terrain, the flight crew engaged the FMS and the aircraft made a right turn which was not immediately recognized as an error. The pilot monitoring and departure control advised of the incorrect heading. The flight crew was unable to identify why the FMS turned the aircraft to the right.
summary: During a B737 departure in IMC and gusty winds, the crew deviated right due to erroneous flight director commands while distracted by high workload. The pilots corrected the course by disregarding the flight director and following ATC headings, though the exact cause of the erroneous commands remained undetermined.

synopsis: B757 flight crew rejected the takeoff at about 90 kts after the right reversers amber warning light illuminated along with several other faults, possibly due to a malfunction of the right ground-air sense switch. The aircraft was returned to the gate and removed from service.
summary: The flight crew rejected takeoff at 90–95 knots due to an amber EPR warning indicating the right engine was in reverse, alongside right-side Air/Ground, Pitot heat, and T-R unit failures. Maintenance removed the aircraft from service after inspection, and the crew departed on a replacement aircraft.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported being alerted at 750 feet AGL that gear and flaps were not in landing configuration. Flight crew continued to an uneventful landing after properly positioning flaps and gear.
summary: The monitoring pilot and Pilot Flying approached ORD Runway 27L in strong crosswinds. A GPWS "too low gear" warning occurred at 750 feet with gear up and flaps 2; the crew extended gear and flaps instead of going around, resulting in a normal but non-SOP landing.

synopsis: A B757-200 First Officer reported the flight crew deviated from proper procedure while dealing with a leading edge slat asymmetry issue.
summary: During climb through FL250, the flight crew received a leading edge slat asymmetry message and later set incorrect reference speeds for a Flaps 20 landing instead of the required Flaps 30 plus 30. This error caused a momentary stick shaker on approach, which the Captain arrested by disconnecting the autopilot, reducing pitch, and increasing thrust before an uneventful landing.

synopsis: Shortly after takeoff, crew received a 'VENT SKIN VALVE FAULT' alert message. While performing the QRH procedure and without coordination with the Pilot Flying, the Pilot Monitoring began to depressurize the aircraft while in a climb to 12,000 feet. Crew then received a 'CAB PR EXCESS CAB ALT' alert and re-pressurized the aircraft. During that procedure the original alert was cleared. Crew continued to destination.
summary: During climb after departure, the crew encountered a VENT SKIN VALVE FAULT ECAM and manually depressurized the cabin, triggering a transient CAB PR EXCESS CAB ALT warning while climbing above 10,000 ft. The fault cleared after cycling valves to ON, allowing the flight to continue normally without diversion.

synopsis: A Q400 Captain reported finding a number of switches incorrectly positioned during preflight. One was missed, resulting in the aircraft failing to pressurize during climb.
summary: The Captain departed with the cabin pressure selector in the dump position, triggering a warning while climbing through 10,000 feet. The incident was caused by an inadequate originating flow, expectation bias, and distraction due to pride, compounded by the aircraft being left in a disordered state by previous personnel.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported overshooting a crossing restriction on an RNAV arrival into LAS when they were distracted with a late runway change.
summary: The Captain descended below the 13,000-foot crossing restriction at CLARR while distracted by runway changes and FMS inputs during the KEPEC3 arrival into LAS. The pilot corrected the descent to 13,000 feet after realizing the error, attributing the incident to divided attention and unfamiliarity with Airbus managed descent modes.

synopsis: A B737-800 flight crew reported they failed to meet a crossing restriction on arrival into BOS due to high workload and distractions.
summary: During descent into BOS on the ROBUC1 arrival, the crew crossed PROVI 3,000 feet high because the Captain refused to delete a conflicting downstream FMC restriction. The Pilot Monitoring failed to notice the "at or above" constraint while managing high workload, resulting in a late level-off at 11,000 feet with no ATC intervention.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A pilot reported of incorrectly entering a waypoint that sounded the same, but was spelled differently. The FMS took the incorrect waypoint because it is in the database. The pilot saw a discrepancy and asked for a vector. Pilot stated that it was unfortunate that there are two fixes so closely spelled and that he and his student both missed it.
summary: The flying pilot and IOE student incorrectly entered "FARMM" instead of "FARRM" in the FMS during departure from an uncontrolled airport in icing conditions. The pilot detected the error via MFD flight time, requested vectors from Minneapolis Center, and was cleared direct to DVL, with the root cause identified as a typo compounded by high workload.

synopsis: Airline crew departing LAS in vicinity of ROPPR intersection encountered several rocket launches that were a distraction and potential hazard.
summary: The flight crew observed five rockets ascending near the TRALR6 departure path while climbing through 11,000 to 17,000 feet MSL. They notified ATC and Dispatch, noting that an early clearance to WILLW likely prevented a collision, though the launches posed a potential hazard to aircraft operating near HND and LAS.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: After departing, the crew experienced multiple bird strikes which resulted in high vibration and compressor stalls in the number two engine. They accomplished the checklist and were able to operate the engine at idle while returning to land at departure airport.
summary: During climb-out at 4,000 feet, the crew experienced multiple bird strikes causing high vibration and compressor stalls in engine 2. The aircraft returned for a visual approach to runway 34R, landed with engine 2 at idle, and was inspected by fire and rescue before normal deplaning.

synopsis: Air carrier flight crew exceeded 250 knots below 10,000 feet to expedite to landing airport due to medical emergency of passenger on board.
summary: The crew diverted to the filed destination after a passenger suffered stroke symptoms, despite an EMT's recommendation to land sooner. They exceeded 250 KIAS below 10,000 feet and maintained 320 KIAS during arrival to minimize taxi time, landing 18 minutes early for emergency treatment.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain on STAR with a runway change overshoots crossing altitude at intersection.
summary: Pilots descending via the ANCHR3 STAR to Denver deviated below the 13,000-foot FULLA block altitude while managing rapid weather deterioration and runway changes. They reported the deviation to ATC, complied with remaining restrictions, and completed the flight with no loss of separation.

synopsis: The B767 pilot received several apparently spurious warnings which also affected some of the flight instruments. Everything returned to normal after about a minute except for the failure of the First Officer's altimeter. The aircraft was diverted to a maintenance base.
summary: During cruise at FL 370, the crew experienced multiple false warnings and instrument failures, including a spinning Captain's altimeter and zero FO airspeed. Maintenance determined a diversion to ZZZ was necessary to exit RVSM airspace, and the flight concluded safely after the crew assessed the risks of the Special Use Airport.

synopsis: An Aircraft encountered severe turbulence in the vicinity of convective weather activity. The event resulted in flight attendant injuries.
summary: The flight crew encountered severe turbulence shortly after departure while deviating west of course at FL280, causing altitude variations and injuring three flight attendants and one passenger. Despite the injuries, the crew stabilized the affected personnel and continued to the destination where medical teams met the aircraft.

synopsis: A321 Captain reported executing a go-around after encountering wake turbulence at 150 ft AGL in trail of a B767 on approach to LAX.
summary: The crew encountered wake turbulence at 150 feet while landing LAX 25L behind a heavy 767 and a slow-accelerating A380. They executed a normal go-around, were vectored for another approach, and completed an uneventful landing.

synopsis: Captain reported being told specific taxi instructions to a runway by Ramp Control. The crew taxied as instructed then contacted Ground Control. Ground informed the crew that they did not have clearance to taxi as they did. Flight crew then received different taxi instructions from Ground and were given a phone number to call. Pilot called the number and was told they would look into it.
summary: The flight crew received conflicting taxi instructions from Ramp and Ground controllers at PIT while taxiing on the south side. Ground initially denied issuing instructions, but the crew clarified the situation, noting no safety risk as the area was empty, and the controller agreed to review the recording.

synopsis: B737-800 First Officer reported receiving a low altitude alert on approach to DCA after following flight director LVL CHG guidance when he thought he was in VNAV.
summary: The pilot reported descending below the glide path during an RNAV approach to DCA in IMC, likely due to selecting LVL CHG instead of VNAV. High workload from weather delays and ATC confusion contributed to the error, which was corrected by hand-flying the aircraft back to the glide path for a safe landing.

synopsis: Air Cargo Captain reported speed and track deviations related to fatigue issues.
summary: The pilot flying a Boeing aircraft at ZGGG entered the wrong departure procedure due to fatigue and rushing, causing an FMS disconnect and stick shaker activation during flap retraction. The pilot manually recovered the aircraft, attributing the incident to unverified FMS inputs, going heads-down while flying, and cumulative fatigue.

synopsis: While on ground power, a maintenance technician noticed the nose taxi light was dimly illuminated. When aircraft power was applied and the taxi lights selected, several circuit breakers popped and smoked was noticed in the cockpit. Damaged wiring was identified in the avionics compartment.
summary: A mechanic discovered dim taxi lights and subsequent smoke while troubleshooting an aircraft on ground power, causing circuit breakers to pop. The issue was traced to damaged wiring in the forward avionics compartment and right pack bay feed-through.

synopsis: BE90 First Officer reported returning to departure airport after the left engine was shut down in flight because power could not be reduced below max.
summary: The pilot reported that on departure, the #1 engine stuck at max power despite normal preflight checks. After 30 minutes of troubleshooting, the crew returned to ZZZ, shut down the engine during the RNAV approach, and landed safely as a single-engine aircraft.

synopsis: A corporate pilot reported a heading deviation caused by miscommunication with ATC when runway information was provided along with the unusual use of call sign information translated into an aircraft registration 'N' number.
summary: During an en route Part 91 flight, the SIC and Pilot Flying missed a Runway 24R assignment in the initial approach clearance due to distraction by the controller's call sign usage. Both crew members subsequently initiated the Runway 23 transition instead of the cleared Runway 24L/R arrival.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: The pilot of a small aircraft became trapped in a mountainous area by weather and approaching darkness. After requesting assistance from ATC, the pilot received guidance through the weather to an airport with suitable conditions.
summary: A VFR pilot encountered unforecasted IMC and darkness while attempting to land at an unlit airport in a mountain canyon. The pilot climbed using highway lights and GPS for terrain separation, received radar vectors from SLC Approach, and safely landed at Salt Lake City International Airport via ILS.

synopsis: B757 First Officer reported he was concerned with ATC procedures on arrival into ATL that increased workload.
summary: A crew approaching Atlanta on the KOLTT 1 RNAV STAR experienced increased workload due to late runway changes, shortcut vectors, and unexpected traffic sequencing by ATC. The situation was compounded by a TCAS failure and conflicting speed instructions, forcing early gear deployment and reducing safety margins.

aircraft: Citationjet (C525/C526) - CJ I / II / III / IV
synopsis: C525B Captain reported he was confused flying into HOU when ATC cleared him to another initial point on the same arrival.
summary: The pilot reported confusion during the arrival into HOU when ATC cleared the aircraft direct to WAPPL immediately after passing PLANB, bypassing the intermediate fix ZEBBB. The pilot attributed this to an inference that the direct clearance was expected, noting that skipping intermediate fixes on coded arrivals can cause confusion.

synopsis: Hawker 4000 flight crew reported lining up with Taxiway T instead of Runway 32 at PIT because the taxiway lights were on bright.
summary: The pilot flying misidentified bright green taxiway lights as Runway 32 during a night visual approach to Pittsburgh at 6,000 feet while configuring the aircraft. The crew executed a go-around after cross-checking with the ILS, and the TRACON confirmed the lights were uncontrolled taxiway lights.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: The pilot of a small aircraft reported that during operation in the Hudson River Exclusion Zone Newark Tower reported an airspace violation. The aircraft altimeter was reported to be reading on planned altitude, but the transponder or encoder was providing an inaccurate altitude signal.
summary: A pilot flying a Piper southbound in the Hudson River Exclusion Zone was told by Newark Tower they were violating Class Bravo airspace at 1500 ft, though the pilot's instruments and recorded data showed 1000 ft. The pilot suspects a transponder altitude reporting error and plans to have the pitot/static system checked.

synopsis: The pilot of an SR22 attempted to descend through a break in the cloud layer only to discover additional clouds, resulting in flight into instrument conditions. When VFR conditions could not immediately be located, a climb was initiated to return to VFR on top flight.
summary: The pilot inadvertently entered a hidden cloud layer while descending through a break in cumulus clouds during VFR flight on top. Contributing factors included sunset shadows obscuring the clouds and a delayed climb, forcing a diversion to refuel before landing safely.

synopsis: The pilot of a small aircraft experienced a loss of engine power during landing rollout due to carburetor ice.
summary: The pilot reported an engine quit on rollout from runway 14 caused by carburetor ice. To prevent recurrence, the pilot plans to ensure the application of carburetor heat.

synopsis: The pilot of a PA32 misidentified the traffic to follow in the pattern and experienced a near miss due to an early turn.
summary: The pilot reported a near-midair conflict with a Sky Catcher during twilight arrival due to the lead aircraft's poor lighting and low pattern altitude. Heavy tower traffic and ambiguous instructions caused the pilot to misidentify the aircraft and nearly overfly it before landing.

synopsis: BE30 pilot reported overshooting assigned altitude because of an air data computer failure shortly after takeoff.
summary: The pilot experienced an Air Data Computer failure causing zero airspeed indication just after departure at night. The resulting high workload led to an overshoot of the assigned altitude before the system was reset and the flight continued normally.

synopsis: CL605 Captain reported returning to departure airport after shutting down the right engine because of a fire indication.
summary: The crew received a right engine fire CAS message while climbing through FL280, prompting an engine shutdown and descent. They returned to the departure airport without incident, though they may have begun descending before receiving ATC clearance.

synopsis: SR-22 pilot reported possible violation of a stadium TFR when he had difficulty establishing communications with the Departure Controller.
summary: The pilot departing HOU on Runway 35 could not contact departure immediately due to controller workload, resulting in three call attempts. The pilot may have inadvertently entered a stadium TFR over the Astrodome but chose to maintain the assigned heading of 300 rather than deviate.

synopsis: C425 pilot reported approach and landing difficulties related to inflight ice accumulation.
summary: The pilot experienced heavy controls and altitude loss during an ILS approach due to heavy ice accumulation, leading to a long landing and runway excursion on a slick surface. The aircraft slid off the taxiway but was returned to the threshold without damage, prompting the pilot to acknowledge the need for more frequent deicing boot activation.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; High Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A general aviation pilot reported confusion with the ADS tower about the inbound VFR arrival and altitude.
summary: A pilot inbound to KADS descended from 2,500 feet after receiving a "proceed direct to the numbers" clearance, interpreting it as a descent instruction. The controller later expressed displeasure, claiming he intended for the pilot to maintain altitude, highlighting a communication misunderstanding regarding vertical clearance.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Corporate jet on final executed a go-around due to traffic that was allegedly number two to land.
summary: The pilot executed a missed approach while on a visual approach behind a Hawker due to a target appearing 100 feet below on the Multi-Function Display. Although the passenger later confirmed seeing the aircraft below, the tower maintained that radar and visual separation reports indicated adequate spacing.

synopsis: A320 First Officer landing during gusty crosswind conditions encountered pilot induced oscillations. Captain recommended hand flying the aircraft more during gusty weather and disconnecting the autopilot earlier during approach.
summary: The flying pilot experienced pilot-induced oscillation during a gusty ILS approach to Runway XXR, causing spoilers to extend and the aircraft to drop below profile. The pilot corrected the descent for a safe landing and attributed the oscillation to over-correcting due to being over-primed by previous difficult approaches.

synopsis: Controller misunderstood a pilot's position on the airport and issued taxi instructions from a different point on the airport than the aircraft was actually at. The pilot did not question the instructions, which led the pilot to cross an intersecting runway that another aircraft was cleared for takeoff on. The Ground Controller received a call from ground personnel that the aircraft had an open door. This keyed the controller to observe that the aircraft was in a different position than he thought. The controller told the aircraft to exit the runway prior to the takeoff aircraft positioning on the runway.
summary: Ground Control issued incorrect taxi instructions to Aircraft X due to expectation bias and simultaneous communications, causing the aircraft to cross Runway 5 while another was cleared for takeoff on Runway 23. The controller ordered Aircraft X to exit the runway and hold short after a door issue revealed its position, preventing a collision.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: DFW Tower Controller mistakenly departed aircraft using RNAV departures rather than vectors. The information display system wasn't showing the types of departures in use.
summary: A tower controller launched five aircraft on RNAV departures instead of vectors because the Information Display System hid the vector status when the RVR page was active. This display glitch caused a separation issue, prompting a complaint from one aircraft and a request to fix the software error.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A Ground Controller issued taxi instructions for an arriving aircraft to proceed down an alley to gate. Unknown to the Controller, that gate was already occupied by an aircraft not visible from the newly constructed Control Tower.
summary: An air traffic controller issued a taxi clearance to Aircraft X for an occupied Gate X, causing the pilot to stop and turn 180 degrees in the alley. This delay prevented a timely advisory to Aircraft Y regarding nearby bag carts, highlighting visibility issues at the new tower.

synopsis: An aircraft departing TRACON airspace climbed through the overlying ARTCC sector without coordination. The automated handoff was in effect with the next ARTCC sector along the aircraft's route of flight.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that a departing aircraft violated their airspace above 9000 feet after TRACON issued a climb without prior coordination. The controller attributed the recurring issue to TRACON failing to perform a point out or handoff before entering adjacent facility airspace.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: One sector pointed out an aircraft to another sector and handed it off to the subsequent sector. The sector the aircraft was being handed off to had conflicting traffic and attempted to coordinate control instructions to the Controller working the aircraft. Due to weather complexities, sectors that were combined were being split to alleviate the workload. In the ensuing confusion of closed sectors being opened and busy traffic, the aircraft was not pointed out to one of the newly opened sectors.
summary: An air traffic controller in the X sector verbally pointed out an aircraft to the Y sector, but the Z sector reported conflicting traffic because they did not receive the point out. The controller attributed the communication breakdown and abnormal descent to poor radar displays and recent sector splits causing confusion.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Approach Controller is advised by a pilot on approach to Runway 24 at OXI of a drone sighting at 3000 feet. No evasive action is taken.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X, conducting an RNAV 18 approach to OXI at 2900-3000 ft, encountered a red and black drone approximately 200 feet west at similar altitude. The pilot took no evasive action as it was too late, and the drone did not appear on radar.

synopsis: A SCT TRACON Controller reported of a FUSION Radar tracking problem. The Controller reported of a track that turned to parallel another aircraft that he was separating the turning aircraft from. The Controller reported the STARS system showing Not ARTS Tracked (NAT) on the aircraft then it jumped back to where it was originally supposed to be flying. Controller wants the STARS turned off and Common Automated Radar Terminal System (ARTS) used again.
summary: An air traffic controller reported that Aircraft X's target on the STARS system briefly displayed an incorrect parallel course to Aircraft Y, causing a temporary loss of tracking. The controller attributed this four-second display error to STARS integration issues with fusion, noting that no actual loss of separation occurred.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported failing to meet a crossing restriction after misunderstanding an ATC clearance.
summary: The flight crew descended early due to turbulence, missing a crossing restriction at FL180 before receiving a new clearance to 16,000 feet. The controller later admitted the restriction was still needed but noted no conflict occurred, attributing the confusion to unclear instructions regarding the descent rate and altitude.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported taking off with the wrong flap setting because of distractions.
summary: The crew attempted an intersection takeoff with flaps set to 1 instead of the required 5 due to distraction and failure to visually verify the flap handle. The error was discovered after takeoff when the Captain called for speed/flaps 1, but the flight continued uneventfully.

synopsis: A First Officer reported the flight crew failed to complete all checklists following failure of the outer pane of forward right windshield.
summary: During cruise at FL410, the right forward outer windshield pane shattered, prompting a descent to FL330 and reduced speed. The crew completed the flight safely but later realized they missed a supplementary checklist due to low type experience and unavailability of the procedure.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported being asked by ATC during the CYRUS Visual to Runway 25 at MROC to extend downwind for departing traffic. The crew was at 4000 feet (1000 AGL) per the procedure and had to climb to avoid rising terrain to the east of the field.
summary: The First Officer, flying a Cyrus Visual arrival into MROC, manually climbed to match rising terrain after extending downwind for a departing B757. This action maintained safe clearance above mandatory crossing altitudes at BELEN and EPABE, resulting in an uneventful landing with no GPWS warnings.

aircraft: Medium Transport; High Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: The crew received a cabin pressure warning when climbing through 10,000 feet after departing LAX. After discovering that the pressurization switch was set incorrectly, they were able to proceed to their destination.
summary: Flight crew experienced a cabin pressure alarm while climbing through 10,000 feet after ground crew left the pressurization switch in 'dump' at LAX. The crew attributed the oversight to complacency during preflight checks, descended to 10,000 feet to complete the checklist, and continued the flight normally once pressurization resumed.

synopsis: ERJ-175 flight crew reported they deviated from cleared track after confusing the similar fixes KLINE and KLYNE.
summary: The crew misinterpreted an ATC clearance for the KLYNE fix as KLINE due to similar pronunciation, causing FMS waypoint errors. After verifying the correct route with ATC, the flight proceeded to KLYNE, and the pilot recommended renaming one fix to prevent future confusion.

synopsis: A B737 Captain reported returning to the gate for de-ice when a deadheading pilot in the cabin noticed the wings were not clear. The reporter expressed concern that the pre-departure Ice check was not performed properly by ground personnel.
summary: Pilots returned to the gate after a deadheading pilot discovered frost on the wings despite maintenance reporting a clean ice check prior to push. The reporter suspects the technician performed only a visual inspection from the ground, missing upper surface contamination, and recommends mandatory upper wing checks.

synopsis: A B737 Captain reported deviating from cleared track when the aircraft entered a 'standoff' condition.
summary: During a training flight approaching SEA RWY 16R, late ATC clearance combined with FMC LNAV functions caused an automated Standoff Mode and disengaged Autothrottles. The Captain manually rebuilt the approach, re-engaged Autothrottles, and completed a stabilized CAT III autoland.

synopsis: On the CREDE3 arrival to the RNAV 16R at DEN, the First Officer prematurely selected Approach and started a descent before being cleared for the approach.
summary: The First Officer, acting as PF on a descent into Denver, prematurely engaged the approach mode without ATC clearance while managing a Captain-imposed RNAV procedure. The Captain intercepted the error at 10,600 feet, leveled the aircraft, and the flight landed safely without incident.

synopsis: After some delay in interpreting a 'Standard Taxi Route' clearance at DFW, the crew began to taxi, but had to made a sudden stop for conflicting traffic.
summary: A flight crew at DFW delayed taxiing to Runway 17R while searching iPad charts for standard routes, causing a near collision with two aircraft crossing their path. The First Officer stopped the aircraft, but Ground Control stated the crew took too long to move and should have cleared the intersection.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant on an A319 inadvertently started to open door 1R before disarming the slide. The First Officer tried to assist, but they were unable to close the door and when it was released the slide deployed.
summary: Flight Attendant #1 accidentally opened the R1 door instead of disarming it at the gate due to personal stress, fatigue, and distractions. The First Officer and Captain attempted to close the door, but it was eventually released, causing the slide to deploy.

synopsis: Captain reported that Lithium Metal batteries can be carried onboard the aircraft under IATA shipper exemption UN 3090 Section II but not declared on the Dangerous Goods paperwork. The reporter recommended a change in policy.
summary: The flight crew discovered undeclared lithium metal batteries in position 4R during a Dangerous Goods inspection, which were legally exempt from manifesting under UN 3090 Section II. This lack of crew awareness caused a 35-minute delay and raised safety concerns regarding emergency decision-making, leading the reporter to call for a policy change requiring all DG to be declared.

synopsis: A B777-200 Captain reported a track deviation on an international flight stemming from a misunderstanding with ATC.
summary: The flight crew accepted an amended oceanic clearance via CPDLC and proceeded to a new coast-out point without a separate domestic clearance. Moncton Center clarified the misunderstanding, noting that the oceanic clearance did not authorize the domestic leg, though no loss of separation occurred.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported ATC issued a clearance that would have taken them beyond the 50 nm from land limit, at least according to their Dispatcher.
summary: During en route flight, pilots accepted an ATC shortcut but received conflicting confirmation regarding 50 NM offshore compliance from controllers versus dispatch. After controllers insisted the route was valid despite dispatch's warning, the crew requested a westward heading, resulting in a revised, approved route.

synopsis: Flight crew experienced an apparent ground spoiler problem on landing roll out and decide to watch the spoilers closer on landing next leg.
summary: During landing rollout, ground spoilers deployed then stowed unexpectedly. The Pilot Monitoring reset the speedbrake handle, but the crew continued to the next destination instead of contacting maintenance, a decision the reporter later deemed poor.

synopsis: An A320 pilot refused an aircraft with an inoperative APU because of terrain and weather considerations.
summary: The pilot refused the aircraft due to an inoperative APU, citing enroute terrain and forecasted weather at ZZZ1. The decision was made to ensure backup pneumatic and electric power availability for safety.

synopsis: The B777 crew forgot to set a hard Mach number for an Atlantic crossing and flew at ECON .79 Mach instead of .82 Mach as cleared.
summary: The pilot flying and relief first officer failed to enter the cleared Mach 0.82 into the FMC during the Atlantic crossing, resulting in an unintentional deviation to Mach 0.79. Distractions from turbulence, equipment failures, and communication issues caused the error, which the crew corrected upon discovery without ATC intervention.

aircraft: Airbus Industrie Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: An Airbus wide body Cargo flight crew reported they were advised upon arrival by ground personnel that the dangerous goods door was not properly positioned for their flight.
summary: The flight crew and load crew discovered the DG container door was unattached during preflight after the First Officer recalled the DG representative securing it while he checked the fire extinguisher hose. The ground crew later found the door leaning against the aircraft frame, prompting a recommendation to witness all locks and hose attachments before leaving the aircraft.

synopsis: Flight crew experienced fumes in the cockpit during climbout followed by an equipment cooling alert. Crew elected to return to the departure airport. Landing was uneventful followed by taxi to the gate.
