These oscillations were determined to be caused by a malfunctioning autopilot system. The autopilot was disengaged, air traffic control notified, and the flight continued safely to its destination.
summary: Pilots of a Hawker 800XP at FL400 experienced altitude oscillations and stiff, ratcheting elevator trim with no cockpit warnings. After switching AFCS systems failed to resolve the issue, they descended to FL280, reported an autopilot malfunction, and landed safely.

synopsis: B737 flight attendants experienced symptoms of toxic fume exposure.
summary: Flight attendants on the second leg reported toxic fume exposure symptoms to the Captain, who dismissed the report citing a lack of procedures and a desire to avoid company alarms. One flight attendant remained unrecovered by the third day of the sequence.

synopsis: After accomplishing checks on two different airplanes, Maintenance neglected to sign off the airworthiness release for an MD11 aircraft.
summary: A mechanic serviced two aircraft and deferred a wing light on Aircraft X but failed to sign the Airworthiness Release (AWR) before the crew arrived. Relying on the Captain's verbal confirmation that the logbook was good, the mechanic launched the aircraft without the required signed AWR.

synopsis: A Learjet Captain reported a failure of the yaw damper system while making a turn during the climb phase of flight. The airplane entered into a Dutch roll which resulted in an overshoot of the assigned altitude. The Dutch roll was successfully arrested and the aircraft was returned to the cleared altitude.
summary: During departure, the flight crew experienced a yaw damper malfunction causing a Dutch roll while turning right to maintain 8,000 feet MSL. The aircraft overshot to 8,400 feet MSL before leveling off, but the crew landed without incident and received no follow-up instructions from ATC.

synopsis: C310 pilot reported a total electrical failure inbound to HUM that resulted in an MSY mode C veil transponder violation.
summary: The pilot experienced total electrical failure at 5,500 feet, rendering instruments and transponder inoperative. After manually lowering the gear and coordinating via cell phone, the pilot received a verbal clearance to land at Houma-Terrebonne, resulting in no injuries but a violation of the Class B encoder veil.

synopsis: BE30 Captain reported a track deviation after departing APC when he was cleared to TRUCK, but navigated toward TRK.
summary: The pilot assumed "TRK" was a valid waypoint near the airport instead of verifying the ATC-issued "TRUCK" clearance, causing an incorrect FMS entry during climb. The crew corrected the error after ATC confirmed the spelling and issued a vector, highlighting a failure to verify waypoints not in the filed flight plan.

synopsis: AC90 pilot reported shutting down the right engine after a passenger noticed sparks coming from the cowling following a generator failure.
summary: The pilot of a twin-engine aircraft carrying three souls experienced a right generator failure and sparks from the engine cowling while en route at 10,500 feet. The pilot shut down the right engine as a precaution, continued to land safely, and reported no fire or smoke upon arrival.

synopsis: BE-200 Captain reported beginning the takeoff roll at DCA without clearance from the Tower.
summary: The flight crew at DCA initiated an unauthorized takeoff from Runway 33 after misinterpreting a new departure clearance as a takeoff authorization. The pilot aborted the roll when Tower instructed them to stop, attributing the error to the controller failing to explicitly instruct them to hold while issuing the new heading and altitude.

synopsis: C182 pilot encountered aircraft and induction icing during descent and was unable to hold assigned altitude. Pilot descended below the freezing level and landed visually.
summary: The pilot encountered severe icing and engine induction issues while descending from 5,500 to 4,000 feet MSL, forcing a descent to 3,000 feet to shed ice. Unable to hold the assigned altitude or contact ATC initially, the pilot relayed the emergency via another aircraft before landing and filing a pilot report.

synopsis: GTF Local Control and a pilot of one aircraft reported an NMAC. Tower Controller instructed one of the aircraft to go-around in order to separate the traffic.
summary: An instrument instructor in Aircraft X and a student in Aircraft Y experienced a near-miss during simultaneous approaches to Runway 21 at Great Falls International Airport. The controller issued conflicting traffic advisories and a go-around for Aircraft Y after neither pilot visually acquired the other until the final approach segment.

synopsis: A pilot of a light aircraft reported icing conditions where the application of carburetor heat was ineffectual, resulting in degraded engine performance. He requested a lower altitude and the icing threat dissipated and engine operation returned to normal.
summary: The pilot encountered persistent carburetor ice at 9,000 feet during an IMC flight, causing RPM loss and a frozen throttle despite using carb heat. After descending to 7,000 feet with ATC permission, the ice dissipated and power was restored, though the pilot admitted poor judgment for continuing into the conditions.

synopsis: A Controller receiving a handoff from a sector did not take appropriate action to issue control instructions for that aircraft in order to avoid other enroute traffic.
summary: An air traffic controller stopped Aircraft X at FL190 to avoid a conflict with Aircraft Y in [ZZZ] airspace after the adjacent controller failed to coordinate or issue instructions. Subsequent conflicting headings from [ZZZ] caused both aircraft to pass vertically close at 18,000 and 19,000 feet, which the reporter attributed to the controller's unsafe actions and lack of interim altitude data.

synopsis: SCT Controller described clearing three aircraft for visual approaches to Runway 31L at PSP and to follow each other. The aircraft third in line, loses track of the second aircraft and comes within 1.5 miles before the Controller intercedes. The Controller wonders what the third aircrafts crew was seeing on their TCAS.
summary: An air traffic controller managing a visual approach sequence to Runway 31L at PSP observed Aircraft Z closing too closely on Aircraft Y. The controller instructed Aircraft Z to maintain visual separation after the crew confirmed sight, noting a potential error in identifying the correct traffic.

synopsis: B777 flight crew reported excessive oil consumption from a newly replaced engine. Crew returned to departure airport.
summary: The crew discovered a new Engine 2 lacked an ETOPS verification flight, but oil quantity dropped from 24 to 13 quarts during the outbound leg. They aborted the verification, returned, and landed with 9 quarts, which rose to 15 quarts after shutdown.

synopsis: A320 flight crew reported responding to an RA on a visual approach into DEN when a small aircraft entered Class B airspace without authorization.
summary: A crew flying a visual approach to 35L in Denver received a climb RA at 8,500 feet due to a small aircraft violating Class B airspace by over 800 feet. The First Officer executed a climb to 10,000 feet to resolve the conflict, which was caused by a departing aircraft from Front Range climbing too high.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: B737 First Officer reported confusing and conflicting guidance for departures from MROC.
summary: Pilots reported confusion during an MROC RW7 departure when ATC assigned the COCOS 5 RNAV SID, conflicting with a Terrain Threat bulletin requiring specific POAS4 procedures. The crew questioned climb gradient compliance and equipment settings, noting discrepancies between the bulletin, 10-7 pages, and the assigned departure.

synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported they were cleared for the RNAV (GPS) Z Runway 17 approach to MTJ in visual conditions. They deviated from their IFR clearance to avoid an aircraft on final without obtaining clearance for a visual approach from Denver Center.
summary: The flight crew, operating a light transport on an IFR approach to Montrose, executed an unauthorized 360-degree turn to avoid VFR traffic without contacting Denver Center. This error resulted from expectation bias in clear conditions and radio mismanagement, though the aircraft landed safely after the crew realized they had neglected to obtain a visual approach clearance.

synopsis: B757 lost all hydraulic fluid from the Left Hydraulic System.
summary: The flight crew experienced a left hydraulic system failure on a Boeing 757 during climb, likely caused by maintenance work on the APU fuel valve. They continued to the destination, landing safely on the longest runway with alternate gear and flap extension, followed by a tow to the gate due to fluid leakage and lack of nose wheel steering.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported they diverted to an alternate after experiencing a compressor stall at FL220 possibly from a light wake turbulence encounter.
summary: The crew encountered wake turbulence from an A330 en route, prompting cabin reports of flames from the right engine. Suspecting an engine stall, they returned to ZZZ1 for a safe landing at maximum weight after communication delays with dispatch.

synopsis: Load planer reported discovering after departure that Customer Service had reseated 9 passengers from coach into first-class cabin producing a nose heavy condition.
summary: Customer service reseated nine passengers from coach to first class without notification, invalidating the weight and balance. This resulted in a nose-heavy Mean Aerodynamic Chord of 4.0 percent.

synopsis: While unloading bags from an A320, ramp crew noticed that the nose of the aircraft started to rise. They stopped unloading from the forward cargo bay until the aft bay was unloaded.
summary: Ramp crew unloading an A320 at the gate observed the nose gear rise 1/2 inch due to forward cargo removal. They immediately stopped forward unloading and increased aft unloading to lower the gear.

synopsis: A pilot of a regional jet reported an inability to control cabin pressurization once established at cruise altitude. A lower altitude and diversion to a suitable airport occurred. The flight landed uneventfully.
summary: The flight crew experienced a loss of pressurization at FL330, with cabin altitude rising to 10,300ft, prompting an emergency descent to ZZZ. The crew donned oxygen masks and followed the QRH procedure, attributing the delayed detection to insufficient instrument monitoring and cross-checking.

synopsis: EMB-175 Captain is informed after gate arrival that bags had been loaded above the fire suppression line on their previous leg. The ground had been specifically asked by the First Officer prior to departure if the bags were loaded correctly.
summary: After blocking in, a ramp employee reported that the forward cargo compartment contained bags above the fire suppression line, violating the placarded limit despite the Seattle ramp crew's prior assurance that all 42 bags were loaded correctly. The Captain attributed the improper load to the ramp crew's failure to adhere to aircraft restrictions and noted that maintenance delays prevented a physical inspection in Seattle.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew elected to start a placarded component, the APU, in order to start engines. All available ground carts were inoperative due to extreme cold weather.
summary: The flight crew and a mechanic operated an APU placarded inoperative to start the engine after air start carts failed due to fuel freezing. Although the flight departed, the crew later learned this violated regulations by operating the placarded equipment.

synopsis: Air carrier Flight Attendant reported that since the merger with another air carrier several pilots have mentioned the training on the aircraft differences are insufficient, and they were unclear on how to operate the PA system.
summary: A flight attendant reported that pilots on a newly merged aircraft could not operate the PA system or interphone due to inadequate Computer Based Training. This inability to communicate poses a serious safety risk, specifically preventing the crew from issuing emergency commands like "BRACE, BRACE."

synopsis: Airbus A320 series Flight Attendant reported their flight returned to departure airport after a strong odor filled the cabin.
summary: A cabin crew member reported a strong exhaust odor filling the cabin shortly after takeoff, which dissipated but returned during the descent back to ZZZ. The fumes caused physical symptoms for the crew, prompting the Captain to divert the flight.

synopsis: C206 Captain reported returning to departure airport after experiencing control difficulties after takeoff. After landing, nose strut was found to be flat, allowing the nosewheel to weather vane, affecting directional control.
summary: Pilots of a Cessna 206 experienced a flat nose wheel strut after maintenance, causing a right yaw in flight and a runway veer on landing. The collapsed strut disabled the self-centering mechanism, forcing a precautionary landing where the crew regained control after the nose wheel hit the ground.

synopsis: C152 pilot reported landing in a field after the engine quit because of fuel starvation.
summary: The pilot of a Cessna 152 experienced repeated engine sputtering and eventual failure during VFR flight due to inaccurate fuel gauges indicating sufficient fuel when tanks were actually empty. After declaring an emergency and receiving ATC vectors, the pilot successfully executed an off-field landing in an open field.

synopsis: C182RG pilot reported taking off and becoming aware the elevator trim had been rigged backwards.
summary: A pilot flying a flight school aircraft after annual inspection experienced reversed elevator trim control during the climb, causing excessive nose-down force. The pilot identified the trim tabs were moving opposite to the indicator, corrected the issue by reversing trim inputs, and executed a full stop landing.

synopsis: Piper Cherokee pilot reported an NMAC in the pattern at LEE airport resulting from ATC communication confusion.
summary: A pilot flying a Cherokee into a busy traffic pattern at LEE experienced a near-miss with an experimental aircraft due to the tower controller misassigning landing positions. The controller's lack of situational awareness and the pilot's failure to verify aircraft order caused the conflict, resulting in the experimental aircraft executing a go-around.

synopsis: The pilot of a C172 reported an NMAC with a helicopter during takeoff at night. The Tower had advised that the helicopter would be no factor, but the reporter disagreed.
summary: During a night takeoff, a pilot reported a near-collision with a military helicopter at 600 feet MSL despite Tower clearance stating the helicopter was "no factor." The pilot avoided impact by applying full forward pressure and idle power, attributing the safe outcome to looking outside and the see-and-avoid principle.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air taxi flight crew reported departing TEB and being given instructions by ATC to 'turn left' from 240 to a 270 heading which would put them in conflict with traffic during the turn. After querying ATC multiple times they were given a right turn. Later conversation with ATC revealed the Controller was using nonstandard phraseology by saying 'turn west' which the crew misinterpreted as 'turn left.'
summary: Pilots on a TEB1 departure from Runway 24 at 1500 ft MSL misunderstood a controller's instruction to turn "West" as "Left," creating a conflict with an approaching 757. The incident resulted from the controller's nonstandard phraseology, which was clarified post-flight after the crew was instructed to call ATC.

synopsis: A ZMA Controller descended one aircraft and climbed another aircraft head on. The Controller issued turns to the aircraft but had less than required lateral separation.
summary: An air traffic controller and two pilots were involved in a near-midair collision at 33,000 feet where conflicting TCAS RAs and delayed pilot compliance resulted in a 3-mile separation. The controller attributed the incident to active warning areas restricting maneuvering space and a pilot's failure to promptly execute climb and turn instructions.

synopsis: B737 crew descending into BWI reported not receiving a handoff from ZDC to PCT TRACON. They queried ATC on the handoff and were switched over to PCT where soon after they noticed ground based laser activity directed at them realizing it was due to the restricted airspace over Washington DC. ATC also asked them of the laser activity soon after and requested their tail number upon landing with no further explanation.
summary: The flight crew descended from FL390 on RAVNN6 to BWI Runway 10 but experienced a lost handoff where ATC initially did not know their position. They later observed green laser lights, which ATC clarified were for restricted airspace, before landing without explanation for a subsequent ground control tail number request.

synopsis: A B737 Captain flying the SFO SERFR2 was cleared descend via except maintain 6,000 feet and then NORCAL alerted they descended out of SFO Class B. Numerous altitude clearance changes on the arrival created a high workload environment.
summary: The flight crew experienced multiple conflicting descent and approach clearances while arriving at SFO on the SERFR2 arrival. The pilot attributed the confusion to frequent ATC instruction changes within 40 miles of the airport, noting room for improvement in handling "descend via" clearances.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported ground vehicles failing to yield to his aircraft during taxi out of an alleyway at LAX, causing a twenty minute delay.
summary: The flight crew of a Boeing 757 at LAX halted taxiing for 20 minutes after multiple ground vehicles ignored the solid white boundary line and entered the aircraft's path. Ramp Tower and Airport Operations eventually cleared the vehicles, but the incident caused delays to other aircraft due to driver inattention and congestion.

synopsis: An air carrier flight crew reported electing to continue approach and land despite close interval spacing of departing traffic on the same runway.
summary: During arrival at SDF, the crew landed Aircraft Y shortly after a wide-body departed 17R, creating a close separation concern. The pilot elected to land rather than go around to avoid conflicting flight paths, exceeding the 1,000 fpm descent limit and receiving a sink rate call before landing safely.

synopsis: CRJ-200 Captain reported an inflight shutdown of right hand engine after receiving a low oil pressure warning message.
summary: The flying pilot and First Officer experienced fluctuating right engine oil pressure enroute, prompting a QRH-directed intentional shutdown. They diverted to a nearby alternate, requested emergency equipment, and landed safely on a single engine.

synopsis: HS-125-900XP Captain reported operating several legs with the rudder gust lock not on board in its proper stow position.
summary: The PIC of an aircraft returning from maintenance failed to verify the rudder gust lock was stowed during preflight due to distractions and mixed communication with the SIC. The missing lock, which also serves as the auxiliary hydraulic pump handle, was discovered post-flight, grounding the aircraft.

synopsis: CRJ-200 flight crew reported taking off with the standby pitot cover still in place, necessitating a return to the airport to get it removed.
summary: The flight crew departed with the standby pitot cover still installed after skipping the acceptance checklist. Upon hearing a flapping sound after rotation, they circled back to land, attributing the error to rushing and omitting required checks.

synopsis: CRJ-900 Captain reported he noticed during preflight that his crew oxygen mask had been serviced improperly and he would not have been able to communicate using it.
summary: The pilot reported that after maintenance replaced the Captain's oxygen mask to fix a leak, the microphone failed because the cannon plug was not connected. This incomplete repair would have prevented cockpit communication and ATC contact during a smoke or fume emergency.

synopsis: B737-800 Captain reported that he was advised FOQA data recorded a hard landing at JFK in gusty conditions.
summary: The Pilot Flying landed a Boeing 737 at JFK in gusty crosswinds after ignoring a late PWS windshear warning at 85 feet. FOQA data indicated the landing gear G limit was slightly exceeded, though the pilot attributed the hard touchdown to weather conditions and the urgency to avoid windshear.

synopsis: B787 First Officer reported confusion on short final regarding final flaps setting, related in part to human factors after a long absence from work.
summary: A returning First Officer on a Boeing 787 international flight created an unstable approach by selecting Flaps 30 below 1000 feet due to task saturation and unfamiliarity. The Captain elected to land in VMC conditions, resulting in a safe landing without incident.

synopsis: A321 Flight Attendant reported she went to the emergency room after arrival because 'dirty sock' fumes in the cabin had caused troubling symptoms.
summary: Flight attendants reported a strong, irritating odor during climb and descent that caused severe physical symptoms requiring an emergency room visit. The Captain logged the incident, and mechanics were consulted, but the specific cause of the recurring air quality issue remains undetermined.

synopsis: Flight Attendants are finding heavy duty seals on the Portable Breathing Equipment (PBE) that has to be cut off in order to use the equipment.
summary: A flight attendant reported that maintenance installed heavy-duty seals on Essex Portable Breathing Equipment above the #2 jump seat, requiring cutting to access. The reporter stated this prevents rapid emergency use, potentially causing loss of life, and recommended replacing them with break-away seals.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: A pilot and flight instructor reported a loss of control and runway excursion during landing at BTL due to field conditions.
summary: An instructor and student pilot experienced a runway excursion off 23R at BTL during landing in snow. Despite a stabilized approach, the aircraft skidded left into a snowbank immediately after touchdown, resulting in no damage or injuries.

synopsis: G-IV flight crew reported diverting to a nearby alternate after a malfunctioning cargo door seal led to a loss of cabin pressure.
summary: The crew experienced a cabin pressure loss at FL450 due to a faulty baggage door seal, triggering a rapid emergency descent. The Captain took control, diverted to an alternate, and landed safely after maintenance confirmed the seal failure caused the incident.

aircraft: Piper Single Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: PA-11 pilot reported losing directional control after landing with a quartering tailwind.
summary: The pilot attempted a landing with a left quartering tailwind, causing the aircraft to depart the runway right and impact a sand berm. The reporter attributed the incident to failing to verify wind direction via an overflight and windsock check.

synopsis: A Cirrus pilot and instructor reported a loss of control and runway excursion at BTL due to field conditions.
summary: A student and instructor landed a training aircraft on a contaminated runway with thin dry snow over ice. Despite stable touchdown, the aircraft veered left and departed the runway surface due to reduced braking action, resulting in no injuries.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported they were on the DSERT2 Arrival to SDL then cleared for a visual approach. Reporter stated ATC then asked them to fly '...east of Pinnacle Peak...' which put them over an area of high terrain.
summary: The pilot reported that after being cleared for a visual approach to SDL, ATC instructed a turn east of Pinnacle Peak, placing the aircraft over high terrain beyond PAPI coverage. The pilot described this as a dangerous scenario requiring rapid descent over terrain, noting a past near-miss and suggesting controller awareness or arrival changes.

synopsis: A319 Flight Attendant reported their flight diverted to an alternate after a mechanical issue caused smoke in the cabin.
summary: Cabin crew responded to smoke in the cabin after departure, using halon and PBE while pilots deployed oxygen masks due to respiratory irritation. The pilots identified hydraulic fluid as the source, diverted to an alternate airport, and completed a normal landing.

synopsis: A Center and Tower Controller disagreed whether an aircraft with an IFR clearance including an initial VFR leg could be released with simultaneous IFR arrivals. The Tower departed the aircraft with an aircraft on approach.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller reported a conflict with a Tower Controller regarding Aircraft Y's clearance from the ground versus over an intersection while Aircraft X and Z were on approach. The Controller refused the ground clearance to maintain IFR separation, noting that management fails to provide direction on this issue despite previous guidance.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 2 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: HSV controllers reported of a runway incursion involving a vehicle. The controllers just thought that vehicles had to be clear of the runway and did not realize that vehicles had to be on the safe side of the hold short bars.
summary: Three vehicles conducting a runway inspection on Runway 33 were classified as causing a runway incursion while an aircraft was inbound for landing. The reporter attributes the incident to a misunderstanding of FAA Order 7110.65, which they believed excluded vehicles from the "clear of the runway" definition despite the vehicles remaining within the runway safety area.

synopsis: D10 TRACON Controller reported a departing aircraft could not contact the correct D10 TRACON sector. The aircraft was assigned a departure altitude which would take it below the minimum vectoring altitude.
summary: An Air Traffic Controller assisted Aircraft X, a propeller departure from DFW, after the pilot reported radio failure while below another aircraft in Dallas South airspace. The controller provided the correct frequency and later noted that the current departure heading and altitude create an unsafe situation if communication is lost.

synopsis: B737 Captain reported executing an abrupt stop when a ground operations vehicle crossed directly in front of his aircraft near the gate area.
summary: During taxi to the gate, a ground vehicle crossed the J-line at high speed in front of the aircraft, forcing the pilot to apply maximum brakes for a violent stop to avoid collision. The pilot reported the incident to ramp personnel, who agreed to review security footage, and emphasized the need for drivers to avoid crossing moving aircraft.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported that after running the QRH for a left flaps transit light they received a stick shaker on approach that was later traced to a malfunctioning stall warning system.
summary: The crew experienced a left flaps transit light and two stick shaker activations during approach, prompting a go-around and a subsequent flaps 15 landing. Post-flight maintenance confirmed the stick shaker check failed, indicating a system fault despite normal airspeed indications.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier Captain reported taking evasive action to avoid a light twin aircraft while on approach at MTJ, and stated the same aircraft has caused problems in the past.
summary: A pilot reported three consecutive close encounters with a slow-moving light twin during visual approaches to Runway 17 at MTJ. The lack of position reports from the other aircraft and simultaneous operations on opposite runways forced avoidance maneuvers, leading the pilot to recommend a part-time tower.

synopsis: B737-800 flight crew reported letting the airspeed get low on approach when their attention was diverted to FMC programming.
summary: During a 737-800 descent into PHX, the Captain became distracted programming the FMS while flying, causing airspeed to decay to 149 knots. The First Officer recognized the low speed, applied maximum thrust, and recovered the aircraft without a stall warning before landing on Runway 25R.

synopsis: A319 FO reported the flying pilot (the Captain) descended early on the LDA-A approach to LGA, prompting a low altitude alert call from ATC.
summary: The Captain hand-flew an early descent on the LDA-A approach to LGA Runway 22, ignoring the Final Approach Fix due to visual contact despite glare. This triggered a low altitude warning from Tower, prompting a climb to re-establish the normal profile before an uneventful landing.

synopsis: EMB-145 Captain reported concern that flight crews are becoming too accepting of wing anti-ice issues in the fleet.
summary: The flight crew experienced recurring anti-ice system failures and bleed temperature cautions during a CAT II descent into ZZZ in icing conditions. The pilot reported that company guidance and QRH procedures to add thrust were ineffective, leading to under-reporting of these issues and concerns about potential aircraft stalling in ice.

aircraft: Medium Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Flight crew experienced a system failure which rendered nose wheel steering inoperative.
summary: During initial descent for ZZZ, the crew received WOW INPUT and PROX SYS FAULT messages indicating potential nose wheel steering failure. Upon landing, steering was confirmed inoperative, requiring differential braking to clear the runway and a tug for the final tow-in.

synopsis: CL600 flight crew reported their right engine shut down after they experienced a lightning strike on approach.
summary: During the arrival descent, the aircraft was struck by lightning, causing the right #2 engine to fail. The crew advised ATC, executed checklists, and landed safely, seeking to determine the cause of the engine failure following the strike.

synopsis: EC-130 Captain reported the left rear door came open in flight when it was not properly checked before departure.
summary: During cruise flight with a patient and nurse on board, the left rear door slid open due to pilot error in failing to fully seal the door frame and a 30-knot crosswind. The pilot descended to land at the hospital, offloaded the patient, and confirmed no damage after maintenance inspection.

synopsis: B757-200 flight crew and Dispatcher reported the aircraft was over fueled by 9000 lbs. The Captain thought the Fueler said 900 lbs, but discovered the true amount while in cruise.
summary: The flight crew misinterpreted a fueler's report of a 9,000-pound overfueling as 900 pounds, resulting in an undetected 9,000-pound excess at takeoff. The error was discovered at FL280, but dispatch never received the crew's ACARS correction due to a system failure, though the flight remained uneventful.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: MD-83 flight crew reported experiencing a stabilizer trim failure on approach.
summary: During approach at 2500 feet, the MD80's stabilizer trim jammed while configuring to flaps 40, causing a nose-down pitch and requiring a go-around. The crew executed the STAB INOP checklist and landed safely with flaps 15, though a GPWS warning occurred due to selecting the wrong override switch.

synopsis: B777 First Officer Relief Pilot reported the aircraft was operated for 'quite some time' with an FMS Navigation database installed that was for another aircraft type. Maintenance Technician responsible for the data load suggested improvements to prevent a future occurrence.
summary: Maintenance personnel inadvertently uploaded an FMS database for a different aircraft type onto a B777 during a software update. The error occurred because similar file names and identical disk labels on the desktop led to the wrong file being transferred to the floppy disk.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A large twin engine transport aircraft flight crew reported blocking in with 5100 LBS of fuel even though the FMS projected 7100 LBS.
summary: The crew encountered unexpected holding over WHOLL while en route to MEM, extending their EFC time and reducing predicted fuel below planned reserves. Although cleared for approach two minutes early, they landed with 5.1 tons and blocked with 4.7 tons, triggering a low fuel alert below their 5.0-ton emergency threshold.

synopsis: EMB175 Flight Attendants reported an inadvertent slide deployment during gate arrival. Lack of hands on training was cited as a factor due to the EMB175 being new equipment for the airline.
summary: A fatigued flight attendant on an ERJ flight accidentally deployed the door slide by lifting the handle instead of the cover during arrival. The reporter attributed the error to stress, fatigue, and a lack of recent hands-on training on the jet after years of flying turboprops.

synopsis: Dash 8 Flight Attendant reported experiencing head injury symptoms after a turbulence incident.
summary: A flight attendant was injured by a major turbulence drop during the landing phase while working in the galley, striking her head, arm, and leg. Two passengers also sustained head injuries, and the crew reported the incident to maintenance and sought medical treatment for the attendant's head injury and blurred vision.

synopsis: A company Mechanic reported that Contract Ramp Personnel were not taking the necessary precautions to prevent aircraft damage during guidance into the gate area.
summary: The pilot stopped the aircraft after ramp personnel attempted to taxi it near FOD, containers, and temporary building walls. The incident was caused by untrained personnel treating the aircraft like a different type, risking container lift-off and wall collapse during a sharp turn.

synopsis: A CE-560 Captain reported diverting to a nearby alternate after experiencing loss of cabin pressure.
summary: The flight crew enroute at FL310 experienced a loud pop and a cabin pressurization climb rate of 4,000 fpm. They requested and received an emergency descent, diverting to an alternate while stabilizing cabin altitude at approximately 13,000 feet.

synopsis: The pilot of a DA42 reported a malfunctioning engine that resulted in a successful return to the departure airport.
summary: Pilots of a Diamond DA42NG experienced a right engine power loss and ECU failure during practice maneuvers. They returned to the departure airport, advising ATC of the issue, and completed an uneventful landing with both engines functioning normally.

synopsis: Beechcraft Travelair pilot reported the use of a voltage converter damaged handheld supplemental electronic equipment.
summary: A pilot reported that using a 12-110 volt power inverter in the flight deck generated static electricity that scrambled an iPhone and Kindle electronic flight bag. The pilot noted that while air carriers forbid such inverters, their status under Part 91 regulations is unknown.

synopsis: It was determined by a maintenance facility that at least part of the aircraft repair/rebuild had not been accomplished properly, had not been documented properly, and was not airworthy.
summary: An instructor flew a rebuilt aircraft over 30 times believing it was airworthy based on logbook entries and preflight checks. A subsequent annual inspection revealed improper undocumented repairs and uncomplied Airworthiness Directives, confirming the aircraft was unairworthy during those flights.

synopsis: SCT Instructor while instructing developmental had a loss of separation due to developmental clearing an aircraft for a visual approach while another aircraft was in close proximity.
summary: An instructor and trainee managing Aircraft X and Y near OKB failed to ensure separation when the trainee cleared Aircraft X for visual approach. The incident occurred because the instructor incorrectly assumed Aircraft X would turn toward the airport, requiring a subsequent MVA violation and Tower coordination to resolve the conflict.

aircraft: Small Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turboprop Eng
synopsis: A CIC reported of a shift where he was in charge and the weather was IFR at the Airport. They could not see the departure or arrival and they thought they had a loss of separation.
summary: A CIC reported a potential runway incursion at ZZZ during low visibility when a local trainee cleared Aircraft X for takeoff without traffic advisories or roll reports while Aircraft Y was on final. The incident resulted in uncertain separation, attributed to the trainee's failure to follow SOPs and the CIC's hesitation to intervene due to interpersonal dynamics.

synopsis: An Air Traffic Controller reported conflicting information regarding proper procedures for clearing military aircraft into block altitudes and for an Altitude Reservation (ALTRV).
summary: An air traffic controller working solo without radar assist cleared a flight of five military aircraft to a fix and altitude block 21,000–23,000 feet, despite the flight plan indicating an Altitude Reservation (ALTRV) and MARSA. The controller attributed the subsequent confusion regarding refueling operations and MARSA status to poor planning, inadequate coordination from TRACON, and a lack of proper briefing.

synopsis: A radar sector reported coordinating an altitude for an aircraft to enter another sector's non-radar airspace. The sector failed to assign the coordinated altitude.
summary: A pilot training a developmental aircraft reported that ZNY Center restricted the flight to FL350 instead of the requested FL360. After the aircraft passed a fix, ZNY contacted the Radar Controller to correct an altitude error, prompting the pilot to recommend ZMA assume airspace to reduce non-radar restrictions.

synopsis: An Air Traffic Controller reported a rocket launch protected airspace within a TRACON boundary. The TRACON was working two aircraft heading toward the airspace and had not been advised the airspace was in use.
summary: TRACON controllers providing VFR advisories were unaware a rocket launch area was active up to 28,500 feet until ARTCC notified them 2.5 hours later. The reporter attributes this to NOTAMs being hidden under different facilities instead of the ZZZ VORTAC, preventing controllers from seeing the airspace restrictions.

synopsis: A controller reported discovering an unprotected flight due to the entry of an incorrect fix estimate time for a flight plan through non-radar airspace causing the flight plan to be removed from the system.
summary: An air traffic controller discovered Aircraft X missing from the system due to a previous controller's transposed time entry at fix ZZZZZ, which caused the ATOP system to delete the flight plan. The controller manually recovered the plan, issued a descent clearance to resolve a conflict with Aircraft Y, and recommended adding time-accuracy logic checks to the system.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: PIT TRACON Controller reported that BVI Tower, a non-FAA facility, recently changed its hours to be closed on Sundays. The PIT Controller recommended the Tower be open on Sundays due to the high levels of traffic.
summary: An air traffic controller managed departures and approaches at a non-FAA tower closed on Sundays, issuing headings to avoid VFR traffic. Conflict Alerts occurred when Aircraft X and Aircraft Y encountered VFR targets, prompting the controller to recommend restoring Sunday tower hours due to high traffic volumes.

synopsis: An aircraft initiated a go-around due to a wind shear alert in the cockpit. The reporter thinks it may have been Wake Turbulence generated by a preceding B737-900.
summary: An air traffic controller advised Aircraft X on final approach that a preceding B737-900 had gone around, but Aircraft X initiated a go-around due to an onboard wind shear alert. The controller suspected the alert was actually caused by wake turbulence from the B737-900, as other traffic reported calm winds.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: A HCF Controller reported of an aircraft that was given permission to depart even though the runway was NOTAMd closed. The airport personnel were gone and the authority was given to the contractor who was also in contact with the pilot. The controller reported that he thought this was wrong.
summary: An enroute controller released Aircraft X for departure from uncontrolled OGG despite a NOTAM closing Runway 2, relying on a paving contractor's assurance rather than airport operator confirmation. The reporter believes this was incorrect because contractors cannot override official runway closures, risking passenger delays if the runway status is misjudged.

synopsis: B737-700 Captain reported operating several legs with only one operable iPad which was contrary to company procedures.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced a JeppFD-Pro update failure affecting both EFBs before departure. After taking off with a single shared EFB, the Captain realized he had incorrectly recalled loaner requirements, purchased a WiFi subscription mid-flight, and restored his EFB by landing.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported that a right overwing slide deployed at approximately 100 kts on the takeoff roll, necessitating a return to departure airport.
summary: The flight crew experienced a right wing slide deployment at 100 knots during takeoff of a 240,000-pound aircraft. Post-flight inspection revealed the slide pack door was open with the slide hanging, causing fuselage damage and noise from metal fittings striking the flap.

synopsis: B777 Captain was informed by Hong Kong Departure of an unidentified aircraft with primary radar only, opposite direction, and at an estimated altitude of 40000 feet and 350 knots. A straight wing military drone was sighted passing overhead.
summary: Hong Kong departure control alerted the heavy aircraft at low initial cruise to an unidentified, non-transponder-equipped drone estimated at 40,000 feet and 350 knots ahead. The pilot observed the drone's contrail but avoided collision due to the altitude difference, criticizing the drone operator's disregard for airway safety and ICAO rules.

synopsis: CRJ700 Captain reported a NMAC with a drone while descending to 2500 ft on the DCA River Visual Runway 19.
summary: A pilot on the CAPSS2 arrival to DCA encountered a non-military drone flying less than 150–200 feet overhead while descending for the River Visual 19. No evasive maneuvers were required, the landing was uneventful, and the incident was reported to the tower chief.

synopsis: CRJ-900 flight crew reported experiencing a low fuel state when their destination changed runway configuration due to shifting winds. The Captain was critical of company fuel policy.
summary: The flight crew encountered a fuel-critical situation during a long final approach in IMC and turbulence due to wind shifts, ATC delays, and a reverse thrust caution. The pilot attributed the outcome to the company's fuel policy providing insufficient margin for off-nominal events, resulting in a landing with only 1,200 lbs of fuel.

synopsis: A helicopter pilot reported inadvertently entering IMC, and requesting an IFR clearance and vectors to the city airport from ATC for an ILS approach.
summary: The pilot and crew encountered unforecasted deteriorating snow while en route for a hospital transfer, forcing an IIMC declaration and diversion to an airport. They executed a safe ILS approach using autopilot vectors, attributing the event to sudden weather changes despite accurate initial forecasts.

synopsis: MD11 Dispatcher was informed by a crew that they are losing oil from their number three engine. The crew elected to continue toward their destination and shut the engine down at top of descent, with zero quantity showing but still good pressure and temperature.
summary: Flight crew reported low and decreasing oil quantity in engine #3, which eventually dropped to zero while pressure and temperature remained normal. The engine shut down 32 minutes before landing, prompting ATC to provide priority handling and dispatch crash/fire services for a safe arrival.

synopsis: A flight encountered moderate turbulence during descent. One flight attendant was injured.
summary: During descent through moderate turbulence at 20,000 feet, a flight attendant fell in the aft galley and injured his left ankle. Paramedics transported the crewmember to a hospital for X-rays, resulting in a 10-day layover before he could return to duty.

synopsis: B767 flight crew reported upon coast out at RESNO an offset of R1 is entered and the FMC dropped the next waypoint. The FMC never caught the offset (LNAV course) and continued to turn to the right. The next waypoint had dropped from the FMC.
summary: The crew experienced an FMC anomaly at RESNO where the active waypoint dropped, causing the aircraft to turn north instead of intercepting the LNAV offset. Pilots intervened using HDG SEL, manually re-entered waypoint N5520, and confirmed routing with EGGX and Shanwick, suspecting a Pegasus FMC or Honeywell database issue.

synopsis: B777-200 flight crew experienced a track deviation crossing RESNO over the North Atlantic when the First Officer entered a 1R offset. The aircraft began a left turn and the N55W020 waypoint had disappeared from the FMS. The waypoint is reentered and the aircraft is returned to track.
summary: A Boeing 777-200 crew en-route at FL380 experienced a navigational error where the autopilot turned left after a right offset, likely due to an FMS anomaly dropping waypoint N55W020. The crew corrected the deviation using Heading Select and re-entered the direct route after Shanwick Oceanic alerted them to the error.

synopsis: B757 Captain reported two wake vortex encounters in trail of a B777 departing LAX.
summary: The flight crew encountered wake turbulence twice while climbing behind a B777, first at 5,000–8,000 feet and again at 20,000 feet. The captain manually turned 30 degrees right to offset the track, preventing further disturbance despite slow ATC response.

synopsis: An A320 Captain encountered extremely slippery ramp conditions and a lack of preparation by the ground crew during gate arrival at DTW. When the stop signal is received the brakes are set, but the aircraft continues to move forward due to slippery conditions and residual thrust. The engines are quickly shut down and the aircraft stops sliding.
summary: The pilot reported that while taxiing a snow-covered ramp to the gate, the aircraft slid forward despite set brakes due to residual thrust and slippery conditions. The slide stopped only after shutting down the engines, as marshals lacked chocks and the ramp was deemed unfit for arrival.

synopsis: Air carrier First Officer reported they became low on final approach resulting in a momentary GPWS alert.
summary: During an LDA 19 approach at DCA, the crew missed the WEVPU fix in the FMS database and descended below its 1,100 ft restriction to 800 ft. This triggered a GPWS Obstacle Alert, but the crew maintained visual contact and executed a safe landing.

aircraft: Embraer Jet Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A pilot of a regional jet reported executed a missed approach due to the inability to obtain a landing clearance in a timely fashion. A subsequent approach was successfully completed, however a flap limit speed was briefly exceeded.
summary: During a River Visual approach, the crew executed a go-around at 200 feet after failing to receive landing clearance due to tower communication issues. Subsequent task saturation during the missed approach caused a brief auto-throttle overspeed exceeding flaps 1 limits before the flight landed safely.

synopsis: During final approach to SFO in weather, the glideslope became intermittent. Flight crew executed a go-around and landed on the second attempt. Other crews commented about the quality of the ILS signal.
summary: The First Officer flying an ILS 19L approach into SFO in IMC and gusty winds experienced an uncommanded autopilot disconnect and a temporary glideslope signal loss. The Pilot Monitoring took control, executed a go-around at 1,000 feet due to instability, and landed safely on a second approach.

synopsis: A319 Captain was informed after parking that the Jetway may have made contact with the left engine at it was maneuvered to mate with the aircraft. No damage could be detected but Maintenance was called.
summary: While parked at the gate, ground personnel reported that a jetway driver struck the aircraft engine. The pilot observed no visible damage and deferred reporting, as local operations arranged for maintenance to inspect the area.

synopsis: A319 flight crew reported a flap overspeed on approach, citing a wake vortex encounter as contributing.
summary: The flight crew experienced an approximate 5 KIAS overspeed on a Boeing 777 during an ILS PRM 10C approach at ORD while maintaining 180 KIAS. The reporter attributed the difficulty to heavy wake turbulence and an incorrect auto-thrust re-engagement sequence that caused a temporary acceleration to 205 KIAS before landing safely.

synopsis: An air carrier Captain and First Officer reported a non-compliant passenger was removed from their aircraft in JAX.
summary: During pre-pushback, a pilot requested law enforcement to remove a non-compliant, threatening passenger who refused to stow a tray table. The passenger was handcuffed and removed after an officer noted he appeared intoxicated, while flight attendants managed the situation professionally.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air Carrier flight crew reported experiencing a medical emergency on descent. ATC was notified and was given priority handling.
summary: During arrival at 17,000 feet, the crew managed a diabetic passenger with chest pains by administering oxygen and food while expediting descent below 10,000 feet. The aircraft landed uneventfully on the right runway, where paramedics met the passenger 21 minutes after initial notification.

aircraft: MD-80 Series (DC-9-80) Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: MD-80 Engine failed during takeoff roll. Flightcrew rejected the takeoff and returned to the gate to de-plane passengers.
summary: The Captain and First Officer aborted takeoff on a de-iced aircraft after a violent engine failure caused by a detached nose bullet on Engine 2. The event resulted in heavy cabin smoke, a flight attendant requiring oxygen, and significant engine damage attributed to potential maintenance inspection gaps.

synopsis: A Flight Attendant reported on some confusion about whether a Portable Oxygen Concentrator was FAA approved.
summary: A flight attendant encountered a passenger using a Portable Oxygen Concentrator (POC) during inflight service who could not provide proof of FAA approval. The passenger admitted he showed no documentation to the gate agent, and the only card found lacked the required brand or approval details.

synopsis: Technician reported a DC-9 oil reservoir cap was left off of Number 1 engine.
summary: A mechanic signed an Airworthiness Release for a DC-9, unaware the previous shift left the #1 engine oil reservoir cap off. The aircraft flew with the cap missing, losing oil until landing with only four quarts remaining, prompting a change to inspect reservoir caps during future checks.

aircraft: Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: After towing an aircraft to the terminal, with the tow tractor disconnected, the Mechanic riding brakes left the cockpit seat before ground power was available to pressurize the hydraulic system so he could set the brakes.
summary: Two mechanics moved an aircraft from the ramp to the gate using a super tug. The aircraft rolled after the pilot left the cockpit to open a door, but the pilot re-applied brakes and maintenance repositioned the tug, resulting in no injuries, damage, or flight delays.

synopsis: When replacing an MO1 Module on an Arriel 2B1 Helicopter Engine, three bolts are removed from the MO5 Module casing to accommodate the tooling. These bolts were left off when the engine was installed.
summary: During an Arriel 2B1 engine teardown to replace the MO1 module, three mechanics overlooked three bolts required for the MO5 module tooling, which remained hidden under the exhaust despite repeated checks. The team initiated safety meetings to enforce stricter checklist adherence and ensure all procedures are followed to prevent future oversights.

aircraft: Light Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: The flight crew of a business jet reported experiencing foreign object damage to an engine at the commencement of the takeoff roll, resulting in a low speed rejected takeoff. It was later determined that the foreign object was a piece of cabin carpet that had been left on the wing to dry and went undetected prior to departure.
summary: The Pilot in Command aborted takeoff after a carpet piece, left on the wing by maintenance, was ingested into the left engine, damaging blades. The incident occurred during a dark preflight where the light-colored carpet blended with the wing, evading detection despite a flashlight inspection.

synopsis: The pilot of a C182 reported that while on a practice instrument departure with a flight instructor, the aircraft entered instrument conditions without an IFR flight plan.
summary: A pilot undergoing an instrument proficiency check with a CFII entered solid IMC shortly after takeoff while using a view-limiting device. The instructor directed a VFR flight away from terrain using GPS instead of obtaining an IFR clearance, which the pilot later identified as a safety error.

synopsis: A general aviation pilot reported the distractions that led to landing on a taxiway rather than the runway at a tower controlled airport.
summary: The pilot landed on a taxiway instead of Runway 34 during a night currency flight due to spatial disorientation caused by excessive instrument monitoring and poor dark adaptation. The pilot attributed the error to distraction over a recent cylinder issue and lack of recent pattern work, though no traffic incursions occurred.

synopsis: A C150 pilot reported the pressures that led to departing into marginal weather and resulted in a descent through IFR conditions to a precautionary landing for fuel.
summary: A senior pilot and aircraft owner flew a marginally equipped Cessna 150 into deteriorating weather due to get-there-itis and reliance on outdated reports. The pilot executed an emergency RNAV approach to an alternate airport, landing safely with only three gallons of fuel remaining after realizing the intended destination was inaccessible.

synopsis: A general aviation pilot reported an airborne conflict with two vintage military aircraft that performed a low approach and break maneuver to a landing without clear coordination with other traffic at a non-towered airport.
summary: A pilot on final for Runway 25 encountered a formation of two vintage war planes performing a low approach. Miscommunication regarding landing sequence caused a near collision when one plane entered short final ahead while the other crossed the pilot's path on base, forcing the pilot to go around.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: Air carrier flight crew experienced a seemingly false GPWS warning due to mechanical malfunction.
summary: The flight crew vectored for ILS 8 to BUR received a false GPWS "Pull Up" alert at 5,300 feet due to a radar altimeter malfunction reading zero. They climbed to 6,500 feet, deviating from ATC clearance, but confirmed the aircraft was safe and landed without incident.

synopsis: A flight instructor in a PA28 reported a runway excursion that occurred when the trainee drifted to the runway edge during landing.
summary: An instructor and a student CFI veered off the runway during landing practice in a 10-knot crosswind after the student released crosswind inputs and handed over controls late. The aircraft entered snow slush and grass but stopped undamaged, prompting the instructor to conclude they should have intervened earlier with a go-around.

synopsis: A student pilot and observing flight instructor reported an unstabilized approach during first solo flight that resulted in a loss of directional control and a runway excursion.
summary: A student pilot on their initial solo flight in a single-engine aircraft exited Runway 03 after ballooning during the flare and bouncing hard. The aircraft crossed Taxiway Alpha and stopped in the gravel with no injuries to the sole occupant.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Small aircraft pilot momentarily entered an unusual attitude while trying to correct to the BUR ILS Runway 8 after the autopilot failed to capture the approach.
summary: A pilot flying an IFR approach to KBUR in IMC failed to capture the ILS glideslope with the autopilot. The delayed manual intervention caused an unusual attitude and course deviation, requiring ATC to revector the aircraft for a successful hand-flown approach.

synopsis: A Hawker 800 Captain experienced an APU fire warning shortly after takeoff. The APU fire memory items were accomplished and the fire bottle was discharged before returning to the departure airport.
summary: During initial climb at 2,200 feet MSL, an APU fire warning sounded. The crew discharged the fire bottle, landed, and evacuated the aircraft, which was later towed to maintenance after fire crew inspection.

synopsis: Private pilot flying as a passenger in an Airbus 330 reports detecting a metallic smell prior to takeoff. He reported this to the crew and continued to experience a slight metallic taste for two weeks after the flight.
summary: A passenger reported a strong metallic smell and fumes in the rear cabin during engine spool-up for takeoff, causing dizziness and unconsciousness in nearby passengers. The crew attributed the incident to the aircraft's age and promised maintenance checks, but the passenger continues to experience symptoms two weeks later.

aircraft: M-20 Series Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A ZBW Controller used MOCA incorrectly for an altitude clearance with an aircraft off airways. The Controller recommends to become more knowledgeable regarding MOCAs ad MEAs.
summary: An air traffic controller cleared Aircraft X direct VLV to avoid climbing, incorrectly assuming a 4,000-foot MOCA applied to the current segment. This error triggered a Minimum Safe Altitude Warning as the aircraft approached the 7,400-foot Minimum IFR Altitude block near Mt. Katahdin.

synopsis: ARTCC Controller reported of a rocket launch they thought had been cancelled. Moments later pilots reported seeing a rocket airborne. Controller reported this to the Front Line Manager.
summary: Air traffic controllers received conflicting information regarding a rocket launch status, initially being told it was scrubbed before multiple aircraft reported it airborne. The supervisor's verification of the scrub status was later contradicted by confirmation of the launch, highlighting a need for improved communication.

synopsis: An A90 Controller reported of a situation involving an aircraft that was near emergency fuel. The controller reported this to Front Line Manager (FLM) and was aware that the runway was closed. The controller wanted runway to be opened for aircraft. Communication problems were cited.
summary: Air Traffic Controllers managed Aircraft X, which reported 15 minutes of fuel remaining, while Massport treated the runway. The situation escalated due to the Front Line Manager's emotional unresponsiveness and lack of urgency, forcing controllers to bypass coordination to ensure the aircraft landed before fuel exhaustion.

synopsis: B737 Captain experienced stick shaker at rotation and after determining that the Captain's instruments are faulty, control is transferred to the First Officer. With the aircraft flying normally the crew elected to continue to destination. Post flight inspection revealed a damaged AOA vane on the Captain's side.
summary: The Pilot Flying and Captain experienced a continuous stick shaker and multiple instrument discrepancies during climbout caused by a damaged Captain's side AOA vane. They continued to destination using standby instruments but violated Flight Operations Manual limitations by pulling the stick shaker circuit breaker to silence the warning.

synopsis: B737-300 First Officer expressed concerns with TRACON's excessive clearance changes during arrival to SFO airport.
summary: Pilots reported multiple ATC clearance changes and non-standard phraseology during the SFO arrival, including a confusing Class B airspace call and a last-minute side-step to Runway 28R. Although the crew managed the high workload without incident, the frequent changes created a high potential for error and safety hazards.

synopsis: B737 flight crew reported on airspeed difficulties on the ILS, followed by a bounced landing and go-around at MPTO.
summary: Pilots on an RNAV ILS 03R approach into MPTO were left high by ATC speed restrictions, causing a momentary low-speed event with a stick shaker. A firm touchdown in gusty winds resulted in a bounce, prompting a go-around and a subsequent safe landing.

synopsis: A B737 Flight Crew reported being informed by a Flight Attendant of smoke coming from an aft lavatory trash bin just after level off at FL330. ATC is advised and the flight returns to the departure airport. The smoke quickly dissipates during the descent and no charred paper is found in the trash bin. At the gate a passenger admits to having smoked an E-cigarette and blowing the smoke into the trash bin.
summary: The flight crew returned to the departure airport after smoke from an aft lav trash bin, caused by a passenger vaping an e-cigarette, was reported at FL330. The crew executed emergency checklists, descended with ATC priority, and landed safely with fire personnel on standby.

synopsis: B737 flight crew approaching minimums on an RNAV approach a crew received a GPWS terrain caution. The crew climbed back to the correct the approach path and landed.
summary: During an RNAV approach in rain, the crew received GPWS terrain and obstacle cautions after inadvertently entering Level Change mode instead of maintaining VNAV Path. The Captain arrested the descent, climbed back to the approach path, and landed safely after visually verifying the aircraft's position.

synopsis: B767-400 flight crew experienced a bird strike at 300 feet after takeoff causing fan vibration. The engine was idled but kept running and the center tank fuel was dumped, before returning to land 5,000 pounds overweight.
summary: A B767-400 crew struck a large bird at 300 feet during a reduced power takeoff, causing right engine vibration. They completed checklists, dumped fuel, and made a normal landing 5,000 lbs over limit before shutting down the affected engine.

synopsis: A300 flight crew experienced an intermittent smoke indication, so they returned to the departure airport.
summary: The Captain and First Officer experienced intermittent Main Deck Cargo Smoke Detector Loop B warnings during climb on an A300 carrying dangerous goods. They returned to the departure airport and landed safely with no fire or smoke found, attributing the event to a faulty detection system.

synopsis: B767-300 Captain experienced a TE FLAP ASYM EICAS message as the flaps were extended to 30 during approach, with no roll or other indication on the flap gauge. The Captain elected to go-around and perform QRH procedures before returning to land with flaps 30.
summary: During an ILS final approach at 1500 AGL, a crew of three pilots executed a go-around after receiving a TE FLAP ASYM EICAS message and inoperative auto-throttles. They managed configuration warnings and terrain avoidance while declaring an emergency, eventually completing a second normal approach and landing with ARFF escort.

synopsis: MD-83 Captain reported that only the TA function of the TCAS system was operational and requested clearance into non-RVSM airspace.
summary: The Pilot Flying reported a TCAS 'TA only' indication during cruise, initially requesting a descent to non-RVSM airspace before the message cleared. When the fault reappeared, the crew descended to FL280, where the TCAS indication resolved shortly after leveling.

synopsis: While troubleshooting an MD83 Nose Landing Gear (NLG) issue, a Lead Mechanic rode on the NLG Wheel well while the aircraft was taxing.
summary: A mechanic rode in the nose wheel well during taxi to diagnose a loud thump on an aircraft with a history of nose gear issues. The reporter approved this unsafe action due to staffing and pressure, later admitting it was a poor decision despite believing no safety risk existed.

synopsis: B747 First Officer described a descent for approach that culminates in a missed approach due to the aircraft being too high and fast to continue, from about 1,600 feet AGL. The decision is made to circle to land visually and again the aircraft is high and fast, but the unstabilized approach is continued to landing with both First Officers suggesting another go-around.
summary: The flight crew executed an unstabilized ILS approach with excessive descent rates, ignoring multiple SINK RATE and PULL UP warnings to land firmly. Mechanics subsequently reported left wing flap damage and classified the event as a hard landing, resulting in an Airplane on the Ground status.

aircraft: Cessna Aircraft Undifferentiated or Other Model
synopsis: A Cessna pilot reported a possible HOU Class B airspace violation while receiving ATC Flight Following service.
summary: A pilot flying a local flight from KSGR requested and received clearance to 3,500 feet, potentially entering Class Bravo airspace, before diverting back to KSGR due to a sick passenger. The controller noted the aircraft was in the Houston Hobby approach corridor, but the pilot reported no formal violation or incident occurred.

synopsis: DA20 Instructor reported sighting a drone in PVU Class D airspace and reported it to the Tower.
summary: A pilot descending through 6000 to 5500 feet MSL in PVU Class Delta airspace observed an unmanned drone at 5500 feet MSL. The pilot reported the drone sighting to the control tower.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Retractable Gear
synopsis: Small aircraft pilot became distracted and landed gear up.
summary: The pilot, instructing a passenger during a busy enroute phase, executed a gear-up landing after a last-minute runway change and distraction caused him to skip the pre-landing checklist. The propeller struck the runway, settling the aircraft on its fuselage and causing an abrupt stop.

aircraft: Small Aircraft; Low Wing; 1 Eng; Fixed Gear
synopsis: The pilot of a general aviation aircraft reported a near mid air collision with an aircraft descending into a nearby airport. Several other similar occurrences were reported to have been observed in the area.
summary: Pilots on two training flights departing Runway 18 reported that flight school aircraft from a nearby airport penetrated their departure leg and traffic pattern at X52. One aircraft crossed overhead missing by 300 feet, forcing an avoidance turn, while the pilots attributed the incidents to the intruders ignoring local airfields.

synopsis: PA28R pilot experienced total electrical failure during practice instrument approaches to CXO in VMC. He elected to divert to his home field. After manually extending the gear and using a handheld transceiver, he landed safely.
summary: A pilot and safety pilot flying a practice RNAV approach lost all electrical power and radios due to a displaced alternator belt. They returned to the departure airport, manually extended the landing gear, and landed safely after confirming gear position via ground inspection.

synopsis: ZKC ARTCC sector requested an aircraft be routed around its airspace due to weather and traffic saturation deviating for the weather. The request was denied. An aircraft was issued a vector to avoid another aircraft but the vector was not enough to maintain required lateral separation.
summary: An air traffic controller reported a near-miss between Aircraft X and Y caused by sector saturation from weather deviations and poor TMU routing. The controller manually resolved the conflict with a turn and descent, noting that lost separation occurred due to inadequate preplanning and failure to reroute traffic around severe weather.

synopsis: Air Carrier pilot is diagnosed with Sleep Apnea by his AME. When filling out information requested by the Aerospace Medical Certification Division he discovered that he may not exercise the privileges of his Medical Certificate until the required documentation provide. There is also a 90 day window to comply and he is not sure if he is in compliance with the regulation.
summary: A pilot diagnosed with Obstructive Sleep Apnea flew multiple trips while awaiting FAA medical certification review after starting C-PAP therapy. The pilot realized they may have violated regulations prohibiting flight privileges until documentation was submitted and plans to contact authorities to determine their legal status.

aircraft: Medium Large Transport; Low Wing; 2 Turbojet Eng
synopsis: After breaking out at 1,400 feet on the RNAV Y 13C at MDW, a Captain discovered that the PAPI lights were not operational, a requirement to shoot the approach during night time, and elects to continue to landing. The Tower indicates the PAPI's are NOTAMed out, but this proves not to be true. All approaches to Runways 13C and 4R at MDW require VGSI for night landings.
summary: The pilot landed an aircraft at MDW on Runway 13C at night after visibility dropped, despite the required PAPI lights being inoperative and not listed in NOTAMs. The crew landed safely but reported that Tower incorrectly claimed the lights were NOTAMed out, highlighting a failure to verify required equipment status before activating the runway.

synopsis: Super tug driver reported being physically injured by the stiff suspension and bouncy ride that it produces.
summary: A ground crew member reported injuries to the testicle and back caused by excessive bouncing on a super tug with a suspension issue.

synopsis: Captain experienced an EGPWS terrain warning at 3,000 feet outside KESLO on the RNAV Runway 08 at MDPP and goes around. On the next approach the aircraft is fully configured and slowed by KESLO and no warning is experienced.
summary: The Captain encountered a nuisance EPGWS terrain warning prior to the FAF on an RNAV approach to runway 08 at MDPP in IMC and heavy rain. The crew executed an escape maneuver to MSA, re-sequenced the approach, and attributed the warning to terrain susceptibility affecting A320 equipment.

synopsis: Embraer Phenom 300 flight crew experienced a brake failure after touchdown. Emergency air brakes were used to stop but the right brake locked up and the right tire burst.
summary: The flight crew of a Phenom aircraft experienced a brake failure immediately after touchdown on a dry alternate runway, triggering a BRAKE FAIL CAS message. The pilot applied emergency brakes, causing the right main tire to burst and the aircraft to stop on the right side of the runway without fire or evacuation.

synopsis: The pilot of a C402 reported a rejected takeoff when a loss of engine power was observed.
summary: The pilot monitoring felt and heard a loss of power on one engine at 80 knots during takeoff, prompting an abort. The pilot assumed control, suspected the right engine, and returned to the ramp where no defects were found, though a logbook discrepancy was filed.

synopsis: Air carrier Captain executed a go-around at minimums after an ILS approach to Runway 7 at MZBZ and enters holding. The second approach is successful, but with no full length taxiway, a turn around and back taxi is required to clear the runway. During the back taxi a Cessna Caravan commences an approach without clearance and is reluctant to go-around when the air carrier aircraft is detected on the runway.
summary: A B737 crew landed at BZE in low visibility while a Cessna Caravan, operating without ATC clearance, descended toward the runway. The Caravan passed within 50–75 feet of the B737's vertical stabilizer after the B737 crew ordered a go-around, highlighting a lack of ATC control and safety oversight.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew reported returning to departure airport following loss of Number 1 engine shortly after takeoff.
summary: The First Officer flying and Captain monitoring received a #1 engine fire warning at 600 feet AGL. The crew executed the QRH, returned to the departure airport for an auto-land, and taxied to the ramp with two engines after a fire department scan.

synopsis: MD-11 flight crew reported Number 2 engine flamed out at initial taxi and smoke was reported coming from the engine, so the fire bottle was discharged and the flight returned to the gate.
summary: During taxi with three engines running, the #2 engine flamed out and emitted smoke, prompting the crew to shut down the engine and discharge one fire bottle. The aircraft was towed back to the gate after fire crews found no visible damage, attributed to an unknown engine or system malfunction.

synopsis: Air carrier pilot stated that the training provided by the company for the new Lido app for the iPad, was inadequate and that critical information often requires too many keystrokes to bring up.
summary: A pilot reported that mPilot CBT training and the company Training Bulletin fail to cover critical app functions, such as locating ARINC maps and Inoperative Component Tables. The reporter warns that complex navigation steps and inconsistent terminology could lead to poor operational decisions and flight disruptions.

synopsis: MD-83 Crew reported a loss of pressurization. Crew descended to lower altitude, ran the QRH procedures and were able to regain pressurization. Crew climbed back to altitude and were able to continue to destination.
summary: During cruise at 30,000 feet, a crew experienced rapid depressurization due to a faulty left pack pressure gauge indicating normal operation while the pack was actually off. After an emergency descent to 13,000 feet and troubleshooting, the crew identified the gauge error, restored cabin pressure, and continued the flight.

synopsis: The pilot of a Decathlon reported electing to land in the grass adjacent to a closed runway when the gusty winds made the crossing runway a safety concern.
summary: The pilot of a tailwheel aircraft, facing low fuel and gusty crosswinds exceeding demonstrated limits, landed in a grass area parallel to a closed runway to land into the wind. This action violated local rules but was executed for safety without incident.

synopsis: CE510 pilot reported continuing descent after loss of the glideslope signal on approach into HKY.
summary: The pilot flying a GPS 6 LP approach into HKY experienced an unreliable glide path signal during descent. The pilot leveled off at 2,700 feet MSL, disconnected the autopilot, and completed a safe landing using LNAV.

synopsis: Several Air Traffic Controllers reported an aircraft on a Visual Approach that landed at the wrong airport.
summary: A pilot landed at the wrong airport (ZZZ1) instead of ZZZ during a visual approach in marginal weather while a trainee controller was distracted by another departure. The incident resulted from pilot confusion regarding airport proximity and controller inattention, though the pilot later departed ZZZ1 and landed safely at ZZZ.

synopsis: ATC reported a VFR transition aircraft and an IFR departure aircraft that passed close enough for one aircraft to receive an RA.
summary: An air traffic controller failed to issue traffic alerts due to inattention, causing a VFR aircraft climbing to 2,000 feet and an IFR departing jet to pass in close proximity. The IFR pilot declared a resolution advisory, and the controller requested release from Local Control duties.

synopsis: ATC reported allowing an aircraft to be routed through Military Special Use Airspace at the time it went active.
summary: Air traffic controllers and a trainee in a busy sector inadvertently allowed Aircraft X to enter active military airspace while climbing from 18,000 to 20,000 feet due to missed activation notifications. The controller subsequently coordinated a climb to 28,000 feet to exit the airspace, citing inadequate warning systems as the cause of the violation.

synopsis: A ZME Front Line Manager (FLM) reported of a loss of separation due to an aircraft getting a mountain wave and descending. The other aircraft first reported to ATC that they were descending for traffic.
summary: An R-side controller managed moderate traffic when Aircraft Y lost altitude due to mountain wave turbulence, causing a separation conflict with descending Aircraft X. The controller resolved the situation by coordinating lateral separation and returning both aircraft to their assigned altitudes.
